name: Gretta
description: Gretta is 61 years old and widowed with two children, one of whom in school. Gretta works very hard to provide for them. She runs a general store in the Philippines and has requested a PHP 29,500 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like shampoo, groceries, etc.  Gretta has been in this business for five years. She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Loun's Group
description: Loun is aged 50 and widowed. She has four children. Living in a village of the Sangke district, Loun has been farming rice and raising pigs for 15 years. She is able to earn about 47,000 KHR per day to support her family’s need.   This is the sixth loan for Loun with VisionFund. She completely repaid the past five loans, which have enabled her family to support her family. Now she is leading her group to ask for a loan. As the leader, she is going to use her portion to by pig feed and piglets for raising. She hopes to fatten her pigs so as to make a better living.

name: Jose Manuel
description: For thirteen years, José has worked hard to help his family get ahead through his plantain sales business. Because of this, he is always investing. Previously, he had requested a loan to stock up on plantains and improve his sales. The results were positive, which is why he is very thankful to the people who supported him. Now, a new sales season is approaching and José thinks that a new investment is necessary. For this reason, he is requesting a new loan that he will use to buy more plantains in large quantities. This will help him save money in his purchases and to project more income, which will allow him to continue growing professionally and personally. After paying back the loan, he is thinking of seeking out new customers in other areas.

name: Ramzana
description: Ramzana is a 39-year-old married woman and a mother of five children. She is a hardworking and independent mother who is helping her family by providing tailoring services at her home. She has been doing this for the past ten years. She very well knows the techniques of stitching. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community.   She started sewing clothes after the birth of her two children, when she observed that her husband couldn't provide everything necessary for them. Then she decided to start tailoring work at home and since then she has been sewing clothes for her community. She wants to enhance the beauty of her craft so she would like to buy a Juki sewing machine. The professionals use this machine for tailoring because of its speed and fine performance.  She knows the techniques of tailoring very well. Her regular customers are mostly her neighbors, relatives and the local community. She has requested a loan to buy a new Juki sewing machine and some packs of zippers and buttons to meet the increasing demand.  Ramzana is very thankful to Kiva and its field partner, BRAC Pakistan.

name: Maa Kalhuni Shg Group
description: Santilata, the lady standing second from left in the first row is a 50-year-old lady who lost her husband in 2004. Since then, she has taken on all the burdens of her family. She lives with her daughter, age 23, and her son, age 20. After her husband passed away, she became involved in an agriculture activity. This is not sufficient to manage her family, so she purchased a cow. Now she is taking care of her cow and selling milk in the local market. From this business, she earns 2,000 to 2,500 INR per month. She wants to purchase one more cow and continue her milk business. She has one year of experience in this field and she has time to take care of the cow.   Santilata, along with her group, requested a loan of 165,000 INR. She will use her portion to purchase a jersey cow and fodder for her cows. She says that this business can strengthen her economic condition and she can pay her children's tuition. She has a dream of educating her children so they can earn for themselves in the future. She does not want her children to face the same kinds of problems in the future.

name: Josephina
description: Josephina proceeds to volunteer as a Camfed Learner Guide. She teaches students in secondary school about life skills sessions.   Her business involves women clothes. She is requesting a Kiva loan in order to develop her women clothes selling business, by purchasing women clothes in town for cheap prices, and then sell them in her shop to get enough profit.   She plans to use the profit she will earn to support her family with daily basic needs. The social interest on her loan will be repaid by Josephina's weekly two and a half hours of volunteering.

name: Mujeres Unidas Group
description: This group is called Women United (Mujeres Unidas) because that is what they are: women who are united and who work and fight for their families. They are in their first loan cycle of the women's committee program, where they all work and help each other get ahead. The group is now performing the [Poverty] Eradication Survey, which identified one of its members [as living below the poverty line]: Andresa. Andresa makes a living selling cleaning products, bleach, and fabric softener that she prepares herself. (We should also note the work performed by the Paraguayan foundation, which continuously follows through with training and accountability programs. They manage to place demands on women while simultaneously motivating them to work hard to overcome poverty.) Andresa is requesting a loan to purchase containers, chemicals, etc., which will help her execute her business plan and improve her income.

name: Shamim's Group
description: Shamim is the mother of seven children; four of them do different kinds of work while the other three are getting an education.  She is a widow whose husband died a few years ago leaving her alone in this world to fight for her and her children’s survival.  She never gave up and started sewing clothes for her local clients.    Now her sons are grown up and they have taken the financial responsibility on their shoulders.  Shamim has applied for a loan for her son who drives a rickshaw which he rents. Now he wants to buy his own rickshaw to minimize his expenses and increase his income.    Shamim is a regular client of Asasah and her credit behavior is very good. This is her fifth year with Asasah.

name: Yudelka
description: Yudelka is an individual loan client with Esperanza. Her story is representative of Esperanza's Haitian and Dominican clients (many of whom recently emigrated to the DR from Haiti). In El Seybo, where she is located, running water (none of which is potable) and electricity are unreliable. She makes her home in a simple structure here, as a single mother with her child.  Yudelka is excited to be taking her seventh total loan and third individual loan with Esperanza after having successfully repaid her previous loan and grown her business. She plans to use this loan to invest in her business raising livestock by purchasing two cows which she will use to produce milk and eventually meat. She will use the profits to save towards the purchase of more land to continue to expand her farm, as well as provide for the needs of her child. She thanks you all for your support.

name: Perlie
description: Perlie is 42 years old and lives in Salimpono, Panaon, Misamis Occidental. She is married with two children who are now at their school age. Perlie earns mainly from their (public utility vehicle) PUV-Van and motorcycle for hire business for the past four years. At present, she is serving as a Barangay Treasurer in her community. She earns approximately PHP 6,000 each month doing this type of business activity.   She has requested a loan to be used in purchasing 2 heads of calves as her new line of livelihood activity. Perlie has been a member of PMPC for 12 years. In the future, Perlie hopes to purchase additional units of PUV-Vans for hire to add to their daily income.

name: Norely
description: Norely is a single woman and is 28 years old.  She has had her business for 4 years, which is the sale of mattresses for different sizes of beds: fulls, singles,  cradle-size, etc.  This entrepreneur has demonstrated that she is a responsible, hard-working person with a desire to overcome, which has permitted her to fulfill her dream to have the tools of her trade. Thanks to the support the Fundación León 2000 has offered with the loan, she wants this to buy more mattresses for sale now that the demand and her customers have increased.

name: Dụng
description: Mr Dụng is 44 years old and married. He has had a service business, laying bricks for more than 10 years.  Dụng lives in Bim Son town, a semi-urban town in Thanh Hoa province. His family is a low-income household in the village. Moreover, his job is unstable .    One of the most critical difficulties that concerns him is not having clean water to use. He is requesting a loan to purchase sand, cement, bricks and equipment to install a clean water system.  This is Dụng's first loan with Thanh Hoa Microfinance Institution. With his business profits, Dụng hopes for his business to do well, to make enough money to provide for his kids, and for his family to be healthy and happy.

name: Phuong
description: Phuong is 55 years old and is married. She has 7 children and lives with them and husband in Ho Chi Minh City. She and her husband have been raising and selling pigs for 5 years. She intends to use her loan to buy food stuff and buy more baby pigs. She hopes her business runs smoothly and will help her to improve her family's living conditions and allow her to save money for her children's education.

name: Mary
description: Mary is an ambitious woman who has a business selling clothes and is also a farmer. She plans to use the loan to buy a water tank to use to collect water during the rainy season. The project will take two weeks to complete and benefit six family members and many neighbors. She is applying for a loan of KES 21,000. The client faces a lack of sufficient water to drink. This is her third loan with SMEP DTM, the previous loan being KES 20,000, which was repaid fully. Family members and the neighboring community will benefit from the project.

name: Merlyn
description: Merlyn solely provides for her child's living. She has been running a transportation services business for more than three years, and she earns well for their needs. She had successfully repaid her previous loan used for her vehicle.   Recently, she had borrowed a new loan from GDMPC micro credit to purchase a new set of tires to improve the services. She always want to improve their living situation in the near future.

name: Carmenza Idalia
description: Carmenza, 59, is a woman dedicated to her home. She has spent the vast majority of her life looking after the well-being and education of her four children. Her children are now adults, and therefore Carmenza decided to set up her own business to keep her occupied and to generate an income to help her husband with the household costs. Her business is located in the living room of her home but she wants to make changes in the courtyard of her home to offer a better service and gain larger profits. For this reason, Carmenza is seeking a loan which she will invest in the purchase of seats and laying a cement floor as her courtyard is of soil.  Carmenza asserts that as long as there is life, there is hope, and that despite her age, her ultimate dream is to become a business woman.

name: Vu Thi Kieu
description: Mrs. L. is 30 years old and lives in the Nghe An Province, in Vietnam. She joined TYM in 2005. She has two children who go to school. Mrs. L. first successfully completed a loan with TYM to start her own family motor-bike repair shop, which is her family's main source of income. With a steady source of profit, Mrs. L.’s shop is able to provide her family with the stability it needs.  Mrs. L. would like to borrow $600 to buy tools and invest in her family’s motorbike repair shop.

name: Juana
description: Juana belongs to the village bank "Manuela de Hoy," located in the district of Ilave, in the province of El Collao, in the department of Puno.  She is 45 years old, married, and the mother of three children.  She completed her primary education.   She has worked with the Manuela Ramos Movement for five years. Her first loan was for 300 soles (about 100 dollars) which she used for the purchase of small livestock.  At this time, she requires another loan of 3000 soles (about 1000 dollars) for the purchase of cattle to fatten and sell at the fairs in Ilave.  Her goal is to continue her business and be able to buy cattle at wholesale, to achieve greater profit.  She likes to save and enjoys the meetings of her village bank.Translated from Spanish by Cathy Coffman, Kiva Volunteer

name: Blanca Lorena
description: Blanca tiene 20 años de edad, vive en unión libre su conviviente trabaja al jornal tiene un hijo Deivid de 2 años de edad, viven en el campo, hace  tres años inicio a criar chanchos, los compra pequeños los cuida, alimenta, luego los vende le gusta mucho su trabajo porque siempre pasa junto a su pequeño niño sin tener que ir al jornal. Blanca con el dinero construirá una chanchera y comprara 4 cerdos, aspira mejorar el cuidado, generar mayores ingresos para ayudar a su esposo con los gastos básicos de este hogar su mayor aspiración es tener una casa propia.Blanca is 20 years old.  She is in a common-law relationship.  Her partner works as a day laborer. She has a two-year-old son Deivid.   They live in the country.  Three years ago she began to raise pigs. She bought them as piglets, cared for them, fed them and later sold them.  She liked this work a lot because she could always spend time with her little son and not have to go out daily to work.Blanca is 20 years old and lives in a common-law relationship. Her partner works as a laborer, and they have a two-year-old son named Deivid. They live in the country. Three years ago she started raising pigs. She buys them when they are small, cares for them and feeds them, and then sells them. She likes her work very much because she is able to spend her days with her young son instead of going out to work. With the loan money Blanca will build a pigsty and buy 4 pigs. She wants to improve

name: Alimardon
description: Alimardon has been living in the Jilikul district of Tajikistan for the past 27 years.  He is married.  He and his wife live with his parents.  They do not have children yet but would love to have some.  Alimardon wants to be a successful entrepreneur and to be financially stable, so that his children can be proud of him one day, and so that he can provide them with everything and give them a good education.  With all these goals in mind, Alimardon is taking a loan which will help him to start a new business.  He is planning to start raising some small livestock (sheep) at home.  He already has a barn which is ready for livestock, and he also has some animal feed.  The only thing he still needs help with is the purchase of livestock.  With this new business, Alimardon will be able to bring home a stable source of income.

name: Justin
description: Imagine going about mundane daily tasks at your small business when, all of a sudden, the assistant of an incredibly famous celebrity walks in and places a large order. This is how Justin felt when he realized that one of his customers was musical artist Nicki Minaj’s assistant. It was probably, he says, one of his proudest moments as a business owner.   After years of working for a wireless internet company, Justin started BK Bottles in January of 2013 because he wanted to earn a living by working for himself. BK Bottles is a spirits store, which he owns and operates by himself, and which allows him to support his mother and himself.  Justin hopes to continue to improve his store and make a net positive impact on his community. However, his greatest difficulty has been keeping the store stocked with the necessary amount of products to meet customer demand. The purpose of this loan is to purchase more inventory.

name: Niño Jesus Group
description: This group, from the city of Encarnacíon, is on its third loan with the "Comité de Mujeres" (Women's Committee).  The group includes 17 women who came together to work, but at this time only 15 of them are taking out a loan.  One of the members of the group is Mirian.  She has a pantry in her house where she has all kinds of basic essential goods, which are needed by her neighbors.  She is married to Eligio, who works for a company.  They have 2 children, on whose behalf they both work relentlessly so they can give them everything they need to have a life without deprivation.  Mirian says that thanks to her group and the support of her friends, she has been able to grow a lot and progress.  She is asking for this loan to be able to invest in buying goods for her pantry to sell, such as meat, vegetables, baked goods, dairy products, etc.

name: Ibrahim
description: Ibrahim is a 63-year-old married man and father of two children.  He has worked as a journal reporter for the past 10 years.  He loves his work and is talented at what he does.    Ibrahim is an Al Majmoua borrower (Kiva partner) of 2 cycles.  His previous loan helped him a lot to cover a family need and he was in good standing repaying the borrower.  Today, his second loan is also requested to cover a certain family need which is very important for his family members’ health.  He will make necessary home maintenance to avoid rain leakage and will also paint where necessary.    Ibrahim is very proud and happy with his cooperation with Al Majmoua.  This is because he has a limited salary that does not afford urgent, unplanned (yet necessary) things.  Through his Al Mjamoua loans, however, he was capable of handling these.

name: George
description: George is 32 years old and single. He runs a retail shop located in the Tena Estate off outering road, where he has a good flow of customers. He was introduced to KADET LTD by the credit officer in charge of the Eastlands office.  George has been in this business for three years and earns a monthly profit of Ksh 20,000.  He has applied for a second loan of Ksh 29,500 from KADET LTD to add stocks of flour, sugar, cooking oil and sweets to his retail shop. If the loan boosts his business, he plans to open another shop.   George hopes to operate a wholesale shop. He describes himself as a very hardworking man.

name: Lesina
description: Lesina is a 42-year-old, married woman with six children.  She has a small plantation and grows taro, taamu and bananas to earn a living.  She has been doing this for many years.  Lesina has requested a loan to buy chemicals, filings, a wheelbarrow and some taro roots. She has been a member of SBPD since 2009. With her profits, Lesina hopes to improve her housing and to support her children’s education.

name: Timoteo
description: Timoteo, is a 69 year old person, his studies were completed up to 9th grade, the reason why he wasn't able to continue with his studies is because at that time high school didn't exist, so he started working in agriculture with his father.  Later, as time went by, he worked in a metal shop and continues to work in that activity today.  His family includes his wife, who sells corn tortillas and two children a girl and a boy, both in school, the girl is in 7th grade and is 12 years old, the boy is in 4th grade and is 6 years old.  The children help her mom to fill the tortilla orders that come to their house.  Timoteo has the shop at his residence, he makes balconies, windows and doors for houses.  He also makes metal bodywork for pick up trucks; he has 20 years of experience, he is very well known in the area.  He learned this trade at a shop that used to be in the city. He then got ready to quit the shop, saved some money to buy some equipment he needed to start a shop and decided to start a shop of his own, he saw that he could earn a lot of money by being independent than being an employee, he also works distributing water to people that need it.  The loan requested is to buy 100 kg of iron, electrodes and to fix or purchase a new welding machine, he also wants to fix a mechanical issue his car has.  The loan he requested will improve his life conditions, because he will have materials to continue working, he indicates that in the future he hopes to finish fixing his house that needs wall touch-ups to have it finally completed.

name: Gener
description: Being a responsible father, Gener aims to improve his farming business to generate sufficient income and satisfy the necessities of his family. He is 45 years old and has three children attending school. Despite the hardship of living, he has the determination to uplift their status of living and educate all his children.   To improve his farming business, he is asking for a loan of 25,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) to buy herbicide, fertilizers and certified seeds, and pay the expenses incurred in vegetable production. He is hoping that his loan will be granted to be able for him to improve the business.

name: Munkhjargal
description: Mr. Munkhjargal, 55 years old, lives alone in Kherlen, an eastern town of Mongolia. He has been growing and selling vegetables to local people for many years. Recently the well he used for irrigation dried up and this incident caused his seed planting schedule to be delayed. He is requesting a loan of 1,500,000 MNT to cover the cost of digging a well on his land. After digging this well and connecting up the irrigation system, he will be able to plant his seeds immediately. He usually grows cabbage, potatoes and carrots. In his town, he is well known for his hardworking and stern character.

name: Flor Maria
description: Flor is a 33 year-old single mother who lives in her parent's home in the Nueva Arica district of Chiclayo.  Flor is a very cheerful person who is well-known and loved in her neighborhood.  She has very good personal references.  Flor has a business raising and selling small animals (guinea pigs, hens, turkeys and pigs) in her district.  She is a hardworking mother who works every day to provide for her small child.  Flor is requesting a loan of 500 Peruvian soles from Edpyme Alternativa, which she will use to purchase nutritionally balanced feed for her animals.  She wants her animals to be of the best quality so that she can sell them at the best prices.  With her earnings from this activity she wants to buy more animals and in this way expand her business.  Flor is a woman who has a strong desire to succeed, and she also has credit experience with our institution.

name: Ferlie
description: As a married parent of four children, Ferlie works hard to support her family.  She has a buy and sell vegetable business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from farming rice. Ferlie is borrowing PHP 20,000 through NWTF to  buy vegetables to sell for her buy and sell vegetable business.  Ferlie has been sustaining her business activities through her past 21 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Vera
description: Vera is a 34-year-old business woman from Liberia. She is a widow and has seven children, all between the ages of 15 and 9 years old.  She describes herself as hardworking. She lives in Nimba, a county in Liberia that shares a border with Guinea and Cote D’Ivoire. Because of its status as a border county, trade is the primary activity in the region. It also has the second highest population in Liberia.  Vera has a shop which has sold drinks such as soft drinks, alcoholic beverages, tissue, and water for the past five years. She works 10 hours at her business. Her greatest challenge in business is the rainy season. She intends to use the loan to buy more goods to sell. Vera started her business with money from her children. She likes her business because it keeps her busy. She hopes to one day buy a car.   Vera is grateful for your support!

name: Hellen
description: Hellen A., currently in the business of selling charcoal, is requesting a loan to buy a motor-bike to transport her product to market.  Hellen, 30 years old and married to a security guard, has four children, all students.  With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to build a house.  BRAC's holistic approach to poverty alleviation and empowerment of the poor encompasses a range of core programs in economic and social development, health, education, human rights and legal services which are delivered through an extensive network of village organizations. BRAC has become one of the world's largest NGOs as measured by the scale and diversity of its interventions.    In 2007, BRAC started operations in Southern Sudan. The microfinance program, which is targeted towards returning war refugees, has already formed 418 village organizations, with more than 14,000 women members.

name: Sor
description: Sor M., aged 30, is married and resides with her two children in Kampong Chnang Province, Cambodia. She is engaged in a business providing public phone services and selling cosmetic products, earning an income of USD 1.9 per day to help cover the family's expenses. Her husband is a teacher, earning an income of USD 3 per day. Their standard of living has improved since Sor M. and her husband have had these businesses. She is requesting a loan of USD 800 to purchase more cosmetic products to sell. This is her second loan from CREDIT, a Kiva partner. (Sor M.'s husband is pictured.)

name: Rhoaina
description: Rhoaina is 37 years old and married. She has two children who are in school. Rhoaina works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a general store in the Philippines. Rhoaina has been in this business for eight years.  She requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more stocks to sell like shampoo, juices, milk, coffee, sugar, etc.  In the future, Rhoaina would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Saidjon
description: T. Saidjon has been raising livestock for 5 years. He learned the necessary skills from by watching his father care for their livestock during his earliest years. He has a good flock, including a pedigree bull and a milk cow. Mr. T. Saidjon raises and sells livestock, and also he works on the collective farm. Mr. T. Saidjon has a good reputation.   Mr. T. Saidjon is applying to KIVA for a business development loan of 2100 STJ ($625 USD) for 6 months to buy rams to expand his sheep business. He thanks KIVA for the support that KIVA provides to small entrepreneurs.

name: Hamrokul
description: Hamrokul A. is a father of 6 children. His wife works on a collective farm. Hamrokul works as a shepherd for the collective farm. He is good at livestock breeding and has had livestock business since he was young. This helps him support his large family. Four of his children go to community college. Hamrokul is applying for a loan because he would like to expand his business.  Translated from Russian by Oksana Buranbaeva, Kiva Volunteer

name: Lemoe
description: Lemoe A. Y. is a member of  the Samatau 3 center. She is thirty-four years of age and one of the successful businesswomen within the programme. Her business is fishing. Her father and brothers are the ones that actually do the fishing. The fishing can be done in the  day time but usually they prefer to do it at night. Lemoe is on her fifth loan and she is still doing the fishing business .Her income for a week is $300.00 tala and $1800.00 a week profit. She explained that fishing is a profitable business and also a very risky one. Lemoe dreamed of having a big boat so that her father and brother will fish more so that her business will become an industry where she and her family can export to the overseas market for a better price. Lemoe is asking for a loan of $1200  to buy fishing nets, hooks and other equipment.

name: Santos
description: Santos is a 53 year old man who has a common-law wife and 2 children. He lives in his own house with his children. The house is located in Caserío Tierras Duras in the district of La Matanza and has electrical service and town water. The place is a community of approximately 80 families. Santos works selling fish and transporting passengers in a motorcycle-taxi. He sells the fish in the local market. He also works as a farmer and has 1 hectare of land where he grows the zarandaja variety of bean, which grow well. He has been doing this for about 20 years and he learned farming from his parents. It could be said that he knows this work perfectly.  The amount of the requested loan is $575, which he will use to buy pesticides, fertilizer, and to pay the laborers for their work. This will enable him to improve his standard of living.

name: Norma
description: As a married parent of fourteen children, Norma works hard to support her family.  She has a used clothing business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from buying and selling fruit and root crops. Norma is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF to purchase additional stocks of used clothes for her business.  Norma has been sustaining her business activities through her past 20 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: Arlyn
description: Arlyn is married with three children and resides in Aurora, Zamboanga Del Sur. Her husband works as a company driver while Arlyn manages their own  farm, planting and harvesting rice to earn a living.   She has successfully repaid her previous loan from GDMPC which she used to purchase farm supplies. She is now requesting a loan of 25,000 PHP to cover the costs of weeding maintenance and fertilizing her farm. In the future, Arlyn wants to make improvements to her house and the general living conditions of her family.

name: Brigida
description: Brigida belongs to the San Isidro D. Yanahura 5th  Paradero Communal Bank.  The bank is located in the Urubamba district, Urubamba province, Cusco department.  Brigida is 44 years old, married, and has five children.  She alternates her daily activities with her business of selling “chicha” (a drink maD. from corn).  She also has a piece of land where she grows corn and potatoes.  She sells chicha at her house in the Urubamba district.  It is through this business that she gets her children ahead.  She wants to expand her business of selling chicha.  She is requesting the loan to buy corn and corn cobs.  She is happy about the loan, and she pledges to make her payments on time.

name: Agnes
description: Agnes is a married woman. She has four children with ages ranging from 18 to 25. She describes herself as a jovial and humble woman. She operates a tailoring store where she sells curtains, couch covers etc. She has been involved in this business for 10 years. Her business is located in between two busy neighbourhoods and her primary customers are local residents. She describes her biggest business challenge to be poor roads leading to her business premises which become impassable when it rains.   She will use the KES 50,000 loan to buy more materials to make couch-covers and curtains to resell to her customers. Her business goal is to be an interior decorator within five years. She hopes that in the future, she will be financially stable with profits she will obtain from the business.

name: Pedro
description: Pedro M. Larrea lives with his wife and their thirteen-year-old son in Villeta, Paraguay. Together they run a small wooden stand from which they sell fast local-food favorites, such as empanadas, sandwiches, and milanese. They have had this stand for eleven years. A year ago, they began working with the Fundación Paraguaya, which utilizes programs like Kiva to give mico-financing to small business owners like Pedro and his wife.   Since their first loan, they have been able to paint their stand. Though otherwise a small achievement, paint is quite expensive, and the loan has allowed them to accomplish this without making sacrifices that would hurt business. In their newly-refurbished stand, they are doing better than ever. However, the couple tells us that they must get up at 3am daily in order to commute into the city and stock their stand. They are forced to shop in the nearby supermarket, though slightly more expensive, because it is the only store open at that hour.  Additionally, all merchandise must be carried to the store for lack of other transportation.  In the future, Pedro and his wife would like to buy a van. The van will allow them to transport their goods with greater ease and purchase more at one time. Also, they want to start a delivery route.  As he continues to improve his business and his life, Pedro tells us that his dream is to open a store closer to his home and to earn enough money to ensure the education of his son. It is important to Pedro and his wife that he have the opportunity to become a professional and not have to sacrifice as they do.   The money will go toward purchasing flour, eggs, meat, and drinks.

name: Maribeth
description: Maribeth is a 37-year-old married woman and the mother of three children. She is trying hard to fulfill their needs. She is in the business of selling grocery goods with the support of her husband who works abroad. Through this, she earns a good amount of income to support the household expenditures. In order to grow her sales, she has requested a loan to purchase additional grocery goods to sell. She wants to see her children successful in their studies in the future.

name: Eden
description: Eden R. is from the village of Benoni, Camiguin. She is 35 years old and married with 4 school-aged children. To make a living, Eden sells both food and daily use products in the local community. Eden has been engaged in her business for over 4 years and earns approximately 5000 PHP a month for these activities.  Eden joined HSPFI earlier this year to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Eden has successfully repaid a previous loan of 8000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to purchase additional products to sell. Eden is requesting a new loan of 11000 PHP which will be used for the same purpose. This loan will be the 3rd loan taken out by Eden from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to continue to improve and expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Florencia Elvira
description: Florencia is a member of the Jesús de Praga Community Bank.  Florencia, 50, is in a common law marriage and has three grown children who work.  Florencia was a street vendor selling breakfast in the Surquillo district.  She had the chance to travel to Argentina to work for a while.  When she returned to Peru, she went to live in a Pueblo Joven (nickname for a shanty town).  She got together with other women and they set up a popular eating spot.  That worked for several years, but the members retired.  She then began sell set menu meals.  Since Florencia has been with Finca she has learned to put much effort into her work in order to make her payments on the loans and to fulfill her dream.  Florencia needs a loan for 1,000 PEN to buy rice, sugar, and oil.  Florencia’s dream is to open a restaurant.  Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Lucia
description: Lucia is determined to reach business success, and wants to expand her variety store someday. She wants to maintain the business’ fund, as it’s what’s essential for the business to continue its operation. Indeed, insufficient capital can be difficult.  When her previous loan request was granted, the amount made a great impact on the business. She bought stocks of grocery items and necessary materials for her variety store. She wants to thank every lender, since the amount they’ve provided became a way for her to increase sales. The business is growing, and each month her total income is approximately PHP 5,000.Lucia wants to thank Center for Community Transformation (CCT) as well for approving her previous loan. She is blessed by God’s abundance and the medium of the blessing, CCT and all of the lenders.  She’s also grateful, as CCT conducts seminars for entrepreneurs. This year, she is requesting another loan of PHP 40,000 that will be used as added capital. She’ll utilize the amount, if granted, to buy stocks of grocery items such as bottled drinks, school supplies, sacks of rice and processed foods. Lucia has been consistent in attending her CCT fellowship group, which consists of 15 to 30 members, where she hears the word of God and testimonies from partners.  This has made her become strong spiritually and dependent on God on every occasion.

name: Mervis
description: Mervis is 23 years old and lives in a town called Lusaka in Zambia. Mervis is looking to start her own mobile money transfer business and be part of the solution to the financial inclusion problem. which most of Africa now faces. Mervis grew up in Lusaka and completed her schooling here. Unfortunately, she lost her father when he died suddenly 10 years ago. He was the sole breadwinner and this caused some severe financial constraints for herself and her mother. Her mother was unable to pay for her tuition and as a result, they were separated. Mervis had to stay with distant relatives who assisted her mother by putting her through school. By the time Mervis was reunited with her mother, things had taken an unfortunate turn and her mother fell ill and passed away. Over and above dealing with the loss of her mother, Mervis is struggling to keep up with tuition fee payments for her three younger siblings,  for whom she is now solely responsible. Zambia is a country that does not see very many female entrepreneurs succeed because society dictates that women should aspire to get married and have children. Girls are taught to aspire to marriage and to make life choices keeping in mind that marriage is the most important. Mervis would like to go against the grain and make a success of running her mobile money transfer business in Lusaka and then she would like to eventually expand into other locations.Mervis is requesting a Kiva loan to start her own business by purchasing a trading kiosk and having the funds needed to serve people who need to access financial services.

name: Solon
description: Solon is 43 years old, married and blessed with two children aged six and 11 years old. He has run a Christian bookshop for the last year; it earns him a monthly income of 30,000 KES.   With a loan of 35,000 KES from KADET LTD, he plans to restock his shop with a variety of Christian books and tapes for sale.  The anticipated profits will be ploughed back into business for expansion. His future dream is to be successful in life

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth is 54 years old and married with five children, two of whom are in school, Elizabeth works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 12,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like canned goods, soap, shampoo, eggs, canned goods, etc.  Elizabeth has been in this business for nine years.  In the future Elizabeth would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Husein
description: Husein is a 25 year-old, single man, who has worked in agriculture for two years. He has a tractor which he uses for ploughing agricultural land. His business is in high demand in his region since most of his regional citizens work in agriculture and request a fast service, which he can provide. He also sells water to irrigate the land with the help of a small container attached to his tractor.  Husein is applying for a Youth loan from Kiva's partner Al Majmoua, in order to change his tractor's tyres, because it is very important to have them in good shape to do his work easily.  In the future, he hopes to be able to buy all the necessary agricultural tools to reply to any special request from local farmers.

name: Thon's Group
description: Thon’s group lives in a rural village in Battambang province in Cambodia. Thon works as farmer to support his family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these men and women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses, and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Yao
description: Yao has opened his restaurant in 2007 and named “Ma Part “ [My share]. His restaurant is next to an intersection, which is why attracts more customers. Yao had already obtained a loan from WAGES in the past and repaid it well. He is now seeking a new loan in order to replenish his food stock by purchasing 16 boxes of pasta, 12 boxes of couscous, 6 cartons of peas, 8 cartons of canned tomatoes as well as oil, coffee, etc. Translated from French by Ekaterina Sukhanova, Kiva Volunteer

name: Mary Lou
description: Mary Lou is a 22-year-old single woman who supports her family by operating a general store and an e-load (phone card) retailing business.  She lives in the Philippine island of Cebu. Mary Lou joined NWTF-Project Dungganon in 2008 because she aspired for something better for her family. With the help of her past three loans from NWTF-Project Dungganon, Mary Lou has been incrementally lifting her family out of poverty by the sweat of her brow. Her previous loan of PHP 10,000 helped her earn a monthly profit of PHP 7,000, uplifting the family's standard of living.  This time, for her fourth loan, she is borrowing PHP 10,000 to buy stock for her general store and also buy electronic load to resell so that she can continue to save up for the future expansion of her business. Mary Lou is a Dungganon woman who is following an honorable path toward the achievement of her dreams.

name: Marleni Azucena
description: Marleni is a member of the “Sacuyo” Communal Bank. She is from the Sacuyo community, Acora district, Puno province, Puno department. She is 21 years old, married, has a son, and has completed secondary school.  She has worked with Manuela Ramos for 1.5 years. She buys and sells beef and handicrafts. Her first loan for 500 soles was used to feed her animals and buy wool.  With this loan for 800 soles, she will be able to buy alfalfa seed to plant and ensure her cattle’s food. This will enable her to obtain greater income, and in this way she will be able to meet her household and her son’s educational expenses. She would like to thank Manuela Ramos for its confidence in her and she promises to punctually pay her loan in three monthly payments.  Translated from Spanish by Cindy Kendall, Kiva Volunteer

name: Maria
description: Maria is 18 years old and lives with her boyfriend and their two daughters. Maria makes and sells shoes in her house, where she has had a small workshop with her boyfriend for one year. They both work very hard to get ahead with their business, but there are always problems with obtaining materials, which are always going up in price. Despite the small difficulties, the business is going well and continues to prosper, which is bringing good results to her family. This young mother wishes for her two daughters get ahead in life, so that they can be hardworking members of society. With the money from the loan, she will buy the materials that she needs to make her shoes. She will make sure that her earnings increase and that her business will grow so that it can be a large shoe-making factory with many workers that will propel it forward.Translated from Spanish by Jennifer Day, Kiva Volunteer

name: Esperanza
description: Esperanza is a 42-year-old married entrepreneur with six children.  Four children attend school.  Esperanza has operated a general store business for 5 years and requests 9,000 PHP through NWTF to purchase more groceries to sell in her general store.   In the future, Esperanza would like to save enough money  to send her children to college.

name: Nara
description: Nara and her husband and newborn son (he is 10 months old) live in Stepanavan city of Lori region. She has higher pedagogical education and already 18 years of work experience in this field. Now she works at the local school as a teacher of Armenian History. She also has a group of pupils to whom she gives paid private courses of Armenian History at her house. In this way, she prepares the pupils for the entrance exams. Nara mentions that she likes her occupation very much and does her best to make her pupils become interested in the subject, which she considers so important for any pupil to study. Nara is asking for this loan of 500,000 Armenian drams, as she wants to buy a computer and also one very important book that she greatly needs during her private courses.

name: Jasmin
description: Jasmin is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a fish vending business in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 20,000 through NWTF to buy more fish to sell.  Jasmin has been in this business for 8 years. She earns more income from food vending.  Jasmin has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams of building and expanding her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Paul
description: The majority of Africa's young people struggle to make their way in the world because of scarce resources and inequalities. This is true for Paul, who is based in the Siongiroi area of Kenya.   Paul has been practicing mixed farming for the past ten years, and he has managed to earn a decent income. His primary source of income has been milk, eggs, crops and some personal business he engages in to make that extra coin. Paul enjoys the farming lifestyle. He has a connection with farm animals that goes deep, to the extent that he names each of them.   He has aspirations of expanding his dairy farm, but due to financial constraints, he has been unable to do so until now. Now Paul is kindly requesting 20,000 Kenyan shillings (KES) from Kiva lenders to buy a high yielding dairy cow. This cow will boost milk production on the farm. As a result, he will have more for both consumption and sales. With the money from the additional sales, he will be able to service his loan on time.   With increased income from the loan, Paul plans to cover the high farming costs of production. Many farmers compromise quality because of the high cost of inputs. However, with his increased income, Paul will not need to take such measures. In the long run, his family's standard of living will improve.

name: Librada
description: Librada is 50 years old and married with four children, two of whom are still in school. Librada works very hard to provide for them.Librada runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 18,000 loan through NWTF to buy more stock.  This includes toothpaste, diapers, sanitary pads, soft-drinks, beer, milk, and seasonings.Librada has been in this business for 5 years and sells a variety of items such as toothpaste, diapers, sanitary pads, soft-drinks, beers, milk, seasonings, etc. In the future, Librada would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Matluba
description: Matluba is married with two school-aged children. She is a hardworking, positive woman who loves her children very much. She earns money to care for her family by keeping livestock and processing the milk. After the long, hard winter she has run out the feed stores she had saved up and she needs to buy additional feed to take care of her livestock. Since keeping the animals and selling the resulting dairy products is her primary source of income, she wouldn't want to sell her livestock due to a lack of feed and therefore lose her means of earning a living.  In order to get the necessary quantity of feed, Matluba needs a loan, for which she has turned to Arvand. She thanks them in advance for the support.

name: Sope Nabi 2 Group
description: The SOPE NABI 2 group is one of the solidarity groups of the RANDOULENE SUD “Banc Villageois”.  The group is composed of 13 women who all come from the same neighborhood.  They are all married and mothers of at least 3 children each.  They develop various businesses, that is to say, small businesses selling apparel, cosmetic products, fish products, bed sheets and shoes.  The leader of the group, on the other hand, sews in addition to running her small business.  Mrs. Maguette N. wasn’t available when the photo was taken and thus wasn’t present.   Aïssatou N., standing in the far upper right of the photo wrapped in a green scarf, is the leader of the solidarity group.  She is 52 years old, married and the mother of seven dependent children.  She also tutors a boy and a girl.  She makes ready-to-wear clothing and sells bed sheets.  She is a seamstress by profession and received training in this field after leaving school around 20 years ago. Her new loan will enable her to better develop her business because the purpose of the loan is to promote that business.  Her objective is to contribute to the improvement of her family’s living conditions in regard to food, health and the education of her children.  She also supports her husband who has been retired for five years. Translated from French by Connie Archea, Kiva Volunteer

name: Gustave
description: Gustave is 23 years old. He is single and he cares for three dependents from his family. He lives in the Northern Province of Rwanda, in the village called Gakenke, where his business is located. This province is a tourism region, the location of Volcanoes National Park, home to the famed mountain gorillas.  Gustave has a retail shop where he sells different kinds of products such as cosmetics, toilet paper, water, and toothpaste. He prefers this business because can use his own house in his business, which is a great opportunity for him. His business is very organized. He employs one person as a helper so that his business runs smoothly. Gustave has been in this field for three years. The hours of his shop are from 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM every day, even on the weekend.  Gustave is requesting this loan from Kiva lenders via Vision Finance Company to expand his business by purchasing more goods at a good price to attract more customers. After this target is reached, Gustave will be able to serve more customers and earn more profits, which will allow him to renovate his house.

name: Oiimar's Group
description: In the photo, Oumar is the man holding two myAgro envelopes.  He belongs to a group of six farmers who live and work in Makandiana, a village in Mali. He is 54 years old; he lives in a family of 80 people which includes 15 children ranging from ages 2 to 50, eight of whom go to school.   Oumar became a farmer out of family tradition and chose to join myAgro for their farming techniques.  For his first year with myAgro he has bought a package of maize for his 1/4 hectare field.   Thanks to this purchase, Oumar hopes to be able to increase his yields, so as to diversify his cultures and build a house.

name: Brenda Mireille
description: BRENDA MIREILLE S. B., 23, lives in the el Porvenir district, Trujillo province, La Libertad department, Perú.  She is a member of the ESFUERZO DE MUJERES II (WOMEN'S EFFORT II) communal bank.  She has finished 9th grade and works selling soups, prepared breakfasts and juices.  With her first 300 sol loan she bought tables and chairs so that she could sell her meals to nearby passersby on the avenue where she sells her products.  With this loan of 500 new soles she will buy a copying machine since her parallel business activity is photocopying.  BRENDA dreams with enlarging her business and setting up a restaurant as well as a grocery store in her home.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Maria Auxiliadora Group
description: This group was formed thanks to the effort of one of its members, who with the desire to help her friends and neighbors, became informed [about the loan process] and this motivated her to form the commitee.  They are hard-working, determined, and very enterprising women, who with a lot of effort and sacrifice fight for their families.  One of the members is Blanca, who works in sales.  She informs us that she sells all types of products, such as blankets, sheets, and other articles, and that it is going very well for her because she already has well-defined customers who always buy from her.  One of her dreams to to be able to have her own place where she could offer her products.  She describes herself as a determined, hard-working, and very enterprising woman.  She requests the loan in order to purchase blankets, sheets, and other articles to later sell.  She thanks the foundation and Kiva for the opportunity that they are giving her.

name: Mirzokul
description: Mirzokul is conscientious person.  He is 33 years old, married, and has four children.  The climate where he lives is great for agriculture and livestock.  For more than 13 years, he has bred animals.  He has a large garden when he grows hay for his cattle.  He sells milk to his neighbors and they are very pleased with Mirzokul's natural milk products.  He also sells cattle after caring for them a few months.  He has many clients at market.  Mirzokul wants to expand his business but he does not have the means to do so.  He is asking for a loan to buy cattle.  With the income, he plans to provide his children with a good education and modern technology.  He awaits your kindness.

name: Tamaz
description: Tamaz is 32 years old. He lives in the small village of Terjola District with his wife, son, parents, brother, daughter-in-law and two cousins. Tamaz requested a loan from local financial institutions several times for family business start-up, but without any success. His loan request was rejected all the time, because of low income and family’s poor living conditions.   The only source of income for the family is from agricultural activities. In particular, they have 4 milk cows and 4 calves, whose milk is used in cheese products. Besides that, they have a vineyard with 450 grapevines and a 0.9 hectare plot of land where different kinds of vegetables are grown. It is hardly enough for food for the family. According to Credo estimations, the family belongs to the subsistence poor category.   Tamaz requested a loan from Credo to start-up a family business. Tamaz has now been approved for a loan within the framework of the new joint initiative of Kiva and Credo. The start-up loan program envisages provision of business start-up and re-startup credits with soft conditions to rural poor people, who do not have access to credit products. These rural poor people are regarded as “high risk borrowers” because of their low income.   With his loan Tamaz will purchase a minibus. After the minibus is purchased, he will get orders to transport cargo and can generate income.  This will increase the income of his family. The new business initiative, financed with the Kiva Start-up loan, will significantly improve the living conditions of the family.

name: Rahima
description: Rahima is a 29-year-old differently able lady living with her parents and her children in a village in Odisha, India. She runs a grocery shop where she sells lentils, rice, edible oil, wheat flour, spices, salt, biscuits, etc. She has very good relations with her customers. She earns 5,000 INR from this shop, which is not enough for her family to survive.  She has a plan to add more stock of what she sells to her shop plus a few more products like hair oil, shampoo, potatoes, onions, etc. Rahima has requested a loan of 30,000 INR to purchase more stock of what she sells and the new products that are mentioned above. She says that doing so will attract more customers as she would be able to fulfill the maximum demands of her customers and will increase her client base.  She has a dream of having her children well educated and saving some money for their future.

name: Meak
description: Meak S., 43, is a widow who lives with her two children in the Kampong Cham, Cambodia. She is a member of the stage performances held in the village and also works selling different kinds of dessert. On average, she makes US$5 each day, but is also supported by two of her children who work in a garment factory and as a mechanic. She would like to take out a loan of US$800 to open a mechanic shop for her son so he can earn more profits to raise their standard of living. In the future, she would like to sell groceries instead of desserts as well.

name: Lorine
description: Lorine is a twenty-five-year-old single woman from Kisumu, who currently supports three people in her family.  Lorine operates a salon, a business she has had for the last four years, and makes a monthly income of 10,000 KES. She is now taking her first loan from KADET, which she will use to buy salon equipment. She will use her profits to grow her business and repay the loan.  Her dream is to have a stable business.

name: Anik
description: Anik is 61 years old and she lives with her daughter-in-law and granddaughter in Sevan city of the Gegharkunik region. For several years she worked at the hotel as a cleaner and for several years she also worked as a cook. Now her only occupation is farming. On her farm she has cows, calves, pigs and chickens. With the help of her son’s wife, they sell milk form the farm, macun (national dairy-product), cheese, curd, some meat and eggs. They sell it right from their farm. Anik also cultivates potatoes on her plot of land, which Anik sells to re-sellers. Anik’s son now is in Russian Federation and he also works very hard in order to support his family financially. This loan of 330.000 Armenian drams Anik will use to purchase fodder for her cattle.

name: Dominga Del Socorro
description: Dominga is a hard working woman, the mother of three children. Her husband is a bricklayer and he works night as a security guard to obtain more income. Together they have been able to support their children. Her business is selling tortillas. She has been doing this for several years. She started with her own money and with few sales. Through the years she has invested more since she palms the tortillas three times. With the previous loan, she was able to put flooring in her home and with this loan she will finish closing in a small porch that is already under construction. She is very happy to make these improvements on her small house with the hard work of her children and her husband, since allof them cooperate for their common wellbeing.   Translated from Spanish by Ellen Donohue, Kiva Volunteer

name: Ahmad
description: Ahmad is a 21-year-old man who lives in Saida, southern Lebanon. Ahmad has been working as a car mechanic for a year. He takes care of electrical systems and car batteries. Ahmad requests a loan of $1000 USD from Al Majmoua in order to purchase tools for his garage. This is the first time that Ahmad has requested a loan. His clients are his friends, neighbors and tourists. Ahmad’s garage is well positioned.  He decided to start his business because he has experience. In the future, he plans to expand his business and improve his working tools.

name: Mouroussiatou
description: Mouroussiatou is a 35-year-old woman. She is married to a tapestry craftsman. She has two children.  Mouroussiatou has been working as a retailer since 2003. She sells grain to clients at home. She purchases her stock in Anié. She works alone. At the moment, she has no difficulties. Mouroussiatou has requested her first loan from WAGES in order to purchase grain. She wants to reinvest in her business.  In the coming years, Mouroussiatou would like to increase the size of her business. She says that she plans to use the profits to take care of her family.

name: Melanie
description: Melanie is married with four children. She is 31 years old and lives in Panta-on, Ozamiz City, Philippines. Melanie is a farmer who cultivates bananas and gardens to earn a living. She has been doing this for 5 years and every month she earns 4,000 PHP from this work. She has requested a loan of 7,000 PHP to purchase manure to use as fertilizer. Melanie has been a member of GDMPC since 2012. Her hope for the future is to improve their living situation.

name: Wilhelma
description: Wilhelma D. C. is from the village of Taguilon. She is 62 years old. Wilhelma is married and has four adult children. To make a living, Wilhelma raises native chickens for sale. Wilhelma is just starting this business.  In 2007, Wilhelma joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Wilhelma has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5,000 PHP from PMPC. Wilhelma is requesting a new loan of 6,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase livestock feed & other supplies. This loan will be the fifth loan taken out by Wilhelma from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About PMPC:  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Tofiq
description: Q. Tofiq is 21 years old. He is a young businessman and owner of a small farm. Aqroinevst CU has approved his application this year for a 1200 USD loan to purchase 1 cow and 1 calf.

name: Lucy Jackeline
description: Lucy is a partner of the Banco Comunal Las Margaritas.  She is married, 27 years old, and has one child.  She makes beautiful crocheted fabrics, such as decorative tablecloths, upon request, an activity that she learned from her mother.  Lucy needs a loan of 1,000 soles, which will be invested in the purchase of wool and thread.  Her dreams are to buy a plot of land and for her son's health to improve.Translated from Spanish by Mark Broscoe, Kiva Volunteer

name: Youssef
description: Youssef is a 38-year-old mechanic living in Chweifat, a suburban area of Beirut. A father of two, Youssef has been working in the spare parts business for 13 years and decided on owning his own business. In 2001, he opened a car spare parts workshop in suburban Beirut and has been successfully managing it since then.  The loan of $1,200 would help him buy car spare parts and cater for his clients growing demands.

name: Mutui Ole  Tako
description: Mutui, now a father of four, has successfully paid off his second loan, owing to the good harvest in the season. He has since acquired a larger piece of land, where he has expanded to wheat farming.  He has acquired a third loan of KES 70,000, which will assist him in the purchase of pesticides and fertilizer for the wheat farm.  He hopes to grow his business and venture into large-scale farming.

name: Feme
description: As a married parent of two children, Feme works hard to support her family.  She has a general store business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from motorcycle rentals.  Feme is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to purchase stock to sell, like canned goods, eggs, noodles, biscuits, candies, etc., for her general store business.  Feme has been sustaining her business activities through her past three loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college and to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Leocadio
description: Leocadio is 53 years old and lives with his wife in the city of Ybycui. Leocadio has a store with a good array of merchandise. He explained that he began this activity with his wife some 10 years ago, originally opening a small stall where they sold stuffed buns and drinks. Thanks to their good service, they grew day by day. At present, they sell fruit and vegetables, and supply these to nearby companies. He can now count on an established clientele.  Leocadio is requesting a loan to buy food supplies, drinks, milk products, garden vegetables, and other products, which are in much demand in his store. He is grateful to the Foundation and to Kiva for the opportunity it offers.

name: Eve
description: Eve is a 26-year-old married woman. She has two children, ages 3 and 7 years. She describes herself to be honest, God fearing and a focused woman. She operates a retail store  where she sells cosmetics such as hair weaves, lipstick, hair oil, etc. She has been involved in this business for 10 years. Her primary customers are local residents.   Eve describes her biggest business challenge to be inadequate stock of cosmetics to sell . She will use the Kes 20,000 loan to buy cosmetics to sell. Her business goal is to improve her business performance with a goal of operating with a capital of Kes 100,000 within 5 years. She hopes that in the future, she will educate her children with profits from the business. This is her first loan with SMEP DTM.

name: Bold
description: Bold Y. is 47 years old and lives with his wife and four-year-old daughter in Huvsgul province in western Mongolia. He and his family live together in a ger, a traditional Mongolian nomadic tent. Bold is a very busy man who operates a taxi service in his town. His wife is handicapped, and their daughter goes to a local kindergarten. Bold began his taxi service in 2005. Since then, he has focused solely on managing his transportation business, which has become his family's only source of income. After several successful years in operation, he was able to repair his car with his business earnings. His wife has a health problem and stays at home, so she cannot help her husband. Bold works long hours every day in his business to provide his family with the things they need. He pays for his wife's medical expenses and saves money for his daughter's future tuition fees. He has been trying his best to help his wife overcome her serious illness, but they have not been successful. So Bold is seeking a way to have his wife treated overseas. Until that time comes, though, he will keep working hard in his business and saving money for his family’s future. Bold is requesting a 800,000 MNT loan to purchase some spare parts for his automobile, as well as to purchase a large amount of timber in order to complete his yard.

name: Julia
description: Mrs. Julia C. M. is 56 years old and belongs to the Women of the Millenium Community Bank. She lives in Mz 14, lot 6, Victor Raúl Parte Alta in the Porvenir district of Trujillo, La Libertad, Perú. She didn’t complete her higher education and studied the basics of sewing for two years. She married Enrique Francisco Córdoba, with whom she has 2 children, who are currently working. Julia used to sew and wouldn’t have dared to do anything else, but now she sells briquette, firewood, sews clothes, and sells sweets and food. She repaid she first loan of 300 soles in 4 installments. She didn’t invest the loan because she was afraid that she wouldn’t be able to repay it. Starting with her second loan, she began to work.  With this loan of 1000 soles, which she will repay in 4 installments, she will buy briquettes, fabrics, and other supplies and firewood because later it will be scarce. She dreams of expanding her business and giving employment to someone without a job. Her great passion, however, is early education.  Translated from Spanish by Avni Shah, Kiva Volunteer

name: Efepania
description: Efepania is 48 years old and married with three children.  She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more stocks of food to sell.  Efepania has borrowed and paid two loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 24 years and also earns an income from buying and selling fermented duck eggs.  She aspires to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Peaceful Group
description: Pictured here are members of the “Peaceful” group from Koidu, a city in eastern Sierra Leone. They are petty-businesswomen who have come to SMT, a partner of Kiva, in order to apply for a loan of SLL 500,000 for each in the group. With this loan, they will be able to add more goods to their respective businesses, attract more customers, make more sales and profit, and consequently improve on their living conditions.   The featured leader of this group of entrepreneurs is Adama. Adama was born in Kombayinde, in eastern Sierra Leone. She is married to a farmer and has three children, two of whom are attending primary and secondary schools.   Adama has been a businesswoman for four years now. She sells market-food items like tomatoes, etc. With her share of this loan, she is going to buy a large quantity of tomatoes, etc. to add to her current stock.

name: Jeys Junior
description: Jeys is a 20-year old young man who is single and lives in the town of Pucallpa with his parents and siblings. He is a very friendly, hard-working and enthusiastic person and has a great ambition of self-improvement. Thanks to his own effort and the support of his parents, Jeys is currently studying professional studies in Accountancy. In his spare time, he likes to continue studying and sometimes cooks delicious "chicharrones" to share with his family.   By personal initiative and with great determination and dedication, Jeys works as an Assistant Accountant in an accounting office in his town. He works everyday for approximately 6 hours. He enjoys what he does and believes he does a good job as a result of his good performance and the friendliness he shows towards people.   Jeys is grateful to Kiva lenders because thanks to their financial support he will be able to buy a printer, which will significantly improve the quality of his academic work. He will continue to work hard to get ahead and accomplish his dream of becoming a good professional and having his own legal business.

name: Alicia
description: Alicia is 37 years old.  She is a hardworking and good-natured woman.  She lives with her partner, the father of her 5 children, in the house they inherited from his parents. They plant and grow agricultural crops such as potatoes, peas and beans to earn their living.  Alicia wakes up at 5am so that she has enough time to prepare the meals and tend to the younger animals. Afterwards, she begins her work in their fields.   Alicia says she enjoys working on a farm.  Since she was a girl, she has helped plow the fields, always thinking about which crops to plant.  Thanks to her husband’s influence, she finds herself more motivated.  Once harvesting is done, they sell their products at the Tarma city market.  They select potatoes of the same size so that they can be placed out for sale at a fixed price.  Through her hard work and excellent pricing of her products, Alicia has been able to pay for her children’s education all these years. Her next goal is to buy additional farmland to increase her output.   This is Alicia’s ninth loan with MFP, and she has responsibly repaid her previous loans. She also has the backing of her fellow communal bank members, with whom she feels very happy. She will use the money to purchase 20 bags of chemical fertilizer, estimated cost of approximately 2200 soles, and with the remainder buy food for family consumption. Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Rosette
description: Rosette is married, with four children and only three of them go to school. She doesn’t take care of additional family members.   She has business of selling charcoal and has been in this for seven years. She has applied for a loan of UGX 600,000 (Uganda shillings) from Micro Credit for Development and Transformation SACCO (MCDT SACCO) to buy more bags of charcoal.    Rosette works in shop seven days out of every week and sells on a retail basis only. Her major business challenges include seasonality and thieves. She is aspiring to become a wholesaler and also to buy a plot of land on which to build her house. She resides in a rented house and the family has access to electricity and piped water. Her monthly expenses include rent, feeding the family, and school fees.

name: Joreta
description: This is Joreta; she is 34-years old and a resident of Intramuros, Manila, Philippines. She is married to Gerardo, a worker, and is the mother to their children. Together with her husband, she manages their household while operating the business. She and her husband are working hard to provide income for their everyday needs.  Joreta maintains a direct selling business. She sells clothing, footwear, undergarments, cosmetics, and other products including popular direct-selling brands like Avon, Fuller life, Natasha, Boardwalk, Marikina Shoe Exchange, and other brands. A customers order is bought in cash by the dealer and then given to the customer with a one-month-to-pay credit. Dealer’s prices are lower than those in the catalog, and these are the profits that dealers are investing in as their income. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community.  She earns a minimum of PHP 2000 in sales every week.  To help her continue operations, she is requesting a PHP 20,000 loan. She will be utilizing the loan to buy additional supplies and merchandise products like shampoo, cologne, deodorant, perfume, soap, fabric softener, undergarments and other products needed in her business. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands.    Joreta dreams to see her business growing and hopes to have their own house. She meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her life and business every week and also draw strength and inspiration from the fellowship and the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Charity's Pendamoyo Group
description: Charity is 42 years old and is a married woman with 2 children, ages 20 and 18. Charity is a market seller, who started in 2003. Everyday, she works from 6am to 6pm at her business and can earn a monthly profit of about $50 from her sales.  In the past, Charity has taken out 1 successful loan from BRAC Tanzania to expand her business. She now hopes for a loan to buy more items (rice, maize, wheat, and tomatoes) for her business. She will share this loan with her subgroup members Joyce and Tatu, who have businesses dealing in food vending and charcoal sales.

name: Isabel
description: Isabel is a mom, she is 42 years old and she lives together with her husband and their children in the Yencala Boggiano sector. It is a rural district of Lambayeque, located more than an hour and a half from the city of Chiclayo.   She raises sheep for a living. She keeps the sheep in a corral near her home. When they have reached a certain time in their development she sells them to the merchants that visit the region. With the profits she earns from this business she is able to contribute with her husband towards the family's finances.  Isabel wants to start raising and selling goats because they grow and develop quicker and they are sold at better prices. In order to meet her objective she has approached Edpyme Alternativa (Kiva Field Partner) for a first time loan in the amount of 1000 nuevos soles.  She is a calm and hard working woman. Those that know her consider her to be a very honest and trustworthy person.

name: Esi
description: Esi M. sells food stuffs. She is married and has four dependents. Her husband is a commercial driver and his income is not sufficient to meet the needs of the family. Esi is working very hard to contribute to the family’s expenses.  She is asking for $525.00 as additional capital to buy more food stuffs to sell.

name: Priscilla
description: Priscilla is 32 years old, single, and has two children. She has been selling handbags for seven years with a monthly income of 20,000 KES, which she uses to support her children.  Priscilla is requesting her first loan from  KADET LTD, which she will use to buy more handbags to sell.  She was introduced to KADET by an existing  customer. With the anticipated profit from the business, she will educate her children. Her dream is to open a boutique shop in the future.

name: Gloria
description: Gloria is 62 years old and married with seven children. Gloria works very hard to provide for her family.  Gloria runs a general store in the Philippines and has requested a PHP 22,500 loan through NWTF to purchase more groceries to sell in her store.  Gloria has been in this business for nine years and sells a variety of items such as sugar, rice, snack foods and other groceries.   In the future, Gloria would like to save enough money to provide financial security for her family.

name: Primitiva
description: Primitiva works hard to support her family. She is married and has a fish vending business in the Philippines.  Primitiva requested a loan of 19,000 Philippines pesos (PHP) through NWTF to buy more fish to sell. She has been in this business for 25 years.  In the future, Primitiva would like to renovate her house and expand the business.

name: Federation Investors Group
description: Greetings from Zimbabwe! This is 43-year-old Innocent from Harare. He is widowed with three children, two attending school. He also cares for his parents. He is a member of the Federation Investors Group. Innocent sells potatoes and orange seedlings and fruits. His business has been in operation for 21 years. He says the main challenges sometimes faced are political instability and times when meetings result in business being disturbed. Innocent has requested a loan of $700 to buy more seedlings and fruits for resale. He says the extra income generated as a result of this loan will allow him to finish building his house. In the future Innocent plans to have a nursery of these seedlings at his own farm.

name: Silvia
description: Silvia, 33, is married to Edwin with whom she has two children who are 14 and 9 years old.  She and her family live in a house of their own in a rural district.  Silvia’s a welcoming and enterprising woman.  She’s been a crafts-person for more than 15 years.  She’s very skilled at knitting.  When she was a little girl she’d knit clothes for dolls and now that she has family responsibility she turned her hobby into her main source of income.
