Now, she has looms that she uses to make blankets and tapestries out of different kinds of wool.  “It’s more profitable to knit with alpaca wool but it’s also riskier because one must invest more,” she mentions.  She and her husband also work in agriculture growing ‘maca’ [an Andean root vegetable] which sells well.  They divide roles: Silvia knits and Edwin farms.  They hope to reach their objectives this way and one of them is to finish building their house.  Her goals focus on developing as a businesswoman but to do so she needs your help in order to acquire more materials.  She belongs to the “Mujeres al Futuro” (Women towards the Future) communal bank and this is her MFP loan #4.  Like in previous occasions, she mentions that she’ll be punctual with her installment payments.  She feels good working with responsible members.  Silvia will use the 1,000 soles to buy several kilos of sheep and alpaca wool and will also buy synthetic thread in assorted colors.

name: Costancia
description: Costancia M. is 45 years old and lives in Dar es Salaam. She is married and has two children, one of whom is already 24, while the other one is only 6 and a half years old. Additionally, she is responsible for taking care of two other children whose parents do not have the means to support the family.  Costancia earns income through various businesses, including raising kuku (chickens), making baskets, and making vinyagos.  Raising kuku is a popular micro-business in Tanzania, especially amongst SELFINA clients. Kuku means chicken in Swahili, and raising them for sale is popular for a number of reasons. The activity requires little start-up capital and space, and, while the chicken are growing, they produce eggs, which can either be sold to provide a supplementary source of income, or eaten to provide a supplementary source of protein.  Due to Costancia's business skills, she has also managed to develop a successful vinyagos-sales venture. A vinyago is a beautiful, hand-crafted statue made from wood by members of the Makonde tribe who come from southeastern Tanzania. Woodcarving is an important part of Makonde life, both in ancestor worship and in their own myth of creation. Their wooden statues are of three main types: traditional masks, motifs of female ancestor worship, as well as more abstract, modern forms.  Costancia works 9-12 hours a day, 6 days a week at her different enterprises with the assistance of one employee.  She currently needs a loan of US$550 in order to expand her businesses. Contancia thanks everyone for their support.  ABOUT SELFINA: SELFINA has taken a lead role as a pioneer of micro-credit in Tanzania through Micro-Leasing. The organization is engaged in the economic empowerment of women in Tanzania through the provision of a leasing and leaseback microfinance facility. Customs and traditions in Tanzania make it difficult for women to own land and assets, thus they are termed non-creditworthy by financial institutions. This leads to poor financial support and poor access to basic needs and services for women with low incomes. One of the primary advantages of microleasing is that is allows clients to use the equipment as collateral for future loans with SELFINA, thus enabling them to borrow larger sums in the future.

name: Alberto Luis
description: Alberto Luis E. lives in Baranoa, a village near Barranquilla renowned for its art and folklore manifestations as well as fried food, particularly the famous pork chops from the Atlantic province. At week-ends and holidays people from nearby villages go to Baranoa to enjoy the delicious, freshly prepared food from the area. That's where Alberto Luis lives with his partner and two young children. They rely on the proceeds from a fried food business he set up 8 years ago that sells pies, cornmeal rolls, yuka pasties, fried green banana rolls and potatoes stuffed with meat, chicken or pork. It is located in an area with a lot of student traffic, which is his target market.   This is his second loan with the Fundación Mario Santo Domingo  and he plans to use it to buy ingredients such as oil, salt and corn in larger quantities. Alberto's goal is to start a second business, selling natural fruit juices such as soursop, medlar, guava, pineapple and sapote among other delicious fruits from the region, to complement his current one. His main challenge is the lack of capital to develop his objetives, so he is working a bit more and persisting to achieve his goals. Translated from Spanish by Alba Sort , Kiva Volunteer

name: Alex
description: Alex is pursuing a business administration career. He says his dream is to graduate and be able to practice his profession to become someone in life.  He wants to break through and become known in the field of his choice, and thus be able to help his loved ones with what he earns from his studies.  He's seeking this loan to be able to pay the fees for his degree so he can continue studying.

name: Claudia Patricia
description: Claudia is a 41-year-old rural woman who carries out various types of agricultural work. She fattens pigs to sell; she sells eggs; and she also owns land where she grows corn. She has been carrying out these different jobs every day without rest for the last 20 years in order to get enough money to take home to her family. She is currently requesting a loan to buy two piglets to raise and fatten and to buy agricultural supplies in bulk (fertilizers, manure, pesticides, etc.) so that she can increase production and increase her income, especially because people buy more pork than usual during the Christmas season meaning that she has the opportunity to increase her sales significantly. The loan will also make it possible for her to reap a better harvest of corn because she will be able to take care of the land better with the agricultural supplies. Claudia wants to carry on working, and her dream is to grow and strengthen her business so that it is more profitable and so that she can improve her family's quality of life.

name: Brenda
description: Brenda, age 46, is married with five children. She resides in Tukuran.   Brenda operates a fishing business to earn a living. She's been in this business for 12 years. Each month, she earns 8,000 PHP doing this type of work. She has requested a loan of 15,000 PHP to purchase additional fish to sell.   This year, Brenda joined GDMPC. In the future, Brenda hopes to improve her business.

name: Florentina
description: Mrs. Florentina is from the city of Santaní. She is a very hard-working and enterprising person, who is dedicated to her sales. She has a store, which has been open for several years. Her husband is a traveling salesman. She says that both of them help to be able to support their home.  She asks for this loan to be able to invest in buying supplies for her store, including vegetables, fruits, meat, drinks, and other things. In this way, she will be able to continue fulfilling her clients’ requests.

name: Millicent
description: Millicent is married with three children, all of whom attend school. She owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is electricity. For the past five years, she has operated a coconut selling business, selling to local neighbors. She faces major challenges of seasonality and the high cost of transportation. She dreams of expanding to improve her living standards. With the KES 50,000, she wants to purchase sacks of coconuts for resale. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Sherlita
description: Sherlita is 46-years-old and married with three children, who are all in school. Sherlita works very hard to provide for them.  Sherlita runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 13,000 loan through NWTF in order to purchase more groceries to sell.  Sherlita has been in this business for two years and sells a variety of items such as canned goods, shampoo, noodles and other groceries.   In the future, Sherlita would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Rizalinda
description: Rizalinda is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a food vending business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing 5,000 PHP through NWTF to purchase additional ingredients like pork, chicken, seasonings, spices, etc., for her business.  Rizalinda has been in this business for 5 years. Rizalinda earns additional income from a general store.  Rizalinda has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams of saving money to expand her business in the future.

name: Jlg-007(A)-Keelathaliyampatti Group
description: Suguna is a 41 years old women. She has formed a self-help group with her friends in the rural part of Karur, in Tamil Nadu. She works hard to support her family of 4, and saves diligently. However, her finances are not adequate for her to access basic necessities like toilets in her home. Her family has to trek long distances at dawn to use the fields to relieve themselves. These unsanitary practices make them vulnerable to infections, and the lack of privacy exposes them to molestation or worse.   Seeking to improve their situation, the group seeks a loan of Rs. 42000 to build toilets in their homes. Your loan will help these 3 hardworking rural Indian families to access basic sanitation, and consequently, safety, improved health, medical savings, and improved productivity.

name: Alexander
description: Alexander sells various home products at the central market in Melitopol city. He has been in business for 12 years. His income is about 5,000 Grivnas a month.  He enjoys selling small things that help make home chores easier.  Alexander is a very happy and enthusiastic person. With his income, he helps his sisters and their parents with whom he lives in one big house. He is not married.  Alexander would like to get a loan of 12,000 Grivnas to increase the assortment of his inventory. He always tries to have a large assortment of small home products to offer something to each client who comes his way.

name: Ameen
description: Ameen is 21 years old. He lives at a sector in Jordan called Mafraq with his seven siblings and his parents. Ameen is in his first year studying for a bachelor's degree in English literature. He is planning to continue his studies to find a job in his study field after graduation to start earning a better income to help his family financially. But he doesn't currently have enough money to pay for his upcoming semester fees. For this reason, he applied for this loan.

name: Marianita
description: Marianita is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a general store business in the Philippines.  She is borrowing PHP 18000 through NWTF to buy items like shampoo, groceries, etc. to sell in her sari-sari store.  Marianita has been in this business for 9 years. She also earns more income from raising livestock.  Marianita has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to save money to expand her business in the future.

name: Lawrence
description: Lawrence is a 45-year-old married man with five children living in Kagadi, Uganda.He is a teacher by profession and has been in service for a period of nine years. In order to supplement his income, he also has a retail shop. He would like to educate his children, upgrade his studies and build a permanent home. Lawrence wants a loan to buy sodas and rice to sell.

name: Chheng
description: Mrs. Chheng C. is a single mother who lives in Phnom Penh City. She has two children, both of whom are employed at different jobs. Mrs. Chheng C. was married years ago, but divorced her husband. Mrs. Chheng C. has rented a market store where she sells chicken to earn a living. She usually goes to buy chicken in bulk at the cheapest price possible from rural people whose houses are full of poultry they raise. To improve her poultry trade, Mrs. Chheng C. is taking out her first loan to purchase small chickens to raise.

name: Diana Carolina
description: Diana Carolina, from Santa Marta in Magdalena, is a young sales and marketing student at the CampoAlto institution. She talks about how being a student has gone for her.  She talks about how her course of study has helped her in her personal and professional life.  Personally, it has helped her to know how to express herself, to be open to any thought or idea. Professionally, it has helped her to be very creative, to be an agile thinker, to have verbal fluency, to know how to be a leader with solid knowledge of the current market, and also to be highly competitive without ignoring ethics and values.  She also tells us how her internship has gone for her. She says that she is very grateful to the institution for having placed her in a very good institution where she has performed marketing duties such as telemarketing and customer service.  She would like Kiva to help her for a simple reason, which is to be able to finish her technical program and thus to be able to start to work and begin to have certified work experience.

name: Maha
description: Maha is a 40-year-old married woman from Madaba, Amman, Jordan and a mother of two children.  Maha produces dairy products and she is requesting a loan of 500 JD to purchase milk for those dairy products.  Maha is looking to expand her project and improve her family's living conditions.

name: Allan
description: Livingstone is home to one of the world’s seven natural wonders, Victoria Falls. This magnificent place is where 30-year-old Allan runs his mobile money transfer business.  Allan started running his business in June 2009 whilst working in an internet café. When he first started, he only served 10 to 20 customers in a day, but this is no longer the case. Allan now boasts of being one of the most successful mobile money business owners in the country. His customers now range from 60 to a 100 in a day. It is because of this growth that in February 2010, he opened his second shop which is also doing well.  Allan believes he is successful in his business because of his commitment to offer the very best customer service. He is happy to be able to provide a service that makes people’s lives easier.   Running a business comes with many challenges. Allan’s biggest challenge is that the trading booth he is currently at his second outlet is not his. It belongs to a bus service. The owner of the bus service was kind enough to let him use a part of his space for his mobile money transfers. The trouble he says is that, his customers are inconvenienced, as there is no protection against weather elements such as rain or sun. He needs the Kiva loan to be able to buy his own trading booth, which will have a shade and some seats so that his customers can sit as they do the transactions.  His appeal to the kiva lenders is that they keep helping small businesses such as his because it goes a long way.  Allan dreams of opening up more shops in his beloved home town as the demand for his services keeps increasing. He would like to see a mobile money transfer shop at every corner in Livingstone.

name: Rosa Alberto
description: Rosa is married and has an adult son who's in the workforce. She lives in a house that she owns. She's an administrative assistant and works 8 hours a day. The amount of the loan will be used to purchase construction supplies (cement, metal sheets, beams and sand) so that she can start building rooms for renting out. In the future she intends to get a bachelor's degree, finish building the rooms and start building a surrounding wall. She'll repay the loan without becoming delinquent.

name: Gemma
description: Gemma is 32 years old and married with one child.   She works hard to provide for her family.     Gemma runs a sari sari (variety) store in the Philippines.  She has been running the store for 10 years and also earns an income from food vending.    Gemma requested a PHP 20500 loan through NWTF to buy more items to sell.  She has borrowed and paid 6 loans from NWTF before this loan.   Gemma aspires to build and expand her business to secure the future for her family.

name: Adzo
description: Adzo is 65 years old, married, and lives in Adidogomé. A mother of five children, she works selling food products, which she procures three times a month from the market. She makes her resales from a kiosk at the front of her home and also by traveling around to the surrounding areas.Adzo wishes to have this loan to make an order for drums of oil. With the earnings that come from good resales, Adzo hopes to improve her point of sale, help her family to flourish, and provide her children an education.

name: Darly Del Socorro
description: Two years ago, Darly's dream began when she opened her restaurant with dreams and aspirations of managing to have good economic stability and improve her loved ones' quality of life, taking advantage of a piece of land near the town where many travelers stopped seeking to satisfy their need to eat.  She cooked her future and two years passed that represent for her a new stage in her life since she has noted the progress as much for her as for her family.  Darly is not satisfied with the successes she has had, and knowing that she can't stay with that she has managed, she asks for a loan to purchase supplies and make some renovations to the site because the town's festivals are approaching and they will be visited by many and there will be thousands of tourists with empty stomachs that she wants to satisfy.

name: Mamntambo
description: Mambo from Mbeya, Tanzania! This is 49 year-old Mamntambo M.. She is married with two children, ages 12 and 15, and has one other dependent, who is her nephew.   In 2003 Mamntambo established a maize business. Mamntambo has already received and successfully repaid one loan from SELFINA, and now requires a loan of $175 in order to purchase additional stock in bulk. She thanks you for your support.   About SELFINA: SELFINA is engaged in economic empowerment of women in Tanzania through leasing and leaseback facility as a practical way to achieve the economic and social emancipation of women.  SELFINA has taken a lead role as a pioneer of micro-credit in Tanzania through Micro-Leasing. Customs and traditions in Tanzania normally make it difficult for women to own land and assets, thus they are termed not-creditworthy by financial institutions as they lack tangible collateral assets. This leads to poor financial support hence poor access to basic needs and services for women with low incomes.  SELFINA buys and leases equipment to women. Where a client needs working capital SELFINA buys equipment from said client, extending a loan to her, then leasing back the same equipment – a process called a sale and leaseback arrangement.

name: Leonard
description: Leonard is a married man. He has 2 children. He describes himself to be capable. He operates a farm where he keeps cows and also grows maize, peas, potatoes. He has been involved in this business for 2 years. His business is located in a good area and his primary customers are locals. He describes his biggest business challenge to be inadequate working capital. He will use the KES 30,000 loan to buy farm inputs. This is his third loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. Previous loans were repaid successfully. He will use the anticipated profits to improve his family's living standards.

name: Esinala
description: Esinala is a 30-year-old married woman. She has three children with ages ranging from 2 years to 10 years. She describes herself as hopeful.   She operates a grocery store where she sells fruits. She has been involved in this business for five years. Her business is located in a populated area and her primary customers are retailers and wholesalers. She describes her biggest business challenges as lack of commodities and transport problems.   She will use the KES 20,000 loan to buy more fruits to sell. She hopes that in the future, she will be able to provide employment to other people. This is her first loan with SMEP DTM.

name: María Concepción
description: María, who is 37 years old, has only a first grade education. She lives with her partner, who is a farmer, and has three children. Two of them live with her but they aren't in school. One is an adult and the other is disabled.  María has had to depend on farming all her life, since that is the legacy she inherited from her parents, who taught her to work hard and to be responsible. She needs the money from this loan to buy fertilizer, foliar products, and pesticides, to pay rent, and to pay for the labor she needs in order for her life partner to work. She would like her son to learn how to work so that when he becomes independent he doesn't have problems getting ahead.

name: Nazeeran
description: Nazeeran is 60 years old and a mother of eight children. She is a housewife, who together with her daughters, looks after the household. One of her son has owned a gold shop for eight years now, and he wants to renovate his shop. That is why his mother, Nazeeran, applied for the loan amount; to help her son in what he is aiming for. She is very happy with Kiva platform and its field partner BRAC Pakistan.

name: Salomon
description: The lines drawn in the corn and chilli crops that Salomon grows are a mark of his passionate work as a farmer for over forty years. The 54-year-old Salomon has been working since he was small, having grown up with the sound of cows and chickens. At the age of 25 he was employed as a farmer, and this experience inspired him to start up on his own. This respectable work has allowed his family to get ahead and improve their quality of life.  Now, every year Salomon is known for the quality of his crop, so this season he plans to invest in his harvest. For this reason he is requesting a loan to buy fertilizer, seeds and to pay for a plow to plant correctly. This will allow him to continue farming effectively to further increase his sales and of course his income. One of his goals is to buy two cows to venture into the world of livestock.

name: Mqbel
description: Mqbel is a 29-year-old married man from Khan Younis with two sons.  Two years ago, Mqbel  opened a store for selling shoes. This is the only source of income for the family.  He would like to improve his business and expand the store in the future. Mqbel requested a USD loan from FATEN. This loan will help him to buy a new collection of women and kids shoes for his store to resell.  By taking this loan, Mqbel will be able to increase his sales and income.  Mqbel appears in the photo in his store

name: Natividad
description: Natividad is 53 years old, married, and has 3 adult children. She has a retail shop where she sells a variety of products in the local community.  Natividad is requesting a loan of PHP 7,000 to buy peanuts, soft drinks, noodles and other daily basic needs to sell. Each month, Natividad earns about PHP 5,000 doing this type of work. In the future, Natividad hopes that her business will improve to support the needs of her family.

name: Francisca
description: Francisca is 64 years old and married with four children.  Francisca works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 15,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase rice, bread, soft-drinks and other groceries.  Francisca has borrowed and paid 25 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 17 years and also earns an income from food vending.  Francisca aspires to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Paulin
description: Paulin is a 34-year-old married man. He and his wife have three children, who are between 1 and 5 years old. Paulin`s wife works as an executive secretary. Paulin is a self-employed businessman selling a variety of goods, as the photo illustrates. Among the goods he sells are cosmetics products like body lotions, toothpaste, soap, toilet paper, and foods like rice, sugar, and cooking oils. His shop is open every day from 6 am to 9 pm.   Paulin is requesting a Kiva loan via Vision Finance Company in the amount of $875 to expand his business by purchasing a large quantity of products.  He plans to also start a wholesale business. By doing so, Paulin hopes to earn more profits which in turn will allow him to provide a secure and stable future for his three children.

name: Beatrice
description: Beatrice is aged 28 and married with four children ages between 7 and 1. She has been in dairy farming for 9 years within her home area of Litein, South Rift Kenya with her milk produce sold to Brookside Dairies.  Beatrice has requested for a first loan of 50,000 KES from Juhudi Kilimo to help her plant both nappier grass and silage for her dairy cows. She says buying animal feed has become costly and it much better for a farmer to grow rather than buy the feed. This she reiterates will save her much and make repayment easier.  Beatrice reiterates the high cost of feed is the main challenge.

name: Robert
description: Roberto is 33 years old and lives in the village of San Juan, Quirino, Isabela with his wife Vilma and their only child April Grace. Their daughter is now in the primary level of education. Robert supports his family through his furniture-making business. He has been in this enterprise for more than two years. He earns a monthly income of PHP 10,000, and the income is being used as rolling capital and in providing for the immediate needs of his family and educational needs of his child.   Roberto requests an initial loan of PHP 4,000 that will serve as additional capital for his business. He will use the loan to purchase new materials needed in making furniture. He wants his business to progress so that he can meet the growing needs of his family. He is thankful that his family is always in good health. He is also starting to save some of his income for future needs. He hopes that someday his daughter will finish her college education.

name: Kubra
description: Kubra  is 35 years old; she is a married woman.  She deals in the business of selling animals. She buys animals (baby goats & calves) at low prices, brings them up and then sells them out in the market at higher prices. She makes enough through her business to contribute to the family income. She also sells milk to generate an extra amount of income.   She needs to improve her business to bear her household expenses. For this reason, she contacted Kashf Foundation and applied a loan of PKR 45000  to purchase more animals to increase her sales. She is very experienced and has good contacts in the market. With this loan, she will definitely expand her business and income level.

name: Kossa
description: Kossa G. is a 47 year old woman. She is married and the mother of 8 children, for whom she is responsible. She is a member of the "Banc Villageois" of BAKIDIOTO and has been granted loans 15 times in a row.  She sells vegetables and condiments on the Tanaff market. From time to time, she goes selling from door to door with a tray loaded with goods. She gets her supplies from weekly markets. She has been in this trade for over seven years and the revenue generated allows her to contribute to her children's education.	 With this loan, she intends to strengthen the capital of her business, which she has been running since she has become a member of CAURIE-MF. She hopes to make more profits in order to better meet her children's needs.		 		Translated from French by Marie-Elodie Bazy, Kiva Volunteer

name: Joseph
description: Joseph is a married man. He has a son who is 3 years old. He describes himself to be keen. He operates a motorcycle  where he provides transportation services. He has been involved in this business for three years. His business is located within a busy town and his primary customers are local residents from the environs. He describes his biggest business challenge to be frequent harassment from the city council.   Joseph will use the Kes 20,000 loan to buy motorcycle spare parts. His business goal is to improve his business  to taxi operation services within 5 years. He hopes that in the future, he will have bought his own car.

name: Allan
description: Allan is 29 years old and is a married man with three children, aged 8 months, 6 years and 8 years. He has a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) business in San Miguel, Bohol. He earns about 9,000 PHP per month with his business. Allan works hard to increase his income and keep up with the increasing needs in his household. He has requested a loan to purchase motorcycle spare parts. He hopes to expand his business in the future.

name: Las Espinozas Group
description: María is this group's coordinator. She is 34 years old and has a partner and five children, aged eleven, ten, eight, four and two years old respectively. María works selling vegetables and seasonal fruits. This season she wants to invest in tamarinds, jocotes, mangoes, tomatoes and more. María also sells hot foods (enchiladas, tacos, plantains with cheese, roast chicken, roast meat and more). María's eldest daughter helps with selling the food.   The other members of this group are 39-year-old María - who sells firewood - and Petrona, 60 years old, who sells tortillas.

name: Valdovino
description: Sr. Valdovino has been married to Sra. Santa for a number of years.  They have one grown son who still lives with them.  Sr. Valdovino was able to get them ahead through his work. Sr. Valdovino has a well-stocked general store in a very busy city neighborhood.  In addition, he works as a street vendor selling basic household goods. Sr. Valdovino is asking for this loan so he can purchase a variety of supplies for his store, such as beverages, meats, bread products and other items.

name: Fortunate
description: Fortunate is a 21-year-old businesswoman who is currently single and lives in the Nyanga District of Zimbabwe. She has been successfully operating a business of buying and selling clothes, shoes, cosmetics, and bags. She has also been volunteering at the local school as a Learner Guide, supporting students with their studies.  With a Kiva loan, Fortunate intends to make bulk purchases of more clothing and shoes. This will increase her profit margins and help her supply more goods to her community. She hopes to create employment in her community and increase her income to become financially independent.

name: Las Primaveras Group
description: One of the characteristics of the state of Veracruz is its music, "Son Jarocho," because of the excellence of the sound of the region. Nevertheless, variants of this style exist which are "Son del Sur," which tends to have a more contrasting rhythm but, at the same time, is slower. Meanwhile, the sound of the central zone has a defined and rapid rhythm. In one of the communities of said state, a group formed called "Las Primaveras" [The Springs] because this season represents happiness and color for the members.The group is made up of: Nohemí, who sells food and cocktails, Yolanda, lingerie and cosmetics, María, perfumes, Rubí, silver items, Perla A., costume jewelry and shoes, Perla B., food and cattle raising, Ana, shoes, Ventura, lingerie, Zuleyma, costume jewelry, Eulalia, typical food and Isidora, food and internet service.Perla B. is an older woman who keeps herself strong and full of goals. She is characterized by being very hardworking, noble and above all for having a picturesque character. For her, the main driver has always been her family, as well as her children and her grandchildren in whom she has instilled the value of work since they were young. She works raising cattle, a job she considers a family activity since she was a girl, she helped her parents caring for the animals. Similarly, she learned from her grandmother to treat certain ailments in an alternative manner, therefore many clients consult her for her to help them. Additionally, she sells typical food on the weekends. "If you don't work, you don't have income and you don't have the satisfaction of being economically independent," she expresses happily.The income obtained during all of this time has permitted her to support with the expenses of the home, cover the education of her children, carry out renovations to her house and enlarge the pens for her animals. On this occasion, she will invest the loan in the purchase of disposable plates, napkins, spoons, bags, gas, to make the pens and to invest in feed for her hens and the growth of her pigs.*The photograph was taken on the patio where, each weekend, the foods are prepared that Perla B. sells; she is dressed in a blue blouse and purple skirt.

name: Manchesta Group
description: Melina is a mother of four children, two girls and two boys, who are in school.  She is in her early forties.  For three years now, Melina has made her life by selling firewood.  She owns a big store at her home where she keeps her stock.  She operates her business on an on demand basis, selling firewood whenever a customer demands.  Melina is able to make a small monthly profit.   This is Melina's first loan from Tujijenge Tanzania, which she will use to buy firewood stock to meet customer demand.  She dreams that one day she will be ale to open another successful business.  She will share this loan with her loan group Manchesta, which totals eight members.  The members of the group will hold each other accountable for repaying the loan.

name: Ruos
description: Mr. P. Ruos was married in 1979 and has 5 children, 4 sons and 1 daughter. He started his horse cart business in1979. With his horse cart service, he helps the people in the community transport goods, and bricks and rocks from one village to another.   His wife has been weaving silk  at home since 1979, after she learned to weave from her mother.   He has borrowed money from MAXIMA four times. Now he is requesting a loan of $200. He will use this money to purchase a new horse cart because the current one is too old and is easily damaged.

name: Va
description: From Ornlong Veng district of Siem Reap province, Mrs. Va is a 37-year-old married woman who has been working in agricultural work. Her husband, Mr. Horn, also works alongside her on their farmland. They grow rice crops and some kinds of beans both in the rainy season and in the dry season. Together, this couple can earn about $5USD each day, used for managing their household expenses and supporting their children to go to school.   Mrs. Va has asked for a loan from Kiva to purchase crop sprayings and mineral fertilizers in order to make her plants grow well. For her future prospects, she hopes to improve her farming business and she dreams of having various agricultural materials like a plowing machine and a pumping machine as well.

name: Marilu
description: Member Marilu is 33 years old and married with two children. She works selling beauty products such as perfume, creams, lipstick, and nail polish. She is self employed and takes her merchandise to different locations, selling to friends and the general public. This member works from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm and has been in business for seven years now. Business is going very well for her. Her dream is to own a store where she could sell her beauty products.   This member is requesting a loan to purchase creams, perfumes, and lipsticks. She is happy with this loan and promises to comply with her payment plan.

name: Kowuvi
description: Mr Kowuvi T. was born in Tsévié. Not having had the chance to pursue his studies much, he got hired early on by a company selling and repairing electronic appliances and used refrigerators. After finishing his training, he opened his own workshop to sell and repair refrigerators. Thanks to his know-how, he won the trust of his clientele. He's seeking a loan to buy a large stock of used refrigerators and freezers in the port of Lomé, in order to resell them. This will help him greatly increase his revenue and his profit.Translated from French by Patrick Stadelmann, Kiva Volunteer

name: Emily
description: Emily is 46 years old and has six children. Emily is married and two of her children are in school.  She is in the agricultural business of pig fattening in the Philippines. Emily requested a 17000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy feed and vitamins for her pigs. Emily has been pig fattening for 5 years now and has borrowed 8 times in the past from NWTF to sustain the business.  In the future, Emily would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Shamiso
description: Shamiso is a 20-year-old business woman living in the Shurugwi district of Zimbabwe. She has been rearing broiler chickens for five months and wants to expand her business. Currently she produces batches of 50 broiler birds every six weeks. She was encouraged by the Mother Support Group in her community to start the business.   When she is not working, Shamiso serves as a Cama (a network of graduates) member who volunteers to work in schools within the community. With the requested loan, Shamiso intends to make bulk purchases of chicks, feeding troughs, and feed in order to increase her production and boost her sales. With the additional profits she hopes to expand into a retail business, create employment in her community, and pay for her university fees.

name: Ismoil
description: Ismoil lives in the Vose region. He's forty years old, married and has four children. He's a salesman at the market. He has an outlet where he sells men's clothes, such as: T-shirts, pants, jackets, etc. He's been doing this for the last six years and is asking a loan in order to buy some summer pants and T-shirts.

name: Abdullah-E-Mubina Group
description: Abdullah is a member of Abdullah-e-Mubina group. He lives in Khir Khana, Kabul, Afghanistan. He is married with four children, one son and three daughters who are enrolled in school.  He has got a shop in which he does embroidery work. He designs different kinds of clothes and does very beautiful embroidery work on them. He needs the loan to purchase embroidery materials and expand his business as well.  He hopes to be a good businessman in the future and that he will progress.

name: Mujeres Lago San Jorge Group
description: About half way up the intense drop from Solola to Panajachel squats the quaint village of San Jorge. In the breathtaking town with perfect views of the lake Atitlan in every corner resides the trust bank “Mujeres Lago San Jorge”, composed of 10 women.  With her child in hand and her ears perked, Juana (the group's elected president) thoughtfully listened as the Friendship Bridge loan officer gave this month’s training session on family planning. 34-year-old Juana, a mother of four, is the owner of a shop which specializes in selling goods for daily consumption.   Having been with Friendship Bridge for various years, Juana hopes to continue her endearing development by reinvesting the loan she will receive into purchasing a larger variety of goods to expand her store as well as her clientele basis. By doing so she holds the aspirations to one day move into a bigger store in a better location.   The money made from her store is put towards the proper education and correct nourishment for her children, for which she gives much credit to Friendship Bridge.   Aside from the family planning session which she received that day, as a part of Friendship Bridge’s Microcredit Plus program, Juana and others are given monthly, non-formal education sessions that include topics such as health, business, and specific subjects about women.     Juana and the trust bank Mujeres Lago San Jorge are beyond grateful for the confidence of Kiva investors around the world for giving them this opportunity for growth through their small business. Without these loans, Juana and her companions could be stuck in a poverty trap that holds nothing short of a bleak future.

name: Solomon
description: Solomon sells automobile spare parts. He is 30 years old and married with a child. He has been in the business for a long time. He hopes for a loan of 100,000 nairas to purchase more automobile spare parts.

name: Joseline Patricia
description: Joseline is 25 years old, and she lives with her parents.  She is single, and she lives in the San Miguel department of San Miguel.  She buys and sells cosmetics and clothes.  She founded this business five years ago.  Her mother helped her start it because her mother has experience in the business.  She works every day from 7:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m.  She is now requesting a loan to buy merchandise like cosmetics, creams, and lotions.  She will also buy clothes for her business.  This investment will help her a great deal.  Joseline does not want to neglect her business.  She plans on having it for a long time.  The business is where she manages to get her own income.  Joseline’s prime objective is to have a profitable business that is capable of taking care of her customers’ demands and covers the family’s expenses.

name: Lilia
description: Lilia is 26 years old and lives at her in-laws’ house, along with her husband and six year old daughter.  She’s been knitting and embroidering for the past four years; a trade she learned from her family and now she produces beautiful quality works that are used in traditional dances throughout the city.  In this way she can contribute to the household finances and care for her young daughter who attends school.  Lilia’s sales are profitable and she wants to make large quantities of embroidered skirts, so that she can take advantage of the approaching festive seasone.  This will be her third loan through MFP, and she’s glad to know that she has financial support.  She’s always been responsible with her payments and is happy to be a part of a communal bank because all of its members are responsible and united people.  She appreciates those who make this loan possible and it will be very useful for her business’ progress.  She will use the money from this loan to buy bales of yarn, fabrics, and thread so that she can increase her production.  Translated from Spanish by Hugo Reyes, Kiva Volunteer

name: Patrick
description: Patrick is a married man. He has five children. He operates a transport business where he transports customers using his motorcycle. He has been involved in this business for four years. His business is located in a good area and his primary customers are locals. He describes his biggest business challenge to be competition. He will use the Kes 20,000 loan to buy a water tank to store clean water for domestic use. His business goal is to own a transport vehicle within five years. This is his first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. He will use the anticipated profits to purchase another motorcycle and employ someone use it.

name: Sary's Group
description: Sary, 41, is a mother of five dependent kids who lives in Banteay Meanchey province. To support her family condition, she raises pigs and works for a labor fee to get additional money for 21 years. Her pigs have not grown well so that she could earn income only about 40,000KHR per day. With VisionFund, this is Sary’s first time to take a Kiva loan. As a group leader of three, she will manage her entire loan portion to buy more pigs and pigs feed to support her business. She hopes that this loan will help her to earn good income and update her living standard.
town: Banteay Meanchey Province, Mongkul Borey District

name: Richard K
description: Richard is 28 years old, has four children, and lives in Kanungu District. He is a market trader selling produce and cereals. His business is located in a daily market of Kihihi. He proudly says he has a great number of customers that includes nearby schools and the town council population. Richard, who has spent seven years in his business, attributes his success to the freshness of his produce, trust that his customers have invested in him, and the availability of produce. Richard is able to meet the daily demands of his customers due to the constant supplies he gets. He also ventured in alcohol sales that has been very critical in increasing his profits.   In the future, Richard plans to expand his businesses and educate his children to higher levels. This is Richard's first loan from Pearl and Kiva and he hopes for the best outcome although his first capital was from a loan through a local Savings and Credit Organization (SACCO). With the Kiva loan, Richard intends to use his hard-working spirit to expand his business by purchasing more cereals for resale.

name: Andrey
description: Andrey grows vegetables in greenhouses. Due to the previous loans he increased the income and bought a truck. Andrey is an active and hardworking young man. He wants to develop his business further. Business expenses have grown more than Andrey expected. At the same time produce prices did not grow that much. Even though Andrey received less profit he is thankful he can continue taking care of his family.   Andrey is asking for a loan of 60,000 UAH to buy fertilizers, film cover and seeds for greenhouses. Andrey wants to get ready to start the new season and get a bigger income.

name: Mary
description: Mary Q. sells rubber and used clothing.  She is married and has 2 children.  Business is doing very well and she wants to increase sale but lacks enough capital.    She is asking for an additional capital to buy more goods for sale.

name: Felicisima
description: Felicisima is a 79-year-old widow and lives in Labo, Aloran, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. She has five adult-age children who love and support her. She is requesting a loan from PMPC to buy her maintenance like milk, medicine, etc. to make her healthier and able to play with her grand children. Felicisima has been a member of PMPC for 10 years. In the future, she wants to see her family happy and love each other.

name: Harrison
description: Harrison is a resident of Malindi, Kenya. He runs a motorcycle transport business in the area. This mode of transport is preferred by many who lack enough money for other transportation and also for movement within short distances in the area. He began the business three years ago. Harrison was introduced to Milango by his friends and is applying for a loan of 21,050 Kenyan shillings to add to his savings and to purchase another motorcycle. Harrison will save the additional income obtained from this loan. The current challenges in the motorcycle transport business are theft of cycles and the high cost of fuel and spare tires. He hopes to own many more motorcycles as he has seen the returns in the business.

name: Daniel
description: Daniel has been in and around the food and customer service industry his entire life. His father made his living working in restaurants, and Daniel has worked for hotels and restaurants all over San Diego. As a first-generation college student, Daniel pursued a business degree with a background in accounting and economics at San Diego State University, eventually transferring to National University, where he had more flexibility to work while earning his degree.   Last year, Daniel’s brother-in-law, who has been a sushi chef for over 15 years, approached him with an opportunity to partner in starting a sushi business. Daniel happily accepted, and they launched Sushi Uno, a pop-up food vendor serving fresh sushi at outdoor farmers’ markets and festivals. The combination of his years of business experience and his new partner's talent as a sushi chef enabled their fledgling business to slowly gain a loyal following at the two farmers’ markets where they regularly sell.  	 Sushi Uno strives to produce the highest quality products possible while keeping it affordable. They buy their fish fresh from Catalina Offshore, a company that is ethical and sustainable, and once their food truck is up and running, Sushi Uno aims to be fully organic.   “Our sushi is something different,” said Daniel. “We want to not only offer the freshest fish available to our customers, but also put our own Mexican twist on it.”  This $10,000 Kiva loan will enable Sushi Uno to go mobile by starting a sushi food truck. They plan to renovate a truck, as well as pay for the supplementary costs, such as permits and licenses. Daniel has done his research on food trucks in the area and sees a lot of room for their unique business. He plans to focus on serving customers outside of breweries, while also maintaining their interest in the San Diego farmers’ markets scene. With a focus on customer service and providing top quality food at affordable prices, Daniel wants to build a top-notch brand while also giving back to the community. 	 Daniel is committed to this business and is pictured above in the center working alongside his employees, Azucena and Bertin. He hopes that diversifying his business revenue will allow him to go full-time at Sushi Uno, and eventually allow him to hire other relatives.  	 Check out their Square website at: http://squareup.com/market/sushi-uno

name: Josephine
description: Josephine is 62 years old and married with 10 children. She earns a living by raising pigs in the Philippines. Josephine is borrowing 25,000 PHP through NWTF to purchase feed and vitamins for her pigs. Josephine has been raising pigs for 15 years and also earns an additional income from buying and selling seaweed.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to repair and renovate her family home.

name: Rosemarie
description: Rosemarie runs a general store in her village. She sells different kinds of vegetables, cooking ingredients and other commodities. Through her business, she is able to earn PHP1,000 (about US$21) weekly. She is 47 years old and married to Johnny P. Sr.  According to Rosemarie, she wants to run her store as an alternative income to her husband’s business. This helps her family to meet their basic needs, which are expensive now-a-days.    Though she earns PHP1,000 weekly, it is still not enough. Rosemarie is requesting a loan of PHP7,000.00 so she can buy more vegetables to sell in their village. This will allow Rosemarie to generate more income and save funds for her youngest daughter to pursue her college studies.   Rosemarie hopes that her loan request will be approved. The loan will greatly help her to earn her more profit and to attain her dreams in life.

name: Gloria Maria
description: With laughter and jumping, the children come up to Gloria's fruit and candy stand, a place where they find their favorite snack. The children always leave contented with the quality of the products and the excellent service they get. She is 48 years old, single, and has an adult child, who is her right hand man. She began her business 25 years ago, selling fruit in baskets in various markets, until she managed to establish a fixed location. Now her little spot is her primary source of income.  She asks for this loan to increase her production of capital. She needs to purchase fruit, such as mango, banana, jocote, and papaya among others, and also candies. Gloria places her confidence in the loan, with which she hopes to expand her customer base in order to increase her income and be able to improve her family's quality of life. She is a woman full of dreams and with a vision for the future. One of her goals is to grow her business, to have a larger place in which she can offer better customer service.

name: Maria Julio
description: Maria has had a business for more than ten years and works more than ten hours a day in her little grocery store. She is unmarried and has five adult, economically independent children. She lives in her own home that she was able to acquire because of the income her business provides. She will use this loan to buy peanuts, beans, and used clothing to resell. In the future, Maria plans to build some extra rooms to rent out so she can increase her income and improve her life. She also hopes to expand her business. She will continue to request loans from Hluvuku-Adsema to reach her goals.

name: Justina
description: Justina, aged 51, is a hard-working woman.  She has lived with her husband Dionisio for some time, and they have four grown children together.  Now they live in their own home, located in the hamlet of Bellavista – Huaracayo.  The days of this valiant woman are centered on hard work.  33 years ago, she began her path in agriculture.  Over this time, she has managed to acquire, thanks to her effort, her own farmlands, her small house, and to move her children ahead in life. According to her, her children help her maintain her crops of potatoes, peas and other vegetables in good order.  What she likes most about her work is being able to spend most of her time with her family.  "Even though I don't live with my grown children, we always help each other out.  They are also farmers", says Justina, very happily.  Her main difficulty is the lack of working capital, which is why she started to work with the communal bank in her area.  She is sure that with this, she will be able to achieve her goal of increasing crop quantity.  She now wants to move into growing corn and peas, from which she will obtain new earnings.    She belongs to the “Señor de Muruhuay” Communal Bank, and this is her first loan through MFP, from whom she is hoping for a small loan to achieve her goals.  She also promises to be punctual with her repayments.  On receiving your help, Justina will invest the requested money in purchasing several bags of natural fertilizers to spread on the pea crops, which have shown little growth.

name: Lanimer
description: Lanimer, 35 years old, is a single mother blessed with three children. They are currently residing in the village of Nappaccu Grande. She has been selling generic and branded medicines in their village for almost 15 years and she's earning a net income of PHP 10,000 every month. She wanted to avail a loan of PHP 15,000 to purchase boxes of generic and branded medicines to sell not only in their village but in different places as well. Her net income is usually spent on their daily expenditures and on allowances for her children. She's hoping that this loan will be granted immediately to improve her business.

name: Phan Thi
description: Ms. H. has been a member of this organization since 2003.  She has 2 children who are now grown adults.  Her family place of residence is in close proximity to a river which allows them to fish.  Beside the family’s fishing business, Ms. H. and her family is able to invest into raising livestock.  Her family’s finances has been steady and growing, averaging 4.000.000d/month from both businesses.  This next loan she is requesting an amount of 10.000.000d to buy supplies for her fishing business.  Translated from Vietnamese by Lynn Nguyen, Kiva Volunteer

name: Carmen
description: Carmen, 54, is married and has two children who are independent adults.  Currently she lives in her own house with her husband.  Carmen's job is selling clothing and cosmetics via catalogue.  She has done this work for 11 years.  She sells in her house and works alone.  When she doesn't have a lot of customers during the day, she goes out to sell her products in the street among her friends, neighbors, and family members.  Sometimes she also goes to other towns where she exchanges her products for other ones that she later sells in her town markets.  Now she wants to get into selling groceries because there's no store in her area and she has seen the possibility of improving her income.  Carmen loves her job and she likes to have contact with people.  Her happiness and mischievousness allow her to constantly attract customers.  She wants to set up a much bigger store in the future where she'll sell a wide variety of products.  This is her fifth loan with Kiva.  She's happy to know that she'll have access to a line of credit to get ahead with her business.  This is why she pledges to make her payments responsibly.  With the requested amount of 2000 soles [PEN] she'll buy clothing for children and adults as well as food products to sell in her house, including rice, sugar, flour, and others.

name: Reygie
description: Reygie A. is 30 years old. She is married and the happy mother of three children. Her husband is a hardworking farmer. They both work hard for the future of their children. Reygie lives with her family in Tagpangi, Cagayan de Oro, Misamis Oriental, Philippines.   Reygie buys and sells fruits and vegetables in their village. She peddles her products every day. Sometimes, she just has her stall standing by their residence and entertains walk-in customers. Reygie works with determination on her business because she considers herself the breadwinner of the family. All of her children go to school and all are still dependents of Reygie.  For now, Reygie is planning to rent a  stall in the market. According to her, this is much better than peddling. In order for Reygie to reach her plans, she wants to take advantage of the loan opportunity given by HSPFI (a Kiva partner). She is now applying for loan amounting to PHP 11,000.00. This amount would cover her rent expenses and additional stocks of fruits and vegetables. She is aiming for a higher income, and she plans to have savings for future use.
town: Tagpangi, Cagayan de Oro, Misamis Oriental

name: Akif
description: Akif, a 53-year-old man, is married with three children. He sells construction materials wholesale. He has 12 years of experience in this field. Construction materials made of wood are quite expensive and, at the same time, are in high demand among local people.  Akif's sales place is located in the central Saatli bazaar. Akif`s customers always come to Akif to buy materials, and he is always ready to make a discount. He serves people not only from his home city but also from neighboring villages and cities.   Akif`s business brings in a stable income of 160 Azerbaijani manats (AZN). He applied for a 1400 AZN loan to purchase more materials and cover customers' demand. He has already demonstrated himself to be a good client with a positive credit history.

name: Ramona Del Socorro
description: Ramona lives in the village of Condega some 35 kilometers north of the city of Estelí. She is a single mother who lives in her own home along with her daughters, whom she has raised and educated on her own for a very long time. She has made a living as a caretaker at a home for the past six years, which provides her with continuity and stability. She works Monday-Friday from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., and on the weekends she travels to some of the surrounding communities to sell all kinds of clothing as well as cosmetics. She came to the offices of Kiva partner CEPRODEL requesting a loan to belong to the water and sanitation alliance. This will allow her to build a bathroom that will include a toilet, shower and sink as well as a septic tank, since the current conditions aren't very good. In this way she will have these essential services inside her home and have a more dignified place to live with improved conditions, since the latrines contaminate the environment and through this project she will be able to enjoy better health and hygiene and avoid illnesses. This program targets the lowest class, because without this funding it would be impossible to build these services.

name: Ulysses
description: Ulysses H. is from the village of Quirino, Solano, Nueva Vizcaya. He is 33 years old. Ulysses is married and has 1 school-aged child. To make a living, he owns and operates a business venture in the services sector. While not the only means of generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from providing transportation services to local community members. Ulysses has been engaged in his motorcycle transport business for over two years and earns approximately 6,000 PHP a month from these activities.  In 2009, Ulysses joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Ulysses is requesting a new loan of 5000 PHP which will be used to repair a transport vehicle used in the business. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Ulysses from ASKI. He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to financially support immediate members of his family.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 25 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly of farmers, fishermen and small business entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Sophorn's Group
description: Sophorn’s group lives in a rural village in Kampot province in Cambodia. Sophorn makes a living cultivating rice to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Aisha
description: Aisha sells apples, detergent, and sachet water in her shop. Aisha has been in this business for a long time. She is a LAPO Microfinance client. Aisha is 46 years old and married with 5 children. Aisha lives in Agege and she is requesting the loan amount of N 140,000 to purchase more apples and detergent to sell. She thanks all who make this loan possible.

name: Abel
description: Abel is 48 years old, married, and the father of four, aged between 14-18 years, all attending school.  He has been practicing  mixed farming for more than ten years.  He produces maize, tea leaves, tomatoes, onions and beans which he sells locally.  He has requested this loan of Kshs. 55,000 from Juhudi Kilimo to buy a dairy cow. Extra income earned from this loan will support the family financially and improve their living standard.  In five years he hopes to have five cows producing at least 30 litres of milk a day.   The challenges he is faces are changes in weather, seasons, and lack of a ready market for his produce.  He is thankful to Juhudi for helping him improve financially.

name: Teymur
description: Teymur A. is 24-year-old man who sell fruits and vegetables in the central bazaar of the Saatli region. He has 4  years of experience in this field. He lives with his parents, and his business is the only income source for his family. Teymur applied for $1200 USD to improve the conditions of his store.

name: Istatoy
description: N. Istatoy is 33 years old. She is married and is the mother of two children.  Istatoy's lack of a stable job and the slow productivity of her husband's business as an ecologist didn't leave enough money to pay the expenses of the family. This was the reason that Istatoy decided to start her own business eight years ago, selling national dresses for women. Little by little she has made her business grow and, by offering her clients installment payments, her orders are getting bigger.  Now Istatoy’s business is running normally. However, she would like to continue bettering herself and her business so that her situation will be stable in the future. She is asking for a loan of 3,000 Somoni that will enable her to buy new garments for her business. The power to help her business grow is in your hands.    More about Tajikistan and IMON International Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium B.C. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit:  www.imon.tj

name: Jose Segundo
description: José Segundo is 56 years old, single, lives in his family home in a rural area of Oyotun district, Chiclayo province, Lambayeque department, Peru. José Segundo has good personal and work references from inhabitants of the area. People in this area primarily work in agriculture, business, and livestock.José Segundo provides services as a farm laborer. He has more than 10 years experience in this business. He seeks a loan to make home repairs and maintain equipment and tools. The investment will enable him to have better conditioned tools and equipment, which greatly influences his work. José Segundo plans to improve the productivity of his services and thus be able to meet the diverse needs of the inhabitants of the area.José Segundo is a recurrent member of Epyme Alternativa. He has had two loans of 500,00 and 1000,00 which were repaid punctually. Since he became an Epyme Alternativa client his business and quality of life have improved.

name: Blessed Mary Group
description: Cecelia K. is the leader of the group of five borrowers called Blessed Mary. She is 44 years old, married and has 8 children who range in age from 8 to 26 years. She also cares for two nephews and a niece. She could not continue her education through 11th grade due to poverty. For 6 years Cecelia has been selling used clothes at the Vai Town market close to downtown Monrovia, Liberia.  She started selling with 7,000 Liberia dollars she received from her brother, as working capital. Cecelia sells good looking used clothing to customers and encourages them to continue buying from her. Cecelia plans to use her 7,500 Liberian dollar portion of this 37,000.00 Liberian dollar group loan to buy used bed spreads and used rugs. Her dream is to become an international business woman, build more houses and to educate her children to the highest level.    In the photo that accompanies this profile, Cecelia is the one holding the sign. And Evelyn is inset at the lower right.  About LEAP: The Local Enterprise Assistance Program (LEAP) is Liberia's largest and oldest continuously operating microfinance institution with 13 branches across the country. Founded in 1994, the non-profit organization has survived periods of civil war and severe socio-economic hardship. LEAP seeks to help rebuild post-conflict Liberia through its group and individual loans to micro- and small-scale entrepreneurs, and puts emphasis on lending to women.

name: Luis Alberto
description: Luis Alberto is 35 years old, in a common-law relationship, and lives with his wife and children who are his highest priority. He intends to use this loan to buy tools and equipment, which will help to facilitate his work in the construction sector. He builds primarily houses, a skill that allows him to take advantage of the knowledge he acquired through his training. Luis Alberto has been in this line of work for years and has worked with people who have much more experience.  Over time, he has been able to practice his craft and is now able to generate better earnings.  As a result, Luis Alberto is able to continue investing in his business activity. He also wants to accomplish some personal goals, as well as be able to build homes that have better finishes.  Luis Alberto can also increase the quantity and quality of his work. With the purchase of this equipment, he intends to build more houses in various designs so that he can fulfill the requests of his customers. This is his first loan that he has received from FUDECOSUR. Luis Alberto has not received any other loans from the state banks, so FUDECOSUR is offering this loan with better terms and a lower interest rate.

name: Portocal
description: P. P. (literally translated, Orange Orange) is one of the leaders of the community in the Sliven Roma ghetto.  His wife began operating a small food pantry 10 years ago while P. drove a taxi in the center of Sliven to generate the capital needed to support the business while it started.  6 years ago, he and his wife moved to a larger location and now continue to operate the small neighborhood grocery store. Now, the one-room store is big enough to employ P., his wife and two daughters, both in their 20s, and support their four children.  P. has taken 8 bank loans to expand his business over the years, and has proudly repaid each one fully and on time.  He is excited about the Kiva program, however, because it permits him to borrow money for dramatically less than he had been paying.    P. is a role model within his community, as his business is one of the very few that has been successful over time.  He is known for his honesty and compassion, extending credit to families that would otherwise go hungry between paydays.  With this loan he plans to increase his inventory and provide a working capital cushion.  The Roma, commonly known as gypsies, is a severely marginalized social group in Bulgaria and throughout the Balkans.

name: Rosario
description: Rosario is a married woman who lives in the municipality of Oslob, Cebu.  She earns her living by operating a fish vending business.  Her husband Quirico, who is 45 years old, works as a laborer to earn his living and helps in his wife's business activities.  They have four children who are 7 to 21 years old. Rosario joined NWTF-Project Dungganon in 2005 because she aspired for something better for her family. With the help of her past 10 loans from NWTF-Project Dungganon, Rosario has been incrementally lifting her family out of poverty by the sweat of her brow.  Her previous loan of PHP 26,000 helped her earn a monthly profit of PHP 22,000, thus uplifting the family's standard of living.  This time, for her 11th loan, she is borrowing PHP 29,000 to use as additional capital for her business so that she can continue to save up for future family needs. Rosario L. is a Dungganon woman who is following an honorable path toward the achievement of her dreams.    About NWTF:  In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF) is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means Honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress from earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem that is bestowed upon a member of a community who has earned the respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work.  Help NWTF continue its mission to help the poorest in the Philippines by joining the NWTF Kiva lending team at http://www.kiva.org.

name: Lwamba Development Group-Mityana
description: 30-year-old N. Fatuma is affiliated with Lwamba Development Group-Mityana. Five years have now passed since she began her pharmacy business in Lwamba trading center. It is a business this happy-go-lucky married mother of three began on completion of her nursing course. Weekly, Fatuma says this business generates shillings 105,000 as profits and she says that with this loan, she is going to purchase more drugs to resell.

name: Las Prosperas De Carabayllo Group
description: Sra. Micaela Jade is 29 years old and has four small children.  She is part of the group “Las Prósperas de Carabayllo”, which consists of eight individuals who reside in the district of Carabayllo.  Her fellow members elected her to be President of the group’s Board of Directors.  Sra. Micaela Jade sells “mazamorra” (corn porridge) and food every afternoon on the doorstep of her house where she has small tables set up for her business.  She began selling porridge after her mother convinced her that she needed to earn extra income to help with the household expenses.  Over the past year, she has increased her business and now sells other foods.  Through her work, she has been able to assist her husband with the family expenses and her children’s school expenses.  Her new goal is to open a well-stocked grocery store.  Micaela plans to continue working very hard, so she believes it will not take her long to achieve this goal.    The loan she is requesting will be used to purchase and install a canopy to cover the space where she serves food and porridge.  Part of the money will be used to buy tables and chairs so that her customers can be more comfortable while enjoying the tasty food that she prepares.  Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Claudia Veronica
description: Claudia is 21 years old, single, and lives with her grandparents in the town of San Martin, a suburb of the City of Chiclayo.  For the past year she’s been selling cosmetics through catalogs.  She started this business out of necessity for generating an income, which she needed for her personal expenses and to contribute to her family’s support.  She’s been putting a lot of effort into her work, and has been improving her sales.  She now has steady customers who request her products.  Claudia would like to expand her business by buying items at sale prices and reselling them, thus increasing her income.  In order to help her meet her objective, she has seen fit to request this first loan of 1,000 PEN ($375) through Edpyme Alternativa.  Claudia is very persistent and hard working.  Her customers prefer to deal with her because of her responsibility and commitment to her work.  Her greatest desire is to provide a better quality of life for her grandparents. Translated from Spanish by Hugo Reyes, Kiva Volunteer

name: Abdurakhmon
description: T. Abdurakhmon is 32 years old. Together with his wife they have 3 children. Bakhtiyor is an experienced bread baker. He has been doing this business for more than 10 years. He is baking the national bread “lepeshka” at home. His wife helps him with his business.   Having many customers Abdurakhmon is selling the majority of his products just from his place. However, he is also running the trading place in the central local market for selling lepeshka.   Now Abdurakhmon requests $1500 USD. He is planning to purchase flour at wholesale as required for his business. Abdurakhmon is grateful for all supporting him and promises to manage the loan with accuracy.      More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History  Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Maha
description: Maha is 34 years old, married and lives in Jubaiha Amman, Jordan. She is requesting a loan for 500 JD to buy women's and children's clothes to sell to her friends and neighbors. She hopes that expanding her inventory of products will allow her to meet her goal of opening a shop and providing her family with a higher standard of living.

name: Sabelita
description: Sabelita is a 53-year-old married woman who is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Sabelita has sold firewood for 5 years and requests 19,000 PHP through NWTF to purchase firewood to sell.  She successfully repaid her previous loan and requests a new loan to further build her business.  Sabelita would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Estelita
description: Estrelita is a hardworking woman entrepreneur with seven children.Estrelita has a general store in the Philippines. She has requested a 20,000 PHP loan through NWTF in order to buy more stock of groceries to sell. She successfully repaid her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her business.Estrelita dreams that one day, she will be able to save money to expand her business.

name: Nguyen Thi
description: Mrs Nguyễn Thị S.  is a TYM fund member since 2001. Her first loan of 1.000.000 VND was used to buy/trade dry food at the market. After that she decided to to switch to raising egg laying ducks and pigs. Today her family income is 4.000.000 VND a month. She is seeking a loan of 19.000.000 VND to expand her operations, increase her revenue.  Translated from Vietnamese by Khang Ho-Si, Kiva Volunteer

name: Blanca Maria
description: Blanca is 46-years old.  She is married and has a young daughter, 13-year old Cintia.  Thanks to her parents' hard work and dedication, Cintia is able to go to school at an institution very close by.  For the last two years, Cintia's mother has earned her living buying and selling cattle.  She is requesting the loan so she can keep investing in her livestock business.  The business has become a great source of income.  Thanks to her business, Blanca is able to help her husband with the household expenses.

name: Rizalie
description: Rizalie works hard to support her family. She is married and has a ice cream vending business in the Philippines.  Rizalie requested a 28,500 PHP (Philippine peso) loan through NWTF to buy additional ingredients for her ice cream business.  She has been in this business for four years now.
