In the future, Rizalie would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Herlinda Fiorella
description: Herlinda is a 22-year-old young woman. She lives in the city of Ica, in the Santiago district with her little 2-year-old son. Unfortunately, for various reasons she separated from her partner. Now she is both parents for her child. She is a fighter, enthusiastic and very determined. She dedicates all her efforts to work to get ahead in life. In her free time she likes to watch television with her child.   Unfortunately, due to lack of economic resources, Herlinda could not complete her nursing degree that she wanted so much, but she dreams that she will be able to very soon.  By her own initiative and thanks to the support of a friend, more than 2 years ago Herlinda started her small beauty product sales business. She works at her business about 8 hours daily, in which she attends to a good quantity of customers. Herlinda believes that her business runs well because of the good products that she sells, as well as because of the likable and respectful treatment she offers to her customers.  Herlinda is very grateful to Kiva lenders. Now thanks to the offered support she will be able to buy merchandise like perfumes, cosmetics, and purses among other items. In this way, Herlinda will have her business well stocked and she will be able to increase her sales and her earnings, with which little by little she hopes to be able to save the necessary money to start her studies and that way to be able to secure the well-being of her young son.

name: Kuña Katupyry Group
description: Description: The communal bank "Kuña Katupyry", was formed in July 2008 by hard-working women in an area not favored with economic development.  During the past three years of taking out loans, they have always tried to keep up with their payments. This communal bank is in an area that does not get much business, so the women have to go to other cities to sell their products. One of the members is Mrs Floriana who makes crafts for a living.  She embroiderers fabrics and clothing and also makes crafts like bedspreads, tablecloths, and other things. Her customers greatly appreciate her work because it has a good finish and is very delicate. Mrs. Floriana's family is very humble and her house is lacking in some comforts which is why she is taking out a loan -- to buy beds for her children.  Translated from Spanish by Shelly Hubman, Kiva Volunteer

name: Diana Lucrecia
description: Diana is 19 years old. She is single and lives with her mother and siblings, who are her biggest priority. With her loan, she intends on buying materials to improve the structure of a greenhouse to use it to plant different vegetables. By purchasing these materials, she hopes to have be more efficient and do work in the best way and the highest quality. The idea to to use the knowledge she has gained over the years she has worked in this field and with the improvements in her technique increase production. With this purchase, she can develop her work with more facility and have some saving which will allow her to have more in her activity. This is the first loan she has received from FUDECOSUR. She has not had any other loans before in state banks, but FUDECOSUR has offered her a loan with more ease of payment and a much lower rate of interest.

name: Conegonda
description: Conegonda is 68 years old and widowed with seven children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Conegonda has a pig fattening business in the Philippines. Conegonda requested a PHP 16,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy feed, vitamins and vaccines for her pigs.  Conegonda has been in this business for 30 years. In the future, Conegonda would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Sri Ram Group
description: In 2009, six women from Muniguda village located in Rayagada district, one of the poorest regions in India, stepped out and decided to build a secure future for their family by sharing the burden of the family with their husbands. They formed a group named Sri Ram (named after Lord Rama who they believe will protect them). One of them is Lalita. The lady standing to the extreme left in the photo is Lalita.   Lalita is 26 years old, living with her husband, two sons aged 9 and 6 and one daughter aged 5. All three of the children are attending school. Lalita started selling vegetables like tomatoes, potatoes, onions etc., and seasonal fruits like mangos and strawberries in the local village market with the help of her husband. Her husband has been involved in vegetable and fruit selling for the last 10 years. He brings stock from the nearby bigger markets which are 300-400 km away and sells to the local wholesalers in their village market.   There was always some left-over stock that was not sold which had to be thrown away as they did not have a storage space of their own. So, Lalita decided to start selling these vegetables on her own by the roadside in the market. She now wants to rent a shop that will help her to have a place to sell the vegetables. It will also help her to buy more stock at a time and house the additional stock of vegetables. Buying more stock will help reduce her frequent travel to the market and eventually transportation and buying costs. A portion of the loan amount will help her to rent a shop in the market and purchase more stock of vegetables and fruits. She would like to grow her business and save enough to have a shop of her own.

name: Salma
description: Salma lives in the coastal town of Mombasa, Kenya. She is married and has five children, all of whom are in school. She earns a living by selling hardware and building supplies such as cement, wood and pipes. She also earns money on the side selling fresh juice. She is applying for a loan for Ksh 80,000 to buy a motorcycle. Her goals are to earn enough money to pay her children's school fees, meet her family's other basic needs and hire an employee to help her with her work.

name: Katala
description: Katala is a young man, aged 31, who works as a wholesaler selling phone credit and juices (retail and wholesale). He lives with a partner and has 3 children, the oldest of which is 6 and the youngest of which is 1. His oldest child goes to school. This loan would allow Mr Katala to meet his client's needs as well as grow his business, lower the amount he has to spend on transport and increase his profits so he can improve his family's quality of life.

name: Monica
description: Monica, a 48-year-old widowed mother of four children ranging in age from 16 years to 27 years, describes herself as ambitious. For the past 10 years Monica has been operating a clothing retail store. Her business is located in a viable location with plenty of customers.   Describing her biggest business challenge as insufficient capital for expansion, Monica has requested this Kes 20,000 loan to buy more clothes to sell. Her goal is to expand within five years, and she hopes that in the future she will excel in the business. This will be Monica's first loan with SMEP DTM.

name: Nigina
description: Nigina is a hard working and intelligent woman. She is 29 years old, married, and has a child. Her husband is a migrant worker in Russia who sends money home. Nigina also works, as she has been a dressmaker for over six years. She works out of her home, sewing traditional dresses for women and children. She also sews curtains to order for houses and offices. She tries to please her clients with high quality tailoring of the clothes and curtains she makes. The money her husband sends is not enough to provide the family with everything it needs, so Nigina needs to expand her business and earn a higher income. She needs a new sewing machine, and also fabric for making more of the traditional dresses. She is asking for a 5000 TJS loan to buy a sewing machine and fabric. She promises that as an honest person, she will repay the loan on time. She appreciates your kindness.

name: Careyl
description: Careyl  operates a transportation business for a living. After three years of running her transportation business, Careyl is happy to say that this helps her family a lot while awaiting the harvest from their crops. She has been able to sustain the business  and has plans to improve the services. She borrowed a loan from GDMPC micro finance to buy new tires to replace the old ones and accessories like helmets and raincoats. In the future, she wants to have a better standard of living with her family.

name: Jasminka
description: Jasminka is a 46-year-old woman living in the town of Tesanj in northern Bosnia and Herzegovina.  She is married and has a full-time job selling clothes.  She currently buys new clothes from a wholesaler and sells them from her home. Even though she doesn't have a store, Jasminka has not been kept from getting far with her business.  In fact, the lack of a store has helped keep her cost of doing business low.  Jasminka now has many loyal customers from her town, and when sales have been good, she has earned up to 1500 KM (US$1130) a month.   Jasminka is requesting her first loan from Zene za Zene in the amount of 1000 KM (US$775).  She would like to buy a large order of clothes that she can sell for the fall and early winter, and she thinks it will be a good idea to stock up on these items now.

name: Eka
description: Eka S. is 27 and married with 4 children (ages 1 month - 6 years).  She owns a business venture, catching & selling ocean-caught fish .  Eka has 7 years of experience in this business.  Eka needs a loan of WST $1500 to purchase a fishing boat.  She plans to use the earnings from her business (estimated to be 100 tala or US $42 per week) to improve/expand the business.  In 2008, Eka joined SPBD.    This is her 2nd loan with SPBD.   SPBD's loans are Eka's only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with traditional banks.  The following social metrics for Eka S. are provided by SPBD*: Overall Social Metric Score:                1.5 out of 3 Level of Education:                              1.56 out of 3 Level of total Household Income:         1.89 out of 3 Quality of Household Assets:              1.99 out of 3  *SPBD measures the living conditions of each of its borrowers to track her loan progress. The overall social metric score, provided by SPBD, is based upon a number of factors, such as the condition of the house/household assets, health, education, income level, and family reputation. A higher number represents a higher score. For example, a ""3 out of 3"" on education would mean that the borrower has graduated from university; a ""2 out of 3"" = secondary/high-school, and a ""1 out of 3"" would mean that the borrower is uneducated.  For more information on this score, please see SPBD's partner page at: http://www.kiva.org/about/aboutPartner?id=15  About SPBD In 2000, Greg Casagrande founded SPBD and since then, it has expanded from the main island of Upolu in Samoa to Savaii, as well as Tonga. SPBD's philosophy of lending is based upon the Grameen Bank lending method.  Please join SPBD's lending team on KIVA to receive on-the-spot updates on SPBD: http://www.kiva.org/community/viewTeam?team_id=8375

name: Mutabarhon
description: A. Mutabarhon lives in Rumi. She is 33 years old and married, with three children. Her husband is in Russia earning money. Mutabarhon herself has been trading on the market for over 12 years, chiefly in groceries. She asks for a loan in order to increase the turnover of the goods she sells.Translated from Russian by Anastasia Uglova, Kiva Volunteer

name: Rosa Marilu
description: Rosa is 43 years old and is in a common-law relationship. She lives in the family house which is made out of solid materials together with her spouse and her child. They live in a rural area of the district of Santo Tomás, Cutervo province, in the department of Cajamarca, Perú. Rosa has very good work and personal  references. The inhabitants of this place work mainly in raising and fattening livestock, raising small animals and growing products like potatoes, peas and corn. Rosa works raising and selling small animals (chickens, guinea pigs, pigs). She does her business with different restaurants in the district and she has 20 years of experience in this field. She also works as agricultural labor which she does in a number of villages close to the district of Santo Tomás. The loan will be used to buy small animals and feed for them which she will later sell. In this way she will generate more income for her benefit and that of her family.Rosa is a new member of Edpyme Alternativa.

name: Choern's Group
description: A villager from a rural area located in the Kandal Steung district of Kandal province, Choern is 53 years old and married. She has four children. The primary source of her family’s income is from rice farming. To better support the family, she also works as a garment worker while her husband works as a taxi-driver. Together, they have been in this business for thirteen-three years. Choern has been a member of VisionFund for two cycles already and she wisely and successfully used the past loans to improve her family’s livelihood and relieve financial burden. Now she is leading her group to ask for a loan. As the leader, Choern is going to use her portion to buy fertilizers and pesticides for her farmland and use a portion of it to spend for labor. She hopes to make more healthy rice so as to increase her family’s income to better off her living condition.

name: Nerissa
description: Nerisa M., 45 years-old, owns a sari-sari (general) store and is also raising chickens. She sells various goods in order to have a regular income for her family. She has five children. She said that she desires for a good life for her children and this is why she is doing the very best she can to be able to achieve her objectives. She is seeking a loan of Php 6,000 from Kiva partner Community Economic Ventures Inc. in order to buy chicks and additional merchandise for her sari-sari store.

name: Beatrice
description: Beatrice is 34 years old, married and lives in Gbarnga in Liberia. Gbarnga is located in the centre of Liberia in Bong County. The majority of the people are employed as farmers, cultivating crops such as rice, palm oil, and cassava.   Beatrice went to school and finished grade 12.  Her husband is a teacher, and she has a nine-year-old child at home who goes to school.    She has had a table business for the past four years, selling rice, oil, pepper, etc.  She works at her business nine hours a day, and she transports her goods to her business by bus. The biggest challenge she faces in her business is insufficient inventory on her table.    With the proceeds from the loan, she wants to buy rice, oil, pepper, etc.  She describes herself as a hardworking woman; she started her business with money from her mother. She is proud of her business because she gets money for her expenses.  In the future, Beatrice wants to own a house.      She wants to say thanks to the lenders who support BRAC Liberia.

name: Thao Thi
description: Mrs. Thao Thi N., 49 years old, livest in the town of Cao Minh - Phuc Yen, province of Vinh Phuc.  She joined the Fund in 1996 and borrowed money to invest in raising livestock and selling clay pots.  Thanks to her hardwork, the livestock and clay pot sales expanded and increased day by day, helping her family's finances become more stable.  Currently Mrs. N. is investing in raising pigs.  Besides that, her family also has a monthly income from her husband's salary as a security guard, so her family's finances are very secure with an income of 6,000,000 VND/month.  In this round of funding she would like to borrow 15,000,000 VND to invest in buying more pigs and feed for the livestock business.Translated from Vietnamese by Chi N., Kiva Volunteer

name: Elvira
description: Elvira is 50 years old, widowed, and has five children. She works very hard to provide for them. Elvira runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 10,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase additional inventory to sell. Elvira has been in this business for 10 years and sells a variety of items such as sugar, coffee, eggs, spices, shampoo, etc. In the future Elvira would like to build and expand her business to secure the financial stability of her family.

name: Janice
description: Janice G., photographed with one of her children, is from the town of Baclayon. She is 27 years old, married and has 4 young children. Janice owns and operates a business providing waste management and motorcycle transport services. Janice works hard to save for her children's education.  Janice joined CEVI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Janice is requesting a new loan of 5,000 PHP which will be used to repair an existing vehicle for better service. This will be the first loan taken out by Janice from CEVI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement her family's income.   About CEVI:  Community Economic Ventures, Inc (CEVI) has increased its portfolio significantly over recent years. Based in Bohol, it has numerous branches throughout the Philippines. In 2009, CEVI was awarded a CGAP silver award for transparency in social performance monitoring. CEVI not only provides credit for its clients but additionally savings, insurance, and training which are provided through regular cluster group meetings.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Donoi
description: Donoi T. is 37 years old and her business is the retail sales of footwear at the wholesale market in the Leova district. As winter is now virtually at an end, she needs to buy shoes for the spring season. The demand for winter shoes is low and T. earns nothing but she still must rent her table at the market. T. has requested a loan from MicroInvest to buy merchandise for the spring season.  In the future, T. would also like to buy clothing to sell during the spring season. This loan will help T. increase her future sales..

name: Mirtha Gladys
description: Mirtha is a 52-year-old woman who lives in the city of Pisco with her partner.  She is a very friendly, hard-working and enthusiastic person who has a great desire to do well in life.  Unfortunately, owing to a lack of financial means and the need to work in order to cover her expenses, Mirtha was unable to study to become a nurse, though she would have loved to have done so.  In her free time, she enjoys taking part in sports and she sometimes cooks a delicious 'duck with rice' to share with her family.  With a lot of determination and commitment, and with the support of her mother, Mirtha set up a small business selling groceries and school supplies.  Every day she starts her work early in the morning.  She can work approximately 12 hours a day and believes that she is doing well in her business because she has good customers who like her services.  Mirtha is very grateful to Kiva lenders because, thanks to their help, she will be able to buy merchandise such as rice, sugar, oil, milk, noodles, tuna, etc.  She will also buy school supplies and a shelving unit.  This will allow Mirtha to keep her business better stocked and equipped.  She hopes, as a result, to increase her sales and her income.  This will be very helpful to her as she will gradually be able to finish building her house and, in the not-too-distant future, she would like to be able to start another business.

name: Grupo De Mujeres De Chuisanto Tomas Sector Escuela Group
description: Cristina is a kind and persevering woman who is 27 years old. She is single and lives with her two sons aged between 1 and 19. This nice family lives in a community of Sololá. Cristina (first on the left in the photograph), with the eagerness to generate an income, has worked in the purchase and sale of typical clothing for four years. Thanks to this work, she has managed to help her family get ahead. Cristina, thanks to the kindness with which she looks after her business, has gained a lot of customers. But now she has realized that day by day, the world is more interested in fashion, and she has to improve her products, but one of the difficulties is that she does not have the necessary capital. For this reason, she asks for a loan, which she will invest in the purchase of güipiles (regional dress), and other traditional garments, to satisfy the needs of her clientele. Cristina hopes to be able to build a house made of brick, and to buy a plot of land for cultivation.

name: Siyeng's Group
description: A mother of five children living in Kratie province, Siyeng is 36 years old. For her family’s support, she grows cassava as the main source of income and works for others for a fee to earn extra income. This is her fourth cycle with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner), and she has fully repaid back her past loans completely. She leads a group of three to get new loan.   As the group leader, she will spend her loan portion to buy fertilizer to support her cassava farm. She hopes that she can get more yield than last year.

name: Nohra
description: Nohra is a 32-year-old musician living in Fourn Al Chebak in Beirut. He learned to play music ten years ago, and because music is his passion, he decided to embrace this profession and became a well-known DJ. Today, Nohra is requesting $1,000 to buy new sound equipment for his business.

name: Rady
description: Mrs. Rady S. (in the photo), 46 years old, and her husband, Mr. Vannak Monh, 47 years old, live in a village along National Road Number Two about 17 kilometers from Phnom Penh. They have been married since 1984 and have seven children - three sons and four daughters. One is married, another one is a garment factory worker and five attend school.  Rady is hired by manufacturers in her village to recycle. Her husband is a construction worker. She is asking for her first loan of $1,200 to dig a well for family use, to fill up the land of her house's foundation and to purchase a motorbike for her daughter to get to work.

name: Albertina
description: Albertina is a member of the “Estrellitas de Oro II” community bank which is located in the district of Puno, in the province and administrative district of the same name.  She is 56 years old, married and did not complete her primary education.  Albertina lives with her four children.  This lady has been working with the Movimiento Manuela Ramos for one year.  The first loan which she requested was for 500.00 nuevos soles with which she managed to increase her business capital. Her business is selling jackets.  She is now requesting a new loan for 1000.00 nuevos soles which will allow her to increase her merchandise, that is to say she will buy more jackets wholesale.  Her dream is to expand her business.  What she likes about the community bank is the interest made on savings.

name: Sambatra Gaspard
description: 55-year old Gaspard earns a living through selling second-hand goods and scrap iron, as does his wife. Each member of this couple has their own selling premises in two different towns. This loan will allow Gaspard to purchase more scrap iron and other used or second-hand goods so he can replenish his stock. This is the second marriage for both members of this couple. Each of them had one child from their previous marriages, so two children altogether, and they have had one child together since then. They have a total of three children living in their care. Gaspard's goal is to further develop his business and to become an ironmonger.

name: Ronald
description: Ronald R. is from the village of Gosi, Tuguegarao City. He is 39 years old. Ronald is married and has two school-aged children. To make a living, Ronald operates a family member's business providing transportation services. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from operating motorcycle transport services. Ronald has been engaged in this business for more than six years and earns approximately 3000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2007, Ronald joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and his ability to engage in business activities. Ronald has successfully repaid a previous loan of 7000 PHP from ASKI. Ronald is requesting a new loan of 7000 PHP, which will be used to repair an existing vehicle for better service. This loan will be the third loan taken out by Ronald from ASKI. He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to pay his children's tuition fees.   About ASKI: ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 29 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fishers, and small-business entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Carmen
description: Carmen is from Remolino Magdalena.  She was displaced to Atlántico department and settled there with her two young daughters who are now 23 and 25 years old.  Through her effort and work, she has managed to get her daughters ahead in their studies.  One of her daughters is now a professional and the other is about to become one.  With the death of her husband and the responsibility she had for her daughters, Carmen was forced to lead her household.  She developed her entrepreneurial abilities and started gaining business experience, selling dairy products and meat in stores in her sector.  She started this in 1998.  Later, the 'Network for Social Solidarity' gave her the opportunity to study dressmaking, a business activity in which she then began working, focusing in particular on making jeans.  Her main market is her local community.  She also has customers who she has been recommended to in other neighborhoods.  She distributes her products to these people for their own personal use or for them to sell.  This combines very well with her initial business activity of selling dairy products and meat.  This Kiva credit is the first loan that Carmen has received from Fundación Mario Santo Domingo and she will use it to buy rolls of fabric and supplies to meet her customers' demands.  Her dream is to finish educating her daughters and to own her own home.  For this reason, she works hard every day to improve the quality of the garments she makes and to increase her number of customers.  She faced her biggest challenge when she had to leave her home town but she feels that she has managed to get ahead in life with her family through her work and her faith in God.

name: Norma
description: Norma is 30 years old and lives in her mother-in-law's house along with her husband Gerardo, who is 31, and their 5 young children. From a young age she has worked the land, watching and helping her parents. This is how she learned all she needed to know for the land to be productive with no problems.     Currently Norma plants potatoes, beans and olluco, an Andean tuber, with her husband. She says that working in the fields can be tedious because she must always be on alert so that the crops aren't lost to weather or pest problems. However, she also knows that the reward for her effort and dedication will be a productive harvest. She will sell this harvest to wholesalers in the city, who offer good prices for quality products.    In addition to working in the fields, Norma also raises cattle and donkeys used for transporting goods. She often rents out the donkeys. In the future she plans to plant larger quantities of crops in order to increase production and improve her sales. This is her 5th loan with MFP [the Kiva field partner] and she is very satisfied with the work of her communal bank group because all of the members are responsible in repaying their loans. Norma plans to use the money from this loan to purchase fertilizer and potato seeds in order to start her next planting without any mishaps.   Translated from Spanish by Catherine Fountain, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sadia's Group
description: Sadia, a 28-year-old mother of one daughter, lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan where her husband works in the private sector. Since 2010, Sadia has been running a small beauty salon out of her home.   As a member of a five-person lending group, she has requested a loan from Kiva's partner BRAC Pakistan to purchase a variety of beauty and cosmetic products for her salon including facial creams, a hair dryer, makeup kits, nail polishes, etc.   Sadia is hopeful that the loan will be a productive one. With the profit she wants to expand her business and put aside some savings for her daughter's future. She is thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Flordeliza
description: Flordeliza is a hardworking woman entrepreneur with eight children, three of whom in school.  She earns a living by raising pigs in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 15000 through NWTF to purchase additional feeds and vitamins for her pigs.  She supplements this income with earnings from her food vending.  Flordeliza dreams that one day she will be able to save enough to buy more farm lands.

name: Susana Janet
description: Susana is 36, single, and has one daughter.  She lives in the Callanca area in the district of Monsefú, an area known at the regional level for it's tourist and religious festivals.  It is located 20 minutes from the city of Chiclayo.  She has raised and sold pigs and poultry for 10 years.  She raises her animals in different areas located behind her house.  When they have reached a good level of development, she sells them to her neighbors and the businesspeople that travel the area where she lives.  With the income she receives, she pays for her home's expenses and takes care of her young daughter.  Susana hopes to make some improvements to her pens and to acquire feed with which she plans to improve her animals' development.  This is why she thought it convenient to request her first loan from Edpyme Alternativa for 500 PEN, which which she plans to accomplish her goal.  She is a determined woman who gives her best every day to take good care of her young daughter.  People that know her in the area consider her an honorable and trustworthy woman.

name: Nakigalala South Najjemba Bena Group
description: N. Bena is a hardworking business who is 21 years old. She is married with two children, of whom one is schooling. She has a stone quarrying business and she has been operating this business for over two years. She is using the loan for her stone quarrying business. The business is improving as well as the family. Her future plan is to get more money and build a house.

name: Vida Y Esperanza Group
description: The Vida y Esperanza group is made up of three, hard-working women who have been earning their livelihood since they were very young.    In 1004, Rosa Amanda C. R. invested some of her savings to sell sour milk.  Currently, thanks to the loans, she sells a variety of dairy products.  Meanwhile, her fellow member Ángela del Carmen A., 50, has a small, unassuming store and Vida Luz C. A. has a tortilla shop.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Flying Eagles Youth Group
description: Grace is a member of Flying Eagles Youth Group which is located in Butula on the outskirts of Kyotera town. He is a single father with six children and he is 40 years old. He lives in a village in Rakai district with his children; five of his children still attend different schools around the area.  He is a businessman and a farmer too. His main business is bark-cloth selling and he has been in this business since 1997. He is also a farmer who deals in coffee growing.  He works six days a week and each day he works for 7 hours. He started this business in order to earn money for paying school fees for his children and to satisfy their day-to-day needs.  He has acquired this loan in order to buy more stock (to re-stock) of the bark clothes. He sells his products to traders in the city. His dreams are to build rentals in a nearby trading centre which can be of more help to his children and to educate the children to the highest level of education. His main challenge is changes in fuel prices which makes transport to the city very costly and this forces him to sell his products from his home at low prices.  He describes himself as an honest and hard working man.

name: Lam
description: Lam is aged 48 years and lives in Boribo district of Kampong Chhnang province. She is a married mother who has seven children, three of whom are dependent on her. To make a living, she has been with her farming for twenty-five years. She is able to earn about 30,000 KHR per day. This is the first loan for her, and now she is applying for a loan to buy a solar panel to generate electricity for her household. She hopes that her livelihood is improving and her children will have plenty of food.

name: Hodaridar Group
description: Our client Mpala, the representative of the Hodaridar group is a dynamic 53-year woman, a widow and the mother of six. Her husband died following an illness. Mpala sells palm oil. She had launched her business with her own funds received from her late husband. She displays her wares at the beginning of a big  road. She reports not having enough working capital. This new loan will allow her to buy five jugs of palm oil. She would like to see her children grow and also to build a nice house and expand her business. She thanks Hekima and its partners for supporting impoverished women who do not have access to traditional banks.

name: Kitungu Group
description: Mustafa, who is in his mid-30s, is married with two children, one son and one daughter.  Both are going to school.    He has been running two types of businesses.  One is buying shoes to sell and repairing shoes.  He has also been selling charcoal for a year and a half now.  He works from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily, and he is able to make a fair monthly profit.  This will be Mustafa's second loan from Tujijenge Tanzania.  He used the previous loan to start selling charcoal, and he also bought more shoes to resell and repaired more shoes because he had managed to get better shoe repair.    He is really happy with the loan because now he is leaving a happy life.  He used the profit to pay school fees and household expenses, and he also bought a plot of land.    He will use this loan to buy more sacks of charcoal, more equipment for shoe repair, and more shoes to resell. He dreams of expanding his business.  Mustafa will share this loan with his loan group "KITUNGU," which has three members who hold each other accountable for paying back the loan.

name: Marites
description: Marites is a 39 year old married woman from Talibon,Bohol. She has 2 children aged 3 and 11 years old. She farms, growing and selling rice. She has been growing rice for almost 10 years. Her husband is a carpenter. To finance her farming livelihood, she requested a loan of 30,000 PHP to buy fertilizers, pesticides and laborers' fees. In the future, Marites would like to expand her farming business to support the education of her children.

name: 05-Đông Hải Group
description: Dong Hai is a poor commune in Thanh Hoa province. The main sources of income of the inhabitants are from farming, livestock raising, and petty trades. Group 05, Ai Son 1 Village in Dong Hai commune nominated Mrs. Nguyen Thi Lam, born 1967, as group leader. Her husband is Mr. Bui Quang Dat, born 1962. Her family has four children, the first two are married, and the last two are still at school at Grade 6 and Grade 4. Previously, apart from farming, her family also raised ducks, chickens, and pigs. In this loan cycle, she wishes to borrow money to buy guavas, pineapples, mangoes, oranges, mandarins to resell to get extra income. All group members are borrowing their fourth loans with the same amount of VND3,079,800 (USD177), as below:   Ms. Le Thi Nhung, born 1962, borrows to raise ducks, chickens, cows.  Ms. Nguyen Thi Phuong, born 1960, borrows to buy fertilizer for her farm, and buy chickens, pigs to raise.  Ms. C. Thi Hoa borrows to buy rice to grow, buy banana leaves to sell, buy chickens, pigs to raise.  Ms. Nguyen Thi Chuy, born 1953, borrow to buy fertilizer, buy chickens and ducks to raise.  Translated from Vietnamese by Tu Duong, Kiva Volunteer

name: Lilias
description: Lilias is 35 years old and a married woman with six children. Five of them are in school. She has had a business selling clothes in Yei, South Sudan for five years.  Lilias is requesting this loan through BRAC South Sudan to purchase clothes for sale. She will use her extra income from this loan to pay her children's school fees.

name: Rosie
description: Rosie is 53 years old and married with four children. She works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 30,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more items to sell like canned goods, eggs, soap, soft drinks, etc.  Rosie has been in this business for 15 years.  In the future, Rosie would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Jose Mario
description: José, 70 years old, went to school up to the sixth grade. He is partnered and has two children, ages 20 and 25.  José gets up at 5:00 a.m. along with his wife and children to do the agricultural work and milk the cows.  José works in agriculture, which he learned from his parents. In the mornings his wife takes care of the household tasks and in the afternoon she works helping her husband to care for the animals and on other plots of land.  José needs to loan to purchase two cows, which an acquaintance is selling him, so that in the future they will produce milk, since his wife wants to make cheese, cream, and requesón [farmer's cheese] to be able to sell it in the areas near their community to get additional income for their family.   José, with the income that he gets from selling milk and his crops, will be able to build a respectable house to live in with his family.

name: Roseline
description: Roseline O. lives in Adeloko, Lagos State, Nigeria. She has been selling fresh fish since 1999. Roseline is 52 years old and is married with 6 children. She has been a LAPO member for the past 3 years. Now she needs a loan of $600 to purchase a deep freezer so that she can meet the demand of her customers and thereby increase her sales.

name: Ineza
description: Ineza is a 51 year old, married woman, from the Zestaponi district. She lives with her husband, who works at a private company and has a fixed salary of 400 GEL. The family ears a living with this income only and that is really hardly enough to meet even basic needs.   In spite of her high education, Ineza can't find any stable job and decided to start her own business. She requested a loan from local financial institutions and was rejected several times for lack of experience and her financial condition. The start-up program that is a joint initiative between Kiva and Credo, enabled her to get a loan of 1,500 USD for starting a trading business.   Ineza will rent a counter at the local store and will sell clothing and jewellery, transferred from Turkey where there is a worldwide market. She will generate her own income and do her bit for the family's welfare.  Ineza is looking forward to your help and kindness and will highly appreciate it.

name: Leonalyn
description: Leonalyn is 50 years old and married with one child who is in school, Leonalyn works very hard to provide for them.Leonalyn has a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 27,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy additional stocks of groceries to sell.Leonalyn has been in this business for five years and sells a variety of items such as sugar, shampoo, canned goods and other groceries. In the future Leonalyn would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Siah
description: Siah is 38 years old and she lives in the West Point area; she’s married with 3 children between the ages of 18 and 20. All of them live at home, and they are in school.  For the past 5 years, she has been involved in the sales of door locks, hinges, nails and other items. Her main challenge is the rise of the prices of goods. She started this business with a small amount of money and she learned it from her mother. She loves it when her customers buy from her, and it makes her proud to see her children in school. She has requested this loan to purchase more door locks, hinges, nails, and other items for her business. In the future she wants to build a shop.

name: Rodney
description: Rodney is studying for a degree in accounting.  His goal is to finish his degree and teach at the university level.  He comments that he comes from a very united family where the family members help each other.  Rodney is requesting this loan to pay for his university fees; this way he can continue to study for his degree.

name: Esther
description: Esther sells drinks and provisions. She is 32 years old and married with 5 children. She hopes to own a big super market in the future. She hopes for a loan in the amount of 50,000 NGN to purchase more drinks and provisions to sell. She says thank you to all kiva lenders

name: Daynor
description: Mr. Daynor Correón lives in a home under the “anticretico” rule.  (Anticretico is a unique, legal method of housing in which the owner of the building allows a person to live for a determined amount of time in exchange for a set amount of money, which will be returned at the end of the living period.)  He lives in the San Antonio zone, east of the city of La Paz.  Mr. Daynor is a public administration employee.    The loan that he is soliciting is to help him obtain social housing that will be paid for in installments, but requires an initial down payment.    This is the first time he has asked for a loan but the socioeconomical analysis that was performed qualifies him favorably and he can access a loan.  Translated from Spanish by Emma Felten, Kiva Volunteer

name: Greda Group
description: The  Grade  group will begin its forth loan cycle with ID-Ghana. It is made up of four members and is led by Kweku. The businesses that they own focus on polyethylene products, insecticide spray, smoked fish, yam, fresh fish, onions and palm oil. The loan that they are taking out will benefit small business owners, of whom Kweku is one. He says that three years ago, he joined ID-Ghana at the invitation of a promoter from the institution who went to visit him at his house. Currently he sells polyethylene products and insecticide sprays. He began this business when he noticed a lack of these products in his zone, and decided to invest some money in entering this field. The loan that he has requested will increase his capital (to buy polyethylene products and insecticide sprays in bulk) that he will get from wholesalers in the city of Accra and later sell from door to door. This type of work allows him to generate income to support himself since he is single and has no children. When asked what he likes about ID-Ghana, he said the health program and the training that the institution offers.

name: Gerame
description: Gerame is a married woman with three children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Gerame is 28-years-old and has one child who is currently in school.  Gerame has a food vending business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 10,000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase ingredients like peanuts, salt, garlic, tempura, etc. for her business.  Gerame has been in this business for six years. She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Piedad Elena
description: Piedad is 53 years old and is happily married to an amazing man. She lives with him in the municipality of Medellin, where she also has had a business since 2005. She inherited a sewing business from her family which has helped her to support her husband and family.Right now her family is going through a rough time because of a lack of money, so she doesn’t have money for her business either. In order to make the business sustainable, she needs some. She’s asking for a loan so she can buy a new sewing machine. She dreams of improving her house. Support this responsible mother and loan now. If you want to know more about the entrepreneurs and the loans from Interactuar, you can join the Lending Team called: “Friends of Interactuar Colombia”: http://www.kiva.org/team/interactuar_colombia

name: Judith
description: Judith is a resident of Kanyanya and a committed small scale business lady. She has operated a small retail shop for 3 years in Kanyaya Stage. She is widely known by most of the locals there and according to the appraisal made, she is of a very good character and worth dealing with financially.She has been dealing mostly with dry foods and other non perishable items, but intends to add a drinks section and this is the reason she has a applied for a loan of UGX700,0000 to facilitate her new initiative. Thank you Kiva lenders for supporting her.

name: Flordeliza
description: Flordeliza is a married woman with four children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Flordeliza is 38 years old and has two children who are in school.Flordeliza has a shell craft business in the Philippines.She requested a PHP 12,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy more shells and other supplies needed in her business.Flordeliza has been in this business for five years. In the future, she would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Abu
description: This is 50-year-old Abu T.. Abu was born in Makeni and is married with 5 children. Abu has sold second-hand clothes (called "junks" here) for the past 15 years now. He is seeking a loan of Le. 3,000,000 to enable him to buy more bundles of “junks” clothes. With a variety of  “junks” clothes in his shop, Abu will make more sales, increase the profit he makes, and consequently improve his family's well-being.

name: Angie Johana
description: This is Angie Johanna, 22. She lives with her husband and their daughter Emilie. Angie is a responsible and honest person with goals and dreams. One of her goals is to finish her degree in Comprehensive Early Childhood Care. A degree she chose because she thinks a human being is made of values and principles but above all with education which can form children in the early years. She strongly believes in Pythagoras’ quote “educate the children and it won't be necessary to punish the men.”   One of her dreams after finishing this degree is studying pedagogy and child psychology because she wants to give the best to her daughter, starting with a good education and help her family. This student was one of the beneficiaries for growth manager but they decided to terminate the agreement with the institution.  Her husband Oscar, who is her supporter, finds it difficult to pay the tuition that CampoAlto offers since he is the only person who earns in the household. This is why she is requesting a loan from Kiva who can give her the subsidy to be able to continue with this project that is very important to her.

name: Cinia Marilú
description: Cinia is a 38-year old woman who studied three years of high-school. She is single and has an 11-year old son who studies 5th grade. They live with her parents and brother.    She has worked as a dressmaker for 10 years. She started with a project for the Mayor's Office and kept learning since then. She also has a small business selling underwear, blouses and perfume, and offers her products to teachers and moms when she brings her son to school, between 10 and 12pm.   She is requesting a loan to buy labor, given that her father has a  7,000 sqm land of corn and a 3,500 sqm land of beans. She also needs to buy fertilizer to obtain a good output. Her goal is to produce a good amount of beans for sale, to invest the profits in her son's education and to continue growing her small dressmaking business.

name: 52 Quảng Hưng Group
description: Duyên N. Thị (82) is a 37-year-old woman living in the town of Thanh Hoá. Duyên is the group leader of a 3-member group loan offered by Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women. While each member of the group receives an individual loan, they all are responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults. The official name of this borrowing group is 52 Quảng Hưng (18.02.52 Quảng Hưng).  Duyên is married and has 2 school-aged children. She owns and operates a food stall, selling seafood products such as fish and shrimp in the local community. Duyên has been engaged in this business for over 5 years and earns approximately 2,100,000 VND a month from it.  In 2009, Duyên joined Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Duyên has successfully repaid a previous loan of 3,079,800 VND from Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women, which was used to purchase additional products to sell. She is now requesting a new loan of 6,000,000 VND which will be used to purchase fishes, shrimps...to resell. This will be the 3rd loan taken out by Duyên from Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve her family's general living conditions.  About the other borrowers in the group:  1.  N. Thị Hiền (84) is a 49-year-old woman who is requesting a 6,000,000 VND loan to support her business raising livestock.   2.  H. Thị Hợp (85) is a 48-year-old woman who is requesting a 6,000,000 VND loan to support her business making and selling food.   About Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women:  The mission of the Fund for Thanh Hoa Poor Women (FPW) is to provide sustainable financial services to disadvantaged women in rural areas in the Thanh Hoa province.   *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in Vietnamese while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.   Duyên N. Thị (82) là 37 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy sống ở thành phố Thanh Hoá.  Duyên là trưởng nhóm của nhóm vay gồm có 3 các thành viên.  Mặc dù mỗi thành viên trong nhóm nhận được từng khoản vay cá nhân, nhưng tất cả họ đều chịu trách nhiệm hoàn trả lại khoản vay của các thành viên trong nhóm của mình nếu một người nào đó trễ hạn hay không trả được nợ..  Tên chính thức của nhóm vay này là 52 Quảng Hưng (18.02.52 Quảng Hưng).   Trong khi không phải chỉ có các phương thức tạo nên thu nhập, mà nguồn thu nhập chính của công việc kinh doanh chủ yếu từ bán hải sản như cá và tôm trong cộng đồng địa phương.  Duyên thực hiện công việc kinh doanh này trong hơn 5 năm.  Từ các hoạt động này, Duyên kiếm được khoảng 2,100,000 VND.  Vào 2009, Duyên đã tham gia Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women để có thể tiếp cận với các dịch vụ tài chính giúp cải thiện  sinh hoạt và khả năng tham gia vào các hoạt động kinh doanh của cô ấy/ anh ấy.  Duyên đã hoàn trả hết khoản vay trước đây là 3,079,800 VND từ Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women.  Khoản vay trước đây được sử dụng mua các sản phẩm bổ sung để bán.  Cô ấy hiện đang đề nghị một khoản vay mới là 6,000,000 VND.   Khoản vay sẽ là 3rd khoản vay của người vay từ Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women.   Về Những Người vay khác trong Nhóm:   1.  N. Thị Hiền (84) là 49 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 6,000,000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực nông nghiệp.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là chăn nuôi gia súc.   2.  H. Thị Hợp (85) là 48 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 6,000,000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực thực phẩm.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là sản xuất & buôn bán thức ăn.   Về Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women:  Nhiệm vụ của Quỹ vì Phụ Nữ Nghèo Thanh Hóa (FPW) là cung cấp các dịch vụ tài chính bền vững cho những người phụ nữ kém may mắn ở các vùng nông thôn tỉnh Thanh Hóa.   *Lưu ý: Để phát huy tối đa hiệu quả & giảm chi phí, khoản vay này đã được thông báo bằng biểu mẫu để có thể được Kiva tự động biên dịch. .  Do việc biên dịch thủ công các danh mục rất tốn kém, nên Kiva đã tạo biểu mẫu này cho phần Field Partner (Trường Đối Tác) cho phép họ tiếp tục thông báo các khoản vay bằng  Vietnamese trong khi cung cấp thông tin có chất lượng & chính xác cho người cho vay Kiva.  ."

name: Wenefreda
description: Wenefreda is 68 years old now and is a married woman with eight children. For the past four years, she has run a tailoring business in the Philippines. Wenefreda is a very hardworking entrepreneur.   Wenefreda is requesting a 5,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy garments and other supplies for her business. In the future, she would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Mujeres Emprendedoras Con Esperanza Group
description: This village bank is one of the first formed in the foundation office in Luque. The Women’s committee is in its 10th loan cycle, and it members are women who were invited by friends who already belongs to a neighboring village bank. Today there are 17 women who invested in various businesses.  Mrs. Francisca Giménez runs the snack bar at a school and invested the money in buying juices, soda pop and food to sell in her snack bar.  Mrs. Edith Mabel O. sells clothing and invested the money in buying merchandise to increase her sales.  Mrs. Mercedes A. sells small domestic electrical appliances and invested the money in buying inventory for future sales.  Mrs. Marcia Isabel O. sells candy and invested the money in buying inventory to increase her sales.  Mrs. Mirtha A. sells fast food and invested the money in buying ingredients to make and sell her food.  Mrs. Elsa A. sells herbal remedies and invested the money in buying inventory to package and sell her herbal medicines.  Mrs. Larissa González sells cosmetics and invested the money in buying products to stock her sales business.  Mrs. Blanca P. sells clothing and invested the money in purchasing merchandise to increase her sales.  Mrs. Liz Rossana M. sells food and invested the money in buying ingredients to make an d sell her food.  Mrs. Hilaria Báez sells food and invested the money in buying ingredients to make and sell her food.  Mrs. Lilia Rosa C. sells clothing and invested her money in buying merchandise at wholesale to later sell.  Mrs. Miguela R. sells fruit and invested the money in buying fruit to increase her business.  Mrs. Luz Adriana M. sells general merchandise and invested the money in buying merchandise at wholesale to then resell.  Mrs. Lidia Cañiza sell cosmetics and invested the money in buying products to stock her business and then sell.  Mrs. Juana P. sells beverages and invested her money in buying soda pop and beer to sell.  Mrs. Katherine González sells decorative items and invested the money in buying decorative items to sell.  Mrs. Nidia A. sells fast food and snacks and invested the money in buying ingredients to make her food.  Translated from Spanish by Cindy Kendall, Kiva Volunteer

name: Segunda Josefa
description: Segunda is 65 years old and a member of the Tesoro Escondido [Hidden Treasure] Community Bank. Her husband is an accounting assistant. They have three children who are all independent.  She has run her business for ten years, which she started with an initial loan of 300 PEN [$110]. She sells sweets and drinks from the entryway of her house, and also raises and sells chickens. She also owns a small farm where she harvests coffee and cocoa. Her dream is to build a country house and a playground on her small farm, and be able to share the beautiful flora of the region with visitors. She will invest part of her new 3000 PEN [$1100] loan in her farm, and will use the rest to purchase new products for her home business. Josefa, as she is called, has worked for years with Manuela Ramos, and is very grateful for her help and support. Now she is the president of her Community Bank, which is a position she is happy to fill due to the importance of its responsibilities.

name: Miriam
description: Beginning in 1980, 33 years ago, Miriam began learning dressmaking from her mother. At first she made clothes for relatives, and when she was ready, she offered dressmaking to order. Today Miriam has her own workshop in her house, where she makes women's, men's, and infant's clothes. She has gained many loyal clients, who ask for tailoring service as well as complete service that includes the materials to make made-to-measure garments. She buys from specialty stores on credit and sells for cash or credit. She works hard each day from 8 a.m. until 7 p.m. Her goal is to remodel her house and daily build her customer base so that she can save, which is one of her main challenges.  Miriam has applied for her first Kiva loan through Fundación Mario Santo Domingo to buy fabric, thread, and accessories for the garments she will make for the year-end season so that her customers and their families can enjoy Christmas, say good-by to 2013 in style, dance at the four festivals, and get ready for the Barranquilla carnival, the city's most anticipated festival.

name: Nicaraguita Group
description: This group consists of three hardworking members, coordinated by 22 year old Meyling. She is married and mother of two children ages 2 and 4. She sells AVON and Zermat cosmetics. With the loan she will buy a variety of products such as makeup, lipstick, nail polish, eye liner, eye shadow, blush, women's perfumes, men's colognes, and more. Another member is 37 year old Alexandra, who sells new clothing from her home and by order. And the third member is 47 year old Isidro who owns a shop that frames and mounts art, and his business is in his home.

name: Genara
description: Genara works hard to support her family. She is married, and has a weaving business in the Philippines.  Genara requested a PHP 5,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional raw materials for her weaving business.  She has been in this business for 6 years now.  Genara would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Pajchani Group
description: The “Pajchani” Association has been a part of the Pro Mujer Bolivia family for several years. The group is based in the Villa Tejada neighborhood of the city of El Alto and currently has 14 members. They have proven to be an organized group in terms of their loan repayments and internal activities. The majority of the group's members are married with school-aged children. Many have older children who have had to abandon their studies due to lack of economic resources. The group's current objective is to work more in order to generate enough income to pay for their children's education, thereby assuring them a better future.  Within the Association there are different businesses, including the sale of plastic folders and neighborhood shops. But, the main activity of the group is sewing and tailoring. They make “polleras” (traditional pleated skirts), jackets, ponchos, and other items which they sell in stands around the city.  The “Pajchani” Association will use this loan to buy the raw materials necessary to increase production. They will then be able to attract more customers and achieve greater earnings, helping them meet their ultimate objective of improving their economic situation.  Translated from Spanish by Kris Vickery, Kiva Volunteer

name: Margret
description: Margret is a 33-year-old married mother of three children living in Hioma, Uganda. Employed by the local government, Margret is a teacher by profession who is very passionate about her job because she loves working with young people.  Margret faces challenges such as hyper inflation in these hard economic times. Because her business goal is to become a farmer, she is requesting this loan to buy land for farming. Her family goal is to educate her children.

name: Cirila
description: Thirty-nine-year-old Cirila is a simple woman.  She lives with her husband Romulo and their three children, whom she cares for in the house they have rented for five years.  In the morning she goes to her farming plots where she grows different produce, such as corn and potatoes, among others.  She tells us that her plots are several hours away walking, so she and her husband work in shifts so as not to leave their children unattended.  She says that she raises her cows and plants her crops in the higher region, but that soon she will start to harvest, so she needs working capital.  She also plans to increase her livestock, which consists of chickens and cows, which she fattens over a period of a few months and then sells for twice the price.  This is her first loan with Kiva and she is thankful for the financial help she is receiving.  She promises to make her payments on time.  Cirila will use the 1,000 soles to buy animals, such as chickens and a cow, to increase her livestock.

name: Faida Group
description: The Faida group is made up of married women who on average are 36 years old with five children. They all live in traditional families in Dioïla, in the Dioïla prefecture, in the Koulikoro region (second administrative region of the Republic of Mali). They met through family contacts, through living in the same neighborhood, and through friendship. They work in catering, the sale of condiments, the clothing trade and the sale of charcoal. This is the fifth solidarity loan for the women of the Faida group.  The client named Awa, the first person on the right in the row of people standing up, is illiterate. At present, she has a catering business. She plans to buy rice, oil, pasta, fresh fish, and condiments locally from the wholesalers. She sells cooked food for cash at the market to a mixed clientele. She hopes to make monthly profit of 60,000 FCFA that she will reinvest in her business.

name: Mwanaisha
description: Mwanaisha is a woman of high integrity, a mother of four. Previously, she used to live in a rental house but thanks to her efforts, she now has her own home. Mwanaisha has been operating a vegetable stall for a long time and during this period, she was also able to start a food stall. She is a very hardworking person who very much wants to get ahead. She is currently asking for a loan to purchase ingredients like wheat flour and corn flour, and also to repair tables and chairs in her stall. She hopes to own even more businesses in future.

name: Lydia
description: Lydia K. is thirty-eight years old. She is divorced and has given birth to one child, a girl, who is currently in the primary school. She lives with her daughter in a rented apartment in a commercial town called Dwenase in the Western Region. Dwenase is a suburb of Sefwi-Wiawso, the district capital.  Lydia is a food vendor. She prepares and sells rice and stew. She sells on a table at the lorry (truck) station in the mornings. She buys her goods from nearby communities and wants a loan to buy bags of rice and other ingredients in bulk. Lydia has been in business for ten years. She aspires to expand her business and give her child a good education.

name: Valentine
description: Valentine is 33-years-old. She is married to Thomas Rono and they have two children. Her business is located along Iten -Tambach road in Eldoret Town.  She has been in the hair salon business for five years and her major clients are residents of Iten-Tambach. Valentine was introduced to KADET by a registered KADET group member. She has applied for a loan from KADET. She intends to use the loan buy equipment, including a blow-drier, and add to her stock of hair chemicals.   In the future, she intends to open a beauty salon and hair dressing college, and to build residential houses.

name: Soenil
description: Soenil wants to thank all Kiva lenders for helping him realize his long-term goals.  He repaid his loan on time and could send his oldest child to town for studies. He paid his fees and wants to save more money to buy land so he does not have to rent. He asks Kiva lenders once again for a loan of SRD 10,000 so he can continue rice production and save more for his family's future.

name: Noura
description: Noura is a 32-year-old married woman from a village near Nablus city. She is a mother of one small son. Four years ago, Noura started her business, which is a beauty salon. She loves her job and the demand for her work is high.  Noura took a USD loan from FATEN. This loan will help her to buy new tools and beauty products for her beauty salon. This will improve her business and attract more clients.  Noura appears in the photo.

name: Tien
description: Tien, 47, is married and has a son. He lives with his wife in Ho Chi Minh City. Tien has been running a general store in front of his house for five years. He is requesting a loan to expand his business by buying a greater variety of products including food, beverages and sanitation products to better satisfy his customers.  Tien hopes his business runs smoothly and will generate a higher income to assist him in improving his family's living conditions.

name: Nedy
description: Nedy finds pleasure in her gardening activities. Not only is gardening her hobby, she earns an income through it as well. At the age of forty-one and being married, she busies herself so she can sufficiently provide for the family. She grabbed the opportunity to become a full fledged member of PMPC. She credits the cooperative with the capital in supporting her gardening activities. Recently, she applied for a loan to purchase gardening tools and fertilizers. In the future, she wishes to become the supplier of flowers in neighboring towns.

name: Bunafsha
description: Bunafsha lives in the city of Khujand.  She is 25 years old, married and has two children.  She has a secondary-specialized education and is a seamstress.  Bunafsha has been involved in sewing for 15 years.  Besides this work, she opened an internet cafe at her home.  Bunafsha has been in this business for four years.  She is requesting this loan for the purchase of computers.

name: Sri Ramajayam Self Help Group 2- Natchiyar Kovil
description: Sri Ramajayam is a self-help group from Natchiyar Kovil village, Tamil Nadu. It is managed by the local NGO called People’s Action for Transformation (PAT). The group has been in existence for more than 5 years. Hemalatha is the leader of Sri Ramajayam Self-Help Group (SHG). Hemalatha is married, and her husband is a farmer by profession. They have a child, and the family is living in their own house.   Now, the group members need a loan to purchase smokeless stoves produced by Greenway Grameen Infra. These stoves cost much less than 1,400 Indian rupees (INR). They reduce indoor air pollution, which means healthier women and healthier families as it is young children and women who spend the maximum amount of time in and around the kitchen.

name: Sonavar
description: Sonavar lives in the Jilikul Region. She is 32 years. She lives together with her husband. She has two young children. Sonavar has finished secondary school. She keeps bees and grows produce by her home. She has been in this line of work for six years. Sonavar is taking out a loan in order to buy mineral fertilizers and increase her harvest.

name: Neida
description: Sra. Neida is a single mother with a daughter attending university.  She manages a store that is well-stocked with gifts and board games.  Neida’s business is widely known in the neighborhood for offering different products at low prices, which is the reason why she has always had many customers.  Her daughter has always helped her with the business, but now she also devotes time to her studies.  Sra. Neida desires to see her daughter become a professional so that she can improve the quality of life for her own family.    She is extremely grateful to Emprender and Kiva for demonstrating their confidence in her by providing this loan.		 			 		Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Tianasoa Jeanne D'arc Victoire
description: Tinasoa is a 26-year-old married woman. Her husband is also a merchant like her. He sells hardware items and accessories. The couple have two children, of whom one is already in school. Tinasoa has been selling telephone accessories since 2011. She and her husband help each other in their businesses, which are developed, since the merchandise for sale is ever-growing in number and variety, thus the use of a large glass case for displaying their merchandise. The couple’s goal is to improve the quality of the products and to increase again the number of items, so as to be able to purchase a plot of land with the profits and their savings.

name: Marvin Antonio
description: Marvin Antonio is 35 years old. He is a hardworking man who loves his job. He sells gold laminate. He has been doing this activity for more than 3 years. He started this business of his own initiative since he had to support his 2 children, whom he is raising. He is asking for this loan at this time for working capital for gold laminate, silver, gold, bracelets, and chains among other things. He wants to continue fixing up his house so that he can leave it to his children.

name: Felecita
description: Felecita works hard to support four children. She is married and has a business raising livestock in the Philippines.Felecita has requested a 6,500 PHP loan through NWTF to install a sanitary toilet. She is getting the sanitary toilet because she wants to have comfort, safety, and privacy.Felecita is aware that by using the sanitary toilet, she is not only saving money, she is also helping the environment and reducing health and hazard risks for her family.

name: Cecilia
description: Cecilia is 54 years old and married with four children. She works very hard to provide for them.  Cecilia runs a general store in the Philippines and has requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like shampoo, condiments, canned goods and other groceries, etc.  Cecilia has been in this business for six years and sells a variety of items. In the future, she would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Webster
description: Webster is 21 year old and lives in Soweto, South Africa. He is a young entrepreneur and a single father of one child, aged 2.  As well as providing for his child, Webster helps to support his mother. At this young age, Webster has already shown his drive and motivation, and has gone from working in a barber’s shop to opening his own mobile phone and computer repair shop.   It has been hard work; Webster works long weeks of sometimes 70+ hours, but the business has been doing well. He is seeking a loan to buy computer parts, phone chargers and new mobile phones to sell. This new stock will help his business attract a more diverse customer base, and increase its profits.   With better business returns, Webster will be able to save for his daughter's education, and also finish constructing his house, which he says is currently in a poor state. His business ambitions for the future are "to have a phone shop that sells and repairs phones, and employ the many young guys sitting idle in this area."

name: Elisa
description: Elisa is a married woman with three children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Elisa is 35 years old and has three children who are in school.  Elisa has a shells craft business in the Philippines. Elisa requested a PHP 10000 loan amount through NWTF to buy more shells and other supplies needed in her business.  Elisa has been in this business for 10 years. In the future, Elisa would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Meena M. Gulzar Group
description: Meena baji is a 56 years old lady. She has been a citizen of the city of Pakpattan, Pakistan for the past 30 years. Her husband, M. G., is a farmer by profession. Meena baji is the mother of four children: two sons and two daughters. Her elder son is a driver and drives a tractor in the fields. The next oldest son is involved in a milk selling business. Her daughters are single and do household work and taking care of the family. Meena baji belongs to a family of farmers, so she spends most of her time in the fields growing several types of crops. She successfully repaid her first two loans from Asasah (a microfinance institute of Pakistan). Now she is applying for a loan to buy another buffalo for her second son so that he will be able to earn good income from his milk selling business.   She is a loan group leader of some of the women in her locality. Razia baji wants a loan to buy chickens to sell. Manzooran baji wants a loan to buy electric supplies (electric wires, neon lights and switches) for her electric shop. Sugran baji wants a loan to buy seasonal fruits for her fruit selling business. Shahnaz baji wants a loan to buy vegetables for her vegetable selling business.   This is a group loan. The loan funds will be distributed among the group members, each of whom will invest in her own business. The members mutually guarantee one another's loans. If one member does not repay, the other members are responsible.

name: Tam's Group
description: Mrs. Tam, born in 1969, is a Thai ethnic woman who joined in the saving and credit program in January 1999. Her family consists of 4 members: Mrs. Tam, her husband and her two sons. Her family is living in Mai Son district, Son La province. Her two sons are both obedient and good at studying. Her eldest son is studying at University and her youngest son is studying at high school in Mai Son district.   Her family’s main income is from growing coffee, and each coffee harvest can bring her VND 60-70 million of income. However, the income is just enough for covering living costs and leaves an insufficient amount. She wants to have money to invest in her children’s education and pay her children’s tuition. Therefore, she wants to borrow a loan for this purpose.   She hopes that the loan will help her family with good conditions for investment in her children’s education, and thereby her children will have a brighter future.

name: Josephine
description: Josephine is a single mother of five children and two of her children go to school. She also takes care of additional family members. She is a tailor and has been in this business for seventeen years. She has applied for a loan of 1,400,000 Uganda shillings from MCDT-SACCO to buy more rolls of cloth material and thread. She works from home six days a week and sells retail. She generates additional income from a payphone. Her major business challenges are seasonality and defaulters. She aspires of educating her children up to university level. She resides in her own house and the family has access to electricity and running water. Her monthly expenses includes school fees and feeding the family.

name: Succès Group
description: Salamata is a member and the manager of the Succès group. These three "warrior women" have been working with ACFIME since 2011 and respect their commitments [with the organization].   Salimata is married and the mother of seven children, six of whom go to school. Her husband is a butcher and she has been selling corn flour for 16 years. With this loan, Salamata would like to take advantage of  the Burkina Faso harvest so that she can stock up on 25 bags of corn that she'll use to make flour.  The rest of the money will help with expenses related to her business.   Her earnings will allow her to continue with her business and help her spouse with the family expenses.

name: Marcelo
description: Sr. Marcelo is a new client.  A couple of years ago, Catholic University gave him the opportunity to manage a cafeteria at one of its campuses.  Marcelo saw a great demand for food among the students and faculty, so he decided to buy the equipment needed to offer fast food since there were no other places to eat.    He needs the money to restock the cafeteria with merchandise and also purchase ingredients for preparing fried chicken, hamburgers, and sandwiches.  Marcelo works with his wife, who helps with managing the cafeteria.  He is grateful to Emprender and Kiva for demonstrating confidence in him by providing this loan.Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Catherine's Group
description: Pictured above is Catherine, who as a group leader is representing her group formed by 9 farmers in Teso District, Kenya. She is married and is a mother to 2 children.  She is known by her community as a very hardworking individual.Initially, Catherine joined One Acre Fund in 2012 because she wanted to earn enough to feed her family. Since she joined the program she says that her life has improved, especially because she has been able to consistently feed her family.  With the profits from the coming harvesting season, Catherine plans to rent more land to cultivate.Between the 9 farmers in Catherine's Group, a total of 6 acres of land will be planted using the maize seeds and fertilizer received with the loan. Additionally, some of the farmers in the group will be purchasing a solar light, so with this loan the group will also receive a total of 3 solar lights.

name: Yarabi Tupe Salama Group
description: Ziada  is a retail businesswoman; she has been selling different items in the Jang’ombe neighborhood of Zanzibar for 3 years. She belongs to Yarabi Tupe Salama  group loan and she currently earns an average monthly profit of  approximately  US$ 40. Every day she works at her business from 7:00 am to 8:00 pm.     She is requesting a loan from BRAC Tanzania so that she can buy more items to add to her current stock. She is hoping that through this loan, her profit will increase and she will be able to grow her business.     Ziada is 27  years old and she is single.  She will be sharing this loan with her fellow group member, Moza, who has her own small business selling firewood, charcoal, and other items in Zanzibar.

name: Letecia
description: Letecia is 63 years old, married, and has four children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Letecia has a butcher shop business in the Philippines. Letecia requested a 30,000 PHP loan amount through NWTF to purchase additional meat to sell.  Letecia has been in this business for 6 years. In the future, Letecia would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Siria Jasmin
description: In the seaside resort of San Clemente, the "1 de diciembre" communal bank meets every fortnight. San Clemente is known for its beautiful beaches that are much visited by many national and international tourists. The town offers a variety of beautiful places to visit, and a rich selection of typical dishes from the region.And it is here that 40-year-old Siria lives. She is married and has three children, ages eleven, six and three years old respectively. All three attend school or nursery.
