Siria's husband is a fisherman.Siria is a great housewife who is taking out this loan so that her husband may buy the necessary resources to do a great job. Siria's husband works as a fisherman; he goes out to the high seas and fishes with one colleague. The two go out in the morning and come back in the afternoon; sometimes they stay out until the next day with the goods that they collect from the sea. Siria hopes to use half of this loan in order to buy cola drinks, water juices and beers as three days of local festivals are approaching and these products sell very well during this time. This will allow Siria to earn a little money to help her family to move forward.This loan will be used in order to buy nets, petrol, rope, fly lines, juices and beers. Siria has been a member of the loan group for 17 years old and likes it because of the help that she receives from the organisation. Siria's dream is to have a big boat for her husband to go out fishing in.

name: C6207 Abishyizehamwe Group
description: Janviere is 26 years old and is married with two children who are 6 months and 3 years old.  She is the president of a group called “Abishyizehamwe” and this group is commonly known for selling a variety of goods in their various businesses, such as clothes, foodstuffs, gasoline, etc.   Janviere and her team are now requesting a loan from Kiva lenders via Vision Finance Company in order to satisfy the demand of their customers which keeps increasing beyond their financial capacity.  With the use of this loan, Janviere and her team expect to earn more profits which, in turn, will be used to reinvest in their businesses.

name: Margaret
description: Margaret is a 43-year-old, married woman with three children.   For the last 15 years, she has been in the hospitality business in Nakuru town. She was introduced to KADET LTD by one of its field officers. This would be her first loan. She plans to use the loan proceeds to buy more chairs and tables for her cafeteria.   In future, Margaret hopes to expand her business and open another cafe in the neighboring town.

name: Fousseni
description: Mr. Fousseni A. is a policeman who sells stamps to make some money. He is 44 years old, married, and they have 3 children. As a policeman, he is charged with giving legal authorization to citizens, which is done by stamping papers or applications with various stamps. Mr. A. sells the stamps themselves on the side to make some extra money to help him care for his young family. He is requesting a loan of 360,000 CFA in order to purchase more stamps.

name: Guadalupe
description: Guadalupe was born in the city of Cusco and is 34 years of age.  She lives in a common law marriage and has three children.    Currently, Guadalupe lives in the city where she was born and where she works.  She sells wholesale meat in one of the most visited markets in the city of Cusco.  It has already been several years since she started working in this business and it is going very well.  For this opportunity, Guadalupe requires a loan in order to purchase more pork and beef.  Guadalupe's dream is to open an emporium.  The Communal Bank “Comuzone I” meets every 30 days in the city of Cusco (Perú). Cusco is known for its tourism, business and for its traditional celebration of Inti Raymi as well as because it is where you find one of the seven wonders of the world: "Machupicchu”.

name: Teresa
description: Teresa is 39 years old and married. She has three children, two of whom are in school. Teresa works very hard to provide for them.  Teresa runs a general store in the Philippines. She has been in this business for four years now.   Teresa requested a PHP 25,000 loan through NWTF to buy item to sell in her general store like home care products and other groceries.  In the future, Teresa would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Las Sembradoras Group
description: “Las Sembradoras” is a group of ladies who gathered recently to access a loan.  They all have different businesses selling vegetables, furniture, clothing, gelatin and other products.  Others sew or weave sweaters, skirts, and blankets.  Another member sells wood carvings.  Their loan will be used to purchase merchandise (baby clothes, tables, and gelatin) and raw materials (wood, yarn, and fabric).  Their president is Silvia M. and she hopes that the group will grow and accumulate sufficient savings.    Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Grupo Iglesia Rey De Reyes Group
description: Santa is a 22-year-old woman. She is married and has a lovely family with a 3-year-old daughter.   This family lives in a community in Aldea Guineales.To obtain income and provide for her family, Santa works buying and selling traditional clothing. She has been in this business for three years. She is a street vendor in the town square  and nearby places. Thanks to her motivation to achieve continued personal growth, she now finds it necessary to invest in her business and keep her customers satisfied.The products she will buy are: huipiles (blouses), fajas (belts), and skirts. Her big dream is to have her own shop and improve her income.

name: Temitope
description: Temitope sells phone recharge cards in large quantities as she has a printing machine, and also runs a viewing center. She has been in these businesses for over three years now and needs a loan of N140,000 to purchase more phone recharge cards and DVD tapes, and to improve the video club viewing center. Temitope is 35 years old, married to I. (a fashion designer) and they have three children. She says thank you.

name: José Manuel
description: José is 22 years old.  His parents made an effort to allow him to attend school through ninth grade.  He started high school, but due to the financial situation of his family, he was not able to continue studying.  His life partner works in fishing and takes care of their home.  She is the only one who lives with him and depends on him.  José works with his father-in-law at a metal structure workshop.  He has been doing this all day for three years.  He started as an assistant without pay in order to learn, and today he does this job very well since he has learned a lot and his boss has a lot of confidence in him.  At night, he also works as a fisherman since there is a lake close to his house.  That is the main income for the majority of the people nearby.  When he returns home, his life partner sells the fish that he was able to catch during the night.  She has done this since she was very young, since her father was also a fisherman and taught her.  He is requesting this loan to repair their small house, since it needs roof repair, and also to purchase some fishing tools so that he can catch a larger quantity of fish and have better profits for him and his family.  His dream is to have his own home so that he and his wife and their future children can have a dignified place to live.  This loan will help them repair where they are living currently and to purchase fishing tools to improve the family income.

name: Maha
description: Maha is a 42-year-old mother of six children. She is married to Abdullah, a building contractor, and she lives in a rented house in Marka. In order to help her husband financially, Maha started a small retail business selling clothes at home. She has been doing this for two years now, and she wants to continue to develop it so, in time, she can open her own store for selling clothes. To be able to do so, Maha has applied for a loan to add more fashionable clothes to her collection and make more space at home for her to grow her business until she has the required amount of money to open her own store.

name: Francisco
description: Francisco is 41 years old, single, and has no dependent children.  He lives with his family in the San Antonio de Padua annex in the district of Lambayeque, a rural area where people mostly work in agriculture and raise animals.  For more than three years, he has worked raising and selling young animals.  He raises sheep in an area located in the back part of his home.  He feeds them natural grasses and when they have reached a good level of development, he sells them to merchants that visit the area where he lives.  The income he earns from this activity meets his personal expenses and allows him to help his family financially.  Francisco would like to expand his corrals and buy balanced feed so that his sheep can develop better and he can earn more money from their sales.  To do this, he has asked Edpyme Alternativa for a loan of 1500 nuevos soles.

name: Joshua
description: Joshua lives in the Kisii area of Kenya, which is a primary bananas and sugar cane growing region. He has two children.   He is a farmer and has been doing this work for 10 years. His primary income sources are milk, eggs, tea, and crops.  He stated what is most enjoyable about farming: "a source of income." His biggest challenge is lack of market and poor roads. Animals on the farm have not been given names.  Asked why he chose Juhudi Kilimo for this loan, he replied that it meets his financial needs. He was also asked what he learned during Juhudi's required micro-finance training session, and he said that it was client-friendly and had a low interest rate.  His highest monthly expense is school fees. When asked how this loan would benefit his family, Joshua replied, "Improve living standard."  As part of Juhudi's loan appraisal process, each borrower's assets are evaluated. Joshua owns cows and poultry but does not own a pig, a pump, a bicycle, a motorcycle or an automobile. Juhudi Kilimo also tries to measure any change in living standards based on this loan. This borrower has in the household a mosquito net, solar power, TV and  DVD but does not have electricity, running water or a sewing machine.

name: Shere's Group
description: Shere is 54 years old and has 10 children. He has been a farmer for more than 30 years and is always said to be a very experienced farmer. Even though Shere is the only one featured in the above picture, he is actually representing his group formed by 9 farmers in Bungoma District, Kenya.Shere started working alongside One Acre Fund a few years ago, in 2009, and decided to do so because he wanted to earn enough to feed his family. Since then, he has seen his life improve; especially in the sense that he has been able to consistently feed his family ever since. This year he decided to represent his group because he wanted to help more farmers.Shere’s Group will receive farming inputs to plant a total of 3.5 acres of land. Additionally, the group will receive a solar light as part of their loan package.

name: Edna
description: Edna is 40 years old, married, and has four children, three of whom are in school.  She is in the agricultural business poultry in the Philippines, and requested a PHP 20,000 loan through NWTF to purchase feeds, vitamins, and other poultry supplies.  Edna has been poultry for three years now, and has borrowed nine times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, she would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Bilquis Fatima M.munir Group
description: Bilquis Fatima baji is a 32 year old widow and has been a citizen of Vehari, Pakistan for the last 10 years. Bilquis baji’s husband left her with five kids: three sons and two daughters. Bilquis baji worked hard to survive. She started making embroidered dresses and selling them in the market. Using her income she sent her kids to school. Now all her kids are getting an education from a school located near her house. Bilquis baji is now starting a business selling clothing. The embroidery business is a time-intensive profession and there’s a strong trend for people to buy ready made garments. She is applying to buy the ready made garments to sell in the clothing markets to earn a good profit.   She is the group leader for other women in her locality. Jamilan begum baji wants a loan to buy groceries for her grocery shop. Nasreen akhtar baji wants a loan to buy cold drinks for her drink corner. Hamidan begum baji wants a loan to buy clothes for her clothing-selling business.   This is a group loan. The loan funds will be distributed among the group members. Each member will invest in her own business. The members mutually guarantee one another's loans. If one member does not repay, the other members are responsible.

name: Agbégnigan
description: Agbégnigan, a young 30-year-old man, has been selling prepaid charge cards in a shop since 2007. He is requesting a second loan in order to buy more merchandise. In the future, he would like to open other shops and get married.

name: Beatrice
description: Beatrice is 32 years old and a single mother of 2 children. She joined Hand in Hand Eastern Africa in the year 2015 to benefit from enterprise development and financial management training.She does cabbages and potatoes farming and she is also a dairy farmer. She is taking a Kiva loan to buy fertilizer and seeds. She hopes this will increase her farm output which will consequently increase her income. She will therefore use the anticipated income to provide food and pay school fees for her children.She is happy with Kiva and their lenders and promises to pay the loan

name: Wildor
description: Cruz Wildor is 40 years old, is married and has 3 children. He lives with his family in the Oyotun district, a community that works in agriculture, commerce and livestock.  It is located in the province of Chiclayo, which is part of the Lambayeque region on the northern coast of Peru.  He has worked for several years raising and selling animals such as ducks, chickens, and turkeys.  He feeds them with local, natural grains.  He has requested a loan through Edpyme Alternativa of 2,000 nuevos soles to buy a variety of animals, in order to fatten them up and sell them at a higher price.

name: Boymahmad
description: Boymahmad is a resident of the city of Dushanbe. He is 45 years old. Boymahmad is married and has six children. The reason for Boymahmad's request is his son's studies at a university. He pays tuition for his studies. He is a very diligent young man. Boymahmad sees how hard he tries and wants his son to obtain college education and find a good job. Boymahmad hopes that there are people who will help him to ensure that his son continues his studies.

name: Alejandrina
description: Alejandrina is both joyful and glad for the support and she wants to continue to participate in this project. She continues to make artisan goods and she still has a small workshop in her home where she makes knitted items like sweaters, scarves, and other things. She also makes woven items with a loom. She continues to participate in the communal bank because she is a responsible and kind person. On this occasion, she needs a loan to buy materials for her work, like alpaca and sheep's wool. She thanks everyone for the loan and she promises to make her payments on time.

name: Merlyn
description: Merlyn A. is from the village of Tumpagon, Cagayan de Oro City. She is 44 years old, married and has three school-aged children. To make a living, Merlyn owns and operates a business venture in the food sector making and selling food. The main source of income for the business comes from selling snacks and other delicacies in the local community. Merlyn has been engaged in her business for over five years and earns approximately 3,000 PHP a month from these activities.  In 2009, Merlyn joined Kiva partner HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5,000 PHP from HSPFI. This loan was used to purchase raw ingredients needed to make products for sale. Merlyn is requesting a new loan of 8,000 PHP, which will be used to invest in expanding the business. This loan will be her second from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated to improve and expand her business.   About HSPFI HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.
town: Tumpagon, Cagayan de Oro, Misamis Oriental

name: Nasreen
description: Nasreen is a 46-year-old married woman living with her family in the area of Lahore, Pakistan. She belongs to an ultra poor family. Her husband owns a small costume jewelry workshop, the only source of income for his family. He manufactures varieties of costume jewelry, including bangles, necklaces, earrings, and rings in the shop.   She is requesting a loan from Kiva's partner BRAC Pakistan for her husband. He will use the loan amount to purchase metal wire coils for making rings, bangles and necklaces.   Nasreen hopes that the loan will be helpful for her husband's business. She is thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Luis Alberto
description: Luis Alberto is 28 years of age. He is married and lives with his wife and their children. He lives in the Ventanas Canton in the province of Los Ríos.   He is a member of the communal bank Señor de la Salud [Lord of Health], located in the Soloma precinct belonging to the Echeandia canton. This bank centers on agricultural work focusing on the short-growth-cycle crops of corn and rice. He earns his living growing corn and rice. He makes his purchases in Ventanas and sells his crops at the daily outdoor markets and especially on Sundays.   He is seeking the loan for buying seed, fertilizers and compost. The loan will supply him with the economic support he needs. He faces challenges such as pests and plant diseases in his crops and the variability of the weather. His dream is to purchase a plot of land.   He likes to play sports.

name: Farhod
description: Farhod is 26 years old. He lives in the countryside as a farmer. Since childhood he has taken care of livestock and has inherited his father's love for animals. In Farhod's youth his father, also a farmer, gifted his son with two lambs and Farhod reared them himself. When the sheep were fully grown he sold them and bought more lambs, which was the start of his business. As Farhod is currently in need of money, he has turned to "Arvand" for help. This will allow him to avoid underselling his livestock before the seasonal rise in prices.

name: Jenny
description: Jenny is 34 years old and has three children. She is married and has two children who are currently in school.Jenny is in the agricultural business, pig-fattening in the Philippines. Jenny requested a PHP 15,000 loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to buy feed and other supplies to raise her pigs.Jenny has been in pig-fattening for three years now and has borrowed five times in the past from NWTF to sustain her business.In the future, Jenny would like to save enough money, so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Luk
description: Luk N., 41, is married and lives with two of her children in the Siem Reap province. She and her husband are farmers who typically make about US$5 each day. They also often purchase a stock of rice to resell to wholesalers at the market for an additional profit to raise their standard of living. The weather conditions have been difficult for farming in Cambodia this past year and inflation has also been out of control. Luk N. is asking for a loan of US$1000 to purchase rice in bulk to get a special discount. She is confident that this loan will allow her to increase her daily income and to better support her family.

name: Samina
description: Samina is a 37-year-old married woman. She lives in Lahore, Pakistan. Samina is the mother of five children. She has taken this loan for her husband.   Samina's husband owns a shop in which he hand-makes embroidery with the help of four workers. He earns a sufficient income, but he does not keep his full income because he has to pay daily wages to his workers. There is not a dependable daily turnover from embroidery.  Samina belongs to a poor family and each member does his or her part to earn income for their survival. Her son drives an auto-rickshaw, and her daughters are school teachers. Her daughters have proven themselves brave women and do not burden their parents.  Samina requested a loan from Kiva’s field partner BRAC Pakistan to purchase stocks of thread, fancy cloth, sequins, and pearls in a variety of colors. She hopes that her husband will keep more of his income and give the full amount to Samina for the family.  Samina is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Farzana
description: Farzana is a 32-year-old woman, and mother of four children. She lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan.   Her husband is a vegetable seller by profession. He sells vegetables such as potatoes, onions, tomatoes, etc. Her husband is the only one responsible for feeding the entire family and managing the household.  Farzana's husband needs to purchase different types of vegetables for resale, so that he can increase the size of his business, improve his sales growth and earn maximum profit.   Due to an unfavourable financial position, her husband is not able to purchase vegetables for his business. Therefore, Farzana has applied for a Kiva loan from its field partner BRAC Pakistan, so she can help her husband to purchase the above items for his business.   She is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Jorge Mateo
description: Jorge Mateo is 26 years old and is married with two children.  He lives with his wife and their children, who are 4 and 2 years old, in Ventanas, which is in the Rios province.  He is a member of VRC Las Palmas, which is located in the Campo Alegre precinct in the canton of Bab, which is an agricultural area.  Jorge has worked in agriculture for 8 years, growing corn and rice.  He makes his purchases and sales in Pueblo Viejo.  He is seeking a loan so that he can continue harvesting and to buy agricultural fertilizers.  With the money from this loan, he will be able to buy seeds.  His dream is to own his own land.  In his free time he likes to play sports.

name: Hugo Roberto
description: The member continues his lodging business. He works from 8am until 6pm. With this business, he is getting his children ahead. His dream is to expand and improve his lodging business. He is requesting the loan to further set-up his business and buy beds and sheets wholesale. He is happy because of the loan and promises to make his loan payments.

name: Lucia
description: Lucia works hard to support her family. She is married and has a food-vending business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for 15 years.  Lucia requested a PHP 18,000 loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. She will use the loan to buy ingredients for her food production business.  In the future, Lucia would like to build and expand her business, to secure the future of her family.

name: Jenalyn
description: Jenalyn S. is from the town of Sta. Josefa. She is 34 years old. Jenalyn is married and has 2 school-aged children. To make a living, Jenalyn owns & operates a business venture in the agriculture sector raising crops. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes from planting and harvesting rice for sale. Jenalyn has been engaged in her business for over 12 years now.  Jenalyn joined CEVI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan  from CEVI. Jenalyn is requesting a new loan of 15,000 PHP which will be used to purchase general farm supplies & equipment. This will be the eighth loan taken out by Jenalyn from CEVI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the family's income.

name: Fapito
description: Fapito  is a 22-year-old single woman, with no children.   She has a small plantation and grows taro, yam, and taamu to earn a living. She has been doing this for two years.   Fapito has requested a loan to buy weed spray, weed killer, fertilizers, spades, baby taro, and a new crowbar.  She has been a member of SPBD since 2011. With her profits, Fapito hopes to use her profits to help her family matters and to improve her business,

name: Kety
description: Kety, who is 28 years old, lives with her partner, with whom she has 3 children aged 10, 5 and 2. They live together in their own home located in a farming and livestock area.   Kety is a young mother with great determination and courage for work. 19 years ago she decided to dedicate herself to farming on the plots that her parents bestowed upon her. Now she also raises livestock, making the most of the good pastures of her settlement, thanks to the altitude.  "I have more than 50 rams, which I raise on high ground. When they are grown I sell them or I slaughter them", she says. She earns a considerable income from the sale of the meat, the skin, the offal, and other things; she sells these at a makeshift stall at her district market.   Kety has high hopes, among these is to extend her farm land and improve the breed of her animals. For now she will work on raising more sheep, to continue her meat business.   She asks for your support in order to purchase 5 sheep, which she will fatten for their later sale.   This is her fifth loan with MFP. She promises to pay the monthly instalments punctually. On the other hand, she recognises the work of her communal bank "Mirando un futuro mejor" as supportive and cooperative. Kety will invest the 600 PEN in the purchase of 5 sheep to fatten up.

name: Mahsad
description: Mahsad G. has successfully paid off another of her previous loans and wants to apply for a new loan to buy seasonal winter assortment of fabrics. At this time her business has visibly expanded. Mahsad has many customers. She is very grateful to Kiva for support and loans. She says that all her achievements in business are because of these loans.Translated from Russian by Elena Fedorchuk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Patrick
description: Patrick is a 39-year-old hard-working married man with eight children. He lives in Kamwenge, Uganda. He used his previous loan to pay workers on his farm. He still deals in farming, alongside buying and selling of produce to earn himself an extra income. He started this business so as to earn a living. He still hopes to be a modern farmer; however, his main challenge is inadequate capital.   He is requesting a loan to mulch his coffee farm.

name: Lisset Christina
description: Lisset is a young woman of 21 who lives in the city of Pisco, known for its beautiful beaches, rich food, and as the city where we find the “Isles of Springs,” visited by many tourists all year round. Also, agriculture is important, especially cultivating cotton. Lisset is a hard-working young woman, but when she has a little time off she likes to listen to music and, on occasions, to eat one of her favorite dishes, which is the tasty “Chicken with Garlic.” She only completed secondary school, but she would have liked to study nursing.  Day after day, Lisset works in her store selling groceries, soft drinks, and beer. She works around 10 hours a day and can serve as many as 35 customers in a day. She thinks her business is doing well, due to her pleasantness and, above all, because her customers have gotten to know her.   Lisset is very grateful to Kiva lenders because, their help enables her to order more merchandise for her business, including canned tuna, soft drinks, vegetable stews, rice, and sugar by the sack, among other items. Thus, by this means, she can have more product variety and improve her income, allowing Lisset to continue struggling day by day to make her grandest dream a reality: to be able to study for a career in Technical Nursing.

name: Epa Furaha Group
description: The client Rumbo is a professional educator and director of Furaha, a primary school which is also a teacher training site. He is an experienced educational administrator. He is married and the father of 13 children, some of whom who study and others already have their own households. His wife sells food products. This loan from Hekima will allow him to pay for the university studies of his children and to use the rest of the funds for house repairs and  furniture purchases. The client acknowledges that he is already thinking about retirement as he is presently 65 years old. He thanks Hekima and its partners for supporting educators who are unable to get loans due to lack of collateral.

name: Dongmod Group
description: Keoaudone is excited the filter was available on an affordable, payment plan.  Keoaudone and her group, along with other villagers, participated in a village meeting where they discussed the costs of treating local water supplies.  Charcoal, firewood, even bottled water were discussed and priced out over 2 years.  The water filter Keoaudone and her group purchased is guaranteed for 2 years but is known to function for up to 5 years.  Keoaudone and her group also discussed the cost of medical care for water-borne disease. And after totaling up the costs, Keoaudone and her group recognized the substantial financial savings the water filter will have for them and their families. The children in the picture are the children of borrowers in the picture.

name: Gina
description: Gina is 46 years old and married with nine children of whom five are in school.  Gina is in the agricultural business, raising pigs in the Philippines. Gina requested a PHP 9,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy medicines and vaccines for her pigs.  Gina has been raising pigs for five years now and has borrowed 9 times in the past from NWTF.  In the future, Gina would like to save money to expand her business and continue to send her children to school.

name: Blanca Rocio
description: 52-year-old Blanca is a hard-working woman.  Her husband died several years ago, leaving her alone and responsible for their four children.  However, this was never an obstacle to her setting up her own business.  Thanks to her cooking experience, some years ago she set herself up in premises where she sold meals, fried food, soda, juices, etc.  However, for convenience reasons as well as to lower her costs, she handed the premises back and continued her micro-business from her home where she sells the same products.  Blanca currently needs a loan to buy a deep-fat fryer so that she can grow her business and thereby increase her sales and income.  This will enable her to improve her quality of life and make some savings with the goal of owning her own premises in the future where she can sell all types of food from different parts of the world.

name: Phalla
description: Mrs. Phalla K. was married in 2001 and now has two sons. He husband earns some money raising pigs. The family all help with their other farming businesses, raising cows and planting vegetables.  Phalla K.'s mother, who lives with the family weaves silk for sale.   In 2003 Mrs. Phalla K. started her own grocery business to bring in extra income for the family. She is applying for this $600 loan in order to purchase more items for her stock and expand her business. She has borrowed money from MAXIMA successfully six times before.

name: Ghazala
description: Ghazala is a responsible mother of three children. She lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan.   Her husband has been providing transportation services by driving a Taxi for fifteen years.  Her husband is responsible for fulfilling the needs of the entire family.   Her husband needs to do maintenance to his Taxi because the current condition of his Taxi is not good and it requires maintenance on a daily basis which ends up costing more.   Due to insufficient financial means he is unable to do maintenance of his taxi. Therefore, Ghazala has applied for Kiva loan from its field partner BRAC Pakistan.  With the help of this loan Ghazala's husband can afford the maintenance cost easily. He will be able to provide better transportation services and earn a  profitable income. Ghazala also plans to make savings with a portion of the profit amount of her husband's income to meet her family's needs in future.  Ghazala is very grateful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Emprendedoras Presente Group
description: This communal bank is called “Emprendedoras Presentes” (Present Entrepreneurs).  It has 20 members who carry out a variety of lines of work among which we have dried fruit sales, clothing sales, shampoo and cream sales, store, animal feed sales, pastry shop, interior and exterior plant sales, street merchant, chlorine bleach and dishwashing soap sales, tango classes and services, among others.  All are from Renca Commune located in the city of Santiago.  Cecilia is communal bank president.  In the photo she is standing in the second row, third from left to right, wearing a black blouse with a brown vest over it; her hair is dark brown and she wears it gathered up.  She works selling miscellaneous, seasonal merchandise like clothes, toys, floral decoration and kites.  She’s been in business 13 years.  She comments that she works afternoons and arranges her schedule to fit her availability.  She buys her merchandise from suppliers and liquidators at low cost which is an economic advantage.  She will use the loan to buy kites, toys and underwear.  Her business goal is to continue growing to increase income and provide wellbeing for her family.  Cecilia lives with her husband who works in construction as a welder and with her 3-year-old daughter.  Her dream at the family level is to finish building her house since it always has something still to do.  She is very happy and grateful for the opportunity provided by Fondo Esperanza because it will make it possible for her to invest in her business.  With respect to her communal bank, she comments that there is good communication.  On the other hand, the training has been useful for her to learn new sales strategies and bookkeeping.  Renca is a commune located in northwest Santiago (Capital of Chile) metropolitan region.  It’s a commune with a strong community work among which the community television station “Renca TV” stands out.  It was created in order to promote the commune’s cultural and artistic activities.

name: Lidia
description: Lidia is 52 years old, married and currently lives with her husband and daughter. She intends to use the loan to buy a machine to clean her coffee fields, pay for some fumigation and for labor costs.  She plans to buy this machine that will weed her coffee in a more agile and quicker manner, thereby maintaining it in excellent condition, so that she can generate more profits and obtain a better quality of life and economic stability.  This is her first loan from FUDECOSUR. She has not had other loans before from state banks. Instead FUDECOSUR easily provided her with this loan and at a much lower interest rate.

name: Bernardito
description: Bernardito is a 60-year-old married man from Talibon, Bohol.  He earns a living for several years through his tricycle transport business.  Bernardito is asking for a loan in order to pay the remaining balance of his tricycle.   In the future, Bernardito hopes to make his business a success.  Moreover, he plans to save money for future use and to repay his loan.

name: Kim Ey's Group
description: A single woman from Battambang province’s Ratanak Mondul district, Kim Ey is 25 years old and she plants corns as her single source of her income to support her living. She has been in this business for almost ten years, earning about 20,000KHR per day but she is able to save about 5,000KHR each day.   Kim Ey’s group consists of two female members who live in the same village. Kim Ey is the fourth cycled client while the other member is the second cycled client with VisionFund. She has successfully used the past three loans to make her family’s living better and to afford sufficient food. Now requesting a loan, Kim Ey, who is the leader, will use her portion to buy fertilizers and seeds for her farmland and use a portion of it to spend for labor and ploughing. She hopes to grow her business with good yields so as to provide a better standard of living.

name: Ameed
description: Ameed is 28 years old and lives in Nablus. Nablus is a city in the northern West Bank, approximately 49 kilometers north of Jerusalem, with a population of 126,132. He is marred and he has two daughters and a son. He sells music CD’s, which is his only financial income. He earns 550$ monthly. Ameed asked Ryada for this youth loan to buy packaging requirements and CD’s. Ameed is very grateful to everyone who helps him to achieve success in his business with this loan.

name: Sekinat
description: Sekinat is 36 years old and she is married with 3 children. She is a tailor and also sells sarongs. She has been in this business for a long time. She hopes for the loan amount of N50,000 to purchase more sarongs to sell. She says thanks to all Kiva lenders.

name: Mujeres Activas Group
description: It all started when Mrs Maria Aquino, who belongs to the committee "Mujeres Unidas" (United Women) from the area around the km 9 Monday_ C.D.E, got in contact with Marina Carballo. Marina Carballo is a very active and supportive women who is well loved and respected within the "Barrio Yboty" neighborhood. Marina, then got in contact with friends and neighbors to build the "Mujeres Activas" (Active Women) group. The group can be described as very responsible and supportive, integrated by women with different professions. Marina lives together with her husband, Juan Ortiz, and their three sons; she sells clothes that she makes herself and the extra income allows her to contribute to the household budget.  The activities undertaken by the different women from the "Mujeres Activas" group are:   	Zulma Beatriz Rodríguez :  Seamstress  	Petrona S. Martínez: Sells cosmetics from a catalog  	De Lo Santa M.: Dressmaker  	Nilda N. Dosantos: Seamstress  	Heriberta Báez: Runs a small convenience store  	Elpidia P. de Galeano: Sells fruits and vegetables  	Arminda González: Runs a small groceries store  	Josefina Florentín: Sells clothes  	Eugenia M.: Seamstress  	Marina G. Vera: Sells clothes  	Lucí Erodita García: Sells clothes  	Idolvina Sánchez de Benítez: Sells chicken  	Zulmira R. Molinas: Sells spices  	Pablina Cáceres: Sells underware  	Ramona Cáceres: Sells cosmetics Translated from Spanish by Jimena Almendares Leistner, Kiva Volunteer

name: Venerando
description: Venerando is a 50-year-old man from the town of Guindulman, Bohol. He is married with six children aged 9 - 29.   He is engaged in a food vending business, a sari-sari (general store) and drives his motorela (motorized carriage) for an income. He has been doing this for six years now. He is asking for a loan to buy fish, seasoning, vegetables and meat.  In the future, he hopes that his business will thrive and increase profitability for his family's needs.

name: Rovshan
description: Rovshan A. is a 34-year-old man who has raised sheep for meat production since 1990. He breeds sheep for local bazaar traders. Once a week he goes to the livestock bazaar in Imishli region to sell his sheep and purchase lambs. Rovshan lives with his family in the Bilasuvar Internally Displaced People Settlement. Because of hyper inflation, Rovshan's earnings are enough to feed his family but not enough to expand his business and increase the number of his sheep herd. To improve the life conditions of his family and expand his business, he has applied for a loan of $800 USD to purchase 10 sheep (for an estimated cost of $60 USD for each sheep and fodder for $200 USD).

name: Iselem Muhamed
description: Iselem is a 36-year-old businesswoman who lives in Juba. She is married and has four children between the ages of four and ten.  All of them go to school.  Iselem runs a clothing store and has been in business for 5 years. She has no employees. She heard about Finance Sudan through other clients. She is taking a loan of 1800 SDG to purchase clothing and many other items.  She has no other source of income besides this business.  In 5 years Iselem would like to expand her business.  Her major challenges include high prices in the market.  Iselem says she is happy about the loans given by Finance Sudan.

name: Teresa
description: Teresa, who is 18, makes wooden baskets and then travels around the various fairs and markets in the city of Santa Cruz to sell them. She also sells them from a number of outlets.  This is Teresa's first loan cycle with the institution and she plans to use the loan to make baskets.  Teresa's work brings it challenges - it is manual work and is tedious and tough.  Teresa is happy and grateful to the institution for granting her the loan and for the help it has provided.

name: Kibibi
description: Kibibi is taking out a new loan to expand her existing business. With this new investment, she wants to buy more clothes to sell. She wants to take advantage of the December holiday celebrations, a time when sales are high. She is sure that this investment will increase her income. Kibibi is grateful for the support her last loan provided. It helped her to grow her business. She plans to expand her business and open more businesses in the future.

name: Mariama
description: Mariama is 34 years old and married with 5 children, aged between 1 and 14 years. She runs a food stand within her community in Kandeh town. She's been in this business for 10 years and sells rice, dry fish, pepper, onions and palm oil.  Her business is the only income she has. She says at present her business is doing well because she is the only one with a food stand in the area, so customers prefer buying her goods rather than going to the big market.   Mariama requested this loan through BRAC Sierra Leone to develop her business by purchasing more rice, dry fish, pepper, onions and palm oil. She says that the extra income from this loan will help her improve her family’s living conditions and renovate her house. In the future, she would like to own a permanent structure where she can house her business. She is grateful for your support.

name: Gurban
description: Gurban is a low income person from Agsu district. He is married has 4 kids. He is 45 years old. He started his business in 1997. In 2005-2007 he borrowed 2 loans from Normicro Agsu branch amounting 300-600$ and used them for business expansion. Now he applies for $1200 to buy more animals and expand the business.

name: Javier Alexander
description: Javier lives in the suburbs of the Paradise of Guayaquil. His wife is a lawyer and they have three children, fourteen, eight and twelve years old. The children are studying in public school. Javier began with a small stall selling vegetables and little by little he was able to expand his business until now he has a store that supplies almost all the needs of his customers. Now Javier gets up very early to work at his store selling noodles, colas, water, etc., sometimes with his wife's assistance. One of the difficulties that he has is body pain because he was in a traffic accident several years ago.  With this loan he would like to buy oil, rice, colas in order to increase the merchandise in his store. In the future he would like to open another store in a good location. Translated from Spanish by Esther Levandoski, Kiva Volunteer

name: Marriam's Group
description: Marriam's group is composed of four hard-working women. Marriam is 17 years old and lives in the town of Iganga, in the Iganga region of Uganda. She has no children. For the past three years, Marriam has been working hard to manage her retail shop selling beans, sugar, flour, and biscuits.   To help expand her business, Marriam has requested a loan of 400,000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy beans, sugar, flour, and biscuits, and will help Marriam generate greater profits and pay school fees for her siblings. Marriam hopes that in the future she will be able to start up a boutique.   Marriam is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities and a forum for life-skills training.

name: Magdalina
description: Magdalina is a businesswoman from Barangay 2, Tangub City. She is 47 years old, married and has expertise in selling. She runs a little store in the market and earns a meager income that sufficiently supports her family. Magdalina is a full-fledged member of PMPC and has taken several loans already. She maintains her membership in good standing without records of default. Now, she applied for a loan to purchase merchandise for her store. Magdalina continues to look for better business opportunities, proof that she has the passion and the energy to make ends meet for her family.

name: Rosenda
description: Rosenda is 30 years old and lives in Colambutan Settlement, Tudela, Philippines. She is single with two children.   To earn a living, Rosenda has a business selling fruits in the local market. She earns about PHP 3,500 each month doing this type of work. Rosenda has requested a loan to buy additional fruits to sell such as banana and melon.  Rosenda has been a member of PMPC for three years.  In the future, Rosenda would like to save for her children's school fees.

name: Sarorn
description: Mrs. Sarorn O. (shown in the photo), 32, and her husband Mr. YO. Kan, 35, have been married since 1996 and have five children: three sons and two daughters. Three of them are in school. They are living across the Mekong River about 15 kilometers from Phnom Penh City.   Sarorn has been selling fish for 10 years. Her husband has been driving a horse cart for five years. Besides these businesses, the couple also farms.  Sarorn is asking for her first loan of $300 to purchase a water-pumping machine to spray her farm.

name: Sophal's Group
description: Sophal, 33, is married and lives with her family in a village of the Dambae district. She has two daughters to take care of and they are still in school. To make a living, she has been farming rice and planting cassava for several years and the current business earns her family about 23,000KHR per day.   There are two members in Sophal’s group and they are both first-cycle clients with VisionFund. Sophal, who is the leader, is leading her group to apply for a loan. She will use her portion to buy fertilizers for her farmland and use a portion of it to spend on labor. She hopes to increase her family’s income from her current business so as to make a living better and keep her daughters in school.

name: Buseesa Farmers Group
description: Jesca a married lady and earns a living from selling alcohol and farming in Kagadi, Uganda. She is hopeful of growing her businesses due to the fact that she is hardworking. Despite being challenged by price fluctuations, Jesca is requesting a loan to buy alcohol for selling. She is a member of Buseesa Farmers Group where each member guarantees the other to get a loan since they don’t pledge securities.

name: Pamela
description: Pamela is a young entrepreneur.  She has a place where she sells refreshments, and it has been going well for her.  Nevertheless, the demand is bigger than she expected, and the business is not able to meet the demand.    That is why she needs to buy more merchandise in order to be able to meet the customers’ demand.  This will allow her to improve her business.  This is the only source of money that the family has.

name: Kan
description: Kan is 33 years old, and a local farmer from Prey Chor district, Kompong Cham, Cambodia. She was born and grew up there on a family farm. Kan has been in the farming business gaining practical experience for more than 20 years. She has a common-law partner, who is a construction worker, and has three school-age children.   Kan has requested a loan from HKL to purchase construction tools to support her husband's business. With the tools, Kan’s husband will be able to provide additional construction services to his customers, and therefore increase the household income. Kan is committed to working hard to ensure a good education and bright future for her children.

name: Carmelita
description: Carmelita is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a tailoring business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 17,000 through NWTF to buy additional materials for her tailoring business.  Carmelita has been in this business for 34 years. Carmelita earns more income from selling ready-to-wear.  Carmelita has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Servanda
description: Servanda is fifty-eight years old and lives in a zone far from the city. She works in agriculture and dairy production, belonging to closest dairy module and sells all her production to the largest dairy processor in the city. In addition, due to there being constant irrigation in her zone, her carrot crop has no problem with sales since it is eaten by most people in the municipality. She has over thirty-four years of experience in these fields of agriculture and dairy production. Now she is asking for a loan to repair her dairy stable and improve her production quality.

name: Alfredo
description: Mr. Alfredo G. and Mrs. Maria Ines Coazozon are the parents of two school-aged children, to whom they want to provide them with the best.   There are some repairs that need to take place to the exterior of their home, but they don’t have the necessary funds to carry it out.   They request a loan in order to purchase the materials they need and to pay for the labor.   Alfredo is a supervisor in a blacksmith shop. With this income he will repay his loan. Maria Ines takes care of the household expenses with the income she earns providing cleaning services.   Maria Ines made the request, wife to Alfredo G.. He was not able to attend the interview because he had to be at work that day.

name: Esterlita
description: Esterlita R., from the village of Calaran, Calamba, Misamis Occidental, is a 44-year-old married mother of four adult-aged children. To make a living, Esterlita owns and operates a sari-sari or general store whose main source of income comes from selling daily-use products such as shampoo, soap, toothpaste, etc.  in the local community.  Engaged in her business for over five years, she earns approximately 3000 PHP a month.   In 2009, Esterlita joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She is now requesting a loan of 5000 PHP to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Esterlita from GDMPC, and she plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the family's income.   About GDMPC: GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three unit offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partners to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Sisanda Group
description: Tamsanqa, 42 years of age, is married with 3 children, aged between 6 and 20, two of whom attend school. She also takes care of two other relatives that live with her. In addition to her business, Tamsanqa has another source of income, the government’s child support grant.   Tamsanqa has been in business for 6 months, selling clothes and cold drinks at pay points in Mandini, South Africa. She has requested this loan through WDB and Kiva to buy clothes and cold drinks. The main challenge in her business is that customers buy on credit and fail to pay on time. In five years time, Tamsanqa would like to have a proper place for her business and have more employees. The extra income from this loan will help her pay for tertiary education for her children. In the photo, Tamsanqa is wearing a yellow top.

name: Shavarsh
description: Shavarsh is 39 years old and he lives in Ddmashen village in Gegharkunik region. He is married and he has two sons and a daughter. Shavarsh is farmer and he has got a small, nice farm where he has livestock and also a large plot of land where he arranges vegetable cultivation. Farming is the only source of income for the family since his wife is unemployed, so Shavarsh works hard to earn more. He is very upset now; since in the winter period is hard for any farmer and he suddenly felt he has health problems. Shavarsh asks for this loan of 1,400,000 AMD (Armenian drams) since passing a medical exam he found out that he must have a long and proper treatment course. He is thankful beforehand and so hopeful that the treatment will basically solve his health problem.

name: Ana
description: Ana is married and has three children.  She has a blacksmith business in the Philippines. She also earns additional income from farming sugarcane.   Ana is requesting her seventh loan from NWTF for 13,000 PHP, which she will use to purchase additional materials like iron, wood, and charcoal for her blacksmith business.  Ana has been sustaining her business activities through her past six loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Fatuma
description: Fatuma is a married woman and has been blessed with three children, all of whom attend school. Together with her husband, she lives at their own house that has neither electricity nor piped water.   She has operated a fish selling business for over three years, selling from home to restaurant operators and passersby. She faces a major challenge of seasonality and perishability leading to losses.  With the 10,000 Kenyan shillings, she wants to purchase bundles of fish for resale. She dreams of expanding her business and establishing another business in the near future.

name: Maria Ignacia
description: Maria is 49 years old. She lives with her husband who works as a taxi driver. They have two children who are 11 and 12 years old. They live in the San Jose district, some 15 minutes from the province of Chiclayo, the capital of the Lambayeque region. This little community is primarily agricultural and livestock-raising. For 25 years, she has been making clothes from her home. She has a sewing machine. She offers a professional, high-quality service, and so she is well known in the area. Her work tool has been damaged, and she is requesting a loan in order to repair it. In this way, she will be able to keep offering her service to the community. Her biggest dream is to have a tailoring workshop and to be able to give work to her neighbors. This is her first loan from Edpyme Alternativa (Kiva Field Partner) and she is grateful to the Kiva lenders for the opportunity offered to her to keep growing her business.

name: Mercedes De Jesús
description: Mercedes, 38, is married and has four children.  She’s been working in agriculture since she was 13-years-old; her father would take her along to help him and would tell her that she needed to learn to work because that would be useful when she had her own home.    Later she took up with someone but it wasn’t good but after that she met a good man that she married.  She helps him with the agriculture and she also likes commerce; she sells fish and also likes the clothing business even though her life is very demanding because she must rise at 4:30 in the morning to prepare her husband’s breakfast and then get her children ready for school and after that head out to sell.  The loan she’s asking Fundación Campo for is to buy two gallons of herbicide to control weeds, a bag of seeds and 8 sacks of manure.  With this investment she will plant corn.  She’s already prepared the soil but needs to buy the supplies.  She dreams with being able to buy a piece of land to build a brick house since she currently lives in a house that is of metal sheeting on land that doesn’t belong to her.

name: Narcisa
description: Narcisa, who is married and with two children, lives in Ballacong, Ilagan, Isabel, Philippines. She has a hog-raising business while her husband works on their farm. Currently, she has more than three pigs, but she is planning to raise additional piglets in order to improve her income.   Since her husband has a limited income from his harvest, their earnings are not enough to buy additional piglets.  They will have to buy item to meet their family's needs and to buy food of her pigs first. So she needs a loan of Php7,000 from an institution which has been helping people like her who want to help themselves. Half of this amount will be used to buy additional piglets and pig food and to add pig pens.     According to her, she does these things for the sake of her children’s education and their brighter future. She strongly believes that faith, religiosity, and strong bonding are the secrets of a successful family.

name: Sylvest
description: Sylvest, age 31, is a very hardworking married man charged with the task of taking care of four children who all attend school in Hoima, Uganda. He ventured into the selling of bicycle spare parts. This is supplemented by income from farming, mainly growing cassava and beans. He desires to expand and develop his business; however, inadequate capital poses a strong threat to his wish. He is seeking credit to buy more bicycle spares to sell.

name: Rugoye Group
description: Samweli who is in his mid 20s is single with no children.  He has been running a library business for three years now.  He works from 08am to 10pm daily and is able to make a small monthly profit.   This will be Samwel’s 1st loan from Tujijenge Tanzania.  He will use this loan to buy good telephone chargers, to sell CD's and to burn music on CD's.  He dreams of owning a mini supermarket.  Samwel will share this loan with his loan group Lugoye which has six members who will hold each other accountable for paying back the loan.

name: Arturo
description: Arturo is fifty-two years old.  He lives along with his wife and their three children.  The family maintains a stable and a happy home.  They live in the district of Tambogrande in the province of Piura.  It is a semi-tropical region in which many small farmers own small fruit plantations or raise animals.  Arturo is a farmer.  He raises sheep and maintains two hectares of mango and lime fields.  He raises the sheep in corrals near his home.  He raises them for meat and other products and sells the animals in local markets when they reach the appropriate size and weight.  He harvests mangos and limes regularly from his fields, given the extended growing season in the region.  Between these two activities Arturo is able to maintain a relatively stable income and provide for his family.  The loan will be used to purchase additional balanced feed for his animals and make repairs to his corrals.  He hopes that this action will improve the health and production of his sheep, thus improving the profits of the business.  He dreams of having a larger herd and additional land to raise them on.  He hopes to be able to continue using his business to meet his family's needs and provide additional opportunities to his children.

name: Alidrije
description: Alidrije, a 32-year-old woman, wants to open up a hair salon in a little town where she currently lives with her retiree father and her sister who works as kitchen help in a nearby restaurant.   Before moving to the town, she lived in a village until her mother passed way accidentally; Aldrije grieved for a very long time. She then moved to the town and started working as a part-time elementary school teacher, but considering the fact that there are almost no new openings in her field, she is certain now that it will take years for her to gain full-time employment in her occupation.   This was the reason why she planned on opening up a hair salon where she could use her hair-cutting skills.

name: Santo Rey Group
description: The Santo Rey group is in its fifth cycle with the women's committee program.  The group is from the city of Concepción, a city that is far from the capital of the country.  Many of the members do not have access to a lot of basic services.Sergia is one of the members.  She lives right in the center of the city, where she has her fruit and vegetable stand.As time passes, and with the help of her group, she wishes to improve her business and to help her family.  She is requesting this loan to be able to buy seasonal fruits and vegetables in order to be able to continue with her sales and helping her family.

name: Josephine
description: Josephine is 48 years old and a charcoal dealer in Mikindani, Mombasa. She is a married mother of three school children. She buys and sells charcoal to the residents of Mikindani, a business she has done for the past three years. She is doing great.  This is her first borrowing from KADET LTD to finance her business. She plans to purchase more sacks of charcoal with the loan.   She will use the proceeds to educate her children and repay her loan. She hopes to have a more profitable business

name: Ketifalawo D Nasalo Shamimu Group
description: Ms. N. Shamimu is a single lady aged 25 years with 2 children, 1 schooling and another one young with 3 dependents. She will use her share of this group loan to sell used clothes, sandals, and air time. She has been in her business for a year now. There has been a positive change in her business.

name: Reema
description: Reema is a 23-year-old hardworking lady. She is living in Rawalpindi, Pakistan with her husband. Her husband is a Suzuki driver by profession but his monthly income is not enough to fulfill the household expenses of his family. Therefore for the past 4-years, Reema has also stitched clothes at home.   But currently her husband is not able to generate any income from the Suzuki, as its engine is not working properly and needs to be repaired. Reema has requested a loan from Kiva partner BRAC Pakistan to meet the amount of repairing the engine of her husband's Suzuki. With the profit her husband wants to open a new auto mechanic shop in the future.   Reema desires to provide quality education to all her children and she prays for the good health of her family and for the growth of her husband's business. She is very much thankful to BRAC and Kiva.

name: Ma. Febrica
description: Ma. Febrica is 57 years old. She is from Cabawan District, Tagbilaran City. She is married with four children; three are adults, and the youngest is 17.    Ma. Febrica is a midwife by profession, and she also owns and operates a small drugstore. Her business is within the health center where she works, providing her customers with affordable but quality medicines.   She is asking for a loan to buy more medicines for her drugstore. In the future, she hopes to have a bigger drugstore that will provide a better service and affordable medicines to her customers.

name: Jose Eulogio
description: Eulogio is 22 years old. He is single and lives in the house of some relatives, which is their own and has water and electricity. It is located in the rural area of the Olmos district, which is an hour from the department of Lambayeque. The people there work in agriculture, raise animals, and sell fruit, especially lemons and mangos.  Eulogio's business is making and selling wooden boxes for transporting fruit. His workshop where he makes them is in the house of his relatives. His business is very profitable since in that area there is quite a lot of business selling fruit, which is transported to other places. Eulogio has his own customers who place orders, and the income that he obtains helps him pay for his personal expenses.  For this reason, he thought it would be convenient to apply to Edpyme Alternative for a loan of 1000 PEN to buy more basic materials (wood, nails, paper, etc) to continue making the wood boxes, be able to complete his pending orders, and remain on good terms with his customers, emphasizing to us the quality of his products. Eulogio is a man who has known how to advance himself with much effort and work to improve in life to continue helping with the expenses of the relatives he lives with.

name: Jesucrifina
description: Jesucrifina is 55 years old and married to Tannie, a farmer.  They have two children: Jerome, 29 years old, working in an Electronics Shop and Lilibeth, 28 years old and married.    Jesucrifina is engaged in retailing DXN products.  She is working double-time hoping that they can improve their way of living and cover their family's needs.   She wants to venture into another business, fruit retailing.  This made  her decided to take out a loan from KIVA lenders amounting to PHP 7,000. She believes that by having this second business, her income will increase.  She hopes that her loan will be approved in order to maintain and further expand her retail business.

name: Nusrat
description: Nusrat is the 36 years old, the mother of four children and lives in Lahore, Pakistan. Her husband has been running a general store that sells goods such as rice, sugar, cooking oil, detergent, soap and biscuits. He provides the family's household necessities from the store, and his relatives also like to buy from it. His voice has an impressive, even tone and he easily wins the trust of others. Due to his behavior and manner, he has built up very good relations with his customers. His general store is very famous in the town, which is why it does well. In fact, his sales have increased a lot, but he does not have sufficient stock to cope with the demand. Thus, Nusrat has requested a loan for her husband so that he can buy more stock of wheat, rice, flour, pulses, soaps, shampoo, detergents and biscuits. She hopes that her husband will use the loan in a positive way; this amount will help him to meet the needs of the family. Nusrat thanks Kiva and field partner BRAC Pakistan.

name: Rose Mwikali
description: Rose is 37 years old and married to a farmer. They have six children, four sons and two daughters, aged 11 and 12 years and up. She describes herself as a quiet and social woman. For the last four years, she has been selling t-shirts, trousers, and shirts to frequent customers. In addition, sometimes she runs a grocery store to increase her income. She faces the challenge of having inadequate funds to add a new stock of shoes to her business. She will use the requested loan of KES 10,000 to buy more shoes. Rose looks forward to running a cereal shop in the future.

name: Kuka
description: Kuka is a 38 year old mother with 4 children, she runs a small business of selling taro and banana in her village to earn a living. Kuka requested for a loan to buy taro roots(seedling), banana tube(seedling), wheelbarrow, rake, shovel, water tank, backpack sprayer, to help her run the business. She will use her profit to expand her business. She became a member of SPBD in 2014.

name: Santalina
description: Santalina is 40 year old a married woman. She has five children, two of whom are in school. She has had a business of selling charcoal in Kator South Sudan for three years.  Santalina is requesting this loan through BRAC, South Sudan to purchase charcoal. She will use her extra income from this loan to build a house in the future.

name: Rebecca
description: Rebecca is 43 years old. She is married to Daudi and they are blessed with three children who are school-going.  Rebecca owns a bakery in the Kitengela market, where she supplies cakes to shops, schools and supermarkets. She has been doing this business for the last year and gets an income of 8,450 Kenyan shillings (KES) per month.  Rebecca was introduced to KADET by a KADET officer. She is applying for her first loan of KES 30,000 from KADET LTD., with which she plans to buy flour, baking powder, sugar and a motorbike for distribution. She will use the extra profit to open a branch in Mlolongo.  Rebecca hopes to establish a big baking factory in which to bake and supply cakes and breads. She is very hardworking.

name: Milagros
description: Milagros is 39 years old and married. Milagros works very hard to provide for them.  Milagros runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 17,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more stocks, such as canned goods, noodles, vinegar, coffee, sugar, and other groceries to resell.  Milagros has been in this business for 10 years and sells a variety of items, such as canned goods, noodles, vinegar, coffee, sugar, and other groceries.   Milagros would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Ruzanna
description: Ruzanna is an experienced farmer from the Verin Artashat village of the Ararat region. She lives with her son, daughter-in-law, and two-year-old grand-daughter. Ruzanna’s son works in the government sector and is currently the main breadwinner for the family. To assist her son in earning a living, Ruzanna is engaged in breeding a livestock of pigs and hens, and in the cultivation of peach, apricot, pears and grapes. The family realizes the agricultural products in the local market. They have a special refrigerator for fruits, where the fruits can remain fresh for a long time.  They keep the fruits in the refrigerator and sell them in winter, when the prices of those fruits are much higher. To continue the agribusiness in a sustainable way and develop it further, Ruzanna needs a loan of USD 2,500 to purchase a piece of land which she can use for horticulture. She and her family will be grateful to all the lenders for their goodwill in helping them develop their agribusiness.

name: Yamyle
description: Yamyle is from the city of San Ignacio. She lives with her sister and they both work in the family business. She is studying for a degree in business administration, struggling to be able to improve her living conditions.She asks for this loan to be able to invest it in paying her program fees, and in this way to be able to continue struggling to study and be someone in life.

name: Marven
description: Marven earns a living offering internet cafe services.  He is 28 years old, married, and lives in Pangi, Siquijor, Siquijor. He is now well known for the nice quality of services he offers.  He has already purchased computer sets and has been able to save from it.  His services are self-sustainable and  profitable, with a net profit of about PHP 10,000 per month.  Marven  is seeking a PHP 30,000 loan.  He would like to use the loan to purchase additional computer sets and equipment.   This is a regular loan, and would be repaid within a few months. This is his availment.  Marven is very diligent and accurate, which only adds to the effective management of his venture.

name: Leonora
description: Leonora is 57 years old and married with three children.  Leonora works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 5000 loan through NWTF to buy more goods to sell in her general store.  Leonora has borrowed and repaid 4 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 5 years and also earns additional income from food vending.  Leonora aspires to save money to expand her business.

name: Vasya
description: Vasya is married with a teenage daughter Vanessa. He lives in Vinogradovo, Western Ukraine. Vasya sells fishing supplies, fishing rods and tents in a small retail store located at a wholesale market in his home town. He doesn’t have many competitors which helps his business keep a solid standing. Vasya launched this venture 5 years ago. Currently, he has 50,000 Grivnyas in inventory. His profit amounts to 5,000 Grivnyas a month.   Vasya is requesting a 14,000 Grivnya loan to increase his working capital. Main characteristics of his business are consistency and stability. Vasya is hoping to keep his business running and efficient in the future. One of his short-term plans is to open one more vending location in his home town of Vinogradovo.

name: La Reforma Group
description: Cristina lives in San Pedro de Macoris with her six children (ages: 23, 21, 18, 16, 13, and 10 years old) and her husband. Cristina sells food from a small stand outside of her house, and she would like to use the proceeds from this loan to buy more merchandise for her business. Her dream for the future is to be able to open her own restaurant, and she would like all of her children to attend university so that they might have a better life than she has had. According to Cristina, her biggest problem as of late is earning enough money to get by on a daily basis. She hopes that with this loan she will be able to expand her business, and that she will have enough money to pay for basic life necessities.   Esperanza would like to thank every Kiva lender for their support and generosity. God Bless!

name: Sitha
description: Mr. Sitha S. and his wife, Mrs. Sokvanna Phauk (pictured together), live along National Road Number One about eighteen kilometers from Phnom Penh.  They were married in 1990 and have three children, two sons and one daughter. Two of them attend school and another one is still young.   Sitha has been a hairdresser for more than eighteen years. He operates his shop in Kor Ky market. His first loan has just been finished. He hopes to organize the house where he lives become neater, so he is asking for his second loan of $1,000 to fill up the land and put an addition on his house.

name: Mujeres Del Mañana Group
description: ZENOBIA JUDITH, is 51 years old and single. She is a member of the “Women of Tomorrow” group, made up of five independent women who want to make a living through hard work in their own businesses.   More than five years ago she started a small business, that was just a tiny stall with some sweets and drinks. Today, thanks to the loans received from Edaprospo that helped her inject capital into her stall, the business has grown and is now a well-stocked grocery that can satisfy her client’s needs and expectations.   She will invest the loan received in buying foodstuffs and drinks.

name: Dao Thi
description: Mrs. Dap Thi C. is 53 years old.  Her husband passed away early and she is now living with one grown up son.  Mrs. C. joined TYM Fund in 1997.  Currently, she is the owner of a retail store selling clothes at Kim Dong district, Hung Yen Province.  With the help of her son, her business has grown and brings her an income of 2,000,000 VND per month.  She would like to borrow 10,000,000 VND to invest in more supplies to expand her business.Translated from Vietnamese by Thiennga Ngo, Kiva Volunteer

name: Vilma
description: Vilma is 34 years old, married and has 3 children.   Vilma works hard to provide for her family. She has been running a ari-sari store in the Philippines for the past 3 years.  She also earns extra income from food vending.   Vilma has requested a 10000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy items to sell in her sari-sari store such as bread, groceries products, etc.   She has  successfully repaid 1 previous loan from NWTF before this loan.   Vilma aspires to save money to expand her business.

name: Filomeno
description: Filomeno is 49 years old, and he lives with his children in a rented house. More than five years ago, he decided to start selling used cars, which he acquires from friends who want to sell their cars. He earns a commission on each sale, and with this capital, he purchases more used cars to sell. He dedicates himself to this work in his spare time, since his main profession is teaching primary school. What Filomeno desires most is to acquire more working capital in order to buy more cars. This is his first loan with MFP, and he is very enthusiastic about reaching his goals so that he can provide for his children's well-being, since his wife has gone abroad. With the loan he is requesting, he will buy a used car in order to sell it for a good price. Translated from Spanish by Patricia Linderman, Kiva Volunteer

name: Leopoldo
description: 57 year-old Leopoldo is a very responsible man.  He is separated and lives in his own home together with his daughter, his son-in-law and his two grandchildren.  Leopoldo has been selling decals for car and motorcycle taxi windshields for 16 years.  His sales location is in a busy central avenue in the city, one hour by car from his home.  He really enjoys his work since his creativity and his good eye for detail have enabled him to attract many customers which means his business is profitable and he hasn't needed to make much investment.  However, the number of people in the same trade who offer their products more cheaply has increased.  For this reason, Leopoldo needs to buy some decals, crystals and mirrors wholesale so that he can compete effectively against them.  Leopoldo does have some loyal customers who always prefer to buy from him which gives him the motivation he needs to continue working in this business.  In the future, he plans to set up a restaurant.  He plans to rent premises outside his house and the market and go into business with his daughter.  This is Leopoldo's 16th loan with MFP and he pledges to continue making his loan repayments with the same responsibility.  He will use his loan to buy  decals, mirrors and crystals so that he can carry out his work.

name: Lilia
description: Lilia is a hard-working and fiesty young woman of 20 years. She lives at her parents' house and wants to work hard to improve her quality of life. Lilia's life has not been easy: she has worried about helping with household expenses from a very young age. Today she has a clothing sales business with a kiosk located at a market in San José (an important location in the city of Juliaca), where she offers many hand-woven garments such as scarves and gloves.   What she likes most about her job is weaving, and she does this very skillfully. She has two years of experience and finds that the most difficult part is transporting her garments to the market, since the bundles she carries are large and heavy. In time, she hopes to have a clothing store where she can attend to her customers more comfortably.   This is Lilia's first loan with MFP and she is determined to pay her installments on time. At her communal bank she is well-liked and respected by her fellow members. With the seven hundred nuevos soles requested, she will purchase more wool to make her garments so that she will have more items to sell. Translated from Spanish by Amanda McDermott, Kiva Volunteer

name: John
description: John is 30 years old and married with three children.  Two of which are in school.  He does mixed farming such as rearing sheep and goats as well as growing wheat.
