John has been successful in growing wheat for the past eight years.  He learned about KADET LTD through a KADET staff member.  He is a good client and has applied for his first loan which he plans to spend part in farming and the remaining amount to purchase more animals.  He hopes to make a profit and educate his children.  He also dreams and hopes to expand his business.

name: Yatta
description: This is 43-year-old Yatta. She is widowed and has seven children aged 21, 18, 15, 12, 10, 6 and 5, all of whom are in school. In 1996, Yatta established her foodstuff business (selling bulgur, garri and cornflour). She began her business in order to effectively play the role of her late husband as a breadwinner. This business is her only source of income. Working seven days a week, and eleven hours a day, she earns about 1,000,000 SLL every month from this business.  Yatta requires a loan in order to buy bags of bulgur, garri and cornflour. She is requesting a loan of 3,000,000 SLL. In the future, Yatta plans to build a back house in her compound, and further support the education of her children. She thanks you for your support.

name: Maravillas Group
description: This group is called “MARAVILLAS” (Marvelous) because its members are very devoted to the religious image of the Marvelous Lord, which is venerated near their community.  They are also proud because they do marvelous things with their money, making it return 100% profit in their respective businesses.  This group is located in Puebla, Mexico and is made up of ten achieving women, each having her own successful business.  This is their fourth cycle working with CreditComun and they have always been punctual with their payments.  They will use the money from this loan to buy supplies (fabric for making stuffed animals, different sizes of artificial eyes, thread, and stuffing).  The group’s treasurer is named María de Lourdes Nieves A.L. and she is the group’s most honest and responsible person.  This is why she was elected to this position among the other officers.  She is 45 years old, has a junior high school education, is single, and makes and sells stuffed animals.  She is a very enterprising woman and designs her own items.  Her peers see her as a person to be emulated, despite her limited formal education.  With a lot of effort she’s been able to establish a large number of customers.  For her, success would mean opening her own stuffed animal factory and creating her own brand.  She also dreams of becoming known throughout the world and exporting her products.  Her goal in life is to create jobs for other women, who, like her, dream of providing good educations for their families, so that they don’t suffer from the same needs that they have had to deal with.  These loans have made it possible for each of them establish their small businesses.  The other members of the group are:  Gabriela A. L. – Cosmetic sales Josefdina G. T. – General merchandise Irma A. L. – Shoe sales Maria Rosa Ignacia G. M. – White sales Olivia Clara A. L. – Juice sales Maria Del Carmen A. G. – Washing Maria Soledad C. C. – Clothing sales Cecilia F. G. – Food sales Susana C. F. – Dish sales Translated from Spanish by Hugo Reyes, Kiva Volunteer

name: Justo Patrocinio
description: Justo Patrocinio lives in the village of Santa Elena, on a road that leads to the Guatemalan border. Justo and his wife Irma have 8 children, the youngest of whom is four and the oldest 22. The older boys helped plant and take care of the cacao farm, and are now searching for jobs in town, while the younger are interested in and counted on for help around the farm.   Justo likes farming cacao because it both brings in money and can be used to make your own chocolate drink. The drink of the Gods, as it was regarded by the ancient Mayas and limited to the elites, is very commonplace in the Maya communities today. You can make it by grinding the cacao beans (usually by hand) and molding cacao balls that can be dissolved in hot water for a rich and nutritious beverage.   Justo is requesting this loan to hire five people for a week to help him clean four acres of cacao. Cleaning underbrush is a routine activity for cacao farmers in the tropical lowlands. Cacao grows in agroforestry-type ecosystems with varying levels of vegetation and on fertile jungle soil that is especially productive and non-selective about what it grows, so farmers have to be.   Like few farmers in his village, Justo has diversified his crops and besides the typical combination of cacao, corn and beans, he grows fruit trees like starfruit and soursop, coffee and cardamom. “It’s hard when you start things because there’s no money at that point. I have to wait for harvest time,” he explains the difficulty in investing to diversify his farm. In the future, Justo wants to invest in more trees and do some reconstruction on the house. If he works hard this year, he says he might afford to buy a solar panel to illuminate the house before his daughter starts high school.

name: Mtama
description: Mtama is a very hardworking and enterprising woman who says that she has been able to greatly increase her income and improved her living standards thanks to her hard work.  She still operates the cafe business and prepares food for her customers.  She is asking for a loan to buy ingredients such as wheat flour, milk, eggs, maize flour, and sugar that will help her to invest back into her business. She is grateful for the new support she has received.

name: Balqees
description: Balqees is a widow. Some years ago, she decided to support her family by starting a business tailoring to meet their day-to-day expenses. Balqees is popularly known in her area for her skill in stitching. However, due to a shortage of raw materials, she is facing difficulty in meeting daily expenses related to her business.   Therefore, she has requested for a loan of PKR 45000. With the requested loan, she wants to purchase stitching materials, such as threads of different colors, laces, zippers and cloth to stitch more dresses on time to generate a healthy income for her family.

name: Pikédinabè
description: Madame T. opened her own boutique called “Ets Rose de Matin” in 2004. She sells food products and her client base continues to grow every day. In order to keep her customers satisfied, she has applied for a loan with WAGES, a Kiva partner, to purchase 14 boxes of soap, eight cases of wine, 10 bags of rice and three boxes of couscous.   She is married, but has no children. With the profits made from her general store, she will continue to contribute to her family’s daily expenses.

name: Guillerma
description: Guillerma works hard to support her family. She is widowed and has an abaca-weaving business in the Philippines.  Guillerma requested a PHP 8,000 loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to buy more raw materials for her business, like abaca fiber.  Guillerma has been in this business for five years now. She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Abdukayum
description: He is what people usually call a man's man. Abdukayum is a 30-year-old man. He was raised in a poor family, and from his childhood, he was helping his parents. After finishing school, he got married. He was the one who supports, feeds, and takes care of his parents and the whole family. He prepared and provided the wedding party for his younger brother too.   Now he is foreman; he builds and reconstructs houses. He has 5 kids. That’s why he needs to overhaul his house. His house is in bad condition. He is asking for a loan of 7,500 TJS to buy building materials for repairing house. He awaits your support.

name: Martha Evelia
description: The Credit Group San Pablo meets every 15 years in the citadel of Costa Azul in the city of Manta, a city known for its beautiful beaches visited all year round and for being a city of unsurpassed beauty with many attractive tourist sites.   Martha is 34 years old and married, and from her marriage, she has four children - 18, 14, 11 and 9 years old.  The three youngest study in high school and elementary school.  Her husband is a fisherman and also has a taxi service that he works in when he is not fishing. In order to keep her family moving forward, Doña Martha has a food supply store in her house.  There, she sells all types of food such as rice, oils, detergent, vegetables, and fruits.  She works every day from 6:00am until 8:00pm, and sometimes, until later.  Her daughter and husband help her in her work whenever they are able to and available.  She has been doing this for 20 years and her business is going well.  This credit will help her to stock her store more.  She will buy rice, sugar, oil, detergents, sausages, and other staples.  She will also buy supplies for fishing such as fuel, nets, lanyards and food for the trip, for her husband.  She is part of the Credit Group for 17 years and likes its because she receives health insurance and group health discussions.

name: Benkadi Group
description: BENKADI is a group of the LOLO association of SANANKORO DJITOUMOU. It groups together women who met each other through relatives and neighbors. They are on average 41 years old and married with on average five children. They run different businesses, such as making flour into biscuits, as does SOUMBADIE, who is sitting to the far left in the photo. They live in nuclear families in SANANKORO DJITOUMOU in the prefecture of KATI (Koulikoro region, republic of Mali). They have been in small business for several years and are highly sought after in their  food-serving businesses: flour and oil. With the concern of satisfying the growing needs of their clientele, the group members decided to integrate Soro Yiriwaso's loan program. They are on their first group loan. SOUMBADJE, who is the president of the group is well known in SANANKORO DJITOUMOU, excels in making flour into biscuits. She plans to use her loan to buy 1 sack of flour and a large quantity of oil. She stocks up in SANANKORO DJITOUMOU. She sells her food in SANANKORO DJITOUMOU at retail for cash or credit to a clientele composed of men and women. She hopes to make a monthly profit of 12,000 FCFA, which will allow her to repay the loan and to invest in her business.

name: Nancy
description: This is Nancy, 56, a resident of Bacoor, Cavite, Philippines. She is married to Alvin and a mother to their children. She, together with her husband, manages their household while operating the business. She and her husband are working hard to provide income for their everyday needs.  Nancy maintains a direct selling business. She sells clothing, footwear, undergarments, cosmetics and other products through the popular direct selling brands like Avon, Fuller Life, Natasha, Boardwalk, Marikina Shoe Exchange, and other direct selling brands. A customer's order is bought in cash by the dealer and then given to the customer with a one-month-to-pay credit. Dealer’s prices are lower than those in the catalogue, and these are the profits that dealers are investing as their income. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community. She earns a minimum of 2,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) in sales every week.  To help her continue operations of her business, she is requesting a 10,000 PHP loan. She will be utilizing the loan to buy additional supplies and merchandise products like shampoo, cologne, deodorant, perfume, soap, fabric softener, undergarments and other products needed in her business. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands her business.    Nancy hopes that her business will grow bigger, and she dreams to have a good life. She meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her life and business every week, and this is where she can also draw strength and inspiration from the fellowship and the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Catarina
description: Catarina is a 41-year old single mother with a nice family of four children between the ages of 10 and 18 years. The family lives in a community of the town Xejuyup. She works in the fabrication and sale of traditional clothing, an activity she has been engaged in for three years. She carries out this activity because it is one of the most profitable businesses in the community. To improve her income, she sells the green "maxan" leaves used to make tamales.   Catarina is an enterprising person who is full of vision. She has the ambition of having her own site where she can cultivate the leaves. She has decided to request a loan for the purchase of a parcel of land for cultivation. Her life's hope is to establish the cultivation and that her family has better living conditions.

name: Jorge Luis
description: Jorge Luis is 40 years old, lives with his wife in the district of Buenos Aires, and they have basic services in their home.  It is in a community dedicated to agriculture, commerce, and livestock, which is located in the Morropon Province in the Piura Region on the north coast of Peru.  He earns a living making adobe and brick by hand to then offer for housing construction.  He has asked for a loan of 1000 nuevos soles to buy corrugated iron panels to improve his house because the rainy season is approaching.

name: Awaot
description: Awaot is 35 years old, married and has four children, all of whom are in school. For the last five years, she has earned a living by selling food from a stall located in Bor, South Sudan. She is applying for a loan from BRAC South Sudan to buy sugar and oil to sell to her customers. She will use the extra income she earns as a result of this loan to pay her children's school fees.

name: Helen
description: Helen is 60 years old and married with four children, one of whom is in school. Helen works very hard to provide for them.She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 16,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more groceries to sell.  Helen has been in this business for 15 years and sells a variety of items such as sugar, soap and other groceries.   In the future Helen would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Irene's Group
description: M. Irene is the leader of her lending group in Mukono. She is 25 years old and married with 3 children aged 5, 3 and 1 year. Her first-born child is in school. Hers is a success story. M. got pregnant with her first child while still very young. Her (now) husband has helped to make sure she continues her schooling at the University on the evening programme. During the day, M. is a businesswoman operating a grocery store. She sells general merchandise in Kirinya trading centre. She also has a poultry business at home with broilers for meat. She is a hard working young lady with a strong drive to succeed in life. Irene needs a loan to help buy more goods for her shop. She will use the funds to purchase sugar, salt, cooking oil, bread and so on, as well as to buy chicken feed for her broilers.

name: Mahtumbi
description: Mahtumbi lives in the town of Kulob. 57 years of age. Married, with two children. She works as a vendor at the local market. She rents out  a stand, where she sells children’s clothing. She has been in this business for 10 years. She is taking out a loan in order to buy goods for the new season.

name: Nath's Group
description: Nath’s group live in a rural village in Kampot province in Cambodia. Nath makes a living cultivating rice to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help Nath and her group members to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Aslambeck
description: A. Aslambeck is 27 years old and he lives in the Mastchokh region of Tajikistan. Mr. A. and his family  raise and sell ivestock. He has a large herd. Mr. A. is requesting a loan of $750 to purchase mixed fodder for his livestock.

name: Dominga
description: Dominga belongs to the Kancharisun communal bank, which is located in the district of Cusco and department of Cusco.Dominga continues with her artisanal business. She is a responsible woman who hopes to earn more so that she can continue supporting her family. She continues selling her artisanal products to her clients who request them. In this way, she can take her family forward.She is thankful for the loan offered and promises to repay the loan according to the established schedule. She requests the loan to buy shirts, among other things.

name: Corazon De Oro Group
description: The “CORAZON DE ORO” community organization will begin its second cycle with Pro Mujer as part of the Collpani center.  It’s made up of eight members and governed by a board of directors where Cecilia serves as president.  The members are involved in various businesses, including: food sales, macramé weaving, food stores, hosiery sales, and sneaker sales.    This loan will benefit their small businesses.  Cecilia is in her third year with Pro Mujer, having joined after being invited by a fellow member.  She has a food business which she began on her mother’s encouragement and help.    She will use the money from this loan to buy tools (utensils) from distributers in El Alto.  She will then produce and sell from her stall.  This type of work allows her to generate income to support her household, as she lives with her husband and her son.   When asked what she likes about Pro Mujer, she says that she likes the training about health, credit, and savings.

name: Mariam's Group
description: Sitting at the left in the photo with her group of 13 women farmers and holding her myAgro booklet, Mariam, aged 65, is the mother of five children, of whom the youngest, a daughter, is in school. Mariam lives in the village of Ouoronina, in Mali. She has been working in  agriculture for over 50 years. She decided to sign up again with myAgro for her 0.125 hectare field of peanuts, since she really appreciates myAgro farming techniques and was satisfied with the yield from her last planting season. Still hopeful, she wishes to raise livestock and do commerce with her next harvest, since she does not want to limit herself to the farming of staple crops. But Mariam is familiar with the problems of: lack of rain and farm equipment (plows, …)

name: Mary
description: Mary is a 60-year-old businesswoman from Vihiga. She is a widow who takes care of four children.  Mary sells maize cereals and has been running this business for the last four years. She makes a monthly income of KES 12,500. She is taking her fourth loan from KADET LTD, which she will use to buy more maize cereals to boost her current stock. She will use the anticipated profits to provide for her family’s basic needs.  Her dream is to expand her business and to educate her children.

name: Anzhela
description: Anzhela is 49 years old. She lives in Artashar village with her 18-year-old son and 25-year-old daughter. Anzhela runs a farm where she breeds cattle. Her children are also involved in the farm's daily activities and always help their mother. Anzhela's farm has a barn and the necessary conditions for cattle breeding.  Anzhela is requesting a loan to purchase two calves. She also plans to use her loan to purchase grass to feed the cattle. Anzhela hopes to get additional income from increasing her herd and this is vital for insuring a brighter future for her children.

name: Mary
description: Mary is a hardworking woman who operates a vegetable stall. She faces a major challenge of seasonality in her place of operation. She dreams of establishing a grocery store in the future.  With the KES 10,000 she wants to purchase stock of green vegetables, tomatoes, potatoes and onions. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Ruth
description: Ruth and her family lives in the town of Ajuy in Iloilo, Philippines. She is married and has five adult children. Her husband works hard as a fisherman while Ruth sells the fish caught by her husband. She also sells dried fish aside from selling fresh fish. Ruth and her husband work together to provide their daily expenses. They also wish to save money for the future. Ruth is a 51-year-old woman who dreams to improve their means of living. She wants to enhance their livelihood. As for now, she is asking a loan to buy additional fresh fish and dried fish to sell.

name: Ma. Teresa
description: Ma. Teresa T. is now 37 years old and married to a driver Samson T. 44 years old. At the long years of their marriage they were given 2 children namely: Khristel Sam now in 2nd year high school and Chivae Rain now 1 year old. Ma. Teresa and her husband is a partner in taking care of their two children and giving them their needs through their growing.  Now as a source of their income her husband is driving a tricycle which is one of main means of transportation in their place. A tricycle is like a cab which has 3 wheels and can ride a maximum of 6 passengers. Although this business is not their main source of income it also contributes revenue for their expense. Also her husband manage their fish cage business, this business give them more income that’s why they focuses on it. As a matter of fact she will use the loan that she received from KIVA field partner Ahon sa Hirap Inc. (ASHI) as additional capital to her fish cage business. They will buy necessary things needed in her business like fish net, mini boat, bamboo and different kind of rope and also payment for the laborer. Ma. Teresa also run a variety store that also gives them additional income that they can use in times they needed it. ASHI approved the proposed loan of Ma. Teresa amounting Php 45,000 because she has a good credit rating. She always attend to a center meeting, always pay on time and her 3 businesses are running good.  One dreams of Ma. Teresa is to see her children finish their studies and living a descent and good life, not experiencing the hardness of life.

name: Savriya
description: Savriya, a 46 years old resident of the city of Vahdat, is starting a new business. She is interested in fattening and reselling cattle. Her family will help her with the new business. Savriya is married and has two sons and one daughter, who are all studying at the university.   Savriya does not work, however currently she has set herself the goal of starting a cattle breeding business. She thinks this is a profitable business, and that through it she will be able ti improve the family's financial situation. However, to realize her plans she needs a loan.   Savriya would like to use the loan to purchase cattle and start her own business.

name: Josephine Wamaitha
description: Josephine has practiced farming in Ndunyu Njeru town for the last 30 years.  She is 49 years old and is married to Joseph M.. They have five children.  She was introduced to KADET LTD by her friend. This will be her third loan. She paid all her previous loans well and in good time.  She plans to use the loan amount to buy fertilizer, potato seedlings and pay for labor.  In the future, Josephine hopes to buy more land so that she can practice large-scale farming.

name: Mugisho Group
description: Mwavita is a dynamic woman and treasurer of the loan group, Mugisho.  She is 47 years old, married to a farmer and mother to nine children.  Five of her children currently attend school.  She began her business in 2005 by selling agricultural products.  Two years later she installed a cassava grinding mill in order to improve the quality of the service that she offers.  Mwavita has requested this new loan in order to buy a second grinding mill and reinforce her stock holding with 1,000 kg of cassava.  The biggest obstacles that her business faces are unpredictable and frequent power cuts, and break downs of her grinding mill.  Therefore, her objective is to become a large-scale supplier of cassava in the town and countryside, and to purchase a sturdy mill powered by oil.  Mwavita is grateful to the field partner, Hekima and their colleagues for the services which they offer.

name: Ifagil
description: Ifagil A. lives in Beylagan city. He is 30 years old. He sells men's shoes at the Beylagan city bazaar. He has worked in this business sector since 1997. In 2006 he borrowed $500 from Normicro Beylagan Branch and expanded his business. This loan was very successful for his business. Because of this, he again applied to Normicro in 2007 and borrowed $1000 to expand his business and buy more kinds of goods.

name: Angelita
description: Angelita owns and manages a general store in her village. From this business, she earns a net of Php 6,000 monthly which is a big help to her family. For additional income, she sometimes sells vegetables which she gathers from her vegetable garden.  Angelita is borrowing Php 8,000 for the development of her business, hoping to have additional revolving capital for her general store. The loan will let her business grow and earn more income. She hopes that her loan request will be approved because she plans to purchase stocks of soft drinks and other merchandise that her valued customers may need.  Angelita is the mother of three children: her eldest just graduated from a short term course and her other two children are still studying and she hopes that they will also be able to finish their studies. Angelita is married to Rolando who works as a cook in a restaurant. Together, they help each other to provide for the needs of their children.

name: Leonarda
description: Leonarda is 45 years old and lives with her partner, who is the father of her four children.  She lives in a rented house in a town located in the Ayacuchan jungle called Palmapampa.  Leonarda never forgot those afternoons in her youth when she watched her grandparents clear the land and plant cacao seeds.  This is the reason why she chose to pursue farming, specifically growing cacao, in order to honor her grandparents’ legacy.  She now develops new farming techniques with the occasional help of her relatives, but she also hires workers for the harvest season.  Cacao has high demand on a national and international level.  Leonarda feels satisfied with the revenue she generates from selling her product to the collection centers in her area.  Later on she wants to buy more land so that she can complete on the same level as her neighbors.  This is her thirteenth loan with MFP.  Leonarda commits to making her payments and conforming to the work methodology of her Communal Bank.  The money she requested will be invested in supplies and organic fertilizers for her fields so that she can improve the quality of her product for the next harvest and sell it at a better price.Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Margaret
description: Margaret is a hard-working woman who is investing well in business. She has a house with neither electricity nor piped water. She is running a business of selling chicken to her customers, to satisfy their needs and also to improve her lifestyle. She is requesting for a loan of KES 30,000, which she will use to buy medicine for her chickens and also to feed them.

name: Morine Jahenda
description: Morine Jahenda E. is a hardworking 32-year-old woman. She is married to Harun Kitui, a driver, and together they have two children ages 8 and 10 years old .She has been operating a green grocery business for about five years and she earns a monthly income of KES 4,000.  She learned about KADET LTD and joined. She had no previous credit history with any other MFI. She has now applied for her first loan of KES. 30,000 from KADET LTD which she intends to use to buy bananas to sell. She plans to use the profits from the expanded business to build a market stall.  Morine hopes to expand her business and become the leading local investor and to see her children realizing their dreams in life through education.

name: Soan
description: Soan is a 41-year-old married woman with 2 sons. She lives in Ho Chi Minh City. Her husband is a bricklayer.   She has been selling handmade pottery products such as floral vases and ornaments since 2000. Her daily income is used to meet her family's basic needs.   Soan requires a loan to provide her with additional capital to buy more products and higher quality vases to better meet her customers' needs. She hopes that the additional products will enable her to generate a higher income and improve the well-being of her family.

name: Ma. Arlene
description: Ma. Arlene is 37 years old and single and she works very hard to help her parents. For the past 10 years, she has run a general store in the Philippines.  Ma. Arlene is requesting an 18,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy items such as canned goods, spices, egg, shampoo, soap, and other products. In the future, she would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Maricel
description: Maricel is 28 years old, married, and the mother of  two children, which are in school. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Maricel has a fish vending business in the Philippines.  Maricel has been in this business for 3 years.   Maricel requested a 12,000 PHP loan amount through NWTF to buy additional fish to sell in her fish stall.  In the future, Maricel would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Imelda
description: Imelda D. is 35 years old. She is married to Manny and they have two children. They live in a rural community in Barangay Manamtam, Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya. Their eldest child is now in first year college while the youngest is a first year high school. They want them to finish their studies till college so that they will find a good job someday.  They were able to send their children to school through their income. They cultivate their rice field twice a year and their main crops are rice and vegetables. When Imelda learned about Kiva, she was encouraged to request a loan of PHP 11,000 hoping that it will be granted for it will be of great help in purchasing farm inputs like fertilizers and insecticides for the maintenance of their farm. She hopes that they may able to increase their production to improve their way of living.

name: Evelyn
description: Evelyn is 35 years old and lives in Compound #3. She is married and her husband is a social worker. They have four children between the ages of 3 and 18. Three of them are attending school, while the youngest one stays at home. For the past 12 years Evelyn has been selling palm oil in the local market.  She is requesting a loan to purchase more palm oil for her business. She plans to sell and help her children to graduate from high school.

name: Mehriniso
description: Mehriniso is a 41 year old woman; she is married and is the mother of 6 children.  Her husband purchases and sells livestock at the livestock market.  Mehriniso fattens the livestock at home.  She helps her husband to develop his business, because she would like to increase their income to marry off her sons.  They would like to use the loan to increase their livestock headcount and increase their income.  Translated from Russian by Sabina Holzman, Kiva Volunteer

name: Gulbibi
description: Gulbibi is a mother of 3 adorable kids. she is very businesslike woman. She has more than one business. So she sells clothes at the market, fattens cattle and sells them and also grows wheat. She is a very unusual woman.  She wants to borrow money to expand her business and also for buying more cattle and fertilizers for growing wheat. Unfortunately Gulbibi wasn’t at the market when the photo was taken so we took a picture of her son who helps her out in her business.

name: G.s. Nagarote Group
description: Dominga, Patricia, and Laura are members of the Nagarote Communal Bank.  They are responsible people, and they enjoy supporting their families through their businesses.  Dominga Dolores has had a store for over 22 years.  She started with a few popular consumable products.  Most of her customers always request a variety of products from her.  Dominga has improved her inventory.  The reason for the loan is to buy basic grains, detergent, soft drinks, juice, cookies, soup, and canned goods, among other products.

name: Carol Elizabeth
description: Carol is a young woman of 22, who works as an agricultural worker on a farm that belongs to the city. The income she receives from her modest position allows her to help with the household expenses. At the same time, with a good deal of effort, she has been able to start a business raising ducks. Carol believes things are going well for her due to her hard-work and struggle. Carol is grateful for the support she receives from the lenders at Kiva. Thanks to their help she can buy the materials like wood, plastic sticks, drinking receptacles, canes, etc. to built cages for the ducks. With this she can improve her business and fight to make her dream a reality: "help her family get ahead".

name: Novalyn
description: Novalyn is a small entrepreneur selling snacks to the people in her village. She is selling siomai (meatballs made of shrimp or pork, wrapped and usually steamed). She buys ingredients at the public market to cook and sell in the afternoon. She usually generates P2,000 each month and it goes for daily meals for the family.  She would like to improve her sales, so she is asking for an additional capital of P8,000 to buy wrappers, cooking oil and ingredients used in cooking siomai to sell. In the future, though she generates only minimal income, she is hoping to increase it to save funds to use when emergency arises.

name: Chan's Group
description: Chan’s group live in a rural village in Kompong Speu province in Cambodia. Chan makes a living cultivating rice and he also does extra work as factory laborer to support his family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women and man to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Reina Isabel
description: Reina, 41, completed second grade.  She’s married and her husband works for a post office.  They have six children living at home with them; three of them work and three attend the local school.  The three that work spend most of their time away.  Reina has been providing snacks at an institution for a year.  She’s also baked cakes at home to sell for the last two years.  She spends her time alone with her three children because the rest of the family members come home late at night and she looks for ways not to be bored.  She also sees the income she earns so she bakes them.  She used to work picking coffee during harvest season but noting that this was just seasonal work she decided to start her cake and fried cassava business.  Her sister helps her and so do her daughters when they come home from school.  The loan she’s asking Fundación Campo for is to buy five sacks of cement and five metal sheets to build a shed over around a toilet because it’s not working now and it’s very useful and sanitary for the family.  Reina’s dream is to finish building the toilet so that her family will be safe from contracting diseases and contaminating the environment.  Also, with the little left over she will buy ingredients needed to make the snacks and to sell the cakes to gradually increase business and profits to move her family forward.

name: Sumaira
description: Sumaira is a 21-year-old married woman in the business of selling goats for the last four years. At the present, she has three goats. Her business is good enough to lead her a decent life.   She purchases small goats, and after nurturing them, she sells them in her community. She has improved her business to meet the day to day expenses of life. It’s her 4th year with Kashf Foundation.   She is happily running her business with the support of it. Now she has requested a loan of PKR 20,000 to purchase two more goats. She hopes to have a good experience with this new loan and dreams of expanding her business in the near future.

name: Nurhayati
description: Nurhayati is 23 years old and is married with one child aged 1. She has a small shop which sells snacks, food, and drinks, along with household products. She can earn $6 per day. Her husband has no fixed income. She would like a IDR 900,000 loan to complete her business. Nurhayati hopes that she can improve her income to use towards her children's education. She is a member of MBK and is willing to repay this loan within a period of 12 months.

name: Nancy Violeta
description: Mrs. Nancy is 55 years old and has three children.  She runs a grocery store and sells essential goods such as rice, sugar, milk, oil and other products.  Her work hours are from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.  Through this business she has been able to support her children.  She wants to expand her store and is requesting a loan to buy products wholesale, such as rice, sugar, milk and oil.  She is very grateful for the support and committed to paying back the loan on time.

name: Gloria Gilma
description: Gloria is a single woman of 49, without children or other people to support her. The only thing she has is a business of selling food, where she generates all the resources to pay her bills and to bring food to the table.   Her business is selling food.  Gloria is a dreamer. She knows that she is poor, but this is not an impediment to dreaming about buying her own house. Every day, with every customer, feeds this dream, and now she needs the help and the heart of people who want to support her by lending her the capital for the purchase of an umbrella, since the heavy rains affect her sales. She will [also] buy chairs and a stock of food for her business.  This loan will allow her to increase the number of customers, since she will have a place to serve them, and they can shelter from the downpours while buying an exquisite cup of coffee with a delicious appetizer.

name: Marlit
description: Marlit is 29 years old. She is single and lives with her two children in her home. For two years she has worked in the business of selling American clothes as a street vendor and in her house.   Marlit's business is located in the community of  San Lorenzo in southern Honduras. In her business she sells all kinds of clothes, both used and new. She also sells "enchape", which is silver and steel jewelry. Marlit is a young woman who is very hardworking and who wants to get ahead.   Marlit is asking for the loan to buy skirts, pants, dresses, shorts, blouses, swim shorts, etc. With the help of the loan she intends to improve her income a little and therefore her quality of life. She is very happy to continue working with Prisma.  Marlit's dream is to improve her home and her business.   San Lorenzo, Honduras - Junio del 2013.

name: Gloria Estefania
description: Gloria is another active member of the community bank "Ensueños". She lives in the city of Azogues, which is characterized by its cold climate, churches, and the beauty of its historical city center where the colonial and modern are mixed together. The people here are very kind and hardworking, including our members who, day in and day out, are searching for opportunities to improve conditions for themselves and their families.  Our member is 22 years old, married, and the mother of a baby who is one year and eight months old. Gloria and her husband work in the cafeteria that they opened 5 months ago. They work Monday to Thursday from 9 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon and at weekends in order to improve the business and prepare lunches, snacks, rice with vegetables, roast meats, and other dishes.  She is in her fifth loan cycle, and it was one of her cousins who invited her to be part of this wonderful group. With the money from the loan, she will invest in growing the cafeteria, buying tables, chairs, dishes, and more kitchenware. He greatest dream is to have her own restaurant in order to best serve her customers.  Translated from Spanish by Alison Hynd, Kiva Volunteer

name: Etelvina
description: Etelvina was born in the district of Homoine, in the province of Inhambane in southern Mozambique. She is married and has four children; three of them have finished their studies and the other is in the tenth grade. She went to school through the fourth grade but had to drop out because of financial difficulties. She lives in her own home with her family, and also supports two grandchildren, her mother, and her mother-in-law, who live with them.  She and her parents left Homoine when she was still small. She's been selling products door to door for more than 13 years and earns about 3,000 meticals a month. She uses her earnings for household expenses and is able to save some in her bank account. She's never had loans from other banks. She learned about Hluvuku from friends who are also clients of the institution. This is her first loan, in the amount of 20,000 meticals, which she will use to purchase construction materials (sand, cement, cinder blocks, rebar, etc.) to continue construction on her house. She hopes to ask for further loans from Hluvuku so she can complete and furnish her house.

name: Nathalie Madinatou
description: A. Nathalie Madinatou was born around 1975 in Porto-Novo, the administrative and political capital of the Republic of Benin.  She is married to DOUROSSIMI Wakili and is the mother of two children, who are both in school.  Nathalie Madinatou lives in Cotonou, the economic capital of the Republic of Benin.  Thanks to her business, she manages to support herself.  What she sells is cloth.  She needs funds to develop her business further.  This is why she's asking for a loan, so as to bolster her working capital.Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Yeang
description: This is Yeang, aged 30, photographed in front of her house situated in Prey Chor district. Here she lives with her spouse and four school-aged children. Yeang and her spouse cooperate well in raising their children and provide them a good education. They work together on their farmland, on which they grow rice and other seasonal crops for sale. Normally, they are able to make about $4 each per day.  Yeang needs to improve her farming practices, so she is taking out a loan of 600,000 KHR to purchase fertilizer for her crops. With the remaining funds, she will add to her existing money to purchase fishing supplies, which will be used by her husband in fishing activities. She hopes that she will be able to yield a good income to satisfy her living needs.

name: Namutebi
description: Jane is single with two children and none of her children go to school. She takes care of additional family members (grand children). She operates a canteen selling samosa, fried cassava, and chapatti.  She has been in this business for 10 years. She works seven days a week.  She has applied for a loan of Uganda shillings 700,000 from MCDT-SACCO to buy baking flour, cooking oil, spices, cow peas, a bag of charcoal, and other snacks. Her major business challenges include seasonality, ever increasing prices of baking flour and cooking oil, and defaulters. She aspires to get a fridge to sell soft drinks. She resides in her own house and the family has access to electricity and piped water. Her monthly expense includes bills and feeding the family.

name: Safiatou
description: Safiatou is 22 years old, married and mother to two children. She lives with her husband in a traditional family in the Heremakono Nord district of Bougouni.   After her marriage she began a small business selling clothes, "pagnes" (pieces of colorful fabric) and linen sets. With five years' experience she now enjoys a significant reputation. Her sales strength is her affordable prices but also her good business sense.   With a view to boosting her business and satisfy customer demand, she is turning to Soro Yiriwaso, and is on her first individual loan with the institution. She plans to use her loan to buy 10 "pagnes wax" (highly decorative pieces of colorful fabric) and one roll of embroidered "pagne".  She gets her supplies from wholesalers in Bamako.   Safiatou sells for cash and on credit, to a customer base made up primarily of women, at the market and from home. She expects to make a monthly profit of 40,000FCFA, which will be used to help her husband with the family expenses and to reinvest in her business. Her ambition is to become a wholesaler in this business.

name: Veronica
description: Veronica continues to make her living in the grocery store. She sells basic items such as rice, sugar, milk and biscuits. She has already spent seven years in the business and it is going very well. Veronica's dream is to expand the grocery store. She is seeking the loan to buy rice, sugar, milk and biscuits.  Veronica is pleased about the loan and promises to meet the repayments.

name: Elsie
description: Elsie is 63 years old and widowed, with three children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur.   Elsie has a food-vending business in the Philippines. She has requested a PHP 17,000 loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to buy ingredients for her food production business.  Elsie has been in this business for 16 years. She would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Munhbat
description: Munhbat, a 35-year-old father of three children, all studying at the secondary school level, lives in Western Mongolia where he started working as a carpenter in 2004. During these years, he earned many regular customers making a variety of house furniture which his wife sells in the market. His plan is to make furniture in increasing quantities.   A diligent man who says, "I would like to extend my wooden furniture business by purchasing necessary materials so that there will be ready products for the customers to buy immediately instead of having to wait, Munhbat is requesting a loan of 1,700,000 MNT to purchase wood and other materials.

name: Deisy Fiorella
description: Deisy is a young woman who is 18 years of age.  She is very enthusiastic and optimistic.  Deisy lives with her mother and grandmother, who she loves dearly.  At the moment, Deisy is working and studying.  She is already supporting the household, but she wants to become a professional and make her family proud.  Her home is located in the city of Chincha, which is known for its warm climate.  It is also the site of the greatest victories in Peruvian sports.  The inhabitants have a gift for preparing dishes that result in delicious flavor.  One of Deisy's favorite dishes is "arroz con pato" (duck with rice).  With what she earns from her job, Deisy is able to study for a degree in Accounting, but she would like to continue on to an advanced degree at the university.    Each day Deisy works as an assistant bookkeeper at a lodge in the city.  She works approximately nine hours and then attends classes at night at an institute in her city.  Deisy believes she is doing well in her job and in her studies because she is responsible, honest, and friendly.    Deisy is extremely grateful to the Kiva lenders.  Thanks to their overwhelming support, she will be able to help her grandmother who has an illness and needs medicines and medical treatment consultations.  This will enable Deisy to help her grandmother improve so that she can have a better quality of life.  She also continues to strive for a better life for herself and to fulfill her greatest dream of studying at the university.

name: Waheed
description: Waheed A., a young man, is one of the active farmers in the Ningarhar province. He is 23, and because of civil wars in Afghanistan during the past three decades, he was not able to go to school, so he was left illiterate.  He helped his father to earn income for their family.  Waheed’s father was also a farmer but now he has some serious sicknesses, and doctors don’t allow him to work. So Waheed is working alone on their agricultural lands growing tomatoes, onions, peppers, and other vegetables.  Actually, they have much better lands in a good area, which is to near a marketplace where they can sell their products easily. However, Waheed still has some complaints about one thing: a lack of irrigation water.  They have faced this problem for several years, and Waheed was so sad about it and didn’t know how to solve it because he didn’t have much money to purchase an electric water pump.   When one of his friends told him about the AFSG micro finance institute, Waheed became so happy and immediately requested a loan of 30,000 Afghanis.   Waheed hopes that through this credit, he will be able to purchase a water pump for his lands and stand on his own feet as soon as possible.  He also dreams of a brighter future for his family, especially for his younger brothers.  He thanks lenders in advance who help needy people like him.

name: Alex
description: Alex is married with 6 children. He is 55 years old and lives in the Philippines.  He operates a service-based business, providing transportation services to local community members to earn a living. He has been doing this for 11 years, and every month he earns approximately 4,000 PHP from this work. He has requested a loan of 5,000 PHP to repair an existing vehicle for better service.  Alex is a new member of GDMPC. In the future, he hopes to finish the studies of his children and to gain double income from his business.

name: Isidro
description: Isidro is from the city of Santaní.  He's married with children and has his own house.  He and his wife fight hard for their family and children: he sells vegetables and his wife raises farmyard animals.    Isidro is a very honest, reliable, and hardworking man.  He started out working as a vendor in a produce shop.  He worked for four years and then left to work on his  own.  He started selling his products from his motor bike and now delivers them by three-wheeled van.  He has a well-established clientele that always buy their products from him.    Isidro is seeking a loan to buy more vegetables to meet his clients' needs.

name: Lita
description: 51-year-old Lita is married and she has five grown up children, but she currently only lives with two of them in her own house. Lita makes a living by hiring out her Moto taxi, but she also makes a living by selling shoes and articles of clothing. She has been hiring out her vehicle for about eight years and during this time she has learnt many things which she uses to improve every day. She works by herself and she feels very comfortable doing so since it allows her to have time with her children and she doesn’t have to neglect the household chores. It is going very well since she has very good earnings. This is her first loan with Kiva and she feels grateful for the financial support she is receiving in order to get ahead. She also promises to make her repayments on time. With the requested amount of 3000 PEN she will maintain her vehicle and buy spare parts.

name: Aigerim
description: Aigerim is a first-year student at the American University of Central Asia, department of Liberal Arts and Sciences. Here is her story.  “My name is Aigerim. I am from Bishkek, Kazakhstan. I graduated from high-school this year and enrolled the American University of Central Asia.  Since I have been at elementary school I have tried to participate in all social events within the school and out of it. In 9th grade I became a volunteer at the Tourist Information Center. I got a huge experience in working with foreigners. I have also participated in the contest 'Stolypin reforms' on behalf of the school, which was organized by the Kyrgyz-Russian Slavic University. I won second place and was awarded an encyclopedia. In the same year I represented our school in the district Olympiad of English language and won 3rd place. At another event, conducted by the International University of Kyrgyzstan, our team took second place. The competition was on developing a business plan. I was awarded a certificate for making presentations at the 'Science nourish young' festival, dedicated to the 300th Anniversary of the university.   I am happy to enroll in AUCA, but unfortunately my family is not able to cover the tuition fees fully. I hope to get a Kiva loan, so that I can concentrate on my studies rather than thinking about finance.”

name: Yefferson Alexis
description: Yefferson has always been an entrepreneurial person and has started several businesses in order to find economic sustainability. He is venturing into the barbershop business which has generated income for his sustainment.  He expects his business to grow much more in the future to be able to have his own place and position himself securely in the market.  The loan will be used to acquire two barber chairs to expand his work and be able to create 2 jobs.  If you want to know more about the entrepreneurs and the loans from Interactuar, you can join the Lending Team called: “Friends of Interactuar Colombia”: http://www.kiva.org/team/interactuar_colombia

name: Abdelwahab
description: Abdelwahab is a 30-year-old married man from Rafah city. He lives with his wife in a humble house in the city. Abdelwahab is an employee at a local company, where he gets a very low wage that barely covers his family's monthly expenses. He also has a mini market in the city where he sells consumption products. Abdelwahab would like to improve his business.  Abdelwahab took a USD Murabaha loan from FATEN. This loan will help him to buy a small refrigerator for his ice cream. This will improve his business and increase his income.  Abdelwahab is shown in his Kiva profile picture.

name: Peace
description: Peace, 41 years old, is widowed and has six children and two dependents who are orphans. Peace is an agriculturalist who majors in banana, millet and sorghum farming. She also operates a maize milling machine in her region to help support her family financially.Peace has managed to pay school fees for her children and to renovate the house which was left to her by her husband. Peace’s major challenge is paying school fees for her seven school-going children, given that she has just lost her husband, which has left her with the worry of how to look after her children.Peace is applying for a loan of UGX 1,500,000 to buy organic fertilizers for her banana and millet plantations. Her dream is to see all her children attend school and graduate with degrees. Peace is honest and hardworking.

name: Tsevelmaa
description: Mrs. Tsevelmaa is a 47-year-old widow who lives with her 5 children in a ger in the Bayanhongor province of Mongolia. Her daughters, Uranchimeg, age 25, Shirenchimeg, age 24, and Odonchimeg, age 22, work in various fields for a living. Her sons, Amarjargal, age 9, is a primary school student and Bilguuntogoldor, age 2, goes to a local kindergarten. The borrower has been heading the family since her husband passed away; she has been running her butcher shop since 2006. Now she is starting a welding service at home by order and the butcher shop will be run by her older daughter. She is now requesting 2,000,000 MNT to purchase large amounts of meat products from herders and sell it to local customers at her daughter's counter. She is a hardworking, strong, and diligent woman.

name: María De Los Ángeles
description: María de los Ángeles S., 41, lives in Santa Tecla with her husband and four minor daughters who go to school.  María has had a bakery for seven years.  She sells the bread in her house.  The earnings from the bread S. were not enough to pay for the household expenses and their four daughters’ expenses.  That is why a year ago she and her husband, who works with her, decided to sell basic needs items at the same time that they sell the bread.  María de los Angeles is asking for a loan to be able to buy beans, rice, and sugar among other products for her store.  She will also be able to buy flour and wood for making bread. Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer
town: Santa Tecla, departamento de La Libertad

name: Maritza
description: Maritza is a member of "La Flor de Canela 2" Communal Bank.  She lives at Urbanizacion Munizipal Mz. A1 Lt. 14. She is 38 years old and has 4 children.  She, along with her husband, began selling fish and with her first loan of 300 soles invested in the establishement of her store to sell fish.  With this loan of 1500 soles she bought a boat so that she and her husband can go fishing thereby incrasing their family's income.  She is grateful for the opportunity that working with Manuela Ramos has given her to get ahead and better herself. Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Enid
description: Enid is 20 years old and lives in the town of Kasese in the Fortportal region of Uganda. For the past 2 years, Enid has been working hard to manage her fresh food business, where she sells sells fresh food like matooke, beans, and tomatoes.  To help expand her business, Enid has requested a loan of 300,000 UGX from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy fresh food like matooke, beans, and tomatoes to sell, and will help Enid to generate greater profits and boost the business and increase their income. Enid hopes that in the future she will be able to be more productive.   Enid is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities and a forum for life-skills training.

name: Rokia
description: Mrs. Rokia, age 40, is married and the mother of five children. She lives in a polygamous family in Kokode, a neighborhood in Koutiala Prefecture, in Sikasso Region.  For more than ten years, her business has been based on buying and selling lengths of Wax "pagnes" (colorful African cloth), bazin cloth, and fabrics.  This business generates sufficient income, and her reputation is good since she has a large number of customers. To satisfy her clientele and expand her business, she's getting help from Kiva's partner, the MFI Soro Yiriwaso, from which she is seeking her fifth loan.  This loan will be used to buy lengths of Wax pagnes and rolls of bazin fabric. She gets her supplies in Koutiala and resell at her home and in various weekly village fairs, to a female clientele.  Thanks to her increase in business, she intends to turn an average monthly profit of XOF 30'000 (ca US$ 60), that she will use to repay the loan and provide for herself. The remainder will be invested in her business.

name: Teresa
description: Teresa is married with three children. Teresa is a responsible mother who is engaged in her recycling business. She earns about 3,000 Philippine pesos (PHP) monthly from it. Her business comes primarily from buying and selling recycled materials.  As of now, Teresa is asking for a loan amounting to 12,000 PHP to buy more recycled materials, cans, metal, and empty bottles to resell in the village. She is hoping that through her business, she will be able to improve her family's living conditions and financial stability.

name: Fegauiai
description: Fegauiai E., 40, is married with six children. She has one year of experience in the pancake business. She sells to the general public three days per week.   She has had one previous loan with SPBD, a Kiva partner. She expects her weekly net cash flow to be 250 Tala (about $104). SPBD loans are Fegauiai’s only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with the traditional banks.

name: Rosita
description: As a parent of one child, Rosita works hard to support her family.  She has a fishing business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from buying and selling dried fish. Rosita is borrowing 10,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) through NWTF to buy fishing materials for her fishing business.  She successfully paid back her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her fishing business.  Rosita has been sustaining her business activities through her past 13 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: Margarita
description: This member belongs to the “Kantu de San Jerónimo” communal bank.  She lives in the province and department of Cusco.  The member is Margarita.  She is 43 years old and is a native to San Jerónimo.  She has a live-in partner and has 4 children.  She is native to Quincemil in the fringes of the jungle on Peruvian territory.  Her partner is a bricklayer and she works making clothing for women, men, and children.  She arranged a small space in her house and she works there making all types of clothing fit to the size and taste of the customer.  She is requesting the loan to be able to purchase fabrics, sewing thread and other items.  Margarita values and is infinitely grateful for the loan provided since it allows her to grow with her business and improve her quality of life.  Likewise, she promises to make her loan payments according to the stipulated time frame.Translated from Spanish by Kathleen O'Connell, Kiva Volunteer

name: Lilia
description: Lilia is 58 years old and married with five children. Lilia works very hard to provide for them.  Lilia runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 30000 loan through NWTF, to buy inventory for her general store, items like beverages, canned goods, rice, home care products and other groceries.  Lilia has been in this business for 30 years.  Lilia would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Teopista Namaganda ‘S Group
description: Teopista is the leader of a group of 4 women.  She is 47 years old, and is widowed with five children, aged between 18 and 26 years. All her children go to school. She rents a one-roomed house where she lives with seven people. Teopista takes care of additional family members. There is electricity but no piped water at her home. The family gets three meals a day. She lives and works in a semi-urban area, which is on the outskirts of Kampala. Teopista has a poultry farm of about 300 laying birds in Kisaasi, one of Kampala's suburbs She sells to an average of 10 people a day and sells to all categories of people.  She works six days a week. Teopista buys her chicks from UGACHICK Poultry Breeders in Uganda and uses public transport to and from shopping. Her major monthly expenses include medication for both her family and her birds, She has been in this business for the last fifteen years.  Before her poultry business, she sold firewood at her home. Her main challenge is the rainy season which stops her customers from coming to her. Teopista has been with MCDT for over six years and is using her twelfth loan, working all this time with the same group mates. She wants to use this loan to buy more chicks and chicken feed. Teopista aspires to see her business grow and to own about 1000 birds  .	 	        .

name: Madukani Grp Musoma Group
description: Zainabu, who is in her mid 40s, is a married woman and the hardworking mother of three school-going children, some of whom are in primary school. She has been in the food vending business for about 15 years. She normally works at her own food stall that sells and serves food to her customers from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m., and she's making some great monthly profit.  This will be her second loan from Tujijenge Tanzania. She used her previous loan as capital for expanding her business. She bought new working materials and a brand new water tank. Zainabu is now happy that her business is going so well, and she has managed to pay back all of her previous loans, supported her husband to pay school fees for the kids, provided food for her family, and reinvested the remaining profit back into her business.  She applied for this loan to restock her food stall with more sacks of rice, beans, and sugar; a 20-liter Jerry can of cooking oil; and other ingredients for making spicy liquid rice and chapatti. She believes that with such additions, her income will increase and she will be able to grow much further as she dreams of having a restaurant in the near future, once her profit grows.  Zainabu really appreciates Kiva for all the good support given to her business and her loan group members of Madukani Grp Musoma Group as they will be accountable for paying back the entire loan amount at maturity.

name: Bujubuli Abeteraine Development Association Group
description: Elizabeth, a 60-year-old married mother of four living in Kyenjojo, Uganda, is a member of a village bank whose members guarantee each other's loan repayments. Elizabeth has been growing and selling bananas for many years, and  she earns additional income weaving and selling baskets, a business she started to diversify her income.  Elizabeth is faced with the problem of inadequate capital to expand her banana plantation into a large farm to serve the surrounding urban population. She is therefore requesting a loan to expand her banana acreage.

name: Musa S.
description: This is 32 year-old Musa. He is single, and has no children. He has one additional dependent, his fiance, who does not stay with him.  In 2007, Musa established his satellite cinema sport and games business. He began his business because he was watching games from other people's cinemas, then began his own.  He raised the initial capital and he started showing games. Working 4 days a week and 4 hours a day, he earns about Le 1,932,400 every month from this business. He would like a loan in the amount of Le 3,000,000.  Musa requires a loan in order to buy a smart card and a dish decoder full set.  He hopes that this loan will enable him to increase his monthly profits by approximately Le 386,480.  In the future, Musa plans to complete his university course and to get married, and also to increase his profit margin. Weather often disturbs satellite transmission but they can overcome after the rains.  He thanks you for your support.

name: Isabel
description: Isabel works as a field operator for a civil organisation.  She has three children who all attend primary school.  She has recently learned of a new initiative offered by the field partner, Hekima.  This offers the opportunity to pay school fees in advance.  So, she will use her loan to pay for the school fees of her children for the complete year 2013-2014.  This will ensure that they do not miss any schooling during the year.  Isabel dreams of a better future for her children and would like them to become computer technicians, doctors, business managers, university professors, reverends or politicians.  Isabel is very grateful for this special initiative, offered by Hekima, which will have a big social impact.  She believes it is particularly important during the time of reconstruction in the east of the country

name: Elisa
description: Elisa is a farmer from the town of Lintugop, Aurora, Zamboanga Del Sur. She is 55 years old, married with five children. She has been in Nipa business making for ten years. This is the main source of her income. Elisa is requesting a loan to buy additional materials for nipa making. With this loan, she will be able to improve the productivity of her business and thus she can provide the needs of their family. In the future, Elisa hopes to make her nipa business more sustainable.

name: Christine
description: Christine is 47 years old and married with five children.Christine works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 25,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy additional stocks of groceries to sell.Christine has borrowed and repaid eight loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 10 years and also earns an income from clothing retail.Christine aspires to save enough money to expand her business and continue to send her children to school.

name: Rogert
description: Rogert is a client of Asociación Arariwa. He is part of a communal bank consisting of 19 members in Anta. The group is called Virgen Inmaculada Concepcion. He is from Anta and lives in Cusco. He is 51 years old and is married with three children.  Rogert has been working as a metal mechanic in a compressor factory for 20 years. He owns 5 machines that are utilized in the mining industry, and he will use the loan to maintain them.  Rogert appreciates and thanks you for the loan and promises to pay the monthly payments on time.

name: Eva
description: Eva is a single woman. She has one child. She describes herself as polite. She operates a retail business where she sells clothes. She has been involved in this business for 10 years. Her primary customers are locals. She describes her biggest business challenge to be inadequate working capital. Eva will use the 20,000 KES loan to buy more stock of clothes. This is her first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: Benkan Group
description: The Benkan group is comprised primarily of polygamous women. On average, they are 31 years old and have two children. They all live in Minkoungo, an area of Bamako. They know one another through neighbors.   The group members sell clothing, utensils, and cosmetic products. With the goal of growing their business, they decided to collaborate with Soro Yiriwaso. This is their second group loan.   Madame Bintou, first on the left from left to right, is well known for her sheet and curtain sales. She will use her loan to buy 10 sheets and 10 curtains for wholesale prices in the Bamako market. She will resell these for retail prices in the Minkoungo market to a clientele comprised mainly of women.   With this loan, Madame Bintou hopes to earn an average monthly profit of 65,000 FCFA that she'll use to reinvest in her business. Like the other group members, she would like to strengthen her business through her relationship with Soro Yiriwaso.

name: Mercedes
description: Mercedes is a 37 year old man who completed up to the 2nd grade, but then because of a lack of motivation or demand from his parents he did not continue going to school. His father used to tell him that none of the school students eat. Accompanying Mercedes, his spouse dedicates herself to housework and also takes charge of raising the children. They have two children, the oldest is 5 years old and goes to kindergarten; the daughter still does not attend school because she is only 2 years old.  Mercedes earns a living through farming, and already has spent more than 20 years working in agriculture. His father, through lessons, made him what he is today, good person for society, taught him how to work and be a responsible man, and this has helped him in his life.    Mercedes has been a responsible man and he has raised his 2 children responsibly. His work is located about 2 kilometers away, a journey he makes on foot. No one is more dedicated to the work, his work schedule is from 6:00 am to 10:00 am.   The loan will be invested in the buying of agricultural components, among them fertilizer, weed-killer, and paying for the labor of those who help him complete his work.    He desires first to have what is most necessary for his family, that his children study and prepare. What he hopes is to work always while God blesses him with health and life. The loan will help him satisfy the need to be able to complete his work, with which he provides sustainability for his family.

name: Erika Marcela
description: Erika is a humble worker who lives in the municipality of Bello. Her life is full to overflowing with dreams, hopes and best wishes for her family. She is the mother of two children, and has always acted with courage and responsibility to provide them with the best life.She now earns a living making and selling corn-based foods such as arepas and empanadas, which she sells from her house. She works at her business for four hours every day.Among the main difficulties that she has to confront in her work, the most significant is the high cost of raw material. She is requesting a loan to buy raw material such as corn wholesale, in order to have good production in this season at the end of the year. In this way she will be able to earn enough income to continue with her business and support her family.

name: Marieta
description: Marieta is a hardworking entrepreneur who has operated a videoke (similar to karaoke) machine rental business in the Philippines for 20 years. She earns additional income from a general store.   Marieta is borrowing PHP 23,000 through NWTF to purchase spare parts for the maintenance of her videoke machine. She has successfully repaid her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her business. Marieta has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams of saving money to expand her business in the future.

name: Randy
description: Randy M. is from the village of Agunod Plaridel Misamis Occidental. He is 38 years old and married with three school-aged children. To make a living, he owns a store selling daily use products such as biscuits, candies, shampoo, soap and toothpaste. Randy has been engaged in his business for over five years and earns approximately 6000 PHP a month.  In 2010, Randy joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and ability to engage in business activities. He is requesting a loan of 10000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Randy from GDMPC. He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the family's income.   About GDMPC: GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three units offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Felix
description: Felix is 50 years old and he is married to Herlinda, 50 years old. As a fruit of their love they have 2 children, both of whom attend school. They work together in their own house. Felix is a very hardworking and active man. He is dedicated to the cultivation of cocoa and coffee. Every morning he starts his day very early to set out to his farm land. He has been working for 30 years and he is an expert of the arduous work that he carries out. During the harvest season Felix hires farm hands to help him complete the task. What he work enjoys about his work is planting seeds together with his family. They give him the strength and desire to move forward. He considers the most difficult part of his work to be battling against insect plagues that damage the cultivation. But despite that, he still plans on expanding his cocoa and coffee plantation. This is the most profitable way for him to be able to cover his children's schooling expenses. This is his seventh loan with MFP (Kiva Field Partner). He knows that his influx will be of great help in the progress of his business. He participates in every meeting held by his communal bank. With the 2,500 nuevos soles which he requests he will be able to sow more cocoa and coffee. He will need to buy seed and to hire farm hands.

name: Matildah Nambalirwa's Group
description: Matildah is 33 and married with four children between the ages of 8 and 16.  All her children go to school. She resides in and owns a three-roomed house, where she is staying with six people. Matildah takes care of additional family members. The family has access to electricity and piped water.   Matildah sells charcoal in Namungoona. She works in the outskirts of Kampala. She has been in this business for six years and also with MCDT for six years, servicing her 12th loan. She doesn’t pay rent for her business premises because she works from her home. Matildah sells to all categories of people, both retail and wholesale. She buys her charcoal from the Owino market, one of the busiest markets in Uganda, and so she incurs transport costs to and from her source. Her challenges include transportation and the rainy season as she works from an open place.   Matildah wants to use this loan to buy more sacks of charcoal. She aspires to see her business grow stronger and to start selling only on a wholesale basis.

name: Mwangaza Group
description: Nancy is a member of Mwangaza Group in Teso District. She is pictured with 16 One Acre Fund farmers, 9 women and 7 men. Nancy is standing on the right with her hand raised. She is receiving an input loan for ½ acre of Sweet Potato, millet, and sorghum cultivation. Nancy is a new One Acre Fund farmer and is excited for the 2013 Long Rains season. She joined One Acre Fund in order to grow enough food for the family and use increased profits to send her children to school.  Nancy described her harvest last year as good, but hopes she can have an even better one as a One Acre Fund farmer. She plans to use the money that she earns from her next harvest to send her children to school and save for the future. For the 2013 Long Rains season, Nancy’s group members will take input loans of ½ acre each. In total, this group will receive input loans for use on 8 acres of land.

name: Marohat
description: Marohat is 32 years old. She is married and is the mother of a two-year old. Her husband, a farmer by profession, does not completely cover all household expenses. To address this situation, she started selling meat products such as: sausages, frankfurters and chicken. She was successful in saving a little money and invested it in expanding her business. She has a lot of experience after 5 years in this kind of business. Warmly accommodating and innately moral, Marohat is requesting a loan of $800 USD to buy more chicken and sausage to meet customer demands. The success of this project will help her family to fully thrive where health, nourishment, schooling, and clothing are concerned.    More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is perhaps best known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road; the end of Alexander the Great's rule; and for it’s famous great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets as: Rudaki, Ibn Sina (Avicenna), Firdousi, Omar Haiyam, Jomi, Mavlavi Rumi and many others. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC.  And, even today, it is a complex mixture of Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But, Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics.  A civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy.  In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable.
