These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia.  While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.   IMON's History Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Emmy
description: Fifteen years ago, Emmy started farming on a small inherited piece of land in Mogogosiek, a remote village in the Litein area of Kenya. Today, this humble mother sells milk, eggs, maize and a variety of food crops. She is a passionate farmer and, because of the immense knowledge she has of farming, she commands a lot of respect from other farmers in her village.   Dairy farming is close to her heart; every day she wakes up to milk her cow and that makes her very proud. Although she makes profits through milk selling, she lacks a proper dairy unit and she is seeking a loan to build a modern dairy unit. Through the loan she will have a better time milking her cow and also feeding.   A modern dairy unit provides a good place where cows can relax and also prevents them from diseases that may arise because of being exposed to harsh weather conditions such as rain. Emmy believes that through this loan her living conditions will change because she is going to have an increase in milk production. She will save money that she used to spend on treating her cows because she lacked a good dairy unit. Emmy waits for your kindness.

name: Jane
description: Jane is a married woman with 4 children. She describes herself to be patient. She operates a retail business where she sells vegetables. She has been involved in this business for 10 years. Her business is located in a good area and her primary customers are locals. She describes her biggest business challenge to be inadequate working capital. She will use the Kes 20,000 loan to buy more stock of vegetables. She hopes that in the future, she will have improved living standards.

name: Rabia's Group
description: Rabia is a 48-year-old, hard-working housewife with three sons and three daughters and is a resident of Rawalpindi, Pakistan. For the past five years, her husband has been driving a van, which is the only source of income for his family.  Rabia is a member of three-person lending group that has requested a loan from Kiva partner BRAC Pakistan to expand her husband's transportation business by buying a new van. This will not only help expand their transportation business but will also help increase their monthly income. She is very hopeful that the loan will be productive so that they can meet the basic necessities of their family and provide education to their children.

name: Tessie
description: Tessie C. feeds and bathes her pigs every day. She has a sow that produces an average of twelve piglets and she sells the young pigs for Php 1,900 each. She said that working in the barn is very hard work, but it’s a feasible business because people buy meat all the time.  Tessie needs a loan of Php 8,000 to support her piggery. She will use the loan to buy feed and also piglets for fattening.  Tessie has three children, and she dreams of having a very successful business to support their needs.

name: Saba'a
description: Saba'a is a conservative person who prefers not to have her photo published online, so her husband appears in her Kiva profile photo. Saba'a is a 32-year-old, married woman, who has four sons and two daughters. She lives with her husband and children in Tulkarm city, in a simple house.  The husband of Saba'a has been working as a taxi driver for ten years, and this is the only source of income for the family. This income can barely cover the family's needs. Saba'a took a USD loan, to help her husband cover the costs of insuring and licensing the taxi. This will help the family meet some of the current expenses they face.

name: Reina Margarita
description: Reina Margarita H. A. lives in the Apopa municipality in the San Salvador department.  Reina lives in her own house with her husband.  Reina always had the dream of setting up her own business.  After many years of savings and loans, she established her bakery.  She has five years of experience, and she makes a variety of sweet breads and the best quesadilla in Apopa.  She has quite a lot of customers because of the quality that only Reina’s bread has.  She is now asking for a loan to buy raw materials.  This will allow her to increase her production of sweet breads and to continue strengthening her bakery.   Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Elie
description: Elie is a 54-year-old man who lives in Tripoli, northern Lebanon. Elie has been working in the sewing business for nine years. Elie has requested a loan of 1000 US dollars from Al Majmoua in order to purchase thread and a new machine for his sewing.   Elie has been a microcredit client for four years now and has always paid on time. His previous loans helped him improve his business and increase his income. His clients are people from his region. When he first started, he had difficulty building networking. Elie decided on doing his business because he likes sewing and wanted to improve his income. In the future, he plans on expanding his business.

name: Asia
description: Asia is 41 and lives with her husband and children in Lahore, Pakistan. Her husband earns a living by making seat covers for vehicles. He has a shop in a vehicle workshop market and works quickly to provide his customers with the covers they need. He began by making seats for motorcycles only but now would like to provide seats for cars as well. This is why he wants to buy various colors and types of leather fabric which he can display to his customers. Asia has requested a loan from Kiva’s field partner BRAC Pakistan so that her husband can buy the fabrics he needs. Asia thanks Kiva and its field partner BRAC Pakistan for their support

name: Margaret
description: Margaret is a single woman. She has one child. She operates a farm where she grows onions, cabbages and carrots. She has been involved in this business for four years. Her business is located in a good area and her primary customers are locals. She will use the Kes. 10,000 loan to buy seeds and fertilizer.

name: Juliana
description: Juliana is a member of the Gregoria Apaza Communal Bank in the Pusuyo community center in the Ilave district, Collao province, Puno department.  She is a 45 year old widow with four children.  She lives in the Pusuyo community.  She did not have the opportunity to get an education.  She has been working with the Movimiento Manuela Ramos for almost four years.  She started with a loan for 300 PEN, which allowed her to increase capital in her business of buying and selling poultry.  She currently needs a new loan for 700 PEN, which will allow her to buy sheep and poultry.  She gets them in Ilave and neighboring communities.  She sells them in regional fairs.  Her biggest desire is to continue working.  She likes the savings and the meetings.   Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Nanga Frida
description: Nanga Frida is married and a mother of eight children. She has always been a hard working  woman with little or no fruits of her labour. This is because she could not lay her hands on a profitable business and even when she did, could not make profit because she lacked capital to invest. Because of this, her children were always suffered from not having school fees and hunger. With these challenges, she sought help from GHAPE in 1998. Since then she has been able to obtain loans with which she sold motor spare parts and raised enough money to pay an apprentice and school fees for her children. Given a loan of $1200, she plans to buy and  sell spare motor parts in the capital city of the country where more people own cars. Her son has built a house for the business so that a building will not have to be rented and she will use his experience to help manage it. She plans to pay her loan in 24 months. The first installment repayment shall be on the fourth month from the date of disbursement.

name: Danaya Group
description: The four women, who are members of Danaya Group, are all married. On average, they are 34 years old and have five children. They live mostly in nuclear families in the neighborhood of Fana Coura in the sub-prefecture of Fana, prefecture of Dioila, in the second administrative region of the Republic of Mali. The group members are neighbors, family members or members of the same business association. They make a living by buying and selling various articles, mostly food condiments and clothes.  After having repaid their previous ten loans on schedule, the women of Danaya Group are now applying for their eleventh group loan, which they will use to buy various food condiments and suits of all kinds and for all age groups. They get most of their supplies from local producers and wholesalers. They sell their products cash, either hawking or at the market, to a clientele made up of women and men.  They expect to make an average monthly profit of 50,000 CFA francs, which they will partly spend on school fees, food and healthcare, and partly reinvest into their businesses. Translated from French by Robert Mouris, Kiva Volunteer

name: Fatuma
description: Fatuma is a married  woman and she is blessed with one child who attends school. They live at their own house that has electricity but no piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is school fees.  Fatuma has operated a tailoring business, making women’s and gents suits for sale at home. She cites seasonality and stiff competition from other tailoring operators to be her major challenges.   With the Kshs 30,000, she wants to purchase cloth materials and sewing tread for her business.   She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Ingrid
description: Ingrid  and her husband Emilio are longtime clients of Emprender. Ingrid sells food in the area of Villa Copacabana and Mr. Emilio is an owner of a small workshop where he repairs electronic equipment in the area of Bajo San Antonio. The whole time they have worked with our institution they have always shown themselves to be punctual and responsible with their loans. Ingrid sells Bolivian traditional food such as fricasee and pork chicharones, as well as beef Milanese and chicken Sajta. She only works in her restaurant on weekends, but even so, she has a lot of customers  who come to eat every weekend without fail. Emilio has his workshop in his parents' house and with his experience and good service, he always has a lot of customers. At this time, they are asking for the loan to buy a bedroom set for their apartment. In this way they will be comfortable and improve their quality of life.

name: Maria Consuelo
description: María Consuelo, a member of the Santa Ana Communal Bank, lives in the San Martín region, in the province and district of Moyabamba.  She works selling groceries in general as well as fruit, and her business is located in her home.  With this loan of 800 soles ($275), which she will repay over 6 months, she will buy essential products such as rice, sacks of sugar, detergents of various brands, preserves, boxes of milk, personal hygiene products, and other products that she needs to stock her business and satisfy the needs of her customers.  María Consuelo is 35 years old and is the mother of four children who are dependent on her.  She is grateful to have this assistance because it will allow her to grow her business.  Her goal is to better stock her business and fix her home to give her business better security. Translated from Spanish by Laura Westin, Kiva Volunteer

name: Aba
description: Aba sells maize and cassava at Asafora near Cape Coast, which she has done for 3 years now. Aba is married and has 3 children. She uses her income to support her husband in feeding her family and paying for their children’s school fees. Aba will use her loan to purchase bags of maize and cassava to sell. With the new profit from her expanded business, Aba wants to personally cultivate the maize and cassava that she sells.

name: Amor
description: Amor, age 40, is a married woman with four children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Amor has three children who attend school.Amor has a buy and sell personal product care business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 12000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like lotion, perfumes, etc..Amor has been in this business for three years. In the future, Amor would like to save enough money to send her children to college.

name: Girishaka Group
description: Berchmans lives in Bujumbura and is a member of the Girishaka group. He is 25 years old and single. He takes care of his three younger brothers who are students.  He has been selling "Primus" beer for three years now.  He is on his second loan from Turame. With the Kiva loan that he receives, he is going increase his capital so that he can buy lots of cases of "Primus" beer to resell and earn more money.  In the coming years, he would like to buy his own plot of land.

name: Nohemy Yolanda
description: Our member, Sra. Nohemy Yolanda, 62, belongs to the SENOR DE MURUHUAY community bank in the Peruvian "departamento" of Cusco.  Sra. Nohemy, 62, is married and has 8 children.  She operates a taxi business.  She has a car in which she carries tourists to places of interest in and around Cusco.  She would like to set up a business selling spare parts.  She is applying for this loan to make a car payment.  Sra. Nohemy is grateful to everyone who has made her dream come true by this means and is committed to repaying the loan in the agreed-upon time.

name: Juana Nereyda
description: Juana Nereyda has been working as an elementary school teacher for the past 11 years in the Unión neighborhood.  According to references from neighbors, who are also colleagues at work, Nereyda is a hard-working woman with a strong spirit of personal and professional improvement.  She loves her work as a teacher since she shares the bread of learning with rural children from her community.  She is asking for a loan in order to invest in a small repair to her kitchen, since it is currently in a bad state and with the climate it is deteriorating even more.  Her greatest dream is to finish a room with better conditions so that her sweet family can remain united and enjoy good health.

name: Olga Zulema
description: Señora Olga Zulema has been working selling shoes for the last five years.  She makes her sales from Monday through Sunday, and also has a relative who helps her by selling her shoes as a street vendor int Caridad Valle area.  Her customers are friends and people she knows who visit the Nacaome market.  She will invest the loan in the purchase of school footwear as the patriotic holidays are approaching.  She needs to invest so as to sell more, and take advantage of the opportunity to achieve more earnings and make up for bad days when she hasn't sold as much.  Her dream is that her family remains united always, and that her business grows so she can achieve better living conditions for herself and for her family.

name: Rem's Group
description: Rem is 52 years old, married, and a mother of four children living in a village of the Thmor Koul district. She still has one child who relies on her. The source of her family's income is mainly from rice farming on four hectares. She has been in this business for ten years. Her main business challenge is lack of working capital to increase crop yield. Rem has been with VisionFund, Kiva's partner, for seven loan cycles already. She paid back the previous loans, which enabled her to maintain positive conditions for her family. She is leading her group of two to get another loan from VisionFund. She and her co-borrower are seeking a loan amount of 1,400,000 KHR each. As the leader, Rem wants to use her portion to buy fertilizer and pay plowing fees for her farmland. With this loan, she hopes to make more income so as to set aside some money for her family needs.

name: Ramona Magdalena
description: The members of the “Damas Emprendedoras De Pachinche” (Enterprising Ladies of Pachinche) Communal Bank meet every two weeks at the place known as Pachinche, which is in the Colon parish in the city of Portoviejo.  It is known for its hard-working people who are devoted to agriculture and to raising livestock.  This is where we met Ramona, age 21.  She is in a common-law marriage, and she has a child who is three years and six months old.  He is the most beautiful thing in her life.  Her husband is a bus driver.    She has been in the communal bank for five cycles.  She likes it because she gets along very well with all of her colleagues in the group.  She lives with her family in a very small house.  She tells us that now that her son is a little bigger, it is a bit uncomfortable because they only have one room.  She needs to make improvements on her house.  She wants to build a room for her son and a kitchen.  That way her house will be more comfortable for the whole family.  She will use her loan to buy construction materials like sand, cement, gravel, and bricks, etc.  Her dream is to have a large, well-finished house.

name: Norlita
description: Norlita is 53 years old and married with eleven children. For the past five years, she has earned a living by fattening pigs in the Philippines. Norlita also earns additional income from a motorcycle transport business.  Norlita is requesting an 11,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy additional feed for her pigs. She is working tirelessly toward attaining her dream of saving enough money to afford to send her children to college.

name: Maria
description: Maria is a married woman with two children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Maria is 39 years old and has one child who is still in school.  Maria has a fish-vending business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 6,000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase additional fish to sell to her customers.  She has been in this business for eight years. In the future, Maria would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Jane
description: Jane is 40 years old and married. She has six children, ranging in age from 8 to 23, with five of them currently attending school.  Jane runs a mixed farm in western Kenya, near the town of Kitale, where she has been farming for over ten years. Milk sales to the Kenya Cooperative of Creameries supply Jane with most of her income, while she also sells other grocery supplies as well. Her current main business challenge is increasing competition in her area.  Jane requested this Kes 20,000 loan through Juhudi Kilimo to expand her poultry farming operations. She says that this loan will help maximize her profits, as increased capital will allow for expansion. In the future, she wants to maintain her poultry project and have a continued lucrative business.

name: Alicia
description: Alicia, 51 years old, is married and a resident of Lobogon, Aloran, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. Her husband is a fisherman. The fish he catches are sold at the public market or to their neighbors. They have been in this business for many years already.  Because she wants to be more productive, she has now decided to enter into business herself, purchasing fish in bulk for resale at the market. In 2008, both Alicia and her husband agreed to join Paglaum MPC to avail themselves of a loan because they wanted to buy fishing nets. But aside from financial assistance they received, they say that they also enjoyed the add-on benefits like insurance and savings.  She has now applied for a loan of 14,900 PHP to buy fish for resale. She is wishing that with Paglaum’s help, and with the patience and diligence of her husband, she is looking forward to being a successful vendor someday and to owning a stall in the public market.

name: Rachelle
description: B. Rachelle was born around 1973 in Cotonou, the economic capital of Benin, but has been living for six years in the Dodji Dangban district in Allada, a city in Atlantique County.  Married to SONON Antoine, a mason, she is the mother of five children who are all in school.  She lives together with her husband and children.  The couple jointly ensure that family expenses are covered.    Rachelle never attended school.  To meet her needs, she sells plastic ware at the Sèkou market.  She has been in this business for six years and gets her supplies in Cotonou.    She has already had an ALIDé loan, which she has repaid.  She would like to raise her level of business in order to satisfy her customers more, but she lacks sufficient funds to do so.  This is why Rachelle is requesting a second loan from ALIDé. Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Matilde
description: Matilde is 61 years old and married with five children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur who has a rice retailing business in the Philippines.   She has requested a PHP 15,000 loan amount through NWTF in order to buy additional rice to sell.  Matilde has been in this business for 13 years. In the future, she would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Tiresa
description: Tiresa is a 37-year-old married woman with two children. She has a small plantation and grows taro, taamu, bananas and yams to earn a living. She has been doing this for two years. Tiresa has requested a loan to buy chemicals, weed sprayer, timber, nails, bush knives and an ax.  She has been a member of SPBD since 2013.  With her profits,Tiresa hopes to improve her business and support her family.

name: Conielyn
description: Conielyn, 32, is a married woman with four children. Two are in school. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur.   Conielyn has a tricycle transport business in the Philippines. Conielyn requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy spare parts and other equipment for her tricycle transport business.  Conielyn has been in this business for 12 years. In the future, Conielyn would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Erdenetogtoh
description: Erdenetogtoh is 44 years old and lives with her husband and a daughter in their apartment in Dundgovi province, Mongolia. Her husband, Enhbat, helps his wife to run their family business, selling clothing at the local market. Her daughter, TSerenchunt, is 20 years old and is a freshman in the university.   Erdenetogtoh has been running her clothing retail business at a rental counter of the local market since 1999. She has lot of regular customers. She is a hardworking, responsible and well-educated woman. She has good taste in the selection of her inventory and is well known among the clients with her good and friendly service. She is now requesting loan of 5,000,000 MNT to purchase clothing inventory from Erlian, China, to sell at her rental counter in order to increase her family income.

name: Inocencia
description: Inocencia is 43 years old and has been married for twenty years to Carlos, who is 47. They have five children, of whom two are school-age and three are adults who work independently.  Inocencia and her husband worked in Argentina for many years until they earned enough money to return to their country and achieve their dream of building their own home, and more than ten years ago they were able to set up a small grocery and butcher shop in that home. Inocencia currently operates the grocery while Carlos works as a driver for a company in order to help his wife with the household costs, in addition to paying for their children's university expenses.  Now she wants to buy more products, such as drinks and essential goods like flour, yerba, pasta, rice and others, which she would like to use to stock her business. That is why she is requesting this loan from Fundación Paraguaya and Kiva.

name: Pauline
description: Pauline is a 39-year-old business lady, married to Samuel who is also a businessman, and they are blessed with three children aged 18, 10 and 5 years respectively. She has been running a butchery for the past five years with a monthly income of KES 10,000 which she uses to support her family.   She is applying for her first loan term with KADET after being introduced by a KADET staff member. Pauline will use the loan to purchase a bull for slaughtering. With the anticipated profit from the business, she will educate her children.   She hopes to open a hotel business which will help her improve the living standard of her family.

name: Rodolfo
description: Rodolfo is a very hard-working and conscientious family man.  Thanks to his efforts to give his family a better life, and with the support of the loan, it was possible for him to remodel his house.  Now his children live in a room that is in better condition and worthy of them.However, Rodolfo also says that as the years pass his children are growing, as are their needs.  For this reason he is requesting a new loan to build a room for his children.  He will use the loan to buy construction materials like cement, cement blocks, sand, and gravel.  His biggest wish is to have the room ready before the end of the year.

name: Jenniffer
description: Jenniffer, born in 1982, is a smallholder farmer who has been doing mixed farming for the last ten years in Nandihills, Kenya. She sells produce from the farm, including milk and crops, at the local market. She also engages in other personal businesses to make enough money to provide for her family. Jenniffer spends a lot of time tending to her animals and land. Spraying is the activity she finds to be the most enjoyable. Jenniffer complains that working on the land is becoming more strenuous with age. One factor contributing to the strain is the type of tools she utilizes. Jenniffer is seeking a loan from Kiva lenders to purchase farm equipment. Smallholder farmers usually use indigenous tools because they are economical, feasible and sustainable. Despite being common, they are generally not preferred to modern tools since they are inefficient and tiring to use. With your funding, Jenniffer will be able to afford modern tools that are properly designed to be more comfortable to use and meet farmers' requirements. These tools will make Jenniffer’s work easier and more efficient. This will boost her productivity and income. Money from this investment will go towards her family's basic expenses.Lend to Jenniffer and empower her family!

name: Sok's Group
description: Sok is the leader of this group of borrowers. She supports her family by working as a farmer.  The members of Sok’s Group live in a rural village in the province of Battambang. In their village, there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. They are therefore requesting a loan in order to buy a water filter to provide safe drinking water for their families.  Having a water filter at home will help each of these borrowers to safeguard the health of their families, as well as to save money on medical expenses. They will also save time previously spent collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Shikeba Pari Gul Group
description: This is the Shikeba Pari Gul group, which is made up of four members. Each of them wants to take a loan of 14000 Afghani. Shikeba wants to take a loan for carpet weaving to buy good quality materials. Zakia wants to take a loan for his brother who has got a mobile shop. Parwin and Pari Gul want to take a loan for the tailoring business. All the members would like to be successful in their businesses and progress well. The total amount they have requested is 56000 Afgani. They admire this process so much and mention that Kiva is a really effective program.

name: Khursheed
description: Khursheed is a 45-year-old married woman. She and her husband have sold  milk for the past 10 years. She has attained a good number of customers and has become famous for providing good-quality milk. She makes enough money to contribute to her family's income.   She has gradually improved her business with the support of the Kashf Foundation. She is currently in her fourth loan cycle and has applied for 45,000 PKR to purchase another cow.   She is hopeful that this loan will be a productive one for her and will bring positive changes to her business.

name: Amitié 2 Group
description: Marie Florence, the group representative, is a married mother to four children who are all currently receiving an education. She has been selling bedsheets for over 10 years. Marie Florence and the other group members are very conscientious when it comes to spending their loan money. They invest savings within our institution and pay back their loans without any problems. With this loan, Marie Florence is planning to purchase bedsheets of varying qualities which will be resold to her customers. The profits will allow her to carry on her business.

name: Entusa
description: Entusa, age 60, is an unassuming and kindhearted woman.  She lives with her husband, Julio, and they have nine children.  Only her youngest child lives with her.  She lives in her own house in Chacas.  She and her husband work the fields, which took years of great effort to manage to get.  Her main products are corn, beans, barley, and peas.  They fertilize, water, and weed them from the early morning hours until the last ray of sunshine.  During each harvest, and with help from their children, they take the products to the city, where they sell them at a main market.  They also have pigs and sheep that they raise for their own consumption.  They also have two cows that produce milk that they consume.  That is how the keep up with their food needs.  Her greatest wish is to continue planting; she likes it a lot.  Therefore, she will get together more capital in order to continue planting in greater quantities.  She belongs to the Sumaq Sonqo communal bank, and this is their third loan with MFP.  She appreciates the opportunity they have given her because she will be able to improve her business.  She pledges to be punctual with her payments.  She likes working with her communal bank where everyone is responsible and supportive.  She will use the requested money to buy natural fertilizers to spread among her corn plants.

name: Gilberto De Jesús
description: Gilbert is a tireless fighter who never gives up. As the economic situation was getting worse he decided to start his own business in the design and production of accessories like earrings, necklaces, rosaries, key chains and other items. He learned this work from his daughter and now the earnings support him.  Today, after being recognized in some schools in the center of Medellin, in the municipality of Antioquia, Gilbert dreams of having a warehouse to sell his products as he does now in the streets, with an armed car to transport his accessories.  Currently he is asking for a loan to buy supplies for the manufacturing and production of accessories, and also to buy a showcase where he can show them in a more organized and pleasing way, and in this way to increase the sales and increase his earnings.

name: Narek
description: Narek is young farmer who is 27 years old. With his wife and two children, he lives in Kirants, a frontier village in the Tavush region. Narek, with his wife, works at the municipality, and they are also farming. On his rich farm, Narek has cows, calves, heifers, pigs, lambs, chickens and bee hives. Narek very skillfully organizes the sale of his farm products such as meat, dairy products, eggs, honey, and also his garden’s harvest such as figs, persimmons and nuts. He sells all these products from his farm during the week. Being young, hardworking, and full of new ideas, Narek is asking for this loan in order to enlarge the number of his farm cattle; he plans to buy a cow, a bull, sheep, and fodder for all of his farm cattle.

name: Alina Emperatriz
description: Alina, age 25, established her beauty salon with a lot of work and long workdays.  She has a little three year old child.  She learned the hairdressing business thanks to attending a course that certified her to be able to work.  In spite of growing up in an area of post conflict and not having resources, she created opportunities herself.  With savings and some loans she has purchased items, and little by little she has established her beauty salon.Alina wants to request a loan to remodel her business, to paint, and to change around several things in order to have more space.  She will also buy a sofa so that her waiting customers are comfortable and happy.

name: Lucy
description: Lucy is a farmer from Pagadian City. She is 54 years old and married with children of school age. She availed various loans from Paglaum MPC to prepare for the next cropping season. She availed a loan of PHP 10,000 to purchase bags of fertilizers and pesticides.
town: Pagadian - Pagadian City, Zamboanga del Sur

name: Emelda
description: Emelda is 45 years old and married with five children, three of whom are in school.  She earns a living by farming rice in the Philippines. Emelda is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to buy fertilzers and other farm supplies.  Emelda has been farming rice for 5 years and also earns additional income from general store.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save money to expand her business.

name: Elsa
description: Elsa is a 31 year-old single mother who lives in a rented home along with her two daughters: Jackelin, 10, and Yasuri, 8, to whom she provides meticulous care and love.  She is a very hardworking woman who has a business selling vegetables in the market in her area.  She has been doing this work for 8 years, and for her this work is very easy.  She does not need a lot of help, and so she is able to do the work on her own, although she enjoys being with her daughters because they are her only happiness.  Elsa's work is very profitable, because she is always selling her produce and in this way she is able to pay for her household expenses as well as her daughter's school expenses.  She will invest this loan that she is requesting in her produce stand.  However, what she desires the most is to be given a snack bar in her daughter's school where she could sell candy as well as cold cuts, because then she could allocate her time between the two businesses and in this way manage to change her quality of life and provide her daughters with a good education.  This will be her 2nd loan with MFP, and she promises to make her payments on time.  Also, she is a responsible member of her communal bank.  With the 2,000 Peruvian soles she requests, she will buy produce such as: carrots, pumpkin, potatoes, sweet potatoes, celery and other products for her post in the market.  Also, she will buy cookies, candy, drinks and other items so that she can put them in her school snack bar.

name: Sonia
description: Sonia, age 46, is a hardworking and earnest woman.  In addition, she is friendly and cordial.  Sonia is separated from her partner, but she lives with her five-year-old daughter. Her nephew and his 11-year-old daughter also live with her in her home.  Sonia sells groceries and soft drinks from a store she opened in her home.  There she provides friendly and cordial service to her customers, most of whom are neighbors who have been doing business with her for more than four years.  Sonia’s daughter helps her in the business.  She is grateful to have a business in her home because she can look after the needs of her daughter and her household.  The amount she earns helps to cover the household expenses since the support from her ex-husband is not enough.  Sonia has achieved good results to date and she has plans to continue and expand her business.    This will be her third loan with the MFP organization.  Sonia hopes to receive assistance so that she can continue with her objectives.  In addition, she gets along with her Communal Bank and considers her group to be responsible and unified.  The amount of 2000 PEN that she requested will be invested in the purchase of more groceries and soft drinks at a wholesale price.  This will increase her profit margins and provide more inventory for her business.

name: Alicia
description: Alicia is 54 years old and married with four children.  She earns a living by having a pig fattening business in the Philippines. Alicia is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF to purchase feed and vitamins for her pigs.  Alicia has been in pig fattening for seven years and also earns additional income from food vending.  She is working tirelessly towards the attainment of her dream: to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Elvin
description: Elvin is 43 years old and lives with her wife and 4 kids. He is a humble farmer dedicated to produce citric fruits inside his community, the lands of cultivation are far away from his home, this is why he has to leave early in the morning and it takes time to go back home too. But when he sees the harvest of his land it comforts him and wants to harvest even more although in order to do that he needs to invest large amounts of money, because he knows that on a larger harvest, he will have better results, and the fruit has to be of better quality in order to get more income from the sales. Elvin bases his effort on the well being of his family, mostly his children. He wants to increase production, to pay for transportation expenses because he wants to take his products to the capital, Lima. Translated from Spanish by Nina Delgado, Kiva Volunteer

name: Fatoumata
description: Fatoumata K. is an internet café manager who has over five years of experience in this sector.  Using an IMCEC loan, she opened this service which now enables her to achieve sales figures of 20,000 francs CFA.  She lives with her husband and does well running her family.  The loan enabled her to repair computers and to increase her customer base. Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Azalsho
description: Azalsho is a kind-hearted, middle-aged man.  He is 58 years old.  He has three children and a caring wife.  He lives in the city and works in a school.  All the money he makes is spent to take care of his family and he is in no position to save any money for any other goal.  The family is getting ready to celebrate an important event and Azalsho needs to buy gifts for his grandchildren, children, for the bride and other relatives.  However, he doesn't have enough money and, for this reason, he has turned to MDO Arvand to receive a loan and hold the event.  He thanks MDO Arvand in advance for their support and their trust.

name: Gifty
description: Madam Gifty L. is a pineapple farmer in the Dangme West district in Ghana. She is very hardworking and can produce more pineapples if given assistance. She is seeking a loan of $1050.00 from Kiva to help her produce more. She also has knowledge about loan management and simple accounting from KSF. She is very capable of paying back the loan.

name: Reynaldo Jose
description: Reynaldo Jose sells a variety of products and he has been making articles of clothing for more than 14 years. He managed to succeed in this business with a great deal of effort. It is not the first time that he has accessed a loan. Reynaldo is a hardworking person and he enjoys making different products every day for sale and for personal use.  His clients request various products and he always makes sure to provide them with good service and with quality products.  He requests the loan to purchase fabrics, threads, scissors, and other items.

name: Merlette
description: Merlette is 42 years old and married. She has three children, two of whom are currently in school.  Merlette is in the agricultural business, pig fattening in the Philippines. Merlette has been in pig fattening for 10 years now, and she has borrowed four times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.   Merlette requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to buy feeds and other supplies to raise her pigs.  In the future, Merlette would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Mila
description: Mila is 40 years old and married with two children. She would like to start a small business, printing elei on puletasi, dresses and on t-shirts.   In order to do this, Mila needs a loan to buy fabrics, an elei board, paints and brushes for her business. She hopes to use her profits to extend her business.   She has been a member of SPBD since 2013.

name: Nulu
description: Nulu lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is married with six children and all her children are in school. She also takes care of additional family members. She operates a retail shop.   Nulu has been in this business for the last 22 years. She works seven days a week. She gets additional income from poultry farming. She has requested a loan of Ugandan shillings 1,300,000 from MCDT-SACCO to buy more bags of sugar, rice, cooking oil, beans, peas, flour and poultry feed. Her major business challenges are seasonality and transportation.   Nulu's goal and aspiration is to build more sheds for poultry farming. She lives in her own house and the family has access to electricity and piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses include school fees and feeding the family.

name: Sadia's Group
description: Sadia I. M. is the wife of I. M. and lives in the Walton area of Lahore City, Pakistan. She has been living in this area for the last seven years. She is the mother of a four-year-old daughter. Sadia baji's husband is a painter, and he paints offices, doors, windows, and walls. For the last four years he has also run a scrap business. Sadia baji is a housewife and prefers to do household work. She has successfully repaid four loans from Asasah (a microfinance institute of Pakistan). Now she is applying for a loan to buy more scrap parts (iron, wastepaper, and bottles) for her husband to resell.   She is joined in her loan group by a few more members. Niamatay M. Ashraf wants a loan to buy beams for her shuttering business. Rani S. M. wants a loan to buy a donkey cart. Bilquis N. P. M. wants a loan to buy an auto-rickshaw (a local three-wheeled motorized vehicle). Maryam W. M. wants a loan to buy electric supplies (tubes, switches and switch boards) for her electric shop.   This is a group loan. The loan funds will be distributed among the group members, each of whom will invest in her own business. The members mutually guarantee one another's loans. If one member does not repay, the other members are responsible.

name: Betsi
description: Betsi is a member of the Perla (Pearl) communal bank.  Betsi is married, 50 years old and has 4 children.  She sells typical meals in her home on Sundays.  In addition, Betsi makes cakes and desserts to order.  Betsi needs 1200 soles to buy flour, gelatin and sugar.  Betsi dreams that her children become professionals and succeed.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Cristita
description: As a married parent of 7 children, Cristita works hard to support her family. She has a food vending business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from buying and selling livestock.   Cristita is borrowing PHP 17,000 through NWTF to purchase additional ingredients for her business of food production and vending. She has been sustaining her business activities through her past 15 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Ufiata
description: Ufiata is a 45-year-old married mother of 10 children.  Ufiata has started a business venture, selling food products in the local community. Ufiata needs a loan of WST 1,000 to purchase new items to expand product offerings.  She plans to use the profit from her business (estimated to be 350 talas or US $146 per week) to improve/expand the business.  Ufiata joined SPBD to gain access to financial services.  Most of SPBD's clients are unable to borrow from commercial banks, because they lack collateral.  This is Ufiata's 1st loan with SPBD.    *SPBD evaluates the living conditions of each of its borrowers.  Generally, a loan manager evaluates a variety of social metrics on a scale out of 3 (the higher the number, the better off the person is) and these are averaged for the "overall social metric score."  For example, a 3 out of 3 on "level of education" would mean that the borrower has graduated from university.    About SPBD  In 2000, Greg Casagrande founded SPBD to improve the quality of life of people living in poverty in the poor island nations of the South Pacific.  SPBD's philosophy of lending is based on a respect for each individual's innate human ingenuity, drive and self esteem. Please join SPBD's lending team on KIVA to receive on-the-spot updates on SPBD.

name: Jiezel
description: Jiezel is 29 years old and has three children. She is married and all of her children are sent to school.  Jiezel is in the agricultural business, raising pigs in the Philippines. Jiezel requested a PHP 6,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy feeds and vitamins for her pigs.  Jiezel has been raising pigs for five years now, and has borrowed 4 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Jiezel would like to save enough money so she can expand her business.

name: Len
description: Len is 50 years old and is married. She has been running a cafe in front of her door for 10 years. She started this business to cover her expenses, and raise her child. They live in Ho Chi Minh City.  Len is requesting a loan to expand her business by offering more food and many kinds of soft drinks so that she will be able to increase the turnover in her business.   She hopes that through the loan she will be able to expand her business activities, and have money to reinvest to her business in the future.

name: Lusine
description: Lusine works very hard in her farming business where she has dedicated most of her life. She puts all of her efforts to expand and continue its further development. She lives with her husband and son. Due to fluctuating market prices, Lusine has financial difficulties and needs your help to overcome this situation. She needs a Kiva loan of $1,300 in order to purchase 1,200 kilograms of potato seeds and 10 packages of fertilizers. Please help Lusine obtain the loan. She will appreciate your help and support very much.

name: Ocha
description: Ocha is a kind woman. She was born in 1953 and is the caring mother of eight children. She works hard to earn a living and to offer good living conditions to her children. Ocha has been busy buying and selling sewing machines for more than 12 years. She sells sewing machines in a local market where she has a store. Ocha paid the wedding expenses of six of her children from the profits of her business.   Ocha’s elder son studies at the Medical University of Tajikistan. Ocha must pay for her son’s tuition at the university and with this aim she is asking for a loan of 1,050 USD. She awaits your mercy.

name: Samuel
description: Samuel C. is single and has one child. He has no educational background.  Samuel goes to the forest, cuts weak trees and branches of old trees and sells them as firewood at Abrodzirum near Shama-Kedzi, which he has been doing since 2007.  Samuel uses his income for payment of fees for the child and payment of utility bills.  Samuel will use the loan to pay for equipment to enable him to improve the efficiency of his work. With the new profits from his expanded business, Samuel plans to save to take care of his child’s education.

name: Eva
description: Eva is 35 years old and married with three children, two of whom are in school. She earns a living by raising pigs in the Philippines. Eva is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to buy additional feed and vitamins for her pigs.  Eva has been raising pigs for two years and  earns additional income from food vending. She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Annarose
description: Annarose S. is from the village of D'ban Calamba Mis. Occ. She is 26 years old. Annarose is married and has 3 school-aged children. To make a living, Annarose owns and operates a service-based business. The main source of income for the business comes primarily from providing repair services to local community members. Annarose has been engaged in her business for over 2 years and earns approximately 8000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2007, Annarose joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Annarose has successfully repaid a previous loan of 4000 PHP from GDMPC. Annarose is requesting a new loan of 6000 PHP which will be used to purchase materials needed to provide service. This loan will be the fourth loan taken out by Annarose from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand her business.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three units offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolk, and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Omon
description: Omon is a 48-year old man from the Nosiri Khusrav District. He is a vigorous and diligent farmer. He has been engaged in the agricultural business since childhood. He is proud of his work because he learned it from his father. Omon is happy that he makes a profit from his favorite activity.  Omon is taking care of his plants and he needs a loan to purchase mineral fertilizers. It will help him to receive a good harvest. So Omon hopes for your support.

name: Tam
description: Mrs. Tam is a hardworking woman who is 29 years old. There are five people in her family. She would like to improve her living standards. The loan can help her to build a sanitation latrine.  She is able to repay the loan from selling chickens, ducks, pigs and vegetables.

name: John
description: John is a forty-three year old married man living in Masindi, Uganda. John's business is making bricks and he enjoys it because it has enabled him to cater for the needs of his family since 2007. He hopes to educate his children and have a better house for his family despite the challenge of seasonal changes - especially too much rainfall - that spoil the bricks. John requests for a loan to buy firewood to help him make more bricks to sell.

name: Robert
description: Robert is a married man, 39 years old with three children, two of whom are school going and he is fully responsible for paying their school fees and meet other basic needs.Robert is very grateful for Ugafode for he has been a client for more than five years and Kiva funders who give support to small business like his.Once again he has applied for a loan of 2,000,000 UGX to invest in his cattle fattening trade such that he can improve his standard of living and be able to meet school dues for his children. From his business income he is able to meet his basic needs of life and feed his children.Robert is optimistic that his business will continually support his family, and meet his dream of having the biggest farmland in the area of Kazo Kiruhura District that can graze up to 200 heads of cattle.However his major challenges that affect his business are poor transport means and bad weather, especially long spells of sunshine that affect the animals' health. Therefore, funding is quite vital for such a client.

name: Virgen Del Carmen De Vizcochoni Group
description: There are the members of the “VIRGEN DEL CARMEN DE VIZCOCHONI” communal bank, located in the Colquepata district, within the Paucartambo province, Cusco department.  Justina is 28 years old, has two children, and is in a live-in relationship. She is a very responsible lady who continues to raise livestock to sell at the area fairs so she can support her family.  She is asking for a loan to fix her stable and other things,  The other members sell cereals, clothing, groceries, or run restaurants. They are grateful to those who form part of this dream and are committed to making their payments on time.

name: Ruzigul
description: Ruzigul is a clever, loving woman of 32. She has two lovely children and a loving husband. She has been working on a collective farm for seven years. Her husband also contributes to the family budget but they are planning a celebration. To put on the party, they need money. With the agreement of her husband, she wants to take a loan from Arvand to conduct the celebration. She gives thanks in advance to Arvand for the support!!!

name: Bose
description: Mrs. Bose O., a yam seller, needs a loan of $275 to enable her to buy more yam to sell. She is 45 years old, married with 4 children, and lives in Benin City. She learnt her trade over 6 months and started her business in 1992. She is a dedicated LAPO client.

name: Hikoyat
description: Hikoyat is a woman who communicates well. She was born in 1978. She is living in a remote district and is a widow. She has four children.  Hikoyat's husband had a canteen at an auto service business. After the death of her husband, Hikoyat inherited that canteen. She has been in this business for almost four years.   Year by year she become more experienced and met the challenge of serving people, but her canteen is in bad condition. Hikoyat wants to make it better and decided to renovate the canteen. Additionally, she is planning to widen her assortment of dishes. She is asking for financial support from KIVA to renovate her canteen and enlarge the assortment of dishes.

name: Elnara
description: Elnara is an Internally Displaced Person (IDP) from the Armenian-occupied territory of the Fuzuli town in Azerbaijan and has settled in Fuzuli region, in Bala Bahmanli village. She was born in 1983. Elnara has been in the buffalo business for 4 years. She is single. Now she needs a loan of US$ 1200 to buy a buffalo to expand her business.

name: Magdalena
description: Magdalena is 76 years old and married with one child. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Magdalena has a business buying and selling bananas in the Philippines. Magdalena requested a PHP 10,000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase more bananas to sell in her fruit stall.  Magdalena has been in this business for 16 years. Magdalena would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Maliemailatoelau
description: Maliemailatoelau L. is 28 and married with 5 children (ages 5 - 11).  She owns a business venture, selling ice-cakes (flavored ice in styrofoam cups).  Maliemailatoelau has many years of experience in this business.  Maliemailatoelau needs a loan of WST $1500 to purchase additional products to sell.  She plans to use the earnings from her business (estimated to be 400 talas or US $167 per week) to improve/expand the business.  In 2008, Maliemailatoelau joined SPBD.    This is her 3rd loan with SPBD.   SPBD's loans are Maliemailatoelau's only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with traditional banks.  The following social metrics for Maliemailatoelau L. are provided by SPBD*: Overall Social Metric Score:                1.5 out of 3 Level of Education:                         1.5 out of 3 Level of total Household Income:            1.4 out of 3 Quality of Household Assets:                1.6 out of 3  *SPBD measures the living conditions of each of its borrowers to track her loan progress. The overall social metric score, provided by SPBD, is based upon a number of factors, such as the condition of the house/household assets, health, education, income level, and family reputation. A higher number represents a higher score. For example, a ""3 out of 3"" on education would mean that the borrower has graduated from university; a ""2 out of 3"" = secondary/high-school, and a ""1 out of 3"" would mean that the borrower is uneducated.  For more information on this score, please see SPBD's partner page at: http://partners.kiva.org/about/aboutPartner?id=15  About SPBD In 2000, Greg Casagrande founded SPBD and since then, it has expanded from the main island of Upolu in Samoa to Savaii, as well as Tonga. SPBD's philosophy of lending is based upon the Grameen Bank lending method.  Please join SPBD's lending team on KIVA to receive on-the-spot updates on SPBD: http://www.kiva.org/community/viewTeam?team_id=8375

name: Tsimbou
description: Tsimbou has been a pagne [traditional West African fabric] seller since 2003. Due to lack of funds she stocks up once a month at the Grand Market of Lomé. She is, by the way, a woman of 44 who lives in Adidogomé and is married with three children. In order to sell, she walks from neighborhood to neighborhood.  Tsimbou is requesting a loan so that she can increase her stock in order to improve sales and make enough income to care for her children and save more.

name: Juana Marina
description: Juana, 35, is separated and lives with her 11-year-old son and her brother in Guadalupe district, Pacasmayo province, La Libertad region, located an hour from the city of Chiclayo, Lambayeque region’s capital.  She has had an Internet café and play station for over a year.  She offers her services to students and youngsters of the area all day.  The business is well-received because there are few households in the district that enjoy this service and Internet is very useful to students for it is an extensive source of information that they can use to complement their school work.  Juana is very happy with the reception her business has had and daily strives to have it succeed since it is her family’s source of support.    The growing demand her services have had has inspired her to think of enlarging it buying an additional computer.  This has motivated her to request a 2000 new sol loan from Edpyme Alternativa to reach this goal.  Juana is a responsible mother who is dedicated to her loved ones; her greatest wish is to continue to expand her business so that her family can progress.  People who know her consider her to be trustworthy. Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Mamary
description: Mamary is a 32-year-old married father of two and lives with his wife and children in his dad's house in the Hérémakono-Nord de Bougouni region. After finishing secondary studies and receiving an accounting degree, Mamary has gone several years without a job. He tried several jobs such as selling cattle, sheep, and goats but with no success, he ultimately decided to sell poultry.  With three years of experience, he is becoming an expert at his job which he learned from one of his friends. To take care of his chickens, Mamary decided to take out a loan through Soro Yiriwaso to purchase: 1 ton of grain for feed, 2 cartons of medicine, and 200 chicks. He is on his fourth loan with Soro Yiriwaso and his three prior loans were all repaid in full. He buys his supplies in Boubouni and in Bamako (capital of the Republic of Mali). The eggs are sold to professional buyers (shops, food industries, and restaurants) and to home consumers. After they are laid, the eggs are sold at the market and in restaurants. With this loan, Mamary hopes to make a monthly profit of 75,500 FCFA. With this profit, he hopes to increase the size of his business.

name: Janice
description: Janice, a 32-year-old married mother of one child, sells dried fish to the people in her village. She has been patiently offering her products on a house-to-house basis for over four years now.   To increase her sales capacity, Janice is requesting a loan of P7,000 to purchase additional dried fish. In the future, she would like to establish a stall from which to sell her products. Janice is praying for her family's good health and a good relationship with her customers with the goal of generating continuous income from her enterprise.

name: Mary
description: Mrs. Mary H. was married in 1980 and now has four children, one son and three daughters. Since 2005 she has run a motorbike cleaning station. Her husband assists her with this business when he has time off from his main job, working as a cook for wedding ceremonies. Two of their children live with them and the other two daughters are married and have moved to live in a different house.     She is requesting a loan from MAXIMA for the first time for $1,100. She will use this loan to purchase another cleaning machine and to repair the house.

name: Araba
description: Araba N. is married and has two children. She has received a senior high education. For the past eight years, Araba has been selling fried fish at Abbrem Agona near Abura, Cape Coast. Her husband is a driver. Araba uses her income to pay for their children’s school fees and their family’s utility bills.  Araba will use the loan to purchase more fresh fish to fry for resale. With the new profits from her expanded business, Araba plans to build a house.

name: Analou
description: Analou is 34 years old and married with three children who are in school.  She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy more household goods to sell.  Analou has been in this business for four years.  She aspires to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Benkadi Group
description: The group BENKADI is composed of married women, who average 40 years of age and four children each. All the women live in traditional families in the village of Dioïla, Préfecture de Dioïla, Région de Koulikoro (2nd administrative region of the Republic of Mali). And they know one another through ties of kinship, community, and friendship. They work in food service and do commerce in tubers and juice drinks.   The women of the group BENKADI are on their 7th solidarity loan. To satisfy the enormous demand of their customers, they turn to the microfinance institution Soro Yiriwaso. These funds will be used to purchase their merchandise as cited above.  This client, WASSA, who is the person standing in the middle in the photo, is illiterate. She is currently a vendor of juice drinks. She intends to purchase 2 sacks of sugar, some empty bottles, plastic backs, and other basic material locally from wholesalers in Dioïla. She then processes the supplies into quality juice drinks. Her sales are made at the retail level to a mixed customer base paying with cash at the market and in surrounding villages. She envisions making an average monthly profit of 60,000 francs CFA that will be reinvested in her business.

name: Hamzeh
description: Hamzeh is a 23-year-old married man from Yatta, a village near Hebron. He lives with his wife and two kids. He works as a construction worker. He also has a barn for raising sheep, which has been operating for the past three years. He sells the meat and milk to local traders. It is a good business but still needs some improvements.  Hamzeh took out a USD loan from Palestine for Credit & Development (FATEN). This loan will help him to buy more sheep for his barn. By taking out this loan, Hamzeh will be able to increase the barn's productivity and also his income.  Hamzeh appears in the photo while he was taking care of the sheep.

name: Pamba W.g Group
description: Greetings from Pamba W.Group in Western Kenya! Irene is the facilitator of the Pamba W.group. This  group joined One Acre Fund in the year 2011 and will re-enroll in the 2012 program.  Irene takes care of two children at home. She joined One Acre Fund in order to access fertilizer and hybrid seeds and ensure food security for her family. In the recent 2011 season, Irene had a very good maize yield, harvesting 16 bags on 1 acre of land. Before joining One Acre Fund, Irene was only able to harvest 10 bags of maize on 1 acre of land.  With this loan, One Acre Fund will purchase fertilizer, seeds, and other important inputs to distribute to Irene and her group during Kenya’s next planting season in February 2012. The distribution of farming inputs is part of One Acre Fund’s integrated agriculture package, which includes training, reliable input supply (such as fertilizer and seeds), credit and insurance.  With income from maize sales, Irene will educate her children and pay back her loans.  In 2012, the members of Pamba W. group will each plant  between ½ and 1 acre of maize.  The photograph shows Irene with her group members.

name: Nilton Yuri
description: Nilton lives in the city of  Ica. It has a warm and pleasing climate. He works in agriculture, especially in growing cotton, paprika, asparagus and more. Nilton lives with his wife, with whom he has an 18 year old son, for whom he and his wife work to give him a dignified life and better opportunities that Nilton had. Because of his low income, he was only able to go to school up to the fifth year of secondary school, but he would have loved to study computer and information technology.   Day to day, Nilton works as a guard at a small security company. With the income from his work he is able, with a lot of effort, to pay for the household expenses. Nilton works around 9 hours a day and he thinks that he is getting ahead with his work because he is very responsible.    Nilton is very grateful to the lenders, since thanks to their help he will be able to buy a refrigerator for his house, since right now he doesn't have a place to keep his food. This way, he can improve his quality of life and keep fighting to make his biggest dream come true: owning his own house and giving his son a profession.

name: Teresa Del Carmen
description: Teresa is 58 years old and lives with her husband, who is a farmer and her children. She studied until Grade 4. Previously Teresa was a farmer but now she raises chickens. She has done this for 5 years and started it because there wasn't much trade in chicken in her community. She also raises pigs. Her pens are on her patio and she cares for the animals here. Her main source of income to get ahead are these activities.   She is requesting this loan to buy 500 chicks and 5 quintals of concentrated feed. She also wants to expand her pens and there is not much space and the animals do not fit in. This would allow her to raise a greater number of chickens and pigs and sell them when they are grown. She can make more profit for her household in this way. Her dream is to have a big farm with lots of chickens and be well-known and provide chickens to other businesses. With those profits she can have a better life with her children and provide them with the education they need to get ahead and become professionals.

name: Marifel
description: Marifel R. is from the village of Kandiis, Magsaysay, Misamis Oriental. She is 30 years old. Marifel is married and has 3 school-aged children. Marifel owns & operates a livestock business. The main source of income for the business comes from buying and raising pigs for sale. Marifel has been engaged in her business for over 5 years and earns approximately 7,000 Philippine Pesos (PHP) a month for these activities.  In 2010, Marifel joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Marifel has successfully repaid her first loan of 5,000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to purchase baby livestock to raise & sell in future. Marifel is now requesting a second loan, for 8,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase livestock feed & other supplies. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand it.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Women Of Gold Group
description: Gloria (54 years old) is the featured member of the group, Women of Gold.  She lives in the Teshie-Accra, Ghana.   She is a businesswoman selling rice, gari (cassava flour) and second hand clothing from door to door. She has been in this business for 5 years and it has been the main source of income for the family. She has one child to take care of.    It is not easy to take responsibilities for herself and child. Gloria's business brings good income and that is why she is requesting for this loan to stay in this business and make more money. She is in urgent need of money to buy stock of her rice, gari (cassava flour) and second hand clothing so that she can save money for herself and child.  The group, Women of Gold, was formed by women of common interest sharing similar economic background to get a loan. The loan will help them to buy inventory for their variety shops, which are the main source of income for their families.

name: Confort
description: Confort is a small-scale fish vendor in her location near Cape Coast. She has had some form of formal education as she is a primary school graduate. She is married and has 6 children. Her husband is a farmer.  Confort has been working as a fish vendor for a number of years. Her income is used to help her husband pay the utility bills and their children’s school fees. She plans on using her loan to purchase an increased quantity of fish, thus allowing her to meet rising customer demand. She hopes to use the profits from her enterprise to develop her business further and ensure that all her children receive an education.

name: Efua
description: Efua sells gari at Enyinase near Elmina. She is married to a farmer and together they have nine children. Efua uses her income to contribute to familial financial responsibilities, such as food purchases and school fees. Efua will use her loan to purchase bags of gari to sell. She plans to expand her gari business with her new profit.

name: Mary
description: Mary is 31 years old, married and has four children, all of whom are in school. She has run a business selling tea in Kator, South Sudan, for three years. Mary is requesting this loan through Kiva partner BRAC South Sudan to purchase sugar and coffee for resale. She will use the extra income from this loan to pay her children's school fees.

name: Bobosho
description: Bobosho A. lives in Yavan town. He is 39 years old and is married with 4 children. He supports his family by selling livestock. He raises calves and sells them at a higher price at the local market. He has been in this business for a  long time. Bobosho would like to get a loan for increasing livestock production. He would be able to pay off the loan within 12 months.    Translated from Russian by Oksana Buranbaeva, Kiva Volunteer

name: Nan
description: Nan, 42, is married and resides with her husband and three children in Takeo Province, Cambodia. She and her husband have been involved in the agricultural business for over twenty years. They have extensive experience and are successful in their career. They are involved in growing rice and fattening up cattle. Additionally, Nan's husband is a carpenter who manufactures tables, chairs, beds, and other furniture to sell in order to generate more income to financially support the family. Her daughter is a garment worker.   In order to increase her family’s income, Nan is requesting a loan of 400 USD to purchase more cattle to breed and to sell for a profitable price when they gain weight. In the future, she would like to expand her agricultural business, build a new house, and support her childrens' studies until they get Bachelor's degrees.  Note: Nan's husband is shown in picture.

name: Lorna
description: As a married parent of six children, four of whom are in school, Lorna works hard to support her family. She has a fishing business in the Philippines, and also earns an additional income from selling vegetables. Lorna is borrowing 15,000 PHP through NWTF to buy fishing materials for her fishing business. She has been sustaining her business activities through her past 2 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her to attain her dream to save enough money so that she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Mujeres Unidas De Boqueron Group
description: The 15 members of this group are women who are heads of family struggling to get ahead so they can provide for their loved ones everything they were unable to have.  Each member is doing her best to grow.  Mirta is one of the members and also the president of the group.  She is a very determined, hard-working woman.  She works making crochet handicrafts and earns a living this way.  The loan she is requesting is to buy needles, thread and other crochet supplies to continue her work.

name: John Jairo
description: His principal dream is to set up a number of sales locations. His only ambition is to improve himself every day. His principal difficulties are the lack of capital to accomplish his dreams. This is John, a patient man who had to wait a number of years for his business location, since in the past he worked in the chicken business. Once he was presented with the opportunity, he succeeded in setting up an ice cream shop that he has operated for a number of years. He hopes to be able to improve and expand his business, since the materials with which he began are secondhand and they are already beginning to show defects. He is applying for help to change the machinery in his establishment and to continue growing as a micro-entrepreneur, offering the community a service as common and as in demand as an ice cream, a little product that makes us happy and brings us a smile every time we consume it. With the assistance [of the loan], he hopes to buy a freezer, a chest of drawers, and merchandise for his business, with the intention of surprising his customers with new services and products.

name: Rithy's Group
description: Living in a wooden house with his family members in a rural village in the Phnom Proek district, Rithy is 29 years old and married with two children. They are still in school. He and his wife earn a living through planting corn and cassava. Having been in this business for six years, he manages to earn about 19,000 KHR per day and can save about 10,000 KHR each day for future needs.  Rithy’s group consists of three members and they are just with Kiva’s partner, VisionFund, this cycle. Now he is leading his group to apply for a loan of 2,000,000 KHR each. As the leader, he is going to use his portion to buy fertilizer and pesticides for his farmland. He hopes to increase his crop yields and earn more income to improve his standard of living.

name: Cheab
description: Cheab P., 54, is married with six children and resides with her husband in the Siem Reap province. To earn a living, she grows corn and vegetables to sell at the market. On average, she makes about US$3 per day. Her husband is a farmer and earns US$4 per day. Cheab P. would like to take out a loan to purchase land so that her husband can expand his cultivation.

name: Robina
description: Robina is a 43-year-old married lady and has been running a low income private school for 16 years. She works hard to make her standards, and desires to provide all facilities in the school.   She could not fulfill her dream due to financial problems. There are 93 students enrolled and 48% are female students. She requested for a loan of 100,000 PKR to buy furniture for the school. She worked hard to bring her school to an advanced level.

name: Alejandro
description: Alejandro was born in the city of Ayacucho but now lives in the city of Cusco.  He is 62 years old and married, and the fruits of this beautiful relationship include his two children.  Alejandro has a small grocery store in his home where he sells different staple products, such as rice, sugar, noodles, breads, containers of milk, juice drinks, sodas, detergents, and much more.  He currently is in need of a loan to buy consumer goods, for example sacks of sugar and rice, since it is more convenient to buy in bulk.  It has been several years since he began this business and it has been going well.  Alejandro is a member of the community bank “Los Andes” in the Asociación Arariwa in the city of Cusco.

name: Yuri
description: Yuri belongs to the community bank “Virgen Inmaculada Concepción”. She lives in the Anta district in the province of Anta, in the department of Cusco.   Yuri is 34 years old and lives with her partner and three children. She attends to her home duties with the help of her husband, who runs an auto repair that offers a complete range of services in the San Sebastian district. Yuri is applying for a loan to help purchase some tools for the auto repair.   She is very grateful for the valuable support offered by Kiva and pledges to complete all her repayments on time.Translated from Spanish by Suzanne Grasso, Kiva Volunteer

name: Marites
description: Marites P. is from the village of Eastern, Wao, Lanao del Sur. She is 41 years old. Marites is married and has 1 school-age children. To make a living, Marites owns & operates a business venture in the retail sector running a sari-sari (variety) retail shop. The main source of income for the business comes primarily from buying and selling different kinds of vegetables in the local community. Marites has been engaged in her business for over 5 years and earns approximately 6500 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2010, Marites joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Marites is requesting a loan of 5000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional vegetables to sell. This loan will be the 1st loan taken out by Marites from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand the her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Puao
