description: Puao is a 52-year-old, married woman with three children. She runs a small sewing business which she has had for more than six years. The people in her community and her usual clients come to her to have their dresses and shirts made. She plans to use this money from this loan to purchase a new sewing machine, fabric materials, thread, and a sewing table for sewing business. With the profits she has been making from her business she has been able to improve the livelihood of her family, thanks in part to the SPBD program.

name: Imelda
description: Imelda is from Clarin, Misamis Occidental. She is 42-years-old, single.   To make a living, Imelda is running a general store, selling a variety of food and home products in the local community such as candies, cigarettes, shampoo, soaps, etc. Imelda has been engaged in her business for over 20 years and earns approximately 4,000 PHP a month for these activities.  Imelda is requesting a loan of 8,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase new items to expand her product offerings. In 2011, Imelda joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her business and living situation. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the loan to save as a reserve for future emergencies.

name: Elsy
description: Elsy, 40, lives with her husband Basilio, who travels constantly, and their two children, Larry, 17, and Sara, 8. They all live together and have their own house.  Seven years ago, Elsy started a business selling food products in the shop she has in her house. This allowed her to provide a better future for her children, as her husband’s income is not sufficient to meet their expenses.   Elsy begins her work each day at 7AM and usually works until about 8PM. Sales are good, as Elsy is very charismatic and is attentive to the needs of her customers. Because of this, she has many friends in the community.   Thanks to previous loans with MFP, she has converted part of her house into a mini-store where she offers beauty products and a few decorative articles and personal accessories.   Elsy wants to keep expanding her business, so she is asking for her this, her 18th loan with MFP. Over these eight years, she has been very responsible in her payments. With this loan, she will buy more merchandise for her store, as she knows there is much demand for the New Year festivities.  Translated from Spanish by jeffrey hersk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Maichata
description: Maichata was born in Sanzana in August 1974 and lives with her two children and husband in a monogamous family in the Binko district of the town of Selingue. She is a teacher by trade but also has an interest in income-generating activities, notably the sale of ginger juice and milk. Having repaid her previous loans in full, Maichata is on her third loan with Soro Yiriwaso, which will be used to buy 150 kilos of ginger and five sacks of sugar from wholesalers. She sells for cash, on a retail basis, from home and in the market at Dalabala to a customer base made up of men and women.  Maichata hopes to make a monthly profit of 70,000FCFA, which will be used to help her husband provide for the family's needs, repay her loan and reinvest in her business.

name: Genara
description: Genara operates a sari-sari (variety) store, selling various commodities ranging from noodles, canned goods, soft drinks, sugar, eggs, soap and beverages. She is a 51-year-old married woman with three dependents ages 4-15 years old, respectively. Her husband earns a living by being a laborer. She also toils the land and grows rice.This time, she would like to improve the content of her store. She has joined CEVI to access financial services.Genara has requested a loan to buy supplies like assorted goods, beverages and feed. With these, she could start to save and be able to do some expansion. She is hoping that someday, she will become a successful entrepreneur and be able to support the needs of her children as well.

name: Dinara
description: Dinara is 38 years old and married.  She and her husband are raising four children.  She has a higher education and makes a living teaching elementary grades at a local school.  Her husband works as an electrician and brings home a stable salary.  In order to make an additional income for her family, Dinara is also involved in animal husbandry and agriculture.  She started in this field 15 years ago with the purchase of livestock for 10,000 som (KGS).  Thanks to her very hard work, her farming business now consists of two dairy cows, one horse, 30 sheep, 15 goats, one heifer and 25 chickens.  Dinara's children are very actively involved with the farm work, and all members of the family are assigned responsibilities for the care of the animals.  Dinara makes a monthly income of 15,000 som (KGS).  Eager to further develop her farming business, Dinara has turned to the bank "Bai Tushum" and requested a loan.  She will use her loan to buy some foals in order to increase her number of farm animals.  She plans to reinvest the earnings from her loan into further increasing her livestock headcount.  She is also planning to save enough money to buy a tractor.

name: Osman
description: This is 30-year-old Osman.  He is married and has two children aged ten and three. In 1992, Osman established his palm oil and garri (cassava flakes) business. He began his business in order for him to be able to take care of his family. Working seven days a week and ten hours a day, he earns about Le 700,000 every month as profit from this business.   He would like a loan in the amount of  Le 3,000,000. Osman requires a loan in order to buy more gallons of palm oil and bags of garri in large quantity. In the future, Osman plans to construct a shop and a house so that his wife can manage the shop. He is thanking you for your support.

name: Ketty
description: Ketty is 43 years old, is in a relationship, and has 2 dependent children. She lives with her family in the district of Pucara, in the province of Jaen in the Cajamarca region in the northern mountains of Peru. In this district, the people are dedicated to agriculture, especially to growing rice. Rice is most of the production and most of the overall business. Ketty is dedicated to making and selling ice cream, gelatin, flan, ice cream cake, etc. She sells these products from her home and outside the high school in Pucara. She has more than 5 years of experience in this work, and she has very good personal references for her moral and financial solvency. The loan will be used to buy supplies and raw materials for making her products. This will lead to sales and allow her to earn enough income to improve her quality of life.

name: Idrissa A.'s Group
description: Salone Microfinance Trust (SMT), a partner of Kiva in Makeni, northern Sierra Leone, is very pleased to present to you this group of teachers from a primary school in Mile-Ninety-One, a town in northern Sierra Leone. They are requesting a loan of SLL 5,000,000; with the help of this loan, some of these teachers will invest in their businesses, others will pay school fees for their children, etc. At the end of each month, the school’s bursar is directly responsible for repaying SMT on their behalf.   Idrissa is a teacher at the school and the leader of this group. The 35-year-old has been in the teaching profession for many years now. A native of a village called Kambrabia Yoni, Idrissa is married and has 3 children. Idrissa has requested a loan of SLL 1,200,000 in order to buy materials for building house - cement and iron-corrugated zinc - for the completion of a project that is underway.

name: Kiyinki B1 South C Group
description: The group leader of this small group is Gertrude N..  She is currently in the business of running a restaurant and is requesting a loan to purchase food warmers.  Gertrude is 33 years old and is a widow.  She has 6 children ranging from age 3 to 14 and her children go to school.  Each week, Gertrude makes approximately UGX 20000 in profits and with the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to cater for home needs and re-invest in her business. Gertrude has taken a loan from BRAC Uganda before in the amount of UGX 300000 in order to invest in her business and the loan was paid back on time.  Gertrude is joined in her small group by Hellen N., Jamawa N., Scovia N., and Deborah N..  Hellen N. has a business selling fuel and wants to invest more in her business.  Jamawa N. is currently operating a restaurant business and wants a loan to purchase a fridge.  Scovia N. operates a restaurant business and wants to add more furniture.  Deborah N. is currently in the business of running a restaurant and is requesting a loan to purchase more raw food.

name: San's Group
description: San’s group live in a rural village in Kandal province in Cambodia. San makes a living cultivating rice, and she also does extra work as a tailor to support her family.  In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of her family and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Zaruro Group
description: Life is not fair, and one person who encountered an experience that made her believe this saying is Patricia. After her husband passed on, she thought she thought her world was over, until her younger sister passed on a week later. These losses left her with four dependants since they had two children and her sister had two of her own. She grieved wondering how she was going to be able to take care of these four children on her own. Luckily she had an old knitting machine which she had kept for years. She had last knitted a jersey as a present for her husband’s birthday and used to knit as a pastime. She then dusted the old machine and sat before it with determination as this was going to be her source of income. Patricia now makes 3 - 4 jerseys a day and she supplies these jerseys to schools in the rural areas of Madziva and Bindura. She also sells to villagers in these rural areas, typically in exchange for peanut butter and maize, as they do not usually have cash. When she returns to Harare, she then sells the peanut butter and maize to her neighbours. For the past two years, she has managed to send all four children to school.Patricia and three other women have approached Thrive Microfinance as a group called Zaruro and are requesting a combined loan of $1,100. Patricia wants to buy wool in bulk so that she can be able to fully supply the jersey orders from the schools as she usually fails to do this due to inadequate resources.

name: Miguela
description: Miguela D. is from the village of Liong, Guinsiliban, in Camiguin Province. She is 42 years old. Miguela is married and has 6 school-aged children. To make a living, Miguela operates a business selling seafood products such as sardines & salmon in the local community. Miguela has been engaged in her business for over 6 years and earns approximately 4500 PHP a month from these activities.  In 2011, Miguela joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Miguela is requesting a new loan of 4000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional fish, like salmon & sardines. This loan will be the 1st loan taken out by Miguela from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Esteban
description: Esteben has a shop that he rents.  He works as a locksmith, and he does all types of locksmith work.  He needs the loan to build a shop so that he does not have to pay rent.  Esteben is married and has two children.  He lives in his own house in the Pasankeri area of the city of La Paz.  This is the first time that he has worked with IMPRO, and it is the first time that he has worked with Kiva.

name: Mario
description: The partner continues raising livestock.  He has cattle that he raises and fattens up and then takes to sell at various street markets that exist in Anta District.  He works from 5am until 6pm and is able to support his children with this business.  His dream is to expand the cattle raising business.  He’s asking for a loan to buy feed for the cattle.  He’s happy with the loan and commits to make his installment payments.

name: Muhammad
description: M. Muhammad is a hard-working business man. He is 50 years old and married and has five children, two girls and three boys. He resides in Mukoko Village in Lukaya District.   Muhammad raises broiler chickens -- he has approximately 300 birds. His business is located at his residence. He is requesting a loan to add layer chickens to his poultry business so he can increase his income and profits. He hopes to expand his poultry business so he can earn more profit and improve his success in life.

name: Rovelyn
description: Rovelyn, 36, is married with three children. Two of her children are currently in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Rovelyn has a fishing business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for five years. She has requested a loan of 4,000 Philippine pesos through Gata Daku Multi-Purpose Cooperative. She will use the loan to buy a new fish net for her business.Rovelyn would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Mohamad
description: Mohamad is a 29-year-old man who lives in Beirut, the capital of Lebanon, with his wife and their three children. Mohamad owns a bakery. He does mankoucheh. A mankoucheh looks like a folded pizza. The most common toppings are zaatar (thyme), jebneh (cheese) and lahm bi ajin (minced meat). You can eat it anytime of the day, but somehow it tastes better in the morning.   Mohamad is special in his work because he is known for his good and tasty mankoucheh. His clients are his friends and neighbors. He requested a loan from Al Majmoua in order to purchase raw materials for his bakery. This is the first time that Mohamad has requested a loan from Al Majmoua. Ahmad decided on doing his business because he always wanted to open a bakery. In the future, he plans on expanding his work.

name: Chamroeun
description: Chamroeun, 33, is married and resides with her husband and five children in Kampong Chhnang Province, Cambodia. She has been working in a garment factory for more than five years, earning approximately $3 per day. Her husband is employed in a mobile phone company. He earns about $8 per day. Her children are still in her care and are in school. Due to the difficulty in her family’s transportation, Chamroeun is requesting a loan of $1200 to purchase a motorbike for commuting. This purchase would enable her to use the saved money on her transportation expenses to support the family. In the future, she would like to run a tailoring shop and help her children earn bachelor’s degrees. Moreover, she hopes to build a new house as soon as possible.

name: Saidmurod
description: Saidmurod lives in a remote village. He has a large family. He has three underage children and also his elderly mother [in his care]. He mainly raises livestock and grows produce. His wife, Gulnora, is the one who mostly helps him with growing produce. This is the third time that Saidmurod is turning to our organization. He launched his business by having two heads of small livestock, and now he has four heads of cattle. He fattens cattle for resale to butchers. He uses the revenue from this business to support his family and improve their living conditions. Saidmurod would like to replenish his working capital, which is why he is applying for a loan in the amount of 12,000 TJS to buy cattle. He is counting on your kindness.

name: Kavule C Group
description: The leader of this small group is Robinah N.. She has a restaurant business and is requesting a loan to expand it.  Robinah is 43 years old and married. She has 2 children, ages 18 and 22, and her children go to school.  Each week, Robinah makes approximately UGX 60000 (~ $35 USD) in profits and, with the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to construct her own business premises.    Robinah has taken a loan from BRAC Uganda before, in the amount of UGX 300000 (~ $175 USD),  to invest in her business and she paid the loan back on time.  Robinah is joined in her small group by Prossy N., Nulu Nabukenya, Angella B., and Florence N.. Prossy N. has a business selling vegetables and wants to add to her business with the loan. Nulu Nabukenya is currently operating a business selling cold drinks and wants a loan to buy another refrigerator. Angella B. sells clothing and wants to purchase more clothes to sell. Florence N. has a restaurant business and is requesting a loan to buy more furniture and raw food.

name: Elsie
description: Mrs. Elsie L. is a PDP-LP (Paglaum Development Program for Landless People) member. She is 40 years old and married with four children. She is from Gabunon, Tambulig, Zamboanga del Sur. Her husband is a farmer and Elsie manages her pig raising business. From her business she earns approximately 4,000 a month.       She joined PMPC to gain access to financial support and to engage in other business activities. She successfully repaid her previous loan of 3,000 PHP taken from PMPC. This loan was used to invest in expanding her business so that she can earn additional income. As of now, she has a new loan of 4,000 from PMPC and this loan was used to purchase additional piglets. It is the second loan she has taken from PMPC.  About PMPC:   Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.   *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Qutfioi
description: Qutfioi is a very kind and responsible woman. She was born in 1953. She is a widow and has 4 children. She deals with buying and selling a variety of clothes and shoes. After her husband’s death, she raised her 4 children on her own despite many difficulties. Qutfioi has been working in her field for more than 18 years. Her children grew up poor and without a father but they help her in all activities. Qutfioi needs money in order to buy more goods for her shop and increase her working capital. She awaits your support and mercy.

name: Ibrahim Sorie
description: This is 45 year-old Ibrahim. He is married and has 4 children aged 22, 19, 17, and 14. In 1998, Ibrahim established his foodstuffs and used clothing business. He began his business to generate funds to support his children's education. His business is located at the city center and his main customers are both men and women. Working 7 days a week and 10 hours a day, he earns about SLL 1,000,000 every month from this business.  Ibrahim would like a loan in the amount of SLL 4,000,000 in order to buy sacks of groundnuts (SLL 2,500,000) and sacks of pepper (SLL 1,500,000). He hopes that this loan will increase his profit level. In the future, Ibrahim plans to build a house in Kenema, to educate his children, and to send his children abroad. He thanks you for your support.

name: Sim
description: Mrs. Sim H., 39 years old, and her husband, Mr. Theng Voch, 38 years old, live along the Tonle Basac River, a tributary of the nearby Mekong River, about fifteen kilometers from Phnom Penh. They have been married since 1995 and have four sons, three of whom attend school and one who is still young.   Sim is a garment factory worker. Her husband sells fruit (mango and guava); he buys it from fellow villagers under contract and transports it to sell in a Phnom Penh market. Sim is asking for her first loan of $500 to help her husband purchase mango under contract for resale.

name: Jona Fe
description: Jona Fe is a 42-year-old married mother of one child, who is in school. She has operated a pig-fattening business in the Philippines for eight years now.  Having borrowed four times in the past to sustain her business, Jona Fe has requested a new loan of PHP 20000 through NWTF to buy feeds and vitamins for her pigs. She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Tsetsegmaa
description: Tsetsegmaa is 41 years old and lives with her husband and daughter in a ger, a Mongolian yurt, in Uvs province of Mongolia. Her daughter who is 17 goes to a secondary school. Tsetsegmaa manages a meat trading business with the help of her husband. She started her business with working capital of 500,000 MNT in 2004. Since then she has been able to build a strong customer base and managed to increase her working capital to 2,500,000 MNT. She has great confidence that she can expand and continue her business successfully. She is a hardworking lady who says, "During National Holidays sales gets higher so I need to increase my inventories before that." Tsetsegmaa is requesting a 3,000,000 MNT loan to purchase livestock for her business.

name: Yana
description: Yana is married, with two children. She sells clothing at the main open market in Novomoskovsk town. Yana has been in this business for eight years. Her hard-working habits and enthusiasm encourage other market venders to continue their businesses in spite of difficult economic times.   Yana's business goal is to start a second location to increase sales. She would like to borrow 13,000 UAH to purchase more inventory for the coming summer season. Yana has used micro loans before. She finds them very helpful for developing her business.

name: Margarita
description: Margarita, 49, is a very loving and hard working mother.  She lives in her own house with her three children; Ruth is 15, Tony is 14, and Juan is 10.  They are the motivation for all of her efforts.  She wishes to give them a good high school education.  What Margarita’s restaurant lacks the least is customers, given that it is located near the terminal to the urban transportation line N° 15.  Her primary customers are the drivers and the collectors who, after a long morning of work, do not hesitate to enjoy the delicious dishes that she prepares.  Margarita’s prices are very reasonable, and they are the primary attraction to her restaurant.  What she likes most about her work is cooking and seeing how the people praise her good seasoning.  She has been doing this for seven years.  The most difficult part is waiting on customers and keeping them satisfied.  In the future, Margarita hopes to make her restaurant one of the most well known in the city of Juliaca.  She knows that she must work very hard to achieve her goals, and she is prepared to do so.   This is her fifth loan with MFP.  Just as she did with her first loans, she will make all of her payments on time.  She is well liked and respected in her community bank for the responsibility that she demonstrates.  She will use the 1,000 PEN that she is asking for to buy more chairs and tables to improve customer service in her restaurant. Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Jeanne
description: Jeanne is 44 years old and she is married with eight children.  Jeanne has owned a knitting machine and it is by using this machine that she earns the basic income for her family.  Jeanne has been in this business for about three years and the business hours are from 8 am until late in the evening.  Jeanne needs to request a Kiva loan via Vision Finance Company.  With this loan, she expects to buy two additional knitting machines and some other clothing items.  If she gets these two additional knitting machines, she really hopes that her customers will increase as well as her profits.  By getting enough profits, she will continue taking care of her family and keep reinvesting in her business for a better future.

name: Marina
description: Marina lives in Bagumbang, Bonifacio, Misamis Occidental with her family. Her husband is a farmer and he often goes fishing to earn a living. She has been raising pigs for 8 years to bolster to her husband's income. She sometimes helps her husband on the farm to earn extra income. She is hopeful that she can gain profit and wants to improve her family's living standards in the future.

name: Gonzalo Enrique
description: Gonzalo Enrique is 28 years old, married, and lives with his wife and children in the canton of Guaranda, in Bolivar province.  The members of V.R.C NUEVA ESPERANZA (V.R.C. NEW HOPE), are located in the sector La capilla, in the Four Corners community in the canton of Guaranda.  Within 25 minutes of each other, the members of this group work in agriculture, business, construction, and stockbreeding.  Gonzalo Enrique works in constuction and home improvement, as well as selling chochos (bean-like seeds), planting corn and wheat and raising animals.  He buys and sells his products in the city of Guaranda.  He requests the loan to purchase fertilizer, seeds, and animal feed.  The loan will help allow him to compensate for his financial needs and improve his farming practices. He faces challenges such as competition, prices and crop damage.  His dream is to build a house and buy land to cultivate.  He enjoys listening to music and celebrating the carnaval.

name: Hanitriniaina
description: Hanitriniaina lives in the centre of Antsirabe. She is a 37-year-old married mother to three children. She is devoted to her family. She works hard to help her husband earn money. She is not yet financially independent. It is for this reason that she decided to take out a loan with Vahatra. She sells various items, such as lamps, radios and cooking utensils. She has her own stand at market and her customers are always looking for new stock. With the profits from her previous loan, she was able to redecorate her family's home. She would now like to take out another loan so she can purchase antennas, radios, lamps and plug socket, as well as other essential day-to-day items. Her goal is to become financially independent.

name: Maria
description: Maria is a recurring client of the foundation. She has a general store in her house, which she was able to set up with much sacrifice. She sells all types of products, like dairy products, meat, sausage, basic necessities, etc.   She lives with her husband and children, and together they advance the growth and development of the business.  She requests this loan because she sees the need to stock her business with more products, such as drinks, dairy products, sausage, meat, and other items, so that she can continue with her work as she has been doing, giving her clients what they ask for.

name: Dandapani
description: Dandapani is a humble, married, differently abled man from a small village in Nayagarh, Odisha, India. He has a son who works in a shop in the town market nearby. Dandapani has been running a betel cum tea shop for the last 10 years in order to provide a better living to his family by fulfilling all their basic necessities. His shop is famous in the market due to the tasty tea he makes and the mouth watering pakoras complementing the delicious tea. The is quite a heavy rush during the early morning hours and at the evening time. Dandapani is quite happy with his business gaining popularity for the quality service he provides.Dandapani is requesting a loan amount of 20,000 INR from Kiva's partner People's Forum to add on more stocks of snacks items to his store and remodel his store in order to provide a good ambiance to his regularly visiting customers.Dandapani is eagerly awaiting your kind help and generous support.

name: Roberto
description: Roberto is a 34-year-old married man with three children. He has a sari-sari (variety) store business in Trinidad, Bohol. Roberto has been running his store for eight years. He sells canned goods, shampoo and sachets of coffee and milk. Roberto also sells rice to the people in his community.  Roberto requested this loan to buy more items to sell, such as rice and sugar. Roberto hopes to expand his store in the future. He also wishes for his children to finish their studies.

name: Jonathan
description: Thirty-four-year-old Jonathan earns a living raising hogs and engages in farming as well.  He has grown rice for eight years now. These are his sources of income.He is a married man and has two young dependents.  He is striving hard to improve his income. Together with his family, he lives in the town of Sikatuna.He would like to avail himself of a loan to buy feed, piglets and rice seedlings.  Slowly, these could help him raise quality hogs and produce more harvest. He could able to provide his family with a nutritious diet and better shelter to live in.Jonathan is determined that in the near future, he could handle both of his sources of income successfully.

name: Katherin Amparo
description: Becoming a dentist has always been Katherin's dream. She is currently attending the Universidad Mayor de San Andrés, working towards her degree in dentistry. She plans on graduating in December 2015, but without a loan from Vittana, she thinks that she may need to take time off to work and save until she can return to school.   Katherin plans on spending the loan towards purchasing her textbooks. As an added expense, textbooks are often not bought to save money. With them, Katherin hopes to be able to better understand her subjects.   Katherin currently works 40 hours a week as a cashier in a store and earns $12 a day. With a degree in dentistry, she expects to earn $73 a day. As the youngest, with one older sibling attending college already, Katherin is unsure how she will be able to finance her education on her own without the assistance of a Vittana loan.

name: Maria Alicia
description: Maria Alicia continues dedicating herself to her business selling beauty products and shoes. She sells lipstick, lotions, and perfumes. Through this business, she wants to go forward. She requests the loan to buy lipstick and lotions.  She is happy with the loan and promises to comply with the loan repayments.

name: Maleyka
description: Maleyka J. is a 43 year old woman, and a mother of four children. She lives with her family in Beylagan, a small city in  Azerbaijan. She and her husband have a business of cattle-breeding. They established their business ten years ago. Maleyka needs a loan in the amount of $1075 to purchase a cow and expand her business.

name: Maxima
description: Máxima L. lives in a house she owns in the Llajeta zone, on the western end of the city of La Paz.  Máxima works as an employee at a restaurant in La Paz, generating income with which she supports herself.    With her savings she was able to acquire a plot of land, on which she now has constructed three rooms that are still unfinished.  The loan she is requesting is to build two rooms that are completed, so they can be used.  This is the third time she solicits a loan, and the financial analysis conducted indicates she qualifies favorably for access to credit.  Translated from Spanish by Mary Lynn Malaby, Kiva Volunteer

name: Nazrbi
description: Nazrbi is a cheerful girl. She was born in southern part of Tajikistan in 1994. She is single and lives with parents. They have a big family and only her mother is working. Nazrbi is a responsible, honest, communicable and generous person. She graduated secondary school with excellence and passed the entrance examination to university.She is studying at the Medical University and is in her 4th year. She appealed to IMON to get a loan to pay her tuition fees. She awaits Kiva lenders’ kindness and support. She hopes loan will help her to pay her higher education costs and she can successfully finish studying and become a health professional.

name: Ala'a
description: Ala'a is a 24 year old single man from Al Ashrafieh, Jordan. Years ago, Ala'a started his spice business by peddling his products on the street.  Now Ala'a has his own shop. Ala'a is requesting a loan of 1350JD to expand his shop and purchase more products. Ala'a aspires to open a second shop.

name: Nguyen Thi
description: Mrs. H. Thi Nguyen, 50 years old, joined the Fund in 2003.  Her family has three children, two of whom are grown and are starting their own families in separate residences, and one who is going to school and living with the parents.  In each round of funding, the family has invested in raising livestock and fish farming.  Her husband is a hardworking man; besides the livestock work with the family, he also works as a construction worker earning an average of 1,500,000 VND per month.  She also trades goods at the market, with a modest income of 50,000 VND/day.  In this round of funding the family is requesting a loan of 15,000,000 VND to invest in a sow, breeding fish, and buying feed.  Their average monthly income is 4,000,000 VND.Translated from Vietnamese by Chi Nguyen, Kiva Volunteer

name: Perla
description: Perla is 63 years old and married with three children. Perla works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 12,000 loan through NWTF to buy more groceries to sell.  Perla has been in this business for 5 years and sells a variety of items, such as shampoo, detergent soap, hair conditioner, coffee, and sugar.  In the future, Perla would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Qatun Llaqta Group
description: The Communal Bank "Qatun Llaqta" which means "Big  Town", has begun it's 5th cycle with 16 associates. The associates are from the district of Socos which is located 40 minutes from the city of Ayacucho.  Each of the associates has a different business. The businesses fall under groceries, food, small animals, farming and handicrafts.  For example:  Modesta is 48 years old, married, has 3 children and owns a general store. She is also an artist and weaves carpets and rugs.  Mariluz is 24 years old, has a partner and has 2 children. She sells food in the park in her district and also sells vegetables in different towns.  Aurora is 36 years old, married, has 3 children and owns a store where she sells groceries. She also works in agriculture and raises cattle.  The associates need several loans in the amounts of 300 soles, 600 soles and 900 soles for a total of 9,950 soles (3 soles = $1USD, approx.) in loans from the Communal Bank.  Their loans would be used to buy firewood, rice, salt, noodles, oil, milk, cheese, wheat, barley, corn and small animals.  The associates wish to one day own their own houses, increase their sales and for their children to become professionals.  Translated from Spanish by Beatriz Yuste, Kiva Volunteer

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth is 47 years old, married with 2 children and lives in Lagos State, Nigeria. She has been selling provisions and drinks for the past 3 years. Elizabeth is requesting the loan amount of N150,000 to purchase more provisions and drinks to sell. She says thanks to all Kiva lenders for their financial support.

name: Casilda
description: Click HERE to see the previous loan.  Casilda is a member of El Triunfo (The Triumph) Communal Bank.  She continues working every day at her grocery store, which she manages by herself.  She needs a loan of 1000 soles to buy beverages.  The money will increase her operating capital so that her store remains well stocked.  She hopes to continue working as long as she has the strength.  Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Kanyamakerre Tukwatanize Group
description: Bena is a member of Kanyamakerre Tukwatanize where members guarantee each other. She has three children and lives in Fort Portal, Uganda.   She sells fresh foods like tomatoes, onions, oranges and passion fruits, and does farming to make ends meet. She is faced with the challenges of competition and price changes that hinder the progress of her business. Besides that, she is hoping to expand her business to new areas and diversify her business to include dairy farming.   Bena has asked for a loan to to add more stock of fresh foods like tomatoes, onions, oranges and passion fruits for resale.

name: Wilson
description: Wilson is 48 years old and married to Margaret Kibusia, who is a housewife. They have three school-going children, namely Moses Kipkurui, Leah Jepchirchir and Kipkemoi Kibusia. He has been in the business of buying and selling cattle for 20 years and right now his monthly income is 6,000 KES.  He is borrowing a loan of 20,000 KES which he wants to pay school fees for his son. He plans to use the anticipated profit from his business to educate his children. This is his fourth loan and he successfully paid his previous loans well and in good time.  His dreams and hopes are to be a successful business man who can fully support his family and especially give the best education to his children.

name: Nizomidin
description: Nizomidin I. lives in the J.Rumy Region. 45 years of age. Married, with three children. Education: secondary. He works as a hairdresser in a barber shop. He has a lot of experience in this area. He is taking out a loan to purchase new instruments and accessories.

name: Keneth
description: Keneth is married and has three children. He is a resident of Obutobelo, Ojwina, Lira district. He operates a small business in which he sells spare motorcycle parts. He earns additional income from agriculture.   Keneth requested his first loan from UGAFODE MDI, which he will use to buy a motorcycle to add to his business. It will be used as a bodaboda, a bicycle for transporting people. He believes acquiring a motorcycle would cause a great change to his standard of living since his revenue would triple.

name: Mujeres Trabajadoras Group
description: Thirteen very hardworking, enterprising women joined together to help their families and children by means of their work as a group.  They want their children to be free of the want and needs they had to go through themselves.  Sonia is one of the members; she sells food.  She relates that she’s getting ahead thanks to her customers always buying products from her.  She’s a very talented person and the dishes she makes are very well-liked; this is how she’s getting ahead.  She requests this loan to buy ingredients like vegetables, meats, condiments and legumes, etc. to continue making her dishes.

name: Nabila
description: Mrs. Nabila is a 35-year-old married woman and a mother of two. She has been in business selling home products for the last twelve years. She purchases bed sheets and towels, etc. from the market in Taxila at wholesale rates and sells them in her community from her home. Her husband is a government employee, but his income is not sufficient to meet all the expenses so she is doing her business fairly.  She has a major contribution in meeting household expenses. Three years ago, she availed a loan from Kashf and increased her profit from the business. Now, she wants to invest more to purchase more items such as bed sheets and towels in various colors and designs. She hopes to earn more income through her large sales.  She dreams of providing good and quality education to her children.

name: Akua
description: Akua S. is 35 years old and married. She takes care of her little sister’s daughter. Akua has managed to send the child to one the best schools in the community where she lives with her husband, who is a photographer. She lives in Dorma Ahenkro in the Brong Ahafo region of Ghana. To support her household, she hawks and sells cosmetics in her neighborhood to her loyal clients. She says selling cosmetics is very lucrative and therefore she wants to expand her inventory to enable her to make a good income for the family’s needs. She is therefore appealing for your assistance to make good sales and take care of her home. She also belongs to the village bank called "Asomdwe," which means Peace.

name: Annaliza
description: Annaliza is a married woman with two children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur. Annaliza is 31 years old and has two children who are in school.  Annaliza has a general store business in the Philippines. She has requested a PHP 29,000 loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to purchase more groceries to sell in her general store.  She successfully paid back her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her general store business.  Annaliza has been in this business for nine years. In the future, she would like to save enough money, so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Angel
description: Ángel is pleased after successfully managing his previous Kiva loans with Fundación Mario Santo Domingo. He states that the loans are issued at interests rates favorable to any micro business; therefore, he is once again requesting a loan to pay cash for flour, oil, sugar, eggs, and other necessary supplies to make the bread and puddings he sells at his business. This way he receives better discounts for prompt payment, which allows him to achieve higher profit margins. He also wishes to buy more groceries and basic supplies to stock the store located within the business.

name: Nguyệt
description: Mrs Nguyệt works in agriculture farming food.  Nguyệt is 35 years old and she is married with two children.  Nguyệt lives with two dependents in Nong Cong district, a  rural town in Thanh Hoa province.  In 2013, Nguyệt joined Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women to improve her  business. Nguyệt has successfully repaid two loans from Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women.  Nguyệt has been involved in this business for five years.  The main hardship that Nguyệt faces in her life is not having a hygienic latrine. She is requesting a loan to purchase sand, cement, bricks, and equipment to build a toilet.  With her business profit, Nguyệt hopes for her children to do well in school, for her business to do well, and for her family to be healthy and happy.

name: Sevilla
description: Sevilla is 54 years old and lives in Sapang Dalaga. She is married with four children.   To earn a living, Sevilla has a business selling snacks. She earns about PHP 3600 each month doing this type of work. Sevilla has requested a loan of 14,950 to purchase 2 sacks of flour and other ingredients.  Sevilla has been a member of PMPC for five years.
town: Calamba-Sapang Ama Sapang Dalaga Misamis Occidenta

name: Janeth
description: Janeth works as a teacher in an elementary school. She has a diploma in education. She lives in her own home, occupying two rooms built from brick with a cement floor in the Las Muñecas area in the city of La Paz. Janeth works eight hours a day to cover the costs of food, light, water, the education of her four children, and other expenses. She needs the loan to remodel her bathroom. She will buy construction materials like cement, plaster, and paint. Janeth's dream is for her children to finish their higher education. This is her second loan with IMPRO and her second from Kiva.

name: Las Comerciantes Group
description: Maria (who is in the center of the three) is a woman full of dreams and goals and fights daily to be successful.   Thanks to a loan, Maria was able to invest in her business of selling clothes, which, fortunately, is generating a good income for her, so she was able to buy a sewing machine. Now she can also manufacture traditional clothes and does not just buy them.  This improvement makes Maria and the rest of the group very happy. But they don't want to settle there. This is why, with the desire to further succeed, they are requesting another loan to invest once more into their business of selling traditional clothes by purchasing a variety of traditional skirts, woven belts, and blouses.  Maria expects to be able to use this loan to continuously improve her business and to be able to pay for a store where she can display her products better.

name: Norqueza
description: Norqueza is 59 years old and widowed with six children.  She earns a living by farming coconut in the Philippines. Norqueza is borrowing 15,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) through NWTF to buy fertilizers and other farm supplies.  Norqueza has been farming coconut for 25 years and also earns additional income from farming rice.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save money to expand her business.

name: Aminu
description: Aminu is a Babban Gona maize farmer from Hayin Malam Yako village.  Aminu joined Babban Gona to create a better life for his children.   Through Babban Gona’s input loan, Aminu will have access to the best farm inputs in the market such as fertilizer, herbicides and improved seeds that will help him earn yields of up to 30 bags of maize/ hectare, double the Nigerian national average of 14 bags. This will see him increase his household income considerably.   Thanks to Babban Gona's support, Aminu now has the opportunity to increase his yields and income and use his additional earnings to diversify his farm and grow other crops.

name: Dexter
description: Dexter is 35 years old, married, and his family lives in Padul. Dexter obtains income through rice farming. He plants and harvests rice to sell to traders.   As a farmer, he uses his net income from the previous harvest for the next planting season. Dexter only gained minimal income from his previous harvest, and that is why he is now asking for additional capital of 50,000 PHP (Philippine Pesos) to buy insect killer, herbicides, and fertilizers used in farming. This will help fight pests that will destroy and affect his crop's growth.   Someday, Dexter hopes to achieve a fruitful harvest so he will pay back his loan from the organization on time. He hopes to save funds for his family’s emergency purposes too.

name: Akouvi
description: This woman has a revenue-generating business selling pagnes (colorful West African cloth).  She is mastering her commerce, which she learned from her mom, who was a retailer.  Her husband is retired, and what she earns in profits enables her to help cover family expenses.  She supplies herself in Lomé.    The holiday period is approaching, and she would like to expand her inventory, which is exhausted, in order to sell more.  These are the reasons for her request for a WAGES loan, so as to buy 30 lengths of HI-TARGET pagnes, 30 of PHOENIX, and 25 of WAX.Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Zoraida
description: Zoraida belongs to the “Women of the Hill II” cooperative bank, located in the San Martín province.  She is married, 33 years old, and the mother of 3 daughters who still depend on her and are in school.    She has been dedicating herself to this type of activity for 1 year, providing urban transportation services using her motokar.  To do the work, her husband is in charge of moving to different parts throughout the city.  She started out with the first loan from Manuela Ramos and, little by little, she saved money to buy replacement parts to improve her services to the inhabitants of the community.  With this loan of 1,800.00 Peruvian soles, she will buy parts and oils such as lubricants and sparkplugs in order to provide a better quality of service and to better tend to the customers.  Today, she is an independent woman and her and her husband are the ones that make the decisions and manage the business.  Zoraida tells us:  belonging to a group of women has helped her know more about her rights and how to work together to be respected.  She is very grateful to the Manuela Ramos movement for helping her get a start in the business arena.  Translated from Spanish by Mary Lynn Malaby, Kiva Volunteer

name: Elite Group
description: Praxidese’s group has 11 farmers and is located in Teso District. Praxidese is pictured on the right of Elite Group, with her hand raised. Praxidese is pictured amongst the two men and nine women of her group.   She will receive input loans capable of planting 0.5 acres with sorghum, millet, and sweet potato. The 2013 Long Rains season will be Praxidese’s first season with One Acre Fund. She joined this year in order to grow enough food for the family and to use increased profits to send her children to school.  Praxidese described her harvest last year as good, but hopes she can have an even better one as a One Acre Fund farmer. She plans to use the money that she earns from her next harvest to send her children to school and to save for the future.   For the 2013 Long Rains season, Elite Group members will take input loans of 0.5 acres each. In total, this group will receive input loans for use on 5.5 acres of land.

name: Juan Felipe
description: Juan is 20, single and lives with his parents.  Their home has running water and electricity, and is located in the district of Olmos, Lambayeque.  This region is known for its agriculture and cattle.  Juan drives a "mototaxi" (a vehicle used for short distance transport which holds 3 people maximum), and has done so for about one year.   He operates the taxi in his neighborhood from the early morning, seeking to transport as many people as possible to increase his income for personal expenses.  Juan seeks a credit from Edpyme Alternativa of 1,500 soles to improve his mototaxi, and to provide better service to clients.  Juan is responsible and hardworking, and hopes to provide for his family.

name: Olivia
description: Olivia is 50 years old and married with five children, two children are currently in school, Olivia works very hard to provide for them.  Olivia runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 4000 loan through NWTF to buy more items to sell like canned goods, noodles, spices, milk, drinks, coffee, sugar, soap, shampoo, snack foods and other personal collection.  Olivia has been in this business for 1 year.   In the future Olivia would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Alma
description: Alma is from Sepac, Sapang Dalaga. She is 42 years old, married and has three children. To make a living, Alma owns and operates a retail specialty store. Alma has been engaged in her business for four years and earns 3,000 PHP a month. In 2010, Alma joined GDMPC. Alma is requesting a loan of 5,000 PHP which will be used to buy products such as canned goods, sugar, milk, noodles, shampoo, soap and toothpaste. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the family's income.

name: Los Vecinos Del Valle Group
description: Alicia is a member of the "Los Vecinos del Valle" (Neighbors of the Valley) community bank which is made up of 20 entrepreneurs who have different businesses such as a bakery, a beauty salon and a business selling clothes and lingerie.  They live in the city of Casablanca.  Alicia is in the front row of this photo, on the left, wearing a black top.  She is in the craft business.  She makes candles, decoupage (a decorative paint effect used on wood and glass), mosaics (geometric, decorative, compositions made with pieces of pottery) and knitted items.  She also sells new clothes  Alicia started out in the craft trade 10 years ago which means that her frequent customers are long-standing and responsible.  She sells her crafts and clothes door to door.  Alicia buys her merchandise in the city of Santiago since the prices there are better for her business.    Alicia lives with her husband and her 10 year-old grandson who she has cared for since he was born because her daughter went off to work in another city and didn't take responsibility for him as his mother.  For this reason, Alicia has had to raise and educate her grandson.  This is her motivation to continue in her business: she would like to provide her grandson with a better quality of life and an education.  She will use her loan to buy clothes for the winter season.  Alicia's dream is to own a car in order to distribute her merchandise to more rural areas.  Right now, she transports her products on a bicycle.  However, during the winter, this task becomes difficult because of the cold and rain in the city.  With a car, she would be able to increase her customer base and, consequently, her profits.  Alicia is very grateful and happy to be working with Fondo Esperanza.  She really enjoys the group meetings because the other entrepreneurs are all responsible.  Alicia is the community bank's representative.  As regards the loans that she receives through Fondo Esperanza, they have been a great support for her business since they have enabled her to invest and increase her income.  Casablanca is a town which is located in Valparaíso province, in the region of the same name.  It has a Mediterranean climate, with summers of prolonged drought and short, heavy, winter rains.  The name 'Casablanca' (literally: 'white house') dates from the 16th Century when there was a 'wall with whitish walls' located on a hillside, at the side of one of the oldest roads in the area called 'Camino Real de Carretas'.  Casablanca's economy is currently based on the service industry, agriculture, transport, agroindustry, tourism and commerce.

name: Zulema
description: Zulema, age 25, is a very unassuming and hard-working mother.  She lives in a rented house with her 26 year old husband, Héctor, and their only child, three year old Sharmely.  They are the motivation for all of her efforts.  Since she was very small Zulema learned to work on the farm with her parents.  They taught her everything about this activity.  Now, she only has land where she plants and produces peas, potatoes, and carrots.  She takes them the wholesale market in Tarma to sell.  What she likes the most about her work is harvesting because she receives the recompense for so many months of hard work.  She has been working like this in the fields for four years.  She considers the most difficult part to be taking care of her crops so that the pests do not affect their development.  In time she plans to buy more land to increase her production.  This is her second loan with MFP.  She knows that she has to make her payments punctually, and she is prepared to do so.  In her communal bank she is a very happy member who is always adding humor to the group.    She will use the requested 500 soles to buy more fertilizer for her crops.  Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Ricamar  Sr.
description: Ricamar Sr. has a mango farm in Aloran. This is his primary source of income for his family. Ricamar  Sr. makes it a point to have good land preparation to have maximum yield and good income. Recently, he needed money to purchase herbicides for growing mangoes and to pay for labor costs for preparing his land. He asked PMPC for the loan. Ricamar Sr. wishes to sustain his business and be able to supply mangoes to fruit stands in neighboring towns.

name: Elias
description: Elias Jilmer, age 40, lives with his wife and children in the village of El Frayle.  It is a rural zone in the Santo Tomas district.  The community has a varied climate and abundant vegetation.  The population works in agriculture, commerce, and with livestock.  It is in the Cutervo Province in the Región Cajamarca in the northern highlands of Peru.  He is engaged in farming and marketing of cattle ranching, has thirteen cattle property, has planted three hectares of his greenhouse where he raises cattle for 20 years, and is also dedicated to the cultivation of corn. He has a close family that works hard. He has requested a loan of 3000 soles to purchase bulls for fattening and then offer them at a better price.

name: Mujeres Unidas 1 & 2 Group
description: Groups 1 and 2 from the Mujeres Unidas Bank of Hope are ready to start their second loan cycle through Esperanza International. The group members all live in Villa Mella, which is located in the northern outskirts of Santo Domingo, which is Dominican Republic’s capital city. Evelyn R. and Josue A. are the group coordinators. Evelyn has five children. The youngest is 12 years old. All her children still live with her. She sells shoes, which she purchases in Dajabon (a city in the northwest of the Dominican Republic, which is about a 5 ½ hour ride from Santo Domingo) as well as in the capital. With this loan, she will buy mostly tennis shoes and sandals. She explains that depending on the time of year, sales increase on a certain kind of shoe (for example, loafers during back-to-school time). Evelyn hopes her profits from selling shoes will allow her to buy a house of her own. This would let her have a more peaceful life. Josue has four children of ages 10, 8, 6 and 3. His current business is selling clothes. He finds greater demand for women’s clothing. Lately, however, he has noticed that people are not buying as much as usual. He will use this second loan to purchase new clothes to sell. During his interview, he commented that he likes the fact that because all the members of his group paid their first loan on time, Esperanza International approved higher loan amounts for them in this second loan cycle. He hopes to continue that trend so he can invest larger amounts in his business and create sustainable growth. Thank you for supporting these entrepreneurs!

name: Maria Angelica
description: María is 40 years old. She is single and has no children. She lives with her sister in the city of Guaranda, province of Bolívar.  She is a member of the Los Pinos communal bank. It is made up of 14 members from the same community. They work in agriculture and are 40 minutes from the Pangua community office.  María works in agriculture, growing potatoes and raising livestock. She is asking for the loan to buy an animal. With the help of the loan, she will be able to increase the number of animals she has. She will make the purchase in the city of Guaranda. The challenges she faces are health problems.   Her dream is to improve in the next 5 years. In her free time, she likes to rest at home and go out.

name: Chap's Group
description: Chap’s group lives in a rural village in Siem Reap province in Cambodia. Chap does work as a farmer to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses, and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Bazaroy
description: Bazaroy is a kind and happy woman. She is 46 years old and married. Bazaroy has a large and close-knit family consisting of her husband, their children and their grandchildren. Their family values mutual understanding, diplomacy and respect for one another, which is especially important for such a large family. Bazaroy's family lives in the Qubadiyon District. To support a large family is difficult, so Bazaroy decided to make her own contribution to the family budget. She is going to practice livestock breeding at her home. Her whole family will help her with this. However, she needs a certain amount of money to start this business and use to buy calves and bull calves. Because she does not have enough money for this, she is requesting a loan.

name: Emma
description: As a married mother of six children, Emma works hard to support her family.  She sells charcoal in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from raising livestock and soft drink retailing. Emma is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to purchase more firewood and charcoal to sell.  Emma has been sustaining her business activities through her past 29 loans from NWTF and more recently, through Kiva. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: Faustina
description: Faustina is divorced and has 4 children. She has received schooling through first level. Ekua Faustina sells provisions and koko (maize porridge) at Dompoase, which she has done for  6 years. With the income from her business, Faustina pays her children’s school fees as well as other household expenses. Faustina will use the loan to purchase provisions like milk, Milo, bread, and soft drinks, as well as maize.  With the new profits, Ekua plans to to continue to expand her business.

name: Rowena
description: "Behind the clouds, the sun is still shining," says Rowena as she sees hope behind all hardships in life that her family is experiencing nowadays. She is already married but she has no children yet. Having a big family is what she dreams of. So far, the couple is focused on improving their businesses.They happily lives in the peaceful village of La Salette.   She is engaged in hog raising. The profit earned from selling grown-up hogs made it possible for her to build her new variety store, which she now manages. Her husband is in full support of her businesses and they hope that they will be able to further expand those.   Rowena is requesting a loan of 18,000 Philippine pesos for the growth of her businesses buying feed, vitamins and grocery items. This amount will be of big benefit especially to her general store, which is starting to grow. She hopes that her loan will be granted.

name: Kenneth
description: Kenneth is married with 3 children and lives in Kyenjojo, Uganda. He deals in the buying and selling of maize, millet, and beans.   Kenneth earns other income from rearing cattle and growing maize. He began his business in order to improve his standard of living and to buy a motorcycle to ease the transport of his produce. However limited capital is still a challenge.  Kenneth will use his loan to buy maize for resale.

name: Aisha
description: Aisha is married and has five children, all of whom are in school. She lives in a home that she rents; she has access to electricity but not to piped water. Her major monthly expenses include school fees, rent and utility bills.  Aisha sells charcoal. She has done so for ten years, and she works seven days a week. Aisha sells her charcoal at retail prices from her home. She also sells tomatoes. The main business challenges for Aisha include thieves and tomato seasonality.  Aisha has requested a loan of 300,000 UGX from MCDT SACCO, which she will use to buy more bags of charcoal. Her goals and aspirations for her business are to start going directly to villages for her charcoal and to sell at wholesale only.

name: Lucio
description: Lucio is a 43 year old widower who has five children aged 22, 16, 15, 12 and 7 years old. He works as a fisherman. He is s good father, enterprising, independent, consistent, responsible and hard-working. His business takes place in ‘Utavicullaguani’ by the sacred Lake Titicaca, an agricultural area where they also raise cattle sheep and members of the llama family. He lives from fishing and also from grains and vegetables of the area like quinoa and chuno (dried potatoes), beams, potatoes. etc. It is characterized by a cold and dry climate with a temperature that varies between 1 to 12 degrees Celsius and where the sun's ray strike the earth's surface with force. Lucio is short, dark-skinned with short black hair. He speaks Aymara and speaks Spanish for business. He shares his life with his children who take care of the agriculture and go to school. His oldest son is independent. He lives in a house made out of adobe with a reed roof that has electricity and a well. His business is fishing with a boat and a net. The fishing on Lake Titicaca is one of the most beautiful fishing arts, small scale and respectful of the lake and the maritime treasures it has. This art consists of throwing in a line of net that is about 30 meters long. The net settles to the bottom where it is left for a day to act as a trap. Then it is collected, making sure it is not dragged ruining the lake floor, only trapping the pieces that are the size of the netting and fishing only the species desired. The "wallage" (local food) has an important fish ingredient that gives it flavor and is called "karachi", he comments. His dream is to have a fish store. He wants to buy a fishing boat as the one he has is old and is no longer safe. He will also buy fishing nets as his are damaged and need repairing. This is his first loan with the institution in the 28 years he has been in this business.  For these reasons Lucio is requesting a loan to buy a fishing boat and nets.

name: Luvisminda
description: As a married parent of 6 children, Luvisminda works hard to support her family. She has a buying and selling fermented shrimps business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from buying and selling dried fish.   She is borrowing PHP 29,500 through NWTF to purchase additional stocks of fermented shrimps. She has been sustaining her business activities through her past 28 loans from NWTF. Luvisminda hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: San Martin Group
description: San Martin is one of the groups that pays their installments on time. The members of this group feel very satisfied to be in their sixth cycle.   Lucila is 55 years old. She is single and has two adult children. She has been selling beauty products by catalog for many years and she also works as a cook in a local restaurant. Lucila's project is to open a store in her home in order to obtain better income. She will invest this loan in purchasing fragrances and jewelry sets that are on sale in order to sell them at a higher price and obtain a higher profit.   The group is grateful to Kiva lenders for this loan. Lucila is the second person from the right. The top portion shows Percy, who wasn't able to be present for work-related reasons.

name: Phearun's Group
description: Phearun’s Group lives in a rural village in Kandal province in Cambodia. Phearun makes a living cultivating rice and he also does extra work as a factory laborer and an officer to support his family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of this woman and  this man to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Betty
description: Betty, 30, is a mother of three children. She is married and lives in Buchanan. Her children are between the ages of three and seven - one lives with her and the other two live with their aunt.   Betty has a table in the market where she has been selling for the past fifteen years. She sells chains, earrings and lappers (local cloth). She learned to sell from her aunt. Because of the way she interacts with her customers, and the quality material that she sells, she makes profits every day. One of the difficulties that she faces is lack of commodities.   She is requesting a loan to purchase more lappers, chains and earrings to increase her sales. Her plan is to educate her children.

name: Teresiah
description: Teresiah is a woman of 29 years, married to James, and a mother of two children. She sells fruits. She has been in this business for 12 years now and gets monthly income of thirty thousand shillings.  This will be Teresiah's first loan with Kenya Agency for Development of Enterprise and Technology (KADET). She plans to use the entire loan to buy different types of fruits to sell. In the future, she wants to expand her business and feed and educate her children.

name: María Virginia
description: María Virginia is a Kubo Financiero client and this is her story:  María is 56 years old, is married and has no economic dependents anymore. She makes a living by confectioning leather articles, specifically cosmetic bags and pencil cases which she sells in downtown Mexico City.  She started to be involved in this business when three years ago her son unfortunately passed away; he ran the workshop so she took over. She asks for this loan to buy more commodities to work more merchandise and be able to supply the demand that the return to school season will bring.  With the effort she puts into her work María likes to decorate her house with articles she likes and aspires to keep on growing the business and increase her income.

name: Ahmadali
description: Ahmadali is a resident of the city of Istaravshan.  He is 35 years old, married and has four children.  Ahmadali's wife is a homemaker.  He is involved in animal husbandry.  He has been in this business for ten years.  Ahmadali is requesting this loan to buy bulls and calves.

name: Juliana Janet
description: Juliana is 37 years old. She lives with her husband and their two marvelous children, whom Juliana loves very much. She works hard and makes sacrifices in order to provide them with a better quality of life and better opportunities. Juliana was only able to complete three years of a high school education, so now she works very hard so that her children will have a better future.   Day to day, Juliana works as a farmer. Currently, she grows potatoes, a native plant to Peru that is delicious and used in many typical dishes. Juliana works about 10 hours each day, especially Monday through Friday since she tries to spend the weekends with her family. Juliana believes that she is getting ahead because she is very responsible and has faith in God.   Juliana is very grateful to Kiva lenders for the great support offered to her. With this loan, she will be able to buy compost and fertilizers for her crops as well as pay to irrigate and plough her land. This will help improve Juliana's crops, which will improve her sales so that she can keep working toward turning her dream of "giving her children the education to enter a good profession and to have her own plot of land" into a reality.

name: Tâm
description: Tình is 36 years old and she is married with 3 children. She has a manufacturing business making mesh nets. Tình has been involved in this business for more than 10 years.  Tình lives with 3 dependents in Hoang Hoa district, a  rural town in Thanh Hoa province.  This is Tình's first loan with Thanh Hoa Fund of Poor Women.  The main harship that Tình faces in her life is not having a water tank and water filter. She is requesting a loan to buy a water tank and clean water filter. With her business profits, Tình hopes to remodel her house, to maintain a successful business, and for her business to do well.

name: Marta
description: Marta is a member of 'Creación' community bank in the town of Chillán.  She has had a stationery store, book store and small goods store in her house for 4 months.  She has also been making shower curtains and sheets for some time.  With this loan she will travel to Santiago, the capital of Chile, to buy goods, that is to say material and articles to replace products in her stationery store such as, for example, silicone glue and little sticks for making scale models.  Her dream is to grow her business and she has her husband's support in this.  She has 3 children but only the youngest who is 22 and studying graphic design at University lives with her.  For Marta, working with Fondo Esperanza has been very good, not only for the loans but also for the pleasant time which she spends with her fellow group members and the Fondo Esperanza advisor.  Chillán is a district in the 'centro sur' (south central) region of Chile.  The name means “Silla del Sol” (Sun's Chair) in Mapudungun, the language of the Mapuche, our indigenous inhabitants.  Chillán is known as “Cuna de la Patria” (Birthplace of the Nation) or “Tierra de Artistas” (Land of Artists) owing to the fact that it is the birthplace of a number of prominent characters in Chile's history such as, for example, the well-known pianist Claudio Arrau.

name: Yasmin
description: Ms. Yasmin is a married woman with four children. She has been engaged in the business of livestock for eight years. She sells milk and desi ghee (clarified butter).   By making extra effort, she makes yogurt from the extra milk and extracts desi ghee from it. This gives her more monetary benefit as compared to selling milk. She efficiently manages her expenses with sales of milk and desi ghee.  Her husband also assists her in looking after her cattle.   Yasmin is providing education to all her children. She always wants to give better food, basic necessities and education to her children.  To make better conditions for her household, she desires to enhance her business by buying one more buffalo. For raising money, she came to know about Kashf Foundation. Kashf Foundation has scrutinized her business condition and after gauging her motivation and hard work, approved a loan amount of Rs. 20,000.

name: Yusufjon
description: Yusufjon S. is 38 years old. He is married and the father of 4 children. He recently returned from working in Russia, since his construction team was slashed and he was left without work. Since there is no work in the village Yusufjon wants to expand his herd of livestock. He enjoys animal husbandry. His wife works as a milker at a local farm and helps her husband in her spare time.   Translated from Russian by Anna Brown, Kiva Volunteer

name: Martha
description: Martha works at a car wash in San Sebastian, where it costs 2.50 soles for small cars, 4 soles for bigger cars and 8 soles for trucks for a wash. She washes 30 – 35 per day. She will use this loan to buy things for her house like a wardrobe, which may cost close to 300 soles.  Martha is 34 years old and lives with her partner and two children – one is in third grade and the other is in 8th grade. She is a client of Asociación Arariwa and part of a communal bank consisting of 26 members in Cusco. The group is called "El Amanecer", which means "Daybreak" in Spanish. She is from Cusco and lives in Cusco.   Martha appreciates, and thanks you for, the loan and promises to make the monthly payments on time.

name: Ahmad Alhaji
description: Ahmad Alhaji is a Babban Gona farmer from Sabon Gari Village. Ahmad Alhaji joined Babban Gona to become a better farmer. Through Babban Gona’s input loan, Ahmad Alhaji will have access to top-of-the-range farm inputs such as fertilizers, herbicides, and improved seeds. This loan will help him earn yields of up to 30 bags of maize per hectare, double the 14 bags per hectare earned by the average Nigerian smallholder maize farmer. With the opportunity to earn high yields and increase his net income, Ahmad Alhaji would like to use his extra earnings to acquire more land to put innto Babban Gona program.

name: Luz
description: For several years Luz N. has been well known for being an excellent seamstress.  Her establishment is located in the municipality of Ciudad Sandino in the city of Managua.  She has stood out due to the fact that she has learned to make all kinds of suits in addition to shirts, pants, blouses, etc.  The situation that she finds herself in today is that she needs to buy materials to continue working and they include scissors, thread, fabric, needles, measuring tape, etc.  For this reason she hopes that Ceprodel will give her a loan in order to buy these materials and so that she benefits from her business.   Translated from Spanish by Hugh Yarbrough, Kiva Volunteer

name: Juliana
description: Juliana is 54 years old and married to Rogelio. She has six children and all have settled into marriage and live separately from them. They have no other source of income except corn production.   Juliana is getting older but still aims to achieve financial independence. According to her, she is still strong to work. She usually earns an income twice a year for about P30,000 per harvest season. It usually falls during the month of March and October. She is now asking for a loan of PHP 35,000 to buy corn seeds, fertilizers and insecticides used in farming. She would like to improve her output to save for future emergencies. She doesn't want to rely on her children's remittances so at her age, she still generates an income.

name: María
description: María is 33 years old, married, manages a food pantry, and raises pigs.  Her husband works as a traveling merchant.  They have three young children who attend school and are financially dependent on them.  María is an enterprising and independent woman who started her own business ten years ago so that she could increase her income and provide her family with a better standard of living.  She has the support of her husband and always tries to resolve any complications that arise in her field of work.  There is currently a good demand for pork, so María wants to buy pigs and feed for her animals.  Working in this field gives her a good perspective.  She also needs to build a solid pig sty so that the animals do not interfere with her other activities.  This will enable her to work by herself when it comes time to feed the pigs.  María wants to invest in this activity because she has a great desire to make progress. Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Janet
description: Fifteen years ago Janet started farming on a small inherited piece of land in Mikinduri, a remote village in the Nkubu area of Kenya. Today, this humble mother of four children sells milk, eggs, maize and a variety of food crops. She is a passionate farmer and, because of the immense knowledge she has on farming, she commands a lot of respect from other farmers in her village. Dairy farming is close to her heart and every day she wakes up to milk her cow and that makes her very proud. Although she makes profits through milk selling, she lacks a proper dairy unit so she is seeking a loan to build a modern dairy unit. Through the loan she will have a humble time milking her cow and also feeding. A good dairy unit provides a good place where cows can relax and also prevent them from getting diseases that may arise because of being exposed to harsh weather conditions such as rain. Janet believes that through this loan her living conditions will change because she is going to have an increase in milk production. She will save money that she used to spend on treating her cows because she lacked a good dairy unit. With your contribution, this honest and humble mum will be able to achieve her dreams. Come on, make a loan.

name: Marvin
description: Marvin C. is from the village of Brgy. Bonfal East, Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya. He is 28 years old. Marvin is married and has two infant-aged children. To make a living, Marvin owns & operates a business cultivating coconut trees & harvesting its fruit for sale. Marvin has been engaged in his business for over four years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Marvin joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Marvin has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5,000 PHP from ASKI. This previous loan was used to pay for services to increase the crop yield. Marvin is requesting a new loan of 7,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase harvesting equipment. This loan will be the second loan taken out by Marvin from ASKI.
