He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of his family.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 29 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Samuel
description: Samuel is 44 years old and married to Maria. The couple is blessed with three children ages one, four, and eight. Samuel is from Nakuru. For the last 13 years, he has been a butcher and his monthly income right now is 20,000 KES.   Samuel is requesting a 30,000 KES loan from KADET LTD to buy some goats to slaughter and sell the meat to his customers. This will be his second loan. Samuel is planning to use the anticipated profit from his loan to educate his children and repay his loan. In the future, he hopes to expand into animal sales.

name: Lorna
description: Lorna C. is from the village of Poblacion, Siayan, Zamboanga del Norte. She is 48 years old, is married, and has two school-aged children.  Lorna owns and operates a general store. This is not the only means for generating revenue since the main source of income for the family comes primarily from the income of her husband as a farmer. Lorna has been engaged in her business for ten years and earns approximately 6,000 PHP a month.  In 2009, Lorna joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 3,000 PHP from PMPC. This previous loan was used to purchase additional products to sell.  Lorna is requesting a new loan of 25,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional inventory, used as working capital and, most especially, used for the education of her two children. This loan will be her 4th from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand her business and for the future of her children.   About PMPC: Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.    *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Soso
description: Soso J. is currently in the business of selling green vegetables such okra and cabbages. She is requesting a loan so she can stock fish to sell.   Soso is 35 years old and is married. Her husband is a businessman. She has five children who are all in school.  With the profits from her loan, she hopes to expand her business.

name: Annie
description: Annie is 49 years old and lives in Buchanan along with six children between the ages of 16 and 26 and her husband. She been selling oil and fufu (an African food made of cassava) for the past eleven years. She is requesting a loan to purchase more oil and fufu for her business, She hopes to build a house.

name: Damzoussi Group
description: Ousmane is the representative of the Damzoussi 01 Saponé group.  He is single, with no children.  He has one person in his care.  He has been raising livestock for two years.  He buys his animals in a village called Ipelcé.    At the moment, he wants to buy eight goats.  He wants to save his profits so as to re-invest in his activity.  He wants to get married, take care of his family, and expand his business.

name: Ndeye Soce
description: Mrs. Ndeye Soce S. is a 46-year-old woman who lives in the Ngaparou section of the Yoff area (Dakar). She is married, the mother of a 14-year-old, who also supports five other people. She has been a member of the U-IMCEC bank since February 2004 and has already received a loan. Mrs. S. has been developing an ice cream and breakfast business for ten years. She has a stall facing the Yoff bank. She chose this business because she has always wanted to live without depending on others. Thus with her profits she would be able to take care of her own personal needs. What interests her most about this business is interacting with her customers whom she enjoys, but also making a profit. She is seeking a loan of 50,000frs and looking to build up her working operating in order to buy several products for the breakfasts she sells. She also plans to equip her stall by purchasing several local benches and tables which would allow her customers to sit comfortably. Thus she is asking for a loan of 50,000frs, and the increased income would give her a bit of help with the daily expenses of her husband. Continuing with its focus on active participation in the fight against poverty, with the positive backing of lenders the U-IMCEC succeeds in supporting populations in operating profitable, income-generating businesses, which promotes valued socio-economic development. Translated from French by Robin Clochard, Kiva Volunteer

name: Lucia
description: As a married parent of three children, Lucia works hard to support her family.She has a food vending business in the Philippines, and she also earns additional income from a general store.  Lucia is borrowing PHP 20,000 through NWTF to purchase ingredients like meat, frozen foods, spices, seasonings, etc. for her food vending business.Lucia has been sustaining her business activities through her past seven loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Christine
description: Christine is a single mother of four children and two of her children go to school. She doesn’t take care of additional family members. She has a business of selling used shoes and has applied for loan of 900000 Uganda shillings from MCDT-SACCO to buy more bales of used shoes. She has been with this business for 14 years working six days out of every week and selling on a retail basis and moves door to door selling used clothes. Her major business challenges include seasonality and thieves. She is aspiring to get a permanent business premise and also to become a wholesaler. She resides in a rented house and the family has access to electricity and piped water. Her monthly expenses include school fees and rent.

name: Georgia
description: Georgia walked past a shabby hair salon in San Francisco’s Mission District almost every day for twelve years without giving it a second glance; it was a far cry from the spaces where she worked as a hair stylist.  Over the years, Georgia has paid other business owners considerable monthly fees to rent chairs in their plush salons. Last year she grew tired of sharing her earnings with salons that did not share her vision. She declared, “I want do something innovative, fun and my own…it is my turn.”  One day, rather than just passing by the shabby hair salon, Georgia marched in and asked to buy the space. From this bold move, “Pretty Pretty Collective” was born.  It is no secret that Georgia loves to create fantasy and imagery. She grew up in England and Canada, left home when she was 14, and has been styling and modeling ever since. Georgia’s vision for “Pretty Pretty Collective” is to create an imaginative venue where she can style clients during the day.  In addition to serving her own client base, Georgia will proudly rent out the space to five other stylists who share her passion and her vision. To help keep overhead costs low and to maximize the real estate, at night the space will transform into a setting for art shows and fundraisers featuring local artists and popular neighborhood vendors. She hopes to host a fundraiser for her son’s school, which, like other schools across California, faces serious budget cuts.  Upon purchasing the salon space last year, a friend referred her to the small business section in City Hall where she found Women’s Initiative for Self Employment, and Opportunity Fund. Georgia will use this $10,000 loan from Opportunity Fund to become an authorized vendor of the Bumble and Bumble product lines and to purchase salon furniture.

name: John M
description: Presented to you in the photo is John, a plumber at a sugar producing company in Sierra Leone. The 52-year-old plumber is married to a businesswoman, and the couple have five children, who are attending secondary schools. John has been working at the sugar company for nine years. With this loan, John is going to buy building materials, including corrugated iron sheets, cement and nails, to build house for his family.

name: Erlinda
description: Erlinda G. is from the village of Sinamar, Roxas, Isabela. She is 58 years old and married. To make a living, Erlinda owns and operates a business venture in the agriculture sector raising crops. The main source of income comes from planting and harvesting corn for sale. Erlinda has been engaged in her business for over 25 years and earns approximately 9000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2007, Erlinda joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Erlinda has successfully repaid a previous loan of 33000 PHP from ASKI. This previous loan was used to purchase fertilizer, such as manure. Erlinda is requesting a new loan of 35000 PHP that will be used to purchase additional seeds and seedlings. This loan will be the 8th loan taken out by Erlinda from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to financially support the immediate members of her family.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 38 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Manzurakhon
description: Manzurakhon lives in Dushanbe. She is 39 years old, divorced, and has three children. She lives with her parents. Manzurahon has a secondary education. She has been sewing for more than fifteen years.  Basically she sews traditional dresses. She is taking out a loan to buy fabric.

name: Raymond
description: When Raymond suffered a serious injury, he realized that the traditional first aid kit is lacking technology that allows people to easily and efficiently analyze an injury, alert the appropriate facilities, and handle the injury to the best of their abilities until the paramedics arrive. A molecular biologist from Ghana, Raymond decided to use his expertise to create a solution. Raymond established CuraKit, and is launching his first product, the “Mobile External Diagnostic Integrated Kit” (MeDiK).  MeDiK is a mobile electronic device that can be used as a first aid response. It essentially combines several first-responder resources into one device. The compact device will be used to record and provide information at the scene of an emergency. It will be able to take blood samples, provide oxygen, locate nearby emergency personnel, and will contain medical supplies such as gauze.   “I wish to use my quantitative strengths to design products that meet the needs of the sporting industry and families.”   However, in order to complete his vision, Raymond needs to source parts and test his product. Help Raymond improve his product so that he is able to help save lives.

name: Guillermo
description: Guillermo is a young man with plenty of energy and the will to take on the world and better himself. He would like to start a business selling cheese and milk. With this business, he would be able to obtain income in order to be able to contribute to his household.He is a very determined young man; he is in school and has the desire to support himself and be a professional.He is requesting a loan for the purchase of a motorcycle, which he will use to deliver cargo and cheese orders.With this loan, he can fulfill his dream of being independent and giving his mother everything she needs, in addition to being able to pay for his education and progressing thanks to the support of Kiva and the Interactuar Corporation.Support this young Colombian entrepreneur's plan!

name: Everlina
description: Everlina is 37 years old and married with two children.   Everlina works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines.  She has been running the general store for 5 years and also earns an income from pig fattening.  Everlina requested a PHP 15000 loan through NWTF to buy additional items like cooking oil, soft-drinks, beers, biscuits, noodles, detergent soap, shampoo, etc. to sell.  She has borrowed and paid 7 loans from NWTF before this loan.     Everlina aspires to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Jane's Group
description: Jane B. is from the village of Alimannao, Penablanca, Cagayan. She is 28 years old. Jane is the group leader of a 6-member group loan offered by ASKI. While each member of the group receives an individual loan, they are all collectively responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults.  Jane is married and has 2 very young children. To make a living, Jane works in a family member's business venture in the food sector making & selling food. The main source of income for the business comes from preparing and selling cooked food for daily meals. Jane has been engaged in her business for over 2 years and earns approximately 1,800 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Jane joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Jane has successfully repaid a previous loan of 10,000 PHP from ASKI. Jane is requesting a new loan of 10,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional inventory and as working capital. This will be the third loan taken out by Jane from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to financially support immediate members of her family.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful micro-finance institutions in the Philippines. It has 25 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly made up of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Armen
description: Armen lives in Nor Kharberd village with his elderly retired parents, wife and two kids.  Armen is a 49 years old hairdresser. He has been involved in this service for ten years and is well known among people living in the region. Armen owns a small space which he uses as a beauty salon. He is the only hairdresser there, so he has to work hard to manage to serve all clients coming to the salon.  Realizing that the gathered professional skills and experience allow him to enlarge his business, Armen has applied for this loan. He asks lenders to support him to  pay for renovation of the salon and purchase tools for providing hairdressing services (hair dryer, accessories, paints).  His loan has been approved within the framework of a new joint initiative between Kiva and SEF International. This program provides business start-up loans to informal businesses that do not qualify through normal channels.   Armen hopes for lenders' support to his small but perspective business.

name: Abdujalil
description: Abdujalil lives in Tursun-Zoda. He is 43 years old and has a wife and three children. Abdujalil has a high school degree and works as a farmer. He has a plot of irrigated land where he grows potatoes and rice. He is an experienced farmer and has been working for 11 years. He is taking out this loan to purchase fertilizer for his potato and rice crops. He hopes to be able to collect a big harvest and use the profits from the sale to pay for the wedding of his eldest son.

name: Urafiki Group
description: Ghati, who is in her early 30s, is single with two daughters who are in school. For a period of 13 years now, Ghati has been engaged with two different businesses. She sells charcoal and she is also a tailor. She does her business from 7:30 am to 6:00 pm daily and is able to make a small monthly profit.   This is Ghati's third loan request from Tujijenge Tanzania. She used her previous loans to increase her stock of charcoal so as to meet her client demand. She has paid back all of her previous loans successfully. She used her profit to pay for school fees and household expenses.  She will use this loan to buy sacks of charcoal and tailoring materials for her business. She dreams of expanding her business.  Ghati will share this loan with her loan group  "Urafiki" which consists of four members who will hold each other accountable for paying back the loan.

name: Mujeres Luchadoras De San Lorenzo Group
description: This committee of women named, “The Women in the Fight,” has worked hard to ensure the safety and health of their families. They are all friends and neighbors and, together, they work to take out a loan, but they also plan activities with all of their families. These women have come together to celebrate birthdays and support each other in pregnancy, births, and through the ups and downs of their businesses.   Together, they are asking for a loan to invest in their different businesses, buying clothing, foods items, cosmetics, refreshments, and household items. They support each other and make sure that all of their loan payments are done on time.

name: Francisca
description: Maria Francisca, 56, is a mother; her address is in a settlement along the León-Managua highway.  She makes handmade handicrafts at home.  She has been in this line of work for 16 years because she needed to provide her family with economic stability and provide her children with an education.  Her husband helps her make the items and then they go out to sell them; sometimes customers come by their house to buy.  She will use the funds to buy raw materials to make clay items to sell.  Her wish is to have enough funds to work with her own capital and provide economic stability for her family.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Adeline
description: Adeline is 46 years old and is married with four children. She sells sarongs of various colors. She is requesting the loan amount of 100,000 NGN to purchase more sarongs to sell. She is grateful to all Kiva lenders.

name: Chinh
description: Chinh is 35 years old and has two school-aged children. She runs a small grocery shop that opened 12 years ago.   Chinh is requesting a loan for 9,184,000 VND to buy more new products to meet the demand of customers. She joined SEDA in 2008 and used loans for expanding her shop.

name: Fortaleza Group
description: The Fortaleza Group is in its first cycle of the Women's Committee Program, where they all help each other to get ahead. They are doing the "Poverty Stoplight" program in order to be able to strive to improve their living conditions.One of the members is Maria who earns a living selling natural remedies, which allows her to be able to support her family in a modest and humble way. She is proud of what she does since it allows her to help her family as best she can.Maria is requesting a loan to buy remedies such as saffron, mint, lemon verbena, tarope, cat's claw, horsetail, wormwood, rosemary, white mallow, and others in order to offer her customers a fresh variety. With a daily effort she will be able to improve her family's level of life.

name: Amelita
description: "Amelita O. is a married woman who lives in Tikoy, Brgy. Bogo, Argao, Cebu. She earns her living by operating a business venture: raising pigs . Her husband Pedro O., who is 37 years old, works as a Tricycle Driver to earn his living, and also helps in his wife's business activities.  They have 4 children who are between 4 to 12 years old.   Amelita joined NWTF-Project Dungganon in 2007 because she aspired for something better for her family. With the help of her past 4 loans from NWTF-Project Dungganon, Amelita has been incrementally lifting her family out of poverty by the sweat of her brow. Her previous loan of PHP 10,000 helped her earn a monthly profit of PHP 3,200, uplifting the family's standard of living.  This time, for her 5th loan, she is borrowing PHP 11,000, which she intends to use to fund her business activity so that she could continue to save up for the future education of her children and for business diversification. Amelita O. is a Dungganon woman who is following an honorable path toward the achievement of her dreams.   About NWTF:  In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means Honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress from earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem that is bestowed to a member of a community who has earned the respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work. Help NWTF continue its mission to help the poorest in the Philippines by clicking  the link to the   NWTF Kiva lending team  on Kiva.org to join our team.

name: Anecita
description: Anecita is 49 years old and lives in Becor,Taboo,Jimenez. She is married with four children.  She does not have a business and is a housewife. She has a requested a loan to purchase additional housing materials. Anecita has been a member of PMPC for 8 years. In the future, Anecita hopes to save for future consumption.

name: Heherson
description: Heherson is married and has three children. His wife is a housekeeper who is taking care of their kids. Heherson is engaged in growing rice in their field. He shares that farm work is not easy to perform, if you have not enough experience in farming. But, even for him it’s hard to make it. He needs to do it because it is his family’s source of living. His generating income from farming business helps him provide his family’s necessities. Heherson depends only on borrowing money from the traders in able to operate his farm. With this, Heherson decided to borrow a loan of PHP 50,000 to buy farm inputs such as fertilizers, herbicides, and pesticides. He chose ASKI in acquiring a loan because he knows they will help him financially, and for having a low interest.

name: Rukia
description: Rukia is 24 years old and lives in the town of Kaliro in the Iganga region of Uganda. She is married and has 3 children, with 1 of them currently in school.   For the past 3 years, Rukia has been working hard to manage her grocery store, which sells things like sugar, cooking oil and other home use items.   To help expand her business, Rukia has requested a loan of 200000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to to buy more items that will attract more customers at her grocery store, and will help Rukia to generate greater profits and see her children go in better schools. Rukia hopes that in the future she will be able to enlarge her grocery shop into a whole sell shop so as to get more profits to sustain her family needs.   Rukia is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities, and a forum for life-skills training

name: La Sagesse Group
description: The affiliate Genevieve is a merchant, treasurer and member of "La Sagesse" community group. She is a dynamic, 50-year-old entrepreneur, and a divorced mother of three children, one of whom attends school and the other two are still infants.  The affiliate sells beverages, and displays her goods at a stand in one of the city's streets. She started her business with the help of her former husband.  Later, she was granted a loan from the Hekima MFI, and has been running her business for the past 12 years. This new loan will serve to re-supply with 80 cases of Primus beer.  Her aim is to educate and feed her children. Finally, she is very thankful to  Hekima for empowering non-bankable women entrepreneurs, especially during this critical post-conflict period in the Eastern part of the country.

name: Faustina's Group
description: The group is comprised of three members who work to improve the economic stability of their homes. They live in the city of Accra-Teshie, the capital city of Ghana. It is the birthplace of great fishermen in the country.  One of the members of the group is Faustina who is in her third loan cycle with ID-Ghana. She likes the group because all the members are good friends. The loans allow her to improve her family's economic stability.  Faustina, 38, is married and has two children, ages 14 and 6. They are schooling. Her husband is also a businessman who normally assists her with sales at home. Faustina has been selling 'silver' cooking utensils for six years.  She plans to use the loan amount of GHS 1000 to buy more 'silver' products to sell to customers. Her dream is for her children to become professionals.  Faustina is standing on the far left in the photograph.

name: Loreta
description: Loreta C. is from the village of Olango. She is 48 years old. Loreta is married and has five adult-aged children. To make a living, she plants and harvests rice to sell. She has been engaged in her business for over twenty-nine years and earns approximately $1057 every harvest season.  In 2008, Loreta joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 31,000 PHP from ASKI. This previous loan was used to purchase fertilizers such as manure.   Loreta is requesting a new loan of 33,000 PHP which again will be used to purchase fertilizers. This will be her 6th loan from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to save as a reserve for future emergencies.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful micro-finance institutions in the Philippines. It has 38 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Chongwa
description: Chongwa says that thanks to the previous loan that he received from Kiva, he was able to provide better products to his customers and the business was able to grow sufficiently. He is very grateful for this support.  He is once again interested in asking for further assistance. He wants to invest again in the store to be able to stock it with more products and a variety of supplies such as chicks, feed and other supplies. He is very grateful for the new opportunity that he is receiving and it will be a great help to him.

name: Teresa
description: Teresa is married with three children. She is 42 years old and one of her children is in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. She has a food vending business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for six years.  She requested a 10,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy ingredients for her food production business.  In the future, Teresa would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: La Solidarite 3 Group
description: Marcel is the leader of la SOLIDARITE 3 group, which consists of two other micro-entrepreneurs from Brazzaville, Congo. Marcel is married and has three children, all in school. He is in his fourth loan cycle with HOPE Congo. Marcel will use the loan to purchase raw materials such as sugar, oil, salt, soap, beans, rice, biscuits and soap, which he sells at a profit. His goal is to build a house for his family, to take care of his children's studies, to travel and mostly to expand his business and open a large shop.

name: Julio Cesar
description: Julio is a 28-year-old man,  married to a loving wife. He  has a young child and is in charge of the economical support of his family. He works hard every day  to provide for his wife and child.  He likes working hard because this allows his wife to take care of their child.Julio repairs cars at his  workshop which employs two people. Julio started to fix cars at his parents'  garage, but  needed to move to a bigger place.  He has  moved ahead and succeeded with his projects.His biggest achievement is getting a business of his own and keeping his clients because of his  quality of work. His biggest goals are to increase the size of his workshop and get more clients.Julio is applying for  10,527.00 MXN  at Kiva through Kubo  to buy extra tools and a scanner (to fix the electric problems of cars).  This will allow him to keep up with the daily standards of his work.

name: Franco
description: Franco is from the city of San Ignacio, is currently studying the degree of industrial engineering, and also works as a way to pay for his studies. He is in the fourth year of his studies, and states that in the future he wishes to be able to apply everything he has learned in order to be a useful professional to others.  He is requesting this loan in order to invest it in expenses for his thesis, and in this way he will be able to keep fighting to achieve his goal to be a good professional.

name: Sogona's Group
description: Sogona, who is the tall woman with the white scarf on the left, is a member of a group of seven farmers registered with myAgro. They live and work in the village of Niaganabougou in the southwest of Bamako, Mali. Sogona, aged 58, is the mother of 17 children, of whom 10 are presently enrolled in school. The anchor of family tradition lies in agriculture, principal source of income and of food self-sufficiency for the household; agriculture also can provide self-sufficiency for her family and this moved Sogona to work in this domain for thirty years now.   Sogona grows peanuts and maize on her plot of land but as a farmer she has to cope with difficulties such as a lack of rain, of agricultural tools, and of arable land. Sogona is beginning her first year with myAgro and joined because of the system of payment and the quality seeds, as well as the certainty of the myAgro agents concerning the profit this myAgro method will bring.   This year Sogoa is making payments to buy a myAgro package of OPV (openly pollinated variety) seeds and fertilizer for growing maize so as to increase her yield on her plot of  0.125 hectare. Sogona has been growing peanuts for their commercial value for 25 years, since they are a foodstuff she can sell profitably at the market.  With the increase in her harvest and her income, Sogona plans to diversify her crops and be able to do small-scale commerce. Finally, she also hopes to cover school fees for her children and build a house for her family.

name: Rosa Maria
description: Rosa, 50, is single and very hardworking.  For a year she has had a grocery store and a restaurant where she works every day.  Her dream is to expand her store, where she sells milk, grains, vegetables, dairy products, and other items, as well as a variety of food.  Currently she is low on stock, which is detrimental because she's unable to provide a lot of products her customers request.  Because of this Rosa decided to request a loan to get more organized and buy wholesale the stock she needs: grains, sugar, cookies, and dairy products to increase her offerings and provide better customer service.  This will also mean an increase in income for her so she can cover her public services, taxes, and the basic needs of all businesses.  She will also improve her own and her mother's well-being.

name: Elidjona
description: Elidjona, a 39-year-old married mother of a 19-year-old, is requesting this loan to buy some tools/equipment for the carpentry shop in the village where she lives, that her husband has been operating since the 2000. "While my husband runs his own activity, I practice my own rural activity. Even though my village is mostly known for largest quantities of the apple and plum fruits due to the soil and climate weather being very supportive of such orchards, my focus has been planting only wheat and corn in the fifteen dynym land that my family owns. My annual gross earnings from wheat is $1,500 and from corn about $350. It's a bit hard for me because I've got no help from my husband, but I do it. As far as my husband's annual net earnings is approximately $5,000," said Elidjona.

name: Njogu
description: Njogu is a 50-year-old business man, who is married to Felista, a business lady. They are blessed with two children. He has been a tailor for the past three years, with a monthly income of KES. 20,000, which he uses to support his family.    He is applying for his third loan from KADET LTD, after repaying the previous loan successfully. Njogu will use the loan to purchase clothing materials for his business.    With the anticipated profit from the business, he will educate his children. His hopes and dreams are to open a beauty salon for his wife and improve his family's standard of living.

name: Kambua
description: Kambua is a married woman. She has three children. She describes herself to be honest. She operates a retail business where she sells fruits and vegetables. She has been involved in this business for eight years. Her business is located in an area with a good number of clients and her primary customers are individuals. She describes her biggest business challenge to be the perishability of some goods. She will use the Kes 20,000 loan to buy more stock of fruits and vegetables. Her business goal is to have different businesses within five years. She hopes that in the future, she will be a great businesswoman. This is her first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: Dania Del Rosario
description: Dania is a teacher who has been teaching for many years.  She has experience teaching elementary school children.  Her job gives her a lot of satisfaction because she is contributing her grain of sand toward the development of our country which needs it so much.  Dania's family consists of her husband and three children who are all in school.  They are a hard-working family who are responsible in meeting their obligations and carrying out their work.  This is a quality that they teach their children.  Through the effort of her work and the loans that she has received from Ceprodel, Dania has managed to improve her house a little.  Her goal is to work on the house so that it has a good environment in which she can live together with her family.  Right now, Dania's main goal is to finish improving her kitchen.  She is requesting her third loan so that she can buy bricks, cement and tiles in order to achieve her goal.  She hopes to receive Ceprodel's help as they have always reached out their hand to help her continue making progress.

name: Tiesiri Group
description: Sèba is the lady holding a daba in the group photo. She is a Malian woman married to a local farmer. She has six children aged 5 to 25, none of whom have received formal schooling. Herself illiterate, Sèba earns a living growing groundnuts during the rainy season to help support her children.   Sèba is seeking a loan from RMCR because she does not have the means or the materials needed to expand and better maintain her farmland.    Sèba will use her loan to buy groundnut seeds and fertilizers, and to pay for the labor needed to plow her field.    This being a seasonal activity, Sèba expects to earn a profit of 125,000 FCFA for the season.

name: Florinda Oliva
description: Florinda is 29-years old, married and lives with her husband and son in their own home. For 4 years now she has worked in a business selling used clothing. She sells pants, shirts, underwear, boxers, tights, t-shirts, dresses, skirts, bras, etc. Her customers are all of her friendly neighbors and the people in the neighboring communities. She is an entrepreneurial woman with wishes of getting ahead and she fights every day to improve her quality of life. Florinda is asking for a loan to buy clothing such as blouses, dresses, pants, shirts, etc. With the support of this loan, she hopes to improve her income and also her quality of life. She is a customer with hopes of working with Prisma. Her dream is to have a good business and increase her clientele, while at the same time improving her future with her family. San Lorenzo, Honduras -  October  2015.

name: Khayriniso
description: In the photo you can see Khayriniso. She is 56 years old. She is married and has three children. Her husband is a teacher. Khayriniso is an honest, friendly and pleasant woman. She works with selling rice.   Khayriniso has for a long time purchased and sold rice at the local market. She would like to expand her assortment of goods to sell. She decided to apply for a loan and use the borrowed money to purchase ropes, strings, utensils, iron chains, dog collars and other products. Selling these types of products is a new activity for her. Not long ago, she purchased only ropes and she is sure that increasing the assortment of goods will also increase her income. She extends her thanks in advance.

name: Khalid
description: Khalid is a young man living in Khanyounis, Gaza Strip. He works in the public sector, where the salary is very low and unstable. As a result of the high cost of living, he decided to  open new business, transporting goods and inventory between traders. A few years ago, Khalid Bought a new rickshaw and became well-known. He also has loyal customers.   Khalid obtained a loan from FATEN. This loan will help him to do some maintenance on his rickshaw. By taking this loan, Khalid can work more efficiently and increase his sales as well as his profits.

name: Leah
description: Leah is 30 years old and married with two children. With one child currently in school, Leah works very hard to provide for them.Leah runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 13,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell such as beverages, canned goods, junk foods, home care products, and other groceries.Leah has been in this business for four years and sells a variety of items such as beverages, rice, etc. In the future, Leah would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Karin Group
description: Jessica L. is a member of the Karin community bank.  The bank has seven members who all live in Lurigancho - Chosica district.  All of the members of this group display great courage and commitment in the businesses that they carry out.  The community bank is characterized by these traits.  Jessica L. is 36 years old and has 2 dependent children.  Four years ago she decided to set up a beauty salon.  This business has provided herself and her household with a lot of financial stability.  She started out in this business with her husband's support.  She was able to open a beauty salon in her own home.  Jessica L. has also been selling beauty products for two years.  This work has enabled her to pay for her children's education and to make improvements to her home which has been very satisfying for her.  She will invest this loan in buying beauty products and making improvements to her work premises.

name: Vision Single Ladies Self Help Group
description: The lady raising her hand is Esther. She is 41 years old, single and a mother of two children. She is a member of Vision Single Ladies Self Help Group which joined Hand in Hand Eastern Africa to benefit from enterprise development and financial management training.Esther does dairy and potato farming. She is borrowing a Kiva loan to buy dairy feed to improve milk production and hence increase her income. She will use the anticipated income to pay school fees for her children.She is very grateful to Kiva and their lenders for the support and she promises to repay her loan on time.

name: Shefa'
description: Shefa’ is a married woman who lives in Jabaa’ village near Jenin. She is only 21, but she is an ambitious woman who is looking forward to improving herself through her education. Shefa’ wants to pay the fees of her education, so she is requesting a loan of $1,300.Shefa’ is a very thankful woman, and she dreams of achieving greater success in her life.

name: Jose Eduardo
description: Mr. Eduardo D. has been in business for 6 months. "I need to buy a little bit of everything. There are things that my clients ask me for that I don't have, so they go somewhere else to buy them. I would like to have a wider selection of products since the location of my business is very good for sales. If I am able to purchase all the products that I need, my sales will increase and therefore, I''l have more income. I am requesting $1,000 to invest in my office supply and gift store business."   Translated from Spanish by Lighthouse Translations, Kiva Volunteer.  El señor José Eduardo D. tiene su negocio desde hace 6 meses. "Necesito comprar un poco de todo, hay cosas que mis clientes me piden y no las tengo en existencia, así que se van a comprarlas a otra parte, me gustaría poder tener variedad en mis productos, el lugar en donde estoy ubicado es muy bueno para las ventas si logro comprar todo lo que me hace falta tendré mas venta y por lo tanto mas ingresos Solicito $1,000.00 dlls para invertir en la tienda de papelería y regalos.

name: Emerita
description: Emerita T. is from the village of Panay, Daku, Clarin, Misamis Occidental. She is 41 years old. Emerita is married and has 5 adult children. To make a living, Emerita owns & operates a business venture in the services sector operating transportation services. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes from operating service-based services. Emerita has been engaged in her business for over 4 years and earns approximately 7000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Emerita joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Emerita has successfully repaid a previous loan of 12,500 PHP from GDMPC. Emerita is requesting a new loan of 15,000 PHP which will be used to repair existing vehicle for better service. This will be the fourth loan taken out by Emerita from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three unit offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Mubinakhon
description: S. Mubinakhon is 54 years old. She is widow and the head of the family with four children who have been the source of her strength to succeed in her business. After the death of her husband, Mubinakhon had to find ways to provide for herself and her four kids. For fifteen years she has had a small business selling the dried apricots. As a rule, she purchases apricots in the market and dries them by herself. Dried fruits, especially dried apricots, are very popular in Tajikistan. Besides, it is very good for the health.  Considering the constant demand for this kind of goods, the business of Mubinakhon is quite successful and brings stable income for the family. At the same time, Mubinakhon raises the cattle with the help of her sons. One of her dreams is that her children progress by means of their studies, for which with great sacrifice she sends them to a university that they can better their quality of life.   Today Mubinakhon requests 2000 Somoni ($600) for the term of 6 months. She is going to spend the loan for purchasing the apricots with the purpose of drying them in order increase the range of goods for selling. Also, part of the loan she will spend for purchasing small cattle.   Mubinakhon expresses her gratitude for everyone supporting her. Let’s support this woman who has a lot of courage and strength to live.

name: Faindu Group
description: Mye B. is the group leader of Faindu. He is 41 years old, married and with five children. He sells stones and sand to builders and has been running the stone mining for three years. With his first loan from SMT, he hired three laborers and was able to break more stones. The loan also enabled him to hire transport to take the stones and sand to the market and this has increased his income greatly. He would like to expand his business by hiring more laborers.  Other group members are Abibatu who sells bread and who would like a loan to purchase wheat flour and yeast on wholesale; Idrisa who owns small grocery shop; and Mariatu who sells clothes. The group is requesting a loan of Le.2,600,000 ($US900) to expand their businesses.

name: Lucy
description: Lucy is a resident of Murang’a in Central Kenya where she lives with her family of two children. She has been in the farming business for three years and currently produces milk and tea for the local market, which helps her meet her family's basic needs.  Lucy has requested a loan of 50,000 KES from Juhudi Kilimo to buy a chuff cutter. This will help ease the feeding of her dairy cow and save her more time to run other family errands. Lucy is optimistic that her dairy cows will improve their milk capacity with better feeding. She will use a larger portion of her income to educate her children. Lucy says the challenge remains rampant fluctuation in milk prices.

name: Resty
description: Resty is a single mother of four children, all attending school. She also takes care of additional family members. She sells firewood from home and has been in this business for two years. Resty has applied for a loan of 200,000 UGX from MCDT-SACCO to buy more firewood for resale. She generates additional income from selling maize. She works seven days a week. Her major business challenges include transportation and seasonality. She aspires to own a delivery van to make transportation easier. She resides in the family home, and the family has no access to electricity or piped water. Her monthly expenses include school fees and paying for utility bills.

name: Patricia
description: Patricia (“Paty”) is originally from Mexico City, Mexico and moved to the States six years ago. She has eight years of experience in the catering and food market business from her home country of Mexico and five years of experience in the States.  Paty’s business, El Sabor del Taco, specializes in making typical Mexican food such as ceviche, moles, guacamole, tamales, and fresh fruit drinks. Paty currently sells her food at a Saturday farmer’s market. The loan will help Paty expand to start selling at a second farmer’s market on Sundays. In addition to the markets, Paty also sells her moles and tamales to a local grocery store and caters to various offices and embassies in the District.   Paty will also use the loan funds to cover a year of commercial kitchen rent, design marketing materials, and purchase kitchen equipment and inventory.   Paty’s future, long-term goal is to open a Mexican restaurant in the District of Columbia.

name: Margarita Isabel
description: In the Portoviejo settlement of the Crucita parish we find a place known as “Los Arenales.”  This is where the members of the “Nueva Generación” get together every two weeks.  This place is known for its beautiful beaches, it’s food, and the warmness of its people.   Here we meet Margarita.  She is 54 years old, single and lives with her mother and sister.  She was part of the group since it began, left, and then rejoined because the loans are of great help for her business.  Our friend has been running a pub at a local school for more than 30 years, where she sells all types of products that she prepares.  She says that she only sells healthy food so that the children develop well.  She sells corviches, empanadas, chicken with rice, fruit salads, and ceviches, among other delicious things.  She also says that she tries not to sell the same things daily so that she can keep the kids happy by giving them a variety.  Now she wants to buy what she needs in order to sell lunches for the teachers who have to stay until the evenings.  She will use the money from this loan to buy ingredients to prepare her food and also fruits for juices.  Her dream is to continue giving the best to the children who are her best customers.

name: Mary
description: Mary is 65 years old, married and has 8 children. She joined Hand in Hand to benefit from the training, especially enterprise development and financial management.  She is a farmer growing spinach, cabbages, potatoes and keeps dairy cattle. She is taking a Kiva loan to buy dairy feeds, which will enable her to increase milk production, hence earn more income to meet her family's expenses.  She is grateful to Kiva and its lenders for the financial support and promises to repay the loan promptly.

name: Zablon
description: Zablon is 56 years old, married to Mary, and they are blessed with two children. He has been operating as a dairy farmer for the last 10 years and earns KES 7,500 per month.   Zablon has applied for her first loan of KES 25,000 from VisionFund Kenya to buy another dairy cow to improve his supply of milk for sale. He plans to use the generated profits to educate his children.  His future hopes are to be financially stable.

name: Janette
description: As a married parent of three children, Janette works hard to support her family.She has a food vending business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from pig fattening. Janette is borrowing PHP 11,000 through NWTF to buy ingredients like meat, cooking oil, spices, bananas, etc. for her food vending business.Janette has been sustaining her business activities through her past 3 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Rafail
description: Rafail was born in 1959. He is an Internally Displaced Person (IDP) from the Armenian-occupied territory of Azerbaijan, Fuzuli region. He is now settled in the Finnish houses in the Fuzuli region. Rafail has a sheep-breeding business and he has five years of experience in this business. Now he needs a loan of 2000 AZN to buy six sheep to improve his sheep-breeding business.

name: Sajjda
description: Sajjda is 46 years old and is a widow woman. She has 4 children; one of her sons is shown in the photo. He is a driver by profession and provides transportation services using his three-wheeled rickshaw. He has been driving a rickshaw for many years to meet the family expenses, but now it requires proper maintenance to keep it in its functional routine.   For this reason, Sajjda  has applied for a loan of 40,000 PKR, for her son. He wants to replace auto body parts and get new tires for his vehicle. This will help him drive more smoothly and provide better transport service to his passengers. Sajjda is hopeful that this loan will be a productive one for her son and will bring positive changes to his business.

name: Sam Orn
description: Som Orn, 47, is married and has four children, one of whom is still in school. Her main source of family income is from rice and cassava farming; she also supplements her income by raising pigs and catching fish to sell. She now earns less than 5 U.S. dollars a day to feed her family.  Som is requesting her first loan from VisionFund. She will use this 250 U.S.-dollar loan to buy cassava seedlings to enlarge her cassava plantation. She hopes this loan will enable her to grow more cassava so as to earn additional income to create a better life. She also hopes to set aside some savings for the future.
town: Kampong Cham province, Ponhea Krek district

name: Wahedullah
description: Wahedullah, son of Sayeed N. lives, in Nangarhar, Jalalabad. He is married and he has a spare parts shop. When he started this business for the first time, he had a small business and he was very weak, but when he got an individual loan he really improved a lot in his business and is furthering his business, attracting some good number of customers, making a good income for his family, and repaying the loan without any difficulty and on time.  Therefore, he has requested his second-cycle loan to enlarge his shop and continue his business with even more success. He is sure that he can be a good business dealer in the future.  He is happy with this loan of 50000(AF). He would like to thank both Kiva and AFS (Ariana Financial Services Joint Stock Company) and all lenders around the world who help workers and people who would like to be strong in their businesses. Finally, he wants to say that this process is a successful one in Afghanistan.

name: Mohammed
description: Mohammed is a very responsible person who is 28 years old, living in Hajah city, Yemen. He is a married man and a father of five children. He works as a solider with a small salary. He has saved part of his small salary and bought a piece of land to build a small house on that land. This cost him a lot of money. Unfortunately, he couldn't complete building the rest of the house as well as make the necessary renovations to prepare it for living. Therefore, he turned to Al-Amal Microfinance Bank and took out a loan of 100,000 YER to purchase windows and doors for his new house in order to live with his family.  Mohammed hopes to improve the living conditions of his family.

name: Leticia's Group
description: Leticia S. is from the town of Silauan Norte, Echague. She is 46 years old. Leticia is the group leader of a 5-member group loan offered by ASKI/Kiva. While each member of the group receives an individual loan, they are all collectively responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults. The official name of this borrowing group is Leticia S. Group.  Leticia is married and has 3 adult-aged children. She owns and operates a general store. The main source of income for the business comes from selling a variety of different products in the local community. Leticia has been involved in her business for over 15 years and earns approximately 4000 PHP a month from these activities.  In 2005, Leticia joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Leticia has successfully repaid a previous loan of 8000 PHP from ASKI, which was used to purchase additional products to sell. Leticia is requesting a new loan, her fifth, of 9000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 25 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Rafael Angel
description: Rafael is a member of the “Bonitas de Platanares” (Beautiful Bananas) community in P. Zeledon, San Jose province. In this zone people practice farming; the inhabitants in their majority are producers of both coffee and cattle.  Rafael is requesting a loan of 600,000 colons to buy cleaning products to sell in his general store, which is named “P.”. He tries to have on hand everything the neighbors need at the moment.  Rafael wants to expand the store so that his micro-enterprise grows daily and he can give his customers the best. His business began as a new source of income to improve the quality of life of his family, and provide a better education for his children. Rafael's goal is to be able to complete all his projects, fulfilling his expectations.  Rafael is a part of the “Empresa de Credito Comunal de las Bonitas” (Beautiful Enterprise of Communal Credit). It is his 1st loan and he tells us that being a member of this enterprise has been an excellent option for obtaining loans, since it is easier, and the processing of paperwork is faster.

name: Attila
description: Attila is a businessman from Beregovo who runs a souvenir sales business. He is a skilled craftsman who carves unique souvenirs out of wood for retail sale among tourists. Attila has been in this business for three years and currently makes about 1,500 UAH net profit each month.   Attila is seeking a loan of 6,500 UAH to purchase a house for his family. He has made some savings but needs additional lending assistance to achieve his goal. He doesn’t have a workshop and is therefore hoping to use one of the rooms in his new private house for that purpose. Attila is very diligent and focused. He strives to see his business flourish so that it will bring him a consistent income in the future.

name: Lay
description: Mrs. Lay S., 53, and her husband, Mr. Kong Bou, 51, live along National Road Number One about seventeen kilometers from Phnom Penh. They were married in 1979 and have seven children: six sons and one daughter. Two of their children are married and live outside the family home. Two other children have full time employment. Two sons study in local schools.  Mrs. Lay has been selling fish since 1992. She buys them from a fishing lot a bit far from her home to sell at the Phnom Penh market and in her village market. Her husband is a chef and assists Lay in the fish selling business.  Lay is requesting a loan of $700 to purchase more fish for resale.

name: Rafael
description: Rafael is thankful for the PHP 50,000 loan assistance that was granted to him, because he was able to purchase more, and a greater variety of, grocery items, toiletries, and beverages that he needed for his business. His earnings were a big help in their personal, household and business expenditures.He would like to apply for another PHP 50,000 loan. He will use this loan to buy groceries, toiletries, beverages, and other products to add in his inventory. The more items displayed at the store, the better. More items to sell will result in a better profit. His profits from his business will definitely help him to sustain their daily needs. He looks forward to this financial increase, with gladness and thankfulness in his heart.In the future, Rafael hopes that his business will continue to cover their everyday needs and that he will always be able to help his family. He meets up with his co-fellowship members* every week, to share stories of his work and to draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God he studies.* All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans

name: Virginita
description: As a married parent of three children, Virginita works hard to support her family.She has a vegetable vending business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from a general store. Virginita is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF to buy more vegetables to sell in her vegetable stall for her vegetable vending business.She successfully paid back her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her business.Virginita has been sustaining her business activities through her past five loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Savina
description: Savina is very pleased with her previous loan because it turned out very well and it helped to increase her business capital.  She continues to live in the community of Mojopata and is still involved in agriculture and raising small animals, such as guinea pigs and chickens.  Savina is still a member of the Communal Bank “Sol Naciente de Mojopata”.  She is taking this opportunity to request a loan in order to pay the cost of fumigating her farmland.  Savina appreciates and values this loan, so she promises to handle her monthly payments with great responsibility.The community of Mojopata is located in the District of Challabamba, Paucartambo Province, Cusco, Peru.

name: Josefina
description: Josefina is  taking a loan of USD 1000 to improve her business. She is married, and she has three children   She is running a kiosk that helps her to generate income for her family. She will use the loan to buy stocks to keep in her store, such as plates, spoons, pots, ladles, rice racks, plate racks, and  buckets. She opened her kiosk since 2008 with her own working capital of USD 600.   She is a hard-working woman, and she hopes to run a bigger business in the future.  And she is happy with this loan because TRM (Tuba Rai Metin) offered it for poor people to improving their living condition.

name: 02.03.1.8 Nam Ngạn Group
description: "Huệ Ngô Thị (39) is a 43-year-old female living in the town of Thanh Hoá.  Huệ is the group leader of a four-member group loan offered by Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women.  While each member of the group receives an individual loan, they all are responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults.  The official name of this borrowing group is 02.03.1.8 Nam Ngạn (02.03.1.8 Nam Ngạn).   Huệ is married and has two adult children.  To make a living, Huệ owns and operates a business selling rice products in the local community.  Huệ has been engaged in this business for over fifteen years and earns approximately $165 a month from these activities.   In 2009, Huệ joined Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation by engaging in business activities.  Huệ has successfully repaid a previous loan of 1,626,900 VND from Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women.  This previous loan was used to purchase raw ingredients needed to make products for sale.  She is now requesting a new loan of 6,000,000 VND which again will be used to purchase morer raw ingredients needed to make products for sale.  This will be her 2nd loan from Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women.  Huệ plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About the Other Borrowers in the Group:   1.  N. Thị Chinh (40) is a 44-year-old female who is requesting a 6,000,000 VND loan to support her business in the food sector running a bakery.   2.  Ngô Thị T. Hằng (41) is a 27-year-old female who is requesting a 6,000,000 VND loan to support her business in the service sector operating a service-based business.   3.  P. Thị Hà (42) is a 43-year-old female who is requesting a 6,000,000 VND loan to support her business in the retail sector running a general store.   About Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women:  The mission of Fund for Thanh Hoa Poor Women (FPW) is to provide sustainable financial services to disadvantaged women in rural areas in the Thanh Hoa province.   *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in Vietnamese while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.   Huệ Ngô Thị (39) là 43 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy sống ở thành phố Thanh Hoá.  Huệ là trưởng nhóm của nhóm vay gồm có 4 các thành viên.  Mặc dù mỗi thành viên trong nhóm nhận được từng khoản vay cá nhân, nhưng tất cả họ đều chịu trách nhiệm hoàn trả lại khoản vay của các thành viên trong nhóm của mình nếu một người nào đó trễ hạn hay không trả được nợ..  Tên chính thức của nhóm vay này là 02.03.1.8 Nam Ngạn (02.03.1.8 Nam Ngạn).   Trong khi không phải chỉ có các phương thức tạo nên T. nhập, mà nguồn T. nhập chính của công việc kinh doanh chủ yếu từ buôn bán các sản phẩm từ gạo trong cộng đồng địa phương.  Huệ thực hiện công việc kinh doanh này trong hơn 15 năm.  Từ các hoạt động này, Huệ kiếm được khoảng 3.000.000 VND.  Vào 2009, Huệ đã tham gia Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women để có thể tiếp cận với các dịch vụ tài chính giúp cải thiện  sinh hoạt và khả năng tham gia vào các hoạt động kinh doanh của cô ấy/ anh ấy.  Huệ đã hoàn trả hết khoản vay trước đây là 1.626.900 VND từ Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women.  Khoản vay trước đây được sử dụng mua các thành phần thô cần thiết để chế tạo sản phẩm để bán.  Cô ấy hiện đang đề nghị một khoản vay mới là 6.000.000 VND.   Khoản vay sẽ là 2nd khoản vay của người vay từ Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women.   Về Những Người vay khác trong Nhóm:   1.  N. Thị Chinh (40) là 44 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 6.000.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực thực phẩm.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là kinh doanh lò bánh mì.   2.  Ngô Thị T. Hằng (41) là 27 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 6.000.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực dịch vụ.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là vận hành công việc kinh doanh trên cơ sở dịch vụ.   3.  P. Thị Hà (42) là 43 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 6.000.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực bán lẻ.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là kinh doanh cửa hàng bách hóa.   Về Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women:  Nhiệm vụ của Quỹ vì Phụ Nữ Nghèo Thanh Hóa (FPW) là cung cấp các dịch vụ tài chính bền vững cho những người phụ nữ kém may mắn ở các vùng nông thôn tỉnh Thanh Hóa.   *Lưu ý: Để phát huy tối đa hiệu quả & giảm chi phí, khoản vay này đã được thông báo bằng biểu mẫu để có thể được Kiva tự động biên dịch. .  Do việc biên dịch thủ công các danh mục rất tốn kém, nên Kiva đã tạo biểu mẫu này cho phần Field Partner (Trường Đối Tác) cho phép họ tiếp tục thông báo các khoản vay bằng  Vietnamese trong khi cung cấp thông tin có chất lượng & chính xác cho người cho vay Kiva.  ."

name: Kibet
description: Kibet, 40, comes from the Nandi Hills area of Kenya where he owns 3 acres of land. His wife and 4 children depend on him and he depends on farming to generate income.   Kibet owns 2 cows, 30 heads of poultry, 80 trees and tea crops. Kibet is seeking a 30,000 KES loan to buy more heads of poultry to increase the quantity of poultry produce that he supplies to the market.   Your loan investment will enable him to grow his business, cut costs and increase earnings. Additional income from the poultry investment will help Kibet pay school fees for his 4 children more comfortably.

name: Bunena Tukwatanise 'a' Group
description: Redempta is a 45-year-old widow with four children living in Kamwenge, Uganda. All her children attend school. Redempta is a member of Bunena Tukwatanise A and she deals in cattle fattening alongside growing of crops and keeping of pigs to earn daily extra income. She has been a farmer for ten years and her clients are the people in and around her community. She hopes to give a great future to her children by educating all of them because they are orphans, but her main challenge is bad weather that affects both her animals and crops.She is requesting a loan to buy feeds for her pigs.

name: Ana
description: Ana is 54 years old, married and lives in Pari-an, Enrique Villanueva, Siquijor, Philippines.To earn a living, she decided to raise pigs. Through Paglaum MPC she obtained the capital to purchase piglets and feed.   Ana is requesting another loan for 14,900 PHP, which she will use to buy additional feeds and vitamins. She hopes that her business will grow and benefit her family. In the future, she wants to build a concrete pig cage to easily keep more sanitary conditions.

name: Massogblin
description: A widow and 46 years old, Massogblin lives in Agoè and has three children to support. Her struggles are great in her business selling fried fish for meeting her own needs and those of her children. She has turned to this loan to put in an order for baskets of fish with the aim of having a significant inventory and maximizing her profit, so as to help out her children’s education.

name: Yusuf J
description: yusuf is a 30-year-old businesswoman who lives in Nimule. She is married and has two children between the ages of four and seven, one of whom goes to school.   yusuf runs a general store and has been in business for two years. She has no employees. She heard about Finance Sudan through promotions and she is taking a loan of 1,500 SDG to purchase more goods.    In five years, she wants to open a big shop.  Her major challenges include the high cost of transporting her goods.   She is happy to take a loan from Finance Sudan.

name: Maicol
description: Maicol is 29 years old and unemployed. He is responsible, respectful, honest, and very devoted to his family. He has a 4-year-old daughter who lights up his life. She means the world to him and he is requesting a loan to support her. He wants to start a grocery store to generate enough capital to build a future for his daughter.The loan will be used to purchase a cooler, counter, shelves, and assorted general food, grocery, refrigerated products, soft drinks, snacks, etc.

name: Christina
description: Christina is a 36-year-old married woman. She has eight children with ages ranging from 4 years to 17 years. She operates a honey-selling stall where she sells honey. Her business is located in a suburban area, and her primary customers are mobile customers. She describes her biggest business challenge to be lack of enough capital.   She will use the 20,000 Kenyan shillings loan to buy more honey to sell. She hopes that in the future, she will succeed in life. She will use the anticipated profits to pay school fees for her children.

name: Restituta
description: Restituta is 50 years old and married with five children. With three children still in school, Restituta works very hard to provide for them.Restituta runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional items like soft drinks, snack foods, canned goods, candies, toothpaste, etc., to sell.Restituta has been in this business for five years and sells a variety of items, such as soft drinks, snack foods, canned goods, candies, toothpaste, etc. In the future, Restituta would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Roeuy's Group
description: Roeuy, 63, is a widowed mother of three children. As a single mother and a breadwinner in the family, she grows rice on a half hectare area and tailors clothes for extra income. The business that she has had for 30 years has enabled her to generate about 27,200 KHR per day.   Roeuy is a seven-time borrower with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). She has fully repaid her past loans with success to improve her living conditions. Now, in a group of two, she is the leader. She is seeking a new loan of 1,400,000 KHR in order to buy potash and pay for the plowing fee for her farmland. She hopes that she can gain a better yield than last year and make more income.

name: Nooraldeen
description: Nooraldeen is a 21-years-old single man from Nablus city. His father works where he gets a low and unstable income. Thus income is barely covers all the family needs. He is a student in the university where he studies Surveying. He wants to take his BSc. degree and find a job in the future to support his family.Nooraldeen took a USD loan from FATEN. This loan will help him to pay the university fees for the new semester. By taking this loan, Nooraldeen will be able to register in the university and pay part of the urgent expenses he has.NoorAldeen appears in the photo

name: Lorena
description: Mrs. Lorena is 30 years old and married. Her husband, Robert Chamorro, is 40 years old. They have three children. Their son is eight years old and their daughters are six and four, respectively.   Lorena and her husband own a grocery and butcher shop. He works with the supplies, and she works with the clients. Robert buys the animals himself, later he butchers and sells the meat in the same business. This process increases the business' income, because he acts as the conduit to sell other products such as noodles, rice, cooking oil, salt, tapioca, and other staples.   Lorena and Robert have developed a base of clients over the past five years, since they opened the store. They began this work by selling milk, and little by little they earned the capital to start their own business, which is now a well-supplied butcher shop and store.   The loan will go toward the purchase of cider, beer, and soda, as we're now getting closer to end-of-the year parties. Translated from Spanish by Sarah Bishop, Kiva Volunteer

name: Joselita
description: Joselita is 50 years old and married with three children. She earns a living by raising cattle in the Philippines. Joselita is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to purchase vitamins and vaccines for her cattle. Joselita has been raising cattle for five years, and also earns additional income from coconut wine vending. She is working tirelessly towards the attainment of her dream, to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Kefa
description: Kefa is 40 years old and lives in the town of Nakifuma in the Mukono region of Uganda. He is married and has four children, two of whom are currently in school. For the past three years, he has worked hard to manage his retail shop, where he sells sugar and soap.   To help expand his business, Kefa has requested a loan of 3,000,000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. He will use this loan to buy more essential commodities to sell, and this will help him generate greater profits and improve his family's living standards. He hopes that in the future he will be able to open another retail shop.   Kefa is a member of BRAC's Small Enterprise Program (SEP).  The program primarily serves small entrepreneurs like Kefa who do not have enough collateral for commercial loans, but have businesses that have grown too large for microloans.

name: Umeda
description: Umeda is 26 years old. She is not married yet. For almost seven years, Umeda has owned a beauty salon. Everyday she services many brides. In general, she offers bride-dresses, manicures, pedicures, make-up and hairstyles. Her salon is always full of clients because she does her job professionally. She wants to take a loan to extend her business. She wants to buy additional equipment and goods for her beauty shop. Umeda likes her job very much, because she likes to see the smiles of happy brides every day.     More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is perhaps best known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road; the end of Alexander the Great's rule; and with it’s famous great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets as: Rudaki, Ibn Sina (Avicenna), Firdousi, Omar Haiyam, Jomi, Mavlavi Rumi and many others. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the Fourth millennium BC.  And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But, Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics.  The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy.  In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable.  These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia.  While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.   IMON's History Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low-income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Walter
description: Walter is 35 and lives in his own home with his wife Jakeline, who makes a living by selling fish but is also his partner in his business.  They have 3 children for whom they care, protect and hope to be able to offer a good education.  Walter grows and harvests palm oil.  He plows and fertilizes the land.  He tells us that when his plants are in the process of growing, it's necessary to irrigate them continuously because of the heat in the city.  He also has to protect them from pests that attack this species of palm.  He does his work 50 kilometers from the city in a community known as "Neshuya."  Here he has 12 hectares of land, which he is cultivating and plowing for planting.  He started this business because the majority of people who live in this community do this work.  The government makes it easy to obtain seeds for this plant.  He does this work with his wife and two workers that he hires to plant, care for, and harvest his plants.  Before he started this business, he had problems generating economic income and couldn't support his family because he didn't have a steady job.
