This is why he decided to start his own business to generate his own income.  He hopes in the future to increase his production and to increase his economic earnings.  This will be his fifth loan with Microfinanzas Prisma.  He wants to keep making his payments on time.  He also knows that the group is made up of friendly and respectful people.  With the 1,500 PEN requested, he will buy manure, fertilizers, and tools like a machete, ax, etc.  And he will pay the workers that help him with his work.

name: Simona
description: Simona is 48 years old and lives with her daughter in a rented house. She has been selling candy, sodas and fruit for 20 years now in the main square of her town. She works there every day with her daughter, who helps her with sales. Her job requires her to work quite hard in order to sell all of her merchandise. She also stocks up on goods every two days. She is happy with her job because it allows her to be independent and to earn money every day which allows her to cover her household expenses. She would like to keep working at her job and to improve and increase the amount of merchandise that she sells. This is her 17th loan with MFP. She is very happy knowing that she has financial support. She is also glad to be part of her community bank because all of its members are responsible and supportive individuals. Likewise she would like to thank everyone who contributes to the loan she is requesting as it will be very helpful for the development of her business. She plans to use the requested loan to buy more merchandise for her stand.

name: Sammy
description: Sammy is 32 years old, married to Susan, and blessed with three children aged 13, 11 and seven years. He sells sacks of maize wholesale, a business he started five years ago, and earns a monthly income of KES. 8,000.   He has requested a fifth loan of KES. 20,000 to purchase more sacks of maize for sale. The profit he earns will aid him in paying school fees for his children.   He hopes to see his business grow as well as to educate his children to higher levels of education.

name: Jacqueline
description: Jacqueline sells children clothing; her husband, who is a sargeant in the military, is stationed in the country's interior.  Their family's income derives from these two activities; this is how they support their family, which is made up of two children, who are 9 and 4 years old.  They live in their parents' house, which is in the Litoral zone of the city of El Alto.  The funds will be used to buy children's clothing to sell.  This is her second loan with Impro; her good behavior with her previous loan qualifies her for another one.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Alice
description: Alice N. was born in 1966; she is married to Vincent Tih Forsuh and is blessed with five children. She shares three rooms with her five children in Ayaba Street, a quarter in the Bamenda North West Region of Cameroon.  Alice has faced difficulties in her life ranging from the inability to meet her daily needs, the inability of her husband to get a job for himself nor carry out any activity that could raise income due to an accident, the inability of her first son to continue his education due to poverty, and the increasing demands of her children. Amongst other challenges, she also has had difficulties of inadequate capital to expand her business.  With this loan, she plans to buy more food stuff like rice, beans, and cocoa yams to cook to sell in her restaurant. She also plans to piglets and feed to open up a pig farm. She thinks her business will succeed, because her business site is close to the road and she is friendly, thus has many clients. Her activity will help her community in reducing the cost of transportation to buy foods in the market and their cordial relationship will give room for negotiation to pay later.  She will use a fraction of her profit to assist her husband, provide for the children’s school needs, meet her personal needs and that of her family. She prefers a loan from GHAPE because of the training she frequently receives, the follow up and moral support given her by the GHAPE office, and the low cost in obtaining and paying back a loan.  About GHAPE: The Grounded and Holistic Approach to People's Empowerment (GHAPE) is a non-profit NGO based in Bamenda, Cameroon. GHAPE works towards the empowerment of the poor and poverty alleviation through a highly multi-faceted approach. Every client is trained in business management, basic health, life skills, financial management, profits and losses, and family values. Clients are also required to contribute a small amount into a personal savings account; most clients save much more than the minimum requirement. GHAPE instils a sense of family and community within its clients and staff and has developed a strong bond of trust between the organization and its clients.

name: Merah
description: As a married mother of three children, Merah works hard to support her family.  She has a nipa-roofing business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from general store. Merah is borrowing PHP 26,000 through NWTF in order to buy raw materials for her nipa-roofing business.  Merah has been sustaining her business activities through her past 20 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough money to expand her business.

name: Laurelio
description: Laurelio is a farmer who plants and harvests various vegetables. He is 54 years old and has two adult-aged children. He wants to improve his farming business so that he can give his family a better life. Laurelio would like to do this by expanding his vegetable farm, but he has limited capital. That is why he is requesting a loan for PHP 10,000 to buy fungicides, fertilizer and insecticides for his farm. Because he is a hard-working father, he believes that he can further improve his business.

name: Santos Raymundo
description: Raymundo is 55 years old, married, and has four children.  His wife takes care of their home and, when she is able, she helps her husband with his farming work.  Raymundo is a tenacious and hard-working person.  His business is growing coffee, a trade that he learned from his father.  He started out growing on one 'manzana' (1.68 acres) of land where he now has his plantation.  He works full time as this is his only source of income.  During certain seasons, the coffee growing business is very profitable for Raymundo as he has good customers who give him a good price for his coffee.  He is requesting this loan to buy fertilizers which he needs in order to improve his coffee crops.  The loan would help him a lot as it would give him a guaranteed source of income and a low interest rate which will mean more profits for him when he harvests his crops.  The problems that Raymundo has faced have been financial.  He has had to neglect his farm for lack of money.  His biggest wish is to improve the physical installation of his farm so that he can increase his profits and thereby improve his household economy.  This is his first loan from FAMA and he hopes to make his loan repayments punctually.

name: Hoima Public School
description: Greetings from Uganda! This is Harriet. She is the head teacher of Hoima Public School, a mixed school in the urban area of Hoima with 1,300 students. Hoima Public School has requested a loan to cover the cost of installing and maintaining a UV water filtration system to provide clean drinking water for its students. The school does not currently have access to consistent clean drinking water and therefore has to spend a considerable portion of its budget on firewood, which is used to boil water for the children. Installing a water filtration system will therefore save the school money in the long term, as the cost of firewood will be reduced. The loan will enable the school to purchase a UV water treatment system with a 1,000 litre tank, which will be big enough to store clean drinking water for the students every day. Hoima Public School will repay their loan from their school fees, which they collect each term. Harriet ultimately hopes that having access to safe drinking water will improve her students' concentration and attendance by reducing the number of children who fall sick from water-borne diseases, as well as increase the number of students coming to the school.

name: Taena
description: Taena is 39 years old and married with 4 children. She wants to start a small business making and selling Porkpun in her community. To do this, she needs a loan to buy sacks of flour, sugar, soya sauce, garlic,  and dripping oil. In the future, Taena hopes to improve her business. She joined SPBD in 2013 to gain access to financial services.

name: Peres
description: Peres is 45 and lives with his family of 7 children, 4 of whom are still schooling. He has been in farming for 20 years and currently employs one farmhand. He produces milk, maize, beans and vegetables which are sold to the local market.  Peres has requested a loan of 41,600 KES from Juhudi Kilimo to purchase and insure a dairy cow. He says he will use the income generated to pay school fees for his children. He has focus of acquiring three more dairy cows to boost his business. Peres, however, laments the high cost of feeds, especially during dry seasons.

name: Chini Devi
description: Mrs. Chini Devi M., 41 years old, lives in Thecho. Thecho is located in Lalitpur district, Nepal. Thecho is one of the developing villages of Lalitpur, and most of the people in this region are engaged in farming. Mrs. M. lives in a nuclear family with her husband, one son, and one daughter. Her daughter and son are studying in grades 10 and 9 respectively.   Her husband, Mr. Gopal M., is a plumber. Her husband’s work is the only source of family income. For his work he needs various types of tools and raw materials. She has already cleared her first loan from Kiva. With the help of her Kiva loan, Ms. M. purchased new tools for her husband's work as a plumber. Now Mrs. M. is requesting her second  loan of Rs 15,000 to buy modern tools for her husband.

name: Lai Heang
description: Lai Heang is 49 years old. She is married and lives with four children and a son-in-law in Kampong Chhnang Province, Cambodia. She has been selling all kinds of drinks for more than 10 years, earning about $4 per day. Her husband is a security guard who earns about $2 each day. Her son-in-law is a photographer who earns about $2 each day.   Lai Heang is requesting a loan of $600 to purchase a camera for her son-in-law. This will help her son-in-law to improve his business and to earn more income to support the family. In the future, she would like to expand her business and help her children earn bachelor’s degrees. Moreover, she hopes to rebuild her house to make it more convenient for her family.

name: Karina Fernanda
description: The communal bank "Primero de Abril" meets every fifteen days in Montecristi, a town that is known for its rich pre-colonial culture and its nationally and internationally recognized handicrafts. Home of the famous "Toquilla" straw hats (also known as Panama hats).   This is where Karina lives. Twenty-one years of age, she is in a common law relationship and has not yet had children. Her husband is a businessman. Karina is a young housewife. She takes care of the home and also earns a living in sales.   She sells clothes and Yanbal products by catalogue including beauty products, cosmetics, perfumes and women's accessories. She sells by going door to door. Every eight days she makes an order, distributes the products and collects payment because she sells her merchandise on credit. She has been in this business for more than 2 years and it has enabled her to get ahead.   This loan is to buy clothes and Yanbal products. She has been part of the communal bank for 2 years now and she likes it because she began her business with her first loan.   Her dream is to own a house because where they live now is rented.

name: Yanet
description: Credit group member Yanet continues to work selling milk and cheese.  She also sells cattle.  She grows and fattens them and then later sells them in different markets.  Her dream is to have a shop where she can sell her cheese and milk.  She is asking for this loan to buy cattle.  She is happy to have the loan and is committed to making her payments.

name: Mary Jane
description: Mary Jane, 35, is a fish dealer and a mother of three. She is married to Rolando, 42, a carpenter. They reside in Coron, Palawan, Philippines.  Operating out of the Coron Public Market for the past 12 years, Mary Jane has mastered the intricacies of the fish business. She finances a group of small fishermen who go out to sea by providing food, fuel, ice and other items they need. Sometimes she may even advance cash to her suppliers. Once the boats come in, the catch is sorted, weighed and packed into ice boxes for shipment to Manila. Mary Jane and the fishermen then square their accounts and the cycle starts anew. Mary Jane ships around 12 50-kilo boxes of fish weekly. She earns about Php700 daily. 	 Mary Jane needs Php 40,000 as additional capital to be able to cope with the ebb and flow of the fish business. It will be used to purchase additional fish and ice as well as for operational expenses like the bills for shipping and wages for those who repack and handle the fish.  On the personal side, Mary Jane finds it hard to cope with some family problems. But it is her three children who give her the determination to succeed. She dreams that one day they will all graduate from college, surpassing her, for she only managed to finish her secondary studies. Mary Jane is an active community partner of C.C.T. She meets with her fellowship* group every Wednesday.  *All C.C.T. community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital and repay Micro Finance loans.

name: Lolita
description: Lolita is a woman with two children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Lolita is 55 years old now.  Lolita has a food vending business in the Philippines. Lolita requested a PHP 3000 loan amount through NWTF to buy ingredients for her food production business.  Lolita has been in this business for 3 years. In the future, Lolita would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Mher
description: Mher is a 40-year-old constructor from Kapan. Mher lives with his wife and two daughters, who are 6 and 10 years old. Mher supports his family's daily accommodations with his handwork and sweat. He renovates houses and flats and is pretty demanded in his hometown as there are a few such professionals as Mher in Kapan. Mher's only obstacle is the low purchasing power of his clientele.  Mher applied for this loan in order to escalate the boundaries of his business. He needs your support to pay for new tools (hammer, angular grinding machine, and tile cutter) to be able to provide renovation services faster and with higher quality. Mher, together with his family, is very thankful for your understanding and is looking forward to your warm response.

name: Charita
description: Charita is 45 years old and with three children, settled for a living in Misamis Occidental with her family. She is a banana grower, and with her income, she was able to put up a retail store to make a living. She had successfully repaid her previous loan, used for purchasing seedlings and organic fertilizer, for the previous cropping season.   She took  a new loan recently to purchase manure fertilizer to restore farm nutrients; a portion will be use to buy grocery goods for her retail store.  Charita hopes to improve her business to ensure a better source of income for the family in the future.

name: Jorge
description: Jorge is 41 years old and single. He lives with his family in the district of La Florida in a rural zone. It is located in the province of San Miguel, Cajamarca region in the North Andes of Peru. The principal activities that take place in this community are agriculture and raising animals. Jorge works offering wood and metal services. He has his own work tools and his business is located at his house. He has more than 4 years in the business and he has regular clients who provide very good work references for him. The loan will be used to buy a greater quantity of wood as well as a machine to cut wood to use in his business. Doing this Jorge hopes to be able to make more chest of drawers, shelves and beds amongst other furniture. In this way he can satisfy the tastes and preferences of his clients. It will have a positive impact of his level of sales and in the end improve the quality of living for his family.

name: Elizabeth Ene Kipa
description: Elizabeth has been rearing animals for resale in Naivasha town for the last five years. She is 37 years old, married to Topoika S., and they have two children.  She was introduced to KADET by her friend, and this will be her first loan.  She plans to use the loan amount to buy 10 sheep, which she will rear and sell later at a profit.  In future, Elizabeth hopes to grow her business so that she may comfortably take all her children to school.

name: Lantoniaina Madeleine
description: Lantoniaina is 23 years old and married. The couple have 2 children, aged 8 and 6, who both attend a private school. Her husband supports her with her business.The couple do not pay rent but plan to extend their house in 2016 and to buy some land if they can afford it with their income and household savings.Lantoniaina has been selling bags and backpacks since 2014. The development of her small retail business depends on knowing the customers' needs and which items sell well. She chose to sell bags and backpacks because the market is currently very promising.

name: Batzorig
description: Batzorig is 25 years old and lives with his wife and a three year-old child in his parent’s house in Ulaanbaatar, the capital city of Mongolia. His parent’s house locates in a boundary area of the city with no running water, minimal roads, and spotty electricity. Batzorig has been renting a cell phone repair counter and sells phone spare parts in the downtown area of the city for 7 years. Every six months, he goes to China’s nearest border to buy phone spare parts.   His wife is a student, but this year she is not studying because she is pregnant and will give birth in November. As he and his wife are expecting a baby, Batzorig has been building a new house on the land of his parents for his family and the house is 80% complete. The loan Batzorig is taking will be used to buy radiators and insulate the roof, floor, and walls with energy saving materials in order to stop the heat loss. If his new house will be warmer, less energy will be burnt. By doing this he and his family will improve their living condition and can cut the usage of coal to warm his house.

name: Lita
description: Lita is 38-years-old and widowed with five children.  Lita works hard to provide for her family. She runs a business of buying and selling recycled materials in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional stock of recycled materials to sell.  Lita has borrowed and paid two loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the buying and selling business of recycled materials for two years and also earns an income from a general store.  Lita aspires to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Patricia
description: Patricia is a single mother of two children: a 20-year-old girl and 19-year-old boy. Both kids go to college and Patricia is the sole breadwinner. Two years ago, she left her employment to concentrate on a business in order to create more income. She concentrated on a property business by building rooms to rent in her backyard. The business has exceeded her expectations and she now wants to add more rooms due to the demand. She is thus requesting a loan to buy building materials as well as pay for the construction of two rooms. This loan will help her offer more space and make more revenue to sustain her family.

name: Balarabe
description: Balarabe is a Babban Gona maize farmer. Before he became a Babban Gona member, Balarabe would have had to sell his maize for low prices soon after harvest, to meet his immediate cash needs. With this loan and Babban Gona’s support, Balarabe can now store his maize at harvest time and sell it a few months later for up to 40% higher than the market price at harvest. When asked about his goals, Balarabe expressed a desire to use the extra income to provide family with food and clothing and, in the long run, become the most profitable farmer in his community.

name: Eliana
description: Eliana is still running her ceviche business.  She sells her ceviche to all her customers who order it.  She's grateful for the loan granted and promises to make her payments punctually, because this is how she gets her family ahead.  Eliana's requesting the loan to buy fish, limes, salt, and other ingredients.

name: Reanalen
description: Reanalen is 22 years old with two children.  Reanalen works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store  in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10000 loan through NWTF to buy additional items to sell like canned goods, home product care, and other groceries.  Reanalen has borrowed and paid 4 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 3 years and also earns an income from buy and sell rice.  Reanalen aspires to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Elma
description: Elma is 54 years old and married, with three children, one of whom is in school. She works very hard to provide for them.  Elma runs a general store in the Philippines and she has requested a PHP 5,000 loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) in order to purchase more groceries to sell.  Elma has been in this business for 25 years and she sells a variety of items, such as bread, soft drinks, and other goods.   In the future, Elma would like to save money to expand her business and to repair her family's home.

name: Tiessiri V Group
description: The 10 members of the Tiessiri V Group are married women who average 37 years of age and have an average of three children each. For the most part, they live in polygamous families in Kenikela, a village in Massigui Commune, Dioila prefecture, in the Koulikoro region (Mali's second administrative region).  The women in this group are working with microfinance institution Soro Yiriwaso with the goal of being able to better organize their businesses at the beginning of the rainy season. The crops being grown are, among others, ground nuts, rice, and a small amount of millet. The group is on its seventh loan with Soro Yiriwaso.  With this loan, Kadiatou Sokourala (the first person on the left in the row that is standing in the photo) plans to purchase farm inputs and minor equipment, as well as to pay the labor costs to maintain roughly two hectares of rice and groundnuts.  After the harvest, the crops will be sold in the city of Massigui to a customer base of men and women. Kadiatou Sokourala makes a profit of approximately 75,000 CFA francs per loan.

name: Uguljon
description: Uguljon was born in 1964. She is married and has three children. Uguljon decided to organize her own animal husbandry business six months ago. She feeds cattle at her house where she has a cowshed. Uguljon is going to develop her new business. She took part in the course ‘To get Ahead’ from a women's organization and got a certificate. She is asking for a loan of 10,000 Somoni to buy cattle to increase the working capital of her new business. She awaits your support.

name: Pheap's Group
description: Pheap’s group lives in a rural village in Prey Veng province in Cambodia. Pheap makes a living cultivating rice to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses, and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Nilda
description: Nilda is a woman of 36 who is responsible for her two little and beloved children. The older is 15 and the younger barely 4. Unfortunately, she separated from her husband 5 years ago due to some difficulties.  It was at that time that Nilda decided to put much more effort into her work and give the best to her children.  Nilda very much enjoys her time making sweaters for her children, since one of her hobbies is knitting. She and her little family live in the city of Pisco, which is famous for El Candelabro, which can be seen from the beautiful Ballestas Islands, a place that is heavily visited by tourists and is located in the district of Paracas.  To be able to generate the income that her little family needs, Nilda sells corn, and at the same time, she has a store, where she works from 7:30 in the morning until 7 at night. She tells us that her business is successful because it has a good location, and this allows her to serve an average of 20 customers a day. It was thanks to her brother that she was encouraged to have this type of business. Since that time everything has been going well for her, and she is thankful for that.  A good idea for her business occurred to her: to buy rice, pasta, milk, and other grocery products for her store. She knows that with this new variety of products her customers will be much more satisfied and thus she will be able to generate the income that she needs to enlarge her business, which will allow her to keep her children in good health and at the same time give them the schooling that they need.

name: Flordeliza
description: Flordeliza D. is from the village of Brgy. Tuao North, Bagabag, Nueva Vizcaya. She is 51 years old, married and has 5 adult-aged children. Flordeliza owns and operates a general store, selling daily use products such as shampoo, soap and toothpaste to the local community. Flordeliza has been engaged in her business for over 7 years and earns approximately 7,500 PHP a month from it.  In 2010, Flordeliza joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Flordeliza is requesting a new loan of 5,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This will be the 1st loan taken out by Flordeliza from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 29 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Gulchehra
description: M. Gulchehra lives in the B. Gafurov region of Tajikistan. She is married with four children. As with many rural women, she doesn't have a specialized education but she is experienced in livestock so she started taking care of home animals when she was a girl and helping her mother.   Today Gulchehra has her own family and owns livestock -- two cows and four rams. She makes milk and sour products and sells them in local bazaar. Gulchehra applies to Kiva for the business support loan of 1,200 STJ for six months to purchase special milk-making equipment. It will permit her to increase milk making and to use modern methods of milk making.   Gulshehra thanks Kiva for its support and wishes all the best.

name: Freddy  Eduardo
description: Freddy Eduardo C. Hernández Freddy is 29 years old, single, expert in marketing with a focus in computers.  He has been doing this for 2 years for as a career.  He is requesting a second loan for household articles, and he has determined that it is a worthwhile investment, since he will benefit from it, and thus be able to make his payments.

name: Neang's Group
description: Neang, age 33 and married, is a citizen in a rural village of Tbaung Khmum district of Kampong Cham. She has three children, two of whom are still under her responsibility as they are in school. To provide for her family's daily needs, she works on a rubber plantation and trades latex for extra income. Currently, she is able to earn about 28,000 KHR per day.   This is the second loan for Neang with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). She can afford to provide three decent meals for her kids and to build a decent house for her family from the original loan which she has fully repaid back. Now, she leads a group of three to apply for a new loan.   She is seeking 1,200,000 KHR while her other two members are seeking 1,400,000 KHR each. As the leader, she will spend her loan portion to buy more latex to resell. She hopes to increase her income so as to upgrade her lifestyle.
town: Kampong Cham province, Tbaung Khmum district

name: Jumriah
description: Jumriah is 44 years old and married. She lives with her husband and her son. She has a business of selling coconut rice and food over the past seven years. She is pleased to be able to help her husband to improve their lives.  She has asked for a loan from KPP-UMKM for 6,500,000 IDR. This loan will be used to buy and build a bathroom, septic tank, and closet at their home to improve access to water and sanitation for their family. She wants to have access to safe sanitation for the family but her families' income is still not enough to build a toilet on their own however, they are able to repay a loan.  Jumriah and her family want to live a healthy life with healthy sanitation. She is very grateful for the opportunity and wants to thank all of lenders.

name: Uzma
description: Uzma has expertise in embroidery, and has been using her skill to provide for her family for over seven years. She started this line of work at a very young age. During the initial years of her business, she barely made enough money to purchase the required material. Today she is proud to be famous in her community, for being the best at making beautiful patterns with thread and beads.  She obtained a loan of Rs. 20,000 from Kashf Foundation, which she will use to purchase spools of thread and packs of sequins, pearls and glittering material, in various colors. She says that the women in her community are becoming more demanding with the passage of time, and satisfying them is a challenge that Uzma has taken up.

name: Hotel Lane Traders Group
description: Meet with members of the “Hotel Lander Traders” group from Magburaka, a town in northern Sierra Leone. They are all entrepreneurs who have come to SMT, a partner of Kiva, to apply for a loan of SLL 800,000. With the help of this loan they will be able to expand their businesses, make more sales and consequently improve their living conditions.   Isatu K. is the leader of this group. The thirty-five-year-old is married to a businessman and they have three children. Isatu has been a businesswoman for three years now, selling ready-to-wear-clothes. With her share of this loan she will be able to expand her business by buying more clothes at wholesale to add to her current stock. This will help her increase her business sales and profitability.   The inserted photo is of a group member who was not able to be present.

name: Renacer Boqueron 2 Group
description: This group has 18 members and they are in the poverty-elimination program putting in their best efforts to improve their living conditions. One of the group's members is Deisy, who has been able to better herself through the poverty-elimination program and her hard work, in addition to her clothing sales business.  She tells us that though the financial situation she is dealing with is very difficult, she is very enthusiastic about improving it. She is requesting this loan to buy different kinds of summer clothing to sell.

name: Yiny Lilian
description: Yini is a 37 year old woman who works selling a variety of merchandise. She sells mainly women's clothing. Her desire and obsession has always been to built a house of solid material (concrete, she lives in a modest wooden house). But the responsibility and commitment of this woman to her work allows her and her 2 children to enjoy three meals a day breakfast, lunch and dinner. Yini at this time is requesting a loan with which she plans to double her merchandise. She will have to work more hours and look for clients but if she can do it, then she can remodel her house and improve the quality of living for her family.

name: Maria
description: Maria Céspedes has been married for 18 years to her husband, who repairs car radiators. Together, they have two children who are in high school.    Her husband's income helped Maria to open her own small business eight years ago. She sells beauty products, like shampoo, conditioner, perfumes, and facial creams. She began as a traveling saleswoman, but now has her own place in a nearby market. Maria began working with her children’s education in mind.  Maria will use the loan to invest in new products. More variety will make for a better income, because her store will be more competitive.

name: Octavio
description: In spite of the difficulties he has encountered as a result of his weight, Octavio has found daily work to support his children who have managed to become independent little by little thanks to his business of buying and butchering pigs that he shares with his wife. He is requesting a loan to purchase 10 pigs so that he may sell the meat to maintain his home income.

name: Usaha Ternak Group
description: Wayan and all members of Usaha Ternak Group decided to continue to borrow from MUK. Because they need to increase the population of their pigs, they need a new loan. They will need a loan until they can support their business by themselves.  Wayan gets full support from her husband. He helps her to maintain the pigs. She now has nine piglets. This loan will be used to purchase superior feed. Wayan needs a Vet who is always ready when she is needed. The profits will be saved to be capital for her business. The group has one new member.

name: Hab
description: Hab V., age 57, sells fresh fish that she buys from her regular suppliers or fishermen. Hab V. sells to her neighbors in and around her village. She is a widow who is blessed with six children; five of them are married and live separately, while the other one is single. She has a few sons who sometimes fish to earn money. In order to earn additional income and make her business more successful, Hab V. is requesting a loan to expand her capital in order to buy more fresh fish for resale.

name: Nhóm 9 - An Thanh 01 Group
description: Mrs Men is 58 years old, employed in agriculture with a monthly income of about 700,000 VND. She and her husband live with two grown children and two grandchildren, who are attending high school. She has been a member of the Women's Union since 1971.   Currently, the family has no flushing toilet, so family members often have to borrow their neighbors’ latrine. With this loan, Mrs Men will use the fund to build a septic tank to improve living conditions, improve the health of her family members and contribute to environmental protection. In the photo, Men stands on the right.

name: Luis Eduardo
description: Luis is a hardworking and cheerful man who knows how to make the most out of life.  At 49 years of age, he works as a gardener.  He is one of the few independent contractors who is in this line of work.  Luis has two children who are ages 12 and 19, a daughter and a son respectively.  He wakes up every day so that he can do his work, which allows him to pay the educational and food expenses for his two children who are his motivation in life.  Luis is having difficulty and in need of a weed eater so that he can continue to perform his job, which represents 100% of his family’s income.  For this reason, he is requesting a loan so that he can buy this indispensable piece of work equipment.  Luis dreams of improving his family’s quality of life.

name: Sanan
description: Sanan is a 48-year-old market vendor who has been selling cosmetics for the last 14 years. Sanan is married and has two sons. His wife actively helps him to run the business, and they have a lot of customers. His business brings in a stable income of 200 Azerbaijani manats (AZN). This is the only source of finances for his family. Sanan would like to expand his business and buy additional merchandise. For this purpose, he applied for a 1500 AZN loan.

name: Vailoa
description: Vailoa is a 38-year-old married woman with two children. She makes and sells pancakes, sandwiches, noodle dishes, etc. in her community to earn a living. She has many years of experience in this business.   Vailoa became a member of SPBD this year. She is applying for a 1000 WST loan to buy the ingredients she uses in her business. She plans to use her profits to help pay for her children’s education.

name: Sokhorn's Group
description: Sokhorn is 39 years old and married with four children. The family lives in Kroch Chhma district, Kampong Cham province. Sokhorn makes a living to support her family by growing cassava.  As the third loan ended, Sokhorn is now leading a group of four members to apply for a loan from VisionFund. She will spend her loan portion on plowing services and to get piglets for raising to generate additional income. She hopes to improve her family's lifestyle.
town: Kampong Cham province; Kroch Chhma district

name: Adela
description: Adela, 40, is a member of the Los Sauces de Compañía communal bank.  The members are from Compañía.  Adela lives with her life partner and their 4 children.  Adela, together with her husband, manufactures bricks, which she sells in her own community.  In addition, Adela sells cochineal and tara (a powder ground from a pod that grows on a bush in the Peruvian highlands that is used in eco tanning).  Adela needs a 750 sol loan to buy firewood.  Adela dreams that her children become professionals and have their own businesses.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Nevzeta
description: Nevzeta lives in Gornja, Zenica with her husband and 2 children, 22 and 28 years old. She is 51 years old. This is her second loan of 1000KM and she is going to use it to buy stock and animal feed. She hopes that she will improve her household and monthly income.

name: Pacita
description: Pacita G. is from the village of Clarin. She is 51 years old. Pacita is married and has 3 adult-aged children. To make a living, Pacita owns & operates a service-based business. This business provides construction services to local community members. Pacita has been engaged in her business for over 10 years and earns approximately 8,000 PHP a month from these activities.  In 1999, Pacita joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and to have the ability to engage in business activities. Pacita has successfully repaid a previous loan of 20,000 PHP from PMPC. Pacita is requesting a new loan of 20000 PHP. This loan will be used to purchase materials needed to provide service. This will be the 18th loan taken out by Pacita from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of the her family.   About PMPC:  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Venice
description: Venice is 28 years old and married with three children. With three children in school, Venice works very hard to provide for them.Venice runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 7,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like beverages, canned goods, snack foods, home care products, and other groceries.Venice has been in this business for five years and sells a variety of items. In the future, Venice would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Damian
description: Damian is from a hard-working family.  He is studying to be a teacher in basic sciences.  He says he is continuing with his studies in order to be able to continue growing as a professional.At the same time as he studies, he is also working in order to be able to pay for his studies.  He is married and they help each other mutually.He requests this loan in order to be able to pay the fees for his course of studies, and in this way to be able to continue with his studies as he is doing.

name: Wungeh Joseph
description: Joseph is married and has five children. In Bailem, Cameroon, Joseph is an operator, and he cuts firewood using a chain saw. Firewood is used a lot in Cameroon, as most kitchens cook over open, wood-burning fires. His services are common. He will use this loan to purchase petrol (gas), engine oil, a chain saw and some sharps.   Joseph says he is a hard worker and is kind to his customers. These characteristics are what he believes makes him a successful business owner. In his community, his business location allows his customers to trek shorter distances and it will enable him to employ local youth.   This is Joseph’s second loan from GHAPE since he became a beneficiary in 2008. With the profits from this loan he will pay for his children’s school fees, save some money, rear pigs and perhaps buy some trees. Joseph takes out GHAPE loans because GHAPE documents his loans and is a truthful organization.    About GHAPE The Grounded and Holistic Approach to People's Empowerment (GHAPE) is a non-profit NGO based in Bamenda, Cameroon. GHAPE works towards the empowerment of the poor and poverty alleviation through a highly multi-faceted approach. Every client is trained in business management, basic health, life skills, financial management, profits and losses, and family values. Clients are also required to contribute a small amount into a personal savings account; most clients save much more than the minimum requirement. GHAPE instils a sense of family and community within its clients and staff and has developed a strong bond of trust between the organization and its clients.

name: Virginia
description: Virginia is a single woman, 28 years old, with two children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur.  Virginia has a fish vending business in the Philippines. Virginia requested a PHP 14,000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase more fresh fish to sell.  Virginia has been in this business for four years. She would like to save enough money so that she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Sofia
description: Sofia is a dedicated mother and lives in Lahore Pakistan with her husband and son. Her husband owns a meat shop in the nearby market and has been running the shop for 5 years now  He is a reliable butcher, so he has gathered a lot of faithful customers within this short span of time. He is only bread winner of his house, so it becomes difficult for him to manage the household at times due to stock shortages.Now he wants to buy several goats which is the most demanded meat, so that he earns enough of the profits and run his family with ease. Therefore Sofia has applied or the loan and thanks the Kiva and its field partner BRAC,Pakistan.

name: Fely
description: Fely G. is a 38-year-old married woman who supports her family selling meat in the local market. She lives in Omilis, Cauayan, Negros Occidental with her husband and their four children, who are 3 – 16 years old with three of them currently going to school.  Fely has been a member of NWTF-Project Dungganon since 1998. She has improved her living conditions with the help of her loans from NWTF and through her own efforts. By working hard in her local meat market business, she is gradually making her family more economically stable. She now earns an average monthly income of 5,000 Philippine pesos (PHP).  Fely is now borrowing 17,000 PHP to use as additional capital for her buy and sell meat business. This will be her 17th loan cycle from NWTF-Project Dungganon. Her previous loan of 15,000 PHP (which she paid off well within its term) was just another step on her journey towards economic freedom. Fely aspires to elevate her family’s living conditions and ensure their future wellbeing by following the “Dungganon” way.  About NWTF: In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress from earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem  that is bestowed on a member of a community who has earned respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work.

name: Sang
description: Mrs. Sang P., 28, lives in the Kampong Cham district of Cambodia with her husband, 38, and their three children who are all students. Mrs. Sang P. is a vendor selling rice-crops, while her husband currently works as a farmer and earns US$1 a day. She intends to use the loan of US$600 to buy a horse and a cart, so that her husband can start a business of transporting people from the village, thereby earning important additional income for the P. family.

name: Edith Yesenia
description: Edith Yesenia R. is a woman that has always taken care of her mom.  Yesenia is married, her husband doesn’t keep her from helping out her mom.  Yesenia’s mom is also taken care of by a son that is not in the city but that always helps out by sending money.  Yesenia wants to provide more comfort to her mom, the woman who took care of her as a little girl.   The house that they live in is part of a social program and is very small, this is why they come to us to request a housing loan and expand the house so that Yesenia’s mom feels good and comfortable. Translated from Spanish by Sofia Burt, Kiva Volunteer

name: Jessica Cryseida
description: Jessica Cryseida F. A. is 29 years old and lives in the Department of Santa Ana with her husband and 14 year old son.  She works Monday through Sunday at her own business, a snack bar where she serves breakfast, lunch, dinner, sweets, appetizers, drinks, and other items.  Her business is situated in an excellent location near the hospital in San Juan Opico.  She is able to generate many sales.    Jessica is requesting a loan so that she can restock her business with supplies, thereby allowing her to offer more food items to those people who are visiting the hospital.  She hopes to increase her sales and considerably improve her family’s household finances.

name: Rapuncel
description: Rapuncel is a 25-year-old single woman. She works very hard to help her parents.   Rapuncel runs a general store in the Philippines. She explains that she has been in this business for 5 years.   Rapuncel is requesting a loan in the amount of 19,000 PHP through NWTF to buy various items to sell to her customers, including shampoo, chips, milk, noodles, eggs, and spices. In the future, Rapuncel would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Aisha
description: Aisha is a 32-year-old mother of 3, and a resident of Tandika. She sells wood and carpentry materials for construction purposes. She orders it from the Morogoro region and the Rufigi area. Recently, the forest authority has restricted deforestation, and this has affected her business. She is in need of a loan to help her expand her business into other areas.

name: Eugenia
description: Eugenia is 53 years old and married.  She has five children. Eugenia works very hard to provide for them.  Eugenia runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 18,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional items like sugar, coffee, detergent soap, canned goods, noodles, etc. to sell.  Eugenia has been in this business for 15 years and sells a variety of items such as sugar, coffee, detergent soap, canned goods, noodles, etc.  Eugenia would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Dromo Group
description: Dromo is a group of three ladies. They all live in Accra-Teshie, Ghana. They are asking for a loan of GHS 2,600 from ID Ghana to sell ready-made dresses, eggs, kids wear, groceries, slippers and underwear.   Esther is a 44-year-old single woman with two children. She has been selling groceries and ready-made dresses for five years. She takes care of the children by herself by selling goods from her residence. She wants to improve her business though, as most of what she earns goes to family expenses. Therefore, she is applying for a loan of GHS 1,100 from ID Ghana in order to buy more eggs, ready-made dresses and groceries which she will sell to her customers.   Esther will save part of her profits and also invest some of it after she finishes repaying her loan.

name: María  Evelyn
description: María is an exemplary woman with a professional license in Education.  Currently, she is the director of a community center, with 27 years of experience in the ministry of education.    At the moment, she is in need of making repairs to her home.  She must reinforce her roof as it is in poor condition, which is why she visited the Ceprodel offices to solicit a loan to purchase materials such as zinc and purlins and pay for labor.  This will allow her to improve her home and quality of life.  She is grateful for Ceprodel and the loan opportunity as well as the support they have given her to reach her dream.

name: Lucy
description: Lucy is a married woman with one child, who is still too young to attend school. She owns a house that neither has piped water nor electricity. Her greatest monthly expense is food. Lucy has operated a tailoring business for the past three years. She makes women's suits and men's suits. Her potential clients are ladies and gents. She dreams of establishing a boutique in the future. With the Kshs 10,000 she wants to purchase cloth material and sewing thread for her business. She decided to join Yehu to access financial support to improve her business.

name: Sarita
description: Sarita peddles pens, diapers, sanitary napkins and other items.  Her husband is employed as a driver.  Together they pool their earnings to cover family expenses.  She lives in the city of El Alto which is in Villa Tunari zone.  The financing will be used to buy more products like those listed above to earn extra income during the Christmas season.  This is her second loan with Impro and her evaluation indicates that she qualifies for the loan.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Edna
description: Edna is a professional teacher. She is 43 years of age and currently living in Brgy. Banglay, Tangub City, Misamis Occidental, Phillipines. Edna is married with one son and one daughter. Both of them are studying in college.   Edna has a salary of Php 20,000 a month.She requested a loan in the amount of Php. 25,000 to pay the school fees for her son, his tuition fee.  Edna has been a member of Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative since 2008. She has a big dream for her son, and that is to finish a Bachelor's degree as well as to have a white-collar job.

name: Elsie
description: Elsie works hard to support her family.  She is married and has an abaca weaving business in the Philippines.  Elsie requested a PHP 13,000 loan through NWTF to purchase materials for her abaca weaving.  Elsie has been in this business for 10 years.  In the future, Elsie would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Phoebe
description: Phoebe is 50 years old and married with three children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur.   Phoebe has a fishing business in the Philippines. Phoebe requested a PHP 16,000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase additional fishing net for her fishing business.  Phoebe has been in this business for 40 years. In the future, Phoebe would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Anonymous Group
description: The client, representative of the loan group, is a 48 year old, married entrepreneur. She sells used clothing. She started her business when she moved from the village where she was born in the province of South Kivu to the city of Goma, where she was introduced to the business by her peers. Her husband is a master builder. The profits from her business are used for savings, and for feeding and educating her children. However, she just obtained her 20th loan from Hekima. Over this period, this client has seen her sales decrease noticeably following the economic instability. Thus she decided to reduce the loan sum this cycle. This new loan will be used for her to stock up with half a bale of used clothing. Additionally, she wishes to see her children grow up and build her house. The client thanks Hekima for its actions in helping poor women excluding from traditional banks to achieve autonomy. One ought to mention that the client is holding her baby.

name: Evelyn
description: Evelyn is 48 years old and married with four children. With three children currently in school, Evelyn works very hard to provide for them.Evelyn runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to buy more groceries to sell in her general store.Evelyn has been in this business for six years and sells a variety of items such as detergent soap, shampoo, soft drinks, cereals, coffee, sugar, etc. In the future, Evelyn would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Zuhra
description: Ms Zuhra is a 50-year-old vigorous married woman. She has been running a business of hand-embroidery for the past five years. She is passionate about her work and client demand is strong. However, business challenges, combined with family expenditures, frustrate her nearly every day. Her husband is employed in a small factory, but he does not earn enough to support his family well. Zuhra’s embroidery patterns are very popular on her street and she is the best earning resource in her household.   She is a mother of seven children. She wants to grow her business, so she requested a loan of Rs 35,000 to buy raw materials such as threads, sequins and pearls in large quantities to meet the increasing demand. She shared her dream of running a training center for girls of her village. She would teach embroidery skills, so she can help her expand her business help others earn money for themselves. She is also interested in opening her own shop in the market to display her work.

name: San Miguel Group
description: San Miguel is a group of enthusiastic women who, in addition to being homemakers, have decided to become important contributors to their households. The members of San Miguel feel fulfilled when starting up businesses run by themselves.   One of the members, Dora Celia, started a fast-food business selling hamburgers and hotdogs. She is a resident of the municipality of Guadalupe and is known for her delicious sazón (seasoning). Dora Celia’s husband supported her to undertake this desire for self-improvement.  She is sure that the loan commitment she now accepts will allow her to invest in the upkeep of the establishment where she currently sells. Dora Celia is confident that her business is moving forward.

name: Rebecca's Group
description: This group is made up of two members. Rebecca is one of them. She is 42-years-old, married and has three children. She has been selling bananas, maize and groundnuts for 20 years.  She has been with the institution for five years and needs this loan to buy more bananas, maize and groundnuts to sell to customers.  Paulina is 40-years-old and she sells bananas, maize and groundnuts.

name: Jacob's Group
description: Jacob, featured in the picture above, is representing his group of twelve farmers in Webuye District, Kenya. He is best known in his community for being a very experienced farmer and is very excited to be joining One Acre Fund for the first time this year.Jacob’s decision to join the program was largely due to the fact that he wanted to get the best quality fertilizer and hybrid seeds. In addition, he was keen on purchasing a solar light that he could afford, as he says that by doing so he would be able to reduce the consumption of paraffin fuel and therefore save more money, which he is very excited about. With the profits he earns from the coming harvesting season, Jacob plans to send his children to school.Between the twelve farmers in Jacob’s Group, a total of 4.75 acres of land will be planted using the farming inputs received with this loan. The group will also receive a total of twelve solar lights.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth is a 31-year-old lady, married with one child. She lives in Fort Portal, Uganda in a rented house. She has a retail shop business which has been in existence for two years now.  Elizabeth also sells air time in her business and says she would like to become an agent for one of the telecommunications companies around her. This is Elizabeth’s first loan from HOFOKAM and she intends to purchase air time to sell in her shop.

name: Pan
description: Pan is a 49-year-old mother of 6 children. She is a farmer and also grows cassava to support her family. She has been in this business with her parents since she was around 10 years old. Pan is applying for her first loan with VisionFund. She wants to plant cassava on her farmland. With this loan, she hopes to expand her cassava plantation and earn more income to better feed her family and build some savings for the future.
town: Kampong Cham province, Ponhea Krek district

name: Eduarda
description: Eduarda is a member of  the  “Señor de los Temblores II” communal bank in the city of Cusco, Peru. She is still selling food as a street vendor. She is a responsible and hard-working person. She continues to produce different types of dishes for her customers who ask for them and this is how she brings her family up.  Eduarda is asking for the loan to buy dried vegetables, oil and other supplies. She is grateful for the loan provided and promises to meet her repayment instalments.

name: Mary Jane
description: Mary Jane P. has been raising pigs for several years. She is 34 years old and the mother of six children. Her husband, Hernane P. Jr., is a farmer. They started their piggery business with only two piglets. Aside form pigs, the couple also grows rice. At present, they have one sow and nine piglets.  Mary Jane would like to ask for a loan of Php 12,000 from CEVI. She will use the loan to buy pig feed. The feed  is quite expensive. She needs additional resource to raise more pigs.  CEVI helps small business grow. CEVI provides not just loans, but training and insurance coverage, as well.

name: Parissin Group
description: Marcel is a 36-year-old farmer. He is the one holding the daba (short-handled hoe) at the bottom of the photo. He is a customer of RMCR in Mali where he lives with his wife and three children. They are five to twelve years of age, and two are in school.  For the past twelve years he has been cultivating groundnuts, selling them wholesale and retail at markets in his area, where he forecasts profits of 17,500 francs a month. The cart in the rear enables him to transport manure to the field.  Marcel rejoices practicing agriculture because it enables him to have lots of groundnuts for sale. Since he doesn't have the required funds he calls upon RMCR.  His dream is to earn more money and buy draft oxen to help cultivate a lot more groundnuts. He hopes this will enable him to deal with all his family's expenses and also pay the children's school fees.  The lack of agricultural equipment and poor rainfall are the major challenges he faces.

name: Gloria Esperanza
description: Sra. Gloria Esperanza C. is 65 years old and has a small business that consists of a grocery store and a food stand where she prepares pork dishes such as nacatamales, fried pork, blood sausage, and chicharrones among other items.  Cooking is a common activity in Nicaraguan families and provides a financial alternative for generating household income.  Sra. Gloria has earned a fine reputation throughout most of the country, especially for the breakfasts, lunches, and dinners she serves on the weekends.    Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Jackline
description: Jackline A.  is currently in the business of selling tomatoes, 'simsim', lemons and greens and is requesting a loan to stock more bags of 'simsim' to sell.  Jackline is 35 years old and is married to a husband who is a policeman. She has 6 children and her children go to school.  With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to buy goats and chickens to rear at home.

name: Idriss
description: Idriss is married with three children, two of whom are school-going. He has a shop in the city center where he sells tailoring materials. He is assisted by his wife at the shop when he is out of town.  Idriss would like a loan of 4,000,000 SLL in order to increase his tailoring material stock. His materials are in very high demand and he would very much like to satisfy his customers.  Idriss plans to use the proceeds from this loan to complete the payment for a piece of land on which he has already made a part payment. He also hopes this loan will enable him to grow his business so that he can support his family. He thanks you for your support.

name: Margaret
description: Margaret is 41 years old, married to Kamau, and they have two school-going children. She has practiced farming for the last six years.  She is also building rental houses to supplement her farming income.   She was introduced to KADET by one of our field officers and this will be her first loan.  She plans to use the loan amount to buy seeds and fertilizer and materials to continue building the rental houses.  In future, she hopes to become a leading farmer in her area and also build more houses for rent, translating to more income.

name: Kadogo
description: Kadogo, who is in his late 30s is married with four children. Three of them are in school and one is still small.  He has been running a business selling clothes for one year now.   This will be Kadogo's 9th loan from Tujijenge Tanzania.  He used the previous loans to sell chips, bought a bajaji for a transportation business and has now opened a big clothes shop.  He has paid back all his loans successfully.   He used the profit to pay school fees, bought a TV set, a deck, a dining table and covered his household expenses.  He will use this loan to increase his clothes stock to sell.    He dreams of building his own house and sending his children to good schools.  Kadogo will make sure that he pays back his loan according to the loan schedule.

name: Oreste Javier
description: Señor Oreste is a small farmer.  He lives with his wife and children in the Ticuantepe area.  His wife, who works alone, helps him with the household expenses.  His plans for the future are to be able to improve his living conditions.  Don Oreste has been growing pineapple for several years.  He suffered a  major set back when he was cheated with the product which caused him to default on his loan.  Now he is very happy because Afodenic and Kiva have placed their trust in him and given him the support he needs to continue farming.

name: Joyce
description: Joyce has continued to sell BrightBox to low-income farmers across Western Kenya and establish partnerships that allow farmers to pay for systems over several months. We are reposting the original loan with a higher loan amount due to the overwhelming demand Joyce has built since our first successfully funded loan in December. Thank you!

name: El Triunfo Group
description: The communal bank "El Triunfo" [The Triumph] is made up of eight members.  All of the members are adults, married, and together they have fifteen children they are responsible for.  They are fighting, hard-working individuals with the desire to offer the best opportunities for their children so that they have a better future.   These members decided to select a communal bank model to qualify for loans and mutually help one another in their different economic activities.  The communal bank was formed in Malpaisillo, a place that is located in the western part of the country.  Malpaisillo is characterized as being an agricultural area where growing crops, like corn and bananas, is the main activity.    Graciela Ramona is the coordinator of the bank and is responsible for the smooth operation of the bank, in addition to paying her own installments.  Graciela sells bananas from her house and also travels to customers' homes to sell.  Graciela's routine is to leave to sell in the community with her small cart of bananas.  For ten hours every day, she offers her products to her regular clients and to potential new customers.    The communal bank El Triunfo is thankful for the help that the Kiva investors have offered to them and to other people with scarce resources in poor countries, like Nicaragua.

name: Basilia
description: Basilia lives in her parents' home in Senkata Pucarani II district of the city of El Alto.  She has two daughters.  Basilia is a caretaker and works in the Pacajes Education Center.  She runs a stall selling sweet treats in the same school.  She uses the income that she makes from these jobs to support her family.  This is Basilia's first loan from IMPRO and her first KIVA loan.  She is requesting this loan as she needs to buy more sweet treats to offer her customers and thereby improve her income.

name: Luis Albero
description: The only thing that Luis has in mind is that to get ahead, one has to work hard and always keep oneself strong in front of the adversities that can come up. For this reason, every day he works in a firm way but without leaving behind his big smile and charisma that have allowed him to earn a place 15 years ago when he decided to open his florist business in the municipality of Medellín.In his business, he sells flowers of many colors and sizes.He asks for economic support to purchase an assortment of flowers of different types in bulk to expand his inventory. He knows that at the hand of Interactuar and with the support of the Kiva lenders, he will be able to have a very well accredited business with the best stability possible.

name: José
description: José P. is 45 years old and has lived with Miriam Trinidad for many years.  They own their own home in the Barrio Quiteria neighbourhood in the city of Encarnación.  José has had a carpentry workshop in his home for more than 2 years.  He is a very hard worker and has made a lot of progress as he has made improvements to his workshop.  Thanks to his work he has always been able to pay the household expenses.  His common-law wife, Miriam, is a housewife and she takes care of the day-to-day household chores.  This client has requested a loan from Fundación Paraguaya in order to buy more wood for his carpentry business, as demand is strong and he wants to fill every single one of his orders.Translated from Spanish by Laure Kwon, Kiva Volunteer

name: Daihanna
description: Daihanna is from the city of Paraguarí and is one who strives for a better quality of life for her family.  She is studying for a career in accounting because she wants to be more useful to others in society.  She is asking for this loan to pay university tuition so she can continue her education.

name: Jean Carlos
description: Jean Carlos is 20 years old, single, living with his family in the Tambogrande farming zone, an area with semitropical weather known primarily for lemon and mango production, belonging to Piura province and located over four hours from the city of Chiclayo.  He has a small, home-based grocery store where he stocks daily use items and groceries for his neighbors.  He tends to customers with dedication and charisma so he has a well-established base of regular customers who prefer to buy in his store.  Income from this activity is used to support the family’s economy.  Jean Carlos would like to stock more products in his store so that sales will grow and he can meet current demand.  Because of this he has asked for a 1000 new sol loan from Edpyme Alternativa to help him reach this objective

name: Alijon
description: Alijon is a very hard working and purposeful man. He is 33 years old, married, and raising four children. In order to provide his family with all necessary means, he has been providing a taxi service for more than 12 years. His children have over the years needed more goods, extra tutoring, computers and internet, and this requires a lot of money.   Alijon needs to develop his business and increase his income. In order to do this, he should repair his car and purchase a new car to attract customers. He requests a loan in the amount of 5,000 somoni. He awaits your kindness.

name: Concepcion
description: Concepcion is a hard-working entrepreneur who has a natural medicines business in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 23,000 through NWTF to buy more stock to sell for her natural medicines business.  Concepcion has been in this business for five years. She earns more income from clothing sales.  Concepcion has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams of saving enough to build a house for her family in the future.

name: Hong
description: Hong is a 46-year-old married woman who lives with two children and her husband in Ho Chi Minh City. Her husband earns money as a driver for hire.  For six years, she has run a food stall selling soft drinks for people in her community.  She would like a loan to purchase a greater quantity of beverages.  She hopes this will enable her to meet the needs of her customers and to attract additional customers.  She also hopes that through her loan she will be able to increase her income and save money for any future difficulties facing her family.

name: Ramon
description: Ramon E. is from the village of Nacional, Jimenez, Misamis Occidental. He is 42 years old and is married.  Ramon owns and operates a general store, selling daily-use products such as shampoo, toothpaste, soap, canned goods, etc., in the local community. He has been engaged in his business for over two years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month.  In 2009, Ramon joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and his ability to engage in business activities. He is requesting a loan of 10,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be his first from GDMPC. He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand his business.    About GDMPC: GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three unit offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Novie
description: As a married parent of two children, Novie works hard to support her family.  She has a dry goods selling business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from raising pigs. Novie is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to buy more stock of dry goods, such as slippers, shoes, dresses, etc., to sell for her dry goods business.  Novie has been sustaining her business activities through her past four loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Luz America
description: Luz is 49 years old and lives in Primavera, Duran (an area on the outskirts of the city which was originally built upon without official permission.  The area has several hills, streams and lakes which are still visible as the remains of a broken ecology).  Luz is single and her business is selling meals.  Luz started her business some time ago.  She set up the business because there was no food business in her neighborhood.  She works alone from 5.00pm to 10.00pm.  With the help of this loan, she would like to buy building supplies to fix up her home, so that she can have a space for her business.

name: Phythias
description: Phythias Mutinda K. is 31 years old.  He is married with one child and resides in the town of Mlolongo along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway.  Apart from his family, Mutinda also assists his elderly father by paying school fees for his twin brothers, who are 16 years old and in secondary school.  He has also taken in his 10 year old nephew after his sister - his nephew's mother - passed away in the year 2000.  After finishing his secondary school education in the year 1994, and not being able to find employment, Mutinda decided to engage into brick making.  Since this work did not require any capital to begin, all he needed to do was learn the skills of brick making.  After learning the basic skills, Mutinda made 5,000 pieces of bricks, which he sold for Ksh 5 per piece.  He earned a total of Ksh 25,000 (USD $368).  From this, he gave his wife Ksh 5,000 for household use, and the rest he saved.  He then made another 5,000 pieces of bricks, which again he sold for Ksh 25,000.  He saved all of this, totaling savings of Ksh 45,000 (USD $662).  With this as his initial capital, Mutinda bought an assortment of goods like spoons, shoes, pencils, books, small transistor radios, shoe polish, plastic plates, sufurias, etc.  He was using a bicycle to sell his wares.  Then, in the year 1996, Mutinda rented a stall in the town of Kitengela, on the outskirts of Nairobi.  The business was doing well, but due to stiff competition from neighbors, he opted to leave Kitengela and decided to try his luck in a neighboring, upcoming town by the name of Mlolongo.  Luck was on his side and he rented a stall, expanding his business by adding TVs, DVDs, and radios.  The business is doing well and Mutinda is still operating from this stall.  Due to the increasing population in Mlolongo, Mutinda wants to add to his inventory so that he can meet the demands of his customers.  He approached one leading micro-finance bank for a loan, but due to the high interest he opted not to take the loan.  Since then, he heard about Action Now Kenya partnering with Kiva, and also saw some of the clients who have benefited from Kiva loans.  Their businesses are flourishing, so Mutinda decided to come to Action Now Kenya to try his luck.  Mutinda, therefore, requests a loan of $1,175.  With this loan, Mutinda will be able to purchase TVs, radios, dvds, vcd players, vcd discs, and cassettes.  This will greatly improve his business, translating into more income.  Mutinda plans to employ a helper to assist him in the day-to-day operations of the business, and intends to repay the loan within 10 months.

name: Luis Carlos
description: Luis started his business in the year 1998. He is a humble and hard-working man who works as a shoe-maker.   Luis decided to set up his own business in order to create financial stability for his family. He has four grown-up children and was able to support and care for all of them thanks to his business.   Luis would now like to focus on his wife and his home and dedicate himself to improving their living conditions and to have money put away as they get ever closer to old age and retirement. Luis's goal is to have enough money that they need not go without.    Luis is seeking a loan to continue with and grow his business, he will use the money to buy materials such as leather, soles and glue. The loan will give Luis the raw materials he needs to be able to generate money to sustain and improve his home.

name: Rat's Group
description: Rat is aged 29 and married. She lives in a rural village of the Moung Russey district of Battambang province and she has three children. To make a living, she has been farming rice for 15 years and she is able to earn about 38,000 KHR per day.   Rat has been with VisionFund for three cycles and completely paid back the past loans. She is leading her group to ask for a loan. Rat wants to buy fertilizers for her farmland and use a portion of the loan for labor. She hopes to increase her crop yields and earn more income to improve her standard of living.

name: Ibtesam
description: Ibtesam is a careful mother of five children. She is a conservative woman and asked her son Ahmad to take ‎her place in the photo. She is a kind and hardworking woman.‎ Ibtesam's husband works and earns a low income, so he cannot cover his son's education expenses on top of the family's household expenses.‎Now Ahmad, who appears in the photo, is a student in his second year and he is doing well. Ibtesam always ‎tries to provide a good quality education to her children, so she asked for a loan to pay for her son's university tuition. She awaits your mercy.‎

name: Jebeth
description: Jebeth is a 23-year-old single woman from the town of Baclayon, Bohol. She has a vegetable business. She sells eggplant, squash, beans, tomatoes, green onions, and other green leafy vegetables to help augment the income of her household.   Jebeth started her business 1 year ago. She is asking for a loan to buy dried fish, oil, and eggs to maintain the inventory of the store. In the future, Jebeth hopes to expand her vegetable business and increase profitability to improve her status of living.

name: Maria Luz
description: Maria Luz D. P. is from the village of Fatima, Liloy, Zamboanga del Norte. She is 31 years old, married, and has two school-aged children. To make a living, Maria Luz works in the retail sector operating a clothing business. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from providing general clothing services to local community members. Maria Luz has been engaged in her business for over one year and earns approximately 2,000 PHP a month.  In 2011, Maria Luz joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Maria Luz is requesting a loan of 3,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional inventory. This loan will be Maria Luz's first loan taken out from PMPC.
