She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand her business.   About PMPC:  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Gilberto Agapito
description: Gilberto is an organic farmer, who cares about the environment. He is 27 years old and has two children, aged four and five, who go to school. His wife works as a merchant selling a type of bean called "chocho."   He has been following this occupation for 12 years now, and his future goals include having a plantation of "tara" (a small leguminous tree or thorny shrub native to Peru), having a basic necessities store, and providing his children with a high-level education.   He will use the loan to buy fertilizers and to increase his production of "tara."  He likes growing "tara" because this is a type of crop that doesn't require a huge investment; the plants have a life expectancy of over 100 years; and this business enables him to provide for his family and give his children an education.

name: Great People Group
description: Mama N., the woman holding the sign, is the leader of a group of five borrowers called Great People. She is 35 years old, single and has six children who range from 5 to 19 years old. She describes herself as hard working and serviceable. Her plan is to improve her business and educate her children.  For 3 years, she has been selling charcoal in Jacob’s Town community, outside of Monrovia, Liberia. She plans to use her 6,000 Liberian Dollars portion of this 30,000 Liberian Dollars group loan to buy more bags of charcoal.    She was not able to attend school due to lack of financial support.

name: Ana Doris
description: Ana studied until high school. She is married. Her husband is a driver and they have a six year old daughter.Ana has been selling French fries with sauce and cheese for five years. She works every evening. She decided on this business because she wanted to help her husband to cover the household expenses. She works at home and her mother helps her.She requests a loan to buy potatoes, oil, tomato sauce and cheese to continue her French fries business. She will also buy chairs for the customers.She hopes to keep her business running so that it generates income every day in order to meet the needs of her family.

name: Edgar
description: 34-year-old Edgar is a hard-working man who lives together with his wife Norma and his two children who he cares for and educates in his own home which is located in the village of Ricrican.  Edgar's main business activity is "farming" and this is the business in which he set off on the long path of hard work.  Edgar started growing potatoes and oats when he was very young.  He grows these crops once a year as his land is "seasonal" which means that they need the rainy season in order to grow anything.  However, in spite of this difficulty, Edgar always makes good profits from his harvests as he puts a great deal of effort into looking after his crops.  He also makes additional income by caring for his sheep.  He fattens the animals and then sells their meat for a good price.  This business makes him the income he needs to feed, clothe and educate his children who he would like to provide with a better quality of life.  Edgar is a member of the "Mirando a un futuro mejor" community bank and this is his 12th loan from MFP.  He is grateful for the support that they have offered him over the years.  Edgar pledges to make his loan repayments on time.  He tells us that he is very happy to belong to a very well-organized community bank.  With your support, he will invest the money he has requested in buying natural fertilizers for the crops which he is about to sow.

name: Mary
description: Mary A. is the 29-year-old mother of four children all of whom are in school. She is married to a businessman and runs her own salon in Nyamasaria slum. She will use the 20,000 KSH to purchase dryers, chemicals and other equipment that will help her grow her business.  Mary recently joined the K-MET volunteer Community Health Worker (CHW) group in Kisumu, Kenya. As a CHW she will be trained by K-MET and will begin visiting members of her community who are sick with a variety of illnesses. Her work will include distributing Nutriflour (a vitamin enriched flour produced by K-MET) to malnourished patients, providing reproductive health education, referring patients to local clinics and hospitals, and providing basic health care.

name: Jose Alfredo
description: Jose Alfredo is single and father to three children, none of whom are dependent on him. Jose Alfredo works to support his household, working from Monday to Sunday from 7:00am to 4:00pm. He has been selling groceries such as raspberries, vanilla, vinager and honey in one of the markets of the town of Chinandega for 10 years. Prior to that, he worked for a business, and with his savings, he decided to buy more merchandise to stock his wife's business. It was when she died that Jose Alfredo decided to continue the business.

name: Patrick
description: Patrick is a 44-year-old, married man, who has five children. He describes himself as a trustworthy and credible father. He is applying for a loan of KES 100,000, which he will use to purchase buckets, blankets, and water tanks for his business. This will help him to increase the stock at his store. The intended profits will be used to improve his family's welfare. This is his third loan through SMEP DTM. His previous loans were repaid successfully.

name: Joselyne
description: Greetings from M. Joselyne who is 24 years old and married. She and her husband have one child of 9 months, and she takes care of two orphans, 16 and 18 years old. This family currently lives in Gasabo, a district of Kigali City, the capital of Rwanda.   M. Joselyne is an entrepreneur who operates her business in Kigali City where she owns a retail shop selling different kinds of merchandise. Her husband produces a regular income of $240 per month.  Joselyne is seeking her first loan from Vision Finance Company of 500,000 Rwf to be repaid within 8 months. She has been running the same business since 2007 and has no employees. She does her daily work from 6:00 to 9:30 p.m. She earns a monthly profit of approximately $55.  With this loan Joselyne intends to expand her business and, from the increased profits, she will buy a house and have more savings.

name: Raeda
description: Raeda is a self made woman living in Khanyounis, Gaza Strip. Also her husband works in the public sector where the salary is very low and unstable. As a result of the high cost of living, she decided to open a new business. Her business idea was to sell some goods and inventory in bulk to the retail trader from the rickshaw.  A few years ago Raeda’s husband bought a new rickshaw and became famous, he also has loyal customers.   Now Raeda has a USD loan from FATEN. This loan will help her to buy some goods and inventory to resell from the rickshaw. By taking this loan, Raeda can help her husband to work more efficiently and increase his sales and also his profit.

name: Kalimer
description: Kalimer is from the Syunik region, which is famous for its severe cold climate. The best agricultural business for the locals is cattle farming and some limited land cultivation. Kalimer is engaged in cattle breeding. She keeps two cows, one mother pig, and six little pigs. Kalimer gets milk and milk products and her husband Artak sells them in the local market. This is the only source of income for their young family, so she and her husband work hard to gather more milk and earn income from the sales. As the farm is small and their income is hardly enough for covering daily costs, Kalimer has applied for this loan. The money from the loan will be used to expand the farm by purchasing two cows and a calf.   This is very important for Kalimer to get more milk and sell it. She dreams to have a big farm and improve her family's living conditions.

name: Kubaro
description: Kubaro was born in 1963. She is divorced, and she has two adult children. Her children are 20 and 27 years old. Kubaro is a highly educated person. Kubaro is a teacher. She has worked for more than 30 years in a local school. She loves her profession and she does her job with pleasure. Kubaro’s pupils like her lessons. She has small salary which is not enough to buy medicines that she needs because she is ill. Kubaro is asking for a loan of 3,500 Tajikistan somoni to buy medicines. She awaits your mercy.

name: Gil
description: Gil D. is from the village of Tagdo, Mambajao, Camiguin Province. He is 23 years old and married.  To make a living, Gil owns & operates a motorcycle transport services business in his local community.  Gil has been in business for over 2 years and earns approximately 4,000 PHP a month.  Gil joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Gil is requesting a new loan of 5,000 PHP to purchase materials needed to provide more transport services.  This loan will be his first from HSPFI.  He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to support his family.  ---------------------------- About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.

name: Alicia
description: Alicia is 57 years old and married with four children, one of whom is in school. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Alicia has a tailoring business in the Philippines. Alicia requested a PHP 12000 loan through NWTF in order to buy new supplies for her sewing machine.  Alicia has been in this business for 14 years. In the future, Alicia would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Nancy
description: Nancy is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a food vending business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for the past three years and also earns additional income from buying and selling school supplies. Nancy has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of loans through NWTF  Nancy is requesting a 30,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase additional ingredients for her food vending business. She dreams of building and expanding her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Veronica
description: Veronica makes a living selling sarongs. She is 49 years old, married and has six children. She lives in Benin City, Edo State, Nigeria. Veronica is applying for this loan to buy more sarongs to sell. She extends her thanks to all Kiva lenders for their help.

name: Elvia
description: Elvia is years old, is happily married to her husband and has 3 children. When she was a child she used to put her parents' cows out to pasture as they had large quantities of them and since she married she has worked in agriculture as her husband works in this.  Now they grow 3 to 4 hectares of potato, she says it is profitable for them,  above all when the market becomes scarce. She recently took them to sell and once that harvest can be stored, it lasts her 3 to 4 months and meanwhile she lives from the sale of her cows and when the price of potato increases she takes it to market. Cultivating her lands makes her happy, but it becomes difficult when she has to fertilize and medicate her lands.  This is her 7th loan with MFP, during this time she has demonstrated punctuality in her payments.  With this money she will buy fertilizers with nitrate, urea and 18 so that in this way her potato crops react well. This will cost her an approximate 3500 to 4000 soles.Translated from Spanish by Aimee Sostowski, Kiva Volunteer

name: Guillermo
description: Guillermo is single and lives with his mother.  He opened his hardware and building materials store with monies he inherited from his father when his father died.  He saved his money and every day added to his stock to expand his store.  His store is in a very busy meeting place in the very centre of the city of Hernandarias.  According to the references we obtained, he is a very hard-working and responsible person.Translated from Spanish by Laure Kwon, Kiva Volunteer

name: Stephen
description: Stephen is a 27-year-old married man with two children who are nine and three years old. They are living in Fort Portal, Uganda. Stephen's main business is retail, in addition to selling cows in order to boost his income.   Stephen is facing a challenge of limited capital and the general price fluctuations of essential commodities. However, he has a vision of constructing rentals to earn extra income. Stephen has asked for a loan to buy general merchandise for his retail business.

name: Jhona
description: Jhona works hard to support her family. Jhona is married and has a motorcycle transport business in the Philippines.She requested a PHP 20000 loan through NWTF to purchase spare parts and maintenance for her motorcycle.Jhona has been in this business for eight years now. In the future she would like to expand her business.

name: Ani
description: Ani is a nice farmer and mother of two sons (her younger son is in the photo).   Ani lives with her grandparents-in-law, husband and two sons. With the help of her family members, she takes care of their family farm. It includes livestock of cows, calves, sheep and chickens, and also arable land where barley, potato and emmer wheat are cultivated.   They reestablished their farm five years ago, and since that time, they were able to develop it into a sustainable and profitable farm. All Ani needs is some financial resources to purchase forage for feeding the livestock and a hand mower needed for the farm.  Because this is her first loan, it has been approved within the framework of the new joint initiative between Kiva and SEF. The first-chance loan program provides loans to people who didn’t have access to credit products before because they have no credit history.  Ani and her family members hope for lenders' support for their farming business.

name: Fati
description: Fati has a small stand where she sells groundnuts, beans, wheat, rice (in tins of "olonka", as it is locally called), and other provisions. She wants to open her own shop. She is seeking for a loan of $800.00 from Kiva to enable her open her own shop.

name: Mishi
description: Mishi is a married woman, and she has four children, three of whom attend school. Mishi lives in a rental house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest  monthly expenses are food and school fees.  Mishi operates a vegetable stall business, selling from home to her neighbours and passersby. She faces a challenge of stiff competition from other vegetable operators in her business.   With the Kshs 50,000 she wants to purchase sacks of tomatoes, potatoes, fruit and green vegetables for resale.

name: Lucy
description: Lucy is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a food vending business in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 29,500 through NWTF to buy ingredients for her food vending business.Lucy has been in this business for eight years. She earns more income from pig fattening.She successfully paid back her previous loan and now she requested an additional loan to further build her business.Lucy has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams of saving enough money so she could afford to send her children to college in the future.

name: Fidel Ángel
description: Fidel is 29 years old and left education after the third grade. He lives with his partner and two children. His partner studied until the eighth grade and looks after the household. Fidel works selling bread and also in farming. He has done these activities for ten years. To sell his bread, he has to travel some ten kilometres by motorbike.  He is requesting the loan to buy weedkiller, seeds and compost for an abundant harvest. Fidel's dream is to have his own home, support his children, prepare them academically and give them a dignified life.

name: Mao
description: Mao, 44 years old, is doing farming and earns $3 per day. Her husband is also a farmer and earns $3 per day. They have five children, four are studying and one more is a farmer and earns $3 per day. Every month, she has to spend $60 on food, $15 on electricity, $60 on school fees, and $30 on transportation.  She would like to request a loan of $1000 to buy cell cards from the mobile phone company to resell so that she can make some profit from it. She plans to sell grocery goods in front of her house after she rests from doing farming. She hopes to be able to send her children to study in the university after they finish high school.

name: Mohammad Nadar
description: Mohammad Nadar lives in district 8 of Kabul Afghanistan. He is not formally educated, but he has been involved in the bakery business for more than 9 years. He learned this business from his father. He is requesting a loan so he can open another bakery that will be his own business.

name: Douglas
description: Douglas is a 39 year old married man. He has five children, with ages ranging from 5 years to 20 years. He describes himself to be a visionary man.  He operates a motorcycle where he provides transportation. He has been involved in this business for five years and employs one staff member. His primary customers are motorcycle and bicycle owners.  He describes his biggest business challenge to be disturbance by local authorities.  He will use the KES 20,000 loan to buy motorcycle and bicycle spare parts.  His business goal is to be the best motorcycle provider of transportation in his home area.   He hopes that in the future, he will expand his business.

name: Future In Our Hands Group
description: John C. is the leader of this group of entrepreneurs. He was born in Makeni about 37 years ago. He is married to a businesswoman and the couple has four children: three in primary school and the other a baby.  For over ten years now, John has been selling different type of bags – school bags, ladies’ bags, traveling bags, etc.  This is the first loan that John and his group have applied for from SMT/Kiva lenders. With the help of this loan, they will be able to expand their businesses, make more sales and consequently improving their living conditions.  John will use his SLL 500,000 share of the loan to buy different types of bags wholesale to add to his current stock.

name: Omar
description: Omar is a 34-year-old, married man, who has been working as a carpenter since thirteen years ago. He is a hardworking man, well-known in his region for the special quality he produces and his special prices.Omar is acquiring a loan from Kiva's partner, Al Majmoua, to buy a special, newly-released saw. This particular saw is important for developing his business, and for producing high-quality, requested products.He hopes that in the future he will work on developing his business more, by buying a mini-truck. He needs a vehicle of this kind, in addition to his required business tools. He would use it to transport wood from the market, and finished work to his customers.

name: Hassan Galadima
description: Hassan Galadima remembers the extreme poverty that his family faced during a particularly bad harvest. This was before he became a Babban Gona Member. Now, Hassan Galadima, like all Babban Gona members, can earn up to $2000/ha this season from growing maize, more than three times the Nigerian farmer’s annual income. The average Babban Gona farmer yields 30 bags/hectare, double the national average of 14. However, Hassan Galadima is ambitious and is aiming to reap 35 bags per hectare this season.  “In 5 years, I want to become the most profitable farmer in my community”, expressed Hassan Galadima.  With this loan, he is well on his way to achieving this dream.

name: Betty
description: Betty is 46 years old and lives in the town of Zana in the Kampala Central region of Uganda.  She is married and has five children.  Three of her children are currently in school.  Betty has a business of rental houses, which she has had for 10 years.           To help expand her business, Betty has requested a loan of 1,500,000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda.  The loan will be used to purchase materials like cement to complete some rental houses.  With the help of the loan from BRAC, Betty hopes to generate greater profits and pay school fees for her children.    In the future, Betty hopes to expand her rental houses.  Betty is a member of BRAC’s Small Enterprise (SEP) Program, which has helped her prospects for the future by improving her standard of living.

name: Bella Mariana
description: Bella is 52-years-old.  She is a widow and has two children that are now adults, but she lives by herself in a suburban zone called Paraíso (Paradise).  She has a small store in the front of her house and a small sewing workshop where all kinds of clothing are brought in for mending or sewing.  In the store she sells chicken, rice, and eggs and in her sewing workshop she makes garments.  She works in both of these activities depending on how her orders go.  In order to continue working in her sewing workshop, she would like to purchase with her loan a sewing machine and fabrics.  In the future she would like to buy more sewing machines in order to have employees to help her and thus increase production.

name: Maximo
description: Maximo is married with three older children.  He works in a bakery located in his home.  Maximo already has an established clientele from having worked in this line of business for six years.  He originally worked in a cousin's bakery and, with a little capital, was able to become independent.  This loan will help to buy a vehicle, which will be very useful for distributing his products.  In the future he wants to expand his business and provide more jobs for the community.Translated from Spanish by Kara Gibson, Kiva Volunteer

name: Thinh's Group
description: Thinh’s group lives in a rural village in Battambang province in Cambodia. Thinh makes a living cultivating rice and she also does extra work as farmer to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: 05.08.01 Điện Biên Group
description: Mrs. Nhung operates a food stall selling beverages. She is requesting a loan to purchase ingredients for making drinks to sell. She has been involved in this business for 6 years. Nhung is 54 years old and is married with 2 grown children.  She and her husband live in Thanh Hoa, an urban town in Thanh Hoa province. Nhung is the group leader of the 05.08.01 Điện Biên solidarity group, which consists of 4 members. In 2009, Nhung joined Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women to improve her business. Nhung has successfully repaid 2 loans from Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women. The main harship that Nhung faces in her business is the lack of capital. Nhung hopes for her business to do well, for her children to find a good job, and for her family to be healthy and happy.

name: Jorge Luis
description: Jorge is 22 years old, single and he doesn't have children. He lives with his parents in "Recinto Terrenal", which belongs to the "The Old Town of the River" Province.   He belongs to the "Ventanilla Terrenal" which is located in "Recinto Terrenal". People in the "Pueblo Viejo" Province work mainly in farming and fishing.   Jorge is a farmer and grows corn. With this loan he will buy supplies such as fertilizer, manure and seeds. He will make his purchase in the city of Pueblo Viejo.   His dream is to buy more land to work. In his free time he likes to go out with his friends and play soccer.

name: Adah
description: Good day lenders! Meet one of KPP UMKM’s clients, Adah, who is 44 years old and married with two daughters and one son.Adah and her husband have been selling snacks for three years. She has asked for a loan of 7,400,000 IDR from KPP-UMKM Syariah. This loan will be used to build sanitation facilities at their home to improve access to sanitation and clean water for their family. Her family income is insufficient to build toilets and water sources, but Adah will be able to repay the loan received.She and her family want to live a healthy life with healthy sanitation and clean water. She is very grateful for the opportunity and wants to thank all lenders.

name: Pich
description: Mrs. Horn Pich, age 33, and her husband, Mr. Sokhoeun Vann, age 37, were married in 1993. They have six daughters and one son. Three of the children are in school and one daughter assists her mother in the business. The family lives on an island in the Mekong River about 15 kilometers from Phnom Penh City.  Pich has been selling vegetables for more than four years. Her husband is a farmer and, besides that, he is a wooden-house builder as well. Pich is asking for a loan of $250 to provide capital for her husband’s farming business.

name: Alexandra Beatriz
description: Alexandra is a young single person without children. She studies and works at supermarket as a cashier. She lives without her parents in the city of Pilar.     She is currently in her first year of study in the Environment Studies College in the National University of Pilar. She says she's doing well in her studies,  that she likes what she's studying, and that each day she puts forth effort. She says her dream is to finish at the university in the best possible way and later she can give back to society and to her parents who have helped her so much in her plans and goals.    She asks for a loan to pay for study materials and fees to be able to take her final exams. She thanks the Fundación for the opportunity given to her, since this is very important to her and her studies are very important.

name: Geraldine
description: Despite the hardships of life, Geraldine still believes that parents should be the best model for their children to follow someday. She and her husband sacrifice much so that their children may have a better future. Geraldine is married to Jose F. of Barangay San Leonardo in Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya where they currently live. They belong to a poor family and were not able pursue a college education. Their two children are studying in the elementary school right now. Geraldine, with the help and support of her husband, is doing her best to give them enough support.   She maintains a hog-raising business in their village in which she has a simple but powerful way to generate income. Her husband is a construction worker in their area. Geraldine is requesting a loan of PHP 6,000 from Kiva lenders to further sustain and grow her business. She also hopes someday to establish a general store to generate a daily income aside from hog raising.

name: Akwei Allah Group
description: Stephen is 48 years old. He is single and lives in his family house in the community where he lives. He works hard to support himself and business.   Stephen is a supplier of local palm fruits and palm oil. Palm oil is produced from palm nuts fruits. The palm oil is processed through various stages to obtain the palm oil, which is used to prepare many local dishes like fried fish and pastries, as well as local soaps. He supplies to food vendors to prepare their meals. He also sells the palm fruits to those who need them for further processing. He wants to use this loan to buy more bags of palm fruits. He believes the loan will enable him make more profit as we enter the Christmas festivities.   Stephen is the leader of a trust bank group called ‘Akwei Allah’, which literary means Except Allah. He is the one standing in the middle in the group photograph. Most of the members of this group are petty traders, food vendors, and farmers. In this group, members guarantee for one another as social collateral to access and repay the loan. The group would be grateful for your assistance.

name: Gina
description: Gina T. earns her living by operating a networking business. Her husband, Rolando T., age 57, works as an electrician to earn his living and also helps in his wife's business activities. They have six children between the ages of 7 and 24. Two of her children are already working while the other four attend school. The family lives in Prk. Caticong, Brgy. Cabadiangan, Compostela, Cebu City.   Gina joined NWTF-Project Dungganon in 2005 because she aspired toward something better for her family. With the help of her past eight loans from NWTF-Project Dungganon, Gina  has been working hard and incrementally lifting her family out of poverty. Her previous loan of PHP 20,000 helped her earn a monthly profit of PHP 7,000, which has helped raise the family's standard of living. This time, for her ninth cycle loan, she is borrowing PHP 23,000, which she intends to use as additional capital for her networking business so that she can continue to save up for the future education of her children. Gina T. is truly a Dungganon woman who is following an honorable path towards the achievement of her dreams.    About NWTF: In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon. Dungganon is a Hiligaynon word that means "honorable." Through this alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress from earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities they could not have imagined. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem that is bestowed to a member of a community who has earned the respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work. Help NWTF continue its mission to help the poorest in the Philippines by clicking the link to the NWTF Kiva lending team on Kiva.org to join our team.

name: Luza Group
description: This group is called Luza, and it is comprised of four ladies who live in Sana`a, Yemen.  Zahra is a 30-year-old woman who lives in Sana'a, Yemen. She is an entrepreneur, and she has been sewing shoes for five years.  She is totally dependent on the income from this business, to feed her family and to cover their living expenses.  She took a loan of 100,000 YER from Al-Amal Microfinance Bank. Her purpose in taking the loan was to purchase an industrial sewing machine for making shoes. This loan will help her to meet the demand of her clients. She hopes to improve her business and increase her profit.

name: Sylvester's Group
description: Sylvester M. is one of the executive members of Semuti group in Mityana.  He is a Chief at his Sub County where he collects taxes and revenue from markets and shops and gives out licenses.    Sylvester also has a retail shop in the Semuti trading center as his business, so whenever he is out of work, he goes to it to help out his wife.  He needs a loan to help with restocking his shop with more goods that can bring in more revenue.

name: Mavjuda
description: This is Mavjuda. She was born in 1975. Her husband is a farmer. It is very difficult for her to support three children with all their necessary needs. Mavjuda has been busy with animal husbandry for more than 3 years. She works in this field with pleasure because she likes animals. She was born and grew up in a village, so she has great experience in this field. Mavjuda buys animals in the local market and fattens them in her barn. After some months she sells the animals in the local market. Her children help her with the business.She wants to increase the number of cattle, so she has to increase her working capital. Mavjuda is currently asking for a loan from IMON of TJS 2,000 to buy cattle. She used her previous loan for her business. She awaits your support.

name: Tahmina
description: Tahmina is a housewife and a mother of 3 children; she requires funds to buy a new rickshaw for her husband. The family's income is generated through the transportation business and they barely make ends meet. Her husband is the main earner of the family and generates all his the income from driving the rickshaw.   Unfortunately the current rickshaw has completely broken down, halting the inflow of income. This has resulted in Tahimas children skipping school due to lack of resources at their mother's disposal.  She wants a loan to help her husband to buy a new rickshaw and start generating income once again which would streamline all her activities and thus send her children back to school to get an education.

name: Veronica Yesenia
description: Veronica is a hard-working, enthusiastic woman who lives in the city of Camaná. Camaná is known for its beautiful beaches, warm temperature and the generosity of its inhabitants. She finished high school and wanted to study cosmetology, but didn’t. Like all good Peruvians, she likes typical Peruvian food; one of her favorites is Parrillada (barbecued meat). Veronica is the mother of 2 children, aged 10 and 12, who are in school. She loves them very much and they are her reason to be and to continue getting ahead.      With much effort and dedication, she was able to save some money and she now has a business selling tamales and humitas, both made with milled corn, seasoning made from spices, and pork, among other ingredients. Her seasoning is so good that the majority of her clients come back for more. She thinks her business is doing very well because her clients come back for more and that motivates her.  Veronica is grateful to the Kiva lenders for the help they will give her. With this loan, she’ll be able to buy a new stove and school supplies she can sell at her business. She’ll be able to prepare more food in less time and have extra income from the school supplies she sells and that way she can continue with her big dream: to see her children become professionals and to see herself grow as a businesswoman.

name: Florencio
description: Florencio is a grower of rice crops within his locality. He is married and blessed with four children.Florencio is an expert in the farming business since he has been cultivating his farmland for more than 23 years. He also raises hogs as an additional source of income for his family.Florencio is now preparing his rice farmland to plant again, but his capital is not enough to buy the necessary farm inputs such as a variety of seeds and fertilizer. With his situation, he is asking for a loan of PHP 20,000.He hopes to obtain the said loan amount to keep his farmland productive.

name: Franqui Alexander
description: Franqui is a man who is very dedicated to his work, he works as a shoemaker he not only repairing shoes but also doing small orders for making shoes.  He started his business out of financial necessity, because he likes to work independently, because this is what he knows how to do, because he is passionate about it and because he has a workshop located in a room of his home.  Franqui is humble, he knows he needs a lot to progress and get out of his poor conditions, but he just has to work honestly and rely on God so that his situation will improve.  He is searching to generate future employment, increase his number of customers, buy his own home.  He is requesting a loan to purchase supplies like glue, soles, spare heels, nails, leather, etc.

name: Lilia
description: Lilia is 59 years old and is married with three children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Lilia has a business selling dried fish in the Philippines. She has been in this business for 2 years. She requested a loan of 6,500 PHP through NWTF to buy more dried fish to sell in her food stall.  In the future, Lilia would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Nget
description: Nget is a 59-year-old married woman living in a rural area of Moung Russey district in Cambodia’s Battambang province. She is blessed with six children, one (a son) of whom is still dependent on her. Nget and her husband offer a decent life for the family by working as rice farmers. To add more income to the family, Nget also has a business selling dessert. They are able to earn around 6,000KHR per day and save only approximately 3,000KHR after canceling out the daily expenses. Nget has been with Kiva’s partner, VisionFund, for five loan cycles already, with which she succeeded in improving the family’s livelihood. She is now seeking a KHR 4,000,000 loan to purchase fertilizer, pesticide, and to pay wages to farm laborers to harvest rice. Nget hopes to harvest a good-quality crop so that she can sell it for a good price, generating more income for the family.

name: Fotemogoban (La Valeur Humaine Est Intarissable)) Group
description: Living in extended traditional families (with children, co-spouses, and in-laws) in the village of Téné in San prefecture (the fourth administrative region of the Republic of Mali), the members of Fotemogoban group are women who are married, and on average are 39 years old with seven children. The group is primarily involved in trading crops (fonio, beans, and peas) and other small items. Working for the past two years with the micro-finance institution Soro Yiriwaso, the loan amounts have gone from 50,000 the first time to 125,000 FCFA for the fourth loan. The current loan will be used to buy bags of fonio (a kind of millet), beans, and peas in Fangaso and Djeli to retail them in the markets in San and Koutiala prefectures to retailers who come from Ségou and Bamako. Turnaround is very quick because the cycle (purchase-sale) is weekly. Thus the profit margin is significant and the members of Fotemogoan group plan to make an average profit of 100,000 FCFA during the loan period.    Translated from French by Liana Bianchi, Kiva Volunteer

name: Thuy
description: Thuy is 34 years old. She has three children. Her 14-year-old son is a carpenter. The two others are learning in high school and primary school. Her husband is a construction worker. He earns about 4,500,000 VND per month. Thuy raises chickens to earn a living. Her income is about 3,000,000 VND. She has done this job for six years. Her family’s total earnings are about 7,500,000 VND per month.   She has participated in SEDA's credit program since 2008. In the last cycle, she borrowed 9,184,000 VND and repaid the loan on time. In this loan cycle, she would like to borrow 9,632,000 VND to buy food for her chickens. She always wants to expand her business and raise her children well.

name: Rosalinda
description: Production of vegetables is the business that Rosalinda M. ventured in. With the assistance of her husband Orlando who is a vendor of charcoal, Rosalinda is able to implement her vegetable production and vending. The couple is thankful because they have been blessed with a boy named Orly, he is now 16 years old and is currently studying. Being a good couple, they are doing their best to give their son a good future by continuously sending him to school and someday earn a degree.   Rosalinda hopes that she could supply sufficient needs of her family. She works hard to double the income she generates. According to her, she also would like to have her business grow and this will be pursued if she could have enough business capital. For this reason, she then applied for loan from KIVa lenders amounting to PHP4, 000. She hopes that lenders will allow her borrow the amount requested.

name: Afes
description: Afes Aliyev is a 31-year-old married farmer who has small sheep herd. Afes lives in the southern Azerbaijani region, Saati, in Alisoltanli village. He is an internally displaced person from Nagorniy Karabakh, who fled to Saatli during Azerbaijani-Armenian conflict in 1993.  He sells mutton to the local and capital traders and he is very successful in his business because meat is in high demand all across Azerbaijan and people use it in homes and cafes a lot. Afes has eight years experience in this field. Now Afes has decided to expand his business and purchase one milk cow and fodder. He is going to sell dairy products like milk and yoghurt. The estimated cost for a cow is 700-800 USD.

name: Breiner
description: Breiner is 23 years old and generates his own income as a merchant in the city of Cartagena. He started his business 4 years ago helping his aunt with a store she owned. When his aunt fell gravely ill, she rented it to him and today he generates income that he pays his aunt with. He makes enough to support himself and to acquire his own equipment. Every day the business belongs to him more and he wants to be able to have enough infrastructure to be able to be totally independent. Breiner sells food, groceries and basic family basket items as well as beverages. Right now he doesn't have enough working capital to meet his goal of growing and paying for things upfront which will bring optimal prices for the items he sells. That is why he turned to a Kiva loan, the first loan he has taken out with the Fundación Mario Santo Domingo. With it, he will buy rice, sugar, oil, beverages and other groceries to have a better selection and keep getting new customers, which will finally make his business sustainable. His biggest dream is to own his own home and become more autonomous every day.

name: Adriana María
description: Adriana is a 46 year old woman with great life ambitions. Since she was very young she has worked in the fields, which has awakened in her a great love for nature and animals. Raising animals has been her commercial activity and she has generated earnings from this work to provide sustenance to her family. Currently she makes a living raising pigs, an activity that she hopes to alternate with raising chickens. For this reason she is requesting a loan that she will invest in making improvements to her pens, sheds and to purchase animals of various ages to ensure the production of eggs and meat during all times of the year.   Thanks to this investment, Adriana will begin with her project of creating a micro-enterprise and will be able to increase her earnings and optimize her space and natural resources that she has in front of her home.

name: Irma
description: Irma is a young woman, 38 years old, from Ozurgeti district. She has a 7-member family, and they don't have any significant income. The family has been designated as "subsistence poor" and are living with poverty. They get social assistance from the local government. Apart from this, they have a small agricultural enterprise: they own a plot of agricultural land, where they grow nut trees and citrus.   Irma has a great desire to do her bit for her family's welfare, and to somehow increase their income. Irma requested a loan from Credo to start a trading business. Her loan request was approved in the framework of a joint initiative by Kiva and Credo. The start-up loan program envisions providing business start-up and restart-up credit with soft conditions for the country's rural poor, who are regarded as "high risk borrowers" because of their low income and lack of access to credit products.  Irma plans to purchase clothing and resell it among her villagers and neighbors. The loan will greatly assist Irma and her family, enabling them to cover daily costs and improve their living conditions. They await your help.

name: Shirin
description: Shirin is a first-year student of AUCA, department of Liberal Arts and Sciences, and here is her story:  “Each of us, after ending school, should choose the university and the faculty where he or she wants to study. People are convinced that a person who goes to his work with pleasure and comes back home gladly every day, is the happiest one. Most of us are supposed to think about our future careers since childhood. But when we become older, we always change our viewpoints and preferences. Not all images, which we dreamed about, satisfy us. We become more realistic, and start envisaging a profession we want to choose. This is the choice of our path to the real life.  The world of departments of universities is prodigious. It consists of huge number of professions. Each of us is responsible for solving a great issue, for the new step in our life. in this moment of our lives, we doubt, take suggestions, hesitate, and listen to parents and friends opinion. This particular line of professions require people be able to make decisions quickly and manage people. Unfortunately, not always that we can define our abilities and make the right decisions at our young ages. I think no one, neither young nor old, can say quickly whatever decision they are up to.   I thought many times and made a decision to enter the Liberal Arts department. What I like in this department is that it teaches leadership skills to us, historic thinking, religion, etc. Another reason to choose this department is that I would like to know little about juridical knowledge too. As a student of the department, it is necessary for me to graduate the university as a highly qualified person who is capable to think critically, and work in group by using my knowledge that I will already have.   Another opportunity that AUCA gives to every student is a Kiva loan. It is what can make dreams come true. I am applying for the loan as well, as I have financial difficulties and am not able to cover my tuition fees fully.”

name: Antonio
description: Antonio is 55 years old and lives in Mialen Clarin, Philippines. He is married with 3 children.  Antonio is a tricycle driver. He earns about 4,000 PHP each month doing this type of work. Antonio has requested a loan to provide capital for his banana cue business to purchase bundles of bananas for his snack vending business. This is Antonio's new business venture for added income.  Antonio has been a member of PMPC for 5 years. In the future, Antonio would like to save and earn more profits.

name: Nazeeran
description: Nazeeran is a responsible mother of 3 children. She lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. For many years, her husband has provided transport services by driving a taxi. Her husband is responsible for fulfilling the needs of the entire family. Her husband needs to replace his taxi's tires because the current condition of his tires is not good, but due to insufficient financial means, he is unable to do so. Therefore, Nazeeran has applied for a Kiva loan from its field partner, BRAC Pakistan. With the help of this loan, Nazeeran's husband can easily afford to replace his tires. This will allow him to provide better transport services and to increase his income. With her husband's increased profits, Nazeeran plans to start a savings to meet her family's needs in future.Nazeeran is very grateful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Rose
description: Rose is 48 years old, married with school-age children from Balintawak, Aurora, Zamboanga del Sur. She is a rice farmer that is her primary source of income. She has been into this type of business for 10 years. She asks for a loan from Paglaum MPC through the loan program intended to farmers like her. The amount that she loaned shall be used to purchase bags of fertilizers. Rose is thankful that she has saved enough and able to purchase another agricultural area for her to till.
town: Pagadian - Balintawak, Aurora, Zamboanga Del Sur

name: Marites
description: Marites runs a manicure and pedicure business. She also manages a small variety store for additional income. She is now asking for a loan of PHP 5000 from Kiva. Marites works diligently so she can send her children to college. She is hoping to provide them with all their needs so that, some day, there will be greater possibilities for them to uplift themselves and their family.  Marites is a woman who has a strong fighting spirit. She never considers problems to conquer her life because she has a principle that says “If you let your worries conquer you, you will never win.” Marites is 34 years old and is married to Samuel L., who carves wood and assembles simple furniture that they purchase in their village.

name: Anna Rizza
description: Anna Rizza is 24 years old, married, and has two children. She lives in Clarin, Misamis Occidental. She owns and operates a farm, planting and harvesting rice for sale, to earn a living. She has been in her business for over two years and earns PHP 4,000 every month. She just joined GDMPC this year to gain access to financial services, and to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.

name: Flor De María
description: Flor de Maria AB. T. belongs to the Community Bank "Mujeres Lideres", located in Jr. Tupac Amaru N° 585 – 09 de Octubre of the District of Callería.  She is 55 years old.  She repairs sewing machines and is a seamstress.  She has 5 children and her husband is a chainsawman.    The first loan she received was for S/.300.00 Nuevos Soles (~$100 USD).  She used the loan to purchase a used sewing machine with which she made shirts, shorts, and pants for children.  She sold her clothes in her district with the help of her husband, who did not have a job at the time.    With the loan for $600 she will purchase needles, spare sewing machine parts, and fabric to continue making outfits for girls.    She travels along the river bank of the Ucayali river, offering to repair sewing machines and selling her hand sewn clothing.    She is very grateful to Manuela Ramos for her confidence and support.    Translated from Spanish by Matthew Raimondi, Kiva Volunteer

name: Barfi
description: Barfi is a resident of the Varzob district of Tajikistan.  She is 50 years old, a wife and a mother.  She works as a cleaning lady in a school, and in addition to this job, she sews clothes for women and children.  Barfi learned how to sew from her mother who taught her all the minor details of this activity.  Barfi has already devoted 22 years of her life to sewing and she now wants to improve her working conditions.  For this reason, she has applied for a loan to buy a new sewing machine.  Please support Barfi now.

name: Yamileth Del Rosario
description: Mrs. Yamileth, thanks to the support that she has been given by Afodenic, continues building her great dream, her own house.  With great effort and much work, she has been able to put up the house and her future plan is to be able to finish it and together with her child have a dignified home.  With this new loan she will be able to purchase materials like iron, cement, and concrete blocks in order to continuing putting up the house.  She is thankful to Afodenic for offering her once again a loan and above all for the confidence shown in her.

name: Damaris
description: Damaris F. started her local store ten  years ago with little financial capital and few products. As time has gone by, she's been able to fill her business' shelves.  The reason for which she's asking for support from Ceprodel is to be granted a loan, urgently needing to purchase retails products to immediately offer her customers and thus to continue her business that requires so much support.  Translated from Spanish by Todd Schmid, Kiva Volunteer

name: Маtluba
description: Matluba Asoeva is 21 years old. She has a secondary education. She is single. Matluba grew up in a poor family so she had no opportunity to continue her education and she learned how to sew national dresses and caps for women. She acquired sewing skills very fast and became a professional seamstress.  Summer is wedding season, so she sews dresses and caps for brides and in winter she knits woolen clothes to provides warmth. Her business brings a good income to her family. She has three years of experience in this business. For the loan amount for $1000, Matluba is going to buy materials for dresses and national caps. Also she is going to buy yarn to knit warm clothes, because in winter the yarn will be more expensive. This loan helps to increase the range of women's dresses and provides inexpensive materials for knitting warm clothes, thus providing good-quality cheap clothes.  Matluba is going to pay off the loan for 12 months.

name: Soa
description: Mrs. Soa Y., age 46, is a widow and the mother of two children, ages 18 and 21. Her 18-year-old son works as a construction worker and make around $3 each day.   Mrs. Y. buys recyclable items from different locations in her town and resells them to the recycling plant, making about $4/day of net income.   In order to make her recycling business operate faster and more easily, Soa Y. has applied for a loan to purchase a motorbike to use for business transportation. With the remainder of the loan, she will buy more recyclable items to sell so she can increase her profit margin.

name: Jefferson
description: Jefferson lives in Compound #3.  He is 34 years old and married with four children.  He is educated through the 9th grade level.    Since 2005, he has been selling cement, building materials and others items.  He learned this method of selling from his parents.  He is requesting a loan to purchase more cement, building materials and other items for his business.  He plans is to educate his children and expand his business.

name: Mary
description: Mary is forty-six years old. She is married and has given birth to six children, all in school. She lives with her husband and children in a rented apartment in a town called Kade in the Eastern Region of Ghana. Kade is a commercial town. However, the majority of the inhabitants practice farming as a hobby or as a major occupation alongside other trading activities.   Mary trades in utensils. She sells at the local market and also treks to other communities to sell on their market days. Mary buys the goods from nearby towns. She has been in business for two years and wants a loan to buy all kinds of utensils to expand her business.

name: Alpha
description: Alpha is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a business buying and selling rice in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF in order to purchase additional sacks of rice to sell.  Alpha has been in this business for 11 years. She earns additional income from direct selling Avon products.  She has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to save enough money so that she could afford to send her children to college in the future.

name: Tomasa
description: This is Tomasa. She previously accessed an 26,000 PHP loan that she used to purchase merchandise items and products needed in her business. Her earnings were a big help in her personal, household, and business expenditures.   She would like to apply for another 26,000 PHP for her to buy more merchandise items and products to increase her product inventory. The more items displayed at the store the better. More items to sell will result in better profit. Her profits from business will definitely help her to sustain her family's daily needs. She looks forward to this financial increase with gladness and thankfulness in her heart.  Tomasa hopes to expand her business and dreams to give a good life to her family. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her work every week.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the word of God, build social capital and pay micro-finance loans.

name: Wanjala
description: Wanjala is married and has children. She owns a house that neither has electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees for her children. She has operated a fish selling business at the market, selling to her town dwellers and neighbors’. She faces a major challenge of high cost of purchasing fish especially during cold currents in the deep sea.  She is requesting for a loan to purchase bundles of fish, cooking  oil and firewood. She decided to join Yehu to access loans at lower cost to improve her business.

name: Paulina
description: Paulina’s story is of an honest, hardworking, warrior woman; a woman who left everything to raise her 7 children. With very few resources, she has pulled through. Paulina is a responsible and diligent smallholder farmer from Lolduka village, who is involved in dairy and maize/corn farming. Her work brings home an important source of income. She gets help with the work from her family members.   Paulina is seeking a loan to purchase quality farm inputs. Paulina will use the money from your loan investment to buy important supplies such as herbicides and pesticides to manage weeds and preserve the harvested produce. She also plans to use part of the money to pay laborers, loaders and transporters.   Paulina is optimistic that this year's harvest will be better than last season's. Income from the dairy will be used to make initial loan repayments until the crops are harvested and sold.  Most microfinancers, particularly in the Nandihills area of Kenya, don’t give loans to smallholder farmers, but Juhudi Kilimo is different. Juhudi Kilimo is expanding into this market and is happy to provide Kiva lenders with the opportunity to support Kenyan smallholder farmers.  Be inspired; make a loan!

name: Bartolomea
description: This is Bartolomea. She sends you her thanks for your generosity because her previous loan has entrenched her business. She was able to purchase additional grocery products needed to increase her product inventory. The loan also helped her provide for their daily needs.  She is very positive that she could improve her business more if you will lend her an amount of 21,000 PHP. This new loan will go to additional stock of groceries, toiletries and beverages. Her customers will be likely to buy more items if she has more of her products displayed in her store. An increase in sales will also result in a significant increase in profit, which will also result in her business becoming viable and sustainable. Simultaneously, she could sustain the needs of her family.  Bartolomea hopes that her business will continue to operate in the coming years. She also wants to have a wider and better place for her business. She meets every week with her *co-fellowship members to share stories of her work and to also draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Saniya Group
description: The ten women of the Saniya group are mainly married into polygamous families and are on average 44 years old with four children. They all live in the village of Gachi in the rural district of Tesserela and became acquainted through neighborhood ties, kinship and their petty trade activities.   They buy and sell soap, charcoal, milk, groundnuts and shallots. In order to increase their working capital, the group members joined Soro Yiriwaso and are on their first joint loan cycle.  Mrs. Mah (second woman sitting from the left in the picture) is known by the whole village for selling different kinds of groundnuts (roasted or not and sometimes peanuts). She plans to use her loan to buy a bag of groundnuts at the Gassola fair. Resale is made for cash and credit to both men and women customers.  With this loan, Mrs. Mah hopes to achieve average monthly profits of 10,000 FCFA to be reinvested in the business and to take care of household needs for condiments. Like the other women in the group, she aims to consolidate her revenue-generating activity in this partnership with Soro Yiriwaso.  Note: absence in the photo of Alimata and Djénébou due to a relative's funeral in the village of Siradoba

name: Anara
description: Anara is 59 years old and married. She raises livestock to provide a source of income for her family. Her farm, which she started during the Soviet period with 20,000 som, today earns around 20,000 som (KGS) per month from sales of milk and dairy products. In order to continue developing her business, Anara has turned to Bai Tushum & Partners for a loan of 60,000 som (KGS) to purchase two calves for fattening and subsequent resale. Anara plans to invest her profits into further livestock purchases.

name: Kuwadzana Kwemadzimai Group
description: Greetings from Zimbabwe! This is 28-year-old Rudiya from Mutare. Rudiya is a member of the group called Kuwadzana Kwemadzimai. She is single with no children. She cares for one dependent. Rudiya runs a retail business selling electrical goods, furniture and clothes. The business has been in operation for four years. She says the main challenges are late payments from clients who buy on credit and high import duties. Rudiya has requested a loan of $600 of the $1,800 group loan to buy television sets and radios for resale. She says the extra income generated as a result of this loan will allow her to send her sister`s son to a better school. In the future Rudiya plans to build her own shop and expand the business.

name: Charles
description: Charles is thirty-four year old and married to Grace. For the past three years he has run a food kiosk and makes a monthly income of 26,000 KES.  This will be Charles' second loan with KADET LTD. He plans to use all of this 53,000 KES loan to buy supplies like rice, flour, sugar, etc. in bulk. In the future he wants to own a hotel and employ more people.

name: Onisa
description: Onisa is thirty-two years old and married with a child.  He runs a general merchandise business in the market of Makeni, in Sierra Leone.  Onisa says he started the business at the age of twenty-two as he could not continue with his education.  The business was small, but with the previous loan from SMT, it has grown to the current level and he is now able to rent a kiosk as business premises. Onisa would like to increase his inventory to be able to generate more profits.  For this purpose, he is requesting a loan of US$ 200.

name: Reycel
description: Reycel works hard to support her family. She is single and has a rafia-production business in the Philippines. Reycel requested a 12,000-Philippine-peso (PHP) loan through NWTF to buy items for rafia to sell to customers. Reycel has been in this business for 10 years. In the future, Reycel would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Ilhom
description: Ilhom E. is a young man of 36, who is married and has four children.  Ilhom sells meat at the Spitamen regional produce market.  In the past he would purchase the less desirable cuts from two head of beef per week, but now he has expanded his selection and he buys four to five steers and three sheep.  Ilhom and his brother buy their livestock at the regional cattle market, as well as in neighboring Kyrgyzstan.  He is quite satisfied with his business as it helps him to feed his large family.Translated from Russian by Joyce ., Kiva Volunteer

name: Patron De San Jeronimo Ii Group
description: The members of the community bank "Patron de San Jeronimo II" are located in the city of Cusco, having their meeting headquarters in the Huanchac district.  Our members alternate their various activities between different business and services. Among the members there are taxi drivers, mechanics, members that have grocery stores, a bookstore, a teacher, and members who sell  beauty products, wood, anticuchos (grilled meats) and another member who sells candy. Our members are requesting the loan to reinvest in their different businesses and in this way see greater earnings in a smaller amount of time.  Our members are thankful and value the loan granted in this manner and at the same time promise to make their repayments on time.   Translated from Spanish by Kate Divjak, Kiva Volunteer

name: Lucila
description: Lucila is a member of the Communal Bank "Amigas Unidas" (United Friends). Lucila lives with her husband and she is 49 years old.  She has two children who are 14 and 12 years old.  They both go to public schools. Lucila has always worked hard to keep her home nice and to take care of her family.  Five years ago she decided to visit a beauty consultant and the consultant told Lucila about how great it would be if she started selling beauty products.  The consultant explained the system of sales and Lucila liked it.  She decided to sell beauty products through catalogues. At the moment she takes products to different companies and also offers the products directly to her friends. Lucila needs a loan $325 (1000 Soles), so that she can buy beauty products out of catalogues to sell. Ever since Lucila has been in the group Finca she has seen that investing money in purchasing more merchandise has helped her to grow her business.  Lucila's dream, is to fulfill all the needs of her children and to have her own business.  Translated from Spanish by San Roque School, Kiva Volunteer

name: Betty
description: Betty K. is currently in the business of brewing and selling local alcoholic beverages at home and is requesting a loan to stock more materials to use. Betty is 29 years old and is married to a driver. She has five children and her children go to school. With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to open up a restaurant.  About BRAC  BRAC's holistic approach to poverty alleviation and empowerment of the poor encompasses a range of core programs in economic and social development, health, education, human rights and legal services, which are delivered through an extensive network of village organizations. BRAC has become one of the world's largest NGOs as measured by the scale and diversity of its interventions.  In 2007, BRAC started operations in Southern Sudan. The microfinance program, which is targeted towards returning war refugees, has already formed 418 village organizations with more than 14,000 women members.

name: Salasala Group
description: Rehema B., age 30, is married and has three children, who are 5, 7 and 10 years old. She sells fruits and vegetables and has been in this business since 2007. From the business, she is able to able to earn a monthly profit of around $110.  This will be Rehema’s first loan from Tujijenge Tanzania, a Kiva partner. She hopes to obtain a loan to increase her business. 	 Rehema will share this loan with her loan subgroup, which includes two other members. The members of the group will hold each other accountable for paying back the loan. Rehema is the woman in the middle of the picture.

name: Irene
description: Irene lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is married with 4 children and 2 go to school. She has no additional family members. Irene operates a restaurant at the market on a retail basis. She has been in this business for the last 20 years. She works seven days a week. She has requested a loan of 400,000 UGX from MCDT – SACCO to buy bunches of green bananas, flour, rice, cooking oil and serving utensils. Her major challenge includes seasonality and transportation. Her goal and aspiration is to buy a fridge to start selling cold drinks. She lives in a rented house and the family has access to electricity and does not have access to piped water. Her major monthly expenses include rent and school fees.

name: Ma. Venus
description: Maria Venus is 44 years old and married with three children. She earns a living by having a pig fattening business in the Philippines. Ma. Venus is borrowing 11,000 PHP through NWTF to buy feeds and vitamins for her pigs.  Ma. Venus has been in pig fattening for 2 years and also earns additional income from buying and selling dry goods.  She is working tirelessly towards the attainment of her dream: to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Kem
description: The people shown in the photo are Mrs. Kem L. and her husband. They are villagers living with their children in a medium-sized home in Kompong Cham Province.  This couple owns 2 hectares (5 acres) of farmland that they inherited many years ago from their grandparents. On their land, they grow different kinds of crops and are able to plant twice a year.  The heavy rains are falling everywhere and this situation is good for planting. However, Kem L. doesn’t have capital yet to use on her farm. Thus, she is looking for a loan to use towards purchasing fertilizer, insecticide, a water pump and seed to grow, and to pay for a laborer to plow their farmland.

name: Lagimaina
description: Lagimaina is a 33-year-old woman who is married with 5 children.   Lagimaina runs a small tailoring business in her community, where she has gained 9 years of experience. She has requested a loan in order to buy rolls of material, a new sewing machine, thread, needles, and a pair of scissors.   Lagimaina plans to use her profits to pay for her family's weekly expenses and help with her children's cost of education. She joined SPBD in 2005 to gain access to financial services.

name: Mable
description: Mable is a 38-year-old single mother with four children living in a semi-permanent house in Fort Portal, Uganda. Her family dream is to build rental houses and educate her children. She has been selling produce for the last five years. She started with 500,000 shillings, but now her business has over two million shillings. Her biggest challenges are the constant price changes and her dream is to own a big food store. Mable needs the loan to buy maize grains for selling.

name: Suhrobjon
description: Suhrobjon A. is a married man with four children. With the desire to generate enough money to send his children to college (so that his children can get ahead in life), he started a business 8 years ago whereby he processes and sells dried apricots. As such, he is very experienced in this line of business, which allows him to attract more and more clients each day. Now, Suhrobjon is seeking a loan in the amount of $825 over a 9-month term. He plans to use the loan proceeds to purchase additional dried apricots, which will be processed and sold in turn. With your help, Suhrobjon will be extremely proud, knowing that (through much effort) his children will be able to attend college and to succeed in life.   Information about Tajikistan: Tajikistan is well known for the following: (1) its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road; (2) the end of Alexander the Great's rule; and (3) its famous great thinkers, philosophers, scientists, and poets such as Rudaki, Ibn Sina (Avicenna), Firdousi, Omar Haiyam, Jomi, and Mavlavi Rumi, to name a few.  The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC.  And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture, and Central Asian traditions.  On the other end of the spectrum, Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics.  The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy.  In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and thus only 7% of the land is arable; accordingly, this confluence of factors has resulted in high levels of unemployment and has forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries (primarily Russia).  Even though the people of Tajikistan are working hard to improve the country's agriculture and manufacturing sectors, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.   IMON International's History: Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low-income clients represent a viable business proposition.  Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need.  To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj.

name: Aliya
description: Aliya (her husband is pictured) is 27 years old and the mother of 2 children. The Isayevas live in the Khachmaz region of Azerbaijan, where they run a butcher shop. They need a loan of $850 to buy more cattle for this business.

name: Marilyn
description: Marilyn works hard to support her family. She is married and has a fishing business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for 27 years.  Marilyn requested a PHP 14,500 loan through NWTF to purchase more fishing gear and other equipment.   In the future, Marilyn would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Nora
description: Nora is a unique woman, always strong and awe-inspiring. She is 44 and, together with her husband Percy, works to get ahead. They own a home in the village of Patay. In spite of the fact that her husband works in another city and they don't have great needs, this hardworking woman likes to be independent and strong. For 20 years she has worked in agriculture. She started with her husband planting crops native to the region like: gladiolus flowers, fava beans, peas and potatoes. Some years ago Percy went to work outside the city, leaving Nora in charge of the farm lands. Thanks to her good judgement she has done well. Once a month she travels to the country's capital to sell her harvest. For all of the capability she is showing, she wants in the future to improve her crops and generate more profits. For now she is focused on her next harvest of potatoes and peas.  She is happy to help others like her to get ahead. She belongs to the village bank "Picaflores de Patay" and this is her 5th loan with MFP. She is the secretary of her association, and is an honest and hardworking member. She hopes that all of you will support her as she continues towards her goals.  Nora will invest the money in the purchase of a bag of pea seeds for which she will need 3 sacks of natural fertilizer which will ensure a good start for her crop.

name: Maria
description: María, 46, is married to Eugenio, 54, and they have three children. They live in a rented, well-built house. She opened a grocery store shortly after leaving her demanding job working as a restaurant cook. The business was very small at first, but over the years she has been able to build it by selling products such as cakes, sodas, and other foodstuffs. Her daughter helps her at times, which lets her spend time with her family.   In order to keep her business stocked and service her customers, she is applying for a loan to buy merchandise. Maria's long-term goal is to grow her business and add gaming machines. This will be her second loan cycle with MFP. She believes this will be a great opportunity to grow her business. She needs 2,000 nuevos soles to buy grains, sodas, cookies, jams, noodles, and sweets.

name: Luciana
description: Luciana is 56 years old, married and lives in Toril, Aloran, Philippines. In order to earn a living she takes in and raises pigs from their neighborhood. The piglets' owners share in the profits upon sale, to be divided 60/40 or 70/30 depending on their agreement.  With a desire to earn more, she decided to raise pigs on her own as well. Through Pauglam PC she obtained the capital to purchase her original piglets and feed. Now, she is requesting a loan of 10,000 PHP to buy additional feed. She really hopes and prays that her business will grow and benefit her family, in addition to the income of her husband. Someday, she wants to build a concrete pig cage to easily keep more sanitary conditions.

name: Dama
description: Dama is a widow. Her five children are all grown up. She owns a house with neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is food for her grandchildren because some of them are orphans.    Dama has run a vegetable grocery for the past three years; her clients are her neighbors and passers-by. She faces a major challenge which is that she doesn't have a legal permit to do business. She dreams of expanding her business.  With the KES 20,000 loan she wants to purchase more vegetables for resale. She decided to join Yehu to get capital to expand her business.

name: Joice
description: Joice J. is currently in the business of selling groundnut paste in the custom market in Juba, and is requesting a loan to stock more groundnut to make paste to sell. Joice is 32 years old and is married. Her husband is a policeman. She has one child, who does not go to school. With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to buy land.

name: My God (2) Group
description: Alexandre runs a small diverse goods shop selling items such as oil, rice, mayo and biscuits. He is a member of the group MY GOD (2), and leads the group of nine other micro-entrepreneurs in Brazzaville, Republic of Congo.   An experienced vendor, Alexandre started out with just a small market kiosk and now has his own shop. Alexandre would like to purchase additional merchandise to sell at his shop through taking out a loan of 400,000 CFA with HOPE Congo.  Alexandre first joined HOPE Congo in 2012, and is currently on his sixth loan cycle. He hopes to be able to continue to grow his business and continue supporting his family.   The father of three children, Alexandre hopes that they will one day be able to grow up to work jobs of their own. Through growing his business, Alexandre dreams of being able to buy his own property and build a home for his family.

name: Nelson Javier
description: Nelson, a young man of 25, lives in the village of Los Ranchos, on the outskirts of the city of León. A salesman by trade, he sells firewood; his business supports his wife and their three children. He started when he was 17, with great efforts, since he travelled extensively to sell firewood as well as watermelons. Due to his being poor, he finished only primary school and was not able to continue further. He will use this loan to buy 2 new rims and tires, which he needs for his cart, as well as a stack of firewood to sell. One of the projects he wishes to accomplish is to plant vegetables and fruit, since at this time of year the demand for these products is quite good.

name: Marta
description: Marta is 30 years old and lives in her own home with her husband Luciano (age 31) and their two children, Luzbeth (age 11) and Dayma (age 5).  As a young girl, Marta’s parents taught her the techniques used in farming.  When she got married and started her own family, she did not hesitate in helping her husband with supporting their household.  She utilized her skills by planting corn in large quantities.  Marta enjoys working in the fields and knows what is needed to succeed and generate good profits.  She sells her crop of corn to the local mill and earns the money to provide security for her family.  The part of the job she dislikes is the need to constantly monitor the crops because birds have been known to destroy a large part of her harvest.  Even with this inconvenience, she enjoys seeing the golden kernels that are the fruits of her labor.  Marta is a very industrious woman who always looks to the future.
