She plans to grow other types of vegetables on her land in order to increase her production.  This is her first loan from MFP.  Marta promises to be punctual in making her payments because she does not want to create tension and ill feelings among the other group members who have placed their trust in her.  She will use the money to purchase seeds for growing peas and potatoes, as well as fertilizer and compost for maintaining her land.Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Marilou
description: This is Marilou, She previously accessed an 8,000 PHP loan that she used to purchase more grocery items and products needed in her business. Her earnings were a big help in her personal, household and business expenditures.   She would like to apply for another 8,000 PHP loan to buy groceries, toiletries, beverages and other products to add to her current inventory. The more items displayed at the store the better. More items to sell will result for better profit. Her profits from the business will definitely help her to sustain her daily needs. She looks forward to this financial increase with gladness and thankfulness in her heart.  Marilou hopes to be able to expand soon, just as she dreams of giving her child a good future through all her hard work on her business. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her work every week and where she can also draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay Micro Finance loans.

name: Yelizaveta
description: Yelizaveta lives in the city Kadjaran which is in Syunik region. She is married and has two children. Her daughter is married and she lives with her family. Her son is also married and he lives with his parents. Yelizaveta works at the hospital as a nurse. Her husband is an electrician. Their son works as a worker in a small workshop. So all of them work night and day, very hard, in order to provide for their family and also to be able to pay for Yelizaveta’s grandson’s treatment.   Her grandson is seriously ill and Yelizaveta is asking for a loan of 600,000 Armenian drams in order to pay for her grandson's medicine and treatment as well.

name: Diego Reynaldo
description: Diego is a responsible young man who works during the day as a delivery driver for a chicken distributor and at night as a taxi drive since he makes a minimum salary and needs to provide for his daughter. Currently he is living with his girlfriend, who works making flower arrangements to sell. They are thinking about formalizing their relationship, but they need more money to be able to wed. They are requesting the loan to help Diego purchase his own taxi so he can earn more income and they can achieve their goals together as a couple.

name: Letecia
description: Letecia is married and she works hard to support her family. She has a cassava production business in the Philippines. Letecia is borrowing PHP 29,000 through NWTF in order to  purchase empty sacks and to repair machinery for her cassava production business.  Letecia has been sustaining her business activities through her past 26 loans from NWTF and more recently, through Kiva. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Tidjani Shaibu
description: Tidjani Shaibu A. sells electrical appliances at Kotokoraba in Cape Coast. Tidjani Shaibu has received technical institutional training.  He is married and has 10 dependents. His wife is a trader. Tidjani Shaibu has been selling electrical appliances since 1993. He is responsible for paying school fees. His loan will be used to buy electrical appliances to sell. He hopes to reinvest his new profits in his business.

name: Esther B Group
description: Alice, the borrower, is a good and honest trader, entrepreneur, and member of the "Esther B" borrowing group. She is 35, dynamic, and the mother of eight children, all of whom go to school. The borrower sells traditional fabric on the city's main road. She started this business with some help from her husband, who is a teacher. Later, she received a loan from IMF Hekima. She has been in this business for 29 years. This new loan will allow her to buy 25 pieces of fabric. With the profits, she plans on feeding her children and paying for their school fees. She is very grateful to Hekima for their help in empowering female entrepreneurs with no bank accounts, especially during this critical post-conflict time in the eastern part of the country.

name: José Luis
description: José Luis C. C. and his wife are the parents of three small children, for whom they need to work to offer them a better quality of life and legacy. Currently José Luis wishes to seal and paint his home both inside and out, more than anything so that in the rainy season the water does not leak and soak their electronic appliances, which would create a short circuit in his home and create an unfortunate accident. It is for this reason that he is requesting the support to complete his project.Translated from Spanish by Amy Schapiro, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sitha
description: Mr. Sitha S. and his wife, Mrs. Sokvanna Phauk (pictured together), live along National Road Number One about eighteen kilometers from Phnom Penh.  They were married in 1990 and have three children, two sons and one daughter. Two of them attend school and another one is still young.   Sitha has been a hairdresser for more than eighteen years. He operates his shop in Kor Ky market. His first loan has just been finished. He hopes to organize the house where he lives become neater, so he is asking for his second loan of $1,000 to fill up the land and put an addition on his house.

name: Silveria
description: Silveria is a member of "La Yunguyeñita” community bank which is located in Yunguyo district and province, in Puno department.  She is 46 years old, lives with her common-law husband, and has two children.  She only studied up to elementary school level.  SIlveria sells pork, beef, mutton and alpaca meat.  Her first loan was for 300 soles and she used that money to increase her business capital.  She has been working with Movimiento Manuela Ramos for five years.  Silveria will use this new loan for 500 soles to buy two sheep which she will later sell as meat in the market.  She also takes meat in large quantities to sell in the towns of Arequipa and Tacna.  She works together with her husband.  Silveria would like to have a sales stall in the towns of Arequipa and Tacna.  What she likes about her community bank is the ease of obtaining a loan and the punctuality.

name: Veronica
description: Veronica is a married woman with three children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur. Veronica is 59 years old and all three children are in school.  Veronica has a fishing business in the Philippines. Veronica requested a PHP 9,000 loan amount through NWTF in order to buy fishing gear and other equipment.  Veronica has been in this business for five years. In the future, Veronica would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Rumnah
description: Good day lenders! Meet one of KPP-UMKM’s clients, Rumnah, who is a 49-year-old married woman with one daughter and one son. Rumnah is a housewife and her husband has been selling glasses for five years. She has asked for a loan of IDR 5,300,000 from KPP-UMKM Syariah. This loan will be used to build water sources at their home to improve access to water and sanitation for their family. Her family income is insufficient to build toilets and water sources but Rumnah will be able to repay the loan received.She and her family want to live a healthy life with healthy sanitation and clean water. She is very grateful for the opportunity and wants to thank all of the lenders.

name: Julienne
description: Julienne is 45 years old.  She is married and the mother of three children, one of whom attends a local school.  Her eldest is 26 years old and her youngest is 6.  Julienne sells hair extensions, hair products and body lotions.  She has been in this business for a number of years.  She stocks up in one of the markets in Benin and also abroad.  With the aim of strengthening her working capital and meeting the needs of her customers, she has requested and received a loan from Finadev which will allow her to increase her supplementary income and contribute towards her child's education.

name: Raida
description: Raida, 49, is an unassuming woman living with Máximo, her husband.  They have seven children but only two of them still live with her: José Luis and Cristian who she cares for in the house she bought twenty years ago.  Her days are centered on continuous work.  Her main economic activity is centered on animal husbandry.  She owns nine cows she gets an average of 40 liters of milk daily from that she sells to a well-known dairyman.  She earns considerable daily income thereby that helps her cover household expenses.  Her secret is the constant support she gets from her husband who always supports her.  “We decided together to plant oats and alfalfa to feed our animals to save on feed costs and provide the best for them,” she comments.    However, since she’s a woman of the land, she also works in agriculture growing olluco [an Andean tuber], potatoes and other tubers that she sells sometimes and also uses for home consumption.  This is MFP loan #9.  She has a good impression of group loans even though there have been occasional difficulties that have served to strengthen her trust in her association.  Today, she renews her pledge to continue being punctual with her installment payments.  Raida will use the requested money to buy organic manure in quantity, an average of 400 sacks, for the oats, ryegrass and alfalfa crops.

name: Deo
description: Deo is a 45-year-old married man with three children living in Fort Portal, Uganda. He is a retailer and at the same time does farming. He faces challenges of high competition and price fluctuations, like other retailers. However, he hopes to have a good business and to educate his children to higher levels of learning. Deo needs a loan to plaster and floor his house.

name: Diosdada
description: Diosdada T.'s main source of income comes from running a tricycle transport service. She is 43 years old, married and has four grown-up children. They are from the village of Canibungan Daku, Clarin, Misamis Occidental. Diosdada has been in her business for over two years and earns approximately 15,000 Philippine pesos (PHP) a month.  In 2004, Diosdada joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living conditions and enable her to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 10,000 PHP from GDMPC. Diosdada is requesting a new loan of 25,000 PHP which will be used to repair her vehicle for better service. This will be her 14th loan from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About GDMPC: GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three unit offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Sam
description: Sam S. is a 42-year-old housewife in the central Cambodian province of Kampong Cham. Her 62-year-old husband, Ang Sen, works as a security guard for a rural company, earning only $1 per day. Of their six children, only one is married and living outside the family home. Suffering from extreme poverty, the family must depend on the children to work and provide financial support. Three of them are employed in a logging factory, making $90 each per month. With this additional income Sam and her husband have invested in their younger children, sending them to school. Because she wants her family to at least enjoy the security of a stable home, Sam’s loan would go towards constructing a well-built house on stilts to better withstand monsoons and seasonal flooding.

name: Myrna
description: Myrna is a hard-working entrepreneur who has a general store business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 20,000 through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to purchase additional stocks, like mineral water, soft drinks, biscuits, and other groceries needed for her general store business.  Myrna has been in this business for 13 years. Myrna earns additional income from food-vending. Myrna has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts, with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to save enough money, so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Elena
description: This is Elena, a 47-year-old resident of Pasay City, Philippines, who is married to Alfredo, a mechanic, and mother to her children. She, with the assistance of her family, manages their household while operating the business. At this time, she is working hard to continually provide income for their everyday expenses.  Elena is a mineral water distributor, purchasing mineral water in containers from wholesalers, and then selling them per container (5 gallons per container) for a profit. She earns additional income by selling personal products such as Avon, Natasha  and other direct-sales products. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community, and she earns a minimum of Php300 in sales every day.  To help her continue operations of her business, she is requesting a Php12,000 loan to bU. more stocks of mineral water and other personal merchandise to expand her product inventory. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands her business.    Elena dreams of being able to give her children a good and high-quality education through all of her hard work. She also hopes to have a growing network of customers. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her work every week and draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Juana
description: Juana is the mother of three children. Her husband’s a taxi driver in Sumpango Sac.  Juana is a weaver and also grows various seasonal vegetables because here in Guatemala this is the planting season because it’s the time of the rains.  She is asking for another loan to invest in farming and in textiles.  She promises to be punctual with her payments.  Her dream is to move her children ahead and to help out her husband.

name: Doreen Faith
description: After you taste Doreen Faith’s homemade dainties and food products, you'll crave them. Since she has the talent of making delicious food, Doreen Faith started to sell her specialties five years ago. And until now, her income from this business has aided in paying for her family’s basic necessities and expenses.   Doreen Faith is 37 years old. She has two children with Neil, an Overseas Filipino Worker (OFW), and they live in Pasay City, Philipiines. The couple has to ensure a secure future for their children, so they are indeed striving hard to provide for the family today.   Hoping that you can help her, Doreen Faith would like to ask for a loan amounting to 10,000 PHP. She wants to improve her small business and she would like to use this loan to purchase additional supplies of raw ingredients for her recipes. She expects that through this endeavor, she can experience a boost in her product sales.   It is her dream to have her own place of business someday and be successful in her field. She meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her life and business every week and it is also where she can draw strength and inspiration from the fellowship and the Word of God she studies.  *All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay Micro Finance loans.

name: Lourdes
description: This member belongs to the “Nueva Luz” cooperative bank, located in the Cusco district of the province of Cusco, Peru.  Her name is Lourdes and she is 30 years old.  Lourdes lives with her common-law husband and has one child.  She has a business buying and selling clothes.    With this loan, Lourdes plans to invest in her clothing business, using it to purchase more inventory.  Lourdes will purchase clothes such as jackets, sweatshirts, t-shirts, and children clothing from wholesale markets in Lima, Peru, and then resell them in the local markets here in Cusco.    She is very happy with the loan granted, and commits to making her payments within the established time frame.

name: Manny
description: Manny, 34 years old, is married. His main source of income comes from planting and harvesting rice to sell. He has five years of experience. With his last crop, he earned about PHP 30,000. Now, he is asking for a loan of 40,000 PHP to purchase fertilizers and seedlings and pay the labor cost for planting his farm. Future loans from KIVA would be very useful to him, as he sees the loans as the only chance for the growth of his business and financial security.

name: Ruth Viridiana
description: Ruth Viridiana Z.'s business is lacking merchandise, but currently there is not enough money to buy more.  Ruth Viridiana and her mother, María Guadalupe, tend to the business, given that it is the source of income for them.  They are asking for a loan so that they will be able to have more inventory in their store and in this way, greater income, with which they plan to pay back this loan.  Translated from Spanish by Anne Rodriguez, Kiva Volunteer

name: Atawa
description: ATAWA, age 33, is a Togolese woman who is single without children. She lives in the district of Adidogomé, in Lomé. She is a reseller of grocery items, and she stocks up 6 times a month at the Adidogomé market. She has a secondary level education.    Atawa is seeking a loan to bolster her commercial activity and increase her profits.

name: Ruth's Group
description: Ruth is 58 years old and has seven children. She has been a farmer for more than 30 years and is always said to be a very resourceful person. Even though Ruth is the only one featured in the above picture, she is actually representing her group formed by 13 farmers in Matete District, Kenya.  Ruth started working alongside One Acre Fund a few years ago, in 2010, and decided to do so because she wanted to get the best quality fertilizer and hybrid seeds. Since then, she has seen her life improve; especially in the sense that she has been able to consistently feed her family ever since. This year she decided to represent her group because she wanted to gain leadership skills.  Ruth’s Group will receive farming inputs to plant a total of 6.75 acres of land. Additionally, some of the farmers in the group will be purchasing a solar light so, with this loan, the group will also receive a total of 9 solar lights.

name: Ediza
description: Ediza is a married woman with two children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Ediza is 34 years old and has two children who are in school.Ediza has a general store business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 12,000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase more groceries to sell in her general store.Ediza has been in this business for seven years.  In the future, Ediza would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Ma Esther
description: Mrs. Ma Esther S. has sold used clothing and sneakers for the past year. "It's been very difficult to save money to purchase the clothing and shoes. This business is our the only source of income for my family.  I would like to buy more Spring and Summer clothes since I have winter clothes which I won't sell at this time of year.  I request $1,000 to invest in my business." Translated from Spanish by Ari Vilhjalmsson, Kiva Volunteer. La Sra. Ma Esther S. tiene 1 año con su venta de ropa de segunda y tenis. “Me ha sido muy difícil juntar un poco de dinero para comprar la ropa y los tenis, este negocio es la única fuente de ingresos que tenemos mi esposo y mis hijos quisiera comprar un poco más de ropa de temporada de Primavera-Verano ya que tengo ropa de tiempo de frío que ya no voy a vender en esta época del año”. Solicito 1,000.00 dlls para invertirle a mi negocio.

name: Deysi
description: Deysi is a 19 year old young woman who lives in the district of Santiago in Ica, Perú. She lives with her parents whom she supports with the fruit of her labor as a worker on an estate in her city.  Due to scarce financial resources, she had to stop studying to be a forestry engineer because she was unable to meet the expenses required. However she says that she works hard every day in order to get ahead despite the problems she faces.  Deysi is very grateful to Kiva lender because, thanks to their help, she will be able to improve her parents’ home: she will install a raised floor because now there is simply a dirt one and there have been health problems because of that.   Deysi said that she will continue struggling to make her dream a reality, which is to finish her studies one day and make her parents proud of her.

name: Umoja Group
description: Umoja Group, located in Bungoma South District, consists of nine women and one man and is led by Elizabeth, pictured on the right with her hand raised. A new One Acre Fund farmer excited for the 2013 Long Rains season, Elizabeth is receiving an input loan for ½ an acre of maize, millet and sorghum cultivation. She joined One Acre Fund in order to gain access to hybrid seed and fertilizer.   Elizabeth managed to harvest five bags of maize on 1/2 acre of land last year. As a One Acre Fund farmer, she hopes to harvest even more and plans on using future profits to send her children to school and perhaps invest in another business. For the 2013 Long Rains season, Elizabeth’s group members will take input loans for ½ an acre each. In total, this group will receive input loans for use on five acres of land.

name: Martin
description: Martín is a 47 year old man, single and with no children in his care.  He lives in his parents’ house located in Tambogrande District.  He lives in the urban zone and has all basic utilities.  The activity that Martín does is passenger transportation service in a mototaxi (a three wheel vehicle with a thick, impermeable plastic top) which is his and has all required licenses and papers in order in order to circulate.  In addition, he also does carpentry jobs in a workshop located in his parents’ house.  Martín and his mother share household expenses.  The loan is for 1500 new soles which will be used to clean and service his mototaxi.

name: Jovita
description: Jovita and her husband are both farmers residing in a rural community. They were blessed with three children and they want them to become successful someday. For this reason, Jovita engages in cooking and selling meals and snacks to generate additional income. She aims to strengthen this business in order to earn more profits.  Jovita is asking for additional capital of 7,000 Philippine pesos to buy pork, dressed chicken, fish, vegetables and seasonings to be cooked and sold in the local community. She is hoping that the loan will help her improve her business.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth dreams of prospering in her business. She manages a rice farm in her town in Agusan Del Sur. She is married and has children.   One of the challenges Elizabeth has faced in farming is the lack of financial support. She said that it is hard to achieve an abundant harvest when the capital is small. Now that she is a member of CEVI, she is grateful to have gained access to its program. She hopes to stay long with the MFI. She is currently requesting a loan of PHP 6,000. This loan will be used for farm supplies like seeds and fertilizers.

name: Lucrisia
description: Lucrisia is a 54-year-old widow from Ormoc City, Leyte. She has one daughter who is already an adult. For the last three months, she has been selling nipa shingles. This is used as a roofing material by some Filipino people. Some people use this because of its affordability, if homeowners cannot afford to buy galvanized iron. Some will also choose this type because it is comfortable. Lucrisia is asking for a loan to buy nipa leaves, bamboo and rope. She hope to keep her business, manage it well and expand so she can support herself.

name: Rosalia Roxana
description: Rosalía is 30 years old and has two children aged ten and one. She makes a living selling second-hand shoes on her stall, located in a popular market in El Alto. This is her first loan with the organisation. Rosalía is going to use this loan to buy an engine and service her vehicle. Her reason for requesting this loan is that she lacks capital and her vehicle is showing signs of problems, which is harming her business, as she uses it to transport her merchandise to her stall.   Rosalía faces challenges in her business, such as competition, since lots of people make a living in this way. She is going to use her profits to continue improving her stall. Her dream for her business is to have a good stock of merchandise to offer her customers.

name: Ninoska Isabel
description: Ninoska is 41 years old. She is originally from San Carlos a municipality in the department of Rio San Juan in Nicaragua but lives in the city of Granada. She is married and has 2 children. She is a storekeeper and has a small grocery store at home. She started this business when she was 39 years old. She started out with very little inventory but with time she increased her merchandise little by little. She managed to establish her business with basic food products that her customers want and are used every day.   She needed the loan to invest in the purchase of products such as rice, beans, sugar, oil, eggs, milk, fruit, vegetables and cleaning soap. This will help her keep her grocery store stocked with products her customers want. She wants to invest in other products to provide variety and attract more customers, increase her sales and improve her income. One of her goals is to convert her small grocery store into a distribution centre for food.

name: Los Pinos De Corazon Group
description: The “Los Pinos De Corazon” communal bank is beginning its third cycle with Pro Mujer as part of the Senkata center.  It’s made up of eleven members and directed by a board of directors where Francisca serves as the president.  The members have different businesses including: vegetable sales, bread sales, food sales, gelatin sales, awayos sales, and meat sales.  This loan will benefit small businesses where Francisca is a member and she says that she has been with Pro Mujer for a year, having joined after a promoter visited her home.  She sells food and began several years ago on her own initiative.   This loan will help her buy vegetables and cereals that she will buy at fairs in El Alto and then sell them in her stall.  This type of work allows her to generate income to maintain her household.  She is separated and has three children.   When asked what she likes about Pro Mujer, she says that she likes the health and financial training.

name: Mavlyuda
description: Mavlyuda is a 35 year old wife and mother. She has three children - two sons and a daughter. Her sons are 12 years old and 5 years old, and her daughter is 3 years old. Her husband is 60 years old. Her son and husband work in animal husbandry at home on their farmstead. Mavlyuda herself offers tailoring services. She has been working in this business for three years. She makes a living by means of offering tailoring services.  Mavlyuda wants to renovate her home and improve the living standards for her children and family. However, they do not have enough funds for the renovations. Mavlyuda decided to apply for a loan, and with the loan she will obtain building materials and pay for the services of a professional. Mavlyuda expresses her thanks in advance.

name: Ninoska
description: Ninoska is part of the Communal Bank “Las Hijas de Maria” (The Daughters of Mary).  She continues to manage her business where she sells liquor.  Ninoska has been in this business for years and it has brought her both financial and personal satisfaction.  She is a responsible and industrious person who helps her family move forward in this manner.  Ninoska is requesting a loan so that she can buy beer and other products.  She appreciates the loan that has been provided and promises to complete her monthly payments.

name: Boren's Group
description: Boren is 30 years old and a mother of two children, one who is too young for school, and another who is still in school.  The rest of her family is living in the Kror Kor district of Pursat Province.  She strives to make a living through selling porridge.   She has been with this business for 7 years, earning about 25,000 KHR per day.    Boren has never been with VisionFund before (Kiva's partner).  Now, forming a group of three, she is the leader.  All of the members are first-time borrowers seeking the same loan amount of 1,000,000 KHR each.  As the leader, she will use her portion to buy more ingredients to support her porridge selling business (rice, sugar, salt, seasoning, etc.).  She hopes to earn more income from her current business so that she can save some money to buy a decent motorbike.

name: Reyna Isabel
description: Reyna is a very hard-working 28-year-old woman who lives in the city of Pucallpa together with her 3-year-old son.  In her free time, she likes to go for walks with him around the warm and welcoming streets of the city.  She often likes to prepare the delicious 'ceviche' (a fish dish marinated in citrus juices) and share pleasant moments with her family.  With a lot of hard work and commitment, and thanks to the support of a close cousin, Reyna works selling sugar cane juice.  She works approximately 10 hours a day in her business and can serve up to 200 customers.  She believes that her business is doing well thanks to her kind personality and the good customer service she offers.  Reyna is very grateful to Kiva lenders because, thanks to their help, she will be able to buy a juicer and a gas engine which she will use in carrying out her work.  This will enable her to increase her income and guarantee the education and well-being of her young son so that, in the not-so-distant future, he can become a successful professional.

name: Rogelio
description: Mr. Rogelio is a trailer driver and his wife, Georgina, is a catalogue saleswoman.  They have one son who is an elementary school student and another small baby son.  As a family, they are seeking a loan in order to add protective bars on the doors and windows of their home to provide greater security for the family.Translated from Spanish by Scott Crandall, Kiva Volunteer

name: Israel
description: Israel has been married for two years, has a baby, and lives in his parents' home in the Villa Nuevo Potosi area of the city of La Paz. Israel has worked as a carpenter since he was young. In this manner he obtains income for his household. The loan requested is to acquire a shop which will be dedicated to selling children's clothing in the city of La Paz and augment his income. This is his first loan and the socioeconomic analysis performed favorably qualified him to access credit.

name: Monte Rancho Group
description: This is a group that is very responsible with their payments. They live in an area very removed from the city and know each other well. They don't have basic services (sewer system, potable water, etc.) where they live. The group is called "Monte Rancho" ("Mountain Ranch)  and is in its fifth loan cycle with its community bank. The group's board of directors consists as follows: Rosa is the president, and she is very responsible and the leader of the group. She is married, has three children and works in her carpentry shop. The treasurer is Patricia, who is also a very responsible mother of three children and is knowledgeable in the handling of money. She will use the loan to raise capital for her neighborhood store. The secretary is Felisia, who is a married mother of three children. Her husband is a construction worker, while she makes and sells empanadas outdoors. She will use the loan to improve her business.Translated from Spanish by Marty Greenstein, Kiva Volunteer

name: Suzette
description: Suzette E. is 48 years old, married, and supports her family by operating 3 business ventures:   a general store, a ready-to-wear clothes business, and an Avon products business.    She lives in Prk. 9 Acco, Aguisan, Himamaylan City, Negros Occidental. She has been a member of NWTF-Project Dungganon for 15 yrs and has improved her living conditions with the help of her loans from NWTF and through her own efforts. By working hard in her general store, ready-to-wear clothes and Avon products businesses, she is gradually making her family more economically stable.   She now earns an average monthly income of PHP 10,000.   Suzette is now borrowing PHP 19,500 so that she can purchase more stocks to sell.   This will be her 16th loan from NWTF-Project Dungganon. Her previous loan of PHP 20,000, which she paid off well within its term, was just another step in her journey toward economic freedom.  Suzette aspires to elevate her family's living conditions and ensure their future well-being by following the Dungganon way.   About NWTF: In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means Honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress from earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem that is bestowed to a member of a community who has earned the respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work. Help NWTF continue its mission to help the poorest in the Philippines by clicking  the link to the NWTF Kiva lending team on Kiva.org to join our team.

name: Ny's Group
description: Ny’s group lives in a rural village in Kampong Speu province in Cambodia. Ny makes a living cultivating rice and she also does extra work as a factory laborer to support her family. In her village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Thorn
description: Living in a wooden house located in Kampong Cham province’s Cheung Prey district, Thorn is now 34 years old and married. She has three children. Thorn and her husband are rice farmers who have engaged in the business for 16 years. To better support themselves, they also work as construction workers. The current business earns them about 43,000 KHR per day to support the family’s needs and they can afford to save about 25,000 KHR each day. Thorn is a first-cycle client with Kiva’s partner, VisionFund. She is now applying for a loan to buy fertilizer and seeds for her rice farming. She hopes the loan from VisionFund will enable her to make more healthy rice to make more income.
town: Kampong Cham province, Cheung Prey district

name: José Antonio
description: Jose's education went as far as high school, he's married and his wife does housekeeping. Currently he lives with his three daughters and the three are attending school so that they can have a better life. One of them is attending college and the other two are attending the local high school.  Jose works in agriculture, growing produce for 8 years and it all started because of the need to earn income for his family and him seeing the possibility of the crop adapting to the place he decided to plant in. Currently he's planted two hectares of peppers and that's where he earns income to support his family.  He needs this loan to purchase agricultural supplies, such as manure and pesticides to grow produce because he's starting his harvest and with these things we would be helping him to make his land more productive and boost his income. He's thinking of working with other types of produce so that he help his daughters get through college and become professionals in the future, so that they can find a good job and help their parents.

name: Teopista's Group
description: Teopista N. looks after 6 orphans and one old woman with goiter disease.  She wants a loan to increase her capital so that she can increase her stock of charcoal and increase her sales and profits.  She needs extra profits to pay school fees for the orphans. Background on BRAC and BRAC Uganda BRAC (Building Resources Across Communities) is a development organization that began operations in Bangladesh as a small-scale relief and rehabilitation project in 1972 to help the country overcome the devastation and trauma of the liberation war and focused on resettling refugees returning from India. Today, BRAC has emerged as an independent, virtually self-financed paradigm in sustainable human development. It is one of the largest Southern development organizations employing over 100,000 people, 61% of which are women, and working with the twin objectives of poverty alleviation and empowerment of the poor. Diagnosing poverty in human terms and recognizing its multifaceted nature, BRAC approaches poverty alleviation with a holistic approach. The successes of BRAC in the international development arena have stimulated a series of discussions, both with African delegations, who have visited BRAC programs, and with donors who work in Asia and Africa. Both the African countries and the donors have encouraged BRAC to join the development campaign in Africa to achieve the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) and more recently to join the campaign of “ending poverty”, which is an area where Africa represents the greatest global challenge.  In Uganda, BRAC registered as a Non Government Organization (NGO) in January 2006 to undertake programs in Education, Health, Water & Sanitation, Agriculture & Livestock and Microfinance. The Microfinance and Education are the pioneer programs launched in Uganda and, as of July 2007, had served 21,273 borrowers and enrolled 1,155 adolescents in its education program.

name: Irine
description: Irine is a married lady, age 24, and her child is 5 years old.   She owns a retail shop and has been in operation for four years, earning a monthly income of KES 10,000.   She is requesting a loan of KES 30,000 from KADET Ltd., and she intends to purchase sugar, wheat flour, necklaces, scissors, maize flour, cooking oil, and washing soaps and detergents for sale. The profits will be plowed back into the business and also used to repay the loan.  She hopes to expand in business and live a happy life.

name: Soumaila
description: Soumaila was born around 1971 in Sikoro, Kadiana commune, one of the sub-prefectures of the third administrative region of Mali.  He has two wives and six children, and lives in a nuclear family in Sikoro.  He began earning money at a young age, by buying and selling cereals and various items in his shop in Sikoro.  Soumaila has fifteen years' experience in his business and has decided to work with the field partner, Soro Yiriwaso, in order to increase his working capital.  This will enable him to satisfy the increasing demands of his customers.  Soumaila will use this, his first loan, to buy ten sacks of maize, ten sacks of millet and three sacks of sorghum from Sikoro and the surrounding area.  He sells to various customers for cash or credit at the market or at home.  Soumaila hopes to earn 40,000 francs CFA a month, and will use this to repay his loan, reinvest in his business and provide for the needs of his family.

name: Las Palmeras Group
description: Carmen is a 54 year old woman.  She lives with her husband and has a 19 year old son and sells traditional Cruceña food.  She is a good, organized, understanding, patient and hardworking mother who runs her business in el Torno, located 32 kilometers southeast of the city. Its streets are completely paved with homes built on both sides of the two-way street on which travelers to the center of the country travel. The climate is warm and sub-tropical with a temperature that varies between 21 and 35 degrees Celsius.  Carmen has olive skin, brown eyes, and short black hair.  She is short with a robust complexion and Guaraní is her native language, which is spoken locally, but she speaks Spanish culturally and in her business (seated to the left wearing a pink sweater).  She is married and works with her adult son.  They live together in their brick and cement home with the tin roof.  They use well water that they pump out, electricity, but no sewage.  The need to expand her business motivated her to head up a group of people with different businesses, such as fruit selling, welding, cell phone repair, salteña sales, dishware sales, second hand clothing sales, and bedspreads, in order to request a loan to improve her business.  She sells traditional local food such as Cogote relleno (Creole chicken necks stuffed with potato), majao (ground salted meat, boiled bananas, and rice), peanut soup (peanut based soup), and other things.  “My customers are reliable, they come at the same time every day…” she says. The advantage in her business is that she has regular customers. The disadvantage is that she needs furnishings and kitchen utensils so she can sell food to a greater number of customers.  Her dream is to open a restaurant and wants to expand her business by buying kitchen utensils such as flatware, dishes, pots etc.  Also some tables and chairs. This is her first loan sequence with the institution and she has been doing this for five years.    This is why Carmen is asking for a loan to buy furnishing and kitchen utensils so she can serve more customers and improve her life.

name: Delia
description: Delia is married and has two children who are in school.  She has a store in her home where she sells groceries, vegetables, and beverages.  Her business is open every day from dawn until nightfall.  On a few occasions, her children help her with running the business.  Delia is a member of the Communal Bank “Lirio” (Iris) and requests a loan for 1000 PEN to be invested in the purchase of rice, milk, and beverages.  She dreams of building a house made of solid materials since her current home is comprised of basic components.  In addition, she hopes to see her children become professionals.  Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Rosemarie
description: Rosemarie is 22 years old and single. Having no other source of income, she operates their motorcycle transport within their community to help her parents in gaining income. She dreams to become successful and financially stable in the future. To attain her goal, she needs to earn and save more income to make an investment someday.   Due to financial hardship, Rosemarie wants to access financial assistance from KIVA lenders amounting to PHP 5,000 to buy the needed spare parts and accessories for the maintenance of her motorcycle. Having this financial assistance, Rosemarie believes that she will continue to operate her motorcycle and hoping that she will earn a higher income.

name: Unidos Por La Flor Group
description: Rita Meliza is a 35-year-old member of the Unidos por la Flor group, named for the area where the group lives. The group is made up of five members.  Rita Meliza makes a living providing transportation services and renting out vehicles for taxis. Previously, she had a job providing cleaning services, but now she makes a living solely from renting out vehicles. The business has gone well for her and she has not had any setbacks.  The loan will be invested in maintaining her cars so that she can provide a good service.

name: Gloria
description: Gloria M. is 31 years old and is married with six children aged between 13 and 2. She also looks after three dependents.  Gloria has been in the business of selling loincloths for five years, working eleven hours a day and creating jobs for two employees. After realizing that her investment is too low to earn more profit, she is now requesting her first loan from Vision Finance Company in order to expand her business through purchasing more loincloths.  By using this loan, Gloria hopes, with the profit she will get, to help her husband to build their own house and pay school fees for their children.

name: Candida Rosa
description: Señora Candida Rosa is 47 years old. She is a single mother with 3 children, all minors, in her care. She sells natural health products. Candida has worked for a long time with the Fundación León 2000. She has been in this business for more than 4 years as she has always enjoyed this kind of work because she always offers her customers the best quality. She is currently seeking funding to invest in the purchase of pills, ointments, herbs, vitamins and other such products. Candida's desire is to improve every day and earn more for her family.

name: San Lorenzo Group
description: Seventeen very hard-working and determined women form this group, which is part of a program to eliminate poverty.  Each woman gives her best effort in order to be able to grow and get ahead.  One of the group members is Deisy.  She comments that she works selling natural medicine door to door and she already has many customers who always buy medicines from her. Deisy is a very self-sacrificing woman who with a lot of effort and sacrifice is moving forward.  She is requesting this loan since she wants to purchase natural medicines in bulk, so that she is able to continue with her sales.   She is grateful for the opportunity that she has received to be able to continue with her sales and provide for her loved ones.

name: Gasi
description: Gasi has always dreamed of being a prominent man who is responsible in the community. He wants to have a prosperous future and ensure that his children do not lack for any basic needs. Gasi is a very open-minded guy who believes in effort and determination.   For the past ten years, Gasi has been operating an animal sales business.  He has regular customers who have enabled him to increase his income. Gasi plans to use this investment to buy goats and cows and to pay school fees for his children.

name: Rica
description: Rica is 39 years old and single.    Rica and her family survived super typhoon Haiyan which swept through the Philippines last November 8, 2013, but her business and family home was wiped out.   Rica is taking out a housing loan amounting PHP 10000 to purchase building materials and pay for construction labor to build a house for her family.   Rica has been an NWTF borrower since 2013 and plans to recover through her buy and sell coconut wine and nipa roofing business.  With your help, Rica can rebuild her house and rebound from the devastation of super typhoon Haiyan. In future, she  would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Peninah
description: Peninah is a 64 year old green grocer at Voi Kenya. She is a widow who supports seven biological children and has been in this business for the last fifteen years earning a good income.   This is her sixth borrowing from VisionFund Kenya to finance her business, she will use the loan to purchase crates of tomatoes for resale and the anticipated profit to educate her children who are in college. She hopes to see all her children get a good education in future.

name: Pauline
description: Pauline lives in the Muranga area of Central Kenya with her family of three children, all of school going age. She has practiced farming for the past four years with her income being crops, eggs, and a retail business. Her biggest challenge is seasons of low sales.Pauline chose Juhudi Kilimo for this loan because they help small scale farmers in their farming projects. During the training, she learnt that micro finance institutions help fund small income earners. This loan will help her to start up dairy farming, which will bring more income and thus improve her family's living standards and also will pay for her children's school fees.

name: Mercedes Yamilleth
description: Mercedes P. is a woman of very few material resources, but with a great spirit of determination to overcome life's challenges. Together with her partner she is working hard to provide her three children with a decent home, as their current residence is in poor condition owing to natural phenomena, the climate, and also the passing of time.  Mercedes has started work on the house, and has succeeded in making the basic structure and building the walls.  She stills needs to buy the materials for the roof, floors, doors, windows and wall paint. For this reason she has approached Ceprodel for a loan allowing her to purchase these building materials and continue construction in her municipality of Somotillo.   Translated from Spanish by Sally Bolton, Kiva Volunteer

name: Regina
description: Regina is 55 years old and married.  She works very hard.  Regina runs a buy and sell nipa roofing business in the Philippines, and requested a PHP 5,000 loan through NWTF to buy more stock of nipa to sell.  Regina has been in this business for 10 years.  She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Bendictar
description: Bendictar lives in the town of Eldoret. Despite her age, she's very clear about what she wants from her life. For that reason, five years ago she decided to begin practicing mixed farming (dairy and crop farming). Maize farming and dairy farming are the most popular and lucrative economic activities for people in the Eldoret area. Bendictar is seeking a loan to venture into horticultural farming. The new venture will marry well with dairy farming, and the combination of the two activities will bring her and her family untold benefits. With your loan, the horticultural farm she will start will complement the existing dairy farm in the following ways: income from dairy will pay for horticultural expenses as crops mature; lump sum income from crop farming will be rolled back into the business to buy more cows and plant more crops in the coming season; by-products from crop farming such as maize stalks, cobs and off-coloured grains will be used as dairy feed; by-products from dairy such as cow dung will be used for bio-gas generation and manure for planting crops. The impact of this investment is sure to have a big impact on Bendictar’s family livelihood.

name: Tuamasaga
description: Tuamasaga is 54 years old and married with seven children. She has a small plantation where she grows taro and bananas that she can sell in her community or at the market. She has been doing this for 10 years.  Tuamasaga needs a loan to buy a machete, chemicals, a spade, a crowbar, crops, a wheelbarrow, and boots. She has been a member of SPBD since 2005. Tuamasaga will use the profits from her sales to pay for her family's weekly expenses.

name: Chinnie
description: Chinnie is 38 years old and is married with five children. Two of her children are sent to school.Chinnie works hard to provide for her family. She runs a sari-sari (general) store in the Philippines and requested a 18,000 Philippines peso (PHP) loan through NWTF in order to buy items like canned goods and personal care products to sell in her store.Chinnie has borrowed and paid back 10 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for five years and also earns an income from farming sugarcane and raising livestock.Chinnie aspires to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Ligaya
description: Ligaya is 50 years old and married with three children.  Ligaya works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and has requested a PHP 5,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like beverages, noodles, personal care products, and other groceries.  Ligaya has borrowed and repaid 4 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 10 years and also earns an income from food vending.  She aspires to save money to expand her business.

name: Nyagota Kilimo Group
description: This group is part of the Nuru International group of farmers called Nyangoto Kilimo and is based within Kuria West District. The members of the group came together in order to grow socially and economically through agriculture.  The person raising his hand is Jacob, 35, who is married with two children who go to school. Jacob has been a member of the group for two years and he is the group’s chairperson.  Jacob has been learning better farming methods within his group and desires to use hybrid seeds and fertilizers on his farm to grow maize, sorghum and millet during the 2014 long rains season. He is, however, constrained financially and is hoping to receive a loan from Kiva that will enable him purchase these farm inputs. He believes that the use of hybrid seeds and fertilizer will increase his yields and he will not only get enough food for his large family but also be able to sell the surplus and invest in a business to obtain money to pay for his children’s school fees and other domestic uses.

name: Caroline
description: Caroline is a 29 year old hardworking married woman with two children living in Kamwenge, Uganda. One of her children attends school and she is determined to pay all fees till when the child attains a very good level in Ugandan Education. She however does cattle and goat fattening which is her main source of income. She also operates a retail shop to earn additional income. Her vision is to expand the business and become financially stable but She faces challenges of little capital and diseases that attack her animals.   She needs money to buy more bulls and goats for fattening at the farm.

name: Kamene
description: Kamene is a 47-year-old married woman. She has five children ranging in age from 13 to 27. She describes herself as social and talkative.   Kamene operates a retail store where she sells cereals such as maize, beans, black beans, etc. She has been involved in this business for 10 years and employs one staff member.   Kamene's business is located within a busy town and her primary customers are local residents of Mwingi. She describes her biggest business challenge as insufficient funds for expanding her business and hopes that with this loan, she will be able to improve the business. She will use the KES 20,000 loan to buy more maize. Her business goal is to sell cereals at wholesale prices within five years.

name: Sima
description: In 2007, S. Sima embarked on a business involving groceries.  She gets her supplies from various local markets in Lomé.  She is low on stock and wants to stock up again to be able to enhance her inventory and her sales.  She is requesting a loan for buying 4 boxes of BF soaps, 6 boxes of popular soaps, 5 boxes of liquid RAD, 6 boxes of sardines, 3 boxes of SIPA couscous, 4 boxes of sugar, and 4 boxes of Jago mayonnaise.  Sima is unmarried, and with the revenues from her business, she supports herself.   Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Asia
description: Asia is 34 years old and a mother of three children who is living with her spouse and children in the area of Multan, Pakistan.  She engages in the bangle-making business to earn an income. She started her business 15 years ago because Asia wanted to help her husband support the family and meet the household expenses. Asia buys several materials from the market. Her husband handles her transactions with her customers. She has become an expert in her bangle-making business.  Asia demanded a loan so that she could buy raw materials from the market. Asia will be thankful to Kiva and field partner BRAC Pakistan.

name: Joyce
description: Joyce N. is 26 years old. She is a married woman with 2 children ages 8 and 3.  She became a cow seller in 2003. Every day, she works from 7am to 1pm at her business and can earn a monthly profit of about $175 from her sales.   Joyce  now hopes for a loan of $175 to increase her stock in order  to improve her business.

name: Roy Eduardo
description: Hello. My name is Roy M.. I have a workshop for metal structures where I make doors, frames, windows, gates, etc. Currently I have various projects, but they are large and I need a little capital to purchase materials and, in this way, meet all the specifications.  For this reason I am requesting a loan. I support my family, which is the most important thing in my life.Translated from Spanish by Todd M. Anderson, Kiva Volunteer

name: Marilyn
description: Marilyn is from the village of Clarin, Misamis Occidental. She is 35 years old, married, and has two school-age children. To make a living, Marilyn has been engaged in a flower-planting and pot-display business for over five years, earning approximately 7,000 Philippine-pesos (PHP) a month. In 2010, Marilyn joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She is requesting a new loan of 20,000 PHP to purchase more pots to display. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family, and she hopes to make a flower shop.

name: Mgeni
description: Mgeni is a single woman. She lives in a rental house that has electricity but no piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and rent.  Mgeni operates a clothes-selling business. She sells at the market to town dwellers and her neighbours. She cites her major challenge to be seasonality. Mgeni dreams of establishing a boutique in the future.  With the loan she is requesting, she wants to purchase two bales of clothes for resale. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Munira
description: Munira is a resident of the Bohtar district.  She is 35 years old.  She lives with her husband and has three children, all of whom attend a school.  Munira works at a market, called "Hochi Sharif."  She sells children's and women's clothing.  Munira has been in this business for four years.  This is her first time obtaining financing from our organization.  Munira is requesting this loan to purchase seasonal merchandise in order to expand the selection of her merchandise.

name: Marithza
description: Marithza A. O. is 41 years old. She has a small business selling sweet bread and white bread that she runs from her home. She gets up very early to buy bread in the city of Choluteca, then sells it in the various neighborhoods near her home.   Sweet breads and cookies are commonly eaten with hot coffee for breakfast, and many people also have a cup of coffee with cookies in the afternoons.  Marithza makes most of her sales in the mornings, and sells what is left in the afternoons. Some days, she has no product left to sell in the afternoons.   This loan will be used to buy more bread and so be able to fulfill the needs of her customers. The bread she sells is popular because it is large and tasty, and she sells it at a price that is affordable by her neighbors. Most people in this zone have scarce economic resources.   Translated from Spanish by jeffrey hersk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Saroem's Group
description: Saroem, 52, is a villager residing in a rural area of the Ratanak Mondul district located in Battambang province, Cambodia. She is divorced and has four children, one of whom is still in school. This single mother, Saroem, feeds her family through cultivating corn on three hectares of farmland. She has been involved in this business for 17 years, earning approximately 20,000KHR per day, and after deducting her daily expenses, she has only 5,000KHR left for her savings.  Due to the lack of working capital, Saroem and her group member, Nget, have decided to seek a loan in the amount of 1,000,000KHR each. The loan portion for Saroem will be spent on buying fertilizers, pesticides, and corn seed. For this first loan with Kiva’s partner, VisionFund, Saroem hopes greatly that her corn field will provide her with better and higher yields so that she can improve the standard of living of her family.

name: Pamila
description: Pamila is 42 years old and married with four children. With three children in school, Pamila works very hard to provide for them.Pamila runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like bread, beverages, canned goods, snack foods, home care products, and other groceries.Pamila has been in this business for 16 years and sells a variety of items. In the future, Pamila would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Josiane
description: Josiane G., about 50 years old, is the mother of six children and guardian for two others, the  children of her deceased aunt.  She is in business selling bath soap (Lagossidi).  This soap is made in Nigeria and Ghana, and everybody appreciates this fact, since the soap is good for the skin and inexpensive too.  Her husband, a substitute teacher in a local private school, has not been able to provide for the family given his meager and sporadic salary.  So, over 75% of household expenses is resting on Josiane herself.  Using an initial loan of $400, which was repaid regularly, she managed to grow her business a little.  To do more would require more substantial funding.     Mrs. G., lacking the funds, must get her stock of soap from retailers who ultimately leave her with only a small profit margin.  So, she is requesting financial support in the amount of $950 as capital to create a significant inventory of soap and to act as a wholesaler.      Translated from French by Daniel Kuey, Kiva Volunteer.   Agée de 50 ans environ, Madame G. Josiane est mère de six (06) enfants et a à sa charge deux (02) enfants de sa tante décédée. Elle a comme activité la vente du savon de toilette (Lagossidi). C’est un savon fabriqué au Nigeria et au Ghana que tout le monde apprécie car c’est très bon pour la peau et économique. Son mari, un enseignant vacataire dans une école privée de la place, n’arrive pas à subvenir aux besoins de la famille avec son maigre salaire et encore très irrégulier. Ainsi, plus de 75% des charges du foyer reposent-t-elles sur la femme. Avec un premier crédit de $400 obtenu et régulièrement remboursé, Josiane est arrivée à augmenter légèrement ses activités qui nécessitent aujourd’hui un financement assez consistant.     N’ayant pas de moyens, Madame G. Josiane s’approvisionne chez les revendeurs ce qui lui laisse pas une marge bénéficiaire conséquente. Aussi, sollicite-t-elle un appui financier de $950 qui va lui servir de fonds de commerce pour faire un stock consistant de savon et agir comme une grossiste.

name: Benkadi 1 Group
description: The Benkadi 1 group is made up of five married women, most of whom have large, traditional families, who are on average 39 years old and have 4 children. They live in the Korobougou village in the rural town of Sébougou in the 4th region of Ségou (4th administrative region of Mali). They know each other from their marriages, families, and neighbors. In the goal of having available farming resources during the winter, they have turned to Soro Yiriwaso and are on their first loan. The group members are going to grow peanuts, millet, and okra. Mrs. Korotoumou B. plans to use her loan to buy 3 bags of grain, 20kg of peanut seeds, and to hire labor to work and hoe in the fields. She obtains what she needs at the marketplace in Ségou. Field labor is done by men, while weeding is done by the women in the village. From a 3-acre area, Mrs. Korotoumou B. hopes to get 8 bags of millet, 18 bags of peanuts and about 30 cups of okra. A part of the crop of grains will be used, and the rest sold. The profits will be used to pay for small household needs and healthcare for the children. Translated from French by Sherry W., Kiva Volunteer

name: Melchor
description: Melchor is  46 years old and has two children. The eldest attends college while the youngest is in elementary school. He runs a farming business as his source of his income. He had been in the rice production business for 10 years and earns approximately 20,000 PHP during harvest.  Melchor is requesting for a loan for 10,000 PHP, which he will use to buy herbicides and pesticides for his farming business. He hopes to achieve an abundant harvest to increase his earnings and keep sending his children to school. Melchor's priority is to support his family and assure them of a brighter future.

name: Azucena Geoconda
description: Azucena M. lives in the department of León. She operates a beauty salon in her own house where she serves her customers. Furthermore, she sells shoes to them.  Azucena approached Kiva partner Ceprodel and applied for a loan to buy working materials for her salon and shoes for sale. She confidently waits to see her loan provided and achieve a good customer satisfaction in her business. Translated from Spanish by Robert Mouris, Kiva Volunteer

name: Chomroeun
description: Chomroeun is a resident of a rural village of Batheay, Kampong Cham. He is a 29-year-old, married man, and a loving father of three children. He has been planting and harvesting rice and other seasonal crops to sell. Aside from farming, he also helps his wife sell kitchen utensils – spoons, plates, bowls, pots, and other related things -- to earn additional income.In order to gain access to financial services and help him develop his business, Chomroeun is taking out a new loan. He will use it to buy kitchen materials to sell in his store. With the income generated from this investment, he aims to pay for his children’s education and cover their daily costs, and save for future emergencies.

name: Siprosa
description: Siprosa is a widowed woman with 3 children. She describes herself as ambitious. She operates a retail business where she sells shoes. She has been involved in this business for 9 years. Her business is located in a busy area and her primary customers are the general public. She says that her biggest business challenge is insufficient capital. She will use the 20,000 KES loan to buy more shoes to sell. Her business goal is to have a bigger shop within 5 years. She hopes that in the future she will earn more profits and have better living standards.. This is her first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: Zabibu
description: Zabibu is married and has four children. She lives in the Vingunguti area in Dar es Salaam. Zabibu is self-employed and owns a shop near her residence. She is a housewife and only has a primary education. She couldn’t get move ahead with her education because her parents could not afford school expenses. After getting married, she decided to start a business. With the help of her husband, she managed to open a shop. The shop sells different consumable items but mainly food items, which have high turnover. The shop provides her with the opportunity to raise her children well. She would like to expand her business by adding additional stock to the shop. She does all this so she can meet the costs of educating her children and help her husband in raising the family. To expand her business she needs USD 550.

name: Crispina
description: Crispina, aged 38, is from Cortes, Bohol. She is married with three children aged 3, 6 and 14. She has been selling home-cooked food for six years now. Crispina is asking for a loan to buy ingredients like seasoning, meat and vegetables so she can always cook for her customers.   She is determined to work hard and earn more for her family's needs, especially her children's education.

name: Roinah
description: Good day lenders! Now it’s time for you to meet one of KPP UMKM’s clients, Roinah. Roinah is 40 years old and married. She lives with her husband and her children. She has one son and one daughter.   She is a food merchant who has made and sold snacks, ‘Kerupuk,’ made from potatoes, for two years.  She helps her husband to increase income.  She has asked for a loan from KPP-UMKM Syariah for 7,200,000 IDR. This loan will be used to buy and build a bathroom, a septic tank, and a toilet at their home to improve access to water and sanitation for their family. She want to have access to safe sanitation for the family.   Her family income is still not enough to build a toilet and water source with cash, but they are able to repay loans received.  She and her family want to live a healthy life with healthy sanitation. She is very grateful for the opportunity and wants to thank to all lenders.

name: Bibiana
description: This member belongs to the "IMASUMAC II" community bank; the bank is located in the Huanchac district in the province of Cusco and the department of Cusco.  The member is Señora Bibiana, who is 67 years old.  The member is married and has 7 children, all of whom are independent, though the member is helping one of the younger children with their higher education.  The member works in retail, she has a stall in the Santa Ana market for purchase and sale of fruits and vegetables.  She is looking for the loan to invest in the purchase of vegetables and fruit at wholesale from the suppliers, and in this way facilitate her business.  The member is requesting the loan to invest in the purchase of fruits and vegetables for sale.  The member is grateful for the support being granted to her, and similarly agrees to comply in a disciplined manner with the payment of dues.

name: Jose Johel
description: Music has been part of Jose, but not in a way that everyone would think, because he does not sing or play any instrument. However, he is responsible for providing sound by installing and selling audio equipment.   Two years after studying training courses and audio systems with the help of his father, he has managed to set up his own audio equipment business at  23 years of age.  The desire to keep growing and the motivation to become a successful person have led Jose to invest in his business, so he is requesting a loan to purchase megaphones, speakers, stereos, cables, among other essential goods. This will allow him to increase his inventory and equipment to have the latest model to offer to his customers.  In the future, he dreams of expanding his establishment and to continue growing firmly.

name: Yilda Argentina
description: Yilda is an affectionate, loving, sweet, hard-working and dedicated mother. Yilda is a head of family who, throughout her life, has looked after herself and driven herself to get an education and raise, feed, and dress her two children. One of Yilda’s children now has his own family, while the youngest is still a teenager. Yilda has a humble business selling food that allows her to earn an income to pay her bills.  Yilda sells fried foods, such as pasties, pastries, rolls, stuffed potatoes, cheese sticks and more. She fries them in the kitchen in her house and then uses a microwave oven, table and a small display case to sell the foods outside her house.  Owing to competition, and people’s desire to work, many food businesses have opened in the area recently. Yilda is therefore applying for a loan in order to buy two fryers so that she can start to sell sausage and chips and chorizo. Yilda will thus use this loan to diversify her goods and offer more products. She will provide two jobs for others. Yilda has thought this through well and wants to carry out her plan as soon as possible.  Yilda’s dream to keep up her health for many years in order to work and continue doing what best helps her to overcome adversity, and what helps her to progress.

name: Suzan's Group
description: Suzan is 18 years old and lives in the town of Siroko in the Mbale region of Uganda. For the past 2 years, Suzan has been working hard to manage her retail shop, which sells sugar, flour, rice and other goods.   To help expand her business, Suzan has requested a loan of 800000 UGX from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy more items such as sugar and rice to sell, and will help Suzan to generate greater profits. Suzan hopes that in the future she will be able to increase her capital and build a home.   Suzan is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities, and a forum for life-skills training.

name: Matar
description: Matar F. is 24 years old and married. He drives a horse cart. In addition, he is engaged in business activities, more specifically selling cereals. He stocks up in the peanut-growing valley (Kaolack), where he purchases large quantities of millet and peanuts and brings them to Mbour for retailing. He knows this business very well and ever had problems moving his stock as the products he sells are very popular with the local population.

name: Marlyn
description: Marlyn is 48 years old, married, and has two children.    She is in the agricultural business, farming vegetables in the Philippines. Marlyn requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional sacks of fertilizer and other farm supplies.  Marlyn has been farming vegetables for four years now, and has borrowed 14 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Marlyn would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Hayrapet
description: Hayrapet is 60 years old and he lives with in Antarashat village of Syunik region. He lives with his beloved wife who is disabled. Their two children are already married and they live with their families. For several years Hayrapet works as a salesman now he is also employed and he works at the television station. He also has a cute farm, where he takes care of two cows and three heifers. He also has a plot of land on which he cultivates beans, potato, tomato and greens. His land’s vegetables and his farm’s milk and meat Hayrapet sells right from his house to his neighbors and regular customers. With his first partnership with Kiva Hayrapet would like to buy fodder for all his farm cattle and he will be thankful very much if he will be supported by Kiva lenders.

name: Girasol Group
description: Gladis, 35, is a member of the group Solidario Girasol (Sunflower Solidarity). She is married and the mother of three children, her husband is a laborer; they are a very hardworking and honest family living in the village of Tepusteca, Olanchito, Yoro.   Gladis started her business 14 years ago; she makes handicrafts which she learned how to do from taking a course in INFOP and also from her mother who was engaged in the manufacture of handicrafts. Her hours of operation start at 8:00 am and end at 6:00 pm, her advantage being that she has very good customers.   Gladis needs the requested loan to invest in the purchase of raw materials to manufacture her handicrafts. With the help of this loan, her life will change now that she will have the material available to create her products and thus have a better income to help support her family. Her dream is to succeed in her business and that her children become professionals. This is the second loan that Gladis is getting from FAMA and thankfully, she has done very well with making her payments.

name: Yaa
description: Yaa is married and has seven children. She sells kenkey (fermented maize dough) in Emissa Krom, near Cape Coast, which she has done for the past eight years. Her husband is a farmer. Yaa uses her income to pay her children's school fees. Yaa will use the loan to purchase bags of maize for her kenkey production. With the new profits from her expanded business, Yaa plans to continue to support her children.

name: Philibus Dogara
description: Philibus Dogara is a 41-year-old farmer from Gogarma.  As a Babban Gona member, Philibus Dogara , is excited about the opportunity to finally have access to credit, good markets and a trained agronomist. Like all Babban Gona members, Philibus Dogara can earn up to $2000/ha this season from growing maize, more than three times the average Nigerian farmer’s annual income. The average Babban Gona farmer yields 30 bags/hectare,  double the National average of 14. However, Philibus Dogara is ambitious and is aiming to reap 40 bags per hectare this season. When asked, Philibus Dogara said “I plan to use the money I make to educate my children; Istipanus, Elezebeth,  and  Augustine, and in 5 years, I want to become the most profitable farmer in my community”. With this loan, he is well on his way to achieving this dream.

name: Chamroen
description: Chamroen is age 34 years and married. She has two children, both of whom are living with her. One is still in school while the other one works as a tailor to help the family generate extra income. Chamroen has been in rice farming for five years and complementing the income by work as a tailor while her husband is a paid construction worker. The current business earns her family around US$9 a day and they manage to save about US$5.   Chamroen has been with VisonFund for three cycles and all these past loans have been repaid back already. The previous loans have helped her relieve the family’s burden and improve their livelihood. Now she is requesting a loan of US$400. She will use this loan to buy fertilizers, pesticides and seeds for her farmland, and will use a portion of it to pay for labor fees. She hopes this loan will enable her to grow rice healthfully and fruitfully so as to improve her standard of living and keep her child in school.

name: Annet
description: Annet is a 30-year-old woman living in Bundibugyo, Uganda. She has four children, but only two go to school. She is a farmer who grows mainly cocoa and also deals in agricultural produce in order to raise money to support her family. Like most farmers she is challenged by the seasonal nature of the crops and inadequate capital to meet the high demand for food in the area. Good mother that she is, she desires to educate her children to attain degrees up to the University. Annet intends to use the loan to buy cocoa and rice to sell.

name: Marelie
description: Marelie is 22 years old and married with one child as can be seen in the picture. Marelie works very hard to provide for them. Marelie runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 5,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase more goods to resell in her general store.
