Marelie has been in this business for two years and sells a variety of items such as cooking oil, sugar, soy sauce, cereals, milk, coffee, dried fish, etc.  Marelie would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Toki
description: Toki B. is currently in the business of selling charcoal at home and is requesting a loan to stock more bags of charcoal to sell. Toki is 30 years old and is married to an engineer. She has three children and her children go to school.  With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to pay school fees for her children.  BRAC's holistic approach to poverty alleviation and empowerment of the poor encompasses a range of core programs in economic and social development, health, education, human rights and legal services which are delivered through an extensive network of village organizations. BRAC has become one of the world's largest NGOs as measured by the scale and diversity of its interventions.  In 2007, BRAC started operations in Southern Sudan. The microfinance program, which is targeted towards returning war refugees, has already formed 418 village organizations with more than 14,000 women members.

name: Janely
description: Janely is married and has two children. She is 20 years old and resides at Prenza, Tangub City, Philippines. Janely operates a family member's business where they plant, harvest and sell bananas for their living and she's been two years in this business. Each month, she earns 3,000 PHP doing this type of business.   She requested a loan of 6,000 PHP to purchase additional seeds, seedlings & young crops to raise. In 2011, Janely joined GDMPC. In the future, Janely wants to make improvements of her house and to improve the general living conditions of her family.

name: Raul De Jesús
description: Raúl is 24 years old.  He studied through the sixth grade.  He has a partner; she works taking care of the home.  He has a child, and his mother-in-law lives with them.  Raúl has worked in agriculture since the time he was ten years old.  He learned this type of work with his father, and it has served him well to get by.  He sows corn and sorghum.  Additionally, he was in the army; he works as a security guard with a company.  His daily routine is a little tiring.  In order to get to where he works, he has to take a pick-up to get to the highway, then he takes a bus to get to the city, and then a minibus to get to where he works.  At times, in order to save, he gets up earlier to go by bicycle.  He will use the requested loan to buy manure, seed, and poison, and to buy a heifer.  His dreams are: to buy a plot of land and build his own house, and that his children would study and prepare themselves academically, and to be able to buy ten milk cows.

name: Farzona
description: Farzona is a single girl. She is 20 years old. Farzona lives with her parents in the capital of Tajikistan. She is a very kind girl.   Now, she is a student of the first course Medical College of Tajikistan. She studies full-time and she is a smart student. She has a dream to work in any hospital after graduating college.   Farzona is asking for a loan of 450 USD to pay for tuition. She awaits your mercy.

name: Uchi
description: Uchi is a hardworking and enterprising woman who owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. She is a married woman with three children, two in school and one underage. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.  Uchi sells goat meat at the market to her neighbors and passersby. She cites seasonality as her major challenge.  With the 30,000 KES she wants to purchase more goats for her business. She joined Yehu to boast her business.

name: Olinda
description: Olinda is single and has six children, all of whom are adults. She lives in a house that she owns and also supports her mother who lives with her. She's a merchant who sells foodstuffs. With the current loan she intends to purchase construction supplies (cement, bricks, sand, rocks, etc.) in order to build an aviary. Her wish for the future is to expand her business and become known as a great poultry farmer. For that reason she pledges to repay the loan as scheduled, so she can request more loans from Hluvuku. The challenge she faces is working harder so that she can repay the loan as scheduled.

name: Osama
description: Osama, age 27, sells used electrical and electronic goods from his small store. He has operated his store for three years. He also helps his family plant and harvest seasonal crops on family-owned farmland.   He lives with his wife in a small house in Attel, a small village near Tulkarm City.   Osama requested a loan from FATEN in order to buy more used electrical and electronic goods to offer for sale in his store. This investment will improve the selection of items available in his store and will increase his sales.

name: Hèrèdiya Group
description: The members of Hèrèdiya Group are all married women living in monogamous families. On average, they are 44 years old and have five children. They all live in Farabougou, a village located in the rural municipality of Téssérèla (fourth administrative region of Mali). They know each other through ties of kinship, marriage and neighborhood.  The group members are businesswomen selling groundnuts, clothes, dried fish and calabashes. The urge to increase their working capital led them to create a team and join the credit program of Soro Yiriwaso. This is their first solidarity loan.  Mrs Alimata Sangaré wants to use her loan to buy 5 sacks of groundnuts from the producers in N'gassola, Tissala and Téssérèla. She will sell the groundnuts from her home and by hawking in the nearby villages and at the trade fairs in N'gassola and Téssérèla. She retails, for cash and credit, to a clientele made up of men, women and children.  Alimata expects to make a monthly profit of 22,500 CFA francs which she will use to repay her loan, contribute to some household expenses, participate in social events (weddings, baptisms and funerals) and increase her working capital. Her ambition is to perpetuate her business through sufficient working capital and own a cart and a donkey for her travelling and transportation needs. Translated from French by Robert Mouris, Kiva Volunteer

name: Elvina
description: Elvina B. is from the town of Benoni, Mahinog Camiguin. She is 39 years old and single. To make a living, Elvina owns and operates a business venture in the retail sector running a sari-sari (variety) retail shop. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes from selling a variety of different products in the local community. Elvina has been engaged in her business for over 20 years and earns approximately 10,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Elvina joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Elvina is requesting a new loan of 4000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Elvina from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the income of her family.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Abena
description: Abena prepares corn dough, kenkey, for sale in the markets in and around Elmina. In front of Abena is a large batch of the corn dough she prepares. She will cover small portions of the corn dough with banana leaves and sell these smaller packages to customers. This is the traditional kenkey recipe and the way Abena's mother made her kenkey when Abena was a child. Abena is married to a farmer in her community and they have nine children together. She uses her income to support her husband with the general upkeep of their family. Abena needs this loan to purchase larger bags of maize and banana leaves for her kenkey production. With the new profit Abena will expand her business.

name: Juan
description: Juan is 30 years old and lives in the indigenous community of Shankivironi (in the central Peruvian rainforest).  There he started his family together with Natalia, his wife of 9 years.  The couple have two children: Cintia and Angie, who they care for in their own home.  This young father's work is 'farming'.  It is his main business activity.  Growing coffee on his 3 hectares of farmland is what he most enjoys doing because he has 10 years experience in caring for and growing this crop.  He has also seen how, over the last few months, the price per kilo for coffee beans has risen considerably.  This year he will sell his produce to the “Café Montaña” and “Bio Azul” cooperative where he hopes to obtain good profits.  However, as he is aware that his coffee harvest only happens once a year, he also works providing a public transport service with a vehicle that he rents.  He covers routes from Pichanaki to Puerto Sotani.  His work is going very well but this year he would like to buy a vehicle of his own which he can also use when transporting his harvest from his farmland to the city.   Juan belongs to the "Los Clavelitos de Shakivironi" community bank and this is his third loan from MFP.  He hopes to receive your cooperation in helping him reach his goals.  For his part, he pledges once more to make his loan repayments on time as he has done with his previous loans.  Juan enjoys being a member of his community bank because all the members are responsible people who are very supportive of each other.  Juan, with your support, will invest the money he has requested by adding it to a sum of money he already has in order to buy a vehicle called a 'torito' (a type of motorcycle taxi which is used for public transportation).

name: Iem
description: Iem is 40 years old and married with five children, two of whom have settled down for marriage. She earns a living by cultivating rice crops on a small farm in Srei Santhor district of Kampong Cham province. She has been in this occupation for almost 25 years and is able to make a reasonable income to cover her living cost.  Iem is borrowing 800 US dollars loan through HKL to build a latrine, as she has insufficient money to buy enough construction materials and pay for labor costs. By having a latrine for her household, she can keep her environment clean, protect themselves from spreading diseases and increase their personal hygiene.   She is very happy and thankful because with this loan purpose, HKL has provided her a special interest rate, rather than its general loan rate. She awaits your kindness and relies on your generosity.

name: Marites
description: Marites is more than glad that she has received continued spiritual and financial support from Kiva, its lenders and CCT to sustain her transportation business. She is again in need of funds in the amount of Php 20000 to pay for the needed maintenance and registration of her tricycle. She thanks you for your continuous support of her livelihood. Her tricycle income is a big help in their daily sustenance.Marites hopes to acquire one more tricycle to improve her income so she could send all her three children get a College Education. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship members every week to share stories of her work and also draw strength and inspiration from the word of God which she studies. *All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the word of God, build social capital and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Palomitas Group
description: The “Palomitas” (Little Doves) communal bank will start the first cycle in Pro Mujer as part of the Villa Exaltación Focal Center.  It has 7 members led by a governing board presided over by Flora.  The members of the communal bank carry out a variety of businesses: blanket weaving, neighborhood store, fruit sales, assorted goods sales, macramé blankets, sweater knitting and ‘salchipapas’ [fried sausage with fried potatoes] sales.  The loan they will take out will benefit small micro businesswomen like Flora who indicates that she’s been part of Pro Mujer for two cycles having joined thanks to an invitation from one of the institution’s advisors that came to visit her at home.  She currently has a business selling meat.  She started it thanks to instruction from her sister-in-law and using her savings.  The loan she’ll take out now is to increase capital.  She will buy meat in the city of El Alto’s street markets and then sell it in her sales space.  This way of working allows her to generate income to support her home as possible since she has a common law spouse and two children.  When asked what she likes about Pro Mujer, she answers that she likes the credit, the training and the health services.

name: Merrylou
description: Merrylou's main source of income comes from planting and harvesting rice for sale. She is 30 years old and married. She is from Malibacsan, Jimenez and been three years in farming, earning 6,500 PHP a month. In 2014, she joined GDMPC. She is requesting a loan of 15,000 PHP which will be used to purchase fertilizers and seedlings for the next cropping. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.

name: Edelmira
description: Edelmira R. D. H. lives in Ciudad Arce, department of La Libertad, along with her daughter Eunice and her 11-year-old granddaughter Zolia, who is in school. Edelmira makes a living selling clothing and cosmetics in a business she runs out of her home. Her wish is to be able to increase her inventory so she can increase her profits, which would allow her to help Eunice, who is only 20 years old and wasn't able to continue her education because of financial reasons. At the moment, Eunice is employed, but Edelmira's dream is for her daughter to have a college degree, and she'll only be able to achieve that if Edelmira can make more money with her business, which would allow her daughter to stop working and dedicate herself to earning a degree. That is the reason Edlemira is requesting the loan, so she can stock her business and increase her profits. Translated from Spanish by Marty Greenstein, Kiva Volunteer

name: Zebo
description: Zebo is 46 years old and fights daily to increase her family's income so that her children have all that is necessary for a good life. She has always fought to provide for her family and educate her five children, two of whom are working adults today thanks to her example. Her perseverance has given her family the assurance that she does everything possible to make their lives pleasant.  Due to Zebo's hard work, she was able to purchase a small plot of land that she is farming together with her husband. However, the produce from the land has decreased and family expenses are using up the little capital they have. In turn, this has reduced the amount of money available for purchasing fuels, lubricants, seeds and fertilizers for the new plot of land in which they have invested. This is why Zebo is requesting a loan of 5000 TJS. The situation which Zebo finds herself in has made her ask for help, with the hope that she will find sensitive collaborators to help her get through these hard times.     More about Tajikistan Tajikistan, a key post on the Silk Road, is perhaps best known for its rich history. It was the location for the end of Alexander the Great's rule, and is known for its great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets such as Rudaki, Ibn Sina (Avicenna), Firdousi, Omar Haiyam, Jomi, Mavlavi Rumi and many others. The country, with its epic mountain passes, is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language and a civilization that dates back to the fourth millennium BC. Even today, it is a complex mix of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  However, Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the USSR, damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93 per cent of the country is mountainous and only 7 per cent of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands of people to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  More about IMON International Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low-income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit:  www.imon.tj

name: Josphine
description: Josephine is 46 years old and from Njabini. She is married to John and they have three children who are all in school.  Josephine has been a farmer for the past ten years. She has applied for her first loan from KADET LTD to enable her to buy fertilizers and manure to put on her farm. She hopes that the farm will do well and that she will have much harvest.  She hopes to diversify into cattle rearing in the future.

name: Roger
description: Roger is patiently providing motorcycle transport services to the people in his village, especially students who go to school. He has been doing this for almost four years now. In this kind of business, he is able to provide daily meals for the family and school expenses for his two children. He is married to Juanita, a housekeeper.   Roger would like to provide his services more efficiently and safely, so he is asking for a loan to buy a new pair of tires and side mirrors for the motorcycle. He is asking for a loan of PHP 13,000.   Roger would like to continuously finance the schooling of his children so they can earn a degree and seek good employment someday.

name: To Purchase More Foodstuffs Group
description: Jamila is married with two children. She owns a small restaurant. She will use the extra profits from this loan to pay school fees for her children. This is a group loan. The loan funds will be distributed among the group members, each of whom will invest in her own business. The members mutually guarantee one another's loans. If one member does not repay, the other members are responsible.

name: Lourdes
description: As a single parent of children, Lourdes works hard to support her family.  In the Philippines, she has a buy and sell nipa business, woven palm mats used for house repair and construction businesses.  She also earns additional income from selling herbal medicines.  Lourdes is borrowing PHP 8000 through NWTF to purchase additional stock to sell for her buy and sell nipa business.  Lourdes has been sustaining her business activities with her past 5 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough money to expand her business.

name: Carlos
description: Carlos L. A. M. is 44 years old, married, and has one 15-year-old son who is his first priority. Carlos has a mobile repair workshop in his truck. He has operated this business for two years. This loan will be used to purchase tools for his workshop so he can offer better service.  This is Carlos’ 1st loan with FUDECOSUR or with any other formal bank. His desire is to live a little better economically, and see that his family is well.  About FUDECOSUR: The Foundation for the Development of Southern Communities is dedicated to economically empowering its clients by providing credit and capacitating programs to improve living conditions of micro-entrepreneurs and their children across Southern Costa Rica. You can obtain more information on FUDECOSUR from the website: FUDECOSUR.orgTranslated from Spanish by jeffrey hersk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Jecinta
description: Jecinta has a tailoring business in Nairobi town and has been running it for the last 19 years. She is 50 years old, married and blessed with three children.  She plans to use this loan to buy more sewing materials for use in her business. These include textile materials of different types as well as threads and buttons. She will use the anticipated income to open another tailoring business. This is her sixth loan term and she paid back all her previous loan successfully.  She hopes to become successful in her business and enable her children to achieve the best education and live a successful life in future.

name: Veronica
description: Veronica is a 27-year-old married woman with three children. She plans to make and sell snacks, soft drinks and cooked food in her community to earn a living. She previously had one year of experience with this business. Veronica needs a loan to set up her business again. She plans to use her profits to build her family a new and better home. Veronica has been a member of SPBD since 2012.

name: Warlito Jr.
description: Warlito, a 32-year old, is a married man of Upper Pulacan, Labangan who has 2 children and is earning from his private transport service business. It started almost 3 years ago and he earns 8,000 a month. To improve business, he would like to borrow 50,000 PHP from GDMPC micro credit, which he just joined recently, in order to obtain accessories and tires. Before long, he’s hopeful of the possibility of expanding his business.

name: Rose Lom Group
description: Nenglhing sells piglets and generates income for the family.  She belongs to “Rose Lom Group” and she is pictured with her hand raised. She is also the featured borrower of the group. Nenglhing subjugates all the challenges one can endure. She has seven kids and lives with her aged in-laws. Her husband earns a living as a sweeper in a military camp with a small regular monthly income.  To manage the family finances with only her husband's income was a big challenge. Debts were piling up while she was trying to look after the kids and the in-laws. School fees, medicinal cost for the in-laws and household maintenance expenses were all borne by only her husband income.  Nenglhing started raising piglets and slowly developed her piglet-selling business.  She is making rapid progress in her business. She usually travels across the neighboring provinces in the state and purchases piglets. The piglets are then sold in her village and the neighboring villages at a profit. She said, since each house raises pigs, selling piglets is not complicated and instead entices her to do better.  The most challenging part of her business is transportation. The public transport is the most convenient option but the passengers sometimes complain. In order not to disturb others, a private vehicle is hired to transport the piglets. The cost is high but that is the only option left for the piglet transportation. She keeps them in the pigsty at the back of her house and does the selling.  She and her husband work side by side to manage the household expenses.  With her financial assistance, the family is now able to pay back the previous debts.  She wants all of her seven kids to get an education because she was deprived of a good education in her childhood days. The family financial conditions did not allow her to pursue further studies and she ended up with a mere primary education.  With the Kiva loan, she will purchase more piglets to sell and meet the demands of her customers. She is also planning to provide her customers with a credit facility if she can successfully avail the loan.  She thanks Kiva and WSDS for the undeniable support and love. She wishes them great success and prosperity. The rest of the group members are engaged in piggery, weaving and vegetable-selling businesses.

name: Alieva
description: Alieva D. has been a client of MicroInvest since 2008 but she recommends herself as a serious and reliable client. D. trades flour and it brings her general income. She works straight with suppliers so she trades at low prices. She has repeat customers and appropriate business skills. Mrs. Alieva D. is applying to KIVA for a business development loan of 3600 STJ for 5 months to improve her business.

name: Florencio
description: Florencio is a married man and is twenty-nine years old.  He has four children, three boys and one girl.  They all live in the small town of Santa María, in the canton of Tablón in Sololá.    He makes a living in agriculture, and has been doing this for ten years.  He chose this activity because through this, he is able to make enough revenue and profits to sustain his family.  Another benefit from this type of work is that he can do it alongside his family.  He is requesting a loan of Q 6,000.00 in order to buy potato seeds and organic fertilizer for his crop.    One of his greatest dreams is to increase his agriculture activity so that he can obtain higher earnings and thereby move his family ahead.

name: Sergei
description: Sergei is married and has adult daughters.  He is from the Privetnoye village.  He is involved in growing early agricultural crops and plant 20 000 heads of cabbage, 15 000 peppers, 20 000 eggplants, 10 000 strawberry plants, 1 000 heads of onions, 30 000 tomato plants and uses 30 sotkas to plant potatoes every year.  Farming has been earning a living for Sergei for 15 years.  He invested 50 000 hryvnia into his large business.  His net profit amounts to 4 400 hryvnia per month.  Sergei wants to invest a sum of 15 000 hryvnia to purchase seeds and fertilizers, and also to install heating, repair greenhouses and re-installing the plastic in them.  Sergei likes to be involved in his favorite business and also likes to earn enough money from it to support his family.

name: Thuong
description: Mrs. Thuong  is 33 years old, married and has three children. She lives in a rural area. Raising poultry and cattle is her main job, which she has been doing for more than 5 years now. The loan can help her to build a sanitation latrine in order to improve her living standards, especially for her children.

name: Michael Angelo
description: Michael Angelo is studying electronics. He chose this field of study because he thinks that this will be very useful since we live in a modern world. He is requesting a loan from Kiva lenders because his parents can’t sustain the cost of his schooling. Michael Angelo is very hopeful that lenders will grant his loan request so he can pay his tuition fees.

name: Anthony
description: Anthony is a married man. He has six children. He describes himself to be focused and hardworking. He operates a welding business. His business is located in a busy area, and his primary customers are locals. He describes his biggest business challenge to be rain, which affects business. He will use the KES 80,000 loan to buy a welding machine and other accessories. His business goal is to have a big workshop within five years. This is his third loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. The previous loans were repaid successfully. He will use the anticipated profits to pay school fees for his children.

name: Muhammad
description: Muhammad is a maize farmer and Babban Gona member. Anticipating a good harvest this season, Muhammad has the opportunity to attain yields of up to 8 metric tones of maize per hectare of land, 5.5 times that of the average Nigerian maize farmer.Before joining Babban Gona, Muhammad would have had to sell his maize at harvest, a period when maize prices are at their lowest in the market, to meet his immediate cash needs. With the help of this loan, he can store his maize and sell it at a future date for up to 37% higher than the market price at harvest.As a Babban Gona member, Muhammad will benefit from marketing support that could see him generate earnings of up to $2000/ha. Muhammad is thankful that he now has the opportunity to improve the life of his children and family and looks forward to using his additional earnings to acquire more land to put into the Babban Gona program.

name: Mehar Deen Muhammad Group
description: "I am Mehar and I’m a 58-year-old married lady. I reside in an area called Kot Radha Kishan near the city of Kasur, Pakistan. I own a two-room brick house and have been living in it with my family for the past 30 years. My husband's name is D. M. and he is a watchman by profession. I am the mother of two sons.   "My elder son completed his education up to 8th standard and couldn’t study further because of lack of interest. He is working in a cotton factory where he fills cotton into sacks. My younger son got his education up to 10th standard and is working as a typist in the high court.   "I belong to a milk-selling profession. This is our family business. My mother was also involved in this business. I get milk from the buffalo by getting up early in the morning. Presently, I’ve one buffalo. I sell the milk in the milk shops and to the community as well. I sell the kg of milk at 34 Pak rupees. I have successfully repaid my first loan from Asasah (a micro-finance institute in Pakistan). Now I am applying again for a loan to buy another buffalo to expand my milk-selling business.   "I’m the group leader for some more women from my locality. Razia baji and another lady called Razia baji each want a loan to buy a buffalo for their milk-selling businesses. A third lady called Razia baji wants a loan to buy wood to re-sell. Irshad baji wants a loan to buy a sewing machine to use to sew clothes."   This is a group loan. The loan funds will be distributed among the group members, each of whom will invest in her own business. The members mutually guarantee one another's loans. If one member does not repay, the other members are responsible.

name: Elbinida
description: Elbinida is 47 years old and widowed with one child. She works very hard to provide for her child.  Elbinida runs a general store in the Philippines and has requested a PHP 13,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like shampoo, groceries, etc. in her general store.  Elbinida has been in this business for 6 years and sells a variety of items such as canned goods, noodles, eggs, sugar, soap, etc.   In the future, Elbinida would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Hannah
description: Hannah is 34 years old and married with three children who are in school. She lives in the Congo town area and has run a restaurant for the past 15 years. Hannah stopped her education at the third grade. Her husband is not presently working and the family depends on her for their livelihood.   Hannah is requesting a loan to purchase more oil, rice, charcoal, and pepper for her restaurant. In the future, she hopes to build her own house and improve her children's education.

name: Abraham
description: Abraham is 60 years old and lives alone in his own home. He separated with his wife a number of years ago and his five children are already grown up and working. This enterprising man makes a living in construction. Since he was a young man he learned from watching his relatives who worked in the trade. Currently he has a construction company, and although he lacks a few permits he manages with three other workers. He oversees them since he is the master builder. He really enjoys his work and says it is heartwarming to see the big jobs completed with good results. It's for this reason he has various clients who recommend him, and he doesn't lack for work since he is always starting or completing construction. For the future, he plans on purchasing a pickup truck so that his workers can move around without problems. This is his fifth loan with Kiva partner MFP, and he promises to make his payments on time since he doesn't want to be in bad standing with the people who made this support possible and so that he can continue working in search of progress. Abraham plans to invest the loan in the purchase of a cement mixing machine since it is an instrument he is missing in order to finish his jobs more quickly, and he calculates that he will earn better profits.

name: Mamadou
description: Mamadou G. is a young mechanic born in Thiès on September 3, 1981. He is married and lives with his wife in the Cité Lamy. From a very young age he has been working with his father near the bus station. He recently opened a spare parts shop. With this loan, he wants to increase his stock of goods.   Translated from French by Véronique Fourment, Kiva Volunteer

name: Emilia
description: Emilia runs a convenience store, which is located right outside her house in Ozamis City, Misamis Occidental. She is 60 years old, married, and has six adult-age children.   Emilia is a member of Paglaum MPC, where she learns to venture into business and access initial capital for her retailing business. Recently, she asked the cooperative for a loan to restock her store with consumable goods such as canned goods, noodles, and others.

name: Tiem
description: Residing in Battambang province’s Moung Russey district, Tiem is 36 years old and a rice grower in the local area. She has struggled to make a living through her current business as a farmer in order to support her family, especially her two children, one who goes to school and a little kid who is too young for schooling. Tiem is able to generate about 48,000 KHR per day from the current business that she has had for ages.   Tiem is a fifth-cycle client with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner) and has repaid her past loans completely. She feels confident that she can improve her lifestyle in a gradual manner. Now, her newly requested loan amount is 3,200,000 KHR. She will use this loan to add to her savings in order to buy an additional plot of farmland to grow more crops. She hopes that she can enlarge her business and get a doubled rice crop so that she can earn more income.

name: Blanca Rosmira
description: Blanca, 55 years old, is separated and is the mother of two adult children. She is characterized as a very responsible and hard-working woman, a visionary and a good businesswoman.   She has always worked as a businesswoman, selling vegetables in the municipality of Medellín and since a short while ago, she has had her own business.   She has known how to overcome difficult times in the business and dreams of buying her own house and having a business that stands the test of time. It is for this that Blanca approached to ask for a loan, which will be used to purchase an assortment of inventory of vegetable supplies and do some improvements to the business's retail space.   Blanca is a very organized woman although she has had to face business competition in the sector.   The sum of all of her efforts offers her whole family an excellent quality of life.

name: Bobo
description: Bobo is a prudent man. He was born in 1952. He works at the gold factory. He is a driver in this factory. He lives on his salary. He lives hand to mouth. His wife has died. His daughter is married. He lives alone. He is ill. He needs treatment. He is suffering from his illness. He decided to get a loan to treat his illness. He needs money. He is asking for a loan with this aim. He awaits your mercy and support for his treatment.

name: Mwanasiti
description: Mwanasiti lives in Likoni, Kenya. She is 50 years old and married with two children. She has been running a food café for the last two years and the business has been doing great. She has been able to employ two people to help her run the business well. In five years time she wants the café to have grown into a restaurant that will generate enough income for her family.   She knew about Milango through friends who invited her to join so that she could save and access credit to fund her business. She is now seeking a loan to buy maize flour, wheat flour and cooking oil for the business. The challenges that she faces include competition and customers not paying on time. Extra income from the loan will improve her living standards.

name: L'amour Divin 2.1 Group
description: Lurdrich is a member of the community bank group L’Amour Divin 2.1 in Brazzaville, the Republic of Congo. Helping to lead a group of eleven other micro-entrepreneurs, Lurdrich runs a small electronics shop as an IT specialist. With his first loan with HOPE Congo, Lurdrich will buy a photocopier and reams of paper for his shop.   In his daily activities Lurdrich faces the challenges of poor infrastructure and power cuts, which affect his business. In order to overcome these challenges, he has purchased a generator so that he can stay open for business when the power is out.   In the future, Lurdrich would love to expand his house further and to purchase more sophisticated IT equipment. With increased profits, he hopes that one day he can finance his degree in computer engineering.

name: Sergio Alfonso
description: Sr. Sergio Alfonso G. Garcia is a hardworking gentleman who covers the expenses of his family by working at a factory.  On the weekends, he performs blacksmithing jobs.    He wants a loan in order to put up a fence so that his family will have greater security.  In order to complete this project, he needs to buy materials and pay for labor.

name: Simon
description: Simon Mwaniki is 38 years old and married. He has no children of his own but has two dependants, his aging parents whom Simon entirely supports. Simon Mwaniki lives in Ruai.  Simon was first employed in a lumber-selling business in the year 2000 and worked for three years. During that period, he managed to save Ksh 40,000 (US$ 615). The three-year experience also gave Simon enough confidence to start his own lumber business, which he still has to date, though with some struggles.      	 Simon’s business suffered a setback in the year 2006 due to his wedding preparations, which ended up causing him huge unforeseen costs relating to the culture and traditions of his tribe that he was expected to adhere to, if he was to receive their blessings to marry his bride.  Through this time and due to the financial strain that Simon experienced, his business suffered and he still finds it hard to bring it back up again. Simon needs support in order to revive his business again.  He is therefore requesting a loan of US$ 1000, which he will use to purchase lumber to restock his business. He will be very grateful if he can receive this support, in order to improve his business.   Simon believes that once he has additional stock, his customers will be able to purchase enough lumber to meet their needs, especially those who purchase in bulk.  This will save them the inconvenience of having to travel all the way to the city center to buy lumber, at a much bigger cost to them. The loan therefore will enable him to serve his customers efficiently and effectively. He will also earn more income so as to uplift himself and his family. The loan repayment period will be 12 months.

name: Otunoy
description: Otunoy is 43 years old.  She is married to an educated person.  Her husband, Mirsharif, works as a teacher.  Otunoy works as a teacher at the Khujand State University.  She is a smart and experienced teacher.  Otunoy has to pay for her son's tuition contract because her son got accepted to a university this year.  Otunoy is requesting a loan in the amount of 650 US dollars to pay for her son's university tuition.  She awaits your kindness.

name: Eric
description: Eric Vincent is a dynamic man who is 41 years old. He is married and has four children, who are all at school. He lives in the town in a house which he was able to build from the profits he has made, thanks to loans he has received from Vahatra. He has been selling fruit in the Grand Market for the past 24 years and has been able to build a loyal base of customers who live in the town but also in the countryside. He is planning to use this loan to buy 1000 pineapples, 500 kilos of papayas and 500 kilos of granadillas. His aim is to buy a truck so he can deliver his fruit in the countryside.

name: Inacio Francisco
description: Inácio was born in the central province of Sofala in the Marromeu district.  He is 33 years old, married, and has two children ages 3 and 7.  His older child attends school.  He completed a degree in Elementary Education 13 years ago in a school in the Manhica district.  He teaches at the elementary school in Boane, earning 7.500,00MT per month, which he uses to support his wife and children.   He owns his own home in Campoane in the Boane district.   He left Marromeu along with his parents in 1988 to move to Boane and he built his own home in 2000.  He previously had a loan to purchase consumer goods through a commercial bank (BIM) and decided not to continue with the bank for additional loans because he had faced difficulties making payments beyond his means for a long time.  Upon learning about Hluvuku from colleagues, he decided to request a loan.  This loan is for 12.000,00MT for the purchase of construction materials (cement, sand, etc.)  He plans to pay back the loan without any problems in order to have access to future loans with the goals of finishing his house and equipping it.      Translated from Portuguese by Michele Magrino, Kiva Volunteer

name: Kenia Ivonne
description: Kenia Ivonne M. lives in the city of San Pedro Masahuat in the district of La Paz. As a single mother, Kenia works every day selling everyday consumer products in order to support her 3 dependent children.    She is requesting a loan to restock her business so that she can generate more income.  This will help her meet the increasing needs of her children. Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Silvia Maria
description: Silvia is a 41-year-old businesswoman. She is in a relationship and has four children. Her business is a mini grocery store in her home, and she has had this business for seven years. She has been a client of the institution for thirteen years; previously she sold general merchandise. She will invest this loan in products such as rice, beans, sugar, canisters of oil, cheese, mortadella, natural sauces, Presto instant coffee, popular medications, etc.

name: Aminata
description: Aminata is 37 years old and married with 2 children, ages 8 and 13. She runs a business in Kissy Sierra Leone.  Aminata has been in this business for 10 years and sells books, pens, paper, and other office supplies at her store. She also earns income from renting a house. She says that her business is doing well.  She requested this loan through BRAC to purchase office supplies. She says that the extra income from this loan will help her improve her standard of living. In the future, she would like to be a big supplier to offices.

name: Carmen Rita
description: Carmen is working to get a 'license' from the wholesaler of "Safire" brand beauty aids in order to sell them via cataloged presentations. With the returns she expects to make out of the sale of these products, she plans to be able to sustain herself together with a now six-month-old child. The father abandoned her, and she must now make it on her own! She lives with her family, as she has no means of getting a house, but her family is as poor as can be, so Carmen needs to come up with at least the basics to maintain herself and the child’s food, clothing and transportation needs.  Carmen tells us that she's realized she needs to go back to school to become a professional, so that's another reason why she needs to earn 'as much as the business will afford'. She wouldn't say the profit margin on the beauty aids selling business, but normally it's something in the neighborhood of 100%, so she will probably do well, and start her schooling days in January, as she is now planning to do!

name: Kadzo
description: Kadzo is a business lady living in Malindi, Kenya. She is a married mother of five children although only the last three attend school. She is a milk vendor, a business she has run for one year. Kadzo is applying for a loan of 15,900 KES to pay for her children's school fees. She looks forward to repay the loan from the proceeds of the milk sales.

name: Seonilyn
description: Seonilyn is a hard-working woman entrepreneur with five children.  She earns a living by raising pigs in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 15000 through NWTF to purchase feed and other supplies to raise her pigs.  She supplements this income with earnings from her motorcycle transport.  Seonilyn dreams that one day she will be able to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Amas De Casa Group
description: This group named "Amas de Casa" is striving to improve the living conditions for themselves and their families by working together.  For this reason, they have joined the poverty elimination program so that they can improve their living conditions.Norma is a member of this group.  She is a hardworking woman who says that all of her efforts are geared toward helping her family.  Since she is the breadwinner, Norma dreams of having a large stand where she can sell fruits and vegetables.  She is grateful for the training that her entire group has received.  Norma is requesting a loan in order to buy fresh fruits and vegetables to sell.  This will enable her to continue working so that she can improve her life and that of her family.

name: Pascuala Del Carmen
description: 64-year-old Pascuala is a hard-working woman who is invested in her work. She comes from the rural region of Pacayita in Masaya.  She is requesting her 24th loan from ADIM, to invest in her business of selling corn-derived products, which she started with a loan from her mom. With the income she will earn, she will be sure to continue paying the loan installments and will improve her living conditions.

name: Eunice
description: Eunice retails home products such as baby powder, napkins, small diepers and skin care lotions for children. Her sales attracts lots of customers as he carries it on her heard and trek to several villages to sell her wares. She has been introduced to the TEACH lending programme. She hopes that if given the $700 KIVA loan she would expand her business.

name: Mercedes
description: Mercedes is 42 years old, married and has three children. Her eldest child graduated from college already, while the rest are still studying. She gets her income through farming. Mercedes and her husband are farmers planting and harvesting rice to sell. She wants to continue ensuring good nutrition for her crops, and she needs additional capital of PHP 15,000 to buy fertilizers, insecticides and pesticides used in farming. This will help the crops grow abundantly and attain a better harvest someday. She will save additional revenue for education purposes for the rest of her children.

name: Glenda
description: Glenda works hard to support her family. Glenda is married and has a motorcycle transport business in the Philippines. Glenda requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to purchase spare parts for the maintenance of her motorcycle. Glenda has been in this business for 5 years now. In the future, Glenda would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Justine's Group
description: Justine is 39 years old and the leader of her lending group in Namugongo. She is a single mother with four children, ages 24 to 14 years, and she takes care of five dependents, including orphans and parents. She is a business lady with a clinic in Bulooli trading centre that she has owned for 11 years, and she is able to make 45,000/= as profits a week. She is a friendly person and this has enabled her to better take care of her patients and the general public. She strives to develop her business more as well as educate and build her home and family well. She needs a loan to be able to buy more drugs so as to increase her capital base.

name: Rosa Elvira
description: Rosa is a 39-year-old woman who has a great desire to boost her business selling sandals and Avon products over the next few years.  Rosa started her business after she separated from her ex-husband.  She decided to take a craft course where she learned to make sandals.  She then started selling sandals.  She works alone all week long.  The difficulty she faces is crime.  Rosa is single and doesn't have any children.  Her biggest dream is to further expand her business.  She would like this loan for her business selling sandals and Avon products.

name: Flora
description: Flora is a happily married woman and the owner of a minibus. Flora needs a loan to repaint her minibus and to make some repairs.  Flora doesn't drive but she hired a driver. Flora lives with her family. Flora's husband is unemployed right now and that is why she needs your help

name: Cielo
description: Cielo and her husband Juan José recently acquired their house through a government loan.  She’s requesting the loan to be able to buy and install the kitchen cabinets and counters that she still needs.    Cielo plans to repay the loan with profits earned from selling beauty products via catalogue since Juan José will be in charge of covering family and school costs with the salary he earns as a policeman.  They hope to improve the quality of life of their three children and to have their main asset in good, secure conditions for them. .

name: Osaafiane
description: "I am proud to be a member of LAPO because LAPO has helped my business grow, and I now can send my children to school," says Mrs. A. Osaafiane, 28 years old.  A. is requesting a loan of $750 for business expansion.

name: 140-008265-01-6 Group
description: Hello! Our group is called Brillante Amenecer and the following people are members: Sra. Sayra R. has for 20 years earned her living by selling cosmetics and plastic products and also for four years making baked goods. She lives in Union Libre with her husband who raises cattle. She has four dependent children. Her husband is responsible for the family expenses, and she contributes what small amount she can. Sr. Andres H. has been a businessman for 20 years. His main business is a small convenience store, a common line of work in our society. He is single but is responsible for the education and daily expenses of his two siblings, plus the cost of food for his mother since his father has passed away. His mother was left without support, so Andres had to take over all the family’s food expenses. Sra. Gloria de Jesus Cáliz is a businesswoman and has been operating a small convenience store for five years now. She lives in Union Libre and has three children who are still dependent on her. Her husband is a farmer and pays for household expenses. With the money that she earns from her store, Gloria covers her own personal expenses and as well helps her husband with household expenses. She also works hard to buy kitchen utensils and household electrical appliances, important things for the home--she has bought these out of the profits from the business. Sra. Yeni P. worked selling cosmetics for many years, but as she is a single mother with a son who is completely dependent on her, the business did not supply enough income to provide for her family. She managed to obtain a small convenience store which greatly helps her to cover household expenses, so she now has two businesses. When she is out selling cosmetics, her son helps her with the store. Translated from Spanish by Jane Agg, Kiva Volunteer

name: Regina
description: A jeepney barker’s wife is our featured story. A resident of Calabayan, Ozamiz City, she is Mrs. Regina C. L., a 46-year- old married mother of six children who are mostly minors and still dependent on their parents for their needs. As a thoughtful and loving mother, Regina has helped her husband in supporting their children. Presently, she is engaged in snack, rice and vegetables vending, having started this business with an initial capital only of Php 2,500.00. Her business is progressing, patronized mainly by neighbors, students and friends in the village.  	 Regina is now requesting a loan of Php 5,000.00 under the Medal Pangnegosyo 2 program of PMPC to increase her capital for her business and to purchase school supplies needed for her children. She is very thankful for the support of her husband and the trust of PAGLAUM MPC and KIVA in micro-entrepreneurs.

name: Jimmy
description: Jimmy, 48 years old, is married and a resident of Calamba, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. His spouse is a housewife.  He has now decided to enter into business himself, purchasing fish in bulk for resale at market.  Last January 14, 2013 both Jimmy and his wife agreed to join Paglaum MPC to avail themselves of a loan because they wanted to increase his sales. But aside from the financial assistance they received, they say that they also enjoyed the add-on benefits like insurance and savings.  He has now applied again for a loan to purchase farm inputs. He is wishing that with Paglaum’s help, and with the patience and diligence of his wife, he is looking forward to being successful.

name: Kyenzige Sacco2 Group
description: Gertrida is married with six children who are all going to school. She operates a retail shop and a bar. On top of this, Gertrida is also practising farming on a small scale so that she can supplement her income. It's from these businesses that she has been able to educate her children and look after the family. She previously borrowed 300,000 shillings from UGAFODE three months ago which helped to increase capital in the business.  Gertrida now wants a loan of 600,000 shillings for her retail business. Her dream is to see her children go to school and also to support her husband in putting up a permanent house for the family. Her challenge is limited capital in the business plus high transport costs. She is optimistic that with UGAFODE through the group, her life and her family status will gradually change.

name: Marianela
description: Marianela is a member of the Bienestar (“Wellbeing”) Village Bank. She is 30 years old and lives with her common-law husband and their son. Marianela and her husband sell foodstuffs like rice, sugar, and oil. They buy the items in the Santa Rosa Market in the city of Ayacucho and bring them to the Ayacuchan jungle in her sister’s truck, where Marianela sells them wholesale to distributors. She has been in this business for three years now.  Marianela is requesting a loan of 3000 soles to buy more rice, sugar, and oil in bulk. Her goal for the future is to build a home of her own, using her FINCA savings. (She currently lives with her in-laws.)

name: Olga Mary
description: Olga Mary V. M. is 45 years old and lives in the district of Mache in the Otuzco province in the department of La Libertad in Peru.  She is married and has 3 children who are dependent on her since they are young and are in school.  She went to school until the third year of high school since she became pregnant at the age of 16 and could not return to her studies.  Instead, she dedicated herself to her husband and to raising her children.  Olga sells products at a grocery store that she has in her house, but she also breeds guinea pigs, chickens, hens, and turkeys.  With her first loan of 300 soles she began to buy her first wholesale food products such as rice, sugar, and oil.  With this loan of 1,000 [soles], she will invest in purchasing wholesale food products as well as guinea pigs and turkeys.  Olga dreams of increasing the breeding of her animals and expanding her grocery store in order to make more money so that she can provide for her children and send them to school.   Translated from Spanish by Anne Rodriguez, Kiva Volunteer

name: Mukadast
description: Mukadast is a resident of the region of Qubadiyon. She raised and is educating her children alone. Mukadast is divorced from her husband. She has three children, a daughter-in-law and grandsons. Her youngest son is a football player and lives in Russia. Her oldest son lives with his family.Mukadast is a budding businesswoman; she wants to open a car wash in the area. Mukadast will run the business with her oldest son. There are not many car washes in the area, and Mukadast decided to open one. For these plans, Mukadast has asked for a loan. She does not have enough money to procure the washing equipment.

name: Jose Elvis
description: José is a 23-year-old father who lives together with his family in the small village of Puplan, in Túcume district, in Lambayeque province, 45 minutes from the city of Chiclayo.  José has been selling livestock for more than three years.  He fattens the animals and then sells them to traders who visit his area.  This business provides him with the income he needs to make progress and financially support his family.  For this reason, he always puts a lot of effort into maintaining it.  In parallel with this activity, he also sells groceries and owns a 'moto carguera' (a motorcycle adapted for transporting cargo).  José would like to expand his business by purchasing more animals to raise and sell.  In order to achieve this goal, he needs to request a loan for 1,500 soles from Edpyme Alternativa.  José is a father who is dedicated to his work and who is always looking out for his family's well-being.

name: Jane-Mary
description: Jane-Mary is a trained tailor. She started her business in 2001, a year after finishing her training.  She operates a tailoring shop at her local community’s training centre. Hence she has access to the customers who are mostly market women. She also makes school uniforms.  At the same premises, she sells fresh fruits in order to supplement her tailoring income.  Through her business, she has brought tailoring services to her community. With the loan of $75 from PEMCI, she wishes to expand her tailoring shop and purchase materials in order to meet the demands of her customers which are increasing day by day.

name: Elsa Andrea
description: Elsa is 24 years old and single. She makes a living selling cosmetics from a catalog. She visits homes and public and private offices in the city of Santa Cruz to offer her products.   This loan is her second with the institution. Elsa will use this loan to buy discounted wholesale cosmetics and jewelry. She will then be able to offer a variety of products to her clientele, increasing her earnings. Her reason for applying for this loan is to continue improving her business. Elsa will use the profits to continue buying a variety of beauty products.   Elsa is a very hardworking person, and she is happy for the opportunity she has been offered as this is her only source of income.

name: Malika
description: Malika H. lives in the Gissar region. She is 27 years old. She is divorced and has one child. Malika has a technical secondary education. She has been sewing clothing for more than five years. She does this at home. She is asking for a loan to buy raw materials so she can provide quality services.Translated from Russian by Elena Fedorchuk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Orgilmaa
description: Orgilmaa is a 37-year-old who lives with her husband and 3 children in a ger in Mongolia's Arkhangai province. She was a herdswoman until 2005. She moved to the center of the province and started helping with her sister's business, selling livestock intestines. Orgilmaa gained lot of experience and regular customers; now, she is planning to open her own meat subsidiary products business. Her husband works at a construction company in Ulaanbaatar. Her 3 children study at secondary school. Her standard of living is normal. In the future, she wants to expand her business and open a meat wholesale business. She is requesting 900,000 MNT to buy a large amount of inventory to sell at retail prices during winter. She is a hardworking and modest person.

name: Anecita
description: Anecita is 53 years old and married with five children. Anecita works very hard to provide for them.Anecita runs a general store in the Philippines. She has requested a PHP 18,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like beverages, home care products, canned goods, and other groceries.Anecita has been in this business for three years and sells a variety of items. In the future, Anecita would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Yun
description: Mrs. Yun S. (51) and her husband (52, pictured here) live in the Kampong Cham district of Cambodia with their four children. The family have several sources of income, and like most families in Cambodia, they pool all their earnings. Yun S.'s husband earns $1 a day transporting passengers by horse and cart. Two of her children work at a garment factory, earning $50 a month each, whilst the other two are students. Yun S. herself earns $2 a day selling vegetables which she grows on the family's land. She intends to use the loan to purchase a water pumping machine to irrigate the land and increase the amount of vegetables she is able to grow.

name: Rosalina
description: Rosalina is 61 years old and lives in Tambulig, Zamboanga del Sur, Philippines. She is married with 3 adult children.   Rosalina manages an internet cafe with her husband, and she has been doing this for 5 years already. She earns approximately PHP 10,000 each month doing this type of business activity. She has requested a loan to purchase an additional computer set unit.   Rosalina has been a member of PMPC for 5 years. In the future, she hopes to expand their business.

name: Lorenzo Urbano
description: Lorenzo Urbano is 53 years old and is married.  He lives with his wife and 14-year-old son in the Caimito 1 district in Ventanas Canton.  The communal bank "LA VERDAD NOS HARA LIBRES" ["The Truth Will Set Us Free"] is located in the Caimito 1 district, which is part of Ventanas canton.  The members of this communal bank work in short-cycle agriculture, growing corn and rice.  Lorenzo Urbano works in agriculture growing corn and rice.  He purchases his supplies in Ventanas, and makes his sales in the market there.  He is requesting the loan for the purchase of supplies, fertilizers, and weed-killers for growing corn.  The loan will help him to increase his income for his family's use.  His dream is to be able to purchase some property, and so be able to enjoy good health and be together with his family.  In his free time, he likes to read the Bible and discuss the word of God with his friends.

name: Marcionila
description: Marcionila is a married woman with seven children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Marcionila is 47 years old and four of her children are in school.Marcionila has a food vending business in the Philippines. Marcionila requested a PHP 18,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy ingredients like fish, vegetables, oil, etc.Marcionila has been in this business for 25 years. In the future, Marcionila would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Nancy
description: Nancy is a 21-year-old, single lady who lives in Irbid, with her family. She is a university student majoring in Accounting. Her ‎family is facing financial crises, therefore she has all the challenges of being able to achieve her dream to complete her ‎education. The income of her father is not enough to cover her university fees, so she applied for a loan to pay for ‎her university fees and achieve her dreams.‎

name: Rusell
description: Rusell G. is from the village of Southwestern Calamba Misamis Occidental. She is 34 years old. Rusell is married and has 1 school age child. To make a living, Rusell owns & operates a business venture in the retail sector operating a specialized retail store. The main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling meat products including pork and beef in the public market. Rusell has been engaged in her business for over 5 years and earns approximately 10600 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2008, Rusell joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Rusell has successfully repaid a previous loan of 25000 PHP from GDMPC. This previous loan was used to to invest in expanding the business. Rusell is requesting a new loan of 30000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional inventory & as working capital. This loan will be the fifth loan taken out by Rusell from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the family's income.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three units offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Jihad
description: Jihad is a conservative woman who is unwilling to upload her photo on the internet. The photo is of her son  Jihad is 45 years old, married and a mother of six children. She lives in Al Karak, Jordan.  Jihad is looking to have a loan of 400 JOD to buy raw materials to make cheese and yoghurt for trading purposes.

name: Maria Del Carmen
description: María, age 36, is married and has two children.  She lives in the town of Quimistán, Santa Barbara.  For 11 years, she has had her own business, a small grocery store.  It is located in her house.  She sells pantry staples such as rice, beans, sugar, bread, dairy products, flour, lard, cleaning products, canned goods, etc.    The loan she is requesting is for 15,000 Lempiras.  This is her fourth loan cycle with the institution.  She will invest the loan in the purchase of basic products to sell, such as lard, flour, rice, sugar, eggs, dairy products, churros, sweets, etc.    Her plans are to keep her business stocked, to always lives with her children, and to manage to have another business.

name: El Progreso Group
description: The communal bank "El Progreso" [Progress] comprises 12 members who are neighbors and know each other well. Maria Elisa is president of the group and has a small store in the front of her house where she displays her merchandise every day. She sells cleaning and personal hygiene products and non-perishable foods such as noodles, tea, rice, and more.  She wants to move forward working with Fundación Paraguaya, and her group is growing stronger by the day. She says she is happy with her committee position and also would encourage her fellow members to keep striving to meet their objectives.

name: George
description: George is a 28-year-old married man. He has one child who is aged one. He describes himself to be ambitious. He operates a retail business where he sells mobile phones and mobile phone accessories. He has been involved in this business for 4 years. His business is located in an urban area and his primary customers are the general public. He describes his biggest business challenge to be insecurity. He will use the 35,000 KES loan to buy more stock of mobile phones and accessories. His business goal is to open more outlets within 5 years. He hopes that in the future, he will be successful. This is his third loan loan with SMEP DTM. Previous loans were repaid successfully. He will use the anticipated profits to reinvest in the business.

name: George
description: George O. O. is a 28-year-old man living in the Nyalenda neighborhood in Kisumu, Kenya with his wife and two children. George moved to Kisumu after the post-election violence in the Central Province of Kenya displaced him from his home there. He has been living in Kisumu for one year and has recently started a poultry business.  George is a boda-boda driver, which means he is the driver of a bicycle taxi (a common, inexpensive mode of transport in Kisumu). Looking to increase his income, George wanted to start a small business that would be easy to maintain while he continued his boda-boda work. He decided on a poultry business, since after feeding and giving water to the chickens he would be free to work during the day.   A new member to the K-MET network, George was interested in becoming one of K-MET’s Community Health Workers so that he could “help the people near him who need assistance.” He also found out about K-MET’s micro-finance program and is now applying for a loan of approximately 150 USD in order to expand his poultry business.  George has 15 chickens at present and sells the eggs to his neighbors. He would like to use the loan money to purchase about 150 chickens. After expanding the number of poultry, he will be able to expand his sales, perhaps getting a stall in the local market.

name: Rosa Elvia
description: Rosa is a member of the 3 de Mayo Communal Bank.  They meet every 15 days in the Picoaza area, which is a parish belonging to the city of Portoviejo in the Manbí province.  Rosa is a fighter and a hard-worker who is dedicated to her family.  She always thinks of her family’s well being.  That is why she comes to the foundation to ask for a loan, which will greatly contribute to her established business.  Rosa has been married to Hernán Arteaga for 30 years.  They have three children; ages 18, 26, and 28.  She sells clothes.  For now she sells in a car together with her husband .  They travel the streets where they live selling clothes and other articles.  Her house is her own, and it is situated in the center of the region in order to deal with her business.  They have lived in this house for ten years.  Rosa dreams of setting up her house to also have a business selling clothes there.  She makes clothes herself, and she has been a dressmaker for 26 years.  Rosa’s business is a family business where everyone participates.  Her husband makes deliveries and also helps a lot selling clothes.  He is a great help and a big advantage.  She will use the loan that she receives to buy fabric, thread, zippers, and buttons, etc. to make clothes and to get some jewelry to compliment the clothes.   Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Gulchehra
description: Gulchehra is forty years old, divorced and has two children, one of whom is an adult.  Nine years ago and with 500 TJS she began selling a variety of children’s clothes and shoes in a local market. Little by little she has developed her business and manages it by herself.   Gulchehra loves little children, and she tries to offer high-quality children clothes for her customers. She renews the assortment of goods every season. She is now applying for a 8,500 TJS loan to buy children’s clothes and shoes for the upcoming season.

name: Rutter
description: Rutter is 41 years old, married, and has four children. His spouse is a housekeeper. Rutter patiently provides motorcycle transport services to the people in his village. He is asking for a loan of PHP 7,000 to maintain his motorcycle, such as by purchasing new tires. He would like to ensure safe travel for his passengers. With good profits, Rutter will be able to pay his children's school expenses and save for their future needs.

name: Concepcion
description: Concepcion is married with six children. Concepcion is 61 years old and lives in Sapang Ama, Sapang Dalaga.  To earn a living, Concepcion is a "nipa palm" weaver business. She has had this business for 20 years. Each month, Concepcion earns approximately PHP 2,600. She has requested a loan of PHP 7,000 to purchase nipa palm in order her to weave and sell to community. Concepcion has been a member of PMPC for five years.
town: Calamba-Sapang Ama Sapang Dalaga Misamis Occidenta

name: Heshima Women Group
description: The lady raising her hand in the photo is Caroline. She is 29 years old, married and blessed with one child. She is member of Heshima Women Group which joined Hand in Hand Eastern Africa to benefit from enterprise development and financial management training.She operates a beauty salon. She is borrowing a Kiva loan to buy more weaves and braids for her salon. She hopes this will enable her to provide quality services to her customers, hence increasing her income.She is grateful to Kiva and their lenders for the support.

name: Shafaqat's Group
description: Shafaqat, age 53 (with hand raised in the photo), runs a boutique business from her home. She purchases cloth from different textile firms and provides it to different tailors and embroidery experts, with whom she has contracts. Their task to complete finished products from the cloth for her to sell in her shop.   She is very active and gives the maximum time to her business every day, which is why her business is going well. She contributes to her family's finances from the proceeds of her business. She has 10 years of experience in her business and is very confident about its growth.    She has applied for a loan from Kiva partner Asasah to apply toward her boutique business. With the loan, she will purchase cloth in bulk to fulfill larger orders on time and to add variety to the display in her boutique. This is her second loan application from Asasah. Over the previous loan year, she has proved herself as a responsible client who always paid her installments on time and never missed any meetings.   Shafaqat lives in the city of Faisalabad, which is located in the Punjab province of Pakistan and is famous for its textile industry. She lives with her parents in a three-room house in an area named Islamia Park.

name: Nhóm 10- Yên Doãn 1 Group
description: Dung is 31 years old and married with 2 children. She is the group leader of the Nhóm 10- Yên Doãn 1 solidarity group, which consists of 4 members.   In 2010, Dung joined Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women to improve her business, and she has successfully repaid 2 loans from them already.  Dung has a manufacturing business making iron furniture. She is requesting a loan to purchase more material to make iron furniture to sell. She has been involved in this business for 7 years. One of the most critical business difficulties that concerns her is lack of capital.  With her business profit, Dung hopes for her business to do well, for her family to be healthy and happy, and to build a new house.

name: Rosalie
description: The person covered in this page is Rosalie. She is 28 years old and married. In Clarin, Misamis Occidental, Philippines, she peddles food items around nearby communities or within the community itself to earn a living. She is named as one of the courteous food vendors in the area in which she has worked for 2 years. Every month, she earns 3,000 Philippine pesos (PHP).  Rosalie is requesting a loan of 5,000 PHP at GDMPC to buy food supplies for a vending job. She was registered as a member in the cooperative earlier this year. Getting involved in this borrowing activity is a way that she can sustain her work and continue what she is doing today. She aims to own an ordinary food stand in the area and sell the best saleable items.

name: Nenita
description: As a married mother of four children, Nenita works hard to support her family.She has a fish vending business in the Philippines and also earns additional income from rice retailing. Nenita is borrowing PHP 16,000 through NWTF to buy more fresh fish to sell on her food stall.Nenita has been sustaining her business activities through her past 22 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money, so she can continue to send her children to school.

name: Yousef
description: Yousef is a 45-year-old married man from Deir Al Balah City, which is located in the Gaza Strip and suffers from power outages 12-16 hours a day regularly. He lives with his family in a small house. As an employee in the public sector, he earns a low income. This income barely covers all the family's needs. Because he is not able to save enough money, Yousef took a USD loan from FATEN.  With this loan, he will buy a solar system for heating water for the family house.  Palestinians use water boilers that use either gas or gasoline to heat the water before a shower, which can be dangerous, expensive and inefficient.  This will help him to provide hot water without using electricity, which is much more expensive.

name: Nymfa
description: Nymfa is from the village of Guam. She generates income through her sari-sari (convenience) store business. She is 23 years old and married, and she has two children. She has been running her sari-sari store for four years and earns about a minimum of PHP 250 a day.  At this time, Nymfa is asking for a loan of PHP 25,000. She will use the loan to buy grocery items to resell at her store, such as canned goods, noodles, assorted breads, biscuits and other kitchen ingredients. She believes that through her loan, she will be able to sell more grocery items. She hopes that she will increase her income, to meet the needs of her family.

name: Reiad
description: Reiad is a 56-year-old man. He is from Dair Al-Balah city, which is located in the Gaza Strip and regularly suffers from power outages 12-16 hours a day. He lives with his family in a small house. As an employee in the public sector, he earns a low income. This income barely covers all the family's needs. Because he is not able to save enough money, Reiad took a USD loan from Palestine for Credit & Development (FATEN).  With this loan, he will buy a solar system to heat water in the family house.  Before a shower, Palestinians use water boilers that use either gas or gasoline to heat the water, which can be dangerous, expensive, and inefficient.  This will help Reiad to provide hot water without using electricity, which is much more expensive.

name: Daphnie
description: At the age of 18, Daphnie is already married and has a one-year-old daughter. Her husband is a welder, while she sells barbecue in their place. She has been in this business for a year and works hard for the future.   Aside from selling barbecue, Daphnie is engaged in a hog-raising business. For this business, she needs funds to buy additional piglets and feed. This will improve her livelihood. In the future, she wants to expand both of her businesses to become sustainable.

name: Srey
description: Srey Y. resides in Battambong province, Cambodia, an area known for quality rice products. Y. sells dessert, earning an income of $2 per day. Her husband is a construction worker, earning an income of $3 per day. Each month, the family has to spend $80 on food and $20 on the other necessary expenses.   Y. is requesting a loan of $1,000 to purchase a motorbike for her husband to commute to work. This will be her first loan from CREDIT, a long-standing Kiva partner.

name: John
description: John M. is married and has three children. The highest level of schooling he has received is junior high school.   John sells electrical gadgets and parts in Elmina, which he has done since 2002. His wife operates a chop bar.
