John uses his income to pay for the children's school fees, rent, utility bills and other financial expenses for his family.  He is requesting a loan to purchase more electrical items to meet the increased demand from his costumers. The profits from the expanded business will allow John to continue building a house for his family, which he has not been able to complete due to inadequate funding.

name: Silvio
description: Silvio is from Encacarnacion city. He is a gardener. He says that, over the time spent working in this trade, he become well-known and has many customers who are always requesting his services.Silvio has been a gardener for ten years. With income from this work, he has been able to give his family a decent life. Silvio is applying for this loan in order to make improvements to his home. He needs to do this in order to give his family a decent home.

name: Flora
description: Flora, 63 years old, is a widow with five children. She currently lives in her own home with two grandchildren, who are 19 and 11 years old, respectively, and whom she has raised since they were very young. It is to help them get ahead that she works so hard every day selling all kinds of sweets, such as chocolates, cookies, candy, gum and various snacks. She works in the vicinity of a busy, well-attended recreation center and fortunately has always had good sales during her work schedule. She has run this business for over 13 years, sometimes with the help of her grandchildren.  What she enjoys about her business is that she is self-employed and can earn an income that enables her to support her grandchildren and to feel she is a useful member of society. However many times she has wanted to stop working due to fatigue stemming from her age. Nevertheless she always feels regenerated and continues to work with great optimism. She also hopes to keep working to insure her family’s wellbeing.  At this time she will request S/. 500 and is grateful for this opportunity and for the confidence shown in her. She promises to make her payments promptly. She will use the loan to purchase more sweets, such as candy, corn chips, cookies and gum, among other items

name: Helmi
description: Helmi is a 49-year-old married father of three children. He has been selling shoes in his own shop since 1998. Helmi has a very good reputation in his region as a hard worker and a trustworthy person.   Helmi is requesting a loan from Kiva partner Al Majmoua to pay for his child's university fees.   He has had four loan cycles with Al Majmoua and he invested his previous cycle in paying for his child's university fees.  Helmi is very impressed with the results he obtained with his loans especially that he is capable of achieving one of his biggest personal goals which is to provide the best education for his children.  He hopes to continue improving his business to provide his family with financial support.

name: Kelvy Enrrique
description: Señor Kelvy is 28 years old, and lives in the south of Honduras with his wife, who helps him with his business. He works as a barber, a job he has had for seven years in the community in which he lives.  Kelvy's business is located at a strategic point, where many people come and go, in the centre of the city where he lives. This means that he has a lot of customers. Kelvy has worked offering his services for a long time. He needs the loan to buy a hairdressers chair, a razor, oil, gel, scissors and various accessories. Kelvy hopes that the loan will enable his business to grow, so that he can satisfy the needs of every one of his customers, who visit him every day because of the high-quality service he offers.  Kelvy's plan for the future is to continue growing his own business and be one of the best in his city, while making greater profits in order to improve he and his family's quality of life.  Choluteca, Honduras  April 2013.

name: Julia
description: Julia is from the city of Luque. She is married to Mr. Pantaleon and has 3 children, all of whom are grown, and for whom she and her husband have fought and worked hard all of their lives. Julia has had a fast food restaurant since 2009 where she works and has created a good clientele.   She is a hardworking person who always wants to keep growing so that she can have more income and improve day-to-day life for herself and her family. She has requested a loan to invest in the purchase of ingredients for her restaurant like drinks, snacks, etc, so that she can offer a greater variety of products to her customers. She is thankful for this opportunity, as it wil be of great help to her.

name: Annah
description: Annah, aged 39 years, is married with six children aged 14, 12, 10, 8, and 6 years. She has applied for a loan of shs 4,000,000 (four million shillings) to buy more cattle for rearing, as well as cattle foodstuffs. She rears cattle as her major source of income. She started in the year 1998 with high hopes of earning income to look after her family. Her business is located in Kayembe, Mashonga, and her clients are people around Kayembe. She is a hardworking woman who works eight hours a day and six days a week, but is faced with challenges of too much sunshine and low prices for cattle products. But Annah hopes to boost her businesses through her hard work and achieve her future dream of establishing a processing plant that adds value to cattle products in Bushenyi. She requests lenders to keep on financing her businesses to boost her returns from the business of cattle rearing.She appreciates the great services.

name: Sofronio
description: Sofronio is 59 years old and a widower with four children.  He earns a living by farming sugarcane in the Philippines. Sofronio is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to buy fertilizers and other farm supplies.  Sofronio has been farming sugarcane for three years and also earns additional income from raising pigs.  He is working tirelessly toward the attainment of his dream: to save money to expand his business.

name: Topista
description: Topista is a single mother of five children all of school-going age. At 37 years of age, Topista is the head of her family and is responsible for the welfare and education of her children. She currently lives in a rented house in Bundibugyo, Uganda and she sells cocoa, beans, and rice as her business activity for income generation.   Topista has been in this business for six years having been a pure farmer before. She says she hopes to open up a retail shop in the future to increase her sources of income and to keep the needs of her family like education and construction of her own family home in sight. Topista intends to use the loan funds to purchase cocoa for resale.

name: Sarin Group
description: In this picture, Sarin appears with her group members. She is 55 years old and is married with four dependent children. One of her children is an accountant at a company, another is an engineer, the third is a veterinarian, and the other one attends school. Since 1979, Sarin has been a rice farmer who also raises livestock. Her husband is 57 years old and is as rice farmer as well. Sarin and her family live in a village in the Takeo province of Cambodia. Together, they earn approximately 16.33 USD daily.  Sarin is the leader of a five-person loan group. She will use her portion of the requested loan to buy piglets to fatten and feed for her pigs. Her loan will help her earn additional revenue to improve her living standards. In the future, Sarin wants to buy additional cows, save money to build a ground-floor room, and support her youngest daughter to earn a college degree.

name: Mily
description: Mily is a member of communal bank Mujeres Activas.  She lives in the San Martin region in the province and district of Bellavista.  She is 37 years old and lives with her husband and two children who are still dependent on her.   Mily dedicates herself to selling groceries.  Her business is located in her home at Jr. Augusto B. Leguia No 298.  She has been working with the communal bank for five years and the bank had helped her expand her business.    She will repay this loan of $975 in six months and will use the loan to purchase necessary products such as rice, sacks of sugar, milk, oil, canned food in different sizes, toilet paper and other products.  This will allow her to stock her business so that her clients can find what they are looking for.   Mily wants to express that Manuela Ramos is a great support for her and her family as well as to other women that want to get ahead.  Mily wants her business to grow and is thinking of expanding it by also selling clothing. Translated from Spanish by Cindy Manzo, Kiva Volunteer

name: Ahmad
description: Ahmad is a 36-year-old married man living in Tripoli with his wife and two kids. Ahmad works as a hairdresser. He owns a beauty salon where most of the ladies visit. Ahmad has an accepted quality of work and this is what helps him keep his clients and progress. Most of his clients are faithful and he knows how to please them. He's requesting a loan from Al Majmoua for the second time in order to buy new tools in addition to furniture for his house. His previous loan helped improve his social situation as he stated. Ahmad hopes to expand his business by adding new beauty services.

name: Wilson
description: Wilson is 46 years old, and is married with three children. He lives in Kasese, Uganda. He has been a policeman for twenty years.   With his little salary he has been able to support his family. He hopes that all his children will finish school. However, his main source of income is his salary, and delayed payment is a challenge. Wilson is requesting a loan to pay school fees for his children.

name: Aisha
description: Aisha is a 25 year-old single woman who owns a small food vending store which she started in 2007. She works everyday from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. and can earn a monthly profit of about $15 from her sales. Aisha now hopes for a loan of $100 to buy more food items for her business.

name: Youssouf
description: Mr. Youssouf  Koné  is a 32-year-old polygamous married man, and the father of three children. He lives within a nuclear family in Soromana, one of the villages in the sub-prefecture of Fakola, part of the Kolondieba prefecture in the third region (Sikasso) of the Republic of Mali.  To alleviate poverty, Mr. Youssouf Koné joined the Soro Yiriwaso credit loan program where he is beginning his second loan cycle. The first loan was reimbursed without any difficulties.  With this loan he intends to buy: 400 kilos of corn, 1000 kilos of millet and 2000 kilos of rice he will stockpile for resale at a period of high retail prices. He gets his supplies from neighbouring villages and hopes to attain average monthly earnings of 30,000 FCFA.  Profits will be used to cover schooling, healthcare, and food costs, and the remainder will be reinvested in the business.

name: Mariposas Group
description: The “Mariposas” (Butterflies) communal bank will start its second cycle within Pro Mujer as part of the Juan Pablo Focal Center.  It has 8 members led by a governing board; Ana is the secretary.  The communal bank members carry out a variety of businesses.  Among them we have a butcher shop, sweater sales, footwear sales, traditional skirt crafts, CD sales, vegetable sales and Herbalife product sales.  Ana indicates that she’s been part of a communal bank for a year and that she currently has a business selling clothes that she’s had for years having learned it from her mother.  The loan this cycle is to expand her stock of merchandise.  She will buy clothes in the city of Cochabamba’s street markets to then resell in her stand.  This way of working allows her to support her family since she’s single and has three children.  When asked what she likes about Pro Mujer, she answers that she likes the credit department.

name: Luis
description: Luis makes glass for windows. He is not married and he has no children. He lives with his parents and helps them with the expenses. Luis learned about his job from his uncle and he is very skilled. Luis needs a loan to buy more glass for his business. He has no debts, he works hard, and he is supported by his family. He hopes you can help him.

name: Abdulhafiz
description: Abdulhafiz is a 38-year-old married who has five children. He lives in Sana`a, Yemen.   He studied up to a bachelor's degree. He has worked very hard for many years to get his family ahead and give them everything they deserve.   He has a grocery store and it is his main source of income.   He started his business three years ago. His business was initially started with limited capital and didn't run well enough to get much profit.  His business is located in a very strategic area. Many people prefer his store because he always has the basic staples at accessible prices, and he provides the best possible customer service. His dream is to see his store flourish.   Due to the current bad situation in Yemen, he has less profit from his enterprise.   So, he took a loan of 80,000 Yemeni Rial (YER) from AMB to stock his business with more products such as eggs, cheese, soft drinks, and mineral water so that his customers will always find what they need and keep coming back.   In the future, Abdulhafiz would like to study for a master's degree in his specialization and hopes to be able to get his family ahead and give them better opportunities in life.

name: Olay
description: As a married parent of one child, Olay works hard to support her family.  She has a buy-and-sell fruits business in the Philippines and also earns additional income from raising cows.    Olay is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to purchase more stocks of fruits to sell for her buy-and-sell fruits business.  Olay has been sustaining her business activities through her past five loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: Adom Ahenwa Trust Group
description: Kenneth is a hard-working man and resourceful on behalf of his family. He is married to a petty trader who sells cereals and together they have four children who are from age 2-12. He is also a trader who purchases brand-new motorcycles from importers and sells them to customers. Motorcycles are one of the most common means of transport in the middle and northern parts of Ghana, hence selling motorcycles is a lucrative job for traders. He also purchases cows from the northern part of the country and sells them to butchers and restaurant operators.  Kenneth and his wife want to make sure they are financially able to support all their children through university education.  Kenneth is currently the leader of a trust bank group called “Adom Ahenwa”, (translated as 'The Seat of Grace'), made up of nine members. The other members are engaged in trades such as manufacturing, baking, grocery sales, used clothing sales etc. They are the major bread winners of their respective families and are requesting a loan to support their businesses. Their common dream is to be financially self sustaining and to be able to support their children through quality education.

name: Rose
description: Rose N. lives in the Kamwokya neighborhood in the city of Kampala, Uganda. She is married and has eight children, four of whom are in school. Rose lives in a home that she owns. She has access to electricity and piped water.  Her major monthly expenses include school fees, food and utilities.     Rose runs a retail shop. She has been in this business for over 10 years, and she works six days out of every week. Rose sells her products from home, by means of retail.   Rose has requested a loan of 1,000,000 UGX from MCDT SACCO, which she will use to buy more bags of sugar, cartons of salt, boxes of soap and cooking oil.   The main business challenges for Rose include transportation and the ever increasing prices of commodities, which affects customers' rate of buying.  Her goals for her business are to own a delivery van and also to own a wholesale shop .

name: Angel
description: Angel is a carpenter, he builds wooden furniture and sells them in the markets of la Paz. He has three sons that depend on him; he works independently so his main source of income is his job. He lives in Villa Dolores, located in El Alto city, and his workshop is in Santa Rita which is an area of La Paz. He creates job opportunities by employing an assistant at the workshop and temporary workers, depending on the magnitude of the projects. The loan would be used to buy raw material (wood). This is the 13th time Angel has applied for a loan with Impro and his good credit makes him eligible for another loan.  Translated from Spanish by Isabel Tan, a Kiva volunteer.   Angel, es carpintero elabora muebles de madera para comercializarlo en las ferias de La Paz, tiene tres hijos que dependen de él, y trabaja en forma independiente por lo que su actividad es su principal fuente de ingresos con que mantiene a su familia. Vive  en la Zona de villa Dolores de la Ciudad de El Alto y su  taller está ubicado en la Zona Santa Rita de la Ciudad de La Paz.  Genera fuentes de empleo ya que trabaja con un ayudante permanente en el talle, y suele contratar personal eventual de acuerdo a la magnitud del trabajo que efectúe. E crédito será destinado para la compra de  materia prima (madera).   Es el decimotercer crédito con Impro, los buenos antecedentes que tiene le faculta a acceder a otro préstamo.

name: Juan Antonio
description: Juan wants to take out a loan for a small solar power system so he can have solar light energy in his home. Currently he and his wife use candles for light, which they don't like because it produces a lot of smoke. At the age of 14 Juan went to live with his parents in a town in Tuma. For financial reasons he only reached second grade of primary school. Since then he has held jobs in the fields such as milking cattle and sowing beans.

name: Ayda
description: Ayda was born in 1978. She is married and has one son. Ayda has been selling home products at a store in her house since seven years ago. She started her project by selling a small number of home products. She found it profitable, so she decided to expand it. Now she needs to buy a larger number of home products as it will raise her income, which will help her in covering her son’s needs, but she doesn't have enough money for them. For this reason, she applied for this loan.

name: Junila
description: Junila B. is from the village of Kiwalan, Iligan City. She is 34 years old, is married, and has four school-aged children.  Junila owns and operates a business raising pigs for sale. She has been engaged in her business for over six years and earns approximately 6,000 PHP a month.  In 2009, Junila joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 8,000 PHP from HSPFI.  Junila decided to request a new loan of 8,000 PHP which will be used to purchase piglets to raise and sell. This loan will be her 3rd from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to support her children’s education.    About HSPFI: HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.    *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.
town: Kiwalan, Iligan City, Lanao del Norte

name: Fatuma
description: Fatuma is from Tiribe, Kenya. She is married and they have four young children who are in school. They both strive to get ahead and provide their children with everything they did not have.  Fatuma has a food pantry in her house. Thanks to the good variety she offers, she has been able to establish a good clientele. She is a hardworking individual and says that she wants to continue growing in her current profession. For this reason, she strives to do her best.  Fatuma is requesting this loan so that she can invest in the purchase of beverages, milk, bread, noodles, rice, vegetables, and other products so that she can continue offering her customers the variety that they are accustomed to having.

name: Frediswenda
description: Frediswenda is a married woman with six children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur. Frediswenda is 55 years old and has one child who is still in school.Frediswenda has a tailoring business in the Philippines. Frediswenda requested a PHP 20,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional materials like fabric, threads, needles, etc., for her business.Frediswenda has been in this business for 20 years. Frediswenda would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Filisita
description: Filisita is a 35-year-old, single woman with no children. To earn a living, she runs a small canteen in her community. She has two years of experience with this business.   Filisita needs a loan to buy sandwiches, pies, donuts, twisties, plastic plates, foam cups, plastic bags, and soft drinks.   She plans to use her profits to pay for her family's weekly expenses. Filisita has been a member of South Pacific Business Development (SPBD) since 2014.

name: Chemutai
description: Chemutai is 38 years old, windowed, and a mother of six children between the ages of 5 and 15 years old. She is  a mixed farmer and she has been in this business for the last six years. Her monthly income is about KES 38,000   Chemutai is currently servicing her fourth loan from KADET LTD of KES 90,000, which will help her to prepare the land and get seedlings. She plans to use the anticipated profits to diversify into livestock farming. Chemutai's dream is to improve the living standards of her family.

name: Rosalie
description: Rosalie works hard to support her family. Rosalie is married and has a business buying and selling mangoes in the Philippines.  Rosalie requested a PHP 20,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional baskets of mangoes to sell.  Rosalie has been in this business for 8 years now.  In the future, Rosalie would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Simon
description: Simon lives in the Ndaragwa area of Kenya, which has one of the cooler climates in Kenya.  He has 2 children and has been doing farming for 5 years.  His primary income sources are milk and eggs.  He enjoys selling farm produce, which is his biggest challenge.  Animals on the farm have been given the names of 'Kadogo, muiru cows’.  Simon was asked why he chose Juhudi Kilimo for this loan, to which he replied, “For their loans are processed quickly”.  This client was also asked what was learned during Juhudi's required microfinance training session.  He replied, “They enable small holder farmers to get loans easily”. Simon’s highest monthly expense is the farming costs.  When asked how the loan would benefit his family, Simon said it would improve their farming.  As part of Juhudi's loan appraisal process, each borrower's assets are evaluated.  Simon owns a cow, poultry, and a bicycle.  He does not own a pig, pump, motorcycle, or automobile.  Juhudi Kilimo also tries to measure any change in living standards based on this loan.  This borrower does not have a mosquito net, electricity, solar power, running water, sewing machine, TV, or DVD.

name: Mary
description: Mary lives in Kamukuywa, a small town in Kitale County. Kitale is located in the Trans-Nzoia district of western Kenya, and at over 6,300 feet above sea level, is one of Africa’s most elevated towns. The rich soil of the area makes it one of the nation's biggest maize producing regions, lending it the nickname of “the breadbasket of Kenya.” Many farmers in the region have started projects planting bluegum trees on their land, which complement the region’s natural forests and provide bees with a variety of food sources. The people around Kitale have been beekeeping for centuries, and the area is dense with strong bee colonies.  Mary is married and has four children. She is a business lady and she also undertakes farming with her husband. They have been farming for 15 years now and they are currently growing maize, millet, potatoes, sweepstakes and sugarcane. Mary is excited about beekeeping as the bees will aid in pollinating their crops.  This is Mary's first loan with Honey Care and she plans to use the proceeds from her beehives to boost her business. Mary's hope for the future is to to build a house and to take her children through school up to college.

name: Sophat
description: Mr. Sophat Y., 37, and his wife, Mrs. Phalla Kong, 36, live along National Road number one about 17 kilometers from Phnom Penh, the capital city of Cambodia. They have been married since 2000 and have three children, two sons and one daughter. Two of them attend school, and the other one is still very young.   Sophat and his wife have been selling kachay cake in their village for 26 years. It is a kind of fried cake of Chinese origin. He is applying for his first loan of $1,200 to build a new house with concrete for its foundation.

name: Tuyatsetseg
description: Lately her apartment has become very uncomfortable and cold to live in because all the window insulation has been removed and there is too much heat lost during the winter time. Therefore she needs to make adjustment and insulation to the windows of her home immediately. The loan she is taking will be dedicated to purchase the building materials to make the renovations to her home.

name: Alma
description: Alma, a 33-year-old mom of five, has been operating her transportation services business with her husband  to make a living. For over 10 years in running the business, she was able to maintain and sustain it. She always finds many ways just to augment their living.   Though she earns a better income from this, she still has financial needs for their house repair. For this, she took a new loan to cover the costs for house renovation. A portion of this loan amount will also be used to buy new set of tires to replace the old and used tires. She has to maintain safety of the services in order to have more loyal costumers that make business with them.  She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the services as a reserve for future emergencies.

name: Shamim
description: Shamim is an independent lady. She is from Madina Colony Gujranwala, located in Pakistan. She is living with her husband and five children. She owns an embroidery business located inside her house. She does not have enough money to continue her business due to lack of finances. She wants to purchase a variety of threads, pearls, sequins, and other raw materials for her work. Therefore she has requested a loan of 30,000 PKR from Kiva’s field partner Jinnah Welfare Society. Shamim is planning to renovate a portion of her house with the profits. She hopes that the loan amount will be helpful for her business.  She is thankful to Kiva and JWS.

name: Palave En Accion Group
description: Nancy is a 36-year old woman who lives with her husband and three children in the community of Palave, a small and impoverished area on the outskirts of the capital of Santo Domingo.  Nancy has a small business selling shoes and clothes to her community. She is requesting a loan so she can have enough capital to buy more merchandise in bulk, and  be able to better meet the needs of her clients.  Without the loan, she is limited in her ability to buy enough merchandise to earn marginal amounts of money that don’t allow her the room to invest in her business, much less accrue savings for her family.  She hopes this loan will help her move her life forward, so that by the end of the year she will be able to have a much bigger business, help proviD. better education and school supplies to her three children, and maybe even save enough money so that she and her husband will be able to buy their own home.  On behalf of everyone here at Esperanza International, and from Nancy herself, we thank you for your support with this micro loan!

name: Emilyn
description: Emilyn, age 32, is married to a tricycle driver and blessed with two children. She has owned and managed a retail store in her village for almost three years. With this business, she's earning a net income of PHP 500 daily. Her daily profits are usually spent on the school fees and allowances of her children. Due insufficient funds to use in her store, she would like a loan of PHP 30,000 to purchase beverages, canned goods, noodles, chips, and breads to sell. She's hoping that her requested loan will be granted so that she can improve her business.

name: Ruth
description: Ruth is twenty years old and lives in the town of Kamwenge in the Fort Portal region of Uganda. She is married and has three children with one of them currently in school. For the past two years Ruth has been working hard to manage her small hotel where she also offers meals.   To help expand her business, Ruth has requested a loan of 300,000 UGX from BRAC Uganda. She will use her loan to buy more fresh food for her dishes. Greater profits will mean that Ruth can buy more plates and cups and stock up on more food for the hotel. Ruth hopes that in the future she will be able to buy goats to start a livestock concern.   Ruth is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities and a forum for life-skills training. The ELA program has increased Ruth's future prospects by helping her to learn how to save money.

name: Maria
description: Maria P., 51, is married with 4 children.  She has 4 years of experience in the handicrafts business. She sells to the general public and tourists, 3 days per week. She has 4 previous loans with SPBD.  She expects her weekly net cash flow to be 600 Tala (~250 USD).  SPBD loans are Maria’s only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with the traditional banks. This loan will be used for the business and also paying children's school fees.

name: Nenita
description: Nenita is 52 years old and she is married to Melecio. Nenita and her husband manage a vegetable farm and vending business in their rural village of Banquero, Reina Mercedes, Isabela. Sending her children to school is very costly, but they are doing their best to provide for the needs of their children and to achieve their ambitions in life.    To fulfill her dream, she is now asking to borrow PHP 5,000 for their vegetable production and sales business. Nenita is hoping that lenders will give her the chance to improve their enterprise for the sake of their family.

name: Delia Filomena
description: Señora Delia Filomena is a hard-working, enterprising woman.  She is 52 years old and has a small grocery store.  She started this business 20 years ago as a project that she set up all on her own.  She paid slowly over a 3 year period.  She is married and has 3 children who are now adults.  She will use the loan to buy staple foods (sugar, oil, rice, beans....etc.).

name: Akua
description: Akua N. is 35 years old, a wife and a mother with five children, who are in school. She has been a food vendor for a year now. She prepares and sells kenkey (a local dish prepared from milled maize and eaten with all kinds of sauces and soups). It is a delicacy many Ghanaians enjoy daily either as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. She sells at the main business center of Agogo. Her business is doing well, and she wants to expand her operation to serve more customers.  With the loan, she wants to purchase more maize grains, vegetables, rice and assorted meat for her operation. She hopes this loan will help her increase her earnings and improve her family's well-being. She would be very grateful for this assistance. Her photo was taking when we visited her. With the loan she wants to add the sale of soft drinks to her operation so that her profit margin can be increased.

name: Nanette
description: Nanette makes a living by operating a general store in her village.  She has earned a good living for the past three years in the business, and is able to provide well for her family's needs.  Nanette took a loan from GDMPC micro finance to buy additional grocery goods to sell.  She always find ways to augment her business and improve her quality of living. She wants to ensure a better income for her family in the future.

name: Taiwo
description: Taiwo is 35 years old and married with four children. She has a retail business selling yam tubers, and has been in this business for a long time. She is requesting a loan amount of 50 000 NGN to purchase more yam tubers to sell. She sends her thanks to all Kiva lenders.

name: Víctor Alfonso
description: Víctor began in sales through a friend who was enrolled with Herbalife, and has been selling since 2012. However, in April of this year he decided to signup for himself and to be in charge of his own sales orders in the mornings and to attend training sessions in the afternoons about the benefits obtained by consuming Herbalife nutrition products.   He is asking for a loan to buy products at wholesale (malts, shakes, dietary supplements, and other items).   Víctor’s dream is to have several nutrition clubs in the city and instruct people in eating habits.

name: Evelia
description: Evelia, 59 years old, is married. She has a retail shop where she sells a variety of goods. Aside from this she is also engaged in raising hogs. Evelia has had this retail shop for ten years and her hog business for five years. Each month she earns about 4,000 PHP in her retail shop and 2,500 PHP in her hog raising business.  Evelia is requesting a loan of 20,000 PHP to purchase bread, soft drinks, sugar, snacks, canned goods, milk, shampoo, soap and coffee for her shop. In the future she hopes to grow her businesses so that she can increase her profits and provide for the needs of her family.

name: Celia
description: Celia is a 33-year-old, married lady with three children, who resides in Buhera District, Zimbabwe. Celia is a Camfed Learner Guide, teaching life skills and leadership education in local schools to improve the well being of students. She also volunteers as a health trainer in her community.  Celia rents a table at the local flea market where she sells products such as sandals, shoes, jeans, shirts, skirts, tracksuits, T-shirts, and bags.  She has been running this business for one year now, and it has enabled her to support her family.    With the Kiva loan, Celia will purchase more bags, shoes, jeans, shirts, skirts, tracksuits, and T-shirts to increase her clothing supplies. Her dream is to grow the business and build several boutiques in her community. This will bring sustainable employment for her and for her community people. She aspires to grow in her business and also to help her immediate family members. She started her business to sustain her life, and to provide good education for her three children.

name: Mary Group
description: This is Mary Group. It has seven members who are engaged in selling such goods as maize, fish, sugar, plastic products, rice and flour. All are from Teshie, a coastal township outside Accra.  Mary, 58, is the group’s leader. She lives with her four children, who help Mary in her business selling maize. She has worked from home seven days a week for the past ten years. She buys her maize in the Brong Ahafo region in central Ghana and other supplies in Accra. She sells the maize to thirty customers in Teshie alone and ten customers from nearby towns.  Mary last took a 1,200 GHS loan with ID Ghana and invested it in her maize business. She repaid it without difficulty. This will be Mary’s fifth loan with ID Ghana. As leader of the group she is applying for a 5,250 GHS loan that will be apportioned among her group’s members.   Mary will use her 1,700 GHS portion of the loan to buy twenty bags of maize and other supplies. She is well placed to use this loan judiciously.   One of Mary’s goals is to own a maize depot so she can supply more customers. By doing so she will increase her income and so improve her quality of life.

name: Mohamed
description: Mohamed has been in his barber shop for about two years. He is 28 and married, without any children. He works very hard to provide for her wife whom he loves very much. They rent the house they live in but they hope to own their house soon.  While Mohamed is busy in his barber shop, his wife works in their vegetable stall. This way they have not lacked any basic needs. Due to the increasing number of customers, he has seen the need to increase the number of electric razors so that customers do not have to wait for long. Mohamed is taking out this loan in order to purchase electric razors. At his barber shop, he is assisted by a friend and plans to employ his cousin once he has bought the new razors.

name: Kort
description: A local farmer living in Siem Reap Province, Kort is 37 years old, and a mother of four children. She overcomes her family’s hardships via rice cropping. Moreover, she also earns more income via cassava growing. This is her first loan with VisionFund, (Kiva’s partner). She will spend her entire loan portion to buy wood to build a new house. She hopes that she can have a house to improve her living conditions.
town: Siem Reap Province, Srey Snom district

name: Samah
description: Samah is 34 years old. She has been married for many years and is a mother of three children. To avoid spare time, Samah ‎insisted on starting a small home business selling clothes. Her business helps in filling her time and helps her ‎husband who is working in the army with low income. Having her business improves their living conditions by adding another ‎source of income to the family, and enables her to provide a good education for her children. Samah is now applying for a loan to ‎increase the quantity of clothes she is selling to prepare for the upcoming spring season.

name: Melrose
description: As a married parent of eight children, Melrose works hard to support her family.  She has a furniture making business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from a general store. Melrose is borrowing PHP 14000 through NWTF to buy materials like woods, nails, and varnish and to pay for maintenance on her equipment.  Melrose has been sustaining her business activities through her past  loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Elijah
description: Elijah is a married man with three children, all of whom attend school. He lives in a rental house that has electricity but not piped water. His greatest monthly expenses are food and rent bills.  He has operated a "nyama choma" (roasted meat) business for the last six months. He sells at the market to his neighbours and passersby. Elijah faces a major challenge of high cost of transportation in his business. He hopes to own a butcher shop in the future.  With the Kshs 20,000 he wants to purchase kitchen utensils (cooking pots, plates, spoons). He decided to join Yehu to access loans to expand his business.

name: Felicidad
description: Felicidad L. is from the city of Dapitan. She is 57 years old, is married, and has eight school-aged children.  Felicidad owns and operates a business raising crops, primarily planting and harvesting fruits and vegetables for sale. She has been engaged in her business for over fifteen years and earns approximately 4,500 PHP a month.  In 2006, Felicidad joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 10,000 PHP from PMPC.  Felicidad is requesting a new loan of 7,000 PHP which will be used to purchase piglets to raise for additional income. This loan will be her 7th from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.    About PMPC: Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.    *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Nilda
description: This member is part of the Manos Juntas de Rumichaca Alta Communal Bank, which is located in the Urubamba district of the province by the same name, department of Cusco.  She is Ms. Nilda, a 44-year-old married mother of 4. She alternates her daily chores with her vegetable business. She sells vegetables like carrots, tomatoes, and cucumbers, among other produce. She takes her vegetables throughout the district of Calca. She also sells chicha, a maize beverage, from her home in the district of Urubamba. The member is requesting a loan in order to purchase vegetables wholesale and to purchase maize to prepare the chicha drink.  Ms. Nilda is happy about the loan, and she commits to repaying it back on time.

name: Yaneth
description: Yaneth is a member of the community bank Yachay Wasi, which means House of Knowledge in Quechua.  Yaneth lives in a common-law relationship, is 23 years old, and has 2 children.  Yaneth and her husband sell lumber.  They acquire their products in the Ayacuchana jungle, where they travel weekly.  They sell their wood to lumber yards on credit and account.  Yaneth needs a loan of 1000 soles ($325 USD) with which she will buy tornillo lumber.  (Tornillo, also known as white mahogany, is a hardwood tree, 100 to 160 feet tall with a trunk over 4 feet in diameter).  Yaneth dreams of owning her own home, a truck to transport her product, and that her children will grow up to be professionals.Translated from Spanish by Laure Kwon, Kiva Volunteer

name: Cruz Antonia
description: The communal bank "Nuevas Amigas" meets every 15 days in Jipijapa canton (Ecuadorian state). This canton is known by the name "the sultan of coffee" because of its extensive plantings of coffee, which have an incomparable flavor.   Mrs. Cruz lives here. She is 51 years old and is the single mother of a 19-year-old son who studies at university and still lives at home. Mrs. Cruz is a woman who likes to work to get ahead alongside her son. She has a grocery store in her house. She sells products like rice, sugar, oils, detergents, water, sodas, and ice cream among other necessities there. She works every day, and on occasion her son helps her with the business, although she is the one who likes being attentive to the needs of her customers. She has spent more than ten years in this business which lets her earn an honest living.   This loan will be used to supply more in her store. She will buy rice, sugar, sodas, water, ice cream, and other supplies. She has been with the communal bank from the beginning, and she likes it because the loans are a blessing for her. Her dream is that her son becomes a great professional.

name: Daniel
description: Daniel D. is single with no children.  He has received a junior high school education.  Since 2004, he has worked as an auto mechanic selling bulbs, starters, and other spare car parts at Siwdo in Cape Coast.  Daniel uses his income to pay for utility bills and food.  He will use the loan to increase his capital to buy more bulbs, starters, and other spare car parts for resale.  With the new profits from his expanded business, Daniel plans to reinvest.

name: Esther
description: Esther O. is 35 years old. She is married and the mother of five. Currently all her children are in are in school. She loves selling goods, the business through which she obtains her livelihood.  She has been selling foodstuffs like plantains, maize, kobe (salt fish), fresh tomatoes, and many more at Takroase for three years now to support her family. Her husband is a cocoa farmer.  She treks to farming communities in and around her village to buy her stock of plantains, yams, salt fish (kobe), maize etc. in bulk from the farmers. This saves her from middlemen who buy from the farmers and resell to her at higher prices. With this loan, she wants to buy plantains, yams, tomatoes, kobe, etc. to serve her customers. She hopes to use part of her profit to support her kids in school. This would enable her save more to support her husband in taking care of the home. Esther belongs to a village bank called ‘Wonderful Jesus.’

name: Grace Group
description: Kumbuka is 36 years old and head of the Grace loan group. She is married to a money-changer and they have seven children, who are all in school.  Kumbuka has worked as a travelling trader since 1998 and is requesting this new loan in order to buy 100 schoolbags. Her ambition is to buy a plot of land.  Kumbuka would like to thank Hekima for the support it offers to women on a low income.

name: Virgen Purificada De Tupac Amaru Group
description: The members belong to the Virgen Purificada de Tupac Amaru ["Purified Virgin of Tupac Amaru"] communal bank. This bank is located in the Urcos district, Quispicanchis province, Cusco department.  Mrs. Bernarda is married, is 58 years old and has 4 children. She works in her business, a grocery store. She sells staples such as rice, sugar, milk and cookies. She works from 8am until 7pm. She has been in this business for five years and it is going very well.  Her dream is to expand her grocery store business. She requests the loan in order to buy rice, sugar, milk and cookies.  The other members make a living selling handicrafts, selling clothes, in the grocery store business, and selling animals.  Mrs. Bernarda is grateful to those who form part of this dream through these means and she pledges to make her payments according to the established time-frame.

name: Helen
description: Helen, 49, lives a simple life with her family in the city of Baybay, Leyte. She is married and blessed with two teenage girl, ages 17 and 16 years old.She is engaged in a direct-selling business where she sells RTW (ready-to-wear) products while her husband does welding. Aside from selling RTW’s, Helen also does food vending.Thus, she is asking for a loan to buy shirts, shoes, sandals, underwear, cosmetics, fragrances, beauty products and other products. The other part of her loan is to buy food to sell. In this way, Helen could possibly run her business continuously and become more productive.Helen aims to save money so she could better start a store business in the future.

name: Faith
description: A. Faith sells building materials including gravel, sand, rods, and cement. She learned the business for 2 years and has been selling business supplies for the past 5 years. She is 45 years old and married with 4 children. She lives near Iyano- Issashi, Lagos State, Nigeria.  Faith has been borrowing from LAPO Microfinance for the past 4 years. She needs a loan of $850 to buy more building materials so that she can meet the demands of her customers. She expresses her thanks to all who make this loan possible.

name: Roselyn
description: Roselyn B. is from the city of Malaubang, Ozamiz City. She is 30 years old, is married, and has two infant children.  Roselyn owns and operates a general store, selling a variety of different products in the local community. She has been engaged in her business for over two years and earns approximately 8,000 PHP a month.  In 2009, Roselyn joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. She is requesting a loan of 10,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be her first from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.    About GDMPC: GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three unit offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.    *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Consolacion
description: As a married mother of six children, Consolacion works hard to support her family.  She has a fish vending business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from tricycle transportation. Consolacion is borrowing PHP 19,000 through NWTF in order to buy more fish to sell for her fish vending business.  Consolacion has been sustaining her business activities through her past 17 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Selestino
description: Selestino is a 60-year-old widower with four children living in Kasese, Uganda. He has been in the retail shop business for four years, and works seven days a week; it is located in the rural area.  He also does farming as an additional income source.    Inadequate capital poses a threat to his business, while his desire is to own a wholesale shop.  Selestino will use the loan to buy sugar, soda, and soap to sell.

name: Wasuk
description: Wasuk lives in Kator. She sells food stall, and has been in business for three years. She is twenty-seven years old, married, and has four children; all of them are still in school.   Wasuk heard about BRAC South Sudan from a credit officer and this is her first loan from BRAC. She has requested a loan of 500 Sudanese pounds in order to purchase beans and rice. She will use her extra income from this loan to pay the school fees of her children.

name: Mary
description: Ten years ago, Mary started farming on a small inherited piece of land in Bonyunyu, a remote village in the Nyamira area of Kenya. Today, this humble mother sells milk, eggs, tea, and a variety of food crops. She is a passionate farmer and, because of the immense knowledge she has on farming, she commands a lot of respect from other farmers in her village. Dairy farming is close to her heart and every day she wakes up to milk her cow and that makes her very proud.   Although she makes profits through milk selling, she lacks a proper dairy unit and she is seeking a loan to build a modern dairy unit. Through the loan she will have an easier time milking her cow and also feeding. A good dairy unit provides a good place where cows can relax and also keeps them from diseases that may arise because of being exposed to harsh weather conditions such as rain.   Mary believes that through this loan her living conditions will change because she is going to have an increase in milk production. She will save money that she used to spend on treating her cows because she lacked a good dairy unit. Mary waits for your kindness.

name: Miguel
description: Miguel is a 44 year-old father who lives with his wife and two dependent children in Capote sector of Picsi district, 20 minutes from the city of Chiclayo.  The need to get ahead in spite of his family's financial limitations, led Miguel to start work as a builder 20 years ago.  For the last 20 years, this has been Miguel's main source of support and it has helped him to get his family ahead in life.  He has gradually become known in the trade and now his work is valued for the responsibility and efficiency with which it is carried out.  Owing to the high demand in his area, he also set up a business making unbaked bricks and regular bricks.  This is helping him to make additional income.  Currently he would like to buy material to expand his business and thereby improve his sales.  For this reason, he is requesting a loan for 1,500 Peruvian soles from Edpyme Alternativa.  Miguel has already had a Kiva loan through Edpyme Alternativa and our seed money product.  He used that money to acquire tools to improve his work as a builder.  He is very grateful to the people who supported him.

name: Las Guerreras Group
description: Lorenzo is a member of the group called Las Guerreras (The Warriors). They decided on this name for the group because the majority of their members are women and all of them fight like warriors to get their families ahead through their business and economic activities. This group is located in Tres Valles where the main activities are trade and growing sugar cane and pineapple.   Lorenzo is 47 years old, he only finished secondary school and he is single. He says that for more than 10 years he has worked selling dough and he does this with the help of his motorcycle. Everyday, Lorenzo gets up very early to start grinding his boiled corn. Afterwards he packs it into kilo and kilo and a half bags to later, with the help of his motorcycle, go out onto the streets to deliver his orders and sell the rest of his dough.   He is very well-known in his community and when he passes by, the women come out to buy. What he likes most about his business is that he has made good friends and he earns his own money.   A loan from VisionFund will help him to buy a tonne of corn to continue his business. He is very happy with his business because it has given him a job and the opportunity to have a better quality of life.   In the future he hopes his business grows and he earns more profits. "Thank you for the loan, which gives me the opportunity to work investing in the business - from it we are taking money for our pay and to eat".  The other members of this group are: Juana - selling soft drinks Sotera Maribel - repairing footwear Daria - selling cheese Hortencia - pharmacy Margarita - selling Guaraches (a type of rough leather sandal) y hauling services Yulma - selling cosmetics María Esther - selling soft drinks and hielitos María Concepción - selling groceries María Josefa - selling tacos

name: Eusebia
description: Eusebia is 60 years old and married with ten children. With one child still in school, Eusebia works very hard to provide for them.  Eusebia runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10000 loan through NWTF to buy more items to sell in her general store.  Eusebia has been in this business for 15 years and sells a variety of items such as canned goods, biscuits, bread, coffee, sugar, detergent soap, etc.   Eusebia would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Suy
description: Mrs. Suy R., age 48, is a widow and a housewife. She has four children, two of whom work in construction and together earn about $10 per day. One child works as a waiter, earning about $60 per month, and one child is married and no longer lives at home. Suy would like to borrow $800 to purchase a motorbike for her children to use as their transportation to work and to dig a well to serve as her family’s water source. They currently do not have running water.

name: Reyna Francisca
description: More than eight years ago, Reyna began to prepare and sell food. Her husband is her primary support. Little by little, she has managed to get ahead with the income she has obtained from her sales. She has been able to build her own stand where she offers her food.  Reyna would like to continue growing her sales and meeting her customer's demands. It is for that reason that she has requested a loan to buy vegetables and meat to make the different dishes that she offers to her customers.

name: 15 De Mayo Group
description: This group is called "15 de Mayo" and is comprised of 23 hard-working members.  Only 21 of them will participate in this loan which marks their fourth loan cycle in the women's program.  All the members work and help each other to get ahead.  They participate in the poverty elimination program and take the survey to help improve their economy.  One of the members is Mirta who sells empanada (meat pie), soup and all types of food.  She is also a seamstress and works hard, especially now that she is a widow and must support the family with her sole income.  Her dream is to have her own business location and give work to more pèople.  She is requesting a loan to buy food supplies such as meat, vegetables, seasonings, etc. so she can have a firm business plan and improve her income.

name: Rabih
description: Rabih is a 32-year-old Lebanese entrepreneur who lives with his wife and their five children. In 2005, he decided to open a restaurant where he sells chicken cooked in various ways, including in sandwiches and roasted. His restaurant is well-known for its good food and great location in the middle of the town.   Today, for the first time, Rabih is requesting a loan to buy a refrigerator and to wire the electricity in his restaurant. His plans for the future include continuing to improve his business and the service he provides to his customers.

name: Luvuno
description: Luvuno is a very hard-working woman who wishes to get ahead through her own efforts and wants her working life to be much more successful. She lives at the Coastal region of Kenya.  Luvuno has a business offering M-pesa services (mobile money transfer), a business which she has run for three years.   She needs to offer her customers better services. For that reason, she requests a loan through Yehu, to invest in the addition of floats (electronic credits to sell) in her M-pesa business.

name: Mustapher
description: Mustapher is a married man. He has 2 children. He describes himself as being honest. Mustapher operates a retail business where he sells sugar, flour, cooking fat and other items. He has been involved in this business for 3 years. His business is located in a busy area and his primary customers are locals. He describes his biggest business challenge as being inadequate working capital.   Mustapher will use the 40,000 KES loan to buy more stock of sugar, flour, cooking fat, salt and other items. His business goal is to have a wholesale business within 5 years. He hopes that in the future he will have improved living standards.   This is Mustapher's second loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. The previous loan was repaid successfully. Mustapher will use the anticipated profits to reinvest in the business.

name: Aprocap Group
description: Aprocap is part of a special project exclusive to growers and is maD. up of members of the Vacahuasi community in the Ocros district, Huamanga province. The community is located next to the Pampas River, which forms the boundary between this and the Apurimac district.  The community focuses its efforts mainly on cultivating fruits such as oranges, papayas, avocados and mangoes.  Mariano is a member of the Communal Bank and lives with his partner and three children, aged 3, 6 and 8. He has worked for 9 years growing avocado trees, having been trained in their care. He currently has 80 to 90 trees and will use his loan to buy fertilizer and insecticides. Mariano dreams of his children becoming professionals.  Fortunato lives with his partner and has three children, aged 9, 14 and 18. He has 60 avocado trees and intends to plant more, to which end he intends to buy fertilizer with his loan. Fortunato dreams of increasing his production capacity and of his children becoming professionals.  The growers of the Vacahuasi community need a 12-month loan, due to the year-long harvest, which will be invested in cultivating produce. It will be repaid following this year period. Translated from Spanish by Eleanor Stilgoe, Kiva Volunteer

name: Rema
description: Rema is a 58-year-old, married woman from Bethlehem city. She is a mother of three sons and one daughter.   Rema has a small workshop where she makes crafts from olive wood. She makes religious gifts and she sells them in her stall or exports them outside of Palestine.  Rema took a USD loan from Palestine for Credit & Development (FATEN). This loan will help her to buy raw wood for her workshop. This will help her to prepare a new collection for Easter. This will increase her productivity and also her income.  Rema appears in the photo while she was working.

name: Mamiarisoa
description: Mamiarisoa is the young father of a little boy.  He lives in Antsirabe in a popular and very lively neighborhood.  He is dynamic and resourceful.  In order to feed his family, he works various jobs depending on the time of year.  His wife helps him by earning her own income; she runs a small restaurant in front of their house.  Mamiarisoa has been a client of Vahatra for four years.  Thanks to his previous loans, he was able to sell cosmetic products and with his profits, he bought a fridge.  At the moment, he wants to take another loan to make and sell yogurts.  He will use his loan to buy some pots of yogurt, 30 liters of milk, some food flavoring, and a freezer.  His goal is to build a house.

name: Nchi
description: Nchi is a divorced woman. She has four children: three adults and one school going child. She owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is food.  Nchi has operated a vegetable stall business for the past three years, selling from home to her neighbors and passersby. She faces a challenge of stiff competition from other vegetable operators in her business.   With the 20,000 KES loan, she wants to purchase sacks of tomatoes, potatoes, fruits and green vegetables for resale.

name: Esperanza
description: Esperanza R. is from the village of Guinsiliban, Camiguin Province. She is 49 years old. Esperanza is married and has three school-age children. To make a living, Esperanza owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) retail shop, where she sells both food and daily use products in the local community. Esperanza has been in business for over five years and earns approximately 2,500 PHP.  In 2009, Esperanza joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Esperanza is requesting a loan of 5,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Esperanza from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand the business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Amor Group
description: The members of Amor group are from Pilas Occidentales, a rural area of Masaya, which is very prone to farming and handicrafts.  Ixida Raquel, Virginia Elene, and Nubia make hammocks which are one of Masaya's outstanding handicrafts.  It is a product that is in high demand and it is made from manila (netted cord), wood, aluminum objects or with vegetable-based fibers like cabuya and pita (agave-based cord).  Ixida, 24, learned this craft from her parents who were hammock makers and she, together with her siblings and nieces and nephews, has continued this family tradition.  Virginia, 66, has made hammocks since she was a young girl and for the last 30 years has had her own workshop where her children and grandchildren help her and she happily transmits this beautiful art form to them.  Nubia, 27, has worked on her own making hammocks for the past 8 years.  They have been working with Adim for the past 4 years which has been a help and they are comfortable with the way it operates.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Ruperto Amadeo
description: Ruperto is 55 years old and in a civil partnership. He lives in his own home made of rustic material with his partner. This is in the district of Santo Tomás, in the province of Cutervo, in the department of Cajamarca in Peru. He has very good personal and professional references from the inhabitants of the area. The majority of the citizens of the area earn a living through agriculture, business and cattle breeding. He earns a living through breeding, fattening and selling beef cattle. To date he has 2 head of beef cattle, with 34 years of experience in the field. Additionally, he breeds and sells small animals (chickens, guinea pigs). At the same time he grows cereals (yucca, bananas, vituca) which at the moment is for his own consumption and sometimes to sell. The loan is for investing in buying beef cattle (2 heifers), so that he can then fatten them up and sell them at a better price. This will obtain a greater number of sales and therefore greater income so that he can improve his quality of life. Ruperto is a new member for Edpyme Alternativa. He cosigns the loan with his partner.

name: Abelina
description: Abelina is 55 years old, married, mother of 3 children who have their own families. She completed 6th grade of primary schools and lives at Jr. Loyola 417, J. district, Chucuito province in the state of Puno.  She is one of the founding members of the Communal Bank “Niño San Salvador” in J.. In the beginning, with a loan for S/.300, she increased her capital to buy material (cloth and wool) for her embroidery business. At 30 years old she began sewing for the artisan store “trenza de oro” (Braid of Gold), where she used to work and export to other countries. She didn’t study because her parents left her with a woman who raised her since she was a little girl. When she retired from the artisan store she began her own business making embroidered items such as pillows, table cloths, wall weavings, etc.  With this loan for S/.1,700, which will be repais in 4 payments, she will buy 100 meters of cloth at S/.500 and 15 kilograms of wool at S/.525.00  Her greatest wish is to continue her business and improve the quality of her work. Translated from Spanish by Cindy Kendall, Kiva Volunteer

name: Juan Angel
description: Juan Ángel  is 56 years old. He does not have children whom he supports. He lives with his wife in their own home, which is located in the San Lorenzo community in the southern valley of Honduras.   For the past 3 years, he has worked at his small general store, selling merchandise like beans, corn flour, butter, oil, beverages, churros, chicken, deli meat, etc. His customers are friends and people who travel to his home daily, since he has his own home.  Juan is requesting a loan to purchase soap, churros, staple grains, beverages, etc. With the loan, he hopes to improve his financial situation and stock his business so that he can earn more income.   His dream is to have a good business so that he can save money for when he is older.

name: Julius Ummaru
description: Julius Ummaru is a maize farmer and member of Babban Gona. Julius Ummaru joined Babban Gona primarily to create a better future for his  children: Fatrik,Paul, and Samaila. Julius Ummaru is excited that Babban Gona offers a lasting solution to ending the cycle of poverty. For the first time, Julius Ummaru will have access to quality inputs such as fertilizer and seed. Without this loan, he would be subjected to buying these products in the open market where the products are not only very expensive but are often diluted with external products such as sand. With access to high quality inputs, Julius Ummaru can reap up to 30 bags/hectare, double the national average of 14 and  earn up to $2000/ha: more than three times the average Nigerian farmer’s annual income.  When asked how he plans to spend the income he will make this year  as a Babban Gona member, he said, “I plan to use the money  to expand my farmland.” Julius Ummaru is not thinking about this year alone; he expressed that his longterm goal is to “ensure my children are educated and have professional jobs”. With this loan, he is well on his way to achieving this goal.

name: Portia
description: Portia is a 29-year-old businesswoman from the district of Nyaminyami in Zimbabwe. She rents a shop at the local market where she sells bags, shoes, jeans, shirts, skirts, track suits and t-shirts. She has been running her business since 2013, and it has enabled her to support her family. Portia also volunteers in her community; she teaches leadership skills to young students. With the first Kiva loan she got, Portia  purchased more clothing supplies for her business. Her hope is to grow the business and open her own store. This will bring stability to her business, and it will enable her to change her family’s status and finances. Portia is thriving with her clothing business. Upon receiving her loan, she ordered better quality clothes and restocked her shop. She has used her profits to diversify the business into chicken rearing. Both of Portia’s businesses are now successful and she is an economically independent young lady. She is using the profits earned to buy food, clothing and furniture for the family.She hopes to get a second loan so that she can further expand her clothing business and purchase a variety of clothes and shoes.

name: Jorge Gregorio
description: Jorge is a 58-year-old man living in Sololá with his wife and 8 children, four boys.  The oldest is about to complete his academic career at the end of the year and the other three younger ones attend elementary school.  He also has four daughters who help Jorge in the fields and sometimes work as domestic employees in the homes of third parties to contribute to family economy.  He’s a hardworking, kind man who comments that he works growing potatoes, onions, beans, green beans or according to the time of year.  This was the same work his parents did and he learned it as time went by.  He comments that he attended elementary school at night while working days and studying at night contributing to his family and his siblings’ economy.  He’s now been working with his wife and children for the last 30 years and noting now that his needs have increased he’s requesting a Q 5,000.00 loan to buy potato and onion seeds as well as organic fertilizer these vegetables need to grow.  In this way his family income will increase.  He hopes with his income and profits generated in the future to be able to have a business like a grocery store and to provide better education for his youngest children.

name: Cecelia
description: Cecelia, age 29, runs a small restaurant business where she cooks food and sells beverages. She has been engaged in this business for the past four years. She is a high school graduate and lives in Gbarnga with her husband, who runs his own business, and their three children. The youngest is five years old and the eldest is 12. All three live at home and attend school.  Cecelia reports that one of her primary obstacles is the high market cost of her customers' favorite beverages. She is requesting a loan in order to purchase these beverages as well as to buy rice and meat to prepare and serve to her customers.  Her goals for the near future are to expand her business and to secure the education of her children.

name: Umut
description: Umut is 44 years old, married and the mother of three children.  She has been involved in animal husbandry since 1994, and this activity constitutes her family's main source of income.  Thanks to her very hard work, she now owns ten cows, five horses and 50 sheep.  Her farming business brings her a monthly income of about 17,000 som (KGS).  In order to further develop her business, Umut has turned to Bai Tushum Bank CJSC and requested a loan of 100,000 som (KGS).  She will use her loan to buy seven lambs and three calves for breeding.  She plans to reinvest the earnings from her loan into further expanding her business.  She also wants to give a decent education to her children.

name: Seyla Shirley
description: Seyla is a 29-year-old woman. She is single, has two sons aged 3 and 7 and a daughter aged 6, and her business is selling used shoes. She is a rebel and a dreamer. Prepared to give her best effort, she walks along silently with the dream of going from failure to success. She carries out her business in the 'cruce villa Adela' [Adela city junction] area, where the roads lead off in the direction of remote settlements in the Altiplano highlands.    Seyla has rough, hard skin which bears the harsh cold of the area. She has long, chestnut hair, dresses fashionably and has a firm and penetrating gaze. Her mother tongue is the only inheritance she has received and for cultural reasons she only uses it with Aymara families. She goes about her life accompanied by her children who study at school and are in the habit of going to church to participate in the improvement of the region.   She is a single mother and is responsible for all the family expenses. They live in a room in a house belonging to her mother, which is constructed of adobe and has running water, energy from electricity and a sewerage system. Her business is selling used shoes. She buys used shoes in large quantities to resell them on her permanent stall. The stall is rented and she has to pay a monthly rent. Her mother wants to help her buy a stall with a little capital. "The rent eats up my monthly profits and I also pay for my children's expenses" she says.   Her business is successful because the merchandise is low cost. The advantage of her business is that the sales are daily. The disadvantage is paying the monthly rent. Her dream is to have a stall of her own so she wants to buy a stall. This is the 1st sequence of loans from the institution in the 6 years she has been doing this business. For these reasons Seyla is seeking a loan to buy a stall so she can stop paying rent.

name: Jhonalyn
description: Jhonalyn is a 43-year-old, married with three children. She is pleased with her store business, where she sells a variety of products to meet each customer’s demands. She has been running her store for ten years, and she is able to earn about 2,000-3,000 PHP a month.   She would like to request an additional capital amount of 10,000 PHP to purchase additional stock such as biscuits, bath soap, shampoo, canned goods and noodles. She knows that the loan will be of great help to increase her sales and therefore allow her to offer a better living to her parents and nephews.

name: Amistad Del Sur Group
description: “Amistad del Sur” (Friendship of the South) is a Communal Bank that consists of nine members who are starting their second loan cycle.  They did not experience any problems with repaying their previous loan.  To date, the members have demonstrated great responsibility with their payments.  They engage in different business activities in order to support their families.  For this reason, they are requesting a loan.  Such is the case with Sr. Agapito.  He currently serves as President of the Communal Bank.  Agapito works in the transportation sector.  He lives with his wife and two children who are attending school.  The money from his loan will be used to maintain his vehicle, which is currently experiencing a few problems.  This prevents him from offering good service.  His greatest wish is to buy a small house because living in a rental property is an enormous expense.    Most of the members are hardworking individuals.  They are grateful to be in a partnership with Emprender.

name: Rpsie
description: Rosie is 53 years old, married with five children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Rosie has a food vending business in the Philippines. Rosie requested a PHP 10,000 loan amount through NWTF in order to buy ingredients for her food-vending business.  Rosie has been in this business for twelve years. In the future, Rosie would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Fousseyni
description: Fousseyni is 33 years old and lives with his wives and two children in the sub prefecture of Kourouba, in the Koulikoro region. Fousseyni never had the opportunity to attend school. He became interested in income-generating activities early on, notably the purchase, storage and sale of grain.  In order to satisfy his customers while maintaining growth, Fousseyni decided to collaborate with Soro Yiriwaso. Having fully repaid his third loan, Fousseyni is currently on his fourth individual loan. He plans to use it to purchase two and a half tons of grains (such as maize, beans, millet, and fonio) from farmers and producers in Dangassa and the surrounding area. Fousseyni will store the grain for at least two months. He sells mainly to wholesale customers consisting of retailers from large cities like Bamako and Sanankoroba.  Fousseyni hopes to earn an average monthly income of 150,000 FCFA, which he will use to repay his loan and to reinvest in his business.

name: Lourdes Yanette
description: My name is Lourdes Yannette.  I have a cosmetics business.  I have been doing this for several years and earn enough to cover my family\\\'s expenses including heath and education costs.  Actually, I need to supply my business because during the Christmas season the volume of sales in increased.  Loan Use: Purchase lotion for men and women, shampoo, creams, lipstick, compacts, nail polish, deodorants, talcs and other supplies. Mi Nombre el Lourdes yanette, cuento con un negocio de venta de Cosmeticos, los que distribuyo de manera ambulante, tengo varios años  de dedicarmen a este tipo de actividad la que me genera ingreso para cubrir los gastos familiares, educacion, salud  y otros.  actualmente necesto surtir mas mi negocio tomando en cuenta que  ya se aproxima la  Navidad, y el volumente de venta es mayor.

name: Ramadhan
description: Ramadhan is a 63-year-old married man. He has four children, with ages ranging from 5 years to 17 years. He describes himself to be a polite man.  He operates a retail store where he sells items such as sugar, salt, cooking oil, and flour. He has been involved in this business for three years. His business is located in a residential area, and his primary customers are local residents.  He describes his biggest business challenge to be insufficient funds for improving the business.   He will use the KES 5,800 loan to buy a solar lantern to use in his business premises. His business goal is to improve his business within five years. He hopes that in the future, he will have had expanded his business.  He has taken three loans with SMEP DTM and managed to repay them succesfully.

name: Elsa
description: Elsa lives in Ozamiz City. She is a widow and supports her only daughter by vending snacks near schools.   She has successfully repaid her previous loan and recently, took another loan which she used to buy flour, sugar, milk, etc for snack vending business.   She wants her daughter to get an education and escape the life of backbreaking work she has had to endure.

name: Darejan
