description: Darejan is a 50-year-old widow who lives in Tbilisi City with her daughter, who works as a hotel administrator and gets a monthly income. Darejan owns and rents rooms in her house. The rent is the main source of income.   Darejan wants to supplement her family's income by renting an additional room, which is mortgaged. She has been unable to get a loan to pay for the mortgage from several local financial institutions. That is why she is requesting a loan from Kiva and Credo, which help people who do not qualify for conventional loans.   She will use the loan to pay for the mortgage and rent the room for a good price. Several people have already expressed an interest in living there.   Darejan hopes that renting out this room will be profitable and will increase her income so that she and her family can improve their standard of living.

name: Juan
description: Juan is 52 years old. He is married and has a beautiful family that includes five children ranging from six to 25 in age. He and his family live in a community in Sololá.  Juan works as a laborer in order to make a living and support his family. He has been doing this for 35 years now, but he also works growing coffee to supplement his income. As head of household, Juan worries about what his family needs. That is why he has now realized that one of their most pressing needs is to replace the roof over their home. However, this is difficult because he doesn't have enough money to buy the sheet metal. This is the reason why he is requesting a loan.  Juan's big dream is for all of his children to have successful professional careers so that they can have better opportunities to improve themselves.

name: Veronica
description: Veronica was born in the city of Quillabamba in La Convención Province, which is in the Peruvian jungle. She is 35 years old and has a 14-year-old son named Luis.  Veronica moved to the city of Calca at the age of 20 and this is where she conducts all of her business activities.  She works at one of the private schools in the city of Calca.  During her free time, Veronica sells beauty products through catalogs.  She is taking this opportunity to request a loan to buy more beauty products.  Her dream is to open a preschool.    The Communal Bank “Milenium III” meets every 30 days in the city of Calca in the Department of Cusco in Peru. Cusco is recognized for being an area for tourism and business. It is also known for the traditional festival of Inti Raymi and for being the home of one of the Seven Wonders of the World, Machu Picchu.

name: Ama
description: Ama is 25 years old and married with 2 children. She supports her husband and their children through her yam sale business. She orders her  goods from fellow traders who go to Techiman for them. Her wish is to be able get enough capital to buy the yams herself at the farmgate. This would allow her to get more profit. She is a beneficiary of KRABAN'S TEACH learning sessions and wants to apply the skills acquired during the training.

name: Grace
description: Grace O. recently joined the K-MET volunteer Community Health Worker (CHW) group in Kisumu, Kenya.  As a CHW she will be trained by K-MET and will begin visiting members of her community who are sick with a variety of illnesses. Her work will include distributing Nutriflour (a vitamin-enriched flour produced by K-MET) to malnourished patients, providing reproductive health education, referring patients to local clinics and hospitals, and providing basic health care.   Grace is 34 years old and a widow. She has 2 children, a girl and a boy, who are both in school. She heard about K-MET from friends and decided that she wanted to join and be trained to work in the community.   Grace has worked in salons for 9 years. She was interested and the practice was easy for her, so in 2002 she took a stylist course in Kisumu in order to get more qualifications. In 2006 Grace started her own salon in the Nyalenda area of Kisumu. She employs one other woman to work in the salon.   This will be Grace’s first loan from K-MET. She has applied for approximately $200 and will use the loan to buy chemicals, hair pieces, weaves, shampoo, and conditioner.

name: Solidaridad De Jicamarca Group
description: The communal bank Solidaridad De Jicamarca is a group whose members share a strong desire to improve themselves and to move forward in their lives; the bank takes its name from the place where the members live.  The group consists of eight individuals, mostly women, each of whom brings a personal history of effort and improvement in course of their lives. One of the members is Eugenia Y., age 51, who lives with her partner and has a son who is already grown. For more than three years, Eugenia has been running a small convenience store where she also sells school supplies; occasionally she also makes hand-woven items to order.  Eugenia started in this business because in her neighborhood there were not that many convenience stores. Thanks to the effort she has put into her work, she has been able to add a second floor to her house and with time achieved a better quality of life.    Eugenia plans to invest this loan into the purchase of school supplies inventory for her business. In the future, she would like to expand the store and increase her earnings so that she could provide more economic resources for her family.

name: Fernando
description: Fernando is 51 years old, married, and has 2 children.  He lives in his own home with his family.  His house is located in La Campiña, sector 4, in a village called La Matanza in Piura state.    Fernando is a farm worker.  He grows pole beans and the money he earns from this activity allows him to improve his family's financial situation.  He has been doing this work for over 10 years and knows a great deal about managing crops.   Fernando is requesting a loan from Edpyme Alternativa  for 1500 New Soles which he will used to make some improvements to his house so that it is safer and more comfortable.  He would also live to purchase a cooler which he will use to store the pole beans.   He is well known in the area where he lives and has regular customers.  This loan will help him improve his living conditions.

name: Ernesto Isaias
description: Ernesto is 23 years old, a high school graduate and married. His wife looks after the home and they have a 4 1/2 month--old daughter. No one else lives with him and just two people depend on him. He is employed and has been for about two years. He has no business. The area where he works is around 8 km from his home and he travels by bus. His work hours are four days on, three days off.  The client will buy wood for completing the construction of his home, and will also install basic electricity service. The loan will improve his quality of life, as he will be able to have his own home.   His dreams are to be able to continue working so that he can have a decent home for his family, and for his daughter to grow up strong and healthy.  A loan will help him greatly, as he can work on his home until he finishes it. From his salary as an employee he is paying off his loan little by little, and expects to meet his obligations very well, so that CrediCampo will keep lending to him.

name: Luis
description: Luis is 60 years old and from Talibon, Bohol. He is married with three grown children. For forty years, Luis has operated a sari-sari (variety) store business offering different merchandise usually consumed by Filipino household. He sells items such as canned goods, chips, cooking oil, sugar, coffee, and toiletries.   Luis is asking for a loan of 5,000 PHP to buy additional stocks of merchandise such as noodles, shampoo, coffee, canned goods, and seasoning.  In the future, he hopes to maintain and expand his business so he can meet his needs for old age.

name: Nelson
description: Mr. Nelson González is single and 28 years old. He is a contractor. In his job he hires people for construction work and works with the architect or engineer to build what is necessary according to the professional plans. He currently employs 5 construction workers, who he hires on depending on the amount of jobs he has.  The start up capital he obtained thanks to the long line of years he worked in Argentina, and he is also currently partnered with his uncle Mr. Sixto Reyes with whom he assumes all the commitments of their work.  They both own their own house, and live modestly thanks to their joint effort to get their business ahead. The credit he requests is for the purchase of tools such as a concrete mixer, floor cutter, wheelbarrow, etc. which will improve and speed up the work and improve the service he provides to his clientèle.  Translated from Spanish by Luis Lopez Martinelli, Kiva Volunteer

name: Francisca Marleny
description: Francisca is a 41 year old woman. She is single. She completed 4 years of primary education. She is a mother but her children are grown up and independent, living in their own homes. They help their mother with some activities in the fields. She learned farming from her parents, as they have worked in agriculture for many years. This activity has been passed down from generation to generation in her family. Her customers include people from other towns, as well as from her local area, and others.  She has requested economic support from the Comixmul Cooperative for the upkeep and maintenance of her coffee crops. This is necessary in order to avoid infestation by insects and also diseases, for example, blight. To do this, she will buy manure, fertilisers and insecticides.   In the short term, she plans to buy some more land in order to continue growing and improving her crops and her income. Her future plans include making improvements to her home and to re-invest in her crops as long as God allows.

name: Rolando
description: Rolando G. Aragon will use this loan to purchase supplies for his silk-screening business. He will purchase paints, T-shirts, and blankets.  Twelve years ago, he began printing blankets with popular slogans and now the mayor’s office is one of his largest clients. He started the business simply as a way to increase his income and this small business has provided for the education of all three of his children. He dreams that his children will also be able to have their own businesses. The greatest obstacle he faces is the cost of transportation, as it is very high and he must travel to buy supplies.

name: Victoria
description: Victoria S., 47, is married with 2 children.  She has 5 years experience in the cabbage & cucumber business. She sells to people of the village 2 days per week. She started her business with a previous loan of US$750 from SPBD.  She expects her weekly net cash flow to be 80 Tala (~US$28).  SPBD loans are Victoria’s only access to capital because she has not been able to qualify for a loan with the traditional banks. This loan will be used to purchase cement, iron roofing & timber. Victoria produces a lot of fruit & vegetables from her garden.

name: Manuel Albito
description: Manuel is another one of the many people fighting to improve their lives through the loans. HE reports that thanks to God and his loan he was able to make an investment in his coffee crop and buy materials. Fortunately, he had a good coffee harvest. Manuel needs a loan again because at this time he needs to change the sheeting on his roof of his house, because it is in very poor condition.  His big dream is to change the roof on his house to improve his home.

name: Simon
description: Simon is 32 years old. He is married and has three children. He has had a motorcycle business for four years and it has been profitable. He will be using the loan to  complete payment of another motorcycle. He hopes this will help him educate his children. His hopes and dreams for the future are to have a stable business and a happy family.

name: Ajina
description: Ajina is applying for a loan of $1,000 to improve her business. She is running a business in her house by selling gasoline and solar. She is making a good income from selling gasoline and solar, and she wants to buy more stock with the loan.   She is living in a town nearby the main road, so many people come to buy, and she is selling every day. She opened her kiosk a year ago with her working capital of $400. She is very happy with this program that is helping poor people to improve their living conditions. Her husband is a fisherman.

name: Na We Cam-Ii Group
description: Here are members of the “Na We Cam II” group from the northern city of Makeni. They are small-scale businesswomen who have come to SMT, a partner of Kiva.org, to apply for a loan of SLL 500,000 for each to enable them to expand their businesses.   Pictured left is Emma B. who is the leader of this group. The fifty-year-old Emma is married with five children – three in primary school and two adults. For many years now, Emma has been selling palm oil (the country’s most popular cooking oil). She also sells containers (used mainly to store palm oil). With her share of the loan, Emma will buy gallons of palm oil and a number of containers to add to her current ones.

name: Sakhavat
description: Sakhat A. is 28 years old. He is single. Sakhava is an Internally Displaced Person. He moved from the town of Fuzuli and currently lives in Baku together with his parents.   For the five last years, Sakhavat has been working as a construction foreman. He learned this trade from his father, who also used to be a foreman. At present he needs 2000 AZN in order to buy necessary tools  for his work.

name: Loriphen
description: Loriphen helps her husband on their farm, raising pigs to sell. For more than two years, she has earned well, aside from her husband's income from their transportation services business. Her previous loan, used to buy feed, was successfully repaid.   Recently, Loriphen took a new loan to purchase piglets as piggery improvement. She plans to improve the business in order to provide a better living for her family in the near future.
town: Sto. Niño, Tukuran, Zamboanga del Sur

name: Haya
description: Haya is a 31-year-old housewife. Her husband has two jobs, one as a public sector employee, the other at a small accessories shop that he owns.   Haya has been trying to support her husband in covering their children's needs for 10 years by running a small clothing sales business at home; she buys her goods at a wholesale price, and sells at a higher price to friends, neighbors, and relatives.   She has now applied for this loan to purchase a new collection of clothes for the upcoming season, and respond to her customer's requests.

name: Noella
description: Noella T. is 32 years old and married with 5 children.  She has many years of experience with preparing and selling chips. She sells to the people of her village and the general public six days of the week. She has had no previous loan(s) with SPBD.  She expects her weekly net cash flow to be 450 Tala (~187 USD).  SPBD loans are Noella’s only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with the traditional banks.The purpose of the loan is to purchase a frying pan, a cooking pot and other cooking equipment.

name: Saroh
description: Saroh is 52 years old and married. She lives with her husband and her children. She has two sons and two daughters. She and her husband have been a farmer and a breeder for over two years to increase the family income. She was pleased to be able to help her husband to provide a better life. She has asked for a loan from KPP-UMKM Syariah for 6,000,000 rupiah. This loan will be used to buy and build a bathroom, septic tank, and closet at her home to improve access to water and sanitation for her family. She wants to have access to safe sanitation for her family. Her family income is still not enough to build toilets and water resources with cash, but she is able to repay the loans received.  She and her family want to live a healthy life with healthy sanitation. She is very grateful for the opportunity and wants to thank to all of the lenders.

name: Chanthoeurn
description: Chanthoeurn, 24, is married, resides with her husband and a kid in Kampong Cham Province, Cambodia. She and her husband have been working as garment workers for three years. Due to less income, Chanthoeurn is requesting a loan of USD 1000 to purchase a motorbike for her husband to use as a motor taxi when he is free from his work at the factory to generate more income to support the family. In the future, she would like to run a sewing shop at home and send her kids to a good school.

name: G.s Ebenezer Group
description: Señora Elsa is a person who has made a living by growing coffee for 15 years.  She now has seven manzanas [a unit of land equal to about 1.75 acres] of coffee.  She sells this product in many places in the city of Danlí. Doña Elsa is asking for a loan in order to buy an 80-watt solar power system because she wishes to change her life by having lights in her home, and to keep updated to what is happening in the country and around the world by using common means of communication like the radio and television, and to avoid having to pay and to walk in order to charge her cell phone.  She is asking for the loan as part of a group loan with the following people:Doña Imelda, who has made a living by growing coffee for 25 years.Don Santos, who has made a living by growing coffee for 25 years.Don David, who has made a living by growing coffee for 12 years.Danli, Honduras – October  2015

name: Julia María
description: Sra. Julia C. is a member of the Communal Bank “Tres de Noviembre” (Third of November).  She lives in the community of the same name, which is in the parish of Cumbe.  In this area, there are livestock farms with large open pastures. Cumbe offers visitors many special recreational areas such as the view of El Calvario, which is a 15 minute walk from the parochial center; El Gulash, which is between Santa Rosa, Cumbe, and Jima; the beautiful Pucará in Sagrada de los Cañaris; the banks of the Cumbe River; and the ruins of Ingahuasi that ascends to Tinajillas.  Sra. Julia is 40 years old and has been divorced for 18 years.  She does not have children and lives in her own house.  Julia raises animals such as guinea pigs, poultry, and rabbits for personal consumption and to sell in the parish.  She also has cows and the milk she obtains from them is sold to the milk carts that exist in the area.    Julia is a founding member of the Communal Bank and has worked with the loans for 15 years.  Her new loan will be invested in the purchase a cow so that she can grow her business.  Julia's goal is to have more animals to sell.

name: Slyvia
description: Slyvia is a twenty-five year old married woman with three children, and she owns a house in Kasese, Uganda. She has been dealing in produce for the last three years and with income generated she has been able to pay school fees for her children. Her hardship is lack of enough capital and her plan is to grow food on a large scale, build a  permanent house and educate her children. Sylvia needs a loan to buy beans and firewood to sell.

name: Bahati
description: Bahati appreciates that her previous Kiva loan has enabled her to improved her living standards. She is requesting a loan to purchase more cashew nuts for resale. Her previous loan enabled her to expand her business and earn a higher income. She thanks Yehu for their financial support.

name: Warda
description: Warda is a married woman with one child. She operates a food stall where she cooks food for sale. She has been involved in this business for 2 years. Her business is located in a good area and her primary customers are locals. She describes her biggest business challenge to be inadequate working capital. She will use the Kes 20,000 loan to buy more stock of ingredients for preparing food. This is her second loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. The previous loan was repaid successfully. She will use the anticipated profits to expand business.

name: Yaneth Milena
description: Humble and hardworking - this is Yaneth. She is a warrior woman who has dedicated a large part of her life to caring for her family. She lives in the municipality of Medellín, where she earns a living selling ice cream. Her products are known to all her neighbors in the area, and they visit her business because they know that they can eat delicious things there. Yaneth has decided to improve her business and increase her sales, and so she is requesting a loan to buy supplies of ice cream in different flavors. The loan will allow her to get ahead with her business so that she can make the profits she needs to continue sustaining her family and her business. Support this woman with a loan and make here dreams reality!If you want to know more about the entrepreneurs and the loans from Interactuar, you can join the Lending Team called: “Friends of Interactuar Colombia”: http://www.kiva.org/team/interactuar_colombia

name: Karina Beatriz
description: Karina is 32 years old and she works as a nurse at a hospital in her city.  This provides her with income to support her household, above all because she is the mother of a six-year-old boy whom she loves very much and for whom she works every day to be able to offer him a better life.    Karina is thankful to Kiva's lenders as it is thanks to the help they have offered her that she will be able to buy household appliances, which will allow her to improve her quality of life so she can keep working to be able to get ahead and work toward her greatest dream:  having her own clinic.

name: Lonie
description: Lonie C. is from the village of Lilingayon, Valencia City, Bukidnon. She is 34 years old. Lonie is separated from her spouse and has four school-aged children. To make a living, Lonie owns & operates a business venture in the retail sector running a sari-sari (variety) retail shop buying and selling junk food, candies, biscuits & snacks like rice cakes in the local community. Lonie has been engaged in her business for over four years and earns approximately 10,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2010, Lonie joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Lonie is requesting a new loan of 5,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products to buy and sell. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Lonie from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Mary
description: Mary is married with four children, all of whom are  at school. She also takes care of her in-laws. She owns a stall in Kalerwe market, selling bananas.   She plans to use this loan to a buy more bunches of bananas. She buys these bananas from villages of Masaka in south central Uganda. Mary uses public transport to and from Masaka, where she goes for shopping once a week. She has been in this business for 10 years and she also sells furniture to get additional income.   She receives an average of 30 people and sells both on a retail and wholesale basis. Her customers are the people in the market and nearby communities. She works seven days a week. She depends on this job for a living. Her business challenges are transportation and seasonality.     She aspires to see her business grow big and to build her own house. Mary decided to work with MCDT because she wanted additional capital.   She resides in and owns a two-roomed house and the family has no access to electricity or piped water. Her monthly expenses include school fees, food and market dues.

name: Sieng
description: Mrs. Sieng V., 51, has a job as a vegetable seller. She sells her vegetables to buyers at the market and she is earning around $3 per day. She has six children who are single and living with her. Four of them are employed. Two daughters are garment workers and two sons are blacksmiths. V. hopes to build her son's business using this loan to buy additional ferrous materials.

name: Tsaghik
description: Tsaghik is 29 years old, and with her beloved husband and their single child, they live in Lchashen village of Gegharkunik region. Tsaghik and her husband are not employed, and their main and only occupations are farming and agricultural activities. On the farm, she takes care of cows, bulls, pigs, sheep, and a lot of chickens. On their plot of land, she and her husband Tsaghik cultivate potatoes, cabbage, carrots, tomatoes, cucumbers, and greens. Besides these assorted vegetables, Tsaghik also sells her farm products such as milk, macun (national dairy product), cheese, meat (beef, pork and mutton), and also eggs. All these goods they sell right from their farm to their neighbors and also to re-sellers. Now this loan of 700,000 Armenian drams will be very helpful for Tsaghik’s family, since with this she plans to buy vegetable seedlings and fertilizer for her land, and also fodder for all her farm cattle.

name: Sixta
description: Sixta is 22 years old. She sells catalog items. She is member of a company that develops its marketing strategy through catalog sales.  She started this business 2 years ago. She listened to her friend's advice, who gave her the idea to start her own business to make an income to bring money to the home, and support her family. She has a husband and a 7 year old daughter. With this business, she'll be able to take care of her daughter, and do the household chores at the same time she is making an income.  She sells to neighbors, family members, and a steady clientele. They buy using credit and also paying in cash. In the future, she is planning on buying a display cabinet so she can protect the merchandise and she can surprise her customers with an awesome presentation of her products.  Sixta is applying to credikiva, first loan she requests to Fundacion Mario Santo Domingo. She'll buy beauty products, perfume, clothes, and underwear with a special discount from the catalog. These products will help to amaze her clientele and it will impact her sales in a positive way.  Credikiva is a good investment for her business. December is a very busy commercial season, normally her income increases because of all the sales.

name: Kaneez's Group
description: My name is Kaneez F., and I am a widow and a mother of nine: six boys and three daughters. I live with my family in a small town called Borewala in Pakistan. None of my kids could attend school, due to our impoverished condition that we had to face after my husband’s death. I need a loan for my son to expand his barber shop. Last year, I received a loan for his barber shop, and with its profits I bought a television for my house. My group members are: Rani T., who requires a loan for her bangles and grocery store; Hasmat B., who will buy a goat with the loan; Shahnaz B., who requires a loan for her poultry farm; and Parween R. needs a loan for her husband’s restaurant.

name: Oksana
description: Oksana has been a farmer since 2001, growing melons like cantaloupe and watermelon.  Her husband and two children (aged 11 and 7) help her with her work.  The growth of her business began by planting cucumbers in an open field.  Oksana has decided to buy plastic to enclose greenhouses.  In the future, she plans on expanding the area of land she farms and to build a new greenhouse.  Her personal plans include saving for her children's education.  She needs your help financing the purchase of plastic sheeting for her greenhouses.

name: Petronila
description: Petronila M. is from the village of Yumbing Mambajao, Camiguin Province. She is 52 years old. Petronila is married and has 1 adult child. To make a living, Petronila owns and operates a business selling snacks in the local community. Petronila has been engaged in her business for over 20 years and earns approximately 4,500 PHP a month from these activities.  In 2010, Petronila joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Petronila is requesting a loan of 4,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Petronila from HSPFI.  She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.   *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Thy's Group
description: Thy’s group live in a rural village in Prey Veng province in Cambodia. Thy makes a living cultivating rice with his family and he also does extra work as a farm laborer to support his family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of member of the group to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Josephine
description: Josephine is 34 years old and married with five children.  She is from Camanga, Tukuran, Zamboanga del Sur.  To make a living, Josephine owns and operates a business raising crops and her main source of income comes from planting and harvesting a variety of vegetables to sell. Josephine has been engaged in her business for 10 years and earns 8,000 PHP a month.   Josephine joined GDMPC in 2011. She is requesting a loan of 17,400 PHP to buy fertilizer such as manure to increase her farm production. She plans to use the additional revenue, generated with her loan, to improve and expand her business.

name: Aurelia
description: Aurelia, age 49, is a hardworking and enterprising woman.  She is separated from her husband and lives with her 14-year-old daughter who she loves dearly and wants to provide a better quality of life.  Aurelia lives in her own home.  She sells fast food and fried snacks, such as roasted chicken and “salchipapas” (sausages and fried potatoes), from a small space inside of her home.  Her business is named “Las Dos Hermanitas” (The Two Little Sisters) and is well-known in the area.  Aurelia has been serving her customers for four years.  In her business, her daughter and another employee help with attending to the customers.  She enjoys cooking and working because it keeps her occupied.  Aurelia started working out of financial necessity since she receives no income from her ex-husband.  Now she wants to grow her business a little more so that she can generate the necessary income to pay for the household expenses and her daughter’s education.  She wants this very much, so she is motivated to continue striving and moving forward.  Aurelia considers her business to be profitable because she has regular customers that she has gained as a result of her good service and charming personality.  She has plans to grow her business by adding the sale of barbecued chickens.    This will be her fifth loan with the MFP organization.  Aurelia is grateful for the financial support she has received so that she can advance her business.  She wants to continue receiving this support, so she promises to continue the completion of her payments just as she did with her previous loans.  Aurelia is pleased to be part of her Communal Bank group because she considers the members to be supportive and responsible individuals.  The amount she requested will be invested in the purchase of an oven that costs 2500 PEN so that she can begin selling barbecued chickens.  The rest of the loan will be invested in ingredients for preparing roasted chickens.

name: Vaai
description: Vaai U., 39, is married with 2 children.  She has 4 years of experience in selling traditional necklaces, earrings, and fans.  She sells to the villagers/public 2 days per week. Vaai will use this loan to expand her alternative business--a taro plantation--and to make home improvements. She plans to purchase chemicals, fertilizer, timber, sand, and cement. Vaai has had 3 previous loans with SPBD.  She expects her weekly net cash flow to be 200 Tala (about $US83).  SPBD loans are Vaai’s only access to capital because she has not been able to qualify for a loan with the traditional banks.

name: Diamantina
description: Diamantina V. V. lives in Cartagena in Guanacaste. She is an excellent leader and she is also a merchant in the community.  She requires a loan in the amount of 500 000 (five hundred thousand colones) to purchase a tub of molasses she needs to start her business selling sugar known as molasses. It is used as feed for cattle and it has become a profitable business in the community.  She is a member of Empresa de Credito Communal de Cartagena, one of the 110 member organizations of Edesa (Kiva Field Partner) in Costa Rica.

name: Grace
description: Grace is a 33 year old tailor in Mombasa. She is married to Musyoki, and together they are blessed with three children aged 12, 6 and 3. She has been making clothes for her customers for the past thirteen years, and is doing great. This is Grace’s third loan from KADET LTD. She plans to purchase a new, modern sewing machine, as well as sewing threads and clothing materials. She will use the anticipated profits from the loan to repay it and to educate her children. She hopes to be a successful business woman.

name: Las Palmas Group
description: Antonio (he´s the first one from the right in the foto) is a man who is working for the well-being of his family. He has been selling grocery products for several years. He reckons that he will do very well with his loan, since with it´s help he could buy his merchandise. Fortunately the investment improves his quality of life, since now he counts with a sale of fried potatoes.With this change he is happy but not satisfied. For this reason he is requesting a new loan, which he will invest in the purchase of more grocery products such as: lemonades, sweets, sugar and rice, to ensure that his shop will continue to offer the best service in his community.Antonio has the full confidence that he will obtain credit to strengthen his business and to have his own shop one day.

name: Julia Adelaida
description: The members of the Luz y Progreso (Light and Progress) Communal Bank meet every two weeks in Portoviejo.  For many years this city has been known as the City of the Royal Tamarinds.  This is where we meet Julia, age 54.  She is in a common-law marriage, and they have seven grown children.  Two of them live in her house.  Her seven year old grandson, who is like a son to her, also lives with her.  He goes to school.  Her husband sells fish.  She is a small businesswoman.  She sells clothes by catalog.  She also has a mini grocery store.  She sells rice, sugar, oil, and detergent, etc.  She works every day from 6:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m.  Sometimes she works later.  She also sells clothes in her store because most of her customers always make purchases in her store.  She takes advantage of this to show them her catalog products.  Her products are delivered to her store.  She tells us that she has had her store for ten years, and she has been selling clothes for two years.  She will use this loan to stock her store with more basic needs items like rice, sugar, oil, detergent, and sausages, etc.  She will also buy clothes because she has several orders.  She has been in the communal bank for 11 years.  She likes it because the loans are very important to her life and to her businesses.  Her goal is to have a well-built house.

name: Eva
description: Eva is a 48-year-old married mother of four children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur.  Eva has a buy-and-sell vegetables business in the Philippines. Eva requested a PHP 20,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional vegetables to sell in the market.  Eva has been in this business for 14 years. She would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Evangeline
description: Evangeline works hard to support her family. Evangeline is unmarried and has a business selling ready-to-wear clothing in the Philippines.  Evangeline requested a PHP 25,000 loan through Kiva partner NWTF in order to purchase more items to sell.  Evangeline has been in this business for three years now, and also earns additional income from vegetable vending.  Evangeline would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Céline
description: Céline is forty-three years old, married and has two children in her care.  She lives in Baguida and sells vegetables.  She buys her supplies twice a month from local gardens and sells her produce at the market.Céline has requested this loan to buy bunches of carrots, onions and vegetables to increase her earnings.  These will be used to provide her children with an education.

name: Adelaida
description: Adelaida is a 45-year-old, married woman, and a mother of 13 children, from Ubay, Bohol. She earns a living by running her sari-sari, or variety store. She has been in this business for more than 14 years. She sells various goods and items to the people in her area.  Adelaida needs a loan to buy additional groceries to resell, like soda, noodles, sardines, bread, chips and other snack foods, soap and toiletries. With the increase in inventory, she will be able to attract and cater to more customers in her store, thus augmenting her sales and profit. Adelaida hopes to expand her business in the future, so that it will continue to generate income.

name: Cecile
description: Cecile is 38 years old and married with two children, both of whom are in school.Cecile earns a living by raising pigs in the Philippines. She is borrowing 12,000 Philippines pesos (PHP) through NWTF in order to buy feed and vitamins for her pigs.Cecile has been raising pigs for two years and also earns additional income from farming sugarcane. She works tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save enough money so she can continue to send her children to school and expand her business.

name: Agustina
description: Agustina works hard to support her family. She is married and has a tailoring business in the Philippines. Agustina requested a 17,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy cloth, needles, and other materials for her tailoring business. Agustina has been in this business for 10 years now. In the future, Agustina would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Njira
description: Njira sells fruits and green vegetables to earn an income. She is the widowed mother of three children, all of whom attend school. She owns a house that neither has electricity nor piped water.  She always struggles to improve her grocery stall in an attempt to boost sales so that she can save money in order eventually to have a more formal establishment. She currently faces the major challenges of transportation and seasonality in her business.   Njira is requesting a loan in order to purchase sacks of fruits and green vegetables to offer for sale.

name: Theresa
description: Theresa is 55 years old and married with seven children.  She earns a living by raising pigs in the Philippines.   Theresa is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF in order to buy feed and vitamins for her pigs.  Theresa has been raising pigs for 15 years, and also earns additional income from selling nipa roofing.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream of saving money to expand her business.

name: Sana's Group
description: Sana is 45 years old and she is a mother with one dependent child, who is still in school. For her living, she sells grocery items, which it is the main source of her income, while her husband repairs motors to earn an income. She has been involved with this business for 27 years and it returns her back about 7.50 USD per day. This business allows her to save 5 USD each day for future needs. She is an former borrower with VisionFund and this is her second loans cycle. She successfully repaid her previous loan and she has used it to better support her living conditions. Now she is leading a group which consists of two members to apply for a new loan.  As a group leader, Sana will manage her loan portion to buy more grocery items for reselling. In the future, she hopes to earn more income from current business to support her living and her child’s education.
town: Kampong Cham province, Ponhea Krek district

name: Hajra Muhammad Ahmad's Group
description: Hajra is married and the mother of seven children. She lives in Chichawatni, a small city of Punjab, Pakistan, that is known for its agriculture industry. For the past 20 years, Hajra has lived in the Al-Fateh neighborhood in a three-room brick house with her family. Hajra is a seamstress who sews clothes for neighborhood clients to share the financial burden with her husband. She is very experienced in her work and is able to make beautiful clothes that satisfy her clients. Hajra’s eldest son works at a grocery store for a low income while another son is a shoe-polisher. Her other children stay at home as Hajra is not financially able to provide for their education.  Hajra’s husband operates a clothes-selling business. He purchases clothing from Multan, which is famous for its clothes and embroidery industry, and sells his inventory to local clients and shopkeepers for a profit. Hajra is applying for her second loan from the Kiva partner Asasah so that her husband can expand his business. He will buy bulk clothing of different varieties to improve his inventory and reduce his travel costs.   Hajra is a responsible Asasah client who has repaid her previous loans efficiently. In this photo, Hajra is shown holding her Asasah Passbook.

name: Jamila
description: Jamila’s son has been driving an auto rickshaw. He pays daily rent, because this rickshaw does not belong to him. He belongs to an ultra-poor family and has been feeding his own children as well. Now his children are growing older, and their needs grow, as well. He was worried for many days about how to stop having to pay the daily rent, so he decided to buy his own rickshaw. Jamila has been making savings for many days, to buy a new auto rickshaw for her son, but at the time of purchasing some money was short. Therefore, Jamila has requested a loan for her son so that he can buy a rickshaw with the contribution of savings.  She hopes that now her son does not have any need to pay daily rent, which was the cause of an increase in expenditures. Jamila is a 48-year-old woman, living with her five children and spouse in the area of Lahore, Pakistan. She hopes that now her son will be able to earn more income, because now he will not pay daily rent to anyone. She  is very happy after taking this loan; she thanks Kiva and its field partner, BRAC Pakistan.

name: Lydia
description: Lydia Q., age 52, owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) shop in her local community, offering such daily-use products as shampoo, soap, toothpaste, canned goods, and snack foods for sale. Lydia has been engaged in her business for over three years and it brings her approximately 10,000 PHP a month. She and her husband live in the village of Sto. Niño, Manolo Fortich, Bukidnon, and have three school-aged children.   In 2009, Lydia joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services. Her goal was to help improve her living situation and increase her ability to engage in business activities. Lydia has successfully repaid a previous loan of 8,000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to purchase additional inventory and was employed as working capital. Lydia is requesting a new loan of 9,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase biscuits, canned goods, and other additional products to sell. This will be the third loan taken out by Lydia from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and reaches out to the poor households of northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Lucas
description: Lucas R. Dávila is a 49 year old entrepreneur with a jewelry business.  He started with C$10,000.00, which he acquired through a loan 15 years ago.  His business is located in the Ayapal Managua neighborhood to the west of the capitol, Managua.  The loan he is asking for is for work capital for his business.  He will buy gold and precious stones, which he sells a lot of during this time of year because of the promotion of students.  He is married, and he is raising three children.  Two of them are school age.  He says that before he had this business he worked as a construction worker.  He has had nine loans over five years with Ceprodel.  He used them to invest in his business.  It has been growing, and he has been diversifying his merchandise.  This is thanks to the loans given through Ceprodel.   Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Juliet
description: Juliet works hard to support her family.  She is married and has a fish vending business in the Philippines.  Juliet requested a PHP 14000 loan through NWTF to buy more fish to sell.  She has been in this business for 8 years now.  Juliet would like to build and expand her business to secure the future for her family.

name: Liwayway
description: Liwayway is 42 years old and is married to Manny. The couple is thankful because they have been blessed with four children. To raise her family, Liwayway engaged herself in hog-raising business. She has been in this business for two years, and usually receives a net income of PHP 7,000 per hog every 4 to 5 months.   To this end, Liwayway is requesting a loan in the amount of PHP 40,000 to buy feeds, vaccines and vitamins for the proper growth of her hogs. She hopes that she can obtain her desired loan to further improve her business.

name: Thok's Group
description: Thok, who is a 42-year-old farmer, lives in Phnom Proek district of Battambang province and she is a married mother of two dependent children who are in school and need better support for their studies. Selling grocery items has been her main business for ten years already. Sometimes, she works for others for a fee to supplement income. These days, a lack of capital to buy more grocery items to resell is the main challenge she is facing. She decided to lead a group of two to apply for a new loan. This will be her second cycle with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner) and she has repaid her past loan successfully. The previous loan allowed her to renovate her house and to provide her children with enough healthy food. As a group leader, she will use her loan to buy more grocery items to sell. She hopes to earn more income to upgrade her living standard much better than before.

name: Janet's S. Group
description: Janet's S's group is located in Teshie Township. The group members are basically involved in the small-scale retail sale of vegetables (cabbage, carrot, lettuce, green pepper, onion), cassava, plantains, and braziers. They have an average age of 36 years and an average of two children. Janet S. is a 40-year-old married woman and a mother of three. Her main business is to supply vegetables (especially cabbage, carrots, lettuce, green peppers, and onions) to vegetable sellers in Accra. She buys the items from the central market and supplies them to customers in Accra. She has all three children going to school. She is standing in the middle of the photograph.   Janet is sometimes supported by her husband, who is a businessman. Her main clients are basically vegetable traders in Accra.   Janet is determined to use the loan request amount of 400 GHS from Kiva partner ID-Ghana to change her and her family's lives by investing it in her vegetable business. She is on the first loan cycle with ID-Ghana. The group need a total amount of 1,600 GHS so that they can increase stock and serve customers better.

name: Felinas Group
description: Felinas is the name that the 7 members chose for the group, since they say the name sets them apart. The group is located in a community close to a sugar factory that's an important part of the area's economy and identity. The area produces sugar cane and once the cane cutting begins the factory resumes operation to produce the most common type of sweetener.  The community also has a chapel that every December 12th awaits the arrival of torch bearers (pilgrims that travel to Mexico City a week before to light their torches and bring it back to the community) on foot, on motorcycle, and on horseback to celebrate the Virgin of Guadalupe with mass, songs, fireworks and food distributed by organizers to those in attendance.  Each member of the group has an activity: Maria-Nursing services Ma. Victoria-Cosmetics sales Trinidad-Clothing and perfume sales Jessica-Candy sales Amada-Clothing catalogue sales Alexis-Tamales and Chiles Rellenos sales Claudio-Pig raising and selling  Claudio is the youngest member of the group, at 23 years of age, and has a four year old child with Karina. Claudio is hardworking, honest and since he was a boy helped his mother work in the field so now he doesn't have any trouble doing the job. He says what he most remembers is shepherding the sheep, cleaning the pigpens, and feeding the piglets. Thanks to his mother, who taught him this line of work, he decided to start raising and selling pigs two years ago. With the profits obtained and the income he earns as a farmworker he pays the household expenses. His wife and daughter are his biggest motivation. The VisionFund Mexico loan will help him purchase food and vaccines to keep his animals in good health.

name: Hadija
description: Hadija is a married woman and has been blessed with four kids, all of whom attend school. She lives at a rental house that has electricity but no piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.   Hadija operates a fish selling business, which has been operational for over five years. She mentioned competition as a challenge in the business. Hadija dreams of becoming a wholesaler of fish in the future.   With the KES 50,000 she wants to purchase sacks of fish for resale. She joined Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Sokhorn's Group
description: Sokhorn’s group lives in a rural village in Phnom Penh province in Cambodia. Sokhorn sells fishes to support her family. In their village, there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Stephen
description: Stephen is a single man. He describes himself to be a visionary and a determined man. He operates a retail store where he sells cereals such as maize, beans, green grams, sorghum, etc. He has been involved in this business for six years and employs one staff member. His business is located in a strategically placed area, and his primary customers are retailers and wholesalers. He describes his biggest business challenge to be insufficient funds for a business expansion. He will use the KES 20,000 loan to buy more cereals to sell. His business goal is to expand his business within five years. He hopes that in the future, he will use the anticipated profits for building a house.

name: Om-Hashem
description: Om-Hashem is 47, divorced and has 3 children. She has a small sewing project that she started to provide a source of income for her children.She is requesting 10,000 EGP loan to buy cloth and sewing supplies to increase her income and help her sons with marriage expenses.

name: Tofaga
description: Tofaga is a 35-year-old married woman with 7 children. She has a small plantation where she grows taro plants and bananas to earn a living. She has been doing this for many years. Tofaga has requested a loan to buy fertilizer, a mist blower, a wheelbarrow, gloves, shovels, a rake, and a bush knife. She has been a member of SBPD since 2009. With her profits, Tofaga hopes to provide for her family's daily needs.

name: Maria
description: Maria is 62 years old and married with eight children. Maria works very hard to provide for them.  Maria runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more groceries to sell.  Maria has been in this business for six years and sells a variety of items such as snack foods, sardines, detergent and other groceries.   In the future, Maria would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Armisa
description: Armisa  is a 25-year-old married woman with two young dependents ages 2 and 6 years old respectively. She has been engaged in  weaving nipa palm( are used by local populations as roof material for thatched houses or dwellings) for more than 5 years now. This is her sole source of income. her husband's occupation is a carpenter.   She would to acquire additional capital to finance her existing livelihood. She is asking for a loan worth 4000 PHP to buy materials such as  nipa  leaves and bamboo. In this way, she could improve her daily production enabling her to deliver more volume of nipa palm to her respective clients.  Armisa  hopes to improve her business so that it will generate more income to sustain the needs of the family and for the schooling of her children.  Any additional income will be used for reinvestment in the same business and for savings.

name: Dolis
description: Dolis is 37 years old. She is the owner of a hair salon in the La Playa neighborhood, where she lives with her spouse and two children, aged 5 and 16. Her business was born when she was 34, after having worked at a hair salon on the north side of the city of Barranquilla where she spent most of her time. As an employee there, she gained a lot of experience and started her business venture in her own house. She received her first support from her mother in law who bought her first chair and mirror so she could ply her trade. Little by little she gained more clientele to whom she offers the services of haircuts, blowouts, coloring, straightening  and scalp massages. A year ago, she approached the Fundación Mario Santo Domingo to access a loan and with it bought a new hairwasher, a display case to keep her products in and materials to operate efficiently. She deals directly with the consumer and does do housecalls, but that is not something her clients ask for frequently. She adjusts her schedule to the client's needs and ususally opens her doors at 8 in the morning and closes at 9 at night. Monday through Sunday. With the previous loan, she has improved the look of the business and when her clients come in they see the image of quality in her infrastructure and the friendly treatment and in the superior quality of what Dolis knows how to do. Right now, she is applying for a new Kiva loan with which she will purchase an air conditioner, and some furniture to organize her waiting area. All of this will contruibute to her clientele being more aware of the service because they will be in a refreshing ambience away from the incessant heat outside the business caused by the strength of the Carribean sun.

name: Narantsetseg
description: Mrs. Narantsetseg is 44 years old and lives with her husband and son in a ger (traditional felt housing) in Huvsgul province of Mongolia. Her husband, Purev-Ochir, provides carpentry services in town. Her son, Huvsguldalai, is a university student.   Narantsetseg has been running an organic fruit and vegetable retail business in a local market since 2007. She has gained a lot of experience and regular customers over the years. She is now planning to grow organic vegetables on her plot of land with the help of her husband and son.   She is requesting 2,600,000 MNT to purchase seeds and seedlings and to cover other expenses. She is a hardworking, friendly and welcoming lady.

name: Graciela
description: Graciela is 43  years old. She is married and has a 7 year old daughter, for whom she works to give her the best. She has a house where she lives with her spouse and her daughter. Graciela's work consists of sewing clothes for women, men and children. She has her own sewing machine and creates her own clothing. She also repairs her customer's clothing who go to her knowing she will do a good job. She has been doing this work for more than 7 years and she has a very rustic workshop in her house. She works alone and helps her husband with the household expenses.   She considers her business to be profitable because of the demand for her services and the good earnings that it brings her. She likes her work because it is in her home and it keeps her busy and she feels like a productive person. She also likes to have income and perform the duties of a housewife and mother. This is loan number 06 with Kiva and she is very grateful for the financial support. With the amount she has asked for, S/.1500 soles, she will buy sewing materials such as fabric, cotton and other products for her small business.

name: Setimba Edith Group
description: Edith S. is 30 years old and is married with two children, ages 4 and 12. She rents a one-roomed house where she lives with her family. She prepares three meals a day, and her greatest expenses every month are her house rent and school fees for her children. She works seven days a week selling her charcoal at the market, serving about 30 customers a day. The main challenge Edith faces is that her customers often want to buy her charcoal on credit, which hurts her ability to conduct business.  She has been with MCDT for four years now. The reason she joined was because she needed a loan to improve her business.  Edith will use this loan to increase her business. She hopes to save enough money from her business to build a house.

name: Debora
description: Debora has owned a small shop in the Usariver neighborhood of Arusha for 8 years.She belongs to Magadirisho "A" (group code 2001) loan group. She currently makes an average monthly profit of $350. Every day she works at her business from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.  She is requesting loan from BRAC Tanzania so that she can buy more items for her business. She is hopping that through this loan, her profits will increase and she will be able to grow her business.    Debora is 31 years old, married, and has four children who age between 4 and 16 years.

name: Bernie
description: Bernie P. is from the village of Lapasan, Clarin. He is 36 years old, is married, and has three school-aged children.  Bernie owns and operates a business providing transportation services to local community members. He has been engaged in his business for over two years and earns approximately 4,000 PHP a month.  In 2010, Bernie joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and his ability to engage in business activities. He is requesting a loan of 12,000 PHP which will be used to invest in expanding his business. This loan will be his first from GDMPC. He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of his family.   About GDMPC: GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three unit offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Auring
description: Auring is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a food vending business in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to buy additional ingredients like spices, meat, vegetables, etc. for her food vending business. She has been in this business for five years. Auring earns more income from her general store. She has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to save enough money to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Silvana Maribel
description: Silvana Maribel B. M. has a printing business.  She started her business with her parents' help and still keeps it all in her parents' name.  Silvana is married and her husband drives a motorcycle taxi which he owns.  Silvana's goal for the future is to grow her printing business so that she can make more income.  She has good references and the loan money will be invested in having maintenance work done on the motorcycle taxi so that her husband could provide a better service to his customers. She is a responsible person who wants to help her family succeed.

name: Tieng
description: Tieng resides in Kompong Cham Province. To earn a living, she plants rice crops on her farmland. On average, she could make about $1.50 profit a day to use for financial expenses. She shares some responsibilities with Tieng, her husband, who is a tobacconist in the mobile place and he earns around US $2 each day. They have been married for many years and they are blessed with a kid who is attending primary school and lives under their income. To expand her husband's business, Tieng would like to borrow funds provided by leaders on Kiva to assist her husband torward buying more tobacco to store for future sale.

name: Norman De Jesús
description: Norman S. is married and has two children for whom he must provide everything they need to grow and develop; he lives in Nagarote.    It's important to point out that Norman is very hard-working and does his best every day at his place of employment because he wants to improve his home's conditions.  He will use the requested funds to buy building materials, like paving stones, to build a stone wall for his home thus providing his wife and children with the necessary conditions for their development.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Elsie
description: Elsie is 45 years old. She is a mother to children ages 17 and 19. Since 2011, she has been engaged in a sari-sari store business for an income. She also helps her husband with their transportation business. Elsie is asking for a loan to increase her inventory of canned food, sugar, noodles, cooking oil, chips, candies, and detergent. She also hopes to buy pistons. She and her husband work hard so that their children can finish their schooling. In the future, she would like to expand her business to ensure sustainability and savings.

name: Magdaline
description: Magdaline and her family are well. She has a poultry, beekeeping, and dairy business that is going well and generates 20,000 KES each month.  Magdaline is requesting a loan to purchase an egg incubator.

name: Norelvis Alejandra
description: Norelvys Alejandra V. is a 21 year old young woman who lives with her husband and four year old son in the Carrizal neighborhood.  Her family works in the leatherwork trade; they make bags, briefcases, and also make t-shirts, robes, and pants.  Norelvys learned this trade, along with her independent, responsible work ethic, from her mother, Liliana F..  This is a great small company that has been associated with Fundación Mario Santo Domingo for 15 years.  Norelvys earned her bachelor's degree and her mother's experience took her to begin her business when she was very young.  She began making articles of clothing, brief cases, and bags, and was not able to continue with her studies.  Now that she is married, she works this trade with her husband and it is what sustains the household.  This will be her second loan through Fundación Mario Santo Domingo.  The first loan provided new fruits because she was able to buy in cash and get better use of the money.  This was reflected in better household income.  She is asking for this Kiva loan in order to buy materials and supplies to make bags, cases, sport t-shirts, and long sleeve shirts to meet the demands of her customers, located in the neighboring country of Venezuela, where she sells in greater quantities.  Her dream is to expand her business, improve its infrastructure, and above all continue studying so that she can obtain a professional career.  Her greatest challenge is not being able to find a large enough loan to cover her immediate production needs, because she is just beginning to establish her credit history, but she knows that, with perseverance, she will continue to advance little by little. Translated from Spanish by Hugo Reyes, Kiva Volunteer

name: Robert
description: Robert is a humble agriculturist and hard-working father. He is a widower and lives with his only child. His hopes to improve their living conditions and support his only child's education.  Robert has been planting corn for almost 15 years. According to him, the greatest challenge he faces today is that he doesn't have the financial resources to purchase farm supplies. He is asking for a loan of PHP 27,000. Robert said this would help him maintain and improve the farmland he cultivates. He believes and hopes that he can overcome all his hardships in life and that his child can earn a college degree.

name: Josephine
description: Josephine works hard to support her family. She is married and has a fish vending business in the Philippines.  Josephine requested a PHP 19,000 loan through NWTF to buy additonal fish to sell. She has been in this business for 10 years now. In the future, she would like to build and expand her business to secure the financial stability of her family.

name: Monica
description: Monica is a single woman with two children, both of whom attend school. She lives in a rental house that has electricity and piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are rent and food for the family.  For the past three years, Monica has operated a laundry business, and her potential customers are neighbors and passersby. Monica faces a major challenge of seasonality in her business. She dreams of expanding her business in the future. Monica plans to use this KES 20,000 loan to purchase a washing machine. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Lorena
description: Lorena is a married woman with four children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Lorena is 32 years old and has four children who are currently in school.Lorena has a business making dried fish in the Philippines. Lorena requested a PHP 15,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy more fish, a sack of salt, bamboo, fish net and other materials for her business.Lorena has been in this business for five years. She would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Evelyn
description: Evelyn L. is from the village of Bocator Tangub City. She is 32 years-old and married with three school-aged children. Evelyn owns and operates a  specialized retail store which sells daily use products such as candies, eggs, shampoo, soap and toothpaste in the local community. Evelyn has been engaged in her business for over five years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Evelyn joined Kiva partner GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Evelyn has successfully repaid a previous loan of 7,000 PHP from GDMPC. Evelyn is requesting a new loan of 9,000 PHP which will be used to purchase new items to expand her product offering. This loan will be the third loan taken out by Evelyn from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three unit offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fishers and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Ivan
description: Ivan S. is married. His family lives in Korolyovo. Ivan sells household chemicals in the central marketplace of his small hometown. Small ventures like Ivan’s become the only source of income for families in remote parts of Ukraine. Ivan’s business has helped him survive when financial recession hit Ukraine again in 2000. Ivan has been in the trade for 5 years. Currently, his inventory amounts to 40,000 Grivnas; his income is about 5,000 Grivnas a month.   Ivan’s business is characterized by stability and positive performance. Inventory he sells is always in demand as people need dishwasher and laundry soap, shampoos, and other household chemicals. Ivan wants to see his business growing in the future, which is why he is requesting a loan of 9,000 Grivnas to increase his turnover capital. He is hoping to boost further development of his business with this additional assistance.

name: Angelina
description: Angelina is 57 years old, married with five children.  Angelina works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 14000 loan through NWTF to purchase more groceries to sell in her general store.  Angelina has borrowed and paid 12 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 12 years and also earns an income from selling vegetables.  Angelina aspires to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Johnny
description: Johnny is an industrious and optimistic person. He is a farmer in their community, tilling a small parcel of land for farming that is their main source of income. He dedicates himself to his farm activities to improve his family’s status of living. Johnny is 43 years old now, married and blessed with three children. His loving wife also helps him in their business to lessen the burden on his part and save more expenses for labor cost. They hardily work together to increase their yields for the future of their children.   Due to financial constraint, he is asking for a loan amount of PHP 15,000 to buy fertilizer and pesticide and to pay for the labor costs required for planting corn. After all, he knows that this is for the sake of their business success. He hopes for further development of their cornfield through those inputs he will acquire through the loan.

name: Thae's Group
description: Thae is a young mother of three children and a villager from Ponhea Krek district of Kampong Cham province. Two children attend school and one is too young for school.   To tackle the financial demands of her household, she grows cassava and rice. She has farmed for ten years and earns 37,300 KHR per day. This is the second cycle loan for Thae and her joint-borrower with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). She and her joint-borrower seek 1,500,000 KHR each. As the leader, she will spend her entire loan portion to buy fertilizer and pay for labor fees. She hopes to produce a better yield than last year.
town: Kampong Cham province, Ponhea Krek district

name: Vladimir
description: Vladimir is married with a seven-year-old daughter. He runs a greenhouse business growing tomatoes, cucumbers, potatoes, cabbage etc. He has got three greenhouses where he grows vegetables for sale. Vladimir has been in this business for 15 years. Making sure that the vegetables mature early in spring provides a good income for Vladimir’s family. Vladimir is requesting a loan of 10,000 UAH to purchase farming supplies for this season – seedling and fertilizers. He also needs to purchase some film to repair his greenhouses. Vladimir enjoys his business and would like to develop it further by building a new greenhouse next year.

name: Eulalio
description: Eulalio is a 57-year-old married man from Antequera, Bohol. He has 5 children. Four are adults and the youngest is 14 years old. He is engaged in a motorcycle transport business. He transports customers from one place to another for a certain fee. He has been operating his motorcycle transport business for 3 years.   He requested a loan of 4,000 PHP to buy tires, fuel and maintenance for the motorcycle. In the future, Eulalio would like to expand his business to have a sustainable livelihood and in preparation for his old age.

name: Julieta
description: Julieta is 44 years old, married and has two children, one of whom is in school.  Julieta is in the agricultural business, farming vegetables in the Philippines. Julieta requested a PHP 14,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy fertilizers and other farm supplies.  Julieta has been farming vegetables for five years now, and has borrowed nine times in the past from NWTF to sustain this.   In the future, Julieta would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Ofelia
description: Ofelia is a married woman with three children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Ofelia is 61 years old and has three children who are in school.She has a fish vending business in the Philippines and requested a PHP 7,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy a variety of fish to sell.Ofelia has been in this business for 2 years. In the future, she would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Truphena
description: Truphena is a 44-year-old married woman. She has three children. She describes herself as determined. She operates a shop where she sells curtains. She has been involved in this business for three years. Her business is located in a competitive area and her primary customers are of all types. She describes her biggest business challenge as lack of capital. She will use the KES 20,000 loan to add stock of curtains for resale. Her business goal is to own a big business within five years. She hopes that in the future, she will own a big stall full of curtains. This is her first loan with SMEP DTM.

name: Argemiro
description: Argemiro is sixty years old and works ten hours a day at a carpenters' shop. He is a humble, committed, and honest person who is currently asking for help in order to grow and improve his income. This loan will allow Argemiro to buy supplies like wood. His business is growing, his customer base is larger, and he needs enough wood to complete some pending projects that will earn him an excellent profit.   Argemiro doesn't have any children, just his wife and his business. He has always been denied financial support, but thanks to Interactuar and its Kiva partners he has found the support he needed.

name: Pedro Joaquin
description: Pedro is a thirty-nine year old man with a creative mind and an energetic personality. He has worked as a photographer for twenty years, and the world is simply fascinating to him. With a lot of effort, he managed to set up his own photography studio. Thanks to his first loan from Kiva and MiCrédito he was able to acquire state-of-the-art equipment which significantly grew his business. This man with the eyes of an artist is asking for the support of Kiva and MiCrédito so he is granted a loan that will let him buy some lights, flashes, and other items that will improve the quality of the photos he takes. His spouse and their three children are his main source of support. In the future, he hopes to open a photography school.

name: Maa Mangala-B Group
description: In the year 2014, eleven women from the village of Duajhar of Nuapada district of Odisha, India united together and formed a Self-Help Group named Maa Mangala-B to avail a loan from Mahashakti Foundation for the further development of their existing businesses. All of them hail from a poor background. Sarojini is one of them and is standing with a raised hand in the photo. She is 48 years old and residing with her husband and a son of 25 years.   Sarojini has a vegetable cultivation farm in her village with a traditional water-lifting system from the dug well. She and her husband look after the farm. They produce vegetables such as brinjal, cauliflower, carrots, cabbage, chilies, cucumber, papaya, ladies finger (okra), popcorn, etc. on the farm. Traders come to her farm for taking the produce.   Sarojini says the traditional water-lifting system consumes more time, energy and manpower, so she incurred some losses due to this. She earns a monthly income of 4,000 INR from the above businesses. For future development of her family, Sarojini wants to expand her business by taking a fresh loan. With this loan, she has planned to buy fertilizer and farm inputs such as seeds and pesticides for her farm and purchase a diesel water pump for lifting water. By this, she can save the time and manpower and can utilize the same in other farm work. She expects a good return from this investment.   Sarojini dreams to construct a house and of the marriage of her son.   The other members of this group are involved in businesses such as vegetable cultivation and vending, Castro oil selling, and puffed rice selling.

name: Agatha
description: Agatha is the mother of 4 children. In 2001, she started selling vegetables in an open air market in a small town. In 2002, she opened a kiosk where she sold only vegetables. Last year, she got a loan of Kshs. 20,000 from SMEP, which she used to buy second-hand clothes. She is now requesting for a loan of Kshs. 30,000 to increase her stock of second-hand clothes, because the demand has increased.

name: Phoeurn's Group
description: Phoeurn is 41 years old and a married mother blessed with three children. She struggles for a living via rice farming and pig raising. Her supplementary source of income is a fish-catching business.    She has been involved in her current business for 15 years, earning about 41,300 KHR per day. This is not the first loan for Phoeurn with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). She has repaid her past loan fully and it has enabled her to provide sufficient food for her family.
