As the leader, she will spend her entire loan portion to buy rice seed, to pay for plowing fees, and to buy pig feed. She highly hopes that she can gain a good yield, better than before, so as she can expand her business.

name: Marilyn
description: Marilyn is 48 years old and married with five children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. She has a general store business in the Philippines and requested a PHP 11,000 loan amount through NWTF in order to buy more groceries to sell.Marilyn has been in this business for five years. In the future, she would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Akouavi
description: Akouavi is a widow who lives in Tokoin and is raising an only child. Aged 61, Akouavi is a dynamic and courageous woman who sells clothing for children in front of her house, in order to make a good living. To reach her goals, Akouavi stocks up twice a month at the market and is asking for this loan to order several dozen garments for children as well as bras and stockings that she can resell well. She wants to finance her business and have a good turnover so that she can cover her daily needs and help her child by paying the school fees immediately at the beginning of this school year.

name: Sadiq Ali
description: Sadiq Ali is a 36-year-old man, living in the area of Lahore, Pakistan with his family. He works hard to provide better living standards for his family by selling laces of various types and colors. He purchases laces in bulk from the market and then sells it to the general public. Most of his sales are for festivals, special occasions and ceremonies. He has become famous in the market due to the various types of laces and has retained many customers. Most of his customers are tailors and the ladies from town.   HIs experience has shown that most of his female customers ask for beauty products and gift hampers as well. This is the reason he decided to offer cosmetics products and gift hampers so he can meet the demand.   Therefore, he requests a loan from Kiva’s field partner so he can buy beauty products, gift hampers and laces. He is very experienced in his business and confident that his business will move in a positive direction as a result of the loan investment.  He is very thankful to Kiva’s field partner’s BRAC Pakistan.

name: Erika
description: Erika, 51, is a friendly and enterprising woman.  She's divorced and has three children but lives in her own house with only one of them.  Erika makes a living selling beauty products, cosmetics, and a variety of perfume.  She sells her distinguished customers well-known brands of fine fragrances, especially for women.  She has a big display case where she shows all her products for sale every day.  She also sells useful accessories such as belts, hairpins, necklaces, pendants, earrings, and women's and men's footwear.  She has done this job for five years, offering cordial service with a broad smile with each sale.  She works alone because she's comfortable that way.  This allows her to distribute her earnings with great prudence.  She hopes to continue working because she thinks her job makes women happy.  Currently she'll request 1,000 soles [PEN].  She's grateful to all the people who make it possible for her to get the loan she needs to achieve her work goals.  With the requested amount she'll buy more cosmetics such as body lotion, face cream, powder, and perfume so she can continue working.

name: Melanie
description: Melanie is 34 years old, married with school age children from Lawis, Sindangan, Zamboanga del Norte. She operates a hog raising business in their place. She is making good income from her business that she was able to expand her hog raising operations by adding more heads of piglets. Recently, she avails a loan from Paglaum MPC to purchase bags of animal feeds.

name: Josphat
description: Josphat is a 29-year-old vendor who works hard at the business of selling bread and cakes in his retail shop. He has been in this business for eight years, and also sells fruits and vegetables to supplement his income. He is married, has three children, and joined Faulu Kenya as a way to increase his income and meet their needs.  He makes good use of his membership to share business ideas, save money and secure loans. His membership has also allowed him to learn how to keep business records.  He has applied for a loan of Kes. 50,000 to buy more bread and cakes to sell to his customers. In the future, he hopes to build houses he can rent out to tenants.

name: Josephine Ann
description: Josephine Ann is a married woman with one child. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Josephine Ann is 23 years old.Josephine Ann has a fish-vending business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for three years.Josephine Ann requested a PHP 7,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy a variety of fish to sell.In the future, Josephine Ann would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth helps her husband in managing their vegetable garden for a living. She has been doing this for six years and she earns well to aid her husband's income as a construction worker. She joined GDMPC and had borrowed a new loan to purchase fertilizer and organic pesticides to boost her vegetable garden. She is hopeful to gain more return from her farm so she can save a portion of it for the future education of her children.

name: Ali
description: Ali is a 28-years-old single man who started running a school 4 years ago. There are 103 students enrolled in his school and 52% of them are female students. The majority of the students in his school are from low income families. He believes that by educating children in his community, he is working towards rural poverty reduction as this would help them in getting better work opportunities in future. The new academic year will be starting in the near future which would result in more student enrollments, but there is lack of furniture and classrooms. Therefore he has requested an amount of Rs. 100,000 to construct additional classrooms and to purchase furniture for the school.

name: Mary Jane
description: Mary Jane is 24 years old and lives in Oroquieta City. She is married with three children. She has managed the business of her mother for almost two years. She requested a loan to purchase additional ingredients like sugar, banana leaf, etc.  She has been a member of PMPC for three years. In the future, Mary Jane hopes to expand the business and help other people.

name: Benkan Group
description: The Benkan group is a member of the Sanouya de N'tentou association. It is made up of women who met through neighbourhood and family ties. On average they are 34 years old. Married with an average of four children, they have various activities such as the commerce of fruit and vegetables like Binta, who is the second person standing from right to left in the photo. They live in large traditional families in N'tentou in the Kati prefecture (Koulikoro region in the Republic of Mali). They have been working in small business for several years and are very sought after in the vegetable trade: bananas, cabbage, carrots, pineapple and tomato. In an attempt to satisfy the increasing needs of their customers, the members of the group decided to join the Soro Yiriwaso credit programme. This is their second solidarity loan. Binta plans to use her loan to buy 10 kg of bananas and a large quantity of cabbage, carrots, pineapple and tomatoes. She buys her stock locally from wholesalers and sells her merchandise retail at Ouelessebougou, for cash or for credit to a clientele of men and women. She hopes to make a monthly profit of 15.000FCFA which will enable her to reimburse her loan and reinvest the remainder in her vegetable business.

name: Hassan
description: Hassan is a 35-year-old farmer from Gidan Gambo.  As a Babban Gona member, Hassan, is excited about the opportunity to finally have access to credit, good markets and a trained agronomist. Like all Babban Gona members, Hassan can earn up to $2000/ha this season from growing maize, more than three times the Nigerian farmer’s average annual income. The average Babban Gona farmer yields 30 bags/hectare; double the national average of 14. However, Hassan is ambitious and is hoping that as a result of this loan, he will be able to acces quality inputs such as fertilizer and improved seeds that will  result in a yield of at least 35 bags of maize per hectare this season.  Hassan is hopeful about what the future holds; he  hopes that with the increased income as a result of a high yield, he will finally be able to afford to educate his children; Meshak and  Obadiah. Hassan’s dreams do not end here: “ultimately, I want to ensure my children are educated and have professional jobs”, he expressed.

name: Habib
description: Habib, 44, lives in Beirut and owns a mini-market that caters to his local neighbors. Habib has requested a loan of $1000 USD from Al Majmoua to purchase a large stock of items for his shop. This will be Habib's second loan with Al Majmoua. His first was repaid in full and on time.

name: Phuong
description: Thanks to her previous loan, Phuong was able to increase her stock of poultry and support her family with the income that she earned.   Phuong would like to further invest in her poultry business by taking another loan to buy more chickens and ducks for raising and selling.   She hopes that with this loan, her income will continue to increase and she can continue to improve the living conditions of her family.

name: Mary Joy
description: Mary Joy is 35 years old and married with six children.  She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 26,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional stock to sell such as canned goods, eggs, milk, sugar, etc.  Mary Joy has borrowed and paid back 7 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 10 years and also earns an income from motorcycle transport.  She aspires to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Hsu Ka Lat Village
description: The fund will help 24 members of Hsu Ka Lat Village Group. The featured borrower, Sein, is 58 years old and married with eight children. The parents are proud that some of their children are working on their own and some are studying. The family has six acres of crop farm and Sein has forty years of experiences in the crop farming business.   Proximity Design's loan will help him to purchase gas for crop machines and fertilizers for the farm.  His goal for this year is to hire more labors than previous years and expand the crop farm up to nine acres. Sein is also taken as leader for social occasions held in the village and has helped many people in their downtimes.   Pictured above are the members of Hsu Ka Lat Village, named, Sein, Mya, Chin, Kat, Chit and Myint. The whole group is comprised of 24 village customers and they will be helped to purchase gas and fertilizers for their farms from Proximity's loan.   The village is located in Ayeyarwaddy Delta Region in Upper Myanmar. They mainly focus on crop farming and also do the plantations.

name: Elvira
description: Elvira is 42 years old and married, with three children.  She earns a living by farming sugarcane in the Philippines. Elvira is borrowing PHP 19,500 through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to buy fertilizer and other farm supplies.  Elvira has been farming sugarcane for three years and also earns additional income from buy-and-sell charcoal and vegetables.  She successfully paid back her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her farming sugarcane and buy-and-sell charcoal and vegetables businesses. Elvira is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save enough money, so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Kem
description: Kem S. H., 27, lives in the Kampong Cham province with her husband and two young children. She makes about $3 daily, selling groceries, while her husband makes $1.50 as a policeman. She is asking for a loan in the amount of $1200 to purchase more groceries to expand her current shop. She is also hoping to purchase a pig to raise and sell with the money from the loan. She sees this loan as a great opportunity to expand her business and is confident that she will see her income increase as a result.

name: Caroline
description: Caroline is 29 years old, single with two children who go to school. She runs a boutique where she sells clothes to earn a living. Her business is located in Embakasi, a few kilometers away from the capital city, Nairobi. She has employed one person. She hopes to grow her business and offer her children a better education in the future.    She has requested a loan of Kes 20,000 from Faulu Kenya to buy men’s shirts, dress tops, and dresses.

name: Mary Jane
description: Mary Jane lives in Tiaman, Bonifacio, Misamis Occidental with her family. She is married with an only child. Her husband worked as a carpenter and she operates their own general store selling goods in their community. She has been six years in this business.  In 2010, she joined Gata Daku MPC and recently borrowed a loan to buy additional goods to offer like dried fish and bagoong (shrimp paste). She plans to expand her business and hopes to support her child's education in the future.

name: Minaver
description: Minaver S. is 27-year-old single woman who lives in the southern region Imishli with her parents. She has six years of experience in animal breeding. Minaver covers all the family's needs. Her parents are very old and ill people. Half of the money she earns she spends on medicine and the rest for food. Minaver's father got ill when she was fifteen and she left school as soon as she finished ninth grade. She didn’t get a university degree and now she is unemployed. Keeping cattle is the only  financial source in her family. This is a very hard time for her and her family. She has applied for 800 USD with repayment term of 15 months. With this amount she is going to purchase one milking cow. Minaver is certain that a milking cow will bring her good income; she would be able to sell milk and yoghurt to the local bazaar traders and to the neighbors.  Owning the cow would allow her family to always have cheese, butter and yoghurt.

name: Valeryi
description: Valeryi offers taxi services in Ivano-Frankivsk. He has been working in this sphere of business for 2 years. Valeryi admits he has benefited a lot from financial assistance he has received from Nadiya Ukraine. Currently, his business has grown to the point where he receives about US$ 40-50 daily.   Valeryi is hoping to buy a better and trendier vehicle in the future to offer more high-class services to his clients. At this point he is only saving some money to make his dream come true. Valeryi thinks this 5000 Grivna loan will help him move closer to the fulfillment of his plans. He is hoping to spend this amount on painting the body of his vehicle to give it a fresh look. Some day when he saves enough, he is hoping to buy a newer but affordable vehicle.

name: Rajmati Kumari
description: Rajmati Kumari is a 21-year-old married woman(the man in the photo is her husband) with two children. They live in a small village called Ghusukpur Tole in Kalaiya Municipality of the Bara district of Nepal.   Within their own house, she has set up a small grocery shop where she sells different types of products like rice, pulse, sugar, etc. She has established herself as a successful micro-entrepreneur in her locality.   As a result of the success of her shop, she feels it is high time to make certain changes to the business. In particular, she wants to make the shop bigger and offer a wider range of products like rice, pulse, sugar, oil, and other non-food items. So, she requested the loan amount of 40,000 Nepalese Rupees to carry out this expansion.   She has very good personal references within her community.

name: Cresencia
description: Cresencia is 60 years old, married, and has four children. She lives in Jemeniz, Misamis Occidental. She owns and operates a retail general store in the local community to earn a living. She has been with her business for over 10 years, and she earns 9,000 PHP every month.  She joined GDMPC in the year 2008, and now she has requested a loan of 10,000 PHP to purchase additional products to sell, like coffee, sugar, shampoo, soap and canned goods. She plans to use the additional profit generated, to improve and expand her business.

name: Ali
description: Ali is a forty-eight-year-old married man, and a father of five children. He has worked as a taxi driver since 2005, and his business is going just fine especially during the high season in the summer when there are tourists. His business is his source of livelihood, which is why he has to take good care of it.   Unfortunately his car's engine broke and he needs additional cash to buy a new engine. This is why he applied for a loan for the first time from Kiva partner Al Majmoua, and he's sure that it will help his business and family a lot.

name: Shahida
description: Shahida is a 55-year-old married woman. She is a mother of seven children and is motivated to provide for her family. She has been facing a lot of problems due to the large family; she has also been facing rainy days due to the low income of her husband.   Her son has been successfully running a small general store in his community for the last year. He offers various goods for daily use. He has good communication skills and counts on a good client list.  Her husband is employed in a small factory and earns insufficient income to support his family alone.   As she wants to grow the business of her son, she requested a loan from Kiva’s field partner, BRAC Pakistan, so that her son can buy stock of rice, sugar and flour from the wholesalers at lower rates. He then would be able to meet the increasing demands consistently.   She is in her seventh loan cycle, and has shown excellent repayment behavior. She has already been investing the amount of her last loan in the same business. She wishes to use part of the revenues to deal with personal expenses and increase her business capital.  She says thanks to Kiva and to it's field partner, BRAC Pakistan.

name: Juntos Para El Exito Group
description: Cintia is 26 years old, single, and has 3 children. For 5 years now she has sold shoes (sandals, shoes, etc.) Cintia has established a loyal customer base which has generated earnings enabling her to cover household expenses.  In the future, Cintia would like to open a shop where she can sell her merchandise and obtain greater earnings. She will use her loan to purchase added footwear.  Cintia and all the other group members are grateful to Kiva for facilitating this loan and for the confidence they have demonstrated in them.   Cintia appears in the photo seated behind the table. She bids goodbye, offering the promise that she will comply with all her proposed targets.

name: Silver
description: Sliver is married with ten children, six of whom are in school while the others are helping him on the farm. Silver deals in cattle fattening as his main source of income. He buys baby cows, feeds them for some period of time and later sells them for a big profit. He has applied for a loan of UGX 2,000,000 to help him buy more cows for fattening. He also has hopes of taking his children back to school after increasing his income. His major challenge is inadequate income for running his business which has affected his progress. Despite these challenges, Silver is a very honest and hardworking man.

name: Al
description: Al L. is 28 years old and single. He is living in the peaceful place of Barangay San Roque Enrile, Cagayan, together with his parents and siblings. He has been operating a sari-sari store business (community-based variety store) in their village for four years. He is also engaged in the rice-retailing business as another source of income to help provide the needs of his parents.   He wants his business to grow, for it is a great help in meeting the needs of his family. He is able to assist his parents by earning an income that is being utilized for the daily allowances of his siblings, who are attending school.  He wants to borrow additional capital for his business because he needs more merchandise, such as rice, biscuits, canned goods and soft drinks, for the improvement of his store. He is in need of 7,000 PHP, and this will be used to buy more goods to meet the demands of his customers. He hopes that Kiva lenders will consider his request.

name: Junith
description: Junith works hard to support her family. Junith is married and has a fish-vending business in the Philippines.  She requested a PHP 12,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional boxes of fish to sell.  Junith has been in this business for 20 years now.  In the future, Junith would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Bebiana
description: Bebiana is a merchant from Bien Unido, Bohol. She is a married woman and a mother of two children. Bebiana operates a sari-sari or convenience store where she sells various goods and items to the people in her area.  Bebiana is asking for a loan to buy more stock of goods to sell in her store such as detergents, toiletries and seasonings. With this loan, she will be able to improve the variety of her stock, which will attract more buyers. In the future, Bebiana hopes to make her business a success to ensure that it provides a sustainable source of income.

name: Mirna
description: Mirna, 23, is married and is studying to be a nurse. She also works as a housemaid.She is a young girl who wants to get ahead in life and improve her standard of living.Her dream is to graduate with good qualifications, find a good job and offer her family a better quality of life.She is asking for this loan to be able to buy supplies for university so she can continue with her studies.

name: Pov
description: Pov, age 51, is a local farmer form Kandal province. She is a mother of five dependent children. For her family's living, she grows rice, as a single source of income.This is her third loan cycle with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). She has fully repaid her past loans. She used them wisely, to improve her living conditions at a gradual pace. She will spend her entire loan to pay tuition for her daughter, who wants to pursue the bachelor degree majoring in Nursing. She hopes that her daughter can get a good job, after graduation.

name: Cipriano
description: Cipriano is 59 years old and has four children. Cipriano is married, and one of his children is still in school.  Cipriano is in the agricultural business of pig fattening in the Philippines. Cipriano requested a 12,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy feeds and vitamins for his pigs.  Cipriano has been in pig fattening for 20 years now, and has borrowed 12 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  Cipriano would like to build and expand his business to secure the future of his family.

name: Taliko
description: Taliko is 46 years old. She is a widow and lives with her 24-year-old son – Otar. The main source of the income of the family is farming. They grow tomatoes, potatoes, maize and onions on family-owned land. Also, Taliko has chickens and a milk cow and produces cheese. She sells harvested produce in nearby villages. In addition, to their agricultural business Taliko works in the local school. She is an accountant and gets a salary. Otar works in the police and gets a salary as well. The total average monthly income of the family is 1000 Lari.  Taliko requested a loan for purchasing fertilizers and seedlings of tomatoes. She will cultivate the land and sow more tomatoes and other vegetables there. She will work hard during spring and summer seasons and after the seasonal work is properly done, she hopes to get a good harvest. As a result of the above-mentioned activities, Taliko will get additional income. With increased income she will be able to repair the house. Taking into account the above-mentioned, the living conditions of the family will improve.

name: Aida María
description: The members of the Salud y Vida Communal Bank meet every 15 days in the city of Charapoto.  This place is known for its traditional culture and for being a few minutes from two of the best beaches in the province – San Jacinto and San Clemente.  This is where we met Aida.  She is 66 years old and separated but she had five children from a marriage from several years ago.  Her children are all adults and one of them lives with her, as he is a little sick and keeps her company.  She has a grocery store in the market of Charapoto where she sells all types of products like rice, sugar, oil, detergent, etc.  She works every day from 7am to 8pm and tells us that she has had her store for thirty years and she loves being there.  Aida buys her products in the center of Portoviejo, although she receives the majority of her products at her store.  She will use this loan to stock her store, buying rice, sugar, oil, detergents, cold cuts, and other basic needs products.  She has been with the communal bank since the beginning and she likes it because these loans are very important for her business.  Her goals are to continue getting ahead in life and to enjoy good health.

name: Radha
description: Radha, 50 years old, is married and has two children. Many years ago, she established her grocery shop business. Working seven days a week and 12 hours a day, she supports her family. She has already received and successfully repaid six loans from Patan BPW and used her most recent loan to buy grocery goods. In the future, she plans to uplift her family's economic condition. She thanks you for your support. In the Kathmandu Valley, the small grocery store, called a pasal, is an important part of the local economy. Fresh produce, milk, and staples such as rice, lentils, and flour are purchased daily for cooking in the home. While a typical pasal might be no more than 100 sq. feet, they are always full of bargaining customers, incoming produce, and shrewd businesswomen. Owners of small grocery stores use Kiva loans to increase their purchasing power and profit margins. By keeping inventory strong and purchasing in larger amounts, owners of these small stores are able to increase profitability.

name: Katiuska
description: Katiuska is 32 years old. She lives with her spouse and they have three schoolage children together. They live together in the community of Santa Rosa, where they have their own house made of wood. Despite not having finished primary school,  Katiuska was undaunted by the adversity in her path. She summoned the necessary strength to start her own business, specifically in agriculture.  Today she produces and sells considerable amounts of cacao to her biggest customers. This brings her good income, due to the timely delivery to each of her customers. Normally, she works with her spouse, but at harvest and planting time she hires farmhands so that it is easier to extract the cacao product and then sell it in the stockpiling centers of her community. Her plan for the future is to expand to other areas. For this she will look for new cropland in strategic areas with the purpose of minimizing time and cost.  This is her first loan with MFP. She is committed to making the payments according to schedule. She is also happy with her communal bank, since it has been very beneficial. With the loan that she is asking for, she plans oninvesting in giving her cacao plantings suitable maintenance.   Translated from Spanish by Ellen Donohue, Kiva Volunteer

name: La Iglesia Group
description: The “La Iglesia” group has three enterprising and hard-working women as members.  The group’s leader is 32-year-old Sadia, who is single. She currently makes a living selling cosmetics and new clothes. Sadia is applying for a loan in order to buy products, such as cosmetics, perfumes, colognes, creams, blouses, trousers, shirts and blouses.  The other members of this group are 45-year-old Rosario who has been preparing and selling tortillas for 12 years; and Gilma, 57, who makes a living selling meals and also working in farming.

name: Josephine
description: Josephine is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a general store business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to purchase more groceries to sell for her general store business.  Josephine has been in this business for seven years. Josephine earns additional income from food vending.  Josephine has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Jumagul
description: Jumagul Y. is the mother of two kids.  Unfortunately, her husband died several years ago, so she had to find a way to survive and feed her kids. First she started by selling kilograms of flour at the market.  Now she has a constant clientele who buy flour from her. But in order to keep her clients, she needs to expand her business and provide more flour. The money she gets from her business now is barely enough to feed her kids. So she decided to borrow money so that she can expand her business.

name: Elcita Mercedes
description: In the Crucita parish of Portoviejo Canton is a place known as Los Arenales, where once a fortnight the Grupo de Crédito Nueva Generación (New Generation Credit Group) meet. The area is known for its beautiful beaches, gastronomy and friendly people.  This is where Elcita lives. She is 51 years old, married with two grown up children, one of whom still lives with her. Her husband earns a living by fishing.  Elcita is a very hardworking woman who likes to earn her own living to help her husband with the household expenses. She runs a snack bar in a school in Los Arenales, selling sandwiches, "corviches" (dough made from grated plantain, deep fried and stuffed with spicy fish or minced meat, topped with salad, mayo, chili), turnovers, juices, soft drinks and water among other snacks.   All her food is prepared as naturally and nutritiously as possible to offer delicious food to her customers. She has run this business for several years and she enjoys her work.  This loan is to buy provisions for the preparation of food. She has belonged to this credit group for three loan cycles and likes the help she receives from being in the group. Her dreams are to be able to give her family the best in life.

name: Neoline's Group
description: Neoline's group is comprised of two hardworking women. Noeline is 20 years old and lives in the town of Bowama in the Masaka region of Uganda. She is single and has one child who is currently in school. For the past six months, Noeline has been working hard to manage her retail shop, which sells cosmetic items.   To help expand her business, Neoline has requested a loan of 300,000 Ugandan Shillings (UGX) from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy more cosmetic lotions to sell. This will help Neoline to generate greater profits to buy basic needs for her family. Neoline hopes that in the future, she will be able to expand the business into a wholesale shop.   Neoline is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities and a forum for life-skills training.

name: Asenta
description: Asenta K. is currently in the business of washing and ironing customers' clothes at the laundry shop and is requesting a loan to stock more bags of washing powder and boxes of soap.  Asenta is 31 years old and is widowed.  She has three children and her children go to school.  With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to build a dry cleaning machine.   BRAC's holistic approach to poverty alleviation and empowerment of the poor encompasses a range of core programs in economic and social development, health, education, human rights and legal services, which are delivered through an extensive network of village organizations. BRAC has become one of the world's largest NGOs as measured by the scale and diversity of its interventions.  In 2007, BRAC started operations in Southern Sudan. The microfinance program, which is targeted towards returning war refugees, has already formed 418 village organizations with more than 14,000 women members.

name: Baraka - Kibaha Group
description: Silvia, who is in her early 40s is married with one child who is still in school. She has been running a beauty salon for one year now. She works from 8am to 7pm daily and is able to make a small monthly profit.This will be Silvia's first loan from Tujijenge Tanzania. She will use this loan to buy up-to-date salon products to meet her customers' requirement. She dreams of opening a grocery store.Silvia will share this loan with her loan group "Baraka - Kibaha" which consists of eleven members who will hold each other accountable for paying back the loan.

name: United For Progress Group
description: Dennis S. is a leader of a group of five borrowers called United for Progress. He is 32 years old and married. He and his family live and work in the VOA community, north of Liberia’s capital, Monrovia. Dennis and his wife have four children, ages three to twelve years old, who attend school (nursery school to seventh grade). He also cares for a little brother and a sibling. Dennis is a high school graduate who was formerly working in agriculture.  Dennis’ business now is selling general goods such as underwear, soap, candles,  etc., which he buys from wholesalers and sells at retail to residents of his community. Dennis sells at an affordable price and talks to customers in a friendly manner in order to encourage customers to continue buying from him. He has been in business for a year and hopes to improve his sales as time goes on.  Dennis started his business with 9400 LD that he had saved when he was farming. He now needs a loan to purchase more goods like underwear, toothpaste, soap, etc. to expand his business. He dreams of giving his children a better education and improving their living conditions.

name: Archil
description: Archil is 37 years old. He lives in Ikalto village,Telavi district, with his 37 year-old wife, Natia, and retired parents. Archil requested a loan from local financial institutions several times for a family business start-up, but without any success. His loan request was rejected every time, because of low income and the family’s poor living conditions.  The family has a vineyard and a small plot of agricultural land. They grow grapes and different kinds of vegetables. Harvested products are sold locally at the markets. Archil also has a car. He is working on private orders and transports different kinds of cargo to bring additional income to the family. Archil requested a loan from Credo to start up a family business. His loan request was approved in the frame of a new joint initiative of Kiva and Credo. The Start-up loan program envisages the provision of business start-up and re-startup credits with soft conditions to country rural poor.  These people do not have access to credit products, being regarded as “high risk borrowers” because of low income. With the received credit, Archil will purchase two damaged cars. He will dismantle them for parts and will start selling them separately. As car parts are highly requested in his area, Archil will make a good profit from his new business. Increased income will significantly improve the living conditions of the family.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth is a single woman with three children, all of whom attend school. She lives in a rental house that has electricity and piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are school fees and transportation.   She has been selling firewood for over two years. She supplies at wholesale to Pwani Oil Company. Elizabeth faces the major challenge of the high cost of transportation. She hopes to establish a company selling cars in the future.  With the Kshs 40,000, she wants to purchase firewood logs and pay for a business permit. She decided to join Yehu to get a loan to improve her business.

name: Lawrence
description: Lawrence, a 49-year-old married father of three children, lives in Hioma, Uganda where he has been a primary school teacher for 22 years. His personal goal is to educate his children, and his business goal is to complete the construction of his rental houses.Faced with the challenges of price fluctuations and inflation, Lawrence is requesting a loan to complete building his rental houses.

name: Kallon Drive Group
description: Aminata is a forty-five years old business woman and a member of Kallon Drive solidarity group, which has four members, all of whom are women. Aminata sells charcoal and has been in this business for the past fifteen years. She opens her business six days in a week from 8am to 6pm. Aminata established her business to help support her children in school. She pays school fees, buys learning material and provides food from the profit she gets from her business. Aminata and her group members need a loan totaling 4,000,000 SLL of which Aminata is entitled to 1,500,000 SLL which she will use to buy 100 bags of charcoal for her business. She hopes that this loan will help her generate more profit to support her family. Aminata is married and has 3 children, some of whom are in school. Aminata was able to improve her stock level during the previous loan.  One of her children graduated from the university and is now a teacher in one of the schools in Freetown. In the future, Aminata still plans to save more money to provide for her children’s university education and to acquire land to build a house for her retirement age. Aminata will be very appreciative to anyone that can help.

name: Luzviminda
description: Luzviminda E. is from the village of Marabulig One, Cauayan City,Isabela. She is 44 years old, married and has six school-aged children. To make a living, Luzviminda owns a general store and she sells lots of beverages.  Luzviminda has been in business for over 30 years and earns approximately 4,000 PHP a month.  In 2008, Luzviminda joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Luzviminda is requesting a new loan of 20000 PHP to purchase new items to expand her product offerings.  This will be the third loan taken out by Luzviminda from ASKI.  She plans to use the additional revenue generated to improve and expand her business.  ---------------------- About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 25 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly of farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.

name: Gilda
description: Gilda is 35 years old and married with 5 children.  With 2 children in school, Gilda works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a sari-sari (variety) store in the Philippines and requested a 10,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase stock for her sari-sari store to sell.  Gilda has been in this business for 4 years and sells a variety of items such as candies, chocolates, biscuits, etc.  In the future Gilda would like to send her children to school.

name: Kotognogontala Group
description: The members of the Kotognogontala group are married women who, on average, are 32 years old and have four children. They live mostly in monogamous families in the Bougoula neighborhood, one of the outer areas of the town of Sikasso, third administrative region of Mali. The group is on their ninth loan with the micro-finance institution Soro Yiriwaso, in order to satisfy their customers' needs.  In this group of women, Ami sells condiments. She is the first person seated on the right in the photo. With her loan she plans to buy 30 baskets of tomatoes and 20 packets of Maggi cubes. She sells these goods at a market and from home for cash to male and female customers.   Ami hopes to earn an average monthly profit of 60,000 francs CFA, in which a part will be used to pay back the loan and the interest and the other part will be put in savings.

name: Evangelyn
description: Evangelyn is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a fishing business in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 16,000 through NWTF to buy additional materials such as fishing net, gasoline, wood, bamboo, etc. for her fishing business.Evangelyn has been in this business for eight years. She earns more income from pig fattening and fish vending.She successfully paid back her previous loan, and now she has requested an additional loan to further build her business.Evangelyn has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college in the future.

name: Ablavi
description: Ablavi is 44 years old and married to an entrepreneur. She has three children, two of whom go to school. They range in age from 8 to 15 years old.   Ablavi has been in the restaurant business since 2008. She works from her home, and is not currently facing any major obstacle. She buys her supplies in Lomé.   Ablavi is seeking her first loan from WAGES to buy rice, tomatoes, and corn oil. She wants to reinvest in her activity.  In the coming years, Ablavi would like to expand her business. She will use her profits to improve her family’s living conditions.

name: Helen
description: Helen, 37 years old, is single and lives in a village close to Nabatieh in the South of Lebanon. Helen is very hardworking and determined to make a difference in her family life. She bakes delicious flat bread on a "Saj," the bakery equipment you can see on the picture. She named her business Al Jawhar (Arabic: The Jewel) and needs a loan of US$300 to purchase ingredients and fuel.  This is the first time Helen has requested a loan from Al Majmoua. She promises to repay her loan on time and thereby prove her seriousness.

name: Berlisa
description: Berlisa M. is from the village of Mabini, Baliangao, Misamis Occidental.  She is 51 years old. Berlisa is married and has 1 adult-aged child. To make a living, Berlisa owns and operates a business venture in retailing. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling of variety of goods in the local community. Berlisa has been engaged in her business for more than 10 years and earns approximately 2,000.00 PHP net a month for these activities. In 2005, Berlisa joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Berlisa has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5000 PHP from PMPC. Berlisa is requesting a new loan of 3000 PHP which will be used for additional capital of sari-sari store. This loan will be the 3rd cycle loan taken out by Berlisa from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of the borrower's family. About PMPC: Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model. *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Samer
description: Samer is a 31-year-old, married man from Rafah city, which is located in the Gaza Strip. He works as an employee in the public sector, where he gets a low income. This income barely covers all the family needs, but he wants to make his family more comfortable and improve their standard of living.  So, Samer  took a USD loan from FATEN, which will enable him to buy a solar system for heating water for his family home. By taking this loan, Samer  will be able to decrease the electricity expenses, while using a cleaner form of energy (rather than gas). Samer ’s family will have an easier time heating water for showers, cooking, and also washing clothes and dishes.   Samer  appears in the photo.

name: Rozilmo
description: Rozilmo is one of these individuals who try to improve living conditions and stimulate the economic conditions of their family. She is married, 56 years old, and she is raising three children. Her husband works as a teacher in high school and receives a small pay. Her oldest children also work, but their income is not sufficient to provide the family with all necessary means.   Rozilmo decided to help her husband and children for the family's benefit. With this aim she attended the course "Bring It On", organized by the Association for Business Women, and she received a certificate. Now she may start her own business and become successful in this area.   Rozilmo would like to set up a business of buying and selling vegetables at the local market, as she has experience in this type of business. She plans to use the income received to provide her children and grandchildren with a good education and hearty food. She requests a loan in the amount of 2,500 somoni for the purchase of food products in order to set up the new business. She awaits your kindness.

name: Tilia
description: Tilia is 38 years old and married with nine children. She works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a buy and sell charcoal in the Philippines and requested a PHP 30,000 loan through NWTF to buy more sacks of charcoal to sell.  Tilia has been in this business for 4 years.  In the future Tilia would like to save enough to build a house for her family.

name: Mercis
description: Mercis is applying for her second loan with Kiva and Mifex. She is a 42 year-old single mother with 4 children, one of whom still lives in the household. When she took out her first loan, Mercis had a stand a where she sold fish to the public during the morning and early afternoon. Thanks to the extra profits from her first loan, she now also sells food in a market starting around 8 pm. She buys extra fish every morning for her stand and she prepares the food with whatever is leftover. Now that her business is growing, Mercis hopes to be able to invest in the necessary utensils and tables for the business. She hopes that she will eventually be able to own a restaurant with her hard work. Most of all though, Mercis wants to finish raising her last child and live with peace of mind.   Mifex offers its clients microinsurance and access to business training and educational programs. For more information about microfinance, Ecuador, and our services, please visit www.mifex.org.

name: Benjamin Mwanzia
description: Benjamin is a 36 year-old businessman who runs a general store at Umoja innercore Estate, which is a highly populated estate. He is married to Annastaia Ngina, who is 26 years old, and they have a two-year-old daughter.   Benjamin has been running his general store for four years and his monthly income is 24,500 KES. He was introduced to KADET by another client and is requesting a loan of 50,000 KES to buy 25 bags of flour (each bag costs 2,000 KES). This is his first loan with KADET, and if his business improves, Benjamin will help the needy such as orphans and helping develop nearby schools.   Benjamin describes himself as a hardworking person who dreams of lifting the living standards of his family.

name: Maria Tomasa
description: Maria Tomasa runs a store selling consumer goods from her home. She also raises animals. Maria is seeking a loan to buy items for her store and chickens.   She is a very responsible person and has had other loans with FAPE, always repaying them punctually. Her dream is to expand her business and buy more stock for it so she can provide her customers with better service.

name: Garik
description: Garik is 37 years old. He lives in Nor Dvin village with his wife and 4-year-old son. He has a plot of land where he grows 300 appletrees.   As agriculture is the only source of income for Garik, he wants to expand that business. With the requested amount Garik will purchase polyethylene cover for his greenhouse and tomato seeds. This will enable him to grow more vegetables and thus increase the family income. This new business initiative will significantly improve the living conditions of the family.
town: Nor Dvin village of Ararat region

name: Zurab
description: Zurab is 37 years old. He lives in Rustavi district with his wife and three children. His wife is unemployed and she stays home and raises the children.  Zurab works as a security guard at the railway station and gets a small monthly income, which is not enough to cover everyday costs.   Zurab decided to start a trading business and requested a loan. The Start Up program, which is a joint initiative with Kiva and Credo, enables him to get a loan of 1,500 USD. With the received credit, he will purchase a car online and will resell it in Rustavi to generate income.   Zurab is very motivated to generate more income in order to improve the living conditions of his family.

name: La Virginia Group
description: This group is called "La Virginia", and is part of a programme to eliminate poverty. The 17 women that make up the close knit, self sacrificing group want to overcome whatever situation they may find themselves in. Andrea is one of the members of the group, and makes a living by selling clothes. The effort she makes to improve herself to provide a better life for her family is worth emphasizing . Andrea is grateful for the opportunity she has by being a part of this group. She is asking for a loan to buy goods for sale, such as: green vegetables, fruit, meat, vegetables, baked goods and so forth. This will allow her to firm up her business plan and help to improve her income.

name: Verónica Maria
description: Veronica Maria Beltran Hernandez lives in Zaragoza in the province of La Libertad. Veronica is 25 years old and is a single mother with two children, Stephanie, 10 years old, and Camilla, seven months old. Veronica sells pupusas on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. She earns a forty-six percent profit on what she sells. Veronica is asking for a loan for supplies to make more papusas. She would like to increase her production forty-six percent, equal to her earnings.Translated from Spanish by Esther Levandoski, Kiva Volunteer

name: Noemi
description: The member belongs to the "ILLARY III communal bank. She continues to work in her grocery store business. She is an an enterprising woman who hopes to continue to support her family through her business. She continues to sell different kinds of products like rice, sugar and milk amongst others. This is the way she gets ahead with her family. The member is requesting the loan to buy oil, milk and legumes amongst others. She thanks the investors and promises to comply with her payments.

name: Florence's Group
description: Florence is a 42-year-old mother of six and a businesswoman. She buys and sells sisal; her husband is a dryland farmer. Her trade business faces the challenge of price fluctuations at the market due to varying demand, and sometimes she has to sell her sisal for no profit. Florence says, "My favorite part of KOMAZA is how the future appears promising because the trees grow very fast." With the proceeds from her KOMAZA tree farm, she plans to pay her children's education fees and expand her business.

name: Julie
description: As a married parent of five children, Julie works hard to support her family.She has a fishing business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from raising livestock. Julie is borrowing PHP 13000 through NWTF to buy fishing gear and other equipment for her fishing business.Julie has been sustaining her business activities through her past 25 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: Lucia
description: Lucia is 50 years old, single, and has three children and three grandchildren. She is a native of Cusco, Peru. Lucia is part of a communal bank consisting of 16 neighbors who live in Cusco. The group is called Santa Rosita de Lima, named after a virgin of Peru.    Lucia sells bedroom products, such as sheets, pillow cases, etc. that she buys from wholesalers in Cusco. She sells goods worth approximately 1,400 to 1,500 PEN each week, but the business is not steady. She will use her loan to buy more products to sell. Lucia appreciates and thanks you for the loan and promises to make the monthly payments on time.

name: Beatriz Elena
description: Beatriz is a person who has always been known for being a hard worker.  This quality has enabled her three children to move forward since she is a single mother  and the head of her household.  A short time ago, Beatriz established her business so that she could generate income after leaving her job.  She manages a stationery shop where she offers her customer excellent service.  Her business was started with very little capital, so Beatriz is taking this opportunity to access a loan so that she can buy paper products to restock her business and provide a wider variety of products to her customers.    Even though her business has been in existence for a short time, Beatriz has been able to hire one employee.  She hopes that her business continues to grow so that she can create more jobs to those who need them the most.  In addition, she dreams that this business generates good income so that her children can enjoy a good quality of life and have access to a high-quality education.

name: Maura Del Rosario
description: Maura is a member of the communal bank named "Las Orquideas", meaning "The Orchids". It is located in the district of Calleria in the department of Ucayali. She is 44 years old, married, and she has an adolescent son.   Her first loan helped her to start up another business that did not require a large investment. Currently, she sells articles of clothing, wallets, shoes, and other accessories. She has been working with loans from Manuela Ramos (Kiva Field Partner) for the last three years. The funds are invested in the purchase of merchandise. In Lima she has someone who takes care of all the shipments.  Her new loan is in the amount of S/.1500 nuevos soles and with it she will purchase: 18 pairs of shoes, and 10 wallets. She will resell the products at affordable prices to be able to bring in more products in less time.  She is able to help her husband with the household expenses through her business. One income is not enough to cover the household expenses. She has a son who has many school-related expenses. Her husband is who covers the food bill for the month and some other basic expenses. She takes care of the other expenses.  She is thankful to Manuela Ramos (Kiva Field Partner) for giving her the opportunity to bring her ideas to light.

name: Johna
description: As a married mother of two children, Johna works hard to support her family.  She has a business selling school supplies in the Philippines and earns additional income from tricycle transport. Johna is borrowing PHP 29,500 through NWTF to purchase more school supplies to sell.  Johna has been sustaining her business activities through her past 12 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving money to expand her business.

name: Gs Nueva Jutiapa Group
description: Sr. Juan is a merchant whose main business activity is selling groceries, but he also performs bicycle repairs and sells the respective spare parts.  He has been in business for more than 10 years.  Don Juan is a hardworking individual and his clientele are from the area and include people who live in the mountains near his community.  Through his business, he has been able to move forward since it is one his main sources of income.  He knows how to attract customers because he gives them special attention.  As a result, he is well-liked in the community.  Don Juan will use his loan to buy tires, chains, rims, handles, cables, rice, corn, lard, soap, detergent, oil, soft drinks, bread, coffee, eggs, and other items.  This will enable him to have a better business.  As a result, he will be able to cover his household expenses and provide a better quality of life for his family.  Don Juan dreams of having a workshop with all of the necessary equipment.  The other members are as follows: •	Don Danilo is a merchant whose main business activity is selling groceries and butchered cows.  He has eight years of experience. •	Don Jorge is a merchant who also has a grocery store.  He has three years of experience.  Danli El Paraíso, Honduras - October 2012

name: Mariam
description: Mariam is a married woman with 5 children, all of whom attend school. She lives in a rental house that neither has electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.   For the past six years, she has operated a food kiosk business selling food including maize flour and cooking fat to her neighbors and passersby. She mentioned high cost and seasonality as her major challenges. She dreams of establishing a wholesale shop in the future.  With the KES 30,000 she wants to purchase maize flour, rice, beans, sugar and cooking oil. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Esperanza Y Progreso Group
description: The “ ESPERANZA Y PROGRESO” group is in its 28th cycle and has been on time with its payments.  This group is made up of five enterprising women who have various businesses.  Naomi is the group's secretary.  She's 37 years old, married, and has three children.  She has been selling food for the past 19 years and works for INABIF.  She makes chocoteja in her spare time.  Her greatest desire is to have a fast food restaurant.  She will use the money from this loan to buy chairs and tables.  The group is grateful to the Kiva lenders.  Naomi is the first one on the left.

name: Emelda
description: Emelda is 44 years old and married with seven children, three of whom are in school. She works very hard to provide for her family.Emelda runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like shampoo, soap, milk, sugar, canned goods, etc. She has been in this business for 10 years.In the future, Emelda would like to save enough money that she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Narcisa
description: Narcisa is married with four children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur. Narcisa is 42 years old and has three children who are in school.  Narcisa has a fish vending business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 8,000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase additional fish to sell.  Narcisa has been in this business for 23 years. In the future, she would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Joyce
description: Joyce is 47 years old and married with seven children.  With six children in school, Joyce works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 13,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like shampoo, groceries, etc. She has been in this business for three years.   In the future Joyce would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Gift
description: Gift is a single man and he operates a retail business where he sells sugar, bread, flour, soap and other items. He has been involved in this business for 5 years. His business is located in an area with potential and his primary customers are locals. He describes his biggest business challenge to be low stock.   He will use the Kes 100,000 loan to buy more stock of sugar, flour, rice and other items. His business goal is to have a supermarket within 5 years. This is his fifth loan with SMEP Microfinance bank. Previous loan was repaid successfully.

name: Emmanuel
description: Emmanuel is a 34-year-old married man with one child. He lives in Fort Portal, Uganda. He owns a stationery shop and repairs computers and photocopiers.   Insufficient electricity supply in the area affects his business operations. His dreams are to buy a generator or solar system to help him run his business efficiently and to restock his stationery shop.   Emmanuel intends to use the loan to buy box files and paper to sell.

name: Chan's Group
description: Chan’s group live in a rural village in Kompong Thom province in Cambodia. Chan makes a living cultivating rice to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women and this man to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Sareth
description: Sareth is a 32-year-old garment-factory worker and she is single. She has worked as a garment-factory worker since 2010. She lives with her old father and a brother in the Kampong Speu Province of Cambodia. Being a garment-factory worker, Sareth can earn approximately $5 a day. Now she would like to request a loan to buy clothes to resell in her free time from work. This loan will help her earn more income to support the family. In the future, she is going to renovate her house.

name: Lenchonghoi Group
description: 26-year-old unmarried Linroukim is the featured borrower member for Lenchonghoi group. Graduated from a government college and possessed a caring and strong personality, sincerity in work and  great determination is Linroukim’s character. She is on the extreme left in the picture with her hand raised. All eight members belongs to a tribal community and live in a village which is about 40 kms away from the state capital of Imphal, which is one of the North-Eastern state capital in India. As an eldest daughter in the family, she takes on the role with passion and has shown immense sincerity in whatever she does for the family and for herself.  Linroukim runs a general store in the village. The store is located at the other end of the village, on the closer side of the town market. The town market is where people from all neighbouring villages have stores and run their businesses. She sells imported rice, salt, chillies, sugar, milk, potatoes, onions, ginger, garlic, different items of cereals, detergent soap, detergent powder, hair oil, sachets of shampoo, local delicacies, etc. She is in charge of the store only in the morning and in the afternoon as she teaches in primary private school during the daytime. Her mother usually replaces her in daytime and she closes the accounts at the end of the day.   Linroukim's father’s income is insufficient to support the family with her three younger siblings in different schools. She initiated all possible ways to share her father’s burden and started earning by opening a general store besides teaching in a school. On restricted holidays she usually gets the supplies from the town market and sells them in the village. The generated income is not enough to refill the stocks on a regular basis as her father’s income in unreliable and irregular. Most of the expenditure is borne by her to fulfill the family's needs.  She wants a loan from Kiva to purchase more supplies for the store. She will buy all the essential goods like rice, edible oil, wheat by the bag, flour by the bag, soaps, shampoos etc. Expansion of the store is the vital plan as she wishes to continue the general store even after she is married. Another future plan she has with her family is to re-construct their house; the leaking roof during rainy season and the dilapidated condition of the roof and mud walls needs to change. If their plans are successful then they will build the house very soon.   Linroukim thanks Kiva and WSDS for helping her achieve some portion of her plan and which will eventually become the platform to start off. She says "thank you so much, Kiva”. She also shares that she will repay the loan on time without fail and will continue to grow.

name: Ruth Melania
description: For the past five years I've been running a shop from my own home.  I sell popular consumer products to all my community.  With this business I've been able to help my children and my family.    Translated by Kiva volunteer Maite Barragán    Hace 5 años que tengo una pequeña Pulperia en mi casa, donde vendo productos de consumo popular a toda mi comunidad. Con este negocio he podido ayudar a mis hijos y mi familia.

name: Barbara's Group
description: Barbara is 50 years old and is a married woman with 1 child, age 19. Barbara has been a chick seller since 2000. Everyday, she works from 6am to 6pm and can earn a monthly profit of about $150 from her sales.  She now hopes for a loan to buy more chicks for her business. She will share this loan with her subgroup members Esta and Fidolina, who have businesses dealing in grains sales.

name: Francis
description: Francis is 38 years old, married, and has two children.He sells cereals, which he has been doing for four years. His monthly income from the business is 20,000 KES.  Francis is requesting his first loan from KADET LTD which he will use to buy cereals cereals, such as rice and maize, beans, and green gram (mung beans) to sell. Francis hopes to open a restaurant in the future.

name: Efia
description: Efia sells vegetables including garden eggs (eggplant) at Jukwa market near Abura. She has been selling garden eggs for 6 years now. Efua has 4 children and so uses her income to feed and clothe her children. She will use her loan to purchase a variety of vegetables to satisfy her customers. With the new profit, she wants to mount a stall for the sale of her vegetables.

name: Pov
description: Mrs. U. Pov, 44, and her husband, Bey Pich, live in a modest wood stilt home.  They have five children who still live at home, in addition to two young orphaned relatives.  Pov has been a weaver since she was 14 years old.  It's a skill she learned from her mother.  Now, she is teaching her own daughter, 19, to weave as well.  They own two looms.  Pich is a moto-taxi driver and operates between their Mekong island of Koh Dach and Phnom Penh.      Pov is requesting her third loan from MAXIMA in the amount of $300.  They will use this loan to purchase materials for home repairs.  The existing corrugated roof is in bad shape and much of it needs replacement.  Pov says the new roof will cost $500, but that they have saved $200 already.  As Pov has successfully repaid previous loans, we feel sure she will repay this new loan as well.

name: Hue
description: Mrs. Hue is a hardworking woman, 33 years old. She lives with her husband and three children. The loan can help her to build a latrine to improve her family living standard. She is a employee and with support from her husband  she is able to repay the loan monthly.

name: Rosas Del Jardin Group
description: The Mission of Friendship Bridge is “to empower impoverished Guatemalan women to create a better future for themselves, their children and their communities through microfinance and education called 'Microcredit Plus'". The vision of the organization is a world in which empowered women eliminate poverty.  Dionicia is 38 years old, married, and President of the “Rosas del Jardin” Trust Bank in Huehuetenango. She, along with her husband, make and sell shoes which are in great demand at this time of year because of end-of-the-year parties, graduations, baptisms, etc. Dionicia needs to inject capital into her business and will use the funds to buy raw materials for the shoes. She wants to take advantage of increased sales at this time of the year.  The women are keenly aware of the value of education for their children. An overwhelmingly majority of them hold this as their highest goal. The ladies have had little or no education and so the training held at their monthly meetings is very important to them. They are eager to learn how to manage their loans effectively and learn about budgeting, planning, pricing, marketing, customer service and accounting. They take better care of their families with information about nutrition, hygiene and the use of medicinal plants. And they become more aware of themselves as women as they learn about how their bodies work and women’s health.  The generosity of Kiva investors is greatly appreciated by Dionicia and the ladies in the “Rosas del Jardin” Trust Bank. Thank you!

name: Roland
description: Roland is a current client and is married with five children, four attend school.  He has operated a coffee trade for over 15 years. He is challenged by limited capital which affects his operations. He joined Ugafode for financial assistance to expand his business and will use the loan to meet his financial needs like paying school fees.   He has applied for 5,000,000 UGX to buy more coffee and increase his profitability. Roland thanks Ugafode for the financial assistance which has enabled him to educate his children, start  a restaurant for his wife,and meet his financial obligations.

name: Ama
description: Ama is married and she has four children. All her children are currently in school. She travels to the northern regions of Ghana to buy her products and retails them in her village. Her village is one of the main market centers in the region and therefore trading in foodstuffs attracts a large market. Ama wants to use her loan to buy more tubs of fresh yams, sacks of onions and gallons of palm oil, to avoid price hikes. She is a member of the group called Francis. Members agree to guarantee for each other to repay the loan.

name: Reynaldo De Jesus
description: The sound of the saw, the smell of varnish and the creativity of the furniture upon entering Reynaldo's business help you you enter the amazing world of this 64-year-old furniture maker.Twenty years ago, this entrepreneur decided to put his creativity to use to create innovative furniture and made it known in his neighborhood. Reynaldo has the support of his wife and their three children who send remittances monthly. This has allowed him to develop his business a little faster. However, he wants to continue to invest, so he is requesting a loan to buy nails, glue, sandpaper, paint, and other essential materials for furniture making. This investment will allow him to complete orders on time and deliver quality furniture. He plans to keep working hard to expand his business.

name: Yorleny
description: Yorleny is 35 years old, married, and lives with her husband and children, who are her greatest priority. With her loan, she plans to purchase fertilizers and other products to apply to the coffee crop, so that they develop well, and in addition to pay for labor costs to apply the products and assistance for the plants once she has a good development of her harvest and, in this way, to assure herself of doing good work.  What she plans is to take advantage of the good climatic and soil conditions that the zone has for this crop, and also to put into practice the experience of some years of managing coffee. In addition, she plans to be able to purchase better products and of better quality so that her plants have a good development and health such as a good harvest, and to have in the short-term a significant production. With the income from the harvest that she hopes to get, she wants to use it for the well-being of her family and to meet some family goals and to continue investing more in her crops. This is the first loan she has gotten from FUDECOSUR. She has not had other loans before from state banks, but FUDECOSUR has offered her the loan with better terms and a much lower interest rate.

name: Gladys
description: Gladys is 52 years old and is married with 5 children; all work independently. She sells general merchandise, principally clothing, toys, perfumes, and used shoes. She has been in this business for more than five years. She began with a small amount of capital and saved little by little until she achieved  a sufficient clientele.   The loan will be invested in the purchase of perfumes, sheets, clothing and mosquito nets for the coming season, since she wants to take advantage of the current low prices. She is a very enterprising and hard working. Her goal is to have a variety store which can be attended to by the members of her family.  Translated from Spanish by Pam McMurry, Kiva Volunteer

name: Julia
description: The member Julia is 50 years old, is married and has five children. The member is in the business of selling tamales, sponge cakes, and sorghum, which are like cakes made from corn. The member sells as a street vendor in a square from 8:00am to 5:00pm. The member has been in this business for 30 years and she likes to make many desserts.   The member's dream is to have a place where she can sell tamales, sponge cakes and sorghum. The member is requesting a loan to buy supplies such as flour, sugar, butter, and eggs in bulk. The member is happy for the loan and promises to meet her installment payments.

name: Mujurizi
description: Mujurizi E. is an individual client from Bushenyi. He is 26 years old and single. He is into the business of selling produce like beans, millet, cotton, groundnuts and maize. hH operates from his home in Nyamirima, selling mostly to other bigger traders from neighboring districts and town dwellers, and he is able to make 420,000/= as monthly profits. He has been in the business for over 4 years, after working for someone else, until he started his own business. His dream is to be able to grow his business and get married. He also grows cotton and coffee on plantations. He is a very hard-working young man, and he needs a loan to be able to buy more produce and cereals for resale.

name: Aqelah Group
description: Aqelah is the group leader of Aqelah group. There are three members in this group. All of them would like to receive money for their own businesses: Nasema and Saleha want to take a loan for the business of tailoring, and Aqelah would like to take a loan for her father's vegetable business. They all want to see progress in their businesses and to earn more money to support their families better.   They say that these loans can be very useful because they provide a chance for poor entrepreneurs to expand their businesses.

name: Helen
description: Helen is a 41-year-old married woman with two children, who are in school. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur. Helen has an upholstery business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for 14 years.   Helen has requested a 10,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy additional materials for her business. She would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Ma. Vilma
description: Like most people in Talibon, Bohol, Ma. Vilma finds her livelihood through raising hogs. This has been her business for eleven years now. She also operates a sari-sari store in her area. It has been a challenging job raising hogs since it takes a while to fatten the pigs. Without quality feed, her animals’ growth will be compromised. But with the quality feed, she can increase her chance of a higher return of investment. She is asking a loan to buy feed for her animals and soft drinks for her store. In the future, she hopes to keep improving and expanding her business for better profitability.

name: Editha
description: Editha is 58 years old and has eight children. Editha is married and has one child who is in school.  Editha is in the agricultural business buying and selling livestock in the Philippines. Editha requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to buy feed and vitamins for her livestock.  Editha has been buying and selling livestock for three years and has borrowed four times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Editha would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Irene's Group
description: Irene, pictured above, has been a farmer for 17 years, and is now proud to represent her group of 5 farmers in Chwele District. She is 37 years old, is married and has 8 children.Irene likes to think of herself as a very hardworking individual. She has been working alongside One Acre Fund since 2014 and decided to represent her group because she wanted to help more farmers.She says that being part of the One Acre Fund community has meant that she has had more profits from each harvest. Irene plans to use the profits from this coming season to send her children to school.In total, Irene’s Group will receive inputs to cultivate 1.5 acres of land. Given that some members of the group will also be purchasing a solar light with this loan, the group will also receive a total of 2 solar lights.

name: Moses
description: Moses is a single man. He operates a transport business where he transports customers using his motorcycle. He has been involved in this business for three years. His business is located in a busy area and his primary customers are locals. He will use the Kes 21,000 loan to repair and service his motorcycle. His business goal is to own more motorcycles within five years. This is his first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: Rose
description: Rose is 47 year single mother of four children aged between 8 and 12 years. All her children go to school .She resides and owns a four roomed house where she stays with six people  Rose takes care of additional family members. The family has no access to electricity and piped water.  Rose works in semi urban area which in the outskirts of Kampala.  She is a tailor in Ndeeba, selling charcoal and so she pays for transport costs to and from shopping as she buys directly from producers in the villages She is faced with the challenge of transportation because when it rains the roads becomes impassable.  She doesn’t pay rent for her business but pays monthly market dues. Rose sells to all categories of people both on retail and whole sale and works seven days a week  She has been in this business for ten years and with MCDT for seven years servicing her sixteenth loan, working with the same group mates. She wants to use this loan to buy more airtime cards. She is aspiring of seeing her business grow bigger and owning delivery vans

name: Oumou
description: Born in August 1985 in Bamako, Oumou lives with her three children and her husband in a monogamous family in the Kangaré neighborhood of the city of Selingue.  Oumou has not had the chance to go to school. She quickly became interested in income-generating activities including hairdressing and the sale of beauty products.   Having repaid previous loans, Oumou is on her fourth loan with Soro Yiriwaso, to be used to buy a large quantity of hair extensions and beauty products from wholesalers in Bamako. She sells retail for cash or credit at her shop in Kangaré, to a clientele composed of men and women.  Oumou hopes to make monthly profits of 100,000 FCFA that will be used to help her husband provide for the family, reimburse the loan and reinvest in the business.

name: Doem
description: Doem D., age 57 (picture with his wife) and his wife Norn Thuch, age 57, live in a small village off of National Road number Two, about twenty kilometers south of Phnom Penh.
