They were married in 1979 and have five sons and one daughter. Three of them are married and live outside the home, three attend school and another is a construction worker.    Doem has been driving a motor taxi for 15 years.  Norn has sold fruits for 10 years. His motorbike is connected to a trailer at the rear. He carries goods and people from his village to Phnom Penh City and back.  Doem is applying for his first loan of $500 to add to his own savings to purchase a motorbike for his son to drive to work.

name: Omolara
description: Omolara is 31 years old and married with 2 children. She has a business centre where she types and photocopies documents for customers. She would like to have a bigger business centre in the future and wants to sell stationary as well. She lives in Ibadan, Oyo state, Nigeria. Her husband is a printer and they both contribute to support the family. She is requesting a loan amount of NGN 50,000. With this, she will invest the loan in the business by buying material and stationery in bulk to get a better price. She say 'thank you' to all Kiva lenders for their support.

name: Anita
description: Anita D., aged 43, and her husband Alex, aged 44, have four children – two are in college, one is in high school and one is in elementary school.  Anita and Alex work hard to cover daily expenses and the cost of their children's education. For the past 15 years, Anita has owned and run her own sari-sari (general) store to generate income to help with the family's expenses.   Anita is requesting a loan of 8,000 PHP to purchase extra inventory for her store, including school supplies, groceries and soft drinks. She hopes the added inventory will attract more customers and that her expanded business will generate more revenue.   Anita has been a member of Kiva partner, the Center for Community Transformation (CCT), since 2009, and has consistently attended weekly fellowship meetings*. She hopes that the income from her business will allow her to continue paying for her children's education.    * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital and pay microfinance loans.

name: Bright Future Group
description: Fortune is 31 years old. She is married and has one child who is going to school. Her husband works as an assistant managing director. They have the husband's salary as additional income.   She is a cross-border trader who buys and sells duvets, seat covers, clothing and footware products. She has been in this business for nine years and is doing well. She faces some challenges in the business, however, as some of the clients fail to pay on time and may eventually default payment.   She wants to open two shops in town and in Chivi in the next five years. With the profits from the business she wants to take her family out for a holiday.

name: Nueva Esperanza  (Cuenca) Group
description: The communal bank "Nueva Esperanza" [New Hope] is formed of eight women who work daily in different economic activities, which permit them to contribute and better the economy of their homes and ensure that their families get ahead. They are women who, in spite of adversities, keep smiling. They are all friends and live in different parts of the city of Cuenca, a city which is characterized by its cold climate, scenery, and the four rivers which run through it. Its historical center transports us to the past, and the warmth of the city's people, culture and traditions win the hearts of those who visit it.  One of the members of this group is Angelita, who is on her fourth loan from the communal bank "New Hope." She lives in the Monay sector of the city of Cuenca, is 24 years old, and is a single mother with three children who are 7, 3, and barely six months old. Her first child studies in a school in the city. She does not have a house of her own, thus she rents her home.  Angelita works from Monday to Saturday from 8 in the morning until 4 in the afternoon, in a restaurant where she has worked for five years. In her home she also works raising chickens, a business which she started with her first loan from the communal bank. She is going to invest her new loan in the purchase of chicken and chicken feed to keep growing in this same business. Her goal is to construct a bigger chicken shed to continue with her business.

name: Epifanio
description: Epifanio, age 41, is a kind and hardworking gentleman.  He lives in his own home with his wife Elida, age 35, and their four beloved children for whom he wants to provide a better quality of life.  Epifanio invests a great deal of effort planting in his fields, which are the main source of sustenance for his family.  His products are in great demand at the wholesale market in Tarma and he has earned a reputation for producing crops of good quality, thus enabling him to sell at very good prices.  What he enjoys most about his work is caring for his crops and protecting them from insects that can have a negative impact.  Epifanio has been farming for 26 years and considers the most difficult part to be tranporting sacks of potatoes, peas, and beans because they are extremely heavy and the work is tiring.  Going forward, he hopes to buy additional farmland so that he can increase his production.  This is his fourth loan with MFP.  Epifanio knows that the loan will be beneficial to the development of his business.  In his Communal Bank, Epifanio is a cheerful member who always tries to keep the meetings organized.  The loan of 2500 PEN that he requested will be used to buy compost and insecticides to help keep his farmland productive.

name: Filoi
description: Filoi is a 43-year-old married woman with 6 children. She has a small plantation and grows vegetables to earn a living. She has been doing this for many years.  Filoi has requested a loan to buy vegetable seeds, fertilizer, chemicals, weed killer, bush knives, a mist blower, etc. She has been a member of SPBD since 2013. With her profits, Filoi hopes to improve her financial support and also improve her family's living conditions.

name: Namuun
description: Mrs Namuun is 22 years old and lives with her brother in Ulaanbaatar, capital city of Mongolia. The siblings reside in their own house on a plot of land.   She has been working as a foreign relations manager and translator at a private business entity for one year and she says she is learning a lot of things from her colleagues. Her brother works at a construction site.   The house they live in has been deteriorating over the years and needs some serious repair work because in winter time, they are chilled to the bone. So she is requesting a loan of 6,000,000 MNT to purchase vacuum insulated windows, hardwood floors, shingles and a metal door.   Installing those items into her house will create a comfortable and warm place to live. Also, the renovated house will reduce their coal consumption; thus releasing less pollutants, which contributes to the clean air efforts.   The borrower is a very hard-working individual, who strives for a better future.

name: Toy
description: Toy is a 44-year-old married mother of three children living in the Trang district of Takeo province.  She does rice planting and has 22 years experiences in this business.  She is able to earn up to 5 USD per day and keeps 2 US dollars each day as savings.  Toy joins VisionFund Kiva’s partner this cycle as a first-time borrower. She is now applying for an education loan to pay for her son’s university tuition. She hopes this loan will enable her to keep her son in tertiary education until graduation and also help relieve the financial burden for her family, thereby she can sustain and grow her business.

name: Aba
description: Aba T. is a widow taking care of  ten dependents.  She is into multiple businesses, such as selling fish, clothes and making gari for sale. Gari is made from cassava. (In this picture, she is peeling the cassava to make the gari). She has been in this business for some time now and she wants to increase the quantity of gari she sells. She needs a loan to purchase more quantities of cassava to process into gari for sale. The additional income realized from the loan will be invested back into her business so she can take proper care of her dependents.

name: Nour
description: Nour is a 20-year-old single woman. She is a sister of eight siblings. Nour goes to college to get a degree. She knows that it is difficult on her family to support so many people, but she insists on continuing her studies. For this reason, Nour is now seeking a loan to help her pay for the next semester's registration fees.

name: Diana Cristina
description: This is Diana, a practical, intelligent, and ingenious woman.  She has always liked everything related to fashion.  To pursue her dream, she started a dressmaking business, since she wants to stay afloat and carry out her passion for fashion in a way that supports her family.    When it comes to continuing forwards with her work, her main difficulty is the lack of resources to buy machines and supplies.  If she can receive help in the form of the money that she badly needs to buy an overlock sewing machine, supplies, and fabric, all of that can change.    Her intention is to grow her business and support her parents, and to be well-known for making new garments that people like that are different from what they have come across in the market.

name: Jean Adrien
description: Jean Adrien’s business is growing so steadily that he is coming back for another loan to increase his stock. This time he is taking out a new loan to purchase more goods in his grocery store. An environmental agent in his locality, Jean is very interested in selling more products to help minimize the effects of charcoal on the environment by reducing carbon emissions and deforestation.

name: Jory
description: Ricster is 18-years-old and is first of the five children in the family. His mother Jory, a member of NWTF, supports the family through her business raising livestock in the Philippines.  Ricster is studying Bachelor in Science in Secondary Education and is currently in the 2nd of this 4-year course.  Jory is borrowing PHP 5,750 to pay for tuition fees of her son Ricster for the second semester of the school year 2014-2015.  Ricster plans to graduate and be gainfully employed.

name: Edwardson
description: Edwardson is 26 years old and married with two kids.   He has managed a farm business for five years. He earns PHP 10,000 per cropping so he can save so that he has enough money to sustain the daily needs of his family.   To have additional income, he is asking for a loan amounting to PHP 12,000 to buy fertilizer, pesticide, and insecticide.  Edwardson dreams that he can save enough money for the future of his family.

name: Reyna Margarita
description: Reyna is 35 years old and has one son, For some years now she has been making a living in agriculture, having been taught this trade by her parents. She wakes up at 4.30am in order to milk her cows and later she goes to help her husband in their 14,000 square metres of land, where they grow corn. At 12.30pm Reyna returns to the house to do the household chores.   Reyna is applying for this loan from Fundación Campo in order to buy seeds, fertliser and seeds to sow corn. With the loan, she will then be able to buy all the necessary supplies to grow her crops on time and be sure she will have this grain which is an important part of her family's diet. Reyna's wish is to acquire more dairy cows in order to sell milk.

name: Relina
description: Hog raising is the primary source of income for Relina. She is from the village of Centro 1 in Isabela. She is now 57 years old, married with four children. She is a responsible mother. To further provide for the needs of her family, she is making a way to improve her hog raising business. For this reason, she is seeking the amount of PHP 15,000 from lenders to buy feed and vaccines for the maintenance and growth of her hogs.

name: Senzakahle Group
description: Ntombi is 32 years old and single with three children, between the ages of two and eleven years. She also takes care of one relative. She runs a retail business selling paraffin, candles and chips in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.  She has been running this business for one year and faces the challenge of customers who buy on credit and do not pay.   She has requested this loan through WDB and Kiva to purchase clothes, chips, sweets and airtime to sell. She says that the extra income from this loan will help her send her children to school and make a profit. In the future she sees her business growing in such a way that she will open a "spazza" shop. ("Spazza" shops are small corner stores where you can buy food, drink, and other basics.)   Ntombi is pictured in the middle and is wearing bright pink.

name: Felomina
description: Felomina is 73 years old and married with three children. Felomina works very hard to provide for them.  Felomina runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional groceries to sell. Felomina has been in this business for six years and sells a variety of items such as soap, snack foods and other groceries.   In the future Felomina would like to save enough money in order to support the financial stability of her family.

name: Delba
description: Delba is a married woman who lives in Narra, Palawan. She earns her living by operating three business ventures:  pig fattening, meat dealing/livestock and farming. Her husband Luis, who is 37 years old, works as a farmer to earn his living. They have two children who are 6 and 11 years old. Delba joined NWTF-Project Dungganon in 2006 because she aspired for something better for her family. With the help of her past seven loans from NWTF-Project Dungganon, Delba has been incrementally lifting her family out of poverty by the sweat of her brow. Her previous loan of PHP 12,000 helped her earn a monthly profit of PHP 8,900, uplifting the family's standard of living.  This time, for her eighth loan, she is borrowing PHP 25,000  to fund her livestock and farming operations and purchase more meat so that she can continue to save up for her children's education and the improvement of her business. Delba is a Dungganon woman who is following an honorable path toward the achievement of her dreams.

name: Indede
description: Indede is a maize farmer. Before he became a Babban Gona member, Indede would have had to sell his maize for low prices soon after harvest, to cater for his immediate cash needs.   With this loan and Babban Gona’s support, Indede can now store his maize at harvest time and sell it a few months later for up to 40% higher than the market price at harvest.   Like other Babban Gona members, Indede is looking to earn a better income to provide more food and clothing for his family, and hopes to make more money for himself and his family.

name: Maria Auxiliadora
description: María Auxiliadora S. Calderón is 47 years, single, and has three children. María sells general merchandise, and her business is located in the municipal market. María began this business three years ago, and little by little, she converted her business from one selling perfumes, creams, and other home products into a business selling clothing and shoes. She proposes expanding her business to buy other places where she can sell her products. María has had three loans from Fundación León 2000 and these have been a help investing in her business. With Kiva’s financing, María will invest in an ample inventory of clothing, shoes and small electrical appliances. She is seeking C$ 14.500 which will be repaid over 12 months.Translated from Spanish by Cindy Kendall, Kiva Volunteer

name: John
description: John is a male Ugandan, aged 41. He is married with 7 children. Four of his children attend school and he pays tuition and provides all the other basic needs for them. John sells used clothing in the outskirts of a village trading centre in Kibale district and also grows coffee as another source of income. He has approached UGAFODE for a loan UGX.800,000,000 to add more stock in his business of old clothes so that he can increase his profits. His main challenge is competition from other traders who have more capital than him. John describes himself as a hardworking and honest business person.

name: Samath's Group
description: Samath’s Group lives in a rural village in Kandal province of Cambodia. Samath makes a living cultivating rice and she also does extra work as a tailor to support her family.In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time needed to collect fuel and boil water.

name: Rasim
description: Rasim J. is 51 years old, married, and has two children. He lives in southern Azerbaijani village Alisoltanli, near Saatli region. Rasim opened his small food store in 1996, when he borrowed some money from his friends. In the beginning, the only items he sold were various sweets. The store revenues increased rapidly, and Rasim was able to start selling also cookies, tea and canned products. Even though the store now brings good income to Rasim to cover his family's needs, he would like to expand the variety of goods for sale at the store, and therefore needs a loan of US$1,200 for the purchase of meat and dairy products.

name: Maferah
description: Meet 50-year-old Maferah from Jui eastern area in Freetown. She is married with four children.  In 2006, Maferah established her retail business. She began her business because she did not go school and she was trained in business.  She works at the business from 8:00 am until 7:00 pm, 7 days per week. She is very hard-working and desires to improve her standard of living  Maferah requires a loan in order to purchase rice, palm oil and cooking seasonings to expand her business. She hopes that the extra income from this loan will allow her to feed her children and expand her business. In the future, Maferah plans to expand her business still more. She thanks you for your support.

name: Felecidad
description: Felecidad is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a food production business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF to buy ingredients for her food business.  NWTF is listing Felecidad's request for another loan in support of her efforts to secure the future of her family.

name: Aggrey
description: Aggrey is 24 years old, married to Esther, and blessed with one child aged one and a half years. He provides transport services using his motorbike, a business he started three years ago, and earns a monthly income of KES 15,000-20,000. Aggrey has requested a third loan of KES 105,000 to purchase another motorbike. The profit he earns will aid him in repaying his loan and continuing to save. He dreams of owning land and building rental houses for additional income.

name: Rodalyn
description: Rodalyn 27 years old, married and had two children. She involved herself in food selling business as source of her income. She wanted to sell more products so she is now asking for a loan of P7,000 to buy eggs, cooking oil, flour and rice to sell. This will help increase her sales and sell more delicious foods and profits as well.

name: Mercedes
description: Mercedes has had to overcome many adversities in life, but her determination to work and get ahead has always allowed her to rise above the difficulties and continue progressing with her children.  She is divorced from her husband, and as the single mother of six children, is the head of household.  Mercedes' only source of income is the general store she has been running for approximately 11 years, thanks to which she has been able to provide her children with a quality household.  Because of her good customer service she has attracted many customers in the neighborhood, which means her sales volume is high.  However, she does not have much working capital to stock her store well and offer her customers a wide variety of products.  So she is requesting a loan to buy more products for the family shopping basket so the customers will have more variety.  Thanks to this business she will be able to get ahead and give her children a quality lifestyle.  Also, Mercedes hopes that an increase in income will improve her situation so the children will have a more stable economy at home.

name: Zosima
description: Zosima is 52 years old and married with seven children.  She earns a living by raising pigs in the Philippines. Zosima is borrowing PHP 14,000 through NWTF to buy feed and vitamins for her pigs.  Zosima has been raising pigs for two years and also earns additional income from banana retail.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save money to expand her business.

name: Fati
description: Fati sells palm oil and palm kernel oil at Elmina. She has been in this business for some years now. Fati is married with 3 children. She uses her income to support her husband in the general upkeep of their home. She will use her loan to purchase palm fruit and palm kernel for the extraction of oil to sell. She will expand her business with the anticipated profits.

name: Antonia Isabel
description: Antonia S., 19, is married and is a weaver.  Together with her husband, who is a weaver also, they have a workshop “Elaboración de Cortes Típicos para mujeres." She has worked as a weaver for the past 4 years.  She lives in Paraje Chibatz, in the Poxlajuj territory, in the Totonicapán department, Guatemala.  Currently, demand from her customers has increased but her financial situation is insufficient for her to be able to increase her working capital.  For this reason she turned to Asociación ASDIR to request a loan with the intention of using it to buy more merchandise to be able to increase sales hoping, too, to provide better living conditions for her family and to get ahead.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Rosemary's Group
description: Rosemary is a member of this group in Lugari District. She is pictured here in a group of five One Acre Fund group leader farmers. The group leaders represent a total of 86 individual One Acre Fund farmers who are not pictured here. Rosemary has been selected to act as the Kiva group representative and is standing on the right with her hand raised. She and the other farmers represented by this group are each receiving one-quarter acre of maize and one-quarter acre of sorghum or millet. Each farmer is receiving an average input loan of 5,349 KES for maize, millet and sorghum cultivation.							  Rosemary is 48 years old and has been a farmer for 10 years. She works as a farmer to provide for her five children. The community and other farmers know Rosemary as friendly, hardworking, reliable, trustworthy and an experienced farmer. Other than farming, she is also involved in her community in other ways, such as the women's group and savings group.  				  Rosemary first enrolled with One Acre Fund in 2013 and is now preparing to be a One Acre Fund farmer during the 2014 Long Rains season. Rosemary joined One Acre Fund in order to get the best seed prices, to learn new farming methods and earn enough to feed the family. She also volunteered to be a group leader and Kiva representative because she is an active community member and wants to help more farmers. Rosemary plans to use the money that she earns from her next harvest to send her children to school, repair the home, and save for the future. She notes that working with One Acre Fund has led to many benefits for One Acre Fund farmers.    One Acre Fund focuses on working with smallholder farmers across Kenya. The organization pre-purchases seeds and fertilizer when prices are low and passes the cost savings onto the farmers. Rosemary and her group will use the Kiva loan to cover this initial cost of purchasing the seeds and fertilizer package from One Acre Fund. One Acre Fund continues providing training and support throughout the planting and harvesting season to ensure a good harvest and repayment. With support from One Acre Fund and your loan, these farmers will have a chance at a successful harvest, increased profits and improved lives.							  The field officer is also included in the photo and is standing on the left.

name: Sergio
description: Sergio is 61 years old, married, and lives in Pagadian City, Zamboanga del Sur, Philippines. In order to earn a living, he takes in and raises pigs from the neighborhood. The piglets' owners share in profit upon sale, to be divided 60/40 or 70/30 depending on their agreement. With a desire to earn more, he decided to raise pigs on his own as well. Through Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative, he obtained the capital to purchase his own piglets and feed. Now, Sergio requests a loan of 12,000 PHP to buy additional feed. He really hopes and prays that his business will grow and benefit his family, in addition to his income. Someday, he wants to build a concrete pig cage to easily keep more sanitary conditions.
town: Pagadian - Pagadian City, Zamboanga del Sur

name: Victoire
description: Victoire is twenty-nine years old, married and mother to two children.  She lives in Tokoin and sells 'Egblin' (fermented, maize paste) from the front of her home and in the surrounding neighbourhoods.  She buys the neccessary supplies twice a month from the market.Victoire has requested this loan to buy bowls of maize and expand her business further.  Her increased income will help provide for her children's education.

name: Mercy's Group
description: Mercy is 23 years old and is often described as a very hardworking individual. She has two children and is married. As a group leader, Mercy is representing her group of 13 farmers in Matete District in Kenya, and is very excited to be working with One Acre Fund for the first time this year.  The decision to join One Acre Fund was largely a result of Mercy's desire to make more farmer friends in her community. Apart from receiving farming inputs, she is also purchasing a solar light as part of her loan. This is very exciting to her as she will now be able to reduce the consumption of paraffin fuel and therefore save more money. With the profits that she earns from this year’s harvest, she plans to save more money for the future.  Mercy and her group will receive a total of 12 solar lights as well as input loans of maize and fertilizer to plant a total of 4 acres.

name: Salamatu
description: Salamatu is a maize farmer from Kwankwani village in Kaduna state. Before she became a Babban Gona member, Salamatu would have had to sell her maize for low prices soon after harvest, to meet her immediate cash needs. With this loan and Babban Gona’s support, Salamatu can now store her maize at harvest time and sell it a few months later for up to 40% higher than the market price at harvest. Salamatu, like other members of Babban Gona, intends to use the extra income to provide food and clothing for her family, and hopes to become the most profitable farmer in her community.

name: Luis Carlos
description: Luis Carlos is 40 years old.  He comes from the country and makes a living growing beans.  He learned this trade from his father, who did this work for all of his life.  Family is Luis Carlos' biggest priority and every day he does his best in order to guarantee better living conditions for them.  His product is sold in the market square in his town.  His biggest challenge is dealing with the climate changes that affect his crops, and variation in prices which result in substantial losses.  Luis Carlos longs to have sufficient resources to build a home on the land where he sows his beans.  In order to bring in the harvest soon, Luisa Carlos is applying for a loan to buy fertilisers, insecticides and fungicides to fertilise his crops and to generate an income that will be used to buy school materials for his nephews.

name: Amani
description: Amani is a 25-year-old married woman from a small village near Nablus City. She is has two sons and one daughter. Her husband is a worker in a local firm where he earns a low income. His income barely covers the family's needs. Two years ago, Amani and her husband decided to open a small grocery store in their village. It is a good business and its income helps them to cover their expenses.   Amani took a 3,000 USD loan from FATEN. This loan will help her and her husband to buy more grocery products for their store. This loan will help them increase their sales and improve their living conditions. Amani's husband appears in this photo, because she is a conservative person who prefers not to have her photo published online.

name: Adelaida
description: Adelaida is 53 years old and a married woman with five children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Adelaida has a food vending business in the Philippines. She has requested a 11,000 PHP loan amount through NWTF in order to buy ingredients for her food business.  Adelaida has been in this business for two years. In the future, she would like to save enough money to expand her business and repair her family's home.

name: Pastora
description: Pastora operates her retail business in addition to farming to earn a living.  Pastora has been in her business for 12 years and she has been able to sustain their living. She joined GDMPC in 2011 and her previous loan that she used for her store was successfully repaid. Currently, she borrowed a new loan to buy organic fertilizer for the farm. In the future, Pastora hopes to improve the general living conditions of the entire family.

name: Nancy Hortencia
description: Nancy lives in El Fortín, an urban sector in north Guayaquil.  She’s a good example of personal improvement since she opened a small but well-stocked grocery store seven years ago.  When she started out her house was made of sugarcane stalks and now it’s cement thanks to her work and to Banco D-Miro which was the first institution that trusted her and offered help.  Her work day starts at 5:30am because since she sells vegetables she has to buy them fresh at the foodstuffs market.  She then opens her store and doesn’t close until 10 at night.  She has no needs since her husband helps her tend to customers.  What she sells the most is vegetables, fruit, rice, sugar, oil, chickens, grains, soft-drinks, milk, cured meats, etc. which are the products she’ll buy with the loan to stock up.  Her future goal is to enlarge her house because she’d like to open a clothing store next door to improve her income.

name: Yaneth Araceli
description: Yaneth is 28 years old and she finished through sixth grade. Her partner works in agriculture, they have three children, of whom two are studying at home.  Yaneth works as a homemaker and is her husband’s “right hand” when it comes to farming corn, beans, and sorghum. She learned to farm when she was very young because her parents taught her how. The place where she farms is 2 kilometers from her house. Her work schedule is from 4 to 5 hours per day.  Yaneth needs the loan to buy a dairy cow, so she can take advantage of the byproducts of the agricultural harvest, which will be ready soon, and thereby have another source of food when the cow produces milk.  Yaneth dreams of seeing her children grow up, study, and become professionals. She also dreams of having many cows so she can sell milk and cheese.

name: Venancia
description: Venancia works hard to support two children. She is married and has a  vegetable-selling business in the Philippines.   Venancia requested a 3,500 Philippine peso (PHP) loan through NWTF to buy a solar lamp.   She is getting the solar lamp because she wants to have backup light in case of emergency.   Venancia is aware that by using the solar lamp, she is not only saving money, she is also helping the environment and reducing health risks to her family.

name: Godfrey
description: Godfrey is a 45-year-old married man with four children living in Kasese, Uganda. For six years he has been operating a retail shop and the business has been very lucrative. He also deals in local brews, coffee and bananas for additional income. Godfrey is requesting money to buy soap, salt and sugar to sell in his retail shop.

name: Ferdinand
description: Ferdinand, age 56, is a rice farmer. He and his wife have a rice field that serves as their primary source of income. His wife also engages in a hog-raising business to earn extra income. They work hard to lift their four children from their poor standard of living. The family lives in the village of Nagrumbuan, Cauayan City, Isabela.  Ferdinand is requesting a loan of 40,000 PHP to buy farm inputs such as seedlings, fertilizers and insecticides to sustain his farm. He hopes that he can receive the amount he has requested to further grow his farm and harvest more rice to offer for sale.

name: Anonymous
description: This borrower is a member of the Communal Bank “Fuente de Vida” (Fountain of Life) which is located in the District of Cusco in Cusco Province, Department of Cusco.  She continues to manage her cafeteria business.  The borrower wants to keep working so that she can continue supporting her family.  She has been in this business for years and it has given her personal satisfaction.  The borrower is requesting a loan in order to buy cookies, sodas, and other products.  She appreciates the loan that has been issued and promises to complete her payments according to the established terms.

name: Myrna
description: Myrna P. is from the village of Upper Disakan. She is 41 years old. Myrna is married and has 2 school-aged children. To make a living, Myrna owns & operates a specialized retail store, selling gasoline in the local community. Myrna has been engaged in her business for over 3 years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2010, Myrna joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. Myrna has successfully repaid a previous loan of 3,000 PHP from PMPC. This previous loan was used to purchase additional inventory & working capital. Myrna is requesting a new loan of 5,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional inventory & working capital. This will be the second loan taken out by Myrna from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to financially support immediate members of her family.   About PMPC:  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.
town: Liloy-Upper Disakan, Jose Dalman, Zamboanga del No

name: Srey
description: Srey, is married and resides with her husband and two children in Kandal Province, Cambodia. She has been selling roasted pigs and roasted chicken for over 20 years, earning approximately 7 USD per day. For over 10 years, her husband has run the business of buying maize to resale for a profitable price, earning approximately 5 USD per day. In order to improve her husband's business, Srey is requesting a loan of 500 USD to raise capital in her husband’s business to purchase more maize to sell to gain more profit. In the future, she would like to expand her business and rebuild her present house to make it much stronger and bigger to provide a better living condition for the family.

name: Mujeres Hacia El Progreso Grupo 1 Group
description: E. is the coordinator of her group Mujeres hacia el progreso (Women Towards Progress). Her story is representative of her group and of Esperanza's Haitian and Dominican clients generally, many of whom recently emigrated to the Dominican Republic from Haiti. Her group is located in Samana, a lush rugged peninsula with a nascent tourism industry, where running water (none of which is potable) and electricity are unreliable. She makes her home here as a single mother (she has three children), in a simple structure which doubles as her bakery.  E. is excited to be taking her third loan with Esperanza, after having successfully repaid her previous loan and grown her business. She plans to use this loan to invest in her bread-making business. She intends to buy a mixing and kneading machine for her home-based bakery and to make structural improvements to the building by installing a cement ceiling. She will use the profits to purchase school supplies for her children, and hopes to save some money for her children's future. She thanks you all for your support.

name: Salomao
description: Salomao is married with no children, lives in his own house and supports his mother.  He's a farmer but he plans to embrace commercial activities and as such he intends to purchase various food products with this loan to begin this activity.  In future Salomao hopes to have a better home, improve his working conditions and purchase a vehicle to help with transporting his products. To this end he commits to duly paying off this loan in order to solicit further loans from Hluvuku.  His challenge is to work hard to overcome financial difficulties both today and in future.

name: Rehmat
description: Rehmat is a 45-year-old married woman. She is a mother of four daughters and four sons. Her husband is a barber by profession. He owns a barber shop in the market which is the only source of income for their family. He is a well skilled person in his profession. All of his customers appreciate his services.   Rehmat is requesting a loan from Kiva's partner BRAC Pakistan for her husband. He will use the loan amount to purchase scissors for hair cutting as well as brushes, combs, and a chair. Rehmat hopes that the loan will be helpful for her husband's shop which is the only source of income for the family. She is thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Rosalina
description: Rosalina is from Baybay, Leyte. She is married and has five adult children. To earn a living, she is doing a hog raising business. She has been doing this for four years. Aside from this, she also engaged in sari-sari store business. With this, she is asking a loan of PHP5000 to buy feeds and grocery items such as toiletries, spices, eggs, cooking oil, noodles, canned goods, sugar, candies, chips and biscuits. In the future, she wishes to improve her means of living. Thus, she wants to increase their livelihood.

name: Banco Del Desarrollo Group
description: The members belong to the “Banco del Desarrollo" communal bank. This bank is located in Cusco district, which is part of Cusco province and Cusco department.   One of the members is Leonor who is 33 years old and has a son.  She works selling cereals such as corn, wheat and quinoa, with a daily schedule of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.  She has been in business for four years and it is going well for her.  Her dream is to have her own locale where she can sell her goods.  She is requesting a loan to buy corn, wheat and quinoa.  The individual photos are of members who were unable to be present for the group photo for work-related reasons.  We hope the entire group will be present at the next meeting.  The other members have businesses such as a laundry service, Internet service, a grocery store and a restaurant.  Leonor is grateful to those participating in her dream and she is committed to paying back the loan on time.

name: Marling Ivania
description: Marling Ivania is 34 years old and married.  She and her husband have five children that all study at public schools.  They make and sell bath scrubbers.  They've been in this line of work for more than six years.  Their children help them as they can because they understand that their family's daily needs are met through this work.     Marling Ivania travels to Mangua to buy certain accessories that are needed to make her products.  She is requesting this funding in order to buy sponge, fabric, thread, scissors, and other products.  Her desire is to buy an industrial sewing machine that will help her improve her products.Translated from Spanish by Rebecca Morey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Liana
description: Liana is 22 years old and comes from Yerevan. She lives with her parents and sister. Liana studies at Yerevan State Slavonic University and currently is in her 4th year of study. Liana doesn't work as she needs to study hard and can't manage work and study at the same time. Her parents are working at a local company and do their best to cover the family's costs.   Currently, the family is facing difficulties which don’t allow Liana to pay for her education. So, she has applied for this loan to pay for university tuition of the first semester and be able to continue her education.  The loan is very important for Liana and she will be very grateful to lenders for their support.

name: Mala's Group
description: Mala’s group live in a rural village in Kompong Speu province in Cambodia. Mala makes a living cultivating rice and she also does extra work as factory laborer to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these woman and man to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Beverly
description: Beverly V. is a young rice farmer from Agusan Del Sur. She is 19 years old and a single mom to a 1-year-old child. Her rice field still needs additional farm supplies. Beverly is a new member of CEVI, and she knows for a fact that its program is helpful for farmers. She is requesting a loan of 6,000 PHP to be used for additional farm supplies. Her income from her farm will be a big help to her family’s daily needs and hopefully will enable her to save up for her child’s education.

name: Astolfo
description: Astolfo has 18 years of experience in this business. He makes roofs for houses, sliding doors, folding screen room partitions, and windows. He learned this business when he worked in a factory. When the factory was liquidated, he bought some of the machinery and started his own workshop. For the past five years he has been running his own business, which is open from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, depending on the urgency of the orders he is working on. He has two employees who help him. The business has been growing bit by bit and he has invested all of his earnings in heavy machinery.   He needs the loan to buy raw materials, such as iron. He would especially like to produce windows that he could showcase at his shop.   Astolfo was born in Simón Bolívar-Juian. He is 49 years old and is married. His wife works in the home. Astolfo is a hard-working and responsible person. Thanks to his hard work, he has his own house that is built of cement and he also is the owner of his place of business. He has been able to manage his finances very well. His hope is to maintain his business and that it will prosper so that he will be able to provide jobs to other people.     Translated from Spanish by Jennifer Day, Kiva Volunteer.  Astolfo tiene 18 años de experiencia en esta actividad. Él elabora: techos para casas, puertas corredizas, acordeones para casas, ventanas. Él aprendió esta actividad cuando trabaja en una fábrica. Cuando lo liquidaron compro unas máquinas y monto su propio taller. Desde hace  5 años esta con su propio negocio que lo atiende de 6:00 AM a 6:00PM todo depende de la urgencia de entrega. Tiene 2 empleados que le apoyan. Su negocio ha ido creciendo poco a poco, toda su ganancia las ha invertido en el negocio comprando sus maquinarias pesadas.  Él necesita el préstamo para comprar materia prima que es el hierro y desea producir especialmente ventanas y exhibirlas en su local.  Astolfo nació en Simón Bolívar-Jujan. Tiene 49 años. Esta casado. Su esposa no trabaja pero le apoya en el hogar. Astolfo es una persona trabajadora, responsable en sus actividades. Gracias a su esfuerzo él tiene casa propia y actualmente es de cemento y además el local del negocio es propio. Él ha podido manejar muy bien sus finanzas. Su deseo es seguir con su negocio que siga prosperando y poder dar trabajo a otros.

name: Arcenia
description: Arcenia is 69 years old, married, and has six children. She is in the agricultural business  in the Philippines. Arcenia requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to pay for rice grains and the laborers' salaries for her rice mill.She has been in this business for eight years now, and has borrowed nine times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.In the future, Arcenia would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Cesar
description: César is 40 years old and lives with Irma, his partner with whom he has two children who are 7 and 19 years old.  This family lives in a rustic house which he built himself in an agricultural annex.  César is a man who takes great pains in all the work that he does.  The agriculture and livestock are his main labors.  On his own land he grows several varieties of peas, also gladiolus flowers, carrots, lettuce, spinach, potatoes, broad beans, corn, etc.  "This month I have planted peas and gladiolus because when I harvest them the prices will be good," he says.  Within two months he will begin the season of large planting, when he has to think about planting potatoes and peas.  He has many plans.  The inclemency of the weather has been his worst adversary, situations that he has learned how to control with many years of experience.  Among his next goals he has planed to fertilize his potato, peas, and gladiolus crops. This is why he asks for your help.  This is his third loan with MFP, an entity to which he feels grateful for it having allowed him to obtain stable finances and wishes for progress, together with his communal bank "Cochayoc Centro".  He promises to be make his monthly repayments on time.  He will invest the 2,000 soles in the purchasing several bags of organic fertilizer for his gladiolus flowers and pea crops.

name: An
description: Mr. An H., 35, and his wife, Mrs. Savang Sang, 39, have been married since 1986 and have three children -- one son and two daughters. The family lives on National Road Number One about 15 kilometers from Phnom Penh City.   An and his wife are farmers and make a living by growing vegetables and flowers. An is applying for his first loan, for $700, to buy seed, fertilizer and pesticide to maintain his farm. He will also use a portion of this loan to add a kitchen to his house.

name: Thérèse
description: Thérèse is a 43-year old married woman. She lives with her six children in Kpota.  Thérèse sells second-hand clothes itinerantly at the market, and creates her revenues thanks to this business. She procures her supplies from the market six times a month, to permanently have some stock.  To place a new order, Thérèse is requesting a loan for women’s clothing. She will retail them to her clients to increase her profits and support her children with getting an education.

name: Rosalia
description: Rosalia H. is from the village of Santa Ines, Talisayan, Misamis Oriental. She is 49 years old. Rosalia is married and has 7 school-aged children.   To make a living Rosalia owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) retail store where she sells food and daily use products in the local community. Rosalia has been engaged in her business for over 4 years and earns approximately 2,000 PHP a month.  In 2006, Rosalia joined HSPFI to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Rosalia successfully repaid a previous loan of 12,000 PHP from HSPFI. Rosalia is requesting her 6th loan from HSPFI, for 14,000 PHP, which she will use to purchase additional products to sell. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement her family's income.   About HSPFI  HSPFI is an accredited partner of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.   Note  To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Wellington
description: Wellington has operated his cereal store in Naivasha for the last two years. He buys cereals in bulk directly from farmers and then sells them at the local market. He is 48 years old, married to Susan and they have two school-aged children. He was introduced to Kiva's partner, KADET, by one of KADET's field officers and this will be his third loan. He repaid all of his previous loans on time. Wellington plans to use the requested loan to buy more bags of maize and beans to sell in his store. In the future, Wellington hopes to grow his business and become a large supplier of cereals in Naivasha.

name: Faustina
description: Faustina works hard to support her family. She is married and has two children. Since November 8, 2007, her business is at home selling soft drinks, bottled water and biscuits.  She is now requesting a GHS 1,500 loan through ID-Ghana to purchase more soft drinks, bottled water and biscuits, and sell them to customers.  With this help, Faustina will be able to increase stock as soon as possible.  In the future, she would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Macaria
description: Macaria works hard to support her family. Macaria is married and has a vegetables vending business in the Philippines.  She has been in this business for 18 years now.  Macaria requested a PHP 10000 loan through NWTF to purchase more vegetables to sell in her vegetable stall.  In the future, Macaria would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Twekembe Women's Group
description: Sarah M. is the chairperson of Twekembe Development group in Mukono. She is married with no child but takes care of her husband's children and 5 nieces, all in school. Her retail shop and milk selling business are doing well thanks to the loans that have helped her cope with paying school fees for her beneficiaries. She has also managed to buy a plot together with her husband, and they are planning to build a house on the same plot. She still has her plans of opening up a dairy shop in Nasuuti so that her income increases tremendously; but right now, she would like to buy more goods for her retail shop once she has access to a loan.

name: Doreen
description: Doreen is a married woman with two children, both of whom attend school. She owns a house that has electricity but no piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is school fees.She has operated a brick-selling business for over five years, selling to the neighbors. She mentioned a major challenge of seasonality in her business.With the loan she is requesting, she wants to purchase materials for making bricks in her business.She decided to join Yehu to access loans and boost her business.

name: Haja
description: Haja is 36 years old. She is married and has an 18-year-old child who is in school. They all live in Montserrado County which is noted as the commercial city in Liberia.   Haja is a grade 2 dropout. Seven years now, she has been involved in the sales of dried fish. Most interestingly, she has many customers since she sells quality fish. She started her business with a loan from her husband and she learned this way of selling from her friends. Haja spends 12 hours on her business each day since her house is closer to the local market where she sells. One of the problems she faces is transportation cost.   Haja is requesting a loan to purchase more dried fish to increase her sales. She plans to open a shop in the near future and to see her child out of college.

name: Frozhan
description: Frozhan lives in district 15 of Kabul, Afghanistan. She is an educated woman. She is widow. Her husband died of cancer 5 years ago. Her children are small she is the only one to support her family. She has a bakery. She wants to take a loan to complete all the necessary things to expand her bakery and find more clients. This will help her provide for her family's education and solve their economic problems to solve. She is very happy now that she can support her family better by taking this loan .

name: Tomasita
description: Tomasita is married and works hard to support her family. She has a general store business in the Philippines and requested a PHP 25,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more groceries to sell.Tomasita has been in this business for 20 years now. She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Maria Cristina
description: Maria is a very enterprising and responsible woman. She is divorced and has a 13-year-old daughter. She studied for a career as an aesthetician, and, in looking for greater professional development, decided to open her own beauty salon. She started out working in the living room of her home. Later, as she got more clients, she rented a location, but she found it inadequate because of its location and condition. So she opted to leave that location and remodel a place within her home to offer her services. Maria's priority is her daughter, and she wants to give her everything she needs, which is why she works so hard, day after day, in her business.  In order to offer better service to her clients and continue growing, Maria needs a loan in the amount of $975, which she will use to buy supplies and equipment such as dyes, treatments, irons, etc. Without a doubt, you can be a fundamental part of the growth of this business and the lives of Maria and her daughter. Please decide to help them.  (Translated from the Spanish by Naomi Johnson, Kiva volunteer)  Maria es una mujer emprendedora muy responsable, está divorciada y tiene una hija de 13 años. Ella estudió una carrera técnica de estilista y en busca de su desarrollo profesional decidió iniciar su propia estética, empezó trabajando en la sala de su casa, después y al tener más clientes rentó un local que no fue el adecuado por su ubicación y las condiciones en las que estaba, así que optó por abandonarlo y acondicionó un lugar en su casa para poder ofrecer sus servicios. La prioridad de Maria es su hija y desea darle todo lo necesario, para lo que se esfuerza día a día en su negocio. Para poder ofrecer un mejor servicio a sus clientes y continuar creciendo, Maria requiere de un préstamo por la cantidad de $ 925 dólares que utilizará en la compra de materiales y equipo que necesita para continuar ofreciendo su servicio, tales como tintes, tratamientos, planchas, etc. Tú puedes ser parte fundamental en el crecimiento de este negocio y en la vida de Maria y su hija, no lo pienses más y decídete a ayudarla.

name: Rose
description: Rose is a married woman. She has three children. She describes herself to be ambitious. She operates a farm where she grows french beans. She has been involved in this business for 10 years. Her business is located in a productive area. She describes her biggest business challenge to be price changes. She will use the KES 40,000 loan to buy farm inputs. She hopes that in the future, she will improve her family's well being. This is her second loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. Her previous loan was repaid successfully.

name: Souad
description: Souad is a 37 year old woman. She lives in southern Lebanon, in Nabatieh.   Souad sells clothes to earn a living. This is the first time she has asked for a loan from Al Majmoua. With the loan, she is planning to buy merchandise to sustain and develop her business.

name: Armando Marcelo
description: Armando, who is 48 years old, is single, extroverted, and responsible. For the past 10 years, he has worked as a taxi driver.  He needs this loan to purchase parts for his taxi, like tires and accessories. His dream is to be able to purchase a truck to transport merchandise.

name: Kuña Guapa Group
description: This group was formed in the city of Carapeguá, it is a close-knit group, where they all put their best into being able to help their loved ones through their work and struggle together.  Maria is grateful for and inspired by the women's committee program. Through the training, she was able to work in clothing and footwear sales which she does as a street vendor, and through this she was able to improve her quality of life.  She asks for this loan to be able to purchase a variety of clothing and footwear to sell, so to be able to continue with her sales and satisfy her customers. She is grateful for the opportunity that she is receiving to improve.

name: Gregoria
description: Gregoria is a jolly person with a strong personality. She lives with her family in the village of Duminit.  Gregoria is engaged in a hog-raising business that primarily involves hogs for breeding. It is a business that she started along years ago. The best way to earn profits was to go to the livestock markets to buy and sell pigs. Now, she needs to increase her business, thus she is taking out this loan of 10,000 PHP that she will use to buy feed, vaccines, and additional hogs to raise. Through this loan, she believes that she can make improvements in her business and she is hoping that she will be successful in carrying them out.

name: Phon's Group
description: The members of Phon’s Group live in a rural village in Kandal province in Cambodia. Phon makes a living cultivating rice and he also does extra work as a tailor to support his family.   In his village, there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help the members of Phon's Group to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Erkin
description: Erkin is 53 and married with three children. His oldest daughter is in university and the other two children are in school. He has a high school education and has been working in agriculture and animal husbandry for 24 years, a business he began with the purchase of one cow. Thanks to his hard work, he currently has three cows on his farm and sells organic milk. In addition, he grows clover for his own use on 1.3 hectares of land. His total monthly income is about 18,000 KGS.  With the goal of further developing his business, Erkin has turned to Bai Tushum Bank for a loan of 50,000 KGS to purchase steers for fattening and resale. He wants to put profits from the loan into further increasing his number of livestock, and plans to save toward purchasing a new family car.

name: Norma Petronila
description: Doña Norma is married. Her husband works as a photographer. Her children number three: one of them is already married and independent while the younger two are in school. She puts all her effort into her work so that she can pay her younger children’s school fees. Thus she works to educate them and, little by little, to make improvements to her dwelling.   She wants to continue with the construction of the perimeter wall that she started with the previous loan. She still has materials but she needs to buy more in order to continue with the project. With this new loan, she will buy more so that she can complete this improvement, which is very important for her family’s well-being and security.

name: Lavdush
description: Lavdush has been photographed here with his son, the second child. He works in construction and his wife in a restaurant. Lavdush, who lives in a city in southeastern Albania, wants to buy a stove and a boiler with this loan.   The city where they live has a very cold and snowy climate yet with clean and fresh air to breath, it is considered helpful to individuals who suffer from breathing problems; the city is also situated on a mountainous landscape. Residents of the city are known for making the best pies called “lakror” still baked primitively in a rounded dish put on top of embers and covered with a lid called a “saç.” Whether the pies are made with fresh spinach, cottage cheese and eggs, with tomatoes and onions or wild greens such as nettles, they are just delicious. In addition, they are known for the baked apples as they are produced in abundance in the region.

name: Esther
description: Esther is a 35-year-old woman. She is married and is the mother of five children, all of whom are currently in school in the community where they live.  Esther is a food vendor and sells banku with soup. Banku is prepared from milled maize grains and it is taken with hot pepper or soup. Esther has many customers since banku is enjoyed by many Ghanaians as breakfast, lunch and supper.  Esther wants to use the loan to buy more raw materials like bags of maize, meat, fish, vegetables and firewood. She hopes to raise an increased income to support her business and to include the sale of cereals in bags to her customers. She saves some of her earnings as an investment for the future.

name: Abduvakkos
description: Abduvakkos works as a security guard at the local bank branch.  The work schedule there is to work 1 day and then have 2 days off.  Because of this Abduvakkos has a lot of free time left after he works his main job and thus he also transports people in his personal vehicle.  On market days he purchases and sells dried fruits at the local market.  All of these activities help him to cover family expenditures.  Abduvakkos is 56 years old, he is married and has 2 children.  Abduvakkos decided to apply for a loan and plans to expand his dried fruit business.  Translated from Russian by Sabina Holzman, Kiva Volunteer

name: Bianca
description: Bianca is a member of the Communal Bank “Futuros Emprendedores” (Future Entrepreneurs) which is located in the town of Peñalolén.  She works in the retail trade, specifically selling handcrafted products, which include clothing from India for women, men, and children, and accessories such as rings, necklaces, bracelets, scarves, and other items.  She offers all of her merchandise from a vending stall at both the open market and at the Persian fair.  Her work schedule is from Tuesday to Sunday.    Bianca says that her venture is a family business that has been in operation for seven years.  She works with her mother and brother.  Bianca purchases her merchandise from different distributors, especially those that offer the most affordable prices.  With this loan she will buy merchandise for her business, mostly innovative products.    Bianca lives with her mother, her brother, and her six-year-old daughter.  She says that she is studying at the university for a law degree, so one of her dreams is to finish her studies.  In addition, she would like to buy a house of her own and provide her daughter a better quality of life.  Bianca is very pleased and appreciative of the opportunity given to her by Fondo Esperanza so that she can invest in her business.  In addition, she says that the assistance she receives not only consists of financing, but it also includes education.  As part of her training classes, Bianca has learned more advanced methods of accounting.  By working alongside her Communal Bank group, she feels united, responsible, and committed.    Peñalolén is located east of the Metropolitana region.  It has several attractions such as vineyards, historical buildings, and natural archaeological sites.  These elements have transformed this area into a tourist haven in the Metropolitana region.

name: Benkadi Group
description: The seven members of the Benkadi group are for the most part married, and average 35 years of age with three children. Most live in polygamous families in Noumousso, one of the neighborhoods of Kadiolo, in Sikasso (third administrative region of the Republic of Mali).  They joined the Soro Yiriwaso MFI to satisfy their customers' needs, and are now requesting a fourth group loan. All three preceding loans were well handled.  They buy and sell shea butter, children’s clothing, food condiments, etc. With their new loan, they will buy: 70 kilos of shea butter, three dozen sets of children’s clothes and five packages of food condiments.  They get their supplies from the main market in Kadiolo and from villages in the surrounding area. They resell in fixed locations on market fair days at the Kadiolo market, and also as itinerant vendors, for cash but often for credit, to a customer base of both men and women.  They expect to reach average monthly earnings of 17,500 FCFA each, of which part will go into savings and meeting family needs, and the remainder will be reinvested in the business activities. Their ambition is to request more significant loans to improve customer satisfaction and eventually become wholesalers. Translated from French by René McConnell, Kiva Volunteer

name: Elman
description: Elman B. is a 55-year-old farmer who owns a small market in the IDP Settlement of the Bilasuvar region. He has run his business since 1995. He sells various kind of goods, beverages and stationery. Elman's store is the only financial source in his family. The income is just enough to cover basic family needs, but not enough to improve his business. He has a very big demand for the products he sells. That’s why he has applied for $900 USD to increase the number of products in his store.

name: Balimaya Group
description: The four members of the Balimaya group are married women who are on average 31 years old with three children. They live in monogamous families in Ouayerma I, a working-class neighborhood in the city of Sikasso (third administrative region of Mali).  They are on their first loan with the Soro Yiriwaso micro-finance institution, seeking to meet the needs of their customers.  Kadia has been trading plantain bananas for about a year and wants to become a wholesaler. She intends to use the loan to buy a few dozen bunches. She resupplies from wholesalers at the Medina main market in Sikasso. She retails them as an itinerant vendor and from her home to both women and men customers, against cash.  She expects average monthly profits to attain 17,500 FCFA, part of which will serve to pay the loan and interest and the remainder will be put into savings. She aims to increase her turnover so she can better satisfy her customers.

name: Anacely
description: In the town of Nagarote, Sra. Anacely L. works extremely hard as a housekeeper.  She feels that she is a very disciplined woman who has great love for her work.  Anacely strives to maintain her home and support her children who attend school.  The loan she is requesting will be used to buy school supplies for her children and also pay for their high school registration fees.  This will prepare them to be outstanding professionals in the future.  Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Zulfiy
description: Zulfiy lives in the region named Dangara. This place is in the south-eastern part of Tajikistan. She is 41 years old and the mother of 2 children. Her eldest daughter goes to medical college. The other one is in high school. Zulfiy does not have higher education.   The family income depends on her business, which she has had for four years. Zulfiy has a sales point at a market in Dangara. There she sells different types of clothing. She would like to increase her turnover and expand her business.   Zulfiy needs a loan which will allow her to increase her family's capital. Sheneeds your help very much. Please help!

name: Marissa
description: Marissa is in the transportation business, particularly jeepney. She is indeed thankful because her husband is supportive of her running her transportation and other businesses. Marissa's husband is a driver and a farmer within her area. The couple also raises hogs as an additional source of income.  Marissa would like to change the wheels and buy gasoline for her jeepney to ensure the safety of her passengers. But due to insufficient capital, she is seeking a loan of PHP 10,000. She knows that this amount will enable her to obtain better income and secure her passengers. Marissa hopes and prays that she can obtain her loan to be able to secure her family's future, educate her three children and improve her living conditions.

name: Bun Lestari Group
description: Bun Lestari Group is renewing their relationship with MUK.  To increase the price they get for their pigs, the group changed the method of maintaining the pigs. Some members still maintain sows, and the other members raise either super-quality pigs for fattening or local pigs for pork roll. With this method, the initial sales of baby piglets will remain within this group, only. The members who have sows, will sell their baby piglets to other members of the group, who raise the pigs for fattening or for pork roll. Later, the fattening or pork roll pig-raisers will sell to the big buyer.  Ni Wayan chose to maintain fattening pigs, and she is using her share of this loan to purchase piglets and feed. She hopes this new method will work, so she and the Bun Lestari Group will get satisfactory results.

name: Susana
description: Susana S. is from the village of San Roque, Valencia City Bukidnon. She is 58 years old. Susana is married and has five adult children. Susana owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) retail shop, where she sells a variety of different products in the local community. Susana has been engaged in her business for more than two years and earns approximately 8,000 Philippine pesos (about $167) a month for these activities.  This year, Susana joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Susana is requesting a loan of 5,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This will be the first loan taken out by Susana from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the income of her family.   Note: This picture was taken at Susana's store during her non-operating day.  About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Rosemarie
description: Rosemarie S. is from the village of Locsoon, Tudela, Misamis Occidental. She is 53 years old, is married and has eight school-aged children.  Rosemarie owns and operates a general store, selling daily-use products such as shampoo, soap and toothpaste in the local community. She has been engaged in her business for over twenty years and earns approximately 2,000 PHP a month.  In 2005, Rosemarie joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 15,000 PHP from PMPC. This previous loan was used to to purchase additional products to sell.  Rosemarie is requesting a new loan of 15,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional inventory and used as working capital. This loan will be her 6th from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to pay her children’s tuition fees.    About PMPC: Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.    *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Analie
description: Analie is 38 years old and is widowed with five children, four of whom are in school. She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 11,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like canned goods, personal care products, etc.   Analie has borrowed and repaid six loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for five years and also earns an income from fishing.  She successfully repaid her previous loan and now she has requested another loan to further build her businesses.   Analie aspires to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Danaya Group
description: The Danaya group is made up of 6 married women who have an average age of 34 and, on average, 3 children. They live in traditional, extended families in the Dialanikoro district of  Bougouni town. They got to know each other thanks to neighbourly and business relationships and friendships. They decided to join the Soro Yiriwaso microfinance institution in order to strengthen their financial capacity and better do business, and are on their 4th loan. The 3 previous loans have been correctly repaid.  Sitan, standing on the left in the picture, is the group member who sells firewood. She plans to use her loan to buy 12 cartloads of firewood from the wholesalers in Bougouni. She makes her sales for cash or credit, at the market and at home, to a retail clientèle mostly made up of women. She expects to make an average monthly profit of 45 000 francs which will be reinvested in her business and used to repay the loan.

name: David's Group
description: David, pictured above, has been a farmer for 15 years, and is now proud to represent his group of 12 farmers in Teso District. He is 41 years old, is married, and has 5 children.  David likes to think of himself as a very reliable person. He has been working alongside One Acre Fund since 2015 and decided to represent his group because he wanted to be more active in his community. David plans to use the profits from this coming season to send his children to school.  In total, David’s Group will receive inputs to cultivate 7 acres of land. Given that some members of the group will also be purchasing a solar light, with this loan, the group will also receive a total of 5 solar lights.

name: Hellen
description: Hellen lives in Chuka area of Eastern Kenya and has one child. She is a farmer who sells bananas, yams, milk, and eggs in the local market. Hellen enjoys farming because of the income she generates. Her biggest business challenge is marketing her produce. She chose Juhudi Kilimo for her loan because they offer better services to small-scale farmers.  Hellen is requesting a loan to purchase equipment for her farm. Her loan will help generate more income and will help with her farming activities. Hellen will use this income to help improve her family's living standards.

name: Homidjon
description: Homidjon B., 24, is married and has a business baking “lepeshka”- the national bread. The family's main income earner, Homidjon operates a profitable business that is not subject to seasonal fluctuations.  Purchasing the necessary ingredients of flour, salt, and yeast at the local market, he arises early each day to bake the lepeshka so that people can enjoy it fresh on their tables for breakfast.   Due to high customer demand, Homidjon wants to increase production volume and so is requesting $600 for a term of 12 months. The loan will be used to purchase the flour and coal for baking the “lepeshka.”    Homidjon deeply appreciates the trust and support you are giving him.    More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is perhaps best known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road, the end of Alexander the Great's rule, and its famous great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets including Rudaki, Ibn Sina (Avicenna), Firdousi, Omar Haiyam, Jomi, and Mavlavi Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC.  Even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.   Sadly, however, Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics.  The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy.  In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable.  These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment, forcing hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia.  While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve agricultural production and the manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.   IMON's History Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need.   To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Antonio
description: Antonio, 47, is a very hard-working man.  He lives alone in his own house and what he most desires is to get ahead in life.  His place of business is located in the Explanada Laguna Temporal (place where the city of Juliaca has its fairs).  He sells clothing which he himself makes in his workshop.  His designs are very novel and showy, reason enough for people to prefer to buy from him.  What he most likes about his job is the weaving which he learned as a child from his mother.  He has been doing this for 16 years and the most difficult part of the job is moving the bundles of clothing from the workshop to the sales stand.  He hopes in the future to be able to buy more knitting machines so that he can produce better quality crafts.  This is Antonio's fourth loan with MFP.  He knows that he must repay in time and wants to do so even if that means having to work even harder.  He is a very well-liked member of his communal bank.  He will use the 2,000 soles to buy more wool with which to produce more items of clothing.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Uani
description: Uani is a widowed woman with one child who goes to school. She owns a house that neither has electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.   For the past eight years, she has operated a shop kiosk business, selling to her neighbours and passersby. She mentioned seasonality as her major challenge. She dreams of establishing a wholesale shop in the future.  With the Kshs 30,000 she wants to purchase sweets, biscuits, bread, milk, soft drinks, rice, beans, and cooking oil.
