She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Guillerma
description: Guillerma is a member of the Winarisun Community Bank.  In Quechua, Winarisun means 'May We Grow'.  Guillerma is 42 years old, married, and has three children.  She has a stall in the large market in the City of Quinua where she sells meat every day.  In addition, she and her husband make fire-wood.  Guillerma needs a loan of $350 to buy hogs.  Her dreams are to better her business and to have her children complete their studies. Translated from Spanish by Harold Sims, Kiva Volunteer

name: Karafuu Group
description: Magreth, who is in her mid 40s, is a widow with grown-up kids. She has been a tailor since 1996.  She works from 8 am to 8 pm daily and is able to make a good monthly profit.  Magreth has had so many loans taken from Tujijenge Tanzania. She used the previous loans to buy three sewing machines and materials for making ladies' dresses and men's suits and has paid back all her loans successfully. She used the profit to buy a plot of land, bought a TV set, a deck, iron sheets, a radio, clothing materials and covered household expenses. She will use this loan to buy a zig-zag machine,  to increase her stock of material and to start selling secondhand clothes. She dreams of expanding her tailoring business.Magreth will share this loan with her loan group "Karafuu" which has three members who will hold each other accountable for paying back the loan.

name: Mely
description: Mely O. is from the village of Estrella, San Guillermo, Isabela. She is 59 years old. Mely is married and has 9 adult children. To make a living, Mely owns & operates a general store. The main source of income for the business comes from selling daily use products such as shampoo, soap & toothpaste in the local community. Mely has been engaged in her business for over 5 years and earns approximately 3000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Mely joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Mely is requesting a loan of 5000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This will be the first loan taken out by Mely from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful micro-finance institutions in the Philippines. It has 25 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Sarah's Group
description: Sarah is 48 years old and has 9 children. She is a group leader and is representing her group formed by 10 farmers in Kakamega North District, Kenya.   Sarah has been farming with One Acre Fund for years now, having joined the program for the first time in 2011. This decision was largely a result of her desire to have access to quality training and acquire new farming methods and, although she described her last harvest as excellent, she believes she could have a better one this year by continuing to work alongside One Acre Fund. Sarah also decided to purchase a solar light as part of her loan, which she is very excited about, as it will allow her to reduce the consumption of paraffin fuel and therefore save more money.  Obtaining this loan means that Sarah's Group will be able to receive a total of 4 solar lights, as well as farming inputs to plant a total of 6 acres.

name: Chitralekha
description: Chitralekha works in agriculture. She is 38 years old and married with two children. She lives and works in Angul district, a rural area in Odisha state.  In 2014, Chitralekha joined Peoples Forum to improve her business and health through Peoples Forum loan products.  Chitralekha has been involved in her agriculture business for more than 10 years. The main hardship that Chitralekha faces in her life is not having an hygienic latrine. She is requesting a loan to purchase sand, cement, and brick to build a toilet.  With her business profit, Chitralekha hopes for her family to be healthy and happy. She is happy with this loan.

name: Marilyn
description: Marilyn is a 32-year-old woman from Antequera, Bohol. She has been engaged in manicure and pedicure services for more than five years now. This is the source of her income.  She is asking for a loan to buy more materials for her manicure and pedicure business, such as nail polish, nail cutter, nipper and others. With this, she will be able to serve more customers, thus increasing her earnings.  In the future, Marilyn dreams of improving her livelihood and exploring another venture to augment her income.

name: Señor Nazareno Group
description: Juan is 45 years old.  He lives with his partner and has 2 dependent children.  He has a business selling groceries, including bread, fruit, soft drinks, dairy products, water, and pastries, from a stall near a motorway that is located in his area.  He will invest this loan in the purchase of chocolate, panettones (Christmas sweet breads), and champagne for the Christmas selling season.  He is a member of the communal bank "Señor Nazareno," which has enabled him to obtain loans to improve his business.  This group thanks the Kiva lenders for the support provided.  In the photo, Juan is seen wearing a turquoise sports shirt with blue and red stripes.

name: Bakhtiyor
description: Bakhtiyor lives in the Hamadoni region. He is 54 years old, married and has one child. Bakhtiyor opened a store where he sells perfumes and food products. He has been in this business for twenty years. He is taking out the loan to buy necessary products.

name: Jane
description: Jane is 54 and is separated. She lives in Clarin and operates a general store to earn a living. She has been doing this for 4 years and earns 5,000 PHP each month. Jane been a member of GDMPC since 2007.   Jane is requesting a 7,500 PHP loan to purchase new items such as candies, milo, shampoo, soaps, etc. In the future, she hopes to improve and expand her business.

name: Kahonzi
description: Kahonzi is a married woman with four children whom all attend school. She owns a house that neither has electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is food and school fees. She has operated a cafe business for the past six years selling food to the neighbours. She mentioned seasonality in her place of operation. With the loan she is requesting she wants to purchase tables,chairs and new utensils for her business. She decided to join yehu to access loans and boost her business.

name: Edwin Amilcar
description: Mr. R. P. works in the Masaya municipality in the Masaya department.  He has worked for three years for a company called ENACAL.  He works as a well operator.  He pays for the family expenses with this income.  His family is comprised of his life partner and his four minor children.  He now needs to pay the balance on a motorcycle that he got on credit from United Motors.  That is why he came to the CEPRODEL offices to request a loan.  The loan is to pay the balance he mentioned.  It should be noted that this vehicle is very important to him.  Before going to work he takes his children to the learning center.  He feels that it is safer to take them himself instead of sending them with another person or alone.

name: Suniah
description: Suniah is a 60-year-old widow. Her husband passed away a long time ago, leaving her to work hard by herself to cover the family's daily needs. She sells vegetables at her stall, earning about US$ 11.50 per week. Previously, she sold other foods, but that business did not grow very well, so she has decided to concentrate on vegetable sales now. She is requesting a loan of US$ 125 to expand her little business and is willing to repay this loan within a period of 12 months.

name: Emmanilyn
description: Emmanilyn, 24, is a single entrepreneur in Cabungaan, Clarin with 1 child. She earns money from her transport service business. She has run this business for almost 5 years now and she earns 7,000 PHP a month. To improve business, she is borrowing 15,000 PHP from GDMPC, which she just joined recently, to obtain accessories and tires. Before long, she hopes for the possibility of expanding her business.

name: Asma
description: Asma is a 28-year-old, married woman. She started her animal business along with her husband to provide a better standard of living. She has been doing this for the past three years. She looks after the animals and is responsible for feeding them, while her husband sells them to different markets in the city. Their business is providing them with enough income to support their family.   They want to expand the business and need to earn much more to meet their everyday expenditures, but the greatest obstacle is to have sufficient capital to increase her sales and obtain better earnings. Therefore, Asma has requested a loan amount of 40,000 PKR to buy more animals for resale purposes to grow her income. She is hopeful that expanding the business will help in improving her family’s living standards.

name: Cecilia
description: Cecilia is a hardworking woman entrepreneur with four children.  She earns a living by farming rice in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 20000 through NWTF to purchase of fertilizers and other farm supplies.   She supplements this income with earnings from her pig fattening. She successfully repaid her previous loan and now she has requested another loan to further build her businesses.   Cecilia dreams that one day she will be able to save enough to provide a secure future for her family

name: Florence
description: Florence is 29 years old and lives in Gardnersville. She’s single and has a child aged 13, who is in school and lives at home. Florence has been selling rice and palm oil for the past seven years. She learned this trade from her mother. Her main challenge is the high cost of goods.  She is requesting a loan to purchase more rice and palm oil for her business. She would like to own her own shop one day.

name: Jovelyn
description: Ms. Jovelyn B. is from the barangay of Bolinsong, Bonifacio, Misamis Occidental. She is 25 years of age, single and blessed with 3 children of whom 2 are now at school age and the other one is still an infant. To make her living, Jovelyn is presently engaged in operating a sari-sari (variety) store business. She is also earning support from her live-in partner, George Cagadas, who is presently working abroad as an OFW (Overseas Filipino Worker). Jovelyn has been engaged in this kind of business for 5 years already and earns approximately 4,000 PHP a month from sales in her sari-sari store business.   In 2010, Jovelyn joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Jovelyn is a newly recognized member under the PDP-LP (Paglaum Development Program for Landless People), a micro-finance program of PMPC.  She is now requesting a loan amount of 5,000 PHP which will be used to add to her capital for her sari-sari store business. This is the first loan taken out by Jovelyn from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family, saving for future use especially for future business expansion and for her children’s education.   About PMPC: Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.   *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Hawa
description: Hawa is 42 years old and lives in the Caldwell area of Montserrado County. This area is becoming one of the populated communities in Montserrado County due to some factors such as good roads, quietness, and the lower price of rental houses.   Hawa is married and her husband is a businessman; together they have three children between 6 and 12 years old. The children are currently in school and live at home. For the past fourteen years she has been selling rice, salt, pepper, vita, etc in the local market, she makes a lot of profit and has many customers.   She is requesting a loan to purchase more rice, salt, pepper, vita, etc. for her business. Her plan is to build her house and educate her children. She would like to say thanks to the donors of BRAC Liberia.

name: Justina
description: Justina is a 59-year-old woman who lives in the city of Baybay, Leyte. She is married and has seven children. Six of her children are already grown up but their youngest is 19 years old and still needs their support. Justina runs a sari-sari store (general store) business where she sells a variety of goods and she has been doing this for years. She has become proficient in this business and she eagerly wants to enhance this livelihood. Her problem is the lack of capital to run this business continuously because her capital is used for other needs such as daily consumption and bills. She needs a bigger loan amount to buy commodities needed for her store. She will purchase grocery items such as canned goods, noodles, spices, eggs, cooking oil, biscuits, chips, bread, sugar, salt and drinks. Part of her loan is also to purchase feed for her pigs as she also raises hogs for additional income.

name: Laurinda
description: Laurinda is taking a loan of $800 to improve her business. She is running a kiosk that helps her to generate income for her family.   She will use the loan to buy stock to keep in her store, such as noodles, cigarettes, sugar, salt, milk, Fanta, coffee and biscuits. She opened her kiosk a year ago with her own working capital of $400.    She is a hardworking woman, and she hopes to run a bigger business in the future.

name: Prescilla
description: Prescilla has a retail shop in Tala town where she sells both household and retail items. She is 62 years old, married and has been in this business for the past 15 years.  This being her third loan from KADET LTD, she plans to buy more stock of goods to sell. These include sugar, rice and flour. She will use the generated income to build a house.  She hopes to be successful in her business and be able to provide the needs of her grandchildren such as school fees.

name: Filberta
description: Filberta, age 28, is married with a 6-year-old. She owns a tailoring business, which she started in 2005. She works from 6am to 7pm daily and makes a monthly profit of about $50.In the past, she successfully took out a loan to expand her services. She now hopes for a new loan for the same purpose. She is a member of a loan group called Ushirika.

name: Iro
description: Iro is a Babban Gona maize farmer from Gangarida Village. He joined Babban Gona to create a better life for his children.  In the past, Iro suffered from poor yields that crippled his ability to feed his family and children. Now that he has joined Babban Gona, Iro has the chance to attain yields of up to 30 bags of maize/hectare, double the national average in Nigeria, and earn an income of up to $2,000/hectare.  Through Babban Gona’s input loan, he will have access to high-quality farm inputs such as fertilizers, herbicides, and improved seeds that will increase his yields and income considerably. With ambitious goals of harvesting 60 bags of maize this year, Iro can now ensure that his children get a post secondary education.

name: Relwende De Kokologho Group
description: Ms. T.ODILE is the representative of the group RELWENDE DE KOKOLOGHO. A married mother, she has six children. The oldest is 22 years old, and the youngest is 2. Five go to school.   Ms. T.ODILE has been selling grains for two years. She gets her supplies from nearby markets. She wants to purchase 5 sacks of millet, 2 sacks of beans, and 3 sacks of peanuts.   She wants to use her profits to help her children thrive. Her ambition is to be a major merchant (wholesaler) of grains.

name: Ben
description: Ben is 35 years old, married to Joyce, and they don't have a child yet. He runs a barber shop in Nakuru town, and has been in the business for eight years.  He will be using this loan to buy more shaving machines for use in his business. This will enable him to serve more customers and thereby make more income, which he will use to expand his wife's cereal shop by buying more stock of cereals.  This is his first loan term from VisionFund Kenya. In the future he hopes to grow his business and be successful.

name: Ana Patricia
description: Mrs. Ana Q. has begun the job of rebuilding her home.  It has been in bad shape for a long time.  She has done it for the purpose of supporting her family which is made up of two school-aged children. She needs to get the money immediately to purchase the building materials.  This is the reason she confidently puts her hopes in Ceprodel to benefit from this loan and therefore get ahead in her business.  Translated from Spanish by Susan Haynes, Kiva Volunteer

name: Maritza Bernarda
description: Maritza Bernarda is 46 years old. This isn’t the first time she has requested a loan. She is a very responsible woman who has 3 children in her care. She provides for them because she is a single mother. Her business is a small grocery store, which she has had for more than 16 years, despite the difficulties she has faced due to the fact that she didn’t have sufficient capital to purchase all of the products she needed. She is now requesting this loan for working capital so she can buy sweets, coffee, juices, bread, cookies, and soft drinks. Translated from Spanish by Jennifer Day, Kiva Volunteer

name: Yolanda
description: Yolanda F. lives in Santa Tecla and is a single mother of two adolescents. She sells staple grains for a living. She has a small business space where she receives a steady flow of customers because of her competitive prices. Yolanda’s children currently attend school, but once they leave school, they go to the shop and help her. Yolanda is requesting a loan that will be greatly beneficial to her family, as she is the sole source of income. Yolanda needs the loan in order to restock her shop.Translated from Spanish by Elizabeth Casian, Kiva Volunteer

name: Jelleny
description: Jelleny is 24 years old, married and has two children. She works hard to provide for her family. Jelleny runs a general store in the Philippines and has applied for a PHP 20000 loan through NWTF to purchase more groceries, such as sardines, soft drinks, bread and other miscellaneous items, to sell. Jelleny has borrowed and repaid seven loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for five years and also earns additional income from motorcycle transport. Jelleny aspires to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Bekaban Allakasson 4 Group
description: The ten members of the group "Bekaban Allakasson 4" are married women averaging 40 years of age and four children each, all living in polygamous families in Kapaga, a village in KADIOLO (SIKASSO), 3rd administrative region of the Republic of Mali. The women are collaborating with the microfinance institution Soro Yiriwaso to carry out their farm work during the rainy season. They are on their seventh loan with the institution. The past loans were indeed paid back.   The crops grown are rice and peanuts, as is the case with Korotoumou, who is standing in the middle of  the photo. With her loan, she intends to purchase farm inputs, fertilizer, and herbicide and to pay for weeding and plowing for maintaining 1 hectare.   After the harvest, the produce is sold in the village at the market. She sells to a customer base  composed of men and women. She plans on making a profit of 50,000 francs CFA per planting. This profit will enable her to repay the loan and also to help her big family to cover day-to-day expenses, as well as to help improve the children's diet.

name: Paul Kiratu
description: This is Paul. He has been doing farming since he was young. He farms vegetables, horticultural products and keeps dairy cattle. To get to this level, he has mostly been leasing land. Paul's vision is have his own land instead of leasing to lower the cost of agricultural production. He wants to build a model farm.   A loan from Kiva helps Paul finance costs of getting his own land and buy farm inputs.

name: David
description: David is 31 years old and has lived with a partner for 6 years to the north of Colomi.  He has a dependent child who is still in school.  David is a farmer who cultivates on his parent's land, rotating crops.  His source of income comes from the sale of potatoes and locoto peppers.  He also has some cattle. Because he lacks financial resources, he is requesting a loan to buy organic fertilizer and agrochemical products.  He needs these because his crops that are in progress need maintenance and phytosanitary control.  This way, he will have a healthy crop and a better harvest.

name: Luz Adriana
description: Luz Adriana is a 34 year old woman who devotes herself mainly to household work and who has started a business breeding pigs. The client started her activities looking for financial freedom, to pay for her children's education, to improve her housing conditions and to have money to fulfil her needs and wishes.According to the client, the greatest challenge facing her business is the strong competition. She needs to have more animals to compete in pricing. That is the reason to request a loan, which she will invest in a sow, and additionally a plant to feed the ones she owns and the ones that will be born. Lastly, she will enlarge the pigsty for the piglets to come.

name: Seydi Xiomara
description: Seydi, 27, is a young, single woman living in her mother’s house with her younger siblings.  She lives in the community of Nacaome in south Honduras.  She’s been selling snacks and fast-food for 13 years; her food stand is located at home.  Her customers are neighbors who come by daily and prefer her because of her kindness, good service, variety of snacks and good environment.  Seydi is noted for being an enterprising woman who very much wants to get ahead.  She’s asking for a 15,000 Lempira loan to buy bananas, vegetables, chicken and plantain.  With support from this loan she intends to meet her business’ financing need while improving her income in the same way.  Her dream is to improve the business still more and to own a house.  San Lorenzo, Honduras - October, 2012.

name: Erlinda
description: Erlinda is a 59-year-old businesswoman from Marapong, Sibutad. She has supported her three children by having a sari-sari store.  She has been able to sustain the store for 15 years and credits PMPC with the capitalization of her business. She took several loans before and was able to pay off all her obligations in a timely fashion.  Now, she has applied for another loan to restock her store with basic commodities. She wants to purchase bags of rice and kinds of canned goods to sell. She deeply hopes to sustain her business and continue to be member in good standing with the Cooperative.

name: Mavluda
description: Mavluda R. was born in 1964. Because of certain circumstances she got divorced and lives with three children. It was very difficult for her to feed all the children alone. She has decided to start her own business to help herself out of her desperate situation. She started a retail business selling children's shoes and it has been fifteen years since Mavluda has started her entrepreneurship. Now she is selling women's clothing and shoes. Her business location is in the Sadbarg trading center. In her inventory stock one can find summer dresses, blouses, skirts, and also a variety of shoes for the ladies such as dress shoes and casual. She buys merchandise from suppliers from Turkey and China. Mavluda wants to take out a loan in the amount of 4100 somoni ($1,200USD) to buy shoes for the fall season.Translated from Russian by Elena Fedorchuk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Al-Arham Group
description: The Al-Arham group consists of 4 women who live in Sana'a, Yemen. They applied for a loan of 180,000 YER from AMB.  Fatima, 30 years old, is married and has children who live in Sana'a. She is a housewife who takes care of her family. She washes her clothes at the laundry because she doesn't have money to buy a washing machine. Fatima has requested a loan of 50,000 YER from AMB to buy a washing machine for the house. She hopes to improve her living standards.

name: Lolita
description: Lolita is 58 years old and married with nine children, one of whom is in school, Lolita works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a general store in the Philippines. Lolita has been in this business for two years.   Lolita requested a PHP 12,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional items to sell like canned goods, eggs, noodles, etc.  In the future Lolita would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth D., 34 years old, is a mother of two children. Her eldest child is 9 years old. Her livelihood is rice farming. She has a 1-hectare farm that she  hopes could provide her with enough income to buy an adequate supply of food, clothes and other basic needs. She started her business in 2000 and joined the CEVI credit program last year in 2008.  She would like to request for a loan of Php 15,000 from Community Economic Ventures Inc. She will use the loan to buy farm supplies to augment her harvest and income.

name: Patricia
description: Patricia is 51 years old and married with three children.  She is a poultry farmer in Tala town.  She supplies chicken and eggs to the market place as well as to various hotels and restaurants.  She also sells cooking oil.   Patricia plans to use this loan to buy more poultry to raise and then sell at a profit. She also plans to buy more cooking oil to sell.  She anticipates that she will generate more income, which she will use to pay school fees for her grandchildren.  This is her fifth loan term with KADET LTD.  In the future, she hopes to live a comfortable life as well as to provide her children with a good standard of living.

name: Abena
description: Abena lives together with the husband ; she cooks rice and fish stew for sale at Putubiuw, near Cape Coast. She is married and has five children.   In front of Abena is the raw rice that she uses in preparing her food for sale.    She has been in this business for 12 years; she uses her income to support her husband in feeding their children.   Abena will use her loan to purchase bags of rice and fish to cook, and then sell.  With the new profit,  Abena plans to expand her business.

name: Maximiana
description: Maximiana has had a business selling clothing and electrical appliances from her home for three years.  She attends to this business personally, and receives help from her husband on the weekends, since he has another job.  They approached us because they want to put ceramic tile in their house.  They are grateful to the Institución for the tremendous support that they have been provided, since this loan will give them the opportunity to provide their family with greater comfort in the home, and will allow them to have a more valuable property.

name: Mwanasha
description: Mwanasha is a divorced woman and has been blessed with four children. Three of her children attend school while the other one is still too young for school. Together with her children, she lives at their own house that has neither electricity, nor piped water.   Mwanasha has operated a fish selling business for over ten years, selling from home to restaurant operators and passersby. She faces a major challenge of seasonality and perishability, leading to losses.  With the KES 40,000 she wants to purchase bundles of fish for resale. She dreams of expanding her business and establishing another business in the near future.

name: Javier Homero
description: Don Javier, has been s a farmer all his life. Since childhood he has been dedicated to agriculture. He has 3 children. His life has been very hard; and he's concerned about not being able to improve his economic conditions in order to provide his children professional studies for them to succeed. He is a good, quiet, hardworking man and enjoys participating in community activities. He grows beans, peppers, tomatoes, but he is worried of market prices which are permanently changing. Today he wants his credit to buy seeds of beans. He considers himself a happy person and always wanting to excel. This will be the opportunity to provide the opportunity to his family for growth and progress.

name: Marilyn
description: Marilyn is a 53-year-old married woman with six children; one child is still in school. Marilyn is a very hard working entrepreneur and has a fishing business in the Philippines.  She has requested a PHP 15,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy additional fishing net, bamboo and other materials for her business.  Marilyn has been in this business for three years. She would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Girineza Group
description: Goreth is part of the Girineza group and lives in Bujumbura. She is 31 years old is married to Désiré, a carpenter. Together, the couple have 3 children, aged between 4 and 8.  Goreth has been selling clothes for 4 years. This will be her second loan from Turame. Her Kiva-sponsored loan will increase her capital and allow her to buy a lot of clothes for resale, so that she can earn more.

name: Ana
description: Ana is a 35-year-old businesswoman. She is single and does not have children. She maintains her mother, with whom she lives.  With the requested amount she plans to buy dried fish to resell at the local market.  Her dream is to have a small grocery store, her own house and a vehicle to transport her products.  Her biggest challenge is the lack of funding. She also says that with the previous loan she could build a room at her mother’s house, where she currently lives. She says that she will pay the loan according to plan in order to be able to apply for more loans.

name: Mariano
description: Mariano is married and the father of two children who are still financially dependent on him.  One is attending a local public middle school and the other is in high school.  Mariano has been working as a manager in a butcher's shop for five years.  Through his work, he has gradually been building wealth for himself and his family.  The house in which they live has been deteriorating over time and he would like to plaster and paint the outside.  He is requesting support to fix up his house.

name: Felicia
description: Felicia is 43 years old, studied through elementary school, and is a wife and mother of two children (a woman age 20 and a boy 9 years old).  She lives in the Municipal neighborhood, in the district of Conduriri, province of El Collao, Puno. She has been a member of the “Maria Parado de Bellido” communal bank in Conduriri since 2005.  When she was 15 years old, she learned how to sell sweets and bread, and at age 20 she married.  She and her husband worked together to gather capital and started their grocery store, which to this day they still run.  With this loan of 1000 soles ($325), which she will repay over 3 months, she will buy two bags of rice for 260 soles ($85), a bag of sugar for 80 soles ($26), three bags of flour for 350 soles ($113), and five bags of noodles for 90 soles ($29), which she will sell in her retail store.  Her dream is to expand her business with the addition of fruits and vegetables, and that her children study and become professionals. Translated from Spanish by Laura Westin, Kiva Volunteer

name: Manzura
description: This is Manzura's first loan from IMON International. She is a conscientious and hard-working young woman. Manzura was born in the countryside in the family of a shepherd, and even as a child helped her father raise livestock. In 1997, she entered the first grade of secondary school. She was a good student, actively participated in extracurricular activities, and successfully finished grade 11 in 2008. In that same year she became a correspondence student at the Tajik Technological University. When Manzura was in her third year of university studies, her only brother was suddenly taken ill and needed a large sum of money for his medical treatment. As Manzura's father is a shepherd and her mother is a nurse, they were unable to find such funds. At the same time, the family needed to pay for Manzura's education. After paying his only son's medical bills, Manzura's father was unable to cover her tuition, and Manzura was expelled from university. Despite this setback, this year she has enrolled in the Tajik State University.   Manzura's family has no source of income other that her mother's salary. For this reason, Manzura has turned to IMON International to obtain a loan to pay her tuition. She is counting on your financial support and would like to receive higher education in order to serve her country in the future.

name: Adonai
description: Adonai C. M. is 44 years old and lives in La Libertad department (state), alongside his wife and their 2 children, 9 year old Maria, and 7 year old Imelda.  Both daughters currently study at primary school. Adonai is a hard-working man, and has established a business where he makes bricks by hand.  His business creates work for 3 other families as well, so Adonai has 3 employees who help him produce his goods.  Adonai requests a loan to purchase raw materials in order to make more goods; in this way, he will be able to increase his production to match his high volume of sales.   Translated from Spanish by Scott Lucas, Kiva Volunteer

name: Jlg-003-Melathaliyampatti Group
description: 21-year-old Ranjani leads a group of three in Kulithalai, Tamil Nadu. She works hard to sustain her family. She and her family have no access to toilets, and therefore have to resort to open defecation using the false privacy of nearby fields and surrounding shrubbery. This puts them at risk of infection, molestation or attack, and even insect or animal bites. All the women in the group face the same problem. Therefore, they have come together to build toilets for themselves in their own homes. They seek a loan of 42,000 INR to cover the cost of raw materials and labor for constructing these toilets. Your loan will provide these three families the privacy of using their own toilet, which will be a big step towards a better standard of living for them. Higher standards of hygiene will also lead to reduced medical expenses, and hence, more savings in the long run.

name: Paulina
description: Paulina A. is from the village of Cabisera 8. She is 51 years old and is married with three adult children.  Paulina owns and operates a specialized retail store, selling bottles in her junk shop. She has been engaged in her business for over two years and earns approximately 2,500 PHP a month.  In 2010, Paulina joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. She is requesting a loan of 5,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be her first from ASKI.  Paulina plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand her business.    About ASKI: ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has twenty-one branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small-business entrepreneurs.    *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Nua Ngam 5 Group
description: For four years, Mrs. Lom, 29, has been a single mom of two girls who are now 10 and 12 years old. After the divorce, she has started her new life and provided for her children independently. They live together in a small low-roofed house with very limited access to necessary facilities. Mrs. Lom has worked very hard to struggle with the life of deprivation, and in spite of the hardship, she is very optimistic and proud of her daughters because they could attend school fully with good results.  Without being trained for work, and because of dropping out of school early, Mrs. Lom can only work at agricultural production.  It is unstable and generates low income, because of the harsh condition of nature, and the lack of access to modern techniques in farming. However, with the experience in farming that she has accumulated since she was very little, and through the training and counselling she has gotten from the Anh Chi Em program, she's actually doing great at cultivating rice, corn, cassava, and raising pigs and chickens.   This is the fifth time she has taken out a loan from the program, and she will use it to buy corn seeds and fertilizer for the cornfield. She is thankful for the support of the program, which is timely and helpful to her. She dreams her children will escape from poverty and have an abundant life. In the picture, she wears the blue traditional Lao dress and stands on the first row, the first from the right.

name: Adjoa
description: At 42 years old, Adjoa is married and lives with her two children in Adakpame. To help with [her children's] development, Adjoa travels her area and sells general goods. She is able to earn enough thanks to this work.  She procures her goods five times a month from a market. Adjoa is seeking this loan to buy packs of candles, batteries, and insecticide so that she can earn a profit that will help to better cover her family's expenses.

name: Savy
description: A resident of Kampong Chhnang province, Savy is 41 years old and a mother of two children. She earns income to support her family by selling grocery items and catching fish. Moreover, she can earn extra income by making wine for sale and pig farming.   This is Savy's first time with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). She will spend her loan portion to buy a solar panel. She hopes it will provide her house with electricity to use.
town: Kampong Chhnang Province, Kampong Leng District

name: Juana Del Carmen
description: Juana works raising and fattening pigs for sale. She is requesting a loan of  $500 to buy new pigs, as well as the feed necessary for fattening them, so that she can offer a better product and improve her earnings.

name: Guillermina
description: Guillermina is from the city of Ybycui. She is 55 years old, lives with her husband and also their son who is an adult and who she could bring to work.For more than twenty years, she has been dedicated to the work of a hair stylist and manicurist. At first, she performed her work at home. Then she put together some capital and, thanks to this, was able to build a salon in her own house.She is requesting this loan to buy supplies to be able to stock her salon, such as dyes, creams, shampoo, rinses, and other items. She is happy for the opportunity she is receiving to be able to improve her living conditions and that of her loved ones.

name: Filomen
description: Filomen is in a common law marriage and has three children.  They have lived within Cochabamba tropics for years; for 12 years in the town of Entre Rios.  Filomen is originally from the San Jose Zudañez Chuquisaca province, one of the poorest areas of Bolivia.  He came from the community of San Jose, like most people, to look for a way to earn a living.  Production is low in his community because of the climate change and each time the production decreases.  He decided to move to the tropical area and bought a plot of farmland with great effort and sacrifice.  Now he raises citrus (mandarin oranges).  He will use the money from this loan to build a house.  This way he will be able to improve his quality of life.  His wife has always been helpful.

name: Dominga
description: Dominga is a 32-year-old businesswoman who wants to make progress in her business. She is married and has three school-aged children.  Her family lives happily in the village of La Salette Province of Isabela.    Dominga makes a living by raising hogs.  She has one mother pig and piglets that she raises in her backyard.  The income from selling some of her hogs helped Dominga open a variety store that provides a daily net income of 300 PHP.  Dominga hopes to have additional capital to improve her new business and maintain her hog-raising business.    Dominga is requesting to a loan of 15,000 PHP for the maintenance of her hog raising business.

name: Alexei
description: Alexei asks for a loan for the purchase of seeds, fertilizer, watering systems and other material for greenhouses.   Thanks to the previous loan, Alexei increased planting, was able to use the land effectively, and received a larger income from the early harvest, because late harvest had a much lower price. He was able to use more modern technologies for farming and planting.   Alexei has long worked with farming, and owns the largest plot of land in the village close to his house. He also has his own sawmill, where he works in his spare time, when there are orders.

name: Mbovoko
description: Mbovoko is a married woman with four children, three of whom attend school. She lives at her own house that has electricity and piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is school fees.She has operated a retail shop business for the past ten years, selling household consumables like wheat flour, maize flour, and sugar. She faces a major challenge of debtors taking too long to repay for goods taken on credit. In addition, she also operates a business of selling vegetables and a motorcycle business that earns her another source of income. With the loan she is requesting, she wants to purchase stock of sugar, rice, maize flour, and wheat flour. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Edwin Enrique
description: Edwin is a 26-year old man. He is hard-working and humble. Three years ago, after being left unemployed, he started to work raising and selling swine. Previously, his sales were very good, but at the moment they have dropped a lot. This is due to competition in the area and from the few pigs that he has. For this reason, he is asking for a loan to buy pigs, chickens, food and vaccines for them. His dream is to continue working, strengthen his business and, in the future, leave it to his two children. He knows that with help from Interactuar and the collaborations from Kiva, his dreams will come true.

name: Maria
description: With this, her second loan, Maria hopes to support her small farm business. She makes good money from her farm and therefore it is a must for her to keep it going. It is the only source of income for her and she needs to sustain it otherwise she will not have any more money for her use and to support her family.

name: Jacob
description: Jacob is a Cameroonian, 39 years old, living in a rural center and operating a small provision store. He is married and a father of three. His first child is in primary school and his wife is nursing the other two at home.   This loan will help Jacob to stock his store with provisions like soap, sugar, salt, chocolates, soft drinks, beer, magi (bullion) cubes, etc. It will equally increase his living standard and that of his household.

name: Mona
description: Mona is 28 years old from Baniswef. She is married with four children; the oldest is in elementary school. Since her husband is a part-time electrician and the money he makes could not cover the family's expenses, Mona decided to start a small beauty salon business. Mona passed a hairdressing training held by TADE, so she requested a 1000 EPG loan to buy a flat iron, hair drier, and some hairdressing tools for her project.

name: Charlotte
description: Charlotte is a 54-year-old widow. She rents a small house in town and is alone in ensuring that the needs of her three children are met. She has been selling mats and baskets for over twenty years at the big market in town. She had already had loans before. The profits from them have enabled her to start a business raising pigs. For this loan, she intends to increase her stock of mats by purchasing different sizes and ranges, so as to satisfy her customers and to attract new ones. Charlotte’s dream is to build a house for her children.

name: Min
description: Mrs. Min T. is 53 years old and lives with her husband and one child in Kampong Cham, Cambodia.  T. runs a small business buying rubber in bulk, then selling it to retailers for a profit.  She is able to earn about $3 per day from this business.  Her husband, meanwhile, runs a roadside petrol station where he sells bottles of gasoline.  He also is able to make about $3 per day from this.  The couple has one child who is still in school.  They hope to use this loan to purchase rubber for T.'s business and petrol for her husband's stand.  In the future, they hope that they will have enough money to build a new house.

name: Um
description: Um S. is a divorced mother caring for three children, one of whom attends the local school and is dependent on her income, while the other two work in a garment factory. A self-sacrificing and determined woman who tries to earn money to support her children, she sells rice and vegetables to  passers-by in her community.   Um S. will use the loan to buy more rice to store for future sale. This will allow her to gain more income and more valued customers, thereby enabling her to improve her family's standard of living.

name: Alfredo
description: Alfredo is 30-years-old and lives with his wife and two children.  He has been a farmer for 10 years, since the time of his marriage.  This work enables him to support his family and it is for this reason that he works so hard and with such determination.  He enjoys planting potatoes and corn on his land and he likes harvesting even more because this is when he can see and appreciate the high quality of his products.  In his city, the sale of potatoes is profitable depending on the quality of potatoes produced.  In general, the production of potatoes in his area is good and there is a great demand for them.  The most difficult part of the business is planting season, especially with the cost of fertilizers that are necessary for good yield.  This is Alfredo’s first loan through MFP; he plans to purchase fertilizer for his potato fields.Translated from Spanish by Ann Molloy, Kiva Volunteer

name: Anacleta
description: Anacleta sells food Monday through Friday.  On the week ends she goes to her community to take care of her animals.  She has two married daughters.  She is a widow, and she rents where she lives.  Selling food is her source of income to support herself.  Her home is located in the Vila Ingave zone in the city of El Alto.  The loan is to buy groceries (noodles, rice, and oil) in order to be able to increase her income.  This is her first loan with Imro.  The completed evaluation qualifies Anacleta for the requested loan. Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sakeena
description: Sakeena is 37 years old and she lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. with her four children. Her husband has been working in a public sector organization for many years and is responsible to fulfill the needs of the family. Sakeena provides sewing services and earns an income to contribute along with her husband to manage the household. She needs different kinds of goods e.g needles, thread, pieces of cloth, machine oil, etc. for her business purpose, but due to insufficient financial means she is unable to purchase these accessories. Therefore, she has applied for a Kiva loan from its field partner BRAC Pakistan. This loan will enable her to purchase these accessories and also help her to increase her monthly sales and profit by providing better sewing services.Sakeena is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Jacinta
description: Jacinta has been involved in activities since a few years ago. She started her business with her own working capital. She is married and is a businesswoman. Her husband is in agriculture, so he is very supportive of her doing business. Jacinta has a kiosk in her house, but her kiosk is very small. So, now she is requesting a loan of $1,000 because she wants to buy more items according to what people like, such as aqua, sardines, milk, candles, coffee, sugar, gambling cards, candies, noodles, soft drinks, and other things to sell. She is very hopeful that with this loan, she can improve her management of her business in the future.

name: Teresa
description: Teresa is a responsible, hard-working, smallholder farmer with a smile. She has a beautiful family, composed of eight children. Other than doing some small business, Teresa is a very hardworking farmer who has been farming for the past five years. She has gained so much experience through those years of farming. Teresa practices mixed farming. She grows maize and keeps dairy cows, and through these activities she has been able to earn a decent and honest income. Because of the passion she has for farming, she has even nicknamed one of her cows. She really enjoys taking care of her cows.   Although Teresa has been making profits through farming, not everything has been easy for this humble and industrious mom. Her farm has not been producing as much of a harvest because of the lack of fertilizer and good seeds and the presence of pests and diseases. That is why she is seeking a loan to buy farm inputs. Through the loan, Teresa will be assured of a greater harvest, and this will translate into more profits and cash. With good seeds and fertilizer, she will increase her profit margins. Kenyenya (her region) has a ready market for food stuffs and through this loan she will be able to fulfill this demand.  Through this loan, Teresa will be able to expand her farming business. She sees a lot of room for improvement and growth. What is lacking is the money to push the positive change. With your loan, Teresa will make enough income to take care of her family and other farming expenses. Teresa wakes up early and goes to sleep very late every day to give her family a decent living and provide her children with a proper education. She has many dreams. The main one is to make her farming business successful so that one day her children can inherit it and keep it so they have something to provide for themselves. You can help Teresa to accomplish this dream and all her goals with just a loan.

name: Digna Cristina
description: Digna, 58, started selling food a year and six months ago; she used to deliver meals to a firm.  She works with her daughter every day from 6am until 6pm.  The difficulty she has with her work is the delinquency that’s rife in her sector.  She’s not married but has two children who are 33 and 32 years old.  She has many hopes with her business because it’s her main source of income which is why she wants to use the loan to buy meat, beverages and grains.  Her goal is to make her food selling business grow even more.

name: Harlinson
description: Harlinson, aged 28, has always lived in the countryside, where he learned about farm work from his family. Currently, he makes a living breeding and fattening pigs, which he sells at the market in the municipality where he lives. This is how he generates the income to support his family.Harlinson has gone through a difficult financial situation; however, through his hard work, determination, and perseverance, he has been able to get ahead. He is requesting a loan to buy supplies and concentrated feed so that he can fatten his animals and later sell them at a better price. This will allow him to increase his production and the income he obtains from each sale and, as a result, improve his family’s living conditions in the medium term. It will also enable him to move a step closer to achieving his main dream: to spread out his production and, in this way, ensure a steadier income.If you want to know more about the entrepreneurs and the loans from Interactuar, you can join the Lending Team called: “Friends of Interactuar Colombia”: http://www.kiva.org/team/interactuar_colombia

name: Munawati
description: Good day lenders! Meet one of KPP-UMKM’s clients, Munawati, who is a 32-year-old women.  Munawati is married and has two daughters. She has had a small shop for five years, and her husband is a builder. She has asked for a loan of 7,300,000 IDR from KPP-UMKM Syariah. This loan will be used to build sanitation facilities at her home to improve sanitation and access to water sources for her family. Her family income is insufficient to build toilets and water sources, but Munawati will be able to repay the loan received.She and her family want to live a healthy, sanitary life with clean water. She is very grateful for the opportunity and wants to thank all of the lenders.

name: Esperanza
description: Esperanza is a very enthusiastic and hard working woman. She lives in the Yarina Cocha district in the region of Ucayali. She is 53 years old and the mother of six children, three of whom are full grown. She sells sweets in the afternoon in different locations around town.   Esperanza is a member of the village bank "Perlas de Pucallpa" (Pearls of Pucallpa). She has been a member for a year and a half and her first loan was for 300.00 nuevos soles which she used to buy fruit to sell from her home.   Now she needs a loan of 600.00 nuevos soles to buy sweets and fruits. Esperanza dreams of  having a small grocery store.Translated from Spanish by Cathy Coffman, Kiva Volunteer

name: Juan Carlos
description: Juan Carlos is an old dog in the area.  He is a man who provides auto and motorcycle mechanic services.  This started his life of independence and his dream of buying a home of his own.  This desire motivates him to rise up to complete it and he is very happy because he has found happiness and sustainment in his profession.  Juan Carlos is asking for a loan to buy motorcycle spare parts, tires, tools, and shop equipment.

name: Imee
description: Imee is a married woman with four children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Imee is 33 years old and has four children who are still in school.Imee has a buy-and-sell sea food business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 6,000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase more crab, shrimp, oysters, mussels and other seafood to sell.Imee has been in this business for 10 years. She would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Sokhom
description: Sokhom is 50 and a widowed mother of two children. She is photographed at the side of her house located in Prey Chhor district, Kampong Cham province.   Sokhom is in the business of growing rice and raising some poultry to make a livelihood. She has been working in the agricultural business for more than thirty years now. From her current business, she is able to earn well for her family.  Through this new loan, Sokhom would like to buy a piece of land to expand her farming area. Through this, she will be able to improve the productivity of her farm, thus augmenting her harvest and yield.   With her profit, Sokhom will reinvest in her business, but also take care of her family’s needs. She expresses her thanks to all lenders in advance.

name: Santa Cruz Group
description: The solidarity group Santa Cruz is formed by three hard-working entreprenuers and is coordinated by María Esther, who is 37 years old and married. She makes Nicaraguan tamales and sells them from her home, and she is requesting a loan to buy pork chunks, pork chops, bacon, plantain leaves, lard, a load of firewood, a quintal (100 lb. or 45 kg) of corn, and the like in order to meet the demand for her product.   The other members are 27-year-old Lylieth and 63-year-old Domingo. Lylieth sells clothes and Domingo sells vegetables in the municipal market.

name: Dilara
description: Dilara Z. is 31 years old and single. For a year she has been selling food in her grocery store. Dilara’s wish is to increase her business by offering a greater variety of foodstuffs to her customers who pass through this market. She has applied for 1000 AZN in order to increase the number of items she sells and to increase her profit.

name: Nirmala
description: Nirmala is 40 years-old. She is married and has 3 children, aged 22, 25 and 29.    In 1999, Nirmala established her cow-raising business. Working 7 days a week and 4 hours a day, she supports her family. She has already received and successfully repaid 4 loans from Patan BPW. She used her most recent loan to purchase a young milk-giving cow. In the future, Nirmala plans to uplift the economic conditions of her family. She thanks you for your support.   Dairy cows are an important source of nutrition and income in Nepal. Cows are never raised for beef, but for their milk, from which curd (duy) and fresh cheese (paneer) are made. Jersey cows are the preferred breed for milking. On average, a dairy cow in Nepal will produce about 10 liters of milk each day.  In the local market, a liter of milk sells for about USD $0.50. In addition to producing milk, cows provide dung that is used in home construction, as fuel for fires, and can be captured in methane storage tanks. The purchase of a dairy cow, made possible through a Kiva loan, is an investment that will repay itself many times over.

name: Heide
description: Heide is a married woman, who has three children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur. Heide is 36 years old, and two of her children are in school.Heide has a buy-and-sell-coconut-wine business in the Philippines. She has requested a PHP 9000 loan amount through NWTF. She will use the loan to buy more containers of coconut wine to sell.Heide has been in this business for five years. In the future, she would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Silvia
description: Silvia is 43 years old and is married with two children. She has been the owner and administrator of a store for 5 years along with her husband.  The loan she is requesting from Fundación Campo is to buy more basic goods such as sugar, oil, rice, beverages, etc. and to expand her store. Her goal is to strengthen her business, improve her earnings and to meet her family's needs, including providing schooling to her two children.  What she wishes for is to offer her family a better quality of life, carry out improvements to her home and have greater family security.

name: Domilyn
description: Domilyn A. is from the village of Gud. She is 34 years old. Domilyn is married and has 3 school-aged children. To make a living, Domilyn owns & operates a general store. The main source of income for the business comes from selling a variety of different products in the local community. Domilyn has been engaged in her business for over 3 years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Domilyn joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Domilyn is requesting a loan of 5,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Domilyn from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand it.   About ASKI: ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 25 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolk, and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Tamara's Group
description: Tamara S. is the leader of the group. She is 44 years old and divorced. She has raised five sons and a daughter. Three sons work in her sewing workshop and the other children study at school.   Ten years ago with an initial investment of 50,000 soms, Tamara opened a sewing workshop. She works there with her sons. By taking orders and selling different clothes, Tamara makes 18,000 soms per month.   She applied for this loan because she needs money to purchase fabric and materials for sewing the clothes. In the future, Tamara plans to purchase more sewing machines to expand her business and buy a flat for each son.  Gulmira T., 43 years old, is married. She has a son who is six years old and a student. In order to make money, Gulmira’s husband works in construction. Five years ago, Gulmira borrowed 20,000 soms from her sister and started to sell fruits and vegetables at the market. Today, by selling fruits and vegetables, she makes 17,000 soms per month. With money received from this loan, Gulmira wants to purchase various fruits and vegetables in order to resell them. In the future, she wants to build a store, and adopt a girl from an orphanage.  Aaly A., 46 years old, is married. He has two daughters and a son. His older daughter works as baker in Bishkek, his son is a waiter in Russia, and his second daughter studies in school. Seventeen years ago with an initial investment of 30,000 soms, Aaly started selling fruits and vegetables. He makes 18,200 soms per month. With the money received from this loan, he wants to purchase fruits in order to resell them at a higher price. In the future, he wants to contribute some money to his daughter’s wedding and to purchase a flat for his son.  Taalaikul J. is the treasurer of the group. She is 33 years old and married. She has two sons and a daughter. In order to make money, her husband works as driver and Taalaikul sells convenience goods in a kiosk. She has been doing this for eight years. Taalaikul started with an initial investment of 10,000 soms and now she makes 11,000 soms per month. With money received from this loan, she wants to purchase various goods to resell in her kiosk. In the future, she wants to build a big store and purchase a vehicle.  --- Where Did This Loan Come From? ---  This loan is brought to you by Mol Bulak Finance, a young, ambitious and socially-focused MFI in Kyrgyzstan.  Mol Bulak Finance is strongly committed to the principles of sustainable development and upholds the triple bottom line – People (building human capital and taking care of its customers as well as society), Planet (keeping environmentally friendly) and Profit (earning revenue to expand autonomously). Mol Bulak is the only MFI in Kyrgyzstan that delivers its services to customers 365 days a year. To learn more about Mol Bulak and view a Video presentation about the organization, please visit: http://www.kiva.org/about/aboutPartner?id=135  If you would like to support and learn more about Kyrgyzstan and microfinance in Central Asia, please join our Lending Team - Supporters of Kyrgyzstan – Mol Bulak Finance at http://kiva.org/team/kyrgyzstan. Members will get special updates and news from Kiva Fellows in Kyrgyzstan and from the Mol Bulak Finance staff.

name: Lucila
description: Lucila is 21 years old and lives with her husband, 2 younger children and father-in-law. In the morning she prepares the family’s meals and then at around 11am, takes it upon herself to deliver her husband’s lunch to him out in the fields, something she has been doing for 4 years, since living with her husband. At first she found it very difficult to adapt to the rhythm of life in the country but now she is used to it. Crop-growing is her husband’s only livelihood yet she has also seen an advantage in rearing and selling pigs, feeding them the potatoes that are not good enough to sell in the markets. For her it is better that the pigs feed on these crops than they go to waste and in this way generating an additional source of income. Lucila is new to MFP and with the loan she intends to buy phosphate and potassium nitrate so that she can fertilise her crops. Translated from Spanish by Sara Roden-Scott, Kiva Volunteer

name: María Santos
description: María is 46 years old and completed a 5th grade education, as her parents could help her study more due to lack of economic resources. She is a single mother of 3 children, only one of whom lives with her. From a young age Maria helped her parents with the corn planting. They also raised cattle, pigs, and chickens. Today, she grows corn and beans. in addition, she continues raising cattle with the help of her son. In this way she is able to obtain income to cover her household expenses. The loan will be used to buy grazing cattle. In this way she will be able to have income upon selling the cattle. Maria's dream is to improve her home and only she will be able to achieve this by working very hard, as she has done up until today.

name: Efua
description: Efua K. produces palm oil locally for sale at Jukwa.To prepare her palm oil, she gets palm nuts from farmers on the farm. She washes them, boils them for a while until they become soft and tender. She scoops the cooked fruits into a big mortar and gently pounds with a pestle to avoid damaging the nut. Water is then added to the pounded fruit. The mixture of water and the pounded fruit is squeezed and filtered to get the juice out and the chaff removed. (The chaff is sometimes used by the local people to light charcoal fires).The juice is boiled again and as it boils the fresh oil will be seen floating on the surface of the pot; it is scooped into yet another pot and left to cool. Fresh oil from palm fruits is traditionally used in eating roasted yam or plantain in Africa – especially on the farms after a hard day's work.  Efua has received junior high education. She is a widow and has four children. Efua has been selling palm oil for some time now. She is responsible for the payment of school fees and utility bills. Her loan will be used to buy more palm fruits to make palm oil for sale. She hopes to use the new profits from her business to save up for her children’s education.

name: Vilma Abigail
description: Vilma is 30 years old and is very well-known as a principled person in the place where she lives.  She keeps up her home and on the weekends she makes pupusas to sell.  She has also made a living selling tortillas daily for the past 5 years.  Vilma lives with and grew up with her parents who are very humble and hard-working people who also make a living selling tortillas and pupusas.  She is the youngest of 3 siblings in her family, which meant that she helped with the housework in her home and with the family business, so it was difficult for her to complete her education and she only studied through the 7th grade.  After a time when she reached the appropriate age she met the man who is now her husband, who makes a living providing transport services.  Together they have a daughter and a son.  The loan that she is applying for from CREDICAMPO is for buying oil, beans, sugar, rice, sardines, bread, flour, corn, and sausages, among other products, to keep her store running.  In the area where they live the closest store is a kilometer away, and therefore they make very good profits.    Her dreams and goals for the future are to finish paying back the loan and then to take out a new loan to improve her home, the facilities where she sells pupusas, and the store, and she will accomplish these with the help of her husband while supporting her children in their education.

name: Artemio
description: Artemio is 58 years old. He is someone who has always worked hard to advance in life. He lives alone in his own home and his greatest wish is to have a peaceful old age. Time has taught Artemio that one has to work very hard if the harvest is going to be the best in the village so it is with a great deal of effort that he has cared for his potato, sweet pea, spinach, and carrot plantations. His products are very sought out in the markets of the city of Tarma. What he most enjoys about the work is the harvest. For the past 45 years he has worked in the business and it has always been very difficult to ward his fields from insects and pests. In time he hopes to cultivate all of his land to improve his yield.  This is the eighth loan through MFP (Kiva Field Partner). He has always been on time with his payments and he plans on keeping his record. In his community bank he is a very engaged member. With the eight hundred nuevos soles he requests he will purchase pea seeds, this being the harvest that sells the best.Translated from Spanish by Erika Lindig, Kiva Volunteer

name: James
description: James, a 50-year-old single man with seven children ranging from 16  to 25 years of age, describes himself as dedicated and goal-oriented. He has been operating a retail store selling paints for 22 years and employs five staff members. His business is located in a busy  environment conducive to business, and his primary customers are local residents.  Describing his biggest business challenge to be delays in customer payments, James is requesting this Kes 20,000 loan to purchase titanium dioxide and paint stains.  His business goal is to be a large supplier of paint.

name: Beverly
description: Beverly previously accessed a 30,000 PHP loan that she used to purchase more quantities and varieties of grocery items and products needed in her business. Through the loan, she was able to increase her income and her earnings were a big help for sustaining their daily family needs.   She would like to apply for another 15,000 PHP loan to purchase more grocery items to sell in her store. Surely, having more items to sell means making a better profit. She looks forward to this financial increase with gladness and thankfulness in her heart.   As she hopes to attain a better living condition someday for her family, she is indeed working hard to earn money to improve her children's education. This is basically because she believes that education is the mere foundation to progress. She meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her life and business every week and where she can also draw strength and inspiration from the fellowship and the Word of God she studies.  *All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans.

name: Sopheap's Group
description: Sopheap’s group live in a rural village in Kampong Speu province in Cambodia. Sopheap makes a living cultivating rice and she also does extra work as a factory laborer to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Blandine
description: Blandine is 36 years old and married to a bricklayer . The couple has 3 children. They are respectively aged 15, 13 and 5 years old. They are all in school . Blandine is a progressive woman who grasps opportunities. She aims to build a house so that she will no longer have to pay rent. She would also like to expand her business. Blandine runs a small tavern since 1995. She used to help her parents but after they died she decided to create her own business. This is her fifth loan with CEFOR. The loan will be used to purchase a freezer, a showcase and edible products  : rice, vegetables, meat, flour and oil .

name: Las Orquideas Group
description: The “LAS ORQUIDEAS” group is made up of members who work in different activities as retailers. Hilda is 30 years old, married, and is raising 3 children. She works  sewing services in a textile business. She is going to invest in buying a computer with her husband's help, in order to improve the quality of her children's education. Hilda's goal is to buy a sewing machine to become independent and be able to spend more time with her children. The group is grateful to the Kiva investors for the loan. Hilda is the third from the right, wearing a white t-shirt.

name: Agustín Leonel
description: Agustín C. is a bricklayer who lives in the Municipality of Nagarote. He has had three loans with CEPRODEL, which have been used to improve the conditions of his home, which had walls covered in plastic. Currently, he is requesting a new loan to use for the purchase of construction materials, such as cement and quarry stone, in order to put up another wall in his house. He has the advantage that he himself can perform these improvements since he works as a bricklayer. With this loan, he will improve the living conditions and security of his family.Translated from Spanish by Tara Binetti, Kiva Volunteer

name: Massa
description: Massa, 31, resides with her husband and two children at Paynesville South. Her children are ages 2 and 13 and are currently in school.   Massa has been selling coal at retail in the community market for the past five years. A difficulty she faces is low sales during the rainy season. Because of her good interaction with her customers, she make profits when she sells. She has requested a loan to purchase more bags of coal, to sell at retail in the market. Her plan for the future is to build a decent house.

name: Qurbonboy
description: Qurbonboy is a resident of the city of Kulob.  He is 27 years old, married and has one child.  Qurbonboy has an unfinished higher education.  He has been working as a taxi driver for three years.  He primarily transports passengers along the Dushanbe-Kulob route.  Qurbonboy is requesting this loan to repair his car.

name: Jhonn
description: Jhonn is single and doesn't have children. He lives in a rented house in the 8 de Diciembre neighborhood in the city of La Paz.  Jhonn's education level is secondary school. He currently works as the employee of a tourism company which pays him a monthly salary.  He needs the loan to buy camping equipment (assembly shopping) to sell it to tourists who visit the La Paz area, thus continuing his own business which, little by little, is giving him extra income.  Jhonn's dream is to have his own tourism business and show off the beauty of our country.  This is the third time he has asked for a loan through IMPRO and the second time with Kiva.

name: Joumana
description: Joumana A. is 45 years old and lives in the area of Ouzai, one of the poorest areas of  the Beirut suburbs. She sells detergents to her surrounding neighbors. She needs $900 to build up a large enough inventory of cleaning products. Being divorced from her husband, she strives to provide a good education for her 2 children with the money she earns from her small business.

name: Anibal Antonio
description: Anibal is 22 years old and unmarried. For the past six years, he's worked as a tax collector for the Juigalpa town government. He doesn't have any children. He lives with his mother and helps her by paying for the domestic expenses (water, electricity, food). He is requesting his second loan in order to do some repairs on his mother's house, replacing the roof and installing support beams, since the current roof is in bad shape and leaks during the rainy season. He wants to complete the repairs before the rains begin so his mother can be more comfortable. He hopes to receive funding from Kiva for this little project, since it is only through these loans that he is able to improve his family's living conditions.Translated from Spanish by Andrea Rosenberg, Kiva Volunteer

name: Akossiwa
description: Akossiwa is a 24-year-old woman.  She is married to a refrigerating engineer and has one child.  Akossiwa has been reselling grocery products since 2008.  She purchases her products at the Grand Market of Lomé and sells them in a shop.  Her main difficulty is a drop in sales.  In order to buy products that will better meet customer demand during the Holidays, Akossiwa has requested her first loan from WAGES.  Akossiwa would like to increase her profits in order to fulfill her family's needs.

name: Zahara's Group
description: Zahara's group is comprised of 7 hard working women. Zahara is 21-years-old and lives in the town of Iganga in the region of Uganda. She is married and has 3 children, 2 of them are currently in school. For the past 3 years, Zahara has been working hard to manage her clothing business.   To help expand her business, Zahara has requested a loan of 200,000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy more clothes to sell, and will help Zahara to generate greater profits and provide school fees for her young children. Zahara hopes that in the future she will be able to own a shop were she can sell her clothes.   Zahara is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities, and a forum for life-skills training.

name: Wilma
description: Wilma is 23 years old and a very hard working entrepreneur who earns a living by buying and selling frozen food in the Philippines. She is requesting a PHP 7,000 loan through NWTF to buy more items to sell. Wilma has been in this business for three years. In the future, she would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Safarali
description: Safarali I. lives in the Farkhor Region. 65 years of age. Married, with four children. His wife is a homemaker. His son raises livestock and lives on his own, together with his own family. Safarali works as a freelance construction worker. In addition, in his free time he raises livestock. He mainly raises farm animals for resale. He has been doing it for over 20 years. He is taking out a loan in order to buy cattle.

name: Clovice
description: Clovice used the previous loan to buy manure and pesticides for his farm so as to increase his production which can be evidenced by the fact that he now has a poultry project alongside farming. His challenges are price fluctuations, inflation, and customers not paying on time. His dream is to educate his children and buy land to grow crops.

name: Josephine
description: As a married parent of five children, Josephine works hard to support her family.  She has a vegetable vending business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from fishing/fish vending.  Josephine is borrowing 6,000 PHP, through NWTF, to purchase more vegetables to sell at her vegetable vending business.  Josephine has been sustaining her business activities through her past 2 loans from NWTF.
