She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Salome
description: Salome is 42 years old, married and blessed with 5 children. She runs a primary school that has been in operation for 6 years now. Salome makes a monthly income of KES 17,000.  This is Salome's 5th loan and she will use it to renovate the school. She will buy more desks, build classrooms and buy more learning materials. She will use her profits to add more classrooms as a way of expanding her school. She paid all her previous loans successfully.   Salome's future hopes and dreams are for her school to grow to a college level.

name: Famille Libakale Group
description: The Libakale Group is made up of three members of whom Aimé is the leader (the man in the middle with a white shirt). His family has been growing coffee for some twenty years since it is profitable in the area. For him, the main challenge is the absence of markets which can permit coffee growers to sell at a reasonable price. Nevertheless, Aimé hopes to grow his income so that he can ensure payment of his children's school fees.

name: Emily
description: Regardless of the great impact that agriculture has on the Kenyan economy, microfinance institutions (M.F.I.s) view lending to fund agricultural activities as a high-risk proposition. Juhudi Kilimo is expanding into this market and is happy to provide Kiva lenders with the opportunity to support Kenyan farmers. Meet Emmy, an ever-smiling, hardworking, and honest mother who is 41 years of age. She hails from the Siongiroi area of Kenya. She is the proud mother of four lovely children. She loves and treasures her children and will go the extra mile to make sure that they are comfortable. Emmy’s primary source of income has come from selling milk, crop farming, and poultry farming. Through these ventures she has been able to earn a decent income. She is a very determined and dedicated farmer who has been farming for 10 years, and throughout, she has never regretted going into farming. Although this humble mum has been making profits, not everything has been a bed of roses. She faces financial challenges, and because the Siongiroi area has proven a ready market for cereals, she is kindly seeking a loan to buy cereals for re-sale and thus improve her income. Emmy’s upbringing was challenging, and she has faced many economic problems. Still, this ever-smiling mum has been making great improvements, and she believes that through your loan she will be able to realize her goal of improving her living conditions and transforming her life. Through Juhudi Kilimo, Emmy has received training and she has proven to be honest and disciplined with finances. She intends to fully repay the loan with the profits from her business. Emmy is quite visionary and - with her accumulated profits - hopes she will be able to open a large cereal-selling shop that will boost her income and turn her life around.

name: Sofya
description: Sofya is 30-year-old student, who lives in Yerevan with her mother and brother. Sofya studies at Yerevan State Medical College and is in her third course.  Besides her studies in the college, Sofya works at local clinic as a recorder.  As her salary doesn’t allow her to save money for education, Sofya has applied for this loan. With the requested amount Sofya, would be able to pay for tuition fee for the first semester and continue her study in the college.

name: Rose
description: Rose is a 34 year old married woman. She has 5 children, ages ranging from 5 years to 15 years. She describes herself to be a confident woman. She operates a grocery store where she sells vegetables such as onions, tomatoes, oranges, peas etc. She has been involved in this business for 3 years. Her business is located within a competitive market and her primary customers are local consumers.   Rose describes her biggest business challenge to be high prices of vegetables and insufficient funds for restocking. She will use the KES 8700 loan to purchase a water tank for her family's use. Her business goal is to expand her business ten times more within 5 years. She hopes that, in the future, she will a great millionaire owning many business premises. Rose had taken a loan of KES 20,000, which she repaid well. She also does farming, which increases her daily income.

name: Blanca Nieves
description: Blanca belongs to the communal bank Las Margaritas, in the district of Coronel  Portillo, department of Ucayali. She is 57 years old, single, and has one child.  She has been working with loans from Manuela Ramos for twelve years. She works making placemats and pillowcases.   She will use her new loan of 2,500 nuevos soles to purchase 22 lbs of flower-patterned fabric, a roll of satin ribbon, half a dozen spools of colored thread, and three sets of needles for her sewing machines.   Her business is small. She has two sewing machines to work with, but lacks a serger so that she can give her products a better finishing. She also needs a space where she can work comfortably. She is grateful to Manuela Ramos for granting her loans with every cycle so that she can stock her business.

name: Andrea
description: Andrea is a young woman who makes crafts and costume jewelry as a way of generating income to meet her needs: to pay for schooling and her personal expenses.

name: Fezy
description: Fezy (his wife is pictured) is 28, married, and has two children. He is an Internally Displaced Person (IDP) from the Armenian-occupied territory of the Gubadli region in Azerbaijan, and is settled in the Absheron region. The F.'s family started a general food business ten years ago. Now his family needs a loan of $1200 to buy more food items to help improve their business.

name: Nataliya
description: Nataliya is married with two sons. In addition to her immediate family, she also takes care of her mother and father-in-law and her nephew who lives with them. Nataliya started her business because there was no other means to sustain her family. Today she runs a couple of kiosks selling bedding and knitted wear for children in the central city market. She has been in this trade for ten years. Currently, she has around $2,500 of working capital. Her monthly net profit amounts to $1,200.   Nataliya is very cheerful and friendly. Her first goal is to please her customers, which has added a lot to the success of her business. Nataliya’s reasonable pricing policy helps her keep loyal clients and attract new customers. The nineteen loans she has received and repaid from “Nadiya Ukraine” have also had a big part in the growth of her business. Not long ago Nataliya was able to purchase another vending kiosk and hire a person to help her with sales.   Nataliya is requesting a loan of $1,000 to purchase bed sets for children from a wholesaler. She is planning to double her assortment of inventory with warm blankets, linen sheets, pillow cases, and diapers that she can purchase in bulk. Nataliya has a couple of goals in mind for her added sales income. First, she would like to assist her nephew with his college tuition. Secondly, she is planning to use part of the income to open two new vending kiosks to sell flower seeds, plants and fertilizers during the spring season. Gardening has always been a hobby of Nataliya’s and she would like to use her knowledge and skills in this area for a new business startup.     Наталя – одружена, в неї двоє синів. Вона також дбає про своїх свекра, свекруху та племінника, який живе з ними. Наталя вирішила займатися бізнесом тому що не було інших можливостей забезпечувати родину. Зараз в неї два кіоски з продажу постільної білизни та трикотажу для дітей. Торгує Наталя на центральному міському ринку. Вона займається торгівлею вже десять років. Зараз сума її робочого капіталу становить приблизно 2500 доларів. Щомісячний прибуток складає 1200 доларів.   Наталя дуже привітна та енергійна. Вона понад усе намагається догодити клієнту, це сприяє успіху її бізнесу. Помірні ціни на товари допомагають Наталі зберегти вірних клієнтів та привабити нових. Дев’ятнадцять позик, які вона отримала та сплатила в «Надії України» також позитивно відзначилися на розширенні її бізнесу. Нещодавно Наталя змогла придбати ще один кіоск та взяти на роботу ще одного реалізатора.    Наталя просить про позику в 1000 доларів для того, щоб закупити комплекти постільної білизни для дітей на оптовому складі. Вона планує вдвічі збільшити асортимент ковдр, лляних простирадл, наволочок та пелюшок. Отриманий прибуток Наталя планує використати для того, щоб заплатити за навчання свого племінника в університеті. До того ж вона планує відкрити дві торгівельні точки з продажу насіння, рослин та добрив під час весняного періоду. Садівництво завжди було Наталі до душі, отже, зараз вона хотіла б використати власні знання та досвід в цій сфері для того, щоб почати новий бізнес.

name: Mary Ann
description: Mary Ann is 25 years old, and her family happily resides in Barangay Estrella.  Mary Ann has been in the direct selling business for three years. She is now generating a monthly net income of PHP 4,000. She is glad that, through patience, she was able to improve her small enterprise.   She wanted to borrow at least PHP 12,000 to buy more products such as lotion, deodorant, powder, and cologne to sell. With this amount, she can sell more products, and hopefully save some of her income for her family.

name: Immaculate's Group
description: Immaculate is 35 years old and is often described as a very friendly person. She has four children and is married. As a group leader, Immaculate is representing a group of 12 farmers from the Butere district in Kenya and is very excited to be working with One Acre Fund for the first time this year.  The decision to join One Acre Fund was largely a result of Immaculate's desire to make more farmer friends in her community. Apart from receiving farming inputs, she is also purchasing a solar light as part of her loan, which is very exciting for her as she will now be able to have light during dark hours for her children to study. With the profits that she gains from this year’s harvest, she plans to buy a cow.  Immaculate and her group will receive a total of nine solar lights as well as input loans of maize and fertilizer to plant a total of eight acres.

name: Noe
description: Noe F. is a farmer.  He is 31 and lives in the Cerco de Piedra region, La Concordia, in Estelí.  He is married and has 3 children.  Noe began farming with his parents and brothers 14 years ago and his family would give him a little money for personal expenses. He decided to go out on his own when he was 18 and his father gave him 2 small fields that he used to begin, and he took out his first loan.  He started planting onions and he also started buying and selling cattle.  He does the latter on a small scale-the income he uses for household expenses.  With this loan he would like to buy supplies to plant onions. He thinks that his crop will be stronger and he can sell it at the market for a higher price.

name: Petra Consuelo
description: Petra is 58 years old. She has a workshop for making clothes. She lives in Fortin de Guayaquil (suburban zone with unpaved roads and hills). Years ago she learned to sew and make clothing while working in a textile factory. With effort and some savings she decided to become independent and work from her own home with a sewing machine. Little by little she obtained a clientele. Now she has a sewing and clothing workshop. She works starting at 6:00 am.   To make more clothes she would like to buy with the loan fabrics, wires, and padding. In the future she would like to buy a car for transporting the clothing.     Translated from Spanish by Machelle Wilson, Kiva Volunteer

name: Munaza
description: Munaza is a 32-year-old woman who lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan with her three children. Her husband has been working for a public sector organization for many years. He is responsible for fulfilling the needs of his family. Munaza is also providing sewing services and earns an income to contribute with her husband to manage the household. She needs different kinds of goods such as needles, thread, pieces of clothes, machine oil, etc. for her business purposes, but due to insufficient financial means she is unable to purchase these accessories. Therefore she has applied for a Kiva loan from its field partner BRAC Pakistan. This loan will enable her to purchase the above accessories and also be helpful for her to increase monthly sales and profit by providing better sewing services.Munaza is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Anabel
description: Being a mother, Anabel T.’s aspirations in life are all focused on the welfare of her children. Despite living in poverty, she is determined to achieve her goals no matter how hard she needs to work to make this happen. She will do this with her husband, who is always by her side and committed to accompany her through life.     Today, Anabel's main goal is to build a home for her family and keep everyone safe from harm. She plans to pay for this home by raising pigs, and with help from her husband, who is an office worker. She joined ASHI in 2007 and has used several previous loans to establish her livestock business. She is now applying for a new loan to increase the number of piglets she can raise and sell for a profit.

name: Tsorkor
description: Tsorkor is a seamstress from Alavanyo, Hohoe. Tsorkor has received a formal education but only up to the Junior High School level.  She is a young, single lady. Tsorkor has been sewing for the past two years. She is responsible for her general upkeep. Her loan will be used to buy and sell cloth in large quantity since her customers who want to sew buy cloth from her. She hopes to use the new profits from her business to save for her future.

name: San Cayetano Group
description: The "San Cayetano" group is known for being very close-knit. It is on its sixth loan cycle as part of the women's committee programme, and its members are undergoing the poverty elimination survey in order to grow, prosper, and learn more in training.  One member of the group is Dominga who, at the last survey, was at level one poverty: this means that she was achieving very low results for all indicators. Dominga tells us that she has a small shop where she works every day from early in the morning. She is fighting for her loved ones in order to give them everything that she could not have.  Today Dominga is applying for this loan in order to to buy drinks, breads, vegetables and other products to stock up her business. She can then continue to offer her customers a good variety of products. Dominga is grateful for this opportunity to continue growing through training.

name: Grace
description: Grace lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is married with five children and all go to school.  She supports additional family members. She sells charcoal at the market on both a retail and a wholesale basis and has been in this business for 10 years.   She has applied for a loan of 2,700,000 Uganda shillings from MCDT-SACCO to buy more bags of charcoal to sell. She gets additional income from rental houses.   Grace works seven days a week. Her major business challenges include seasonality and transportation. In future she would like to build more rental houses. She resides in the family home where the family has access to electricity and piped water. Her monthly expenses include school fees and feeding the family.

name: Ghazala Liaqat Group
description: Ghazala baji, wife of L., has resided in the city of Lahore, Pakistan, for the past ten years. Lahore city is famous for its historical places and its Punjabi foods.  Ghazala baji is a very active lady. She performs her duties and manages her family very effectively. Her husband runs a grocery shop in the community. People are used to coming to him for groceries because of the reasonable prices and good quality. She is requesting a loan to buy more groceries to advance her husband’s grocery shop.   This loan consists of four additional people:   Nasira baji wants a loan to buy plastic water bottles to sell.  Farzana baji wants a loan to buy a sewing machine for sewing clothes.  Salma baji wants a loan to buy another water-buffalo for her animal-selling business.  Shagufta baji wants a loan to buy sanitary supplies (pipes, taps) to sell.  In the photo, Ghazala baji is standing in the center of the group, showing her member Salma baji’s water-buffalo.

name: Nida
description: Nida is a hardworking 40-year-old mother of two school-age children who is engaged in vegetable-vending business to contribute to the family income.  Due to the hardships of living, she and her husband help each other in earning income to pay for their necessities and finance the education of their children.   Nida is requesting a loan of P10,000.00 buy additional stocks of string beans, eggplant, pechay, bitter melon, tomatoes, squash and onions to sell. She hopes to improve the business and make it more profitable through patience and hard work.
town: Brgy. Ineangan, Dupax del Norte, Nueva Vizcaya

name: Avelita
description: Avelita V. is from the village of D'BAN, Calamba, Misamis Occidental. She is 44 years old. Avelita is married and has 3 school-aged children. To make a living, Avelita owns & operates a business manufacturing flower pots and native baskets. Avelita has been engaged in her business for over 7 years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month.  In 2008, Avelita joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to improve her living situation and give her the ability to engage in business activities. Avelita has successfully repaid a previous loan of 7,000 PHP from GDMPC.This previous loan was used to purchase materials needed to expand the business. Avelita is requesting a new loan of 10,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional materials needed for her business. This loan will be the third loan taken out by Avelita from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the family's income.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three units offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Maudy
description: Maudy, 32 years old, is a woman with a great desire to move forward and provide her family with a better quality of life. She is married to Augusto, who has a job and is the father of their 2 children ages 3 and 2. Together, they live comfortably in their own home. Maudy sells regional food dishes, which is why she will set up a stall in front of her house where she happily attends to her customers. These are primarily neighbors and passers-by of the area. She is restarting this business since she previously had to leave it due to personal problems. Now she is getting the necessary items such as plates, pots, and other products. She plans to run it on her own.  She believes her business is fairly successful because there is a high demand in the area because she is well-known and popular. Her neighbors were the ones who asked her to reopen the business. On the other hand, she mentions that she has financial problems because her husband's income is not enough to cover all their expenses. Therefore, she wants to help him earn additional income. This will be her third Kiva loan and she is very grateful for the financial support she receives. This allows her to move forward in her initiative to reopen her business.  With the requested amount of 1200 nuevo soles, she will buy items such as pots, glasses, and plates in addition to tables and chairs, which are necessary for her food stall.

name: Santos Gilberto
description: Santos, 22, is a very hard-working and responsible young man who devotes himself entirely to his family’s well-being. He lives in San Francisco Gotera, Morazán, together with his wife, 20, who does household chores, and their three year-old daughter.   Santos works buying and selling livestock, which he breeds in his home, located in the rural part of San Francisco Gotera. He learned this trade from his family, which is why he already has 7 years of experience. He is well-known in the area and trusted by many people who buy his livestock.    Santos is a young man who strives to find new customers and make new sales. Every weekend he comes to people’s homes to market his livestock, thus earning extra income. Santos requests a loan as a means to buy more livestock and all of the feed and vitamins necessary for optimal breeding, allowing him to offer a better product.  Translated from Spanish by Samantha Cerone, Kiva Volunteer
town: San Francisco Gotera, departamento de Morazán

name: Delia
description: Delia is 54 years old and has one child.  Delia is in the agricultural business farming vegetable in the Philippines. Delia requested a PHP 20000 loan through NWTF to buy fertilizers and other farm supplies.  Delia has been in this business for 6 years now, and has borrowed 1 time in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Delia would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Fe
description: Fe is 59 years old. She is very responsible in handling her household obligations, and she has always been known to provide the best for her family. She currently lives with her husband and three children at Brgy. Minsubong, Tangub City, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. She is a farmer who plants bananas, and she also teaches day care students in the area.  Fe wants to increase her sales. Consequently, she has requested a loan that will enable her to purchase seeds, compost, and fertilizer, among other items, so that she can continue to put food on the table in her home.

name: Jeanne
description: Mrs. Jeanne S. was born in 1964, she is a native of Abomey in the department of Zou. She is divorced and financially responsible for 4 children. She attended school until 7th grade, middle school. The lack of financial resources forced her to abandon her schooling. Later, she received a training as a typist, but, unfortunately, was never able to practice. Thus she began selling food, then later, sold manioc flour (gari), peanut fritters,and liquor. In the last few years, she has specialized in the sale on credit of charcoal, bundles of firewood and the distribution of pagnes (traditional wrap around fabric) and other goods to civil service employees. To increase her business capital she is requesting this second loan of  140,000F to stock up on corn, coco yams and pagnes.  Translated from French by Véronique Fourment, Kiva Volunteer

name: George
description: George is a married man. He has 6 children. He operates a transport business where he transports customers using his motorcycle. He has been involved in this business for 3 years. His business is located in a good area and his primary customers are the general public. He describes his biggest business challenge to be inadequate working capital. He will use the Kes 60,000 loan to service and maintain his motorcycle. He hopes that in the future, he will be financially stable. This is his fifth loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. The previous loan was repaid successfully.

name: Sevil
description: Sevil Aliyeva is a 42-year-old married woman with 3 sons and 1 daughter. She keeps sheep for meat production and poultry. But her main activity is livestock-raising.   Sevil started her business in 1997  and since that time she has learned a lot and has become a skilled entrepreneur. Sevil and her husband are otherwise unemployed. Sevil`s sons help her a lot and she believes one day they will continue the family business. She has applied for a loan in the amount of 800 USD to purchase one milch cow and continue to struggle to help her beloved family get ahead and improve their economic situation. Let's be a helping hand   to make this wish come true!

name: Marieta
description: Marieta is married with two children. Marieta is 52 years old and lives in Dolipos Bajo, Oroquieta City. Marieta is engaged in buying & selling to earn a living and has had this business for 5 years. Each month, she earns PHP 3,000 doing this type of work. She has requested a loan for PHP 10,000 for additional capital for her business of buying & selling whole coconuts. Marieta has been a member of PMPC for 3 years. In the future, Marieta hopes to have more savings and wants to live comfortably with her family.
town: Oroquieta-Tui-an Dolipos Bajo, Oroq., Mis. Occ.

name: Daniel
description: Daniel is a Kiva borrower. He operates a retail business where he sells sugar, bread, soap, soda and other items. He has been involved in this business for 10 years. His primary customers are locals.  He will use the Kes 50,000 loan to buy more stock of sugar, soap, soda, flour and other items.  His business goal is to have a mini supermarket within 5 years. This is his third loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.  Previous loans were repaid successfully.

name: Harriet
description: Harriet is a married lady living in Fort Portal, Uganda. She has a business of rentals and at the same time has a motor vehicle transport business that adds to her income. She is faced with the challenge of inadequate capital that hinders progress of her business. However, she has hopes of buying more land to build more houses for her rental business. Harriet has asked for a loan to help her buy land where she will construct houses to rent.

name: Adja
description: Adja is a retail merchant of grain cereals, with a seniority of 1.5 years in this commercial activity. She gets her supplies from the local market in Agoé, and now also retails charcoal as a side business to increase her income.  Wishing to resupply she is requesting a loan from WAGES to buy five bags of corn, two bags of millet and various items. She is married and the mother of two children.Translated from French by René McConnell, Kiva Volunteer

name: Dúo San Antonio Group
description: Dúo San AntonioThis duo is composed of Aura and Petrona, both from the municipality of San Pedro Sacatepéquez. Aura, 34, is married and is the mother of two children.  For eight years, Aura has been making a living selling, in an itinerant manner, a variety of traditional clothing. She offers her customers, mostly ladies, items such as belts, blouses, traditional tunics, traditional skirts, aprons, etc.; in their homes. She has a small business selling daily consumer goods. She is requesting this loan to purchase traditional clothing to sell.
town: Aldea Vista Hermosa, San Pedro Sacatepequez

name: Maria
description: Maria is an accounting student. She is studying in the last year of the program. She works in an accounting firm as an assistant, and she aspires to graduate next year and begin to work as a professional.She is requesting this loan to be able to pay the bills for her program and in this way be able to continue with her studies as she has been doing.

name: Gloria Betty
description: Gloria Betty is 36 years old and owns her own home. Her husband, Don Juan, is a professional illustrator. They have two children. Gloria works in her father’s home, selling gifts, which helps to pay their household expenses. This loan will help Gloria buy new merchandise, cellophane paper, wrapping paper and gift boxes. People buy a lot of gifts this time of year, so Gloria’s sales are quite high.  Translated from Spanish by Corinne Gilroy, Kiva Volunteer

name: Wenifreda
description: Wenifreda A. is from the village of Mibantang, Quezon, Bukidnon. She is 56 years old. Wenifreda is married and has 7 grown children. To make a living, Wenifreda owns & operates a mini-restaurant, serving a variety of different meals to customers in the local community. Wenifreda has been engaged in her business for over 7 years and earns approximately 10000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Wenifreda joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. Wenifreda has successfully repaid a previous loan of 11000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to purchase food & drinks for the restaurant. Wenifreda is requesting a new loan of 14000 PHP which will be used to invest in expanding the business. This will be the 4th loan taken out by Wenifreda from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Remegia
description: Remegia runs and operates a printing business in Brgy. 7, Tangub City, Misamis Occidental. She is 69 years old and married, with adult-age children. She has local customers as well as customers from neighboring towns. In need of a new printing machine and other materials, she is asking for a loan from Paglaum MPC. The amount shall be spent to purchase a new printing machine, bond paper, and other materials.

name: Fatuma
description: Fatuma is hard-working and enterprising, the widowed mother of four children, who are adults. She owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is food .  Fatuma prepares dumplings using sugar, cooking oil, and wheat flour and sells them to neighbors and passersby. She cites seasonality as her major challenge.  With the KES 30,000, she wants to purchase more wheat flour, sugar, and cooking oil for her business. She joined Yehu to boost her business.

name: Pen
description: Mr. Pen C., 54, is a widower with 3 children who works in construction in Siem Reap Province. He  normally earns about $4 a day. To save on commuting expenses, he is requesting a loan of $300 from Kiva to purchase a motorbike. In the future when he has enough capital, he will open a small business for his children selling grocery products. He thanks you for your consideration.

name: Ermelinda
description: Ermelinda is 50 years old and married with two children. With one child in school, Ermelinda works very hard to provide for them.  Ermelinda runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 10,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) loan through NWTF in order to purchase more groceries to sell.  Ermelinda has been in this business for 19 years and sells a variety of items such as snack foods, canned goods and other groceries.   In the future, Ermelinda would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Ana Del Socorro
description: Ana, 48, is from Estelí.  She’s single and the mother of three children who are 14, 20 and 25 years of age respectively.  She’s a merchant and owns a grocery store; she’s had it for over a year.  She started out in commerce in the sewing business at the age of 45 with her own capital and gradually earned profits.  From there, she decided to go into grocery sales and she feels proud because she’s succeeded in earning extra income on her own.  She has regular customers and her expectation is to make her business grow.  She’s asking for this loan to buy basic grains like beans, sugar, rice and a display case to display her goods.  She feels that this loan will help her busy all the merchandise in general that she does not yet stock to increase sales and earn higher profits.  Among her future plans it to expand the area her grocery store is in.

name: Kean
description: Kean L., age 36, is married and lives with her husband in Prey Veng, Cambodia. Since 2005, she has been selling groceries from her home and raising pigs to earn a living.  She is able to earn up to US$5 of profit per day. Since 1995, her husband, Kat Sovan, age 40, has supplemented the household by working as a local teacher in one of the high schools in the village. On average, he makes around $3 per day. Together, this couple has three children and all of them are students. Mrs. Kean told a loan officer that she needs to pay around US$100 on food, US$12 for utilities, and US$120 for her children’s education.  Mrs. Kean is seeking a loan of US$1,000 from Kiva via Credit, a local partner, to build a bigger cage and purchase more pigs and feed for her livestock.    CREDIT MFI is an independent Cambodian faith-based organization. It aims to empower the economically active poor and small entrepreneurs by providing inclusive financial services.

name: Remedios
description: Remedios and her husband work together as farmers. Their marriage has been blessed with six children, two sons and four daughters. They have three grandchildren. Their family happily lives in Barangay Rizal province Isabela. Here, people are united in their work for their community and for their families.  Aside from farming, Remedios and her husband also raise two hogs and vend cogon (a native grass). The couple is doing everything they can to earn a living.  In order to avoid asking for credit from traders, Remedios would like to take this opportunity to request a loan of PHP 30,000. This will provide for their farm and help to maintain their hog-raising business.  Remedios said that they must work hard in order to improve their lives.

name: Fred
description: Fred is a married father of three. He is an agriculturalist who also makes and sells bricks. He used his previous loan to produce more bricks, which increased his income. Fred now needs another loan to buy fire wood so that he can bake more bricks. He is hard working and thanks Kiva lenders for their generosity.

name: Al-Majd Group
description: The Al-Majd Group consists of four women from Al-Hodeida governorate, Yemen. They are requesting a loan of 150,000 YER, which they will use to buy clothes and cosmetics to sell.   Badria is 29 years old, married, and the leader of the group. Her husband works for many hours every day to cover the expenses of his family. She decided to help him and started a small business. She sells clothes and cosmetics door-to-door, which she has been doing for four years. She wants to buy more clothes and cosmetics to meet the demands of her clients. She is requesting a loan from AMB for 50,000 YER. She looks forward to opening her own clothes store in the future.

name: Musayamhuja
description: Musayamhuja is a hardworking man. He is married and has two children. He has a 22-year-old son and a 15-year-old daughter. Musayahuja works as a cashier in IMON, and he is one of the best employees of IMON. Musayamhuja always strives for the well being of his family. His wife is a housewife and that’s why Musayamhuja is the breadwinner of his family.   Musayamhuja’s son is a student of the Tajikistan State University Politic and Business School. He studies at the magistracy. Musayamhuja must pay for the education of his son but he does not have the money. He is asking for a loan of 1,100 USD with this aim. He awaits your support.

name: Liz
description: Liz is studying in the field of surgical nursing.  She lives with her parents and wants to be a successful professional one day.  She works along with pursuing her studies.  In this way she is able to have the means to continue growing and getting ahead.  She is asking for a loan in order to invest in the payment of tuition for her program.  In this way she will be able to move forward with her studies.

name: Melissa
description: Melissa is 28 years old, married and has two children who are in school. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Melissa's house was destroyed by super typhoon Haiyan which swept through the Philippines last November 8, 2013. She has restarted her buying and selling fish business and is committed to regain what she lost. Melissa is taking out a 10,000 PHP housing loan through NWTF to purchase building materials and pay for construction labor to build her a house for her family.  Melissa has been with NWTF since 2012 in her pursuit to rise out of poverty. With your help, she will be able to start once more in a new home. In the future, Melissa would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Severina
description: Severina is a married woman with one child. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Severina is 56 years old now.  Severina has a buy and sell fruits business in the Philippines. Severina requested a PHP 20000 loan amount through NWTF to buy variety of fruits, and other supplies needed in her business.  Severina has been in this business for 31 years. In the future, Severina would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Amoneh
description: Amoneh is a 29-year-old married woman from Yata, a village near Hebron city.  She is a mother of two sons and one daughter.  Her husband works as a construction worker where he earns a low and unstable income due to the demand.  Amoneh started her own business two years ago, opening a barn to raise sheep.  She sells her product in the local market.  Amoneh took a USD loan from FATEN to help her to buy additional sheep to raise in her barn.  This will increase productivity and income.  Amoneh appears in the photo.

name: Baltazar
description: N. is married with four children. He lives in Tandika area of Dar es Salaam. He owns a small shop in Tandika market where he sells new imported clothes.   He is planning to add a shoes line, along with selling clothes. His capital is not sufficient to cover this new business line. He is in need of USD 400 to facilitate his plan.

name: James
description: James G. is from the village of Dicoloc, Jimenez, Misamis Occidental. He is 38 years old and is married. James owns & operates an agricultural business, planting & harvesting a variety of vegetables for sale. He has been engaged in his business for over 1 year and earns approximately 1,500 PHP a month.  In 2010, James joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and his ability to engage in business activities. He has successfully repaid a previous loan of 10,000 PHP from GDMPC. This previous loan was used to provide additional capital for his business. He is requesting a new loan of 3,000 PHP which will be used to purchase fertilizers such as manure. This will be his second loan from GDMPC. He plans to use the additional revenue generated to improve and expand his business.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Norely
description: Norely, 30 years old, lives in the department of Chinandega in the western part of the country. Since she was very young she has sold mattresses, faux leather, pillows, and other items. She is the owner of this business. She makes her purchases at distribution trucks and sells to regular and casual customers on credit and in cash. She has had this business for 6 years, and with so much effort she has been able to move ahead. She started her business selling at bus stops. Currently she is asking for a loan to increase her working capital and supply her business in order to be able to obtain better earnings and support her household. Norely is thankful for the help the Kiva lenders provide to people with scarce resources and in poor countries such as Nicaragua to have a means of dignified work.

name: Mariam
description: This is Mariam. Her previous loan was a big help with her business. She was able to buy more items for her kiosk shop. She has been in this business for years now, and it keeps on growing.   She would like to apply for a loan of 40,000 KES to buy more stock of household consumables such as sweets, maize flour, soft drinks, rice and sugar for resale. The more items displayed at the kiosk, the better.    Her profits from the business will definitely help her to sustain her daily needs.  She looks forward to this financial increase with gladness and thankfulness in her heart.

name: Ali
description: Ali is a Babban Gona maize farmer. Before he became a Babban Gona member, Ali would have had to sell his maize for low prices soon after harvest to cater to his immediate cash needs. With this loan and Babban Gona’s support, Ali can now store his maize at harvest time and sell it a few months later for up to 40% higher than the market price at harvest.   When asked about his goals, Ali expressed a desire to use the extra income to provide his family with food and clothing, and in the long run to make more money for himself and his family.

name: Joseph
description: Joseph is a farmer in the town of Ndunyu Njeru and this will be his second loan.  He used his first loan to buy fertilizer and seedlings.  He was able to plant and harvest and it was very profitable.  He plans to buy more fertilizer and seedlings as well as spraying chemicals for use in his farm.    In the future, Joseph hopes to start large scale farming and become one of the leading farmers in the Ndunyu Njeru area.

name: Lan's Group
description: Lan is a 32-year-old married woman. She lives with two children and her husband in Ho Chi Minh City. Her husband earns money as a worker for a local company. For 2 years, she has run a business of selling soft drinks and fruit juice to people in her community.  Lan is the Group Leader of a 5-member loan group that lives in Ho Chi Minh City. In the picture she is the second one from the left. Each of the other group members are requesting loans to fund income-generating activities.  Lan would like a loan to purchase a variety and quantity of soft drinks and fruit to better satisfy her customers. She hopes this will enable her to better meet the needs of her customers and attract additional customers.   She also hopes that through her loan she will be able to increase her income and save money for any future difficulties facing her family.

name: Alianza Group
description: The “ALIANZA” (Alliance) communal bank is a new group in the agency.  It’s in its first cycle.  It’s composed of responsible, hard working people.  The bank is represented by the following members:   Mabel, President, is the group leader.  She sells seasonal items so is currently selling school supplies.  She will use the loan to buy school supplies.  Guillermina is Treasurer.  She’s separated and has two school age children.  Her business is home-based food sales located in the La Chimba zone.  She will use the loan to buy ingredients like noodles, rice, etc. to make her dishes.  Mayra is the Secretary.  She is married and has a son.  She makes sportswear to sell.  She is a young, active person and will use the money to buy fabric and thread to make her items of clothing.  All of the group members are asking for the loan for capital increase.They are all responsible and hard working people who in many cases support their families alone, and are profoundly grateful to the institution for their support.

name: Sol De Los Andes Group
description: The Banco D. Emprendimiento Sol D. los Andes (Sun of the Andes Communal Bank) is composed of 8 female members, and Cristina is the president of the bank. She previously formed part of another bank that encountered internal problems, but since her reliability and solidarity maD. of this lady an excellent customer, she was invited to create a new group, that is the Sol D. los Andes bank, of which she was elected president. A very cheerful, enthusiastic and tenacious woman, she engages in selling bedding overstock. She buys bedding overstock and remnants from the polar fleece factory, she embroiders them with her sewing machine and then she sells them in the traD. fair located in the 16 D. Julio area. With the loan she has requested Cristina will buy stocks of fabric. Her family is composed of 5 members, herself, three children and her husband who engages in different activities: he is a mason, a musician and a referee, and he helps his wife achieving their dream of finishing building the house they are currently paying for.

name: Jasmin
description: Jasmin is 41 years old, and she is married with 5 children. 4 of her children are in school.  Jasmin works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and has requested a 20,000 PHP loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation in order to purchase additional inventory of groceries to sell.  Jasmin has borrowed and repaid 7 loans from NWTF before. She has been running her general store for 5 years, though she also earns income from farming rice.  Jasmin aspires to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Wafa
description: Wafa is a 42-year-old mother of three daughters and two sons who are school and college students. The oldest is 21 years old while the youngest is 6 years old. Wafa's husband drives a taxi car in the city of Gaza in Gaza Strip. He bought the car a few years ago through his friend and agreed with the owner to pay a fixed amount. He needs to pay the last $3000 and took out a loan from FATEN to be able to pay smaller amounts of money every month.  Wafa's husband, Abdul Hafeez, appears in the photo as Wafa is a conservative woman and doesn't want her picture posted on the web.

name: Maurice
description: Maurice is a 52-year-old supporting seven people in his family. He has a tailoring kiosk, a business he has been doing for the last 13 years and generates a monthly income of 25,000 KES. He has requested his first loan with Vision Fund Kenya, which he will use to purchase more clothes materials. He will use the anticipated income to plow back into the business.His dream is to have a stable business.

name: Eswat Group
description: Febronia has owned a small shop in the Sakina neighborhood of Arusha for 2 years.  She currently earns an average monthly profit of $60. Every day she works at her business from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.  She is requesting her first loan from BRAC Tanzania so that she can buy more items for her business. She is hopping that through this loan, her profit will increase and she will be able to grow her business.    Febronia is  married, and has nine children: ages 30, 27, 25, 22, 20, 18, 15, 13 and 8. She also cares for two additional dependant ages 90 and 20. She will be sharing this loan with her fellow group members, Anna, Maimuna, Asha, and Antusa. Each of these women also has her own small business in Arusha

name: Laidou Group
description: The Laidou group, made up entirely of married women, are on average 35 years old with an average of 3 children each. All of the women live in traditional extended families in the village of Djekonobougou in the Wacoro community, located in the Dioila area of the Koulikoro region (the second administrative region of Mali.) The women came to know each other through family, neighbors, and as friends.  The women are in the business of selling poultry, spices, soap, pastries, cereals, bread, etc. They are on their second group loan, which they will use to purchase the different merchandise for these businesses.  Setou is the first woman pictured standing on the right; she sells bread. She plans to purchase two and one half bags of flour for making loaves of bread which she will sell in the village of Djekonobougou, in Wacoro, and the surrounding area. She hopes to earn an average monthly profit of 15,000 francs CFA which she will use partially to purchase flour and goats and for savings.

name: Karen Yelitza
description: Karen is 30 years old and is an enterprising dressmaker in the city of Barranquilla. She started her own business 10 years ago, an initiative that today allows her to have a better lifestyle and that guarantees a secure income for her family. For her, sewing was a profession inherited by family tradition. Her mother always did this work. However, her selling skills allowed Karen to be much more diligent and to establish herself quickly in the dressmaking area by volume. She has completed contracts with schools to make school uniforms and also works with individuals for whom she makes dresses, blouses, skirts, pants, and entire women's outfits. She is currently requesting her first loan with Kiva through Fundación Mario Santo Domingo. She plans to invest these resources in buying raw materials such as fabrics, threads, and accessories to meet the demand that the year-end season generates. Her main challenge is to expand her range of products in order to earn a higher income for the economic benefit of her family.

name: Rosalia
description: Rosalia is now 56 years old.  She continues with her artisan work, which she says is going better and better.  She is a very enterprising woman.  She weaves blankets and handmade tablecloths and her husband sells them in installments.  This is her third loan with Kiva.  She says that her previous loans have been of much help and now she requests a new loan to be able to buy thread, embroidery frames, needles, and other things so that she can continue her work as she has been doing.  She is grateful for the opportunity to be able to continue growing in this way.

name: Jiguiya Group
description: The 7 members of the Jiguiya group are mainly married women with an average age of 42 and, on average, 5 children. They primarily live in polygamous family settings in Kadiolo Koko, one of the circles of Sikasso. They are on their 21st loan with the Soro Yiriwaso microfinance institution and their previous loans have been properly repaid.  Alima, sitting with a red scarf in the picture, has been buying and selling clothing for around 20 years. She gets her supplies in Sikasso and often in the Ivory Coast, a country bordering Mali, before reselling them in Kadiolo and the surrounding area, for cash or credit to a clientèle composed of men and women. She makes her sales at the market and door-to-door. She plans to buy 3 dozen items of children's clothing. She makes an average monthly profit of 50 000 francs, part of which is used to repay her loan and interest, whilst the rest is used to build up her savings.

name: Digao
description: F. is from the village of Tuyabang Alto, Oroquieta City. She is 53 years old, married and has one adult child. To make a living, F. runs a business selling fish in the community.  F. has been engaged in her business for 20 years and earns approximately 6,000 PHP a month. F. joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities.   F. is requesting a new loan of 5,000 PHP with which she will purchase more fish to sell. This loan will be the fourth loan taken out by F. from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand her business.   About PMPC: Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.   *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.
town: Oroquieta-Tuyabang Alto Oroquieta City Misamis Occ

name: Gladys
description: Gladys K. is fifty-two years old. She is married and has given birth to four children, all of whom are still in school. She lives with her husband and children in a rented apartment in a busy commercial town called Suhum in the Eastern Region of Ghana.  Gladys is a trader and works to support her husband so as to be able to provide for the family. She trades in smoked fish. She sells on a table in the market square of her community and treks to other towns to sell on their market days as well.  Gladys has been in business for over thirty years and wants a loan to buy smoked fish in bulk. She aspires to sponsor all her children in school to the higher levels.

name: Mwanajuma
description: Mwanajuma appreciates her previous loan that improved her living standards. Her previous loan enabled her to expand her grocery business and earn a higher income. In addition to the fruits and vegetable business, she sells coconuts and dumplings.  She would like to apply for a loan of ksh.40,000 to buy more coconuts, wheat flour, and cooking oil for her business.   She thanks Yehu for their financial support.

name: Eliada
description: Eliada L. is from the village of San Juan, Panaon, Misamis Occidental. She is 46 years old. Eliada is married and has 4 adult-aged children. To make a living, Eliada owns and operates a business venture in the agriculture sector raising crops. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from planting and harvesting a variety of vegetables for sale. Eliada has been engaged in her business for over 5 years and earns approximately 3,000 PHP a month from these activities.  In 2009, Eliada joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Eliada has successfully repaid a previous loan from GDMPC. This previous loan was used to purchase additional seeds for her farm. Eliada is requesting a new loan of 7000 PHP which will be used to purchase fertilizers such as manure. This loan will be the fourth loan taken out by Eliada from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three unit offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Lea
description: Lea is a 54-year-old married woman and a mother of five grown-up children from Iloilo, Philippines. Lea has been engaged in the fishing business with her husband for more than five years now.  Lea is a hardworking woman. She helps her husband in their fishing venture.  Lea would like to take a loan to buy new fishing nets, lead weights, hooks and others items. With a loan, Lea and her husband will be able to improve their catch thus giving them more fish to sell in the market.  In the future, Lea hopes to make their fishing business a success.

name: Nancy
description: Nancy is a smallholder dairy and poultry farmer dying to get her hands on the agricultural products market. She is the mother of two and has been doing crop farming too, but for subsistence purposes. She also grows vegetables, a bit of maize and grass for her cow. She is seeking a loan to buy more land and grow her farming on a bigger scale for commercial gains. The demand for different varieties of food crop (vegetables, fruits and maize) has grown steadily in Kenya in recent years. As much as they have become one of the top traded agricultural products, there is still plenty of room to expand.   Nancy is very excited to start the commercialization of her crops. With your loan, this can be easily achieved. She will rely on other sources of income to make initial installments of the loan but in no time, the farm will start pumping in income. The profits will be ploughed back into the business to fuel growth. Her increased income will uplift the living standards of her family.  With her drive and ambition, Nancy sees herself in the medium term in a position to generate employment, always with the helping hand of KIVA lenders and Juhudi Kilimo Kindly help her out!.

name: Gemeniano
description: Behind the walls of Intramuros City lives a reliable and hardworking father named Gemeniano, 55, a tricycle driver. He is married to Amalia, 50 years old, who works in a distant land as an Overseas Filipino Worker (OFW). Away from each other sometimes, Gemeniano admits that he misses his wife. But, for their family' sake, the couple tries to understand, live and cope with their present situation.   Gemeniano knows how hard it is to work abroad. That's another reason why he perseveres and works hard in his current job as a tricycle driver. For seven years, he has been driving people to and from their destinations. Each ride regularly costs PHP 8.00 per person, and each day he just earns enough. In a month, he can subsist on an average of PHP 9,000.   However, it's a challenge for him when uncontrollable situations come, like heavy rains. At times like this, his motorcycle very often will not operate.   Now, he comes to you to request a loan that he will use for buying another motorcycle. He needs an amount of PHP 8,000 for this.   "I really dream of acquiring more motorcycles in time. And it would be a big help for me indeed if I get access to this loan. I hope Kiva will help me realize this so I can add income for the family," he said.   He meets up with his co-fellowship** members to share stories of his life and business every week and where he draws strength and inspiration from the fellowship and the Word of God he studies.  ** All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that are each composed of 15 to 30 community partners and that gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans.

name: Lamaranah
description: Lamaranah is  21 years old, married, and has two children.  She sells dried fish in Dogolia village in the Koinadugu District of Sierra Leone.  Lamaranah needs to increase her income to better care for her children.  She is hopeful that by strengthening her business she will be able to accomplish her goals.  She is requesting a loan of Le 800,000.  Lamaranah is the entrepreneur on the right in the photograph.

name: Carlos
description: Carlos is 21 years old, lives with his parents in a rural area of Cayaltí, whose population works in farming, business, and raising livestock, in an area located two hours north of Chiclayo city, on the northern coast of Peru.He provides service in public transportation with his own motortaxi, transporting his passengers to different areas of their communities. He has had this business for more than two years. He has asked for a loan of 1000 nuevos soles to perform maintenance on his vehicle and in this way continue providing service in a safe and regular way, generating greater income for his family.

name: Ben-Ton Group
description: Nouhoun Allaye is from Mali and raises goats. He is 37, married, and the father of three children whose ages are 6, 4, and 1. The oldest goes to school. His spouse sells cow's milk. She collects milk from producers in the village and distributes it to small retailers and end consumers. Nouhoun Allaye has been raising goats for three years. He buys young goats at the weekly markets and raises them. He decided to work with RMCR to boost his business. His loan will allow him to buy more goats, all while bolstering his technical capital. His monthly revenue allows him to earn 30,000 FCFA worth of profit, which allows him to meet the needs of his family—namely healthcare costs, schooling costs, and investments in improving his family's nutrition. Despite the difficulties Nouhoun Allaye encounters with his business, such as goat feed being expensive in the area, he wishes to continue to with his business by increasing the size of his operation and buying goat feed when it's less expensive. To improve his production, he is looking to reinforce his intellectual capital with training.

name: Hafsa
description: Hafsa is 39 years old. She is married with 7 children, aged between 6 and 23 years old. She owns and runs a small shop. Every day, she works from 7am to 3pm at her business and can earn a monthly profit of about $70 from her sales.   Hafsa now hopes for a loan to buy more products for her business.

name: Mari Suyapa
description: Mari is 35 years old.  She is a coffee grower and has 10 years experience in managing and growing coffee.  This is her source of income with which she covers her family expenses.  Mari is a single mother and also cares for her parents.  She will use her loan to buy a solar panel so that she can light up her house at night.  In the community where she lives they do not receive this basic service and, her whole life, she has lit her house with oil lamps and candles which are harmful to her health.  Thanks to this solar panel, she will improve her own quality of life as well as that of her family.

name: Esther
description: Esther is a married woman and has been blessed with three kids who attend school. She lives in her own house that has electricity and piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is school fees.   Esther has a poultry-selling business, which has been operational for over two years. She mentioned disease outbreak causing losses as a challenge in the business. Esther dreams of becoming a wholesaler of poultry in the future.   With the Kshs 30,000, she wants to purchase chicks and poultry feed. She joined Yehu to access loans to boost her business

name: La Nueva Esperanza 4 Group
description: Rudelania is the coordinator of her group, La Nueva Esperanza (The new hope) 4, which is composed of five micro-entrepreneurs and located in the city of San Pedro de Macoris. Their community is a rural area surrounded by fields of sugarcane.  Rudelania has operated a business selling jewelry and accessories mainly for women. She runs a little 'fantasia' (a small store where she sells different products). She will use her loan to increase her inventory by buying miscellaneous products such as cosmetics, jewel, etc.  Rudelania and her long-term partner live together with their three children. Her most important challenges are to work hard to gain extra income and to better her home structure. She is receiving her first loan from Esperanza Internacional. Rudelania would like to save her profits to build her house.

name: Rebecca
description: Rebecca B., from the town of Sto. Niño, is married and the mother of six grown children. To make a living, Rebecca plants and harvests rice to sell, a business she has operated for over 30 years now.   In 2008, Rebecca joined CEVI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Having fully repaid a previous loan  from CEVI, she is now requesting a new one, her sixth, of 15000 PHP to purchase fertilizers such as manure. Rebecca plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement her family's income.

name: Gina
description: Gina is 36 years old, married with two children.  Gina works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 17000 loan through NWTF to buy more items to sell in her general store.  Gina has borrowed and paid 8 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 12 years and also earns an income from electronic mobile load retailing.  Gina aspires to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Dulamragchaa
description: Dulamragchaa S. is 46, and is a single mother who has two daughters. Her family lives in Uvurhangay, one of the Mongolian central provinces.  Dulamragchaa has been running a retail business for the last twelve years. She began her business selling salt. After a few years she started working as a saleswoman at others' food stalls and sold rice and flour. Since she became experienced in selling those food products, she has rented a stall at the local food market to sell rice and flour. Her eldest daughter, Altantsetseg, 26, who lives with her, helps her mother’s business. Her youngest daughter, Dolgorsuren, 19, is an Arts and Culture university student in Ulaanbaatar, the capital city.  Dulamragchaa purchases rice and flour at wholesale prices from the wholesale food center and bags them to sell at retail prices. She says "I really wanted my eldest daughter to become educated. Unfortunately I didn't have enough funds to pay for her tuition. Thus, I’m working hard and saving small amounts to pay for my youngest daughter’s university tuition. My dream is to have my own food stall and have a sufficient amount of working capital."  With this loan, Dulamragchaa is planning to go to Ulaanbaatar, the capital city, to purchase more rice and flour at cheap prices. Thanks to her open, friendly, and hard working personality, she should do well.

name: Mariame
description: This lady is 47 years old and a married mother of six with a secondary education; she sells women's and children's clothing for a living. She has sold her wares from the market since 1993, and generates daily sales between 20,000 F and 35,000 F.  She will use her loan to purchase more stock, such as: large boubous (loose robes) for women, trousers, jackets, girls' dresses, children's suits, mixed pants, bras, hairpins and headscarves. She sources her goods from a market in the town square.   Her plans are: to drive her business further, and to generate higher sales so that she may one day become a wholesaler herself, and import boubous, pagnes (wax cloths) and children's clothing from West Africa.   Her main concern is that she remains financially independent so that she can meet her family's needs.

name: Marites
description: Marites is 32 years old and married with three children. With three children in school, Marites works very hard to provide for them.  Marites runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 13,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like shampoo, condiments, personal care products and other groceries. She has been in this business for two years and sells a variety of items such as rice, sugar, soap, and other groceries.   In the future, Marites would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Oscar Alexander
description: Oscar resides in the El Tránsito municipality in the San Miguel department of El Salvador. He is 23 years old and is an employee. He is married, and lives with his mother, his brothers, his wife and his first child who is one year old. Everyone in the house goes to work.  Oscar started his job at the bus terminal in the department of Usulután two years ago. He works from 7:00am to 4:00pm. He is in the process of fixing up his house, and he is therefore requesting a loan to pay for flooring and doors. This will help him improve the condition of his house and provide a cleaner safer home for his family.  His aspiration is to make his loan repayments on time and do well at his job so that he can look after his family's well-being.

name: Irma Carolina
description: Irma Carolina is 33 years old and she has 3 children who are in school. She has an internet cafe business and she also sells household items such as shampoo, detergents, fabric softeners, etc. Her business is installed in her home and, with the help of her husband; she has had a great deal of demand for her business. She needs t anew loan to purchase computers, a desk, and products for the home. She will be able to provide her clients with a better level of service. She thanks God for having found this organization that has supported with a loan. The previous loan she had was paid on time.

name: Saliou
description: Saliou N. has been a storekeeper for five years, selling foodstuffs and staples. The loan he is requesting will enable him to expand his business. At 26, he is married and a father. The income from his business allows him to pay for the upkeep of his family.Translated from French by Sarah Llewellyn, Kiva Volunteer

name: Melissa
description: Melissa is a 38-year-old married woman with six children, four of which attend school.  She is a very hard working entrepreneur.  For the past 4 years Melissa has operated a buy and sell charcoal business in the Philippines.  She requested a 7,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase sacks of charcoal to sell.  In the future, Melissa would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Imoya
description: Imoya M. is 40 years old and married to a peasant. She has one child, who does not go to school. Imoya is currently in the business of selling charcoal  and is requesting a loan to stock more bags of charcoal to sell. With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to buy a motorbike for hire.  About BRAC BRAC's holistic approach to poverty alleviation and empowerment of the poor encompasses a range of core programs in economic and social development, health, education, human rights and legal services, which are delivered through an extensive network of village organizations. BRAC has become one of the world's largest NGOs as measured by the scale and diversity of its interventions. In 2007, BRAC started operations in Southern Sudan. The microfinance program, which is targeted at returning war refugees, has already formed 418 village organizations with more than 14,000 women members.

name: Nida
description: Nida is 47 years old and lives in Gango, Ozamis City, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. She is married and the mother of four children.   Nida owns and operates a banana farm as her source of income. She has been engaged in this business for seven years, and each month she earns 5,000 PHP.    Nida has requested a loan of 8,000 PHP to purchase additional seeds, seedlings, and young plants to raise. Nida has been a member of GDMPC since 2009. In the future, she hopes to increase her income to support her family's daily needs.

name: Llesica
description: Llesica is married and has two daughters, aged seven and four. She has been working with Kiva partner, Manuela Ramos, for eight years and has used her loans for a variety of different business ventures. Llesica's husband runs a vehicle repair shop and gets a lot of customers from a bus company located nearby. Llesica has helped him to expand and improve his shop.    Llesica also invests in raising and selling chickens. Currently she is trying to decide whether she should invest in raising chickens or turkeys for the upcoming Christmas season. While chickens are easier to raise, turkeys have the advantage of selling for a higher price.  Llesica also sells barbecued chicken and sodas and beer at the weekends. She can earn 160 PEN over the course of one weekend with this business. Finally, she used a previous loan to purchase a motorcycle taxi which she rents out for 20 PEN daily to a driver. She plans to use this loan of 2500 PEN to purchase another motorcycle taxi.   Llesica reports that her business ventures are doing well. Her goals are to expand her barbecue business, increase the size of her chicken coops in order to raise more chicks, and to eventually have a fixed  business locale (such as a restaurant) that she can leave to her children. For this last goal, Llesica must first purchase a piece of land upon which to build her home. She and her family are currently living with her husband's parents.

name: Angela
description: Angela, age 26, prepares and sells ice snacks to earn her living. She offers her goods for sale in her local neighborhood as well as at the market. She has been engaged in this business for three years. She lives with her husband in Honiara.  Angela is a new member of SPBD, and she has requested a loan in order to invest in her business by purchasing a cooler, an aluminum dish, containers, a bale of sugar, milk, flavorings, and colorings.   She plans to use her increased profits to improve her business as well as to meet the daily needs of her family.

name: Rubiela De Jesus
description: Rubiela, age 57, is a very hard-worker in spite of her health problems.  She has gotten her three children ahead after her ex-husband went away from the country and left her alone with the responsibility of the household.  For 30 years Rubiela has worked in her own store.  She sells fruit, vegetables, fast food, and staples.  She works every day with the help of one of her daughters.  Her schedule is from 6:00 a.m. until 10:00 p.m.  Rubiela needs to make some improvements to the floor and the roof of her store.  The winter has damaged her facilities.  She will also buy a stock of staple products, which are in the most demand by her customers.  Rubiela’s dream is to have a restaurant and to get her family ahead.

name: Mahmadrachab
description: Mahmadrachab K. lives in the Abdurahmon Jomi district.  He is 53 years old, married and has 8 children.  His son currently works in Russia.  Mahmadrachab has been involved in animal husbandry for over 7 years.  He raises and sells livestock.  He has consistent clients.  Mahmadrachab is requesting a loan for the purchase of livestock.Translated from Russian by Anna Sorokina-Hailey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Mejumaa
description: Mejumaa is married with six children: two have finished school and four are still going to school. She has been operating her firewood and charcoal business for three years and sells from her home to her neighbors.    With the Kshs 40,000 she wants to buy a bundle of firewood and two sacks of charcoal. Mejumaa's other source of income is her husband's earnings.   The major challenges in her business are the high cost of transportation and theft. In the future, she hopes to run a wholesale shop and to increase her profits.   She decided to join Yehu to get a loan to boost her business.  Mejumaa owns a home with electricity but no piped water. Her major challenge is food.

name: Bang
description: Bang is a 37-year-old married man living in Ho Chi Minh City. He has two children. He and his wife earn a living running a food store, which they have done for three years.   Bang would like to take loan to buy a greater variety and quantity of foods, such as tea, beverages and confectionery, to stock his  store. He hopes this will enable him to better meet the needs of his customers and increase the turnover of his business. He also hopes that through the loan his business will generate a higher income and will help him to improve his family's living conditions and enable him to set aside some savings.

name: Tehreen
description: Tehreen, age 23, operates a stitching business to earn an income. She has been engaged in this business for the past two years. Her husband works as a laborer, but his income is not enough to meet the household expenses, which is why Tehreen began stitching. In this way, she is better able to meet the needs of her family. She has gained many regular customers over the past two years.   At present, her sewing machine needs considerable repair work. She has decided to purchase a new one, but due to her limited income, she contacted Kashf Foundation and applied for a loan of Rs. 10,000/-. This investment will help her to stitch clothes better and in less time.   She wishes to spend her expected profits on the betterment of her family members' standard of living.

name: Gregoria
description: 54-year-old Gregoria lives with her family in her own home which has piped water and electricity.  It is located in Cayaltí district, in Chiclayo province.  The people in this area farm and raise livestock.  For eight years, Gregoria has been raising and selling farmyard animals (pigs and poultry).  Her pens are located behind her home and they are suitable and spacious.  She feeds her animals with nutritionally-balanced animal feed so that they reach an optimal level of growth and she is able to sell them in the different markets in her area.  This makes her good profits with which she covers her household expenses.  Gregoria has requested a loan for 1,000 soles from Edpyme Alternativa to buy more animals and nutritionally-balanced feed for them.  She will use the profits that she makes from selling her animals to repay her loan and proviD. her family with a better quality of life.  Gregoria is a woman who, through her efforts and commitment, tries to proviD. her family with the best.

name: Umazi
description: Umazi is a married woman with eight children, seven of whom attend school, and one is grown up. She lives in her own house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.  For the past 15 years, she has been selling goat meat at the market to the general public. The main challenge for her business has been unstable market prices.   She joined Yehu in order to gain access to funds.  She is requesting a loan of  50,000 KES to purchase more goats for her business.

name: Maria Elizabeth
description: Maria Elizabeth continues with her business of selling food. She is a hard-working young woman who has been doing this work for many years to support her family. She needs more capital so she can buy meat, chicken, potatoes, rice, and oil. She is committed to making her repayments on time and she is grateful to Kiva for the loan.

name: Gloria
description: Gloria is 41 years old and married with four children.  Gloria works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 13,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy items to sell such as shampoo, groceries, soap, milk, sugar, etc.  Gloria has borrowed and paid back two loans from NWTF prior to this loan. She has been running the general store for 15 years and also earns an income from raising pigs and farming sugarcane.  Gloria aspires to save enough money so that she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Mariam
description: Mambo from Dar es Salaam, Tanzania! This is Mariam N., who is married with four children, aged between 8 and 18.  Mariam owns a business selling fish and salt, and requests a loan of $275 in order to purchase additional stock in bulk. She thanks you for your support.

name: Michael Kazungu
description: Michael Kazungu M. is a 34-year old farmer who lives in Malindi and is married to Janet Kangombe. They have five children between the ages of 11 years and 9 months.  Michael has been in the farming business for the last five years. He was introduced to KADET by an agricultural officer in Malindi.
