With this loan, Michael plans to pay for farm labor and to buy petrol, farm seedlings, and pesticides. He intends to open his own farm store to sell supplies directly to farmers. (Currently, the farmers buy supplies from brokers.)  He also dreams of building his own hardware shop and describes himself as quiet, focused, and hardworking.  About KADET: The Kenya Agency for the Development of Enterprise and Technology (KADET) is dedicated to economically empower its clients by providing financial services to improve living conditions of micro-entrepreneurs and their children across Kenya. KADET is the microfinance subsidiary of World Vision Kenya. Obtain more information on KADET from the website: www.kadet.co.ke

name: Martha Francina
description: For three years, Martha Francina R. O. has been working as a cashier at ENACAL (Nicaraguan water supply and sewerage company), in the town of Masaya, in Masaya department.  She is a single mother who has two dependent children.  She tries to meet all their needs.  One of the needs that Mrs R. O. has is that of improving her home.  For this reason, she has decided to request a loan from CEPRODEL's offices so that she can purchase the building supplies that she needs to meet her needs.  In this way, she will be able to provide her children with a decent home and better safety.  Mrs R. O. feels that this work on her home will protect her children's health.  She would prefer to carry out the work before the winter comes.

name: Phy's Group
description: A mother of five children, Phy is 53 years old and married.  For 27 years she has been a rice and cassava grower residing in the Battambang province of the Moung Russey district in Cambodia.  Phy is not a first time borrower with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner).  She has completely repaid her past loan, allowing her to gradually uplift her lifestyle.    Phy now leads a group of two obtaining a new loan.  As the leader, she will spend her entire loan portion to buy fertilizer, and to pay for plowing fees.  She hopes to harvest a better yield than her last crop.

name: Katukole Kisambo Farmers Group
description: Patrick is a member of Katukole Kisambo Farmers Group. He is a thirty six year old man, married and a resident of Masindi district. His livelihood and that of his family entirely, depends on crop production of maize and beans, having stayed in this business for ten years. He is happy with the achievement of managing to sustain his family. Patrick wants the loan to buy seeds and to plough his garden. His aspiration is that of becoming a self sustainable finances man, using modernized agricultural methods of farming, although unpredictable weather changes affect his level of productivity. The group members are mainly involved in farming and the extra person in the photo is a group member with savings, who has guaranteed others but has not taken the loan.

name: Rechel
description: Rechel is 22 years old and a resident in Iloilo, Philippines. Like the other people in the community, Rechel and her family also engaged in fishing business. It has been their source of income since then. To uplift their livelihood, she dreams to have a new boat that can be used in fishing. She wants to improve their business and with that, she asks to lend money to buy new fishing net and fishing weight.

name: Isabel
description: Isabel is a member of the community bank “Empecemos” (“We begin”).  Isabel is married.  She is 56 years old and has 4 children.  Isabel has a printing press called SEGMI, from which she provides various services like printing and card making.  Her business location is rented, and is located in the center of the city Ayacucho.  It is an activity that she does with the help of her children.  Isabel needs a loan of 2600 soles, money that she would invest in the purchase of framework and toner.  Isabel’s dreams are that her children finish their studies in university and that she can implement modern machines in her printing press. Translated from Spanish by Jessica Kaminsky, Kiva Volunteer

name: Richard Emilio
description: Richard lives with his parents in the Las Lomas neighborhood of the city of La Paz. Richard works as a salaried employee of the Concepción lumber company; this is his primary source of income. He will use this loan to cover his university tuition, which is paid on a monthly basis. He is studying Public Accounting. This is his first loan from IMPRO.  Translated from Spanish by Cynthia McMurry, Kiva Staff

name: Agnes
description: Agnes is a 37-year-old boutique owner. She is a married mother with one child. She has been running this business for the last three years with great success.  This is Agnes’ third loan from KADET LTD to finance her business. She plans to purchase more shirts, skirts, trousers, and handbags to resell to her customers.   She will use the anticipated profits to educate her child and repay her loan. She hopes to have a bigger, more profitable boutique.

name: Sokheng
description: Mrs.  Sokheng D. married in 1996 and has three children, one son and two daughters. She learned to weave silk from a relative who was living in the same village in 1995. Then she started her silk production in the same year. She has never attended even primary school. Her husband also weaves silk at home. In addition, he is a construction worker, doing farming and raising animals. He did not finish grade 3 at the primary school.     Mrs. Sokheng D. has borrowed money from MAXIMA twice already. Now she is asking for a loan in the amount of US$ 400. She will use this loan to purchase silk materials and sewing thread and pay fees for selecting and preparing silk on the loom.

name: Reynaldo
description: Reynaldo B. is from the village of Guinsiliban in the Camiguin Province. He is 51 years old and married and with 10 school-age children. To make a living, Reynaldo owns and operates a business providing motorcycle taxi service in his local community. He's been in his business for over 5 years and earns approximately 3000 PHP a month.  In 2009, Reynaldo joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and ability to engage in business activities. He has successfully repaid a previous loan of 8000 PHP from HSPFI, which was used to to repair a transport vehicle used in the business. Reynaldo is requesting a new loan of 9000 PHP that will be used to invest in expanding the business. This loan will be his 3rd loan from HSPFI. He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand his business.   About HSPFI: HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Grupo De Mujeres Sector Zapeta Group
description: Maria (she is the lady who appears second from the left in the photo) is a married woman who has four children between ages 3 and 9. Maria is 37 years old.  Maria is  a woman who fights every day towards generating income, she works purchasing and selling traditional clothing, for now she only sells in her community market, one of the reasons why she doesn't sell in the surrounding areas is that she doesn´t have enough capital in order to buy more merchandise.  Due to this difficulty, Maria is searching for a loan in order to buy more merchandise and thus be able to generate more revenue and overall profit. She does not have another source of income but with this business she affirms that it is effective. Maria´s goal for the future is to be able to afford finding other markets to sell and generate more revenue, and to have diversity in skirts and güipiles(a traditional Guatemalan dress) that are up to date, since the world is changing and every day products are modernized. Maria has full assurance in obtaining the loan and her dream will come to be reality.

name: Ami
description: Ami A. is a young woman of 35; she is married and has a little boy. She is a hairdresser in Avetonou, a village located about 100 kilometers from Lomé, the capital of Togo. The quality of her work has allowed her to win the confidence of her clients. To make her services even more professional, she would like to use this loan to buy a hairdryer, and hair extensions for resale.  Translated from French by Alison Dent, Kiva Volunteer

name: Susana
description: Susana is taking a loan of $1000 to improve her business. She is running a second hand clothing business that helps her to generate income for her family. She will use the loan to buy stocks to keep in her store such as trousers, shorts, and shirts. She opened her kiosk a year ago with her own working capital of $200. Susana is a hard-working woman and she hopes to run a bigger business in the future.

name: Sadriddin
description: Z. Sadriddin is 34 years old. He is married with two children. Sadriddin is running the business already for 5 years. He is selling the household appliances such as: TV set, air conditioner, refrigerator and many others in his store. The business generates the significant income for the family allowing improving the living conditions. Today Sadriddin requests $800 USD. He is going to spend the loan for purchasing new goods for selling. Sadriddin is very thankful for those lenders who supports him.     More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History  Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Qmenvinah
description: Qmenvinah is 24 years old and lives at the West Point area, which has the most populated market in Montserrado County. She is single and completed grade 12. She described herself as a hardworking woman.  For the past five years, she has been running a shop where she sells soft drinks in the local market. She sells six days a week from 7 A.M. to 5 P.M. She likes her business because of the ways customers buy from her. She started this business with money given to her by her mother. She uses a shared taxi to get her goods to her business spot.  She is requesting a loan to purchase more soft drinks for her business. She plans to build a house for her children. She likes to say thanks to the lenders who support BRAC Liberia.

name: Florida
description: As a married mother of two children, Florida works hard to support her family.  She has an internet café business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from a general store.  Florida is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF to buy computer supplies for her internet café business.  Florida has been sustaining her business activities through her past five loans from NWTF.   She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Waukae Group
description: Khatima, who is in her mid 30’s is married and she’s a hard working mother of one school aged son. She has been in food vending business for the past seven years, working at her own food stall that sells and serves food to the customers from 6 am to mid night and she is able to make great profit. This will be her second loan from Tujijenge Tanzania, where she used her previous loan as capital for expanding her business. She bought new working materials and paid house rent.Khatima is now happy that her business is going so well and she has managed to pay back all of her previous loans, paid school fees to her son, provided food for her family and reinvested the remaining profit back into her business.She applied for this loan to restock her food stall with more sacks of rice, beans, sugar, a 20 liter Jerry can of cooking oil and ingredients for making spicy liquid rice and chapatti. She believes with such additions her income will increase and she will be able to grow much further as she dreams of having a restaurant some day.Khatima appreciates Kiva for all the good support given to her business and her loan group “WAUKAE”, as they will hold each other accountable for paying back the entire loan amount at maturity.

name: Akeela
description: Akeela is a 27-year-old married woman. She has been involved in the business of cloth trade. She purchases a variety of cloth at low prices from the city market and sells them in her own town. She has a strong customer base. Akeela has requested a loan of 40,000 PKR. She wants to buy a greater variety of cloth in different colors for her business, to get a boost in her earnings.

name: Dan
description: Dan is a 53-year-old married man. He lives with two children and his wife in Ho Chi Minh City. His wife is a teacher.   Dan earns an income to support his family by selling soft drinks in front of his house. He has done this for the past 10 years. He intends to take a loan to buy a greater range of beverages to increase his income.  He hopes that his business will go well and provide him with enough income to repair his home.

name: Rashad
description: 47-year-old Rashad lives in the Salyan region, Yenikand village. He is married and has two children. Rashad breeds calves. He supports his  family with this business. Now he needs a loan of $1200 to buy a cow and baling presses. He wants to breed cows in order to get more milk and to improve his  business and income. He has run this business for 10 years.

name: Liliana Isabel
description: Liliana, 44, lives in the city of Barranquilla with her spouse and three children whose ages range from 12 to 20.  She sells natural and medicinal products from various laboratories.  Her business began because of her interest in sales and when she saw that she received a warm welcome she became excited and now dreams with increasing her growth and later on to have a store with all the legal requirements so that her children will have a firm where they can generate income to finish their university careers.    Her greatest challenge is the lack of working capital to increase sales like she’d like to because she falls short of having sufficient funds to buy enough to meet demands of her growing clientele.  Her Kiva loan will be her first financing with Fundación Mario Santo Domingo and she’ll use it to buy natural medicine at wholesale so that she can qualify for good discounts and be able to offer much more competitive prices that will help her sustainability in the marketplace.

name: Hatem
description: Hatem is a 48-year-old married man from the city of Rafah city, which is located in the Gaza Strip. He is employed in the public sector and earns a low income which barely covers the family needs.  He wants to make his family more comfortable and improve their standard of living. He requests a USD loan from FATEN to buy a solar system to heat water for the family's house. Hatem will be able to decrease the electricity expenses, while using a cleaner form of energy (rather than gas). Hatem’s family will have an easier time heating water for showers, cooking, and washing clothes and dishes.

name: Diana Marcela
description: Diana is an enterprising 21-year-old woman, and a mother of a 3-year-old daughter.  During her productive life she has worked in different garment workshops as a machine operator, which is why has expertise in handling this type of business. However, already tired of working in other workshops and hoping to spend more time with her daughter, she decided to start her own sewing workshop. For this, she moved to apply for the loan to be invested in the purchase of an overlock sewing machine.   This will allow her to launch her productive project that she expects will generate a good impact in the sector. This will lead to a favorable return and to helping her fulfill the dream of entering the market.  With her drive and ambition she projects in the future in the medium term to generate work for herself, but always with a hand from the Corporación Interactuar (Interact Corporation).

name: Nely
description: Nely is 61 years old and widowed with two children. Nely works very hard to provide for them.  Nely runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a loan of 15,000 PHP through NWTF to buy items such as canned goods, personal care products, detergent, spices, noodles, bread and snack foods to sell.  Nely has been in this business for 10 years.  In the future Nely would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Tojiniso
description: Tojiniso is a hardworking country woman from the Yavan District. She is 49 years old. She grew up in the family of a communal farmer and has been familiar with agricultural farming since childhood. After graduating from school, Tojiniso got married and gave birth to six children. She and her husband have four sons and two daughters who range from 15 to 28 years old.  For the past 12 years, Tojiniso and her family have actively taken up crop farming.  They mainly grow garden crops. As the sowing season has begun now, Tojiniso has prepared the land for the new round of sowing. She is taking out a loan to buy vegetable seeds and tractor fuel. Thanks to the loan, she will be able to carry out sowing on time and receive a good harvest. With the profits, she plans to marry off her son. This loan is very important to her.

name: Kirinkai
description: Kirinkai is 35 years old, married to Jennifer and the father of three children. For the last ten years, he has farmed his own piece of land and earned a good income. Wheat has proved to be doing well in his area due to good climatic conditions.  Kirinkai learned about VisionFund Kenya through their staff. This will be his fifth loan after successfully repaying off the previous loans. He plans to buy farm inputs and hire machinery and pay for labor for preparation of the land.  With the profits he hopes to make from the proceeds of this loan, he plans to re-invest in the farm and plant more acres of wheat.  Kirinkai’s future dreams are that he will be able to buy a bigger piece of land, plant more wheat for commercial farming, buy his own farm machinery, and educate his children. He is a hardworking man who is focused on his set goals.

name: Abdufatto
description: Abdufatto's first loan from Microinvest funded the purchase of building materials for continued construction of his house. He liked Microinvest's loan conditions, and since he has a business he decided to request a loan for its development. Abdufatto is 51 years old, married, and has five children. His business is in the city's top restaurant, where he rents the bar. Two people work at the bar (the vendor is in the picture). Abdufatto hopes that the loan will allow him to further develop the business, and that he will be able to continue to receive loans in the future.     Translated from Russian by Anna Brown, Kiva Volunteer

name: Lucas
description: Lucas is 63 years old and married. He has five children, but only three grandchildren live with him. He grows corn and coffee and he has been in this line of work all his life. He learned the business because his parents used to work on that and all the neighbors work in coffee plantations and sow corn.  He buys the supplies in a town located about 30 minutes from his home, and he walks for about 10 minutes in order to get on one of the pick-up trucks that carry passengers.  He'll use the loan to purchase five sacks of compost so that he can use them in his coffee crop and obtain a better coffee harvest.  By using the fertilizers he'll ensure that his harvest will improve and that his farm will yield more profits. Also, he'll obtain higher earnings for his family and for continuously investing in the farm.  His goal is to sow the waste lands, grow coffee on them and improve his farms.

name: Juliet's Group
description: Juliet is 23 years old and lives in the town of Iganga in the Iganga region of Uganda. For the past three years, Juliet has been working hard to manage her retail shop, where she sells bags.   To help expand her business, Juliet has requested a loan of 100,000 UGX from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy different types of bags to sell, and will help Juliet to generate greater profits and add another business of selling clothes. Juliet hopes that in the future she will be able to complete her parent’s house.   Juliet is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities, and a forum for life-skills training.

name: Elvira
description: Elvira is 30, has two children, lives with her husband who works selling wood.  Four years ago she started raising chickens in a small area built behind her house, she then takes them to the market and sells them for the best offer.  What she likes about her job is raising good chickens so that her clients have no complaints about size or weight.  This is a profitable business because in approximately 35 days the chickens are ready for sale.  The difficult part of her job is not having an appropriate location, because the small area in her house is not suitable to properly raise the chickens.  With MFP she has two loans, she likes to work with the community bank because everyone is responsible and helpful.  The money now requested is to be invested in buying baby chickens as well as feed to raise them.Translated from Spanish by Sofia Burt, Kiva Volunteer

name: Marvie
description: Marvie is 43 years old, married and has four children. They live at Amulung where she put up a small buying station for rice and corn. Her spouse is her partner in managing the business. Marvie also works as a teacher.  Marvie is now asking for a loan to invest in expanding their business. She hopes to keep increasing income for the education of their children. She is asking for a loan of 50,000 Philippine Pesos (PHP) to buy additional farm supplies (fertilizers) to sell. She will also use her loan as additional revolving capital in buying corn and rice to re-sell.  Someday, with good profits, she will achieve financial stability and give the best education to her children.

name: Sirojiddin
description: Sirojiddin was born in 1994 year. He is young and industrious man from North Tajikistan. He lives with his parents in a rural area. Sirojiddin has been busy with growing crops more than 5 years. Little by little with the passing of the time he develops business. His parents help him with managing business. Sirojiddin is asking for a loan of 1000 Somoni to buy seeds and mineral fertilizers for because he must make autumn sowing of crops. Sirojiddin awaits your mercy because he needs to your support.

name: 1 De Diciembre Group
description: The committee “1 de Dicimebre” is in its second cycle, and is beginning with many hopes to be able to improve the life conditions of each of the members through united work.  Maria is very good with sales and works selling perfumes and colognes of every kind. In this way she earns an honest living and with it, she helps her family. Maria works and makes an effort in order to be able to help her family and give them everything that she wasn’t able to have and so that their needs aren’t overlooked.  She asks for this loan in order to be able to buy a variety of perfumes to sell and, in this way, be able to continue with her sales, fulfilling the orders of her clients. All of the members are happy to be part of the group and to receive training.

name: Irma
description: Irma, 23, has two children; one is four and the other is one year old.  She’s been living with her spouse for almost two years in a humble house that’s hers, though.  She and her husband farm fields they own where they grow coffee, bananas and some manioc for family consumption.  Essentially, they live off coffee sales.  On the other hand, her husband earns extra income working as a day worker on other fields but he doesn’t do this too frequently.  Irma is starting the farming chores.  Her family is still young so she’s always had inconveniences because of that like the lack of budget, for example, and lack of personnel and land.  Later on if her plans for the fields prosper she hopes to do some home improvements, to replace the rustic roof with plywood as well as some other details to provide her children with a better quality of life.  This is her first MFP loan and she hopes it will be continuous because she very much wants to grow.  Work with “Los Yorinis” (her communal bank) is pleasant and serves as inspiration for her to continue enterprising.  She will use the money to buy sacks of manure and fertilizer that she figures will cost about 150 soles per sack and coffee seeds to start the new planting.

name: Seniwe Group
description: Tiowa is the gentleman holding the donkey’s rope among the members of his group. He is 49 years old, married to three women, and the father of fifteen children, aged 4 to 22. All of the children are out of school. He is a farmer but for fifteen years he has also been raising livestock to sell. He gets his supplies from local markets within an approximately 20 km radius. He resells the animals at the local markets, as well as in neighboring villages, with a profit margin of 125, 000 francs CFA. HIs three wives are all homemakers, who help him with the fieldworld and the animal maintenance and who take care of the housework.Tiowa has turned to RMCR loans to develop his business by buying more animals in order to satisfy his customer and make a profit. He likes this business a lot, despite the multiple risks (theft, accidents, illnesses, animal deaths). For the future, Mr. Tiowa dreams of becoming a major retail merchant of animals. With the profits earned, he will be able to build sturdy housing and to purchase bicycles for his children, who will sign up for schooling at the next academic year, since the school is located 10 km from his home. This explains why his children are out of school.

name: Chhean
description: Chhean, 28, lives in Banteay Meanchey Province, Cambodia. She is a lovely mother of two children, who are currently in school. To make a living, she has been in the farming business, growing rice and selling her agricultural products to local dealers and customers on the market. Besides this, she also raises pigs for sale. On average, she generates an earning of 7.00 USD per day.   Chhean wants to improve the general living conditions of the entire family by having a latrine to use, because there is no latrine in her house now. Therefore, she is borrowing a loan from Kiva to build a latrine. By doing this, she can help her family members gain access to sanitation, promote their health, and help to lessen environmental deterioration.   She is thankful for the loan granted through HKL with a much lower interest rate than other general loan products.

name: That
description: That T.  L. is 58 years old.  She is a farmer whose main activities are focused on raising cows . She has milk to sell every day.  That T.  L. earns a  stabL. income from these activities to help support her family.  She has been a SEDA client since 2004 and has used her loans very effectively in expanding her cattL. raising. Last year she borrowed 4,142,000 VND to  buy grass and baby trees for food for the cows. Currently, she is requesting a loan of 5,450,000 VND to improve housing for her cows.

name: Emmanuel
description: Emmanuel has been in farming for three years, doing dairy, maize and vegetable farming in his rural home area in Kitale, Western Kenya. He is married with one child who is 4 years old.  Emmanuel has made a loan request amounting to 30,000 Kenyan shillings (KES) from Juhudi Kilimo to buy poultry birds. He says the new venture has great potential for growth due to a ready market. He notes, however, that poultry farming is not without challenges, with disease outbreak being a threat, and needs proper management.  Emmanuel says seasonal changes limit the gains from farming, but he is hopeful that poultry farming faces the least challenge from this.

name: Patrick
description: Patrick is 65 years old married to Priscillah. They have four children and he is supporting his 12 and 16 year old.  Patrick is a farmer from Ndunyu Njeru.  Patrick is requesting his seventh loan from KADET LTD to buy fertilizer and pay for labor. He hopes to use the profit from his loan to expand his farming business and pay school fees.

name: Jovanna
description: Jovanna is a young woman of 25 who lives in her parents house. Two years ago, she decided to become economically independent forming her own business, selling food in her restaurant. She depends on the help of her mother in attending to clients. Jovanna has good taste because everday her customers enjoy her tasty and healthy food. For this, every morning she supplies the necessary ingredients for the food and once finished with her sales, cleans the plates and utensils, leaving everything ready for the next day. Although the job is exhasting, for Jovanna it is enjoyable to have her own business. For this reason she looks at the future with much enthusiasm.   This is the fourth time that she has had credit with MFP. She is one of the most active clients in the communal bank as she is punctual in her payments. The money she is now soliciting, she will use in the purchase of ingredients and in the the improvement of her restaurant, changing her table cloths and other utensils.  Translated from Spanish by karl baumgarten, Kiva Volunteer

name: Moses
description: Moses is twenty nine years old. He is married and has two children who are in school. Moses is an auto mechanic and a retailer of engine oil, brake fluid, gaskets and other car spare parts. He buys his supplies from oil filling station operators in barrels and sells in smaller quantities to his customers. Moses is handicapped by low working capital since oil prices have gone up. He therefore needs a loan to remain in business. He wants to use the loan to buy additional barrels of engine oil, gallons of brake fluid and spare parts to serve his customers. Moses believes this will enable him to make a good income from his business. He would be grateful for your assistance.

name: Rolita
description: Rolita is 43 years old and married with five children, four of whom are in school. She is in the agricultural business, farming vegetables in the Philippines.   She has requested a PHP 11,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy seeds and fertilizer for her vegetable farm.  Rolita has been farming vegetables for five years now and has borrowed from NWTF six times in the past to sustain her business. In the future, she would like to save enough money so that she can continue to send her children to school and repair her family's home.

name: Vilma
description: After finishing her high school studies, Vilma got married to Victor A. and they live happily at Barangay Aliaga Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya. They were blessed with four children. Three of them are now in their college education, therefore, they have to work hard to provide their children with their important needs.	  They earn income thru farming as their major source of livelihood while Vilma manages a general store as an alternative source of income to support their daily needs. She is requesting a loan amounting to PHP 5,000 so that she will be able to expand  her selling business further. She also hopes  to improve her store by saving little amounts from her daily income. She believes that she will become successful in her business endeavor through patience and hard work.

name: Hout
description: Hout H. was born in 1959 and has established a small family in the best part of Phnom Penh, Cambodia. She stays at home taking care of daily duties. The family is supported by Hout’s  husband who owns a motorcycle that he uses to provide a taxi service. They also receive help from her daughter who is employed in Malaysia.   Hout’s husband’s motorcycle is old and often breaks down, resulting in a decline in income. Hout hopes to resolve this problem by obtaining a loan for her husband to replace his broken taxi.

name: Giang
description: Mrs. Giang  is a hardworking woman, 34 years old. She is married and has two children. The loan can help her to build a latrine to improve her family living standard. Her family’s income is mainly from small business and fishing. With more than 10 years experience and has support from her husband, she is able to repay the loan monthly.

name: La Alegria Group
description: The “Alegría” (Joy) committee has been working with the Fundación for more than a year; its members have been carrying out productive activities and through this work are able to help their families.  Matilde is one of this committee’s members.  She joined with the hope of being able to grow and earn higher income to support her family.  She works buying, selling and gathering recyclable materials like plastic, aluminum, cardboard, etc.  Through this honest, dignified work she’s able to help her family providing for their needs so they can have a life that’s free from wants.  Matilde is very proud of her work which is her family’s support and is asking for this loan to invest in plastics and cardboard that she’ll be able to resell and earn higher profits.  She’s grateful for this new opportunity she has because it will be of much help to her.

name: Daniel
description: Sr. Daniel D. G. has been operating his blacksmith business for more than a year.  He needs to build a roof over his patio since that is where he performs his work.  Due to the sun and the rain, he is not able to finish his outstanding orders and can only work in the morning.  He decided to install a roof made of tin and wood so that he can be protected from the sun and the rain while he is working.  Dante is requesting a loan so that he can buy the necessary materials to complete this improvement.  He plans to repay the loan using part of the earnings from his blacksmith business, which is the source of income for his family.  Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Nalukolongo 2(A) Group
description: Shakira is 28 years old and married with three children. Her husband is a mechanic. Shakira has a beauty salon business and usually earns about shs 70,000 in profits each week. She wants to use the extra business profits to pay school fees for the children and also increase salon business. Hadijah has a retail shop and wants to use the loan to increase stock. Nulu sells used clothes while Joyce sells raw foods in the market.

name: Wilma
description: Wilma owns & operates a "sari-sari" (general) store, selling both food & daily use products in the local community for more than six years. She earns well for the family. She had successfully repaid her previous loan used in her business for capital.   In 2009, Wilma joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities.  Recently, she took a new loan again to purchase additional grocery goods to sell.  She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.

name: Giovana
description: The member belongs to the Siempre Adelante (Always Moving Forward) Community Bank. The bank is located in the Ollantaytambo district in the province of Urubamba and department of Cusco.  The member is Giovana. She is 40 years old and is married with four children. The member balances her daily life with the business of selling snacks. She has a small booth in the train station. [The trains] go to the Machupicchu district and stay four hours in the city of Cusco because Machupicchu is a place where many tourists visit each year. It is very popular because it is a beautiful place for refilling one's energy. The member works from 3 am to 9 pm. In the midst of running the tiny business she cares for her children. The member wants to grow her snack sales business. The member requests this loan to purchase snacks such as crackers, sweets, lollipops, and chocolates wholesale.  The member is happy to receive this loan and promises to make her payments on time.

name: Ibrahima Bao
description: Mr. Ibrahima Bao T. lives in Camberene. First, he is an electrician. In addition, he raises livestock. He has five years of experience in his work. He has been a member of the Camberene branch since August 2009. He is seeking a loan of 100,000 of West African Francs in order to purchase livestock and start a new cycle. This loan will allow him to increase his revenues and better provide for his needs.

name: Ty
description: Mr. Ty P. (pictured) and his wife, Mrs. Ny Son, live in a small village in the suburbs of Phnom Penh, the capital city of Cambodia.  They have been married since 2001 and Ny just got pregnant.    Mr. Ty P. is a motor taxi driver and assists his wife in their joint business when he is free.  The couple has supplemented their income with a new business of raising chickens. They are now requesting another loan in the amount of $1,000 to purchase additional chickens to raise.

name: Charles
description: Charles, lives in Kantozi TC, where many of the men had viable business ideas, but didn’t have enough capital to start his own business. Until he joined Ugafode, where he attained training on how to establish and run profitable business activities.Charles is a married man aged 40 yrs. He looks after 6 children. All of them are school going and he is fully in charge of paying their school fees and providing other basic needs.                                                        He wants a loan of UGX3,000,000 for corn and beans in order to supply his customers (schools) so that he can improve production and also improve his family’s living standards. His additional income is from selling goats. This loan will also expand his business.Charles expressed his sincere gratitude and appreciation for this great support that is really improving and changing lives in ibanda district. And therefore funding is vital for this client.

name: Abena
description: Even though Abena grew up in poverty without an education, this has not stopped her from fulfilling her dream of achieving a better life for her and her family. Currently, Abena is an entrepreneur. She sells yam and rice in Onyaadze (near Cape Coast). Her business enterprise has grown substantially since she began two years ago. She uses the income from her business to help her husband raise their four children. Abena has identified that there are growing demands among consumers for her product. Nevertheless she is unable to meet their needs due to limited inventory capacity. Thus she aims to use her loan to purchase more yams and rice to sell. With the new profits from her expanded business, Abena wants to buck the trend by ensuring that all her children will be given the opportunity to further distance their family from poverty.

name: Rachel
description: Rachel, is aged 47, married to a farmer and blessed with three children. She has owned and managed a retail store in their village for almost 22 years and earns a net income of PHP 1,500 daily. Her net income from this business is usually spent on their food expenses and school allowances of their children.   Due to insufficient funds, she would like to avail herself of a loan amounting to PHP 40,000 to purchase canned goods, milk, noodles, biscuits, and beverages to sell. She's hoping that her business will continue to improve and become more profitable.

name: Joseph
description: Joseph is 42 years old and lives in the town of Makindye in the Kampala north region of Uganda. He is married and has three children who are all currently in school.   For the past five years, Joseph has been working hard to manage his metal workshop which deals in welding metals.   To help expand the business, Joseph has requested a loan of 2,500,000 UGX from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy more welding machinery and metals. This will help Joseph to generate greater profits and to build rental houses.   Joseph hopes that in the future he will be able to buy plot of land.

name: Dayyabu
description: Dayyabu is a maize farmer and member of Babban Gona. Dayyabu joined Babban Gona primarily to create a better future for his  children. Dayyabu is excited that Babban Gona offers a lasting solution to ending the cycle of poverty. For the first time, Dayyabu will have access to quality inputs such as fertilizer and seed. Without this loan, he would be subjected to buying these products in the open market where the products are not only very expensive but are often diluted with external products such as sand. With access to high quality inputs, Dayyabu can reap up to 30 bags/hectare, double the national average of 14 and  earn up to $2000/ha: more than three times the average Nigerian farmer’s annual income.  When asked how he plans to spend the income he will make this year  as a Babban Gona member, he said, “I plan to use the money  to expand my farmland.” Dayyabu is not thinking about this year alone; he expressed that his longterm goal is to “become the most profitable farmer in my community”. With this loan, he is well on his way to achieving this goal.

name: Cheer
description: Cheer is 48 years old and lives in Dicoloc, Jimenez, Misamis Occidental. She is widowed with two children. Cheer has a store and sells groceries and other consumer products. She earns approximately 5,000 PHP each month doing this type of work. She has requested a loan to be used in purchasing additional goods and other consumer products for retail.   Cheer has been a member of PMPC for one year. In the future, Cheer hopes to expand her business.

name: Benkadi Group
description: The ten women of the group "Benkadi" are married for the most part in monogamous families. The women average 32 years of age and four children each, all living in the Missira district in Ségou (4th administrative region of the Republic of Mali). They know one another through ties of community, kinship, marriage, and especially their revenue-generating businesses. The group members work in small-scale commerce involving hair extensions, ointments, lipstick, dresses, and perfumes.   With the goal of increasing their working capital, the group members decided to collaborate with the microfinance institution Soro Yiriwaso and are now on their first solidarity loan cycle.  Ms. Fanta, (first woman standing from the left in the photo) has a great reputation for selling hair extension, ointments, and lipstick of all kinds. She intends to use her loan to purchase several packets of hair extensions, containers of ointment, and lipgloss. Sales are made in cash or on credit at the market and by going door to door. Her customer base is composed of women.   With this loan, Ms. Fanta hopes to make an average monthly profit of 35,000 francs CFA that will be reinvested in her business to expand it.

name: Celia Sanjuanita
description: Celia is a very friendly and responsible person who has been living in Piedras Negras for 30 years. Just like her husband she is originally from Nuevo León, but due to her husband's work, they had to move city, today her husband has been retired from the Comisión Federal de Electricidad (Federal Electricity Commission) for several years. Her children are already adults and have their own family. Celia works as a nanny looking after two children who are her grandchildren and she is very happy about looking after them as she feels at ease with them.  Celia is seeking help from Kiva to be able to build a wall which she started but wants to finish so that her grandchildren can play outside near the house and she can remain where she is safe in the knowledge that they are fine. Particularly as at this moment, there is a lack of safety in the city and she wants the best for them, both for herself and her husband as well as her grandchildren.

name: Melati Group
description: To continue and develop their businesses, the Melati group will continue taking loans. One of the members has resigned from the membership, and the group continues with only 14 members.  The loan will be used to support the members' pig businesses. Ni Ketut already has a sow. The loan will be used to buy feed and fix the cage. Because the cage is now inadequate to accommodate the pig, the piglets get loose in her garden. She hopes that the cage will be fixed immediately so the pigs do not roam and disturb neighbors. With this effort, Ni Ketut supports her husband to fulfill the needs of the family.

name: Nkechi's Group
description: Nkechi is 49 years old and she is engaged in full-time palm oil processing. This is a trade she has known with since her youth, but because of limited capital, she finds it very difficult to meet up with her annual family responsibilities. As a single mother, she has the responsibility of taking care of her seven children living with her. Since she joined Nke-Anyi Farmers Multipurpose Cooperative Society, she has learned to save through our weekly Osusu contribution and this has help her to manage her income wisely. This loan will help her and her group members to increase production this season, and support her family. Thanks to all Kiva lenders who find time to read through and support this loan.

name: Srey's Group
description: A rural villager from the Moung Russey district, Srey is 44 years old and married. She has four children; three are dependents. She is a farmer who has grown rice and cassava to make a living for two years.   Srey is a third-cycle client with VisionFund; she has successfully used the past loans to better support her family. She is now leading her group to ask for a loan. She is going to use her portion to buy fertilizer for her farmland. She hopes to have more yield from her farming business.

name: Parven
description: Parven is a 26-year-old lady who is very poor and needy. Her husband provides sheltering services to generate income to feed his entire family. He has been doing this business for many years and has been using wooden planks and bamboo, which have been depreciating over time.   Now he is unable to continue his business without wooden boards and bamboo. Therefore, Parven has requested a loan for her husband so that he can buy new smooth wooden boards, bamboo and a drill machine to continue his business again. She hopes that this loan will bring positive changes in her life and that her husband will earn maximum profit with the help of this loan.  Parven is very thankful to Kiva and its field partner because they empower her husband to buy new sheltering material.

name: Awilda Altagracia
description: Awilda Altagracia is a young medical student who is asking for a loan to pay for her studies. This is her story:  My name is Awilda Altagracia, I am 21 years old and live in Sabaneta, La Vega. I live with my mother who is a housewife and my father who is a farmer, as well as my two sisters and one brother. I am studying medicine at UCATECI and am in the seventh semester. I like this career as I will be able to use it to serve those in need in society. My favourite subjects are anatomy and microbiology. My reason for needing a loan is that I don't have enough money to carry on studying and in my area a lot of doctors are needed to help those most in need. My goal is to be successful in my studies and get good grades so that one way or another my parents will feel proud of me and, as I already mentioned, to help those who need me. I hope to be lucky with the loan so I can continue towards my big goals.

name: Heghnar
description: This nice lady’s name is Heghnar and she is 33 years old. With her husband and two children, she lives in Tsovagyugh of Gegharkunik region. She has vocational pedagogical education but never managed to work in that field. From the time she got married till today, she has been farming with her husband. In the farm she has cows, a pig, piglets, a calf, sheep, and chickens. She sells produce right from her farm: milk, macun (a traditional dairy-product), curd, and eggs. The sale of her farm meat is her husband’s duty; he sells it to city butchers. Together this lovely couple also cultivate potatoes and tomatoes and they sell those to re-sellers. With great plans and expectations of having more income for her family, Heghnar is asking for this loan of 700,000 Armenian drams in order to buy one more cow for her farm and also fodder for her farm cattle.

name: Héctor Manuel
description: Héctor is 46 years old and studied up to eighth grade at school. He is single and lives with his parents, who depend on him.  Héctor has been a farmer for 30 years. He learned this work from his father, who wanted him to have a trade. Héctor always accompanied his father in his work. Héctor now works from 6 a.m. until 11 p.m.  This loan will be used to buy farming supplies, such as weed-killer - as weeds are not good for crops - and manure. Manure is currently being sold cheaply and so Héctor wants to take advantage of the low price.

name: Marisol
description: Sra. Marisol is a member of the Communal Bank “Unidos Para El Triunfo” (United for the Triumph), which is located in the district, province, and department of Cusco.  She is 41 years old, married, and has three children.  Marisol divides her time between her daily activities and her business of selling Christmas decorations.  She travels to Juliaca and Puno to acquire her merchandise and then sells it to her customers in Molino.  Marisol is requesting a loan to buy more merchandise for her business.  She is grateful to those who helped fulfill her dream and promises to complete her payments by the established deadlines.

name: Héctor Eduardo
description: Mr Héctor Eduardo Perez has already had two loans with FVP which he repaid punctually and with which he began construction of two rooms on the top floor of his house.   He is now requesting a loan to finish the rooms which will be for his daughters since they are growing and need their own space. He plans to repay the loan with earnings from his work as a truck driver.Translated from Spanish by Daniel Burke, Kiva Volunteer

name: Haneefan's Group
description: I am Haneefan B. from Kot Radha Kishan, a small town in Pakistan. I live with my family in a five-room brick mud house here in KRK. I am a mother of seven: four boys and three girls. I stitch and embroider clothes on order from women of my locality. My husband is a cobbler.  Earlier, we invested loans in this business and managed to increase our income.  With the increased income, I bought a television for my house and built a toilet in my house. Now, we want to buy a stock of items that are used in repairing shoes in bulk and therefore, we need a loan. I, on my behalf, request loans for few other women who are: Nasreen B., who needs a loan for their used items trading; Asiah B., who supples candies and toffees to various shops in the city and needs a loan to improve their business;  Salma B., who requires a loan for their cloth business; Rizwana B., who will invest their loan in their restaurant.

name: Tamaz
description: Tamaz is seventy years old and lives with his wife in the village of Bazaleti in the Dusheti region of Georgia. As his retirement pension is not enough to make a living, he started to cultivate a small farm. At his farm, he has grapes, fruit trees, a vegetable garden, one cow and a few pigs. He sells the crops, milk and meat to generate additional income.  With the help of the loan, Tamaz will buy two more cows and three pigs. When there is plenty of work, Tamaz hires some neighbours to help him. They are glad to have the extra money.

name: Sonia
description: This member belongs to the “QORIWASI” cooperative bank, located in the district of Cusco.    Her name is Sonia, she is 43 years old, and the single mother of 1 son.  She alternates her daily activities, and is also a tourist guide traveling to different areas to lead tours.  She would like to have a travel agency.    She is requesting this loan to do some repairs to her home.  She thanks everyone who may take part in this dream of hers via this medium, and commits to repaying the loan in the agreed upon time frame.

name: Aisha
description: Aisha lives in Kampala, Uganda.  She is single and has 4 children, all of whom are in school.  Aisha has a business of tailoring.  She has been in this business for 8 years, and she works 7 days out of every week. Aisha sells her products at the market, by means of retail.   Aisha  has requested for a loan of 400000 Ugandan Shillings from MCDT SACCO, which she will use to buy more rolls of clothing materials.  The main business challenges for Aisha include seasonality and defaulters.  Her goals and aspirations for her business are to own a tailoring school and also to educate her children up to university.   Aisha lives in a home that she rents; she doesn't have access to electricity and doesn't have access to piped water.  Her major monthly expenses include rent, feeding the family and school fees.

name: Raisalam
description: This is Raisalam, a 47-year-old mother and resident of Payatas, Philippines who lives with Abdul Jalil, her business partner. She and her partner manage their household while operating the business. At this time, she is working hard to continually provide income for her everyday expenses.                              Raisalam operates a phone accessories retail business. Buying her items from a wholesaler, she sells them per piece/pack for a profit. Products can range from cell phone accessories like head phones to cell phone holders and other such products. Customers are attracted to buy due to the low selling prices and the many options she offers. Raisalam also offers school supplies and jewelries in her store.  Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community.  She earns a minimum of 500 Philippine Pesos (PHP) in sales every day.  To help her continue operations of her business, she is requesting a Php 8,000 loan to buy more quantities and varieties of accessories to expand her product inventory. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands her business soon to give her family a good future. As well, Raisalam faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her work every week.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Armando Rigoberto
description: Armando is 29 years old. He lives with his common-law wife and their children in the Ventana Canton in the Los Rios Province. He has two children.   The members of the ‘Jesús Nos Ama’ [Jesus Loves Us] communal bank are located in the Los Amarillos community in the Ventanas Canton. This group is dedicated to short-cycle agriculture, planting corn, rice, and beans. They have been engaged in this business activity for a long time.   Armando is a farmer, and he grows corn, rice, and cocoa.  He purchases his products in Agripac Eicopa, and he carries out his sales at the fair in Ventanas.   He requests a loan to purchase agricultural products and fertilizers that he needs to plant corn, rice, and cocoa. With this loan he will have the financial support to provide for his needs.  He faces difficulties such as pest infestations, disease, and the changing weather.   His dream is to buy a car for his work and a plot of land upon which to build his house.

name: Sarojini Self Help Group
description: In 2008, 10 women from Balugaon village stepped out and decided to build a secure future for their family. They formed a group named Sarojini Self Help Group. The members of Sarojini Self Help Group are all women from the district of Khurda in Odisha, India. One of them is Mrs. Sarojin, who was selected as their president. The lady in the blue saree sitting first from the left hand side in the photo is Sarojin. Sarojin is 47 years old and is staying with her husband and her two children. Her husband is a farmer and has been involved in cultivation for a long time. She got the idea of doing paddy cultivation from her husband, so she gathered some other women from her neighbourhood and told them about her plan. They liked her idea and appreciated her. She took on leadership of the group and started to cultivate paddy and sell them in her village. She has very good relationships with her customers as she sells paddy or rice, whichever is required by the customers, on time. Now she has a new idea, which is to lease more land for cultivation so that she can do paddy cultivation on a large scale. For this reason, she has requested a loan to purchase seeds and fertilizers.

name: Touch
description: Touch P., 29, is a local farmer who lives in Kompong Chhnang Province. Touch P. earns about $1 per day. His wife, Mrs. Neang Sokunthea, is a 25 year-old farmer who also makes about $1.  With two young children and growing family expenses, Touch P. needs to increase his income. He is requesting funds to purchase and raise small pigs and to purchase ducklings for eggs. By using the Kiva loan, he will get a higher profit and will be able to support his family effectively.

name: Kasifa Namakula ‘Sgroup
description: K. is a leader of five members of a group.  She is a 65-year-old single mother of two children aged 45 and 35 years.  None of her children goes to school because they are all old with five children of their own aged between 17 and 25 years. Only three of their children go to school. She resides in and owns a four-roomed house where she is staying with five people. K. takes care of additional family members. There is electricity and piped water at her home.  The family gets three meals a day. She resides and works in a semi-urban area, which is in the outskirts of Kampala. K. stays in Mulago zone selling second hand clothes in Kalerwe one of Kampala suburbs. She incurs extra transport costs to and from shopping or work. K. also sells chicken and pig's food. She sells to an average of 20 people a day and sells to all categories of people excluding children. She works six days a week. K. sells mainly on retail only. Her major monthly expenses include school fees and rent for her business premises.  She has been in this business for the last five years. K. has been with MCDT for over five years and is servicing her 10th loan, working with the same group mates. She wants to use this loan to buy clothes for resale.  K. is aspiring to see her business grow bigger and to own a permanent business premise.  .

name: Gloria
description: Gloria finds pleasure in doing her hog-raising business in Pagadian City.  Not only is she doing things she likes, but she also earns an income as well.   At the age of 54 and married, she busies herself to sufficiently provide for the family. She grabbed the opportunity to become a full-fledged member of PMPC. She credits the cooperative for providing her capital in supporting her gardening activities.   Recently, she applied a loan to purchase bags of animal feed. In the future, Gloria wishes to become a supplier of pork in the neighboring towns.
town: Pagadian - Pagadian City, Zamboanga del Sur

name: Rosalie
description: Rosalie D. is from the village of Baluarte, Lumbia, Cagayan de Oro City. She is 33 years old. Rosalie is married and has 2 school-aged children. To make a living, Rosalie owns & operates a business venture in the retail sector operating a specialized retail store. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from buying and selling of firewood in the local community. Rosalie has been engaged in her business for over 5 years and earns approximately 6000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Rosalie joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Rosalie has successfully repaid a previous loan of 8000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to purchase additional products to sell. Rosalie is requesting a new loan of 11000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional inventory & working capital. This loan will be the 3rd loan taken out by Rosalie from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand the business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.
town: Baluarte, Lumbia, Cagayan de Oro, Misamis Oriental

name: Joyce
description: Joyce is forty four years old. she is married with three children between the ages of twelve and seventeen years. Her husband is a commercial driver and is very supportive with their children's school fees. Joyce is a seamstress and also sells sachet water. She has been selling sachet water for five years now. According to her, the sachet water business moves faster than tailoring.   She will use this loan to purchase more sachet water and sell to increase her income. She believes that in years to come her sachet water business will grow and expand.

name: Juan
description: Juan was born in the city of Huayllabamba but lives in the city of Yucay. (The peruvian districts of Yucay and Huayllabamba are two of the seven districts in the province of Urubamba, located in the Department and Region of Cusco, Peru.)   Jun, age 42, has has two children as a result of his happy marriage. His main economic activity is selling maize, animal fodder and vegetables. Juan is seeking the loan to buy more vegetables, such as maize.  Juan es integrante del banco comunal “Virgen Natividad” y el grupo está conformado con 15 socios que viven unos en la ciudad de Huayllabamba y otros en la ciudad de Yucay.

name: Kototala Group
description: The KOTOTALA group is part of the BENKADI association of TIELE. It consists of married women who know one another as neighbors and through ties of kinship. They average 29 years of age and three children each. They practice various activities including restaurant services as offered by SALI, standing 2nd from the left in the group photo. They live in large traditional families in TIELE, sub-prefecture of BAGUINEDA (Koulikoro region, Republic of Mali).   They have been engaged in small trade for many years and they are in high demand for their restaurant services offering meat, fish and beans.  In an effort to meet their customers’ increasing demand, the group members joined the Soro Yiriwaso microfinance institution 3 years ago. This is their 5th group loan cycle.    SALI, the group’s president, is well known around TIELE and highly skilled in her restaurant activity. She plans to use her loan to buy a large quantity of meat and fish and 2 sacks of beans for her restaurant. She buys her stock in Bamako and from local wholesalers. She retails her food products in TIELE, cash or credit, to a clientele consisting of both men and women.      Sali hopes to earn a monthly profit of 20,000FCFA, which will allow her to repay her loan and to reinvest in her restaurant activity.

name: Kol
description: Kol is 60 years old and is a single mother of three children, two of whom are married while her last-born child is studying in a 4-year program at a local university.  He is majoring in medicine and is going to graduate soon. At the same time, he works for a Christian organization using his medical skills to support his living.  Being a helpful mother, Kol is requesting this loan to help her son cover his expenses to write his thesis in order to earn a bachelor degree. Kol hopes that her son will be able to graduate and earn a degree through the loan support. She appreciates to all kind lenders

name: Julian
description: Julian is 57, single and lives in his own home with his son in the district of Cayalti which is in the province of Chiclayo, in the department of Lambayeque, Peru . He has very good references, as many personal as work, from the people in the area. The people in this town generally earn a living from agriculture and the livestock trade. He earns a living from the manufacture of furniture, doors, chairs, beds, etc. and has more than 7 years experience in the trade. His business is based in his own home and he is applying for a loan in order to buy wood for furniture manufacturing. With this he can grow his business, earn more and improve his quality of life. Julian is a regular member of Edpyme Alternativa and has had six loans, the last one of S / 5,000.00, which he repaid in a timely manner.

name: Let God Be Group
description: Tenneh K. is the leader of a group of five borrowers called Let God Be. She is 39 years old and a single mother with three children between the ages of 6 and 16 years old. Their educational levels range from nursery to ninth grade.  Tenneh and her family live and work in Saye Town, a community that has both poor and middle-class Liberians, in Monrovia, the capital of Liberia. She was never able to go to school herself due to lack of financial support from her parents.  Tenneh’s business is the sale of general goods such as rice, oil and other cooking ingredients. She buys her goods from wholesalers and sells retail to residents of Saye Town. She has been running this business for nine years and is hoping to own a shop in the near future. Tenneh started selling with 4,000 Liberian Dollars but now operates with about 10,000 Liberian Dollars.  She communicates with her customers in a good manner and sells good products in order to encourage customers to continue buying from her. Tenneh needs this loan to purchase rice, oil, seasoning, etc., for resale. She dreams of being a good provider to her family and well-known as a businesswoman.  In the photo that accompanies this profile, Tenneh is the one holding the sign.  About LEAP: The Local Enterprise Assistance Program (LEAP) is Liberia's largest and oldest continuously operating microfinance institution with 13 branches across the country. Founded in 1994, the non-profit organization has survived periods of civil war and severe socio-economic hardship. LEAP seeks to help rebuild post-conflict Liberia through its group and individual loans to micro- and small-scale entrepreneurs, and puts emphasis on lending to women.  Join the Team LEAP - Liberia lending team on Kiva today!

name: Talananeh Group
description: These are Marie K., Mabinty B., Nenneh B., Fatmata K., and Kadiatu K.. They named their group "Talaneneh". They are all local entrepreneurs in Waterloo, a small town twenty miles from Freetown. This is the first loan these entrepreneurs are requesting from SMT/Kiva. Each of them is requesting a loan of Le 500,000. With this loan, they will be able to increase the sizes and qualities of their businesses and consequently make better profit and improve their standards of living.   Marie (right) is the leader of this group. Marie is thirty-seven years of age. She was born in Port Loko, in northern Sierra Leone. She is married with two children who are still in primary school. Marie sells palm-oil (the most popular cooking oil), gari (a food produced by grinding cassava) and palm kernels. She has been a businesswoman for over seventeen years now.

name: Dolores
description: Dolores works hard to support her family. Dolores is married and has a food vending business in the Philippines.  Dolores requested a 12,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase ingredients, such as meat, cooking oil, spices, vegetables, flour, etc. for her food production business.  Dolores has been in this business for 20 years now.  Dolores would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Langmet's Group
description: A citizen from a rural village of Kampong Cham province’s Ou Rang Ov district, Langmet is 54 years old. She has two children to take care of. To feed her family, she has worked hard as a rice farmer who has been growing rice and cassava for 34 years. The current business earns her about 30,000 KHR per day to meet the family’s needs.    Langmet is with VisionFund this cycle. Now she is leading her group of two to ask for a loan of 1,000,000 KHR each. As the leader, Langmet is going to buy fertilizers for her farmland and spend a portion of it on labor fees. She hopes to make healthy rice and cassava to increase her family’s income so as to make their living better.
town: Kampong Cham province, Ou Reang Ov district

name: Happy Group
description: Zainabu who is in her early 30's,is a single with one kid who is in school. She has been running a cereals shop for nine years now. She works from 6am to 10pm daily and is able to make a good profit each month.This will be Zainabu's Fourth loan from Tujijenge Tanzania. She used the previous loans to increase on her general store stock and has managed to repay all her loans successfully. She used the profit to repay loan, to pay school fees for her kid, to reinvest in her business and covered household expenses. She will use this loan to restock the out stock items especially cereals such as rice, beans, peas, maize etc. She dreams of opening a hardware in order to raise her capital.Zainabu will share this loan with her loan group HAPPY which has three members who will hold each other accountable for repay the loan.

name: Janeth Angelie
description: Janeth Angelie is a 32-year-old woman who lives in Tubigon, Bohol with her family. She is a mother of a nine-month-old baby girl. A few a months ago, Janeth Angelie successfully started a rice retailing business. Aside from this, she also helps her partner in fishing. She dreams of a better and more comfortable means of living. That is why she wants to improve their income. To do this, she needs our help by lending her an amount that will help increase her sales. She will buy sacks of rice to sell and a new engine for their fishing boat.

name: Aurelia
description: Aurelia has started her small time business and became a boss with her sari-sari store. She has managed to have enough inventory and rolls up her capital to gain more profit. Everyday she makes good sales since she is the only store in their barangay. Recently she approached Paglaum for her much needed capital to restock the store with basic commodities. In the future, she hopes to have a decent home for the family.
town: Sindangan-Talinga, Leon B. Postigo, Zamboanga del

name: Nelly Kati
description: Nelly is a hardworking and charismatic woman.  She is married and has two children whom she continues to support.  At age 40, Nelly has managed to achieve some dreams such as improving her home and keeping her business.  She feels happy about her achievements.  She sells food, which she delivers.  This began with a desire to have a business of her own and she is able to generate income for her home.  She is asking for a loan to buy supplies and utensils for her business.  Her greatest desire is to have a restaurant so she can have greater earnings.  Nelly is grateful to those who help other countries with their progress and she promises to continue being socially responsible.

name: Lucy
description: Lucy, in her late 40s, is married with four children who are still in school. She has been running several projects: growing and selling broiler chickens, selling clothes and shoes and selling dried foods, like sugar, beans, wheat flour, baking flour, cooking oil, salt and tea leaves.    She has been in her business for six years. She works from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily and is able to make a very good monthly profit.  This will be Lucy's ninth loan with Tujijenge Tanzania. She used the previous loans to buy chicks and open a shop. She is doing fine and has been able to pay back all her loans successfully. She has used her profits to pay school fees, buy a plot of land, build her house and cover household expenses.   Lucy will use this loan to buy chicken feed and chicks to raise into layers. She will make sure that she pays her loan according to the loan schedule.  She dreams of building a rental property.

name: Monina
description: Monina P. is from the village of Poblacion, Aurora Zamboanga del Sur. She is 49 years old. Monina is married and has five adult children. To make a living, Monina owns & operates a business selling clothes. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling clothes in the local community. Monina has been engaged in her business for over 10 years and earns approximately 10,000 PHP a month for these activities.  Monina joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Monina is requesting a new loan of 15000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the fifth loan taken out by Monina from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand the borrower's business and to support her family's basic needs.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Shoira
description: Shoira is a hard-working woman. She was born in a rural area. She lives in a small town. She is married and has three children. About 10 years ago, she began working in the agricultural sphere. She plants seeds and vegetables. She plants and sells barley, cucumbers and onions. She has a friendly family. Shoira and her husband are the keepers of their family. She wants to increase her business. Shoira is planning to buy livestock. She needs financial support to do business.

name: Rigoberto Armando
description: Rigoberto is single and lives in the highland region of Totonicapan, Guatemala. He has a university education and has no children.   Rigoberto works as a loan officer at another institution and has been doing so for about six years (he started his career with ASDIR). He hopes to continue to develop his career as a loan officer and one day become the head of an agency.   Rigoberto is requesting a loan to help pay for some recent personal expenses. This is Rigoberto's sixth loan through ASDIR, and the others have been paid back in full.

name: Julieta
description: As a married parent of two children, Julieta works hard to support her family.  She has a fishing business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from fish vending. Julieta is borrowing PHP 4000 through NWTF to buy fish net, bamboo and gasoline for her boat for her fishing business.  She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Jose Lorenzo
description: José has a small but well-stocked grocery shop. He lives in a peri-urban zone in Paraíso de Guayaquil, a zone characterised by its dirt roads and mountains.  He began his business 10 years ago with one glass case and a stand. Owing to the demand for his groceries he began to purchase rice and oil, and little by little with force and some sacrifice, he now owns and works in his own business. He works from 6am until night time.   With this loan José wants to buy groceries such as rice, canned goods, sugar etc. In the future he wants to continue working and expand his business.    Translated from Spanish by Jane McCrory, Kiva Volunteer

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth is a 46-year-old, married mother of two children. Due to the low financial situation of her husband, she decided two years ago to use her twenty-five years of experience to start tailoring and selling clothes on her own. In this way, she helps her husband in covering the needs and expenses of their family.Today, Elizabeth is acquiring a loan from Kiva's field partner, Al Majmoua. She will use the loan to expand her business and increase her business merchandise with new, winter season, fashionable clothes and textiles. These will help her satisfy her customers' requests.Elizabeth hopes to open her own tailoring shop in the future, to improve her family's living conditions and increase her income even more.

name: Patricia
description: Patricia lives with her children in the city of La Paz.  Patricia has a law degree. Patricia has a problem with a wall in her kitchen that is connected to the patio because the rain and humidity have caused it to crack and deteriorate. She wants this loan to be able to repair this wall, and in this way, give her children an inviting home.   Patricia's dream is to be able to gather enough money to rent her own law office and have better income to improve her family's quality of life.

name: Rosa Leonidas
description: Rosalia is a member of the Violet Communal Bank. She is 69 years old and has eight children. Rosalia has a market in her house where she sells groceries and drinks. She operates her store everyday with her children’s assistance. Rosalia needs a loan of eight hundred soles in order to buy rice and sugar. Rosalia’s dream is to improve her business  Translated from Spanish by Esther Levandoski, Kiva Volunteer

name: Saveth's Group
description: Saveth is a resident residing in a rural area of Sangke district located in Battambang province, Cambodia.
