She is 31 years of age and married with three dependent sons, all of whom are currently in school. To offer a decent life for her family, Saveth has a business raising pigs. Her husband works for others as a paid worker in order to add more income to the family. Through the current businesses, this couple is able to earn around 33,000KHR per day and save approximately 13,000KHR after offsetting the daily expenses. This is Saveth’s third time requesting loan via VisionFund, Kiva’s partner. The previous loans have helped Saveth to strengthen her pig-raising business, which has enabled her to earn more income for the family. Now she is leading a loan group of three female members to apply for a loan in the amount of 3,800,000KHR in total. The group representative, Saveth, will use her requested loan portion, which is 1,400,000KHR, to purchase seven heads of pig to raise. Saveth’s biggest hope in the future is to be able to support her dependent sons’ education so that they can have bright future and become potential youths in society.

name: Sharon
description: Sharon is a 19-year-old businesswoman living with her parents and siblings in Umguza district in Zimbabwe. Sharon has been selling clothes at a flea market for the past eight months. She also gives back to her community by volunteering to support children who have dropped out of school. With the loan from Kiva, Sharon hopes to purchase more clothing for her stall. She intends to use any additional proceeds to enroll in nursing school and train as a nurse.

name: Mejumaa
description: Mejumaa is a married mother of three children, all of whom attend school. She owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are school fees and household consumables.For over three years, she has operated an open air food-selling business, selling from home to her neighbours and passersby. She faces a major challenge of seasonality in her place of business. With the KES 20,000 she wants to purchase bundles of wheat flour, maize flour, tea leaves, and cooking fat. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Said
description: Said lives in Tandika in Temeke District of Dar es Salaam.He is married with four children.Said sells water storage drums of 100 litres to 200 litres.He buys them from Dar es Salaam Port after being emptied the materials they come with.In his area public water supplies are irregular.People uses drums as water storage equipments.Said has recently acquired another store to be used as a selling point.The new store demands more working capital.More drums will be stocked,carriage and storage cost will also increase.Said is in need of USD 950 to open his new store.

name: Mbeyu
description: Mbeyu appreciates her previous Kiva loan that improved her living standards.  Besides the poultry business, Mbeyu practices a fruits and vegetable selling business. She is requesting a loan to purchase onions, tomatoes, vegetables and potatoes for resale.   Her previous loan enabled her to expand her business and earn a higher income. She thanks Yehu for their financial support.

name: Erlinda
description: Erlinda T. wants to strengthen her food-selling and sari-sari (variety) store business to be able to increase the amount of profit she earns through it.  A sari-sari store basically sells small quantities of various foodstuffs, grocery items and beverages. “Sari” is a word in the native dialect of Antiquenos meaning “variety”. This is just a small store that is either attached to the owner’s house or in a small native cottage not far away from the owner’s house. Items sold through this business bring convenience to people in the village, especially those who live far away from the town proper where the market is located.  Erlinda started operating this kind of business when she first received a loan from Kiva through ASHI. Now that she has been able to pay back the whole amount of the loan she received, she would like to request a loan almost double the amount of the previous one. This would be used to grow her store and increase the volume of inventory she has for sale. Hopefully, by this she will achieve her goal of helping her neighbors to have access to food and other basic things they need for their everyday lives.  With faith that one day her life, along with that of her children, will be changed and will be better, Erlinda is determined to face a lot of challenges, even without a partner. Having her two loving children with her is such a great inspiration for her to be strong and determined.

name: Zeitun's Group
description: Zeitun is the leader of Zeitun's Group. She is a 26-year-old mother of two children. She and her husband are both dryland farmers, so their agricultural endeavors face the challenge of frequent droughts. Zeitun plans to use the income from her KOMAZA tree farm to educate her children.

name: Charlyn
description: Charlyn is a married woman with four children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Charlyn is 27 years old and has two children currently in school.  Charlyn has a abaca (fiber from abaca palm leaf) weaving business in the Philippines. Charlyn requested a PHP 19,000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase additional materials, such as abaca fiber, etc. for her business.  Charlyn has been in this business for seven years. In the future, Charlyn would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to school.

name: Mariam
description: Mariam is 30 years old, married, and has six children. She lives with her husband in the rural part of Mwambalazi, Coast province.  Mariam has a grocery store. She loves her job, since it gives her ample time to socialize with her family members. The challenge that Mariam faces in her business is the high prices of commodities.   She is requesting this loan to buy oil, rice, sugar, soap and instant foods. With the help of this loan, she will be able to increase her business.

name: Tomas
description: Tomas is a Kubo Financiero client and this is his story.  Hi my name is Tomas, I am 36 years old, have been married for 8 years but don´t have sons. I sell women's clothes in flea markets, usually working 5 days a week from 7 am to 6 pm. I will use the loan for inventory, by having more product variety I can increase sales. I have been doing this work for the last 20 years and fortunately have been able to grow the business, achieve some financial stability and pay my debts on time.  My biggest accomplishments are buying my apartment, a car and a piece of land. My next goal is building a house.

name: Sharifgul
description: Sharifgul considers the most pleasant thing to be when a person earns an honest living through hard work. She has been working in livestock for around 6 years. Sharifgul is a very honest and responsible woman, and she always adheres to her principles. She is from the Farkhor district. She is 56 years old, and her husband is 58. She has lived with her husband for a very long time. Her husband works as a barber. Sharifgul plans to expand her business by buying several head of cattle. For this she needs a loan. Sharifgul is asking for your help and support. All hope is on you.

name: Jane Wanjiru
description: This is Ms. N.’s second loan with Kiva.  She has fully repaid her first loan of US$450 with Kiva, and is requesting an enhanced amount of US$750 to purchase some fashionable clothing items to supply the seasonal needs of her Market.She believes that with a larger stock she will be able to cater better to the needs of her growing client base and capture a larger market segment. Ms. N. is a single mother of 4 children. She deals in new clothes, moving from one market to another throughout the week. She has been doing this kind of business for over 20 years. Ms. N. is a very enterprising lady and well experienced in this kind of business. The business has been a source of support for the education of her children and livelihood of her immediate and extended family. Her goal is to grow her business to wholesale level, which would give her better stability and improve her income generation capacity. Women like Ms. N. are a big inspiration to others in Africa and deserve our support. By empowering them, we are empowering the communities of Africa in view of the key role that they play. Well worth our support.

name: Myriam Magali
description: Myriam, 22 years old, lives on the outskirts of Guayaquil.  She still lives with her parents but works as a Yambal vendor (Yambal is a company that sells cosmetics by catalog, which helps the women of Ecuador become potential vendors).  To get started as a Yambal vendor, Myriam's parents lent her money to buy products and cosmetics.  Little by little, with effort and dedication, cosmetics sales have become her main income so she can begin to become independent.  She sells perfumes, creams, shampoo and cosmetics.  Her schedule varies.  To have a greater variety of products, Myriam wants to buy perfumes and creams with the loan.  In the future, she wants to have her own cosmetics store.Translated from Spanish by Danielle Maxson, Kiva Volunteer

name: Mounira
description: Mounira is a 52-year-old widow who lives in Saida, in southern Lebanon. She has been working as a seamstress for eight years. She sews at home and also cooks when she is asked to. Mounira requested a loan of $500 from Al Majmoua in order to purchase thread for her sewing and some raw materials for her cooking. This is her second cycle and she has always paid on time.  Mounira is special in her work because she does it well and has experience. Her clients are her friends and neighbors. When Mounira first started her business, she didn’t have enough money. She decided on doing her business because of her experience and her precise work. In the future, she plans on expanding her sewing business and opening a restaurant.

name: Mariam
description: Mariam is married and has three children, two of whom attend school. She owns a house that neither has electricity nor piped water.   She operates a coconut selling business, selling at the market to her neighbours and passersby. She faces a major challenge of seasonality in her business.  Her dream is to establish a wholesale shop in the near future.   With the 20,000 KES loan, she wants to purchase six sacks of coconuts to sell.  She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Jane
description: Jane is a thirty-nine-year-old lady from Migori. She is married to Samson and they have six children aged three to twenty years old.  Jane operates an agro-veterinary shop selling livestock drugs, a business she has been doing for the last eight years. She makes a monthly income of KES 8,000. She is taking her eighth loan from KADET LTD. which she will use to buy more animal drugs to sell.  She will use profits to repay back the loan. Her dreams and hopes is to grow her business and provide basic needs for  her family.

name: Nadezhda
description: Nadezhda is from Novaya Kahovka.  She has been involved in a small entrepreneurship, selling socks, stockings and swimming suits, at one of the local markets in her native town for 16 years.  The size of her working capital is 21 000 hryvnia.  The current net profit is about 6 000 hryvnia.  Nadezhda requested a loan from Kiva in the amount of 10 000 hryvnia to purchase 40 sets of swimming suits and also 100 pairs of socks for subsequent resale.  Having expanded her merchandise selection, Nadezhda hopes to have an opportunity to continue supporting her family and providing them with all of the necessities due to an expansion and increased profit.

name: Adela
description: Adela is married and has three children; all of them are going to school. Adela makes and sells cheese. She sells her products at Achacachi. Adela has her own house, and her husband drives a tractor so he provides services to all the farmers of the community. Adela needs a loan to buy a milking cow. She and her husband are having a lot of expenses at their home; that is why Adela is asking for help.

name: Savoeun
description: Mrs. Savoeun V., age 37, is a widow with three children: two sons and one daughter.  Her husband passed away recently.   Silk weaving is her main business for supporting her family. Therefore, she is asking for a loan of $1,200 in order to purchase silk materials to continue her weaving business.

name: Estrellita
description: Estrellita M. is from the village of Poblacion 2, Banisilan, South Cotabato. She is 41 years old. Estrellita is married and has four school-aged children. To make a living, Estrellita owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) shop. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from buying and selling biscuits, milk and chocolate drinks in sachets, snack foods, shampoos, soaps and detergents in the local community. Estrellita has been engaged in her business for over six years and earns approximately 10,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2010, Estrellita joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Estrellita has successfully repaid a previous loan of 8,000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to invest in expanding the business. Estrellita is requesting a new loan of 11,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional inventory and working capital. This loan will be the third one taken out by Estrellita from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue she generates to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Elisa
description: Elisa is 36 years old and married to Antonio. They live prosperously together and have four minor children. They own a house made out of wood, located in Kimbiri, in the Cusco region.  As a child she was trained on how to produce organic cocoa beans along with her parents on several pieces of land that belonged to her grandparents. She has been working independently with her husband for twenty years, and sometimes they hire laborers to help with heavy work such as weeding and harvesting.  She gets up very early each morning and after sending her kids to school she goes to her land and comes back at dusk. She really enjoys her work because she is proud to continue her family's production methods.   Every season she inspects her land for plants that may have outgrown their useful cycle. Currently she has found several trees in this condition that must be replaced by grafting technique. She needs capital in order to do this.   Her plans for the future go towards rebuilding her home with higher quality materials for her children's wellbeing.   She needs to have 1,000 nuevos soles to purchase mastic trees as well as bird guano, and later hire laborers and replace old cocoa trees through grafting.

name: Hadjah
description: Hadjah N. lives in the Kawempe neighborhood in the city of Kampala, Uganda.  She is single and has three children, all of whom are in school.  She also takes care of additional family members (orphans).  Hadjah has a business selling snacks like samosas, Chapatti and pancakes.  She has been in this business for six years and she works 7 days a week. Hadjah sells her products at the market at wholesale and at retail. Hadjah has requested a loan of 300,000/= Ugandan Shillings from MCDT SACCO, which she will use to buy more cooking oil, wheat flour and charcoal. The main business challenge(s) for Hadjah include seasonality and defaulters.  Her goals and aspirations for her business are to see her business grow big, own a big bakery and a plot of land. Hadjah lives in a home that she rents; she doesn't have access to electricity or piped water.  Her major monthly expenses include rent, food and school fees.

name: Abundia
description: Abundia is 53 years old, married, and has nine children.  Abundia is in the agricultural business, raising livestock in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 23,000 loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to purchase additional livestock and other supplies for her business.  Abundia has been raising livestock for ten years now, and has borrowed seven times in the past from NWTF to sustain her business.  In the future, Abundia would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Mariam
description: This pretty lady’s name is Mariam and she is 30 years old. She lives in Yerevan city. She has a higher education with the specialty of linguist and pedagogue.   Many years she worked at the Yerevan poultry factory as an assistant of accounting. Now, to her delight, she works in her specialty at the Language Teaching Center as a teacher of English language. She says she likes her work very much and is happy to work in this field. She also gives private courses in English language at her flat.   Mariam is married and she has a nice daughter. Her husband is employed and together they try to sustain their young family’s needs.   Maraim hopes to have this loan since she must take part in training courses for which she must pay and she will also buy some professional literature.

name: Edita
description: Edita joined Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative and she appreciates the programs, services and continuous education of the co-op. She is a member in good standing and very active in attending the various programs and services that the Cooperative offers. She has a small piece of farm land near her home. She is requesting a loan in the amount of PHP 3,000 to buy farm fertilizers. She dreams of nothing more than to have a happy, healthy life and an adequate income out of her business.

name: Toch
description: Toch is 47 and is married with three children. She lives with her family in Takeo Province, Cambodia, an area known for its pre-Angkorian sites. Toch is a farmer and her husband works in road construction. The couple works so hard every day to earn income to help cover the family’s expenses.   Toch is requesting a 1,200 USD loan to purchase a motorbike for her husband to commute to work. By doing so, her family will be able to increase its income. This will be her first loan through KREDIT, a longstanding KIVA partner. In the future, she would like to use any additional income to repair her house.

name: Charlyn
description: Charlyn is 28 years old and married with two children.   Charlyn is in the agricultural business, raising pigs in the Philippines.   Charlyn requested a PHP 5,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy feed and vitamins for her pigs. She has been raising pigs for two years.  In the future, Charlyn would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Zaynabjon
description: Zaynabjon is a conscientious woman. She lives and works in the north of Tajikistan. Zaynabjon loves her country very much and tries to work for the benefit of her native land. She has higher education.   Zaynabjon has worked as a college teacher for more than 18 years. She lives her profession very much and has many students. Zaynabjon is youth mentor. She has a small pay and this pay was not enough to provide for three children. She raised her children alone, as her husband died early, and she was left as a widow.   Zaynabjon started her business of buying and reselling dried fruits 9 years ago. She manages her pedagogical work and her business in parallel. She plans to replenish her working capital. She requests a loan to purchase dried fruits. She awaits your kindness.

name: Rebeccah
description: Rebeccah is a woman who has been engaged in selling maize and millet for 12 years to earn a living. She is 39 years old, married, and has three children, ages 15, 13, and 5 years old. Her husband works hard as a carpenter to raise their family.Aside from selling maize and millet, Rebeccah also sells vegetables. With this, she is in need of an amount to help her run her business continuously. She will buy food stock such as millet, maize, and vegetables to meet her buyers' expectations.In the future, Rebeccah is aiming for business improvement to uplift their livelihood and to be able to give good education to their children."With loyalty and determination, I will work harder for the repayment as the term and conditions applied," she says.

name: Keo
description: Keo K. is 50 years old, married, and has one child living at home. She lives with her family in the Takeo province. She buys and sells rice, typically making US$1.60 each day, and her husband does construction work. Her husband typically makes about US$6 each day. Keo K. would like a loan of US$600 to purchase more rice to sell in the market.

name: Zamira
description: Zamira lives in Yavan. She is 26 years old, divorced, and has five children. Zamira lives with her parents. She has a vocational education. She works as a cashier in a high school. Additionally, she has worked in animal husbandry for two years. She breeds cattle for sale. In so doing, she helps her parents and brother. She is taking out a loan to purchase a cow and a calf

name: Paulina
description: Paulina, who is in her mid 40s, is married with six children. Two of them are still in school and four are grown up. She has been selling crafts for twenty-two years now. She works from 7 am to 6 pm daily and is able to make a good monthly profit.This will be Paulina’s twenty-first loan from Tujijenge Tanzania. She used the previous loans to increase the crafts stock and has managed to pay back all her loans successfully. She is happy with the loans. She used the profit to pay school fees for her kids, to repay the loans, bought a plot of land, built her own house, bought a TV set, a radio, cupboards, beds, mattresses, a sofa set and covered household expenses. She will use this loan to buy the best selling crafts to meet her customers' requirements. She dreams of owning a hardware shop.

name: Armen
description: Armen finished middle school in Kadjaran, the city of his birth. He's married and has three children. Armen's wife takes care of their household and his elder daughter attends school, while his two younger children go to daycare. Armen's retired mother lives with them.  Three years ago, Armen converted his basement into a workshop in which he now makes furniture on a by-order basis. His main focus is on kitchen furniture and computer desks. In order to increase his income, Armen rents a a small store where he places products ready for sale.  Because of his business, Armen was able to purchase a truck. He transports building materials from Kapan and made furniture from Yerevan on it.  Armen is asking for a loan of 1,000,000 drams to purchase building materials for new furniture. In order to successfully support his family, he works till late without weekends.

name: Mardy
description: Mardy is a married woman with five children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Mardy is 44 years old and four of her children are in school.  Mardy has a business of buying and selling dressed chickens and frozen foods in the Philippines. Mardy requested a loan of 13,000 Philippines pesos (PHP) through NWTF to buy additional dressed chickens and frozen foods for her business.  Mardy has been in this business for 11 years. In the future, Mardy would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Kousar
description: Kousar  is a 43-year-old married woman. She is the mother of four children.  Some years ago she started her business selling animals in her community. Her husband fully supports and assists her with her work. Now, she has requested a loan of 45,000 PKR. She wants to use this loan to purchase more cattle for reselling in the market. Kousar  has gained great confidence in the business as she has learnt how to deal with other individuals within the business, allowing her to feel empowered.

name: Silen
description: Silen, 27, is married, has two children and resides in a rural village located in the Kandal province’s Sa Ang district, Cambodia. For the last five years, she has been selling garlic and her husband works as a taxi driver to earn more income. She can earn about US$20 per day.  Silen has been with VisionFund for two cycles and completely paid the loans. Now she is requesting a loan. With this loan, she is going to buy garlic seeds for her plantation. She hopes to grow more garlic so as to improve her family’s living condition.

name: Nhóm 01 Thôn 9 Quảng Hải Group
description: Mrs. Trần works in agriculture raising poultry, and is requesting a loan to buy more baby poultry to raise and sell. She is 48 years old, married and the mother of one child. Trần leads the Nhóm 01 thôn 9 Quảng Hải solidarity group, which consists of five members. She lives in the Quang Xuong district, a  rural area of Thanh Hoa province. This is her first loan request from the Thanh Hoa Fund of Poor Women. Tần has been involved in her current line of work for more than ten years, and the main challenge she faces is a lack of capital. With her business profit, Trần hopes for her family to be healthy and happy, for her business to do well, and for her child to succeed in school.

name: Aymen
description: Aymen is 23 years old and lives in Sana'a, Yemen. He has been operating a grocery store. He is ambitious to work in this field so that his life will go well. Aymen benefited from the first loan which was funded through Kiva.  With this loan, he is planning to expand his business and stock it with additional products. He asked for a loan of 200,000 YER from AMB to buy grocery items to generate greater profits. He thanks Kiva lenders for funding him the first loan.

name: Teresita
description: Teresita is 56 years old and has ten children. She is married, and two of her children are in school.Teresita is in the agricultural business, raising pigs in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy feed and vitamins for her pigs.She has been raising pigs for four years now, and has borrowed six times in the past from NWTF to sustain her business.In the future, Teresita would like to save money to expand her business and continue to send her children to school.

name: Cathrine
description: Catherine is a 19-year-old living in Zimbabwe’s Buhera District. As a clothing merchant at a local flea market, Catherine sells shirts, shoes, pants and other items. On top of that she also volunteers as a Learner Guide at the local school teaching life skills to students. With a Kiva loan she wants to boost her business by purchasing jeans, shoes, shirts, skirts, blouses and suits in bulk quantities to increase her profit margin. This would take Catherine one step closer to achieving her dream of opening her own shop and creating employment in the community.

name: Mary Ann
description: As a married parent of five children, Mary Ann works hard to support her family.  She has a general store business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from selling food. Mary Ann is borrowing PHP 11,000 through NWTF to purchase additional stocks like coffee, milk and sardines to sell in her general store.  Mary Ann has been sustaining her business activities through her past three loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough money to be able to afford to send her children to college.

name: God Is Able 2 Group
description: The three women who make up the God Is Able 2 group live in nuclear families in the Teshie neighborhood in Accra. They average 48 years of age and three children each. The women know one another through community ties, kinship, marriage and their revenue-generating businesses in the district.   They each have small-scale businesses involving second-hand clothing, kenkey (cook corn paste), yam, sweet potatoes, fish and materials. With the goal of increasing their business capital, the group members decided to join the micro finance institution ID-Ghana and are now on their eighth loan cycle.   Esther (standing in the middle of the photo) is a major vendor of kenkey (cook corn paste) and second-hand clothing. She intends to use her loan to purchase kenkey (cook corn paste) and second-hand clothing in the market at Accra. Her sales are made to a mixed customer base, paying with cash. She operates this business at her residence on a pavement.   With this loan, Esther hopes to make a good monthly profit that will be used to meet her needs and to increase her capital. She would like to continue collaborating with ID-Ghana. She is single, 49 years old, and lives alone.

name: Action Women Group
description: In the photo are members of the “Action Women” group. They are small-scale businesswomen based in Kenema, a city in eastern Sierra Leone. This is the first loan these entrepreneurs are accessing from SMT/Kiva lenders. With this loan, they will be able to expand their respective businesses, make more profit and consequently improve their standard of living.  The leader of this group is Seibatu. Seibatu is age 32. She was born in Kailahun Town in eastern Sierra Leone. She is currently residing in Kenema City, together with her husband and two children. Her husband is a businessman. One of her children is attending primary school and the other one is not of school-going age. For many years now, Seibatu has been selling fish. With this loan, she will buy a large quantity of fish to add to her business.

name: Samaila
description: Samaila is a maize farmer and Babban Gona member. Anticipating a good harvest this season, Samaila has the opportunity to attain yields of up to 8 metric tonnes of maize per hectare of land, 5.5 times that of the average Nigerian maize farmer. Before joining Babban Gona, Samaila would have had to sell his maize at harvest, a period when maize prices are at their lowest in the market, to meet his immediate cash needs such as food and clothing. Thanks to Babban Gona’s support, Samaila can store his maize and sell it at a future date for up to 37% higher than the market price at harvest. As a Babban Gona member, Samaila will benefit from marketing support that could see him generate earnings of up to $2000 per hectare of land. Samaila is thankful that he now has the opportunity to improve the life of his children and family and looks forward to using his additional earnings to acquire more land to put into the Babban Gona program.

name: Davaatseren
description: Davaatseren is 57 years old and lives with his wife and two children in a small house in the Niseh district of Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. His 43-year-old wife, Zayabat, works at a local hospital as a nurse. One of his children, 18-year-old Temuulen, just enrolled in university, whlie his other child, 12-year-old Tsolmon, attends local school. He has been driving a big truck for 12 years and has become well-known for providing transportation services within the area. He is hardworking, welcoming and communicative. He is requesting 2,500,000 MNT to cover his older child's university tuition fee and other expenses.

name: Rosita
description: Rosita is a 48-year-old married woman with eight children. Two of her children are still in school. For eight years, Rosita has run a fish selling business in the Philippines. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.   Rosita is requesting a 15,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy a variety of fish to sell and supplies needed in her business. In the future, she would like to save enough money to afford to send her children to college.

name: Dúo Raquel De Santiago Group
description: The Raquel De Santiago Dúo is represented by Maria Claret. She is a single mother of two children, one of whom studies. Claret has been working selling daily use products such as the sale of candies, grain sales like beans, corn, pasta and also soft drinks, chicken and sausages for five years. She works out of necessity given her situation, for her children and to be able to have more time with them. She is happy since she started selling with very little capital and now she has much more invested. This is her second loan. Her dream is to leave her children a better life than what she had. She is requesting this loan to buy food products to sell.

name: Quang
description: Quang works in agriculture,  farming poultry and cattle. Quang has been involved in this business for 9 years. Quang is 33 years old and he is married with 1 child. Quang lives with one dependent in Hoang Hoa district, a rural town in Thanh Hoa province.  The main hardship that Quang faces in his life is not having a latrine. He is requesting a loan to purchase sand, cement, bricks and equipment to build a toilet. This is Quang's first loan with Thanh Hoa Fund of Poor Women.  In the future, Quang hopes to build a new house, for his family to be healthy and happy, and to be able to buy more supplies and equipment for his business.

name: Leonida
description: Leoida 42 years old, married and had five children.  She has been engaged in selling mobile auto-loadmax for five years.   With her dedication to increasing her sales, she is applying for a loan of PHP 5,000 to purchase a higher amount of load for mobile phones.   In the future, Leonida hopes that she will build a sari-sari business so that she can meet the needs of her family.

name: Ric Marcial
description: Ric Marcial is 42 years old and lives in Lapasan, Clarin, Misamis Occidental Philippines. He is a married man and a father of two school-age children.  Ric Marcial has a retail store that sells basic food items like, rice, corn, oil, milk and sugar. He has been engaged in this business for more than two years with a monthly income of PHP 10,000. Ric Marcial requested a loan of PHP 20,000 from GDMPC to purchase assorted food products to sell.  Ric Marcial is a new member of GDMPC. In the future, he hopes to expand his business and allow customers to have a greater choice.

name: Fareeda
description: Fareeda  is a 32 year old, divorced woman. She has been in the business of animal purchases and sales for many years. She wants to contribute to the family income as she is living with her parents. Fareeda is motivated to expand her business for a prosperous future. She has requested a loan of 60,000 PKR. She intends to utilize this loan amount  to purchase more baby goats and calves to cater more customers. She is hopeful that her business will generate greater revenue in the future.

name: Ellen
description: Ellen is 42 years old and lives in Tukuran, Molave, Zamboanga del Norte, Philippines. She is married with three children. Her business is an internet cafe, and she serves those students who does not have their own computer for their paper work like  encoding, printing and research. She has had this business for 10 years with a monthly income of Php 15,000 which she has used for the studies of her three children.  Ellen requested a loan to buy another computer to meet the demand of her clients. She has been a member of PMPC for four years. In the future, Ellen hopes that God will bless her business so that her children can finish their studies.

name: Moises
description: Moises is a single, 22 year old youth who has no children. His business is making hand-make shoes. He is intelligent, enterprising and very hard-working. He does his business in the ‘Aurelia’ neighborhood an area that borders the rural and the city. Moises is dark-skinned, short and thin. His native language is Aymará and he speaks Spanish. His business is making traditional cholito (native) shoes which are characterized by a low heel and are strongly influenced by fashion. The people that use them are women who wear traditional clothing (hats, shawls and skirts) and they are also used for traditional dancing that use all traditional attire. "My father taught taught me the trade and I became independent and need machines in order to continue" he commented. The advantage of his business is that it has continual sales, his disadvantage is the lack of capital to buy a straight stitch sewing machine and pay for the cost to expand his workshop. His dream is to stabilize his business. This is his first loan with the institution in the two years he has run his business. For these reasons Moises is requesting a loan to buy a straight stitch sewing machine and pay for the cost of expanding his workshop.

name: Eliana
description: The borrower is still working in the business of selling ceviche, and has been in this business for some time and it’s going well thanks to the effort she puts in each day to her business. She is a street vendor and sells to all her customers that look for her. She wants to continue working in this way so she can continue supporting her family.  She is asking for a loan in order to purchase supplies such as fish, lemons, and more.  She is grateful to have a loan granted and she promises to complete her payments as established.

name: Divina
description: Divina is thirty-nine years old. She is a single lady residing in Pallua with her parents. To generate income, she raise hogs and sells them to butchers upon achieving the desired size. From this, she is able to gain PHP 3,000 from each hog she sells.   She is now borrowing PHP 7,000 to buy piglets, feeds and medicines to attain good growth. This will help increase her net income and will allow her to save funds to use in times of emergencies.

name: Amneh
description: Amenah is a 55-year-old married woman who has one family member from Madaba, Jordan. She is requesting a loan of 300 JOD to pay for her home improvements. She would like to repaint her home and to do maintenance on the home. In the future, she hopes to buy a new furniture.

name: Mary's Group
description: Mary, pictured above, has been a farmer for 10 years, and is now proud to represent her group of 15 farmers in Kakamega South District. She is 41 years old, is married and has five children.  Mary likes to think of herself as a very hardworking individual. She has been working alongside One Acre Fund since 2012 and decided to represent her group because she wanted to help more farmers. She says that being part of the One Acre Fund community has meant that she has been able to consistently feed her family. Mary plans to use the profits from this coming season to send her children to school.  In total, Mary’s Group will receive inputs to cultivate nine acres of land.

name: Janet Norma
description: Janet is a young woman 24 years old.  She's married and with her husband has a young child, age 2, whom she loves a lot.  Above all, he's her reason for living and her goal for getting ahead every day to be able to give him a decent live with a lot of love.  Janet is very hardworking, and with a lot of effort she managed to start her business selling clothing three years ago.  She can serve up to 15 customers a day, and with the fruit of her work she can help her husband with the household expenses and be able to get her young child ahead.  She believes it's going well for her in her business because she's very friendly with the customers and especially because she has a great desire to get ahead.  Janet is very grateful to the Kiva lenders because thanks to their help she'll be able to buy merchandise for her business, such as jeans, track suits, shirts, and t-shirts, among other things.  This way she'll be able to have a greater variety of products and improve her income, which will allow her to continue to fight every day to make her biggest dream come true: "To give her son a good education and to be able to give him a better quality of life."

name: Sonik
description: Sonik lives in Goris town with her mother-in-law and husband. Her husband provides a vehicle repair service in their village, and Sonik herself is involved in pig breeding. She keeps a mother pig and six piglets. The family's living mostly depends on agricultural income, therefore it is very important for Sonik to successfully keep her livestock.  Sonik has now asked for this loan of 3,000 USD to be able to purchase six more pigs and thereby enlarge her livestock. As Sonik does not have enough land to cultivate forage for her livestock, she has to purchase forage, for which she also needs sufficient funds. This loan will be a huge support for this hard working farmer and she hopes for your support.

name: C1241 Abakundumurimo Group
description: Leopold is 49 years old and is married with seven children who are between 6 and 25 years old. He is the leader of this group called Abakundumurimo which is well-known in the business of selling drinks made from sorghum. Leopold and his team have been in this business for about one year.  Leopold and his team need to request a Kiva loan via Vision Finance Company to purchase a large quantity of sorghum. This will enable them to start wholesaling to the retailers in their business area and, in addition to that, increase the quantity of drinks for sale.  If successful, they will keep reinvesting in their business for better financial stability.

name: Gina
description: Gina sends you her thanks for your generosity because her previous loan enriched her business. She was able to buy additional gallons and supplies needed in her water distribution business. The loan also helped her provide for their daily needs and expenditures of her family.  She is very positive that she could improve her business if you will help her borrow an amount of 15,000 PHP.  This new loan will go to additional supplies of gallons for mineral water to increase her profits. An increase in profits will also result in her business becoming viable and sustainable. Simultaneously, she could sustain the needs of her family.  Aside from water distribution, Gina also offers rooms for rent for additional income.  She knows that all her hard work in business will pay off someday. She meets every week with her *co-fellowship members to share stories of her work and to also draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  *All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Enedina
description: Enedina, 36, lives in her own house with her husband, Carlos, 42, and their four children who she wants to provide a better quality of life for.  She is a very hardworking woman.  She sells groceries in a stand she set up at home.  Her husband helps her working in the fields; he grows cocoa beans and coffee.  Profits from both activities generate good support to improve their quality of life.  What she likes best about her work is that she can have peace of mind because she can take care of her children.  This is her 4th MFP loan and she feels happy because of the help provided.  She commits to be punctual and to make her installment payments in a responsible way.  She will use the requested 4000 new soles to stock her store with groceries.  She’ll also buy fertilizer and manure for her parcel of farmland.

name: Swaleh
description: Swaleh is a married man with six school-going children. He lives in his own house that has electricity but has no piped water.  He has operated a retail shop business for the past three years, selling household consumables like wheat flour, maize flour and sugar.   With the loan he is requesting, he wants to purchase stocks of sugar, rice, maize flour, soap, tea leaves and wheat flour for resale. He decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost his business

name: Jocelyn
description: Jocelyn  N. is a married woman who lives in Purok Punta Tundo, Brgy. Pilar, Hinigaran, Negros Occidental. She earns her living by operating two business ventures:  Fishing and Pig Fattening businesses. Her husband Reymondo N., who is 47 years old, works as a fisherman to earn his living, and also helps in his wife's business activities.  They have four children who are between 2 and  13 years old.   Jocelyn  joined NWTF-Project Dungganon in 2006 because she aspired for something better for her family. With the help of her past 17 loans from NWTF-Project Dungganon, Jocelyn  has been incrementally lifting her family out of poverty by the sweat of her brow. Her previous loan of PHP 8000 helped her earn a monthly profit of PHP 10,000, uplifting the family's standard of living.  This time, for her 18th loan, she is borrowing PHP 19,000, which she intends to use to buy fishing gear  so that she can continue to save up for the future and for the education of her children.   Jocelyn  N. is a Dungganon woman who is following an honorable path toward the achievement of her dreams.   About NWTF:   In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means Honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress from earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem that is bestowed on a member of a community who has earned the respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work. Help NWTF continue its mission to help the poorest in the Philippines by clicking  the link to the   NWTF Kiva lending team  on Kiva.org to join our team.

name: Angel
description: Angel, a 66 year old widow from Tudela, a father of eight children. He hopes to have his finances supported so that he can renovate his house for a comfortable home he and his family can live in.

name: Talaave
description: Talaave is a 36-year-old married woman with 3 children. She runs a small crafts business in her community. She has been doing this for 7 years.   Talaave needs a loan to buy pandunus leaves, varnish, brushes, wood paint, wood glue, and a carving kit. In the future, Talaave hopes to pay for her family's weekly expenses.   She joined SPBD in 2008 to gain access to financial services.

name: José Ramón
description: Señor S. has worked as a plumber for ENACAL in Masaya for three years. He is married, and his family consists of himself, his wife, and their two children.  He currently wishes to make some improvements to his home so he visited the offices of Kiva partner CEPRODEL to ask for a loan so he can provide a decent home for his family to live in.

name: Phourn
description: Phourn S., 31, sells Chinese noodles, earning an income of $20 per day. S. is married and resides with her husband and two children in Siem Reap Province, Cambodia, an area known for the Angkor Wat Temple.   The family has to spend $40 on food, $10 on electricity supply and $70 on other necessary expenses every month. Her husband is a carpenter, earning an income of $17 per day.   S. is requesting a loan of $1,000 to purchase more materials to improve her husband's carpentry business. In the future, she would like to use any additional profit to repair her house. This is her first loan from CREDIT, a long-standing Kiva partner in Cambodia.

name: Anjali
description: Anjali is a 34-year-old widow living with her two daughters aged 16 and 15 years  and two sons aged 14 and 12 years. All her children are schooling. She is engaged in the activity of selling fresh and dried fish in the market and earns 2,000 INR per month. She buys fish directly from the local fishermen and sells some of them fresh and dries some of them to sell as dried fish. She sells 10 to 12 kg of fresh fish and 18-20 kg of dry fish by roaming door to door in the nearby villages.  She wants to establish a shop where she can sit and sell fish. She says that doing so she would be able to give time to her children and properly manage her family.  She has applied for a loan amount of 20,000 INR for setting up a shop and for purchasing more fish. She has a dream: to provide the best possible facilities to her children and give them a good education.

name: Leonora
description: Leonora has a collection of ornamental garden plants. She finds pleasure in doing her gardening activities and earning as well for her family. As a microfinance member of Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative, she sought financial help to purchase a variety of ornamental plants that she can grow and sell. In the future, Leonora wishes to become the supplier of flowers for neighboring towns.

name: Nasreen
description: Nasreen is 43 years old. She lives with her spouse and children in the area of Lahore, Pakistan.   Nasreen's husband owns a scrap shop in which he sells damaged and useless scrap material such as plastic, iron goods and aluminum accessories. He purchases scrap from persons who live in the locality and sells it to recycling factories. He has been doing this same business for many years and earning a reasonable profit for his family.   Due to a rapid increase in household expenses and in family needs, Nasreen's husband wants to increase his scrap purchases capacity.  Therefore, Nasreen requested a loan so that her husband can buy more scrap goods and increase his income. Nasreen hopes that this loan will enhance her husband's purchasing capacity so that he can save more than he previously did.    Nasreen seems very glad after taking this loan and says thank to Kiva and to its field partner BRAC Pakistan.

name: Mathew
description: Mathew is a Babban Gona maize farmer. Thanks to Babban Gona’s support, Mathew is thankful that days of poor yields are long gone. As a Babban Gona member, he has the opportunity to achieve yields of up to 8 metric tonnes of maize per hectare of land, 5.5 times the yield of the average Nigerian farmer. Traditionally, Mathew would have had to sell his maize for low prices at harvest to meet his immediate cash needs such as food and clothing. With Babban Gona’s support, Mathew will store the maize he harvests and delay its sale until a date later in the season when he can obtain a significantly higher price for his maize at a premium up to 37% more than the harvest price. With the opportunity to earn up to $2000 per hectare of land, Mathew now has the opportunity to actualize his dream of growing his agriculture business for himself and family members and would like to use this additional income to ensure that all his children get a postsecondary education.

name: Chantha Group
description: Chantha is a 43-year-old married mother with four dependent children. She lives in the province of Takeo, Cambodia. Chantha has cultivated rice and fattened animals since 1996. Her husband is a 47-year-old sharecropper. One of her children is a construction worker, while her other three children are schoolchildren. Together, they can makes around $13 each day. Chantha is shown first from the right. As the group leader, she would like to request a loan for a group of three members and she will use her share to purchase zinc sheets to roof her house. This loan will help her and her family have enough money to build a new house. In the future, she wants to enlarge her farming, save money to build a new house, and support her children to earn higher education.

name: Susan
description: As a single parent of two children, Susan works hard to support her family.She has a buy-and-sell bananas business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from motorcycle transportation. Susan is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to buy more banana fruits to sell in her food stall for her banana business.Susan has been sustaining her business activities through her past one loan from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Ernesto
description: Married, is 47 years old. He is from the Huasteca region, where cheeses are very popular.  When he arrived to Mante and observed that they are not sold much there he decided to start her cheese business and in the future will also sell perfumes as they are requested a lot.   He is requesting the support for a refrigerator to keep his cheeses to prevent them from going bad.  It has gone well for him and almost everything that he sells is by special order.  His desire to work has made him very well-known in the area where he lives.  There is a great demand for cheese, but he does not have anywhere to keep it.  In terms of the perfumes, it was an extra that has been selling very well.  Translated from Spanish by Aimee Sostowski, Kiva Volunteer

name: Doung
description: Mrs. Doung S. is 39 years old and has been selling fresh fish in the busy local market for more than sixteen years. She sells fish that she gets from her husband’s fishing or buys from her wholesale supplier and other fishermen. She is married to Soun Sophan, 43, who fishes in and around the lakes of his community. The couple has seven children; five of whom attend school, while the remaining two help in their parent's business. They reside in a wooden house located along the river.   Currently, the quantity of fish caught is declining due to their lack of fishing gear. That is why Doung S. has requested a loan in order to purchase more equipment for her husband to use when fishing.

name: Nusrat
description: Nusrat is a 54-year-old woman. She lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, with her four sons and one daughter. Her elder son has been running his own business of clothes selling for three years; her son is solely responsible to feed the entire family and manage the household. Her elder son needs to purchase different types of clothes in bulk for reselling purposes, but due to insufficient financial means, her son is unable to purchase these clothes. Therefore, Nusrat is applying for a Kiva loan from its field partner BRAC Pakistan so that she can assist her son to purchase these clothes in bulk for his business. Her son can also increase the size of his business and earn maximum profit with the help of this loan amount. Nusrat is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Heang's Group
description: A villager in the Battambang province of the Thmor Koul district, Heang, is aged 56 years and married with five children, one of whom is dependant on her.  Fishing is the main source of income.  After this business, she is works in a paid job. She has been working in this business for twenty years and earns 40,000 KHR per day.   This is her second loan with VisionFund, and the first loan has helped her family to have sufficient food. She is now leading her group to suggest a loan 400,000 KHR each. She, as a group leader, will use her loan portion to renovate a house. She hopes her family will have a better living.

name: Maimouna's Group
description: Maimouna, who is wearing a blue scarf over her pagne in the photo, is a member of a group of six farmers who live and work in Toba, in Mali. Maimouna, who is 30, lives in a family of 30 people of whom seven children. Five of them attend school. She decided to become a farmer to guarantee food self-sufficiency for the family, but has to cope with difficulties such as lacking quality fertilizer, and access to the market. She decided to register with myAgro for their payment system and to obtain better production. For her second year with myAgro, Maimouna bought fertilizer for growing peanut and okra for her field of 1/8 hectare. Through this purchase, Maimouna hopes to be able to increase her production so she can start livestock farming (sheep), and ensure food self-sufficiency.

name: Ara
description: Ara has been involved in cheese production for 6 years. He started the production in a small garage and then was able to expand and improve working space.Ara is the only breadwinner in his family of four: he lives with his mother, wife and two children. He applied for this loan to purchase raw materials (milk and dairy produce) for producing smoked cheese. Ara purchased new equipment and started specializing in smoked cheese production. Ara greatly hopes for lenders' support.

name: Vilma
description: This partner, Vilma, is 51 years old and is married. She alternates her daily work with a shoe store business and the sale of beauty products. The partner sells her merchandise to her customers who request it from her like friends and family, among others. The partner has made a living from her business for a long time and it does well thanks to the efforts that she puts into her business every day.  The partner would like to be able to keep working so that in this way she continues supporting her family.   She asks for a loan for the purchase of perfumes for women.  The partner feels grateful for the granted loan, and promises to meet the payments.

name: Luz De Luna Brillante Group
description: The “Luz de Luna Brillante” (Light of the Shining Moon) communal bank will start their second cycle with Pro Mujer as part of the Collpani regional office.  It is comprised of 11 members, and it is directed by a board of directors, which is headed by Alicia.  The businesses that the members of the communal bank carry out are varied such as selling pots, neighborhood store, selling jeans, making rubber sandals, electrician, selling food, making cherry treats and chutney, and selling sweets.  Alicia says that she has worked with Pro Mujer for over five years.  She became a member of the institution by invitation from a friend.  She currently has a business selling sweets, which she has been doing for years.  The loan that she will now take out is to increase her capital (to buy sweets).  She will buy the sweets in La Ceja, and later she will sell them at her stand.  This way of working allows her to generate resources to support her family.  She has three children and a life partner.  When asked what she likes about Pro Mujer she answered that she likes the saving.

name: Yeat
description: Yeat is married to Rom and has two children; they are school-aged. Presently, she is a vegetable seller in a market far away from her house, located in Siem Reap Province of Cambodia. Her good relationships and good characteristics make her sell better than others. As her sales increase, it generates more income for her. With her husband’s help, they’re all getting ahead in life.   She says that her work requires lots of effort and she does it all so that she can provide a better future for her children and so that they don’t have to face the same challenges that she did.   She is asking for a loan from Kiva in order to purchase a motorbike for transporting vegetables, which will help her meet her customer’s demand in a timely manner. She is grateful to the foundation for the opportunity it provides her.

name: Martha
description: This is Martha from Liberia.  She lives in Paynesville North, which is a suburb of the capital city of Monrovia.  Paynesville North has the largest market in Montserrado County.  The area is home to “round time marketers”, traders that travel to the interior to purchase various goods to sell throughout the county. As a result, there is a high concentration of wholesalers in the area who distribute to various markets around Montserrado County, including Monrovia.  She is 39, and single with two children.  Her children ages are 12 and 7. They are currently living at home and are in school.    Martha owns her own shop selling beer, Guinness, soft drinks, etc., for the past two years. She will use the loan proceeds to purchase more drinks for her business.    On average, she works from  7 am to 8 pm at her business. She started her business with help from her fiancee. She transports her merchandise by taxi. She cites lack of inventory as her biggest challenge. Her favorite part of her business is the flow of customers.  In the future, she would like to build a modern house.    She is grateful for your support!

name: Teresa
description: For 12 years in Pandahan, SND, Teresa, a 43-year-old married mother of six, has made a living through the operation of a general store selling a variety of food and home-use products. She earns 5,000 PHP a month from these activities.  In 2011, Teresa joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her business and living situation. She is now requesting a loan of 7,000 PHP to purchase new items such as candies, Milo (a malted chocolate beverage), shampoo, soaps, etc. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the loan as a reserve for future emergencies.

name: Taraji
description: Taraji is a young Palestinian woman, 30 years old. She is married with four children who are still at school.  Taraji started her business two years ago with the help of her husband to increase their income. Her husband works as a police officer and his salary is not enough for a family of six members, especially when everything in Gaza is getting more expensive due to the constraints. In addition, the family went through a tough time when the government salaries were stopped for more than a year in 2006/2007 when the USA and the EU stopped their support of the Palestinian National Authority after the 2006 election.  Taraji and her husband buy lambs, raise them, and then sell them to butcher shops. Taraji has requested 1,000 USD from FATEN to buy more lambs. In addition to that they plan to start their own butcher shop as the profit will be even greater.  Taraji appears in the photo with her husband at the barn carrying one of the lambs.

name: Siti
description: Hello, lenders! Meet Siti. She is a housewife who runs a micro-business by selling mobile phone air-time credits and utility bill payments. Siti is happily married, and she and her husband have been blessed with two beautiful daughters: one is five years old; the other is one year old. They live in Bekasi, the satellite city located to the east of Jakarta.   About one and a half years ago, Siti decided to join Ruma. She was excited about becoming a Ruma agent because she wanted to start a business and learn about mobile phone technology. Siti is hoping to get a working capital loan from Kiva to help the business to continue to operate. She will use the capital to process more mobile air-time credits and utility bill payment transactions, especially on the weekends.   In the photo, Siti is the one who is looking at us: she was serving her customer when the photo was taken. She thanks you for your support.

name: Idja Group
description: Bernadette is the head of the group. She is married and mother to seven children, of whom six are in school. Bernadette's group is on its fifth loan with ACFIME and all previous repayments have been made on time.  This courageous woman has been selling cereals for eight years. She requires this loan to buy two bags of rice, millet, maize, beans etc. To allow her business to progress, Bernadette is very welcoming and respectful towards her clients. She also offers good quality products.   After making the sales, Bernadette's profits will allow her to continue running the business and pay for her family's expenses.

name: Mtumwa's Mnyonge Hanuni Group
description: Mtumwa, 24 years old and married with one child aged two, has been a clothng and shoe seller since March of this year. She works everyday day at her business and can earn a monthly profit of about $67 from her sales.   Mtumwa  is now requesting a loan to buy more clothes and shoes for her business. She will share this loan with her subgroup members, who won a salon and a food vending business respectively.

name: Lolita
description: Lolita is 63 years old and lives in Tabo-o, Jimenez, Misamis Occidental. She is widowed with four children who are now adults. Lolita is engaged in fishing activity particularly operating a fishing boat. Lolita earns approximately PHP 3,000 each month doing this type of business activity in which the said amount is so helpful to meet her needs.   She has requested a loan to be used in purchasing additional fishing nets and other fishing equipment. Lolita has been a member of PMPC for 14 years. In the future, Lolita hopes to expand her business.

name: Filemu
description: Filemu is 51 years old. She runs a small business selling ice cake in her community to earn a living. She has been doing this for more than a year.Filemu requested for a loan to buy a sack of sugar, plastic bags, ice bag and coolio to help her run the business.She will expand her business using her profit. She became a member of SPBD in 2014.

name: Trust We Group
description: These are a group of local entrepreneurs in the small town of Waterloo near Freetown. They named their group 'Trust We' and made Mamusu B. (in the middle of the photo) the leader of the group. These entrepreneurs have applied for a loan of SLL 1,500,000 (or SLL 500,000 each) from SMT, a partner of 'Shine on Sierra Leone' in Waterloo. With a loan at their disposal, they can expand their businesses by adding more goods. Consequently, sales and sales-to-profit margins will increase for these entrepreneurs. They will thus be able to better support their children in terms of feeding, clothing and in paying their school fees and other school related expenses.   Mamusu was born in Kambia, in northern Sierra Leone. Mamusu is divorced with two children. One of her children is in Junior Secondary School III and the other is in Primary School V. Since 2000, Mamusu has been selling fried meat, fried chicken, roasted fish and bread. Mamusu wants this loan in order to buy in larger quantity the materials she needs in preparing the meat, fish and chickens she sells – condiments, gallons of oil, charcoal, and so on.

name: Afouchata
description: Mrs. Afouchata was born around 1967 in Zisilo C/Sikasso. She is the married mother of seven children, and lives with her husband and their children in a traditional family in Sanoubougou II, a populous area of the city of Sikasso, in the third administrative region of the Republic of Mali.   After conducting a lot of unsuccessful activities, this courageous woman began retailing yams, vegetables, and okra. She resupplies at the main market.  To satisfy the needs of an increasing number of customers, she is requesting an eleventh individual commercial loan from the Soro Yiriwaso micro-finance institution. All previous loans have been fully repaid.   This loan will enable her to buy 5 bags of yams, 6 bags of vegetables, 8 bags of dried okra, for retail sales at the market, to a clientele composed of men and women, for cash and on credit.  She hopes to attain average monthly profits of 72,000 CFA francs, which will enable her to pay off the loan and its interest, and put the remainder into savings.

name: Florence
description: Florence is a hard-working woman who lives in the coastal region of Kenya. She is married with four children, none in school. She lives in her own house that has both electricity and piped water. She operates a taxi business in the coastal region, carrying her passengers from one place to another. She is requesting a loan to purchase spare parts for her three-wheeled taxi. She joined Yehu to boast her business.

name: Nabonswende De Bingo Group
description: Augustin is the representative of the Nabonswende de Bingo group. He is married and the father of one child, who is 18 months old and does not attend school.  Augustin has been a farmer and sold cereals for more than 40 years. He stocks up in the market of his village. He wants to purchase 3 bags of millet and 1 bag of corn. With his earnings, he would like to help his family prosper.  Augustin's dream is to become a big farmer.

name: Maria
description: María, a member of the Virgen del Rosario community bank, lives in the village of La Libertad, in the province and district of Bellavista, in San Martín region. She deals in soft drinks and food, and her business is located in her home in Porvenir, on lot 7, block C.    María began her business because she needed to generate income in order to cover her children’s expenses, especially all the school expenses. With this six-month $375 loan (1,100 nuevos soles), she will buy bottled water, various brands of soft drinks in individual, medium and family sizes, as well as ingredients for preparing the dishes she serves to her customers.    María is 41 years old, and lives with her husband and one of their two children.  She is a very diligent and responsible woman, who wants both her children and her business to prosper.  In the future, she would like to refurbish her eatery to make a good impression and raise its prestige in the community.    Translated from Spanish by Joyce ., Kiva Volunteer

name: Arlene
description: Arlene, age 40, is married with two children. She is from Jimenez, Misamis Occidental. Arlene manages a retail store for a living. The work gives her a total monthly income of PHP 7,000. In 2012, she joined GDMPC. She has requested a loan of PHP 8,000 from the cooperative to purchase additional products like canned goods, noodles, sugar and coffee. She hopes to spare a portion of her earnings for maintenance costs and to expand her current business.

name: Trinidad
description: This is Trinidad. She previously took out a 15,000 PHP loan that she used to buy groceries, toiletries, and beverages to expand her product inventory. She expects a boost in her income as she expands her business. Her earnings were a big help for her personal, household, and business expenditures.   She would like to apply for another 20,000 PHP loan to buy groceries, toiletries, beverages, and other products to add to her inventory. The more items displayed at the store, the better. Having more items to sell will result in a better profit. The profits from her business will definitely help her to sustain her daily needs and pay for her children's educational expenses. She looks forward to this financial increase with happiness and thankfulness in her heart.   Trinidad hopes to be able to expand soon, just as she dreams of being able to give her children a high-quality education through all of her hard work on her business. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her work every week and draws strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans.

name: Suy
description: Suy K. is 54 years old and lives with his wife in the Takeo province. He is a cow dealer who is able to make a living of US$8 in revenue each day, while his wife is a farmer and makes US$1 per day. This couple lives with one child. Suy K. is asking for a loan of US$500. He needs to purchase cows to resell.

name: Gloria Maria
description: Gloria lives in Santo Domingo de los Tsachilas, a city on the coast with an agreeable climate. It's a very commercial city since it serves as a port and links the coast with the mountains. Gloria is 44 years old and lives alone with her three children after her husband abandoned her some time ago. She works in a restaurant in the mornings helping to cook since she's very experienced in this area.  After 4PM she sells cosmetics and travels throughout her neighborhood visiting all her clients. Gloria does everything she can to help her children move forward and she's had to work very hard through all this time. With the loan from Fundación Alternativa and Kiva, Gloria will buy more cosmetics for her business because she wants to increase her sales this month since it's a good one for business in general. She's very grateful to the institution and Kiva because with this loan she'll be able to grow her business and improve her quality of life.

name: Rin
description: A modern wooden house located in Kompong Cham Province belongs to Mrs. C.'s family. C. is 30 years old and a mother who has given birth to two children. The children are still young and are pupils. She is married to Bun Thorn, 30, who is a taxi driver for a company.  C. currently is a domestic produce trader: She always buys produce in bulk from the farmer to store in the family home and then resell to make an income.   C. is requesting a loan of $500 in order to purchase potatos and green beans to sell. The loan will help C.'s family attain a better standard of living.

name: Soei's Group
description: Soei’s Group lives in a rural village in Kompong Thom province in Cambodia. Soei cultivates rice to support her family. In their village, there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Ricardo
description: Ricardo is 34 years old, married and lives with his wife and three children in the district of Olmos, an agricultural area that has a lot of business since it is located in the province of Lambayeque, about and hour and a half from the city of Chiclayo. Ricardo provides transportation in his mototaxi in the route Olmos and its hamlets. He has been doing this work for 8 years and because of it he knows his work to perfection, his main customers are salespeople that wish to transport their merchandize to their stalls, neighbors going to their hamlets and others. Thanks to his work he is able to meet his family’s expenses. Ricardo wants to repair his vehicle so that he can provide good service and have greater income for his family and that they will be able to have better living conditions, which is why he decided to go to Edpyme Alternativa for the first time to get a loan of 1300 nuevos soles.

name: Tatu
description: Tatu is married and has five children, four of whom attend school. She owns a house that has electricity and piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is school fees.  For the past ten years, Tatu has owned real estate houses, renting to tenants. Her major business challenge is delayed payments by clients who take on credit. Tatu dreams of expanding and establishing more real estate houses in the future. Tatu plans to use this KES 25,000 loan to furnish and renovate her rental houses. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Jovita
description: Jovita is a 53-year-old married mother of four children, one still in school. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur.   Jovita has a beauty salon business in the Philippines. Jovita requested a PHP 11,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional materials for her business.  Jovita has been in this business for 18 years. Jovita would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: N'tisse's Group
description: N’Tisse, who is in the center in the photo, holding the myAgro pouch, is a member of a group of 8 farmers signed up with myAgro, all of whom live and work in Sokoro village, southeast of Bamako in Mali. N’Tisse, who is 68 years old, is the father of 13 children aged between 8 and 37, 3 of whom have been to school at this point. His family's tradition in farming, the principal source of revenue and food security for the household, is why he started to farm 22 years ago. N’Tisse grows corn, peanuts, millet, vegetables and cotton on his land, but faces challenges such as lack of rainfall and agricultural materials. N’Tisse is in his second year with myAgro, and signed up for a second year because of the agricultural trainings. Moreover, N’Tisse emphasizes the positive impact myAgro's payment system had on his life as a farmer. This year N’Tisse is making payments to purchase a packet of myAgro hybrid seeds and fertilizer in order to grow corn and increase his yield on his 1-hectare holding. It has now been more than 10 years since N’Tisse started growing corn for its profitability as a cash crop. N’Tisse plans, with the increased yield and revenue, to diversify his crops. In the end he hopes to also pay for his cihldren's weddings.

name: Alicia
description: Alicia is 58 years old and is married with 2 children who have now left home. She works as a street vendor selling ice creams at different schools, squares and football pitches. She lives in the Bajo Llojeta area.   This loan is her fourth cycle within the institution. Alicia will use the loan to buy a cart to sell her ice creams. She's requesting this loan due to her lack of capital and in order to improve the image of her business. Alicia faces the challenge of expanding her business, and she will use the profits to improve the distribution of her products. Her desire is to expand her business much more widely.

name: Rosalinda
description: Rosalinda is 43 years old and married with three children.  She earns a living by farming vegetables in the Philippines. Rosalinda is borrowing PHP 7000 through NWTF to buy fertilizers and other farm supplies.  Rosalinda has been farming vegetables for 20 years and earns additional income from motorcycle transport and pig fattening.  She is working tirelessly towards the attainment of her dream: to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Adjovi
description: This young lady is married and the mother of one child.  She lives in the Adidogomé district of Lomé.  She is an itinerant seller of quality jewelry.  She stocks up in Benin and in Ghana, which are two neighboring countries.  Usually she sell to business women in the private sector, to women civil servants, and to girl students at the University of Lomé, all as her customers.  She's requesting a WAGES loan for new orders of jewelry from Ghana and Benin.  She has been in this business since 2003.Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Ayda
description: Ayda is a 47-year-old widow with four children. She has a small animal fattening project that she started to provide a stable income for her family.   She is requesting a loan of 10,000 EGP to buy a head of cattle to expand her project, and sell the calves and the cheese and butter she creates in the local market.

name: Maria Elena Moyano Group
description: These are 6 responsible women with different commercial activities. All of them live in the district of Agustino. They are the members of the communal group, “María Elena Moyano”. One of them is Carmina. She is 58 years old and a widow with 2 grown children. Carmina has worked for 4 years in the sewing business (overlock), at a small place every morning. Carmina tells us that she has gained her customers' loyalty, which has generated income to cover the household income. In the future, she would like to have her own locale where she can sell the clothing products she makes for women and men, and earn more profits. With the loan, she will invest in buying a sewing machine to have more income. Carmina in the first on on the right, distinguished buy her light pink, short sleeved sweater. She takes her leave with a hug for Kiva and telling you that she will attain all of the goals she has set.

name: Janet
description: Janet is a married woman; she has five children, all of whom attend school. Janet owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.  Janet has operated a charcoal selling business for four years now, selling from home to her neighbours and passersby.
