She faces stiff competition from other firewood operators in her business.   With the Kshs 50,000 she wants to purchase sacks of charcoal for resale. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Ma. Annalie
description: Maria Annalie is 45 years old, married and has eight children.Ma. Annalie is in an agricultural business fattening pigs in the Philippines. She requested an 11,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy feeds and other supplies to raise her pigs.Ma. Annalie has been in this business for 3 years now, and has borrowed 3 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.In the future, she would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Comfort Ngum
description: Comfort is a widow with three children to look after. The death of her husband, who was the sole bread-winner, and the continuous poor health of one of her children, who is a sickle cell patient are her motivations.   Determined to make life still worth living, she took her first loan in 2003. With her previous loans she has succeeded in providing her community with meat and her family with minimal basic needs. She has training in marketing techniques and credit management; experience in the utilization and repayment of previous loans; and available support from group and center members. With a loan of $700, she plans to buy more chicks, feed, and vaccines in order to provide fowls for domestic consumption and celebrations. She also intends to buy available raw food-stuff in bulk and retail.   She plans to repay the loan during the term. The first installment of repayment shall be made on the fourth month from the date of disbursement.

name: Ubale
description: Ubale is a maize farmer and Babban Gona Farmers Organization member. Anticipating a good harvest this season, Ubale has the opportunity to attain yields of up to eight metric tons of maize per hectare of land, 5.5 times that of the average Nigerian maize farmer. Before joining Babban Gona, Ubale would have had to sell his maize at harvest, a period when maize prices are at their lowest in the market, to meet his immediate cash needs, such as food and clothing. Thanks to Babban Gona’s support, Ubale can store his maize and sell it at a future date for up to 37% above the market price at harvest. As a Babban Gona member, Ubale will benefit from marketing support that could see him generate earnings of up to USD 2,000 per hectare of land. Ubale is thankful that he now has the opportunity to improve the life of his children and family and he looks forward to using his additional earnings to provide employment to members of his community, through his farm.

name: Hureltulga
description: Hureltulga is 27 years old and lives with his wife and son in a ger (a Mongolian yurt/ nomadic tent) in Bayanhongor province, Mongolia. His wife helps with his business and his son goes to kindergarten. Hureltulga operates a photography studio. He started his business in 2009. He is very talented for a local photographer, however, his camera is broken, therefore he needs to buy a replacement part. He is a talented young man who says "It has been horrible since my camera got broken and I have to do everything I can to fix this". He is requesting 800,000 MNT to repair some other piece of his reducer machine - copy machine that alters the size of pictures, which is broken.

name: Marites
description: As a married mother of two children, Marites works hard to support her family.  She has a business selling personal care products in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from selling soft drinks. Marites is borrowing PHP 40,000 through NWTF to buy more stocks of personal care products to resell.  Marites has been sustaining her business activities through her past 14 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Evelin Sabrina
description: Evelin is a young, Ecuadorian woman. She is single at the moment, and she doesn't have any children. Thanks to the efforts of her parents, she managed to finish secondary school, but a subsequent lack of economic resources meant that she had to start working from a very young age in order to support herself. Despite having a job that takes up much of her time and effort, she spends a lot of time working in her small business, an internet café and photocopying shop.   Evelin lives with her parents in the centre of Pujilì, which is located in the province of Cotopaxi in the Republic of Ecuador. Pujilì is to the east of the city of Latacunga, and as an area it is famous for its traditions and folklore, and it is known as a centre for music. Its inhabitants perform these activities day to day, and although it is a fair distance from the city, there are families who undertake every kind of activity in order to meet their needs and the needs of the community.   Today, Evelin is asking for a loan in order to buy another photocopier for her business, since her sales have increased. This will help to improve her lifestyle and that of her family. Evelin is grateful to the Fundación Alternativa in Ecuador, and to Kiva for making the growth of her working and personal life possible.

name: Yolanda
description: Yolanda is 46 years old and is a very happy and hard-working woman.  She has one son but she lives alone in the community of Huaracayo.  The years of dedication and service she spent raising her son taught her that there is no better reward in life than seeing your children progress.  Ten years ago, she began to work in agriculture, raising corn and peas.  After growing them, she takes them to the central market in the capital where she sells them wholesale.  Now, she would like to open a small hardware store in the central area of her native city of Tarma, because she understands that she does not have the strength that she used to; she feels alone and wants to be close to her son who lives in the city.  This is her first loan through MFP and she is very happy to belong to a village bank that is very well-respected in her neighborhood.  She knows that with the help of the bank, she will be able to achieve her goal.  With the loan, she will purchase fertilizer and contract workers to help her with the harvest.

name: Monica
description: Monica is a female Kiva borrower. She operates a retail business where she sells drinks, sweets, biscuits and other items. She has been involved in this business for five years. Her business is located in a conducive area and her primary customers are the general public. She describes her biggest business challenge as the lack of enough capital to buy stock. She will use the 70,000 KES loan to buy more stocks of drinks, sweets, and other items.

name: Sally
description: Sally R. is from the village of Nabuna. She is 36 years old, is married, and has four school-aged children.  Sally owns and operates a sari-sari (general) store, selling a variety of different products in the local community. She has been engaged in her business for over four years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month.  In 2008, Sally joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan from PMPC.  Sally is requesting a new loan of 7,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be her 3rd from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand her business.    About PMPC: Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.    *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Juan Bautista
description: Juan, 44, lives in a periurban zone in La Perimetral.  He’s single.  His business is frozen treat sales and cargo hauling with a three wheeled cart.  He started 15 years ago; a friend recommended it to him and he liked the activity because he can travel throughout the city.  He sells from 8am until 6pm going throughout the city.    He wants to use the loan to buy more merchandise for the frozen treats and a new three wheeled cart to be able to work better and increase his profits.  In the future, he’d like to finish building his house because he still needs to plaster and seal.

name: Adama Tiecoura's Group
description: Adama, the second one standing from left to right in the photo wearing a traditional wax outfit and holding a myAgro case, belongs to a group of six farmers who live and work in the village of Saguele in Mali. Adama is  54 years and lives in a family clan of 16 people. He has 11 children ranging from one to 25 years of age, eight of whom are or have been in school. Adama has become a farmer due to family tradition. He has decided to join myAgro because of its system of installment payments.   For his first year with myAgro, Adama has bought a packet of OPV (Open Pollinated Variety) seeds for his field of 0.5 ha [1.2 acres]. Thanks to this purchase, Adama hopes to be able to increase his yield in order to expand his cultivable land, buy farm supplies, pay school fees for his children and ensure food self-sufficiency for his family.

name: Damian
description: Damian, 52 years old, is married and blessed with three children. He's been engaged in a hog-raising business for almost ten years. Due to insufficient funds, he is requesting a loan amounting to PHP 8,000 to buy additional piglets for his hog-raising business. He really loves to raise hogs and wants to earn more income in this business.

name: Mapenzi
description: Mapenzi is a married mother of three children, all of whom attend school. She owns a house that has electricity but not piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are school fees and household consumables.For over five years, she has operated an open air food selling business, selling from home to her neighbors and passersby. She faces a major challenge of seasonality in her place of business. With the KES 20,000, she wants to purchase bundles of wheat flour, maize flour, tea leaves, and cooking fat. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Dominga
description: Dominga is 65 years old and married with three children.    Dominga is in the agricultural business, raising cattle in the Philippines. She requested a 15,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase vitamins and other supplies for her cattle. Dominga has been raising cattle for 8 years now, and has borrowed 10 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Dominga would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Adrian Asuncion
description: Adrian is over 40 years old and lives with his wife and their two children.  For the last 7 hears he has worked repairing and selling tires, a job he does from his home.  His primary customers are people traveling from Honduras to Nicaragua, and vice versa.  He has many customers as his business is located in a very strategic point on the side of the street.Adrian is seeking a loan to buy tires, tubes, wicks, glue, etc., in order to better supply his business, as every day he has many demands from his customers.  He is very content with the support Prisma can provide him.  His dream is to have one of the best tire businesses in the area and to be able to provide a better life to his family.Choluteca, Honduras –  October 2015

name: Awanyo
description: Awanyo is married and has one child. She has never received any formal schooling. Awanyo is a petty trader and also a food vendor at Wegbe, Hohoe, which she has done since 2009. Her husband is a farmer. Awanyo uses her income to help her husband provide with the basic needs of the home. Awanyo will use the loan to purchase bags of rice, maize, gari, and a gallon of oil. With the new profits from her expanded business, Awanyo plans to save for the expansion of her business.

name: Manavi
description: Manavi is 46 years old and lives in Adidogomé. Married, she has one child under her care and she works actively to support her husband with their [family's] development.  Manavi works selling general food products in her shop in order to earn a good profit. She procures her goods three times a month from the Grand Market in Lomé.   She is seeking this loan to buy boxes of fish and trays of tomatoes. Profits will go towards her child's education.

name: Cresencia
description: Crecencia is a member of the Doradinas in Action Community Bank and lives in the San Martín region of Peru. She makes a living selling popsicles, ice creams and snacks, taking advantage of her area's climate with the products she offers. She has a freezer that allows her to store a good amount of treats and she has an employee who sells items at the local schools. With the loan she is requesting, which she plans to repay within four months, she will purchase ingredients to make and serve her treats, such as sugar, little bags and glasses, food dyes and fruits. She plans to make popsicles and snacks like carmels, chocolates, gums and various types of cookies to better supply her business. Crecencia is 59 years old and has seven children, all of whom are grown up and independent. She now lives with her husband and two granddaughters, whom she cares for as if they were her own children. Her goal is to fix up her home so she can put in a convenience store.Translated from Spanish by Marty Greenstein, Kiva Volunteer
town: San José de Sisa - San Martin

name: Ubaldo
description: Ubaldo lives in the state of Campeche, in a very remote community far from the city and from services such as electricity.He is dedicated to cattle. He owns 50 cows and is dedicated to care for them. These cows represent the source of income for Ubaldo and his family and are very important to them.Nowadays, he wants to have a solar fence to take care of his cows because sometimes they run away outside the wood fence, and also some animals can hurt his animals.Also with the system he will be able to illuminate his house and replace the use of candles and ocote, which are very bad for health, especially for the respiratory tract.Thus, In addition to improving his quality of life, he will save approximately $100 MXN per month and will be able to take care of his livestock and make it grow.

name: Tamarisco Group
description: The communal bank Tamarisco is a new group where the members have put their hopes into a committee, which will allow them to grow not only economically, but also as people. More than that they are in the Poverty Stoplight program as a mechanism to help them with various aspects of their lives.  One of the members is Patricia who is at poverty level one, which is to say, that through her effort and ongoing work and the application of the vital behaviors that the foundation wants a successful woman to initiate, she can improve her poverty situation. On top of this she does her work, which is selling clothes, thereby helping her family, and other loved ones.  She is asking for this loan in order to invest in the purchase of some jeans, blouses, and some lingerie items so that she can lower the costs in order to gain a greater profit. She is grateful for this opportunity she is receiving to improve her life.

name: Charles
description: This is 47-year-old Charles. He is married, and has one child, age one. In 2011, Charles began operating a mobile phone shop. He began his business to be self-reliant after coming from the village to Accra. His business is located in the city center and his main customers are everybody. Working seven days a week and twelve hours a day, Charles earns about GHS 120 every month from this business.   Charles would like a loan in the amount of GHS 1,200 to buy a specific phone ordered by a customer. He has already received and successfully repaid three loans and now requires a new loan. He hopes that this loan will help him to increase his stock and to make more profit. In the future, Charles hopes to improve his business and expand to other towns. He started the business hawking around the town and now owns a small shop. He thanks you for your support.

name: Benkadi Group
description: The Benkadi group is made up of ten members; 7 are married women and three are widows. They are all around 46 years old and have six children each. They generally live in polygamous families in Bougoulaba, a village in the Niena municipality in the Sikasso region (the third largest administrative region in the Republic of Mali). They are on their third loan with the Soro Yiriwaso microfinance association, with the aim of better satisfying their customers' demands. They have successfully repaid all of their previous loans. These ladies are led by group leader Korotoumou D. and sell various products, such as shea butter. Korotoumou D. aims to use her loan to purchase 50kg of shea butter which she will source from the Bougoulaba market. She re-sells this butter by retail or wholesale at the Bougoulaba market, to her family members, and to a customer base made up of women and men.  She aims to generate an average monthly wage of 40,000 FCFA which she will use to meet her family's everyday needs. She aims to boost her revenue in order to better meet her customers' demands.

name: Boubacar
description: Boubacar B. sells woodland products such as palm fronds and bamboo which serve to build fences and roofing in touristic sites. Thanks to this business, this father of a family of 7 children, manages to make a living. He is requesting this loan to reinforce his business. Translated from French by Teresa Kramer, Kiva Volunteer

name: Virginia
description: Virginia is 33 years old. She is married with two children. She lives in Alindahaw, Tukuran, Zamboanga del Sur, Philippines. Virginia is a retailer of various ready-made or RTW products like lotion, perfumes and more. Every month she earns PHP 8,000. In 2011, Virginia joined GDMPC. She has applied for a loan of PHP 15,000 to procure more items such as soaps, shampoo, lipstick, etc. She expects to gain more revenue to improve the general living conditions of the family.

name: Joel
description: Joel, aged 36, operates a buy and sell business. He usually sells green peppers, bananas and pechays in the market with the help of his kind wife. They wish for a higher income in order to give a good life to their child.    To earn higher profit, Joel is requesting a loan of PHP 5,000 to purchase more vegetables such as cabbage and eggplant. He hopes his request will be approved in order to have a better quality of income.

name: Maryam
description: Maryam is a 55 year old refugee from the Zangilan region situated in the east part of Azerbaijan, which is now part of the Azerbaijan-Armenian conflict zone.  Right now she lives in Baku with her family of her husband and six children.  She started her business of food stuff trade in 1992, right after being relocated because she had to earn a living for her family as her husband is jobless and it is difficult to find a job.  She rents a small space near the location where she lives.  At the beginning, she applied to Normicro Baku branch and borrowed her first loan to start her small business.  Now she wants to expand her business by buying a better booth or shop.  To do this, she has applied for a loan of $700.

name: Las Triunfadoras Group
description: The 'Las Triunfadoras' committee was created with the idea of all the members helping each other through the work that they carry out as part of the group.  The members are all heads of families who work hard to get ahead and continue making progress.  One of the members of this group is Perla, who sells fruit and vegetables.  She describes herself as a tenacious person who has been able to make progress thanks to all her efforts and hard work.  She is requesting this loan to invest in buying fruit and vegetables so that she can continue working and helping her family.  All of the members of the group are grateful for the opportunity that they are receiving as it will be a great help to them in enabling them to continue working and helping their families.

name: G. S. En Victoria (La Paz Centro) Group
description: The Solidarity Group "En Victoria (La Paz Centro)" is made up of three members who are single mothers with eight minor children who go to school. La Paz Centro is known for its handicrafts and typical food of the region. They are responsible, hard-working women with a desire for self-improvement. Regrettably, they were not able to go to school and were seen as needing to work from an early age to help with costs at home. Currently, they struggle day to day to support their children with a better future and to give them a better quality of life. To meet their dreams and goals, like any other person, they need to make their business grow so that they can give their children an education; physical, economic and emotional stability; and make improvements to their living conditions.Thanks to their desire to be successful, the coordinator is Reyna and she earns a living by producing and selling clay bricks. She has run the business from her home for the last ten years, and she does it with pleasure. The aim of the loan is to invest in raw materials to make the bricks and to give her clients a better service. Solidarity Group En Victoria is grateful for the help that Kiva investors give to people with few resources and poor countries such as Nicaragua so they can have a dignified way of earning a living.

name: Josefina Aurora
description: Josefina is 37 years old. She has been married to Mr. Diego Gil Quiroz for 10 years. They have two daughters who are in school.   Together they make comforters and sheets for beds. They have been manufacturing these for 8 years.   They require the loan to purchase thermal fiber to make the comforters. Winter is approaching and they need to build an inventory of comforters so they can be sold in other cities in the country. The sales increase a lot during winter.     Translated from Spanish by Ellen Donohue, Kiva Volunteer

name: Bushra
description: Ms. Bushra is a 49-year-old lady and enjoys doing work of hand embroidery. She started doing this work with her daughters. Her embroidery patterns are very popular in her territory. Due to an increase in demand of her embroidery designs, she is indulging other women in her business. She has two daughters and one son. She is separated from her husband. She is motivated to provide her family basic necessities of life, including food, clothes, and education.   In order to meet her growing demand of embroidery, Bushra needs to employ some more women. Now she requested a loan of 15,000 Pakistan Rupees (PKR) from Kashf foundation. In this way she can manage to buy more frames, needles, and threads of different colors, which will help in generating more income. She hopes to have a good experience with this new loan.

name: Ninfa
description: As a married parent of seven children, Ninfa works hard to support her family.  She has a rice mill business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from her general store. Ninfa is borrowing 29,000 PHP through NWTF to purchase spare parts for the maintenance of her rice mill business.  She successfully repaid her previous loan and has now requested another loan to further build her business.  Ninfa has been sustaining her business activities through her past 16 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Lourdes
description: Rice farming is the main source of income for Lourdes, 49.  She is also involved in her businesses of quail raising and canteen vending. She has 100 quail and sells their eggs at her canteen. She supports her 9-year old child.  Lourdes joined Community Economic Ventures, Inc. to get a loan with low interest to finance her businesses.  She’s requesting 15,000 PHP to buy farm necessities so she can sustain her family.

name: Uranbileg
description: Uranbileg is 40 years old and lives with her husband and two children in a house in the Uvurhangai province of Mongolia. Her younger son goes to secondary school while her husband works as a carpenter. She manages a wooden product making business with family help. She started her business in 2002 and has gained much experience. During summer her older son, her husband and Uranbileg work as interior decorators and during winter they make their wooden products such as chairs, tables and hangers. With their earnings they are planning to build a winter house for family use. They are all very diligent and hardworking people who are going to continue and expand their business. She says, "We are planning to complete construction work of our winter house in August." She is requesting a 3,000,000 MNT loan to purchase wood for her business.

name: Selvina
description: Selvina is a married woman with two children, 1 girl in secondary school and 1 boy in primary school. Her husband is employed. She sells charcoal to her neighbors and passersby.  Selvina has been running the business for five years and before she was unemployed. With the KES 80,000 loan, she wants to add more stock of charcoal and start selling coconuts at a wholesale price.  Her main business challenge is coping with harassment from the tax collectors. She would like to build her own house in future as she currently lives in a rented home with electricity but no piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are school fees and food. She decided to join Yehu so as to access loans for her business and to improve her living standards.

name: Honorine
description: Born in 1961 in Abomey Calavi in Benin, Honorine H. lived her past 17 years in Cocotomey, in the Abomey Calavi commune. Married to Joachim ADANHOUNDE, she is the mother of three children, all having attended (or still attending) school. She lives with her children and her husband. The couple jointly shares family expenses.  Honorine has not attended school; for the past ten years she has been an itinerant vendor selling pieces of fabric, which allows her to meet her needs and those of her children. She buys her products in Dantokpa, Benin’s international market, and also in Lomé, Togo.  Honorine has already been granted one loan from ALIDé, which was repaid in full. She is considering the increase of her stock supply in response to strong customer demand. She is therefore requesting a second laon from ALIDé to reinforce her working capital. Honorine’s ambition for the future is to open a shop where she can display and sell her fabrics. Translated from French by René McConnell, Kiva Volunteer

name: Tujumuike Group
description: MOHAMEDI, who is in his early 20s, is married. For six years now, MOHAMEDI has been running a clothes business selling second hand clothes. He works from 6 am to 6 pm each working day and is able to make a good return per month. From Tujijenge Tanzania, this is MOHAMEDI's third loan request, which he will use to purchase more clothes to resell. With the previous loans, all of which he paid back successfully, he managed to improve his business by purchasing more clothes. His business profit, used to cover his home expenses, bought land. He used part of his profit to cover his marriage expenses. MOHAMEDI dreams that one day he will be able to own a big business and build a house. He will share this loan with his loan group "Tujumuike", which consist of nine members. The members of the group will hold each other accountable for paying back the loan.

name: Rosa Natividad
description: Rosa is a 46-year-old woman, she was born in the small town of Loja where she finished secondary school and then got married to Jesús who is 59 years old and is a farmer. They have two children who are still studying. Rosa currently lives with her husband and children in the Abrahan Calazacón parish in Santo Domingo, the main city of the Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas province, an area which has very strong commerce as it has become a terrestrial port for trade between the mountains and the coast in Ecuador. In addition, domestic and foreign tourists have strengthened the activities of the entrepreneurs who set up their business around the city several years ago. This city is the third most populated in the region and it also contributes to activities such as agriculture, cattle rearing, fishery and manufacturing.  For the last four years, Rosa has been making her living in agriculture. She learnt this honorable trade from her parents who were also farmers. She spends a lot of her time in the mornings and the afternoons alternating between the household chores. She is always caring for her crops, watering, cleaning, harvesting and sowing in order to offer the goods to her customers at good prices.  The biggest obstacle that Rosa has faced is the difficulty in authenticating the land in which she works. However, she has continued to work hard to support the household and support her children's education. Rosa has been a customer of the Fundación Alternativa for four years and she has had a lot of openings with the 3 loans she has taken out. Rosa is very satisfied with the agility and support given to micro-entrepreneurs in the rural sector, as it is only in this manner that she has been able to keep the farm and her crops in such good condition.  Rosa now needs a loan which she will use to repair the internal and external infrastructure of her home and also buy fertilizers for the upkeep of her crops. Rosa thanks everyone who has been financing her growth on a personal and work front via Kiva. She will always work to achieve her dream and that of her husband – to see their children become upstanding professionals.

name: Juana Maria
description: Juana is the coordinator of the group “El Castillo” (“The Castle”).  She started the business because of necessity, given that she was a single mother and the only means of support for her two children.  For this reason, she decided to work for herself.  She started a little more than five years ago helping an acquaintance with food sales, and she now has her own enterprise.      Blanca started in business to help her husband support their household expenses, since his wages were not enough to cover them.  She started six years ago selling second-hand clothing only to acquaintances but, over time, she has increased her customer base and therefore her sales and orders.      Rosa started in business to get ahead, given that her husband’s earnings were not enough to cover their household and child-related expenses.  She started three years ago selling clothing on order, giving small demonstrations at the houses of friends and neighbors or door-to-door.  Now, she has established herself in several of the markets and has increased her sales.      These women need a loan of $1,125.00 USD, to be repaid over six months, in order to purchase raw materials and merchandise so they can continue with their endeavors.  With your help, they will get ahead!!      Translated from Spanish by Mary Lynn Malaby, Kiva Volunteer

name: Velda
description: Velda, 35, is a good, kind, very hardworking woman.  She and her spouse have two children who are 9 and 6 years old.  They live together in their own house where her parents and grandfather also live and who she and her spouse care for providing necessary comforts so that they can have a good lifestyle.  She works selling food.  She heads out to the market very early to look for the best vegetables and the freshest meat returning home to start preparing her delicious plates of food that she’ll sell in the afternoon in a space she has set up in front of her house.  She’s been in this business three years and is very happy to have many customers who feel good with her and go daily in search of good service and excellent tasting food.  She likes her work because she can have time to do her household things and because she earns good income.  Although it was difficult at first to acquire customers based on effort and much sacrifice added to the good service and tasty dishes, she eventually succeeded.  For later on, she hopes to expand the variety of her dishes but to do so needs help for the investment.  This is her 3rd MFP loan and she’s very happy to know that she’ll have financial support because she will feel surer of advancing with her business and be able to continue growing.  On the other hand, she commits to continue being a responsible member like she was with the previous loan.  She also mentions that she’s very happy to work in the communal bank she belongs to because all are good and above all very mutually supportive.  She will use the 1500 soles requested to buy an industrial stove and some utensils to continue with her work as well as some ingredients and supplies needed for her exquisite dishes of food.

name: Amina
description: Amina is a married woman with three children, all of whom attend school. She owns a house that has electricity and piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is school fees.   She has operated a poultry business for the past two years, selling from home to her neighbors and passersby. Amina faces a major challenge of seasonality in her business. She hopes to expand into a wholesale business in the future.   With the Kshs 50,000 she wants to purchase chicks and chicken feed. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to expand her business.

name: Akouavi
description: Akouavi is a 38-year old married woman and the mother of three. Akouavi lives and works in Agoe. She sells staple food items in order to make a living and help her family. Akouavi stocks up twice a month at the market. Akouavi is requesting this loan to buy some jugs of oil and bags of sugar so as to earn a revenue allowing her to help her husband support their family and provide a good education to their children.

name: Felipe
description: Felipe, 54, is married to Amelia, also 54.  They live together in their own home with their three children and a 7-year-old grandson.    He is a man who feels that he has reached his goals in life; what makes him most happy, however, is knowing that his children are happy.  He has been a farmer for the last 25 years.  He has a 20-hectare lot, 12 of which are planted.  He also has two grocery stores and a locksmith shop where he repairs door locks and makes metal window grilles.  Sometimes he works his fields alone.   But when it’s time to clear, clean and harvest the fields he hires hands to help him with these arduous chores.  His wife tends to the stores thus helping him cover household expenses.  For the future he plans to finish planting plants that are native to this area in his remaining fields because he hopes to earn additional income that will benefit his children and grandchildren.  This is his 6th loan with MFP and, as group leader; he’s always striving for them to be unified and understanding among themselves.  For this reason, he is well liked and respected and he feels good working with them.  He will use the requested 2000 soles to buy hundred of sacks of guano to equalize his fields’ productivity. Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Corazon
description: 61-year-old Corazon P. recently joined the KIVA field partner ASHI in the Philippines to be able to access a loan. Corazon's husband is a farmer. With the  loan that she is requesting, she can finance the starting of a business and have her own source of income. With this business she hopes to make enough profits to allow her only child to attend college, as well as pay for some of their their other personal needs. Corazon is hopeful that through this loan, through ASHI and KIVA, her family’s poor lifestyle will be improved and her child to have a brighter future.

name: Aba
description: Aba sells maize in Brenu Auyinim near Elmina. Aba has received schooling through middle school. She is married and has three children. Her husband is a farmer.   Aba has been selling maize and other foodstuffs for 25 years. She is responsible for paying her grandchildren's school fees. Her loan will be used to buy more maize in bulk. She hopes to use the new profits to continue to expand her business.

name: Robina
description: Robina is a 34-year-old widow woman and the mother of six children. She lives with her children in the area of Multan, Pakistan. Five of her children attend school. She is responsible for fulfilling the needs of the entire family. She has been running a clothing sales business since four years ago. Because of lack of capital, her income to cover the needs and expenses of her children is limited. She sells clothes in her colony and other cities with the help of her son. Robina is trying hard to improve her family's living conditions. The challenge she is facing is to have sufficient capital  to run the business and to be able to support her family in its present form. As such, today she is acquiring a loan from Kiva's field partner BRAC Pakistan to increase her clothing sales business so it can be a better source of income.Robina and her family will be thankful to Kiva, its lenders, and field partner BRAC Pakistan for helping them by funding this loan to improve their living standard.

name: Malahat
description: Melahat is 46 years old and lives in the town of Khachmaz, located in north-east of Azerbaijan. She is married and has two children. She has one section in the big food market. She buys goods from Baku and sometimes from local wholesalers. Last year she borrowed her first loan in amount of $300 to invest in her business. She successfully repaid her first loan and now applies for the second loan in amount of $1000 to buy more food stuff to be sold in the shop.

name: Juana
description: Juana started her business out of necessity to earn an income that would help her feed her children. Her husband had passed away and Juana was left with the responsibility for her children. She looked for various alternatives to earn money and this was the best way to accommodate her needs, because she can also care for her children while she works. This is a better life, and Juana enjoys sales. First Juana began washing and ironing clothing and cleaning the houses of her neighbors, plus a couple of other activities that combined, earned enough income to support her children. In April 2002 Juana began to sell used clothing when her son, who lives in the U.S., sent her boxes of used clothing. She sold them, and was able to support her other children and help her grandchildren. Thanks to a previous loan with Kiva, Juana could buy more boxes of clothing. Now she'd like to buy used clothing for autumn and winter.   Juana needs a loan of US $400, which she'll repay in 5 months. She'll use the money to buy more boxes of clothing so as to offer better supplies to her clients and increase her sales and income. Translated from Spanish by Sarah Bishop, Kiva Volunteer

name: Karanjung Lestari 2 Group
description: Ni Made and the Karanjung Lestari 2 Group received their third loan with the same members and loan size. The loan will be used to increase the pig business by purchasing superior piglets, local piglets, and feed. Ni Made used her loan to purchase superior feed only because she still has pigs remaining in her cage. Beside using her loan to purchase feed, she also uses it as capital for her other business, fish-selling.

name: Eda Elena
description: Eda is a partner of the Community Bank of Señor de Huanca. Eda is married, 43 years old, and has 8 children. Eda travels to different festivals in the region where she buys cheeses andsmall animals, products she sells house to house in the city of Ayacucho. She needs a loan of $225 that will be invested in the purchase of cheese and chickens. She dreams of giving a good education to her children and having her own house. Translated from Spanish by Amy Schapiro, Kiva Volunteer

name: Cynthia
description: Cynthia is 24 years old and has worked as a typist for 2 years while also studying law at the same time. She would like to get a better job in order to help her partner with household expenses.  She has the support of her partner, who is an accountant. In this way they both help each other. Cynthia is a self-sacrificing woman who is going to a lot of effort to have a better quality of life and a respectable future.  Cynthia is requesting the loan because she has to present her thesis. Additionally, she has many education expenses that she was not able to palliate right away for lack of available funds.

name: Solange's Group
description: Greetings from Solange N. who lives in the Nyarugenge district of the capital city Kigali, Rwanda! Nine years ago, Solange started a business selling men's and women's clothing.  She employs one person to help her run the shop and earns approximately 116,000 Rwandan Francs in profit each month ($230 USD).   Solange is requesting a loan worth 500,000 RWF from Vision Finance Company, S.A. to expand her business. Specifically, she hopes to increase her inventory by buying clothing in bulk to sell to her clients.  She will repay this loan over eight months on a monthly basis.  Solange is 26 years old and married with three children.

name: Monica
description: Monica is 38 years old and has two children who are in school. As a result, Monica works very hard to provide for them.   Monica runs a general store in the Philippines. She explains that she has been in this business for 15 years now.   Monica is requesting a loan in the amount of 8,000 PHP through NWTF to buy items to sell, such as canned goods, shampoo, and coffee. In the future, Monica would like to save enough money so that she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Majd
description: Majd is 32 years old, a married man and the father of two children who are 3 and 1 years old. He lives in Taiz,Yemen. He has been a person who has gone through many adversities in his life. Some time ago he had a great difficulty in that he was unable to find employment so was unable to generate sufficient income to cover his household expenses. He decided to open his own grocery store where he sells basic staple items. Thanks to the store, he generates enough income to help his family cover household expenses.  Majd`s sales are currently very good and his customers know him in the neighborhood because of his good service. He’s not been able to meet all his customers’ needs, however, because he has little merchandise and not much variety. Because of this, he wants to stock the store by buying basic staple items but he does not have enough capital to make these purchases and this is why he took a loan of 80,000 YER from AMB that will allow him to buy  items such as rice, beans, soft drinks, and cheese to increase the variety of items he stocks for his customers.  In the future, he is hoping that he can provide his children with opportunities to study in school.

name: Exemple De Bordemer Group
description: Jodelin is the coordinator of her group Exemple de Borddemer. He is a merchant and lives in the BOR-DE-MER region, where electricity is rare and water is very limited. Jodelin has been running his general store for eleven years.   Jodelin would like to use this loan to invest in purchasing a variety of goods, such as shoes, clothing, cosmetics, etc. He hopes his loan will help him to expand his business. He says his main challenge is becoming a major merchant. He says his main goal and dream is to own a big business through his capital and by the grace of God.

name: Mauricio David
description: Mauricio David is 21 years old. He is single and lives in his family home, together with his mother, in the town of Pucará, in the province of Jaén, in the state of Cajamarca in Perú. Mauricio David has good personal and work references from the residents in this area. The residents in this community mostly work in agriculture, commerce and livestock farming. Mauricio David works providing public transportation services in the town of Pucará and adjacent hamlets. He has his own mototaxi with which he provides the aforementioned services. Mauricio David has more than two years of experience performing this work. He is seeking a loan to invest in repairs to maintain his vehicle and to purchase accessories for his home.Mauricio David is an recurring member of our institution, Edpyme Alternativa, which has a firm guarantee.

name: Josefina Group
description: Josefina is 42 years old and is married with four children. She lives in Poblacion, Concepcion. Josefina has a grocery store business and she earns approximately 3,600 PHP each month. She has been a member of PMPC for one year. Josefina is the leader of this two-person loan group. Although she and her partner are borrowing as a group, each of them has her own business.   Josefina is requesting a 5,000 PHP loan to purchase more stock for her grocery store.

name: Mary
description: Lace cloth is very adorable and it is used to beautify homes as curtains, tablecloths, and decorations. This has created high demand for lace in Ghana. Mary, a married woman with two children, has made hawking of lace an enjoyable business and wants to increase her inventory. She believes this loan would help her to save. She would use her savings to register to join the national health insurance scheme to enjoy free medical care and also to support her husband to pay their children’s education.  Mary is a member of the group called Gift. Members agree together to guarantee for each other as social collateral to repay the loan.

name: Hindatu
description: Hindatu is a maize farmer from Sabon Gida Kanti village. As a member of Babban Gona, Hindatu is excited about the opportunity to become a better farmer. With Babban Gona’s support she has the opportunity to attain yields of up to 8 metric tonnes of maize per hectare of land, 5.5 times the average yield in Nigeria. Before joining Babban Gona, Hindatu would have had to sell her maize at harvest, a period when maize prices are at their lowest, to meet her immediate cash needs. With this loan and Babban Gona’s support, Hindatu can store her maize and sell it in the future for up to 37% higher than the market price at harvest. Hindatu is grateful to be part of the Babban Gona family and in the end hopes to use her increased earnings to move into a better home with her family.

name: Hadjah
description: Hadjah is married with eight children, four of whom go to school. She also takes care of additional family members (her grandchildren and in-laws). She lives in her own house, and the family has access to electricity and piped water. Her monthly expenses include school fees and feeding the family.  Hadjah has a business selling beer and local gin. She has been in this business for the last 5 years and she sells to all categories of people on a retail basis. She has requested a loan of 2,000,000 Ugandan shillings from MCDT SACCO to buy more crates of beer and jerrycans of local gin.    Hadjah doesn’t have any other income-generating activity. Her business challenges include thieves and defaulters. She aspires to see her business grow large enough that she can run a fully stocked pub.

name: Ruth
description: Ruth is 39 years old and lives in the town of West Point. She is single and has four children between 1 and  19 years old, who live with her at home and go to school. She attended school through the fourth grade. Over the past eleven years she has been running table businesses which sell Vita, pepper, salt, onions, oil, seasoned oil, etc., in the local market. She started with her own money and with the high price of food ingredients in Monrovia she thought of selling food ingredients. Ruth has requested a loan to purchase more Vita, pepper, salt, onions, oil, seasoned oil, etc., to attract more customers. In the future, Ruth hopes to be a big business woman and have her own store. She is glad to be a BRAC-Kiva borrower.

name: Chhin
description: Mrs. C., 32, is the mother of three young children who are enrolled in the local public school and who are dependent on her. She is married to Yoeung Chan, 34, who works for a small firm in the building field.  C. is a garment laborer who has been doing her job since she was single, earning a specific salary of $110 a month. She has also been using her income to help solve the family’s financial crisis.  In the paste, C. hired a taxi to go to work or anywhere else because she doesn’t own a vehicle. She right now hopes to avoid the taxi fares and is asking for a loan to buy a used motorcycle to provide transportation for her family.

name: Lagunas De 2014 Group
description: The “Lagunas 2014” communal bank is starting its second lending cycle with Pro Mujer, as a part of Centro Focal de Collpani.  The communal bank is made up of nine members and overseen by a board of directors, of which señora Felipa is the president.  The communal bank members' businesses are varied and include selling tracksuits, selling clothing, alcohol sales, running a neighborhood shop, blanket sales and selling sweaters.    The loan they are taking out will benefit small, micro-entrepreneurs, of which señora Felipa is one.  She says that she joined Pro Mujer four years ago at the invitation of an adviser from the institution that found her in a jam.  Señora Felipa was interested in the way the institution worked.  She currently has a business selling sweaters.  She says that she started the business several years ago by learning from two of her neighbors how to sell sweaters.  The loan señora Felipa is taking out is for increasing her capital: to purchase wholesale sweaters, which she will acquire from the vendors in El Alto and later sell from her sales stall.  This type of work allows señora Felipa to generate income to help her family financially.  She lives with her husband and has five children.   When asked what she likes about Pro Mujer, señora Felipa says that she likes the health information and the trainings that the institution offers.

name: Gladys
description: Gladys lives in the Nyamira area of Kenya, which is a popular banana growing region. She has 3 children. Gladys has been farming for 21 years and her primary income sources are eggs, tea, crops and personal business. Gladys states that tea farming is the most enjoyable aspect to farming and that her biggest challenge is growing tomatoes. One of the animals on the farm is named 'Nyabarati'.   Gladys has requested a loan of 30,000 KES from Kiva partner Juhudi Kilimo to help her buy poultry. When asked why she chose Juhudi Kilimo for this loan, Gladys replied, "The interest is favourable."  When asked what she learned during Juhudi's required micro-finance training session, Glady replied, "that savings is an important part of it." Gladys' highest monthly expense is school fees. Gladys states that this loan will benefit her family by enabling her children to get adequate education.  As part of Juhudi's loan appraisal process, each borrower's assets are evaluated. Gladys owns a cow, poultry and a pump but does not own pigs, a bicycle, motorcycle or automobile. Juhudi Kilimo also tries to measure any change in living standards based on this loan. Gladys has in her household mosquito nets but does not have electricity, solar power, running water, a sewing machine, TV or DVD.  Note: To create this loan profile, Juhudi Kilimo used a mobile device to gather information in the field and sent the data to a central online repository, thus reducing paper use, making the process more efficient, and keeping costs down.

name: Hilario
description: Hilario, age 58, is a certified organic cacao farmer of MMC. The farmer lives in the beautiful village of Santa Cruz in the southern most part of Belize. Hilario together with this wife, Maura, raised twelve children with four still living at home.  Maura spends most of her days doing crafts and on weekend she assists her husband on the farm.  Hilario was inspired to plant cacao with the assistance given by a local association.  Hilario cultivates different farm crops such as corn, beans, etc. He states that his farms need to be clean every other week due to the rain. The rainy season in southern Belize affects the farmers by requiring more farm management.   Hilario is requesting this loan to hire people to assist him in cleaning the area around his mature cacao trees.   Hilario’s future goal is to expand his cacao farms so as to increase production yields and increase the family income. His goal is to educate his last four children in order for them to have some sort of employment or become a farmer.

name: Obura
description: Obura is a 31-year-old mother, from Kisumu County. She is married and supports three people in her family. Her spouse's name is Vincent, who is formally employed. She has two children who are five years and seven months old, respectively.  Obura sells stationery, a business she has been doing for the last five years. She makes a monthly income of KES 40,000.  She is applying for her fourth loan which she will use to purchase more stocks of stationery for resale. She will use the anticipated profit to grow her business.  She has a dream of growing her business into a large one, so as to earn more profit, to help cater to her family's needs.

name: Señor De La Esperanza Group
description: LORD OF HOPE COMMUNAL BANK  Mila is a member of the “Señor de la Esperanza” (Lord of Hope) communal bank which has 7 members.  All are enterprising people in different commercial and service activities in the Matucana area.  She comments that a friend encouraged her to participate in the Prosperidad-EDAPROSPO program.  Mila, 48, with her spouse sells building materials and supplies like: sand, cement, concrete, etc.  She has been in this line of work for 20 years.  The idea for the business came from her husband’s ability and experience and also because it’s profitable.  Mila also sells fast food or fried snacks like: salchipollos (fried potatoes with fried chicken) and hamburgers, apple juice and other snacks at her doorstep. This is how they managed to finish building the first floor of their house.  They also have a car port in Matucana’s high zone that they lease to a transportation firm for parking.  She doesn’t have any savings because her earnings cover her capital needs and household expenses.  Mila’s goal is to form a small contracting firm buying demolition and perforation equipment to lease to mining firms in the area.  The loan she got recently will be used to buy some building materials and supplies.

name: Beatrice
description: Beatrice T. is 42 years old and a mother with three kids. Two of them are in school now and the youngest has not started school. She has been selling grocery products for five years on a table in her neighborhood, to support her family. She says business is doing well, and she therefore wants to use the loan to buy more products to increase her inventory. Beatrice believes the loan would help her increase her savings towards the welfare of her two children who are in school now. She is a member of the group called Boldness. Members in the group agree in unison to guarantee for each other to repay the loan. She does not sell on group meeting days and her picture was taken during her group meeting. Her child is also in the photo.

name: Sopheap
description: A villager from a rural area in the Korng Pisey district of Kampong Spuer province, Sopheap is 36 years old and married. She has three dependent children, two of whom are in school.The primary sources of her family’s income are from rice farming and pig raising. To better support the family, her husband also works as a policeman. Having been in this business for 18 years, Sopheap can earn about 15 USD per day and manages to save about 3 USD each day after expenses. The main challenges for her family’s business are the drop of rice’s price and unhealthy rice crops.Sopheap has been a member of VisionFund for five cycles already. This time, she is asking for a new loan to pay for her daughter’s tuition fee at university. She hopes this loan will allow her daughter to stay in school until her graduation.
town: Kampong Speu Province, Korng Pisey District

name: Khon
description: Khon S., 29, is married and lives with her husband in the Kampong Cham province, Cambodia. She sells coffins. Her husband is a goldsmith at the local market and earns approximately $10 every day. She and her husband have one young child. Mrs. Khon Sokhheng requests a loan of $800 to purchase a small truck to transport coffins.
town: Tboung Kmum district, Kampong Cham province, Cambo

name: Maria Lucas
description: Maria is 24 years old and currently living with her husband and her child in Kilosa district. She volunteers as a Camfed Learner Guide, when she leads secondary school students to find their own strengths and to think about how they can create a better world. She is requesting a Kiva loan to improve her vegetable farm.  She will use her loan to buy fertilizers and water for her farm. The profit earned will be used to support her family members with basic needs.In future she plans to own a big vegetable farm. The social interest on her loan will be repaid through Maria's weekly two and a half hours of volunteering.

name: Carmelita
description: Carmelita is 58 years old and is married with three children. Carmelita works very hard to provide for them.  Carmelita runs a general store in the Philippines. She has been in this business for thirteen years. Carmelita requested a PHP 50,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more groceries to sell, like milk, coffee, canned goods, spices, noodles, cooking oil, drinks, breads and other personal care products.  She would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Jean
description: 39-year-old Jean has been a rice farmer since 1990.  Her rice field in Banga, South Cotabato is one hectare.  She’s married to Romulo and has four children. Her eldest child is 18 years old.  Currently, she is applying for a loan from Community Economic Ventures, Inc. of PHP 15,000.  She joined CEVI and took a loan with only 2% interest.  The loan will help her purchase fertilizer for her field and send her children to school.

name: Jambalnyambuu
description: Jambalnyambuu T. is 52 years old and lives with her husband and two children in Arhangai province, Mongolia. She and her family live together in a ger, the Mongolian nomadic tent.   Her husband, Bayrsaihan, operates a transportation business in their town. They have been living together in their current home for 10 years.   Jambalnyambuu operates a vegetable trading business in town. She has been operating this business since 1998, and has steadily expanded. She rents a counter at a local trading center. She has gained significant experience over the past 12 years. She started her business with a working capital of 60,000 MNT. However, with a lot hard work and determination, she has managed to increase her working capital to 1,600,000 MNT.    With her business profits, she has been saving money to build a house for her family. Jambalnyambuu is an open and very hardworking person. She says, “I would like to expand my business. My dream is one day to create my own workplace. ”  She is requesting a 2,000,000 MNT loan to purchase more vegetables to resell to her many customers.

name: Julieta
description: Rice is a staple food in the Philippines, thus it is always in demand. It is therefore wise to include it in a “sari-sari” (variety) store inventory if a vendor has enough capital.   Julieta, of Bacolod City, Negros Occidental, is trying her best to use her capital wisely, and she combines her variety store business with rice retailing. She also helps her husband, Rodel, in fish selling. They are doing their best to sustain their everyday needs and support their children, who are studying in college. It is their dream to complete their children’s education because just like many Filipinos, they consider education as the best inheritance to bestow on their children.   Julieta’s business is not always smooth sailing, however. Stiff competition hampers her income and squeezes her family’s everyday sustenance. Therefore, she aims to improve her business further, and she appeals for PHP 15,000 in additional capital to buy more sacks of rice and grocery items for her variety store. She will also use part of the loan to pay for assorted fish to sell in the market.   Your kind generosity will help her a lot in strengthening her business. In due time, she plans to invest in another enterprise when her current businesses are stable.   She is committed to CCT Credit Cooperative’s vision to alleviate poverty and she meets with her co-fellowship* members every week to share stories of her life and business and to draw strength and inspiration from the fellowship and her religion. *All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study religion, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Marie
description: Marie L. was born in 1949 in Sèkandji, in the community of Sèmè-Podji. She has been living for some twenty years in Agblangandan, in the community of Sèmè-Podji. Married to Avocè Dansou, marie is the mother of two children, both of whom go to schol. Marie lives together with her husband and children. The couple takes care of the various family expenses jointly. Marie did not attend school. In order to provider for her own and her children’s needs, she retails sauce condiments (tomatoes, onions, hot peppers, canned foods, palm oil) as well as charcoal out of her home. She stocks up in Dantokpa, the international market of Benin. She has been in this business for 22 years, and had previously obtained two credits from ALIDé, both duly repaid. Facing ever increasing customer demand, she is seeking a third loan in order to expand her activities and to better meet her customers' needs. Translated from French by Ekaterina Sukhanova, Kiva Volunteer

name: Rosalinda
description: Rosalinda is 54 years old and married with eight children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.   Rosalinda has a business selling frozen foods in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 20,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more frozen foods to sell in her food stall.  Rosalinda has been in this business for five years. In the future, she would like to save enough to support the financial stability of her family.

name: Venis
description: Venis J. has enjoyed spending the profits from her vegetable farming business and sari-sari store ventures.  “Sari” means variety in the native dialect. A sari-sari store basically sells several types of food stuffs, beverages and household necessities.  The store is either operated from the owner’s house or a small cottage not far away from the owner’s home.  Because of her two ventures she has able to sustain the needs of her family and has been able to improve their lives.  With that, Venis is encouraged to work harder and plan further for her business and family.  Because she has her own business that supports their financial needs she can access loans to support her business.   Therefore, Venis wants to take this opportunity to grow her businesses by requesting another loan of 35,000 PHP from our Kiva lenders for use as additional business capital.  Venis wants to maintain and support the needs of her farming business to grow more vegetables to sell and sustain the operation of her sari-sari (variety) store.  Her long term goals are to have a successful vegetable farming business, a full-fledge grocery store and to support her family financially.   With the support of Kiva lenders, she is determined to achieve business success with her new entrepreneurial endeavor.  Venis’s wish is to offer her children hope for a better future and that is what fuels her pledge to her business endeavor.  Venis is very happy to be a Kiva borrower and says thank you for offering financial support for her business dreams.

name: Sarah
description: Sarah lives in Montserrado County, where there is the capital city of Liberia, well-known as the commercial city of Liberia. She is 40 years old, married and has four children between the ages of seven and 22 years old who are in school and live at home.  For the past ten years she has been selling charcoal in her community, but now she is selling slippers from a table in the local market. She started this business with the help of her mother and learned this way of selling from her. She likes her business because it gives her profit. She is requesting a loan to buy more slippers for her business. She wants to get more money to educate her children and build a house.

name: Grupo Xojola Nuevo Group
description: Juana is a 41 year old woman. She is happily married and has two children aged between 6 and 12. This modest family lives in a community in Nahualá. Juana (the second on the left of the photograph) makes a living selling coffee to be able to obtain the income to maintain her beloved family. She has been doing this for ten years. These days Juana has some plots of land on which she grows coffee that now needs to be maintained, but one of the difficulties that Juana has is that she does not have enough money to buy fertilisers and to pay for labour. For this reason she is asking for a loan along with a group of people who have the same needs. Juana hopes to be able to buy ten plots of land to be able to grow more.

name: Luis Alonso
description: Luis is 72 years old. He currently lives with two of his children aged 36 and 32 years old and a 6 year old grandchild. His business is planting and growing vegetables, a business he has carried out for more than fifty years. His specialty is growing chayote, ayote (a squash) and limes. He works full time together with his son. With the capital he can buy sprayers and hose besides paying for the installation of a gravity irrigation system. In this way his vegetable crops will have better development. So he thinks he will have greater production and thus increase his sales and income. His goal is for his son and grandson to learn this work in the field growing vegetables so they can have a better future.

name: Arlene
description: As a married mother of four children, Arlene works hard to support her family.  She has a business selling vegetables in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from fishing.  Arlene is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to buy more vegetables to sell to her customers.  Arlene has been sustaining her business activities through her past 5 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream: to save enough money so she can continue to send her children to school.

name: Elvia Petra
description: Elvia is a 60-year-old woman; she is single and she is the mother of three sons who have grown onto adults and have families of their own. None of them depend on her.  Elvia's biggest accomplishment is rising three kids as a single mother; she is really proud of herself and now she has been rewarded with grandchildren.In order to make a living, Elvia has been selling clothes; she has been in this line of business for a very long time, but two years ago she made a change. She decided to stop buying t-shirts to sell them. Instead, she bought a sewing and a printing machine to craft clothes of her own. Kubo Financial looks up to her because she become more independent and employs two people who help her.  She is applying for a 10,527 MXN loan which will allowed her to cover the client demand for the upcoming Christmas season by buying fabric, thread and printing material.Elvia runs her business along with her sister, and they have both doing well with it. They think that with this loan, can get a huge profit from the upcoming season.

name: Salisu
description: Salisu is a maize farmer and Babban Gona Farmers Organization member. Anticipating a good harvest this season, Salisu has the opportunity to attain yields of up to eight metric tons of maize per hectare of land, 5.5 times that of the average Nigerian maize farmer. Before joining Babban Gona, Salisu would have had to sell his maize at harvest, a period when maize prices are at their lowest in the market, to meet his immediate cash needs, such as food and clothing. Thanks to Babban Gona’s support, Salisu can store his maize and sell it at a future date for up to 37% above the market price at harvest. As a Babban Gona member, Salisu will benefit from marketing support that could see him generate earnings of up to USD 2,000 per hectare of land. Salisu is thankful that he now has the opportunity to improve the life of his children and family and he looks forward to using his additional earnings to acquire more land to put into the Babban Gona program.

name: Las Intelectuales 3 Group
description: Rosa is the coordinator of the group called "Las Intelectuales" (The Intellectuals). Her story is representative of both her group and of Esperanza's Haitian and Dominican clients, many of whom recently emigrated from Haiti to the DR. Her group is based in the area surrounding La Romana, an agricultural area where the economy focuses around the sugar cane harvest, where running water is unreliable and not potable, and electricity are unreliable at best. Here she makes her home as a single mother with her two children.  If you have ever wondered where clothing that the Salvation Army cannot sell ends up, Rosa's business can provide part of the answer. Rosa intends to use the money to buy "paca de ropa" or packages of  used clothes, which are sold in bulk after being shipped to the DR from wealthier countries. She intends to use her first loan to invest in this business and sell the clothes in her neighborhood. Its a good business and she expects the profits to allow her to provide for her children's school supplies and to keep expanding her business. She thanks all of you for your support.

name: Saeed
description: Saeed is a 33-year-old married man from Rafah city, which is located in the Gaza Strip, which has had an economic blockade imposed by the Israeli authorities since 2007. Saeed is a farmer who also has a lag farm around his house. It is a good business and makes a good profit. He has good experience. He sowed different types of vegetables according to the season. But plants always need attention and  fertilizer. Saeed took a USD loan from FATEN. This loan will help him to buy plant food and fertilizer for his farm and a little grain. With this loan Saeed can improve the quality and quantity of agricultural crops this year. Saeed appears in the photo.

name: Edwine
description: Edwine O. is 24 years old and married to Mwajuma. They have one school-going child. He has been in the auto-repair business for the last five years in Naivasha town.  He was introduced to KADET by a friend and this will be his first loan with the organization. He is planning to buy a buffing machine for use in the garage as he has noticed that this is a service that can give him a competitive edge.  In the future, Edwin wants to open up his own garage since he is currently employed.  About KADET:  The Kenya Agency for the Development of Enterprise and Technology (KADET) is dedicated to economically empowering clients by providing financial services to improve the living conditions of micro-entrepreneurs and their children across Kenya. KADET is the micro-finance subsidiary of World Vision Kenya. Obtain more information on KADET from the website: www.kadet.co.ke

name: Mwajuma
description: Mwajuma is 55 and a strong and energetic mother of six. She sells charcoal, a business she has been doing for the past three years. She recently obtained business training organized by the Youth Self Employment Foundation. She sells charcoal at her home. She is in need of $225 to help her prosper business.

name: Amematuna
description: Amematuna is 29 years old. She is married to a career soldier. They have two children.  Amematuna has been a seamstress since 2007. She sells food products out of her home-based store. She buys her supplies at the markets in inland cities of the country. She has hired someone to help her.  Amematuna came to the microfinance institution WAGES and applied for her second loan to buy 4 sacks of corn, 2 sacks of beans, 1 sack of groundnuts and 1 pile of yams.

name: Lalita
description: Lalita was born in the Namaacha district of Maputo province in Mozambique. She is 30 years old and is a single mother with one child who is in school. She is not financially responsible for anyone else.  Lalita has worked at a mineral water processing plant for more than nine years, earning a monthly salary that she uses to cover household expenses and also to pay for a home construction project. With this loan she would like to continue with this home construction project by buying materials like blocks, cement, sand, iron and posts, and any other materials she might need. This is her third loan with Hluvuku [Kiva Field Partner].  In the future, Lalita would like to buy a vehicle and continue with her education through college.

name: Imtiaz
description: Imtiaz is 44 years old and is a married woman. She is shown in the photo with her husband. She buys animals (baby goats & calves) at low prices, brings them up and then sells them out in the market at higher prices. She makes enough through her business to contribute to the family income. She also sells milk to generate an extra amount of income.Imtiaz needs to improve her business to bear her household expenses. For this reason, she contacted Kashf Foundation and applied for a Murabaha loan of 25,000 PKR to purchase more animals to increase her sales. She is very experienced and has good contacts in the market. With this loan, she will definitely expand her business and income level.

name: Salvadora De Jesus
description: Sra. Salvadora is 49 years old. She is unmarried and has three children, of whom one is still dependent on her. She is also responsible for two of her grandchildren. Doña Salvadora is a hardworking and enterprising woman, who is struggling to succeed. She mentioned that since she was very young, she did washing and ironing because she had to support her three children and underwrite their studies through her work.   However, it was not until two years ago that she obtained a job in a government institution, where she works as caretaker in a maternal home. There she is in charge of keeping the place clean and in addition of fixing meals for the pregnant women.   In addition to her steady job, she has also been operating a small business (selling basic grains, detergents, soft drinks) in her home for two years. It is on behalf of her business that she is requesting a loan. Her objective is to expand her business, which is currently being run by one of her daughters. Her goal is that her business prosper so that her earnings will increase and provide her children and grandchildren with a better life.

name: Javier
description: Javier is an entrepreneur who sells beef and viscera.  His business is located downtown.  He has 38 years of experience and remembers that he started with a table in a public space, selling small quantities.  Little by little, he has been growing and has grand dreams for his business.  His wife currently helps him and their shared income.  He has been able to educate his two children who are now 34 and 36 years old.  His future goal is to expand his business, relocating to a new commercial spot with lots of traffic, with his wife who has been insturmental in the good performance of the business.    This Kiva loan is his first through Fundación Mario Santo Domingo.  He will use it to buy meats and viscera with cash and in large quantities.  His investment will be successful because it will give him new working capital to make purchases in cash and in larger quantities, responding to a new clientele that increases his sales during the Christmas and New Year season.  He will be able to use his loan for his business in a season when there is an upturn in sales and lots of money circulating.

name: Estrellitas De Magisterio Group
description: The communal bank “ESTRELLITAS DE MAGISTERIO” is beginning its second cycle with the field partner through the field partner’s Santiago II regional office. This group is made up of eight members and is directed by a board of directors, of which Josefina is the president. The businesses of the members are varied and include vegetable sales, a corner store, knitting sweaters, blanket weaving, sewing of skirts, fruit sales and sales of chicharrón (a Bolivian dish made of pork).  The loan will be used in some small businesses of which Josefina is a member. She became a member of the field partner one year ago at the invitation of some members of the group. Josefina currently has a business selling chicharrón. She says that she learned this business seven years ago, when she noticed the possibility of selling this product in her area.  Josefina will use this loan to increase the capital of her business by buying pork from wholesalers in the city of El Alto. She will use the pork to make chicharrón and sell it in her area. She says that this business allows her to earn income to pay for as many of her household expenses as possible. She lives with her partner and has four children.  Asked what she likes about the field partner, Josefina says that she likes the training programs on credit and on health.

name: Celia
description: Celia, aged 51, lives with Victor, with whom she has four children. She and her family live in their own house in the neighborhood of Tiambra, located in the district of Huasahuasi in the province of Tarma. Celia is a farmer and owns a few fields scattered throughout several hills of the district. Celia grows potatoes and peas. "Each year I sow two bags of peas, twice a year," she says. Although potato production is profitable, she has to invest a lot to get a good crop. January, February and March are the months with the highest demand for potatoes. Merchants from other cities travel to her district and buy a sizeable proportion of her crop. What is left over will be transported by her to the city of Tarma. She does well in her business.  Celia has been working in the fields for thirty years, actively helped by her husband and her children, who are grown up by now. Farming is an activity that demands sacrifices. The rain and the inaccessibility of her lands make her work difficult, but this does not prevent her from looking after her potatoes and peas. Celia is a courageous woman.  This will be her twelfth loan from the microfinance institution Microfinanzas Prisma. She promises to be punctual in paying the monthly installments. "Santa Rosa de Tiambra" is the name of her communal bank, with which she identifies because it is made up of responsible people. She will use her loan to buy 20 bags of organic fertilizer at 120 new soles each to fertilize the potatoes that are currently growing, on one hand, and to fertilize a field that she is about to sow with peas, on the other hand.

name: Yolanda
description: Yolanda N. is from the village of Camating, Tudela Mis. Occ.. She is 49 years old. Yolanda is married and has 3 school-aged children.
