To make a living Yolanda sells personal home products to tourists and local community members. Yolanda has been engaged in her business for over 3 years and earns approximately 3,500 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2008, Yolanda joined PMPC to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Yolanda successfully repaid a previous loan of 5000 PHP from PMPC which she used to to purchase additional products to sell. Yolanda is requesting her third loan from PMPC, for 4000 PHP, which she will use for the same purpose. She plans to use the additional revenue  to supplement her family's income.  About PMPC  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.    Note  To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partners to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: David
description: David is 41 years old and married with seven children. He earns his income through the sale of crops and livestock products. He grows coffee, beans maize and bananas. He also has cows, sheep, donkeys and chickens.  David looks forward to becoming a Community Knowledge Worker (CKW). As a CKW he will use the materials in his business-in-a-box (smartphone and solar charging set) to disseminate vital agricultural information to the other members of his village, helping them to improve their crop yields and increase their incomes.  With the additional money that he will earn as a CKW, David will buy an exotic cow for rearing. His biggest dream in life is to educate all his children in better institutions of higher learning.

name: Carmen
description: Sra. Carmen C. T. joined the organization a year ago because she needed a loan to buy wholesale merchandise, so she could sell it in her stall on Max Paredes Street in the Rosario neighborhood. She also plans to snag an "anticrético" to live in, since she's now living with her aunt and would like to get ahead and no longer depend on her aunt or pay rent. (An "anticrético" is a type of living arrangement in Bolivia in which a contract is signed with a property owner to be able to live in a house for a period of time for an established sum of money up-front. At the end of the period, if the house is still in good shape, all the money is returned to the occupant, or the occupant gets to keep the property.) She lives with her younger brothers, who are of school age, and takes care of all the family expenses with her earnings from her stall.Translated from Spanish by Andrea Rosenberg, Kiva Volunteer

name: Adovi
description: This man's business is the sale of electronic devices.  He also installs sound equipment.  His clientele grows from day to day.  To be able to satisfy them all properly he must grow his stock of merchandise.  For this reason he requests a loan from WAGES to increase his stock with 40 tall speakers and 20 14-inch screens.  He is married and is the father of 3 children.  His wife is a dealer.  With what he earns from his business he provides for the family expenses. Translated from French by Barbara (B) Brown, Kiva Volunteer

name: Ana Maria
description: Ana Maria is a member of the 'San Isidro de Compone' community bank which meets once a month in the city of Izcuchaca, in the community of Compone.    Ana Maria is 22 years old and lives with her common-law husband.  She has one child.  Ana Maria was born in the community of Compone and this is where she carries out her business activities.  She buys and sells cheese and dried grains.  On this occasion, she requires a loan to buy more merchandise and supplies such as corn, barley and milk.  She has been in this business for several years and it is going very well thanks to the effort that she puts into her work.  Ana Maria is grateful for the loan and appreciates it.  She pledges to make her monthly repayments on time.

name: María Ofelia
description: María Ofelia, 58, lives in the city of El Sauce and has two children.  She has been a teacher at a local primary school for more than thirty years, work that has allowed her to raise her children and buy a house of her own. María Ofelia teaches at a school some 10 kilometers from El Sauce and walks to work because there are no buses at the time she has to go. In spite of her age, María Ofelia is a dynamic teacher.  She loves her students and often sings to them.  She supervises their coloring and teaches them to read. María Ofelia is applying for a loan to pay healthcare costs.  She isn't well and will use the loan the pay doctors and buy the medicines she needs.

name: Sonia
description: Sonia, 33, is responsible for her two children. She lives in Nueva Frontera, Santa Bárbara. She has operated her own business, a grocery shop where she sells basic items, for several years. She offers margarine, sugar, rice, beans, canned goods, sausages, chicken, corn, canned goods, churros, pills, and more.   She has applied for another loan of 15,000 lempiras to buy merchandise and build her customers base. She will buy chicken, sausages, corn, beans, margarine, and other items. Her goal is to grow her business and improve her family's standard of living.

name: Brigida
description: In the Mayoreo market in Managua, Mrs. Brigida H. has a business selling clothing. She conducts the sales personally at her stall, where she sells all types of clothing for women, men, and children.  She is asking for a loan to purchase clothing such as pants and shirts.  She is confident that her loan will be granted, and that she will continue in said business to improve her living conditions.   Translated from Spanish by Erin Kurten, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sandy
description: Sandy is originally from the Dominican Republic and has lived in the U.S. since 1999. He opened Ydalia’s Hair Design in 2006, with an experienced hairstylist as his partner. The salon offers the full range of hairstyle services, from coloring to extensions to keratin treatments. The business also offers retail products.  Sandy’s work supports himself and his three sons.  Given how hard the hair salon business is, Sandy is most proud of being in business for eight years. Sandy would like to finish renovating his salon and will use this loan to buy furniture. Sandy looks forward to helping his children through a stable, well-respected salon business.

name: Hue
description: Hue is a 46-year-old married woman with three children. She lives with her family in Ho Chi Minh City.  To earn a living, Hue and her husband buy water morning glory, a kind of vegetable, and cut it into small pieces to sell to food stands and markets. They have been engaged in this business for nearly ten years. This business brings in a minimal income to support the family because they have to buy at retail prices. Hue would like to deal with wholesalers who own water morning glory growing ponds so that she could sell her products at lower prices. She would like to take a loan to invest capital for this purpose. She hopes that this will enable her to earn a higher income and improve her family's living conditions.

name: Besik
description: Besik is 30 years old. He lives in Ozurgeti district with his parents and pensioner grandmother. The family is involved agricultural activities. In particular, they have an agricultural plot of land, where they grow nut trees and mandarin trees. Besik and his parents sell the harvested products locally to generate income. Besik decided to start additional business and requested a loan. The Start Up program, which is a joint initiative with Kiva and Credo enables him to get a loan of 5200 GEL. With the received credit he will start trading fruits and vegetables. He will also purchase a minibus and will trade fruits and vegetables from village to village. This will increase his income and with increased income will be able to improve the living conditions of his family. Besik awaits your support.

name: Luvuno
description: Luvuno is a married woman blessed with five children, all  attend school. They live at their own house that is without electricity and running water. She has operated a home-based fish selling business for  five years and sells to restaurant operators. She faces a major challenge of competition in her business.She will use the loan to purchase bundles of fish to resell. She dreams of expanding her business and establishing another business in the near future.

name: Maqbool
description: Ms. Maqbool is 47 years old and a mother of four children. For 17 years, she has been running a business selling milk with her husband. The man shown in the photo is Maqbool’s husband. She initiated her own business by buying a buffalo to support her family when her husband was the only bread earner at that point in time. With the passage of time her sales increased, as did her income. Now she has seven buffaloes and two cows. This has all happened due to her hard work and determination. Her husband is happy with her support and respects her a lot. While talking to the Kashf officer, she shared the feeling of achievement she got by renovating her house with the profit she earned through her business. She is in her 3rd loan cycle with Kashf Foundation and has shown good repayment behavior. She has some savings and applied for a loan of PKR 30,000 to purchase another buffalo. She expects a boost in her income as she expands her business. She is very thankful to Kashf for its support.

name: Jocelyn
description: Jocelyn is a married woman with four children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Jocelyn is 33 years old and all of her children are in school.  Jocelyn has a fish vending business in the Philippines. She requested a 15,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy more fish to sell at her business.  Jocelyn has been in this business for four years. In the future, she would like to save enough money so she that she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Sanu Thapa
description: Mrs. Sanu Thapa M. lives in Sainbu-Bhaishepati, Lalitpur. Sainbu-Bhaishepati is one of the developing villages of Lalitpur and most of the people in this region are engaged in farming. Mrs. Sanu Thapa M. lives in a family with her husband and two sons. Her husband, Mr. Rajendra Thapa M., is a farmer. Her older son is studying in grade 8 and her younger son is in grade 6. Mrs. Sanu is engaged in selling cow’s milk. She already owns two cows and makes sales in her neighborhood. Nowadays the demand for cow’s milk is increasing constantly in the region. To meet the demands of the customers, she needs another young dairy cow. So, she is requesting a loan of 30,000 NPR to buy a cow.

name: Alberto Trinidad
description: Alberto makes one of the best "petos" in his hometown.  Peto is a drink made of white corn with the addition of water, sugar, milk, and cinnamon.  The corn is soaked the previous night, then cooked in the water and salt.  The milk and sugar are added, the heat is lowered, and the peto is stirred constantly until thickened a little for serving.  He started this job 10 years ago because it was an alternative source of income after he became disabled.  He was left without a leg 13 years ago when he stepped on a land mine while walking.  He makes his sales in cash, and the main customers who buy his delicious beverage are students, employees, and and the community in general.  Currently Alberto's requesting a Kiva loan, his first financing from Fundación Mario Santo Domingo, to buy corn, sugar, and cinnamon wholesale and in cash.  He'll also invest in making a hot-dog cart so he can add fast food sales.  His biggest desire is to pay for his 3-year-old son's education.  That's the reason for the big challenge of working persistently to be able to save and realize his dream of prosperity.

name: Sibongile
description: Sibongile is a 33-year-old business lady and volunteer Camfed Learner Guide, living with her brother and one child in the Mwenezi district. Her work involves selling clothes from door to door as well as at the market on days when the market is open, in order to pay school fees for her child and help her wider family too. Also volunteering as a Camfed Learner Guide, she leads life skills sessions with students at her local high school, covering active citizenship and personal confidence. She is now requesting a Kiva loan in order to boost her business. She also wishes to employ someone to assist her selling her products during market days.

name: Sun
description: Sun S., 30, has three children and lives in the Kampong Cham province with her husband, Him Channy (pictured here). They work together selling rice from their home, and they make around $8 US each day. All of their children are students. Sun S. is asking for a loan of $300 US to expand her rice stock. They believe that with the loan, the expansion of their business will bring about an increased income and a higher standard of living.

name: Susan
description: Susan is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a food production business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 20,000 through NWTF to buy ingredients for her food business.  Susan successfully paid back her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her business.  NWTF is listing Susan's business profile again in support of her efforts to secure the future of her family.

name: Maa Aghorkali Shg-A Group
description: Kameni, 47, is the lady standing on the left hand side in the photograph. She only went to school for four years because her parents couldn't cover the household expenses and those of education. She is a divorcee and she has five children only two of whom depend economically on her. She says, "that my children go to school and have a good quality of life is what motivated me to begin selling soft drinks and food 5 years ago." These are the words of Kameni, as she is known in the community. She says that she didn't want history to repeat itself with her children.For five years, she has worked selling food and soft drinks and says that she began just with soft drinks, chips and cookies, but with the passing of the months, the customers began to ask her for food and then she began, with the help of her group member and using part of the earnings she got, to build a small structure where she set up her refrigerator for the soft drinks, the chips, and cookies, and five tables and a burner where she makes the food. Kameni, along with her group member, is requesting a loan amount of 30,000 INR to purchase oil, meat, vegetables, cream, cheese, soft drinks, chips and two tables.She is awaiting your kind and generous hearts to help her.

name: Amna
description: Amna is 49 years old, married, and she has been running a buy-and-sell animal business with the help of her husband for many years. She also sells milk in her locality to earn extra amount of income.   Her business has provided her family with a decent life. She is a mother of 7 children. She is very motivated to provide them a beautiful life with good education, food and clothing. She has requested a loan of 40,000 PKR, and she intends to utilize this loan amount to purchase more baby goats and calves to cater to more customers. She is hopeful that her business will generate greater revenue in the future.

name: Juan
description: Juan continues to be dedicated to his transportation business.  He has a taxi business, providing service to various people and places.  He's been in this business for several years and it goes very well.   His dream is to increase his taxi business.  He asks for a loan to buy tires for his car.    He is grateful for the loan and is committed to making the payments required.

name: Eva
description: Eva manages her business of selling beauty products such as lipsticks, crèmes, and perfumes.  She works from 8:00 A.M. to 7:00 P.M.  Eva has been this business for several years.  Her dream is to have a shop where she can sell beauty products.  She is requesting a loan in order to buy crèmes, lipsticks, and perfumes.  Eva is pleased with the loan and promises to complete her payments.

name: Jane
description: Jane is a married woman. She has two children. She describes herself to be God fearing.   She operates a retail business where she sells shoes. She has been involved in this business for two years. Her business is located in a good area, and her primary customers are the general public. She describes her biggest business challenge to be insufficient capital.   She will use the Kes 20,000 loan to buy more stocks of shoes. She hopes that in the future, she will educate her children. This is her first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: Ntito  Ene
description: Ntito has been rearing animals for sale in Naivasha town for the last 10 years. She is 32 years old, married to Lokongo Ole K.. They have two children in school.  She was introduced to KADET by her friend and this will be her first loan. She plans to use the loan amount to buy five cows which she will rear and sell later at a profit.  In future, Ntito hopes to open a wholesale store for selling skin and hides.

name: Concepcion
description: Concepcion is a 29-year-old married woman with one child. She engages in fruit vending, particularly in mangoes. She buys mangoes and sells them at the market. She aims to increase her income because of the high price of commodities and the increasing needs of her family. Recently, she decided to take a loan to buy more mangoes to sell in her stall.  Concepcion plans in the future to expand her business to sustain the needs of her family.

name: Byron Jose
description: Byron M. is originally from Rio Abajo, Pueblo Nuevo, in Esteli. He is married and has 2 children. He was unable to finish school because of a lack of financial resources, and was obliged instead to drop out right after he finished 8th grade. He started farming when he was young, growing staple grains and tobacco. Currently he is planting produce such as tomatoes. He had a little money saved when he started, and the help of a brother-in-law. He has requested this loan to purchase supplies for buying tomatoes. He hopes to turn a good profit this Easter, to keep growing his business a little at a time and not have to depend on his brother-in-law.

name: Luisa Marina
description: Doña Luisa continues to work as a janitor, for the common good of her family, for through this hard work she has been able to move ahead with the improvements to her home.  Her husband works in construction and they also have the support from their son who is also working. The previous loan was for the replacement of  the roof.  There has been an increase in robberies in the neighborhood of which she was a victim when her electric appliances were stolen.  This has changed her focus to finishing the wall that was pending.  She needs additional materials to be able to enclose it all and be certain that her property is protected by the beautiful wall that has been built.  This improvement can be done more quickly with the help that Afondesic provides.

name: Kimorn's Group
description: Aged 64 years old, Kimorn is a widow with five children. She still supports three children who work for others for fees as they receive only minimal wage. The two-hectare of rice farming that she has been doing for 40 years is the main source of income.  Kimorn joined for her first loan with VisionFund 6 years ago. The past loans, which she completely paid back, have helped her to improve her family’s living conditions and enabled her to save some money to support her child's wedding ceremony. In a confident manner, she and two other members of her group are seeking a new loan. As the group leader, she will use her loan’s portion to buy fertilizer for her farmland. She hopes to earn more profit and to maintain the family's living conditions.

name: Maricor
description: Maricor B. is from the village of Villa Sudiacal, Liloy, Zamboanga del Norte. She is 35 years old. Maricor is married and has three school-aged children. To make a living, she owns and operates a restaurant, serving a variety of different meals to customers in the local community. She has been engaged in her business for over nine years and earns approximately $192 a month for these activities.  In 2010, Maricor joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 25,000 PHP from PMPC.   Maricor is requesting a new loan of 25,000 PHP which will be used to purchase raw ingredients for her different viand of her restaurant. This will be her 2nd loan from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the family's income.   About PMPC:  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.
town: Liloy-Villa Sudiacal, Liloy, ZAmboanga Del Norte

name: Joesela
description: Joesela works hard to support her family. She is married and has a business making and selling coconut vinegar in the Philippines.  Joesela requested a 15,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy more gallon containers for her coconut vinegar. She has been in this business for 10 years.  In the future, Joesela would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Rosy Ynes
description: Rosy is an enterprising young woman, she is 21 years old, single, and lives in Ica with her family.  With much effort and dedication, she could open a beauty salon where she has worked for some time, and with the income she earned, help her family.  She is a person with a strong desire to improve herself and always works with a lot of enthusiasm in order to get her family ahead.  Rosy is grateful to the Kiva lenders because with the help they have offered her, she will be able to purchase materials to stock her business and in this way get more income to be able to, in the future, open a much larger salon.

name: Dorjnamjil
description: Dorjnamjil is 56 years old and lives with his wife and daughter in a house in Han-Uul district, Ulaanbaatar, capital city of Mongolia. They live with their two disabled relatives and take care of them. Dorjnamjil is a photographer who works at Suhbaatar square, is the central square of Ulaanbaatar city, Mongolia. It is scene of major state ceremonies, cultural events and exhibitions. Therefore many people gather at this square and like to be photographed to keep their precious memories. He started his business in 2001.  In 2004 his wife, Altantsetseg, also began working as a photographer too. His daughter, age 25, helps with the family business by picking up the films in order to process them at a laboratory. They prefer to use advanced cameras in order to provide quality service for their customers. So they began using digital cameras to capture images electronically which allowed them to print their pictures in a minute. They also offered a very special service of taking one's picture with Mongolian traditional clothes on. They are planning to continue and expand their business in the future. Dorjnamjil is a hardworking man who says, "By depositing my business earnings I want to pay the education cost of my daughter." He is requesting a 2,500,000 MNT of loan to renew his camera and to purchase more photo papers.

name: Abosede
description: Abosede O. is 41 years old and is married with a child.   She sells hair extensions at retail prices to her customers. This is the high season for her business, and she hopes to meet the demands of her customers.   She hopes for a loan of NGN 70,000 to purchase more hair extensions to sell. She hopes to expand her business in the future. She loves this business because of the personal interaction that she has with her customers. She says thanks to all Kiva lenders.

name: Rosa Obdulia
description: Sra. Rosa is a member of the Communal Bank “Bankito Progresista” (Little Progressive Bank).  She lives in Cuenca, which is the most visited city because of the beauty of its colonial center.  Cuenca is surrounded by four rivers and its people have maintained their culture and traditions.  A large variety of cuisines are available to captivate the taste buds of both locals and foreigners alike.   	 Doña Rosa is 34 years old, married, and has four children (ages 15, 14, 12, and 7).  Her oldest child works, the next two attend high school, and the youngest is enrolled at an elementary school in the city.  Her husband works as a merchant.  They own the house in which they live.  Sra. Rosa is a merchant who sells all types of meats.  She has been in this business for 15 years.  Rosa has her own shop at a market in the city.  She works from 5am to 3pm.    Rosa is receiving her fifth loan with the Communal Bank.  This new loan will be invested in the purchase of meat for her business.  Her dream is to not have any debts.

name: Kweterana Kyabatega Farmers Group
description: Tegrasi lives in the town of Masindi, Uganda. He is married with 6 children. He grows maize and beans to earn a living.  Tegrasi is a member of Kweterana Kyabatega group, where members guarantee each other in order to acquire a loan. He dreams of constructing a permanent house for his family. However, pesticides, infertile soils, and price fluctuation affect his business.  Tegrasi would like to acquire a loan to prepare his garden (weeding, ploughing, and buying fertilizers) in preparation for the next season.

name: Tep
description: Tep N. now resides in Siem Reap province. He is a 27-year-old single man who earns a daily income as a repairer of the machine that is used to link boats for local fishermen, and he also sells and rents the boat machine for additional profit. He currently lives with his father who has the same occupation.   Tep N. is going to use his loan funds as capital in order to buy more additional machinery tools for resale.

name: Mónica
description: With her previous loan, Mónica was able to improve her sales and invest in merchandise such as food products, sweets, and caramels to restock her business and sell at every opportunity.  She currently offers professional services, such as beauty consulting, and has also done very well in these ventures.  At one point, business was slow and she encountered financial difficulty, but she was able to recover.   Mónica plans to improve the services to her customers and buy a larger quantity of food products and various merchandise to restock her business and gain better positioning.    Her message to Kiva lenders is as follows:  "I am grateful to Fundación Mario Santo Domingo and Kiva for the financial resources that have been given to me so that I can continue my business and improve my family life, as well as grow personally and financially.  I hope to continue receiving your support."

name: Edson
description: Edson a married man with children is requesting a loan to buy fish to sell. He lives in Bundibugyo, Uganda, where he grows cocoa, which is the major economic activity for people in this area and he operates a stall where he sells fish and cassava flour in the market. He acquired starting capital from the cocoa business and has no regrets about starting his business because he has been able to achieve a lot through paying school fees for the children and starting up the building of his residential house. Edson dreams of formalizing his marriage through introducing his wife by paying dowry and wedding her, plus completing his house, though he lacks enough capital to do so.

name: Anastasiya
description: Anastasiya M. is 26. She is married with two children. Anastasiya is selling makeup and cosmetics. She has been in the business for two years already. Anastasiya is dreaming of expanding her business and opening her own store.  She wants to establish contacts with the constant suppliers of well-known producers. Anastasiya and her husband are working hard in order to have sufficient funds for educating of their kids so that they become highly sought-after experts in the future.   Now Anastasiya requests US $900 in order to purchase new make-up, such as lipsticks, mascaras, powder, skin cream, etc. with the aim of increasing the range of goods she sells. Anastasiya would like to thank everybody supporting her and promises to pay the loan.   More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists, and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History  Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Hoeun
description: Mrs. Hoeun L. and her husband, Mr. Sin Kroch, both 46-year-old silk weavers living on an island of the Mekong River about 15 kilometers from Phnom Penh, were married in 1980 and have five children, two sons and three daughters. One of their children is married and lives outside the family house; three study in local school, and one daughter is acquiring tailoring skills.   Hoeun has been a silk weaver for 20 years, a skill she learned from her relatives. She sells her finished products to the middleman, who then takes them to sell in Phnom Penh. Hoeun is now requesting a loan of $600 to purchase additional silk material for weaving.

name: Miguelina
description: Mrs. Miguelina, is a customer of the Communal Bank “Las Orquideas II”, Tarapoto District, San Martin Province, San Martin Department.  She is married, 48 years old and mother of 3 children all of whom are still her dependents.  Miguelina is devoted to her family, joyous and charismatic.  Her qualities help her in her line of business, the sale of beauty products from the “Esika” brand.  She has many years in this and has an established clientele.  Her sales are paid in cash or credit, payments are maD. on a daily, weekly, biweekly or monthly basis.  With a loan of 1000 soles she will buy beauty products such as: aftershaves, perfumes for men and women, fashion jewelry, earrings, necklaces and rings.    Her goal is to strengthen her business and have a good stock of products to satisfy her regular customers.  Miguelina’s dream is for her business to grow and be a top seller.  She is grateful with the Manuela Ramos movement for helping her and other women like her start their business and grow personally and professionally. Translated from Spanish by Andrea Wright, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sitren
description: Sitren, age 30, lives in a rural village in the Sampov Meas District. She has two dependent children – one of whom is in school, while the remaining one is too young for school. She is a rice farmer who grows rice on 2.5 hectares of farmland, while her husband is a paid worker. Having been in this business for ten years, Sitren is able to earn about 60,000 riels (KHR) per day to meet the family’s needs.  Sitren has been with VisionFund for one cycle and completely paid back her past loan, which has helped her relieve their financial burden and improve their livelihood. Now she is requesting a new loan of 610,000 KHR to buy a hand tractor for supporting her paddy business. She hopes to make more income from her rice paddy, so as to make a better living and keep her children in school.

name: Joice
description: Joice K. is currently in the business of selling beans, simsim, bread and fish by the side of the road and is requesting a loan to stock more bags of simsim and beans to sell. Joice is 30 years old and is married, with a husband who is a soldier. She has one child, who does not go to school. With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to expand her business.

name: Embala
description: Embala is 29 years old and lives in the Azerbaijani town of Khachmaz with his two children. He has been running a general store for four years and is applying for  a loan of $1,200 to buy more goods for the store. He hopes that offering more goods in his general store will help improve his income.

name: Erika
description: Through her 30,000-square-foot storage facility, Erika says she “provides a secure, full-service storage operation, for short and long-term storage,” in her hometown of Houston, Texas. The 30-year-old runs her business with one part-time and three full-time employees and plans to hire two full-time employees in the future.   “Our dry storage space offers high standards of pest control and cleanliness, giving our customers the peace of mind that their product retains its integrity,” she says. “Storing product in our warehouses allows our customers to operate their business in a fast adequate time frame.”  To allow her business to become more efficient, Erika turned to a friend for advice: Accion Texas Inc. was the non-profit microlender recommended to keep the warehouse, Vee Express, operating as projected. The 10-month-old business is growing to the point where Erika ventured to Accion for a loan to fund the purchase of another forklift.  “At Vee Express we specialize in handling and storing plastic polymers and resins of any type…. Storing your product with us not only allows you easy access to one of the biggest ports in the world, but it also allows your product to be stored in an important hub for chemicals or petrochemicals, making your company that much more competitive,” she describes. View her website for more information: www.vee-express.com/.

name: Joselito
description: Joselito D. is from the village of South Cogon, Misamis Oriental. He is 45 years old. Joselito is married and has 4 adult-aged children. To make a living, Joselito owns & operates a business venture in the retail sector running a sari-sari (variety) retail shop. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling both food & daily use products in the local community. Joselito has been engaged in his business for over 2 years and earns approximately 10000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Joselito joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Joselito has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to purchase additional products to sell. Joselito is requesting a new loan of 4000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional inventory & working capital. This loan will be the 5th loan taken out by Joselito from HSPFI. He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand the borrower's business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Yhon Oscar
description: Yhon Oscar is 22, and lives in Ica, Peru. Ica is located in the Sechura Desert, close to four hours south of Lima, the capital of the country. It is celebrated by Peruvians as the "The Land of the Sun."  It is known in Peru for its frequent earthquakes (an 8.0 in 2007, and 6.9 in 2011), its production of grapes, asparagus, and olives, and perhaps especially, as the source of the traditional national drink of Peru, pisco. The home and business of the client is found in this warm and arid climate.  Yhon drives a mototaxi. He works 10 hours a day. In one day, Yhon can serve 50 customers, and this allows him to earn up to 40 soles a day and on a good day, he can earn up to 60 soles. This helps him meet some extra household expenses, and allows him to invest in his business. He thinks that it's going well due to the fact that he is friendly with the customers.  Yhon is very grateful to the Kiva lenders, as thanks to the support he has been offered, he will be able to make the down payment on his mototaxi. With this improvement, he won't have to pay to rent it anymore, as he didn't have is own.  In this way, he will be able to continue saving to fulfill his great dream, "To have a mototaxi company."

name: Sofia
description: Sofia is studying for a degree in accounting. Her goals are to finish her studies and to grow professionally. She wants to work in companies where she can apply what she's learned. Sofia is requesting this loan to pay for tuition fees and thus continue studying.

name: Ayida
description: Ayida is 24 years old, married and has 2 children. Ayida has a secondary-specialized education and has been involved in agriculture since 2009. Her business consists of 2 cows, 6 sheep, 3 goats, and also 1.60 hectares of irrigated land, where she grows tomatoes, cotton and onions. Ayida is known as an honest, decent and reliable person with strong principles. Today, her business yields a monthly profit in the amount of 22,000 som (KGS) from sales of milk, livestock and agricultural products. Ayida is a participant of the "Kyzyl-Tuu" group that, besides her, is made up of two more people. There are three of them all together. In order to further develop her business, Ayida requested a loan in the amount of 20,000 som (KGS) from the "Bai-Tushum" Bank to buy two calves. She plans to use the earnings from the loan to develop her business and intends to buy a car for her family.

name: Krouch
description: Mrs. Krouch L., 40, works as a farmer, generally making about 3 dollars a day. Her husband Mr. Sok Houy, 29, is a wedding chef making on average in profit US$ 5.00 a day. This couple has two daughters and both of them are students. To produce more profit they are now requesting a loan to purchase pigs to raise and resell  when they are grown up for profit.

name: Lorn's Group
description: Lorn’s group live in a rural village in Kampong Speu province in Cambodia. Lorn makes a living cultivating rice and she also does extra work as a tailor to support her family. In their village, there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Davit
description: Davit is a taxi driver from Yerevan town. He lives with his retired mother and likes his job as a taxi driver.   Davit applied for this loan to pay for renovation of his car and bring it to normal working condition. He has been approved for a loan within the framework of a joint initiative between Kiva and SEF International. The start-up loan program provides business start-up loans with soft conditions to informal businesses that do not have access to credit products.  Davit hopes to receive lenders' support, as this work is the only source of income for his family.

name: Les Fideles Des Dilaire Group
description: Paulimus is the coordinator of his group Fideles de Dilaire. He is not married, and he has three children. He lives in northern Haiti, where electricity is rare and potable water is very limited. Paulimus has been running his business selling cosmetic products for the last seven years. He hopes that this loan will help him to expand his commerce.   Other members of Fideles de Dilaire have need of a loan for businesses selling products, such as cosmetics, charcoal, shoes, etc.  He says that his main challenge is to become a bigger merchant. His main goal is to have a larget business, which will facilitate the construction of a larger house with loans from Esperanza Int.

name: Jessenia Margarita
description: Jessenia, age 24, lives in Guayaquil.  She started her business selling ‘fomix’ [craft foam] products by order to her friends.  Later, she was able to make and buy pillows in order to get more customers and to be able to distribute more products.  The difficulties that she has are thieves and people who do not pay.  She is not married, and she has a two year old child.  Her dream is to continue together with her child, to be able to have her own house, to grow her business, to contribute financially so they are not in need, and to brighten up her life.  Therefore, she wants to use the loan to buy fomix and pillows in order to improve her income and to make her dreams come true.

name: Alfredo
description: Alfredo, 40, lives in a common-law partnership together with his wife, with whom he has four children and they live in the town of Nueva Frontera, Santa Bárbara. He has always worked in agriculture, growing corn and beans, but 18 years ago he decided to grow coffee which he sells in grains in the same area.   Alfredo is requesting the second loan cycle which is for 10,000 Lempiras and which he will use to buy fertilizers and pay to clear the crop, therein improving the crop and obtaining larger profits.

name: Gabriela
description: Gabriela is a person who is striving to become somebody in life. For this reason, she puts all her efforts into becoming a good professional. She says that she used the previous loan to pay her university fees, which meant she was able to continue with her studies.  She says that when she finishes university, she wants to be able to continue training so she can grow in her profession.  She is requesting a new loan so she can pay her university fees again.

name: Cirila
description: Cirila is from Tambo Real, a rural community located in the Zurite district of Anta, approximately an hour and a half from the city of Cusco. She is forty-eight years old and married with five children.  Cirila makes dairy products at home from the milk that her cows produce. Every weekend she sells cheeses at the Huancaro market in Cusco for 2 to 3 soles (approximately 75 cents to $1). Right now the space she has to keep her cows is too small. She plans to use the loan to build an enclosed area in front of her house to comfortably hold them (the picture shows the land that will be developed).   Cirila is a member of the Real Solidarity Bank, made up of fourteen members who are in their second loan cycle with Arariwa. They are collectively committed to repaying the loan on time, and are also collaborating in a group savings account that serves as emergency funds for their members should anyone default.

name: Enhtuya
description: Enhtuya is a 29-year-old woman who lives with her husband and two children in Ger, in the Bulgan Province, Mongolia. Her husband is a driver in the Ikh-Alt LLC.   Enhtuya graduated from the university and has been working as a salesperson in clothing retail for 2 years now. She has obtained lots of experience in this business, and now she is planning to open her own clothing retail business. Her short-term plan is to own a clothes shop in her own place. She is requesting 1,600,000 MNT to purchase clothes and other goods to sell at her retail counter.

name: Amal
description: Amal is a conservative person who prefers not to have her photo published online, so her husband appears in this photo.  Amal is a 32-year-old married woman from Deir el Balah City. She lives with her husband, son and daughter in a small simple house. Her husband works as an employee in the public sector where he earns a very low income. Amal and her husband would like to improve the family home and buy the stuff they need.   Amal took a USD loan from FATEN. This loan will help her to buy a water purification machine for her home. By taking this loan, Amal will be able to provide pure water for her family.

name: Seng
description: Seng, age 44, is married with four children, two of whom are themselves married. One of their single children is a sewing worker.   She is a domestic rice farmer in the Prey Chor district. Aside from her current occupation, she also sells sugar cane juice in front of her house for extra income as the photo above shows.   Her husband is a motor taxi driver in the local market and earns a profit of about $1.50 per day. Usually Seng generates around $1.60 of profit a day to meet the needs of her family.   Previously she prepared the wedding party for one of her children, but hasn't paid for some of the expenses yet. This is the main reason she has decided to seek a loan: to pay the remaining wedding-ceremony expenses.

name: Akosua
description: Akosua  is a seamstress.  She is married to a teacher and has 2 children. Akosua has been sewing for 8 years now. She uses her income to assist her husband to pay their utility bills. Akosua makes dresses for sale so she needs a loan to purchase fabrics for the dresses she makes. With the new profit, she will expand her business.

name: Clemencia
description: Clemencia P., 54 years old, is from the village of Sto.Niño, Tukuran Zamboanga Del Sur. She is married and has two older children. To make a living, Clemencia owns and operates a hair salon and beauty parlor. While not the only means for generating revenue, she has been engaged in her business for over two years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2008, Clemencia joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Clemencia has successfully repaid a previous loan of 7,000 PHP from GDMPC. This previous loan was used to purchase materials needed to provide services. Clemencia is requesting a new loan of 7,000 PHP which will be used to purchase materials needed to expand her business. This loan will be the third loan taken out by Clemencia from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living condition of her family.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.
town: Sto. Niño, Tukuran, Zamboanga del Sur

name: Ali
description: Ali is a resident of western Kenya where he has farmed for 12 years with the help of one farmhand.  His farm produces eggs, bananas and beans which he sells at the local market.  He also does carpentry work for additional income.  Ali requests a loan of 70,000 KES to purchase more poultry birds and milk cans for his dairy farming business.  He is optimistic that his dairy business will double in size in five years, and this will help him improve his family's standard of living.  Ali laments rampant animal diseases and the high cost of farm inputs.

name: Adelaida
description: Adelaida is 39 years old, a teacher, and an entrepreneur. She performs well in her job as a teacher and efficiently manages her direct selling business, photocopying services, and school canteen. It’s amazing how she tackles all these tasks besides raising her five children with Rufino, also a businessman.   Just recently she was promoted in her direct selling business. It means she has to handle and train several dealers under her. At times she has to pay in advance for pre-ordered products for her dealers, especially if the dealers have insufficient capital. Adelaida needs supplementary capital to sustain her new responsibility. A PHP 20,000 would be very helpful for her. She will use it to pay for shoes, sandals, ready-to-wear clothes, bags, personal care and household products.   All of her endeavors are geared toward complete college educations for her five children. She also wishes to purchase a lot for future investment. Regarding her business, she envisions it will expand from municipal to provincial wide. She’s a woman of many dreams and big faith to achieve all of them.   Adelaida is a devoted member of CCT Credit Cooperative and she regularly meets with her co-fellowship members every week to share stories of her life and business. She also draws strength and inspiration from the fellowship and the Word of God. All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Ludovic
description: Ludovic is a Cameroonian, aged 37 and married, with seven children. The oldest is 19 and in high school, while the youngest is 2 and in nursery school. Ludovic has been in this business for the past four years, which makes her very stable and experienced. This loan will increase her turnover from 750,000 to 950,000 XAF. Her standard of living will be improved as well.

name: Patrocinia
description: Patrocinia is from Inroad, Aurora, Zamboanga del Sur. She is 33 years old, married and has five children.   To make a living, Patrocinia owns and operates a general store. Patrocinia is been two years in this business and earns 3,000 PHP a month.   In 2007, Patrocinia joined Kiva partner GDMPC. Patrocinia is requesting a loan of 5,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products like canned goods, noodles, sugar and coffee. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the loan to improve her family's general living conditions.

name: Savuth's Group
description: Savuth’s group live in a rural village in Kampong Speu province in Cambodia. Savuth makes a living cultivating rice and he also does extra work as a tailor to support his family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women and men safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses, and save time spent collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Cecilia
description: Cecilia is 52 years old and married with six children. She works very hard to provide for them.She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional stocks like rice, soap, sardines, etc. to sell.Cecilia has been in this business for 10 years.She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: C8687 Duharanirekujyambere Group
description: Uwimana F. is 43 years old and married with 8 children, aged 2 through 21 years old.  Together they live in the Rubavu district in Gisenyi province, near Kigali.   Uwimana's business employs 7 other people in her community and has been in existence since 1999, making this her 10 year anniversary of successful operation! The hours of her successful retail banana business are from 8AM - 5PM daily.  She serves locals and passers-by delicious, fresh bananas and for this she projects a monthly profit of 40,000 RWF (approximately US$ 80).  This loan will help her to buy more inventory and get better pricing which will help her to become more profitable and efficient.    This is Uwimana's second loan from VFC and her previous loan was repaid in full and on time.  She is grateful to VFC and Kiva for their support of her business.

name: Rosalina
description: Rosalina is 48 years old and married, with six children to look after. She has a small bakery shop. She is applying for a loan of $600 from TRM to improve her business. She will use the loan to buy flour, oil, blue band, sugar, and a stove. She opened her bakery shop a year ago with her own working capital of $50.

name: Raul
description: Raúl, 28, is single and has a son.  He manufactures Alpaca wool sweaters in a small workshop he has in Cusco.  He works in his workshop making Alpaca sweaters in quantity with his staff and then sells them in different crafts markets.  He also works to fill third-party orders.  He is asking for funds to buy Alpaca wool dyed in a variety of colors and in natural state.  He is a member of the “NUEVA VICTORIA - CHINCHERO” (Chinchero New Victory) communal bank located in Chinchero district, Urubamba province, Cusco department.  It’s located 45 minutes from the city.  He avails himself of this forum to express his gratitude for the loan and to commit to repay it in a timely fashion.  Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Juana
description: Ms. Juana Gonzalez lives in the community of San Francisco [Mexico]. Her business is selling produce at the market in her community, and also traveling around. She says "I cannot wait and sell only in one spot because I don't run out of merchandise that way. That's why I must move around and that is the most difficult part of my business: traveling all around on weekends." This is difficult because she has to load and unload the merchandise, and in addition to the physical labor also runs the risk of having the fruit spoil.   She has asked for this loan to earn a greater income and thus lead a better life. Her dream is to sell much more produce, and see her business grown. With the earnings, she plans to fix up her house and pay the education expenses of her children, which is very important to her. Juana has 5 children, three of whom depend on her and her husband.  Juana is 43 years old and has been married for 13 years. Her business is a family one, since her husband also works selling fruit and vegetables.

name: Nelly
description: Nelly is 30 years old and is married with 2 daughters, one who is 5 and the other just turned 9 months. Her husband, Paulino, works purchasing and selling bricks, a business which he carries out in the capital city.   Nelly is a hairdresser and has worked in this profession for the past 8 years. Coming from a poor family, she was only able to study up to her third year in high school. For this reason, she decided to study hairdressing and work in this profession to earn a living.   Due to her hard work and entrepreneurship,  she has established a good clientele and has even managed to acquire another location that she is currently working on furnishing. Nelly needs a loan in order to purchase things like mirrors, chairs, and sinks so that she can open this new branch of her business.

name: Mary
description: Mary P. is a 52 year old woman. She is married and has six children. Three are in school and the rest are traders in the market. She lives with her husband in her matrimonial home in  Koforidua, a suburb of Offinso in the Ashanti region of Ghana.   Mary has traded in bananas, oranges and plantains in the Koforidua market for more than ten years. She treks to surrounding villages in the central part of Ghana to purchase bulk stocks of bananas, oranges and plantains from the farmers and then sells retail to her customers. For lack of adequate working capital, Mary is not able to buy enough stock to make a sufficient profit to support her family. Mary is asking for a loan of $750. With the loan, she wants to purchase bulk supplies of bananas, oranges and plantains to enable her to increase her sales. She believes the loan would allow her to save more income which she could use for her children's education. Mary belongs to a village bank called ‘DaNyame ASE’ which means "Give thanks to God".

name: Peter
description: Peter started wheat farming in 2000. He is 34 and married to Christine Nkosira. They have two children.  He was introduced to KADET by his friend and this will be his second loan. He applied for a first loan of Kshs 35,000 which he repaid on time. He plans to use the new loan amount to buy fertilizer and pesticide for the wheat in his farm. Peter hopes to buy his own tractor in the future to use on his own farm and also get extra income by hiring it out to other farmers.

name: Tatyana
description: Tatyana is single and is a successful entrepreneur from Mukachevo. Tatyana sells perfumes in one of the busy local markets. She has been in this business for about 5 years and her products have been in stable demand over the years.    Presently, Tatyana has about $2,000 in inventory. She has a long-term view of her business development and is disciplined with all her business plans. All this has promoted the successful growth of her business. Moreover, Tatyana is not afraid of serious amounts of hard work which reveal her great entrepreneurial potential and allow her to make prompt loan repayments. Tatyana is requesting a 5,000 Grivna loan to increase the variety of perfumes sold in her store.

name: Sadriddin
description: E. Sadriddin has always been a hard-working man, who has made sure from a young age that his family never went hungry. He is married with two children. Six years ago, and with a starting capital of only $100, Sadriddin started a grocery store for selling different kinds of foodstuffs. Thanks to his perseverance and dedication, his business has expanded and now his whole family is involved.   Today Sadriddin needs to increase the range of goods he sells.  For this purpose he is requesting a loan of $900.  He is ready to work even harder and to make sacrifices to achieve his goal of becoming a successful entrepreneur.                More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC. Even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History  Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Chantha
description: Mrs. T. Chantha has been married since 1978 and has 5 children: 2 sons and 3 daughters. She learned to weave from her neighbor in 1971 and was soon afterwards employed to weave for the village. She started her own home-based silk-weaving business in 1981. Now her 3 daughters weave silk at home as well. Mrs. T.'s husband is a motor taxi driver in Phnom Penh city.   She is requesting a loan from MAXIMA for the first time. Mrs. T. will use the US$500 to purchase silk materials, sewing thread, and fees for selecting and preparing silk for her daughters' weaving looms.

name: Shadi
description: Shadi is a 37-year-old man from Jabalia City, married and father to two sons and a one little daughter.  Shadi was living with his family in a small humble house, but during the latest war on Gaza, his house was destroyed completely, so he had to rent a small apartment in the same area.  Recently Shadi took a USD loan from Palestine for Credit and Development (FATEN) to help repair part of his old house. The loan will allow Shadi to finalize the needed construction in a short time and return his family to their normal life.

name: San Cayetano Group
description: The San Cayetano committee was formed by a group of friends and works with hope for the goals of each.  The members formed a group that is very united and capable of accomplishing activities together that strengthen their unity.  One of them is Mrs. Nilda, who does many things within the Committee with the help of her fellow members.  One of these things is preparing food for sale.  She makes her dishes and transports them to the market where there are many people to sell to.  Her job takes sacrifice, as she must get up very early to work and take the bus to market, but she wants the best for her children and for her husband, who is a day laborer.  She is thankful for the loan, as it will help her work, and she will use it to buy meat, seasonings, flour, pastries, and other ingredients.Translated from Spanish by Zach Powell, Kiva Volunteer

name: Susana
description: Susana is a 28 year-old married woman with two children. She makes and sells ice cakes (flavored water frozen in cups) in her community to earn a living. She has one year of experience with this business. Susana needs a loan to improve her business. She plans to use her profits to improve her business and family needs. Susana has been a member of Kiva partner SPBD since 2011.

name: Munavvar
description: Munavvar N. is 50 years old and has a secondary-level education. He is married and has 6 children. Munawar grew up in a poor family and always loved cars. He participated in a driving course and worked as a driver in an organization where he drove a truck. He has a lot of experience with driving. Nowadays he has his own truck and provides a transferring service. He transfers sand and crushed stone for building purposes. This kind of activity has a big demand among local habitants. The truck needs repair so Munawar needs money to buy a new engine. For the loan amount of $1000, Munawar is going to buy a new engine for his truck and provide his services for local habitants. He is going to pay off the loan amount over 12 months.

name: Cipriana
description: Forty-eight-year-old Cipriana is a strong and hard-working woman.  She became a widow sixteen years ago and has since cared for her six children, two of which live with her in the home that her community granted her twenty years ago.  She has extensive areas of land in her community, thanks to her efforts in agriculture, an activity that she has carried out since she was a young girl.    She has managed to acquire the economic support to care for her children.  She plants pumpkin, corn, and potato seeds.  In her fruit orchard she also has apples, cherimoya, and some citrus fruits.  "I do whatever type of agricultural activity to make the necessary money," she says.  She has spent more than twenty years in agriculture.  She gained all of her experience thanks to her parents and grandparents, who were also farmers.    Now she finds herself in the corn harvest and preparing the land to plant pumpkin seeds.  "I am working without stopping, hiring laborers to help me.  I am sure that this season will be good," she affirms.    This is her ninth loan with MFP.  In this new opportunity, she promises to be punctual with her repayments.  The financial support that she has already received helps her to improve the quality of her animals.  She likes to work with her association.  Cipriana will invest her money in buying balanced food for her animals and in pumpkin seeds for sowing.

name: Jocelyn
description: Jocelyn is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a welding shop business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 23,000 through NWTF to buy additional materials and equipment for her welding shop.  Jocelyn has been in this business for 13 years. Jocelyn earns more income from tricycle transport.  Jocelyn has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams of saving money to expand her business.

name: Basma
description: Basma, 48 years old and widowed, is caring for seven sons and daughters.  Being an illiterate woman has limited her chances in getting a job to support the family, and for that reason she opened her own business which is a food products store.   She has applied for this loan to bring in more food products and other goods for the store.

name: Joseph
description: Mr. Joseph is an old client who has applied for a loan of UGX 2,000,000 to buy cows for his business. He is 54 years old and married with six children; three of whom attend school. His business is cattle trading and his customers are cattle traders. His business is located in Kitwe, Kyabugimbi, Igara, Bushenyi District. He is a hard-working man who works eight hours a day and six days a week. Joseph is faced with the challenge of competition but he is ready to overcome it through his hard work. He hopes to grow his business and become financially stable.

name: Edilina
description: Edilina is 46 years old and married. She has five children. She is in the agricultural business, fattening pigs in the Philippines.Edilina has requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF. She will use the loan to purchase feed, vitamins, and other supplies for her pigs. She has been in pig fattening for five years now, and has borrowed five times in the past from NWTF, to sustain it.She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Irma Luz
description: 43-year-old Irma studied up until the sixth grade. Her partner is a day labourer. She has four children, who live with them. Two of her children are working. Only one of her children (a daughter) is studying; she is currently in the eighth grade.  Irma has been selling pupusas (stuffed tortillas) for more than ten years, and she has had a store for five years. She started her business in order to contribute towards paying for the household expenses. When her partner comes back from work, he helps her to sell her products. They open the store early every day and she makes the pupusas in the afternoon and evening.  She needs the loan in order to build a small café to put the store in, since at the moment it is in a room of her house and it takes up a lot of space. For this reason, she will use the loan to pay workers and to buy cinder blocks, cement, sand, and iron.  She hopes that her business will keep increasing and attracting more clients every day so that it becomes a large store in the future. She also hopes that her daughter finishes the school year with good grades.

name: Philister
description: Philister lives in the Litein area of Kenya, which houses a campus of Mt. Kenya University. She has three children and has been farming for 15 years. Her primary income source is from selling milk. She stated what is most enjoyable about farming: 'feeding the cows, and milking!' Her biggest challenge is the high cost of feeds. The cow is named 'Lelkina'.  Philister was asked why she chose Juhudi Kilimo for this loan, to which she replied: 'existence of grace period'.  This client was also asked what was learned during Juhudi's required micro-finance training to which she replied 'loan management'.  Her highest monthly expense is school fees. When asked 'How will this loan benefit your family?', Philister replied 'Family income will increase'.  As part of Juhudi's loan appraisal process, each borrower's assets are evaluated. Philister owns a cow but does not own 'pig, poultry, pump, bicycle, motorcycle, automobile'. Juhudi Kilimo also tries to measure any change in living standards based on this loan. This borrower has in the household 'mosquito net, running water' but does not have 'electricity, solar power, sewing machine, TV, DVD'.  Note: To create this loan profile, Juhudi Kilimo used a mobile device to gather information in the field and send the data to a central online repository, thus reducing paper use, making the process more efficient, and keeping costs down.

name: Angelina
description: Angelina is 55-years-old and married with eleven children.  Angelina works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 6,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional stock to sell like sugar, coffee, eggs, chips, etc.  Angelina has borrowed and paid five loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for two years and also earns an income from farming rice.  Angelina aspires to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Kapamba Group
description: Segereta M. is in her early forties and is married with three children. For the past two years, Seregeta has been running her own pharmacy shop . The store is open between 08:00 am and 09:00 pm and earns Seregeta a low monthly profit.   This will be Segereta's second "Motisha" loan with Tujijenge Tanzania. A "Mothisha" loan is a product offered by Tujijenge Tanzania that allows borrowers with good credit ratings to pay back their original loans faster and receive extra money before their original loan term has ended. Segereta used her previous loan to increase the stock of medicine for her business. This loan has now been successfully repaid. With her second loan, Segereta aims to once again increase her stock of medicine. Segereta's dream is to one day have a big and modern pharmacy.   Segereta will share this loan with her loan group Kapamba, which totals 9 members. The members of the group will hold each other accountable for repaying the loans.   In the picture, Segereta can be seen wearing white and black, 1st on the right.

name: Nawal
description: Nawal is a married woman from Lebanon. She is 43 years old and lives with her husband and three children in Chouf area. Nawal is a beauty specialist and she works individually and at her house. She provides waxing, makeup, scrub, and mask services. She applied for a loan from Kiva's partner Ibdaa for the first time to buy new products for her business and pay part of the college tuition for her daughter. She requested 1,543,658 Lebanese pounds and she aims to grow her business and increase her income to support her family.

name: Cruz Del Carmen
description: Cruz del Carmen is 46 years old, single, has one dependent child and lives in the Nacaome community in the south of Honduras. She has her own home and has worked for seven years selling groceries. She is a hard working woman with hopes of getting ahead. Cruz del Carmen is very thankful for Prisma for the support they have always given her when she needs it. In this instance, she is asking for a loan in order to stock her business with products such as basic grains, juice, meat, cold cuts, detergent, flour, sweets, etc. She is a client with various loan cycles and hopes that this investment will allow her to carry her family forward and be able to cover her household expenses.San Lorenzo, Honduras – September 2015.

name: Tomás
description: Tomas is a married man of 37. He lives in Sololá department with his eight children. He has three boys: the eldest does tailoring and the other two go to school and help maintain the family's plot of land. He has five girls: three of them help with the household chores and the other two are minors.   He is currently a tailor; previously he worked in agriculture, but because of economic circumstances decided to opt for this activity, which has generated greater income and earnings.   He comments that he is been doing this work for 18 years which has helped to contribute to the family's finances, so now he is requesting a loan of 3,000 quetzals to buy construction materials so that he can renovate his house. He will pay this loan with the income and earnings that he generates from his business. His dream is to finish building his home so that he can improve his family's living conditions.

name: Buscando El Exito  (Cuenca) Group
description: The "Buscando el Éxito" communal bank is made up of 15 members, the majority of whom work in a market in the city, and carry on various businesses, such as selling fruit and vegetables or preparing and selling food. These businesses give them the opportunity of improving their household finances and helping their families move forward in life.   All are enterprising women who seek prosperity. They live in various parts of Cuenca, a city that has a cold climate. Its historic center is a mix of modern and colonial architecture, and it has a great variety of traditional cuisine that delights the palate. Its people still keep alive their culture and traditions.   One of the members of this group is Nancy. She is taking out her second loan as a  member of the "Buscando el Éxito" communal bank. She lives in the Totoracocha area of the city Cuenca. She is 40 years old, married, and has three children, ages 16,14 and 5. Her first two children go to a school in the city, and her youngest child goes to preschool.   Her husband is a merchant, and the house where they live belongs to them. Nancy does her household chores and spends her time looking after the whole family.   To help with the household finances, she works knitting a great variety of items, such as scarves and sweaters. She learned this work on her own, as she had an aptitude for it. Now she sells to her friends and acquaintances. She is going to use the loan to buy yarn, so that she can continue this work.  Her goal is to have a restaurant.

name: Akossiwa
description: Born on January 19, 1978 in Kévé in the Zio region, Mrs. Akossiwa K. is one of a large family that has known many hardships.  She was adopted by her uncle and was taught how to do business by his wife.  Very early on she began an onion business.  Married and a mother of two children, she also takes care of another child from a deceased aunt.  She has been selling onions for the last three years, which allows her to contribute money to support the family.  Her husband is a tailor who does not have enough business as he does not have a studio of his own.  Very dynamic and an entrepreneur, she is a good business woman and has thus far been able to reimburse all of the loans she has received.    At this time she would like to improve her business by buying in bulk quantities from Burkina Faso.  In order to do this she is asking for a credit of $900 which will serve as funds to use when placing the order, stocking and selling the ognions.  Translated from French by Chloe Tuot, a Kiva Volunteer.  Née le 19 Janvier 1978 à Kévé dans la préfecture du Zio,Madame K. Akossiwa est issue d’une famille nombreuse et a connu toutes les difficultés. Adoptée par son oncle, elle a appris à faire du commerce avec sa femme. Très tôt elle a su se prendre en charge et s’est lancée dans le commerce des oignons. Mariée et mère de deux (02) enfants, elle a à sa charge un (01) enfant de sa tante décédée. Cela fait 3 ans qu’elle exerce cette activité de vente d’oignon très florissante, ce qui lui permet de contribuer aux charges du ménage. Son mari est un maître tailleur qui n’a pas assez de clientèle car il n’a pas d’atelier. Très dynamique et entreprenante, elle arrive à bien gérer ses activés et a su rembourser tous les  crédits qu’elle a obtenus.   Elle souhaite aujourd’hui améliorer son commerce en commandant en gros ses produits depuis le Burkina Faso. Pour cela elle sollicite un crédit de $900 qui va servir de fonds de commerce pour la commande, le stockage et la revente des oignons.

name: Porvenir 1 Group
description: This group is called Porvenir 1. It has this name because all the members are united in searching for a good future (porvenir) for their families by working together. They are also part of a poverty elimination program.  Miryan is one of the members and, in the last evaluation, was found to be at level one for poverty, which is to say that in many of the evaluation categories she had a low score. She works selling fast food that she also makes and then sells herself in the street. She is an enterprising woman who is fighting to get ahead.  Myrian is requesting this loan to buy meat, condiments, chicken, ham, cheese, and more so that she can keep making her meals and so to be able to fight to help her family every day.

name: Senderos De Paz Group
description: The “Senderos de Paz” (Peaceful Pathways) is comprised of five members. The have different economic activities in the village of El Carbonal in Silca, Olancho.  Prisca Beatriz C. is the coordinator of the group.  She is 46 years old, married, and has six children.  She lives with her family in the El Carbonal village in the municipality of Silca, Olancho.  Prisca started selling some grocery products, and she realized that the earnings were very good.  That is how she decided to establish a small grocery store in her house.  She tends the store herself from 6:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m.  She is requesting the loan to buy sugar, rice, soft drinks, shortening, meat, chicken, sausages, and bread, etc.  With help from the loan she will have a business that is better stocked.  Her customers will be able to find everything they need to prepare their food.  Prisca does not currently have any health problems.  There are periods of time when sales are low, but there are also times when her earnings are good.  Her goal is for the sales in her business to remain stable in order to be able to support her family.  She has been with FAMA for 16 cycles, and she is very grateful for the support she has received.

name: Carla
description: As a married parent of three children, Carla works hard to support her family.  She has a buy and sell charcoal business in the Philippines, and earns additional income from buying and selling coconut. Carla is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to buy additional sacks of charcoal to sell for her buy and sell charcoal business.
