Carla has been sustaining her business activities through her past three loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Lucia
description: Lucia lives in the Alto San Isidro zone, which is located 25 minutes from the center of the city. She is married to Romualdo who works as a construction worker. Together they have five children, two of which are adults while the three minor children are of school age.   Lucia makes a living hand weaving cloth and alpaca wool fabrics. These are artisan fabrics and she sells them at a good price. However, it takes her a week to make a complete piece of fabric and more for the fringe.  Lucia is requesting the loan to buy thread and alpaca wool to weave fabric as she already has an order to fulfill. Her biggest dream is to see her children have a profession and be good people.

name: Erick Cristopher
description: Erick, 28, enjoys playing soccer with his friends in his free time as he considers it to be a relaxing activity after spending the day sitting in his vehicle. This young man is currently living in the city of Ica, a place where one can tour the enormous sand dunes on the famous tubular dune buggies.   Erick works an average of 10 hours a day, time that brings him to different destinations throughout the district of Parcona, Ica, Perú, the place where he is employed. His work is allowing him to progress bit by bit and he is very happy with the income he has received.  With the help of Kiva, Erick will buy a motor taxi, as he is currently working with a rented one. With this support he will earn additional income as he will no longer incur rental costs. Knowing that he will increase his income and profits will allow him to enjoy the dream of owning his own home.

name: Wilkister
description: Wilkister is 26 years old, married to Joseph, and they are blessed with two children. She has been a small-scale farmer for the last eight years, and the business earns her KES 5,000 per month.   Wilkister has applied for her first loan of KES 25,000 from Vision Fund Kenya to buy a dairy cow to supply milk, in order to increase her income. She plans to use the generated profits to repay the loan and start a cereals supply in the area.  Her future hopes are to be financially stable and expand her agricultural produce.

name: Mary Grace
description: To make a living, Mary Grace helps her husband in their fishing business. They have been doing this for more than nine years as their main source of income. She earns well from this, to provide for the family and she had successfully repaid her previous loan from Gata Daku Multi-Purpose Cooperative (GDMPC). She used her loan to purchase fishing materials.   Currently, Mary Grace has taken a new loan  to buy new engine motor of their fishing boat in order to improve her business. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.

name: Khaled
description: Khaled is a 38-year-old man, married and father of three, working in construction. He lives in Beirut and has six years of experience. He makes aluminum frames (for windows and doors) and kitchen cabinets. He is committed to his business and considered an expert in his field. His clients can be anyone in need of such a service. He reports that he has not faced any obstacles because his experience and hard work helped him a lot.  He is requesting his first loan from Al Majmoua in order to buy necessary tools such as a special gun to open holes as well as to fix the bathroom in his own house. In the future, he hopes to open a new branch of his business.

name: Elizabeth
description: As a married mother of two children, Elizabeth works hard to support her family.  She has a clothing retail business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from tricycle passenger.  Elizabeth is borrowing PHP 19,000 through NWTF in order to buy more items like blouses, school uniform, pants and other ready-to-wear clothing to sell.  Elizabeth has been sustaining her business activities through her past 27 loans from NWTF and more recently, through Kiva. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: Laura Ines
description: Laura, 50, was born in city of Lamay, where she lives and earns a living.  She sells basic necessities like rice, sugar, noodles, oil, milk, etc.  She currently needs a loan to buy soft-drinks.  Laura belongs to Asociación Arariwa's "Virgencita de Fátima de Lamay"  [Our Lady of Fátima of Lamay] communal bank in the province of Calca, department of Cusco, Peru.    Laura appreciates and values the loan and promises to make  all of her monthly payments.

name: Daniel
description: Daniel is married. He has been dealing in the produce business for 10 years now. He has the responsibility of paying his children's school fees. He faces a challenge of price fluctuations in his business; however, he manages it by selling a variety of produce like beans and coffee, among others. Daniel now wants to add stock of maize in his shop, it being selling like hotcakes because of the favorable good season. The capital at hand is not enough. He requests credit to buy stock of maize to sell.

name: Hermelinda
description: Hermelinda is 54 years old and married with four children. Hermelinda works very hard to provide for them.  Hermelinda runs a general store in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional items to sell like canned goods, beverages, and groceries.  Hermelinda has been in this business for 5 years.   In the future, Hermelinda would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Nhean's Group
description: A 56-year-old married mother blessed with five children, Nhean supports her entire family via rice cropping and her paid-working job. It is the business that she has had for 15 years. Including this loan, Nhean is a sixth-cycle borrower with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). She has paid back her past loan completely and it has improved her lifestyle gradually.   Now, she leads a group of two to get a new loan. As the leader, she will spend her entire loan portion to buy fertilizer, insecticide and seed. She hopes that she can gain a better yield than before.

name: Antonio
description: Antonio is 49 years old, married and has five children to provide for. To earn a living he engages in cassava production.   He wants to give his family a good living, so he decided to borrow a loan to purchase fertilizer for his cassava farm so that he can produce a good quality of cassava and can sell more cassava in the market that will generate more income.  Antonio's plan for the future is to save money from his business income.

name: Bernardita
description: Bernardita is 57 years old and married with four children. She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and has requested a 19,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy more grocery products like soft drinks, canned goods, etc. to sell.  Bernardita has been in this business for seven years and has previously received funds through Kiva. She aspires to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Tenes Ole
description: Tenes has been in livestock farming for ten years. He is 37 years old, is married to Teeka Ene T., and they have three children.  Tenes was introduced to KADET by his friend and this will be his first loan. He plans to buy ten sheep and five goats to rear and sell later at a profit.  Tenes also wants to build rental houses on his piece of land in the future, and improve his living standard with the increased income.

name: Kweterana Kyabatega Farmers Group
description: Tegrasi is a 74 year old married male who lives in the town of Masindi-Uganda. Tegrasi grows maize, groundnuts, sunflower, and burns charcoal to supplement his income. He needs a loan to buy maize for planting this peak season. Tegrasi has got dream of building a house and educating her children. However he is challenged by weather plus seasonal changes, and price fluctuations.He needs a loan for to buy maize for planting this peak season. Tegrasi is a member of Kweterena Kyabatega group where members guarantee each other in order to acquire a loan.

name: Vine
description: Vine is a married woman of 48 years with 5 children.  Vine owns and operates a business venture, planting and harvesting taro for sale. She has many years of experience in this business. Vine needs a loan of WST $1500 to purchase general farm supplies and equipment. She plans to use the profit from her business (estimated to be 250 talas or US $104 per week) to financially support immediate members of her family.  In 2011, Vine joined SPBD to gain access to financial services. Most of SPBD's clients are unable to borrow from commercial banks, because they lack collateral. This is Vine's 3rd loan with SPBD.     *SPBD evaluates the living conditions of each of its borrowers.  Generally, a loan manager evaluates a variety of social metrics on a scale out of 3 (the higher the number, the better off the person is) and these are averaged for the "overall social metric score."  For example, a 3 out of 3 on "level of education" would mean that the borrower has graduated from university.    About  SPBD  In 2000, Greg Casagrande founded SPBD to improve the quality of life of people living in poverty in the poor island nations of the South Pacific.  SPBD's philosophy of lending is based on a respect for each individual's innate human ingenuity, drive and self esteem. Please join SPBD's lending team on KIVA to receive on-the-spot updates on SPBD.

name: Narciso
description: Narciso lives in Los Limos, located 10km from the Santa Rita community in the town of Torno. He has a 10-hectare lot of land where he plants and raises cattle. He has five children with his wife. Two of them go to school and the others are still too young to go. His wife raises the animals and takes care of the children while he works in agriculture.   The loan will be used to sow rice and sorghum which are the products that bring the most revenue during the year. His wife helps him sell his produce at Torno's market. He is very thankful to the institution for the support he has been granted. 	Translated from Spanish by Betyna Almeida-Covarrubias, Kiva Volunteer

name: Fortunata
description: Fortunata is a member of the “Corí Soncco” Communal Bank which means Heart of Gold in Quechua. Fortunate is married, 56 years old, and has 5 children. Fortunata travels to different markets in the region where she sells general merchandise such as cleaning items, padlocks, flashlights and wool. She does this work with the help of her daughter.  Fortunata needs a loan for 1000 soles which will be investeed in the purchase of flashlights and wool. Fortunata dreams of providing a good education and food to her children.  Translated from Spanish by Cindy Kendall, Kiva Volunteer

name: Mahmadali
description: In recent years construction works around the whole country have been proceeding at an extremely quick pace. Many workers earn a good living at these construction jobs and contribute to the family budget. This man is also one of these construction workers, who is engaged in building homes and buildings. He is Mahmadali. He lives in Hamadoni region. This person is a very professional worker who knows the trends in construction. Mahmadali married a wonderful woman from the neighbouring courtyard for love. She has given him two children. He is a loving husband and father.   Mahmadali cares for his family and tries so that his family wants for nothing. For the past few years this work has provided for his family. His work takes place in cities, where there are regular constructions of houses and different multi-storey buildings. Mahmadali has already gained enough experience and currently he needs to improve the quality of his work with the help of modern tools for construction. This loan is very important to Mahmadali and he is appealing to you for help. He is hoping for your understanding and kindness!

name: Jamila
description: Jamila  lives in  Uganda.  She is married and has three children, two of whom are in school.  She also takes care of additional family members (her in-laws).   Jamila has a food stall.  She has been in this business for over 10 years, and she works 7 days out of every week. Jamila sells her products at the market, by means of retail. Jamila has requested a loan of 600,000 Ugandan Shillings from MCDT SACCO, which she will use to buy more bunches of bananas and sweet and Irish potatoes.   The main business challenges for  Jamila include seasonality, thieves and defaulters.  Her goals and aspirations for her business are to start selling wholesale only and also to start going to villages for foodstuffs.    Jamila lives in a home that she owns; she has access to electricity but doesn't have access to piped water.  Her major monthly expenses include school fees and feeding the family.

name: Fatima
description: Fatima lives at Mabantad with her parents. To make a living, her brother provides daily motorcycle transport services to the people in their village. This way, the family earns about PHP 300 each day and has just enough for meals and daily expenses of their family household. Fatima would like to make improvements in their business so that their income will increase, too.   She would like to ask for a loan of PHP 10,000 to pay for franchise renewal and buy tires and crude oil for the motorcycle. The rest of her loan will be used to buy frozen food to sell for extra income. She would like to ensure safe travel for the passengers and for her brother as well. Fatima is also praying for good health and a happy family.

name: Mbande Group
description: Mwajuma V. is in her mid thirties. She is married and has one son. For the past two years she has been running her own pharmacy. The pharmacy is open between 7:30 am and 9:30 pm and earns Mwajuma a good monthly profit.   This will be Mwajuma's 2nd motisha loan with Tujijenge Tanzania. A Mothisha loan is a product offered by Tujijenge Tanzania that allows borrowers with good credit ratings to pay back their original loans faster and receive extra money before their original loan term has ended. Mwajuma used her first loan to increase her stock of medicine, a loan which she has successfully repaid. With her second loan, Mwajuma aims to once again increase her stock of medicine.  Mwajuma will share this loan will her loan group, Mbande, which totals 8 members. The members of the group will hold each other accountable for repaying the loans.   In the picture, Mwajuma is seen as the woman holding a baby.

name: Marvin Alonso
description: Marvin is a 48-year old man, married and father of three children who are under his responsibility. He is from Managua, located in the central part of the country. He is known for being a hardworking and responsible man with a strong willingness of self-improvement. Unfortunately, he could not attend university and needed to work since he was very young. For this reason, he fights every day to provide his children with a better future.   Thanks to his hard work and willingness to get ahead, he started his business selling spare parts for vehicles. He enjoys his job and works approximately 10 hours per day. He will use the loan to invest in working capital and to buy spare parts for his business, such as wheel rims, oil, breaks and tires, with a final goal of improving his income in a near future.   Marvin is grateful to Kiva lenders for the support they provide to people with limited resources in poor countries like Nicaragua and for making it possible for them to have decent jobs.

name: Marta Victoria
description: Marta Victoria C. D. H. is 52 years old and lives with her three children in Santa Tecla, which is in the Department of La Libertad.  Marta manufactures garments, most of which are produced based on submitted orders.  On occasion she will produce a few items to sell on her own so that she can earn some extra income.  Marta has been in this business for seven years and has attracted many customers.  At the same time, she has garnered very good references because her customers have recommended her with great confidence.    Marta is requesting a loan from Apoyo Integral so that she can have the necessary funds to buy a large quantity of fabric in different colors and patterns.  She hopes to be able to take in more work so that she can generate more income, which will benefit her in a great way.  Since she is a single mother, Marta fights for the welfare of her children who are her main source of motivation to continue striving to be better.  Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer
town: Santa Tecla, departamento de La Libertad

name: Kadzo
description: Kadzo, age 43, is a married woman and lives with her husband in their own house, which has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.   Kadzo has operated a firewood and charcoal selling business for the past two years. She sells from home to her neighbors and passersby. In addition, she also farms, which earns her another source of livelihood. She mentioned high cost of transportation in her business as a challenge.  With the 30,000 KES she wants to purchase more stock of firewood and charcoal for resale. She dreams of expanding her business to earn more income in the future.

name: Aurelia
description: Aurelia is from the village of Tigdok, Tudela Misamis Occidental. She is 70 years old, married and has one adult-aged child. To make a living, Aurelia has a business venture running a retail store selling a variety of products such as shampoo, toothpaste, soap, etc. in the local community.  Aurelia has been engaged in her business for 15 years and earns approximately 2,000 PHP a month for these activities. Aurelia joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5,000 PHP from PMPC. This previous loan was used to purchase additional products to sell.  Aurelia is requesting a new loan of 5,000 PHP with which she will purchase additional inventory and use for working capital. This loan will be the sixth loan cycle taken out by Aurelia from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About PMPC Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.   Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Luisa
description: Luisa is a single mother of two children, ages 10 and 15 who are in school. They live in the city and she also supports her mother who doesn't live with them. She used her previous loan to finish the home where she lives now, and she wants to use this loan to buy 10 bags of cement, 6 iron rods, 30 braces and to pay the mason.  She is happy about working with Hluvuku and Kiva because she was able to fulfill her dreams of building a home of her own, which was at the time her biggest challenge. She is happy professionally, but she would like to finish high school, but she doesn't have the time and sometimes she can't make it due to her work schedule.

name: Mot's Group
description: Mot’s group lives in a rural village in Kompong Speu province in Cambodia. She makes a living cultivating rice and also does extra work as a factory laborer to support her family. In Mot’s village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water.   Mot is requesting a loan to buy a water filter to provide safe drinking water for her family. Having a water filter at home will help each of these group members safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses, and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Camilia
description: Camilia is 53 years old, single, and lives in a small village near Habaya in Southern Lebanon. Camilia is an active member of the group A. Namla, which means "the ant" in Arabic. Camila's ambitions, however, are certainly not ant-like. She has requested a loan of $200 to open a new business selling clothes. This is the first time Camila has requested a loan from A. Majmoua.

name: Susana
description: Susana is 47 years old and single. She helps her parents to earn an income.  Susana runs a general store in the Philippines and she has requested a PHP 5,000 loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to buy additional household goods to sell, like canned goods, eggs, sugar, shampoo, and soap.  Susana has been in this business for seven years. In the future, Susana would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Talisuaga
description: Talisuaga N. is a 32-year-old woman living in the town of Faleasiu Tualesolo.  She is married and has 2 school-aged children.  To make a living, Talisuaga owns & operates a taxi.  Talisuaga also owns a plantation, where she grows taro (a starchy root), bananas, and cocoa.  Talisuaga has been engaged in this business for over 3 years and earns approximately 400 WST a month from these activities.  In 2009, Talisuaga joined SPBD to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities.  Talisuaga is requesting for the first time, a loan from SPBD.    Talisuaga is requesting a loan of 1000 WST which will be used to purchase materials needed to provide service. Talisuaga plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business  to improve/expand her taxi business.  Talisuaga has not been affected by the tsunami which hit Samoa on 9/29/09.  About SPBD: SPBD's mission is to improve the quality of life of people living in poverty in the poor island nations of the South Pacific.  SPBD's philosophy of lending is based on a respect for each individual's innate human ingenuity, drive and self esteem.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders."

name: Ralf
description: Ralf, aged 26, has suffered financially. Presently, he is requesting PHP 7,000 as additional capital to buy vegetables such as eggplants, squash and okra to further grow his business.   This may be a great help in developing his business, and can let him save funds for the future education of his two children.

name: Abdulrazaq
description: Abdulrazaq is a young man who is getting married this summer and needs to cover some of the expenses that he can't cover directly as he is an employee with a meager salary.  Abdulrazaq took out a loan from FATEN to pay for the wedding hall and chair rentA. to have the wedding on time.  Abdulrazaq is photographed in the picture above.

name: Edwin Francisco
description: Edwin has a wife and two children who depend on him economically and whom he supports thanks to his job as a taxi driver. They are currently living in his wife's relative's house, but they have land in the Chontales department where they are progressively building their home. Edwin wants to provide his family with a secure home and that's why he is requesting a loan. He'd like to use the loan to finish the walls, doors and windows in order to make it livable and move his family into their new home.

name: Carlos Eduardo
description: Carlos Eduardo, 29, lives with his wife in Buenos Aires district, a community dedicated to agriculture and commerce in Morropón Province belonging to Piura Region on Peru’s northern coast.  He provides photography, video and photo-montage services and has asked Edpyme Alternativa for a 500 new sol loan to invest in service and improvement of his work equipment thus offering better customers service.  He’s noted in his community because he’s the only one offering this service.

name: Dúo Sajcabilla Group
description: The Sajcavilla Duo  This group includes Deura, who has made traditional aprons and blouses for 7 years. She started with her sister's help, since she was the one who taught her to use industrial sewing machines to make this clothing. Her business is located in her home where her customers seek her out in the afternoon. In the mornings, she goes out to sell in the San Juan Sacatepéquez park. Her biggest wish is to keep buying materials to vary the color and style of her clothing. In this way, she gets ahead with her only daughter. She hopes that you can help her with the loan she has asked for.

name: Servando
description: Servando sends you his thanks for your generosity because his previous loan had enhanced his business. He was able to buy groceries and other supplies he needed to increase his product inventory. The loan also helped him provide for their daily needs and expenditures.  He also operates a transportation business and he is very positive that he can improve his business more if you will let him borrow again an amount of 40,000 PHP. This new loan will go to additional supplies of accessories and spare parts of his jeepney. He will also use the loan to pay for the maintenance cost of the unit. Simultaneously, he can sustain the needs of his family if the unit is regularly maintained and in good condition.  Servando wants to buy another jeepney unit for his transportation business. He only dreams that his children will be able to complete their studies. He meets every week with his co-fellowship* members to share stories of his work and to also draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God he studies.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Loida
description: Loida works hard to support six children. She is married and has a food-vending business in the Philippines.She requested a PHP 10,400 loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to invest in a solar lamp.She is getting the solar lamp because she wants to save money by minimizing her kerosene expenses. Loida is aware that by using the solar lamp, she is not only saving money, she is also helping the environment and reducing health and hazard risks to her family.

name: Musu
description: Greetings from Sierra Leone! This is 27-year-old Musu from Moriba town, Bo. She is married with 2 children between the ages of 3 and 9 years. Her children are attending school and there are also four additional dependents at home.  Musu runs a baby clothing business; she sells baby shoes and baby clothing. She has been running this business for 5 years. She works at the business 11 hours a day, 6 days per week. Musu says that the main challenge to her business is insufficient capital to run it.  Musu has requested a loan in order to buy more baby clothing for resale. The extra income from this loan will allow her to educate her children and increase her business. In the future, she plans to own a shop. She thanks you for your support!

name: Analyn
description: Analyn is 32 years old and married with two children. With one child in school, Analyn works very hard to provide for them.Analyn runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like biscuits, beverages, canned goods, home care products, and other groceries.Analyn has been in this business for two years and sells a variety of items. In the future, Analyn would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Ilhomiddin
description: Ilhomiddin S. lives in the region of Yavan. He is 38 years old. He is married and has five children. He lives together with parents. His wife is a homemaker and his brother is working in Russia. Ilhomiddin does animal husbandry. He makes a living by breeding large cattle and has been in this business for six years. He is taking out the loan to buy large cattle.

name: Riffat
description: Riffat is a 51-year-old woman, residing in Lahore, Pakistan. She is a mother of one son and seven daughters. She maintains her household activities properly.   Riffat's daughter has been running a beauty salon for the last few years. She is a trained beautician. Due to her efficient and good work, her number of clients has increased day by day, so she requires some beauty salon-related items such as facial creams, combs, and furniture items like dressing chairs, mirrors, etc. So Riffat made contact with Kiva's field partner BRAC Pakistan. BRAC staff visited her daughter's enterprise and issued a loan.   Riffat is very thankful to BRAC Pakistan and Kiva.

name: Marcelino Eloy
description: Marcelino is a hardworking man. He is 52 years old and he lives in the district of Camaná with his family. For several years he has worked growing onions, rice and other excellent quality products. Since he was very young he has worked to be able to give his children a better future and a good education.  Marcelino is grateful to the Kiva lenders because because with their support he will be able to buy materials such as fertilizer, and agro-chemicals to be able to do maintenance on the plants and the crops to obtain the best quality products. With it, he will obtain better profits that he will be able to use to furnish his home and improve his family's quality of life.

name: Ana Daisy
description: Doña Ana is 55 years old and lives with her husband and mother in the Department of Usulután.  Her children have already established their own households.  Ana sells food and pupusas from a business that she has managed for 15 years.  The income she receives from her sales is used to cover her expenses.  Ana manages her business Sunday through Friday and on occasion she receives help from one of her daughters.  The loan she is requesting will be used to invest in supplies so that she can acquire some more business.  With the proceeds, Ana will be able to provide better service to her customers since she will have the necessary products for preparing her dishes such as rice, chicken, sugar, vegetables, meat, and other items.  This will allow her to keep up with demand.  Her main goal is to complete each of her loan payments, increase her customer base and be able to meet their needs, improve her living conditions, and generate more income for her family.

name: Justus
description: Justus used the previous loan to buy pigs to sell. He is a 48-year-old hardworking married man living in Kagadi, Uganda. He owns a butcher shop that he has run for a period of 12 years. He specifically sells pork and the business is very profitable. He says price fluctuations and inflation are affecting the business. He would like to educate his children and expand his business to new markets. Justus is requesting for a loan to buy pigs to sell.

name: Ana Milena
description: Ana Milena M. M. (pictured with Christina from the Kiva team) is 26 years old, married, has a four month old son, and resides in the subdivision of La Playa, which is a rural area of Barranquilla.  She lives in a rented house with her parents, where she also has a space set aside for her business called “Sala de Belleza Milena M.” (Milena M.’s Beauty Parlor).  There she offers a variety of services such as hairstyling, manicures, pedicures, and haircuts.  Milena began cutting hair six years ago and started her own beauty salon four years ago with the help of her parents.  She now has 120 established clients and several others who come to her shop occasionally.  Milena also provides home services.    She has been affiliated with Fundación Mario Santo Domingo since 2008 and her previous loan was used to buy equipment for her work, which was a great help to her.  In addition, she has different administration skills she desires to keep up to date so she attends seminars to refresh her knowledge.  Milena is requesting a loan of 2,300,000 COP to buy a backwash station (for shampooing hair), salon chairs for adults and children, and a minisplit (a small air conditioning unit).  With the development of her business, she hopes to fulfill her dreams:  open her own beauty salon in Barranquilla and purchase the house that is being rented by her parents.     Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Miguel
description: Mr. Miguel S. is from the city of Carapegua Cnia. Espartillar. He is 27 years old and married to Mrs. Monica Leon. They have two small children.  He has been a street vendor in various communities in his area for more than 5 years. His products are of goof quality and his many costumers are happy with them. Every week he offers products like small household appliances, sports shoes and local crafts.  Mr. S. has requested the loan to buy household appliances and sports shoes.

name: Angèle Mawussi
description: A widow and the mother of two children, Angèle is 60 years old and lives in Baguida. She sells general food products, which she procures four times a month from the market and resells in the shop at her home.Angèle is seeking this loan to make an order for cartons of detergent, with the hopes of increasing her stock and making better sales. This will help her to provide her children with an education and support her family's everyday needs.

name: Musarat
description: Musarat is age 32, living with her five children in the area of Lahore, Pakistan. Her husband is a mechanic by profession; he provides services for troubleshooting motorbikes and rickshaws. He always keeps busy repairing vehicles and does not have enough time for his family. He has been recruiting two young kids, teaching them mechanical work.There are not any spare part shops close to his workshop; customers have to go far away to buy problematic spare parts. He thus, in addition, wants to offer spare parts so that his customers do not encounter any issues during the repair of their vehicles. Therefore, Musarat has requested a loan from Kiva’s field partner, BRAC Pakistan, so that her husband would be able to buy spare parts and can replace worn tools. Musarat thanks Kiva and its field partner. BRAC Pakistan.

name: Sokha's Group
description: Sokha, 54, lives in a rural area of the Ek Phnom district of Battambang province, and he is married with eight children. The family’s main sources of income are farming rice and fishing. Sokha has been in these businesses for 15 years.  He has been with VisionFund for three cycles and completely paid back the loans, which have helped him relieve the family's burden and improve their outlook. Now he is leading his group to ask for a loan to buy seeds and fertilizers for his farmland. He will use a portion of it to buy fishing materials. With this loan, Sokha hopes to make more income so as to make a better living.

name: Leyli
description: Leyli is 30 years old and married. She is the mother of one son and one daughter. Her husband doesn’t work. She is an IDP (internally displaced person) and lives with family in the Bilasuvar region. She is skilled, respected, honest and also a responsible and professional person. Leyli is a dairy farmer. She started keeping dairy cows 10 years ago. Ever since she has developed and grown this business steadily to a point where she is able to get more then 12 litres of milk every day that she sells to her society. Leyli started this business with an amount of capital. Thanks to her hard work she has been able to improve and expand her merchandise. The profits from this business have allowed her to expand her sales volume. Leyli has already borrowed loans from Agroinvest in the past. Now she needs money and wants to buy food for her cows. She thanks Kiva lenders for their support.

name: Catalina
description: Catalina is a divorced woman. She lives in Guadalupe, Nuevo Leon. She used to work as a teacher in an elementary school, but now she is retired. She has a daughter who is a student.  After her retirement she started to sell beauty products with some of her friends, relatives and neighbors. Now, she has a large customer base and has also incorporated the sale of food supplements into her business, which has been very well-received by her clients.  In order to grow her business Catalina needs a loan of $850 to purchase more merchandise. She promises to pay this back in six months. You can help her to have a successful business. She will appreciate your help.

name: Donabel Mary
description: Donabel Mary dreams of becoming a successful business woman in the future. She is 43 years old, married, and has two school-aged children. Due to a lack of job opportunities, she engages in selling footwear and RTW in a public market. ("RTW" means ready-to-wear clothes.) She has been operating the business for almost two years and usually earns a profit of PHP 8,000 a month. She usually spends her profit for her family's daily consumption and the costs of sending her children to school.   Due to the high cost of commodities and school fees, she aims to strengthen her business to generate a higher income. But due to insufficient capital, she is asking for a loan of PHP 12,000 to buy additional stocks of sandals, slippers, shoes and RTW, to resell in her community. Despite competitors in the area, she believes that she can improve the business as she continues to work hard and strive harder.

name: Davaasuren
description: Davaasuren is 44 years old and lives with her husband and son in a ger (Mongolian yurt) in Uvurhangai province, Mongolia. Her family helps with her business. She started her sewing business in 2009. Before she started the business, she used to work in a sewing factory, therefore, her sewing skills are excellent. She is a sharp and hardworking woman who says "To open my own business was the best decision of my life and if I could work a little harder, I would be able to send my son to college". She's requesting 1,000,000 MNT to purchase additional sewing machines and upgrade current equipment.

name: Musarrat
description: Musarrat is a 44-year-old married woman who has been selling milk for many years. She has two buffalo and one cow for milk. She sells milk to many of her neighbors, along with butter that she makes from the milk. Her business is good enough for her to lead a decent life. She is very motivated to provide her family with a beautiful life, a good education, and food and clothing. She has improved her business to meet the day-to-day expenses of life. It’s her sixth year with Kashf Foundation. She is happily running her business through Kashf Foundation’s support. Now, she has requested a loan of 40,000 PKR to purchase one more buffalo, which will allow her to inflate her sales and profits.

name: Nieve
description: Nieve is 33 years old and is mother of three beautiful girls of 15, 14 and 10 years old.  Six months ago, she started a little business with the purpose of tending to her girls' needs.  The father of her daughters doesn’t live with them and is not regularly contributing to solving household problems.  She is now selling clothes, shoes, curtains, sheets for beds, and other houseware.  As she began the business with a very small amount of merchandise, she now wants to have sufficient inventory to offer to clientele.  This way, people will have more purchase options when visiting her business. The loan requested will positively help this woman achieve her goals and help her family.

name: Peter
description: Peter has been running his retail store in Njabini, in the outskirts of Naivasha Town, for the last five years. He is 32 years old, married to Gladys Wangari, and has a 9-month-old baby boy.  Peter was introduced to KADET by his friend and this will be his 6th loan from the organization. With the loan, Peter plans to buy more retail stock (in bulk which will be cheaper for him) to sell in his shop.  Peter hopes to one day open a supermarket in Njabini.   About KADET: The Kenya Agency for the Development of Enterprise and Technology (KADET) is dedicated to economically empowering its clients by providing financial services to improve the living conditions of micro-entrepreneurs and their children across Kenya. KADET is the microfinance subsidiary of World Vision Kenya. Obtain more information on KADET from the website:  www.kadet.co.ke

name: Edith
description: Edith is 38 years old and married to 40 year-old Julián.  The couple have four children and live in Puerto Mayo community, in Pichari district.  Edith remembers that she started out farming when she was still a girl, on her parents' farm.  She spent most of her time sowing and harvesting products such as cacao and coffee.  Edith saw an opportunity.  She saw that cacao was in great demand and so started setting out her own plantations.  She then started farming independently from her parents after having thanked them profusely for the training that they had given her.  Edith currently produces cacao in large volumes which provides her with a good profitability.  For this reason, she tries to protect her main source of income from any pests that appear and she normally receives help from her partner.  However, during harvest season, she needs help from laborers who make it easier for her to pick her produce efficiently and effectively.   This is Edith's second loan from MFP.  She pledges to be punctual in making her loan repayments so that she can ensure she is able to take out further loans in the future.  She will invest her 1,000 Peruvian soles in having her cacao plants pruned.  Edith is happy to be a member of her community bank because all the members are very supportive of each other.

name: Andres Jr.
description: Andres Jr. owns and manages a farm while his wife runs a general store to make a living. He always finds ways how to improve his farm and many ways to generate profit.   He had successfully repaid his previous loan used for his farm.  Recently, he took a new loan  to buy planting materials and organic fertilizer.  He wants to improve the general living situation of his family in the future.

name: Umoja Ni Nguvu Group
description: Siuzike, the leader of the business group called "Umoja ni nguvu", is an entrepreneur approximately 47 years old, married and the mother of three young children. Her husband is a government official; she is a partner in a restaurant, and has been doing this for ten years now. Nonetheless, she has recently completed her tenth loan cycle in the Hekima credit programme. She will use this new loan to purchase three baskets of potatoes, five litres of oil, twelve kilogrammes of flour, two cases of Fanta, milk, tomatoes, etc. Furthermore, she wants to see her children grow up and build her business.  The client welcomes Hekima's initiative in favour of poor, unbanked women.

name: Gloria
description: Gloria is 58 years old. She has been married to Pascual for more than 40 years. She works selling different products such as beauty supplies, perfume and underwear. She sells from her house and has many recurring clients. Her biggest accomplishment is earning money to cover her expenses and also helping her husband. She is asking for a loan to buy more products and increase her sales during the Christmas season.

name: Shubana
description: Shubana is the age of 38, living with her six children in the area of Lahore, Pakistan.   Her husband is providing services for polishing newly constructed floors. He polishes the concrete and marble floors. For this purpose, he uses a floor-polishing machine. He has been providing this service for many years.   A few days ago, her husband's polishing machine has become out of order, due to a fluctuation in electricity. For this is reason, he wants to buy a new machine, but he does not have enough cash in hand.  Therefore, Shubana requested a loan from Kiva’s field partner, BRAC Pakistan, so that her husband would be able to buy a new polishing machine and continue his services again.

name: Sros
description: Sros is a 28-year-old, single garment worker and she lives with her farmer parents in Kampong Speu province of Cambodia. Sros has been a worker since 2013, earning approximately USD 5 a day. Her parents fatten and breed cows for calves to sell.   Now, Sros would like to request a loan to buy cement, bricks, zinc sheets, and wooden pillars to build a toilet and a cow stable for her parents. This loan will provide Sros and her family with hygienic living conditions and help her parents have enough space for their cows.   In the future, Sros is going to build fences around her house.

name: Arlene
description: As a married parent of three children, Arlene works hard to support her family.She has a making of hollow blocks business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from raising pigs. Arlene is borrowing PHP 29,000 through NWTF to buy additional materials like sand, cement, etc., for her business.Arlene has been sustaining her business activities through her past 17 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Ziad
description: Ziad is 39 years old and a single man. He has completed secondary school, and is living in a poor area in Taiz.   His house is very old and in a miserable situation. He has accumulated some money to renovate his house. It is known that house renovation needs a lot of money. He has started renovating his house, but now he is short of money. He needs to complete the renovation task, so he asked for a loan of 500,000 YER (Yemen rials) to buy cement and carpentry help. He hopes that after the completion of the house renovation, he will start accumulating money to improve the life conditions of his family.

name: Lili
description: Lili is 58 years old; she lives in a small village with her family: her two daughters and grandson. She runs an agricultural business; in particular she is busy with farming. She has 0.5 hectare of land where she grows 200 vine trees and nuts. She sells the harvested products at the local open market. The total average monthly income of the family is 450 Lari.   Lili requested a loan to purchase calves. She will be able to produce more dairy products and sell them in nearby villages. Thus, she wants to expand her business in order to make the desired profit. With the increased amount of profit, she will be able to reinvest in the family agricultural business. Due to the above mentioned, the family’s living conditions will be improved.

name: Mercy
description: Mercy is married and has three children who live with her. All of her children attend school and help her with household chores. Mercy is a merchant. She lives in Kisauni, where she has a small, well-stocked grocery store. She provides her neighbors and occasional other customers with all kinds of items of daily use for the home, such as sugar, rice, milk, a variety of drinks and other products.  Mercy is requesting a loan to buy these products and increase the stock in her store so that she can improve her family’s income and their quality of life.  She is an established client with Yehu Microfinance who has shown herself to be a very enterprising and hardworking woman who works hard for the well-being of her family. She also works to continue growing as a small business owner each day and as a leader of her family.

name: Eva
description: Eva is a married woman with three children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Eva is 49 years old and has two children who are still in school.  Eva has a fish vending business in the Philippines. She has requested a PHP 15000 loan through NWTF to buy more fish to sell to her customers.  Eva has been in this business for 4 year. She would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Akua
description: Akua A. is 38 years old. She is married and has given birth to five children. She is a petty trader who sells items like rice, tin tomatoes, onions, cooking oil, pepper, canned foods, evaporated milk, soaps, etc. on a table in her neighborhood. She is very grateful for her previous loan, which provided her with working capital. At the moment, two of the children have completed senior high school and are ready to enter university this year. Akua is determined to work harder to give her husband the needed financial assistance to support the children in school. She wants to use the loan to increase her stock of rice, sugar, beans, evaporated milk, soaps and also to include the sale of charcoal. Akua believes this will help raise enough income to finance her children's education. She is a member of the community group called “Megyefo Tease” (My Redeemer Lives) Trust Group and she was photographed at her group meeting. In this group, members serve as social collateral to access loans and to apply a little peer pressure as encouragement and support to repay the loans.

name: Ketilut
description: Ketilut is 36 years old. She is an entrepreneurial woman and has three children, ages 19, 10, and 3. She lives with her children and her husband Ángel in their own house. Ketilut's business is selling basic food products such as rice, sugar, condiments, sausages, milk, eggs, beverages, candies, and other items. Every day at a very early hour, she opens the doors of her store to wait on her customers, who arrive in search of some product, with the certainty that there they will find what they need. Her store is the best stocked in her neighborhood, and her customers don't hesitate to buy from her, not only for this reason, but also because of the quality of the brands of the items that she offers. In addition to this, her very cordial treatment and the friendliness that she expresses in each one of her words are the perfect qualities to make her customers always appreciative. She has been in this business for 10 years and always receives the assistance of her husband and children.   At this time she is applying for 1000 PEN. She is a very responsible and supportive member of her loan group. She is grateful to those who offer her the loan, which she needs in order to continue developing her business. She is confident that she will continue being a loan customer who is very punctual with her payments.  With the amount she has applied for, she will buy a larger quantity of products such as rice, sugar, eggs, pasta, vegetables, fruits, and other items, with which she will stock her store.

name: -Đào's Group
description: Mrs Đào is standing first from the left in the photo. She is a widow with two children and her family lives in a small house in a village in Quang Xuong district, a rural area of Thanh Hoa province. In this group, Đào’s circumstances are the most difficult as her husband passed away seven years ago. She must work hard to keep her two children in school and look after her old and weak mother. Her main income is from raising poultry and pigs, and in addition she tries to plant vegetables for more income. The main hardship that Đào faces is lack of capital. Đào invited her friends and neighbors to establish a group to request loans from Thanh Hoa microfinance institution so they can improve their businesses. She is requesting a loan to buy more baby poultry to raise and sell in the future. With the profits from her business, she hopes for her family to be healthy and happy, to make enough money to provide for her children and mother, and to continue sending her children to school.

name: Jackline
description: Jackline is a married woman. She has 2 children. She describes herself as ambitious. She operates a retail business where she sells clothes and shoes. She has been involved in this business for 1 year. Her business is located in an area with potential, and her primary customers are of all types. She describes her biggest business challenge to be inadequate capital. She will use the Kes 50,000 loan to buy more stocks of shoes and clothes. She hopes that in the future, she will be financially stable. This is her third loan with SMEP Microfinance bank.

name: Betty
description: Betty is a kind and gentle woman.  She is 38 years old and lives in the home that her mother gave her recently.  Her husband Walter is 39 years old and her lovely daughter Solhas is 13 years old.  What she wants most is to get ahead.  For the past eight years, she has been selling beauty products in order to generate good sales.  She travels through the streets of the district every afternoon offering her products.  Since then, she has become recognized in her neighborhood.  At the moment, Betty has birthday parties and other events to visit so she needs to maintain the stock of products at her home.  During the relevant seasons she sells clothing, uniforms, school supplies, and other items.  This enables her to generate good earnings which she uses to pay for the household expenses and the education of her daughter.  She enjoys her business and is convinced that her hard work will help others.  Betty will be able to replace the roof of her parents’ house.  Afterwards, she will continue with the construction of the second floor of her house so that her daughter will be comfortable and have a better quality of life.    This is her first loan with MFP.  Betty says that she trusts the organization and is confident that she will complete all of her payments on time because she wants to receive further assistance.  The loan she requested will be used to buy cement, sand, and crushed stone so that she can change the roof from corrugated metal to cement.

name: Silvia
description: Silvia G. is grateful to Kiva lenders who helped to fund her previous loan.  She currently needs to build a perimeter wall around her home and to finish off some work to the outside of her house.  However, she doesn't have the money she needs to carry out these improvements.  Silvia is a widow and has two teenage children in her care.  She wants the best for them.  Silvia works as a nanny in a private home.  Some of the income that she makes from this job will be used to pay back her loan.

name: Flordeliz
description: As a married parent of nine children, Flordeliz works hard to support her family.  She has a coffee shop business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from farming sugarcane and food vending. Flordeliz is borrowing PHP 13,000 through NWTF to purchase coffee, milk, sugar, etc. for her coffee shop business.  Flordeliz has been sustaining her business activities through her past 5 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Muhammadjon
description: Muhammadjon got married right after graduating from college. He has a secondary technical education. Muhammadjon is married and has two daughters and a son. He is 31 years old. When Muhammadjon was little, his father had a big herd of cattle, but now his father is old and gray and no longer has cattle. Muhammadjon wants to put together his own herd like his father and start his own business buying and selling cattle. He already had a cow barn and hay, all he has left to do is buy cattle. He is taking out a loan to buy two cows. His wife will be able to help him with this business and his father with be able to share his experience with him. We hope that he receives what he is asking for. Muhammadjon awaits your support.

name: Los Inversionistas Exitosos Group
description: The "Los Inversionistas Exitosos" [Successful Investors] communal bank belongs to the Arariwa Association.  One of its members, Amanda, is 46 years old, married and with 3 children. She alternates her daily activities with her job as a teacher in one of the universities in the city of Cusco. She has had this occupation for quite some time and she does well thanks to the effort she puts into it every day. She wants to continue working to be able to support her family.  Amanda requested this credit to pay for her children's studies.  She is thankful for the loan and promises to repay it on time.   The bank member that appears on the attached photo had to be late to the meeting for work reasons.

name: Germaine's Group
description: Germaine, who is seated in the center with the child wearing pink on her lap in the photo, is a member of a group of 7 farmers who lie in the Sougoula village southeast of Bamako in Mali. Moussoni, who is 50 years old, lives in a family with 40 members, 25 of whom are children. Farming allows her to see to her family's food needs for the whole family, and to be independent. She decided to sign up with myAgro for another year in order to access good seeds and have god yields. myAgro changed her farming practices by introducing some complicated new techniques for growing, especially the planting system. For her third year, Germaine purchased a package of seed and fertilizer to grow corn on her .125 hectare holding. With this purchase, Germaine hopes to increase her yields, become a good member of myAgro and see to her family's food independence. In the end, Germaine would like to see cohesion and joy in her home, and in the whole village.

name: Julieta
description: Julieta is married and she works hard to support her family.She has a business buying and selling mineral water in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from selling purified drinking water and vegetables. Julieta is borrowing PHP 10,500 through NWTF in order to buy feeds and other supplies to raise her pigs.Julieta has been sustaining her business activities through her past 47 loans from NWTF and more recently, through Kiva. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to build and expand her business, to secure the future of her family.

name: Sami
description: Sami, a 29-year-old married man from the city of Rafah, lives with his wife and three small sons in a very simple house. He works as an employee in the public sector where he earns a low income; he is his family's sole source of support.   Sami is also studying accounting, hoping to earn a BA degree and find a better job in the future so he can help his family to improve their living conditions. He has requested a loan from FATEN to help him buy a laptop for his studies. The purchase will enable Sami to more easily write his research papers and prepare his seminars.

name: Analyn
description: Analyn is a married woman, with four children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur. Analyn is 31 years old and has two children who are in school.  Analyn has a buy-and-sell dry goods business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 10,000 loan through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to purchase more stocks to sell to her customers.  Analyn has been in this business for 18 years. In the future, Analyn would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Benny
description: A hardworking and passionate business woman, Benny is 54 years old, is married and has a son. She has sold cosmetics, clothing, shoes, skin cosmetics, jewelry and veterinary products since 2007. As an independent woman, Benny is always looking for new opportunities to provide a better life for her family. For that reason, a loan of MXN 20,000 will help her invest in skin cosmetics and veterinary products to supply her business. She will be able to increase her sales to expand to other regions. Benny has a dream: to leave a legacy to her son. She is not worried about the challenges that she may encounter on her way to success. To continue growing professionally, Benny will begin a sales course at an online institution for the next three years. She is very grateful to all who support this business. This is Benny's sixth loan with Konfío, and she has always been on time on her payment dates.

name: Alejandra
description: Alejandra is 43, and a hard-working woman. She lives with her husband Pablo, whom she loves very much. They have been together for 25 years. They have eight children, but only live with four of them in their own house, located in the settlement of Atocc.   Currently, her main focus is on the sale of unroasted coffee beans, potatoes, and other basic staples at the various markets in the city of Huancayo, Pampas, and the country's capital, Lima. Meanwhile, she continues working on her potato, olluco (a root vegetable), and lima bean crops, that she sells in the city of Lima, where she travels constantly.   In addition, she looks after her cows, who are of good quality, and provide her with rich milk. From this she gets extra earnings. In the same way, she has sheep that she fattens, to sell at a higher price to the butcher shops.   Now she want to raise more money, to get her business going. She is optimistic, and knows that with her group's help she will succeed. She belongs to the "Sol Naciente" communal bank, and this is the fourth loan with MFP.  She feels she is developing as a person, as its members are supportive and very hard-working people. In addition, she promises to pay her instalments on time.   On receiving the loan, Alejandra will use the money applied for, to buy natural fertilizers to nourish her potato and olluco crops.

name: Ana Marie
description: Ana Marie is 29 years old, married, and has one child in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Ana Marie has a restaurant business in the Philippines. She applied for a PHP 9,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy ingredients for her restaurant business. Ana Marie has been in this business for ten years. In the future, Ana Marie would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Beenish
description: Beenish is a 35-year-old woman. She lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan with her two sons who are both studying. Her husband has been running his own garments shop for fifteen years and is responsible for feeding his entire family and managing the household. He needs to purchase different types of clothes in bulk to resell, but due to insufficient financial means he is unable to purchase these clothes. Therefore Beenish is applying for a Kiva loan from field partner BRAC Pakistan so that she can assist her husband to purchase these clothes in bulk for his business. This will help him to expand his business and earn profits.  Beenish is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Judith
description: Judith is 40 years old and has six children, five of whom are in school. Judith is widowed.  Judith is in the agricultural business, raising livestock in the Philippines. Judith requested a 10,500 PHP loan through NWTF in order to buy feed and other supplies to raise her livestock. Judith has been raising livestock for nine years now, and has borrowed six times in the past from NWTF to sustain her business.  In the future, Judith would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Rashila Talle
description: Rashila Talle is a maize farmer and a member of Babban Gona. Rashila Talle joined Babban Gona primarily to create a better future for her children: Gabrel, Nura and Loise.   Before she became a Babban Gona member, Rashila Talle would have had to sell her maize for low prices soon after harvest, to cater for her immediate cash needs such as food and clothing. With this loan and Babban Gona’s support, Rashila Talle can now store her maize at harvest time and sell it a few months later for up to 40% higher than the market price at harvest.   When asked, Rashila Talle  spoke of her ambition to use the additional income to educate her children, eventually hoping to ensure her children are educated and have professional jobs.

name: Ma. Gemma
description: Ma. Gemma is 43 years old, married and has three children, one of whom is in school.  Ma. Gemma is in the agricultural business, farming rice in the Philippines. Ma. Gemma requested an 11,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) loan through NWTF in order to buy fertilizers and pay for cultivation of her farm.  Ma. Gemma has been farming rice for five years now, and has borrowed three times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Ma. Gemma would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Virginia
description: Virginia is 59 years old and has three children. She works very hard to provide for them. She operates a general store in the Philippines, which she has been doing for 13 years, selling a variety of items.  Virginia requested a loan from NWTF for 15,000 PHP, which she will use to purchase items to sell such as canned goods, liquor, home care products, and other groceries. In the future, she would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Sinauta
description: Sinauta is a 60-year-old married woman with six children. She runs a small bakery in her community to earn a living. She has one year of experience with this business.   Sinauta needs a loan to buy a bag of brown sugar, yeast, baking trays, baking soda, a new stove and a gas bottle.   She plans to use her profits to pay for her family's weekly expenses. Sinauta became a member of SPBD this year to gain access to capital.

name: Shabana
description: Shabana is a 40-year-old married woman who, along with her husband (also shown in the photo), has been running a school for 4 years. Today, there are 100 students in the school, of which more than half are girls.   Shabana wanted to contribute to the cause of education in her community for several years, and feels very happy that she has been successful. However, she is committed to continue to invest in her school so it can grow.   She requires a loan of PKR 100,000 to buy chairs and desks for her students and to repair a classroom.

name: Karina
description: Karina is a member of the Milenia Community Bank.  She is 21 years old, lives with her husband, and has a one year old son.  Karina travels to the different trade fairs of the region to buy cereals which she later sells at the wholesale food market in the city of Ayacucho.  In addition, she works as an assistant in the kitchen of a restaurant.  She needs a loan of $500 with which she will buy barley, corn and wheat.  Karina's dream is to own her own house and buy a car so her husband can go to work.     Translated from Spanish by Ian Nicoll, Kiva Volunteer

name: Leah
description: Leah is 48 years old and married with five children. Leah works very hard to provide for them.  Leah runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like spices, junk foods, biscuits, etc..  Leah has been in this business for 14 years and sells a variety of items.   In the future, Leah would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Tayyaba
description: Tayyaba is a 43-year-old hardworking lady. She is a mother of three children and is motivated to provide her family with good quality food, clothing and health.   She has been successfully running a small general store with her husband. The man shown in the picture is her husband. Her husband purchases stock of goods of daily use from the market at wholesale rates. Both are happily doing it together to meet the expenses of their family members.   She wants to grow her business, so she requested a loan of PKR 40,000 to buy packs of salts, biscuits and beverages to meet the increasing demand of her customers. Its her sixth loan cycle; she is expecting a boost in her earnings and dreams of expanding her business in the future.

name: Estela
description: Estela is 61 years old, widowed with four children.  She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 28,000 loan through NWTF to buy more stocks of household goods to sell like spices, noodles, soft drinks, spices, etc.  Estela  has borrowed and paid 14 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for eight years and also earns an income from buy and sell charcoal.  She  aspires to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Chou
description: Chou C., 40 years old, is a rice and vegetable grower from the Pursat Province. She runs her business on her own farmland where she grows different kinds of crop like cabbages, rice, potatoes, and morning glories, which she will sell to a buyer when they have matured. She currently earns an average of $4/day and has been running the business for years. Her husband who helps her with the farmwork, stands next to her in the picture. Chou C. has two school-aged children. Chou C. and her family are also facing difficulties with transportation because they have no vehicle to get around. Chou C. is therefore pursuing a loan to buy a used motorcycle.

name: Mujeres Luchadoras Group
description: This group is in its twelfth cycle of the Women's Committee Program.  They are all hard working women who above all are fighters.  They are also doing the poverty elimination survey so that they can grow and get ahead.  Lucila is improving her poverty situation according to the survey.  This is thanks to her work in clothing.  She is very good at what she does, which is why her situation is getting better.  Lucila is asking for this loan to buy fabrics and needles so she can continue selling clothes. She is grateful for this opportunity which will help her a lot.

name: Silvia Amparo
description: Silvia is an enterprising person and has always been known for being a very hard worker who provides for the welfare of her family.  She works with her husband in a hostel business that they established.  They provide lodging and food services to tractor trailer drivers who travel along the highway in her town.  Silvia has always wanted her business to become recognized, so she worked hard with the intention of growing and becoming the strongest in her region.    Thanks to the good service she offers in her hostel and restaurant, Silvia’s inventory level in her restaurant has greatly diminished.  For this reason, she wants to buy cafeteria and restaurant products so that she can provide high-quality service to her customers.  However, Silvia does not have the capital to make these purchases.  She is hopeful that a loan will give her the opportunity to purchases cafe products such as coffee, sugar, and other items.  In addition, she will buy restaurant supplies such as vegetables, legumes, and other items so that her customers can have a wide variety of products.    Silvia hopes that her business continues to grow so that she can generate income to maintain the household expenses.  In addition, she hopes that her two children will have access to a quality education and have financial stability in the future.

name: Nguyet
description: Nguyet is requesting a new loan to buy a range of beverages to restock her cafe. This purchase will help her to better meet the needs of her customers. Her previous loan enabled her to improve her business and offer her customers a greater variety of products. She hopes that her new loan will assist her in increasing the size of her cafe, thereby increasing sales, and help her to improve her living conditions.

name: Daniel's Group
description: Daniel, Pedro and Sergio live in the community of “Adolfo Lopez Mateos,” a highly marginalized area in the state of Campeche.  They have known each other for their whole lives.  They began harvesting fields when they were very young, mainly corn and zucchini, and this activity has become their primary source of income.  The problem that they have to face is that they live very far from their workplaces, so they have to wake up very early in the morning to get there in time and make enough money to make a living.  Given the lack of electricity in their community, their productive activities are limited to sunlight.  This is why purchasing a home solar system will help them to improve their family's economic situation and give them a better quality of life.

name: Linda
description: Linda is a student applying for a loan to purchase a laptop to assist in her studies at Strathmore University and this is her story:   I am 21 years old and currently studying at Strathmore University where I am taking a Bachelor of Commerce degree and a professional course in accountancy. I am the first born in a family of six. All my siblings are at college, high school and primary school. My parents are teachers by profession.  My biggest challenge is school fees. I chose to pursue university education because of who I want to be in the future, and I chose Strathmore University because of the good quality education and the high level of discipline it upholds. This loan will help me purchase a laptop that I will use in my studies. Most of my course work is on the e-learning site and it is difficult to access if you don't have a laptop. My area of interest is accounting and to become perfect in it I have to do a lot of reading and practice.   My desire is to have a country where all people are treated equally and also to see Kenya becoming a better place for all.

name: Mariam
description: Mariam used her previous loan to buy clothes to sell. She is a 39-year-old single mother with three children living in Kasese, Uganda .She has been selling clothes for two years and this has enabled her to provide the necessities to her children, as she has sole responsibility for taking care of them. Her hardship is inadequate capital to meet the high demand. Her personal goal is to educate her children and her business goal is to expand her business to new markets. Mariam intends to use the money to buy clothes to sell.

name: Srouy
description: Srouy is 33 years old and lives in Kompong Thom province. She has one child and he is studying at the university.   Srouy sells bicycles and raises pigs to support her family. This is her fourth cycle with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner) and she has successfully repaid her previous loans which enabled her to gradually improve her living conditions.   Srouy will use her  loan to pay her son's school fee.  He wants to earn a bachelor's degree in Accounting. She hopes that her son can get a new job after he graduates.
town: Kampong Thom Province, Kampong Svay District

name: Oisulov
description: Oisulov is a 62-year-old widow. She is raising her grandchild as his parents are working in Russia. As a source of income for her family, Oisulov is engaged in raising animals and agriculture. As an additional source of income for the family, Oisulov does sewing and national trade.   Starting in 2010 with a sum of 35,000 som (KGS), Oisulov was able to develop a good farm with a monthly income of 8,000 KGS.   With the goal of further developing her business, Oisulov appealed to Bai-Tushum and Partners for a loan of 65,000 som (KGS) to buy sheep for a summer activities.   Oisulov plans to invest income in further expanding her count of livestock.

name: Niña Charry
description: Niña Charry is 29 years old and married with two children.  She earns a living by farming rice in the Philippines. Niña Charry is borrowing PHP 11000 through NWTF in order to buy fertilizers and other farm supplies.  Niña Charry has been farming rice for six years and also earns additional income from raising pigs.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream which is to save money to expand her business.

name: Omar Antonio
description: Omar is 30 years old and he attended school through the 7th grade. He is married and his wife is a housekeeper. They have four children, of whom only two are school aged. Since he stopped going to school, Omar began to work as an assistant to a stone mason. Later, he worked for 8 years in an auto body and painting garage where he learned this trade. Currently, he has spent five years running his own auto body and painting business and in this manner he helps his family.He needs this loan to purchase tools to complete his work. Omar dreams of improving his home and providing his children with the opportunity to study and to be able to prepare themselves academically.

name: Joel
description: Joel A. is borrowing PHP 23,000 from Kiva lenders as additional working capital for his farming business. He is married to Rosemalyn and they have three children. They reside in the peaceful, but distant village of Baranggay San Vicente in Angadanan, Isabela.   Joel manages three hectares (7.5 acres) of farm lot owned by his father-in-law. He also maintains a banana plantation that serves as another source of income, while his wife manages a village store. Joel hopes to become successful in his farming business and to be able to cultivate his own farm lot.

name: Kaliman
description: Kaliman is 60 years old and married. She has brought up four children. For 35 years Kaliman used to work as a store salesperson. Now she is retired. In order to provide income for her family, Kaliman raises livestock. Having started in 2002 by purchasing two bulls costing 25,000 KGS, she now has a farm brining in about 15,000 KGS monthly from sales of dairy and milk product. Thanks to Kaliman’s hard work, her livestock now includes two cows, one horse, four bulls and five sheep. In order to develop her business further, Kaliman turned to “Bai Tushum & Partners” for a loan in the amount of 80,000 KGS intended for purchasing livestock. Kaliman plans to invest her revenues into increasing her livestock further.

name: Cirilo
description: Cirilo, 46, is married and has a 7-year-old son who is school aged.  He is a glazier.   He does all kinds of jobs with glass.  He has lived in his brother’s house as a custodian for the last six years.  Cirilo also has a public phone booth in his glass shop that he tends to daily.  Cirilo found himself in the need of requesting a loan from our institution to buy glass, frames and adhesive due to the demand he has now because he has several pending jobs to deliver.  He has a good credit history and is a longstanding client of the institution with a good repayment history.  He feels grateful to the institution for the support it’s always given him.

name: Patricia
description: Patricia is a repeat client with Ugafode micro-finance. Her previous loan of UGX 3,000,000 helped her to buy stock of clothing material that really sold fast, having been a festive season. The profits she made helped her to pay off the loan and now she is asking for another loan of UGX 3,500,000 that will help het to buy more stock of fabric for sewing to sell. Patricia does tailoring. She wants to take advantage of the low prices in the market. This will help her to prepare for the Easter season without pressure. She is assured of sales and profits. She is a married woman with children. She is very grateful for the support of Kiva funders through Ugafode microfinance. Patricia and Fred, the UGAFODE credit officer, are pictured.

name: Piosi
description: Piosi A. A. is sixty-two years old, married, and has eight children--three boys and five girls. His wife does maize farming for home consumption and also for selling on a small scale. For the last five years, Piosi has been engaged in two types of businesses in a busy market at Serem in Kakamega. Most of the time, he likes spending time rearing his livestock and sells the milk he gets from his cows to the local shopkeepers and the hotels.
