He also has a timber business where he sells timber to the local people. Particularly, he is using his loan to buy timber to sell. He hopes to set up a timber yard in the future to grow his business and also buy more grade cows to supply more milk. Piosi has a dream to give quality education to his children and buy a plot where he will be able to build a residential house. He is very hardworking, talented and generous.

name: Grace
description: Grace is a married woman with one child. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Grace is 43 years old, and her child is in school.  Grace has a buying and selling of bananas business in the Philippines. Grace requested a 15,000 PHP loan amount through NWTF to purchase more bananas to sell to her customers.  Grace has been in this business for 20 years. Grace would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Marta
description: Ms. Marta is wise and very friendly. She has 8 children who are all economically independent of their parents; Ms. Marta started her business  when faced with her husband\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\'s illness when she became responsable for her home\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\'s expenses. Five years ago she began her business; her children help, but she needs economic support to give the business a boost. Currently Ms. Marta and her husband live off what her small business makes, but they need your support and generosity.  She needs a $200.00 USD loan to buy merchandise that will enable her business to have more products in order to meet with her business\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\'s high demand.  Support Ms. Marta. She thanks you for your kindness and generosity.  Translated from Spanish by Alison Rives, Kiva Volunteer.  Doña Marta es una persona sabia y muy amigable, ella tiene 8 hijos y todos son económicamente independientes de sus padres; Doña Marta inició su negocio al enfrentar la enfermedad de su esposo y tener que ser la responsable de los gastos de su casa, hace 5 años que ella empezo su negocio, sus hijos ayudan en el mismo, sin embargo este necesita de un apoyo económico para ser impulsado. Actualmente Doña Marta y su esposo viven de lo que su pequeño negocio les proporciona, sin embargo necesitan de tu apoyo y generosidad.  Ella requiere de un préstamo de $200 USD para comprar mercancía que le permitirá tener mas cantidad de productos en su negocio y de esta forma enfrentara la alta demanda que tiene su negocio. Apoya a doña Marta, ella agradece tu cariño y generosidad.

name: Leolisa
description: Leliosa, 35, is a resident of GMA,Cavite City, Philippines. She is married to Daniel, and mother of her five children. With her husband, Leliosa manages their own household while operating the business. At this time, she is working hard to continually provide income for their everyday expenses.  Leliosa operates a buy and sell business. She buys general merchandise from wholesalers and sells them piecemeal, with a little profit. Products can range from tools to household wares and other products. Customers are attracted to buy due to the low selling prices and the many options that are offered. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community. She earns a minimum of PHP1500 in sales every day.  To help her continue operations of her business, she is requesting a PHP23, 000 loan. She will be utilizing the loan to buy more quantities and varieties of products to expand her product inventory. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands her business.    Leolisa dreams to be able to give her all of her children a good and high quality education through all her hard work on her business. She also hopes to have her house renovated by the end of the year. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her work every week.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Sarah
description: Sarah is a married woman. She has two children. She describes herself to be God-fearing. She operates a retail business where she sells soda, sweets, toothpaste and other items. Her primary customers are loyal. She will use the KES 80,000 loan to buy more stock of soda, sweets, toothpaste and other items. This is her second loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. The previous loan was repaid successfully. She will use the anticipated profits to puchase additional stock.

name: Silivier's Group
description: Silivier's Group is formed by 10 farmers in the Webuye District and is being represented by Silivier, who is the group leader pictured above. She is 35 years old, is married, and has four children. Silivier has been a farmer for 10 years and is often referred to as a very experienced farmer.  Silivier isn’t new to One Acre Fund, she actually joined the program in 2013 and has since noticed her life has changed, especially in the sense that she has had a healthier life, ever since, due to better nutrition. This year, Silivier will not only get fertilizer and maize seeds as part of her loan, but will also purchase two solar lights. She is very excited about this addition since now she will be able to have light during dark hours for her children to be able to study.  Using this loan, Silivier's Group will purchase a total of nine solar lights and use the farming inputs received to plant a total of 4.75 acres.

name: Nazir
description: Nazir, age 51, has a business buying and selling animals. She buys animals (baby goats and calves) at low prices, brings them up and then sells them in the market at higher prices. She makes enough through her business to contribute to the family income. She needs to improve her business to cover her household expenses. For this reason, she contacted Kashf Foundation and applied for a loan of 40,000 PKR to purchase two more baby goats. She is very experienced and has good contacts in the market. With this loan, she will definitely expand her business and income.

name: Victor Edison
description: Victor needs your help. Before, this man made an independent living, however due to bad results he had to close his business. Victor is a father of two children, and has always liked to work independently. He has not found a way to go back to start his profession, principally because of the lack of resources. Now that before him is the possibility of restarting his work of selling clothes, he wishes to request a loan with which he will buy youth's clothing for males and females, without leaving his job to the side.

name: Ouch
description: Ouch K., 50, is a village woman living in Kompong Cham Province. Since the beginning of 2005, Ouch K. owned an old bicycle and used it to pick up a few products to sell door-to-door around her village. She sells items like pork, fish, and vegetables, and typically makes $3 profit a day to meet her family’s daily expenses. Her husband, Om Pho, 55, is a local farmer. This couple has four children who are married. With this loan, Ouch K. will purchase a plot of plantation from a villager in order to greatly grow various kinds of crops. This will enable the family to accrue an extra profit to meet their daily expenses. Ouch K. was not available for the photograph, so her husband is in the photo instead at their house.

name: Lilliam
description: Lilliam is an entrepreneurial woman who earns a living making jams. She is asking for a loan of one million colones  (₡ 1.000.000) to purchase kitchen equipment for this business so that she can increase her household income.

name: Juan
description: Juan is 46 years old and is married to Gloria who is 37.  The couple have seven children.  They live together in their own home which is located in the community of Teresa, Pichari.  Juan always planned to have a business which would make him profits and so decided to work in agriculture.  He knows the techniques and the work which must be done in order to bring his crops to maturity.  He grows and harvests cacao, a product which is in high demand in both the national and international market and is therefore very profitable.  However, in order to make profits, he must wait months and so, for this reason, he also supports himself by renting out farmland.  He is happy to have chosen this line of work as it makes him good income.  He generally works alone but he sometimes receives the support of his partner and children.  At harvest time, however, he needs more labor in order to pick his fruit.  He normally sells his produce in his own community at market price.  This is Juan's first loan from MFP and he pledges to make his repayments on time.  He will use his 3,000 soles to maintain his farmland.  He will hire laborers to help him prune, weed and fertilizer his land.

name: Javier Alberto
description: Providing jobs, increasing available stock, buying a home, paying for his seven- and five-year-old children’s education – these are just some of the things going round Javier’s mind. At 32 years old, this businessman owns a garage. He learned this trade from a friend and his life is now filled with other car fanatics.  Javier needs your support in order to improve his business. He needs tools, supplies such as oil, and some commonly-requested spare parts. Unfortunately, Javier does not have the capital to purchase these items. It is easier for Javier to pay in smaller quotas; he is therefore applying for a loan in order to buy oil, hand tools, and spare parts.  Your support will be very important as it will give Javier the necessary tools and supplies to continue with his work.

name: Einar Roberto
description: Einar Roberto is 48 years old, married, and has two young daughters who still depend on him.  He is from the town of Chinandega, located in the western part of the country, an area dominated by business, tourism, and its beautiful beaches.  He is known for being a hardworking, responsible man with a personal desire to get ahead.  He spends his free time doing recreational activities with his family, such as going to the park, the movies, and spending quality time together.  Einar is asking for a loan to buy pebbles, dirt, rubble and other things for a 6m by 20m (120 square meter) plot of land.  He needs to do this because they live near the beach.  He currently works for a company as a security guard.  Einar has worked with the foundation and has shown himself to be responsible with his payments.  His dream is to see his children become professionals and be able to build a house so that he will have a roof over his head.

name: Ali
description: Ali is a 28 year-old single man and owner of a big transportation truck since 2010.  He transports rocks, sand and alot of construction tools and machines, in addition to any other requested products to be transported.  Ali is a hardworking man.  He seeks perfection in everything, especially in his business and with his customers.  Ali applied for a loan from KIVA partner, Al Majmoua, in order to do necessary maintenance for his truck, to keep it in a good shape all the time.  Ali is looking forward to expanding his business more and more in the future.  He hopes he will be capable of buying another truck.

name: Eliud
description: Eliud is still a married man and a very hardworking farmer. He paid his previous loan well and in good time. He is applying for his third loan, which he plans to buy a water pump and a pumping machine.  His monthly income is 7,800 KES, which has actually gone up slightly, but he still hopes that this loan he is taking will help him to improve on his agricultural activity and will give good returns in the future.  With the anticipated profit from the business, Eliud will buy more farmland. His hopes and dreams are to educate his children up to university level, buy a pick-up for transporting the bales which will help him improve the living standard of his family.

name: Y's Group
description: Y is 47 years old. She has three children, who are carpenters. Her children have gotten married. Her husband is a builder to earn a living. His income is about 5,000,000 VND per month. Y is a farmer, a builder's helper and a carpenter. She has done this work for 21 years. She earns about 4,000,000 VND per month. Her family’s total income is about 9,000,000 VND per month.   Y's challenge in work is a lack capital to buy a wood cutting machine, and to buy more wood. She wants to open her own woodworking shop. Her dream is to enlarge her carpentry business with all the machines to do the work most efficiently, and her children would work at the family's own carpentry workshop, established by their mother. This loan is one step helping her to reach for her dream. Y is a hardworking woman.  She participated in SEDA’s credit program since 2012. In the last loan cycle, she borrowed 5,152,000 VND to perform carpentry work, and she repaid on time. In this loan cycle, she wants to borrow 7,392,000 VND, which she will use to buy wood for her carpentry workshop. This purchase will enable her to gain earnings and save profit, to build a home.  Other members who are part of Y’s group include the following: Truyen is 39 years old. She has two children. She is a laborer. She wants to borrow 5,152,000 VND to breed pigs. Nga is 30 years old. She has two children. She is a carpenter. She wants to borrow 5,152,000 VND to make carpentry.  Nga is 26 years old. She is a carpenter. She wants to borrow 5,152,000 VND to make carpentry.

name: Nai
description: Nai is a married woman with three children, living in Kampong Speu Province. She is a housewife, her husband is a carthorse rider, her two children are factory laborers, and her youngest child is a student. All of them can earn around $13.75 per day. Now, she would like to apply for a loan of $1,500 for renovating her house. She hopes she can enlarge her house more and her youngest kid can get a diploma.

name: Tue's Group
description: Tuệ Thị Nguyễn was born in 1964.( ID number: 010102110011). She lives in Cau Ca village. Her two sons are workers. Tue’s main job is farming. Beside, she raises chicken, pigs and gwows vegetables. Her family has a monthly income of about 4.000.000 vnd. This time, she wants to borrow 6.758.000 vnd( ~ 400 USD) to buy food for pigs and chicken.  Đoan Thị Nguyễn was born in 1972. ( ID number: 010102110013). She has two children. She wants to borrow 5.014.000 vnd ( or 300 USD) to buy scrap- iron to resell.

name: Jane
description: Jane is 34 years old, married to Samuel, and they have three children. She is a timber dealer and has been in the business for the past 12 years. This is her first loan with Kadet. She was introduced by a Kadet client. She will use the loan to purchase a stock of timber for resale.  She hopes to own a plot of land and build rental houses.

name: Oul's Group
description: Oul’s group lives in a rural village in Kampong Speu province in Cambodia. Oul grows rice and  works as tailor to support her family. Villagers have no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses, and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Flora
description: Flora is 63 years old and widowed with seven children. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur who has a business selling fruit and vegetables in the Philippines. She has requested a PHP 20,000 loan through NWTF to buy more fruit and vegetables to sell to her customers. Flora has been in this business for 50 years. She would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Cheam
description: Cheam C., 31, is married and resides with her two children in Kampong Chnang province, Cambodia, an area known for palm products. C. sells food in front of a garment factory, earning an income of USD 7 per day. Each month, the family has to spend USD 44 on food and USD 28 on their other necessary expenses. C. is requesting a loan of USD 1,000 to purchase a sugarcane squeezer to improve her food selling business. In the future, she would like to use the additional income to repair her house. This will be her first loan from CREDIT, a longstanding Kiva partner.

name: Khakverdi
description: Khakverdi Q. is a 46 years old farmer who keeps a sheep herd in a  small southern village of Azerbaijan. He has twelve years of experience in animal breeding and sales. He sells sheep to the local bazaar traders for meat production. He is married and has two children. Everything is going well in his business and it brings him good enough money to keep his family in good condition. However to keep animals in a good herd is impossible because of the shortage of income. Khakverdi has applied for a 1200 USD loan. He is going to expand his sheep herd and purchase 15 sheep for estimated price 60 USD each, and for the rest of the amount, 300 USD, he will build a good shed to keep the  animals safe and warm during the  winter season.

name: Bakhrom
description: Bahrom P. lives in the Shahrituz region. He is 30 years old, married and has three children. His wife is a homemaker. Bahrom is a farmer and grows melons and watermelons. He has been in this business for more than six years. He is taking out a loan to buy seeds and mineral fertilizer. Bahrom wants to expand his business. He plans to sell his product on the market.Translated from Russian by Elena Fedorchuk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Aristides
description: Aristides continues as a member of the Imasumac II community bank.  He also continues his business making, purchasing, and selling handicrafts.  He has had this business for many years and it is going well.  When he does not have time to make handicrafts himself, he has to purchase them from his colleagues so that he does not stop distributing merchandise.  Many people request his products such as alpaca sweaters and ceramics since they are of very good quality.    He is requesting this loan to purchase merchandise such as ceramics.  He is grateful for the loan provided and promises to make his payments on time.

name: Beva
description: Beva is a businesswoman; she has a spot in the Number One Market in Villarrica.  Her husband, Mr. Gustavo Chamorro, is a businessman as well; he also works as a mechanic for high-revolution machines.  They live in the city of Villarrica.  The pair began their clothing sales business more than five years ago with their own capital.  Their friends kept telling them that their business could be very profitable, and so they began to go through the paperwork to apply for a spot in the Number One Market.  They were quickly accepted for the spot.   Beva and Gustavo are asking for a loan to buy more wholesale merchandise.  As their sales have increased substantially this season, they do not want to lose out on the opportunity to grow their business. Translated from Spanish by Mairead Harris, Kiva Volunteer

name: Aroosa
description: Aroosa is the age of 22, living with her two children in the area of Lahore, Pakistan. Her husband has been running a small vegetable shop for many years in a nearby town and earning insufficient income. To grow his business, he is thinking of selling fruits in the evening so that he can grow his monthly income.   With the passage of time, inflation increases day by, day but the sources of income remain constant. To increase income, he wants to turn his enterprise toward progress. For the purchasing of fruits, he does not have sufficient cash in hand; he tried to borrow some money from his friends and relatives but nobody helped him.   Therefore, Aroosa has requested a loan for her husband so that he would be able to buy additional fruits to sell in the evening.

name: Loryn
description: Loryn B., 26, is making sure that her family has enough provisions for their daily needs. Married to Marvin B., an electronics repair man, they are blessed with one child. She makes sure to contribute to her household's earnings so that their family can have a better life.  She has been managing her own "sari sari" (variety) store for several years.  Loryn has been a regular member of Center for Community Transformation* (CCT) since April last year. She regularly attends their weekly fellowship meetings and pays her weekly dues consistently. Because of her good repayment performance with her previous loans, she was able to borrow a few times through CCT’s Cooperative.  She is consistent in paying her dues because she used the money she previously borrowed to buy more stock for her business.   Her business lets her earn a profit of about 12,850 Philippine pesos per month.    Now with your help, she would like to get a 12,000 Philippine peso loan. This amount will be used as a source of additional capital for her expanding business, with which she plans to buy beverages, assorted snacks and canned goods.  Loryn dreams that her business will grow and be more profitable, so that one day her family can buy their own house.   * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Evangline
description: Hog-fattening is the business of Evangline, who lives in Tudela, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. She is 61 years old, married, with three children. She has been in the business for many years, in which she generates income to support her family.   With this loan, Evangline will borrow money amounting to PHP 12,000. This will help her a lot, especially in boosting her income!

name: Fatmata
description: Greetings from Sierra Leone! This is 45-year-old Fatmata from Waterloo, eastern rural area of Freetown. She is married and blessed with five children. She started her business to take care of her family.  Fatmata runs a palm oil business from home; she sells palm oil and peppers. She has been running this business since 2000. She works at the business throughout the week from morning to night. Fatmata says that the main challenge to her business is the cost of transportation and insufficient finances to expand her business.  Fatmata has requested a loan in order to buy more gallons of palm oil for resale. The extra income from this loan will allow her to educate her children and increase her business. In the future, she plans to expand her business. She thanks you for your support!

name: Akossiwa
description: Akossiwa is a retailer of grocery items and sewing supplies. She is 33 years old and lives in Lomé with her husband, a retailer, and her two children, aged 6 and 10, both in school. She started her business twelve years ago. Today, she employes one salaried worker to help her.   Akossiwa is completing her third loan cycle at WAGES. She again is requesting a loan to increase her stock of grocery items and more. She plans to redeploy the profits to be made in order to renovate her shop. Over the long term, she hopes to be able to open a second shop.

name: Elena
description: Elena is 62 years old and lives in the village of San Pedro with her three children. She is now widowed.  Her main source of income comes from planting and harvesting rice for sale. She has been engaged in farming for over 30 years and earns approximately 30,000 Philippine Pesos (PHP) every season. She also sells vegetables in the local community to have an extra source of income. She needed additional capital to sustain her farming yield to support her family's immediate needs. She would like to request a loan in the amount of 18,000 PHP to purchase seeds, insecticides, and fertilizers needed in the maintenance of her farm.

name: Bashiru
description: Bashiru is 32-years old and married with a child. He lives in Oyo State, Nigeria. He sells oil and crack palm cannel, which is a cleaning and sanitizing agent.  He is requesting a loan for $675 so he can purchase more inventory and service more customers. He thanks all Kiva lenders.

name: Pedro Alfonso
description: Sr. Pedro Alfonso has a small business selling basic grains at a market in the city of León.  He has been in this business for more than 13 years since it is an important source of income for him and his family.    The loan he is requesting from CEPRODEL will be used to buy goods directly from the producers in bulk.  This will also enable him to obtain a better quality product that he can offer to his customers, thus allowing him to generate more income and improve his financial situation.

name: Yolanda
description: Yolanda, 53 years old and married with five children, two of them in school, works very hard to provide for her family. She has been running a general store in the Philippines for seven years now.  Having repaid her previous loan, Yolanda has requested a PHP 10000 loan through NWTF to buy more items to sell such as canned goods, sugar, eggs, home care products, and other groceries.   In the future, she would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Sinuch's Group
description: Sinuch, 27, is married, with one son, residing in a rural village of the EK Phnom district, of Battambang province. To support the family, he and his wife have been farming rice and selling fish for three years.  Sinuch’s Group consists of two members, one male, one female, and they both have been with VisionFund Cambodia for one cycle. Sinuch completely paid back the loan with VisionFund Cambodia and successfully used the loan to better support his family.   He and his group member are applying for a loan of KHR 1,200,000 and KHR 1,000,000, respectively. Sinuch will use his portion to buy pesticides for his farmland. He hopes to grow more rice to increase his family’s income, to make a better living.

name: Kauli
description: Kauli is a kiosk operator of 42. He is married, a father of six children, and lives in Mwambalazi. He has been selling miscellaneous products (both food items and non-food items) for four years. Kauli is requesting a loan of KSH 50,000 to strengthen his working capital and develop his business by purchasing more merchandise. This will make him more profits which will mean he can pay fees for his children and look after his family.  Kauli is keen to grow his business and would like, one day, to become a wholesaler. This will allow him to take better care of his family.

name: Jeanna
description: Jeanna is 42 years old and married with four school-aged children. She is from the village of Camanga, Tukuran, Zamboanga del Sur. To make a living, Jeanna owns and operates a business raising crops. Her main source of income comes from planting and harvesting fruits and vegetables for sale. Jeanna has been engaged in her business for over five years and earns approximately 1,000 PHP a month.   Jeanna joined GDMPC in 2011 to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She is requesting a loan of 5,000 PHP to purchase fertilizer for her farm. This will be the first loan taken out by Jeanna from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated with her loan to improve and expand her business.    About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has seven branches covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Jean
description: Jean is a 20-year old college undergraduate.  She lives in La Carlota City.   She is married to Alfred, who works as a sugarcane laborer.  They have a 1 year old daughter.  Their total monthly family income is only Php 4000 ($91).  Jean has long seen the need to help her family but didn’t have the means until she learned about the 2 months training program of BagoSphere that could lead to a call center job.  Now that she has passed BagoSphere’s selection process, she needs your help to finance her tuition.  Once Jean starts earning, she can help provide her family’s basic needs and then save some money for her daughter’s education.

name: Helen
description: Helen is a woman with two children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Helen is 35 years old and has two children who are in school.Helen has a fishing business in the Philippines. Helen requested a PHP 15,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy fishnets, gasoline, and other supplies needed in her business.Helen has been in this business for six years. In the future, Helen would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Segundo José
description: Segundo José, 23, is single living with his mother and his children in Guaranda Canton, Bolívar Province.  He has two children.  The NUCANCHI KAWSAY communal bank is located in the community of El Rayo, Guanujo Parish, Guaranda Canton 25 minutes from the Cooperative’s office.  The members are in a variety of occupations like: farming, cattle raising, commerce, small farm animal raising, bricklaying and saw mill.  Segundo is a farmer.  He farms potatoes, wheat, barley and corn on land belonging to relatives.  He has six head of cattle, two pigs and two sheep.  Purchases take place in Guaranda’s market and sales happen at the wholesale market in that same city.  He is asking for the loan to buy supplies and animal feed.  Support from the loan will help him economically to meet his needs.  The challenges he faces are insect infestations, diseases and weather variations.  His dream is to buy his own fields and build a house.  He likes to relax, go on excursions with his children and participate in the festivals that come up.

name: Natalia
description: Natalia is a young 24-year-old. She is an enterprising and hardworking countrywoman. She is ready and willing to support her family. She wants to support her business that has been a tradition in her family, which is farming and raising pigs. She has learned this activity from her parents.  Her desire to succeed comes from her son. She is a happy person who is willing to work hard and sweat just to generate a better quality of life and a promising future for him.  Natalia wants to borrow to pay off an entire previous loan and use part of the capital to improve her pig pens and purchase piglets.

name: Orlanda
description: Orlanda has been involving in business activities since a few years ago, she started with her own working capital. And now she is requesting a loan of $ 1000.00 to improve her business. She has come to age of 47, but she still keep the spirit to run her business. She has a small kiosk in front of her house and she taking a loan from Tuba Rai Metin, because she wants to open her business a bigger store in the future, so she will use this loan to buy additional supplies to keep in her kiosk including card gambling, hand body, soaps, biscuits, noodles, toothpaste and other things to sell.

name: Nasreen's Group
description: Nasreen lives in a city called Borewala in Pakistan.   Her husband does not work due to his poor health, while her three sons do different kind of work to financially support the family. She does embroidery work to share the financial burden with her sons.    She has applied for a loan from Asasah for her elder son, who wants to buy seasonal vegetables to sell. He has been in this work for more than 10 years. Nasreen is sure that by adding more vegetable stock to his shop, he will be able to sell more and generate good profit on it.   Nasreen wants to change the financial condition of her family, and she is hopeful that with the help of a loan her family can enjoy a better standard of living and she can give her husband better medical treatment as well.

name: Vanessa
description: Vanessa is a member of the “HUAYNA PICCHU” community bank.  The bank is located in Cusco district, in the province and department of the same name.  She is 24 years old, a single mother and has one child.  She divides her time between her grocery store business and her poultry store business.  Through these small businesses she provides for her son.  She works from 6.30am to 8.00pm and wishes to improve her businesses.  Vanessa is requesting the loan to buy merchandise for her grocery store and chickens for her poultry store.  Vanesssa thanks those who are helping her to achieve her dream by funding her loan and pledges to make her repayments in a timely manner.

name: Jordin Alexander
description: Jordin is 22 years old and lives in San Lorenzo, which is in the southern valley of Honduras. For the past two years, he has worked selling new clothing to his friends and others.  Jordan is a hardworking young man with dreams of getting ahead.    He is seeking a loan to purchase pants, skirts, shorts, blouses, shirts, etc. in order to offer better service to his customers.  He hopes that this investment will allow him and his family to get ahead.  With the help of this loan he hopes to get ahead.  This is his second loan.  His dream is to have his own house and a successful business.  San Lorenzo-April, 2015

name: Merigrace
description: Merigrace is 45 years old and has a child. She is a vendor selling food while her spouse manages a farming business. Merigrace wanted to improve her sales and she needs to add additional items to sell for added income. She is now asking for a loan of P10,000 to buy beans, biscuits and other grocery items to sell. She hopes to keep making her sales profitable and improve her profits as well.

name: Jeanneth Del Socorro
description: Jeanneth, a humble countrywoman, is from the community of San Lorenzo on the outskirts of Teustepe. She is the mother of 6 children and her husband is a farmer. She took the initiative to sow irrigated rice, and her children have supported her from the beginning. At first, she was afraid that she would be denied a loan because she is a woman; but despite this, everything went well, thanks to God. MiCredito has supported her from the start and decided to provide her with a Kiva loan. She sells her rice in the same area where she lives, and some buyers travel from other regions in search of her product. She does not leave the area to sell, because this would be expensive; her plots of land are small. However, she would like for her production to increase in time so that she could sell outside of her community. Her business has been very profitable, and she has other sources of income which she gets from tending to the water pump that supplies her community. She needs a loan to buy products for planting two lots of irrigated rice. Jeanneth works very hard to provide her children with an education and to prepare them to be someone in life. This is her goal. At the moment she wants to get ready to bring in a good harvest and sell it all, repay her loan, and keep moving forward and working every day.

name: Rostro De Dios Group
description: There are three members who make up this group of enterprising and successful women. One of them is Yorleni, a 28-year-old single woman. Her business is selling mobile phone accessories, which she has been doing for five years. She began by selling top-up vouchers for mobile phones.  She sells her products at a market in her area. She will invest the loan in purchasing accessories, such as hard cases, universal chargers, soft cases, and wallet-style cases. Paubla is a 23-year-old woman whose business is selling clothes, and Lourdes is 30 years old and also sells clothes.

name: Hasifa
description: Hasifa is 22 years old and lives in the town of Bulenga in the Kampala west region of Uganda. She is single and has two children who are both currently in school. For the past one year, Hasifa has been working hard to manage her small business, which sells charcoal.   To help expand her business, Hasifa has requested a loan of 500,000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy more sacks of charcoal for resale, and will help Hasifa to generate greater profits and pay school fees for her children. Hasifa hopes that in the future she will be able to build a residential house.   Hasifa is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities, and a forum for life-skills training. The ELA program has increased Hasifa's future prospects.

name: Godfrey
description: Godfrey, a divorced man, sells produce and operates a bar in Kagadi, Uganda for income generation.  He desires to grow his business into new markets and own a big produce store in town.  Despite being hard working, he is challenged by price fluctuations that affect his returns and is requesting for credit to buy maize to sell.

name: Fadia
description: Fadia is a 29-year-old lady and the mother of two children. She started her own small home business designing and sewing clothes a long time ago. She has gained a wide base of clients through the years. Now she is applying for a loan to buy a cutting machine that will help her productivity. In the future, Fadia would like to have her own sewing workshop and wants to be able to start a fabric trading business.

name: Kuluda
description: Kuluda is a 41 year old married woman with three children all attending different schools. She is an agriculturalist who grows matooke (green plantain) and is also involved in maize milling. She works six days a week, six hours a day. She also works as a primary school teacher, where she gets an additional income to support her family and has been a teacher since 1998. She was motivated by the desire to supplement the family income so that she can provide necessities for her family. Kuluda hopes to use the loan to buy a maize milling machine so that she can improve her business. She usually sells her products to local customers and fellow traders around Kitonezi and surrounding areas. Her hopes and dreams are to diversify her agricultural business and start poultry farming. However, she faces challenges of drought and pests and diseases, especially banana wilt, which affects her greatly. She is described as an honest and hard working woman and asks lenders to improve on the loan processing speed.

name: Ezra
description: Ezra is a 48-year-old married man living in Bundibugyo Uganda with his eight children. He has a cocoa garden alongside renting other cocoa gardens to yield more income and get better profits.  He is very hardworking and hopes to complete his residential house and educate his children despite having limited capital and enduring seasonal changes. He needs a loan to pay for the rental of the cocoa gardens and pay school fees for his children.

name: Clara Berta
description: Clara is 33 years old and her business is selling tortillas.  She has been in this business for more than 20 years.  She started out in this line of work through her own initiative.  It has been difficult for her to keep her business going because she has suffered from health problems.  Clara has three children.  She is a very hard-working and responsible woman who has always been a good mother to her children.  She is requesting this loan to buy raw materials such as corn, firewood, lime, bags and a 'comal' (a special dish for cooking tortillas).  She dreams that her business will continue to grow.

name: Uk
description: Mrs. Uk S. and her husband appear in the photo above. This couple earns a living as local cultivators in the village. They live with two single children, while another three are now married and live separately. This rainfall, which is the season for farming a rice crop, Uk S. is lacking some materials for her farming business. Thus, she requests a loan to buy fertilizer, insecticide, and rice seed for cultivating.

name: Shallon
description: Shallon is a 42-year-old, married woman and a mother of an 11-year-old son. She is currently engaged in a stationery business for four years now. She and her husband also are invested in banana farming and a transportation business using their motorcycle.Shallon works hard in order to give support to her husband in meeting their financial needs. However, she lacks the funds or the capital to be used for the increase of her business. At this time, she is asking for a loan to buy additional stock of merchandise for her stationary such books, papers, pens, manilas, and markers among other items.Shallon believes that if she will be provided with financial support through the loan, she will finally be able to purchase the necessary stock for her business. She is looking forward to the future when her son can graduate from college.

name: Tomas Elmer
description: Tomas Elmer F. H., 34, lives in Cayultitán in the department of La Paz. He lives together with his wife and his two younger children, who are students. Tomas sells tamales which are filled with chicken meat. This type of meat is very appealing to people in this area, as his business is located in Olocuilta, a place that is very famous for their pupusas (thick tortillas typically stuffed with cheese, meat, and/or beans) and is visited by many tourists from all over the country as well as foreigners. These tourists allow Tomas to sell great numbers of tamales. He is asking for a loan so he can buy greater quantities of corn to make the dough for the tamales and so he can buy more chickens and vegetables. The loan will allow him to increase the number of tamales he produces and thus take advantage of his client base and increase sales. The tamales are his only source of income with which to support his family. It is for this reason that Tomas must be able to improve the conditions of his business, as his family is completely dependent upon the profits generated by it.  Translated from Spanish by Erin Sindewald, Kiva Volunteer

name: Elanie
description: Elanie is a farmer from Aloran. She is married and has a big heart for her farming activities. She focuses on growing corn, which primarily supports the income for her family. Recently, she applied for a loan to pay for seedbed and land preparation. Elanie is hopeful to have a good harvest this season so she can save more and start the renovation of her family's house.

name: Samorn's Group
description: Samorn is a villager from Tbaung Khmum district of Kampong Cham province and she is 45 years old. She is also a mother of four children.   To strive for a living, she is growing cassava as the sole source of her household’s income, which she has done for ages. This current business has returns her about 31,900 KHR per day.   Samorn has never before been with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner) and now she leads a group of two for the loan. She and her co-borrower are requesting loans of the same amount of 1,000,000 KHR each. As the leader, she will spend her entire loan portion to pay for land preparing and buying cassava seedlings. She highly hopes to uplift her situation better than before.
town: Kampong Cham province, Tbaung Khmum district

name: Mariana De Jesús
description: The Avance y Desarrollo Community Bank meets every two weeks in Junín canton, an area well known for its friendly and hardworking people as well as the best aguadiente (fruit-based brandy) in the province and Ecuador.  38-year old Sra. Mariana lives here. She is married and has three children aged 17, 13, and 5. The two older ones attend high school, and the youngest primary school. Her husband is a businessman.  Mariana is taking on a loan for her husband’s business. He buys and sells fruit, plantains, and vegetables. He travels into the countryside to buy oranges, mandarins, lemons, watermelon, melons etc. and then transports them to the town of Playas where he sells the produce to wholesalers. He makes this journey two or three times a week depending on production and the sales he has to make. It’s a job he’s been doing for more than ten years.   Mariana also has a grocery store in her home where she works every day. The loan is to buy different kinds of fruit and basic supplies as stock for her store. She’s been a member of the Community Bank for eight years and enjoys it because of the benefits she’s received from Fundación Espoir.   Mariana’s dream is to own a truck for her husband’s business.

name: Chey
description: Chey S. is a local landlord in Phnom Penh and she is using this loan to buy another home.  He husband works as a mototaxi driver and earns $2/day and 2 of her daughters work in a garment factory.  The households combined income is not enough to support their children in going to school, so instead they must work in the factories.  The house Chey S. will buy with this loan will be rented out to garment factory workers who come in for work from the provinces and are away from their families.  As she receives more income, she plans to buy yet another home for renting out until she has enough income to send her children to university.

name: Chhun
description: Chhun is from Ang Snoul district. She is 47 years old and a good mother of six children. Recently, her oldest child got married and now lives separately with an independent life. Chhun is operating a pig-fattening business, from which she yields approximately $4.00 per day.  Chhun now is taking out her first loan to invest in her pig-raising business. She will use it to buy feeds and vitamin for her pigs. She is very happy and hopes to get this loan from our kind lenders to further develop her present project.

name: Ann
description: Ann is a brilliant, hardworking 57-year-old Kenyan lady whose home is on a small farmland in Kerugoya. She gets a lot of help and support running the business with her husband and their children. In a bid to expand her farm, Ann is seeking a KES 30,000 loan to purchase farm inputs, farm implements and animal feed. Currently, she sells crops at Kerugoya Town. To boost the quantity of produce she sells, she needs a loan investment from Kiva lenders to purchase farm inputs such as seeds and fertilizer. She also needs to purchase tools and implements that will be used to work on the increased acreage. Ann also grows fodder for her cattle. With the loan, she will buy a wider range of feed from that available in the locality. Ann will use any money made from this investment to help her husband meet the family's basic needs. She will also save for future investments in the business.

name: Thao
description: Thao is 48 years old and is married. She lives with her husband in Ho Chi Minh City. Her husband earns money by working as a bricklayer.   Thao earns an income to support her family running a business selling leather shoes. She intends to use her loan to buy a great quantity and variety of  shoes to sell.  Thao hopes her business runs smoothly and will help her to improve her family's living conditions and save money for any future difficulties.

name: Gloria
description: Gloria A. manages a rice farming business. She owns a 1-hectare rice field in Norala, South Cotabato.  She sustains her family through the income she receives from her farm.  She has four children; her eldest is 29 years old.  She is now requesting a loan from Community Economic Ventures, Inc. in the amount of 15,000 PHP.  It will be very helpful to finance her business with a low interest rate. She will be able to send her children to school.

name: Mart
description: Mart, 52, is married and resides with her husband and four children in Kampong Chhnang Province, Cambodia. She has been selling fish paste for more than ten years, earning approximately USD 8 per day. Her husband is unemployed. Two of her children are employed in a garment factory. They earn about USD 6 per day.   In order to improve her family’s living condition, Mart is requesting a loan of USD 1200 to raise capital in her business to purchase more fish paste to resell. By doing so, she will earn more profit to financially support the family. In the future, she would like to use the profit to expand her business and help her children get bachelor’s degrees.

name: Juan Adolfo
description: Juan is 34 years old, lives with his wife and children, and has his own house.  He lives in a village of San Lorenzo in southern Honduras.  For 16 years, he has made a living selling vegetables, and his clients are friends and neighbors from his community.  Juan is a hardworking man with a strong desire to get ahead.  He is requesting the loan to purchase potatoes, bananas, chili peppers, onions, cilantro and yucca to be able to stock his business and to offer his clients more products and meet the demand that he has.  He also hopes to make the money he needs to get ahead with his family.  His dream is to improve his house.

name: Blanca Rosa
description: Blanca is 61 years old and single for the last 15 years due to widowhood .  She has six children who are 9, 16, 18, 19, 22 and 24 years old.  She lives in a rural village in Santa Cruz de Yojoa.  She’s been farming for 30 years.  She grows corn, beans and coffee.  She has a manzana [Central American land measure] of farmland and she sells her crops in the local market; most of her buyers come to her home to buy.  Her husband left her the farm and it’s well managed by her and her children; they dedicate the necessary time to the crops.  This is the sixth loan and she’s used them for coffee, corn and bean crops maintenance.  She has managed to increase the technology level in her farm and cover the educational expenses of her children.  Her goal is to improve the crops to have good harvests and be able to do some home improvements.
town: La Boquita, Santa Cruz de Yojoa

name: Raida
description: Raida is 43 years old and married with five children. She earns a living by farming rice in the Philippines, and has requested a loan for PHP 20,000 from NWTF to buy fertilizer and other farm supplies. She has been farming rice for six years and also earns additional income by running a general store. She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Tungulilege
description: Mambo from Dar es Salaam, Tanzania! This is 40-year-old Tungulilege S.. She is married and has 4 children aged between 14 and 24. In 1994 Tungulilege established her fruit and vegetables business. Tungulilege requires a loan in order to purchase additional stocks of fruit and vegetables in bulk. She thanks you for your support. When you walk down the streets of Dar, you are greeted at almost every corner by a stall or wheelbarrow full of mangoes, pineapples, bananas, or sugarcane. For customers, these luscious fruits provide welcome refreshment from the searing heat, and for the sellers a regular, if limited, income.

name: Omina
description: Omina N. is 36 years old, and is the loving mother of 4 children. Omina's husband is currently working in Russia.Omina sells dried fruit, such as apricots in the local market. At the same time she also breeds cattle. She has two cows, one of which is a dairy cow. Omina works hard, as she wants her children to have what they need, and dreams of providing all of her kids with a higher education.Omina is planning to purchase more dried fruit in order to enlarge the range of goods for sale.  With this purpose in mind, she is requesting a loan of 300.00 US Dollars for a term of 4 months. This is the first loan for Omina and she would like to assure everyone supporting her that she will do her best to repay the loan in a timely manner.

name: Joy
description: Joy is 42 years old and has seven children. She is married and has six children who are in school.Joy is in the agricultural business, raising pigs in the Philippines. Joy requested a PHP 14,000 loan through NWTF to buy feeds and vitamins for her pigs.She has been raising pigs for 10 years now, and has borrowed 5 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.In the future, Joy would like to save enough money so she can continue to send her children to school.

name: Anjali's Group
description: Anjali hails from a low-income household from an interior, remote village of Odagaon, Odisha, India. She is a married lady living with her son and two daughters. The lady standing to the left-hand side in the photograph is Anjali. Anjali has struggled a lot in her life in order to sustain herself and her family. She is a lady with sheer determination and strong willpower.Lack of financial resources had never allowed her to build a hygienic toilet at her home and get access to basic sanitary facilities. This has compelled her and her family to walk long distances at odd hours in order to defecate and urinate. This practice is not safe and feasible in the long run. Therefore, Anjali, along with her other group members, is requesting a loan amount of 30,000 INR. She will use her portion of the loan amount to build a well-equipped toilet and attach all the requisite sanitary fittings to it.The loan amount will help her in getting access to basic sanitation facilities and thereby improving the health of her family. Anjali is in dire need of your kind help and is eagerly awaiting your support.

name: Silvio
description: Silvio is studying medicine and lives in Concepción. He tells us that ever since he was a boy his dream was to be a doctor, and thanks to these studies he is reaching his goal.  He wants to be able to help people, and this is why he always makes an effort to be the best at what he does. He is requesting a loan to be able to buy his study materials, since he wants to be able to relieve his parents of the burden as they have already helped him a lot.  He is grateful for the opportunity that he's receiving because he'll be able to relieve his parents of the burden and he can feel useful also.

name: Alpana
description: Fifty-two-year-old Alpana hails from Maynaguri. She is married to Subrata, 52 years old, who does a very nominal job in a private farm. Both have higher secondary education. She lives with her husband and two sons in a small village at Maynaguri, Jalpaiguri. Both her sons were deprived of education, so they did not expect any respectable job, and now they are working laborers on a daily wage basis.  The job which Alpana's husband does offers a very meager income, and her sons have no consistent income. To give the family financial assistance, Alpana is engaged in a garment selling business. Alpana sells clothes and saris in her house. She purchases from the wholesalers and resells to the people of her locality.   The assortment of goods she sells is not that big and needs to be updated and expanded periodically in order for her small business to be productive and compatible. Alpana currently needs a loan to buy new clothes to resell to her customers.  She has been approved for a loan within the framework of a new joint initiative between Kiva and BJS. The loan she asks for is very important for her to purchase a new stock of clothing. She hopes it will generate more income to give financial sustenance to her family and to help her become successful in her business.  She is grateful to her lenders, BJS and Kiva.

name: Rosie
description: Rosie is 43 years old and married with five children. Three of her children are in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.   Rosie has a variety store business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 20000 loan amount through NWTF in order to purchase more items like snack foods, canned goods, noodles and other miscellaneous items.  Rosie has been in this business for two years. In the future, she would like to save money to expand her business and continue to send her children to college.

name: Lily
description: Lily wants to see her children become professionals someday. She patiently works on her farm to provide her family necessities. Lily is married and has two children. She and her husband are not getting tired doing some rice farming activities just to save some of their expenses. Lily wishes to continue operating the business until her children finish their education. Lily believes that she will reach her wish by continuing to keep on working hard. Lily is requesting a loan of 50,000 PHP to pay some of the labor cost in farming and buy farm inputs needed in farming. Someday, Lily will attain her wish through the help of her loan.

name: Darejan
description: Darejan is 49 years old. She lives with her husband in a small village in Senaki district. The family runs an agricultural business. In particular, they have a milk cow, whose milk is used in cheese production, and two pigs. In addition, Darejan has 1.5 hectares of agricultural land, where different kinds of citrus fruits are grown. She sells the harvested products and cheese locally in an open market at a good price.   Darejan is a very hard-working woman and has rich experience in her business. She has requested a loan for purchasing two milk cows. After purchasing these additional milk cows, she will expand her number of cattle and thus increase the income of the family. With increased income they will be able to improve their living conditions. Darejan awaits your support.

name: Lilian Estenia
description: Lilian is 37 years old, she studied up to 9th grade, she is married and has three children, her husband is a clothing maker and her children are studying high school.  Lilian also works making clothes like her husband, she has been doing this activity for 10 years.  She learned this trade through courses that were provided in her community.  They run the business from home and their children help.  She needs a loan to buy fabric to make school uniforms.  Lilian’s dream is to continue working hard to get her children ahead, expand her business, improve her quality of life and generate employment for people in her community.

name: Blanca
description: Blanca is studying sciences in education, through her career she wants to help people who wish to study and widen their knowledge. She also wants to help her family and repay them for all the help they have given her. She is asking for this loan to cover degree costs, and thus be ever closer to achieving her dream.

name: Felipa
description: Felipa O. is a hardworking mother of two.  She is currently working in a small convenience store which she runs out of her house. Her husband is a successful baker. He used to sell baked goods out of their house but now he works at a local supermarket baking their breads and sweet treats.  Through his work, Felipa was able to open her own small convenience store at their house, and with the combined incomes, they can support their two children. Felipa is asking for a loan of $225 to buy cooking oil, meats, eggs, and other popular food items.  With a greater  variety of food, she is hoping her profits will increase.

name: Francis
description: Francis lives in kakamega. Kakamega county is located in Western Kenya and is famous for having the only tropical rain forest in the country. Most farmers in Kakamega grow maize, but sugarcane, papaya, bananas and tea are also popular crops. The variety of crops grown in the region, as well as the abundance of vegetation in the old growth forest, make Kakamega particularly attractive for beekeeping.  Francis is married and has eleven children. Both he and his wife are farmers. They have farmed for thirty five years and grow maize, sugar cane and bananas. Francis is looking forward to beekeeping because it is not an expensive venture.  This is Francis’ first loan with Honey Care. He intends to use the proceeds from his beehives to buy food for his family and to educate his children. Francis’ hope for the future is to have his children get good jobs after schooling and that his family will live a happy life.

name: Phork
description: Mr. Phork S. is 46 years old, married, and the father of two children. He lives with his wife in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. In order to support his family, S. works as a mechanic at his home and typically makes around 2.50 USD per day in profit while his wife rents out rooms in their house to garment workers. Her income serves to supplement S.’s for their family's upkeep. One of their children is a student and the other is still too young to attend school.   Due to recent increased demand from his clients and the needs of his household, Mr. S. would like to increase his inventory. He is asking for a loan of 500 USD to purchase vehicle repair tools and a variety of vehicle spare parts to run his shop. He would be grateful for your help; you can play a very important role in his business's growth.

name: Rea
description: Rea is a married woman, 29 years old, with three children, two of whom are still in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.Rea has a food vending business in the Philippines. She requested a 5,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy ingredients like meat, fish, spices and noodles, as well as materials needed for her food production business.Rea has been in this business for one year. She would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Ny
description: Mrs. Ny, age 38, has been living in the province of Siem Reap. To make a living, she and her husband both work as firewood sellers in and around their community. They always buy firewood in bulk from their wholesale suppliers at a low price and then they sell the firewood to gain a net income. From this, the couple can earn about $6 per day to support their family expenses. Besides their current job, they have been planting rice crops as an annual activity. Mrs. Ny is requesting a Kiva loan to buy two cows to assist her on the farm, as her old cow doesn’t support her during the plowing process. Mrs. Ny is blessed with four single children. A few of the children help her sell firewood.

name: Usaini
description: Usaini is maize farmer from Kwankwarmi village. As a member of Babban Gona, Usaini is excited about the opportunity to become a better farmer. With Babban Gona’s support, he has the chance to attain yields of up to 8 metric tonnes of maize per hectare of land, 5.5 times the average yield in Nigeria. Before joining Babban Gona, Usaini would have had to sell his maize at harvest, a period when maize prices are at their lowest in the market, to meet his immediate cash needs such as food and clothing. With Babban Gona’s support, Usaini can store his maize and sell it in the future for up to 37% higher than the market price at harvest. Usaini is grateful to be part of the Babban Gona family and in the end hopes to use his increased earnings to ensure that all his children get a post secondary education.

name: Neftalí Antonio
description: Naphtali  Antonio M. is 47 years old and lives in the town of Ilopango, located in the department of San Salvador. His family is comprised of his wife, who is engaged in household chores which helps Naphtali to concentrate on his work, and their three daughters, ages 12, 10 and 9, who are studying in school . Naphtali takes to the task making reed beds, an uncommon trade. He can sell them at very good prices as a handmade product, which are sold largely to foreigners. Their point of sale is located on the main street of Ilopango, where the beds are placed on the sidewalk, thereby obtaining greater visibility to potential customers. Naphtali requesting a loan so that he can buy more reeds and the raw materials necessary for the production of beds. He is a very responsible parent, who works very hard to get ahead with his family.Translated from Spanish by Andrea Kellogg, Kiva Volunteer

name: Khim's Group
description: Khim’s Group lives in a rural village in Phnom Penh province in Cambodia. Khim works as driver and she also does extra work as a factory laborer and a construction worker to support her family. In their village, there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Miguel
description: Miguel is a single 60-year-old man who has 7 children, 3 men and 4 women, who live in Caserio Central, in the village of Xajaxac, and province and department of Solola.     Miguel is a farmer, cultivating carrots in the location where he lives. He learned this skill from his father while a child.  Since then, Miguel has had the opportunity of working with other people and in this manner, he acquired more knowledge, well beyond what he already knew.  Miguel now has some 20 years of farming experience and is obtaining good earnings growing carrots. For this purpose, Miguel is requesting a loan of 1,000 quetzals to purchase carrot seeds and fertilizer so that he can grow and harvest his crop, thus improving his family's income.  Miguel dreams of purchasing another plot of land so he can produce more and advance his family.

name: Ma. Elena
description: Ma. Elena is 53 years old and is married with five children. With one child in school, Ma. Elena works very hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 29,500 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase more stocks of groceries to sell. Ma. Elena has been in this business for five years and sells a variety of items, such as soap, canned goods, soft-drinks, and other groceries.   In the future, Ma. Elena would like to save enough money to expand her business and repair her family's home.

name: Manzoor
description: Manzoor is a 44-year-old married man running a school for a year. His community's children travel a lot to reach a school and he initiated this school due to that reason. His school holds 94 students out of whom 58% are female students studying in his school. He requested PKR 100,000 to construct a school building for new rooms. He has a great passion for children's education.

name: Lennox
description: Lennox lives in the Malindi area of Coast Province, Kenya. He is married and has one school-going child. He owns a food cafe which he has been operating for five years. In this café, he sells fries. He also owns a motorcycle which provides transport in the area. He employs four other people in the café. Lennox learnt about Milango through friends who invited him to the group, and he joined with the aim of accessing credit to improve his business operations. His main challenges are competition and the effect of season changes.  Lennox is applying for a loan of 21,050 Kenya shillings to buy food stock e.g. rice, cereals, wheat flour, cooking fat etc. His extra income from the loan will be added to his savings to pay school fees for his child and improve on his living standard. His dream is to open another food cafe.

name: Malaea
description: Malaea, 47 years old, is married and has 3 children. For the past 5 years, she has run a BBQ stall and a flea market selling veggies from her garden. Malaea needs a loan to buy a large BBQ grill set, 2 large tables, a tarpaulin, a new wheelbarrow, iron poles and fresh meat. She will use her profits to pay for her family's weekly expenses. Malaea joined SPBD in 2009 to gain access to financial services.

name: Slobodanka
description: Slobodanka D. was born in 1937. She is a widow and is in retail. She is a very healthy old women, and she does not like to just sit. Slobodanka keeps busy by embroidering. She does that in a traditional way and it is very popular. Slobodanka also does the frames. Now she needs a loan to buy needed things for her work such as thread, frames, needles and similar items. She decided to take a loan from WWI.

name: Arminda
description: Arminda is a very hardworking and determined person who is making an effort to get ahead and be someone in life. She is working in her grocery store everyday from very early hours in the morning. She states that she used her previous loan to buy supplies for her store.  Today she requests a new loan to be able to buy drinks, baked goods, dairy products, and other things, so that she will be able to continue with her sales as she has been doing. She is grateful for the opportunity she is again receiving to be able to continue growing.

name: Helena
description: Helena is a married woman. She has four children and all are enrolled in school. Helena operates a vegetable stall and sells her goods as retail. She's worked in this business for five years. Her primary customers are passers-by and neighbours. She describes her greatest business challenge to be scarcity of vegetables supplied in the market. Her highest monthly expense is food for the family. She owns a house that has electricity but no piped water. Helena will use the 30,000 KES loan to purchase crates of tomatoes and potatoes. Helena aspires to expand her business in the future. She joined Yehu in order to access capital.

name: Elias Stalin
description: Stalin, 42, has many aspirations for his repair shop business to prosper in the next few years.  His story starts when he was an employee at a company and decided to become independent since he was barely making a living. Now he’s very well known in his business and has a few clients. He works alone, but when he has many cars to repair, he hires an assistant. He hasn’t any difficulties. He’s single and has no children.  His dream is to own his own house, as he currently lives with his mother. He is requesting a loan for his repair shop, to invest in tools in order to improve the service to his clients.

name: Ny's Group
description: Ny resides in Takeo Province, where silk weaving is the most popular business. She is 59 years old, married, and blessed with two children. She does silk weaving as her main source of income and rice farming for supplementary income. She has been involved in silk weaving for 30 years, earning about 8,000 Cambodian riels (KHR).  Ny has never been with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner) before.  She now leads a group of three to apply for a latrine-construction loan. Ny will spend her entire portion, 600,000 KHR--the same amount as her co-borrowers--to build a decent latrine for her family. She hopes to have a proper latrine for her kids to prevent illness related to lack of hygienic practices.

name: Geronima Esperanza
description: Gerónima Esperanza is 65 years old and has been selling tortillas for more than 43 years.  This is not the first time she has received financing since she has been a good client and has completed her payments on time and according to terms.  One of the major challenges that she must deal with is her health problems.  Gerónima wakes up early and works from 6am to 6pm.    Her plans for this loan are to buy firewood, lime, a metal hotplate, bags, and other supplies.

name: Soeub
description: Soeub is a resident of the Srey Snom district of Siem Reap province. She is a 51-year-old married woman, and also a mother of six children. She has struggled to make a living by doing crop farm for about 30 years. She earns extra income to support the family by raising pigs to sell.   This is the first time that Soeub is applying for a loan from Kiva’s partner, VisionFund. She requests a new loan of in order to pay for her child's vocational training fee.   She optimistically believes that her child will finish the course and be able to earn a living with the skill.
town: Siem Reap Province, Srey Snom district

name: Mujeres De Fe Group
description: Maritza Cecilia is a member of the solidarity group called “Mujeres de Fe” (Women of Faith).  She is 38 years old and has a son who is a student taking general education courses.  They reside in the community of Tierra Blanca.  Maritza has been selling tortillas since 1998 and learned this trade from one of her aunts.  Her schedule for making tortillas begins at 6am and lasts through 11am.  She receives orders from restaurants and school cafeterias.  Her biggest concern is when the schools go on vacation break because it is a long period that she must go without a source of income.  Maritza has to earn a living through another type of business, so occasionally she sells seasonal fruits.    The loan she is requesting will be used to buy corn, firewood, and a hand mill because the lack of electricity is a huge problem throughout the country.  With the help from this loan, she will be able to continue working and cover all of her household expenses since she does not receive assistance from anyone else.  Maritza will also be able to continue paying for her son’s education because he is an outstanding student in all of his classes.  Her business goals are to have more customers and to sell tortillas that are packaged and in bags.  With respect to her family, she would like to see her son graduate and secure a good job, such as a teacher, so that he can help her move forward.    The other member of the group is Virginia del Carmen, who sells tortillas and firewood.  Both of them are participating in their second loan cycle and place their trust in God that they will complete their payments in a timely manner.

name: Kulnara
description: Kulnara is 51 years old, divorced, and has three children. Kulnara lives with her daughter and granddaughter. She has higher education. She has worked in field and animal husbandry for 15 years in order to provide income for her family.   Thanks to Kulnara's persistence, purposefulness and hardworkingness, today she has a cow and forty sheep. She also has a 1.20 hectare plot of land, where she cultivates beans and clover.   Kulnara's monthly income is about 16,000 som (KGS). These means are not sufficient for a respectable life or for supporting her family. Thus, Kulnara has applied to Bai Tushum Bank for a loan of 70,000 som (KGS) to buy livestock in order to increase their headcount. Kulnara intends to further increase the livestock headcount and develop her business.

name: Dinalyn
description: Dinalyn is 20 years old and has one child. She works very hard to provide for her family.Dinalyn runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 5,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like canned goods, snack foods, home care products, and other groceries.Dinalyn has been in this business for two years and sells a variety of items such as biscuits, snack foods, candies, condiments, etc.In the future, Dinalyn would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Salvie
description: Salvie D. is from the village of Mozzozzin Norte. She is 25 years old and is married with two school-aged children.  Salvie owns and operates a business raising and fattening pigs for sale. She is just starting this business.  In 2010, Salvie joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. She is requesting a loan of 5,000 PHP which will be used to purchase piglets to raise and sell. This loan will be her first from ASKI.  Salvie plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to financially support immediate members of her family.    About ASKI: ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has twenty-one branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.    *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Viviana
description: Viviana is 29 years old and she lives with her spouse and two children, aged 7 and 9, in the city of Soledad. she has a variety store there and sells various household items, women's accessories and paper products, etc. Before having this business, she had already started a cell phone service business and sold various merchandise via specialized catalogs. A year ago, with money from her husband, she bought three display cases and she converted her business into a retail space where she shows displays shoes, paper products, etc. she charges upfront and has some customers who make monthly payments according to a payment plan. Her Kiva loan is the first loan she has taken out with the Fundación Mario Santo Domingo. With it, she will buy a display case that she will fill with merchandise that she hasn't been able to organize. With it, she plans on increasing her short term accounts payable and on buying discounted merchandise that she will pass on to the customer. While this is going on, she has a contribution margin of 29% and she plans on projecting her potential growth fro there.

name: Akouvi
description: Akouvi is a 46-year old woman. She is married to a nurse, and has four children, one of whom is in school. Her first child is 30, and the youngest is 18.   Akouvi sells used clothes. She sells from home and in the countryside markets.  Akouvi has obtained her first loan from WAGES in order to buy bundles of used clothes.  She wants to buy a car to transport her merchandise, and to take care of her family.

name: Chin
description: Mrs. K. is 32 years old and since 1979 has made a living by farming a small plot of land that she owns. She grows various kinds of produce, and is able to raise two crops a year. She is also the devoted mother of two school-aged children, who live with her. Her husband, Mr. Orm Yam, 39, earns a living by building houses. Mrs. K. has applied for this loan to buy a used motorbike which she needs to transport her family. The motorbike mean lower expenses because the family will be able to get round without paying for taxis.

name: Segundina
description: Segundina is 47 years old and married with seven children. With two of her children in school, Segundina works very hard to provide for them.Segundina runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to purchase items to sell such as beverages, eggs, home care products, and other groceries.Segundina has been in this business for five years and sells a variety of items such as coffee, eggs, condiments, oil, dried fish, etc. In the future, Segundina would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: 14 De Agosto Group
description: 14 de Agosto  [14th of August} is the name of this group from the city of Itá.  The members of this group have various occupations so as to be able to continue growing and improving.   They are also carrying out the survey for ending poverty which will allow them to know the circumstances of each member and be able to work in accordance.  One of the members of this group is Isabelina who,  besides being part of the group,  is its director.  She is a very hard working person, who starts every day at an early hour, since she must prepare the pastries she sells.  She already has attracted a good customer base thanks to always doing good work very acceptable to everyone.   Isabelina is asking for this loan to buy flour, eggs, butter, yeast and other products so that she can continue to make a stock of pastries to sell. She is thankful to have this opportunity which will help her a lot.

name: Nancy Asturia
