description: On San Eduardo Street, in the city of Portoviejo, known as the city of the Royal Tamarind since colonial times, every 15 days the members of the Loan Group 16 of July gather together. In this place lives Nancy, she is 50 years old, she cohabits and from this relationship she has four children who are adults. Only one of them still lives with her.  Her husband is a taxi driver. A few years ago, she learned tailoring and dressmaking in an academy in the city. Nancy is a woman who has always liked to earn her own money, and help her husband to get ahead. This is why over 10 years ago she opened a small sewing workshop in her home. There she makes all types of garments, but mostly for women and children. Sometimes she makes school uniforms, buy only in the season when school starts. She works for six hours every day depending on what she has to make. Sometimes she hires workers when she has a lot of sewing to hand in. Currently she hopes to buy an industrial machine, and improve the quality of her work. This loan she will use to buy materials for sewing and an industrial sewing machine. She has been with the loan group for more than 4 years, and she likes it because with the loan she can get ahead. Her dreams are to keep improving her workshop.

name: Alex
description: Thirty-five-year-old Alex used the previous loan to buy cassava for milling and making flour to sell. He still operates the same businesses and owns milling machines, which all earn him an income. With too much zeal for farming, he usually has targets. Now that it's a season of planting Irish potatoes, Alex does not want to be left behind as he does not have enough land for farming. That's why he is requesting a Kiva loan through Hofokam to rent land and cultivate it to grow Irish potatoes. He complains of unpredictable weather changes as he dreams of educating his children and buying more land for farming.

name: Ana Lucia
description: At the age of 43, Mrs. Ana Lucía has one child and has worked in her own sewing workshop for 12 years. She makes clothing and uniforms, and learned this work from a friend. Ana Lucia works with a neighbour and a family member in her workshop. She wants to buy an overlock sewing machine in order to improve her production; it will take her less time to complete an order with this machine. With this loan, Ana Lucia will be able to increase her income and improve her family's quality of life. Her dream is to have a large workshop and generate direct employment for her friends and family.

name: Catarina  Marisela
description: Ms. Marisela Y. Y. is from the community of Chiya. It is a place visited frequently by national and international tourists because of the caves of San Miguel. She learned the art of tailoring in the assembly plants of San Lucas Sacatepequez, Guatemala. Three years ago, she started her own business in the production of ladies' aprons and girls' uniforms. Today she needs the support of the ASDIR institution for a loan which she will invest in the purchase of fabric, because she has an order for uniforms from a community school. Translated from Spanish by Ellen Donohue, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sahib
description: Sahib Q. is a married man with three children. For several years has dedicated himself to cattle breeding. He has attended to this work with great effort in order to maintain his home. He has the duty of supporting his family and for this reason, he decided to come to AqroInvest Credit Union for help in buying young cattle. It is his dream to develop his business with more loans and in this way continue to maintain his humble home. Sahib promises to repay this loan in a timely manner and thanks all KIVA lenders for trusting and supporting him.

name: Myrna
description: Myrna, 40 years of age, is married, and blessed with three school-aged children. She is engaged in a direct selling business in which she sells cosmetics and apparel products such as make-up, lotions, talcum powder, and clothes. She earns PHP 9,000 monthly. She would like to request a loan of PHP 20,000 to purchase more make-up and perfumes to sell. She hopes to create another income-generating source for the family's daily needs and to gain more income.

name: Sally
description: Sally R. is from the village of Capellan. She is 29 years old, married, and has two school-aged children. To make a living, she runs a general store,  selling a variety of different products in the local community. She has been engaged in her business for over two years and earns approximately $90 a month for these activities.  Sally joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 10,000 PHP from ASKI. This previous loan was used to purchase additional products to sell.   Sally is requesting a new loan of 10,000 PHP which again will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This will be her 7th loan from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated to improve her business.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful micro-finance institutions in the Philippines. It has 29 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Narcisa
description: Narcisa works hard to support her family.  She is married and has a food vending business in the Philippines.  Narcisa has requested a PHP 7,000 loan through NWTF to buy more items like peanuts, salt, garlic, etc. for her business.  She has been in this business for 23 years now.  In the future, Narcisa would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Moses
description: Moses is 46 years old and married with two children. His wife is a caterer and she also supports her husband in meeting the basic needs of their family. Moses is well-loved in his community, especially by children, because he sells ice cream. He sells his ice cream at retail prices to his customers.   He hopes to expand his business. His greatest challenge is funds and he hopes to overcome the challenge.  He is requesting a loan of 100,000 Nigerian naira to purchase more ice cream to sell. He says thank you to all Kiva lenders.

name: Solange
description: Solange S. was born on April 23, 1968.  She is married to Ahanhanzo Armand GLELE and has five children, ages 20, 18, 16, 14, and 3, who are all in school.  She herself had been provided with a primary school education and has been working for ten years.  In the beginning, she sold various goods.  Currently, she distributes them.  Her customers order pagnes (colorful West African cloth), necklaces, and shoes that they buy from her.  She acquires her stock in Lomé.  Her husband has helped.  The other Kiva loans have enabled her to expand her offering.  In the future, she would like to open a fish shop and to sell various goods in bulk.  Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Alejandro
description: Alejandro is a client of Kubo Financiero and this is his story:  Alejandro is seen as a responsible, hard-working and humanitarian person. He has been married for 21 years and they have three children aged 17, 19 and 21 years. He has lived in the house of a family member for 22 years.Alejandro has been selling woman's clothing for the past 15 years. as his wife enjoys it. But it was him who started selling to his neighbors and now to his co-workers at the taxi company. Fortunately things have been going well for them. They sell clothing on order and have a system of credit  for their customers.This loan is needed to buy seasonal  merchandise such as blankets and quilts. His main achievement is to have run his business up to now and his dream is to buy his own home.

name: Charles  Odhiambo
description: Charles has been in the quarry business, extracting and selling stone blocks, for 15 years. He is 38 years old and married to Milka Akinyi, with whom he has five children.    He was introduced to KADET by his friend, and this will be his first loan. He plans to use the cash to buy another plot from which to extract stones.  In the future, Charles plans to start livestock farming, which he will run simultaneously with the quarry.

name: Nozim
description: Nozim K. is 30 years old, and is married with three children. Nozim lives with his parents, and is the main bread-winner for his large family.Nozim sells fruit, such as apples, oranges, and pears, in the central local market. He has been in this business for 11 years. After such a long time, Nozim has acquired the knowledge and skills required for the business. For instance, he knows how to store the fruit to keep their marketable condition and not lose their taste and useful properties. Being located in the biggest central market, Nozim's business has a large clientele and is rather stable, generating the main income to support the family.Nozim has proved himself to be an honest reliable client. Today he is requesting 600.00 US Dollars for the term of 6 months. He plans to use the loan to purchase fruit, such as apples, oranges, and pears in order to increase the range of goods for sale. He would like to thank everyone for their support and promises to manage the current loan with accuracy.

name: Thang
description: Thang was born in 1977. She has two sons who attend primary school and secondary school. Her husband is a construction worker. His income is about 6,000,000 VND per month. Thang sells groceries to earn a living. Each month, she earns about 5,000,000 VND. She has done this job for 10 years. The total income of her family is about 10,000,000 VND. Thang has taken part in SEDA’s microfinance program since 2004. The last cycle, she borrowed 9,810,000 VND and repaid the loan on time. In this loan cycle, she wants to borrow about 11,118,000 VND to buy more noodles, candy, beer, and biscuits for her grocery store. She always wants to enlarge her business in the market.

name: Anara
description: Anara is 40 years old, married, and the mother of five children. As the main income provider for her family, from 2002 she has worked in animal husbandry and agriculture. Today, Anara has five cows on her farm, as well as 1.5 hectares of her own land, where she cultivates potatoes and beans. Her total monthly income comes to about 16,000 som (KGS).  In order to further develop her business, Anara has applied to Bai Tushum Bank for a loan of 60,000 som (KGS). This will help her to buy ten sheep for fattening up and reselling. She plans to invest the funds from the loan in the further expansion of her farm.

name: Body Spray Group
description: This is 38 years old Isha, she is married and has three children, who are all in school.  Isha belongs to a solidarity group of 4 women, who have come together to complement each other achieve their individual dreams.  “Body Spray” is the name of Isha’s solidarity group.    The women have named their group “Body Spray” because they are determined to repay their loan on time.  “Body Spray” group needs a total loan of 4,000,000SLL.  Isha will receive 1,000,000SLL which she needs in order to buy three boxes of soap, one box of body spray, one box of tooth paste, one box of toilet rolls and ten dozens of body spray etc for her business.   Isha stands on the right hand side of the photo.  Isha established her cosmetics business in 2000; she established the business to ensure her family gets enough money for their basic needs.  She uses the profit from this business to provide livelihood for her family and support her children’s education.  She opens her business Monday through Saturday every week.  Isha is a hardworking woman.She hopes that this loan will help her generate more profit to support her family. Isha is a married with three children ages of 17, 12 and 4 years and all are school going childrenIn the future, Isha plans to support her children to acquire university education.  She was able to increase her business and the livelihood of her family based on the profit she raised during the last loan.    She thanks you for supporting them.

name: Nver
description: Nver is 41 years old and lives in the village, Vahagni, in the Lori region. He has a very nice large family; he lives with his wife, two school-aged children and his retired parents. Thanks to his father’s precious and useful advice, Nver has become a very skilled and clever farmer who owns a very nice large farm. He is also engaged in bee-keeping and in fish keeping.   Nver has built a small artificial lake by himself where he breeds a fish called ‘’sazan’’ (European carp). As he says, this type of fish is greatly demanded by people and is very tasty. He sells the fish to his villagers and to fast-food centers. His farm also is rich with livestock such as cows, calves and piglets. His mother helps him to sell their farm's dairy products and also honey which is pure and very tasty.   Nver is asking for a loan of 500,000 Armenian drams in order to buy some fish forage as during winter months he must take care of his fish properly in order to sell them in spring.

name: Efua
description: Efua cooks banku (a dish made from corn dough) for sale; she serves it with fried fish, pepper and tomato sauce at Adum Enyinase, near Elmina. She is a widow and has four children. Efua has done this for six years. She uses her income to feed her family and pay her accomodation bills. Her loan will be used to purchase bags of maize and fish which she uses in preparing her banku for sale. She hopes to use the new profits from her business to mount a stall for the sale of her cooked banku and fish.

name: Flores De Chontola Group
description: The community of Chontola is located in a rural area outside of the Western Highland town of Chichicastenango in Guatemala. There are eleven women who live here who have formed the Friendship Bridge Trust Bank “Flores de Chontola” or “Flowers of Chontola”. They share an enthusiastic spirit and an optimistic outlook. The majority of them work in traditional textile production.  Herminia is a 39-year-old member of the Trust Bank with eight children. Although she only was able to attend school for a year, she has a lot of drive and vision to empower herself, raise the standard of living for her family, and provide education for her children. Herminia prepares and sells delicious snacks during the week, delivering them to the homes of her customers. She also has an orchard where she grows apples and peaches and sells her fruit in her community on market days. Herminia is requesting a loan that she will use to purchase ingredients and supplies for her snacks as well as insecticides and other materials for her orchard.  It is impossible for a woman like Herminia to walk into a Bank in her area to secure a loan. There is no where for her to gain new skills and information. The Microcredit Plus Program of Friendship Bridge (loans+education) helps her and the members of the Trust Bank step into a new world as empowered and more educated women and mothers. Thank you KIVA investors for funding these much needed loans!

name: Leoncio
description: Leoncio is the happy father of a family, married to a wonderful woman with whom he has home full of love. They have 3 children, and they give their all to offer them better opportunities in life.  For more than 10 years now, he has sold vegetables and lentils for a living, in his city's fairgrounds. He believes that everything is going well for him because of all his effort, his hard work every day, and because he is a very good person.  Leoncio thanks the lenders on Kiva for the support they provide. He will be able to purchase seeds, such as lima beans, to sow on his fields. This will give him better sales and allow him to expand his business and offer more products to his customers in the future.

name: Mary
description: Mary  is 39 years old.  She is a married with 7 children between 9 and 20. She has owned a small cafe since 2003. Every day, she works from 6am to 10pm at her business and can earn a monthly profit of about $175 from her sales.   Mary now hopes for a loan to buy more items for her business.

name: Josefa
description: Josefa is a married parent of five children. She sells fish and raises pigs in the Philippines to earn money to support her family. Josefa has taken out and successfully repaid 25 previous loans through Kiva's field partner NWTF to help sustain her fish business. She is now borrowing 19,500 PHP to buy additional boxes of fresh fish to sell. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Jaime
description: Jaime lives with Mrs. Juanita G. Rayas. They have their own salon, which they have been working at for the past 11 years. In addition to the salon, they also run the "Nefertiti Beauty Institute." Their business is very well-established; they have regular clients and also train students to be stylists.   They are requesting this loan so that they can buy more merchandise and pay their providers in order to better serve their customers with great comfort and high-quality beauty services.   Translated from Spanish by Cynthia McMurry, Kiva Volunteer

name: Wilson
description: Wilson is a 40-year-old businessman. He is married to Nelius, a businesswoman. They are blessed with two children. He has been running an auto spare parts business for the past ten years, with a monthly income of KES 10,000 which he uses to support his family.   He is applying for his third loan term from KADET LTD after repaying the previous loans successfully. Wilson will use the loan to buy more stock of spare auto parts for his business.   With the anticipated profit from the business he will educate his children. His hopes and dreams are to expand his business and improve the family living standards.

name: La Santa Cruz Group
description: This group is called LA SANTA CRUZ, a family group. They chose this name because they’re natives of the community, “Ranchería La Cruz,” in Nacajuca, Tabasco where they celebrate this festival. There are 3 members of the group, Vidalia J. O. and Cástulo H. G. (married), who sell fruit and vegetables, and María Santos V. S. who sells shoes by catalog.  The married pair, doña Vidalia y don Castulo, sell fruits and vegetables and will invest their loan in this. They have their stall in the Pino Suárez market, located in Villahermosa, capital of the state. They also sell products in their home from the entryway of their house. They have three children that are studying in secondary and primary schools.  Their long-term dream is to have a well-stocked fruit shop that will allow them to employ their family and have a steady income. It would be a self-sufficient business that could pay their children’s tuition. They are motivated and thankful, because thanks to the loan granted by Kiva and Fundación Realidad, their business is moving to meet their dreams. Translated from Spanish by Rebecca Towle, Kiva Volunteer

name: Cristina
description: Cristina is 55 years old and married with four children.  Cristina works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more groceries to sell in her general store. She has been running the general store for 15 years and also earns an income from poultry.  Cristina has borrowed and repaid two loans from NWTF before this loan.   Cristina aspires to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Meas
description: Mrs. Meas M., age 33, works selling grocery products at home, earning around $4 each day in revenue. Her husband is a teacher, earning around $4 each day. They have four students who are students. She would like to request a loan of $700 in order to purchase 15 piglets to raise and buy feed for her livestock supplies.

name: Edelina
description: Edelina is 48 years old and has two children.  Edelina is married, and both of her children are in school.  Edelina is in the agricultural business, raising pigs in the Philippines. Edelina requested a 23,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) loan through NWTF in order to buy feeds and vitamins for her pigs.  Edelina has been raising pigs for 10 years now, and has borrowed ten times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Edelina would like to save enough money in order to support the financial stability for her family.

name: Miomboni Group
description: Sili, who is in her late 40s, is married with five children, four in school.  She has been running a grocery store for two years now. She works from 3:00 p.m. to midnight daily and is able to make a small monthly profit.   This will be Sili's first loan from Tujijenge Tanzania. She will use loan to buy drinks for the store. She dreams of owning a supermarket.  Sili will share this loan with her loan group "Miomboni," which consists of eight members who will hold each other accountable for paying back the loan.

name: Liberty
description: Liberty is a married woman from Concepcion, Iloilo. She is 48 years old and a mother of four children, three who are adult and one who still need their support. Liberty earns a living by running a sari-sari (variety) store business. Aside from this, she also helps her husband in fishing. Although she and her husband work together, still the profit that they earn is not enough. That is why Liberty comes up into a decision of borrowing money to operate their business continuously. She is asking a bigger amount of loans for additional capital to buy grocery items such as noodles, canned goods, eggs, cooking oil, coffee, powdered milk, powdered chocolate drink, sugar, toiletries, candies, chips, biscuits and drinks. In the future, Liberty wants to improve their business and able to augment their livelihood.

name: Rikana Ole
description: Rikana Ole N. 57 years old. He is a farmer and supports five people in his family. His spouse is Mashipei N. and they have five children. Mashipei is a housewife and she helps Rikana with his farming activity.  Rikana has been wheat farming for the last 15 years. This will be his first loan and he is planning  to spend 10,000 Kenyan shillings to buy chemicals and fertilizer and 10,000 shillings on the cost of spraying his wheat farm.  He is planning to use the anticipated profit from his farming to expand his farming activity by renting a bigger piece of land to increase his wheat production.  His hopes and dreams are that he will become a large-scale farmer owning a bigger piece of land and being financially stable to support his family.

name: Nyaruhanda Twimukye, Ibanda Group
description: K. Wily, aged 45, is hardworking and dedicated to his farming business where he deals in a variety of farm aspects that include a banana plantation enterprise and animal rearing. He has been doing this for over fifteen years and it has earned him a profit of 200,000 Ugandan shillings monthly that has helped in providing basic needs for his children and family as well as business expansion.  This loan will be of great value for Wily to purchase farm tools like hoes, fertilizer and to modernize his plantation to improve on his banana crop (which is commonly used by customers for making a local dish). He will also be able to buy pesticides for the pests and diseases which are a great threat to his business products. This will increase his sales revenue and enable him to pay his daily bills including his children’s school bills.  Wily belongs to a group of members who hold each other accountable and insure one another in paying back the loan.

name: Lourdes
description: Lourdes, 26, has a five-year-old child and is pregnant.  Previously she worked in the home of a family and gradually she got together the money to open a small business, to be near her son.  This way she became independent and, thanks to her sales strategy, she grew.  She is a very hardworking person and she shows it every day working in her small store, thanks to which she gives her son everything he needs.  She is requesting the loan to buy a variety of beverages, and sugar and flour.  She is grateful to the foundation for the opportunity it is giving her; it is very important support for her because the loan is the only opportunity to grow her business.

name: Pacita
description: Pacita is married, and she works hard to support her family.  She has a guitar-making business in the Philippines. Pacita is borrowing 13,000 PHP through NWTF to buy materials needed for her guitar-making business.  Pacita has been sustaining her business activities through her past six loans from NWTF and, more recently, through Kiva. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth is a 35-year-old married woman from Getafe, Bohol, Philippines. She has four young children and has been in the fishing business for more than 15 years. Her husband works as a fisherman.  Elizabeth is a hard-working woman. She gives her best to provide support to her husband in meeting the needs of the family, especially for the schooling of their children.  Elizabeth will be able to use the loan to buy a new fishing net, fuel, and for the repair of the fishing boat, so that her husband can enhance his daily catch.  In the future, Elizabeth wants to make their way of living a success. More importantly, she wants to send her children to school for a better education and a bright future.

name: Ranohon
description: Ranohon is forty-three, married, and has raised three children.  Her son is grown and works in construction in the Russian Federation, earning 10,000KGS per month.  Her middle daughter is a paraplegic and receives a monthly stipend of 3,800KGS.  The youngest daughter is in school.  Her husband is very active in helping out on the farm.  Ranohon has a middle school education and is a very industrious, honest, and responsible person.  As the family's main breadwinner, she farms crops and breeds livestock.  She started out twenty-five years ago with 5,000KGS and today the farm brings in nearly 8,000KGS per month selling milk and milk products.  Ranohon currently has one cow with a calf.  The farm consists of .52 hectares of land and she rents a one hectare plot where they raise potatoes, corn, and cotton.  In order to expand her business, Ranohon has turned to Bai Tulum for a loan of 50,000KGS so she can buy two calves.  Down the line they will produce more milk and Ranohon can increase her income.

name: Amélé
description: Amélé is 21 years old, married, with one child under her care.  She lives in Baguida and resells spices. She buys her goods at the market twice a month and resells them from home and in the neighborhood.  Amélé is taking a loan in order to buy several bowlfuls of dry okra and crushed chili.  Her goal is to sell enough merchandise to make a profit and help her husband take care of the children's education.

name: Rehema
description: Rehema is a hard-working woman, who works hard to facilitate the life of her family and to boost their living standard. The previous loan helped her to purchase ingredients for juice preparation. Here again, she comes to you requesting a loan. This time, the amount she is borrowing is KES 40,000, and she will use it to buy more fruits, sugar and squash, for her juice business. She appreciates the support.

name: Bibiroy
description: Bibiroy D. lives in Yavan.  She is 50 years old, a widow, and has five children. Bibiroy tailors women’s clothes.  She has been doing this for more than twelve years. This business helps to support her large family.  Bibiroy’s children are still in high school. Now, the client wants to buy a more modern sewing machine. Therefore, she has decided to take out a loan for nine months.Translated from Russian by Melissa Kniazeva, Kiva Volunteer

name: Cecilia
description: As a married parent of six children, Cecilia works hard to support her family.  She has a butcher shop business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from prepared food vending. Cecilia is borrowing PHP 25,000 through NWTF to purchase more meat to sell for her butcher shop business.  She successfully paid back her previous loan and now she has requested an additional loan to further build her business.  Cecilia has been sustaining her business activities through her past 21 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Norma's Group
description: Norma E. is from the village of Holy Friday. She is 52 years old. Norma is the leader of a seven-member group loan offered by ASKI. While each member of the group receives an individual loan, they are all collectively responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults. The official name of this borrowing group is Norma E.'s Group.  Norma is married and has four school-aged children.   To make a living, Norma owns and operates a specialized retail store, selling daily use products such as shampoo, soap and toothpaste in the local community. Norma has been engaged in her business for over four years and earns approximately 4,000 PHP a month.  In 2006, Norma joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her business and living situation. Norma has successfully repaid a previous loan of 12,000 PHP from ASKI. This previous loan was used to purchase additional products to sell.   Norma is requesting a new loan of 13,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase new items to expand her product offering. This will be the 12th loan taken out by Norma from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to pay the tuition fees of her children.   About ASKI: ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 38 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Hussein
description: Hussein is a 33 year-old married father of two children. He owns a farm where he rears cattle and different kinds of birds. He makes his revenue by selling cow milk and chicken eggs. His wife is unemployed, and both his children are still in school.  Hussein's income is insufficient to provide a healthy life for his family, especially since schooling expenses are costly. As a result, Hussein contacted Al Majmoua to acquire a loan and purchase more cattle, which would greatly increase his output and thus also increase his revenue. As for the future, Hussein wishes to expand his farm.

name: Abrabo Pa Group
description: Grace is a 48-year-old woman who describes herself as hard-working.  She has 3 children.    For the past 8 years, Grace has operated a food retail business selling items such as rice, stew, gari (cassava grits), beans and cooked yams.  Gari is processed from cassava.  She will use the loan to purchase more food supplies for her business.  She would like to expand her business by opening a wooden structure where she can sell her food items.    Grace is the leader of the group named 'Abrabo Pa', which means “living a decent life ” in Twi, the language most commonly spoken in Ghana.  There are 10 members in this group.  The other members in the group operate retail businesses selling items such as fish, groceries, body cream and body spray.

name: Mayela
description: Mayela V. Z., 49, is a widow and lives with her three daughters.  She will use the funds to buy a computer.  She wants to buy the computer so that her daughters that are in school will have a tool that is so important nowadays for school so that they can do their assignments.  Mayela is a farmer, specifically coffee.  This is her first loan request from FUDECOSUR and she is very happy with the terms offered.  She hopes in future to provide a better quality of life and improved financial stability for her family as well as to continue to grow both as a person and as a farmer.   Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Pleg Group
description: This is 39-year-old Gertrude from Gweru, the capital of the Midlands province in Zimbabwe. She is married with four children. Three of her children are attending school.  Gertrude runs a clothing business selling clothes and shoes. The business has been in operation for 14 years. She says the main challenges faced are high competition, seasonal sales, transport costs and low demand. Gertrude has requested a loan of $400 to buy winter wear such as jackets, boots and blankets. She says the extra income generated as a result of this loan will allow her to pay her children’s school fees, and improve her family's standard of living in terms of better food and more disposable income. In the future, Gertrude plans to have a shop at another flea market and venture into the poultry business.

name: Madeline
description: Madeline is a hardworking, entrepreneur who has a business selling personal products in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 9,000 through NWTF in order to buy more items like body-lotion, perfume, shampoo and other personal products to sell to customers. Madeline has been in this business for six years. She also earns more income from fish vending. Madeline has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to save enough money to expand her business and repair her family's home.

name: Flora Julieta Del Carmen
description: Flora is 68 years old. She is a widow and lives with her eight children in the Ventanas canton of Los Ríos province in Ecuador.  Flora makes a living selling fast food and drinks. She is applying for this loan in order to have working capital to expand her business. Flora buys her supplies in Ventanas. Her goal is to increase sales of fast food. One challenge Flora is facing is illness. In her spare time, Flora likes to go to mass.

name: Phuong
description: Phuong, 49, is married and has three children. She lives with her family in Ho Chi Minh City. Her husband earns an income as a bus driver. Phuong started a general store nine years ago.   She is requesting a loan to expand her business by buying a greater variety of beverages and household items to sell at her store so that she can better satisfy her customers. She hopes her business will run smoothly and will generate a higher income to assist her in improving her family's living conditions.

name: Mary Jane
description: Mary Jane L. is a married woman who lives in Purok 1, Brgy. Culipapa, HInobaan, Negros Occidental.  She earns her living by operating 2 business ventures:  fishing and a fish selling business.  Her husband Randolf, who is 42 years old, works as a fisherman to earn his living, and also helps in his wife's business activities.    They have four children who are between the ages of 2 to 16 years old.  Mary Jane joined NWTF-Project Dungganon in 2005 because she aspired for something better for her family. With the help of her past 13 loans from NWTF-Project Dungganon, Mary Jane has been incrementally lifting her family out of poverty by the sweat of her brow.  Her previous loan of PHP 13,000 helped her earn a monthly profit of PHP 20,000, increasing the family's standard of living.    This time, for her 14th loan, she is borrowing PHP 15,000, which she intends to buy fishing gears and equipment for the fishing boat so that she could continue to save up for the future education of her children.  Mary Jane L. is a Dungganon woman who is following an honorable path toward the achievement of her dreams.   About NWTF:   In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means Honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress from earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem that is bestowed to a member of a community who has earned the respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work. Help NWTF continue its mission to help the poorest in the Philippines by clicking  the link to the   NWTF Kiva lending team  on Kiva.org to join our team.

name: Irshad's Group
description: Irshad lives in the mid-sized city of Vehari, which is known for its agriculture industry. She owns a 3 room brick house where she has been living with her family for over 20 years. She is 42 years old and the mother of five sons and two daughters. Her husband is illiterate and is involved in the animal selling business. He also owns a small piece of land where he grows wheat and sells it to his customers.   Irshad's eldest son has a mobile phone shop where he sells used mobile phones to his customers. The other two sons work in the field along with their father, helping him grow wheat. Her other children are very young and are getting their education from a local school.   Irshad has applied for a loan from Kiva's partner, Asasah, for her eldest son’s business. He will use the loan to buy used mobile phone sets to sell in his shop. Irshad is hopeful that her son will be able to successfully improve his business by making this investment in it. Irshad is a new loan applicant with Asasah and she is hopeful that it will be a profitable experience for her.

name: Emilio
description: Emilio is an honest, responsible, and hardworking individual.  He is also enterprising and cheerful.  Emilio enjoys challenges so that he can get better each day.  His aspiration is to become a well-known and important rancher.  The first step toward achieving his goal is to study for a degree in Agricultural Management, which will open doors.  Emilio is requesting this loan so that he can continue his studies as he strives to reach his goals.

name: Editha
description: Editha A. runs a grocery store selling household items such as canned goods, etc., in her community. She is 46 years old, married and has two school-aged children. They are from the village of Mitimos, Rizal. Editha has been in her business for over five years and earns approximately 3,000 Philippine pesos (PHP) a month.  In 2006, Editha joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living conditions and enable her to engage in business activities. Editha has successfully repaid a previous loan of 7,000 PHP from PMPC which was used as additional capital for her business. Editha is requesting a new loan of 14,500 PHP which will be used to purchase additional stock to sell. This will be her 8th loan from PMPC.   About PMPC: Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.  Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Miguela
description: Miguela is 39 years old and a cheerful hardworking mother.  She lives in her own home with her husband Edgar, age 38, and their ten year old daughter Leonela for whom she wants to provide a better quality of life.  Miguela has worked hard to maintain her fields that produce the necessary foods to support her family.  Before the first rays of sunlight can be seen, she leaves her house and walks for nearly an hour prior to arriving at her farmland where she grows beans, potatoes, corn, ulluco, and peas.  These crops are later sold at the wholesale market in the city of Tarma.  She greatly enjoys her work, especially the cultivation phase.  Miguela has been farming for seven years and considers the most difficult part of her job to be transporting her products to market since the sacks are extremely heavy and exhausting to carry.  Her greatest wish is to buy more land so that she can increase production.  This is her fourth loan with MFP.  In her Communal Bank, Miguela is highly respected because she seeks to restore order in all of the meetings.  The loan of 1000 PEN that she requested will be used to buy more compost to make her land more productive.  Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Mujeres Forjadoras Group
description: Ms. Irma is a 54-year-old divorced mother of three. She is a member of the Mujeres Forjadoras community bank, a group that is comprised of 10 members who own small businesses. Irma has been making and selling bed sheets, bedspreads, and slipcovers for a living for 24 years. She launched this business because she did not want to depend on her partner since he did not let her work and treated her badly. Consequently, Irma got a divorce and had to support her three children, so she set up the sewing shop in which she currently works. Irma states that it was not easy. She had to knock on some doors and sell her merchandise, but thanks to her dedication and efforts, she has managed to obtain better profits, a better quality of life, and a good education for her children. Her eldest son even has his own business now. This loan is for purchasing livestock (cows and bulls) so that she can sell them; this is a new business that she is planning on getting into. We know that Irma will reach her goals with her hard work and efforts, and that these Edaprospo loans will help her.

name: Nancy
description: Nancy is a member of the community bank "Unidas Triunfaremos" (United we will triumph). She lives with her partner, is 30 years old, and has two children, aged 9 and 3, who attend the state school. Nancy herself never went to school because since she was a girl she has always worked, helping her mother to sell fruit. Now she rents her own locale in the same market, selling fruit. Each day she buys stock of fruit (10 boxes) and works from 7am to 5pm. She has done well since aligning herself with Finca; she has more capital and has learned how to save. Nancy needs a loan of 1200 soles to build a food-selling business and buy chairs, tables and plates. Her dream is to have her own business selling food.Translated from Spanish by Pamela Carreón, Kiva Volunteer

name: Yerly Gihovana
description: Good day meet Yerly Gihovana. She is studying at Campo Alto in the Oral Health program, entering her third semester. She wants to request a loan from Kiva as her family is in a favorable financial situation and the installment fees are not high. They live in a rented apartment.   Her father died when she was small and since then her mother has taken charge of everything financial, including education and basic necessities. Her mother works as an operator in a sewing company. Her salary isn't high enough to pay their food, rent and services. So a loan from Kiva would allow her to finish her studies in a satisfactory manner as she postponed her first semester of practicum due to lack of financial resources.   Her mother was without work and Yerly had to find work, in a restaurant as a waitress to help with the household expenses. Now Yerly is without work and her mother is who is paying for her studies at Campo Alto. She hopes to graduate to help earn what is needed for her family and enjoy a better quality of living.   Yerly is grateful for this opportunity offered her to finish her studies. She has had experiences which really affect her. After the death of her father she has dedicated herself to helping her mother get ahead in spite of the difficulties and particulars that have befallen her and her mom.

name: Marvin
description: Marvin is an older gentleman who wants to move forward with his family. For that, he needs to do some repairs in the kitchen where he prepares food. He needs a loan of one million colones (1,000,000) to make these arrangements. He wants a better future for himself and his family.

name: Rosemae
description: Rosemae is a married woman with two children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. She is 35 years old and has two children who are in school.  She has a dressed chicken business in the Philippines. Rosemae requested a PHP 10,000 loan amount through NWTF in order to purchase more dressed chicken to sell in her food stall.  Rosemae has been in this business for six years. In the future, she would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Balqees
description: Balqees is the age of 40; she is the mother of four children. She lives in Lahore, Pakistan. She is a house wife and looks after her family at home.   Her husband works in dairy products, like milk, curd, and butter, for sale. He owns a small dairy farm that consists of buffaloes and cows. He daily sells milk to different tea stalls. He is an honest man. He manages his household necessities from his earning from milk sale.    He speaks with an even tone which is impressive and he easily wins the trust of his clients. He was in need of one buffalo to increase his income through the milk sale business, so Balqees requested a loan. In this way she can support her husband's business.  She thanks Kiva and field partner BRAC Pakistan.

name: Virgen De Copacabana Group
description: Felicitas is 49 years old, separated, and has three adult children.  She is a member of the Virgen de Copacabana group, made up of 13 responsible and enterprising members.    Felicitas works selling groceries.  With the goal of improving her store and helping with the household expenses, she is requesting a loan to purchase rice, sugar, and oil.  Her greatest wish is to continue working at her store.    The Virgen de Copacabana group is grateful to everyone who made this loan possible.  Felicitas is the third from the left, dressed in a black shirt.

name: Sirush
description: Sirush is 60 years old and she is a very clever and successful businesswoman. She lives in Ijevan city in the Tavush region of Armenia. She has a son who is married and lives with her. He is a constructor. Sirush’s daughter-in-law works at the school as a teacher. Sirush for some time worked at different workshops and factories as a worker, then she had a clothes trading business, and now she has a food shop of her own. Her shop is located near her house which is very close to the central road of their city. It is greatly visited buy the citizens and passersby, and Sirush is satisfied with her business income. In her shop she sells a great assortment of candies, dairy-products, alcoholic drinks, sausages, etc.  Sirush wants to enlarge and refresh her shop’s food and non alcohol drinks assortment and she asks a loan of 700,000 Armenian drams for the purchase of those products.

name: Akuvi
description: AKUVI is a young, 34-year-old widow. She lives in the Nyékonakpoè neighborhood with her three children. She has been selling pagnes (traditional wrap-arounds) since 2011. In order to satisfy the constant needs of her clientele and to diversify her products, AKUVI is seeking a loan to buy 5 pieces of pagnes. This loan will also allow her to increase her business numbers and to take care of her children’s needs, which falls on her alone.

name: Grethel Cristhina
description: Grethel started her own business when she was very young.  She did this because she has always liked being independent.  She lives with her life partner and her child in the San Juan neighborhood in the Concepción municipality.  She will use the loan to buy merchandise like women’s clothes, which is her greatest demand.  However, she will also take advantage of the national holidays this month in order to buy uniforms and shoes.  She will do this in order to get greater income.  This way she will be able to improve her living conditions.  Grethel is grateful for the support that AFODENIC and Kiva are providing.

name: Luisa Amanda
description: Luisa Amanda, 50, is married and lives in the Villa Reconciliacion neighborhood. She has three childres, ages 17, 23 and 26. Luisa's business is the sale of plastic wares. Her husband and she work together and have seen their business grow since they started with the help of loans 15 years ago. Luisa is requesting a loan to purchase constructions materials to repair the roof in the her daughter's room.  In the future, her goal is to purchase a wider variety of products to satisfy her customers' demands. Her dream is to provide a good education for her youngest son.    Translated from Spanish by Maria B., Kiva Volunteer

name: Sector Xon Group
description: The 8 women of “Sector Xon” trust bank live in the rural outskirts of Chichicastenango, an Indigenous Maya K’iche city high up in the mountains of central Guatemala, in the department of Quiché. They take advantage of the huge market of Chichicastenango every Thursday and Sunday, which brings people from all over, to sell their products: farm-fresh peaches, which they grow, and harvest, and huipiles, blouses traditional to their culture. Rosalía is the president of the trust bank. She is 32 years old, and has 2 children, studying in primary school. Her husband works in agriculture, and Rosalía runs a weaving business, creating huipiles, traditional mayan blouses, embellishing them with elaborate embroidered designs. When she is not creating her beautiful detailed product, Rosalía is in the market of Chichicastenango selling it to locals and travelers who come to the market. With the loan that she is requesting from Kiva, this talented woman will invest in materials for the creation of her huipiles, threads and dyes to diversify and color her designs. Rosalía has been with Friendship Bridge for 2 cycles, and her work with this organization has relieved some of the stress in her life and strengthened her business. With between 30 and 60 years of age, some of these women did not have the opportunity to study and those who did only studied though some level of primary school. Most of the women are married and have from 2 to 11 children of their own who are in school. These ladies greatly appreciate the opportunity to receive quick and consistent credit through Friendship Bridge and Kiva.

name: Holane
description: Holane, age 42, is married and she has five children.  She resells household goods and has been involved in this activity for the past five years.  She is taking a loan to increase her stock.

name: Asmaa
description: Asmaa is a 50-year-old married Palestinian refugee who has been working in her own house as a tailor for nine years to help her husband make a living and cover their needs. She has a very good reputation in her region, with her special talents and the customer service she provides. She puts much effort into developing and expanding her business, to make sure that she can remain capable of covering her family’s needs.  Asmaa is acquiring a loan from Kiva's field partner Al Majmoua, to legally register her house as she wants to maintain her husband's taxi car.

name: Erna
description: Erna is 41-years-old and is a married woman with 3 children. The oldest child is 16-years-old.   Erna is in the business of raising hogs. She earns about 6000 PHP from this business. Erna also runs a small sari-sari store business. She sells items like vinegar, soy sauce and canned goods to the people in her community. Erna has requested this loan to buy pig feed and more items to sell such as canned goods and noodles. She hopes for her business to progress. She also hopes to be able to sustain her children's education.

name: La Buena Amistad Group
description: Elsa belongs to La Buena Amistad Communal Bank.  She's single and lives with her father and her son.  Elsa works as a merchant.  Her business is located in a market in her area.  She sells grocery products: all types of legumes, pasta, and canned goods.  Her job allows her to support her son and help her father.  Elsa's proud to have her own business and she goes to a lot of effort to offer quality products so her customers will always buy from her.  The loan she has requested is to invest in her business by buying groceries so her business will continue to grow.  Later she would like to have another place to increase her income.  Elsa's grateful to the investors for their support through this loan to both her and her communal bank.  In the photo she's the second from the left (standing); she's wearing a black sweater.  The photo on the right is of Rosa María.

name: Shushanik
description: Shushanik lives in Dzoravanq village with her husband and two sons. Her elder son currently serves in the army and other one is employed in the private sector. Shushanik and her husband are running a farm. They have a big and beautiful farm with livestock (cows, sheep, chickens and pigs) and arable land where a large variety of fruit trees and vegetables are cultivated.  Shushanik has requested this loan for enlarging her farm. The loan of USD 3,000 will be a big support for her to buy 14 more calves.  She will be very grateful to lenders if they support her to develop her farming business. Although her sons bring income to the family, the income gathered from the farming business is very important for Shushanik to cover everyday expenses.

name: Jackline
description: Jackline resides in Namwela, a remote village in the lush hills of Bungoma, in the Rift Valley of Kenya. As the key breadwinner of her family, she has been practicing mixed farming for the past 11 years. Her primary sources of income have been milk, sheep farming, eggs, and sugar cane crops. Although she has been making profits from farming, she has identified a big market for sugar The only big challenge she faces is lack of funds to increase her sugarcane farming. Jackline is seeking a loan to buy more seeds and increase her sugarcane farming.Market for the sugarcane is never a problem because the demand is always high and she plans to take advantage of that. She plans to increase her market by using word of mouth to reach more customers and markets. You can help this mother achieve her dreams with this loan, which will surely bring big profits.With your support of this loan, you will be promoting the farming ideas of a Kenyan!

name: Puttaraju
description: Establishing seed diversity centers, entrepreneurial stewardship for farmers, availability of healthy wholesome food and market independence from brokers is of prime importance today.  Puttaraju is a dedicated organic farmer growing millet and potatoes. His interest is to develop a market for uncultivated wild food crops and make them accessible to urban consumers.  Puttaraju is married and has two children. Both of them are studying. His son is in fifth grade and his daughter is in tenth grade. He lives in a small house with basic amenities.   Puttaraju has established a basic seed bank at his house. He has even received good media coverage for it. He also entertains exchange of seeds with other farmers from various places.  He is seeking this loan to realize his dream of showcasing the traditional varieties of uncultivated food crops under one roof, which will help other farmers and interested people to explore all possible avenues. Such a showcase will allow him to identify the specific needs of buyers and also to network with people across this sector.

name: Dilnoza
description: Dilnoza is a conscientious, goal oriented and hardworking woman.  She was born in an agricultural area that has good conditions for raising livestock and growing crops.  Dilnoza's family was poor and she helped her parents since childhood with raising livestock and growing crops.  Dilnoza herself has had a lot of hardships in life, because she lived in a poor family.  After finishing high school, Dilnoza married a livestock breeder and helped her husband raise livestock and grow crops.  They mostly raised livestock, purchasing livestock at the market at a low price, fattening it for a period of time and selling it at a high price.  Because of unfortunate weather and climate their business did not have positive returns.  Because of this, Dilnoza's husband plans to travel to earn money in the Russian Federation.  This is why Dilnoza turned to our organization for a loan for the purchase of a plane ticket for her husband; she plans to continue raising livestock.  Dilnoza hopes for your charity and mercy.

name: Carolina
description: Carolina is married with five children, and lives in Sindangan, Philippines. She is a diligent and determined mother, who has always been known to provide the best for her family. Carolina earns a living by making snacks that she sells and also on consignment in shops and cafes. She decided to expand her business after learning that she could obtain financial assistance through PMPC. Consequently, she has requested a 5,000 PHP loan to buy additional ingredients to increase production. Her goal is to be able to display her snacks in every shop and place to eat in the area. With the help and support of her husband, Carolina smiles at the thought of having a good standard of living for her family.

name: Eligia
description: Eligia is taking a loan of 600 USD to improve her business. She is running a mini-shop that helps her to generate income for her family.  She will use the loan to buy such things as shirts, long pants, shorts, and long-sleeved and short-sleeved t-shirts. She opened her mini-shop a year ago with her own working capital of 400 USD.  She is a hard working woman and she hopes to run a bigger business in the future.

name: Cesáreo
description: Cesáreo T.’s house needs some improvements done to the exterior, but he does not have the necessary money to make the improvements that his house needs.  This is why he is requesting a loan to buy materials and hire a person to finish his house.  Cesáreo works for the Mexican Postal Service in the mail delivery department.  He will pay off the loan will this income, as he is a widower and his children already have their own family.

name: Arcadio
description: Arcadio, is aged 51, married and blessed with nine children. He sells fish in their village for a living, and he's been in this business for almost eight years earning a net income of PHP 300 daily. His net income from this business is usually spent on the school allowances for their children.   Due to lack of capital to run his business, Arcadio would like to access a loan amounting to PHP 7,000 to purchase ten kilos of fish to sell. He's hoping that his business will continue to grow and become more profitable.

name: Lilia
description: Lilia is 54 years old, married, and has six children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Lilia has a general store business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 19,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional items to sell in her general store.She successfully paid back her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her business.Lilia has been in this business for seven years. In the future, she would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Alma Elcarte's Group
description: Alma is married and has 4 school-aged children.  She is 42 years old and lives in Malaubang, Ozamiz City.  Alma sells pork barbeque to earn a living and has had this business for 2 years. She has requested a loan of 5000 PHP to purchase ingredients like pork and sauce.  Alma has been a member of PMPC for 3 years. In the future, she hopes to expand her business to the neighboring town in Ozamiz.

name: Dina Ruth
description: Dina, aged 44, is an enterprising woman. She is married and is a homemaker devoted to her family and home.  Dina has been selling fish for 20 years. She goes out to sell her product in the neighbourhood every morning.  She needs a loan to buy fishing nets and more supplies for her business.  Dina hopes to improve her home and give her children the opportunity to study until they become professionals.

name: Evelyn
description: Evelyn is 53 years old and married with 1 child. She earns a living by farming rice in the Philippines. Evelyn is asking for a loan of PHP 5000 through NWTF to buy fertilizers and other farm tools. Evelyn has been farming rice for two years and also earns additional income from pig fattening. She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save money to expand her business.

name: Wakakooma Group
description: Mrs. Aminata is the leader of the Wakakooma group. She is doing well. She is married with a 6-year-old child who goes to school. She supports two people.    Aminata has been selling firewood and charcoal for 3 years. The firewood is delivered to her home, and she gets the charcoal from local wholesalers. Her clients are men and women from the area.   She wants to buy six sacks of charcoal and two piles of firewood. She will use her profits to bolster her activity. Her goals are to expand her business and to help her husband with the household expenses.

name: Mery Margot
description: Mery is an old client. She obtained a loan previous in the agency El Tejar for four loan cycles but she cancelled without problems. Now she is with the communal bank "Ejecutivos de Eors". She makes a living selling clothes and sports shoes in the local fairs of Patacamaya, the mining areas of the city of Potosí and in various galleries of the city of La Paz.   This loan is for buying clothes wholesale due to the orders that she already has. She is single, with no children, and lives in the area of Lower Sopocachi in her mother's house. At the moment the house in under construction and work had to stop due to the rain. With this activity she contributes towards the costs of construction and the household bills. She is a hard working, responsible person who feels very grateful for this opportunity which has been given to her.

name: Nelson Fernando
description: Fernando is a hardworking young man, studious, loving, responsible, and with dreams for the future. He has a job that he loves to do as it lets him show his abilities in selling and delivering good service. He works for an insurance firm. However, although this is his current job, he has always loved working with children so he chose to pursue a career in early childhood care since he has children and he sees the need for his country to have better education and he wants to help improve this and create a good future for his kids and for the other kids in his country.  He has good ideas for bringing this about, but he (like everyone else) needs resources to implement his projects and he needs Kiva's help for this. During his first semester of his degree he benefited from a Kiva loan and he hopes to be able to count on one for finishing his course as he has had a good educational base and is sure that he will continue to be able to reach his goals. In addition, his time at college has been good for him as he is the only guy in his class and he shares his day with 6 women. His professor, on seeing that he was the only man in the class, made him the monitor who offers support to his classmates and represents them both in the college and outside. He feels privileged to have this position and has taken it seriously, as he demonstrates with his final grades from the first semester and with his commitment and dedication to all that he does. For this and other reasons, he is politely requesting support for what remains of his training so that, one day, he can give back what he receives.

name: Kapuna
description: Kapuna is a 43 year old widow with 3 children. She makes and sells elei printed fabric to earn a living and has been doing this for 2 years. Kapuna has requested a loan to buy material, fabric paint, stencils, brushes, rollers, wooden carved designs and rubber gloves. She plans to use her profits to pay for her family's weekly expenses. She joined SPBD in 2014 to gain access to financial services.

name: Bendictus
description: Bendictus A. K. is 38 years old and married. They do not have any children yet. His business, known by the name Dragon Accessories, is located near a bus stop in a residential area in Nairobi. He has been selling mobile-phone accessories, like SIM cards, chargers, headphones, mobile batteries and mobile-phone covers, to the local people of Kariobangi for the last six years. He says the business is very profitable, although at times there is unavailability of some items.   He is using his loan of 40,000 Kenyan shillings to buy more phone accessories to expand his business. In the future, he hopes to move to the city center where there is more business. He describes himself as respectful and aggressive.

name: Pascual
description: An opportunity was what he hoped for.  It was not only an open door, but also what was behind the door.  What he found was something that defined what he wanted to be.  He is 42 years old and married.  He is from the Suchitepéquez department.  He has five children. The first one is married and has his own family.  The last four go to the school in the community where they live.  He makes an impressive effort, in spite of his age.  He is an enterprising man.  He says that it is never too late to start to develop and have a vision for the future.  His business activity, which has respectfully engaged in for three years, is buying and selling groceries in the community.  It is through this that he is able to get income for his family and earnings to improve their living conditions.  Pascual will use the requested loan to buy groceries in order to have his store stocked and to not lose the customers that he has.  His dreams are for his family’s living conditions to be adequate in the future and to give his children an education so that they become professionals and improve their living conditions.

name: Tumelo
description: Tumelo is a Business Management Student at the Maharishi Institute. Joseph is 22 years old and was asked the following questions by a staff member of the Institute: This is his story:What do you study at Maharishi Institute? Which classes you enjoy most I am studying towards a Bachelor of Arts Degree in management. The classes which I enjoy most are marketing management, business law and ethics and career strategies to name a few. However, I would say that all my classes have been pleasant and I have learned and grown from all of them.  What are your goals after graduating from the Institute? Please be specific: In which sector do you expect to work? In which city would you like to work? Would you like to travel? My goal is to find myself a decent work that will enable me to fulfil my needs, after that I would like to start the business in green sector. My goal here will be to reduce the harm that most of the company has already done. Johannesburg or Durban is my main city for this. Yes I would really like to travel outside of the country Tell us about your background. Where were you born? Do you have brothers and sisters? What do your parents do for work? Are you married? Do you have children? I am the only child in my family. I was born in Free State. My parent are domestic workers and I am not married and do not have children. What do you like to do in your spare time? In my spare time I would like to read, be with friends, go to the mall, watch movies and sometimes relax with my mother. How will a Kiva loan change your life? Describe how the loan will affect your studies and your lifestyle: will there be significant changes? Kiva loan will help me pay for my school fees, transport and have some money left for personal use. Because I will not have stress about my fees, I will be able to concentrate more on my studies.

name: Rene
description: René is married and has two children who are 5 and 7 years old; he lives in a neighborhood in Choloma, Cortes.  He started his own business about 7 years ago making leather belts.  He used to work for a private firm.  He started this business with his own funds and has kept it stable by means of loans.    He is currently asking for a 26,000 lempira loan to buy supplies like leather, buckles, rivets, thread and others he needs to make the belts.  He will buy these materials in a nearby country because it’s less expensive.  Most of his customers live outside the city and have requested products he has to deliver.  His goal is to make the business grow and eventually have his own commercial site.

name: La Esperanza Group
description: This communal bank, La Esperanze (The Hope), is from the city of San Lorenzo. The members of the bank are very hard-working people and have great eagerness to progress and succeed. Their goal is to improve the conditions of their families and help them to have a better way of life.  Señora Juliana is one of the members. She sells clothing of all types. She comments that she has good sales, since thanks to the good quality of her clothing, she already has a well-defined clientele who always buy from her. Her goal is to continue working and in this way help her family. She is applying for the loan to purchase clothing, with which she will be able to offer greater variety to her customers and at the same time attract more.

name: Horm
description: Mrs. Horm N. is 36 years old and lives in Kampong Cham Province.  She works as a vendor at the market, earning about $6/day in revenues.  She is married to a farmer, and together they are raising 4 children.  This loan will be used for the family to purchase a horse to help on their farm.

name: Rustam
description: B. Rustam is a very responsible and optimistic person; he has two children and a wife whom he has to support. Rustam wishes to develop his business. This business consists of raising cows in his village because there is a very high demand for milk from villagers and especially from customers who come from enclosed towns.   Rustam is helped by his wife. He is currently faced with many problems because his children are growing and, accordingly, their expenses are growing, too. The only way to get out of this difficulty is to succeed in business, so we hope that his capabilities and the services provided by IMON International will help him improve the business.    More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History  Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Mayisik
description: Mayisik is from the Hartashen village of the Syunik region, which is famous for its severe cold climate. People there are mostly involved in cattle farming and some land cultivation.   As a father of three children, Mayisik works hard to gather income and sustain his family. Mayisik breeds cattle. His livestock currently includes 12 cows, 10 calves, a pig and five chickens. He also cultivates wheat and sells the gathered harvest to locals.  As the sole financial income of the family comes from agriculture, Mayisik would like to expand his farm. He has applied for this loan to purchase two cows and forage for feeding the livestock. The loan is important for Mayisik to be able to expand his farm and gather more income, which will help him to improve his family's living conditions.

name: Jona
description: Jona is 47 years old and widowed with nine children. Five of her children are in school.Jona works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF in order to purchase more items such as biscuits, canned goods, noodles, and other groceries.Jona has borrowed and repaid seven loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for eight years and also earns an income from food vending.Jona aspires to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Dante
description: Dante is 55 years old. He has been planting and harvesting tobacco in his village for three years. Dante is a widower, which is why he is fully devoted to his business. Dante is requesting a loan of PHP 22,000 to buy fertilizer and seed for his tobacco farm. He hopes to expand his business.

name: Monica
description: Monica is a single woman with two children, both of whom attend school. She lives in a rental house that has electricity and piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are rent and food for the family.  For the past three years, Monica has operated a laundry business, and her potential customers are neighbors and passersby. Monica faces a major challenge of seasonality in her business. She dreams of expanding her business in the future. Monica plans to use this KES 20,000 loan to purchase a washing machine. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Nom
description: Nom, 56, is widowed and resides with two children in Kampong Chhnang Province, Cambodia. She is a rice farmer. Additionally, she makes flat baskets to sell. Her children are employed at a garment factory. Since the factory is far away from home, Nom is requesting a loan of $1000 US to purchase a motorbike for her children to commute to work. In the future, she would like to renew her house.

name: Annie
description: Annie is 42 years old and married with one child in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.  Annie has a frozen foods business in the Philippines. She requested a loan of 10,000 Philippines pesos (PHP) through NWTF in order to buy more stock of frozen foods to sell.  Annie has been in this business for five years. In the future, she would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Fe
description: Fe is a responsible mother who requests a loan from PMPC which she will use to increase her inventory.  She earns well with selling fried chicken. She wants to buy more kilos of chicken for retail. This way, she will be able to sell more products which will allow her to earn more money and provide her family with a better quality of life.

name: Rakma
description: Rakma is a hardworking, 19-year-old woman living in Lilongwe, the capital city of Malawi. She would like to set up her own business as a mobile money transfer agent so that she can provide a service to people who need to access financial services.Rakma is the breadwinner in a family of four. Her dream is to run her own business so that she can provide the basic needs for her family. Rakma’s challenge is that she does not have the capital needed to start running her own business. She is excited about the opportunity to be connected to Kiva lenders, as she sees this as an opportunity to change her life and that of her family.With this loan, Rakma will be able to purchase a trading trolley which she will set up outside one of the farmer’s shops in Mangochi. Rakma will also use this loan to purchase a web-enabled phone, which she will use to make the actual transactions. The loan will also provide Rakma with the float needed to serve her customers.Rakama’s dream is to influence some of the young people in her family to become entrepreneurs like her. She is hopeful that this will improve her standard of living.

name: Maxwell
description: Maxwell is an Organic and Fair Trade certified Oil Palm farmer who lives in Akim-Abaam in the Kwaebibirem District of the Eastern Region of Ghana, West Africa. He is 46 years old and married with three children. His children are having their Basic and Senior High School education. Maxwell believes Organic Oil Palm is sustainable and helps develop his community through job creation and infrastructural fair trade projects. In this regard, he wants to secure a Kiva Micro loan so that he can buy a Malaysian knife for pruning and harvesting of cocoa and oil palm.

name: Samiha
description: Samiha is a 52-year old married woman. She owns a small market for daily use products, in addition to baking Saj bread. Samiha opened her store 11 years ago so she has had long experience in this business.  She seeks to improve her business through increasing the different types of goods she sells. She wants to add fireworks for Christmas and New Year’s celebrations. She will also start selling toys for children, which is a good step forward.That’s why she is requesting a loan from Kiva partner, Al Majmoua.   Samiha is known for the good quality of products she sells, and good customer service. She aspires to give her customers better quality and prices with the help of the loan applied for, and through expanding her business more in the future.

name: Teresita
description: Teresita is 26 years old, single, and lives with her son, parents, and siblings who are her main priority.  She will use the money from this loan to buy a sewing machine, which she will use to make clothing and be able to take advantage of the training through INA.  She will also be able to buy fabrics and other supplies so she can better finish her clothing and increase her production.  With this she will be able to make more clothing and fulfill more orders in the short term.  This will be her first loan through FUDECOSUR.  She has not had previous loans through state banks, but FUDECOSUR has provided a loan with ease and at a much lower interest rate.

name: James' Group
description: James lives in a home with mud walls, a dirt floor and iron roof in Nyaigena village in Kuria East Sub-county, Kenya with his family which includes one child. The community of Nyaigena village collects their drinking water from a local well because there is no piped water supply in this part of rural Kenya.
