This water is easily contaminated with bacteria that can cause diarrhea and other water-borne diseases often making Nyaigena’s inhabitants sick and unable to work or attend school.  A new chlorine dispenser program offers a solution to the burden of sickness caused by unsafe drinking water. The dispenser is installed at the local water source where users turn a valve to add chlorine to their jerricans and then collect water as usual. The chlorine disinfects the water and provides residual protection from re-contamination. Nyaigena community will benefit from having access to the dispenser and safe water. James has volunteered to be the dispenser promoter who is responsible for refilling the chlorine and encouraging the rest of the community to treat their water and keep themselves and their families healthy. There are 4 other volunteer promoters from the surrounding community who are part of this group loan: Samuel, Mourice, Meteti and Peter.  Nyaigena community needs a loan to cover the costs of installing and maintaining the dispenser. James believes that the chlorine in the dispenser will help kill germs in drinking water in his community. The Kiva loan will be repaid by Evidence Action (www.evidenceaction.org) on behalf of the community through the sale of carbon credits. Using the chlorine dispenser generates carbon credits by avoiding the need to boil water to make it safe to drink. Revenues from the sale of carbon credits to organizations and individuals wanting to reduce world carbon footprints will be used to repay Kiva lenders and also to make sure that James’ community can have access to safe water now and in the future.

name: Natalya
description: Natalya is from Melitopol.  She is married and has two grown children.  Natalya sells women's underwear and hosiery in her own kiosk at the local market near the railway station.  She has a lot of experience in sales.  Natalya needs 10,000 hryven (UAH) to buy seasonal merchandise for selling at her kiosk.

name: Juan Jose
description: Juan Jose, 20, is single, and studying psychology at the university. He chose this major so he can help people who are emotionally unstable.   One of his goals is to work as a couples and family therapist.    Currently he works as a teacher and psychiatric consultant.   The loan will help to pay for the academic year and the fees to get his professional title.

name: Yiovanna Roxana
description: Yiovanna is a young woman of 28 years old who lives together with her husband and son of 7 years old.  Her house is located in the department of Ica.  The department of Ica is the only one on the south coast that is formed of plains.  It also has coastal prairies, since the mountain range of the Andes is far inland.  In Ica there are many deserts, such as the Pampas de Lancha and the Pampas de Villacuri, where the heat is intense.  It features beaches and hot springs, various marine fauna, site museums and excellent hotel services.  As a good Peruvian, she likes food a lot and one of her favorite dishes is the delicious "Aji de Gallina" (Chili Pepper Chicken).  She only studied until the fifth year of middle school, but she would have liked to study to be a teacher.  Because of this she works hard to give her son what he needs so that he can be better than her.  With a lot of effort and more than anything all the help from her husband, Yiovanna achieved having her own business selling clothing, to which she dedicates about 10 hours a day.  She can serve up to 20 customers each day.  She believes that her business is successful because she sells quality products at good prices and because of this her customers always return to her business.  Yiovanna is very thankful to the Kiva lenders since thanks to their help she will be able to buy more merchandise, and especially summer clothing.  This will allow her to have better revenue and so continue struggling to complete her greatest dream: "to give a good education to her son and to have her own shop in the city."

name: Medelina
description: Medelina is 47 years old and married with 4 children. She works very hard to provide for them. She runs a sari-sari (variety) store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 29,500 loan through NWTF to purchase more stock to sell.  She has been in this business for 6 years and sells a variety of items such as soft drinks, canned goods, noodles, spices, sugar, etc. In the future she would like to repair and renovate her family home.

name: Clarisa
description: Clarisa is 32 years old and married with four children. With four children in school, Clarisa works very hard to provide for them.  Clarisa runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 7,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase additional items to sell at her store, like canned goods, beverages, eggs, groceries, etc.  Clarisa has been in this business for two years and sells a variety of items, such as coffee, milk, juices, sachet, sugar, candies, shampoo, etc.  In the future, Clarisa would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Joel Isai
description: Joel is 25 years old.  He has a partner and will soon become a father for the first time.  He is a responsible, hard-working person who has a desire to make progress in life together with his family.  Joel has been raising and fattening chickens for five years.  He started out while he was still studying.  Owing to a lack of financial resources, he was not able to continue with his studies.  He needed to find a way to make a living.  He gradually started gaining knowledge and now he knows his business really well and would like to increase his production.  Joel buys his chickens and supplies in a city which is located two hours away by car or bus.  He needs more financial resources in order not to have to travel so much.   Joel is requesting a loan from Fundación Campo so that he can improve the shed where he will put the new chickens that he is going to buy.  He would also like to have cash available for buying supplies that he needs such as feed, vitamins, antibiotics and more equipment.  This will mean he will have the capital he needs to work in a more ordered manner, with an increased use of technology.  He hopes to increase his income because he will soon become a dad and so will need more income.  He would like to open more markets for his products, see his family do well, and be an exemplary father who his children will feel proud of in the future.

name: Chilufya
description: Chilufya is 25 years old, born and bred in the Southern Province of Zambia, home of the one of the eight wonders of the world, the mighty Victoria Falls. Chilufya comes from a humble, simple family. Her mother is a stay-at-home mother while her father is a local bus driver. That has left Chilufya to be a co-breadwinner of the family, supplementing the efforts of her father. She also helps to pay school fees for her three siblings.However, Chilufya, despite all her tireless efforts, still struggles to make ends meet. She is hampered by a serious lack of capital to sustain her business. She is therefore hoping that this Kiva loan can help her run her business profitably so she can also take herself to college one day and realize her dream of becoming a teacher. In her spare time, Chilufya loves to watch movies and is a passionate singer, especially of gospel music, which she also sings in church. Chilufya has requested a loan in order to help her start running her own business as a Zoona mobile money transfer agent.

name: Ruben Jonattan
description: Ruben is a young single man of 20 who works selling cleaning products in the market of Huaraz, his city of birth. Due to life circumstances, he was not able to study for a professional career, and for this reason he has worked since he was very young to help his parents. The ethic with which he works is the result of all the values inculcated in him by his parents. Every day he works with much more motivation because he wants to offer a better future to his family.  Ruben is very grateful to the Kiva lenders because with the support that they have offered him, he will be able to buy merchandise to put his business in place. In this way, his income will improve and thus in the future, with much effort and dedication, he will be able to buy his own house.

name: Kahindi
description: Kahindi is 27 years old. For the last two years, he has earned a living by operating a general store in Malindi. He earns a monthly income of KES. 12,000 from the business.   Kahindi was introduced to KADET LTD by a credit officer, and is applying for his second loan of KES. 35,000, to buy additional stock for his store such as fruit, soft drinks, sweets, some stationery, and cooking oil to sell to his customers. He will use the profits made possible by this loan to expand the business to a well established retail shop in the area and help pay school fees for his nephew as well.  His goal for the future is to continue growing the business so that he may uplift his financial stability.

name: Bevena
description: Bevena is 45 years old, married with four children.  Bevena works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10000 loan through NWTF to buy more groceries to sell in her general store.  Bevena has borrowed and paid 5 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 10 years and also earns an income from raising pigs.  Bevena aspires to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Nieve Margarita
description: The Ruta Del Sol communal bank meets every two weeks in Puerto López. It is a place surrounded by beautiful beaches and many tourist attractions. Every year the humpbacked whales appear, an event that attracts many tourists at that time of year.   Here lives Nieve. She is 50 years old, married, and has four grown children. A daughter who is a single mother lives with them with her little girl. Her husband is a merchant.    Nieve and her husband have a well stocked small grocery store. The sell every type of groceries and miscellaneous products. There they sell fish ceviche in the morning, which brings in good income. They work every day and have had the business for more than 15 years. It allows them to get ahead.   She is going to use this loan to buy grocery items for her store and fish for the ceviche. She has been in the communal bank for more than 8 years and she likes it because the loans are quick and they offer a lot of help.   Her dream is to grow her business more.

name: Abida
description: Abida is the age of 44, mother of three children, living with her spouse and children in the area of Lahore, Pakistan. Her husband is a green grocer by profession, and he has been selling fresh fruits at a shop in a nearby town for many years. Her husband offers seasonal and fresh fruits to his customers. He has been feeding his family through the generated income from this fruit shop.   Nowadays, the needs of his family suddenly increased and he does not have other sources to cope with these needs. So he decided to expand his current business. He wants to increase his stock on a daily basis so that he can maximize sales out of the fruits. Therefore her wife, Abida requested a loan from Kiva’s field partner, BRAC Pakistan, so that her husband can buy excess seasonal fruits. Abida thanks Kiva and it's field partner, BRAC Pakistan.

name: Juliet
description: Juliet is 43 years old, married to Richard, and supports a family of six members. Her children are between the ages of seven and seventeen. She is a maize farmer and she has been in the business for the last ten years. Her monthly income is KES 16,000.   She is currently requesting her first loan from KADET of Kes 30,000 that will facilitate the harvesting of her maize and transporting it to the market. She plans to use the anticipated profits to educate her children and develop her plot. Juliet's dream is to improve the living standards of her family.

name: Alaa
description: Alaa is a 24-year-old married woman from a small village near Nablus city. She is a mother for four young boys. Alaa's husband is a construction worker with a low wage. His job is seasonal and not stable. Alaa and her husband would like to improve the home conditions since it became very old.   Alaa took a loan from FATEN. This loan will help her to pay the costs of repairing the home, especially the paint. This will offer the family better living conditions in their home.   Alaa appears in the photo in FATEN branch.

name: Innocent
description: Innocent is a first-time borrower applying for a loan of two million shillings (UGX.2,000,000), He is married with two children who are in school. He and his family live in a trading center along a busy road. He has a small retail shop/canteen in a school which he runs with his wife. Innocent says he has customers with a ready market of over 1,070 students. He wants to stock his business but lacks capital so he is applying for a loan. Innocent expects a cash inflow increase by UGX 800,000 every month from boosting his business. He expects to pay off this first loan and get subsequent loans.

name: Loreta
description: This is Loreta, 60, a resident of Manila, Philippines. She is a widow with five children.  She, together with her children, manages their household while operating the business. At this time, she is working hard to continually provide income for her everyday expenses.    Loreta operates a tailoring business. She mainly offers curtains, bed sheets, blankets, and other home trappings. Seasonal demands for clothing like uniforms and such are available all year round. She also does repairs and alterations. Aside from this, she sells dried fish for additional income. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community.  She earns a minimum of PHP 1,000 in sales every day.  To help her continue operations of her business, she is requesting a PHP 50,000 loan. She will be using the loan to buy more quantities of raw materials like fabric, thread and other items needed in her business. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands her business.    Loreta hopes her business grows and dreams of being able to give her family a good future through all her hard work in her business. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her work every week and draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Agnes
description: Agnes is a 35-year-old married woman. She has 3 children whose ages range from 9 years to 17 years. She describes herself as ambitious. She operates a grocery store where she sells bananas, kales, fruits, and other vegetables. She has been involved in this business for 10 years. Her business is located in an area with plenty of customers, and her primary customers are local residents. Agnes describes her biggest business challenge as inadequate finances. She will use the KES 20,000 loan to to buy more stocks of bananas, kales, fruits, and other vegetables. Her business goal is to be self-reliant within 5 years. This is her first loan with SMEP DTM.

name: Grace
description: Grace wants a loan to buy more local alcohol and beer for reselling in her bar. She is a 31-year-old married woman with four children living in Kyenjojo,Uganda in a semi-permanent house. She brews alcohol locally and sells beer. She dreams of brewing local alcohol on a large scale and expanding her bar with better standards.

name: Ma. Salvacion
description: Ma. Salvacion A. is 32 and is married to Eduardo A., who is 36. They have 2 children.  Ma. Salvacion sells food while her husband worked as an electrician in a privately-owned electronic shop, which repairs televisions and other electronic devices. Television repair was his major task. Though both Ma. Salvacion and her husband were earning, their income could not meet the increasing financial needs of their family. Therefore, Ma. Salvacion and her husband decided to request a loan from ASHI in order to start up their own business.  In Ma. Salvacion's house, a mini-electronic repair shop was set up and is managed by her husband, while she sells barbeque and entertains customers that come in. Eventually, her business grew and they were able to acquire many customers from all over the municipality. Ma. Salvacion requests a larger loan to sustain the increasing and growing demand of their business. Someday she hopes to have her own shop that can employ other people to work with her husband. She also dreams of sending her two children to college and that they have their own careers in the future.

name: Eang's Group
description: A single woman is 35 years old, Eang living in a rural area of Kampong Thom province’s Sandan district. Nowadays, she does rice farm and grows cassava as the main sources of her family’s income. Moreover, she sells grocery items to earn additional income to complement her family’s needs. She has been involved in her businesses for fifteen years. Her daily business income is about 27,000KHR per day and she is able to save around 10,000KHR each day after offsetting her family’s expenses. Her cassava has been destroyed by insects, which allow her to sell it in a very low a price.   Due to having not enough money to build a private toilet for her family’s use, she is now leading a group of four members will spend her entire loan portion to buy a decent latrine. This is her first time to apply for a new loan with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). She hopes that this loan will help her and her family members to have good health.

name: Annie
description: Annie is a hardworking woman entrepreneur with two children.  She runs a home products retail business in the Philippines and requested a PHP 29,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional stocks of home products to sell.  She industriously earns additional income through other business ventures like a general store.  Annie dreams that, one day, she will be able to save money to expand her business.

name: Sokunthea's Group
description: Residing in Bovel district of Battambang province, Sokunthea is 31 years old and the mother of two children. For her family, seven hectares of rice cropping and one and a half hectares of cassava planting are the main sources. She can supplement her income via her paid-working. This is the first loan for Sokunthea with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). Now, she has teamed up in a group of three to get a new loan. As the leader, she will spend her entire loan portion to pay for the plowing fee, seed, and to buy fertilizer. She strongly believes that she can gain a better yield than before.

name: Tom
description: Tom is 57 years old, married and living in Bundibugyo Uganda. He deals in the cocoa business, mainly buying and selling in the markets.  He also gets additional income from rentals.    Tom started his business to raise income for his family and pay school fees for his children. His main challenge is limited capital. He hopes to expand his business and construct a residential house. Tom has asked for a loan to buy more cocoa for selling.

name: Phal's Group
description: Phal is 35 years old and married. She lives with her five children in a village of the Tbaung Khmum district of Cambodia. Of her five children, she still has three dependent children to take care of. They all are still in school and also work at the family's business. She earns a living through farming rice as her main business. Having been in this business for 17 years, she can earn US$3 per day from her current source of income.   Phal has been a successful client of VisionFund for several years. Because of this, Phal is leading her group of two members to apply for a loan. As the leader, she will use this entire loan to buy a small plot of a rice field to extend her farmland. This loan will enable her to increase her farming business and she hopes to increase her crop yield so as to earn more income. This will allow her to better feed her children and also keep them in school.
town: Kampong Cham province, Tbaung Khmum district

name: Khoeng
description: Khoeng K. is 38 and the father of three school-aged kids. Khoeng K. and his wife now live in Phnom Penh City.  Khoeng K. earns his income as a fish trader in the busy market with his wife. This couple always buys fresh fish in bulk from fisherman in the rural area, and then they sell it to gain daily income.  Generally, Khoeng K. used his old motorbike for picking up his product to take to the market, but it broke while driving. He wants to buy a new one, but his personal savings are insufficient. So Khoeng K. would like a loan in order to buy new motorcycle to replace the broken one, and with the rest buy more fish to sell.

name: Balqys Group
description: Palwasha is the group leader of Balqys group. Each of the four members of this group would like to receive a loan for her own business.  Balqys and Habiba would like a loan for their husbands' fruit cart businesses, so they can buy necessary materials. Palwasha would like a loan to enlarge her leather-sewing business. Mastora would like a loan for her tailoring business, to increase her inventory.  With this loan they can improve their businesses and support their families, thus making a better future for themselves and their families.

name: Jesus Vivant De Petitanse Group
description: Dieula is the coordinator of her group "Jesus Vivant de Petitanse". She lives in the Petitanse region, in Trou-du-Nord, Haiti, where electricity is rare and water is very limited. Dieula has been running her business selling a variety of goods for the last seven years. She is a widow and has two children.   Dieula would like to use this loan to invest in clothing, shoes, cosmetics, etc. Other members of the group have need of a loan for businesses selling diverse goods, such as cosmetic products, clothing, shoes, grocery items, and charcoal. With this loan, she hopes to grow [her] enterprise.

name: Cristina
description: This is Cristina, 57, from the province of Silang, Cavite, Philippines. She is married to Ernesto, a farmer, and they have four children, of which three are already married and their youngest is in High School. Her family may not have luxuries in life but the couple is happy that they have raised their children well. They have a tricycle and buy and sell fruits.Cristina has been operating a tricycle for five years already. A tricycle is a motorcycle with a side car that carries around four passengers. It is a common means of transportation in the Philippines and serves as a kind of taxi for short distance travel.Proper and regular maintenance of her tricycle is necessary to ensure efficient and safe service. In view of this, she is humbly seeking your help in the amount of 19,000 PHP to pay for new tires, tune up, change oil, and fuel for her tricycle. This will allow for good performance of her unit and result in a steady income for her family's needs and in sending her child to school. She aims to buy more tricycle units to increase her income. Just like any loving mother she dreams of buying her children a house and lot. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her work every week and where she can also draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies. * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital and repay Micro Finance loans.

name: Ahmed
description: Ahmed is a maize farmer and member of Babban Gona. Ahmed joined Babban Gona primarily to create a better future for his  children: Zakariya, Mathew, and Bilkisu. Ahmed is excited that Babban Gona offers a lasting solution to ending the cycle of poverty. For the first time, Ahmed will have access to quality inputs such as fertilizer and seed. Without this loan, he would be subjected to buying these products in the open market where the products are not only very expensive but are often diluted with external products such as sand. With access to high quality inputs, Ahmed can reap up to 30 bags/hectare, double the national average of 14 and  earn up to $2000/ha: more than three times the average Nigerian farmer’s annual income.  When asked how he plans to spend the income he will make this year  as a Babban Gona member, he said, “I plan to use the money  to expand my farmland.” Ahmed is not thinking about this year alone; he expressed that his longterm goal is to “ensure my children are educated and have professional jobs.” With this loan, he is well on his way to achieving this goal.

name: Kinaawa C(I) Group
description: Ruth is 38 years old and married with four children. Her husband is a driver. She has a poultry business. She wants to use the extra profits she earns to invest in the piggery and cultivation businesses. Sophia and Rehema sell used clothes and want to use the loan to increase their stock. Noeline sells firewood.  This is a group loan. The loan funds will be distributed among the group members, each of whom will invest in her own business. The members mutually guarantee one another's loans. If one member does not repay, the other members are responsible.

name: Gladis
description: Gladis is an unpstanding women and dedicates herself to the retail sale of Bijao leaves (a type of banana leaf that is commonly used in her region to cook typical foods).  Gladis also exports this product to the capital, since she is already growing this plant.  Gladis is 42 years old, a mother of three school age children.  Her husband, Guillermo supports her in her objectives and also with her business, since he is the person that picks the leaves from the plant.  To continue moving forward, Gladis would like to rent an appropriate space to sell her banana leaves and later enter into the fish-selling business as well.  She estimates that this capital will help her to make that objective a reality in the near future.Translated from Spanish by Lucia Franzese, Kiva Volunteer

name: Nydia
description: Nydia is 58 years old and married with four children. She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a sari-sari (variety) store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more stock to sell.  Nydia has borrowed and repaid 22 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the sari-sari store for two years and also earns an income from running a junk shop.  Nydia aspires to save enough money to buy a tricycle (motorcycle with sidecar) for transport.

name: Virgen Del Rosario Group
description: This group comprises 15 hardworking women, who are in their fifth loan cycle with the women's loan program. They each have a goal of helping their families through their work. Silveria, one of the members, sells food and fruits during the summer and purses and lingerie during the winter. She is never still and is always looking for ways to improve; she adjusts to temperature and season changes. She has applied for a loan to purchase lingerie and purses so that she can keep selling and earning the income her family requires.

name: Sam-Un
description: Mrs. Sam-un  V., 41, and her husband were married in 1984 and have five two sons and three daughters. One of her children is married and lives outside the family home. One of daughters works in a garment factory and other two children are in school. Her husband has been a mechanic for over ten years. The family lives on an Island in the Mekong River about fifteen kilometers from Phnom Penh.   Sam-un has been in the business of selling fruits, fishes, and vegetables such as tomatoes and cucumbers since 1984. She buys them from farmers in her village to resell at the market in Phnom Penh. Now is in that mangoes ar in season, Sam-Un needs some money to buy mangoes from farmers on contract (pay money first before harvesting).  She is requesting a loan of US$600 to purchase mangoes on contract from farmers  for resale.

name: Martha
description: Martha has a stationery shop and also works as a lawyer. Martha sells notebooks, books, pencils, erasers and other products. She works from 8am to 9pm and has five years’ experience at the business. It is going very well.   Martha’s dream is to expand her stationery shop. She is applying for a loan in order to buy notebooks, books, pencils and erasers.  Martha is happy with this loan and promises to make her repayments.

name: Anasa Group
description: Anasa is the group leader of the Anasa group. There are four members in this group. All of them would like to receive a loan for his/her business.   Leda and Anasa want to take a loan for their business of tailoring. Zabayda wants to take a loan for a business of her husband’s. Mena wants to take a loan for her business of tailoring. They all want to expand and progress their business.  They would like to thank all the lenders from around the world to Kiva and AFSG in Afghanistan for providing this process for loans to a poor country.

name: Soklam's Group
description: Soklam is aged 35 years old and a mother of two dependent children. She is living in Kampong Thom province. To earn income to survive her family’s living expenses, she grows rice and has been raising pigs for five years. Due to having not enough capital to fulfill her family’s needs, she is now leading a group of three to apply for a loan via VisionFund in order to buy a decent latrine. She hopes this loan will help her to improve her family’s lives and health.
town: Kampong Thom Province, Stoeng Sen District

name: Peter Mambo
description: Peter is 45 years old and is married to Margaret. They have two daughters and one son aged 13, 7 and 6 years respectively.  Peter, together with his wife, has been operating a general retail shop business for the past year. He also operates a motorcycle transport business as his other source of income.  Peter was introduced to KADET by a KADET credit officer through marketing outreach. Peter plans to add more stock, i.e. handkerchiefs, tomatoes, bread, etc., to his retail business with the amount he has applied for. He intends to save the profit generated from the business.  Peter’s future hopes are to start a large-scale poultry farm. He describes himself as an ambitious and hardworking businessman.

name: Ederlyn
description: As a parent of two children, Ederlyn works hard to support her family.  She has a fish-vending business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from buying and selling rice. Ederlyn is borrowing PHP 8,000 through NWTF to buy more fish to sell in her fish-vending business.  Ederlyn has been sustaining her business activities through her past 3 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: Geneviève
description: Born in 1976 in Cotonou, the economic capital of Benin, Geneviève T. is married to Placide REKPE  and is the mother of two children. The couple also takes care of two other children. Only some of them have had schooling. The family has been living for the past six years in Hêvié, in the Abomey Calavi commune. The couple jointly shares family expenses.  Genevieve has learned hairdressing, an activity she has practiced with passion for over 12 years, and which allows her to meet the needs of her family. As a side business in her beauty salon, Genevieve sells hair extensions and various beauty products.  Genevieve has already been granted one loan from ALIDé, and has repaid it in full. Given her customers' demands, she is now requesting a second loan, to strengthen her activity and increase her stock of supplies. Translated from French by René McConnell, Kiva Volunteer

name: Zekeria
description: Zékéria is a father of a 16-year-old child who attends school. He is a reseller of car batteries in the port area. He began his business in 2010, and acquires his merchandise in the same area and resells them to his customers. In the future, he would like to expand his business and provide for the needs of his family. He is 35 years old.

name: Laurito
description: Laurito is a father of 4 children. He is a widower and is 62 years old, residing at Dolores, Clarin.  Laurito is operating a raising crops venture, in particular bananas for sale, to earn a living. He has been in this business for 26 years.  Each month he earns 5000 PHP doing this kind of business.  He requested a loan of 5552 PHP to purchase fertilizers such as manure. Laurito just joined GDMPC this year. Laurito hopes to save as a reserve for future emergencies and to purchase more farm land.

name: Eduardo
description: Eduardo is 57-years-old and has 2 children. He lives with his mother in the Pacora district of the Lambayeque province, which is one hour away from the city of Chiclayo. He has been repairing footwear for more than 10 years. He has a workshop set up in his mother's house and there he receives customers who have need of his services. His experience in this area has led to his business having a regular client base who appreciates the quality of his work. This is the only source of income that he has to cover his personal expenses and to take care of his children and mother, who is elderly. Due to the constant demand for his services, Eduardo has to constantly travel to the city of Chiclayo to obtain materials which allow him to continue doing his work. Despite the fact that he relies on a permanent stock, he always has to refill it. It is for exactly this reason that he feels the need to request a loan of 1500 nuevos soles from Edpyme Alternativa, which he plans to invest in thread, soles and pieces of leather. Eduardo is a very hardworking man and he has earned the trust of his customers and of the people who know him. He has previously worked with our institution and demonstrated timeliness and responsibility when making his payments. Translated from Spanish by Tara Binetti, Kiva Volunteer

name: Analyn
description: This is Analyn. The loan that she acquired helped her to buy more products for her business. It also helped in the education of her children and in their household expenditures. Analyn and her husband, George, work hard to continuously provide for their everyday needs.  She would like to apply for another 20,000 PHP loan to buy more merchandise and products to increase her product inventory. The more items she has on display and available on hand, the better. More items to sell will result in better profits. Her profits from the business will definitely help her to sustain her children's education and daily needs. She looks forward to this financial increase with gladness and thankfulness in her heart.   Analyn dreams that her business will continue to grow and hopes to always have good health. She meets up with her fellowship co-members to share stories of her work every week and draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Aba
description: Aba is married and has 4 children.  Aba produces Fanti kenkey (fermented corn dough wrapped in leaves) for sale.  In front of Aba is the kenkey she has   produced.  She has been in this business for 6 years.  Aba uses her income to support her husband in feeding and clothing their children, as well as paying for school fees.  Aba will use her loan to purchase bags of maize, leaves and firewood to produce her kenkey for sale. With the new profit, she will expand her business.

name: Samvel
description: Samvel is 50 years old and he lives in the city of Kapan in the Syunik region. He is married and he has a son, who now is completing his military service in the army, and a daughter, who is school-aged. Samvel’s wife works as a deputy of the school director.   Samvel is a skilled driver and for many years he has operated a private company, providing transportation in his own car. Samvel has one more car, which his friend drives as a taxi, and they divide the income from it.  Samvel is asking for a loan of 1,000,000 Armenian drams in order to repair and buy winter car tires for his two cars.

name: Saima
description: Ms Saima is a 20-year-old lady. For about 6 years she is been in work of hand embroidery. She makes beautiful patterns for the people of her community. Her designs are much in demand and she has managed to consolidate a clientele that allows her to contribute to the expenses of her home. To help her to continue her operations, she has requested for a loan of Rs. 15,000 to buy reels of threads in different colors with the packs of beads, sequins and stones for its embellishment. In this way she would be able to cater more customers consistently. She is hopeful to get increase in her income by targeting more customers. Saima desires to build her own house as she is living in a rented house with her family. She is in her 2nd loan cycle and is very much thankful to Kashf for its tremendous support.

name: Yaa
description: Yaa is married with three children and her husband is a petty trader. For the past seven years, she has been selling plantains, cassavas, and yams in Twifo Praso, near Cape Coast. Yaa has been educated through junior high school.  She is responsible for supporting her husband to pay her family's utility bills and school fees.   Yaa is requesting a loan to purchase more produce to sell. She hopes to use the new profits from her loan to expand her plantains, cassavas, and yams business and increase her capital base. In the long run, Yaa wants to expand into neighboring villages.

name: Sourou-Guetom Group
description: Nassirou was born in 1954 and is married with children. In 1994 he started up agriculture in the Central Region and has two assistants. This is his third loan from Wages and will enable him to buy tools so that he can cultivate a larger surface area. He hopes that with the additional profits he will be able to start a business selling planks and ensure his family's well-being. It should be noted that he is in charge of a group named SOUROU-GUETOM that is made up of farmers who all grow corn and hope to see their businesses and their families develop.

name: David
description: David M. O. is 25 years old. He is married and has two children. His wife is a business lady.   David's business is located at Harambee-Kakamega where he engages in passenger transportation services as well as selling cereals to the local people. David is using this loan to buy cereals to expand his business. In the future, he hopes to buy more motorbikes and a matatu, and to open a store to supply to a bigger market. He is a God-fearing and determined person.

name: Hà
description: Hà is 32 years old, and she is married. She has worked in agriculture, raising poultry, for seven years. Hà lives in Bim Son town, a semi-urban town in Thanh Hoa province. Her family is a low-income household in the village; moreover, her job is unstable.  One of the most critical difficulties that concerns Hà is not having clean water to use. She is requesting a loan to purchase sand, cement, brick and equipment to install a clean water system.This is Hà's first loan with Thanh Hoa microfinance institution. With her business profit, she hopes for her business to do well, for her children to do well in school, and for her family to be healthy and happy.

name: Madjigui Group
description: Mrs. BINTOU is the representative of Madjigui Group. She's married and the mother of one child, who is seven and attends school. She has one person to support.  She's been selling galettes (pancakes) for nine years. She gets her supplies at the Zeem Passego market. Her customers are her neighbors.  She wants to buy two sacks of millet, two 20-liter cans of oil, and two 50-kg sacks of sugar. She saves up her profits in order to stock up on millet.  She ambitions to open a grocery store and continue selling galettes, but also stock up sacks of millet, corn, etc.

name: Rhona
description: Rhona is married with two children who attend school.  She also takes care of her sister’s children.  She has a business selling charcoal and has been in this business for many years.  She also generates additional income from operating a retail shop.  She works from her home and sells to all categories of people seven days a week.    She has applied for a loan of Uganda shillings from MCDT-SACCO to buy more bags of charcoal.  Her major business challenges include thieves and seasonality.  She aspires to become a wholesaler and also to build rental rooms.  She resides in her own house and the family has access to piped water and electricity.  Her monthly expenses includes school fees and paying for utility bills.

name: Ondougou Dah 9 Group
description: The members of the Ondougou Dah 9 group are all married women with an average age of 29 years, an average of 5 children each, and all living in polygamous families in Bandiagara in the 5th administrative region of Mali. The have partnered with the microfinance organization Soro Yiriwaso in order to better run their agriculture businesses during this end of the rainy season. The women are on their first loan with the organization.  Yanéme, pictured standing second from right to left in the photo, is primarily in the onion business. With this loan, she plans to purchase seeds and fertilizer. She sells her crops in the villages of Bandiagara and Mopti after her harvest, to a customer base made up of both men and women. She hopes to earn a profit of 23,000 francs CFA at the end of the season, which will allow her to help her husband with the family expenses (food, education for their children, and basic health needs) and to reinvest the rest in her business.

name: Enrica
description: Enrica is 40 years old and married with one child in school, Enrica works very hard to provide for them.  Enrica runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 16000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like beverages, canned goods, junk foods, home product care, and other groceries.  Enrica has been in this business for 15 years and sells a variety of items such as rice, sugar, soap, and other groceries.   In the future, Enrica would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Godfrey
description: Godfrey is a 45-year-old married man with four children living in Kasese, Uganda. For six years he has been operating a retail shop and the business has been very lucrative.  He used the previous loan to buy general merchandise to sell. He also deals in the local brew, coffee and bananas for additional income. Like most traders he is challenged by price fluctuation and high cost of transport. His vision is to become a leading coffee exporter.  Godfrey intends to use the loan to buy coffee to sell.

name: Princisita
description: Princisita is 54 years old and married, with four children.    Princisita is in the agricultural business farming vegetables in the Philippines.  She has requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional seeds and fertilizer.  Princisita has been farming vegetable for three years now, and she has borrowed four times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Faustino
description: Faustino is a twenty-nine-year-old married man with two children living in Kamwenge, Uganda. His main business is brick making but he also sells goats and sheep in order to earn additional income. He has hardships of weather changes especially the rainy season, where his bricks take a long time to dry yet he expects constant income. His dream is to have a machine for making bricks.   Faustino intends to use the loan to buy materials to make more bricks to sell.

name: Yadira De La Concepcion
description: Yadira lives in the municipality of Ticuantepe. She is a single mother, hardworking, and  conscientious. Her greatest dream is to improve her conditions and give her son a better future. She has been a merchant for more than three years. She sells new and used clothing. With the loan she has been granted she will buy one bale of clothing and one of shoes, since her clients are asking her to sell shoes. With this she hopes her business will grow and that she will improve her income. She appreciates that Afodenic and Kiva have provided her support.

name: Andrea Gabriela
description: Andrea is a very hardworking young woman and above all she is very enthusiastic. She is 21 years old and lives in the city of Ica, a city that is characterized for having a very warm weather and it is known as the land of the eternal sun. Agricultural development takes place there, specially the cultivation of cotton, asparagus, grapes and paprika, among others. Andrea is a very happy young woman and when she has some spare time she likes to listen to music, since it helps her to relax and unwind. One of her favorite meals is the delicious red tagliatelle with huancaína potatoes. With her will to get ahead in life, Andrea works as a cashier in a gas station and with the fruits of her labor she manages to study to get her degree as a systems analyst. She thinks she does well at her job because she is very responsible and above all because she is very honest and customers always recommend her. Andrea is very thankful to Kiva lenders since thanks to their help she will be able to pay for some university expenses, which will allow her to continue studying and keep working and fighting every day to make her biggest dream come true: "Have a house of her own and become a great professional".

name: Rosalinda
description: Rosalinda is 53 years old, married, and blessed with six children.   She helps her husband in gaining income through buying and reselling fruits and vegetables within their community. She aims to further improve this business in order to earn a higher income.   Due to insufficient capital, she is asking for an additional of PHP 10,000 to buy more stocks of the said fruits and vegetables to resell. Being a hard working mother, she believes that, someday, she will further improve her business.

name: Roula
description: Roula is a 20-year-old married mother of one child, who has been working in preparing and selling mouneh (preserved food), at her house since three years ago. Roula helps her husband in making their living, especially now that they have a small, beloved baby girl, whom they have to work hard to provide with the best living and education ever.  Roula is applying for a youth loan from Kiva partner Al Majmoua, to buy raw materials to start preparing and conserving them for the coming seasons.  Roula hopes to move her home-based business in the future to a wide store to display all of her products and increase her customers.

name: Benkadi Group
description: Group Benkadi is composed of four married women, who are on average 43 years old with six children. They live in traditional families. These women reside in the Faraba neighborhood of the city of Bougouni (Mali's third administrative region). They got to know each other through business relations. In order to satisfy their customers and to grow their business, they decided to join micro-finance organization Soro Yiriwaso to retail soft drinks and shoes; so does Maimouna, who is the women to the right with a child by her feet. They are on their third group loan, the previous loans having been repaid punctually. With this new loan, Maimouna is planning on purchasing 15 dozen pairs of shoes from sellers coming from Bamako. She retails cash to a diverse clientele in her kiosk located in the Faraba neighborhood of Bougouni. With this loan, she is counting on a monthly profit of 40,000 FCFA, part of which will be reused to pay back her loan, with the remainder to be reinvested in the business.

name: Gansuh
description: Gansuh is 31 years old and lives with his wife and two sons in Hovd province, Mongolia. He and his family live together in a ger, the Mongolian nomadic tent. His oldest son, Uuganbayr, is nine years old and attends a local secondary school. His youngest son, Suhbaatar, is two years old and doesn't yet attend school. During the day, Gansuh operates a motorcycle spare parts trading business in his town. There are very few shops that sell the same products in his province, which is a great advantage for him. He has been successfully operating his business since 2003. Gansuh is taking a loan for the second time from XacBank. He has been planning to expand his spare parts trading shop.  Gansuh is a very hardworking person who has strong selling and communication skills. He is focused on the future and says, “I would like to expand my business and to build a house for my family on a plot of land that I purchased recently.” He is requesting a 300,000-tugrug loan to purchase more motorcycle spare parts at wholesales prices in Ulaanbaatar, the capital city of Mongolia, and resell them at his shop for a profit.

name: Padmini
description: Every second brings a fresh beginning. Every hour holds a new promise. Every night, dreams are brought with hope and every day is what a man chooses to make.   This is what inspires Padmini, 41, a resident of Kandhamal district, who is married and blessed with two children. From nothing, Padmini now owns a grocery store. But before she stood where she is right now, it took her a long road of sweat, tears, pressure, faith and persistence. But ceasing never occurred in Padmini's vocabulary, instead, without hesitation, she chose to continue pressing forward.  Padmini does not have access to a toilet in her home.Therefore,she is requesting a loan amount of 15,000 INR to build a toilet and install all the necessary sanitary equipment.  She hopes that you will understand her need and will extend your helping hands.

name: Freddy Raul
description: Thank you for supporting Freddy, who bought materials to make doors and windows with his previous loan. He is currently applying for a Kiva loan to by tools such as drills and materials to have products in stock, making an impact on his clientele with new designs.   Freddy sends his lenders the following message: "I am very grateful for the loans and I hope to continue counting on this support. I hope that when I need a higher amount you can help me."

name: William
description: William C. is 46 years old, married to Pyllis Chemwetich, and is a father of four. He has been in the dairy farming business for the last three years.  From this business, William gets a monthly profit of Kshs 4500. With the loan of Kshs 20000, he intends to buy a dairy cow worth Kshs 18000. The remaining Kshs 2000 will be used to purchase dairy feed.  William intends to use the business' profit to buy more dairy heifers and cows in order to increase his income.  As this is his first loan with Kadet, William hopes that he will be able to pay back the loan and borrow more in the future to expand his dairy farm.

name: Salome
description: Salome is a single woman with 3 children. She describes herself to be determined. She operates a retail business where she sells peas. She has been involved in this business for 17 years. Her business is located in a strategic place and her primary customers are locals. She will use the Kes 30,000 loan to buy more stock of peas. She hopes that in the future, she will be successful. This is her third loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. Previous loan was repaid successfully.

name: Harriet Namugabo ‘Sgroup
description: Harriet is the leader of a 5-member group.  She is  45 years old, married, with four children aged between 24 and 30. All her children go to school. She resides in a four-roomed house where she lives with three people. Harriet takes care of her sister’s children.  There is electricity and piped water at her home.  The family gets three meals a day.  Harriet resides and works in a semi-urban area which is on the outskirts of Kampala.  Harriet is located in Lugala, selling natural medicines in one of Kampala's suburbs.  She incurs extra transport costs to and from Kalerwe where she buys her crude  medicines.   Harriet  sells to an average of 20 people a day and sells to all categories of people, excluding children. She works six days a week. Harriet  sells retail only. Her major monthly expenses include school fees and rent for her business premises and home.  She has been in this business for the last 10 years.   Harriet has been with MCDT for over three years and is servicing her sixth loan, working with the same group mates. She wants to use this loan to buy more jerrycans of natural medicines.  Harriet aspires to see her business grow bigger and own permanent business premises.

name: Yusuf
description: O. is married and blessed with five children who are excelling in school. She is 40 years old and is a native of Edo State, Nigeria.  O. is into the business of tailoring and the sales of sarongs and has been in this business for fifteen years. She sews lovely Nigerian and Western styles for her customers and hopes to own a world class tailoring stall in the future. She has been able to care for her family with the proceeds of her business.  O. needs the loan of NGN 70,000 to purchase more tailoring materials and sarongs to sell. She says thanks to all Kiva lenders.

name: Vugar
description: Vugar is an Internally Displaced Person (IDP) from the Zangilan region of Azerbaijan. He is 34 years old and is married with three children. Vugar started his dental business eight years ago. The business is developing well and he is currently applying for a loan to buy dental equipment in order to increase the quality of service.

name: Carmencita
description: Carmencita G. runs a sari-sari (variety retail shop). She is 46 years old, married and has seven school-age children. They are from the village of Duka, Medina, Misamis Oriental. Carmencita has been in her business for over five years and earns approximately 1600 pesos a month.  In 2009, Carmencita joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living conditions and enable her to engage in business activities. Carmencita has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5000 pesos from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to purchase additional inventory and for working capital. Carmencita is requesting a new loan of 9000 pesos which will be used to purchase additional inventory and for working capital. This will be her third loan from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue to support the education of her children.   About HSPFI: HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Eliphas
description: Eliphas is a Kiva borrower. He describes himself to be passionate. He operates a farm where he grows crops for sale and for own consumption. He also does business to earn extra income. He describes his biggest challenge to be lack of pumps and pipes.   He will use the KES 55,000 loan to buy a water pump for irrigation in his farm. He hopes that in the future, he will improve his economic status and maximize land productivity.   This is his second loan with SMEP DTM. Previous loan was repaid successfully.

name: Two In One United Group
description: Pictured here are Fatmata K., Fatmata M. and Memuna K.. They earn a living working as small-scale businesswomen in Makeni city, located in northern Sierra Leone. This is the first loan these entrepreneurs are requesting from SMT/Kiva. With this loan, they hope to be able to expand their businesses, make better profit and improve their current standard of living.  Fatmata K. (on the left) is the leader of the group, named Two in One United. Fatmata was born in Makeni 29 years ago. She is married and is the mother of two children. One of her children is in grade three and the other is in grade one. Fatmata sells shoes, onions and fish. She has been working in this business for 10 years now.

name: Rehana
description: Rehana is a 36-years old married woman and a mother of 4. Her financially condition is not good. Her husband has been driving a moto rickshaw (a type of three-wheeled rickshaw). This rickshaw is being driven over local roads and for small distances. Its body is made of polyester, which is not strong enough to bear the jerks of the roads. Now the rickshaw body needs to be replaced, because it rattles during driving. This is the reason her husband wants to buy a new body for his moto rickshaw.Rehana requested a loan so that her husband can buy the rickshaw body, so that he can drive it smoothly. Rehana thanks Kiva and field partner, BRAC Pakistan.

name: Jennifer
description: As a married parent of four children, Jennifer works hard to support her family.  She has a general store business in the Philippines, and earns additional income from farming corn. Jennifer is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to buy items to resell, such as shampoos, milk, coffee, soap, etc. for her general store business.  Jennifer has been sustaining her business activities through her past two loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Salma
description: To make a living, Salma is engaged in fish selling.  She has been in her business for 4 years and earns a monthly net income of 2,500.  Salma G. is 42 years old and is married with 3 adult-aged children.  She is from the village of Bitibut, Sapang Dalaga.  In 2010, Salma joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities.  Salma is requesting her 1st loan of 3,000 PHP which will be used as additional capital for her business.   About PMPC:  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Sopheap's Group
description: Sopheap’s group live in a rural village in Kampong Speu province in Cambodia. Sopheap makes a living cultivating rice and she also does extra work as tailor to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women and man to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Abla
description: Abla is a married woman who lives with her husband in Adidogomé. Abla is 32 years old and she prepares and sells wrapped maize dough called  « Kom ». Abla buys the necessary ingredients for the preparation of her dough once a month at the market and sells the dough by going from neighborhood to neighborhood and out of her home. Abla is asking for this loan to order bowlfuls of maize so as to earn more profit and be able to cover the needs of her family and then improve her daily living conditions.

name: Hannah
description: Hannah, 35, has run a boutique for ten years in Naivasha. She is a widow and the mother of two school-going children.  She was introduced to KADET by a KADET customer and this is her second loan. She intends to use this loan to add childrens wear, skirts and blouses to her stock.  Hannah’s future dream is to enlarge her boutique to increase her profit.

name: Ezekiel
description: Ezekiel is a 45-year-old married man with six children living in Bundibugyo,Uganda. He deals in cocoa sales and his business has been very lucrative. Ezekiel’s business challenges include customers not paying on time and the seasonal nature of his product.  Ezekiel is requesting a loan to buy cocoa to sell. His personal goal is to build a permanent commercial house in town and expand his business into new areas.

name: Tweweyo Tukore Grp Group
description: Aidah, a single mother of 5 children, lives in rural Lyantonde. Having no source of income to depend on except subsistence farming, Aidah resorted to selling charcoal since it was in demand by the town dwellers who can not afford gas, let alone the high cost of electricity. Through the sales she has managed to save some money to pay for her children's tuition as well as meet other household demands.   Because her capital base was so small she, together with eleven other members from the same village, sought out financial assistance. There was no better alternative than Ugafode since the other institutions in their reach are commercial banks that can not lend to her category of people (rural poor).   She will use the loan to buy more stock such that she can increase her profits and buy a plot of land on which she will build a residential house in the future. She is a hardworking woman, though her challenges are that she has no alternative sources of income and has to strain the business for all the household needs.

name: Luatasi
description: Luatasi K., 32, is married with 3 children.  She has 2 years of experience in the taro, banana, and vegetable business. She sells to the village people and public 5 days per week. She is a new member and this is her first loan request. She has no previous loans with SPBD.  She expects her weekly net cash flow to be 90 Tala.  SPBD loans are Luatasi’s only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with the traditional banks.

name: Ma. Junosie
description: Ma. Junosie is 49 years old from Getafe, Bohol. She is married with four children ages 12 through 28. For 18 years now, she has been operating a sari sari store business. She sell basic household items like seasoning, canned goods, noodles, eggs, toiletries, snack food, and soft drinks. She is asking for a loan to buy additional stocks of canned sardines, cooking oil, coffee, toiletries, and soft drinks. She is hoping that with the loan she will not experience lacking the items needed by her customers. Her income will be for family daily consumption and school fees.

name: Sreypov's Group
description: Sreypov’s group lives in a rural village in Kompong Thom province in Cambodia. Sreypov makes a living cultivating rice and also does extra work as a construction worker to support her family.   In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help both of these women safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Analyn
description: Analyn is 50 years old, married, and works hard to support her family. She has a buy-and-sell dressed chicken business in the Philippines and also earns additional income from making fermented fish.   Analyn is borrowing PHP 15,000 through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to buy dressed chicken and a new refrigerator unit for her buy-and-sell dressed chicken business.  Analyn has been sustaining her business activities through her past nine loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: Ibtihaj
description: Ibtihaj is a 33-year-old married woman and mother of four children. She has been working in the food business since two years ago. She is a hardworking woman who puts in so much effort to provide her family with the necessary needs. That's why she always needs an external support to better improve her business to increase her income.   Ibtihaj is applying for a loan from Kiva's partner, Al Majmoua, to help her husband start a new business to increase the family's income and improve their living. She will also support her business through buying necessary merchandise for her store, especially for the coming spring and summer seasons.  She hopes that this loan will be a good step forward for improving her family's social and financial living.

name: Rafaela
description: Rafela, age 57, never went to school. She and her partner are farmers. They had four children, but all have their own homes now, and just one granddaughter lives with Rafael and her partner now.Rafaela has a farm where she fattens chickens. She also sells tamales, chicken sandwiches, and other typical food. She's been making these sales for seven years, and she started the business out of necessity.Rafaela needs this loan to buy 150 chickens, two hundredweight of concentrated feed, and all the necessary vitamins and medicines the chickens will need.Rafaela's goals are to continue working her farm, to have a better quality of life, and to see her granddaughter stay in school and earn a university degree.

name: Jabeda
description: Jabeda, 45 years old, is a rural woman from the village of Baroghoria in Dhupguri in Jalpaiguri district. She is married to Safikul, 54 years old. They are raising two grown-up sons who were deprived of an education due to their poverty.  So, they work as laborers on daily wages.  Jabeda and her husband are also illiterate and can just sign their names. They live in their own pacca house (concrete made).  Jabeda's husband owns ancestral land where he cultivates seasonal vegetables.  He has been in this agribusiness for the last 15 years. Now he has grown old and feeble, so he is unable to make the same efforts as before.  Moreover, his main challenge is capital, without which he can't grow his agribusiness.  His sons have no fixed income.  As a result, they are unable to give sufficient financial sustenance to their family. Jabeda has been engaged in her livestock business for many years.  She purchases baby goats, raises them, and then offers them for sale to the nearby markets. She has gradually improved her business and it has been a great financial help to the family.  She now wants to purchase two more goats, for which she is requesting a loan from BJS (Kiva's partner).  She hopes to grow her business and dreams of being able to offer a good, high quality lifestyle to her family.  She aspires to have a cattle herd in the future by purchasing more cows and goats.  She appreciates the financial help of her lenders, BJS and Kiva.

name: Savang
description: Mrs. Savang R. (pictured here), 32, and her husband, Mr. Saroeung Soem, 37, were married in 1993 and have two children: one son and one daughter. Both of them are in school. They live with their parents on an island in the Mekong River about 15 kilometers from Phnom Penh, the capital city of Cambodia.   Savang has been a silk weaver for 12 years, a skill she learned from her mother. She sells her finished products to a middleman who then takes them to sell in Phnom Penh market. Her husband has been a farmer for over two years. She is requesting a loan of $700 to purchase fertilizer, pesticides and seeds to maintain her husband’s farm.

name: Betty's Group
description: In Kapsaoi village in Vihiga, Kenya, Betty has volunteered to be the promoter for a new chlorine dispenser. Betty is a hardworking, well-liked member of the community with 9 children. Betty is 47 years old, works as a commercial farmer, and lives with her family in a house made of mud walls, sand or dirt floor, and an iron roof.  Kapsaoi village does not have a piped water supply, so the community collects their water from a borehole. This water is easily contaminated with bacteria that can cause water-borne diseases. Chlorine dispensers offer a solution to this problem by allowing people to treat their water to make it safe to drink. Betty and the 34 other households using the local water source need a loan to cover the cost of installing and maintaining chlorine dispensers at the water sources in the area.   Betty has volunteered to act as the promoter to encourage the community to use the dispenser and to refill it with chlorine when the tank runs low. Betty volunteered to be the promoter because she wants to educate the community to use chlorine dispensers and improve people's health. There are also three other volunteer promoters from nearby communities who are part of this group loan: Phylis, Vincent, and Rose.  The Kiva loan will be repaid by Evidence Action (www.evidenceaction.org) on behalf of the community, through the sale of carbon credits. Using the chlorine dispenser generates carbon credits by avoiding the need to boil water to make it safe to drink. The sale of carbon credits, to organizations and individuals wanting to reduce their carbon footprint, will be used to repay Kiva lenders and also to make sure that Betty’s community can have access to safe water now and in the future.

name: Mary
description: Mary A. is married and has three children. She has received a high school education.  Mary sells porridge at teterem near Elmina, which she has been doing since 2009. Her husband is a trader.  Mary uses her income to help pay school fees and utility bills. Mary will use the loan to purchase more milo, milk and also buy millet for the making of the porridge to sell to her costumers who prefer to take their breakfast at her shop. With the new profits from her expanded business, Mary plans to educate her children.

name: Cinforosa
description: Cinforosa is 60 years old and married with four children. Her occupation is selling food at various markets around the city of Cusco. She sells all types of typical Peruvian food such as sopas, lomo saltado and papas fritas.   Cinforosa is asking for a $1,000 loan in order to buy more ingredients to make her food. She plans to purchase rice, potatoes and oil. She works very hard selling her food at the market every day. Cinforosa is committed to making all of the necessary loan payments.

name: Xiomara Magalis
description: Mrs. Xiomara is a young person that is 27 years old, single and without children. Despite her young age, she has worked for fifteen years in agriculture.  One of her main goals is to have a home. One of the obstacles she faces, that she has experienced in her agricultural career, is the way the theft of crops greatly affects earnings. It is with the economic support of her parents, who began this agricultural business, that she is requesting this loan. The loan will be used to provide a greater variety of plants that are generally utilized in the capital city or the outskirts. With this loan she will buy supplies, plants, fertilizers and pesticide, which will help her reach her goals. This will allow her to plan the construction of her house in the future.  Translated from Spanish by Esther Levandoski, Kiva Volunteer

name: Josephine
description: Josephine C. is from the village of Manticao, Misamis Oriental. She is 30 years old. Josephine is married and has four children. To make a living, Josephine operates a specialized retail store. The main source of income for the business comes from making and selling charcoal in the local community. Josephine chooses to remain at a loan amount of 5,000 Philippine pesos for her third loan cycle. Josephine has been engaged in her business for over four years and earns approximately 3,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2008, Josephine joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Josephine has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5,000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to purchase new items to expand her product offering. Josephine's new loan of 5,000 PHP will be used to purchase additional products to sell. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Ekua
description: Ekua lives together with her husband, who is a farmer, and 5 dependents. Ekua sells cloth, she has been selling cloth for 2 years now. Ekua uses her income to assist the husband to pay their utility bills.  Ekua will use her loan to purchase more cloth to sell. With the new profit, she will expand her business

name: Eda Maria
description: Eda, together with her husband who is retired and children who are already independent, has done her duty as a mother of getting them all ahead. Today she lives and supports her home expenses by renting out rooms in her home.  She is requesting a third loan from Afodenic and Kiva in order to change part of her roof and plaster her house. In order to do this she needs to buy sheets of zinc, cement and sand in order to improve the conditions of her home. This would not be possible without financial support, which is why she is very thankful for this lending program.

name: Veronicah
description: Veronicah, age 39, is a matatu operator, providing transportation. She has been engaged in this business for the past 13 years. She and her husband Joseph have seven children.  This is her first term loan. She was brought to KADET Ltd by an existing KADET client. She will use the loan amount to repair the seats and tires of her vehicle.  Her hope is to own a chain of buses for transport.

name: Faatutu
description: Faatutu is a 39-year-old mother with five children. She operates a small business providing services to people by cutting grass to earn a living. Faatutu requested a loan to buy a lawn mowing machine, chemicals, celluloid, safety boots and a safety uniform to assist her in running the business. She has been doing this for more than a year. She will expand her business using her profit. She became a member of SPBD in 2011.

name: Mirta Esperanza
description: Mirta is a woman with great ambition in life. She is kind, sincere, and persevering in life. She is 40 years old, married, with a family of two children - a girl and a boy. This beautiful family lives in a community of Samayac.Mirta's main financial income comes from buying and selling casual clothing for women, men, and children. She has had this business for eight years. This business is not enough for Mirta, which is why she also sells goods of daily consumption. With the end of the year approaching, it is important for Mirta to invest in buying clothing items like pants, blouses, skirts, and shirts. With this, Mirta hopes to satisfy the needs of her customers.Her great goal in life is to finish the construction on her house and open a new store.

name: Tatu
description: Tatu is 22 years old and lives with her siblings in the Kilosa District of Tanzania. She volunteers at a secondary school in her village as a way of giving back to her community. She teaches students life skills to improve their learning performance.   Apart from this, she is also a young businesswoman who sells women’s clothing, specifically dresses. She uses the profits she earns to pay her siblings’ school fees and take care of her family, who depend on her.   Tatu is requesting a Kiva loan to increase the stock items in her shop to better serve her customers. With the profits she makes, she hopes to hire someone to help her manage the shop in her absence.

name: Nazik
description: Nazik is from Arevadasht village in the Armavir region. She lives with her son and husband who is agronomist. They run a farm. It includes 10 cows, 4 calves and arable land where they cultivate eggplant and forage for the livestock.  Nazik also keeps an orchard where she grows 20 apricot trees. Nazik's husband sells the gathered agricultural harvest in the local open markets and the family is able to sustain its living.  Nazik has now applied for this loan to be able to purchase a cow, fertilizer and forage for feeding the livestock. The loan is very important for these hardworking farmers to enlarge their agribusiness and sustain their living.

name: Zoila Elena
description: 44-year-old Elena is a single mother with 5 children. Three of them, aged 5, 10 and 20, still live with her and the two younger ones go to school. Elena makes a living as a farm labourer and also raises calves.  She will use the money from the loan to buy calves, which she will keep in fields which some neighbours are lending to her.  Elena's dream is to keep working hard to give her children everything they need, especially their education.

name: Omari
description: Omari lives in Kitunda area of Dar es Salaam.He is married with two children.He owns a retail shop near his residence.The shop sells different consumable items especially food items,rice in particular. Rice is one of staple food in Tanzania.Jafari plans to increase the stock of rice.There is an expectation of rice price rise.Having enough stock now will help him make more money later.The extra stock demands more funding.Through his savings he managed to contribute 20% of the required stocking.The strategy will help him increase income.The aim being to sustain the family and pay for school fees for his children. To implement his plans Omari needs USD 550 as a working capital.

name: Ailein
description: Ailein is a 31-year-old married woman with three children, two of whom are currently in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.  Ailein has a fish vending business in the Philippines. She has requested a PHP 15,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy more variety of fish to sell. She has been in this business for 5 years. In the future, Ailein would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Matlab
description: Matlab S. is 54 years old and lives with his wife and four children, to whom he is a devoted father. He makes the most of every opportunity, such as when he started selling foodstuffs in the food market. He gives his business constant attention all day long, everyday, and in this way he has attracted customers. His income enables him to contribute to the home finances.  In addition he also works as veterinarian. He is motivated in his work by the need to support the family finances and take care of his children's education in school. Matlab is requesting a loan which he will invest in merchandise for his shop. He wishes to stock it with more products and offer the best products every day.

name: Ana Maria
