description: Ana María makes a living producing cheese from cow's milk, which she sells in various markets in the city of La Paz.  Her husband works for the police.  Her family lives in the community of Achica Bajo in Ingavi Province in the department of La Paz.  She needs the loan to buy milking equipment that will help her optimize the time for milking as well as be able to have a higher-quality and healthier product.  Ana María's dream is to be able to become one of the largest cheese producers in her area and improve her family's living conditions.

name: Anastasia
description: Anastasia Q. is a hairdresser. She is a divorcee with one child. Her customers are increasing but she lacks enough funds to buy more creams and other items she needs to keep the business running smoothly.  She is asking for $325 as an additional capital to buy more creams, artificial hair, TCP, and other items for the expansion of her business.

name: Mehman
description: Mehman B. is a 43-year-old café owner. He opened his café in 2001 offering tea but, little by little, he expanded his tea house to a café and now offers meat and chicken meals among with tea. His son helps him.  Now, Mehman needs 1,600 AZN to purchase new tables, chairs and dishes.

name: Alba Nelly
description: Alba is a person who characterizes herself as being very charismatic and a hard worker. For some time now, she has worked selling merchandise, something she learned from her sister who is also in this line of work. With the impetus of helping her husband with the household income, Alba, decided to start working and she actually has a good amount of customers who prefer her products because of the good customer attention she provides.  Alba also wants to help her community so she is taking a course on infant-toddler and pre-school care.  Thanks to her increasing sales, Alba has lots of orders from her customers. However, she doesn’t have enough capital to buy merchandise from her suppliers. This is why she has the hope that a loan will afford her the opportunity to buy personal care products like lotions, creams, shampoo and make-up, among other things, to fill her clients' orders.    Alba dreams that her business will continue to provide income in order to help her husband with the household income, and that way, provide a better quality of life for her 4 children. Alba also dreams of having a big store where she could hire many people who are in need of household income.

name: Jocelyn
description: As a married mother of three children, Jocelyn works hard to support her family. She has a fishing business in the Philippines, and earns additional income from food vending.   Jocelyn is borrowing 15,000 PHP through NWTF to buy fishing nets and other equipment for her fishing business.  Jocelyn has been sustaining her business activities through her past five loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money to expand her business and to continue sending her children to school.

name: Habiba's Tuko Imara Group
description: Habiba, is divorced and takes care of her four children (ages 25, 22, 18, and 20). She makes a living by tailoring dresses and selling chickens. She works from 8am to 4pm daily at these businesses. She is able to make a monthly profit of about $85 from her work.  Habiba hopes for a loan to purchase more dress materials and more chickens. She will share this loan with her subgroup, who are part of loan group Tuko Imara. The members of this loan group guarantee one another in paying back their loans.

name: Rufiji Group
description: Mwajabu is a married mother of five children. She's in her mid-50's.  She owns and runs a food vending business famously known as "Mama lishe" for 15 years now. She works from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily, and she is able to make a good monthly profit.   This will be Mwajabu's fifth loan with Tujijenge Tanzania.  She used her previous loans to reinvest in the same business so that it grew further. By doing such improvements, she has managed to pay back all her loans successfully and appreciates Kiva for the support given to her loan group, which is now doing great.   She used her profit for loan repayment, food for her family, reinvesting in the same business, and covering household expenses.     She will use this loan to add more sacks of rice, cans of cooking oil, sugar, and beans to prepare for Christmas sales.   She dreams of providing a better education to her children from the profit that she makes out of her food stall. Mwajabu will share this loan with her loan group 'RUFIJI," which consist of two members who hold each other accountable for paying back all the loan.

name: Hosiyatkhon
description: Hosiyatkhon is 27 years old and married with a three year old son. She is hard-working, cheerful and conscientious. In order to provide a primary income for her family, she farms and raises livestock. On the farm she has one cow and a 0.61 hectare plot of land where she grows peaches, corn, wheat, and grapes. Her monthly income is approximately 5,000 som (KGS). Hosiyatkhon wants to grow her business, so she has applied for a loan of 50,000 som (KGS) from Bai Tushum Bank in order to purchase fertilizer and seeds and to pay for the costs of cultivating the land for growing organic produce. She plans to invest the income from this loan in developing her business and taking care of her son.

name: Medius
description: Medius lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is single with seven children and all of them attend school. She is not looking after other family members.  She has been selling second hand clothes in the market at both wholesale and retail for the last 15 years, working six days a week. She does not earn any additional income.  She has requested a loan of UShs 1,100,000 from Kiva partner MCDT- SACCO in order to enable her to stock more bales of shirts, blouses, trousers, dresses and skirts to sell.  Her challenges include thieves and seasonality. Her dream is to accumulate sufficient profits to enable her to acquire land to build a house and also to become a wholesaler. She joined MCDT because of the relatively low interest on loans. She rents a house with access to electricity but no piped water.  Her major monthly expenses include rent and school fees.

name: Mariam
description: Mariam is a first time borrower from UGAFODE Microfinance Ltd (MDI), applying for ugx.1,000,000. She is a single mother of two children with whom she lives in one of her brother’s rental units in the outskirts of the city. She operates a food business from her home. This has helped her be able to take care of her children and educate them. Besides looking after her children, she has also managed to buy a small piece of land. Her major challenge is staying in her brother’s small house yet she has mature children. This has forced her to start building a simple house that she would like occupy in the near future. She is constrained by her finances; this is why she is applying for the loan. Her future plan is to work hard, complete her own house and send her children to good schools.

name: Vivencia
description: Vivencia is 45 years old and has four children, three of whom are in school. Vivencia is married.  Vivencia is in the agricultural business raising pigs in the Philippines. Vivencia requested a PHP 5,000 loan through NWTF to buy feed and vitamins for her pigs. Vivencia has been in this business for five years now, and has borrowed once in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Vivencia would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Lolita
description: Lolita is a 60-year-old married woman from San Jose, Talibon. She has been engaged in rice farming together with her husband for more than 10 years now.  Lolita works hard to support her husband in meeting the needs of the family. Lolita hopes to expand their business but lacks the capital to do so. She wants to take a loan to buy more fertilizer and pesticides for the farm. Through this, they will be able to improve their harvest and yield.  In the future, Lolita hopes to make her business a success and save money for the future.

name: Reim's Group
description: Reim’s group lives in a rural village of Takeo province in Cambodia. Reim works as a farmer to support her family and she also does extra work as seller by selling groceries. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these group members to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses, and save time collecting fuel in order to boil water.

name: Arslonbeck
description: MicroInvest loaned Mr.A. Arslonbeck money to buy a pedigree bull, which he paid back on time.  He is engaged in the livestock business. He dreams of having a large flock and in future opening a trade outlet to sell meat and the milk-sour products. Now Mr. A. Arslonbeck applies to KIVA for a business development loan of $625 for 8 months to build a new cowshed.

name: Sret's Group
description: Sret lives in a rural village of the Ou Reang Ov district of Tbaung Khmum province, Cambodia. She is 50 years old and married with six children. Two of her children are in school, while one is too young for school, so she has three dependents. To support the family, Sret has been growing rice, corn, and soybeans for more than 32 years. The current business earns her about 50,000 KHR per day to make a living, and she can afford to save 25,000 KHR each day after expenses. Low crop yield resulting from drought and insect pests have been a challenge for her business. This is Sret’s group loan with Kiva’s partner, VisionFund. She and another member are just members of VisionFund in this cycle. Sret is leading her group to ask for a loan. As the leader, she will use her portion to buy fertilizers and seeds for her plantation. With this loan, she hopes to make healthier crop yields to increase her family’s income. She hopes to make a living better and be able to afford buying household necessities for the family.
town: Kampong Cham province, Ou Reang Ov district

name: Deborah
description: As a married parent of four children, Deborah works hard to support her family.  She has a general store business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from boarding house rental.  Deborah is borrowing PHP 28,000 through NWTF to buy more items to sell like soap, shampoo, canned goods, chips, etc. for her general store business.  Deborah successfully paid back her previous loan and now she requested this additional loan to further build her business.  Deborah has been sustaining her business activities through her past eight loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Florence
description: Florence is a 50-year-old widow with five children who owns a house in Kasese, Uganda. Ever since her husband died, she has been solely taking care of her children and her desire is to see them employed or setting up income generating activities. She has been in the stationery business for 17 years in which she acquired capital from her late husband's pension. Her hardship is bad debtors and her vision is to set up at least two more stationery shops. Florence needs the loan facility to buy books, pens, papers, files, gift cards and success cards to sell.

name: Virgenia
description: Virgenia is 57 years old and married with five children. She has earned a living for the past four years by having a pig fattening business in the Philippines. She earns additional income from farming vegetables.  Virgenia is borrowing PHP 17,000 through NWTF to purchase feed and vitamins for her pigs.  She is working tirelessly towards the attainment of her dream: to build and expand her business to secure her family's future.

name: Maria Luisa
description: Maria Luisa is 48 years old and married with six children. Maria Luisa works very hard to provide for them.  Maria Luisa runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 6,000 loan through NWTF to buy items like home product care and other groceries.  Maria Luisa has been in this business for 3 years.   In the future, Maria Luisa would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Melahet
description: Melahet M. and her husband own and operate a market in the small northeasterly Azerbaijani town of Devechi. She and her husband have been working in this store for the last 16 years and have four children, some of whom also work at the store. Melahet and her husband are currently seeking funding so that they can increase the quantity and variety of their inventory.

name: Saima
description: Saima is a 35-year-old married woman and a mother of seven children. She has been running a successful general store for five years with the support of her husband, who is shown in the photo with her. They started their business on a very small level and expanded it gradually. Over time they have retained many regular customers. To stock her store more fully, Saima has applied for a loan of PKR 25,000 from Kashf for the fifth time. She intends to use this money to purchase sacks of rice and flour, and packs of cleaning products.  She wishes to spend part of her revenue on providing a quality education to her children.

name: Seina's Group
description: Seina’s group lives in a rural village in Kompong Thom province in Cambodia. Seina makes a living cultivating rice and she also does extra work as a tailor to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Mapatano B Group
description: Odetta T., age 39, is a widow and has two children (ages 18 and 15). She has a tailoring business which she started 7 years ago. The business is open from 7 am to 3 pm daily, and allows Odetta to earn a monthly profit of around US$34.  Odetta hopes to receive a loan from Tujijenge Tanzania in order to expand her tailoring business and to open a new food sales business. She will share this loan with her sub-group members who have businesses in the sale of fish, sarongs, cosmetics, table tops, and milk, and in running a bar.   In the picture, Odetta is the first one on the left.

name: Shamim
description: Shamim lives in a small city near Lahore, Pakistan called Kasur, which is known for its leather industry. She is 40 years old, married to M. A. and is the mother of three sons and two daughters. She lives in a three room brick house with her family. Shamim is a business woman who operates a business selling bangles. She sells bangles from her home, collects orders from different jewelry shops and supplies the bangles to them to make an income. She also sells bangles to her neighboring community and earns a good profit.   Shamim couldn’t educate her children, except for her 12 year old son who reads to the 5th standard. It was not possible for her to afford his school fees but now her current business situation makes it possible for her to bear his education expenses. Her eldest daughter keeps herself busy doing household chores, while her eldest son supports the family financially by working in a shoe factory which pays a monthly wage. The other two are free and don't do anything.   Shamim has applied for a loan from Asasah for her bangles selling business. With the loan amount she will buy bangles in bulk because Eid, the Muslim holiday which marks the end of Ramadan is approaching and she has a large order to fulfill. Bangles are in high demand for the Eid celebrations and there is potential for making a lot of income. Shamim is a regular loan user of Asasah and is in her 2nd loan cycle. For her previous loans she maintained good credit behavior and never missed a meeting.

name: Genaro Ii
description: Genaro Ii runs an automotive machine shop. He caters services like motorcycle repair, wheel alignment, and other kinds of vehicle repair services. He is a married man and has one young dependent. He has been operating an automotive shop for 11 years now. This time, he needs additional funds to purchase a machine that is very useful to his day-to-day operation.Genaro Ii decided to take a loan to invest in the automotive machine. This will enable him to improve his services to his customers and produce quick results that he hopes will lead to customer satisfaction. Thus, more customers would prefer to avail themselves of the services he renders. Thus, his income will be augmented and will improve the family's living condition. He hopes to become a successful businessman someday.

name: Mwanakombo
description: Mwanakombo is a 52-year-old married woman with two children, one child is enrolled in school.   Mwanakombo operates a food stall, which is located at the market centre. She has been in this business for 1 year, and she aspires to open a restaurant in the future. Mwanakombo lives in her own house that has neither electricity nor piped water. She joined Yehu to access funds, and she describes market competition to be her major challenge.   With the loan of 10,000 KES, she will be able to add stock of rice and wheat flour to her food stall.

name: Nurana
description: Nurana  was born in 1983. She is single and lives in Khachmaz town. Three years ago she started a cafe and now needs a loan of $1200 US to buy necessary equipment for the cafe.

name: Lilibeth
description: Lilibeth lives a peaceful life near her rice paddy in the town of San Miguel, Bohol. She is a mother with five dependents aged two to thirteen. Five years of farming allowed Lilibeth to raise her children, feed them, and send them to school. She is asking for a loan to buy fertilizer to make her farm productive and increase her yield and harvest; thus for her income to follow. Lilibeth dreams of the best living for her family and for her children to continue schooling for their better future.

name: Luz Mila Del Socorro
description: With her hard-working hands, Luz Mila has struggled hard to grant her daughter the opportunity to study and be able to realize herself as a person. She is a friendly woman and has a business selling breakfasts and lunches in the municipality of San Pedro De Los Milagros.Her daughter and her fiance depend on this business. For this reason, she asks for a loan to purchase supplies and ingredients such as meat, rice, vegetables, grains, and more, so to be able to have a greater quantity of supplies available to prepare her food. Support Luz Mila to get her business ahead with a loan. If you want to know more about the entrepreneurs and the loans from Interactuar, you can join the Lending Team called: “Friends of Interactuar Colombia”: http://www.kiva.org/team/interactuar_colombia

name: Donatus
description: Donatus is 32 years old and married. He sells hair extensions, hair cream, etc. He is a stylist and has been in this business for years. He is very hardworking and he makes sure he has food on the table every day through his hard work.   Donatus plans to increase his sales during this festive period. He is requesting for a loan of 80,000 NGN to purchase more hair products to sell. Donatus hopes to be able to have a big vending stall in future. He says thank you to all Kiva lenders for support.

name: Elsa
description: Elsa D. owns 1-hectare of land in her village. She grows rice and other crops like "camote," which is the Philippine name for sweet potato. She also raises chickens to support the needs of her family. She has 6 children and a husband, who spent his entire life, since he was just a kid, on the farm.  She is requesting a loan of Php 15,000 from CEVI. She will use the loan to buy quality rice seeds and fertilizers needed to increase her yield. This loan will truly help her family grow their business.  CEVI is a non-profit organization that aims to help alleviate poverty. It helps people start and own businesses. They not only provide credit, but training and insurance coverage, too.

name: Elsa
description: Elsa, 39, is a married woman with five children, two of whom are currently in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.   Elsa has a buy and sell rice grains business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for five years.  Elsa requested a PHP 15,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy more sacks of rice grains to sell.  In the future, Elsa would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Phin
description: Phin C., 38, lives with her husband, Kis Thy, in Phnom Penh with their three children. She sells duck eggs and yams, typically making US$ 7 per day, while her husband is a motor-taxi driver who makes around US$ 3 each day.   Phin C. has asked for a loan of US$ 500 to purchase a trailer to attach to her husband's motorbike. This trailer would really serve two purposes that the couple could benefit from. First, it would allow her husband to transport more passengers and increase his income each day. It would also allow Phin C. to transport her yams and other vegetables to better reach customers. She believes this investment can help her family improve its standard of living and increase its income in the long term.

name: Mohamad
description: Mohamad is a 52-year-old man who lives in Nabatieh, southern Lebanon, with his wife and their three children. Mohamad has owned a grocery store for ten years. Mohamad requested a loan of 1500 US dollars from Al Majmoua in order to purchase merchandise for his store. This is the first time that Mohamad has requested a loan.  Mohamad is special in his work because of his store location since it is in the middle of the town. His clients are his friends and neighbors. When Mohamad first started his business, he had financial issues. In the future, he plans on expanding his business.

name: Ndaro
description: Ndaro is a married woman; she has six children, all of whom attend school. Ndaro owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.  Ndaro operates a charcoal sales business, selling from home to her neighbors and passersby. Her major business challenges are stiff competition from other firewood operators and transportation.   Ndaro wants to use this KES 50,000 loan to purchase sacks of charcoal for resale. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Truly Group
description: Theresa is 51 years old. She is a widow and has given birth to five children. Her children are all in school. She lives with her children in a rented apartment in Axim. Axim is along the coastal area in the western region of Ghana. The major occupation of the people is in the fishing industry. Theresa is a caterer. She is the leader of a trust bank group called Truly. The members of the group are mainly in the fishing business and other commercial activities. The group requests a loan to procure goods in bulk to expand their businesses. Theresa, the group leader, is second from the right in the photograph. It is the group's desire to give their children the best education they can afford.

name: Marife
description: This is Marife, 42, a resident of Silang, Cavite, Philippines. She is married to Nelson, a driver, and is a mother to their children. She and her husband manage their household while operating the business. She and her husband are working hard to provide income for their everyday needs.  Marife sells different beauty products. She gets her products from a direct manufacturer with a lower cost, then sells them at a higher price. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community. She earns a minimum of 2,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) in sales every week.  To help her continue operations of her business, she is requesting a 15,000 PHP loan. She will be utilizing the loan to buy additional supplies and merchandise, like cologne, deodorant, perfume, soap and other products needed in her business. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands her business.    Marife dreams to have her own factory for her products and hopes to have a good life. She meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her life and business every week and draw strength and inspiration from the fellowship and the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Tha Pyae Kan Village Group
description: This Tha Pyae Kan Village community is located in Myanmar Ayeyarwaddy Delta region. The group is composed of five CBO (Community Based Organization) members overseeing 20 village customers. This loan will help group members purchase ducks and high-quality feed (costing $28 for six days feeding 100 ducks). These uses will boost villagers' income from selling more duck eggs.  Hmaw Bi village has a population of over 440.  Besides duck raising, those villagers with arable land cultivate rice and plant seasonal vegetables and fruits such as bananas and coconuts. Villagers also raise pigs for additional income. Some households have a small grocery or dry food store that they operate out of their houses. Pictured above are the CBO members from Tha Pyae Kan Village Group named Daw Tin, U Aung, U Win, U Myo and Daw Thandar. Included in the picture, Daw Tin (first from right) is 45 years old and married with nine children. Her husband runs their farm and sometimes goes fishing, selling his catch in the town market. Daw Tin takes care of the ducks and plants seasonal foods. Daw Tin will use Proximity loan to purchase high-quality feed for ducks that will boost income of Daw Tin's family.  Daw Tin plans to use part of the additional income to reinvest into their duck business and part for discretionary spending such as her children's education.

name: Luz Karina
description: Luz Karina, 27, is a member of Asociación Arariwa’s “La Unión de Ollantaytambo” communal bank.  She is single and has two children.  Her main commercial activity is the sale of alcoholic beverages like chiha (made from fermented corn) and beer; she has been in this line of work for a year and does very well.  Luz Karina is a hard-working, enterprising person who is always looking for opportunites to get ahead in life and, through her own efforts, raise her children.  She is asking for funds to equip her pub.  Luz Karina is grateful for the opportunity provided though this means and pledges to repay her loan in a timely fashion. Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Kwabena
description: Kwabena O. is married and has one child. He has received schooling through the junior high level. His wife is a fishmonger.   Kwabena makes artifacts and crafts and sells them at Coconut Grove near Elmina. He has been in this business since 2003. Kwabena uses his income to pay his utility bills and other family expenses.   Kwabena will use this loan to purchase carving tools, wood, and other materials for his business. With the new profits from his expanded business, Kwabena plans to improve the living conditions of his family.

name: Ibraheem
description: Ibraheem is a 23-year-old single man from Jabalia city, which is located in the Gaza Strip and suffers from power outages 12-16 hours a day regularly. He lives with his family in a small house. As an employee in the public sector, he earns a low income. This income barely covers all the family's needs. Because he is not able to save enough money, Ibraheem took a loan from FATEN. With this loan, he will buy a solar energy system for heating water at his family's house.  Palestinians use water boilers that use either gas or gasoline to heat the water before a shower, which can be dangerous, expensive and inefficient.  This will help him to provide hot water without using electricity, which is much more expensive.

name: Nenita
description: Nenita earns a living by selling dried fish. She is from Sindangan, where fish are abundant. She makes dried fish by herself, and earns more out from it. She is now increasing her inventories by buying more kilos of fish and salt. She learned the craft from her parents, who are into fishing.   Now she applied a loan to build bamboo nets and a stall where she can sun dry her fish.   In the future, Nenita wants to buy a motorcycle for easy transport of her retailing business.
town: Sindangan-Doña Josefa, Sindangan, Zamboanga del No

name: Adzo
description: Adzo T. keeps bar in Danyi, a town situated approximately 175 kilometers from Lomé, the capital of Togo.  51-years-old, Adzo is married and the mother of six children.  Over the course of the last year, her good management enabled her to earn a decent profit.  To better meet customer demand, with her second loan Adzo wishes to expand her business by ordering drinks by the case. Translated from French by Joyce ., Kiva Volunteer

name: Saolin's Group
description: Saolin is a rice farmer who has two hectares of farmland. She is also a paid worker, working on another farm to get a fee. She lives in Kampong Thom province. She is 41 years old and a married mother of a child who is still depending on her. Through her businesses, she could earn about 20,000 KHR per day and have around 9,000 KHR daily for emergency needs. Saolin has been with VisionFund for three cycles already and fully repaid back the loans. The previous loans help her to have a better house to stay.  Now she is leading a small group to apply for a new loan via VisionFund to buy more farmland to expand her farming area. She hopes to earn more income to improve her family living and give her the ability to keep sending her children to school.

name: Emily
description: Emily N. is a widow with three children. Currently, two of them are in school and the other has completed high school. She lost her husband through a prolonged illness. According to Emily, she works very hard because the total responsibility of the kids rests on her shoulders as a single parent. She is now 62 years old. She sells home products like cooking utensils, plastic bowls, buckets and plates, and bottle of drinks. She makes her sales by 'hawking', which is door-to-door sales. Emily is an achiever and her focus is to save enough to support her kids in school. She wants to use the loan to buy an increased stock of plastic materials, kitchen sets and assorted drinks to serve her customers. She would be very grateful for the support. She belongs to the group called Be Serious Trust Group. The group provides assistance and support to one another to repay the loan. She is in a photograph during her group meeting.

name: Gabriella
description: Gabriella, a young woman, 31 years old, has a husband who is an entrepreneur. And she is a mother of two children (7 and 2 years old). One of the children is in school. To help meet family needs, Gabriella has been selling grocery items in her shop since 2005. With many customers and not wanting to disappoint them, she is taking out her fourth WAGES loan to purchase more merchandise (rice, sugar, detergents, ….) For the future, she hopes to have a big spot for selling in bulk and for ensuring her family’s future.

name: Eleazar Rafael
description: Young Eleazar Bermúdez is 25 years old. He has been a tailor for the past 9 years, he learned from his mother and started the business with his own money. The customers who bring sewing to him leave 50% down and this helps him to be able to finish the work. He lives in the Villa Reconciliación neighborhood and is single. This is his second loan with Afodenic, which he will use to buy a bolt of fabric, thread and other things that will help him work. His plans are to buy an industrial sewing machine so he can grow his business and be able to provide good service to his customers. Translated from Spanish by Molly Puglisi, Kiva Volunteer

name: Clara Yudy
description: Clara is a single mom, who has earned her life working hard in order to raise her son well. Currently she is unemployed, but since she wants to improve her economic situation, she decided to rent a place with all the necessary assets to start her own general store. She learned this business while living with her grandparents, who owned a similar business. She is asking for a loan to support her in buying stock at wholesale prices (grains, cookies, coffee, chocolate, cleaning products, dairy products, cold meats, sodas, among others), so she can start her productive project with which she hopes to produce good results for the welfare and living expenses of her son. This will allow Clara to fulfill her dream of strengthening her business so it becomes her main source of income to guarantee her son's access to a good education and a better quality of life.

name: Orlette
description: Orlette T. is from the village of Sugbongcogon, Misamis Oriental. She is 20 years old. Orlette is married and has one school-aged child. To make a living, Orlette owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) retail shop. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling both food and daily-use products in the local community. Orlette has been engaged in her business for more than two years and earns approximately 10000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2010, Orlette joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. Orlette is requesting a new loan of 4000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Orlette from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI: HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Maria
description: Maria goes to school and works and is from the city of Caacupé. While she is a student, she also works. She plans to achieve her objective with the help of Fundación Paraguaya, with the loan she is requesting since, with it, she wants to pay university fees and purchase books.  She has consistent business in a butcher shop where she works every day. She is a very hard-working and self-sacrificing person.

name: Cristita
description: Cristita is a 33-year-old married woman. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. She has three children who are in school.  Cristita has a vegetable vending business in the Philippines. She requested a 17,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase more vegetables to sell. She has been in this business for 6 years.   Cristita would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Asif
description: Asif M. is 26 years old and a very enthusiastic young man who has been selling different kinds of domestic goods since 2005. Asif is single but responsible for supporting his parents who are unemployed. His shop is the only source of income in Asif's family but the income that his shop brings him is not enough to build his own family.   Asif believes one day he will have a big family with many children. For this purpose Asif applied for a loan in the amount of 1600 AZN, as he believes this loan will help him to increase his profit. Let’s do our best to help this hard-working man.

name: Jocelyn
description: Jocelyn is 48 years old and married with two children.  She earns a living by farming and buying and selling vegetables in the Philippines. Jocelyn is borrowing 12,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) through NWTF to purchase additional seeds, fertilizers and other farm equipment.  Jocelyn has been farming and buying and selling vegetables for 10 years and also earns additional income from food vending.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save money to expand her business.

name: Saidi
description: Saidi, aged 50 years, is a married man with seven children who lives in a permanent house in Kyenjojo, Uganda. He wants his children to study and have their own stable income.  Saidi deals in cattle. He wants a loan to buy more cattle to resell at a profit.

name: Santos Milagro
description: Santos is 34 years old.  She is a hardworking woman who did not attend school, but learned to read and write as an adult.  Her parents did not want her to attend school, and since she was young, she took care of the household chores.  She lives together with her life partner who works at the border.  She is the mother of two children, a 16 year old daughter and a 19 year old son.  Only her daughter and her granddaughter live with her.    She sells enchiladas, fried yucca, and other food items.  She has had this business for more than 12 years.  She learned to make different traditional foods when she was young.  She works from her house and her daughter helps, since her husband works.  She makes sales in the afternoons three times a week.  She will use this loan to purchase more merchandise such as yucca, corn, oil, beans, bread, and seasonings, since a soccer tournament is coming up in her community.  She will be there all week, and she is lacking capital to purchase ingredients.    In the future, she plans to continue working in the same way.  She wants to improve her business day by day and be able to work hard to move forward like she has always done.  She would like to have a fixed location in a location with more commerce to increase her profits.

name: Mujeres Unidas 1 & 2 Group
description: Groups 1 and 2 from the Mujeres Unidas Bank of Hope are ready to start their second loan cycle through Esperanza International. The group members all live in Villa Mella, which is located in the northern outskirts of Santo Domingo, which is Dominican Republic’s capital city. Evelyn R. and Josue A. are the group coordinators. Evelyn has five children. The youngest is 12 years old. All her children still live with her. She sells shoes, which she purchases in Dajabon (a city in the northwest of the Dominican Republic, which is about a 5 ½ hour ride from Santo Domingo) as well as in the capital. With this loan, she will buy mostly tennis shoes and sandals. She explains that depending on the time of year, sales increase on a certain kind of shoe (for example, loafers during back-to-school time). Evelyn hopes her profits from selling shoes will allow her to buy a house of her own. This would let her have a more peaceful life. Josue has four children of ages 10, 8, 6 and 3. His current business is selling clothes. He finds greater demand for women’s clothing. Lately, however, he has noticed that people are not buying as much as usual. He will use this second loan to purchase new clothes to sell. During his interview, he commented that he likes the fact that because all the members of his group paid their first loan on time, Esperanza International approved higher loan amounts for them in this second loan cycle. He hopes to continue that trend so he can invest larger amounts in his business and create sustainable growth. Thank you for supporting these entrepreneurs!

name: Teresa
description: Teresa is 63 years old and a married woman with three adult children. She is a farmer from the town of Santa Josefa, Agusan Del Sur.   Teresa primarily grows rice to sell. She has requested a loan of 10,000 PHP because she needs to purchase fertilizers and other farming necessities. Teresa hopes this loan will help to improve her farm.

name: Rose's Group
description: Rose, pictured above, has been a farmer for 12 years, and is now proud to represent her group of 10 farmers in Chwele District. She is 36 years old, married and has seven children.Rose likes to think of herself as a very hardworking individual. She has been working alongside One Acre Fund since 2014 and decided to represent her group because she wanted to help more farmers. She says that being part of the One Acre Fund community has meant that she has had more profits from each harvest. Rose plans to use the profits from this coming season to buy a cow.In total, Rose’s Group will receive inputs to cultivate 5.75 acres of land. Given that some members of the group will also be purchasing a solar light, with this loan the group will also receive a total of seven solar lights.

name: Sarah
description: Sarah is 69 years old and has four children with two dependents.  She runs a business selling livestock.  She has been in this business for 10 years.  Right now, her monthly income is KSh 10,000.  She is borrowing KSh 30,000 to buy three cows, two for sale and another one for milk production for her  family.  This is her first loan from VisionFund.  She hopes and dreams for future business so she can have dairy cows for milk to sell and educate her children.

name: Santiago Felipe
description: Santiago is 37 years old. He is married with two children. For the last eight years he has worked raising, fattening and selling chickens. He has three salaried workers, and to be in the institution you have to be a client for four consecutive years.  He had problems with losses of a considerable sum in the production of chickens with epidemics. He has an advantage in that he is an farmer with land sown with basic grains, which helped him cancel the debt with the institution.  Currently he is asking for this loan to invest in chicks which he can raise, medicine for any pests and animal feed in bulk, like purina.

name: Burulkan
description: Burulkan is 62 years old and married. She is a mother to three children and a grandmother to two grandsons. Burulkan is responsible, joyful and hardworking. She has a secondary education and is retired. Since 1973, she has practiced agriculture. Thanks to Burulkan's hard work, she currently has 3 cows and 10 sheep on her farm. She also grows barley for use on her farm and for sale. The income from this business is 10,000 som (KGS) per month. For the further development of her business, Burulkan turned to Microfinance Bank "Bai Tushum." She is requesting a loan for 50,000 som (KGS) to buy a cow. Burulkan plans to invest the earnings from the loan in the further development of her business so that she can save money to build a house for her family.

name: Lucio
description: Sr. Lucio lives in the neighbourhood of La Colorada in a friend’s house. He is her caregiver and does not pay rent. He doesn’t have a wife or children to support.  Lucio managed to obtain a vehicle after working hard and saving his money. It now requires servicing and repairs so he is seeking a loan to pay for this. He will then be able to use the vehicle for transport and business, and thus save time. He has earned his living doing bodywork and painting vehicles for ten years, working from the house where he lives.  Lucio’s great hope for the future is to save enough money to buy some land and build a house of his own.

name: Saon's Group
description: Saon is a 48-year-old married woman with four children. She lives in a rural area of Kampong Thom province. For 20 years, she has been growing rice and pigs-raising to support her family. Her rice did not grow well this year and she is able to sell it in the lower price than before.   Saon is requesting a loan with VisonFund (Kiva’s partner) in order to build a decent latrine to upgrade her family’s living. This is will be the first loan cycle for her and her member with VisionFund. She hopes that she can improve her family's living and having better health through this loan.
town: Kampong Thom Province, Prasat Balang district

name: Marion
description: Marion is a married mother of three children and two of them go to school. She takes care of additional family members. She sells used clothes at the market on a retail basis, and has been in this business for 10 years. She has applied for a loan of 900,000 UGX from MCDT-SACCO to buy a bale of used clothes. She generates additional income from selling piped water.    She works seven days a week. Her major business challenge is transportation. She is aspiring of owing a fully stocked stall and also of buying a plot of land.  She resides in her own house and the family has electricity and piped water. Her monthly expenses include food and school fees.

name: Judith
description: Judith continues working at her business selling clothing and her business offering mobility services. She sells pants, blouses and shirts.  Through this business, the member wants to get ahead; her dream is to have a bazaar.  She asks for this loan to purchase shirts, sweaters, shirts and blouses.  She is happy for the loan and promises to make the payments.

name: Kate
description: Kate U.  is 32 years old and married with no children. She lives in Benin City, Edo State, Nigeria. Kate is a hardworking woman  who has run a small business selling clothes, shoes, bags and baby products for 5 years. As she acquires more customers, she needs capital to expand her business.  Kate has been a LAPO client for 3 years and is seeking a $325 loan to expand her business. "I believe my business will improve with the above loan amount," explained Kate when talking about her reasons for requesting a loan.

name: Rugashali Tukole Group
description: Maria is 36 years old, and is married with five children ages 15,13,11, 9, and 1 years old. Four of her children attend school and her husband pays their tuition. She is the woman standing at the far left in the first row of the photograph. Maria has worked as a farmer for the last 15 years, which is her major source of income supporting her family. She also operates a small retail shop at home to add to her earnings.  Maria has applied for a loan of 600,000 Ugandan shillings for her farming activities, which she will use to buy mulch for her banana plantation and pay workers to plow it. Maria's dream is to buy a motorcycle to help carry manure to the banana plantation and to transport her children to school.  Her major challenges are limited capital, the bad weather that affects local agriculture, and price fluctuations in the market. Maria thanks Kiva for being their savior in a time of need.

name: Elna
description: Elna R. is from the village of Abu, Baylao, Mambajao, Camiguin Province. She is 46 years old. Elna is married and has four adult children. To make a living, Elna owns & operates a business venture making & selling food. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes from making & selling snacks & other delicacies like "siopao" (steamed buns), banana "cue" (deep-fried banana on a stick), & sweet potato delight in the local community. Elna has been engaged in her business for over 6 years and earns approximately 6500 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2011, Elna joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Elna is requesting a loan of 4000 PHP which will be used to purchase raw ingredients like sugar & bananas needed to make products for sale. This will be the 1st loan taken out by Elna from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HHSPFI is an accredited partner of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and reaches out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Brigida
description: Brigida is a 64-year-old married woman. She lives in Cabungaan Clarin, Misamis Occidental, Philippines.  Brigida plants, harvests and sells bananas for a living. She's been in the business for 20 years and gains 2,000 PHP a month from this business. She has requested a loan of 4,433 PHP, which will be used to purchase fertilizers such as manure.  In 2011, Brigida joined GDMPC to seek assistance to improve her business. She hopes to improve their living conditions and to save a reserve for future emergencies.

name: Maria
description: Maria is a 31-year-old, married woman. The income generated by her husband is insufficient to cover all household expenses, so she initiated her business of milk sales. She has been doing it for many years and has become famous for providing good quality milk in her locality. With the support of Kashf Foundation, she has gradually improved her business. Currently, she has requested a loan of 40,000 PKR to purchase another buffalo to increase her sales and earn profits for providing her family with the basic necessities of life. Maria aspires to further expand her business and increase the number of animals she at present owns.

name: Ximena Gabriela
description: Ximena is a 24 year old woman who lives with her partner. She has a five year old child. Her business is buying food and primary need products in her neighborhood store.She has many virtues and defects. She is gentle, loving and compassionate, persevering, devoting all her efforts with dignity. Her business takes place in the 'Kollpajahuira’ area which is located on the east slope of the city, where the streets are markedly steep. Ximena is brown-sugar skinned with long dark hair, dark as a stolen piece of the night and full lips like succulent fruit. Her native tongue is a secret that her mother taught her and that she only practices with her Aymara family members. She speaks Spanish in daily life. She shares her life with her partner who works as a builder and her son who studies in Kindergarten. They live in an adobe house that is property of the family that has potable water, electricity and sewage. Her business is a neighborhood store. She started the business not being able to find room in the labor market. With the help of her parents and a minimum of capital she opened her store with basic foods like bread, soft drinks, toilet paper and others. "In spite of the sales, stocking the store is difficult as the distribution trucks don't enter the neighborhood as the roads are too mountainous" she commented. Her business is successful as she has no competition nearby. Her disadvantage is the lack of merchandise and services in the area. Her dream is to improve her business. She wants to buy a telephone cabinet to offer this service. This is her first loan with the institution in the 3 years she has been in this business. For these reasons Ximena is requesting a loan to buy a telephone cabinet for her store to offer this service and expand her store.

name: Pinena
description: Pinena, 57, is a married woman with two children who are in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Pinena has a food-vending business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for 37 years.Pinena requested a PHP 23,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy ingredients like coconut, sugar, banana, etc. for her food-production business.In the future, Pinena would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Valientes Group
description: This group is called “Valientes” (Brave Ones) and is located in the Mexican state of Morelos.  It has 9 members and this is the first time they have requested a loan from CrediComún.  Ignacia S. M., 49, is a group member.  She has a nixtamal (tortilla dough) mill.  This activity has been beneficial to her because most of the people in her locality make tortillas at home every day to eat.  Therefore, the service Ignacia provides is basic which has provided her with guaranteed daily income.  This has allowed her to improve her locale because at the beginning it was made from cardboard sheets, as was her house, and now it is stone.  She uses the loan to provide maintenance and repair for the mill and to buy parts, like gears and bearings, to replace deteriorated ones.  These parts need to be changed periodically due to use and this isn’t counting some breakdowns caused by the machine’s age since it has been in operation for 60 years.  She has 6 children (3 boys: Gustavo, 23, Daniel, 19 and José Manuel, 17, and Antonia, 28, Juana, 26 and Guadalupe, 21).  She has been in this line of work for 26 years.  Her son Daniel is currently in college in the state of México and she has to work to support his efforts because she’s always dreamed with her children becoming professionals.

name: Ahit
description: Ahit S. is 44 years old and lives with his wife and two children in Bayan-Ulgiy province, western Mongolia, in a traditional nomadic housing tent called a "ger." His elder son Bazarbek, who is 22, works for a local private company while the younger son is a student. Ahit operates a food retailing business with the help of his wife. He began his business in 2002 in a small room of his house, but expanded his operation and set up a small shop called "Tsetsegt" two years later with working capital of 500,000 MNT. His wife is responsible for their food retailing business. Ahit has purchased a small car with his business earnings as well as his son's salary and has started running a taxi service in his town. He hopes to continue his success in the future and says, "My wife and I are working hard to save money for our son's education." He is requesting a 1,000,000 MNT loan to increase his working capital.

name: Regina
description: egina,26, is a young mother of three that lives with her family in Totolapan, Morelos. Regina works selling the crops of her neighbor and roughly makes around one dollar per day. Her working hours are long and has to manage to cook and do other chores. Regina lives in a one bedroom house where she sleeps with her husband Eri, a local driver, and their two children Margarita and Santiago. Regina and Eri have been living here for the last 10 years, working hard to save and continuously improve their house.  Since Regina and Eri do not have formal jobs and their income is low and variable, neither of them have access to credit from banks or other organizations. Regina wants to cover the dirt floor in there children's room with cement as well as the floor in the living room. She is now asking for a loan to complete the payment of materials needed. The family will receive supervision visits from certified technicians to monitor the quality and progress of the construction. With the new floor the room to give the kids their own space to play, sleep and study will be completed as well as the family room.   Regina and Eri did not have the chance to finish their education and were forced to drop out after elementary. They want to make sure they take the right steps to give better opportunities to their children, and support them as they work their way through school.

name: Elsa
description: Elsa is taking a loan of $600 to improve her business.  She is married and she has three children.  She runs a kiosk that helps her to generate income for her family.  She will use the loan to buy stock to keep in her store, such as oils, fish, milk, bread, slippers, coffee, sugar, and salt.  She opened her kiosk a year ago with her own working capital of $ 300.  Elsa is a hard-working woman and she hopes to run a bigger business in the future.

name: Erlinda
description: Erlinda G. is from the village of Punit. She is 59 years old, married, and has 1 adult-aged child. Erlinda owns and operates a specialized retail store which offers a variety of products to the local community. Erlinda has been engaged in her business for over 3 years.  In 2009, Erlinda joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Erlinda has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5000 PHP from ASKI. This previous loan was used to purchase additional products to sell. Erlinda is requesting a new loan of 5000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional inventory. This loan will be the 3rd loan taken out by Erlinda from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 29 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly of farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Rael
description: Rael is a thirty-four-year-old farmer in Kisii county in Kenya where she lives with her husband and five children who are all schooling. She has been farming for the past six years, producing milk, beans, maize and sugarcane, which she sells at the local market in her area. Poor roads and poor markets are her major challenges in farming. She also operates a small retail shop and sells secondhand clothes as an additional source of income.   She is requesting a 50,000 KES loan from Juhudi Kilimo to buy a dairy cow, which will give her more milk and increase her income, which will help her improve her living standards. She will use part of the money to pay for her children's schooling. Rael is very thankful to Juhudi Kilimo for giving her the loan.

name: Paola Andrea
description: This is Paola Andrea.  She chose to go into nursing because when she was a kid she wanted to be a nurse.  She wanted to help people.  One day her grandfather came to the house and was very sick.  She worried a lot about his health and started to take care of him, but his illness was very serious and he died.  This was when she developed a desire to help people, regardless of their social class, race, or the type of illness they might have.  She has an understanding and tolerant personality which has helped her in working toward her dream of being a nurse.  She studied nursing at Sena for a semester but had to leave the program for reasons beyond her control.  Now she is studying at CampoAlto, where she has been given the opportunity to achieve her dreams as well as financial assistance since her family has limited means.    Paola's mother, Veronica, is 57, and her father, Jaime, is 59.  They used to be well off, they had everything, but violence forced them to abandon everything and move to the city of Villavicencio.  They started a new life there with their two kids, and the city took them in, providing them with stable work.  The whole family worked very hard there and they bought a house which they later sold to support one of the siblings who wanted to enter the police force.  He was accepted and given a job in Bogotá so they left Villavicencia where they didn't have income because all of the money had been invested in their son.  Paola is 18 years old.  She was raised in the city of Villavicencio until she was 11 when they moved to the city of Bogotá.  Since then she has been a good student and a responsible, honest, tolerant, respectful, understanding person who wants to get ahead and help her family and the whole world.

name: Carmen Jessenia
description: 28-year-old Carmen is single and lives in her own home which doesn't have basic services.  Her house is located in the rural part of Catacaos district, in Piura department.  Throughout this area, local people work in farming, livestock raising, handicrafts and tourism.  Carmen makes and sells 'chicha de jora' (a delicious drink made from corn which is drunk a lot in the north of Peru).  She has been in this business for several years.  It is a custom which has been handed down from generation to generation.  Recently, sales of 'chicha de jora' have increased in Carmen's area which has been good news for her.  She has been able to increase her income and improve her standard of living.  As she has the opportunity to improve her business, Carmen has requested a loan for 2,000 Peruvian soles from Edpyme Alternativa to buy tables, chairs and supplies for making 'chicha de jora'.  She will also make some repairs.  Her goal is to make more profits and increase her number of customers.  This will enable her to repay her loan and improve her financial situation.

name: Hernán
description: Hernán uses his car as a Radio Taxi and is also a mechanic. He is single and lives in his parents’ house in the Achachicala area of the city of La Paz. His loan will be used to buy tools to set up a mechanics workshop and so improve his quality of life and his income. This is the third time he has requested a loan through Impro, his file shows that he is a number one client, that is to say he reliably repays his loans. Translated from Spanish by Lara Francis, Kiva Volunteer

name: Jesus Edgardo
description: Jesus is a farmer. He is 45 and married to Nely with whom he has three children to feed and support.  He currently produces coffee, however he wants to start a production of organic bee honey. This will allow him to diversify his source of income so that his family's wellbeing won't depend solely on the income from the coffee.  Honey production is a new and very successful activity in the region, since the good plant density favors an abundant production of honey. Additionally, the bees contribute with pollination to the abundant harvest of the other products in the region.  Jesus needs a loan now to buy beehives and start the honey production work as soon as possible. This will allow him to count on an additional source of income so that he will not depend on a single crop. This loan will help him by giving him better chances to provide a decent quality of life for his family and the option of a good education for his children.

name: Alberto
description: Alberto believes there is no waste, only resources. He invested in a Sistema Biobolsa biodigester in order to fully experience and live this, and start transforming his cows' and sheep's manure into renewable energy and organic fertilizer. Instead of piling the manure up in a corner of his farm, where it generated bad smells and was emitting greenhouse gases, he will now treat it and transform it into a productive resource. He will produce his own biogas to replace the wood and LP gas he used to buy. These inputs are not only expensive and contaminating, but the burning wood was also exposing his wife and family to the risk of contracting pulmonary diseases. From now on, they will cook and heat water with clean energy, and fertilize the corn field with nutrient-rich, organic fertilizer, shifting towards a model of sustainable farming.Alberto needs this credit to finance the outstanding 22% of the cost of the biodigester; he already made a cash downpayment and received a government subsidy for the remainder.

name: Emily
description: Emily is 25 years old and married with three children, one of whom is in school. For three years, she has earned a living by raising livestock and running a general store in the Philippines. Emily is borrowing 7,000 PHP through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation in order to buy feed and other supplies to raise her livestock. She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Ayaba
description: Born in 1970 in Lomé, Mrs. Ayaba T. is married to a teacher and is a mother of a child. The income of her husband, a substitute teacher, is too low to provide for the needs of the household; therefore, she started selling cloths in the Hédzranawoé market.  Today, in spite of her hard work, due to her limited means, her business has not taken off. In order to increase her buying capacity in department stores and contribute to her household needs with an increased profit, she is asking for a credit of $800 which will be used as capital for the purchase and sale of the fabrics. Thus her family will have a better standard of living.   Translated from French by Ivana Kostic, Kiva Volunteer.  Née en 1970 à Lomé, Madame T. Ayaba est mariée à un enseignant et est mère d’un enfant. Le revenu du mari, un enseignant vacataire, étant trop bas, pour suppléer le dans les besoins du ménage, elle s’est lancée dans le commerce de pagnes au marché de Hédzranawoé. Aujourd’hui, malgré son dévouement et avec le peu de moyen dont elle dispose, son commerce n’arrive pas à décoller. En vue d’augmenter sa capacité d’achat dans les grands magasins et réaliser un profit maximal pour contribuer aux charges du ménage, elle sollicite un crédit de $800 qui va lui servir de fonds de commerce pour l'achat et la vente des tissus pagnes. Ainsi sa famille connaîtra un niveau de vie meilleur.

name: Excel School
description: Greetings from Uganda! This is Jenipher. She is the Head teacher of Excel Infant School, a mixed school in the Peri-Urban area of Kyebando with 92 students. Excel Infant School has requested a loan to cover the cost of installing and maintaining a UV water filtration system to provide clean drinking water for its students. The school does not currently have access to consistent clean drinking water and therefore has to spend a considerable portion of its budget on firewood, which is used to boil water for the children. Installing a water filtration system will therefore save the school money in the long-term as the cost of firewood will be reduced. The loan will enable the school to purchase a UV water treatment system with a 450 litre tank, which will be big enough to store clean drinking water for the students every day.   Excel Infant School will repay their loan from their school fees, which they collect each term. Jenipher ultimately hopes that having access to safe drinking water will improve her students concentration and attendance by reducing the number of children that fall sick from water-borne diseases as well as increase the number of students coming to the school.

name: Channa
description: Channa, 23, is married and resides with her husband and one child in Kampong Cham Province, Cambodia. She has been a farm worker for over two years, earning approximately USD 3 per day. Her husband is employed in a factory and earns approximately USD 6 per day. Currently, she has two hectares of farmland. In order to grow agricultural crops on this farmland, Channa is requesting a loan of USD 600 to hire a farm worker to clear the jungle on the land. In the future, she would like to run a small pig farm and help her child get a bachelor’s degree.

name: Karolina
description: To instruct and to teach is something admirable and honnorable. Karolina is a charismatic and caring woman who has worked as a primary school teacher for 13 years. She decided to study for this profession because she loves to learn and she observed that, in her community, many people have difficulty with writing.   Karolina asks for this loan to be able to pay for her university tuition, and thus be able to improve her economic income and to strive for a master's degree. This hardworking woman's goals and plans are to improve her home and to continue studying for her master's degree. Becoming a teacher satisfies Karolina, because it helps her to overcome her troubles and to correct and answer others' questions.

name: Emilly
description: Emilly, who is 42 years old, is a charismatic young woman and a strong example of hard work. Emily is a farmer and salesperson who has access to many sellers throughout the food business. On her farm she keeps cows and has a small cash crop garden and trees. To earn additional income, Emily makes a commission on sales for which she helps arrange the logistics of getting farm produce from local farmers to their buyers. She has been doing this business for over a decade. She continually makes an effort to build strong relationships because reputation is everything in her line of work. Given that Emilly can arrange a sale more easily than regular farmers, she prefers to deal with larger volumes of produce. She is seeking a loan to aggregate more produce from local farmers at fair prices and use her better understanding of the market conditions and prices to sell it at a profit. Your loan will help Emilly’s clients to focus on production rather than sales, and it will help her family to earn a better income to uplift their livelihood.Support her dream by giving Emilly a loan!

name: Mary
description: Mary is a married woman with three children, all of whom are enrolled in school. Her husband, Augustine, is employed and contributes to the provision of the family’s basic needs.  Mary lives in a rental house with neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is food for her family.   Mary has operated a vegetable stall for the past three months and her potential clients are the local area residents. She faces a major challenge of seasonality. Mary dreams of expanding her business.  Mary wants to use the Kshs 10,000 loan to purchase more vegetable stock, such as tomatoes, onions, and cabbage, for resale.  She decided to join Kiva partner Yehu to access loan opportunities to expand her business.

name: Jacqueline
description: Jacqueline is 22 years old and married with two children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.     She has a tricycle passenger business in the Philippines. Jacqueline has requested a PHP 9,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy spare parts for her tricycle.  Jacqueline has been in this business for three years. In the future, Jacqueline would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Henie
description: Henie is 49 years old, married and has four children, two of whom are in school. She and her family survived super-typhoon Haiyan, which swept through the Philippines on November 8, 2013, but her business and home were wiped out. She is requesting a loan for PHP 9,066 to buy building materials and pay for labor to build a new house for her family. Henie has been a NWTF borrower since 2012, and plans to rebuild her general store. With your help, she can rebuild her house, rebound from the devastation of the typhoon and save enough money to expand her business.

name: Parfaite
description: Parfaite A. is born on April 18th, 1977 in Allada, in the Atlantique department. Parfaite is married to Jules DAGNITO, a primary school teacher, and is the mother of three children, of which only one is her dependent. Parfaite settled in the Gbowèlè neighborhood of Allada almost four years ago, and lives there with her family. The couple shares various family expenses. Parfaite didn't attend school for very long. For about seven years, she has run a business selling sandals, bowls and coolers as well as castor sugar in Allada. Parfaite gets her supplies in Cotonou, the economic capital of Benin. She has already benefited from an ALIDé loan, which she paid back without problem. Parfaite would like to increase her working capital and her product stock to grow her customer base. That is her objective in requesting this second loan.Translated from French by Charlotte Buecheler, Kiva Volunteer

name: Marrieta
description: Marrieta is 53 years old and lives in Poblacion Sinacaban, Philippines. She is married and has three children. Marrieta has a motor and vehicle business. She earns approximately PHP 3,000 each month doing this work. She has requested a loan to purchase needed equipment for her motor/vehicle shop.Marrieta has been a member of PMPC for six years. In the future, Marrieta hopes to supplement her family's income and to expand her business.

name: Eduardo
description: Eduardo, 39, is a resident of Silang, Cavite, Philippines. He is married to Rustic, is self-employed, and has one child in high school. He works hard to provide for his family and to send his child to school.  Eduardo owns and operates his own jeepney transportation service. He has one jeepney (14-16 person capacity). Jeepneys are the most common and cheapest form of public transportation throughout the many islands of the Philippines. They are one of the remnants of the American military presence in the Philippines during the Second World War and are still to be seen throughout the country, in many colors and all over the place. The Filipinos, being creative, saw the possibility to turn these vehicles into a real form of transportation by making them about two meters longer and by putting in two long seats, one on each side, from the front to the back. Since then, jeepneys have been used as small buses for the cheap transportation of people, goods, and sometimes even little animals.  To help him continue operating his business, Eduardo is requesting a loan of 40,000 Philippine pesos (PHP), which he will use for the maintenance and registration of his jeepney. It is very important that his unit always be in good running condition to ensure efficient service. He thanks God and you in advance for the financial help that he will receive.  Eduardo hopes to buy another jeepney unit. He dreams of giving his child the best education. He prays for his and his passengers' safety in every trip. Every week, he faithfully meets up with his co-fellowship members* to share stories of his work and draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God, which he studies.   * All Center for Community Transformation (CCT) community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Rosiry Elena
description: Rosiris, 43, is a resident of San Juan de Nepomuceno, where she lives with her husband and children. There she has a small business making "bollos," or corn rolls. She decided on this activity after seeing the success her sister had in the same business. Her husband works selling pork and chickens. Together they have succeeded in getting ahead and securing their children's wellbeing.Rosiris is applying for a loan through Kiva partner Fundación Mario Santo Domingo to buy sweet corn to make corn rolls and to buy pork and chickens to improve her inventory, thereby increasing sales. Her hope is to continue in this business, to learn other trades to improve her quality of life and to make improvements in her home.

name: Cristina
description: Cristina is a member of the Desarrollo (“Development”) Village Bank.  She is 53 years old and married with four children. Cristina lives in the city of Pichari, in the Ayacuchan jungle. Cristina has a seafood restaurant called Palacio D. los Mariscos (Shellfish Palace). Her son administers the restaurant, and has two employees to help him. Cristina also has a clothing store in a rented location, where she sells baby clothing.  Cristina needs a loan of 2000 soles to buy baby clothes.  Cristina dreams of buying a plot of land, of having her own store, and of buying a car.   Translated from Spanish by Cynthia McMurry, Kiva Fellow  Cristina es socia del Banco Comunal Desarrollo.  Cristina es casada, tiene 53 años y 4 hijos, Cristina vive en la ciudad D. Pichari que esta en la selva ayacuchana, se ubica a 7 horas D. la ciudad D. Ayacucho, Cristina tiene una Marisquería llamado Palacio D. los Mariscos, su hijo es quien se encarga D. al administración D. este negocio, para lo cual cuenta con el apoyo D. 2 personas. Además Cristina tiene un bazar en un local alquilado,  en donD. venD. ropa D. bebes.  Cristina necesita un préstamo D. 2000 soles dinero que será invertido en la compra D. ropa D. bebe.  Cristina sueña con comprar un terreno, tener local propio y comprar un carro.

name: Benjamín
description: Benjamin, 22, works in agriculture, a trade he learned from his parents.  He has a high school education and a wife who is a homemaker.  Benjamin gets up at 5:30 a.m. to go work on land he rents.  The rest of the day he sells dairy products such as cream, cheese, curd, etc. in surrounding areas and rural communities in order to earn extra income.  The loan he is requesting is to buy more cheese, cream, cottage cream and curd to strengthen the business he has.  He wants to begin offering his products in other areas to expand his business.  In the future and with the help of another loan, Benjamin plans to buy a vehicle to transport his products more easily.  Right now he uses a motorcycle and is unable to carry very much which limits his income.

name: Amon
description: Amon is a 30-year-old determined farmer who started farming in 2003 with a hope of getting a clear source of income that would help him cater to his family's needs. He is married and has two children aged six and three years old. He gives the farming business, which is his sole source of income, an average of six hours each day. His farm is located in a local area in Katunda Parish-Mitooma Sub County. He would like to use the loan money, 700,000 UGX, to buy construction materials to finish his incomplete residential house that has stalled over time due to limited resources. His family will enjoy a decent accommodation when its complete. He will pay the loan using money from his banana plantation. His customers are traders from the same area. He says he is mainly faced with a challenge of Banana Bacterial Wilt, but believes that it will be solved with time and he will hence have financial stability.

name: Hilario Roberto
description: Hilario is 27 years old and lives with his partner and their five children. Hilario lives in the Mocache canton of the Los Ríos province.  Luis is part of the "Los Luchadores" communal bank, located in the La Guayas area. La Guayas is part of the Mocache canton. The members of the  communal bank here make a living in farming work, and in raising livestock.  Hilario works in farming. He grows corn and rice. He buys his supplies in Ventanas, in a shop called "Agroquímicos Briones", and sells his own products at the market in Ventanas.  Hilario is applying for a loan in order to buy manure, urea and liquid fertilisers in order to sow corn and rice. This loan will help him to support the household economy.  Hilario's dream to buy a plot of land.  Hilario likes to travel with his family.

name: Manuel
description: Manuel B. is from the village of Tabuan, Tukuran, Zamboanga Del Sur. He is 55 years old and married. To make a living, Manuel owns and operates a specialized retail store, selling daily use products such as shampoo, soap and toothpaste in the local community. He has been engaged in his business for over four years and earns approximately $68 a month for these activities.  In 2010, Manuel joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and ability to engage in business activities. He has successfully repaid a previous loan of 10,000 PHP from GDMPC. This previous loan was used to purchase new items to expand his product offering.
