Manuel is requesting a new loan of 12,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This will be his 2nd loan from GDMPC. He plans to use the additional revenue generated to expand his business.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three unit offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Pedrita
description: Pedrita works hard to support her family. Pedrita is married and has a raising livestock business in the Philippines.  Pedrita requested a PHP 10000 loan through NWTF to buy feeds and other supplies to raise her livestock.  Pedrita has been in this business for 7 years now.  Pedrita would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Teresa
description: Mrs. Teresa M., 42 years of age and married, is a resident of Mantic, Tangub City. She is blessed with six children: four are now in their teenage years and the other two are still minor dependents. Presently, she buys and sells Chinese medicines. She has been in this business for six years and earns an average net income of not less than 3,000 Philippine pesos (PHP) a month.   As a new member of the Paglaum Development Program for Landless People (a micro-finance program of PMPC) she was given the privilege of taking out 5,000 PHP as her first loan to add to capital for her current business. Her income is used to meet her family's daily needs and for savings. She is hoping that with this business she will be able to send all her children to school for a good future.
town: Tangub-Mantic, Tangub City, Misamis Occidental, Mi

name: Claudia Cinthia
description: Claudia is a 19-year-old woman who is single and has no children. Her business involves washing cars. Claudia is sweet, loving, sensible, sincere, generous, understanding, responsible, and hardworking. She conducts her business in the District of Villa Fátima, an area that is known for wholesale trade. Trucks carrying fruits, vegetables, and meats arrive from the north in order to be sold in this place in bulk. The weather is cold and dry as a result of the winds that blow from the mountains.  Claudia has a dark complexion, long black hair that is tied back, and dark eyes. Her native language is Aymará and she speaks Spanish in order to integrate into the general culture and to conduct business. Claudia shares her life with her mother, who manages a store in their neighborhood. They live in a rented brick house that receives running water, electricity, and sewage services. Her business involves washing cars. Every day she sets up her business at the corner of a gas station where cars line up and wait to be washed.  She cleans the interior and exterior, washes the tires, and vacuums the seats. At the end, she polishes the body of the vehicle. “I have regular customers who come once or twice a week. The average time I spend for each car is 30 minutes.  On the days when it rains, I have no work,” says Claudia. Her dream is to become a professional and to work at a large company. Claudia wants to invest in her business by purchasing a vacuum cleaner and a water sprayer so that she can work more efficiently. This is her second loan cycle with Emprender. She has been in this business for three years.  For the reasons, previously mentioned, Claudia is requesting a loan in order to buy a vacuum cleaner and a water sprayer so that she can wash cars at a faster pace.

name: Walaa'
description: Walaa’ is 35 years old and lives with her husband and six children in Gaza. She has been working at a society for deaf children for five years, but her husband lost his business after the war.Today, Walaa’ is requesting this loan because she needs support after the Gaza war. Her house was destroyed, so she wants to rebuild it. As a start, she wants to buy building materials and pay for the workers to start work.One of her biggest dreams is to see her children grow and to give them the best education so that they can become professionals. This loan will help her to improve the house conditions for her family. She is grateful to everyone who helps her to start this step.

name: German
description: German is married and is a responsible father of two children. He is a conscientious and hardworking person. German has been involved in growing agricultural crops for over six years. He grows rice. When he started this business, he had two hectares of land and now he plans to expand his land. He wants to gather a good harvest and maximize his profit. German wants to obtain a loan in the sum of PHP 22,000 to purchase mineral fertilizers for his farm business.

name: Bunly
description: Bunly, 50, is widowed and has four children. Her family lives in a house with thatched roof, located in Kampong Cham province’s Cheung Prey district and the main sources of her family’s income are from farming rice and working for others for a fee. She has been running her business for years, earning about KHR 60,000 per day and she is able to save about KHR 40,000 each day.  Bunly is just with Kiva’s partner, VisionFund, for this cycle. Now she is applying for a loan to buy fertilizer and seeds for her farmland. She hopes to increase her crop yields to earn more income to make a better living.
town: Kampong Cham province, Cheung Prey district

name: Wilberforce
description: Wilberforce is thirty years old and married with two children. He operates a barber shop which he started in 2010 to employ himself. He also earns extra income by charging phones. He needs a loan to buy a solar charging system plus machines to use in his barbershop. Although Wilberforce faces great competition, he hopes to expand his business in the future and own more barber shops, so that he can earn more income.

name: Khum's Group
description: Khum’s group lives in a rural village in Kampong Speu province in Cambodia. Khum makes a living cultivating rice and he also does extra work as a factory laborer to support his family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women and men to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Murodali
description: K. Murodali is 51 years old. He is married and has 4 children. Murodali has a middle special education. His specialization is engineering. But he went over to agro-business because the salary was small. And with that small salary he has to feed his family and pay for his children’s education.   Murodali works hard to cultivate his produce and also to raise cattle. He works from early morning till late at night hoping to have a rich harvest. Murodali sells his crops at the market where they are always in high demand due to their good quality. His work fills him with great optimism and allows him to help his beloved children. His goal is to improve the quality of his agricultural produce even more and expand his cattle breeding business. Today Murodali is requesting a loan of 4500 Somoni to buy greater quantities of seeds and fertilizer. Let's help Murodali as he works hard to improve the quality of life for his family.     More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History  Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Margaret Njoki
description: Margaret has been farming in Ndunyu Njeru town and has been a loyal loan borrower from KADET LTD, this being her fifth loan term. She used her previous loan amount to buy fertilizer and seedlings for planting on her farm. She was able to plant and harvest and it was very profitable. Margaret repaid all the loan amount well and in good time.  She plans to use this loan amount to buy fertilizer, pesticides and seedlings for planting during this rainy season. With the anticipated profits, she plans to increase her cattle stock and thereby boost her dairy farming too.  In the future, Margaret hopes to improve her farming methods and become one of the leading farmers in Ndunyu Njeru town.

name: Deborah
description: Deborah is a thirty-six-year-old, hard-working, married woman living in Kamwenge, Uganda. She deals in agriculture as her main source of income though she has other side businesses, including selling produce for extra income. She started this business to sustain her family and improve their standard of living. She faces the challenge of seasonal changes that affect her agricultural production. She has a dream of constructing a big, permanent house in the future.  She is requesting a loan to buy manure and mulch for her farm.

name: Solomon
description: Solomon is a resident of Mariakani, Kenya. He is married and has six children. He sells spare parts, mainly bicycle parts and accessories; a business he has run for the last fourteen years.  He is applying for a loan of 80,000 Kenya shillings to add stock of retail items to his store. He aspires to open a hard ware/work shop in future. The rent received from this venture will help him pay school fees for his children besides the dream of building a retail house.

name: Blanca Gladys
description: Blanca B. is a member of the 'Corazón de María' (Heart of Mary) community bank and lives in Yanaturo community, in the city of Cuenca.  This city is renowned for the beauty of its streets, its historic center, its food and the warmth of its people.  Blanca is 45 years old.  She is married and has 3 children aged 27, 23 and 18.  Her eldest son is married and lives independently, her second son works and helps towards the household finances.  Her youngest, a daughter, is single and helps in the house.  Her husband has a taxi cooperative and works in his own vehicle.  Through their joint work, they have managed to build their own home.  Blanca is a saleswoman.  She sells all kinds of clothes.  She works 5 days a week.  On 3 of these days she travels to the coast to sell her merchandise.  The remaining 2 days she sells her clothes in a market in the city where she has her own stall.  She does not have fixed working hours.  This is the second loan that Blanca has had with her community bank.  She was invited to join the group by one of her nieces.  The money from her new loan will be invested in buying more clothes to stock her business for the Christmas period.  Her goal is to expand her business.

name: Karen
description: Karen lives in her sister’s house in La Paz’s Las Lomas neighborhood.  She is a single mother of a five year old daughter.  She sells Broasted-style chicken in a store she runs at her home address.  The loan is to equip her business since she inherited it from her mother and she needs to refurbish furniture, stove and other items.  The business is her only source of income so granting the loan is advisable; this is the first time she has requested a loan.

name: Byambaa
description: Mrs.Byambaa is a 50-year-old widow who lives with her two daughters in a ger, a Mongolian yurt, in the Govi-Altai province of Mongolia. Her two daughters go to the secondary school, while Byambaa has been working as a veterinary doctor for 11 years. She also learned tailoring in Oyu-tolgoi project's tailoring course in 2011 and has been tailoring her and her daughters' clothes since then.   Byambaa  is now planning to establish a tailoring business, and so is requesting a 2,000,000MNT loan to purchase equipment and inventory and pay the initial rent of her work premises. She is a hardworking and friendly woman who says, "My short-term goal is to increase my income and save money for my children's further education. They will be enrolling in university by next year."

name: Ferzana
description: Ferzana is a 34-year-old married woman. She has been operating a business of selling bangles for one year in order to contribute to her family's income. Her husband has a job in a factory but makes an insufficient amount of income to fulfill the demands of his family.   Ferzana offers various types of bangles in different colors and sizes to the people of her community. She also sells the sets of bangles in the market at reasonable rates. For the further improvement of her business she contacted Kashf Foundation and applied for a loan of Rs. 30,000. In this way she would be able to purchase more variety of bangles in various sizes, colors and designs. She is expecting a boost in her earnings, and she dreams of expanding her business in the future.

name: Kunthea's Group
description: Kunthea is a 40-year-old, married resident from the Thmor Koul district of Battambang province.  She has three children.  To support her family, she works for others and also grows vegetables for resale.  This business earns her about 38,900 KHR per day.  This is not the first loan for Kunthea’s group as they have been with VisionFund, Kiva’s partner, for the past three cycles.  The past loans, which she has fully repaid, supported the basic daily needs of her family and helped to grow the business at a good pace.   Now, she is requesting a 400,000 KHR loan while the other members are requesting 300,000 KHR each.  As the leader, she will spend her loan portion to buy potash for her farmland.  She hopes to earn more income so that she can set aside some money for future needs.

name: Marvin
description: Marvin is 40 years old and is single. He is a small farmer in the area where he lives. He is requesting his second loan, which he will use to buy four calves of 200 kgs each. He will rear these calves until they are a good size and weight, then he will sell them at a price that will earn him a good profit.  His biggest dream is to see his herd grow strong so that he can leave his children a good inheritance that they can work in order to have a good life.

name: Accrington
description: Accrington is a resident of the Nkubu area in Central Kenya where he has been practicing mixed farming for ten years, producing mainly fruits like mangoes and bananas for the local market. He is aged forty six years and married with three children aged between 20 and 7 years.  Accrington has requested a loan of 40,000 KES from Juhudi Kilimo to help him buy piglets. He says the venture will help him generate enough income to educate his children. He notes he will also save part of the income for a venture into dairy farming.  He says the main challenge remains lack of capital for running farming as a business.

name: Marvin
description: Marvin is a 42-year-old pepper producer and the father of four, who lives with his family in the region of Upala, in the northern part of Costa Rica, minutes from the Nicaraguan border. Marvin is a dedicated farmer. He plans to focus his efforts on the planting and harvest of habanero peppers. He works to strike a balance between accomplishing the daily tasks associated with agricultural production and the completion of domestic responsibilities. The land he works is his own. In addition to his agricultural activity, Marvin feels it is important to be an active member of his community. As a result, he dedicates a significant portion of his time to community meetings, groups and events. The rural zone where Marvin lives is sparsely populated with infrequent bus service and a general lack of infrastructure. Marvin is working hard, striving to reap the maximum benefits from his land and his labour.   Although this is an individual loan, the community in which Marvin and his family live is very close-knit and interdependent. Neighbours help and support one another by sharing experiences and expertise acquired over the years. All individual members of the Upala community are dedicated to the improvement of living conditions for the region as a whole.  This loan will be used to finance the production of habanero peppers. Specifically, the loan will be used to finance the purchase of a variety of necessary agricultural nutrients, fertilizers and chemicals in order to ensure a healthy harvest. All labour and logistical tasks associated with production will be carried out by Marvin. The productive cycle (from planting to harvest) for this type of peppers is roughly one year. Marvin planted his peppers 4 months ago and will expect to harvest in the next 8 months. Typically, he dedicates the hours from 6:00 AM to 4:00 PM everyday to his agricultural activities.   Piper and Capiscum Processors Compañía Agrícola Industrial, or PROPICA, is an international buyer and seller of chili pepper and ground pepper products. In cooperation with Fundación Mujer, PROPICA has guaranteed to purchase the agricultural products (the peppers) that are to be produced with the help of this loan. PROPICA acts as a guaranteed client for small agricultural producers in the area of Upala, thus ensuring that their products will reach market.   The main obstacle Marvin and other producers in the Upala community face is a lack of access to working capital funds. The collaboration of Fundación Mujer and PROPICA represents a unique opportunity for Marvin, his family and community. By offering a source of start-up capital and a guaranteed client to purchase what is produced, there is a chance to improve living conditions for Marvin as well as the community at large. Above all, Marvin wants to take advantage of the current opportunity that has been presented – he wants to profit from this collaboration and see improvements in his home and neighbourhood.

name: Jonalyn
description: Jonalyn is 30 years old, married, with one child who is in school. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.Jonalyn has a fishing business in the Philippines. Jonalyn requested a PHP 15,000 loan amount through NWTF in order to buy fishing gear and other equipment.Jonalyn has been in this business for 15 years. In the future, Jonalyn would like to save enough to support the financial stability of her family.

name: Bernadeth
description: Bernadeth M. is a young mother residing in Barangay Sinili, Santiago City. She is engaged in charcoal and vegetable vending as her way of assisting her husband in providing for the needs of their family.  She is married to Marlon, a tricycle driver who also works as a farmer.  They have two children and all they want is to give them a better life.  Through their hard work and patience, they believe that they will succeed in life.  Their two children are Reymark - 2 years old and Rachelle - 2 months old.   Bernadeth would like to access a loan amounting to PHP 4,000 for the improvement of her vending business. This amount will be of great help in fulfilling her plans for her business.

name: Un
description: Un S. O. is a 49 year-old man who lives in the province of Kompong Thom. Un S. O. is a local farmer who has been planting a variety of crops since 1990. He has a life partner in his wife who sells fresh fish in the busy market. They have given birth to five children: three are single and two are married. One of them is a farmer as well as fisherman.   Un S. O. is currently planting a peanut crop O. his own farmland, but he lacks capital to complete the project. In order to deal with this problem, Un S. O. hopes to use his Kiva loan to rent a plowing machine to plow his farmland. He will also purchase seed and fertilizer for growing.

name: Felipe
description: Felipe is 79 years old. He is known in Tambulig area for his rice mill. He is actively participating in the various programs and services that the PMPC offers. He hopes to live comfortably, in a decent house, for which he has applied for a loan to pay for labour, paint and cement. Felipe hopes to sustain his business so that he can continually provide for his family.

name: Lenin
description: Lenin is 50 years old.  She lives together with her husband in her own house.  Her two children that she has are already independent and have their own family.  For more than 6 years she has worked selling clothing.  Her method of sales is to visit her customers and after a period of time, she prepares to collect the money for her product.  This work is her main source of income so she visits the malls, the most popular in her city, to acquire a variety of clothing in various colors and designs that are attractive for her customers, of whom the majority are female.  She hopes to continue working like until now, gaining a good amount of customers to improve her economic earnings and in the future, to be able to have a large clothing store.  This is her third credit with MFP and she promises to be very punctual with all of her payments.  With the loan she is requesting, she will be purchase more clothing to increase her earnings.Translated from Spanish by Kathleen O'Connell, Kiva Volunteer

name: Edwin
description: Edwin lives in the Tiquina street of the Villa Ingenio zone in El Alto city.  He lives with his wife and his two little children who are 6 and 3 years old. They all live in a single rented bedroom.  Edwin has a small beauty shop located at the zone's plaza. He's been working there for more than five years. His wife helps with the family expenses with the weekly wages that she earns as an assistant at a micro-enterprise in charge of  paving streets.  Edwin will use the loan to purchase tools for his shop (he needs a new pair of scissors, towels, dyes,etc.)  This is Edwin's first IMPRO loan. However, the evaluation performed by IMPRO qualifies him to receive the loan.   Translated from Spanish by Yael Schwartzman, Kiva Volunteer

name: Aira
description: Aira is from Quezon, Nueva Ecija.  Their family’s source of income is farming. What they earn is sometimes not enough, therefore she wants to access a loan of PHP 70,000 to be used to pay her tuition fee. Aira is taking a BS in Business Administration at the College of the Immaculate Conception. She wants to finish college to achieve her dreams and help her family.

name: Dorothy
description: Dorothy is married and has three children who attend school. For the past two years, she has operated a fish selling business. She also sells charcoal to local neighbors.   Dorothy is requesting a loan from Yehu for 20,000 KES, which she willl use to purchase more dry fish and charcoal to sell to her customers. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business. Dorothy faces a major challenge of the high cost of transportation. She owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is food for the family. She dreams of establishing a vegetable stall in the future.

name: Vigen
description: Vigen K. is from the village of Aghin in the Shirak region of Armenia. He is married with a 6-year-old daughter and a 1-year-old son.    Vigen has a high school education and for the past 15 years, he has been in the vegetable-growing and pig-breeding business. At this time of the year, animal feeds and additional livestock are less expensive. Therefore, Vigen has chosen to take a loan at this time to grow his business. He has chosen microfinance as the services are well organized without complications.    With the loan, Vigen is going to purchase feed and additional livestock. He is expecting his family income to increase by up to 20 percent with this investment. His dream for the future is to save enough money for his children to attend university. He enjoys the village life and being a farmer.

name: Nabeela
description: Nabeela’s husband has been driving an auto-rickshaw and pays a daily sum because this rickshaw does not belong to him. He belongs to an ultra poor family and has been feeding his children alone. Nabeela has been putting aside savings for many days to buy an auto-rickshaw for her husband but at the time of purchasing, some money came up short.   Therefore, Nabeela has requested a Kiva loan for her husband so that he can buy a rickshaw with the contribution of savings.  She hopes that now her husband will not have any need to pay a daily sum which becomes the cause of his low income. Nabeela is a 38-year-old woman, living with her three children and spouse in the area of Lahore, Pakistan.   Nabeela hopes that now her husband will be able to generate more income because she is very happy after receiving this loan; she thanks Kiva and field partner, BRAC Pakistan.

name: Abida
description: Abida is a 45 year old, married woman.   The man shown in the photo is Abida’s husband who is a driver by profession and provides transportation services using his three-wheeled rickshaw. He has been driving a rickshaw for many years to meet the family expenses, but now it requires proper maintenance to keep it in its functional routine. For this reason, Abida has applied for a loan of 40,000 PKR for her husband. He wants to purchase some auto spare parts and tires for his vehicle. This will help him drive more smoothly and provide better transport service to his passengers.   Abida is hopeful that this loan will be a productive one for her husband and will bring positive changes to his business.

name: Khun
description: Khun is 60 years old, is married, and lives with her family which consists of six members. Her oldest child is already settled for marriage while the remaining three are single and employed as paid workers, so that they can contribute their income to uplift their standard of living. Khun is in the business of cultivating rice as well as selling fish supplied by her husband, who is an operator of fishing activities along the river. Khun's business has provided a supplementary income that she can use to pay for her daily sustenance. She has been doing this for over 12 years.   To maintain her fishing business, Khun really needs new fishing materials to apply to the business at the right time but she has insufficient funds now. Therefore, Khun is requesting a loan of 1,500,000 KHR to purchase fishing materials. With this purchase, she believes that her fish supply will increase and she will receive better income.

name: Rosa América
description: Rosa is 63 years old.  She is divorced and lives alone in Santo Domingo. It is one of the country’s youngest cities and has now become the connection point between Sierra and Costa de Ecuador.  It is a special place, known not only for its rich ethnicity but also for the unusual landscapes found at the entrance to this beautiful city.  Santo Domingo de los Colorados now belongs to the recently formed province of Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas.  Santo Domingo’s main festival is celebrated with an influx of visitors that engage in commercial and cultural exchange.  A big fair takes place on the premises of the Asociación de Ganaderos where the best examples of breeds and crossbreeds raised on the region’s farms are shown in competitions.    Despite having only completed a primary school education, this hard-working woman has managed to survive. For the past thirty years, she has been selling clothing and household items such as sheets and quilts.  With this income, she lives a modest life and despite the fact that she works six days a week and often carries large bags of clothing, she is optimistic.  She has raised working capital through credit, and this time she requires a loan to invest in merchandise because the school season is very good for sales and she plans to take advantage of it.    Competition has increased as now there are more merchants on the street. However, Gloria believes that by making this investment, she will have a wider variety of products to offer and in this way, she will maintain and perhaps even increase her clientele.

name: Afi
description: The mother of four children, Afi is a 49-year old married woman who lives in Adidogomé. Afi makes cakes and obtains the necessary ingredients twice per month at the market. She is requesting this loan so that she can order bags of wheat flour, jugs of oil, sugar and charcoals. With the resulting profit margin, Afi will be able to extend her activity and promote her children's education.

name: Phanice's Group
description: Phanice is 38 years old and has six children. She has been a farmer for 16 years and is always said to be a very hardworking individual. Even though Phanice is the only one featured in the above picture, she is actually representing her group formed by 14 farmers in Chwele District, Kenya.Phanice started working alongside One Acre Fund in 2010, and decided to do so because she wanted to get the best quality fertilizer and hybrid seeds. Since then, she has seen her life improve, especially in the sense that she has been able to consistently feed her family ever since. This year she decided to represent her group because she wanted to be more active in her community.Phanice’s Group will receive farming inputs to plant a total of 7.5 acres of land. Additionally, some of the farmers in the group will be purchasing a solar light, so with this loan, the group will also receive a total of five solar lights.

name: Busime Group
description: This client, Margerite, is the vice-president of the business group Busime. An experienced entrepreneur, she is 50 years old, married, and the mother of four children, who already have their own households. This client sells fish and other food items. She sets up her products in front of her home. She started this business with her own funds gotten from her husband. Later on, she benefited from Hekima loans. She has been in this business for twenty years.  This new loan is going to be used to purchase 60 kg of fish, 12 kg of young fish, 2 containers of palm oil, etc. She would like to grow her capital. In conclusion, she thanks Hekima very much for its micro-loans supporting women entrepreneurs to be autonomous.   It should be noted that certain clients in the photo are carrying their babies and that the photo was taken in a hurry during a lot of yelling, since a rainstorm was threatening the village of Kavumu.

name: Nasreen
description: Nasreen is 45 years old. She is a responsible mother of five. She is a housewife and looks after her family, which is comprised of eight. She is well-trained in cloth stitching. She provides stitching services to people from her house. She needs to purchase a sewing machine and a variety of stitching materials for her work, including thread, needles, and cloth. This is very important for her to continue her work efficiently and professionally. However, due to the lack of money, she finds it difficult. So Nasreen is requesting a loan from Kiva partner BRAC Pakistan. BRAC Pakistan issued her loan, as she requested. Nasreen is very thankful to Kiva's partner, BRAC Pakistan.

name: Martina
description: Martina is requesting a loan to have her house waterproofed and painted, as during the rainy season water filters through consequently damaging the roof. Martina wants to prevent this problem from getting to serious and therefore costing more money than estimated. In order to pay for the expenses she works as a make-up artist Mondays to Fridays, and in some occasions she does overtime to make extra money. Martina is a single mother of three children, and she wants them to become good citizens and to reach a better economic status. She will give them the best education she can, acting as both mother and father.  In order to carry out her project she needs to buy construction materials and paint to protect her house.

name: Victor
description: Victor is married and is the father of five children who go to school.  He lives in his own home and doesn't support anyone else besides his family.  He works as a criminal investigation agent for the Republic of Mozambique Police Department.  He will use this loan to buy construction materials (cement, beams, metal sheets, etc.) to finish work on his home.  In the future, he hopes to finish his home.  To do this, he promises to make his payments on time so he can request more loans from Hluvuku.  His challenge is the elevated cost of living that is reflected day after day due to the financial crisis.

name: Bibiana
description: Bibiana is a thirty one year old single mother of five children who owns a house in Kasese Uganda.  She has been dealing in dried fish for nine years.  She formally dealt in selling beans and when her capital increased she switched into fish selling.   Her hardship is high taxes levied on her.  Her vision is future business growth and to have a good residential house.  Bibiana needs the loan to buy fish to sell.

name: Mtvarisa
description: Mtvarisa is a 47-year-old woman from Senaki district. She isn't married and lives alone. Mtvarisa doesn't have her own business and she earns her living with the help of her daughter, who is married and has her own family. Mtvarisa has a great desire to be involved in her own business and not depend on her daughter's charity.   Mtvarisa requested a loan from MFO Credo and was approved with the start-up program that gives people a chance to start or re-start businesses. She plans to purchase stock of clothing and various home products and will sell the products among her community at increased prices. This new business will be a really good motivator for this hard-working woman and will greatly assist her in living better. She will highly appreciate your help.

name: Nasim
description: Nasim is a 34-year-old married woman and mother of one child. She is motivated to provide everything for her family. That is why she has been running a general store with the support of her husband for a period of about two years. She offers a variety of grocery items at a reasonable price and has retained many customers who regularly shop at her store. She makes enough to provide for her family. To fully stock her store, she requested a loan for 20,000 PKR which she will use to buy rice, sugar and flour from the market at lower rates. In this way, she will be able to meet the increasing demand consistently. She wishes to utilize part of her revenues to increase her business capital.

name: Hope
description: Hope lives in Uganda. She is single and has one child who is in school. She also takes care of additional family members (eight orphans from her late sister). Hope has a business selling local medicine.  She has been in this business for four years and she works seven days out of every week.  Hope sells her products door-to-door, by means of retail. Hope has requested a loan of 500,000 Ugandan shillings from MCDT SACCO, which she will use to buy more bottles and tins of powdered local medicine. The main business challenge(s) for Hope include defaulters and seasonality.  Her goals and aspirations for her business are to get a permanent business premise, to be a wholesaler and to buy a plot in order to build her own house. Hope lives in a home that she rents. She has access to electricity and piped water. Her major monthly expenses include school fees and feeding the family.

name: Maria Mercedes
description: Businesswoman María Mercedes S. Gutiérrez is 34 years old and married. María has 3 children of whom only one son is her care: he is aged 6 and in the third grade in primary school.  Her partner works as a security guard.  Their aim is to expand her business so that Maria's customers are satisfied and their dreams are to construct a house in order to leave a place to live to their children as it's very important to her husband that they all live together as a family.  Her husband has already taught the children many important lessons on how to be good men and women serving society.  Their wish is to improve their family's quality of life, as they have only managed so far with their business to secure stability through the payment of certain debts.  A further desire is to travel abroad as there she would be able to work and send back money to her sons to cover all the necessary expenses.    Maria's economic activity is to run a grocery store in which she offers good such as:  basic grains, sweets, natural juices and bread.  Her business is located in her home, and she has run her business for 6 years.  María began her business because she possessed some of her own funds and saw the opportunity to start-up a business in her house. As the place where her house is located was a new delivery point, she decided to start with a few products such as soft drinks, sweets and fire wood.  As a result she had few customers as the area wasn't very populated but with the little she sold she was able to increase her stock which would serve right up to the present day when as a result of this source of income she has been able to obtain all that's necessary for the maintenance of her family.  The loan is for wok capital designated for the purchase of more products for her grocery in order that she can quickly satisfy customer demand.  Translated from Spanish by Katy Long, Kiva Volunteer

name: Beatrice
description: Beatrice is 29 years old, married, and has three children who attend school. She lives in the town of Kinubi in the hoima region of Uganda. For the past two years, Beatrice has been working hard to manage her retail shop, which sells general household items.   To help expand her business, Beatrice is requesting a loan from BRAC Uganda for 2,000,000 Ugandan Shillings, which she will use to buy more household materials. This loan will help Beatrice to generate greater profits and pay her children's school fees. Beatrice hopes that in the future she will be able to complete her residential house.   Beatrice is a member of BRAC's Small Enterprise Program (SEP).  The program primarily serves small entrepreneurs like Beatrice who do not have enough collateral for commercial loans, but have businesses that have grown too large for microloans.

name: Leoncia's Group
description: Felicitas, Alejandra, and Leoncia are members of the Village Bank Huascahura.   Leoncia is married, 68 years old and has five children. Leoncia and her husband make handicrafts on the loom, such as tapestries, which they sell at the markets in the city of Ayacucho.   Felicitas is married, 36 years old and has three children. Felicitas sells meat, cheese and young animals from house to house. She buys the animals at the fairs and they are very beneficial to her.   Alejandra is married, 56 years old, and has seven children. Alejandra and her husband buy cattle from different towns around the region and sell them in the fair at Ayacucho.  Felicitas, Alejandra, and Leoncia need loans of 600 soles, 300 soles, and 600 soles, money which will be invested in the purchase of pigs, sheep, cows, thread and dye.   Felicitas, Alejandra, and Leoncia's dreams are to better their businesses and that their children finish their studies.

name: Gulomjan
description: Gulomjan is 29 and lives in the Spitamen region of Tajikistan. He is married with a son and a daughter and works as a press operator in a cotton mill. His parents live with his family. Gulomjan has decided to start his own livestock business on the side to improve his family's living conditions. He already  has cattle feed and 3,000 TJS in savings. He asked for a loan to cover the cost of two cows to help him get started raising cattle for resale. As he becomes more successful, he will expand the business.

name: Gemma
description: Gemma is a married woman with two children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Gemma is 41 years old and both of her children are in school.  Gemma has a fish vending business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 18,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more fish to sell to her customers.  Gemma has been in this business for 24 years. In the future, Gemma would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Patricia Albertina
description: For 5 years, Patricia has operated a pharmacy in her home. She is widely known for having fairly-priced items and customers favor her store amongst the other pharmacies for this reason. Her home and business are located in the central part of the city near the banks, so she is assured of good foot traffic.  With this loan of 20,000 gold cordobas (NIO), Patricia will purchase a variety of medicines to restock her inventory.  Patricia’s husband works as an engineer in an agricultural factory. Together, they continue to follow their ambition of improving their economic situation.

name: Esteban
description: Esteban lives and works in Ica, Peru.  Ica is located in the Sechura Desert about four hours south of Lima, the country's capital, and is hailed by Peruvians as "The Land of the Sun." It is known in Peru for its frequent earthquakes (an 8.4 in 2001 and 8.0 in 2007); its production of grapes, asparagus, and olives; and perhaps most notably, as the source of the Peruvian traditional national drink, Pisco. In this hot, arid climate one can find the client's home and business.  Esteban is a 28-year-old single man who works in the transportation sector.  He chose this line of work because he likes transporting people and the work is profitable.  Esteban is a determined, persevering, and responsible man who has tremendous drive to succeed each day.  He started his transportation business in 2007 and earns 290 PEN each week.  Esteban works approximately 12 hours a day, six days a week.    With this loan of 1000 PEN that he will receive thanks to Kiva, Esteban will invest in the general maintenance of his motorcycle taxi so that he can better serve his customers.  His dream is to have his own automobile so that he can earn more income and have a better quality of life.  His loan officer believes that he is an excellent client and will submit his payments on time.

name: Naranjargal
description: Naranjargal A. is 36 years old and lives with her husband and two children in Tuv province of central Mongolia. She lives together with her family in a ger, which is a traditional Mongolian nomadic housing tent, in her parents' yard. Her daughter, Uranchimeg, studies at high school in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia's capital city, while her son, Temuujin, attends a local kindergarten.   Naranjargal manages a shoe-making business in her town with help of her husband. She graduated Mongolian National University as a teacher. She started her business in 1997 and has built a sustainable operation. Her family's standard of living has improved greatly after operating the shoe-making business. Over the years of successful operation, her business has grown fast and she owns all the tools and equipment which are used in making shoes.  She and her husband work together, and plus she hired one worker. For the future, they plan to expand their business by increasing production capacity and to have their own shoe shop. She says "I work very hard to expand my business and also I teach my shoe-making skills to two handicapped children. In the future, I plan to establish a big shoe-making factory and open my own shop."    She is requesting a 3,000,000 MNT loan to purchase a large amount of materials used in making traditional shoes.

name: Paul
description: Paul is a hard-working, 47 year old man and a father of 3 children. All of his children attend school in Kasese Uganda. Paul is a retired teacher who now owns a school. He also has a transport business to earn a living and look after his family, given the fact that he is no longer employed. Paul dreams of giving his children and the community the best academic services, however, with day to day expenses he runs short of enough money. Paul is requesting a loan to pay school fees for his children as we approach the first term.

name: Elie
description: Elie is a 51-year-old married man living in Bourj A. Moulouk, Bint Jbeil, Southern Lebanon, with his wife and four children. Elie owns a shop where he has sold agriculturA. fertilizers and medicine since 2004.   Elie requested a loan from A. Majmoua in order to buy speciA. agriculturA. equipment important in his business. Elie has two years of micro-credit experience and he believes it was a successful experience. Elie had some financiA. problems at the beginning of his project, but he overcame them through micro-credits.   Elie’s customers are farmers and neighbors from all over the area. He hopes to expand in the future through selling large agriculturA. equipment.

name: Claudia Patricia
description: Claudia, 37, is single and has no children.  She’s studying Psychology and has trained in subjects dealing with drug dependency.  Due to the lack of employment opportunities and wishing to practice the profession she’s preparing for, she’s decided to start a rehab center for people with drug dependency problems and for victims of sexual abuse.  To do so, she has the support of a friend who is a professional psychologist who will guide her in the exercise and treatment she must have with her future clients.  Claudia hopes to get ahead by means of her enterprising vision and her high social sense and is motivated thus to request a loan to buy tables and chairs, cabinets and to make physical upgrades to the locale.  All of this is aimed at being able to treat her patients in a humane, comfortable and safe way that will make it possible for her to carry out activities like family conferences, therapy and companionship for these people who are in danger of being socially excluded.  With this, Claudia hopes to make progress and to acquire resources to subsist but what motivates her the most is knowing that she’ll be able to reach her dream of helping people that need special attention, love and companionship and to contribute to improving her patients’ and their families’ quality of life.

name: Deyanira
description: A loan of 15,900 pesos allows Deyanira to purchase provisions such as half a sack of rice, half a sack of sugar, a tin of oil, milk, eggs, and soft drinks for her little grocery store. Deyanira lost her job eighteen months ago, and she used her unemployment benefits to open this store, which enables her to help her husband support their household. He works at a book store. They have three children, who are seventeen, fourteen, and eleven, and all three attend the neighborhood public school.  Deyanira has come to understand that if she wants to maintain a steady customer base, she needs to always keep her business well-stocked with fresh groceries. That is why she has requested this loan. Both her and her husband want the business to do well and generate enough income for them to help their children go to college.

name: G.s Villa Nueva#2 Group
description: Luis Alfredo is 54 years old, he lives with is housemate, he is the father of 2 children, he works raising cattle, coffee production, agriculture and also works in milk production and grazing steers. He has more than 30 years experience working in this type of economic activity.  Luis Alfredo is requesting a loan to buy a solar power plant as he doesn't have electric power service and with this investment he hopes to reach his dreams of having electricity in his home and improving his income to cover family expenses and financial commitments.  Luis Alfredo's dream is to improve his family's living conditions and having financial stability in the future for his family, with the support he receives from the loan which will contribute to achieving his dreams.  Nilbia has raised cattle for many years. Leyda works as a teacher and also has a small farm. Israel works in coffee production. Anelda works raising cattle and growing coffee.  Trojes, Honduras - July 2014

name: Valerie
description: Valerie is 24 and a very industrious, honest, and hardworking mother from the Nkubu area of Kenya, near the famous Mount Kenya. She has been farming and over the years, she has gathered much experience and is considered among the best farmers in her village. She has been practicing mixed farming. Her primary sources of income have been milk, eggs, maize, crops, and some small business ventures that help him make ends meet.Although she makes profits from farming, she is not comfortable and has always wanted to increase her income by buying seeds so that she can plant them and sell them after harvesting. That is why she is seeking this loan to buy seeds. Kenya's Nkubu area, one of the country's populated regions, has a high demand for food. Accessing funds has been a challenge for Valerie, but she now feels farmers like her turn their farming dreams into reality through training and loan financing. Valerie has many dreams in her life but, as expected, her family is the principal one: she wants to give them a good quality of life, to pay for her children's education and, someday, buy a house so that they can all live safely and comfortably. You can help Valerie to fulfill all of these goals with a loan that will get her a lot closer to achieving them.

name: Harriet
description: This borrower lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is married with four children and all attend school. She is also looking after additional family members. She and her husband live in her own house with no access to electricity and piped water. Her major monthly expenses include rent.  She has been selling dry fish at the market for the last ten years, working seven days a week. She also does some farming and sells the farm produce in order to earn more income. Protecting her merchandise from thieves is one of the challenges that she faces. Her dream is to upgrade from retail to wholesale.  She joined MCDT because of its timely loans. She has requested a loan of UGX 700,000 from MCDT SACCO to buy more fish to sell.

name: Djobo
description: In 2008, this gentleman got started in the commerce of rice.  He has a large customer base.  Many restaurant owners come to him to stock up.  The demand over these last few days is fairly strong due to the year-end holidays.  He wants to resupply himself to respond to the demands of his customers.  For these reasons, he's requesting from WAGES his first loan to buy 30 sacks of rice and to start selling beverages with 30 boxes of drinks and various other items. Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Alejandra
description: As a widowed parent of four children, Alejandra works hard to support her family.  She has a restaurant business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from food vending. Alejandra is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to buy additional ingredients like meat, fish, vegetables, etc for her restaurant business.  Alejandra has been sustaining her business activities through her past 20 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Alimaa
description: Alimaa J. is 59 years old and lives with her family in a ger- a traditional Mongolian nomadic dwelling- in Huvsgul province, Mongolia. She is married to Dorjjav, who helps in her business, and she has a 18 year old son. Her son, Damdindorj, currently studies at a Mongolian National University. Alimaa operates a vegetable growing business in town. She started to plant a variety of vegetables on her own 0.5 hectare field in 2000. Her farming business experienced tragedy when she lost all her harvest in a flood. Today she has gained significant experience as a farmer. She also makes and sells a variety of handicraft items for foreigners, to supplement her earnings selling vegetables.   She is a hard-working and very energetic person. She has used her earnings to pay her children's tuition fees as well as to improve her family's quality of life. Alimaa is requesting a loan of 1,000,000 MNT. The loan she is requesting will be used to reap a harvest and to purchase more supplies and materials for her handicraft business.

name: Analyn
description: Analyn B. is a 31-year-old married woman. She has an 8-year-old child who goes to school. Analyn dreams for her child to finish college someday and find a decent job.  Analyn is engaged in rice farming. She earns approximately 5000 PHP a month. Analyn works hard to increase her harvest and earn better. She currently needs fertilizers for her farm. She also needs to pay the laborers she hired to help with the tilling.  Analyn requests a loan of 17000 PHP to be used for her farm needs. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the loan to improve her business.

name: Nini Johanna
description: Nini, 21, is a young woman living with her spouse in the southwest part of the city where she has a small store she got from her parents four years ago for her to manage that sells snacks, foodstuffs, groceries and soft-drinks.  She’s gradually been investing in the business because she learned from her parents while still very young how to make it grow.  Her sales from 7 in the morning until 9 at night are cash based.  She makes her purchases from suppliers downtown that offer competitive prices.  Her main customers are neighbors and people who live around her.  Her goal for later on is to have a roomier space to provide more excellent customer service and to continue with a professional career to complete making home improvements.  Nini says: “There are obstacles but they aren’t impossible to overcome especially if the business is located on the main street.”  She’s currently applying for a Kiva loan, her first financing from Fundación Mario Santo Domingo to buy rice in quantity, oil by the five-gallon container, soft-drinks and meat products, among other basic staples that rotate quickly and must be readily on-hand for her customers thus making her Kiva loan successful.

name: Shadrack
description: Shadrack, a married father of four, describes himself as visionary. Shadrack has been operating a carpentry business where he makes furniture for 18 years. His enterprise is located in a semi-urban area, and his primary customers are locals. He describes his biggest challenge as insufficient working capital.   His previous loan repaid, Shadrack has requested his second loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank for Kes 100,000 to buy more carpentry materials. His business goal is to have more business outlets within five years. He hopes that in the future, he will be successful.

name: Adela
description: Adela is a member of the El Roble Communal Bank.  She is 39 years old, married and the mother of two sons.  She became a member of FINCA Perú two years ago and she has a small store where she sells groceries.  The lesson that Adela has learned most during her time as a member of  FINCA Perú is to be punctual and to attend all the meetings of her Communal Bank.  Her dream for the future is to have properties that she can rent.  She will invest the loan she is requesting in the purchase of beverages and groceries to sell in her small store like rice, sugar, oil, milk, juices, and sodas.

name: Bertha
description: Bertha is a 34 year old mother who lives with her husband and children in Hualtaco, Tambogrande district.  It is an agricultural area belonging to Piura province located in Piura region.  It is over three hours from the city of Chiclayo, Lambayeque region capital.  She sells catalogue cosmetics.  She has a group of customers who buy regularly from her.  The more orders she places the more points she earns from the firm that supplies the products and thus more profits.  Because of this Bertha works hard to acquire more and more customers each time.  Bertha wants to have stable capital with which to acquire more products and have fixed stock of cosmetics on hand so that her customers can get what they want quickly and not have to wait until the end of the month which is when her orders are filled.  She is, therefore, asking Edpyme Alternativa for a 1000 new sol loan that will help her reach her goal.  Bertha is a hard working woman who likes to stay active.  In the area where she lives she is quite well known and held in high esteem by her neighbors.

name: Pov
description: Pov, 43, is widowed with no kid. Her family lives in a house with a thatched roof house in the Sa Ang Village of Kandal province and the main source of the family’s income is selling rice and snacks. Pov can earn about US  $5 per day to meet the family’s needs.   This is the second microloan for Pov with VisionFund. She fully repaid the past loan which has helped her better support her current business. Now she is asking for another loan to buy a motorbike for her family’s commuting.  She hopes to have a decent motorbike for her family to commute to work so as to reduce money on a motor-taxi’s fee.

name: Paola Andrea
description: Paola is an enterprising woman, age 38.  She is the mother of one child, age 1, and lives with her partner in a common-law relationship.  During her working life, she has worked in various seamstress workshops as a machine operator, so she has experience and knowledge in managing this type of business.  However, being tired of working in other workshops and having a desire to spend more time with her son, she decided to set up her own sewing workshop.  Because of this, she wants to ask for a loan which will be invested in the purchase of a serger sewing machine, an interlock sewing machine, and sewing supplies such as fabric and thread.  This will allow her to put her project into action; she hopes to make a big impact on the sector in this way, in order to generate a favorable profit and so make her dream of being well-positioned in market come true.  With her ambition and drive, she sees herself offering jobs to others in the mid-range future, always working alongside Corporación Interactuar.

name: Leonora
description: Leonora L. is a married woman who lives in Sitio Cagay, Brgy. Buenavista, Escalante City, Negros Occidental. She earns her living by selling fish. Her husband, Danilo, age 44, works as a fisherman and also helps with his wife's business. They have seven children who are 4 to 21 years old.   Leonora joined NWTF-Project Dungganon in 1999 because she wanted something better for her family. With the help of her past 14 loans from NWTF-Project Dungganon, and by the sweat of her brow, Leonora has been incrementally lifting her family out of poverty. Her previous loan of 19,500 Philippine pesos (PHP) helped her earn a monthly profit of PHP 8,000, improving her family's standard of living. This time, for her 15th loan, she is borrowing PHP 19,500, which she intends to use as additional capital for her fishing vending business and for fishing materials so that she can continue to save up for future home repairs. Leonora L. is a Dungganon woman who is following an honorable path toward the achievement of her dreams.   About NWTF: In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress from earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem  that is bestowed on a member of a community who has earned respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work. Help NWTF continue its mission to help the poorest in the Philippines by clicking the link to the NWTF Kiva lending team on Kiva.org to join our team.

name: Ana
description: From a young age, Ana learned how to cook and her good seasoning has allowed her to maintain a restaurant business since 1994, which was opened on this day. When she started, she only sold soup (in Colombia, food with a broth base with added vegetables and meat, served with rice primarily at lunchtime). Now, she offers breakfast, lunch, liquor, and beer. Her main customers are people who live in the area and want to have her delicious meals once in awhile for fun and relaxation.  She makes her sales in cash so she has a good cash flow. She makes her purchases in the central part of the city using cash. Currently, she is applying for a Kiva loan, which is her first with Fundación Mario Santo Domingo. With the loan, she will buy cases of beer. This loan will help her sales. She averages around 45 cases weekly. Her return on this investment will be quick and she will reinvest it to make better profits.Ana, 46, is a mother of a 23-year-old son and three daughters, aged 22, 20, and 18. Her long-term goal is to travel with her family and her business goal is to grow it and improve her stock.

name: Lideres De Santa Rosa Group
description: The communal banking group "Leaders of Santa Rosa" is made up of 10 entrepreneurial members. Rosa is one, and she is 59 years old. She is separated with two grown children.  She works selling toys and perfume.  She has been working in this field for the past ten years. Thanks to her efforts things are going well and she has been able to improve her quality of life.  She is requesting a loan in order to purchase dolls, perfume and cologne.  The group "Leaders of Santa Rosa" thanks all the Kiva lenders for making such loans possible.  Rosa is the first woman on the left side in the picture, and she is wearing a light blue jacket.

name: Edah
description: Edah is 32 years old and the mother of  a child aged 15. She sells beverages such as mineral water, soft drinks, etc. She can earn US$ 15 per day. Her husband, B., is a laborer who only earns a small income. Edah has to work hard to help her husband cover their family's needs. She is requesting a loan of US$ 125 to buy more goods for her stall and she's willing to repay this loan within a period of 12 months.

name: Marvin
description: Marvin is a very enterprising man, maintaining the gardens in his community and doing all types of ornamental work outside homes and institutions.  In order to provide better service, he needs up to date tools that will help him do the work in less time.  In this way he can increase his number of customers and provide better quality service.  He needs a million (¢1,000,000), colones, with which he will buy a weed whacker and a trimmer.  He says that he is happy with the loan.

name: Lucy
description: I am a single parent, mother of 4. I sell groceries to earn a living for myself and my children. The loan will help me diversify and expand the business so as to be able to pay school fees for my children.

name: Kanini
description: A 59-year-old businesswoman, Kaninishe is a widow with six grown children.  For the past 10 years she has been running a hair beauty shop as her primary business and a retail shop as a secondary business, earning a monthly income of KES 13,800 which she uses to meet family needs.  An existing KADET customer introduced  Kaninishe to KADET, and she is now applying for her first loan with which she will buy beauty products such as shampoo and a blow-dryer, and add a stock of sugar, rice, maize meal to her shop.  With the anticipated additional profits arising from the loan, she will educate her children to university level.  Kaninishe's hope is to purchase  land and build rental houses to generate additional income.

name: Mercy
description: Mercy is a single woman who lives in a rental house that has no electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and rent.  For three years, Mercy has operated a beauty salon. She faces a major challenge of seasonality in her business. Mercy dreams of establishing a well-furnished beauty salon business in the future. Mercy plans to use this 40,000 KES loan to purchase bundles of cosmetics and hair weaves. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Svetlana
description: Svetlana is married with one adult son. She runs a small farm growing vegetables in greenhouses. Svetlana has been in this business 11 years. Her experience helps her to have good crops and sell the produce at a good price. Svetlana is a hardworking and enthusiastic person. She would like to develop her business further.  Svetlana is asking for a loan of 12,000 UAH. She is going to purchase fertilizers, seeds, and film (plastic) for three greenhouses.

name: Joseph
description: Joseph is 52 years old. He is divorced from his wife. He supports his four children, who are all in school. He is a farmer, and has been in the business for the past five years. He gets a monthly income of 10,000 KES from his business.  This is his second loan from KADET LTD.  He has paid his previous loan well and in good time.  He will use the loan amount to pay school fees for his children.  He hopes to educate his his children to the highest levels.

name: Elvisa
description: Elvisa is a married woman with three children. She is 46 years old and one of her children is currently in school. Elvisa is a very hard-working entrepreneur. She has a fish vending business in the Philippines and has been in this business for five years.  Elvisa requested a PHP 6,000 loan through NWTF to buy a variety of fish to sell. In the future, she would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Robert
description: Robert is 41 years old and lives in the town of Nakaloke in the Mbale region of Uganda. He is married and has three children with two of them currently in school.   For the past 10 years, Robert has been working hard to manage his charcoal business.   To help expand his business, Robert has requested a loan of  Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy sacks of charcoal and will help Robert to generate and earn greater profits.   Robert hopes that in the future he will be able to have increased stock.

name: Kari
description: Sra. Kari is a member of the Communal Bank “Mujeres Forjadoras” (Forging Women) in the District of Yarinacocha, Department of Ucayli.  She is 28 years old and married.  Kari provides manicure and pedicure services from her home.  She has been in business for two years and experiences great demand, especially on the weekends.    With her new loan of 2400 PEN, she will buy ten nail polishes in different colors, one bottle of nail hardener, one foot crème, one neutralizer, six towels, one nail dryer, and one aromatherapy spray.    Since she does not have children, she is able to devote herself to her work without any problems.  Her husband works as a teacher.  Sra. Kari says that her work also serves as a distraction and a means of helping her husband with some of the household expenses.  She is happy because the three years she has been with Manuela Ramos have enabled her to buy the things she needs for her business.

name: Stheyse Jhanneth
description: Stheyse is grateful to the Kiva lenders and thanks to their help she has been able to buy supplies for her business, such as pots, plastic containers, spoons, bags, chairs, and other things that will allow her to provide better service to her customers and improve her business and income in this way.  She will continue striving to get her two month old son ahead and work to make her dream a reality, “To have home of her own and provide a dignified life to her son.”

name: Carlaine Joseph
description: Carlaine  is 38 years old. She is married and the mother of four children. She runs a little grocery store. Thanks to this business she is able to earn income to care for her family. She is asking for a loan to expand her stock of spaghetti.

name: Felicidad's Group
description: Felicidad A. is from the village of Cabisera 5. She is 52 years old. Felicidad is the group leader of a six-member group loan offered by ASKI. While each member of the group receives an individual loan, they are all collectively responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults. The official name of this borrowing group is Felicidad A..  Felicidad is married and has two adult-aged children. To make a living, Felicidad owns and operates a general store, selling a variety of different products in the local community. Felicidad has been engaged in her business for over four years and earns approximately $65 a month from this activity.  In 2007, Felicidad joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation by engaging in business activities. Felicidad has successfully repaid a previous loan from ASKI. This previous loan was used to purchase additional products to sell. Felicidad is requesting a new loan of 25,000 PHP which again will be used to purchase additional products. This will be her 7th loan from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated to further improve her business.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful micro-finance institutions in the Philippines. It has 25 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Socorro Isabel
description: Socorro is the mother of an eighteen year old daughter who she loves very much. Socorro lives in the city of Camana, a city known for its warm climate and the generosity of its people, as well as for its agriculture, principally its rice crops. It is also known for its delicious shrimp stew, a traditional meal in the city. In her free time, Socorro enjoys watching movies as well as eating her favorite meal, which is the delicious “Fried Fish.”  Socorro sells clothing on Sundays in the open market in her neighborhood. She also sells floor wax. She works for around eight hours a day, but she also works as a cook in a house. She is very hardworking. She believes her business is doing well because she puts a lot of effort into it and enjoys her work.  Socorro is very grateful for the Kiva lenders since thanks to the help they have provided her she will be able to purchase more merchandise for her businesses, both clothing and wax. She will be able to offer a variety of products for sale and increase her profits. This way she will keep working and be able to get ahead each day and be able to achieve her greatest dream: “Give her daughter a profession.”

name: Ly's Group
description: Ly is a 49-year-old mother of four children and earns a living through farming rice. To supplement her income, she also sells snacks. She has been in this business for 31 years and the current business earns her about 25,000 KHR per day to feed the family.   Ly is a first cycled client with VisionFund. She is now leading her group to apply for a loan. As the leader, she is going to use her portion to buy rice seeds for her farmland.   She hopes to increase her income through the current business to improve her family's living standards.
town: Kampong Cham province, Kang Meas District

name: Rebecca
description: Rebecca lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is single with seven children (three attend school). She takes care of additional family members. She lives in a rented house with access to electricity, but she does not have access to piped water. Her major monthly expenses include rent and school fees.   Rebecca has been selling sugarcane retail at the market for ten years, working six days a week. Her challenges include high transport costs and the seasonality of sugarcane. She joined Micro Credit for Development and Transformation SACCO (MCDT SACCO) because she did not have enough capital. She has requested a loan from MCDT to buy bundles of sugarcane. Her dream is to buy a plot of land.

name: Run
description: Mrs. Run is 40 years old and a resident of Kompong Cham province, where she earns a living by planting a few crops on her own land. On average, she earns a profit of around $1.50 a day to support her family’s needs. Mrs. Run is married with six children; five of them have already started new families and the last one is married. Her husband, Mr. Soun, also works on the farm. Mrs. Run has applied for a loan from Kiva’s partner, HKL, in order to rent some of the neighbor’s land to enlarge her crop plantation and to buy insecticides, fertilizers, and potato seeds for planting. Mrs. Run and her husband appear in the photo.

name: Samuel
description: Samuel, 24, is a single farmer who was born in Santa Cruz; he is Isaac’s son.    For lack of economic resources he had to drop out of school because he didn’t have support from his parents.  He decided to go into farming and he works alongside his brother, Limber.  They plant corn, peanuts and manioc.  They also extract lumber to be used in carpentry and they make charcoal during seasons that planting is impossible.  But their main focus is on agriculture.  The money from the loan will be used to buy seed for their crops.  The crops are then sold in El Torno’s market.  They live 10 kilometers east of Santa Rita.  They own and live in their house on their own piece of property.

name: Raúl Enrique
description: Raúl Enrique P. L. lives in the town of Tonacatepeque, which is in the town of San Salvador.  He lives with his wife and their four children.  The P. household is never quiet because their youngest child is only 3 months old.    Raúl has a pizzeria in his home that he manages with his wife.  Having four children is not easy.  For this reason, Raul is requesting a loan to reinvest into his business so that it can continue to grow.  This will enable him to provide a better life for his family and his newborn son. Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Eric
description: Eric M. is thirty-three years old and married with two children. He lives with his wife and the children. Currently one child is in school and the other is still breastfeeding. Eric is a local manufacturer of soap. He combines materials like palm oil, soda powder, cocoa pods and coconut oil to make his soap. He is not able to produce in large quantities for lack of funds. He wants to take advantage of the loan facility to buy more raw materials and processing equipment to scale up production. He hopes to raise his income to support his children's education. He belongs to the village bank called Nkwagyedom, which means 'savior of the many'.

name: Lelis Teresilda
description: The 'San Pedro De Pueblo Nuevo' community bank meets once every two weeks in Pueblo Nuevo parish, in Santa Ana canton.  The locals are decent people who earn a living by farming and raising livestock.  The people are friendly and the countryside is beautiful.  This is where Lelis lives.  Lelis is 47 years old, lives with her partner, and has three children from her relationship.  Two of her children are already adults but her youngest [daughter] is 15 years old, attends school, and still lives with her parents.  Lelis' husband is a farmer.  Lelis has a small grocery store in her home which has been a great help to her as her husband doesn't earn a lot of money from his farm work and sometimes only grows enough to feed the farmyard animals that they keep.  In addition to basic food products, Lelis also sells drinks, iced treats, fruit, vegetables and other miscellaneous items in her store.  She works every day but makes most of her sales on the weekend as this is when people come from the fields to stock up with food to eat during the week.  Lelis has been in her business for more than 12 years and it allows her to cover her household expenses.  Lelis will use this loan to buy basic food products so that she can further stock her store.  She has been a member of her community bank for four loan cycles and likes it because of the loans which have allowed her to improve her store.  Lelis' dream is to continue expanding her business.

name: Emprendedoras De Buena Vista Group
description: This “Bella Vista” group is from the city of Encarnación; it arose thanks to contact made by one of the members with the Fundación.  It’s in its 13th cycle and has been operating with the Fundación since 2011.  One of the group members is Remigia.  She’s single and has four children.  She’s been selling fruit and vegetables for several years.  Remigia relates that she asked for financing to buy fruit and vegetables to sell to her customers.  She’s very grateful for the opportunity she’s getting because the loan will be of great help for her.

name: Chim
description: Mr. Chim C. is a local farmer who grows a few vegetables to earn a living. He is 44 years old and has established a small family home with other family members. His wife works on the field with him. They are good parents who have tried to earn money to feed their four children since they were young. One of their children is now married and the other three are single. The approaching rainy season is the time Chim C. would normally grow his crops, but he does not have enough supplies to use on his farm. For this reason, Chim C. is applying for a $250 loan to help him buy supplies to plant vegetable crops.

name: Kototala Group
description: The KOTOTALA group is made up of married women who are 45 years old on average, and have 4 children each. They all live in traditional families in the village of Kofra Bamana, in the Dioïla prefecture, in the Koulikoro region (the second largest administrative region in the Republic of Mali). They met through family, neighbours and friends. They work in food preparation, the sale of cereals, pancakes and baskets. The KOTOTALA group women are on their fifth loan.   In order to satisfy their large customer demand, they are seeking a loan from Soro Yiriwaso.  One of the group's members, FANTA, the second from the right, is illiterate, and currently sells pancakes for a living. She aims to purchase oil and baking flour from the wholesalers in Massigui.  She sells her goods at retail at the market, for cash sales and to a mixed customer base. She aims to generate an average monthly profit of 40,000 FCFA, which will be reinvested in the business.

name: Lili Sundari
