description: Good day lenders! Now it’s time for you to meet one of KPP UMKM client’s, Lili Sundari. Lili Sundari is 32 years old and married. She lives with her husband and her child. She has one daughter. She sells clothes and the method of payment is gradually or credit for three years. Her husband has been an employee in a shoe factory for five years. They pull together to increase their income.  Lili Sundari has asked for a loan from KPP-UMKM Syariah for 4,000,000 IDR. This loan will be used to buy and build a bathroom, septic tank, and a toilet at their home to improve access to water and sanitation for their family. She would like to have access to safe and easy sanitation for her family.   Her family income is still not enough to build sanitation by cash, but they are able to repay loans received by installment. She and her family want to live a healthy life with healthy water and sanitation. She is very grateful for the opportunity and wants to thank to all of the lenders.

name: Salma
description: Salma is a 32-year-old married woman, living in the area of Lahore, Pakistan.   Her husband has owned an enterprise of stitching and selling embroidery by machine in his nearby town for many years. He has been recruiting skilled people for embroidery work for daily wages; he also brings some material to home for Salma, because she helps him with the embroidery work. He is very expert in his profession; he is especially famous for bridal dresses. People like his art, and appreciate him for his efforts.   He wants to cope with the demand for bridal dresses; that is why he wants to buy stock of thread, fancy cloths, sequins, and pearls in various colors.  Salma requires some capital to buy desired inventory for her husband, but she does not have a sufficient amount.   So that's why she made a humble request to BRAC Pakistan for a loan. After getting this loan, her husband would be able to buy a stock of thread, fancy cloths, sequins, and pearls in various colors.  Salma is very glad and thankful to BRAC Pakistan and Kiva.

name: Rosemarie
description: Rosemarie is 45 years old, married, and has four children, one of whom is in school. Rosemarie is in the agricultural business of raising pigs in the Philippines.  She has requested a PHP 19,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy feed and other supplies to raise her pigs. Rosemarie has been raising pigs for seven years now, and has borrowed 13 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it. In the future, Rosemarie would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: By His Grace Rubiri Group
description: By his grace Rubiri group is a new group located in Rubiri -nyamityobora, Mbarara district. It’s comprised of  women who have changed their homes through cooperation and have managed to improve their standard of living  via working together as a group and these people believe in praying to bless whatever they are doing.   The group members have been in business for over 11 years and all of them are in retail business purposely to educate their children looking after their families economically.  They applied for a group loan from UGAFODE Microfinance Ltd to boost their businesses.  Their prime target is to expand their shops and get enough money to cater for their families and get income to expand their business.  Also to place their children in better schools in the country. But they are limited by capital and funds to enable them achieve their dreams and compete with other people in the area who have similar business. Lukia will use her loan specifically to buy groceries for sale. This will increase her sales and profit.

name: Mammad
description: Mammad, 42, is married and has three children. He is an internally displaced person (IDP) who lives in the Bilasuvar IDP Settlement with his family.   Mammad is a farmer and has grown seasonal fruits and vegetables for the last fifteen years. He grows pears, apples, peaches, plums, pomegranates, cucumbers, tomatoes, carrots, and potatoes. He chose to grow fruits and vegetables because it is profitable and there is a high demand for produce.  Over the years, Mammad has gained enough skills and experience to run his business.   People in Azerbaijan eat fresh vegetables everyday and consider them to be healthy. Vegetables are featured in many national dishes, such as pilau and dolma. Fresh fruits are served on every table in Azerbaijan and are also used to make fresh punch.    Mammad usually sells his crops in the central bazaar. His monthly income is 70 AZN. Mammad wants to expand his business and grow more fruits and vegetables as his produce is in high demand. For this reason, he is requesting a 1000 AZN to buy new garden tools, seeds, and fertilizer.

name: Vergenia
description: Vergenia N. is from the village of Villa Verde, Balulang Cagayan De Oro City. She is 47 years old. Vergenia is married and has 7 adult-aged children. To make a living, Vergenia owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) retail store. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling both food and daily-use products in the local community. Vergenia has been engaged in her business for over 3 years and earns approximately 12,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2010, Vergenia joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Vergenia is requesting a loan of 5000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Vergenia from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.
town: Villa Verde, Balulang, Cagayan De Oro, Misamis Ori

name: Miguel Ángel
description: Miguel is 60 years old and is one of those people who is worthy of admiration and respect, who teach that your attitude and desire to progress is the most important thing in life.  Despite being disabled after losing his right hand, this man continues to fight for those most important to him: his family.  For 25 years he has worked as a traveling salesman in order to make a living for himself and his family.  Every day he goes out to the streets with his cart, where he sells mangos and avocados.  In this way, Miguel has managed to provide a better life for his family.  Today he is asking for this loan so that he can invest in an umbrella (for his cart) and an assortment of fruits in order to increase his level of sales and not have his business harmed by the constant rains.

name: Sofia Del Rosario
description: In the beautiful city of Bahía de Caraquez, known for its beautiful beaches, for its rich and varied cuisine and for the warmth of its people, the communal bank Sociedad de Bahía meets twice a month.  We meet here Sofía, who is 50 years old. She is single and lives at home with her parents. She has been with the communal bank for five years and she likes it because the loans are a big help and the interest is very low.  Our friend works as as public employee, but she also sells clothing, shoes, handbags and costume jewelry. She tells us that she sells her items at her workplace and in her free time and at night when she has time she drops off items on credit and collects payment twice a month, buying her merchandise in Guayaquil when she needs to. She is able to help her parents who are elderly.   This loan will be used to buy clothing, shoes, handbags and costume jewelry among other items.  Her goals are to get ahead and to buy a car for her traveling sales work.

name: Ngang Eunice
description: Ngang Eunice is married with 2 children. She lives in Mankon, North West Region, Cameroon. The family shares 2 rooms. She, as many other people, has faced major challenges in her life, especially when her parents and brothers died. She has also suffered from the hands of early marriage. She got pregnant at a stage when she did not expect and dropped out of school.   With her first loan, Ngang Eunice expanded her business of sewing uniforms for school children, particularly those at the primary level. She was so happy with the fact that she was able to provide the school needs to her children, while many people around her find it difficult to do so. Given a loan, she plans to buy more fabric and produce more uniforms for school children that she will take to far-off villages. She will be able to sell there since very few persons go so far to do this particular business. Ngang Eunice hopes the business will succeed with the experiences she has in doing this for so many years and the location of her business site in the central town. Also, she is able to withstand the stress of traveling to far-off villages.  She will put the proceeds from this loan toward catering for her children's needs. She will ensure that her health and that of her children is taken care of by paying for their education.   She prefers loans from GHAPE because of the training GHAPE gives and the ease of obtaining and paying back.  About GHAPE The Grounded and Holistic Approach to People's Empowerment (GHAPE) is a non-profit NGO based in Bamenda, Cameroon. GHAPE works towards the empowerment of the poor and poverty alleviation through a highly multi-faceted approach.  Every client is trained in business management, basic health, life skills, financial management, profits and losses, and family values. Clients are also required to contribute a small amount into a personal savings account; most clients save much more than the minimum requirement. GHAPE instils a sense of family and community within its clients and staff and has developed a strong bond of trust between the organization and its clients.

name: Rebecca
description: Rebecca is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a business selling vegetables and spices in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF to buy additional vegetables and spices to sell.  Rebecca has been in this business for three years, and she earns additional income from a general store.  Rebecca has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams of saving money to expand her business in the future.

name: Paula
description: Paula is a 34-year-old married woman with 3 children. She has a small taxi business to earn an income. She has 2 years with this business.   Paula needs a loan to buy a new taxi sign indicator, new seat covers, air-con re-fill, and petrol. She will use her profits to pay for her family's weekly expenses. Paula joined SPBD in 2012 to gain access to financial services.

name: Rosecery
description: Rosecery is 28 years old, married with one child who is in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.Rosecery has a shellfish business in the Philippines. Rosecery requested a PHP 17,500 loan amount through NWTF in order to buy more shellfish to sell to customers.Rosecery has been in this business for three years. In the future, Rosecery would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Daisy
description: Daisy is a 35-year-old single mother of one child living in Kasese, Uganda. She has been a policewoman for twenty years, and she is proud to be part of keeping the peace and law enforcement. Her personal goals are educating her child and building a permanent house. Daisy wants this loan to pay school fees for her child.

name: Eufenia
description: Eufenia is 59 years old and married, with six children. She earns a living by farming rice in the Philippines. Eufenia has been farming rice for two years and also earns additional income from food vending.  Eufenia is borrowing 12,000 PHP through NWTF to buy fertilzer and other farm supplies. She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Maria Rina
description: Sra. Maria, 46, is married and the mother of two daughters, 10- and 6-years old, respectively.  She operates a business buying and selling paintings, posters, videos, etc.  She sells her merchandise in various markets around the city of El Alto.  This loan is Sra. Maria's second from the bank and she will use it to buy wholesale stocks of the merchandise she sells.  The investment will increase her income because she can buy larger quantities of merchandise from a wholesaler at a discount and better compete with other similar businesses.  Sra. Maria says that she is grateful for the opportunity that this form of lending delivers.

name: Rolly
description: In an effort to increase his sales, Rolly is seeking the opportunity to access a loan of Php 7,000 so that he can buy hardwoods to produce charcoal for sale. This will enable him to offer a greater amount of charcoal and increase his sales. He hopes to attract more customers to his business and provide them with better service. By earning more income, his family will enjoy a better quality of life. He will also be able to continue to save for the better future of his five children.

name: Unidas Group
description: Unidas is in its 15th cycle of the Women's Committee program, where they all work and help each other get ahead. They are participating in a study to eliminate poverty, and 5 members are under the poverty line, with very low income.   One of the members is Carmen. She has always had to work and strive to get ahead to give her family what they need. She sells all types of clothing and this is how she has the means to help her family. Her goal is to keep working hard so that little by little her business will get better.   She is asking for this loan to buy winter clothing, sine cold weather is coming and this way she can have more clothing to offer her customers.

name: Cristy
description: Cristy is 23 years old and single. She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a loan of 12,000 Philippine pesos (PHP) through NWTF to buy items to sell such as shampoo and groceries.  Cristy has previously taken out and repaid 7 loans from NWTF. She has been running the general store for 1 year and also earns income from buying and selling charcoal.  Cristy aspires to save money to expand her business.

name: Chansey's Group
description: Aged 28 years old, Chansey is a married mother of two children living in a rural village of the Kror Kor district of Pursat province. Rice farming is the main source of family’s income and her husband supplements family income by working as a laborer in the local area. They have been in this rice farming business for six years and she is able to earn about KHR 10,000 per day and can manage to save about KHR 4,000 each day after daily expenses.  Chansey has been with VisionFund for three cycles and completely paid back the loans while the other group member has been with VisionFund for one cycle. The past loans have helped Chansey to have sufficient food for her family. Now she is leading the group of two to apply for a loan. Chansey is going to use her portion to buy fertilizers for her farmland and use a portion of it to pay for laborers. She hopes this loan will enable her to earn a good living.

name: Hala
description: Hala is 29 years old, married and has three children. She runs a small grocery store in Al-Jalazoon camp in Ramallah city. Hala chose to take out a loan from ACAD to buy a new refrigerator for her grocery store since her sales went up. Hala started her business when she was 24 years old.The grocery store is the only source of income for Hala and her family. She says that the extra income from this loan will help her improve her living status. Hala says that the challenge for her business is the difficulty in getting the goods from the suppliers. In the future, Hala would like to expand her grocery store into a small supermarket. She thanks you for your support.

name: Dúo Luchadoras De Los Chajones Group
description: DUO CHAJONES   Gloria Florencia Chajon is the leader of the group and tells us that she is requesting this loan to invest in her little store of everyday foodstuffs that she has had in her house for three years.  She needs to invest because her store is still small and is lacking in many products.  In addition, the area that her store is located is very good because things sell well, but she doesn't have sufficient capital to buy enough stock.  Her store benefits the community because they don't have to travel every day to make purchases.  She wants to sell fruits and vegetables, which is what people ask for the most.    Because of this, she is requesting this loan to invest again in her store since she needs to buy more foodstuffs and thus increase her earnings and continue helping her husband.

name: Sayora
description: Sayora, age 46, is a seamstress.  She lives in the city of Isfara with her husband, her two sons, her daughter and daughter-in-law.  Her husband works in construction and house repair.  Sayora herself has been involved in sewing for the past three years.  She sews curtains and drapes of different designs and takes her business very seriously.  Each one of her orders is custom-fit and she is happy with the results of her work.  Sayora's only daughter helps her to run the business.  She now wants to expand her activity and to do so, she is taking a loan.  She would like to buy an additional sewing machine in order to increase the quantity of curtains and drapes that she produces.  She really needs this loan.

name: Olivia
description: Olivia is requesting a loan of $1,000 to improve her business. She has a place to sew where many people come every day. She will buy some additional supplies such as sewing machine needles and thread. She has been involved in business activities since 2010. She feels comfortable running her business because she can earn money every day. Running a business has made Olivia independent because she can be responsible for herself, and she can also help her family. She hopes to run a bigger business in the future.

name: Paubla Esperanza
description: Paubla Esperanza is 64 years old. She prepares and sells food. Paubla is a one of many strong, entrepreneurial women in our country. She has always liked working and improving her life in a humble way. For the past 5 years she has dedicated herself to this business.   When she started it, she didn't have enough resources to get ahead, but with some help through financing she acquired her own business where she sells food outside her home every night. She is now requesting a loan for working capital: the purchase of staple grains, chicken, and fruit, among other things. She hopes to one day have her own house.  Translated from Spanish by Vivian Lu, Kiva Volunteer

name: Acelia
description: Acelia, age 44, is the mother of three children who regularly attend school.  She resells food products.  She is requesting a loan to develop her activity and increase her stock.

name: Geisel Maria
description: Geisel is an inhabitant of the city of León and is a single mother. She has two children who are 21 and 12 years old. The oldest is at university and the younger is in secondary school. She began her business a year ago with economic support from her ex husband. She bought a shelf, a candy jar, cookies and gum. These were her first products. Little by little she increased her sales and at the same time added more products to form the store that takes care of her family.  She needs a loan to buy rice, sugar, oil, soups, soda, juices, dairy products, oats, canned goods, chicken and toothpaste. They are the products that are in highest demand and of which she needs to have stocked. Her dream is to convert her small store into a variety store where she can offer a variety of products for the home.

name: Maryam
description: Mrs. Maryam L. Okeya is a business woman who sells fairly used clothes, and also has a hairdressing salon. She is 47 years old and is married with 7 children. She hails from Asaba, Delta State, and wishes to improve her business with the above loan.

name: Esther
description: Esther is 46 years old and she is from Nakuru. She is married to James and they are blessed with two children, aged 14 and 2 years old.  Esther is a farmer and has been working in this occupation for the last 24 years. She has applied for her first loan of KES 12,500 from VisionFund Kenya, which she will use to buy a water storage tank. Esther believes that after she has purchased a water storage tank she will be able to collect rain water and, therefore, the time she has been spending going to the river to fetch water can be used working on her farm for more yield and greater profits.  Right now Esther's monthly income is KES 5,000 and she hopes that this income will increase. In the future, she hopes to be a successful farmer.

name: Osman
description: This is 29-year-old Osman. He is married and has two children, aged 5 and 2 years. He has seven additional dependents who live with him because they are his relatives. In 2007, Osman established his used clothing business. He got his initial capital from his uncle.   "This business is my only source of income to provide food and other basic things for my family," said Osman.   Working seven days a week and nine hours a day, he earns about 1,000,000 Sierra Leone leones (Le)  every month from this business. He would like a loan in the amount of Le 3,000,000. Osman now requires a loan in order to buy more used clothing for his business. He hopes that this loan will enable him to increase his monthly profits by approximately Le 200,000. In the future, Osman plans build a dwelling house for his family and to give his children a good education. He thanks you for your support.

name: Victoria Isabel
description: Victoria is a very hard-working woman.  She is 29 years old, married, and she and her husband have two children, ages 6 years and 18 months.  Her husband works driving a mototaxi, but also supports her a lot in everything she does.  He is her right hand.  Victoria, as a good Peruvian, loves our food and one of the meals that she enjoys very much is the delicious "Pollo a la Brasa" (Peruvian roasted chicken).  She could eat this everyday without getting tired of it.  Since her parents didn't have sufficient economic means, she could only study until the fifth grade of secondary education, but she would have very much liked to study computation and information.    Victoria sells general and staple goods.  She works around 15 hours a day and attends to about 20 customers a day.  She works at this business because her mother did before her. However, they deceived her with counterfeit money and for this reason, she became discouraged and closed the business.  In time, she decided to reopen the business and through it, has saved a lot to invest in it.  She thinks that her business is going well because she is attentive to her customers, and moreover, she offers good quality products.  Victoria is very grateful to the Kiva lenders since with their support, she can purchase merchandise for the school year (school supplies, uniforms, among others) and can offer them in her store.  With this improvement, she will have greater income and can continue growing her business, allowing her to continue saving to be able to complete her greatest dream: giving her children a profession and having a store.

name: Mujeres Trabajando Contra La Pobreza Group
description: Lucia M. R. is a group coordinator for the group called “Mujeres Trabajando Contra La Pobreza,” which in English means Women Working Against Poverty. Lucia is the owner of a small convenience store, where she sells food items such as rice and oil to her community. This will be Lucia’s third loan with Kiva's partner Esperanza and she is hoping this one will improve her business as much as the first two did. Lucia has two grown children, one of whom lives with her and her husband, Gabriel M..  Lucia dreams of continual growth for her business and also continually learning skills through her business and her experience with Esperanza. She dreams that her grown children will have a good position in society and also be able to own their own businesses one day. Because of her faithfulness in repayment of her first two loans, Lucia has been able to receive more with this current loan. Lucia’s loan is for 15000 Dominican pesos (about $420).  On behalf of Lucia M. R., Mujeres Trabajando Contra La Pobreza and all of us here at Esperanza International, thank you for your support!

name: Melba
description: Melba works hard to support her family. Melba is married and has a general store business in the Philippines. Melba requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional stock like sardines, biscuits and other groceries needed in her business.  Melba has been in this business for four years now.  In the future, Melba  would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Juana
description: Juana is a member of the Bonanza Communal Bank.  She is 56 years old, married, and has 4 children.  She has a shop in her home where she sells groceries.  Juana manages her business every day with the help of her son.  She needs a loan of 1050 soles to buy rice and sugar.  Juana dreams of improving and expanding her store. Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Arthur
description: Arthur B. is from the village of Cabisera 5, Ilagan, Isabela. He is 28 years old and is married with two infant children.  Arthur owns and operates a business planting and harvesting rice for sale. He has been engaged in his business for over eight years and earns approximately 23,000 PHP per harvest.  In 2010, Arthur joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and his ability to engage in business activities. He is requesting a loan of 10,000 PHP which will be used to purchase fertilizer such as manure. This loan will be his first from ASKI. He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand his business.    About ASKI: ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has twenty-one branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.    *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Thành
description: Thành works in agriculture farming poultry and cattle. He has been involved in this business for five years.Thành is 38 years old and is married with two children. He supports two dependents with his business in Quang Xuong district, a rural town in Thanh Hoa province.This is Thành’s first loan with Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women. One of the most critical difficulties that concerns him is not having a hygienic latrine. He is requesting a loan to purchase sand, cement, bricks, and equipment to build a toilet.In the future, Thành hopes for his children to do well in school, for his business to do well, and for his family to be healthy and happy.

name: Heroina Del Consuelo
description: Heroína Consuelo R. S. is 52 years old and has been in the shaved ice business for 13 years.  This is icy treat that is sold at a reasonable price and is very easy to make.  She is also a docent at a public school, but her income isn’t enough to cover her family’s expenses, which is why she began selling her products as a mobile vendor.  Her business has grown little by little, and now has a tricycle from which she sells her shaved ice.  The financing she is requesting will go towards working capital.  Her dream is to provide her son with a university education, as she cannot currently afford to provide him with one.  Translated from Spanish by Maya Wisnievitz, Kiva Volunteer

name: Letecia
description: Letecia signed up for her membership with PMPC and obtained money to start a sari-sari store. She is thankful for the capital that was extended to a small-time borrower like her. Letecia is able to turn the tide in her favor and is making good sales these days. She wants to take advantage of the good fortune. Recently, she took a loan to restock her store with basic commodities so that she can save and improve their living condition. In the future, she hopes to build a decent home for the family.

name: Isabel
description: Isabel, 41, is a cheerful, kind woman who is also a hard worker and determined to get ahead.  She is divorced from the father of her beloved four-year-old daughter, Joselin, who she lives with comfortably in her own house.  Isabel works selling different brands and flavors of sodas and sweets that she buys at shopping centers in the city.  She buys everything in cash and sells from home to passers-by who are her habitual customers.  She has been in business for over five years and, for now, is helped out only by her mother who attends to customers when she is not home.  She believes her business is profitable because of the earnings she can make.  When she divorced her daughter's father, things were difficult because the pension he paid was not enough to cover food and education costs, so she decided to work for herself.  She likes what she does because it gives her an income and keeps her busy.  And, since she works at home she has free time to dedicate to other activities.  Therefore, she has plans to expand the business and go into the fast food sector.    This is her third loan through MFP and she is hoping a small loan will help her meet her goals.  She says she is happy with her communal bank because she likes the work it does toward helping people.  The 1,000 PEN loan will be used to buy merchandise such as different brands and flavors of sweets and sodas.  She will pay cash and seek out the lowest prices in order to increase her earnings.

name: Analita
description: Analita is 41 years old and has eight children. She is married and seven of her children are currently in school.  Analita is in the agricultural business, fattening pigs in the Philippines. She requested a 10,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy feed and vitamins for her pigs.  Analita has been in this business for four years now, and has borrowed 19 times in the past from NWTF to sustain the business.  In the future, Analita would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Ep Don Bosco Group
description: Alice is a teacher in a Don Bosco primary school. She is 27 years old, married and the mother of two young children. This client has already undertaken small trading projects (clothing, sale of jewelry, makeup etc) to support her finances. Her husband is a student at the university, and additionally a professional photographer. This new loan will allow her to strengthen these small trading activities, and she will use the rest of the loan as a deposit for buying a plot of land. She regrets the growing insecurity in the region and the negative collateral effects this has, notably on her projects. Finally, she thanks Hekima for its help with mico-credit.

name: Marlyn
description: Marlyn, age 37, sells seafood to earn a living. She has been in this business for two years. She and her husband have two children, both of whom attend school. Marlyn is a very hard-working entrepreneur.  Marlyn has requested a loan in the amount of PhP 15,000 through NWTF. She will use her loan funds to buy seafood to offer for sale.  In the future, she would like to save enough money to expand her business. Her goal is to send her children to college.

name: Evdochia
description: Evdochia is a very hardworking woman because she loves her job. In childhood she went through many difficult moments, and now it is much easier for her to survive. Evdochia cares for her 3 children. Evdochia has a small business in the central market of Kagul town where she sells children's clothing. She rents a table at the market from a friend, and she pays rent monthly. At the moment, sales have fallen for some months so she only has money for payment of the monthly rent. She still wants to increase the stock of goods because she has the opportunity to buy merchandise at a very reasonable price in the city of Odessa.  Thus, Evdochia will pay the monthly payment to her friend and then have the profits needed to support their children.

name: Joyce
description: As a married parent of two children, Joyce works hard to support her family. She has a fish vending business in the Philippines and also earns additional income from running a general store. Joyce has been sustaining her business activities through her past seven loans from NWTF.  Joyce is requesting a 10,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy more fish to sell to her customers. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of building and expanding her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Sushila
description: 45-year-old Sushila is a rural housewife from the village of Ramthenga in Falakata. She lives there with her husband and one son. Both her daughters are married. For financial reasons, Sushila could not provide higher education to her children. Her son has been educated till primary level, he is now engaged in cultivation with his father. Sushila has a hard life and a low income, but a kind heart and a good character. Her husband has been involved in growing agricultural crops, such as potatoes, beans, chillies, etc. for over five years. Sushila also helps her husband in his agricultural work. They sell the resulting harvest in the local market which is the main source of income for the family. Now they decided to grow cauliflower on their farm land, which is a crop that is much in demand in winter in West Bengal. Now, in order to provide their family with a better living standard, they need to develop their business. So Sushila has taken a loan from BJS (Kiva’s partner) to purchase seeds and fertilizers to execute their plan. They want to get a larger harvest to provide the family with all the necessities. She dreams of giving well-being to her family members and constructing a concrete house for them in the future with the business profit.She is very much grateful to the lenders (BJS and Kiva).

name: Ezra
description: Ezra used the previous loan to buy land. He is twenty-four years old, married with three children, and lives in Kasese, Uganda. Ezra works very hard to put food on the table for his family. He has a dream of buying a bigger plot of land for farming. However, he is faced with a challenge of market competition. Ezra wants money to buy materials for making men suits.

name: Gloria
description: Gloria is 45 years old, married, and has four children.  She earns a living by farming citrus in the Philippines. Gloria is borrowing 15,000 PHP through NWTF to purchase additional variety of citrus plants and fertilizers.  Gloria has been farming citrus for seven years and also earns additional income from selling fruits and vegetables.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Imelda
description: Imelda, age 55, is raising hogs as a source of income. She raises hogs to help her husband improve their poor living conditions.   She has requested a loan of 6,000 PHP to purchase feed and additional piglets to sustain her business. Her goal is to maximize her hog raising business and to improve her income. Then, she could be able to support the educational needs of her three children.

name: Savoeurn
description: Mrs. Savoeurn M., 47, grows and sells vegetables, earning around $1 per day. She is married with five children, three of whom are married and other two are single. Two work as garment workers in Phnom Penh. Her husband, Mr. Pan Long, 48, makes wood bed, earning around $2.50 per day. Savoeurn requests a loan of $700 for her husband to purchase more wood to make beds and to buy 200 baby ducks to breed.

name: Bwikara Tweyimukye Group
description: Sadam is a 40-year-old hardworking married man living in Kagadi, Uganda with seven children between 16 and 3 years old and all attend school. He has been operating a butcher shop alongside farming since 2001 to generate income and educate his children. He hopes to build a commercial house in spite of the challenges of inadequate capital. Sadam intends to use the loan to buy more cattle to sell. He is a member of Bwikara Tweimukye Group where each member guarantees the others to get a loan since they don’t pledge securities.

name: Lorielice
description: Lorielice is a married woman with two children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Lorielice is 29 years old and has one child who is in school.  Lorielice has a native bag making business in the Philippines. Lorielice requested a 10,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) loan amount through NWTF to buy additional materials for making native bags.  Lorielice has been in this business for 10 years. In the future, Lorielice would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Zarina
description: Zarina H. lives in the Shahrituz district.  She is 32 years old, married and has 2 children.  Her husband works in Russia.  Zarina has a secondary education.  She started her own business after her husband left for work.  Currently, she leases a retail outlet at the district's central market, where she sells children's and women's clothing.  Zarina primarily brings her merchandise from the city.  She has been involved in this business for 4 years.  She is requesting this loan in order to increase goods turnover.

name: Hean
description: Hean, 49, is married. She lives with her family in a village of the Koh Sotin district of Kampong Cham province, Cambodia. She has five children. For the last 31 years, Hean and her husband have been working as construction workers. Together, they can earn about 50,000 KHR per day from the current business.  Hean is just with VisionFund for this cycle. She is now applying for a loan to buy an electric generator ​​​​for supporting her business. She hopes this loan will enable her to earn more income from her current business.
town: Kampong Cham Province, Koh Sotin District

name: Nory Edith
description: Nory R. G., 44, lives in San Jacinto Bolívar with her husband, who is a farmer, and their two children, who are 20 and 17 years old.    She manufactures hammocks and bags.  She inherited these skills from her mother and she has done this kind of work since she was 12 years old.  She finished high-school at night because she would spend days making hammocks and bags.    Currently, Nory has a workshop where she, her mother and her sister-in-law work.  They weave these artesanal items on a wood loom where the thread is hooked and woven.  Her customers are in her same town but she sometimes sends her items to Cartagena.    Since her incorporation into the communal bank, Nory has received 5 loans from the Fundación Mario Santo Domingo in amounts that vary from $100.000 that she began with to the one she is requesting now for $1.500.000, which she will use to buy cordage to make her hammocks and bags.  She has repaid all her previous loans on time.  She has used them to add to her family income.  Thanks to her and her husband's earnings, the living conditions of her family have improved; they own their own home now.  Her goal is to see that her sons finish their college education in Chemistry, Pharmacy and Medicine.  Her most notable challenge is the great effort entailed in calling upon all her creative energy to create new and attractive designs for her products in order to ride out times of lowered sales.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Hellen
description: Hellen N. lives in the Busega neighborhood of Kampala, Uganda. She is single and has one child who is not in school.   Hellen sells charcoal. She has been in this business for 2 years and she works 7 days a week. Hellen sells her products from home. Hellen has requested a loan of 300,000 Ugandan Shillings from MCDT SACCO, which she will use to buy more charcoal.her main business challenge is transporting the charcoal from Natete to her home in Busega.  She hopes to start going to villages of Luwero for charcoal. Hellen lives in a home that she owns with electricity and piped water. Her major monthly expense is food.

name: La Fortaleza Group 2
description: Dionorat is the leader of the group L. Fortaleza 2, which translates as "The Strength." This group is seeking a loan to help them grow their small businesses in the town of Hato Mayor on the eastern sector of the Dominican Republic. This is a group maD. up of friends and family that has successfully taken out three loans in the past and has supported one another in their entrepreneurial ventures.   Diornat owns a clothing store that she started two years ago. With this loan, she will buy more pants and blouses to sell in her store. She hopes to increase her profits so that she can continue to support her two children, aged 13 and 16, and be able to send them to college.   Diornat and the entire L. Fortaleza 2 group have greatly appreciated the opportunities that their microloans have given them and they hope to continue in their success.

name: San Jose Group
description: The San José community bank has nine members who are all women aged between 30 and 60.  They have 15 children in their care and live in the town of El Sauce, in the north of the country.  El Sauce is known for its milk, curds and cream production, for its corn growing and for its pig raising.  All the members of this group are hard-working and responsible people.  Maribel is the coordinator of the community bank.  She is responsible for ensuring that every member makes her payments on time and in full.  Maribel's business is selling 'cosa de horno' which is a traditional cake made from corn, curds and cinnamon.  Maribel's routine involves getting up at 4.00am to make her 'cosa de horno'.  She then goes out to make her sales as an itinerant street vendor.  She works until 4.00pm, carrying her products in a basket on her head under the intense daily sun.  The San José community bank are grateful for the help that Kiva investors provide to people with limited resources in poor countries such as Nicaragua.  It enables them to make a decent living.

name: Mouy Kea
description: Mouy Kea is 59 years old. She is widowed and blessed with two children in Takeo Province, Cambodia. She has been selling grilled chicken for more than ten years, earning approximately $6 daily. One of her children is a construction worker who earns about $3 each day.  In order to improve her family’s finances, Mouy Kea is requesting a loan of $1000 as working capital  to purchase more chicken to grill and sell. By doing so, she would be able to make more profit to support the family. In the future, she would like to expand her business and send her youngest child to a good school. Moreover, she hopes to build a new house as soon as possible.

name: Mana
description: Mana is a 37-year-old widow with a dependent child living in the Bé district. She has a small business buying corn that she uses to prepare a gruel that she sells at the roadside. Mana buys her stock once a month at the market in Akodessewa. Mana requests a loan in order to expand her business and make a bigger profit.

name: Matia
description: Matia is 26 years old and is married with two children living in Kasese, Uganda. He runs a retail shop with general merchandise. He has been in this business since 2010 and also practices commercial farming, growing crops such as beans and maize to get additional income. He began the business to improve his family's standards of living.   Matia is a hardworking man dreaming of a wholesale business. He wants money to buy rice, soap, sugar, salt and other general merchandise to sell. High transport costs are a hindrance to his operations.

name: Soroyiriwaton Group
description: Nana is the one with her hands on the bag of groundnuts in the photo. Nana is a 56-year-old Malian, married with three daughters, none of whom attend school. Her husband is a farmer.  She is a small retail merchant and stores rice and groundnuts. She has 11 years' experience, gets her supplies from surrounding markets and resells them in the same locations.  The profit she realizes enables her to help her husband support the family's needs. She calls upon the RMCR to borrow money so she can stock a large quantity of grain cereals at the most advantageous time.  She is often faced with the problem of poor sales on the market. In the future Nana wishes to become a major merchant of cereals.

name: Salima
description: Salima is married to a driver and is mother to three children, who are all at school. Her eldest child is 11 years old and her youngest five. She is 36 years old and is a retailer by trade. She carries out her business alone in her shop and sells general grocery products. In order to strengthen her capacity and become the best in her neighborhood, Salima, who has already had two microloans from WAGES, is requesting a third so that she can buy general groceries. With what remains of her income, she would like to save enough to diversify her sources of income and ensure a good future for all her family.

name: Tram's Group
description: Tram is 57 years old and lives with her three children and husband. Her husband is a laborer in a local company.   For the past 5 years, Tram has run a food stall from the front of her house to earn an income to support her family. Tram is the Group Leader of a 7-member loan group that lives in Ho Chi Minh City. In the picture, she is second from the right  and wears a grey jacket. Each of the other group members request loans to fund income-generating activities.  Tram requests a loan to purchase better quality food to sell from her stall.  She also wants to buy new furniture to attract more customers to her stall. She hopes this will enable her to better meet the needs of her customers and attract additional ones.   She also hopes that she will be able to increase her income and save money for any future difficulties facing her family.

name: Sath's Group
description: Sath’s group lives in a rural village in the Kompong Thom province of Cambodia. Sath makes a living cultivating rice, and she also does work as a salesperson, selling groceries from home to support her family. In their village, there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expense,s and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Hjiadi Group
description: This group is called HJIADI and is located in the community of Lerma, in Mexico. These women based their group’s name on an Otomi word that means Sun and Moon. The group is made up of 9 members, including Remedios S. P. who is in charge of holding group meetings at her home. Remedios is 54 years old, attended high school and has been married to Miguel Angel Guzman for 34 years. At first her husband’s salary, from his work as a general assistant at a company in Mexico City, was their only source of income. Her hope to improve her family’s situation required her to take on various jobs ranging from growing corn and beans to catalogue sales. Recently she was invited to join a group of like-minded women. She is requesting a loan to buy sweets for her business. She has always hoped that her children will have access to quality education. She also hopes to one day have a soda fountain because her business is located near the community’s high school.

name: Berard
description: Berard is a 35-year-old married man.  He has 5 children. He describes himself to be self-motivated man.  He operates a food stall  where he sells cereals such as maize, beans, etc. He has been involved in this business for 3 years and employs 1 staff member. His business is located within a potential business area.  He describes his biggest business challenge to be the high transportation cost of cereals.   Berard will use the KES 20,000 loan to buy ten bags of maize.  His business goal is to be a large supplier of maize within 5 years. He hopes that in the future he will be a successful businessman.  Berard also does farming, which increases his business income. This is his first loan.

name: Jose Vicente
description: Jose is 25, and lives in a town called Playas (Beaches).  Playas is one of the Ecuador's tourist sites, known for its diverse available types of seafood. He drives a motor three wheel cycle (this is a quick and efficient transportation system, and it can go places where a car cannot). Since the age of 13 he began working with his motorcycle by helping people in the market who needed assistance with packages and needed transportation.  Then, because he needed to bring in more revenue, he decided to buy a motorcycle and turn it into a motor-tricycle. Now, he works at the market, transporting people home from the 07h00am until 20h00pm every day. The most difficult part of his job is driving on roads, which are in poor condition.  With this loan, Jose would like to buy a bigger motor-cycle body (cart) so that his customers have more space for merchandise. In the future, he would like to have his own house.  Currently, he and his wife, live with his parents.

name: Cipriana
description: Ciprina started a business because it is something that she wanted to do.  She enjoys making different crafts very much, and it is an activity that she can perform in her house whenever she wants.  At the same time, she can take care of her grandchildren.  She began the business in March 2006 thanks to a teacher that taught her to make crafts.  She first started making handbags and bathroom sets, and later began making things related to each coming season, such as paper flowers for the Day of the Dead and decorations for Christmas, Friendship Day, Children's Day, Mother's Day, etc.  Thanks to God, she has been getting more customers through recommendations from other people who liked her work.  She needs a loan of $6,000 MXN that she will repay in 12 installments that she will use to purchase raw materials such as cloth, glue, foamy, thread, scissors, paper, etc.  This will allow her make decorations that her customers entrust her to make for special dates and events.Translated from Spanish by Josh Wilcox, Kiva Volunteer

name: Amukeni Group
description: Hellen is a member of Amukeni Group in Kakakmega North District. She is pictured with 10 One Acre Fund farmers, 6 women and 4 men. Hellen is standing on the right with her hand raised. She is receiving an input loan for ½ acre of millet and sorghum cultivation. Hellen joined One Acre Fund during the Long Rains 2011, and is now enrolling in the Long Rains 2013 season. Hellen joined One Acre Fund so that she could grow enough food for the family and use increased profits to send her children to school.  Hellen reports that before One Acre Fund, she was able to grow about one bag of maize per ½ acre, but with her One Acre Fund input loan during Long Rains 2012, she harvested four bags per 1/2 acre! She plans on using future profits from the harvest to buy a cow and send her children to school. During the 2013 Long Rains season, each group member will receive ½ an acre of agricultural inputs on credit. Hellen’s group will receive 5 acres worth of inputs on credit.  The field officer is standing on the left of the photo.

name: Artak
description: Artak is a happy father of three little kids (in the photo). Together with his wife (in the photo), Artak is involved in agriculture. They keep 2 cows, 3 oxen and 10 colonies of bees. Artak's wife milks the cows and produces cheese for selling locally.   As agriculture is the only source of income for Artak, he would like to enlarge his business. He has requested this loan to purchase 4 oxen and forage for feeding them. This will enable Artak to gather more income and with increased income he will be able to improve his family's living conditions.

name: Shihadeh
description: Shihadeh is a 56-year-old married man from Rafah city.  He was living with his family in a small humble house, but during the latest war in Gaza, his house destroyed completely, then he had to rent a small apartment in the same area.Recently Shihadeh took a USD loan from Palestine for Credit and Development (FATEN) in order to rebuild his old house. The loan will allow Shihadeh to finalize the needed construction in a short time and return his family to their normal life.Shihadeh appears in the photo.

name: Mwongeli
description: Mwongeli is married and has two children, one of whom goes to school. She rents a house with neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest challenge is paying for food and rent. She runs a retail kiosk where she sells vegetables and charcoal.  Mwongeli is kindly asking for a loan of KES 25,000 to buy various kinds of vegetables and six bags of charcoal for sale to her clients.

name: Solange
description: Solange, 35 years old and in a common-law marriage, is the mother of two. She has been selling cosmetics, such as shampoo, deodorant, etc., for over six years. The loan is enabling her to diversify her products more and to attract more customers.

name: Russel
description: Russel A. is 32 years old. Russel is married and has 1 school-aged children. To make a living, Russel owns & operates a business venture in the agriculture sector raising crops. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes from planting & harvesting coconuts for sale. She is also engaged in buying copra from the neighboring villages. Russel has been engaged in her business for over 10 years and earns approximately 10,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2008, Russel joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Russel has successfully repaid a previous loan of 14,000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to pay for services to increase crop yield. Russel is requesting a new loan of 17,000 PHP which will be used to invest in expanding the business. This will be the 5th loan taken out by Russel from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the income of the family.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is an accredited partner of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and reaches out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: William
description: William is a farmer in Kitale area of Western Kenya where he has had twenty years in active farming and meets all family needs through farming income. His farm currently produces milk, millet, eggs, sorghum, beans and potatoes.  William has requested a third loan of 100,000 KES from Kiva partner Juhudi Kilimo to help him put up a dairy unit at a cost of 30,000 KES and also boost his poultry business by expanding the housing unit at 40,000 KES with the remaining 30,000 KES to go into purchasing chicks. William is planning on concentrating more on poultry and dairy farming in the coming years.  William says Juhudi Kilimo loans have empowered smallholder farmers with him being among the beneficiaries of the loans. He however notes poultry diseases are a challenge and farmers must learn management to avoid gross losses in their businesses.

name: Josefina
description: Josefina is 65 years old, married, and the mother of three children. She works very hard to provide for her family by running a general store in the Philippines and has requested a PHP 13,000 loan from NWTF to buy additional items to sell such as soap, milk, sugar, eggs, rice, and noodles. Josefina has been in this business for twelve years and would like to save enough money to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Genie
description: This is Genie. She previously obtained a PHP 20,000 loan that she used to purchase more quantities and varieties of grocery items, toiletries, and beverages needed in her business. Her earnings were a big help in her personal, household, and business expenses.  She would like to apply for another PHP 30,000 loan to buy still more groceries, toiletries, beverages, and other products to add to her current inventory. The more items displayed at the store, the better. More items to sell will result in better profit.   Her profits from her business definitely help her to sustain her daily needs. She looks forward to this financial increase with gladness and thankfulness in her heart.  Genie dreams of expanding her business and having more products. She meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of their work every week and to draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet every week. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay their Micro Finance loans.

name: Fumilola
description: Fumilola,an active LAPO client, is 36 years old and married with one child. She has a video store where she rents out VCDs, and she also sells drinks at both the wholesale and retail level. Fumilola hopes for the loan amount of N80,000 to purchase more drinks to sell.

name: Kimbat
description: Kimbat P. is a single mother of two daughters.  She graduated from Trade college and worked as an accountant for four years. As it was very hard to bring up the children by herself on a low wage, Kimbat decided to start her own business in trade.   Starting in 2007, she managed to broaden her business by renting a small shop and achieving success. Her loyal customers were attracted by her careful attitude and cheerfulness.   But in June 2010, violent clashes caused by the deposed political regime broke out in the city of Osh. Kimbat lost her business, which was burned to ashes.  Kimbat doesn’t give up, however, and she is ready to resume her lost business and to continue to work. That is why Kimbat is applying for a loan of 100,000 KGS, which she needs to restart her activity. She plans to rent a selling point at the local market to sell womens clothing.   Kimbat is a very optimistic person who believes that giving a small chance to another person can inspire them for a great future.    Bai-Tushum and Partners uses Kiva funding to target the especially vulnerable population. Bai-Tushum and Partners is one of the leading Microfinance Institutions in Kyrgyzstan. As a reliable financial partner, Bai-Tushum contributes to the economic development of the Kyrgyz Republic through the delivery of microfinance services in rural and urban areas that lead to increased employment and meet the interests of its clients and investors.

name: Erlinda's Group
description: Erlinda D.'s main source of income comes from tending a canteen near a school. She is 30 years old, married and has two school-aged children. They are from the village of Banquero. Erlinda has been in her business for over three years and earns approximately 3,500 Philippine pesos (PHP) a month.  In 2006, Erlinda joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living conditions and enable her to engage in business activities. Erlinda has successfully repaid a previous loan of 13,000 PHP from ASKI which was used to purchase new items to expand her product offering. Erlinda is requesting a new loan of 10,000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This will be her 9th loan from ASKI. She plans to use additional income to improve and expand her business.   Erlinda is the leader of a five member group accessing a loan offered by ASKI. While each member of the group receives an individual loan, they are collectively responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults. The official name of this borrowing group is "Erlinda D.'s Group".  About ASKI: ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 38 branches covering the central and northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Sabina
description: Sabina S. is a 24-year-old married woman who lives in Tikhedewol, Lalitpur. Tikhedewol is one of the growing towns in Lalitpur. Most people in this region are engaged in small business. Mrs. S. lives with her husband and one daughter. Her daughter is studying in grade 3.  Mrs. S. 's husband's name is Kumar. He is a photographer who works in a photo studio. He is not satisfied with his salary and it's difficult for him to meet the requirements of his family. He decided to open his own photo studio but due to lack of funds he cannot do this.   So to help her husband open his own photo studio, Mrs. S. is requesting an Rs 10000.00 loan.

name: Carmen
description: Carmen is a small business woman who runs her own business, a pulpería [small grocery store] where she sells a variety of products. She also makes tortillas by hand. Her business has been growing and she has been increasing her capital. She has the economic support of her husband, who works as a taxi driver.  With the help of previous loans, she has been able to increase sales of consumable goods, which is what her customers demand.  Of her three children, one is independent and the others are enrolled in school. As a mother, she is happy to be able to give her children a good education.  With this new loan, she will be able to buy staple items like rice, sugar, corn, beans, a drum of oil, boxes of soap for cleaning and bathing, and other products to satisfy her customers.

name: Jenny Gricelda
description: The "Urb. Las Viviendas" communal bank meets every fortnight in the canton of Jaramijo. This place is known for it's beautiful beaches and the majority of inhabitants are very hard-working and work related to the sea. Jenny lives in this place. She is 32 years old, married and from this relationship has 4 children aged 16,15 13 and 11 years old. Three of them study in Secondary school and one in primary school. Her husband is a businessman. Jenny is a woman who has always liked to work to help with the expenses for the education of her children. She has a store at her house where she sells water in barrels or gallon containers, colas and beer amongst other drinks. She also delivers to homes with a three wheeled motorcycle she has. Her children help her with this as does her husband when he is not working. She has been in this business for 2 years and she makes good profit. She will use the loan to buy plastic jerry cans of water and all the other varieties. She has been in the communal bank since it's inception and she likes it because of the help the loans provide. Her dream is to continue to improve her business.

name: Julie
description: Julie is 45 years old and married with four children.  Julie works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 20,000 loan through NWTF in order to purchase more groceries to sell in her store.  Julie has been in this business for nine years and has previously received funds through Kiva.  Julie aspires to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Rubiela Amparo
description: Rubiela is married with two children to whom she promises a good quality of life.  Thanks to her business, she generates income and contributes financially to the household, along with her husband, so that the financial situation in their home may improve, and they can have a good quality of life.    Over ten years ago, she began selling goods, working as a street vender and, thanks to the hard work she did, she managed to set up a store inside her home. There, she has had her business where she has been selling stationary products until now.  Because her clientele is growing, and increasingly demanding more products, Rubiela is seeking a loan to purchase household products and offer her customers a wider variety of products in her general store. In this way, her business will succeed, and she will be able to provide her home with a good income so that they can continue having a good quality of life. .

name: Tevan
description: Tevan lives in the unbelievably beautiful village Srashen of Syunik region. As he says, he is a happy father of three clever, cheerful, and brave boys, who are still school-aged.   Tevan got married very early and, since he became the head of the family, he established a nice farm, where he takes care of 13 sheep, 4 lambs (he keeps them in a barn built by himself), and 20 chickens. He also has large plot of land, part of which gives him a harvest of vegetables (tomato, cucumber, beans, onions, and greens)  and also a colorful orchard with a sweet harvest of apple, plums, peaches, persimmons, and figs.   All his farm work he does properly and with care. He also manages to work at farms in his village, being paid for doing different work there, such as harvest gathering or some land cultivation. So he catches any chance to earn more money for his big and lovely family.   Tevan’s wife works as a cleaner at the local school. Tevan needs this loan in order to organize autumn sowing activities and impatiently waits for this loan in order to start.

name: Matlab
description: Matlab is an Internally Displaced Person from the Lachin region located in the southwest part of Azerbaijan. He and his family were relocated to Sumgayit as a result of the Armenian-Azerbaijan military conflict over Garabakh. He rents a shop and trades mobile phones. As mobile phones are very popular now, the business is going well. But the number and variety of mobile phones is poor. Matlab wants to increase the volume of business. As he has little of his own funds, he has applied to Normicro Sungayit branch for a loan in the amount of $1200 to invest in his business. He will repay the loan in 12 months.

name: Cossy
description: Cossy is a 22 year married with two children aged 11 months and 4 fours.  One of her children goes to school. She resides and owns a two roomed house where she is staying with three people. Cossy takes care of additional family members There is electricity and piped water at her home.  The family gets three meals a day. She resides and works in semi urban area where she deals in cold drinks and refreshments.  She incurs extra transport costs from and to shopping. Cossy sells to an average of 10 customers a day and sells to all categories of people. She works six days a week. Her major monthly expenses include school fees. Feeding the family She has been in this business for the last five years Harriet has been with MCDT for years servicing her twelfth loan, working with the same group mates. She wants to use this loan to buy more bales of second hand clothes.  Cossy is aspiring of seeing her business grow bigger and owning a rental rooms     .

name: Ady
description: Ady works hard to support her family. She is married and has a food vending business in the Philippines.  Ady has requested a PHP 16,000 loan through NWTF to buy ingredients and items to sell to her customers. She has been in this business for 4 years now and earns additional income from a general store.  She successfully paid back her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her business. She would like to continue to build and expand her business to secure her family's future.

name: Lani
description: Lani is 44 years old and married with one child who is in school. Lani works very hard to provide for them.  Lani runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 11,000 loan through NWTF in order to purchase more stocks of groceries to sell.  Lani has been in this business for five years and sells a variety of items such as shampoo, canned goods, soft-drink and other groceries.   In the future Lani would like to save enough money to expand her business and repair her family's home.

name: Percy
description: Percy, 38, lives in the city of Pucallpa with his wife and little five-year-old son who he loves and is his reason for living.  He’s a very kind, hardworking, enthusiastic man who along with his wife focuses all his efforts into moving his family forward.  Sadly, due to the lack of economic resources and the need to start working very young, Percy was unable to study auto mechanics.  In his free time, he enjoys going on family outings along the warm, welcoming streets of his city.  On his own initiative and with munch effort and dedication, Percy works as a sales assistant for a commercial firm in his city and he also sells lumber.  He works every day for about 10 hours daily and believes he does well because of the good way he does his work and the kind customer service he provides.  Percy is very grateful to Kiva lenders because thanks to the support provided he will be able to build a small bathroom at home in order to have all the necessary hygienic services to provide better hygiene and well-being for his family.  In this way, Percy will continue striving and working towards his great dream of having his own auto spare parts business.

name: Sudi
description: Sudi is a married man with two children who are still too young for school.  He owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water.  His greatest monthly expense is food.  He has operated a vegetable selling business, for over three years.  His potential customers are his neighbours.  Sudi faces a major challenge of price fluctuation due to seasonality of the products.  He hopes to expand and establish a cereal business in the future.   He decided to join Yehu to access loans to improve his living standards.  With the Kshs 20,000 he wants to purchase sacks of vegetables for sale.

name: John
description: John is 53 years old, from Olkalou. He is married to Martha, who produces additional income for the family. They have five children, ages 16, 14, 10, 8 and 5. He is in the business of quarrying, which has been in operation for the past three years, and his monthly income at present is KES 12,000. He has applied for his third loan from Kadet Ltd, of KES 20,000, and his plan is to use it to  hire more laborers to work in his quarry. John intends to use the anticipated profits to expand his quarrying business, and his hope and dream is to buy a plot of land and build rental houses in the future.

name: Tserennadmid
description: Tserennadmid S. is 35 years old and lives with her husband and two children in Ulaanbaatar, the capital city of Mongolia. She and her family live together in a ger, the traditional Mongolian nomadic tent.  Tserennadmid currently operates a raw materials trade in her district. She started her business in 2003 and has found success in her business. She is now renting a small food shop in the Chingeltei district of Ulaanbaatar in order to improve her quality of life and stabilize her family's financial situation.  Tserennadmid dreams of possessing her own food shop in the future. She is requesting a 1,500,000 MNT loan to purchase raw materials and food supplements for her shop.

name: Magdalena
description: Magdalena, 28 years of age, is married to a private employee and blessed with three children. She has owned and managed a vegetable production business in their village for almost four years, and earns a net income of PHP 300 daily. Due to insufficient funds, she would like a loan of PHP 17,000 to purchase eggplant, bitter gourd, squash, and string bean seedlings. She's hoping that her requested loan will be granted so that she can improve her business to earn more income.

name: Donald Miguel
description: Donald Miguel García A. is a buyer for the Rubén Darío National Theater.  He is married and has four, school age, children under his care.  He has had four loans with CEPRODEL over five years that he has used to make improvement on his home.  The funding requested now will be used to buy building materials, like flooring and cement, for his home.  Donald stated that thanks to loans from CEPRODEL he has been able to make improvements to his home to the extent that now he has a safer home for his family.  Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Selina
description: Selina P. makes a living selling rice, seeds and other items, and is applying for this loan to buy bags of rice from Uganda to sell to her customers.  She is 33 years old, married to a driver, and has eight children, four of whom are currently in school. She plans to use the profits generated by this loan to pay her children's school fees.

name: Teresa
description: Teresa is 56 years old, is in a common-law marriage, and lives with her husband. With her loan, she plans to purchase some chickens to fatten and some laying hens which are just beginning to lay, so that they have a longer laying period. The idea is to take advantage of the good conditions of the place where she lives to develop this activity. In addition, she will be able to sell the animals once they are fattened and the eggs to the members of the community and in this way not pay for transportation and to be able to sell the products fresher due to the proximity of the consumers. With this purchase, she will be able to develop an additional activity, and at the same time have savings that will allow her to have more animals and invest more in her business. It is the first loan that she is getting from FUDECOSUR. She has never had other loans before at state banks, but FUDECOSUR offers her the loan with better terms and a much lower interest rate.

name: Uuganbayar
description: Uuganbayar is 27 years old and lives with his wife in Ulaanbaatar, the capital city of Mongolia. He operates a clothing retail trading business out of a stall in the largest outdoor market, Narantuul, in the city. He started his business in 2010 with working capital of 900,000 MNT, which has increased to a 1,000,000 MNT within a short period. His business is located in a popular spot of the market where he attracts many customers. He wants to expand his business in the future. He is requesting 800,000 MNT to purchase more varieties of shirts for his clothing sales business.

name: Noemi
description: Noemi is thirty-nine years old with two children, who are both minors and in school. She has made her living for the past fifteen years washing and ironing for other people who pay for her services. She offers this service in her clients' homes.  The loan that she is requesting from Fundación Campo is to repair the roof of her house, which it needs in order to be livable—that is, in order to protect them from sun and rain and so that they can feel safe at night, and have privacy. She tells us that after paying back this loan, she will request another in order to continue improving her home.

name: Sonia
description: Sonia is a member of the "Juntos Podemos" communal bank. Sonia is 46 years old, single and has three children. She looks after her home and also has a business making traditional boots for customers. Sonia has had the business for some time and it is going well thanks to her determination. Sonia is applying for a loan in order to continue working and keep on supporting her family.  Sonia is applying for this loan in order to buy leathers and other materials.  Sonia is very grateful for this loan and promises to make her repayments.

name: Naseem
description: Naseem is a hardworking, 58 year old woman. She is successfully running a small general store. She has become popular in her community for providing good quality products and makes enough to meet the expenses of her children. Currently, she is requesting a loan of 30,000 PKR  to purchase more grocery items including grains, peas, flour, sugar and tea to cater to the maximum number of customers to generate a healthier source of income. She is positive about her future earnings and will spend part of her income on buying more items for her store.

name: Jamson
description: Jamson is a hardworking married man with six children living in Kamwenge, Uganda. He also takes care of eight more dependants because his home is near the school where they study. Jamson used his previous loan to buy bags of fertilizer for his coffee farm.Jamson makes and sells local brew and produce though he also earns more income from farming and working as a builder, which has helped him improve his family's living standards. In his struggle to educate his children and maintain a stable income for his family, Jamson is limited by little capital and scarcity of raw materials to make the brew. He is requesting a loan to buy more raw materials such as sorghum, millet and others to make brew for sale.

name: Lan
description: Mrs. Lan is a hardworking woman who is 26 years old. She is married  and has two children. She needs loan to build a sanitation latrine to improve the health of her family and also for protection of their environment. Her family’s income is from husbandry, so they have regular monthly income to repay the loan as scheduled.

name: Thelma
description: Thelma A. is a 50-year-old married woman who supports her family by engaging in her general store and tricycle business. She lives in Barangay Daan Banwa, Kabankalan City, Negros Occidental with her 46-year-old husband, Eusebio, who drives their own tricycle.  They have 3 adult children who are between 16-26 years old.  Thelma has been a member of NWTF-Project Dungganon since 1998 and has improved her living conditions with the help of her loans from NWTF and through her own efforts. By working hard in her general store and tricycle business, she is gradually making her family more economically stable. She now earns an average monthly income of $140.  She is now borrowing 15,000 PHP for the operations of her general store and tricycle business. This will be her 16th cycle loan from NWTF-Project Dungganon. Her previous loan of 25,000 PHP, which she paid off well within its term, was just another step in her journey towards economic freedom. Thelma aspires to elevate her family’s living conditions and ensure their future wellbeing by following the “Dungganon” way.
