About NWTF: In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means Honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress out of earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem that is bestowed to a member of a community who has earned respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work.

name: Zhenishbu
description: Zhenishbu is 38 years old and she is married.  She lives with her husband and they are raising four children.  She has a high school education and she raises livestock and grows crops with her husband.  They started doing this 20 years ago with the purchase of livestock for 5,000 som (KGS).  Thanks to her hard work, Zhenishbu now has three horses, two cows and ten sheep on her farm.  Their monthly income is 10,000 som (KGS), and they also work a 1.30 hectare plot of land, on which they grow barley.  With the goal of developing her business further, Zhenishbu has turned to Bai Tushum Bank for a loan of 35,000 som (KGS) to buy heifers to increase her head of livestock.  She plans to use the income from this loan to further increase her head of livestock and she wants to save up money to make repairs on her home.

name: Mailyn
description: Mailyn is a married woman with two children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Mailyn is 42 years old and her children are in school.  Mailyn has a food vending business in the Philippines. Mailyn requested a PHP 10,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy ingredients like meat, fish, spices, cooking oil, additional utensils and other materials for her food production business.  Mailyn has been in this business for 10 years. She would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Noah
description: Noah is a 32-year-old married man with two children living in Masindi, Uganda. He has been a policeman for five years. Peace and harmony are virtues he respects. He feels that the best way to experience them is to be in a position to provide peace and harmony to others and that is why he joined the police force. With his income he has been able to pay the school fees for his children and to buy land despite the challenges of a low salary and price fluctuation. Noah intends to use the loan to renovate his house.

name: Janett Del Socorro
description: Janette del Socorro has a business selling general merchandise. Her business is located in the market and the majority of her clients know that she gives them accessible prices. She starts her days very early in the morning to set up her stand and to attend to her clients.  She requests a loan to purchase uniforms, shirts, skirts, suits, shoes, cosmetics, bath towels, bed sheets, and pants. This is not the first loan that she has accessed for her business.

name: Jamina
description: Jamina is a 45-year-old woman married to Nurul, 60 years old. They live in a small town, Dhupguri, in Jalpaiguri district. She is blessed with four children. All of them are now totally involved in studies. Jamina and her husband are basically illiterate and only know how to sign their names. In spite of being illiterate, they have a keen interest to give education to their children.   Jamina herself is busy in housekeeping, while her husband makes foundations for houses in their rural area. The profit that comes from this business is not sufficient for them to cover their family expenses along with their children’s education.   Jamina now decided to give financial support to her husband by taking the loan from BJS (Kiva’s partner) so that she can help her husband to buy more raw materials or supplies like wood, bamboo, straw, ropes, etc. for making firm foundations for houses. She is very much confident that she can earn more profit by increasing the quantity as well as quality of those raw materials.   In the future, she wants to extend her business to provide her family a better pakka (concrete) house for living comfortably and to give her best to establish her children. She is very much obliged to Kiva and BJS, as they came into her life as a light of success.

name: Nora
description: Nora is 19 years old. She is single and has no children. She lives in her parents' house, situated in the city of Santa Rosa, and her greatest wish is to continue going to school and have a career. She is known for being a very hard-working young woman, and she demonstrates this in her uncle's restaurant, where she receives a good salary. But her priority is to study for a career in agronomy. In this way she can contribute to the family expenses, but to do that she needs to prepare herself. It is for that reason that she tries to exert herself in her work. There, she relates that she feels comfortable, since she has the opportunity to socialize with a number of people. This will be her third loan with MFP, and she has been very punctual in her past payments. She hopes to benefit once more from the help of all of you to reach her goals.  The money that she is applying for will a great help in paying the matriculation fees of the institution where she will begin to study.

name: Roberto José
description: Condega, located within the Estelí department, is known as the land of the potters because of its arts and hardworking people.  Roberto lives there, is happily married, and is a businessman who has a hardware store where he sells building materials.  He also raises livestock and is an entrepreneur with five children, but only two still depend on him and he must provide them with an education and prepare them as he did with the other three.  This gentleman has ten years’ experience in selling hardware and 30 years in managing livestock.  He has been successful and has improved his home and provided an education for his children.  Today Roberto needs to invest in two steers to fatten up so that he can take advantage of the best grasses on his farm.  He approached CEPRODEL for a loan which he plans to invest to help increase his income and improve his quality of life.

name: Rodelyn
description: Rodelyn is 33 years old and has six children. Rodelyn is married, and five of her children are currently in school.  Rodelyn is in the agricultural business of pig fattening in the Philippines. Rodelyn requested a PHP 11,000 loan through NWTF to buy feeds and other supplies to raise her pigs.  Rodelyn has been in pig fattening for two years now, and has borrowed three times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Rodelyn would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Mucungwe Group
description: Férdinand is part of the Mucungwe group, and lives in Bubanza.  He is 41 years old, and married to Suzanne.  Together they have six children, aged between three and eighteen years old.  Four of his children attend school.  Férdinand has been selling Primus beer for six years.  This will be his first loan with the field partner Turame.  He will use his Kiva loan to increase his business capital, and buy eight cases of Primus beer to resell.  In this way, he hopes to increase his earnings.  In the coming years, Férdinand would like to buy some land to grow food produce, and see his children study.

name: Reina Isabel
description: Reina, 34 years old, went to school up to the third grade. Her parents separated and she was left living with her mother who didn't have enough to cover household expenses, much the less to be able to continue with schooling. Reina is a single mother. She has two children, one age 17 and the other age 10.  Only her younger daughter is a student right now, but they both depend economically on her.   She makes cheese tortillas to sell, work that has been her source of income for many years. Since she was young she worked in this business.  Her mother taught her how to earn a living since she was little.   Reina gets up at 4:00 am to to everything in the process of tortilla-making and leaves for the market to purchase cheese, which the tortillas include. She doesn't have any other sources of income, she has always worked in this business, no one else is involved in the work, and her schedule for sales is from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.  The loan will be used as working capital to purchase basic supplies for her business such as cheese and corn. With this money, she will buy in bulk and will store the supplies in her house to be able take out what she needs every day.  Reina will be able to be relaxed since she will have her own funds and won't have to worry about looking for someone to loan her the money.   Reina hopes that her sales grow and also to have more income and to be able to cover all her needs and those of her children. The earnings will be invested in making the payments and expanding the business.

name: Tiessiri Group
description: The women of the Tiessiri group are all married. On average, they are 35 years old and have 3 children. They all live in extended traditional families in the village of Yamadibougou, prefecture of Barouéli, sub-prefecture of Konobougou in the Ségou region (fourth administrative region  of the Republic of Mali).  They met through family ties and are engaged in the sale of shop goods, salt and wheat flower. The women of the Tiessiri group are on their ninth loan, which will be used to purchase shop goods, salt and wheat flower.                                                                                    INDA S. gets her supplies of shop goods almost every a week at the Konobougou market. She sells the goods in the village center, for cash or credit, to a customer base of women and men.  She hopes to make an average monthly profit of 20,000 CFA francs that will be used to pay the loan installments, to cover health, food and schooling expenses, the rest will be reinvested in the business.

name: Evangeline
description: Evangeline is 61 years old and married with 4 children.  She lives in Señor, Sinacaban, Philippines.  Evangeline is a farmer who raises pigs to earn a living. She has been doing this for 10 years. She has requested a loan to buy additional feed.Evangeline has been a member of PMPC for 7 years. In the future, Evangeline hopes to improve and expand her business.

name: Bonifasi
description: At a tender age, starting a new family and home with a small piece of land is a challenge for people in the Kitale area of Kenya. Bonifasi, a lovely family man overcame this and has been practicing mixed farming for the past ten years. His primary source of income has been selling eggs, milk and some personal business he engages in to supplement his meager income.   Bonifasi passionately loves poultry farming and feeding his poultry makes him very proud. Waking up every day in the morning to collect eggs from his poultry makes him feel fulfilled. Although this humble father makes a profit through selling poultry, the biggest challenge he faces is meeting the demand of the market that is available. He is seeking a loan to buy additional poultry.   Through Juhudi Kilimo, which is an institution that serves poor, small-landholding farmers, Bonifasi has acquired both financial and technical training. With the loan, he intends to increase his egg production from one crate a day to three crates a day. A crate of eggs goes for 450 KES, and with three crates, he will be making 1,350 KES per day. With the loan, he will be able to increase his income and move from subsistence to more commercial farming. With this loan, he will be able to improve his living conditions and enhance his food security and that of his community.

name: Ebtihaj
description: Ebtihaj, 27 years old and a single lady, lives with her mother and sister after their father passed away. Her only brother is married and helps in supporting the family as much as he can.   Ebtihaj feels that getting support from her brother is a lot to ask of him as he has his own family to look after, so she has recently started a small business at home selling clothes and blankets. Now Ebtihaj is applying for a youth loan to bring in more clothing items to increase her revenue.

name: Chuacante I Group
description: The women from the mujeres Chuacante group live in a popular tourist destination, San Pedro La Laguna, Lake Atitlan. They enjoy their community and are proud to have lived in it since childhood. Amongst the highlights of living in their town is the fact that they all own land there and enjoy a healthy church life and festive season, such as the town fair coming up in early June. The microcredit group that they are part of has brought them closer to each other through “unity and love amongst us,” as Norma G. described her experience. 	When at home or in the workplace, these women, who are mostly mothers, dedicate their lives to weaving. Some are bead-workers and others are dedicated to selling fruit and vegetables.  The weavers make traditional clothing such as colorful belts, aprons and tops (guipiles) and the bead-workers make bead belts and bracelets. They sell this merchandise to intermediaries who take it all over the region and re-sell it to stores, tourists and shoppers.  	Norma G. began her business a few years ago and took out very small loans at high interest. Recently, she has switched over to loans of virtually no interest, which are generously provided online. She can now confidently take out large loans (and growing) of 340 USD and with it help pay the wages of her 6 employees who work with her to produce many more products than before, and sell them for cheaper, while still making a profit. 	When asked about how their business was going, they complained about the rainy season and the drop in sales during this time of the year. They said that this lull in sales didn’t mean less work, but a whole other load to be taken care of.  The credit that they receive from microlenders goes towards more cloth and string, which they can buy by bulk and get a cheaper deal. At the same time, they can invest in their business to produce better and more products. Secundina E. said that she “could see a difference” from the time she began to take out loans. She explained that she could now buy more, for less money, and realize larger profits.  	The hard work, combined with the loans, allows them to successfully send their children to public school, and accomplish what Josefa B. described as one of her largest dreams: to create a successful business and make it grow to the point where loans are no longer needed, and financial self-sustainability of the family and business are reached and maintained.

name: Sylivia
description: Sylivia lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is single with four children. Two children go to school.   She sells fresh fish at the market on a retail basis. She serves all kinds of people. She has been in this business for the last three years. She works for seven days a week.  Sylivia has requested a loan of 200,000 UGX from MCDT SACCO to buy fish. Her major challenges include ever increasing prices of fish and seasonality.   She aspires to buy a plot of land and also start selling dried fish. She lives in a rented house, and the family has access to electricity, but does not have access to piped water. Her major expense includes food and school fees.

name: Phuong
description: Phuong would like to take a further loan to buy many kinds of noodles and other food to sell from her stall. Phuong's previous loan enabled her to increase her sales and earn a higher income to support her family. She hopes that another loan will assist her in increasing the size of her business, attracting new customers and increasing sales. She also hopes that through the loan she can increase her income and improve her family's living conditions.

name: Irma Veronica
description: Irma is 28 years old. She is a single mother who has two children: John, who is 11 and goes to a local school, and Sheila, 4, who stays with her mother. She has been raising chickens and hens for ten years. She buys the chicks, takes care of them and feeds them every day, and when they are big, she sells them.Besides this activity, she washes clothes and cleans houses, which helps her to feed, educate, and buy her children's clothes, and pay the rent of the place where they live.Irma will use the money to buy three dozens chickens, concentrated feed, corn, and vitamins to increase her production and generate the income she needs to cover her and her children's basic needs. In the future, she would like to own a house.

name: Fabio Nelson
description: Fabio is a humble farmer, who goes to work on his farm everyday. He is completely dedicated to his work. This man only thinks about progressing, and he delivers a good product since he knows that many people consume it. Because of this, every drop of sweat that drips from his forehead represents the effort that he puts in so that his products are pure and of quality.  Like every good farmer, he always wants to implement repairs and improvements for his crops, but he knows that these repairs and implementations are very costly. For this reason, he requests a loan to adapt his farm and to buy supplies, such as fertilizers and irrigation, to maintain his fruit crops. His only goal is to improve his way of growing, which will make his work easier and will ensure his clients get a quality product.

name: Irene
description: Irene continues to be a member of the Communal Bank “Reyna de Los Angeles de Urquillos”.  She sells food products such as rice, sugar, milk, cookies, and oil.    On this occasion, she is requesting a loan in order to buy sacks of rice, sacks of sugar, milk, and cookies in bulk so that she can keep her grocery store in operation.  Irene has been in business for several years and is doing very well thanks to the effort she puts into her work.  She is pleased with the loan and promises to complete the payments.

name: Norah's Group
description: Norah is 50 years old and has five children. She is a group leader representing her group formed by 14 farmers in Webuye District, Kenya.   Norah has been farming with One Acre Fund for years now, having joined the program for the first time in 2009. This decision was largely a result of her desire to get the best quality fertilizer and hybrid seeds.   Although she described her last harvest as excellent, Norah believes she can have a better one this year by continuing to work alongside One Acre Fund. She has also decided to purchase a solar light as part of her loan, which she is very excited about, as it will allow her to have an overall improved quality of life.  Obtaining this loan means that Norah's Group will be able to receive a total of 14 solar lights, as well as farming inputs to plant a total of 7.75 acres.

name: Debora
description: Deborah A. is currently in the business of selling foodstuffs in her restaurant and is requesting a loan to stock more foodstuffs to sell.  Deborah is 38 years old and is married to a husband who is a police man. She has two children who both attend school.  With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to extend the floor of her restaurant.  BRAC's holistic approach to poverty alleviation and empowerment of the poor encompasses a range of core programs in economic and social development, health, education, and human rights and legal services which are delivered through an extensive network of village organizations. BRAC has become one of the world's largest NGOs as a measured by the scale and diversity of its interventions.  In 2007, BRAC started operations in Southern Sudan. The microfinance program, which is targeted towards returning war refugees, has already formed 418 village organizations with more than 14,000 women members.

name: Ngo Thi
description: Mrs Ngô Thị Bảo is 30 years old. She is a TYM fund member since 2007. Her husband is a carpenter, she raises pigs, poultry and takes care of their 2 young children. Her husband work is stable, her animal raising business is good. They make a good combined income of 3.500.000 VND a month. For this loan cycle, she is requesting 6.000.000 VND to invest in her husband's business: to buy wood.    Translated from Vietnamese by Khang Ho-Si, Kiva Volunteer

name: Helena
description: Helena M. is from the town of Katipunan. She is 48 years old. Helena is married and has 3 adult-aged children. To make a living, Helena owns & operates a business venture in the retail sector, operating a specialized retail store. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling ready-to-wear clothes in the local community. Helena has been engaged in her business for over 3 years and earns approximately 4,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2006, Helena joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Helena has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5,000 PHP from PMPC. This previous loan was used to purchase additional products to sell. Helena is requesting a new loan of 5,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional inventory and working capital. This loan will be the 6th loan taken out by Helena from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About PMPC: Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Elvira
description: Elvira has a store located in the Munaypata zone of our city.  Her home is located two blocks away, on the same street.  She carries a large variety of products, despite the fact that the space she occupies is small.  Elvira is married and has 3 daughters, ages 22, 15, and 12.  They are all studying, one in the university and the other two in school.  Her husband is a locksmith and works in the Obrajes zone of the city.  They tell us they started with nothing and, through hard work, managed to buy a little house and put themselves in an acceptable financial situation.    They are very proud of their work, and always demonstrate responsibility with their loan payments.  They are a very tight-knit family.  Elvira’s wish is to see her daughters all become professionals.  She will use the money from the loan to buy merchandise to supply her store.  She is very grateful to Emprender and Kiva for the confidence they’ve shown in her by granting credit. 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 Translated from Spanish by Mary Lynn Malaby, Kiva Volunteer

name: Setu
description: Setu is a 29-year-old mother with 2 children and has a small business of selling vegetables (cabbage, eggplant, cucumber) in her community to earn a living. She has been doing this for more than a year. Setu has requested for a loan to buy vegetable seeds, chemicals, a wheelbarrow, a water tank, a rake, a shovel, hand gloves, and safety boots to assist her in running the business. Setu hopes to expand her business by using her profit in the near future. She became a member of SPBD in 2014.

name: Margarita Concepcion
description: Margarita started the business because she wanted to feel useful and because she likes sales.  Her children are grown now and can take care of themselves so she has plenty of free time.  She started the business in February 2006, on the patio of her house, selling used clothes.  Later, a neighbor gave her the idea to buy bundles of used clothes which were selling very cheaply and quickly turn them around.  Things have been going well ever since.  Margarita's sales have increased bit by bit and she can now count on a good number of customers who buy used clothes brought from the United States.  She needs a MXN$7,000 loan that she will pay in 10 14-day installments.  She will use the money to buy bundles of used clothes appropriate for the coming spring and summer seasons so that she has a good supply for her customers.Translated from Spanish by Jere Wiseman, Kiva Volunteer

name: July Ann
description: July Ann is a married woman with three children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. She is 25 years old and has two children who are in school.  July Ann has a fish vending business in the Philippines. She has requested a PHP 5,000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase more fish to sell. July Ann has been in this business for 5 years. In the future, she would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Franis Yanira
description: Yanira, who is 41 years old, went to school through third grade. She left school because of the dangers that she had to go through because of the armed conflict. It was for this reason that she worked at helping her mother with the household tasks. Then she married and had two children. One is in eighth grade, and the older one is studying in the second year at the university. It is for them that she, together with her husband, works hard every day.  Yanira is a very hard-working person. She has a store that she tends in order to generate income to help with the household income.  This loan will be destined for buying merchandise for her store, because she has a lot of demand and wants to stock various products in order to have more variety.  Yanira dreams of expanding her store more and continuing to send her children to school so that they can practice professional careers.

name: Linda
description: Linda is a 60-year-old married woman and the mother of ten grown children from Bohol, Philippines. She has run a tricycle transport business for about 20 years. This is the source of their income.  Linda is in need of additional capital for the business. She is asking for a loan to buy spare parts and to repair the tricycle. Through it, the good working condition of the vehicle will be revived.   Linda hopes to make the business successful, so that it will continue to support the needs of the family.

name: Ivan
description: Ivan is a repeat client to the institution; he is married with three children, two of whom are attending school.   He does transport as his major source of income in business. He has done this business for a period of five years. He also deals in selling firewood.   His previous loan helped him to buy shutters for the rentals, courtesy of Kiva lenders.   Ivan has now applied for a loan of ugx.3,000,000 to buy cement, paint and pay labour for the rentals. This will help him finish his rentals and increase his income sources.  Ivan thanks Ugafode for the financial assistance, which has enabled him to buy his own car, which he uses for his business, meet his family financial needs, and so he will be able to finish the rentals.   He is hardworking and honest.

name: Leonita
description: Leonita is 41 years old and married with one child who is in school. She works very hard to provide for them.Leonita runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 20,000 loan through NWTF in order to purchase more groceries to sell.Leonita has been in this business for three years and sells a variety of items such as sugar, soap, noodles and other groceries. In the future, Leonita would like to save enough money to expand her business and repair her family's home.

name: Emely
description: Emely is a married woman with two children. She is 35 years old and she has a business selling frozen foods and different kinds of vegetables such as string beans, squash and eggplants. She has been running her business for almost 1 year.   She is requesting a loan of PHP 20,000 to purchase seeds to plant and vegetables such as string beans, squash and eggplants to sell. Her husband is a worker, and adds to their daily income. Each month, Emely earns PHP 6,000 net income. This helps her support their daily needs, especially her children's education.   She dreams that her business will become more productive so she can continue to send her children to school and to give her family a progressive standard of living.

name: Mourn's Group
description: Mourn, aged 41, lives in a rural area of the Thmor Koul district in Battambang province, Cambodia. She is the married mother of four children, three of whom live with their family, sometimes working as construction workers to support their living. To earn a living, Mourn has been working as a rice farmer for almost 20 years. However, the lack of capital to support her paddy field is still the main challenge for her business.  Mourn has been with Kiva’s partner, VisionFund, for one cycle and she completely repaid her previous loan while the other member is a first loan cycle client. Now, Mourn is leading her group to apply for a loan with VisionFund. As the leader, she is going to use her portion to buy fertilizers and rice seeds for her farmland, and will use a portion to buy gasoline to pump water onto the farmland. Mourn hopes to increase her crop yield in order to increase her income to achieve a better standard of living.

name: Chreb
description: Chreb is 44 years old and has three kids who are in school. She strives for a living via rice farming and sells duck eggs. She has been involved in the current business for several years.   With VisionFund (Kiva’s partner), she is in the first loan cycle, and is seeking an education loan to pay the school fee for her daughter. She hopes that her daughter can get a job after she graduates.

name: Riza
description: Riza is 47 years old and married with seven children, three of whom in school, Riza works very hard to provide for them.  Riza runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 22000 loan through NWTF to buy additional items to sell like shampoo, soap, egg, spices, sardines, etc..  Riza has been in this business for 8 years.  In the future Riza would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Liz
description: Liz is 29 years old.  She is a hard-working and earnest woman who has a great desire to get ahead and be successful in life.  She lives with Segundo, who is a doctor and the father of her only son.  She lives with them in her own house and she loves them very much.  Her motivation is to work and to offer them the best quality of life.  Liz makes a living selling pharmacy products and other health products from a drugstore that she opened in a specially-created area of her own house, which saves on rent.  She started the business more than 5 years ago and relies on her husband who supported her with the capital she needed to buy the necessary merchandise for her neighbors in the area, where they often cannot count on the medicine needed for their ailments.  She considers her business profitable due to strong earnings and regular clientele.  Before starting the business, she found herself in financial straits, as her family grew very rapidly with the arrival of triplets and expenses exceeded her income.  She looked for a solution and decided on this business which right now is going well and has eliminated many of her financial difficulties.  For this reason, she has plans to continue with the business and buy more merchandise so that she will have available inventory to sell.  This is her second loan with MFP.  She is very happy to know that she can count on the line of credit to advance her business.  For this reason she promises to complete her payments and have a good credit record so that she will have more access to credit in the future.  She also says that she feels good about the work of her communal bank and for the support they offer to people who need it.  With the amount she is asking (1200 nuevos soles), she will invest in the purchase of pharmacy products like medicine, pills and others, seeking out the best wholesale prices so she can offer her customers the lowest prices and support their needs.

name: Maria
description: Maria L. is from the village of Wigan Cordon. She is 28 years old. Maria is single. To make a living, Maria owns & operates a business venture in the food sector operating a fishing business. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from catching and selling fresh-water fish to the market. Maria has been engaged in her business for over 2 years and earns approximately 3000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2006, Maria joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Maria has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5000 PHP from ASKI. This previous loan was used to to purchase additional fish to sell. Maria is requesting a new loan of 7000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional fish to sell. This loan will be the 8th loan taken out by Maria from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 29 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly of farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Leonida
description: Leonida runs a sari-sari (variety) store. She sells basic commodities such as noodles, canned goods, cooking oil, soap, and condiments. She has been engaged in that kind of business for four years now. She is from Talibon, Bohol and is a 62-year-old married woman with three grown children. She has requested a loan to buy feed, a sack of rice, and canned goods. These will help Leonida fill her store and improve its variety. Her earnings will augment her income and help her to be able to manage her finances. With these, she would be able to set aside some savings for emergency purposes.In the future, she dreams to expand her business to make it sustainable.

name: Joel
description: Joel is a strong-willed man who pushes his ability when it comes to his poultry business. He is a hands-on businessman and father who never gets tired of supporting his family.   Recently, he availed a loan to purchase bags of laying mash for his poultry business to sustain his chickens and double his income through more produce of eggs.   Someday he hopes to have an expansion of his poultry farm business in a nearby municipality.

name: Vincent's Group
description: This season is not the first one that Vincent is working alongside One Acre Fund. He has been a member for a few years now, having joined the program in 2012 and, although he is the only person featured in the above picture, he is actually representing his group of 10 farmers in Chwele District, Kenya.Vincent is often described by his community as a very hardworking individual and decided to be the one to represent his group because he wanted to help more farmers. Like many of his fellow farmers, Vincent decided he wanted to be part of the One Acre Fund community in order to earn enough to feed his family and hopes to use the profits from this year’s harvest to send his children to school.This loan will not only help Vincent but the whole group, who will receive maize seeds and fertilizer to plant a total of 6 acres of land. Additionally, some of the farmers in the group will be purchasing a solar light so, with this loan, the group will also receive a total of 5 solar lights.

name: Bernadette's Group
description: Bernadette B. is from the village of Pulay, Luna, Isabela. She is 37 years old. Bernadette is the group leader of a five-member group loan offered by ASKI. While each member of the group receives an individual loan, they are all collectively responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults.  Bernadette is single and has two school-aged children. To make a living, Bernadette owns & operates a general store where she sells food & daily use products in the local community. Bernadette has been engaged in her business for over three years and earns approximately 4,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Bernadette joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Bernadette is requesting a new loan of 7,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Bernadette from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 25 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Selevano
description: Selevano is a widower with five children ages 22, 20, 14, 9, and 7. He has a motorcycle (boda boda) business and also earns income from selling milk. He faces a challenge of competition and long distances to his milk customers but hopes to educate his children. Selevano needs a loan to pay school fees for his children

name: Luz María
description: Luz María, 48 years old, is married and the mother of 5 children. She makes a living sewing, which she has done for several years in a small space in her house. She sews uniforms, dresses, seams for her clients, among other things.   Due to the fact that she has numerous orders, she needs to buy necessary supplies to be able to satisfy her clients, who always choose her for her high quality work. She dreams of being able to extend her work space and that her business sales increase, in order to give her children the education and basic welfare they need.

name: Adela
description: Junk, who can believe that there is still money in junk? While many people find it useless, Adela, 54 years old, still finds it as a way to generate a living. Aside from this, she also has a piggery business where she gets additional income for their family necessities.   Since, trash is not well-managed in the country and is just thrown anywhere along the sidewalks and riverbanks, street dwellers usually collect such things that are still recyclable like copper, papers, plastics and metals. After collecting, their next destination is to the junk shop where they sell such for a corresponding price depending on the material. Usually, metals cost higher. Junk shops then stack, clean, and gather huge quantities of these materials and sell them back to foundries and factories.   However, stable income from this kind of business is hardly predictable. Sometimes, the revolving fund that the junk shop operators use is not enough. This is why Adela is taking out a loan worth PHP 22,000 to add to her current revolving fund and also for improving the shop.   With her husband, Emilio, they are truly hopeful that someday their lives will get better and that their children will finish their studies and build decent lives on their own. She meets up with her co-fellowship** members to share stories of her life and business every week and to strength and inspiration from the fellowship and the Word of God she studies.  ** All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans.

name: Humberto
description: Humberto is 55 years old living with his wife who supports him in everything he does.  They have six children together and their house is located in the city of Chincha, a city noted for its hot climate, beautiful beaches and also for being the birthplace of great Peruvian sports heroes.  It’s also well known for its cuisine; its residents are known for preparing very tasty dishes and one of his favorites is the very delicious “Carapulcra con sopa seca” [pork with noodles].  With much dedication, Humberto works as a bricklayer.  He works about 9 hours per day depending on the type of construction job he has.  He believes that he does well in his business because he does good jobs with good finishings.  Humberto is very grateful to Kiva lenders because thanks to the help they’ve given him he will be able to buy a cement mixer which will allow him to have a very necessary work tool to provide better service to his customers which will make it possible for him to continue working and striving toward making his dream a reality: “To have contracts with large firms.”

name: Ayyob
description: Ayyob is a 27-year-old, single man from Jenin City. He lives with his family in a small house.   Ayyob works as an employee in a private company with a very low income. He is also a student in a local university where he studies elementary education studies. He would like to take the BA degree and find a better job to help his family.  Ayyob took a USD loan from Palestine for Credit & Development (FATEN). This loan will help him to buy a new laptop for his studies. By taking this loan, Ayyob will be able to read articles and easily write the reports.  Ayyob appears in the photo with his laptop.

name: 12 Corazones Group
description: The communal bank '12 Corazones' (12 Hearts) will begin their twelfth cycle with Pro Mujer as part of the Panamerican regional hub. The group is made up of nine members and is led by an executive board. Nancy is the president of the board. The businesses that the communal bank members run are varied and include selling meals, fish, clothes, skirts, and cheese.  This loan will benefit the small group of microbusinesswomen that Nancy is a part of. She told us that she joined Pro Mujer six years ago after being invited by a friend who was a client of the institution. Nancy currently runs a business selling meals and she let us know that she started this business several years ago with a small amount of capital to set it up. She also mentioned that she learnt how to run this business from her niece who has a similar business.  The loan that Nancy is currently taking out will be used to increase her capital (buying groceries and meat in bulk) that she will acquire from vendors in the city of El Alto and later use to create meals which she will sell in her workplace. This form of work allows her to generate an income to financially support her family since she is married and has three children.  When asked what she liked about Pro Mujer, Nancy replied that she liked the training and the health service offered by the institution.

name: Hilda
description: The member belongs to the community bank Las Palmeras de Amaybamba. The bank is located in the Huayopata district, which belongs to the La Convencion province and the Cusco administrative division.   Hilda works in the restaurant business. She is an enterprising woman who, by means of this business, hopes that her children can finish school. Her dream is to own a large restaurant. The member is requesting a loan to buy chicken, vegetables, rice, and meat.   The member is grateful for this loan and promises to make all her payments on time.

name: Heng's Group
description: Heng’s group lives in a rural village in Kompong Thom province in Cambodia. Heng makes a living cultivating rice and he also does extra work as village coordinator to support his family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these men and woman to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Maritza  Del Carmen
description: Maritza is a hard working woman that works selling basic grains and beef.  She lives in a neighborhood of the capital city Managua called Neighborhood 380.  She is 38 years old and has a 9 year old daughter that is in elementary school.  Her husband works in a university as the manager of a store.   Maritza's business is selling beef and chicken, which she started two years ago and has gained many customers.  The business has been her income source to help her family.    With this loan she would like to invest it in her house to repair the roof of her porch, which is in bad condition, as well as improve her sewer drain so that she has more security and better living conditions.  In the long term she would like to be able to sell other products to gain more income and customers and to remain in good health to be able to provide an education for her daughter. Translated from Spanish by Donald Allen, Kiva Volunteer

name: Diana
description: Diana is the owner and operator of a general store in Obuasi.  She is requesting a loan to help expand the variety of products she can sell at her general store. During the day, Diana is a schoolteacher and her mother Rose operates the store in her stead. In the evenings, Diana returns to operate the stand. Rose is pictured above.  Diana is a member of the trust group David. The trust group uses peer pressure as a type of social collateral that ensures each member repays their share of the loan.

name: Baba
description: Baba, 22, is proudly pursuing his university degree.  His study years are from 2008 to 2012 in the faculty of Mathematics and Physics at Agjabadi Teacher`s University.  His mother, father and brother are working, and his father pays his tuition fee. Baba wishes to complete his education and start working as a school teacher and so is requesting a loan for 1200 AZN to pay his final year of education.

name: Wariti Group
description: Lubira has been a merchant for 16 years and is a member and the president of the Wariti group. She is a dynamic entrepreneur, 58 years old, a widow, and a mother of eight children, who all go to school. Lubira sells salted fish. She started this business with funds from her family. She displays her goods in a central town market.   She is seeking a loan though Hekima in order to increase her business. [With this loan] she is going to buy two sacs of fish.  In the future, Lubira wishes to increase her capital, build a house, and feed and school her children.  She thanks Hekima for their support of female entrepreneurs who lack access to banking services.

name: Geronima
description: Geronima is 48 years old.  She is married and has 3 children.  She earns a living by raising hogs in the Philippines.  She has been raising hogs for 3 years and also earns additional income from a carenderia (restaurant).  Geronima is borrowing PHP 19000 through NWTF to purchase feed and vitamins for her pigs.   She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Corazon
description: Corazon is married, and works hard to support her family. Corazon has a buy and sell recyclable materials business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for 8 years now.  Corazon requested a PHP 25000 loan through NWTF to buy more recyclable materials to sell.  In the future, Corazon would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Memunatu
description: Memunatu M. sells salted fish, tomatoes, salt, and other provisions at Abura.  She is married and has two children. She has received senior high education and is married to a farmer.   Memunatu helps her husband in taking care of their family with the money she makes from her sales. Memunatu will use the loan to purchase more foodstuffs and provisions to sell. With the new profits from her expanded business, Memunatu plans to reinvest back into her business.

name: Cristina
description: Cristina belongs to the communal bank “Vilcanota”.    Cristina is 55 years old and is a single mother, so she acts as the father and mother for her son. She and her son live in the province of Urubamba which is located to the north of the city of Cusco. She has a small snack shop. She has already worked for several years and she has done very well thanks to all the effort she has put into her work. Cristina is a working mother and an enterprising woman who wants to keep going for her son. She is asking for a loan to buy merchandise such as candies, cookies, sodas, and gifts for this Christmas holiday. In this way she will be able to increase her business' capital and have a bigger income so she can give her son a better quality of life.  Cristina is thankful for the opportunity provided through this loan and she promises to complete her payments on time. Translated from Spanish by Alison Fanning, Kiva Volunteer

name: Josefa
description: The most beautiful thing about Guatemala is its women because they fight to give their families a good chance in life. They are the ones who are concerned with the wellbeing of their children and the family's economic situation. This is true in the case of 45-year-old Josefa, who has to look after her four children who are her motivation to get up every morning and fight to make a living to improve their living conditions.   Her job involves buying and selling stock for grocery stores in her community and it is through doing this that she is able to make an income. Five years ago her husband told her that you can make a good income doing this kind of business and so she took the initiative. The other work she does is in an agricultural supplies store which is also in her community. She has found a big business opportunity because she has customers and doesn't have any other competition in this field.   She will use the loan to buy stock for her general store so she can have a range of goods on sale.  Her personal goals in the next few years, depending on the profit she makes, are to expand her business, buy more land for her children and give them an education so they can become professionals.

name: Elsa Leonor
description: The Nuevos Horizontes (New Horizons) communal bank meets every two weeks in the Jijijapa canton.  This canton is known as "La Sultana del Café" for its extensive fields of incomparably flavored coffee, its cuisine, and the warmth of its people.  This is where we meet Elsa, age 62.  She is divorced, but she has four children from this relationship.  The children are grown and independent.  She has been in her communal bank for over seven years.  She is very happy with everything in the group, with her colleagues, and with the loans that help her a lot in order to get ahead.  She sells all types of clothes door-to-door with the intention of earning a living with which she is able to get ahead.  She works every day because at times she travels.  She also has to leave to collect for her products because she leaves them on credit.  She collects weekly.  Every 15 days she goes to Guayaquil to buy merchandise that she needs.  She has been doing this business activity for eight years.  It is going very well for her, and thanks to this she is able to get ahead by herself.  She will use this loan to buy merchandise like pants, blouses, and t-shirts, among other garments.  Her dream is to have very good health in order to move forward.

name: Aniceta
description: Aniceta is grateful for the loan, and things have been going very well for her. She continues to dedicate herself to farming, raising livestock, handicrafts, selling fruits and vegetables, and raising small animals. She continues to operate a small sales stand near one of the markets of the city of Huancarani. She is happy about participating in the communal bank program of the Arariwa Association, because she is a cheerful and responsible person. On this occasion, she needs the loan to buy merchandise such as vegetables and fruits.

name: Ismael
description: Ismael is 21 years old, and lives with his partner and their two children, ages one and five. He has made a living for the past five years selling ornamental plants. He started his business five years ago with capital that he received in a package when he ended his previous job at a plant nursery. In his time spent working in the nursery, he learned how to grow and cultivate plants, and when he was ready to tackle the trade on his own, he started by planting seeds and growing plants in the patio of his home. He sold his products to clients of various nurseries, and still continues those sales.  His goal is to grow his business a little bit every day, and to increase the amount of seeds and plants he can buy. He wants to buy larger pots for growing beautiful plants that will one day live in the homes and offices of his clients. This goal of growth has led him to request a loan through Kiva and the Mario Santo Domingo Foundation. His dream is to own his own home on a large lot where he can cultivate plants and offer a wider variety of products to fill more niches in the market.

name: Sunyande
description: This is 48-year-old Sunyande.  She is married, and has five children a woman aged 30 (a trader), a 21-year-old male who is in form 5, an 18-year-old male and a 16-year-old male both in form 3, and a 7-year-old girl. She has no additional dependents living with her.   In 1999, Sunyande established her fence posts and wood business. She began her business as a means of assisting her husband with domestic needs. Working 7 days a week and 6 to 7 hours a day, she makes about SLL 600,000 every month from this business. She would like a loan of SLL 3,000,000. Sunyande requires a loan in order to improve her business. She hopes that this loan will enable her to increase her monthly profits to approximately SLL 900,000. In the future, Sunyande plans to educate her children and also she hopes to be a great business woman.     She is thanking you for your support.

name: Sonia
description: Sonia is a member of the Las Surcanitas community bank.  Sonia is separated, is 56, and has no children.  For many years Sonia has been selling books outside of schools in the mornings, and in the afternoons she goes to other schools.  These months are good for her because the school season has started and she has various orders.  She needs a loan of 1200 PEN to buy school books and literature.  Since she has been with Finca her business vision has grown.  She wants to rent a space to sell books.  In Finca she learned to organize herself and manage the business.  Sonia’s dream is to have book stands close to the schools.  She would also like to make a cooperative agreement with the schools.  Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Paulina
description: Paulina L., 52, was born in San Miguel.  She’s a widow and has five children.  They live in their own house in the community of Palmapampa which is an annex in Samugari district.    Paulina is the family breadwinner.  Since she was a little girl her parents taught her how to work the fields.  Paulina is a farmer and she has four hectares of land where she grows bamboo, cocoa beans, coca leaves and barbasco (a plant from which progesterone is synthesized), which are plants native to the jungle in the Apurimac River Valley.  She has been working her land for 23 years and she still enjoys the work, most of all harvesting, because that’s when she feels that the months of hard work are being rewarded and she sees that her harvest is composed of high quality products.  However, it is difficult to transport her crops from her fields to the city of San Francisco which is where the best prices are offered for her grains and coca leaves.  In the future she wants to buy new fields to increase her crops.  This is her 9th loan with MFP and she knows that if she repays on time she will be eligible for future loans more easily as well as not cause problems for her communal bank.  She will use the requested 1000 new soles to buy fertilizer and insecticide to improve her plantings thus obtaining good results.

name: Luis Alberto
description: Thank you for supporting Luis in his business of handcrafted gifts and making garments.  With his last Kiva loan, he was able to buy fabric, thread, paint, wood bases, etc. in large volume and with cash.  His Kiva loan was of great help, because he was able to increase production, decrease his costs and increase his sales as well as his customers.He is currently applying for a Kiva loan  with which he will buy wood, thread, paint, lacquer and cloth, in order to have a good production of handicrafts, just in time for the approaching school and carnival seasons.  His investment will be very successful just filling orders.

name: Henry
description: Henry is 36 years married with 4 children. Henry is a primary school teacher and also does retail trading as another source of income. He also does tree planting to protect the environment. Henry has managed to look after his family using the income from those resources.  He has applied for a loan of ugx 1,200,000shs to boost his retail shop by buying more stock for trade in order to meet his customer’s needs.    His dream is to own the biggest shop in his region. He believes with continous financial boost his dream will soon come to pass.  He is honest and hardworking.

name: Santos Evaristo
description: Santos is a small-scale farmer who grows beans, wheat and corn.  He has more than 20 years experience in this line of work because his parents started him growing these crops when he was young.  They are highly nutritious foodstuffs which form an important part of the Nicaraguan diet as beans are the basic ingredient of the traditional dish 'gallo pinto', and wheat and corn are used to make the delicious tortillas which are indispensable to Nicaraguan cuisine.    Santos is grateful to the people who will support him in his noble cause by providing loans to entrepreneurial farmers so that they can fulfill their dreams.  Without this opportunity, they would be unable to grow their businesses and support their families.

name: Hanan
description: Hanan is married with two children. Her husbend used to work in Israel but after the closure he helps her in her business.  Hanan established her workshop six years ago and currently has three workers in addition to herself and her husband. The sewing workshop is the only source of income for the family. She buys the cloth and sews it. She appears in the photo at her business.  Hanan has approached FATEN for 1,500 USD to buy a new sewing machine.
town: Taqou' Village, Bethlehem City, West Bank

name: Islomidin
description: Islomidin S. is 39 years old and married with three school-aged children. Islomidin has been in the business of selling cows for over eight years. He buys them from villagers and throughout the nearby province to raise them for resale to abattoirs and farmers. His wife has been a fruit seller for two years. Islomidin is requesting a loan of $1,500 USD to purchase additional cows. This loan will allow Islomidin to expand his business and better provide for his family.   More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History  Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Melati Putih Group
description: Kadek is 41 years old and lives in Pejarakan, North Bali.  She is married and has three children, aged 25, 17  and 10.  Her two sons are in school and her older son is already married.   Her husband works as a farmer.  Though Kadek often helps her husband, she also raises pigs in her yard to supplement her family’s income.  She has been raising pigs for five years.    Kadek is the head of the Melati Putih group, which is made up of 10 neighbors from the same village.  This is the group’s first loan with MUK.  With the Rp.1,000,000 that Kadek receives, she will purchase two piglets and pig feed.  She plans to sell the piglets after five months for use as pork.  With her earnings, she plans to purchase more pigs.  With the income from her pig raising, she hopes to be able to pay school fees.

name: Carmelo Antonio
description: Carmelo is originally from Urabá in Colombia, a place he had to leave owing to the critical level of violence that the town was experiencing.  Since then he has been living in Itagüí, a town in the metropolitan area of Medellín, where he has his own business selling and repairing cell phones as well as taking photos.  At 65 years of age, this entrepreneur feels proud that he has successfully searched for a new way of life and a way of earning his own income.  Carmelo's dream is to turn his business into the most well known in his area.  He currently needs a loan to buy cell phones and cell phone accessories which will make him more income.

name: Annie
description: Annie is a widow and 32 years old with 3 children.  Annie owns and operates a business venture, selling chips.  She has 2 years of experience in this business. Annie needs a loan of WST $1,000 to purchase raw ingredients needed to make products for sale.  She plans to use the profit from her loan to improve the business.  In 2009, Annie joined SPBD to gain access to financial services.  Most of SPBD's clients are unable to borrow from commercial banks because they lack collateral.  This is Annie's 3rd loan with SPBD.     *SPBD evaluates the living conditions of each of its borrowers.  Generally, a loan manager evaluates a variety of social metrics on a scale out of 3 (the higher the number, the better off the person is) and these are averaged for the ""overall social metric score.""  For example, a 3 out of 3 on ""level of education"" would mean that the borrower has graduated from university.    About  SPBD  In 2000, Greg Casagrande founded SPBD to improve the quality of life of people living in poverty in the poor island nations of the South Pacific.  SPBD's philosophy of lending is based on a respect for each individual's innate human ingenuity, drive and self esteem. Please join SPBD's lending team on KIVA to receive on-the-spot updates on SPBD.

name: Nam
description: Nam is a 47-year-old garment factory worker who earns $3 per day. Her husband is a farmer who earns $1 per day. They have three children, all of whom are working, earning $2 per day each. Every month, Nam has to spend $55 on food, $10 on transportation and $15 on other expenses. Nam would like to request a loan of $1,000 to buy a motorbike for use in the family.  Nam wants to embark on a new career that her husband also can share. In this way, they will be able to improve their family income. Nam doesn’t know what that new career will be until she completes this loan and has some start-up money.

name: Francis
description: Francis is a married man with one school-going child. He has a house with electricity and piped water. His greatest monthly expenses are for his family and school fees.  He has operated a pharmacy for the past three years; in addition, his wife also contributes in the family expenses. His potential clients are his local area neighbors. His major challenge is finding customers for his business. He dreams of establishing a wholesale pharmacy in the future.  With the 20,000 Kenya shilling (KES) loan, he wants to purchase drugs for his pharmacy. He decided to join Yehu because of low loan repayments rate.

name: Sakina
description: Sakina, age 53, has had a business selling milk for a period of about four years. Over that time, she has become famous in her area for providing good quality milk. She counts on a good client list and makes enough to contribute to her family's income. Sakina's husband is employed in a mill but his income is not sufficient to meet the needs of the family. She is requesting a loan of PKR 30,000 through Kashf Foundation to purchase another cow. In this way she will be able to increase her sales. She expects a boost in her earnings with her loan and plans to spend her profits on expanding her business.

name: Flora
description: Flora is continuing with her business  selling vegetables and cereals.  She sells her products in various places.  She sells corn, wheat, and barley, and she also sells onions, tomatoes, and squash.  She's had this business for a number of years, and it is doing very well.  Flora dreams of having her own shop where she could sell cereals and vegetables.  She is requesting a loan to buy corn, wheat, and barley, and to buy vegetables such as onions, carrots, and tomatoes. Flora is happy to be getting this loan, and she promises to comply with the payment terms.

name: Isidora
description: Isidora is 56 years old. She is married and lives with her spouse in her house located in San Lorenzo, in the valley in southern  Honduras. For a long time she has worked selling snacks as a street vendor.   Isidora is asking for the loan to buy corn, firewood, vegetables, meat, chicken., milk, rice, beans, etc. With her profits she wants to buy more products to sell and keep progressing and improving her quality of life.   Isidora is a very humble and hardworking person who day to day prepares to go out and sell her products that she prepares every day to offer her customers.   Isidora's dream is to improve her income and finish repairing her home. She wants to re-finish the walls and paint it.  San Lorenzo, Honduras - September of 2014.

name: Adelight's Group
description: Adelight is 40 years old and has 5 children.  She has been a farmer for 19 years and is always said to be a very reliable person.  Even though Adelight is the only one featured in the above picture, she is actually representing her group formed by 11 farmers in Webuye District, Kenya.Adelight started working alongside One Acre Fund a few years ago in 2012, and decided to do so because she wanted to earn enough to feed her family.  Since then, she has seen her life improve, especially in the sense that she has been able to consistently feed her family ever since. This year she decided to represent her group because she wanted to help more farmers.Adelight’s Group will receive farming inputs to plant a total of 5.75 acres of land. Additionally, some of the farmers in the group will be purchasing a solar light so, with this loan, the group will also receive a total of 2 solar lights.

name: Josefa
description: Josefa L. is a widow who lives in Hda. Claudio, Poblacion II, Sagay City, Negros Occidental. She earns her living by a food vending  business.  She has 5 children who are 16 to  32 years old, with 2 of her children having their own families, 1 works and 1 is currently studying.   Josefa joined NWTF-Project Dungganon in 1999 because she aspired for something better for her family. With the help of her past 9 loans from NWTF-Project Dungganon, Josefa has been incrementally lifting her family out of poverty by the sweat of her brow. Her previous loan of PHP 19000 helped her earn a monthly profit of PHP 8000,  uplifting the family's standard of living.  This time, for her 10th cycle loan, she is borrowing PHP 19000, which she intends to use to purchase of more food to sell so that she could continue to save up for future security of her family and her youngest child's education. Josefa L. is a Dungganon woman who is following an honorable path toward the achievement of her dreams.   About NWTF:  In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means Honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress from earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem that is bestowed to a member of a community who has earned the respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work. Help NWTF continue its mission to help the poorest in the Philippines by clicking  the link to the   NWTF Kiva lending team  on Kiva.org to join our team.

name: Clotilde
description: She's single and has a son who attends school. She lives in her parents' house and doesn't support anyone else. She works as a sales promoter for a private company. With the current loan she intends to purchase construction supplies (cement, sand, rocks, bricks, etc.) in order to continue building her house. In the future she would like to own her own business providing marketing services. For that reason she pledges to repay the loan as scheduled, so she can request more loans from Hluvuku. The challenge she faces is getting a license for her business and having a workspace of her own.

name: Lory
description: As a married parent of four children, Lory works hard to support her family.  She has a food vending business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from rice retailing. Lory is borrowing 18,000 PHP through NWTF to to buy ingredients such as meat, spices and cooking oil for her food production business.  Lory has been sustaining her business activities through her past 19 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Sosefina
description: Sosefina P., 34, is married with two children. She has one year of experience in the popcorn business. She sells to the village people six days per week. She expects her weekly net cash flow to be 150 Tala (about $49).    SPBD loans are Sosefina’s only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with the traditional banks, and this is her first SPBD loan. She wishes to use it to purchase corn, an oven, a frying pan, oil, and plastic bags.

name: Armando Efrain
description: Sr. Armando lives in Guayaquil.  He was in the military reserves, but later left the service so that he could acquire his own business.  Armando bought a taxi and now he works every day by himself.    His main concern is crime since he works in very dangerous places where robbers could climb into his taxi.  He is also afraid of his wife and children being able to take care of themselves should something happen to him.  However, his family provides him the strength that needs to pursue the goals that he wants to achieve.    Armando is married and his wife helps with the household chores.  They have three children (ages 6, 10, and 12), all of whom attend a state school.  For this reason, Armando is requesting a loan in order to buy uniforms and school supplies for his children since they are already back in school.  (Armando appears in the photo with his wife and three children.)  He wants to provide them with a better education.

name: Gitangu High Breeders Self Help Group
description: The person raising his hand in the photo is Nicholas, a member of Gitangu High Breeders Self Help Group.He is fifty two years old, married and blessed with five children who have completed school. He earns a living in dairy and poultry farming. He is grateful to Hand in Hand Eastern Africa for the training on enterprise management which has equipped him with skills that has enabled him manage his farming effectively through keeping proper farm records.However, Nicholas is constrained financially and needs money to expand his dairy farming by buying quality fodder for his dairy cows so that they can improve on their milk production. He hopes to generate more income to provide food in his household. He is grateful to Kiva for the financial support and promises to repay the loan promptly.

name: Maricel
description: Maricel is 31 years old and lives in Deboloc, Plaridel, Misamis Occidental. She is married with 2 children.   Maricel has a pig fattening business and earns approximately PHP 1,000 each month doing this type of work. She has requested a loan to purchase feed and vitamins.   Maricel has been a member of PMPC for 8 years. In the future, Maricel hopes to have more savings for her children's education.

name: Mejumaa
description: Mejumaa is a married and has five children who attend school. She owns a house that has electricity, but not piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.  Mejumaa has operated a fish selling business for the last five years, selling at the market to her neighbors and passersby. She faces a major challenge of seasonality in her business. With this KES 50,000 loan, Mejumaa wants to purchase more stock of fish for her business. She decided to join Yehu to acquire financial services for her business.

name: Lineth
description: Lineth, age 35, lives in the Linda Vista neighborhood of New Guinea.  She is the single mother of an 11 year old son who is in sixth grade.  She has worked as an administrative secretary to the Supreme Court of Justice for three years and three months.  She is requesting her third loan from Kiva to finish building a wall and an annex, which will give her family better amenities.  She recently finished her post graduate studies in the Uraccan University.  She is characterized as being very responsible, honest, and having a lot of desire for personal and professional success.  Lineth’s dream is to have work and that her son studies so that he can become an upstanding citizen and useful to society.  Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Kyzzhibek
description: Kyzzhibek is 26 years old, divorced, and has a child. Kyzzhibek has secondary education. She sells soap and detergent products, cosmetics, and perfumes. Initially, she used to sell fruits and vegetables. She has goods of 250,000 som (KGS) in circulation.   Kyzzhibek has applied to Bai Tushum Bank for a loan of 50,000 som (KGS) with the aim of developing her business, by increasing the assortment of goods. Kyzzhibek will invest the funds from the loan in the further development of her business, and will also buy a car.

name: Jacob
description: Jacob is applying for a third loan to support his studies through his graduation in December 2015 at the Maharishi Institute. He has provided the following update on his progress since receiving the second loan: “I have been to attend school everyday because of the stipend that I have received, travelling has been easier. My studies have improved and I look forward to completing my degree.”

name: Thy's Group
description: Thy, a rural villager from the Thmor Koul district, is 26 years old and single. To make a living, she has been providing tailoring services. Having been in this business for five years, she currently can earn about 90,000 KHR per day, and can manage to save about 40,000 each day after offsetting daily living expenses.   This is the microloan for Thy’s group of two.  She is a client in her first loan cycle with VisionFund. Now she is leading her group to apply for a loan. As the leader, she is going to use her portion of the loan to buy fertilizers for her farmland. Thy hopes this loan will enable her to increase her family’s income and to provide them a better living.

name: Namo Group
description: Vongsa’s village sources much of their drinking water from local wells, streams, and collected rainwater.  These sources of water are not safe to drink without treatment by boiling.  Vongsa and his group are excited that the filter was available on a payment plan that made it much more affordable.  Treating drinking water requires cash and time, which now he can shift to other pursuits.  Vongsa and his village also understand the impact unsafe drinking water has on their family’s budgets. The filter is guaranteed for 2 years; within this 2 years filter users, like Vongsa’s family, identify a substantial decrease in illness and associated medical costs.

name: Malali
description: Malali lives in district 15 of Kabul, Afghanistan. She is educated. She graduated from school but then she married. Her husband does not allowing to work. Her husband is a truck driver. He needs money and his wife wants to take a group loan for her husband so that he can buy supplies that he needs for has truck, like  an engine and tires. He wants to establish a close relation with some construction companies so that he can expand his business and support his family.  Note: The picture featured in this business profile is the  husband of the borrower. In Afghanistan, it is culturally unacceptable to many people to post a picture of a woman to the Internet.  However,  the loan is to the female entrepreneur. AFSG only makes loans to women.

name: Tiisetso
description: Tiisetso is a single mother of a 14-year old boy and a 12-year old girl. She is employed and works hard to feed her children and pay their school fees. Tiisetso is smart and understands business. She is one of the founding members of a self-help group looking to change their community. Tiisetso is asking for a loan to buy an eviscerating trough for slaughtering poultry. This equipment will be part of an abattoir being developed by Tiisetso and her group. "I want to play my part in eradicating poverty by employing those in need," says Tiisetso. She is hopeful that in the next 5 years, the abattoir will be supplying meat products across the entire South Africa.

name: Chhern's Group
description: Chhern’s group live in a rural village in Kandal province in Cambodia. Chhern makes a living cultivating rice and she also does extra work as factory laborer to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water.
