Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Maria
description: María is 69 years old, is single, and lives with her sons and daughters in her own home.  She has worked for 20 years in the business of pork and beef sales.  With the help of her two sons she does this work twice a week.  They butcher the pigs and later sell the meat to all of their customers.  She also has her own electric mill to grind corn, where her customers come every day for this service.She lives in the town of San José, Choluteca, in the south of Honduras.  She is an enterprising woman with dreams of geting ahead and she fights day by day to improve her quality of life.  She is requesting a loan to stock her business with more pigs and also buy 6 sacks of concentrated feed for the pigs.  With the support of this loan she intends to increase her income and also her quality of life.  She is a returning client who wishes to work with Prisma and Kiva. Her dream is to have a good business and increase her clientele and at the same time improve her future with her family.San Lorenzo, Honduras - October 2015

name: Jenifer
description: Jenifer lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is single with seven children and four go to school. She takes care of additional family members. She operates a stall selling fish at the market on retail basis. She has been in this business for the last six years. She works seven days-a-week. She gets additional income from rearing cattle. She has requested a loan of 300,000 UGX from MCDT – SACCO to buy fish. Her major challenge includes seasonality and transportation. Her goal and aspiration is to expand her business to selling fruits and vegetables. She lives in a rented space and the family has access to piped water and electricity. Her major monthly expenses include school fees.

name: Majed
description: Majed is a 47-year-old married man with three children who lives in Tarik A. Jadidah in Beirut. When he was 27, he started working in a detergent manufactoring plant. In 2001 he opened his own shop, where he manufactures detergents and sells them to the nearby supermarkets. Majed wants to borrow $1,200 in order to buy more raw materials for his business, so that he can increase his production and sales.

name: Emelia
description: Emelia is 56 years old and married with two children. Emelia works very hard to provide for them.Emelia runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 30,000 loan through NWTF to buy more stock to sell in her general store.Emelia has been in this business for four years and sells a variety of items such as canned goods, soft drinks, beer, candies, cereals, coffee, shampoo, etc. Emelia would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Old-Lady
description: This is Old-lady from Liberia.  She lives in Paynesville North, which is a suburb of the capital city of Monrovia.  Paynesville North has the largest market in Montserrado County.  The area is home to “round time marketers”, traders that travel to the interior to purchase various goods to sell throughout the county.  As a result, there is a high concentration of wholesalers in the area who distribute to various markets around Montserrado County, including Monrovia.  Old-lady is 32.  She is married and has five children.  Her children's ages are between 15 and 5.  They  all are currently living at home and in school.   Old-lady has owned her own table business selling pepper, red oil, cold water, etc. for the past three years.  She will use the loan proceeds to purchase pepper, red oil, cold water, etc.  On average, she works 10 hours at her business.  She started her business with money given to her by her husband. She transports her merchandise by shared taxi.  She cites the rainy season as her biggest challenge.  Her favorite part of her business is the profit she makes every time.  In the future, she would like to buy a piece of land and build a house.  She is grateful for your support!

name: Corazon
description: Corazon is a hard-working entrepreneur who has a fishing business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 10,000 through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to buy additional fishing nets for her fishing business.  Corazon has been in this business for nine years. She earns additional income from raising pigs.  Corazon has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts, with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: 031004010003.thiệu Chính Group
description: Thanh works in agriculture raising cattle. She is applying for a loan to purchase more baby cattle to raise and sell in the future. She is 47 years old and married with two children. Thanh is the group leader of the 031004010003.Thiệu Chính solidarity group, which consists of 8 members. She lives in Thieu Hoa district, a rural town in Thanh Hoa province.  In 2012, Thanh joined Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women to improve her business. She has successfully repaid two loans from Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women. Thanh has been involved in this business for more than 10 years. The main hardship that she faces in her business is the lack of capital.  With her business profits, Thanh hopes for her business to do well, for her children to find good jobs, and to maintain a successful business.

name: Firuza
description: Firuza is the type of young woman you don't meet very often: she is only 18 years old and already an independent seamstress.  She sews women's clothes and is very skilled at her work.  She helps her parents to support the family and makes her own money, working from home.  Her father works as an electrician in an aluminum plant.  Her mother is a homemaker.  Firuza's sister also works as a seamstress.  The sewing machine that you can see in the photo is actually very old, older than Firuza herself.  For this reason, Firuza wants to buy a sewing machine of the "Yamata" brand, so that she can continue to grow her business.  Because she doesn't have enough money for this purchase, she is taking a loan.  This loan will help her to buy a new sewing machine and have a stable job.

name: Song
description: Song O. is a fisherman who lives in Taream Village, Siem Reap Province. He has been fishing for four years in Tonle Sap Lake and earns about $2.66 per day. His wife, Mrs. ChO. Nun, 32, is a farmer and purchases rice to stock for resale. Nun can earn about $3 per day. They have one small child. Now O. is seeking a loan of $700 to purchase fishing tools to expand their fishing business. They hope this loan will help to improve their family’s income and living conditions.

name: Hilda
description: Thank you for helping Hilda, who with her previous loan from Kiva managed to buy an overlock sewing machine. She now has a greater work capacity and an employee who helps her with her work. Hilda has received more orders and has gained the trust of her clients because she finishes orders on time and earns more money. She sends the following message to her financial backers: “I am very grateful because you have opened the doors of my business for me; what a joy it is that there are people who help us to achieve our dreams”. Currently Hilda is applying for a new loan with which she will buy fabric, thread, buttons, and zippers. She plans to be successful because the end of the year is approaching and she will be prepared for it.

name: Sulait
description: Sulait is a married man aged 42 years with seven children, five of whom are attending different schools. He lives with his family and mother who is very old and two of his nephews who lost their parents. He is in the produce business where he purchases coffee, beans, and maize, and he also carries out agriculture, which he considers as his side business. He started his business in 1999.He works seven days in a week and 13 hours per day and started his business because a friend advised him to carry out such a business after he explained to him the good profits one can make out of such a business. He is requesting this loan to buy coffee seedlings for planting this season so that he can increase his productivity. His clients are traders from nearby villages.His future hopes are to be the leading supplier of coffee in his home area and to educate his children. The main challenge he faces is too much drought, which affects the quality of coffee. He is hardworking and honest.

name: Mary's Group
description: Mary lives in Senende village in Vihiga, Kenya with her husband and 7 children. The community of Senende village collects their drinking water from an unprotected spring because there is no piped water supply in this part of Vihiga Kenya. This water is easily contaminated with bacteria that can cause diarrhea and other water-borne diseases, often making Senende’s inhabitants sick and unable to work or attend school.  A new chlorine dispenser offers a solution to the burden of sickness caused by unsafe drinking water. The dispenser is installed at the local water source, where users turn a valve to add chlorine to their jerricans, then collect water as usual. The chlorine disinfects the water and provides residual protection from recontamination. In Senende, 15 households will benefit from having access to the dispenser and safe water. Mary has volunteered to be the dispenser promoter, who is responsible for refilling the chlorine and encouraging the rest of the community to treat their water and keep themselves and their families healthy. Two other volunteer promoters (Joan and Henry) from the surrounding community who are part of this group loan.  Senende village needs a loan to cover the costs of installing and maintaining the dispenser. Mary believes that the dispenser will provide safe water that will help prevent waterborne diseases. The Kiva loan will be repaid by Evidence Action (www.evidenceaction.org) on behalf of the community, through the sale of carbon credits. Using the chlorine dispenser generates carbon credits by avoiding the need to boil water to make it safe to drink. The sale of carbon credits, to organizations and individuals wanting to reduce their carbon footprint, will be used to repay Kiva lenders and also to make sure that Mary’s community can have access to safe water now and in the future.

name: María Dolores
description: Maria Dolores R. (44) lives in San Lorenzo in a neighborhood called Cerrito. She is married to Pastor Severiano Vergara (64) and both have 4 children; each one of them works   independently.   As the owner of DESPENSA ÑA MARIA, Maria Dolores plans to enlarge her grocery store in order to offer a wider variety of products and attract more customers. The difference between Maria Dolores’s grocery store and the competition is that since she is a lovely person, everyone in the neighborhood knows her and wants to help her. Consequently, they prefer to buy goods from the Despensa Ña Maria instead of others' grocery stores. In rural areas in Paraguay, the Despensas could be considered as a meeting point, where people not only buy products but also gather and gossip. That is why is Despensas are a very profitable business in those areas.

name: Merlita
description: Merlita G. did not pursue her studies in college. She once worked as a maid in one of the rich family in Manila to help her parents earn a living. After many years of serving as a housemaid, she married Romeo G. and they are blessed with four children. They help each other to earn a living and support the studies of their children because they wanted them to become successful in the future. Her family lives peacefully in the village of Lactawan Solano, Nueva Vizcaya.   Romeo, her husband, earns a daily income by operating a tricycle transport business. Because his business income was not sufficient, Merlita manages a tailoring business using her own knowledge and skills in sewing. She also raises hogs to provide her family with a better living. Her tailoring business is working well, but because she wants to improve and develop it, she is requesting a loan of PHP 20,000 from KIVA lenders to use as additional business capital. She knows that the amount she is borrowing will be very beneficial in making her business productive some day.

name: Julia Xiomara
description: Julia Xiomara is an enterprising and hard-working 31 year old woman.  She works in an independent way.  She sells general merchandise.  She started her business through her own efforts.  She started selling clothes, and she later decided to turn to the commercial houses to sell cosmetics.    Upon seeing that she had regular customers, she decided to maintain this business.  She did this because she has an obligation to support her two children.  That is why she is asking for this loan to buy raw material.  She dreams of improving and continuing to provide her family with their daily bread. Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Chynarkul
description: Chynarkul is 50 years old. Alone, she has raised 4 children. Chynarkul works as a teacher of the Kyrgyz language in the school of the Bokombaevo village. As a source of additional income for her family, she has also been growing crops and raising livestock for the past 20 years, having started her business with a purchase of a dairy cow. Thanks to Chynarkul's hard work, her herd currently includes 2 dairy cows with offspring, 10 goats and sheep, and 2 horses, while the business' monthly income amounts to roughly 10,000 som (KGS).  As the autumn season is particularly busy in agriculture, Chynarkul, like many other farmers, needs financial support in order to develop her business. In light of this, Chynarkul has turned to Bai Tushum & Partners for a loan of 80,000 som (KGS) to purchase livestock for fattening. She plans to invest her profits from this loan into further expansion of her business.

name: Osman M.
description: This is 38-year-old Osman M. He is married and has four children aged 11, 8, 5 and 7 months, three of whom are going to school. He has no other dependent.In 2004, Osman M. established his used tyres business. Working six days a week and 11 hours a day, he earns about Le 2,545,000 every month from this business.He would like a loan in the amount of Le 6,000,000. Osman M. has already received and successfully repaid three loans, and now requires a new loan in order to purchase different sizes of used vehicle tyres.In the future, Osman M. plans to build a house, reinvest in and expand his business, and provide quality education for his children. He has completed the payment of his land, and business has improved.He thanks you for your support.

name: Fanny Stella
description: Fanny, 49, is the mother of five children.  She is a responsible mother and has been able to sustain her large family thanks to working as an agricultural producer on a farm. She is requesting a loan in order to initiate her own business, a small operation which she will start with piglets which she will raise and feed in the corrals of her farm.  She took the initiative basically for her children because she wishes to enjoy with them a better life, that they study and that every day they have a reason to smile. Support this businesswoman who wants to show that she can get ahead!

name: Melva De Los Angeles
description: Mrs. Melva de los Ángeles U. V. is 53 years old, and her marital status is married. Doña Melva has 4 children who are all students. Doña Melva's business is selling cheese and cream. She has been in this business for more than 12 years. Doña Melva uses the technique of bringing the products and distributing them to her customers' homes, and during the week she collects the money for her products. The cheese is purchased in Managua. Doña Melva's intention is bring her product to more customers. The financing is used for working capital for which the products are purchased by the quintal, and to make the sale more affordable she travels to Managua, Sauce and other departments. Doña Melva's wish is to expand her business to gain a better quality of live. Translated from Spanish by Heather Nicholson, Kiva Volunteer

name: Rosita
description: Rosita is 64 years old and from the town of Duero, Bohol. She is married with five adult children. She lives with her husband in her home, and he engages in farming. Rosita is also in farming. She has farmed vegetables and spring onions for 10 years now.   She is asking for a loan of 8,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) to buy fertilizer, seeds and a sprayer. This will help so she can maintain a healthy vegetable garden and expect a better harvest soon.  In the future, she hopes to have a bigger farm for an increased business profitability.

name: Nida
description: Nida is 47 years old and married with six children, four of whom are in school. Nida works very hard to provide for them.  Nida runs a business buying and selling charcoal in the Philippines and requested a PHP 14,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional sacks of charcoal to sell. Nida has been in this business for 2 years.  In the future Nida would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Ladie Claire
description: Ladie Claire S. is from the village of Sagay, Camiguin Province. She is 24 years old. Ladie Claire is a widow and has two school-aged children. To make a living, Ladie Claire owns and operates a specialized retail store. The main source of income for her trade comes from a la cart business. She grills chicken parts like chicken feet, hot dogs and intestines, to sell in the local community. Ladie Claire is just starting this business.  In 2009, Ladie Claire joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. Ladie Claire is requesting a new loan of 4,000 PHP which will be used to invest in expanding the business. This will be her 1st loan from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated to further develop her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Madhabi
description: Madhabi is 36 years old. She is from Maynaguri. She lives with her husband, Madhab, and their only son in the village of Tekatuli in the district of Jalpaiguri. She and her husband both completed primary education, and could not continue further studies due to their poor economic condition. Their only son is a student of grade 7 in a local school.  Madhabi's husband is associated with agricultural activities. He cultivates different kinds of vegetables and sells them in the local market. Being a housewife, Madhabi manages all the household work and then assists her husband in the farming activities. Both of them give hard labor to take care of their farmland and to generate income.  Now they have decided to cultivate jute on their farmland, as it is a most useful and profitable crop. So, she thinks this will be a lucrative business because jute is in great demand. It is the high time to cultivate this crop, as it is a rainy season crop.  She has taken a loan from BJS (Kiva's partner) to purchase jute seeds and fertilizers to start cultivation as early as possible.  She is much hopeful to earn a good profit from this new cultivation, which will help her to reach to her goals of leading a decent lifestyle, educate her son properly and purchase an auto-rickshaw to give it on rental for another means of income.  She gives her thanks to BJS and Kiva.

name: Lorn
description: Mrs. Lorn S. (pictured above), and her husband, Mr. Broshun Nhoem, have been married since 1998 and have two young daughters. One of them attends school and the other one is still a baby. The family lives along National Road Number Five about seventeen kilometers from Phnom Penh City.   Mrs. Lorn S. and her husband sell fish, making their purchases from fisherman in the village and then transporting them to Prek Phnao market to sell. The couple does not their own shop within the market to sell their fish, and as a result, must spend a lot of money on rental fees which makes it very difficult to support their family. They want to buy their own space at the market, but they do not have enough money.      Therefore, Lorn is asking for a loan of $500.

name: Norma
description: Norma is 62 years old and married with four children. She works very hard to provide for them.  Norma runs a general store in the Philippines and has requested an 11,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy items to sell such as canned goods, personal care products, sugar, eggs, noodles, spices, milk and other snack foods.  Norma has been in this business for two years. In the future, she would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Fidela
description: Fidela A. is from the village of Seaside, Lapasan, Cagayan de Oro City. She is 40 years old. Fidela is married and has three adult children. To make a living, Fidela butchers and sells pork in the market. Fidela has been engaged in her business for over three years and earns approximately 5,000 Philippine pesos (PHP) a month from it.  In 2010, Fidela joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Fidela is requesting a new loan of 5,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional inventory and as working capital. This will be the first loan taken out by Fidela from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.
town: Lapasan, Cagayan de Oro, Misamis Oriental

name: Joseph
description: Joseph is 27 years old.  He started running his mobile-phone money transfer business two years ago.  He has been able to sustain his business because of his hard work.  He has also set up some space for photocopy services in the same business premises.  Joseph also does farming for extra income.  He hopes to open other outlets of his business in the future.  He has requested 20,000 Kes to add E-float to his business.

name: Athanas
description: Athanus is a farmer living in the Siongiroi area with his wife and three children, all of whom are of school-going age. He has been doing farming for eight years with his primary income source being from producing and selling milk, eggs, maize, beans, and sugarcane. He loves farming because of the good returns he gets out of it. He experiences a challenge when there is a season of drought and his crops don't do well and so he succumbs to losses.  Athanus chose Juhudi Kilimo because they give loans to small-scale farmers at low interest rates and their loans have a grace period. This loan will bring in more income because of purchasing the chaff cutter which means his animals will have enough provision of food and hence produce more. Which means more milk, and this will improve their living standards and also cater for his children's school fees.

name: Elsa
description: Elsa is 50 years old, widowed and has 3 children and 2 are married already. She been in a sari-sari store business for 8 years already and it is a profitable business for the family because it earns P 2,500.00 a month that helps them in their daily needs of the family.   She aims to increase her income so she decided to borrowed a loan at GDMPC to buy additional grocery items for sale to increase her store inventory and have more sales so that it will generate more income.  Elsa plan for the future to expand her business to sustain the needs of her family.

name: Alma
description: Alma M. is from the village of Abu, Baylao, Mambajao, Camiguin Province. She is 29 years old. Alma is married and has six school-aged children. To make a living, Alma owns & operates a specialized retail store. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes from buying & selling used clothing or "ukay-ukay" in the local community. She is also making and selling snacks like sweet potato & banana "cues". Alma has been engaged in her business for over 10 years and earns approximately 6000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2011, Alma joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Alma is requesting a loan of 4000 PHP which will be used to purchase additional ingredients like ripe bananas & sugar and as working capital. This will be the 1st loan taken out by Alma from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is an accredited partner of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and reaches out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Trishna
description: This is 26-year-old Trishna B..  She is married and has one child, aged 9.  In 2004, she established  her tailoring shop business.  Working 7 days a week and 7 hours a day, she supports her family.    She has already received and successfully repaid 4 loans from Patan BPW and used her most recent loan to purchase raw materials for her tailoring work.  In the future, Trishna plans to uplift the economic condition of her family.  She thanks you for your support.  In the Kathmandu Valley, clothing is made to order.  Tailor stalls line the streets where store owners sell material and work their sewing machines.  These skilled tailors make school uniforms for children as well as the the traditional women's kurta surwal and men's daura surwal.  With a Kiva loan, BPW borrowers are able to purchase additional cloth material or sewing machines that will increase production and profitability.   This loan was administered by Kiva's local partner MFI, Patan Business and Professional Women. Patan BPW became Kiva's first field partner in Nepal in 2007.  Patan BPW operates throughout the Kathmandu Valley, offering microcredit and business training programs to low-income women.  In addition to providing economic opportunity to their clients, Patan BPW seeks to empower Nepali women within the home and community.  For more information about Patan BPW, visit our partner page and keep an eye out for new loans and borrower updates:  BPW Partner Page.  Join our lending team: BPW Lending Team.

name: Lourdes Rosa
description: Lourdes is 50 years old. She is married and as a result of this union has two children. She was born in the city of Puno. Today she lives in the city of Cusco. Lourdes works in the administrative area of the educational field as a librarian. She works from 7:45 a.m. to 3 p.m. from Monday to Friday. She also has a small beauty salon in her home where she sees customers in the evenings. She has been in this business for several years. It is going well for her thanks to her dedication to her work. At this time Lourdes needs this loan for personal use. Specifically, she needs it for her son’s college tuition.  Lourdes belongs to Los Solidarios communal bank, part of Asociación Arariwa. She is grateful for the opportunity this program offers her. She promises to make all repayments according to schedule.

name: Piri
description: Piri is 46 years old. He lives in the small village of Bolnisi with his wife. He is involved in agricultural activities. In particular, he has 2 calves and a 0.3 hectare plot of land where he grows potatoes, cucumbers and peppers. The harvested products are sold locally at a good price. Piri works hard to ensure a good harvest. He has requested a loan for purchasing calves. After purchasing these calves, he will expand his livestock. He will raise them and sell beef to the villagers. This will increase the income of the family. With increased income they will improve their living conditions. Piri awaits your support.

name: Rabi
description: Rabi is a maize farmer and Babban Gona member. Anticipating a good harvest this season, Rabi has the opportunity to attain yields of up to 8 metric tonnes of maize per hectare of land, 5.5 times that of the average Nigerian maize farmer. Before joining Babban Gona, Rabi would have had to sell her maize at harvest, a period when maize prices are at their lowest in the market, to meet her immediate cash needs such as food and clothing. Thanks to Babban Gona’s support Rabi can store her maize and sell it at a future date for up to 37% higher than the market price at harvest. As a Babban Gona member, Rabi will benefit from marketing support that could see her generate earnings of up to $2,000 per hectare of land. Rabi is thankful that she now has the opportunity to improve the life of her children and family and looks forward to using her additional earnings to build a house for her family.

name: Gabriel Marcelo
description: Gabriel is 53 years old and is single with no children. He lives with some relatives in Chillanes, Bolívar Province.  He is a member of the communal bank VRC SAN JUAN BAUTISTA. This communal bank came together and was set up in the city of Tambanal, at a distance of 40 minutes from the cooperative’s office. The economic activities carried out are agriculture and animal rearing.  Gabriel works in agriculture. He sets maize and beans and he also rears livestock.  He is requesting this loan to buy livestock. With the help of this loan he will be able to buy one animal. He will purchase it in Chillanes.  His dream is to have his own land to sow. One of the challenges for him is the heavy that damages his crops.  In his free time he likes to play sport, especially indoor bowling, and he enjoys living in his community and the festivities held in the area.

name: Meriam
description: Meriam, 32, is married and has three children, two of whom are currently in school. For the past three years she has farmed cassava to earn a living in the Philippines.Meriam took out and successfully repaid a previous loan through Kiva's field partner NWTF. She has now applied for a 7,000 PHP loan to buy fertilizer and other farm supplies. She is saving money so that in the future she can send her children to college.

name: Jose Alberto
description: Jose Alberto is 33 years old and is in a common-law relationship. He lives in the rural part of Cayaltí which is located in the province of Chiclayo, Lambayeque region, on the North Coast of Peru. The inhabitants of this district work mainly in agriculture, raising livestock and commerce. Jose Alberto works buying and selling small animals like pigs, ducks and turkeys amongst others. His business is located at his house. He has a number of years experience in the field and has very good personal and work references in the area. The loan he is requesting will be used to buy a greater quantity of animals like pigs and piglets amongst others as well as balanced feed for them. Doing this Jose Alberto hopes to offer a better product to his clients which will allow him to generate greater income and in the end improve his quality of living and that of his family.

name: Juan Arturo
description: Juan, 30, has a bakery in the front part of his house. He lives with his wife (seen in the photo) and their two children in an urbanized area in the el Fortín section of Guayaquil characterized by its dirt roads.   In order to provide a better life to their two children who are three and one years of age, he began buying yeast, flour and dairy products and started making bread and pastries with the help of his wife. Little by little and inspired by his children and wife he has stayed in business now for years. He sells every roll and pastry for $0.10. He also sells highly sweetened pastries that he prepares with his wife's help called "enroladitos" and "rosquitas" [roll-ups and wheel-shaped].   To maintain his business he wants to purchase flour, drinks and dairy products. In the future he wants to incorporate more sweet pastries into his product line in order to give good variety to his customers.

name: Parveen
description: As is the case for many women, financial constraints led to Parveen approaching Kashf Foundation for a loan. Parveen is 59 years old, married, and a mother of three children. In order to support her husband in taking care of the family, she started a milk selling business.In her town, she is known for providing good quality milk. She owns buffaloes for milking. She is happily supporting her family with the income she generates. She has requested a 40,000 PKR loan to purchase another buffalo to increase her sales and generate more income to cover her daily expenses.

name: Lycheilyn
description: Lycheilyn Q. is from the village of Tupsan, Mambajao in Camiguin Province. She is 23 years old. Lycheilyn is married and has 4 small children. To make a living, Lycheilyn sells seafood products, including fish like sardines and milkfish, in the local community. Lycheilyn's husband is a fisherman who catches fish for their business. He also trades fish as a wholesaler. Lycheilyn has been engaged in her business for over 2 years and earns approximately 4000 PHP a month from these activities.  In 2011, Lycheilyn joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Lycheilyn is requesting a loan of 5000 PHP to purchase additional fish to sell, like mackerel and salmon. This loan will be her 1st loan from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Maria Zulema
description: Zulema is a returning client of Edpyme Alternativa (Kiva Field Partner). She is the loving mother of a family and she is attentive to her 3 children and her husband. She is 43 years old and she lives in a community (a poor rural community) located in the district of Pitipo in the province of Chiclayo, Lambayeque.  Zulema has a great deal of experience in working the land. She has been dedicated to agriculture for the past 10 years. She has 2 hectares of hard yellow corn and it needs upkeep. For this reason Zulema requests a loan from Edpyme Alternativa (Kiva Field Partner) of 3000 nuevos soles. This will help her fertilize and weed her fields. Zulema will achieve a greater yield per hectare and this will help her earn a greater income for her family.  Zulema has had two past loans and they were both paid on time and responsibly. They help her capitalize the plantation by sowing on additional hectares of agricultural land.

name: Rosario
description: Rosario makes quilts and sheets.  Now she is making snowmen to fill with candy and sell.    She is a long time, punctual client.  She is very well known in the region for her very good quality products.    Her children are now independent.  She lives in her youngest daughter’s house.  This daughter just had a baby.  Her husband is in the city of Sucre because of health problems.  The loan is to buy by fleece to make the snowmen.  She has orders for the Christmas holidays. 		 				 				 				 				 Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Um
description: Mrs. Um Y., age 54, works selling foodstuffs and provisions, earning only $1 per day of profit. Her husband, age 56, works as a farmer, making about $1 each day. They have seven children, two who are mechanics, two who are students, three who are married and live separately. She would like to request a loan of $300 in order to purchase piglets to raise for additional profits. Her husband is pictured in the photo as she was not available at the time of the photo.

name: Yesenia
description: Yesenia studied in school up until the 9th grade.  She is in a relationship and has two young children who depend upon her.  Her mother also lives in the house.Yesenia has a small eatery in which she sells breakfasts and lunches.  She has had this occupation for 3 years.  Her sister gave her the motivation to start the business and she has it about 15 minutes from her house.  She is now thinking of extending her work and selling clothing in order to improve her income.She needs this loan to buy and begin to sell clothing for all ages, and also she will buy food to cook and sell in her eatery.Yesenia dreams that her new clothing business will produce good results.  She would like to become a great businesswoman and she will work hard to reach her goals.

name: Zeenat
description: Zeenat, age 26, is a married woman. She has four children. She has been running a business selling animals for a period of about six years. She buys animals (baby goats & calves) at low prices, brings them up and then sells them out in the market for higher prices. She makes enough through her business to contribute to the family income. She needs to improve her business to bear her household expenses. For this reason, she contacted Kashf Foundation and applied a loan of PKR 40,000 to purchase more animals. She is very experienced and has good contacts in the market. With this loan, she will definitely expand her business and income level. She is in her 3rd loan cycle and has shown good repayment behavior

name: Lai
description: Lai T. N. is 53 years old and has 2 children who attend high school. She is  a very hardworking farmer. She is currently growing rice, beans and corn in a paddy of 4,200 square meters. Her agricultural products are used to support her family's food demands and some is also sold  to earn daily income. Lai T. N. joined the Seda credit program in 2007. She has used the loans very effectively and has always repaid them well. Lai T. N. wants a loan of 7,630,000 VND to buy seeds and fertilizer for her next crop,

name: Sokros
description: Sokros is 28 years old and has an embellishing shop where she earns $3 per day. Her husband is a worker earning $3 per day. They have two children: two years old and two months old. Every month, she has to spend $30 on food, $10 electricity, $10 on transportation, and $10 on other expenses. She would like to request a loan of $1000 to buy a motorbike for her husband to travel to work. She wants to expand her embellishing shop and provide more services but she needs a long time to save the money to achieve her plan.

name: Asha's Group
description: Asha's Group is formed by 15 farmers in Matete District and is being represented by Asha, who is the group leader pictured above. She is 40 years old, is married, and has four children. Asha has been a farmer for more than 20 years and is often referred to as a very trustworthy person.  Asha isn’t new to One Acre Fund; she actually joined the program in 2013 and has since noticed her life has changed; especially in the sense that she has been able to consistently feed her family. This year, Asha will not only get fertilizer and maize seeds as part of her loan, but will also purchase a solar light. She is very excited about this addition since now she will be able to reduce their consumption of paraffin fuel and therefore save more money.  Using this loan, Asha's Group will purchase a total of 12 solar lights and use the farming inputs received to plant a total of 8 acres.

name: Kate
description: Kate is 50 years old and has two children.  She earns a living by farming rice in the Philippines. Kate is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to purchase fertilizers and other farm supplies.  Kate has been farming rice for 10 years and earns additional income from food vending.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Inomjon
description: Inomjon is 30 years old, married and has three children. He has a secondary education and has an animal-husbandry business. He has a small cow-house where he breeds calves. Because he does not have a specialized education, animal husbandry is the only source of income for his family.   Inomjon buys calves on the market at a low price, feeds them and then resells on the same market at a more profitable price. He provides the markets with meat and his family with the necessary food. Inomjon wants to buy young cattle and needs money, so he decided to apply for a loan. He is very grateful to all those who can support him.     More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which being includes a key post along the Silk Road, and for the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History  Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low-income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Eliakim
description: Eliakim lives in Ogongo, a small town in Homa Bay County. Homa Bay county is located at the south-western tip of Kenya, and its northern end is dominated by Lake Victoria, the largest lake in the Southern Hemisphere. Lake Victoria extends into three east African countries, allowing cross-border flows of goods and people.  There is  a market day in a lakeside town in Homa Bay county which attracks traders from Ugandan, Tanzania and Kenya.  The traders arrive in boats to sell their wares. Although the semi-arid nature of much of Homa Bay county means that poverty rates are quite high, many people in the region hold a strong cultural emphasis on education. Therefore, school attendance figures around Homa Bay are above the national average.  Eliakim is married and has one child. He is a preacher and a businessman. His wife has a small business cooking and selling donuts. Both he and his wife are farmers. They have been farming for ten years  and  grow sunflowers, maize, cowpeas and beans. Eliakim is looking forward to beekeeping because it is a profitable business and it will provide him with honey for food.  This is Eliakim’s first loan with Honey Care and he intends to use the proceeds from his beekeeping to expand his business. Eliakim’s hope for the future is to expand his beekeeping project and to encourage his community to take up beekeeping.

name: Lekea
description: Lekea is a 53 year old mother  with 6 children. She operates a small business cooking and selling BBQ in her community to earn a living. Lekea  has requested a loan to buy a box of chicken, a box of sausages, mushroom soy sauce, onions, plates, aluminum foil, bananas, a sack of rice, etc to help her run the business. Lekea  hopes to build a small restaurant in the near future using her business profit. She became a member of SPBD in 2015.

name: Celestina
description: Celestina works hard to support her family. She is married and has a buy-and-sell ready-to-wear business in the Philippines.Celestina requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more stock of ready-to-wear to sell to her customers.Celestina has been in this business for three years now.Celestina would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Top 10 Solidarity Group
description: Mariama is a member of Top-Ten solidarity group (see group picture, Mariama  stands in the middle).  She sells cooking condiments.  Mariama has been selling cooking condiments for the past 6 years.  She uses proceeds of her business to pay for her children’s education and to provide livelihood for hers family. She has been able to buy a piece of land from savings she made from her business. Mariama and other group members of Top-10 solidarity group are requesting for their first loan. Mariama and her group members are in need of a loan of 5,000,000SLL. Of this amount, Mariama will personally receive 1,000,000SLL which she will use to purchase more bags of rice, unions, gallons of oil, packets of Maggi etc. for her business. Mariama is thirty-four years, married and has two children age thirteen and nine years old. Mariama hopes that her business continue to exist so that she can save enough money to build a dwelling house and educate her children well.                                                                         Mariama and her group members thank you for financing their businesses

name: Dugersuren
description: Dugersuren is 37 years old and lives with his wife and three children, one son and two daughters, in their own house in Zavhan province, Mongolia. His wife is a salesperson in a private retail trading store. His twins, a boy and a girl, attend secondary school while the youngest child, age 3, goes to kindergarten. He operates a public transportation service between Zavhan and Ulaanbaatar, capital city of Mongolia. He started his business in 2002.   Since then he deposited and saved his earnings in order to buy a small plot of land where he built a house for their family. Before that he used to live in a ger, a Mongolian traditional nomadic housing tent, in someone else's backyard. Also he managed to renew his car twice with profits he earned.   Now he wants to finish the construction work on his house that has been left to be fixed in the future. He is a hard-working and honest man who says, "I am doing my best to better my family's living conditions." He is requesting a 3,000,000 MNT loan to purchase construction materials for his house.

name: Napié
description: Napié lives in the Vakpossito quarter with her five children. She started a food products business and corn porridge restaurant from her home ten years ago. She stocks up once a week at Bassar and Adjengré, villages that are found around 400 km from Lomé. This micro credit is necessary for her to buy one bag of corn and thirty yam tubers. The profits will allow her to contribute to the flourishment of her family.

name: Robelyn
description: Robelyn is 35 years old and has eight children. She is married and has seven children who are in school.  Robelyn and her family survived super typhoon Haiyan which swept through the Philippines last November 8, 2013 but her business and family home was wiped out.   Robelyn is taking out a housing loan amounting to 7,071 PHP to purchase building materials and pay for construction labor to build a house for her family.   Robelyn has been a NWTF borrower since 2012. She plans to recover through her pig fattening business.  With your help, Robelyn can rebuild her house and rebound from the devastation of super typhoon Haiyan. In future she would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Natividad
description: Natividad, 51, is a hardworking, cheerful woman.  She’s separated from the father of her children.  She lives with her aged mother and her son, Joel, 29, who she loves very much.  She lives in a house that’s her property and that she inherited from her father.  Natividad’s activity is selling groceries and foodstuffs.  To do so, she opened a grocery store inside her house because economic need was severe and the stipends or child support she got wasn’t enough.  She decided to start this business six years ago and this time has served her to grow and expand.  She has many customers most of which are neighbors who she tends to with help from her mother occasionally.  She considers her business to be quite profitable because it’s well-received and it’s in high demand; it yields good profits.  She likes her activity because it allows her to socialize with her neighbors and have more friends and to be able to talk about topics she’s interested in; she also likes to feel occupied and to be a productive person.  Thanks to her income she’s able to cover her household needs.  On the other hand, she does not like it when her customers are late making their payments on the loans credit she gives for her products’ sales.  She’s thinking about not providing this credit any longer in order to have more cash on-hand and invest in expanding the business.  This is MFP loan #12 and she feels happy about having this support to make business progress so she commits to make her payments punctually.  She also feels comfortable in her communal bank because she considers the members to be responsible and mutually supportive.  She will use the requested 1,000 new soles to buy edible products like rice, sugar and noodles, among others to stock up on merchandise for her store thus continuing to satisfy her customers.

name: Rocio Veronica
description: Rocio lives with her husband and daughters in the Valle Hermosos parish, a tourist area with many spas.  In the village, crops such as cocoa, pepper and palms are also grown.  The parish is very well known in the area.  Rocio is very dedicated to her daughters.  One of them attends the local school and the other one is small and stays at home.  That is why Rocio sells her food goods from a cart outside her house.  She has many customers who like her attentiveness and delicious foods.  Thanks to her business she is able to earn an income and take care of her daughters.  Her husband changed employment and works at a company.  Rocio will use the loan to buy meat, bread and a larger cart, as well as tables and chairs to improve customer service.  She and her family are very grateful to Kiva and the institution for allowing her to expand her business.

name: Durga
description: Durga, a 26-year-old young lady, lives in a remote village of Dhupguri in West Bengal. She is married to Bhim. Together they have has two children (a daughter and a son). Her son reads in grade two and her daughter is in grade one.Durga is a housewife and her husband is an enterprising man who is engaged in the business of selling Ayurvedic medicine from his house. Durga also helps her husband in this business. Ayurvedic medicine is in very good demand in their area, as in their locality medicines shops are very far away. But they need to develop their stocks of Ayurvedic medicines, and they do not have sufficient capital to invest in their business.  For that reason Durga is requesting the loan from Kiva’s partner, BJS, to purchase Ayurvedic medicines from the wholesalers. She hopes this loan will give a boost to their business and attracts more customers.Her dream is to expand their business in order to strengthen the family's economy. She is grateful to the lenders (BJS and Kiva) for the loan.

name: Abel
description: Mr. M. Abel is 40 years of age. He has been running a small retail shop in Kabwohe for the last four years. He is married to a woman who is a primary school teacher and a hard working mother. The couple has 3 children, whom they take care of very well.  Abel is requesting a loan to purchase sugar, rice, flour, and cooking oil. He dreams of transforming his retail shop into a wholesale business.

name: Novie
description: This is Novie. She previously accessed an 12,000 PHP loan that she used to buy groceries, toiletries and beverages to expand her product inventory. She expects a boost in her income as she expands her business. Her earnings were a big help for the education of her child and in their personal, household and business expenditures.   She would like to apply for another 15,000 PHP loan to buy groceries, toiletries, beverages and other products to add to her inventory. The more items displayed at the store, the better. More items to sell will result in better profit. Her profits from business will definitely help her to sustain her daily needs and the educational expenses of her child. She looks forward to this financial increase with gladness and thankfulness in her heart.   Novie hopes to be able to expand soon, just as she dreams of being able to give her family a good future through all her hard work on her business. She faithfully meets with her co-fellowship* members every week to share stories of her work and to draw strength and inspiration from her studies of the Word of God.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans.

name: David's Group
description: David is 65 years old and has 7 children. He has been a farmer for more than 30 years now and is always said to be a very hardworking individual. Even though David is the only one featured in the above picture, he is actually representing his group formed by 14 farmers in Chwele District, Kenya.  David started working alongside One Acre Fund a few years ago, in 2009, and decided to do so because he wanted to get the best quality fertilizers and hybrid seeds. Since then, he has seen his life improve; especially in the sense that he has been able to consistently feed his family ever since. This year he decided to represent his group because he wanted to spread the story of One Acre Fund farmers.  David’s Group will receive farming inputs to plant a total of 8.25 acres of land. Additionally, some of the farmers in the group will be purchasing a solar light, so, with this loan, the group will also receive a total of 9 solar lights."

name: Kom
description: Mrs. Kom Y. is a 45-year-old resident of a local village in Kompong Tom Province. She is a mother of five children, four of whom are single. Her husband Krin is a fisherman, while Kom  owns a piece of farmland that she inherited many years ago from her grandparents. She planted rice and vegetable crops two months ago, and her crops are growing well.    Kom presently earns a living raising ducks in a cage behind her house, selling their eggs to people who come to buy in bulk at her house.  She is now applying for a loan from Kiva’s partner HKL in order to purchase additional ducks to produce eggs for sale.

name: Mgeni's Maendeleo. Group
description: Mgeni is 45 years old. She is divorced and cares for her fifteen year old child. Since 2002, Mgeni has made a living selling porridge, soup, and bites (snacks). She works daily from 8am to 6pm and earns a monthly profit of about $125 from her sales.    Mgeni is requesting a loan of $500 to expand her business. She will share this loan with her subgroup members who have their own businesses selling snacks and potatoes.

name: Song
description: Song S. T., 42, is married and resides in Kampong Cham Province where she works in a grocery store and earns about $7 per day, while her husband, a motor-taxi driver, has an income of about $5 per day. This couple has three school-aged children. Song S. T. would like to take out a loan to increase her stock of grocery items.

name: Elvira
description: Elvira makes a living sewing clothing for women (dresses, skirts, blouses and general alterations). She lives in the Villa San Antonio zone, down from the city of La Paz.  She rents. She is separated from her husband and has a daughter in her care. The loan is for the purchase of raw materials (cloth, lace, thread, lining material and buttons). This is her fourth loan from Impro.  Her credit history qualifies her as a #1 customer, meaning that she has complied with the terms of repayment. Her desire to work gives her the opportunity to be able to request this loan, she is a very responsible person. Translated from Spanish by Laura Bobbit, Kiva Volunteer

name: Margarita
description: Margarita is a member of the 'Arco Iris' (Rainbow) community bank.  Her business is selling meat in open-air markets.  Thanks to the training that she has received, Margarita has learned to manage her business well.  She has learned to save, and to be punctual and responsible.  She is grateful for all the loans that she has been given because, thanks to them, she has had more capital available and been able to provide her children with a better education.  She recalls that when her husband became seriously ill, Finca were the only ones to help her.  She will never forget this.  The training that she has received has helped her to value herself as a woman and she has learned to be happy with what she has.  She will use the loan that she is requesting to buy meat.

name: Alicia
description: This is Alicia, 55, a resident of Quezon City, Philippines. She is married to Alberto, 59, who is self-employed. She is childless but enjoys being a wife and keeping herself busy with her business.  Alicia owns a sari-sari (variety) store. She buys groceries like canned goods, condiments, milk, sugar, and primary commodities that are needed in every household. She earns money by getting supplies at wholesale prices and selling by the piece. She also retails electronic cell phone loads. Her store is located adjacent to her house. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community. She earns a minimum of 950 PHP in sales every day.  She is requesting a loan amounting to PHP 50,000 that will help to continue her business well. She will be using the loan to buy groceries, toiletries and beverages to expand her product inventory. It will also help her to attract more customers to buy household needs. Her profits from business will definitely help her to meet her daily needs.  Anita dreams that her sari-sari store will turn into a grocery someday. She hopes to improve her family’s future so they can enjoy a comfortable life. She never fails to attend to the fellowship* every week as the teachings and sharing of the word of God continue to strengthen her every day.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Gloria
description: Gloria, age 45, engages in fishing to earn an income. She has been engaged in this business for six years and is a very hard-working entrepreneur. She and her husband have 12 children, five of whom still attend school.  Gloria requested a loan in the amount of PhP 13,000 through NWTF. She will use her loan funds to buy netting and other fishing supplies.  In the future, Gloria would like to save enough money to be able to afford to send her school-going children to college.

name: Muhidin
description: Muhidin is 21 years old. He and his wife and parents live in Jilikul region. Muhidin is a young farmer. He has an irrigated land plot, where he grows wheat, onions, and corn. Muhidin has been in this business for three years. His wife helps him with the job on the land. This winter he has already sown cotton and corn.   Muhidin is requesting a loan. He wants to buy more mineral fertilisers in order to cultivate the winter seedlings. In the future Muhidin hopes to receive a good harvest, and expand the business thanks to its profit.

name: Carmen
description: Carmen, age 42, lives in Villa Guadalupe, a neighborhood in the Colinas municipality.  She has been married to her husband, Julian, for 15 years.  He dispatches materials in a hardware store.  They have four children; age 11, 12, 15, and 17.  The children go to school.  Carmen is a seamstress.  She specializes in making curtains, bedding, and clothing.  She started her business 15 years ago.  She bought fabric at the factories in order to make children’s clothes.  Later, she started making curtains.  She took six loans to stock her business.  She bought an electric sewing machine because she already had a pedal sewing machine.  The income from her business has helped her educate her children and buy some domestic appliances for her household.  She now works from nine in the morning until four in the afternoon making items to fill her orders.  When she does not have many orders she only works in the afternoons.  She requested this loan for 6,000 lempiras to buy material to make curtains and children’s shorts.  She hopes to obtain greater sales and income to help her children graduate.

name: Adelfa
description: As a married mother of three children, Adelfa works hard to support her family.  She has a food production business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from a general store.  Adelfa is borrowing PHP 18,000 through NWTF in order to buy ingredients for her food production business.  Adelfa has been sustaining her business activities through her past eight loans from NWTF and more recently, through Kiva. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Nicholas
description: Nicholas is 45 years old, married with three children between 18 and 15 years. His primary business is poultry-keeping, besides having a workshop. He has been in the business for the past three years.  This is his third loan through KADET. He repaid his previous loans successfully. He will use the loan to buy more layers. Anticipated profits will be used repay the loan and to pay school fees for his children.    His dream is to build his own house.

name: Judity
description: Judity is a married woman. She has 1 child. She describes herself to be committed. She operates a retail business where she sells phone accessories. She has been involved in this business for 2 years. Her business is located in a suitable area and her primary customers are the general public. She will use the Kes 25,000 loan to buy more stock of phone accessories. She hopes that in the future, she will have a successful business. This is her first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: Thessane Armen
description: A 30-year-old client, single with no children.  After earning her degree and being unable to find work, she launched a pastry business where she now makes beignets, sweet breads, and milk breads.  She brings in an average of 18,000 to 25,000 Congolese francs every day.  She sells her cakes both retail and wholesale in various markets, and sometimes in little food shops in her neighborhood.  She plans on using her first loan to purchase some basic supplies: 2 bags of flour, a 25-liter jug of oil, 50 kg of sugar, 25 kg of powdered milk, yeast, vanilla sugar and cartons of eggs.  She has several strategies for moving her products, including low prices and friendly customer service.  In the future, she plans on opening a small pastry shop of her own and hiring another person to work with her.  She also wants to save money to fulfill her dream of one day opening a tea room.

name: James
description: James is 36 years old, married, and a father of two children who are one and three years of age. He is in the transport business and also runs a tailoring business in Kilifi. His business has been in operation for the last four years and has been a success.   James has been a KADET client and this is his second loan to finance his business. With this loan he plans to service his tuk tuk and use the remaining amount to purchase cloth materials for tailoring.   The anticipated profits will be used to repay the loan and to gradually expand his business. James' dream is to prosper in life.

name: Samuel
description: Samuel is a Kiva borrower. He describes himself to be humble. He operates a farm where he grows egg plant, onions . He has been involved in this business for 15 years. His business is located in a good area and his primary customers are locals. He describes his biggest business challenge to be inadequate working capital. He will use the Kes 20,000 loan to buy farm inputs. He hopes that in the future, he will expand the business. This is his first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. He will use the anticipated profits to improve the business.

name: Leiner
description: Miss Leiner belongs to the "Prosperidad" ["Prosperity"] communal bank. This bank is located in the district of Cusco, which is part of the province and department of Cusco.  Leiner is 24 years old and single.  She alternates her daily activities with working in her mother's grocery store.  Leiner goes to school in the mornings and helps her mother in the afternoons. She is requesting this loan to by more goods for the grocery store.  Leiner is grateful to all those who, through this means, will support her dream. She also promises to make her repayments according to the established schedule.

name: Katia Diana
description: Katia Diana is a member of the “VIRGEN ASUNTA DE OROPESA” community bank which is located in Oropesa district, in Quispicanchis province, in Cusco department.  Katia Diana is 25 years old and single.  She divides her time between her daily activities and her business which is running a store offering multiple services.  She makes photocopies, types documents and sells stationery products.   She works from 9.00am to 6.00pm.  Through her business she is able to save so that she can study for a professional degree.  She would like to expand and improve her business.  Katia Diana is requesting this loan to buy paper and stationery products wholesale.   She is happy to be receiving a loan and pledges to make her repayments on time.

name: Zabiullah Panjsheri Group
description: Fariba is the group leader of Zabiullah Panjsheri group and lives in district 11 of Kabul, Afghanistan. She and her husband have three children, who are in school. She wants to take out a loan for her home-based bakery, and will use this money to buy stock for her business as well as help her husband and her children. Finally, she wants to thank all lenders of Kiva and AFSG in Afghanistan.

name: White Rose Group
description: Fanil, who is in his early 30's, is single with one son who is still at school.  He has been running two projects, a retail shop and a chip-selling business, for four years now.  He works from 6 AM to 9 PM daily and is able to make a good monthly profit.  This will be Fanil's second loan from Tujijenge Tanzania.  He used the previous loan to buy retail shop inventory like sugar, salt, beans rice, flours, cooking oil, and charcoal, and has paid back his loan successfully.  He used the profit to pay school fees and covered household expenses.    He will use this loan to buy shop inventory, Irish potatoes, cooking oil, and charcoal for cooking chips. He dreams of improving his business to the international level.  Fanil will share this loan with his loan group, White Rose, which consists of four members who will hold each other accountable for paying back the loan.

name: Ashkhen
description: Ashkhen is 21 years old and a fourth year student at Yerevan State Agricultural University in the Food Industry Economics and Management department. Ashkhen is studying by correspondence while working at a wedding salon as a shop assistant and designer in Sevan.   Ashkhen is requesting her second loan from Nor Horizon for 220.000 Armenian drams, which she will use to pay her tuition fee for second semester.

name: Phi
description: Phi is a 57-year-old widowed woman with three sons. She lives with her family in a small house in Ho Chi Minh City.   Phi earns an income to support her family by running a food stall in front of her house. She has been running her business for the past 13 years.  Phi would like to receive a loan to purchase furniture, bowls, plates, and chopsticks, as well as more food to sell. She hopes that this will enable her to earn a higher income, improve her family's living conditions, and set aside some savings for family emergencies.

name: Latofat
description: Latofat is a modest but very hardworking country woman, who lives in the region of Vose. She is a woman of middle age; she is 35 years old. She has three children, and they are 13, 10 and 6 years old. Two of them attend school, and the third one will start this year. Latofat's husband works with selling food products at the market and at the same time helps his wife with her business.   Latofat has worked with cattle breeding for a period of 15 years. She breeds young bulls for selling. Latofat takes a loan to expand and increase the number of livestock. She would like to purchase some young bulls, as the favorable season for cattle breeding has already started. With the arrival of spring, the grass grows on the local pastures - and this is fodder for cattle.

name: Jose
description: Jose is married and has seven children. Five are in school. They live in the village where there is more agricultural business. Jose and his wife aim to become financially stable so they can support the education of the children.  Jose is engaged in a livestock business wherein he is raising seven piglets. He has been doing this kind of business for almost three years. The income gained from his business was used to pay his previous accounts, their daily household expenses and school allowances.   Since he repaid his previous loan, now he is asking for another loan amount of PHP 35,000. He will use this amount to buy hog feed, vitamins and medicine to ensure proper growth of his piglets. Jose believes that providing proper nutrition to his piglets will enable him to sell them at a higher price. In this way, he can support his children's education and improve their way of living.

name: Janny De Jesus
description: Janny is 24 years old and proprietor of a clothing-making business, a skill he learned from his father who has operated a tailor shop from his home for many years. Some 3 years ago, Janny became independent and acquired his own machines, with which he fulfills clothing contracts for various customers. He has made outstanding progress while working with considerable enterprise while receiving help from the Fundacion Mario Santo Domingo, where he received 4 loans for expanding his work infrastructure. He bought new machines and improved the quality of his products.  At present, Janny is applying for his 1st Kiva loan and will buy cloth, thread, zippers, and general supplies for making clothes. The end-of-the-year season is approaching when, usually, sales increase.   The greatest challenge in this type of business is the lack of necessary capital at the end of the year. For this reason, Janny hopes that with this injection of capital through a Kiva loan, he can once again expand his business and augment his income and, at last, improve his residence and raise his standard of living.

name: Fernando
description: Fernando is 41 years old. He is married with 3 children who attend grade school and high school. He is a businessman and he lives in a house that he owns with his family. He will use this loan to buy used clothes in bulk to resell at the local market to secure the support of his family. In the future, he wants to build a grocery store to start a new business and have a better income as his expenses have increased over time. His biggest goal is to repay this loan on time and be sure to have access to future loans from Hluvuku.

name: George
description: George is from a small village in Khashuri district. He is 49 years old and lives alone in his house. George is involved in the agricultural business. In particular, he runs a small dairy farm of two milk cows and four calves. George milks the cows and sells the dairy products at the local market. He has three pigs as well. In addition, he owns six hectares of agricultural land, which is cultivated and grows maize. He also produces hay to feed his cattle. George is a very hard-working person, with a rich experience in his work.  He has requested a loan to buy a piece of agricultural land. After the land is purchased, George will be able to sow and harvest more maize and produce more hay. He will do all the relevant seasonal work to ensure a good harvest, which will significantly increase his income. With the increased income, George plans to expand his animal husbandry business and buy additional livestock. He awaits your help and kindness.

name: Lucia Maribel
description: Lucia is a married woman. She has three children, who are 3, 6, and 11 years old. The older children go to school. Her husband works as a bricklayer.  Lucia works raising small animals, and she also sells them. She will invest the loan in the purchase of pigs, in order to sell them at the markets of the towns nearby. Lucia hopes that her business will increase, and that her sales will improve, so that she can increase her income. She does all this to offer her children a good quality of life.

name: Vấn
description: Vấn is 57 years old, and he is married with 3 children. He lives and works in Thieu Hoá district, a  rural area in Thanh Hoá province in Vietnam.  This is Vấn's first loan with Thanh Hoá Fund for Poor Women.  While Vấn has been working at his business for more than 10 years now, he nonetheless faces the hardship of not having enough money to build a hygienic latrine.   Vấn is requesting a loan in order to purchase sand, cement, and brick so he can build a toilet for his family.  For the future, Vấn hopes to continue to maintain and grow a successful business.

name: Marjorie
description: 29-year-old Marjorie is a rice farmer from San Miguel, in the province of Bohol, Philippines. She is a married woman with two sons, aged two and five.   Her husband is a security guard and sometimes supplements his income by working as an assistant electrician. Marjorie works hard and perseveres on her farm, anticipating a good yield in four months.   Marjorie has decided to take a loan so she can renovate her house and make more improvements. She is asking for a loan to buy nails and amakan (woven bamboo wall cladding) to repair her walls. Marjorie has faith that everything will fall into place for her business, her family and the house that she would like to have for her family.

name: Firuza
description: N. Firuza is married and has 4 children. She is a hard-working woman who, in order to help her husband cover the household expenses and pay for her children's education, decided to start her own business 2 years ago.   Firuza started selling blankets and quilts, and later she started selling fabrics for sewing traditional dresses. The response from her customers has been very positive and business has increased. She is currently handling many orders placed by her customers. In order to fill these orders, Firuza is seeking a loan of US$ 500 to buy merchandise. Become an important part of the growth of this business and the lives of Firuza and her family. They will be forever grateful.    More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is perhaps best known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road; the end of Alexander the Great's rule; and with it’s famous great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets as: Rudaki, Ibn Sina (Avicenna), Firdousi, Omar Haiyam, Jomi, Mavlavi Rumi and many others. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC.  And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.   But, Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics.  The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy.  In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable.  These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia.  While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.   IMON's History  Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Virginia Azucena
description: La Señora Hernández is used to working.  She is divorced and has never had to depend on anyone.  All her children are married and live with their respective families.  She doesn't want to bother them, and therefore she sells used clothing.  She has been doing this very successfully for four years.  She wishes to invest the loan proceeds in her business and increase profits.

name: Duo Torre Fuerte Group
description: Strong Tower Duo  Iris del Rosario is 20 years old and has one child.  She sells everyday food products.  Iris is requesting a loan to buy more merchandise to restock her food store.  She needs more operating capital to help increase her earnings.  Luz Adelaida is 20 years old.  She has been selling used clothing for one year.  Luz says she needs a loan to buy one bale of clothing so that she can restock her business and provide a greater variety of styles for women, men, and children.

name: Luzmienda
