description: Luzmienda L., 56, is a widow with five children, all married --  one of whom is working abroad, two were not able to finish college.   She lives in a small barrio of Sta. Cruz, Jimenez, Misamis Occidental. Her main source of income is duck-raising. She started with 20 ducks and has grown the business with 350 ducks.  She sells duck eggs to the neighboring localities.   She had already nine loan availments from PMPC. With the Kiva loan, she wants to buy more ducks to produce eggs thus, increasing her profit as well.    She hopes to help her married children financially, the other two (2) to finish college and enough money to get her by when she gets old and could no longer work.

name: Sandy Catalina
description: Sandy is a young entrepreneur who decided to establish her own business after leaving a low-paying job.  She is 22 years old and has a business of renting out video games.  Sandy offers her customers a great service.  Attracting good customers has guaranteed her the chance of generating good sales.  Despite having little capital in the beginning, her business grew within months and the results are reflected in the large number of customers she has attracted to date.  Her ability to gain so many customers over a short period of time is due to the great demand for this service.  Sandy seeks this opportunity to obtain a loan so that she can purchase a video game console and a television.  This will increase her capacity so that she can serve all of her customers.    As a result of this loan, Sandy will be able to serve her entire market and her monthly sales will increase considerably.  In addition, she will gradually fulfill her dream of having a successful business to ensure her economic future.  This will allow her to provide her parents with a good quality of life and more economic opportunities.

name: Brenda Damaris
description: Brenda lives in the town of Ticuantepe. She is married and is the mother of one school-aged son. She sells clothing and her husband is a farmer. She also works for a private business. She asks for a loan to buy clothing like pants, blouses, skirts, etc. She hopes that she will have good earnings so that she can contribute to the construction of her home, since they are planning to improve it. She is grateful for the support that has been given to her.

name: Gulmira
description: Gulmira has successfully repaid her loan, having used the money as intended. She thanks Kiva and everyone who helped finance her loan. Thanks to her tireless hard work, today Gulmira has 4 cows and 10 sheep. In order to further develop her business, Gulmira applied to the bank Bai Tushum for a loan in the amount of 40,000 som (KGS) to purchase calves for fattening and resale. With income from the loan, she plans to invest in the further development of her business.

name: Muhabbat
description: Muhabbat is from the Spitamen region of Tajikistan.  She is 53 years old, and lives together with her husband, 3 daughters, and her son.  Her husband works in a cotton-processing factory as a press operator, whereas Muhabbat bakes flatbread in a bakery and sells it at a local market.  She is currently a tenant on a 2-hectare plot of land where she grows rice.    Lately, Muhabbat has been thinking it would be a good idea to start raising livestock at home.  She has no previous experience doing so, but her neighbors do, and are willing to help her if need be; nearly two-thirds of the population in Spitamen raise livestock.  Muhabbat will be using her own money to build a cow shed and buy cattle feed for her new business, and hopes to use a loan to buy cattle (4 cows and 4 calves).

name: Actable The Best Group
description: Rehema, who is in her forties, runs two enterprises: a restaurant and a cosmetics business. She has been engaged in these endeavors for the past five years and both are thriving. She works from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily and is able to make a good profit each month.  Rehema and her husband have two boys and two girls, all of whom are enrolled in school.    This will be Rehema's fourth loan from Tujijenge Tanzania. She used the previous loan funds to increase stock items in both her businesses. This has allowed her business revenues to cover household expenses and pay school fees. She has paid back all her loans successfully.   She will use this loan to replenish items presently missing from both her businesses so as to meet customer demand.   Her dream is someday to be able to build a premises for her cosmetics business.   She will share this loan with her loan group "Actable the Best," which totals 16 members. The members of the group will hold each other accountable for paying back the loan.

name: Parveen
description: Parveen is 45 years old. She lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, and has one child. Her husband has been working in a public sector organization for many years. He is responsible for meeting the needs of the family. Parveen provides sewing services and earns an income to contribute to managing the household with her husband.   Parveen needs different kinds of goods such as needles, thread, fabric, and machine oil for her business, but due to insufficient financial means she is unable to purchase these items. Therefore she has applied for a Kiva loan through its field partner BRAC Pakistan. This loan will enable her to purchase these items and will help her to increase her monthly sales and profit by providing better sewing services.  Parveen is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Rosaline
description: Rosaline is a married woman. She has four children. She describes herself as humble. She operates a retail business where she sells cereals. Her business is located in a good area and her primary customers are locals. She will use the Kes 51,000 loan to buy more stock of cereals. She hopes that in the future, she will own land. This is her first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. She will use the anticipated profits to open another business.

name: Trinidad
description: Trinidad is 63 years old and married with one child. Trinidad works very hard to provide for them.Trinidad runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 18,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like bread, noodles, junk foods, and other groceries.Trinidad has been in this business for two years. In the future, Trinidad would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Alejandrina Bernardina
description: Sra. Alejandrina is 49 years old, married, and has three children (ages 21, 18, and 11).  Only her 11-year-old is still in school.  Her husband is a construction worker.  Alejandrina sells beauty products house-to-house to her regular customers.  With the income she earns, she is able to help with the family expenses.  Alejandrina has been in this line of work for more than two years.  The money from this loan will be invested in the purchase of more beauty products such as perfumes, crèmes, talcum powders, jewelry, and other items.  She will also purchase a display cabinet in order to showcase her products.  Her dream for the future is to grow her business so that she can generate more income and have a better quality of life.  Alejandrina is very pleased with the support that has been provided.

name: Be
description: Be would like to take a further loan to buy materials to make doors and windows. She hopes that another loan will assist her in increasing the size of her business, attract new customers and increase sales.   She also hopes that through the loan, she can increase her income and improve her family's living conditions.

name: Mylie
description: Mylie is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a fruit vending business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 13000 through NWTF to purchase more fruits to sell for her fruit vending business.  Mylie has been in this business for 3 years. Mylie earns more income from food vending.  She has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to save money to expand her business in the future.

name: Juanito
description: Juanito is 51 and married with three school-age children. He lives in a village, planting and harvesting rice and vegetables to sell. He aims to increase his yields and income so he can continue sending his children to school to give them a better life. Due to the high cost of commodities and school fees, he needs to increase his income to cover his family's needs.   Juanito is requesting a loan of PHP 19,000 to buy fertilizers and pesticides and to pay for labor to plant rice. He believes that the loan will enable him to improve his farming business.

name: Procesa
description: Procesa is 67 years old and a widow from Pagadian City, Zamboanga del Sur.   She landed at the right place for her needed capital when she joined PMPC. She knew this would be her last chance to get back on her feet when she went broke after her husband died. PMPC came as a rescue to Procesa, lending her money when she needed it the most.   Now, she availed another loan for the next cropping season. She borrowed an amount of PHP 14,900 for fertilizers and a knapsack sprayer for her gardening business. Procesa perseveres and always believes in reaching her goals to continuously provide for her family.
town: Pagadian - Pagadian City, Zamboanga del Sur

name: Lily
description: Lily is a married woman. She describes herself to be proactive. She operates a farm where she grows tea. She has been involved in this business for 20 years. Her business is located in a rural area and her primary customers are locals. She describes her biggest business challenge to be fluctuation of tea prices. She will use the Kes 20,000 loan to buy more stock of tea. Her business goal is to have a stable business within 5 years. She hopes that in the future, she will have a better life. This is her first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: La Esperanza Group
description: There are 22 women who decided to join together so that they could work as a team and provide everything for their families that they were not able to have.  They are participating in the poverty elimination program so that they can overcome their poverty situation.  Maria is the president of this group.  She is a woman who is known for her enthusiasm and her drive to succeed.  Maria strives to do her best each day at the small snack bar that she owns.  This business allows her to support her family.  Maria is requesting a loan so that she can buy supplies for preparing the food that she sells from her modest snack bar.  She is grateful for the opportunity she has received to improve her life and that of her family.

name: Djiguisseme Group
description: The Djiguisseme group is entirely made up of married women who have an average age of 34 and, on average, 4 children, and who all live in traditional, extended families in the village of Chakabougou, Koulikoro region (second administrative region of the Republic of Mali). They got to know each other through family and neighbourly relationships, and friendships. They sell shoes, condiments, groundnuts and various other shop items. The women of the Djiguisseme group are on their second group loan, having properly repaid the previous one.  N'Dja, the woman standing in the middle of the back row, plans to buy a dozen pairs of plastic shoes from the wholesalers of Dioïla and Fana, so that she can resell them locally in her village. She expects to make an average monthly profit of 5 000 francs, part of which will be used to meet her family's needs and part of which will be reinvested in her plastic shoe-selling business.

name: Oliva
description: Oliva, 59 years of age, is married and blessed with four children.   She has owned and managed a rice farm in their village for almost 20 years and earns a net income of PHP 10,000.  Her income from her business was spent on her hog-raising business. Due to insufficient funds on her farming business, she would like to avail a loan amounting to PHP 25,000 to purchase fertilizers, seedlings, and insecticides for her farm.   She's hoping that her business will continue to grow and become more profitable.

name: Sairakul
description: Sairakul is 51 years old, married, and is raising three children while also running her own farm. She has a secondary-level education, and as the primary source of income for her family, she raises animals, which she began doing 25 years ago with the purchase of livestock for 10,000 som (KGS). Thanks to Sairakul's very hard work, her farm now has 8 cows. Her monthly profit is around 23,000 som (KGS).In order to continue developing her farm, Sairakul has applied to Bai Tushum Bank CJSC for a loan of 100,000 som (KGS) to buy some steers for fattening and resale. Sairakul plans to use the income from her loan to continue increasing her quantity of domesticated livestock, and to construct a grocery store near her house.

name: Ana Cecilia
description: ANA CECILIA M. D. A., lives in the city of Soyapango, on the outskirts of the capital of El Salvador.  At 50 years of age, she lives with her mother, her husband, and children.  Thanks to a middle education, Ana Cecilia began a small store in her own home, where she works to sell products of basic necessity, things like eggs and soap, food mixed with other products.  Because of this her sales are very good.  Ana Cecilia needs to augment the products in her store and to be able to get better income in order to meet all the needs of the household.  Since she doesn’t have the necessary resources, she is asking for a loan in order to be able to complete her desire of increasing the inventory in her business, to get more profits and to be able to improve her family’s life.Translated from Spanish by Jessica Kaminsky, Kiva Volunteer

name: Shamim
description: Shamim is 31 years old and the mother of five children. For 10 years, Shamim has been running a business selling milk. She initiated her own business by buying a buffalo to support her family at a point in time when her husband was the only breadwinner. With the passage of time, her sales increased and so did her income. Now she has two buffaloes and one cow. This has all happened due to her courage and determination. She also deals in animal sales and purchases on a seasonal basis. Because of her work, Shamim is respected in her home. She helps her husband in all family matters as well as financial matters. She has some savings and applied for a loan of 45,000 PKR to purchase another buffalo. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands her business. She is in her 4th loan cycle and has shown good repayment behavior.

name: Edna
description: Edna is 30 years old and single with two children. With two children currently in school, Edna works very hard to provide for them.  Edna runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 8000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional items to sell like beverages, canned goods, junk foods, and other groceries.  Edna has been in this business for 5 years and sells a variety of items.   In the future, Edna would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Ulviyya
description: Ulviyya V. lives in the Bilasuvar Internally Displaced Settlement to which she and her family fled during the Azerbaijan-Armenian conflict in 1993.  A young and ambitious single woman of 24 caring for her pensioned parents, she operates a business selling wedding dresses. The enterprise is going very well due to the advice that she renders to clients plus the fact that it is the only shop offering such products for many kilometers.  Now Ulviyya would now like to further develop her business and is therefore requesting a loan of $1200 to purchase wedding accessories to offer for sale in her shop.  Let’s help this young girl in her small business!

name: Nigora
description: Nigora is a farmer. She was born in 1983 and has three children. She is married. She deals with farming and animal husbandry. Her husband deals with animal husbandry. She is a main provider for her family. Her children do very well at their studies. She wants her children to be educated, and she wants to have good home conditions for their studying. She wants to get a loan to repair her house. She is asking for a loan of 1,500 TJS to repair her house. She awaits your help and understanding.

name: Habib Begum
description: Habib Begum is a house wife of 44 years of age. She looks after her family, including three children. She is a very hardworking and punctual lady. Her son is the sole earner for the family. He works in laundry related services. His practice is to gather clothing from door to door for dry cleaning services. He buys necessary raw materials such as laundry soaps, iron, detergents, surfs etc.from the market. He works hard and honestly for a better earning to support her family; he is providing better services.   Habib Begum wants to take a loan so that her son will be able to get more raw items and can iron a maximum amount of clothing on time. In this way Habib Begum’s son is able to provide better financial support to the family to maintain their living standard.  Habib Begum is very thankful to kiva and field partner BRAC Pakistan.

name: Hem
description: Hem Y., 41, sells dried fish at the local food market and typically makes $5 per day in net income. Her husband, Chim Doeun, is a fisherman who catches shrimp and other fish, making $6 per day. They live in Kampong Chhnang province with their six children and two of their children help their parents with the fishing business. It is a large family to support and the education needs of the four children are costly. Hem Y. has asked for a loan of $1000 to help her husband improve his fishing business through the purchase of a new, faster boat. Her husband frequently has to travel a long distance to reach the fishing area where he can catch the shrimp. This purchase can really help his business out and the family hopes that it can improve their standard of living and increase their income. Hem Y. was unavailable for a photograph at the time of the interview, so her husband, Chim Doeun, and his boat are pictured above.

name: Ruth
description: Ruth is 24 years old. She is energetic and friendly. She is the third born in a family of four and she lives with her brother in a household of four. Ruth has completed training with Zoona to start running her own Zoona mobile money transfer business in her hometown of Blantyre in Malawi. Her business will provide the services of sending and receiving money to a lot of people in her community.  Ruth is requesting a loan to help her start her business. This loan will help Ruth pay for her set up costs. She will be able to purchase a trading kiosk, a mobile phone to be used to serve her customers, a chair where she can sit as she serves her customers, and a cash box where she can keep her cash for safety. This loan will also provide Ruth with the float needed for her to serve her customers.   Zoona has done market research in the area where Ruth is going to set up and has determined that the location for this kiosk is ideal. Ruth will be one of the main operators of Zoona mobile money transfers in Blantyre and a large number of families will be using her service to send and receive their monies.   Ruth’s dream is to create employment to her fellow young people. She explains that employment in Malawi is very scarce and that by starting her own business, she will hopefully be able to empower other young people. Ruth explains that she finished high school in 2010 and went to college but did not complete her course because she did not have the financial support. With her business, she hopes to help other young people in similar situations to be able to earn money and pay for their education. Ruth thanks the Kiva lenders.

name: Moses
description: Moses is a 22-year-old  single man with no children.  He earns his income selling crops and earning profit from his retail shop. He grows coffee, bananas, maize, cowpeas and beans. He also has chickens and goats.  Moses looks forward to becoming a Community Knowledge Worker (CKW). As a CKW he will use his business-in-a-box (smartphone and solar charger) to disseminate vital agricultural information to the other members of his village and help them to improve their crop yields and increase their incomes.  With the additional money that he will earn as a CKW, Moses will establish a small retail shop in his community. His biggest dream in life is to educate  his children to the university level.

name: Rebecca
description: Rebecca is 28 years old, married, and has two children, one of whom is in school. Rebecca works very hard to provide for them.  Rebecca runs a buy and sell coconut business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for three years and requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more coconut to sell.  In the future Rebecca would like to build and expand her business to secure the financial stability of her family.

name: Peter
description: Peter is applying for his second loan with KADET LTD after repaying the previous loan successfully. Peter will use the loan to buy seedlings and fertilizer for his farm. With the anticipated profit from the business, he will educate his children. His hopes and dreams are to venture into pig rearing, which will increase his income and improve the living standard of his family.

name: Myagmarsuren
description: Myagmarsuren is 31 years old and lives with his 9-year-old daughter in the province of Khovd in western Mongolia. He and his family live in a ger, a traditional Mongolian nomadic tent. His wife must stay at home due to a disability and his daughter attends a local secondary school.   Myagmarsuren operates a transportation service in his town. He transports coal and firewood to the local residents. He began his business in 2001 and since then, he has expanded and grown his business steadily. Firewood and coal are the main home heating fuels in Mongolia and transporting them to the soums and villages is an important service.   In the future, he is planning to purchase a new truck and grow vegetables so that he can sell them at the local market for extra income. He says, “I have planted a small number of vegetables in past years and I am planning on planting a larger number of vegetables next year.” Myagmarsuren is requesting a 1,100,000 tugrug (~770 USD) loan in order to purchase replacement parts for his truck so that he can continue delivering firewood and coal this winter.  About XacBank  XacBank was founded in 2001, and listed its first loan on Kiva in January 2009. It is the largest microfinance organization in Mongolia, but also has mainstream commercial operations. XacBank has the vision, scale and innovation to develop and implement new solutions to poverty. It is currently utilizing Kiva’s 0% lending interest rate to return 9% of interest paid from borrowers to them in the form of a savings account at the end of their loans. This not only allows borrowers to gain financially, but also encourages them to save.  To get regular updates from XacBank, please join our lending team.  To lend to more Mongolian borrowers, please click here.

name: Dede
description: Dede is 26 years old and married with a 7-year-old child. She sells clothes on credit and also household tools. She usually earns $5 per day. Her husband, Endih, sells fruit in Jakarta and earns $15 income per day. She really needs a $50 loan to buy more goods and to expand her husband's business. She is willing to repay this loan within a period of 12 months.

name: Tumurpurev
description: Tumurpurev S. is 27-year-old and lives with his 22-year-old wife and daughter in Arhangai Province, one of Mongolia's central provinces. His daughter is just 2-year-old and stays home with her mother.   Tumurpurev is a talented carpenter. He makes various items of furniture, including tables, chairs, and beds. Since he opened his  business in 2005, he has been doing great and expanding his business. His business capital has increased from 200,000 MNT (~ $140) to 800,000 MNT ($550). With his business profits, he was able to purchase a small piece of land with a small house for his family. He says that he would like to expand his business and make better quality furniture for locals.   He is requesting a loan to purchase cut wood for his carpentry business.

name: Ghaith
description: Ghaith is 24 years old and a single guy. He has five brothers and sisters.  Ghaith is a university student who is majoring in economics, and he has applied for this loan to pay for his semester fees.   After graduation Ghaith would love to work in the  field of economics.

name: Erlinda
description: Erlinda F. is from the town of Malibangcao Clarin, Misamis Occidental. She is 61 years old. Erlinda is married and has 1 adult-aged child. To make a living, Erlinda owns and  operates a specialized retail store. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling firewood in the local community. Erlinda has been engaged in her business for over 5 years and earns approximately 6,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2007, Erlinda joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Erlinda has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5,000 PHP from GDMPC. Erlinda is requesting a new loan of 3,000 PHP, which will be used to invest in expanding the business. This loan will be the fourth loan taken out by Erlinda from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three unit offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Sitan
description: Sitan was born around 1965 in Mandela, Sikasso Cercle, in the third administrative region of Mali. She is the mother of four children and still lives with her ​​husband in Mandela. She has been in the business of buying and selling grain for more than 7 years. Her experience in this trade has earned her a good reputation, and she receives orders from a variety of clients.   In order to have the resources necessary to meet her clients' needs, Sitan partnered with Soro Yiriwaso three years ago. Her previous loans have been repaid. This new loan will allow Sitan to purchase fifteen 50-kilogram bags of fonio (an important species of millet that was among the first grains to be cultivated in West Africa) and five bags of maize. She buys her stock in the surrounding villages of Mandela and usually sells to men and women locally and in Sikasso. With this loan, she hopes to make an average monthly profit of 32,000 CFA francs per month. These profits will be used to pay the interest on her loan, and the rest will be reinvested in her business. She is counting on becoming a well-reputed wholesaler in order to satisfy her growing customer base.

name: Penina
description: Penina S. is a young talented woman of thirty-two who believes in herself.  She is a mother of five children, and they spend most of their time with her husband developing their business. She strongly believes in her small farm because her husband and her two brothers are giving her support.  She sells her products at the market, and she has no doubt that she will succeed because of the growth of the customers each and every day of the week.  Penina suggested that her business would never fail because her family works full time to maintain their farm in good condition.

name: Prosperidad Group
description: The “PROSPERIDAD” communal bank will start its 10th cycle in Pro Mujer as part of the Cascada Focal Center.  It has 11 members and its President is Roset.  The businesses of the members are different.  Among them we find: commerce, production and services.  Roset, group President, states that she’s participated in Pro Mujer for three years and became part of the institution through an invitation from the advisors.  Currently Roset is weaving blankets thanks to skills learned from her mother.  She’s been in this line of work for 6 years.  The loan she’s taking out now will be used to buy fabric for blankets that she’ll get at the 16 D. Julio market.  Later, she’ll sell them at a fixed stand she has at the market.  This work method allows her to generate income to support her family because she has a spouse and a daughter.  When she is asked what she likes about Pro Mujer she answers that she likes the training.

name: Mirleny
description: Mirleny is a very hard-working woman. She is requesting a loan of $700 in order to buy building materials. Her goal is to make the necessary improvements to her home so she can make it safe for her family and improve their quality of life.

name: Sol De Verano_Media Lina Group
description: There are six members of the group “Sol de Verano, Media Luna” (Summer Sun, Half Moon). They are a united and happy group. Beatrice, 52 years old, sells rice and sugar in the Garita Zone. Charo, 29 years old, sells vegetables in the “Max Paredez”. Noemî, eighteen years old, makes dolls. Eusebio, 62 years old, sells clothes in different fairs and Victoria and Evelin sell products on credit. All of them need a loan to buy merchandise and to offer a variety to their customers.Translated from Spanish by Esther Levandoski, Kiva Volunteer

name: Josephat
description: Josephat is a 41-year-old married father of 3 children, ages 9, 14, and 16 years old.  He is from Thika and practices dairy farming with his wife, Jane.  Josephat has been in the farming business for the past four years. He earns a monthly income of KES 21,500, which he uses to support his family. This marks his third loan term with VisionFund Kenya, after successfully repaying his previous loans. He will use the loan to buy another dairy cow and animal feed for his cows.  The additional income created will allow him to improve the standard of living for his family and to reinvest the remaining amount in his business. In the future, Josephat would like to buy more dairy cows.  He hopes to save money to educate his children to the university level.

name: Karina
description: Karina is 19 years old, single, and lives with her parents and siblings who are her greatest priority.  She will use the money from this loan to repair part of her home because the water leaks in when it rains.  She wants to take advantage of the low prices and sales on good quality building materials to make the repairs.  With these repairs she is hoping for better stability and wellbeing for her family so that they can spend the New Year in peace and begin 2013 with better living conditions and hope.  This will be her first loan through FUDECOSUR.  She has not had any previous loans with other banks, but FUDECOSUR provided her a loan with no problems and at a much lower interest rate.

name: Paulina
description: Paulina, who is in her late 50s, is married with five grown children. She has been running a poultry business for 10 years now. She works from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily and is able to make a good monthly profit.  This will be Paulina’s fourth loan from Tujijenge Tanzania. She used her previous loan to improve her business and has paid back all her loans successfully. She used the profit to cover household expenses and loan repayment and to reinvest in business.  She will use this loan to improve her business through buying more broilers (poultry). She dreams of making her business grow.   Paulina will make sure she repays her loans within the loan schedule time.

name: Zuwena
description: Mambo from Tanzania! This is 29 year old Zuwena J. from Mwanza. She is married with two children, between the ages of 3 and 11 years old. Zuwena has been running a Mobile phone accessories business since 2005. It is amazing how many people have mobile phones in Tanzania. This is probably attributable to the fact that it is the only form of phone communication available to most people, because there are few landlines, and followed closely by how relatively cheap mobile phones are here. She works at the business for 12 hours per day, days per week. Zuwena currently earns about 150USD from her business. She is requesting a loan of 400USD in order to purchase more mobile phone accessories. In the future, she plans to expand her business. Zuwena thanks you for your support!  ABOUT SELFINA! SELFINA has taken a lead role as a pioneer of micro-credit in Tanzania through Micro-Leasing. The organization is engaged in the economic empowerment of women in Tanzania through the provision of a leasing and leaseback microfinance facility. Customs and traditions in Tanzania make it difficult for women to own land and assets, thus they are termed non-creditworthy by financial institutions. This leads to poor financial support and poor access to basic needs and services for women with low incomes. One of the primary advantages of microleasing is that it allows clients to use the equipment as collateral for future loans with SELFINA, thus enabling them to borrow larger sums in the future.

name: Azizkhuja
description: K. Azizkhuja is dedicated to agriculture and to the growing of grapes, which means that he can be around his family, helping to raise their quality of life and educate his three children.  Azizkhuja has been characterized as a person who is hardworking, since he has been working in agriculture since he was very young. This kind of work requires effort, dedication and above all, strength, as it can include heavy work, meaning that people get tired quickly.  In spite of this, Azizkhuja is determined to raise to the standard of living in his family, and to improve the quality of the seeds he cultivates. For this reason, he is asking for help in order to be able to receive more credit from IMON International.   More about Tajikistan and IMON International Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium B.C. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit:  www.imon.tj

name: Tatiana Rocio
description: Tatiana is 23 years old, in a common-law marriage, and has children. She lives with her husband and children in the area of Desvió De los Amarillos, part of the Ventanas Canton in Los Ríos province. She belongs to the PEQUEÑOS AGRICULTORES communcal bank which is located in the same area. The people here earn a living through agriculture and livestock.  Tatiana earns a living by farming corn and raising corralled animals such as chickens and pigs. With this loan, she will be able to buy supplies such as fertilizers, manure, seeds, urea, insecticides to prevent infestations and diseases, and animal feed. The purchases will be made in Ventanas city.   Tatiana's dream is to buy land to continue farming. She enjoys celebrating during the holidays for the area's patron saint.

name: Eusebia
description: The member continues to be dedicated to work in a public institution and also opened a shop where she sells clothing like pants, blouses and  sweaters. The member sells for men, children and women. She has been working at the institution for eight years. Her dream is to expand her clothing shop business. She is requesting the loan to buy polos, sweaters and pants and wholesale.  The member is happy about the loan and promises to make her payments on time.

name: Saodat
description: Saodat is married and has one son. She decided to start a new business with her husband that involved animals in order to generate an income with which she can contribute to her home’s finances. She studied a course about how ‘To get ahead’ at a women's organization and she got enough skills about business.  Her son will help her with the business. She will be a very successful business woman as she is hardworking and smart. She is asking for a loan of 5000 somoni to buy cattle to organize a new business. She awaits your support.

name: Ma. Theresa
description: Ma. Theresa previously accessed a 30,000 PHP loan that she utilized to buy feed and poultry needed in her business. Her earnings were a big help for the education of her children, and also in her personal, household and business expenditures.  She would like to apply for another 35,000 PHP loan. She will be utilizing the loan to buy feed and poultry needed in her business. Her profits from this business will definitely help sustain their daily needs and the education of her children. She looks forward to this financial increase with gladness and thankfulness in her heart.  Ma. Theresa dreams to be more successful in her business and hopes to have their house renovated. She meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her life and business every week and draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God that she studies.  *All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans.

name: Maria Isabel
description: Maria Isabel P. is a responsible woman who is dedicated to selling groceries. She has a small store in her house. Currently, her business is not well stocked. This business is located in a strategic place since the influx of people is quite large.   She will use the loan to buy more products and better stock her business. She has told us that her sales have grown but she doesn't have enough capital to be able to buy more products. She needs her earnings to cover her house and family bills.   Translated from Spanish by Kate Divjak, Kiva Volunteer

name: Florence
description: In the rural areas, people talk more about their farm animals than they do about their businesses. In many ways, they can count on their animals to keep them sustained more than they can count on their businesses. Much talk between neighbors is about the health and productivity of their animals. “How’s your cow?” “Not so well, she only gave 4 liters of milk yesterday. How’s your chicken?”  Along with animals, people always cultivate the soil and plant a few banana trees, sweet potatoes, beans, maize, cassava and even a little coffee, usually just enough for their own use. This year there has been a drought so the yields are quite small.  Florence has one adult cow and two calves. It would be rare to have someone have more than this in this rural area of Uganda, the plots of land are far too small. But Florence has a large plot and she even hopes to buy another cow. She has cross breeds which tend to be less prone to disease and give more milk.  Florence also sells new children’s and women’s clothing in the market. She has been selling clothing for 7 years, and has been a member of her lending group for two and half years. With her loan, she will buy more clothing to sell.

name: Cristina
description: Cristina is a 42-year-old mother who lives in her own home together with her husband and her children who are still dependent on her.  They have a small house in a rural village called "Sialupe Baca de Punto 9" which is located some 20 minutes from Lambayeque district, which is 15 minutes from the city of Chiclayo.  The people in Cristina's village mainly work in farming and livestock raising.  It is a developing area and, right now, the only basic service they have access to is electricity.  Cristina's daily business is raising and selling animals such as cattle, sheep, farmyard birds (ducks and turkeys), guinea pigs, etc.  This is a business that she has always worked in and she has approximately 10 years experience.  She inherited the business from her parents who taught her, from a very early age, how to buy and sell animals.  She has set up spaces on her property where she raises these animals.  In addition, Cristina also makes daily income selling 'chicha de jora' (a traditional, corn-based drink).  Her children and husband work together with her in undertaking new family projects.  They work every day to achieve their goals and thereby improve their living conditions.  Cristina has clear and established goals.  She would like to buy nutritionally-balanced feed which she will use to fatten her animals.  She will also buy ingredients for making more 'chicha de jora'.  Cristina has requested a loan for 700 soles from Edpyme Alternativa which will help her to make more income.  This will enable her to improve her quality of life and also repay her loan.  Cristina has been an entrepreneurial woman since she was very young thanks to the values that her parents instilled in her.  These values are now recognized by her neighbors who have a great deal of admiration for her because she is always looking out for her family's well-being.

name: Rashid
description: Rashid is a 35 year old multi business man. He is married with three children, all below ten years. Rashid is a cameraman: he runs a photo studio, a poultry business and a vegetable garden. He has been a cameraman for the past 15 years; the poultry and the vegetable businesses are just  three years old. Rashid gets tenders to shoot and supply chickens  for  weddings and other ceremonies. He has recently received business training from Youth Self Employment Foundation and photo studio management training from KODAK. He has employed three people to assist him. His wife also assists him in the poultry and vegetable farming business.   Rashid is now requsting USD 400 to help him buy some equipment for his studio and to stock more chicks.

name: Veronica Leticia
description: Verónica Rodríguez, 30, lives in the outskirts of Guayaquil along the city's Perimetral (ring road) in a cement house.  Her husband sells fish from a bicycle.  They have a son who is 10 years old.  She started out as a domestic employee; when she lost that job she bought fish in the market in Guayaquil and decided that this was going to be her main economic activity.  Now she works in the area outside her home selling fish and shrimp each day.  Her husband helps her with the sale of shrimp on his bicycle.  She sells fish at $2.00 per pound, the shrimp at $2.00 per pound and the calamari at $2.00 per pound.  One of the complications of her business is dealing with crime.  With this loan she wants to buy fish, shrimp and calamari for her business.  In the future she wants to have a place to sell seafood.  Translated from Spanish by Lisa Grobar, Kiva Volunteer

name: Neang
description: Neang N., 39, has been in the farming business since 1990 in the province of Pursat. Her husband helps her in growing crops. The family work hard every day at their business activities and never waste time because they want to send their four children to study at high school and university.   The family are facing a problem in the farming business because their farmland is full of water during the rainy season; that is why they hope to buy a piece of land by looking for a loan on Kiva. Neang N. plans to use 30% of the loan to pay for plowing a field.

name: Rowena
description: Rowena is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a buy and sell dried fish and vegetables business in the Philippines. Rowena has been in this business for 10 years. She earns additional income from food vending.  She is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF to buy additional dried fish and vegetables to sell for her business.  She has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She hopes to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college in the future.

name: Wilbert Isaias
description: This member is still working in school transportation. He has a van he uses for transportation. He works from 8:00 a.m. until 1:00 p.m.and has been doing this job for 6 years. With this job, he wants to get his children ahead. His dream is to buy a new car. He has asked for the loan to buy tires for his car.  He is happy with the loan he has been given and grateful to the  Kiva investors.

name: Myrna
description: Myrna, 46 years old,  is married to Cornelio B., and they are blessed with four children: Marvin - 21 years old, fourth year college student at Isabela State University; Maybel - 16 years of age, a high school graduate; Morena - 15 years of age, in fourth year high school at Villa Concepcion National High School, and Mark Carlo - 7 years old, a grade one pupil. Their house is located near the Barangay hall and elementary school.  Myrna has managed a typical village store for almost a year now, earning a daily net income PHP 500.00.  Her husband, who works as an electrician, a farmer, and a private driver, earns PHP 1,000.00 for each trip. Myrna is requesting a loan of PHP 6,000.00 from KIVA lenders for the additional requirements of her business. She is hopeful that the loan will result in increased income from her store.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth is 52 years old and married with 5 children.  Elizabeth works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and has requested a loan of 25,000 PHP through NWTF to purchase additional stocks to sell.  Elizabeth has borrowed and repaid 9 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 4 years and also earns an income from electronic reloading, food vending and selling vegetables.  Elizabeth aspires to save money to expand her business.

name: Mary Ann
description: Mary Ann is 24 years old and married with five children, three of whom are in school. Mary Ann works very hard to provide for them.She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 4,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell such as soft drinks, soap, milk, sugar, eggs, noodles, etc.Mary Ann has been in this business for one year.In the future, Mary Ann would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Evelyn Rosario
description: Evelyn is seeking refinancing for a sixth loan to invest into making improvements to her home (building a new room).  She has worked as a teacher at the César Augusto Salinas Pinell School for the past 10 years.  She has an 11-year old daughter who is in fifth grade.  Her husband works in construction and they share the household expenses.  In addition, she helps to take care of her elderly parents.  Evelyn has high hopes of personal success, is very responsible, and an educator who loves her work since she helps many children learn to read and write in an urban zone of New Guinea.  Her dreams include finishing her degree in Education Sciences, having stable employment, good health, living in a home with better conditions.  She is thankful to AFODENIC, since the previous credits have allowed her to slowly improve her living conditions.    Translated from Spanish by Mary Lynn Malaby, Kiva Volunteer

name: Onyinye
description: Onyinye is a peaceful and hard-working woman. She lives in Lagos state. She sells drinks and cooked food in her shop. She cooks mouth-watering Nigerian foods for her customers. She is married with five children. Her children are still in primary school and she hopes they become graduates in the future. Onyinye has a lot of responsibility. That is why she is very optimistic about the prosperity of her business and that of her family. She is 34 years old and her husband is a businessman. She hopes for a loan of NGN 100,000 to purchase more drinks and foodstuffs to cook and to sell. She says thank you to all KIVA lenders.

name: Jorge Luis
description: Jorge Luis is a responsible man who is concerned with getting ahead together with his family. He works long hours as a taxi driver during the night shift, which makes his work dangerous at times. With his income he covers the basic needs of his two children, one of whom is 16 years old and the other just 4 months of age. His desire is to see them become true professionals with a range of work opportunities that he was not able to have. Jorge Luis is requesting the loan to invest in his taxi unit. He is constantly having to invest money in it, because of the bad state of the roads in Managua, which do not provide good conditions for his vehicle, causing it to deteriorate. He needs to invest so that he can continue working and covering his household expenses.

name: Anastacia
description: Anastacia lives in San Francisco Gotera, in the department of Morazán. She sells food like tortillas and pupusas--a traditional Salvadoran dish made of handmade corn flat bread stuffed with cheese, fried pork rind, and/or refried beans. She lives with her husband and three children. Her business is located downtown in a rented space. She has been in business for approximately 3 years.  She is requesting a loan in order to purchase corn, quesillo--a type of soft cheese, and other ingredients to make the dishes she sells. This loan will help her increase production and provide better customer service.  Anastasia's goals are to improve her business, to help her children get an education, and to invest in her home.

name: Aida
description: Married with one adult son and three grandchildren, Aida has been a banana lands worker since she was 15.  She aims to buy construction materials with the loan, such as corrugated metal and beams, to improve her housing conditions.  In the future, she wants to finish her home and start her own business to increase her income.  She is committed to repay the Hluvuku loan in order to request future loans.  The challenges she faces to complete her project are unemployment and illness.

name: Melaia
description: Melaia F., 55, is married with 3 children.  She has 2 years of experience in the sales business. She sells to the villagers 7 days per week. She has 2 previous loans with SPBD.  She expects her weekly net cash flow to be 550 Tala (~229 USD).  SPBD loans are Melaia’s only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with the traditional banks.

name: Esquipulita Group
description: The Friendship Bridge Trust Bank “Esquipulita” is made up of seven women from the rural community of Santa Lucia La Reforma, located in Southwestern Guatemala.  All of the women are enthusiastic, hardworking and very determined. Antonia is one of the members of the Trust Bank who is 46 years of age and has four children. One of her children is in school.   Antonia was never able to attend school but has had her own business since she was a child. She is a role model for her friends in the Trust Bank who see by her example that it is possible to transform poverty into opportunities. Antonia has several businesses. She makes baskets with ribbons that one of her children sells. She has a “tortilleria” in a nearby town, where tortillas are made three times each day. With the help of one of her daughters and two other women, the business is flourishing and sales have increased to the point where Antonia is considering opening another one. She is requesting a loan to purchase more material for baskets, and supplies including corn, lime and gas for the “tortilleria”.  The women of the Trust Bank “Esquipulita” are grateful for the “Micro-credit Plus” Program (loans + education) that Friendship Bridge provides them. They acquire knowledge about a variety of subjects. Each month, a Loan Officer from the organization shares relevant information with the ladies in their own language about women’s health and women’s rights as well as leadership and self-esteem. They have also learned about budgeting, accounting, pricing, marketing and customer service. These are just a few examples of what the ladies are learning.  The women are most appreciative to Kiva investors for funding their loans and believing in their ability to improve their lives and succeed. They are determined to reach their goals and dreams.     A report on their progress will be given in the very near future. Thank you, Kiva investors!

name: Fanta
description: Ms. Fanta Kébé is 31 years old, married, and the mother of two children.  She lives in a large traditional family in the Médine district of Ségou (4th administrative region of the Republic of Mali).  For societal reasons, she dropped out of school early, so as to sell fish along side her mother.  Her apprenticeship lasted only six months or so.  Today, she is more than a fledgling, advancing on her own and enjoying recognition and a large customer base.  Her selling power is due to the quality of her goods.   With plans to increase her business capital, in order to realize more profits, she turned to micro-finance institution Soro Yiriwaso.  She has been associated with it for the last 48 months and has properly repaid four solidarity loans and two individual loans.  She is now on her third individual loan.    Fanta intends to use this loan to buy 200 kg of capitaine fish.  She supplies herself locally.  She accepts cash or credit from customers composed of women and men.    With this loan, she envisions realizing a monthly profit of 100,000 francs CFA.  This profit will enable Fanta to bolster her capital and to help her father with covering family expenses.  Her ambition is to build a house. Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Melecio
description: Melecio is 35 years old and single. He lives in Clarin, Misamis Occidental.   He owns and operates a food vending business, selling dried fish, canned goods, coffee and sugar in the local community to earn a living. He has had this business for over three years and earns 5,000PHP every month. He joined GDMPC in 2011 and has requested a loan of 8,000PHP to purchase additional products to sell. He wants to save money for emergencies.

name: Dilsa
description: Dilsa is 49 years old, the mother of 3 children, 2 of them are independent, she currently lives with the youngest of her daughter's and her husband who is in ill health. She has sold groceries for 15 years in her home. What she enjoys about her job is to be in contact with her customers with which she has many conversations with and has made many friends. This business is very profitable, as it is located in a very good area so it is doing very well. Due to her husband’s health, she has to ensure the livelihood of her household, which tends to be a heavy burden for Dilsa, but the love of her family gives her the will to continue. This is her ninth loan with MFP, and throughout all this time she has proven to be very responsible with her group and with payments. With the money she requests she will expand her store and buy more products as necessary.Translated from Spanish by Jennie Campos, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sr. De Huanca De Coya Group
description: Janet’s 29-years-old and in a common law relationship; she has two children.  She’s from Calca Province in Cusco Department.  She is an enterprising, responsible mother who supports her family.  She sells food; she has a small restaurant in the city of Coya in Calca Province.  She opened her small restaurant four months ago and does well thanks to the work she does.  On this occasion, Janet needs the loan to buy merchandise like sacks of sugar, sacks of rice, boxes of noodles, oil, vegetables and meats, among others.  (Janet is raising her hand in the photo).  This group is composed of friends and neighbors who formed the “Señor de Huanca de Coya” communal bank in Calca Province, Cusco Department.  The members are people who are constantly seeking ways to get ahead and by means of their work provide a better future for their children.  As a group they are grateful for the opportunity being provided them and commit go make their various installment payments as scheduled.  Cusco is located in Cusco District and Province belonging to Cusco Department in the very heart of the ancient city of the Incas.  It’s noted for being a tourist destination because of its archaeological sites, historic city center, scenery, history and for being a charming city in the southern region of the country.  Cusco is also known for its traditional Inti Raymi festival and because one of the Seven Wonders of the World, Machupicchu, is located here.

name: Alejandra Apolinar
description: Alejandra is a single woman who makes her living through the independent sale of merchandise, such as shoes and accessories. As you can see, she is a head of household who is getting ahead thanks to her occupation, which she does door-to-door. Thanks to the clientele that she has developed throughout her career, she sells products from home, affording her customers installment payments. She is a responsible and happy person who is disciplined and very organized. She is requesting a loan to buy a lot of shoes, clothing and accessories, as the purchase will be much more affordable that way and she will see increased earnings when she sells the merchandise. If you want to know more about the entrepreneurs and the loans from Interactuar, you can join the Lending Team called: “Friends of Interactuar Colombia”: http://www.kiva.org/team/interactuar_colombia

name: Ana Rocio
description: The San Patricio Community Bank meets every 15 days in the Cuba barrio in the city of Manta, which is known for its beautiful beaches and for being a place of unmatched beauty with many tourist attractions. It is here we find Ana, who is 41 years old and has twin 3-year-old daughters with her common-law husband, who is a master carpenter. Along with being a great mother and housewife, Ana makes a living selling fish by the pound. She has a space set up in her house to sell fish in the morning and to sell fast food in the afternoon and evening. She loves to work because she makes her own income to help her husband with the tough task of providing for the household. At her business she sells hot dogs, hamburgers, empanadas and fruit smoothies. She has more than 20 years of experience with this work and it has been going rather well. She plans to use the loan to purchase fish, meat, sausages, bread, fruit and other items to prepare her meals. She has been with the community bank since its inception and likes it because thanks to the loan she has been able to purchase certain things necessary for her business. Her dream is to have a big store or restaurant.

name: Elizbath
description: Elizbath is a 31 years old woman, with one child, who lives in Lahore, Pakistan. Her husband is a rickshaw driver by profession. He has been running an auto rickshaw for the last six years from the past many days his rickshaw is not working properly because of regular use. He feels that most of its parts are out of order. So he is unable to generate any amount of income. He wants to buy a new auto rickshaw. However due to the lack of money he finds it difficult to cover the cost of new rickshaw. Therefore she has requested for a loan from Kiva's partner BRAC Pakistan to help her husband to cover the cost of a new rickshaw. This will help him to continue his business. Elizbath is so much thankful to Kiva and brac Pakistan

name: Larrisa
description: Larrisa is 47 years old and has five children. Larrisa is married and has one child who is currently in school.  Larrisa is in the agricultural business, pig fattening in the Philippines. Larrisa requested a PHP 25000 loan through NWTF to buy piglets, feeds and other supplies to raise her business.  Larrisa has been in pig fattening for 10 years now, and has borrowed 27 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  Larrisa would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Jhon
description: Jhon (24 years old) is a hardworking, single young man. He lives with his mother, Agripina, with whom he has forged his destiny and work, in his own home located in the town of Pampas.  Along with his mother he opened a beauty salon, with not only haircutting services, styling, and dyeing hair, but also they have steam relaxation therapy machines, also massages and they rent evening wear and suits for men. All of this means they offer a complete service.   In this work they also have hired people to help his mother, as he is in charge of managing it, and he visits during business hours, as he is studying psychology at the university in town, and he also works in a video game business where he maintains the machines. “This work is not all day, they only call me when one of the machines breaks down,” he says. Now they are about to start the project of renewing their machines to save energy and especially to help with the environmental conservation. Also, he plans to reduce costs with the acquisition of supplies in quantity, “doing this, the price of purchase per unit of products deployed will drop considerably,” he says.  This is the fifth loan through MFP and he is grateful for the support given, with which he could better his business and as a consequence, his income. In addition, he promises to be punctual with the repayment of his loan, because he wants to continue achieving his goals and working with the members of his group, who are trustworthy and united.  Jhon will invest the money from the loan in the purchase of an appliance for shampooing hair, hair dyes, shampoo, and other supplies in quantity, in order to do his work.

name: Samnang's Group
description: Living in a rural village of the Battambang province, Samnang is 24 years old and a mother of one kid. She is a carpenter and this is her main single source of her income. She can save her daily income to support her family about 2.5 USD per day and she has been with this business for ages. She has been with VisionFund for two cycles and this is her third micro loan. The previous loans, her family’s business has improved gradually. She leads a group of two to seeking a new loan. As the group leader, she will manage her entire loan portion to buy more paint to support her business to get more income for her family. She wishes that she can earn more income to expand her business to be bigger than before.

name: Baraka Group
description: Philip is a member of Baraka Group in Kakamega South District. He is pictured with 17 One Acre Fund farmers, 13 women and 4 men. Philip is standing on the right, with his hand raised. He is receiving an input loan for 0.5 acres of maize, millet, and sorghum cultivation.   Philip first enrolled with One Acre Fund during the 2011 Long Rains season and is now preparing to be a One Acre Fund farmer during the 2013 Long Rains season. Philip joined One Acre Fund in order to access the best input prices and grow enough food for the family.  Philip reports that before One Acre Fund, he was able to grow about eight bags of maize per 1.5 acres, but with his One Acre Fund input loan during Long Rains 2012, he harvested 15 bags per acre! He plans to use the money that he earns from his next harvest to invest in livestock and save for the future.   For the 2013 Long Rains season, Baraka Group members will take input loans of 0.5 acres each. In total, this group will receive input loans for use on 8.5 acres of land.

name: Fidel Angel
description: Fidel Ángel is a 40 year-old gentleman who lives in San Rafael Oriente, in San Miguel department, together with his wife and children aged 17, 14 and 12.  Fidel has been growing corn and beans for 25 years.  He learned how to farm from his father and works regularly every day from 6.00am to 3.00pm, or longer if need be.  Fidel is currently in the process of sowing a new crop of basic grains.  He is requesting a loan to invest in buying manure and fertilizers.  This purchase will enable him to better care for his crops and take care of their growth.  He hopes to obtain good fruit from his crops.  There are always risks in this business as everything depends on weather conditions which can favor or damage crops.  Fidel is motivated by his desire to continue working since his family depend on him.  In particular, he wants to prepare his children as he hopes that they will become professionals in the future.
town: San Rafael de Oriente, San Miguel

name: Parveen
description: Parveen is a 44-year-old woman who lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. She has one child. Her husband is responsible to fulfill the needs of family. Parveen also provides sewing services, thereby earning income to contribute to the management of the household. Parveen needs different kinds of goods like needles, thread, pieces of cloth and machine oil for her business purposes, but due to insufficient financial means she is unable to purchase these materials. Therefore, she has applied for a Kiva loan from its field partner BRAC Pakistan. This loan will enable her to purchase the above materials, helping her to increase her monthly sales and profit by providing better sewing services.Parveen is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Dioan
description: Dioan is a widow who is 48-years-old and resides at Locsoon, Tudela, Misamis Occidental, Philippines.   Dioan owns and operates a coconut production to earn a living, and she earns 4,000 PHP doing this business. Aside from  doing this, she also manages a store selling goods in their community. Recently, she requests a loan of 4,500.00 PHP from Kiva partner GDMPC micro credit in order to buy additional canned goods and dairy products to sell.  In the future, Dioan wants to make improvements to her house and to improve the general living conditions of her family.

name: Cecilia
description: Cecilia, 46 years of age, is a hard-working woman who earns a living through selling boiled peanuts.  Her work is done around the main streets of her town. She is also seeking ways to improve her quality of life so she wants to have adequate funds to support her on going livelihood. She is married woman with five children. Three of them are still attending school.  She decided to join CEVI to purchase more peanuts  and cellophane.  In this way she hopes to improve her financial income. These would enable her to  start saving money for emergency use. In that way, she could provide her family with basic necessities.  She is hoping that she could have other sources of income to continue support the schooling of her children for brighter future.

name: Maria
description: Maria S. is a farmer. She grows rice a short distance from their house. She is 47 years old and has two children. Her husband, Jose S., is also a farmer. He is the one managing the farm. Maria worked previously in Manila as a salesclerk. She stopped working there because she was paid less by her employer.  She is asking a loan of Php 10,000 from CEVI. She will use the loan to buy fertilizers and other farm necessities. The loan will truly help her increase the yield of her farm. She is looking forward for the upcoming harvest once she can purchase the things she needs for her farm.  CEVI is reaching out to more people to help them grow their business. It provides credit assistance, training and insurance coverage as well.

name: Susan
description: Susan is a married woman. She has four children. She operates a retail business where she sells clothes and shoes. She has been involved in this business for 10 years. Her business is located in a good area and her primary customers are locals. She will use the Kes 60,000 loan to buy more stock of clothes and shoes. Her business goal is to have a large store within five years. She hopes that in the future, she will be successful. This is her third loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. Her previous loans were repaid successfully.

name: Francisca
description: Francisca is 47 years old and married with 5 children.  Francisca works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 20000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like shampoo, groceries, etc. for her general store.  Francisca has borrowed and paid 11 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 2 years and also earns an income from buying and selling livestock.  Francisca aspires to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Rosita
description: This is Rosita, 45, resident of Intramuros, Manila, Philippines. Her partner is Eduardo. She, together with her partner, manages their household while operating a business. At this time, she is working hard to continually provide income for their everyday expenses.  Rosita operates a junk shop. Trash is not actively segregated in the Philippines, and while waiting for their local dump trucks, people scavenge garbage dumps and trash bags for recyclable materials like metal, copper, plastic, paper and other materials. They sell these to junk shops for a little profit. Junk shops then stack, clean, and gather huge quantities of these materials and sell them back to foundries like factories and others of the like. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community. She earns a minimum of Php1,000 in sales every day.  To help her continue operations of her business, she is requesting a Php,25,000 loan. She will be incorporating the loan on her current revolving fund to buy recyclable materials from collectors.   Rosita dreams of having a better living and hopes that her business will flourish. She meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her life and business every week and where she can also draw strength and inspiration from the fellowship and from the Word of God she studies.   * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Omaira
description: Omaira is a woman with experience, wisdom, and a lot of patience.  She has one son, and she has worked practically her entire life in order to get him ahead.  She has a small business in which she sells meals that she makes herself at her house.  She works every day from 5:00 a.m. until 3:00 p.m. in order to have her product ready and fresh for her customers.  They are mostly the neighbors in the area where she lives.She wishes to capitalize her business and to have a large amount of supplies on hand and an inventory of products.  To do so, she turns to a loan to buy a new stove and inventory like grains and vegetables for the meals that she prepares.  One of her main difficulties is the lack of money to invest in her business.  However, she puts her trust in  the help of the Interactuar Corporation and the good heart of the Kiva lenders in order to get ahead in her business activity.If you want to know more about the entrepreneurs and the loans from Interactuar, you can join the Lending Team called: “Friends of Interactuar Colombia”: http://www.kiva.org/team/interactuar_colombia

name: Hut
description: Mr. Hut, 25, is a married man who earns a living by fishing in the river with different kinds of equipment. He lives in the province of Siem Reap. Mr. Hut often sells his fresh fish in bulk to his customers who are retailers in the market. Mr. Hut’s wife is a fish breeder and they currently live with her elderly mother. Mr. Hut will use his loan to purchase additional fishing equipment for his business and to buy some fish for feeding.

name: Romualda
description: Romaulda lives in the beautiful city of Paucartambo and is an entrepreneurial and hard working woman who is dedicated to farming, livestock and raising young animals like guinea pigs and hens. At this time, she needs the loan to buy guinea pigs and pigs.

name: Nadezhda
description: Nadezhda is single. She lives in Berdyansk. Nadezhda owns two vending locations at different local markets. She sells men’s and women’s outer clothing and footwear. Nadezhda uses effective marketing techniques, which help her business stay sustainable and profitable. She launched her venture five years ago. Ever since, her turnover capital has increased to 10,000 Grivnyas. Her income amounts to 8,000 Grivnyas a month.   Nadezhda is requesting a loan of 9,000 Grivnyas to increase assorted merchandise in her kiosks. She is an entrepreneur of integrity who can handle challenging situations and is always polite with customers. One of Nadezhda’s future plans is to open one more vending location and expand her business as a result.

name: Karina Ruth
description: Karina is 26 years old, single, and lives with her parents and siblings in the village of Rama Tepo, a rural area in the District of Mochumí, Lambayeque Province.  This community is located an hour away from the city of Chiclayo.  For the past eight months, Karina has been selling groceries from a store she established in her home.  This business is important because it provides the necessary income to cover her personal expenses and support her family.  Her father works in agriculture, but they need an activity that provides a stable income so that they can get ahead.  Karina’s business has been well-received thanks to the quality of service that she provides.  Her store provides daily consumer products that are not readily available in the area because they live far away from the nearest town.  Karina wants to expand her business so that she can meet the demand of her customers.  For this reason, she is requesting her first loan from Edpyme Alternativa in the amount of 500 PEN so that she can invest in the purchase of groceries and achieve her objective.  Karina is a responsible young woman who enjoys her work.  Her neighbors and acquaintances consider her to be a trustworthy person.  Karina's greatest wish is to continue growing as an entrepreneur. Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Genoveva
description: Genoveva, 25, is a serious young woman.  She lives in the company of Paul, her mother and sisters who she loves very much and cares for in the house she was born in.  She studied teaching at a well-known university and finished her career a short time ago and hopes to develop all her skills.  Her main work centers on agriculture, an occupation she learned since childhood helping her mother with the hard work.  There she learned everything necessary to be able to develop her work and improve her income which made it possible for her to pay for her studies and care for her young son.  Now, she’s growing her agricultural products like potatoes, corn, peas and especially starchy potatoes which are her specialty.  She belongs to the “Niño Jesús” communal bank and this is the third MFP loan.  She is grateful for the opportunity for progress and promises to be punctual with her installment payments.  She likes being a member of her association where all are united and supportive.  Genoveva will invest the money in the purchase of organic manure to nourish her crops.

name: Helen
description: Helen is 40 years old and is married with four children. She is a hardworking woman and she is focused. She sells planks to make a living in Warri, Delta State, Nigeria. She loves this business because of the one-on-one interaction that she has with her customers. She also loves her business because it is highly profitable.  Helen is a LAPO client. She hopes for the loan of NGN 100,000 to purchase more planks to sell. She hopes to be a plank distributor in the future. She says thanks to all Kiva lenders.

name: Marsudi
description: Mrs. Marsudi has a family of two and lives in a town in Sidoarjo Regency in Java, Indonesia's most heavily populated island. In Indonesia.  You cannot drink city water and most people don't even have access to piped water. Therefore, most Indonesians depend on purchasing or boiling water.   Mrs. Marsudi heard of a new option for disinfecting water when the promotion crew from Nazava water filters held a safe water training in her vicinity. Nazava Water Filters filter well, rain, and city water so it becomes safe to drink without boiling, without using any fuel or electricity. Mrs. Marsudi who is also a health worker in  her neighborhood seized the opportunity and became the sales representative of Nazava in her area.   Mrs. Marsudi will use this loan  to buy about 20 filters and sell them to her neighbors on credit  making safe drinking water available to 100 people.

name: Margarita María
description: Margarita María is a member of the "MOSOQ ALLPA” community bank which is located in Cusco district, in Cusco province, in Cusco department.  Margarita María is 58 years old, widowed, and has 3 children.  She works for a public company from Monday to Friday, from 8.00am to 1.00pm and from 3.00pm to 7.00pm.  She is a very cheerful person who has a great desire to get her family ahead in life as they are the most important thing that she has.  Margarita María is requesting this loan for her own (non specific) personal use.  She is happy to be receiving the loan and pledges to make her repayments on time.

name: Carlos
description: Carlos is 72 years old, did not attend school, and is in a relationship.  His partner works at home.  He has 5 children, but they do not live at home. They are already in relationships, and they have their own homes.  Two of his grandchildren live with him, but they do not depend on him.   Carlos works with cattle and in agriculture, which he has done for more than 50 years and which he learned from his parents.  He decided to do this in order to bring in extra income to be able to support his family and to send his grandchildren to school.  The distance to his crops is about 1 km from his house and he travels either on foot or by cart.  His partner helps him in life, and one grandchild helps him to do the job.  His work schedule cannot be measured.  The loan he is requesting through CREDICAMPO is to buy more cattle.
