This loan will help him a lot because he will have the opportunity to get more livestock, and will therefore increase his income and have a better quality of life.  His dreams are, in spite of his age, to work as best he can so he is able to have a good life in his old age.  For his grandchildren, he hopes that they study and prepare themselves academically.

name: Nadia
description: Nadia, 29, is a very calm and hard-working young woman.  She lives in a rented room.  What she wants most of all is to improve her quality of life.  Her business is located in the San José market (an important market in the city of Juliaca).  The woven creations that she offers are very much in demand because the items she makes are very original.  She weaves the garments she creates herself, and she gives them the desired finishings.  On the other hand, what she likes best about her work is weaving.  While she is doing it she feels better.  She has been in this business for eight years.  The most difficult part is taking her creations to the stall where she sells them because she lives far from there.  In the future she hopes to get together enough money to set up a store where she can sell her garments more peacefully.  This is Nadia’s first loan with MFP.  She expects to be very punctual with her payments; she does not want to cause problems for her communal bank.  She is very happy with the communal bank, and she knows it will help her progress.  She will use the 1,000 PEN she is requesting to buy more wool in order to increase the quantity of garments she produces.  Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Kadiatu
description: Kadiatu S. is 38 years and married with 6 children. She has been running her bakery business for 17 years on a very small scale. She was renting the bakery from other bakers but after her third loan, S. built a small bakery within her home. She does her housework in addition to the business, and it is really hard. With no one to assist her, she could not increase production. She would like to expand her business and hire 2 workers to assist her in the production. Kadiatu is therefore requesting a $375 loan.

name: Tania
description: Tania, 36, is a good, kind, very hardworking woman.  She lives with German, 38, with whom she has two children: Gabriela, 16, and Angélica, 4.  She works very much every day to provide her children with a better quality of life.  She’s lived in her own house for many years.  Tania’s work consists in selling cosmetics like talc, perfume and accessories and other merchandise like clothes and shoes according to the season she’s in.  She heads out daily seeking customers who for the most part are her friends, neighbors and family members.  She’s been doing this work for 14 years and has always done it alone.  She also has a display case at home where she places the products she has in stock to sell to customers who come by her house.  In time she learned that in order to be successful in this type of work she needs to go out looking for customers using persuasion techniques to sell enough to earn good profits.  She hopes to continue to work and to have much success in future.  Her sales are very good now and this means her income is better and that helps her improve the living conditions she’s able to offer her family.    Because of this, she is grateful for the opportunity and for the trust placed in her to receive this loan.  On the other hand, she commits to make her installment payments punctually.  She enjoys being part of her communal bank because she’s noted that all the members are responsible, mutually supportive people.  She will use the requested 1,000 soles to buy merchandise comprising clothes and some cosmetics she needs to continue with her work.

name: Latofatkhon
description: Latofatkhon is widowed and the very devoted mother of two grown children. Five years ago, she went into the business of buying and selling children's clothing. Her business developed little by little as she increased her working capital. Now, she has her own shop where she sells perfumes, gifts, and other items. Latofatkhon is a very hardworking woman and a repeat client of IMON with a good credit history. After using previous loans to improve her business, she is requesting a new loan for 6,000 somoni to buy more gifts to sell. She wants to thank Kiva lenders for their support.

name: Josephine
description: Josephine is married and works hard to support her family. She has a business culturing seaweed in the Philippines. She has been in this business for five years now.  She requested a PHP 25,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional seaweed seedlings, plastic rope and other materials.  She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Hendrita
description: Hendrita is a resident of Malindi, Kenya. She owns a café and has been in the business for five years, selling food to the surrounding people. The business has been the source of income for the married mother of children, both of whom are in school.   Hendrita was introduced to Milango by her friends. She is applying for a loan of 21,100 Kenya shillings to purchase food stock and utensils.   She intends to save the additional income for future projects. Her main ambition is to increase the size of the business and also open a grocery stall in the near future.  Hendrita believes this will help improve her standard of living, especially her children’s education.

name: Run
description: Mrs. Run P., age 31, works selling various kinds of fruits at Phsar Suong market in Kampong Cham, making on average around $2.40 each day in revenue. Her husband is a blacksmith making around $6 per day in revenue. Her two children are too young to attend school. She would like to request this loan of $1000 in order to expand her inventory of fruit to meet her clients’ needs. The remainder of the loan is to buy blacksmith’s tools to facilitate her husband’s work.

name: Juliet
description: Juliet works hard to support her family. She is married and has a furniture making business in the Philippines. Juliet has been in this business for four years now.  Juliet requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy more materials like woods, paints, nails, etc. for her business. She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Carmen Amelia
description: Carmen is 28 years old, she is in a common-law partnership and has a son. Alejandro, 9 years old, is studying in an institution very close by their town. Her mother is a very responsible and hard-working person, who makes a living buying and selling pigs. She has been performing this activity for more than one year.This is for Carmen her only source of economic income. She is requesting the loan to continue investing in her business growth so that her income will increase and she can continue helping her partner with the expenses in her humble home.

name: Nerissa
description: Nerissa is thankful for the financial assistance that was extended to her because she was able to purchase more quantities and varieties of grocery items, toiletries and beverages needed in her business. Her earnings were a big help in her personal, household and business expenditures.  She would like to apply for another 15,000 Philippine peso (PHP) loan to buy groceries, toiletries, beverages and other products to add to her current inventory. The more items displayed at the store the better. More items to sell will result in better profit. Her profits from business will definitely help her to sustain her daily needs. She looks forward to this financial increase with gladness and thankfulness in her heart.  Nerissa desires to buy her own house. She wants for her business to grow and expand. She meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her life and business every week and she can also draw strength and inspiration from the fellowship and the Word of God that she studies.  *All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay Micro Finance loans.

name: Luis Fernando
description: Luis is married and has four children.  To generate household income he has a vegetable shop where he offers his customers all types of vegetables.  He has several years’ experience in this activity and the great advantage he has is that there is no nearby competition which makes it possible for him to gradually grow with the business and improve household income.  Seeking to overcome the difficulty his business has with capital, Luis is looking for a loan to buy vegetables and increase the variety of products he has in stock.  In this way he will be able to buy the vegetables his customers are constantly asking for and at the same time increase his income considerably.  His dream is to see the business grow constantly and to see how his four children move forward with a good education.

name: Janet
description: Janet is a member of the 'Siempre Adelante' (Always Moving Forward) community bank which is located Cusco district, in the province and department of the same name.  Janet is 27 years old.  She lives with her partner and has one child.  She divides her time between her daily activities and her hairdressing business.  Janet provides different styles of haircut, for both women and men.  She also colors hair and provides manicures, pedicures and other services.  She is very happy with her business since she is working in a job she likes and she also has time to spend with her son, to see him and be with him.  Janet is requesting this loan to keep her hairdressing salon running.  She is happy to be receiving this loan and she pledges to make her repayments on time.

name: Faalagilagi
description: A loan amount of 1,000 WST will help Faalagilagi to buy taro roots (seedlings), banana roots (seedlings), chemicals, a backpack sprayer, chainsaw, and a wheelbarrow to help her run the business. Faalagilagi is 46 years old with three children. She joined SPBD in 2015. She will use her profit to expand her business and assist her family.

name: Asia Group
description: This group is called Asia. It is made up of four women from Hodeida, Yemen. They are hardworking and enterprising women. They took a loan of 120,000 YER.   Rashida is the group's leader. She is 20 years old, married and has children. She has had a business selling new perfumes and incense for three years.  She has professional experience in this field. She attracted more customers, which helped her family to cover household expenses. She is using her share of the loan to invest in her business by buying more perfumes and incense and reselling them to her customers. This loan will allow her to increase her revenue. She thanks Kiva lenders for financing the first loan.

name: Khongorzul
description: The lady shown in this picture is a 23-year-old young entrepreneur named Khongorzul, who lives with her spouse and daughter in a ger - a traditional Mongolian felt tent - in an outer ger district (a district without basic infrastructure) in Ulaanbaatar city, Mongolia. Her daughter attends a local kindergarten while Khongorzul’s husband runs a taxi business.   Khongorzul has been operating a clothing sale business since 2007 at the largest outdoor market in Mongolia. When she first started her business, it was very difficult for her, but she was patient. Now, she has 2.7 million MNT (Mongolian Tugriks) in working capital. Also, she imports her jackets once or twice a month from Ereen, a border city between Mongolia and China. Using her business profit, she bought a car for her spouse last June so her husband drives a taxi and sometimes helps her to operate the business.   Khongorzul and her spouse’s wish is to own a plot of land and real estate. Therefore, they need money to purchase more jackets to sell. So she is requesting a 1 million MNT loan to import jackets and suits from Ereen city.

name: Ma. Cristina
description: Ma. Cristina is 23 years old with two children. With one of her children currently in school, Ma. Cristina works very hard to provide for them.Ma. Cristina runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 7,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional items to sell like beverages, condiments, eggs, home care products, and other groceries.Ma. Cristina has been in this business for three years and sells a variety of items. In the future, Ma. Cristina would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Yuvisa
description: Yuvisa has an agriculture business.  She has a plot of land where she grows cacao and coffee.  Yuvisa works from 6:00 A.M. to 5:00 P.M.  She has several years of experience in this business and is doing very well.  Her dream is to expand her farmland.  Yuvisa is requesting a loan in order to buy seeds and fertilizers.  She is pleased with the loan and promises to complete her payments.

name: Cruz Elena
description: Cruz Elena has been making crafts for 8 years, an activity that she earns her livelihood through for herself and her four children.  She’s always wanted to provide her children with the best possible education so she hopes that sales will increase to be able to improve their quality of life.  Cruz Elena dreams with setting up her own business where she can sell the crafts she makes and thus leave a good economic stability to her children.

name: Tamaraneh Ii Group
description: Isha F. (left) is the leader of this group. Isha has been a businesswoman for seven years now, and she sells bowls, dishes, spoons, sheaves, funnels, etc. She is married to a nurse and they have seven children. Some of their children are in secondary schools and the others are in primary schools. Isha is approximately 28 years of age. She was born in the small town of Mile Ninety-one, in Northern Sierra Leone.   Isha F., Adama K. and Yeabu S. are members of the Tamaraneh Group. Tamaraneh is Temne meaning “Let’s help each other”. They are local entrepreneurs in Waterloo small town – 20 miles from Freetown. This is the first loan these entrepreneurs are requesting from SMT, a partner of Shine on Sierra Leone in Waterloo. They are requesting a loan of Le 500,000 each, to enable them to improve their businesses. With this loan, they will be able to expand their businesses both in terms of size and quality. Consequently they can make better profits and improve on their standard of living.

name: Yulia
description: Yulia lives in Novaya Kahovka. The town has several shopping centers and Yulia rents retail space in one and sells stylish and fashionable women's clothes. She has had her business for 7 years. Yulia is planning to purchase a batch of fall clothing for resale during the fall-winter season, specifically she wants to purchase cardigans, sweaters, skirts and slacks using the loan of 4000 griven.

name: Citizen School
description: Greetings from Uganda! This is Christine. She is the Head Teacher of Citizen Primary School, a mixed school in the Peri-urban area of Masajja in Wakiso with 600 students. Citizen Primary School has requested a loan to cover the cost of installing and maintaining a UV water filtration system to provide clean drinking water for its students. The school does not currently have access to consistent clean drinking water and therefore has to spend a considerable portion of its budget on firewood, which is used to boil water for the children. Installing a water filtration system will therefore save the school money in the long-term as the cost of firewood will be reduced. The loan will enable the school to purchase a UV water treatment system with a 450 litre tank, which will be big enough to store clean drinking water for the students every day.   Citizen Primary School will repay their loan from their school fees, which they collect each term. This will be supplemented by the sale of carbon credits, which the school will generate from using the water tank. Christine ultimately hopes that having access to safe drinking water will improve her student’s concentration and attendance by reducing the number of children that fall sick from water-borne diseases as well as increase the number of students coming to the school.

name: Astar
description: Astar  is 44 years old; she is a married woman.  In order to meet her household expenses she started her business selling animals. She buys animals (baby goats & calves) at low prices, brings them up and then sells them out in the market at higher prices. She makes enough through her business to contribute in the family income. She also sells their milk to generate an extra amount of income. She needs to improve her business to bear her household expenses. For this reason, she contacted Kashf Foundation and applied a loan of PKR 40000  to purchase more animals to increase her sales. She is very experienced and has good contacts in the market. With this loan, she will definitely expand her business and income level.

name: Marissa
description: Marissa S. owns a hectare (2.5 acres) of cornfield and a hectare of rice field. This enterprise helps her support her family’s needs.  S. is aged 40, married to Glen, and they have four children. Her eldest child is 18.  S. would like to obtain a loan of Php 15,000 from CEVI to finance her business. The loan will be used to supply her needs like seedlings, fertilizer, and other farm supplies.

name: Mariana
description: Mariana (23), she is living with her parents in Handeni District. She is volunteering as a Camfed Learner Guide she teaches students in secondary school about life skills sessions. She has plans to start selling women clothes near her home. Mariana is requesting a Kiva loan to launch her women clothes business. She will use the profit to repay her loan and help her family with basic needs like food, clothes and shelter. The social interest on her loan will be repaid through Mariana's weekly two and a half hours of volunteering.

name: Roselyne
description: Roselyne, a courageous mother of four, has been a small business operator in the Mukuru informal settlement of Nairobi, Kenya for many years.  Roselyne is also a trained community mobilizer. She has gained invaluable business experience both from running her own businesses as well as working for other people. However, she had to stop running her businesses and quit her job due to health problems.  A Fresh Life Toilet will give Roselyne the opportunity to generate extra income for her family. She foresees that the amount of effort needed to run this business is manageable with her health problems.  Roselyne hopes to use the profits to add more Fresh Life Toilets within her community, as well as educate her children to the highest level possible.

name: Mujeres Todas Juntas Group
description: These are 20 women from the city of Caaguazú, with the hope of helping themselves by working and adding this to the foundation’s capabilities.  From this idea comes the group “Mujeres Todas Juntas,” whose members want to continue moving forward and overcome all of the obstacles they could have.  Elva is part of this group and says that she sells cheese and milk.  She begins working very early in the morning to be able to meet her customers’ demands.  She has become very well known, thanks to the good variety of products she sells.  She is asking for this loan in order to buy cheese in quantity so that she will have a large stock on hand, now that the year-end festivals are approaching.  She wants to have a good stock.

name: Charan's Group
description: A farmer from Cheung Prey district of Kampong Cham province, Charan is a 25-year-old married father of one kid. To support his family, Charan farms rice while his wife earns additional income by raising pigs. Together, they can earn about 47,000 KHR per day. Drought is the main challenge for his business.   Charan’s group has been with VisionFund for one cycle. He successfully paid back the previous loan. Now he is leading his group to seek a loan. As the leader, he wants to use his portion to buy seeds and fertilizers for supporting his farmland. He hopes to make more income from his current business so as to improve his standard of living.
town: Kampong Cham province, Cheung Prey district

name: Juma
description: Juma is a very determined man who is fully dedicated to his business and running his retail shop. It has produced good results and he works hard to see it expand. Juma tell us that he used his previous loan to fully invest in his shop.   Thanks to the support given he has been able to increase his sales. Stock has gone down and he wants to increase his inventory, however, he does not have enough capital to reach his goals. He is requesting another loan in the amount of KES 40,000 to add more stock of rice, bales of flour, sodas, and other small items like sweets. He still focuses on his dream of owning a wholesale business.

name: Maria Judit
description: This woman is a member of the community bank "KIMOYGANAKERA MAGANIROIGI". The partner María Judit continues to make a living in agriculture and through her grocery store. With these businesses she wishes to succeed. She would like to increase her agricultural production by harvesting more fruits and a variety of tubers.Maria is requesting a loan to buy seeds and fertilizer. She is infinitely grateful to the Kiva lender for continuing to believe in her and her efforts.

name: Gulnora
description: For Gulnora, this is the first loan from IMON and KIVA.   She is a widow and has 5 children.  A few years ago, her husband passed away and she, along with her 5 children, were left without a provider .  She decided to start a new business in animal husbandry in order to generate an income.   She attended the course ‘To get ahead’ with a women's organization and learnt business skills.  Her children will help her with the business. She will be a very successful businesswoman because she is hardworking and smart.  Gulnora is asking for a loan of 2000 Somoni to buy cattle.  She will use the loan and her business will have a good source of income, so her family can have a good quality of life and better financial opportunities. She awaits your support.

name: Mounir
description: Mounir is a 26-year-old single man and the owner of an accessories shop since 2008. Mounir is very happy with his business, because he enjoys the variety of products that he serves in his shop to please his customers. He sells perfumes, beauty creams and cosmetics in addition to good quality accessories.  Mounir has expanded his business a lot in order to keep his customers satisfied. He applied for a YOUTH LOAN from Kiva partner Al Majmoua, in order to support his business with a new accessories collection.   This is his first time applying for a loan, but he is very excited that it will respond to his customers' needs and will increase his capital. Mounir hopes to start a wholesale trade in the future and to expand his working region.

name: Omar
description: Omar is a 38-year-old married man from Rafah city, which is located in the Gaza Strip, which has an economic blockade imposed by the Israeli authorities since 2007.  He is a father of three sons and two daughters. He works as an employee in the public sector where he gets a low income.   Omar also has a grocery store where he sells basic grocery products. Omar  took a USD loan from FATEN. This loan will help him to buy a new refrigerator for his grocery store. With this loan, he can buy more goods for his store to resell. Omar  appears in the photo

name: Kubatana Gwamakunguvo Group
description: Greetings from Zimbabwe! This is 29-year-old Tinashe from Masvingo. He is married and has two children. He also cares for one dependent. Tinashe is a grocer and sells a variety of food and household goods. The business has been in operation for one year. In his business, Tinashe faces challenges transporting his stock.   Tinashe has requested a loan of 400 USD to replenish his stock. He says the extra income generated as a result of this loan will allow him to increase profits and save for a car. In the future, Tinashe plans to open another shop.

name: Ahmad
description: Ahmad is photographed in the construction workshop. Ahmad is a 51-year-old man. He is married and a father to three sons. He is a construction worker and earns a low income which is not enough to cover all the family's needs. Ahmad wants to improve his work, so he is requesting a 1,500 USD loan from FATEN to help him cover the costs of purchasing a new construction kit, which is necessary to provide better quality to his work. This will ensure Ahmad's better work and living conditions.

name: Elsa
description: Elsa F. is from the village of Canicapan. She is 46 years old. Elsa is separated and has 3 school-aged children. To make a living, Elsa operates a food products business. Elsa has been engaged in her business for 5 years and earns approximately Php1,000.00 a month from these activities.  In 2009, Elsa joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Elsa is requesting a loan amounting to 5,000 PHP, which will be used to invest in expanding the business. This will be Elsa's first loan from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About PMPC:  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Ma. Dolores
description: Ma. Dolores is 48 years old, married, and the mother of three children, two of whom are in school. She works hard to provide for her family by running a general store in the Philippines, and has requested a PHP 40,000 loan from NWTF to buy more groceries to sell. Ma. Dolores has borrowed and repaid eight prior loans from NWTF and has been running her general store for 21 years. She supplements her income by farming sugarcane. Her goal is to save enough money to expand her business and continue to send her children to college.

name: Sarah
description: Sarah lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is married with five children and two of her children go to school. She does not have additional family members.   She sells fruits and vegetables at the market on a retail basis. She has been in business for the last 15 years. She works six days a week.   She has requested from MCDT–SACCO a loan of 400,000 to buy a box of tomatoes, onions, pineapples, watermelon, and cabbages. Her major challenge is seasonality and transportation. Her goal and aspiration is to build rental houses. She lives in a rented house and the family has access to piped water and electricity. Her major monthly expenses include school fees.

name: Veronidia
description: Veronidia is a hardworking woman entrepreneur with four children, two of whom are in school.  She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like shampoo, groceries, etc.  She industriously earns additional income through other business ventures like fishing.  Veronidia dreams that one day she will be able to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Dolika
description: Dolika is a hardworking woman with four child living in Bundibugyo Uganda. Her business is mainly buying and selling food stuffs on top of fish mongering and cocoa farming for supplementary income. She is in need of a loan to buy fish to sell to her customers. She has a great desire of accumulating more capital and becoming a prominent business woman in her area although she complains of the difficulty of high transport costs, unpredictable weather changes and limited capital hindering her expected returns.

name: Cazadoras Group
description: This group is called “LAS CAZADORAS” (The Huntresses) and is located in the state of México.  They decided on this name because legend has it that the place this town now sits on was once favorable for hunting and gathering during the Pre-Hispanic era, just like its name indicates.  It is in Cerro del Chapulín and has 11 members.  One of the members is Mrs. Patricia González.  She has three children who are 15, 11 and 3 years of age, respectively.  Before starting her business she was exclusively a housewife but need and the desire to get ahead led her to seek new sources of income.  With saving she had they decided to open a general store which has been her family’s support.  Her dream is that her children have a better quality of life some day and that they go to school since she never had the opportunity to develop as a great professional.  With the loan the institution grants her she wants to acquire more merchandise so that her business will grow and someday she’ll be able to open a minisupermarket that will give her and her family tranquility.

name: Mercy
description: Mercy I. is married with 4 children. She is 54 years old. She has been borrowing from LAPO micro finance for the past 7 years. She sells rice and river fish. She has been in the business for 8 years. She is soliciting the loan of $450 to buy more bags of rice and river fish. This loan, she said, will help her meet the high demand of her numerous customers and also increase her profitability. She thanks you.

name: Mary Ann
description: Mary Ann, 49, is married to an overseas Filipino worker and they're blessed with five children.   She has owned and managed a retail store in their village for almost a year and and earns a net income of PHP 500 daily.   Because she has insufficient capital, she would like to avail a loan amounting to PHP 20,000 to purchase beverages, chips, fish sauce, cooking oil, breads, coffee, sugar, and canned goods to sell. She is hoping that her business will continue to improve and become more profitable.

name: Lucia
description: As a widowed parent of five children, Lucia  works hard to support her family.  She has a general store business in the Philippines, and she also earns additional income from food vending and raising livestock. Lucia is borrowing 18,000 PHP through NWTF to purchase additional stock like soft drinks, sugar, rice, groceries, etc. to sell for her general store business.  Lucia has been sustaining her business activities through her past 24 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: Elsa Lucila
description: Elsa, 43, sells staple grocery items in the front part of her house. Her husband is a mason and together they have one son, who is 19 years old. They live in a canton called Playas ["Beaches"], which is one of Ecuador's tourist destinations and known for its great variety of seafood.  Ten years ago, Elsa started her store in order to help her husband with household expenses. She set it up in the front part of her house so that she could dedicate time to her son as well. Little by little, she stocked up with merchandise and started working at 8:00 a.m. every day.  At night, her son tends to the store so that she can make dinner.  She will use this loan to buy rice, canned goods, sugar, etc. for her store.  In the future, she hopes to fix up her house and to better-stock her store.

name: Rahab
description: Rahab lives in the Nanyuki area of Central province, Kenya. She is a married mother of two children. She owns a tea tree farming business. She also has an agricultural farm dealing in maize, beans, potatoes, etc. at a small scale. This business has been running for seven years. She also has other businesses, namely a poultry farm and a timber yard.  She learned about Milango through an employee who invited her to the group and she joined with an aim of accessing credit to better her business operations. The main challenges Rahab faces are lack of water and theft of the farm produce.  Rahab is applying for a loan of 31,450 Kenyan shillings to buy a water tank for her farming business. Her extra income from the loan will be added to the savings to expand the agricultural business. Her future plan in five years' time is to increase the number of her dairy cattle.

name: Adelaida
description: Adelaida is 54 years old. She is married and has 3 children. 2 of her children are currently in school, and Adelaida works hard to provide for them.  Adelaida runs a general store in the Philippines, a business she has been in for 2 years now.   Through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Adelaida is requesting a loan of 13,000 PHP to be able to purchase additional items to sell in her general store, such as canned goods, beverages, groceries, etc.  In the future, Adelaida would like to save enough money to be able to afford for her children to continue their studies at college.

name: Teodora
description: Teodora, 45, is a hard working, noble mother.  She lives in her own house with her husband and two children.  Her business is selling fish.  Very early in the morning every day and on weekends she and her husband sell ceviche (marinated fish).  They do quite well with the business.  Since her son works at the municipal fish gathering center when he gets off work he buys fresh fish and takes it home where Teodora prepares this very typical Peruvian dish.  She has managed to win over many customers who prefer her due to the service she provides.  What she enjoys most about her work is chatting with her customers.  She has been in business for 15 years and considers the most painful thing to face as a mother is being unable to rehabilitate her son from a paralysis he has in half his body.  For this reason she hopes to soon finish building her house to offer him a better quality of life.  This is her 13th loan with MFP; she’s aware that she has to repay punctually and is willing to do so; she is a very cheerful, responsible member of her communal bank.    She wants the loan to buy building materials and supplies like: cement and fine sand because she wants to have the floor in the house in very good condition.   Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Mary
description: Mary is 46 years old, married to Edward and has two children. She has practised farming in Njabini town for the past 10 years.    She was introduced to KADET LTD by one of our field officers and this will be her first loan. She plans to use the loan to buy seeds and fertilizer for planting during this season.  In the future, Mary hopes to buy more land and to practise large scale farming and, also, to open a retail shop.

name: Ling's Group
description: Ling’s group live in a rural village in Kompong Thom province in Cambodia. Ling makes a living cultivating rice and raising pigs and  she also does extra work as farmer to support her family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water.   Having a water filter at home will help each of these women and man to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Hernan
description: Hernán, 40, lives with his wife and two children who are 12 and 16 years old in Puerto Colombia on the shores of the Caribbean Sea where its beaches, breezes and sea make it delightful for its residents and tourists who visit to be nearer to nature.  Hernán owns a store that’s also become a restaurant where in addition to packaged snacks, food items, liquor and soft-drinks he also sells seafood and daily specials according to his customers’ wishes.  His entrepreneurial idea arose when he was unable to secure employment and was looking for a way to generate income to support his family.  Today, his store provides housewives with what families consume daily and on weekends especially he sells prepared food to passersby and tourists who pass by there.  He sells for cash and also on credit to customers who he knows are responsible with their payments.  His goal for later on is to turn it into a self-service store and to build a second story to move his family into thus separating the living quarters from the business area which is very necessary in order to provide serenity for his family.  Since he plans to attain his dreams little by little, he’s applying for a Kiva loan, his first financing with Fundación Mario Santo Domingo to buy food items, snacks and soft-drinks in larger amounts to qualify for special discounts and have stock on-hand to meet customer demand for end-of-year festivities that are approaching; this is an opportunity to have everything his clientele needs so he can sell much more.

name: Vicente Wilfrido
description: Vicente lives in the city of La Libertad, Ecuador. He began selling bananas in the mornings in the city market, and as it went well, he planned to someday have his own shop. This is how currently, after great deal of effort, dedication and discipline, he set up his own shop.   His wife also has a small business and sells clothing. The loan he is currently undertaking is to buy more crates of bananas, as he wishes to expand his number of customers.

name: Husam
description: Husam, who appears in the photo, is a 32-year-old married man from Rafah city and is the father of two sons and one daughter.   He works as an employee in the public sector and gets a low income which is not enough to cover all the family needs. He would like to improve his family living conditions and buy all that they need.  Husam took a USD Murabaha loan from FATEN. This loan will help him to buy a water purification machine for the family house. This will enable him to provide clean water for his family.

name: Temps De La Grace Plus Group
description: Gyka K. is 68 years old and a father of six children. He is the leader of the Community Bank group named “Temps de la Grace Plus,” which means “grace period” in English. It is composed of fifteen members united in solidarity through receiving loans from Hope, a Kiva partner, with the goal of developing their businesses.  Since 2005 Gyka has been in business selling flippers and miscellaneous goods. He joined one of Hope’s groups (part of a DRCongo microfinance program) in 2007 and has received fourteen loans that he repaid properly. Thanks to Hope’s loans, Gyka’s business has prospered and generates a profit of $10 per day.   Gyka intends with his next loan to diversify his business by buying different plastic items to resell at a profit in order to increase his capital. His ambition is to open a plastic goods shop due to high demand in his neighborhood. He has been working hard to achieve his dream.

name: Jean Pierre
description: Jean Pierre has been an artisan all his life. He had his own crafts workshop in his native Congo before moving to the US as a refugee in 2007. After almost three years of working with a non-profit that produced and commercialized African crafts, he decided to start his own business. Jean Pierre uses his connections with African artisans living in the US to purchase crafts, but he also buys products from Africa whenever he can purchase in bulk. He resells all the crafts at fairs and shows in his area. These shows take place during the weekends, which enables him to keep his full-time job. Certain shows and larger clients require more business formality, which in the industry translates into websites and product portfolios. Jean Pierre hopes to open a big crafts store in the United States some day.  Jean Pierre wants a loan to set up a business website to expand his clientele and to be able to sell during the weekdays. The remainder of the loan proceeds will go to make bulk purchases.

name: Safina Group
description: Asha N., age 33, is single with two children aged 4 and 2 years. She has a beauty salon which she started in 2000. She opens her salon from 8 am to 9 pm daily and she is able to make  a monthly profit of about  US$ 148 .  This will be Asha’s fourth loan from Tujijenge Tanzania. She used the previous loans to buy salon equipment and she has paid back the loan successfully. She hopes for a new loan to further improve  her salon inventory.  Asha will share this loan with her subgroup, Safina Group, which totals 7 members. The members of the group will hold each other accountable in paying back the loan.   In the picture, Asha is second from the left behind, in a blue dress.

name: Susan
description: Susan is a married woman with seven children, two of whom attend school. She owns a house that neither has electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.   For the past two years, she has operated a retail shop business, selling to her neighbors and passersby. She mentioned seasonality and theft as her major challenge. She dreams of establishing a wholesale shop in the future.  With the loan, she wants to purchase maize flour, rice, beans, and cooking oil for resale. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Cresencia
description: Cresencia is 56 years old, married with seven children. Two of whom are in school.  Cresencia is in the agricultural business, farming sugarcane in the Philippines. Cresencia requested a PHP 9,500 loan through NWTF in order to buy fertilizers and other farm supplies.  Cresencia has been farming sugarcane for ten years now, and has borrowed 23 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Cresencia would like to save money to expand her business and continue to send her children to school.

name: Monica
description: Mónica is 28 years old, is married and has three young children. She is dedicated to her small convenience store that she has had for 3 years in her house. This business allows her to augment her income and also helped her to be together with her children, this is what she likes about having a business in her home. In addition, sales at her convenience store are favorable because in her community there are few stores. The difficult part is acquiring the goods required in the shop because she has to go into the city to purchase things. This is her fourth loan with MFP; she has not had delays in her payments. Mónica will invest the money in the purchase of essential goods, those that are most needed in her community. Translated from Spanish by Helen Smith, Kiva Volunteer

name: Ruben
description: Rubén, 43, lives with his common-law wife, Lourdes, 35, and they have 5 children who all live in their own house where happiness reigns. Rubén is a man who receives a lot of benefits because he performs  his work enthusiastically.  He is a farmer and has various crops: cacao and coffee.  He has been farming for 16 years and he hires help during harvest time.  His income-producing plants are cacao and coffee for which he receives good money for each kilo from the businesses who collect crops from the farmers.   The biggest problem of his work is that he can’t fight the insects that infest the fruit of the plants.  In the future he hopes to save more money to buy cacao and coffee plants to increase his yield.  This will be his first loan with MFP and he feels that it will help him progress in his business.  The communal bank is very appreciated by his companions since they all feel very much a part of it.  He will use the 1500 new sols to buy cacao and coffee plants to increase his crops.

name: Paul
description: Paul is 41 years old and married to Basantine. They have been blessed with two children who are in primary school. He does electronics repair and also sells electronics, a business he has run for nine years.   Paul will be using this loan to purchase electrical items for resale. He will also buy electronic equipment and instruments for use in his business. This will enable him to serve more customers and make more profits which will enable him to pay school fees for his children.   This is his fifth loan term with VisionFund Kenya, after having paid his previous loans well. His future hopes are to become an electronics supplier in the region, and make more income to educate his children to higher levels of education.

name: Margaret
description: Margaret W. W. is a 46-year-old married mother of three children. She lives in Kiembeni and runs a grocery store in Kongowea, Mombasa. She has been in the business for four years.  Margaret is borrowing her first loan from KADET and she plans to use it to purchase new stocks of potatoes to sell in Kongowea. She will use her profits to expand her business. She hopes to live a satisfying and successful life.

name: Mary
description: Mary A. is currently in the business of selling charcoal from her home  and is requesting a loan to stock more bags of charcoal to sell.  Mary is 42 years old and is married. Her husband is a peasant. She has 3 children and her children go to school.  With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to pay the school fees for her children.

name: Duvan Antonio
description: Fredonia's a land of farmers and a place of thriving, persevering, honest, and hardworking people like Duvan, who works with pigs and fowl.  He's the father of a little three-and-a-half-year-old baby.  Only parents know that love for children, an inexplicable feeling that makes one work and improve, as well as give everything for that child--or at least that's the way Duvan feels.  Duvan's looking for a better quality of life for his family.  He wants to request financial support to buy four pigs and concentrated feed for his pigs and his fowl.  His business is his source of income for his family, so he's requesting support for his business to be sustainable over time.

name: Julia
description: Julia lives in the city of Huayopata, which is located in the province of La Convencion in the department of Cusco. Her primary economic activity is agriculture as she plants and harvests coffee, cocoa and tea. She is a responsible and friendly person that has belonged to the communal bank “Buena Vista” of the Arariwa Asociation for many years. In this opportunity, she needs the loan to buy seeds.  Julia is thankful to the investors for the loan and she promises to pay the dues with much responsibility.

name: Elnora
description: Elnora is 43 years old and married with four children.She earns a living by raising chickens in the Philippines. Elnora is borrowing PHP 17,000 through NWTF to buy feed and other supplies to raise her chickens.Elnora has been raising chickens for 10 years and earns additional income from tailoring.She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Tom's Group
description: Tom, 45, is a rural villager living in Kampong Cham province. She is a mother of two children and one of them is in school while the other one is too young to go to school.  Growing rice on two hectares farmland and factory worker are the sources of her family’s income for twenty two years. She could earn about 64,000KHR per day.   Now she is faced with a problem of lacking fund to help the farm, so she decided to form a group to apply for a Kiva loan via VisionFund.  As a group leader, she will use her loan portion to buy seeds for farming. She hopes to gain more yields than last year and improve her family’s living standard.
town: Kampong Cham province, Prey Chhor district

name: Echim
description: Ms. T. is a cook by profession. She lives in the village of Cetireni, along with her husband.  Ms. T. worked as a cook in the school in the village, then she worked for nearly 2 years in Moscow. Because of the instability of jobs in Moscow, Ms T. returned to her own country. And because she has a lot of land, 3 hectares, and room for animals, she decided to grow pigs. Last year she sold 4 pigs, but she currently owns 15 pigs, 3 of the biggest pigs and 12 small pigs.   Ms. T.  began to grow pigs about a year ago. She has requested a loan worth 10,000 lei, 5000 lei of which will be used to rebuild her pigpen (she wants to increase its size), and 5000 lei to buy feed for pigs, sheep, and cattle.   Pigs are kept till they reach the weight of 100-120 kg, bringing a price of 40 lei / kg. So a mature pig can bring in about 4000 lei. Expenditures for growing pigs and maintaining them are reduced, because she has agricultural land which mainly provides food for the pigs. At the end of the first year of ACTV, calculated, she will collect a cumulative net flow of 11,480 lei, and at the end of the second year's activity, the cumulative net flow will be worth 40,460.  Ms. T.'s business advantages are: a stable demand for pork at the market in Ungheni; reduced maintenance expenses for pigs; business may be released in small proportions (with small investments) and extended as possibilities appear; pigs easily accommodate the different technologies and increased exploitation.

name: Esther
description: Esther operates a provisions store and sells sauce pans as well. The TEACH lending program has improved her knowledge in trading through the Kraban Support Foundation. She needs a Kiva loan of $850 to expand her business.

name: Allani
description: Allani N. is 36 years old dynamic woman. She is married to a mechanic welder and has 2 children. She lives with her family in Port-Bouët, a very populated suburb in the south of the Abidjan District. Allani is a good tailor and clothes accessories seller on the Port-Bouët’s market. She has more than 12 years work experience. She consistently contributes to her family revenues generation. N. has got an important order of school dresses to be delivered for a primary school. N. who joined AE&I microcredit program in July 2005 has been a good performer. She has always reimbursed her loans in good manner

name: Maa Khandeswari Shg Group
description: Sumitra is a member of the Maa Khandeswari Self-help Group in a small village in the Puri district of Odisha. She has stories to tell about how she made her living and gradually improved her lifestyle by making leaf plates. She, along with her husband, prepares leaf plates and sells them in the local market.   The business of leaf plates began long before she got training from Peoples Forum, but the business did not flourish because of a lack of capital. It was through joining hands with Peoples Forum that her business got the much-needed push to witness progress. The family now owns a concrete house and wishes to sell their leaf plates in the main market rather than the local market.   The production has subsequently increased, as they now have their vehicle to take the product to the market. She now does not have to worry about her children's study expenses. It is she who has started the habit of saving money in her family. Over the course of time, she now prepares leaf plates of different sizes and according to the demands of various customers. She, along with her husband, even sells these leaf plates to various sweets shops, small stalls selling eatables, etc.  Now she will use her loan portion to buy a leaf plate-making machine to increase her production.

name: Chey
description: Chey S., 43, is married and resides with his wife and three children in Phnom Penh City, Cambodia, an area known for being the most populated city in the country. S. is a motor-taxi driver and earns an income of USD 8.50 per day. His wife sells food to workers at a garment factory, earning an income of about USD 4.60 per day.   S. is requesting a loan of USD 400 to purchase a new motorbike to attract more clients to patronize his transportation business.  This is his first loan from CREDIT, a long-standing Kiva partner in Cambodia.

name: Sivouch's Group
description: Sivouch, a mother of six children, is originally from the Prey Chor district of Kampong Cham Province. She is 48 years old and a rice farmer on one hectare of farmland, which she has been doing for 30 years. Her main challenge is the shortage of working capital for supporting her business. Therefore, she formed a group of four to seek a new loan. This is the fourth time that she has been with VisionFund, Kiva’s partner. After the successful loan that she paid back fully, she feels confident that she can make a good living for her family. Now, the entire group loan is 4,600,000 KHR. Sivouch's loan portion is 1,400,000 KHR. She is going to spend it on fertilizer, rice seed, and gasoline for water pumping for her farmland. She hopes that this purchase will boost her productivity and make more income for her family.
town: Kampong Cham province, Cheung Prey district

name: Abubakr
description: Abubakr was born in 1995.  He is a well-mannered and kind young man.  There are six people in his family.  He is not married.  Abubakr graduated from a secondary school this year.  He studied excellently in school and participated in all school events.  After finishing school, Abubakr was accepted to the State Technology University with a world marketing major.  He will be studying in English.  Abubakr has to pay for his university tuition.  His father is a migrant worker, and mother works as a teacher a secondary school.  They cannot pay for his tuition.  Abubakr is requesting this loan to pay for his university tuition.  He awaits your kindness.

name: Remberto Isaias
description: Remberto is a man of the countryside who works buying and selling livestock. He also produces milk, an activity which his parents taught him starting when he was a boy. With these activities, he has been able to get ahead. He has a family, made up of his life partner, with whom he lives in a common-law marriage, and their two children. He is requesting a loan to buy milk to produce dairy products, as well as calves to raise. If you want to know more about the entrepreneurs and the loans from Interactuar, you can join the Lending Team called: “Friends of Interactuar Colombia”: http://www.kiva.org/team/interactuar_colombia

name: Semona
description: Semona is a very hardworking 45-year-old woman who lives in her own home with her three children: Carlos, 15; Miguel, 12; and Jhosep, 10. Her children are the reason behind her efforts. Every morning Semona goes out with her three-wheeled cart to sell delicious quinoa juice (hot juice made from liquidized quinoa, cornstarch, and apples) that she makes herself. The hot beverage is in great demand because in this region temperatures are cool in the mornings, which encourages people to drink something warm. What Semona likes most about her work is that she can drink the glasses of juice she wants when she's hungry. She has been in this line of work for 5 years and believes that the hardest part is having to wake up early and go out in the cold streets in order to sell. In the future she longs to have a store where she can work with greater ease and better serve her customers.   This is Semona's second loan with MFP (Microfinanzas Prisma) and she feels very confident that she will be able to make her payments on time. She doesn’t want to cause any problems with her community bank where she is beloved for being such a happy person. She will use the 600 Peruvian soles (US$225) to buy more ingredients in order to make the delicious quinoa juice that she sells.  Translated from Spanish by Erin Sindewald, Kiva Volunteer

name: Helen
description: Helen is a 44-year old married woman with 4 children living in D'ban, Calamba. In order to add income for the family, Helen entered into a rice trading business which she started 2 years ago.  She usually gets PHP 5,000 per month.   With the help of GDMPC microcredit, Helen is able to buy more rice to sell because of the money amounting to PHP 5,000 rendered to her. She is new with GDMPC.  Helen hopes for much greater revenue in the future for her  business expansion.

name: Elchin
description: Elchin is 30 years old, married, and has one child. He is an Internally Displaced Person (IDP) from the Armenian-occupied territory in Azerbaijan, Fuzuli town, and he settled in Baku city. Four years ago he started a taxi business. Now he is requesting a loan of $1200 to buy the spare parts for repairing his taxi.

name: Baltazar
description: Baltazar is a man of 68 years old, he is a widower and he takes care of a son. He lives in his own house in the small country village of Peñarol, in the district of Tambogrande. His village now has some basic services. The activity that the aforementioned carries out is the harvest of lime in a parcel of 3 self-owned acres and the breeding of cattle, sheep and fowl. The workload is shared with his oldest daughter, as she lives with him, and his grandsons, they all support each other. Baltazar has made a living in agriculture and livestock breeding for approximately more than 15 years.     The amount of the loan solicited is for 2400 nuevos soles, which will be invested in the purchase of a motorcycle-taxi for the transportation of the lime harvest from the parcel to the city. For the purchase, the client accounts for a part of the value of the vehicle.

name: Urla
description: Urla, age 41, is a very responsible and honest mother.  She lives in her own house with her husband and their four children.  After venturing into making earrings, Urla decided to sell coal and food.  This turned out to be more profitable for her than her previous business.  From then on her daily activity has been very hectic.  She buys the necessary ingredients and prepares food for five people who buy the food from her.  They work at a business that is close to her house.  After she finishes the work of preparing the food and putting it in plastic containers, she transports it to where her diners work.  She has been doing this work for six months.  She does this work from the comfort of her own house. In the future she is thinking of expanding and installing a restaurant in her house.  She also wants to raise pigs.  This is her 13th loan with MFP.  Once again, she pledges to be responsible with her payments.  She considers this loan to be very useful to the progress of her business.  She will use the requested loan to buy pigs to raise.  She will also buy tables and chairs to formally set up her business in her house.

name: Warlito
description: Warlito runs a cafeteria in his village in Aurora, Zamboanga del Sur. He has three children and is still studying. For ten years, he has managed this business and wants to improve it in order to gain more profit. He requests a loan of 15,000 PHP to buy raw ingredients and pots for his cafeteria. His ultimate dream is to build a house to improve his family's living conditions.

name: Ros
description: Mrs. Ros U., 47, is a farmer growing seasonal rice crops. She typically makes around $2 each day. Her husband works at a carpentry store and generally makes around $5 each day. One of her children is employed by a nearby garment factory and the rest are currently unemployed. Mrs. Ros U. hopes to use this loan to purchase another piece of farmland to grow more of a variety of crops to enable her generate more income for her entire family.

name: Mena
description: Mena cooks Konkonte, a powdered cassava that has been prepared in a Banku form.  It is normally served with groundnut soup.  She has been in this business for about two and a half years.    Mena is married and lives with her husband.    Her loan will be used to buy cassava to process into powder for the preparing of Konkonte. She plans to reinvest the profit into her business.

name: Meherrem
description: N. Meherrem is 51 years old and the father of 4 children. He is from the Fizuli region of Azerbaijan Armenian conflict territory  in West Azerbaijan. Right now he lives with his family in Sumgayit city. He supports his family through his taxi driving business, which he started 14 years ago. Meherrem has had a lot of experience and is good driver, but this job is very hard because he does not own a car himself, and must rent one to run his business. Mehrrem has some money saved to invest in a car but he does not yet have enough. For this reason he would like to take out the $500 loan to purchase the car and to build a garage. In the future, he dreams of expanding his business further and providing well for his family.

name: Joseph Sepunke
description: Residing in Vianzi, Joseph is 50 years old, and a father of 6 dependent children. To support the family, he has been a farmer as his main business and he also has different side jobs in order to supplement his income.Joseph spends up to 25% of this income for kerosene, which only provides a very dim light and emits toxic gases. He is determined to change this through acquiring a solar home system. This technology would considerably increase the living standard of the whole family. The kids would finally be able to do their homework in the evening hours and the parents would save money, which could be spend for more useful purposes than kerosene.

name: Esperacion
description: Esperacion is a married woman with three children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Esperacion is 36 years old and has three children who are in school.  Esperacion has a computer services business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy materials like computer ink, bond paper, etc. for her business.  Esperacion has been in this business for 10 years. In the future, she would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Tokuru-Omarsu Group
description: Meet the members of the “Tokuru-Omarsu” group from Makeni, a city in Northern Sierra Leone. They are all local entrepreneurs who have come to SMT, a partner of Kiva.org, to apply for a loan of SLL 1,000,000 for each. With the help of this loan they will be able to expand their businesses, make more sales and consequently improve their living conditions.   Mabinty is the leader of this group. The 48-year-old is married to a businessman and they have three children - one in primary school and two in secondary school. Mabinty has been a businesswoman for more than 20 years now. Currently, she is selling gara-lappers (locally dyed cloth). With her share of this loan, she is going to buy gara-lapper making materials like inks, caustic soda, powder, white cotton cloth, etc. in order to produce a large quantity of gara-lappers to add to her business inventory.

name: Gina
description: Gina B. is from the village of Cabisera 25, Ilagan, Isabela. She is 38 years old. Gina is married and has two school-aged children. To make a living, Gina plants and harvests corn for sale. Gina has been engaged in her business for over 20 years and earns approximately 9,000 Philippines pesos (PHP) a month from it.  In 2007, Gina joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Gina has successfully repaid a previous loan of 15,000 PHP from ASKI. This previous loan was used to purchase fertilizers such as manure.   Gina is requesting a new loan of 29,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional seeds, seedlings and young crops to raise. This will be the eighth loan taken out by Gina from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to pay the tuition fees of her children.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 38 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Noor
description: Noor is 36 years old, married and has three children. She decided to work with her husband to support her family for a better future. Eight years ago she began stitching work in her house. She stitches clothes for half of the people of her community. Through this business, she earns income to support her entire family. However, due to lack of funds she is unable to meet all the orders given by her customers. She is currently in her second loan cycle and requested a loan of 20000 PKR from Kashf Foundation. She intends to use this loan amount to buy raw materials including leather, zippers, spools of thread, etc. With this loan she will be able to complete her orders on time which ultimately will help her earn more profit.

name: Francis
description: Francis is 56 years old. He is married to Sarah and together they have eight children. He operates a quarry site whereby he mines stones and sell to his customers and has been in the business for the past 28 years.  This is his second loan from KADET LTD. He paid his previous loan well and in good time. He will use the requested loan to expand his business by purchasing another quarry site.  He hopes to own a large quarry and provide stones to most builders in his area.

name: Lourdes Sara
description: Lourdes continues with the same activity, selling cosmetics via catalog. She says that the previous loan went well for her, because she used it to buy cosmetics and jewelry. At this time, she is asking for the loan to buy jewelry, since that is the product that has the most profits. She is grateful to Kiva for this opportunity that is being offered to improve her business and therefore her quality of life.

name: Henry Arley
description: Henry is 37 years old and is a man with big plans.  He is a locksmith and makes chain mail, having learned this after working for a company in the trade.  He decide to go independent a few months ago and start his own business so he can improve his financial condition and provide a better quality of life for his family.  His customer base has increased considerable because of his good and friendly service, so he is asking for a loan so he can refresh his tools that are currently deteriorated from use.  This investment will allow him to increase his income and guarantee a higher education for his three children.

name: Gianina
description: Gianina, 28 years old, is separated and has a 9-year-old son. She resides with her mother, 2 siblings, her son, and her sister-in-law. They live in a house that her father left as an inheritance. Gianina dedicates herself to selling meals in her own restaurant. She has nearly 11 years experience in doing so, attending very ably to her customers with the help of her mother, her sister-in-law, and her brothers. Since she initiated this restaurant,  she has obtained great gains, and her sales were always favorable. Eventually, she also sold items of clothing.  Gianina likes her work very much, since it allows her to remain occupied and to generate the income necessary to cover her personal expenses and those of her son, whom she loves very much. Viewing the good results of the restaurant, she wishes to provide it with better furnishings and other accessories that will offer her customers comfort.  Gianina wishes to solicit a loan of 800 new sols.  And she wants to thanks all those who make her loan for continuing her objectives possible. And, also, she is very committed anew to punctual compliance with her payments.  The requested funds will be invested in purchasing 4 tables with their respective chairs, plus some ingredients needed to continue her restaurant business.

name: Ester
description: Ester works hard to support her family. Ester is married and has a fish-vending business in the Philippines.She requested a PHP 30,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional boxes of fish to sell.Ester has been in this business for 20 years now.In the future, Ester would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Erlinda
description: Erlinda, who is married, works hard to support her family. She owns an ice cream vending business in the Philippines. Erlinda has been in this business for 5 years now. She is requesting a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to purchase ingredients for her business. Erlinda would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Oeun
description: Oeun, age 51, is a married mother of three children, one of whom is still in school. To strive for a living, she has been farming rice on five hectares and growing cassava on six hectares of farmland as the main source of the family’s income while her husband works as a paid laborer. She has been involved with this business in Ponhea Krek district of Kampong Cham province for a long time.   Oeun has never been with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner) before. Now she is requesting a loan of 3,500,000 KHR to buy fertilizer and pay for labor to plant her cassava. She hopes to have a high yield and earn a larger income.
town: Kampong Cham province, Ponhea Krek district

name: Abdu's Group
description: K. Abdu is the leader of Bugolo group. He has a retail shop that has been operational for over 10 years. He sells essential items that are needed by the locals in his area and he says that although there are many shops next to his, he has many customers that he has managed to win because of the good care he offers them as well as having sufficient stocks of goods. This is also possible because of the loans he gets from Pearl microfinance that enable him to stock more bags of sugar, salt, maize flour, and others from Jinja town.

name: Zareena's Group
description: Zareena, age 47, is the leader of this borrower group. She adores her family, and her husband works very hard so that his family can have a good and respectable life. Her husband offers embroidery services which is the only source of income for his family.   Zareena is requesting a loan, as a member of a two-persons lending group, from Kiva partner BRAC Pakistan with the goal of improving her husband's business. He will use the loan amount to purchase embroidery threads, needles, buttons of various colours and clothes for his business. This will help him to increase his sales and net income.   With the profits expected from this loan, he intends to expand his business so that he can eventually construct a small house for his family. Zareena hopes that the loan will be helpful for her husband's business. She is thankful to Kiva lenders and to BRAC Pakistan.

name: Anzazi
description: Anzazi is a married woman with four school-going children. Anzazi owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expenses are food and school fees.  Anzazi has operated a fruits and vegetable stall business and also sells goats, selling from home to her neighbors and passersby. She faces a major challenge of seasonality in her business.   With the KES 20,000, she wants to purchase sacks of fruits, green vegetables and goats for resale. She joined Yehu to boast her business.

name: Luzmila
description: Luzmila, 42, is a member of the "Las Abejitas" communal bank, which is located in the Moyobamba district, Moyobamba province, San Martín department.  She has two small children who are in school and who depend on her.  Luzmila is a hard-working and tenacious woman who sells beauty products.  Despite the difficulties she has had in life, she has forged ahead.  She has been in this line of work for 8 years and she sells catalogue-listed products of the Avon brand.  She is very happy to have accomplished this.  With this 800 sol loan she will buy beauty poroducts to stock her inventory like: perfumes for women and men, creams, compact powder, talcs for adults and babies, lipsticks, nail polish, as well as a display case to exhibit her wares.  Luzmila, with her level of maturity, is an example to many women who are starting out in business and who, with perseverance, reach their goals.  She is very grateful to the Manuela Ramos Movement for helping her to start her own business and for helping other women as well to grow as entrepreneurs.Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: Machinjioni Group
description: Chemela who is in his early 50s is a married with five children, four of them are grown up and one is still in school.  He has been selling second hand clothes for three years now and works from 08am to 06pm daily and is able to make a small monthly profit.This will be Chamela’s 3rd loan from Tujijenge Tanzania. He used the previous loans to keep on increasing the second hand clothes stock and has managed to pay back all his loans successfully. He used the profit to pay school fees, loan repayment and covered household expenses. He will use this loan to buy the fast class second hand stock and meet his customers' request.  He dreams of opening another second hand clothes shop.Chemela will share this loan with his loan group  MACHINJIONI which consists of six members who will hold each other accountant able for paying back the loan.

name: Ter
description: Ter, 49 years old, resides in Siem Reap, a province known for its ancient temples and tourism. Ter buys and resells recycled items, earning $3.50 per day. Her husband works for the government, earning $5 per day. The couple has six children: five are studying and one is a construction worker, earning $4 per day. Each month, Ter spends $80 on food, $5 on electricity, $10 on school fees, $5 on transportation, and $10 on other expenses.   Ter would like to request a loan of $500 to buy recycled items for resale. She can earn a good income with this job and therefore wants to extend it when she has enough money. Ter hopes to support her children to study and to at least finish high school.

name: Gumercindo
description: Gumercindo is a hardworking man who, along with his family, is looking to get ahead. He provides for two of his children, giving them food and their education. Along with his wife, he sells fish as a traveling salesman. With this business activity, he survives and pays his household expenses, among others.   Gumercindo would like to plaster the floor of his living room and build a frontal wall for his humble home. Therefore, he is applying for a loan to buy construction materials for this project so that he can improve his living conditions little by little.

name: Marites
description: Marites B. is a resident of San Roque, Panaon, Misamis Occidental. Her husband works as carpenter and earns only a meager income. She registered as a regular member of Paglaum MPC in June 2006, and she is very responsible about meeting her weekly obligations, such as savings, share capital, and insurance.   She is starting a hog raising business. In need of capital to begin this venture, she has reached out to Paglaum for funding for her project, applying for a loan of PHP 10,000. She particularly needs to buy sacks of feed as well as vaccines for her pigs.  She is very thankful to Paglaum as her financing partner. She looks forward to seeing her piggery become successful.

name: Hoan
description: Hoan S., 24 years old, lives with her family in the province of Siem Reap in Cambodia. Her husband is a vegetable grower and they do not have any children. For over a year, she has been working in the rice trade business: collecting rice from farmers and re-selling it to earn profit. She currently earns average of $10 per day.   Hoan S. believes her investment is doing well because she is gaining more regular customers. This business is S.'s main source of stable income for the family. In order to continue improving the business, S. is asking for a loan of $1200 to buy additional rice to sell in the future.

name: Nilda Helen
description: Her name is Nilda Helen, 33, resident of Coron, Palawan, Philippines. She is married to Generoso, a boat captain, and the have three children, two of whom are in High School and one is in the Elementary Level. She manages her household while operating the business. She works hard to augment their income to support and meet their daily personal and household needs and to send her children to school.   Nilda Helen has a small general store in their province. In the Philippines, a general store is basically a small convenience store which sells fresh, dry, and packaged commodities directly to consumers. Almost all products are essential household items and food. It is the place to go to buy one sachet of shampoo, a Php5-worth of cooking oil, or an egg. She earns by buying supplies at wholesale prices and selling by the piece. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community. She earns a minimum net income of Php 1,000 a day.   To help her continue operations of her general store business she is requesting a Php 24,000 loan which she will use to buy grocery items such as sacks of rice, beverages, cookies and other grocery stuff. She expects an increased demand for grocery items in preparation for the Christmas Holiday. The store earnings are the family's source to meet their daily needs and to send the children to school. Nilda Helen is thanking God and you in advance for the financial help that will be given her. She wishes everyone a Blessed Christmas!  Nilda Helen hopes to maintain and grow her business so she could uplift their lives. She aims to give her children the best education possible for a better future. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her work every week and where she can also draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.   * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital and repay Micro Finance loans.

name: Sonali
description: Sonali is 32, married, a housewife and a young mother of three children (two sons and one daughter). She is married to Mintu. aged 33 years.  Sonali has a primary education, while her husband is uneducated and can sign his name only.  They are struggling to provide education to their children who are in grades 2 and 4.  They live in Domohoni in Jalpaiguri district.  Sonali's husband is engaged in a small business selling spices and mustard oils. He started his business five years ago.  He runs the small shop from his home.  He sells different kinds of spices such as cardamom, coriander, turmeric, cumin, pulses  (lentils) and mustard oils which are daily necessities for local people.  He purchases these food items from wholesale shops and sells in his locality.  He has earned the goodwill of his customers for selling good quality spices.  His business is going well and he wants to expand it by purchasing more stocks of spices, pulses and mustard oils to meet his customers' demand.  Unfortunately, he does not have enough capital.  So Sonali has come forward to help her husband.  She has taken a loan from BJS ( Kiva's partner) to purchase more stock  for her husband's business with an aim to grow it. She looks forward to improving his living standards with the profit earned.  She wants to further expand their business to give a secure life to her children and better education as well. Her full thanks go to BJS and Kiva.

name: Sophat's Group
description: Residing in Kampong Cham province, Sophat is 43 years old and a widow. She has two children, one of whom is in school.
