To struggle for a living, she manages rice farming on 1 hectare of rice farm, a business that she has been involved in for ages.    This is the first microloan for Sophat with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). She is now forming a group of two to get a new loan. As the leader, she will spend her entire loan portion to buy fertilizer and rice seeds for her family. She hopes that she can gain a good yield from her crop so she can earn more money to expand her business.
town: Kampong Cham province, Cheung Prey district

name: Rosa Amelia
description: Rosa, 48, lives in a suburb of Guayaquil.  She has a general store, but to start it she had to work very hard along with her children, since she was a single mother.  She had to invest her savings because what little income she had was from the father of her children.  She began selling provisions from her house to her neighbors and acquaintances, and little by little with hard work she was able to make those sales into a small store.  Because of this good decision, she has a fairly well-stocked store, and works from 7:00am to 11:00pm every day.  Even though her children have grown and married, she continues working.  To grow her store, she wants to use the loan to buy rice, oils, and vegetables for her store, and in the future wants to finish building her house and continue her business.Translated from Spanish by Zach Powell, Kiva Volunteer

name: Guarani Group
description: The committee named “Guarani” was formed as a result of several neighbors from the city of Santaní joining together.  Each member gives her best so that they can continue working and helping their families.  These women are the heads of their families, so they work with humility and sacrifice in order to get ahead.    All of the members raise and sell domesticated animals such as chickens, ducks, sheep, and other livestock.  By investing great effort and sacrifice, they have been able to help their children and cover their daily expenses.  Rosalva, one of the members, is requesting a loan in order to buy balanced feed for her animals.  This will enable her to continue working and generating a good income.

name: Penina
description: Hello Kiva lenders! Meet Penina, a young farmer from Maraa, a remote village in Nkubu, Kenya, who has defied the common thinking about most Kenyans that agriculture is for the older generation. Penina is happily married and, together with her husband, blessed with a lovely family. Her primary sources of income are dairy farming, crop farming, and some personal business. Penina practices agriculture with a difference, employing youthful energy, enthusiasm, and knowledge from the many agricultural trainings she has been attending to broaden her skills. Although she earns handsome profits from farming, she faces one big challenge and that is high prices in fertilizers, seedlings, and inputs, and this is a result of the monopoly that is enjoyed by the only agro vet shop in her area. She is requesting a loan to start an agro vet shop. The Maraa area has only one agro dealer who is catering for thousands of smallholder farmers who solely depend on him for agricultural inputs. The agro dealer has been making a killing from farmers by charging them extra amounts since he is the only agro dealer and enjoys monopoly. Penina wants to change this and seize the business opportunity. Through your loan, she will start an agro vet shop and tap into the potential agricultural market. Penina will also help the smallholder farmers in her area who for a long time have been having a serious problem accessing affordable farm inputs. Through increased income from the loan, she will improve her living conditions and her future plans are to open more agro shops so that she can make her services easily available. She patiently waits for your kindness.

name: Benedicta
description: Benedicta Q. is a 39 year old entrepreneur and mother of four children. She has a sari-sari store business. She started her business in 2007 using her own savings of Php 3,000. Until today, she sells different kinds of goods. She plans to make it a grocery store someday.  She would like to ask for a loan of Php 10,000 from CEVI. She will use the loan to buy additional merchandise to sell. The loan will really help her achieve bigger sales and income for her family.  CEVI is reaching out to many people to start and have their own livelihood. CEVI provides not just loans but training and insurance coverage as well.

name: Zainab
description: Zainab is 23 years old and single with one child.   She runs a palm oil business in Jui eastern area in Freetown. She started the business because she wanted to create a permanent source of living.  She's been in this business for three years now and sells palm oil at a particular market place. She describes her major hardship as inadequate funds to run her business and transportation problems.    Zainab requested this loan through BRAC Sierra Leone to purchase more gallons of palm oil to expand her business. She says that the extra income from this loan will help her increase her business and repay her loan. In the future, she would like to open a big palm oil store. She is grateful for your support.

name: Elsa
description: Elsa works hard to support 6 children. She is married and has a sugarcane farming business in the Philippines.  Elsa requested a PHP 3,500 loan through NWTF to buy a SOLAR LAMP.  She is getting the solar lamp because she wants to have a good light-source that is waterproof during the rainy season.  Elsa is aware that by using the solar lamp, she is not only saving money, but she is also helping the environment and reducing health and hazard risks to her family.

name: Mary Ann
description: Mary Ann is 39 years old and has three children. Mary Ann is married and has three children who are presently in school.Mary Ann is in the agricultural poultry business in the Philippines. Mary Ann requested a PHP 12,000 loan through NWTF to buy feeds and other supplies to raise her chickens.Mary Ann has been in this business for six years now, and has borrowed two times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.In the future, Mary Ann would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Amina
description: Amina is a 50-year-old mother of five children living with her spouse and children in the area of Lahore, Pakistan. Her husband is a green grocer by profession, and he has been selling fresh vegetables at a shop in a nearby town for many years. Her husband offers seasonal and fresh vegetables to his customers. He has been feeding his family through the income generated from this vegetable shop.   Nowadays, the needs of his family have suddenly increased and he does not have other sources to cope with these needs. So he decided to expand his current business. He wants to increase his stock on a daily basis so that he can maximize sales of vegetables. Therefore, Amina asked for a loan so that her husband would be able to buy more vegetables for selling.  Amina is very thankful to Kiva and field partner, BRAC Pakistan.

name: Maria Elena
description: Maria is 35-years-old.  She has a grocery store.  She lives in a region called Playas (Beaches), one of the touristy regions of Ecuador that has a lot of seafood.    When she was 14-years-old, Maria started to sell sweets to be able to pay for her studies as at her young age her family didn’t have many resources to allow her to study.  Since that time, she has been able to save money and have her own store, but when she was pregnant she had health problems and had to close the store for some time as it was risky for her to have her baby.  But now, with more financial stability, she opened it again and stocked it with more groceries.  She works from 7AM to 9PM and sometimes her father helps her to attend to her business.  With the loan she would like to buy rice, oil, and canned goods to be able to stock the store better.  In the future she would like to have a large business space and for her children to study in a good school.

name: Ahmedwali Abdiasis
description: Ahmedwali Abdiasis is 20 years old. He studies at Gollis University, Faculty of Medicine.    He is junior student, and his problem is the lack of a laptop to watch video tutorials and for reading medical lessons when given in soft copy.    He cannot pay the money all at one time. He approached Kaaba MFI; then Kaaba will provide him with a laptop that he can pay for in installments.    In the future, he hopes to be a doctor.

name: Nhim
description: The man appearing in the picture above, Nhim S., age 30, resides in a village located near Phnom Penh city. He currently owns a truck that he uses to provide transport service for a fee. He has a partner in his wife who stays at home to do housework. The couple married a few years ago, but they do not have a child yet.   From the business, Nhim S. is able to generate an average of US$ 10 per day to cover family expenses. Recently, his truck has often broken down and his income has also been affected. That why Nhim S. is applying for a loan to be used to mend his broken-down truck.

name: Rosita
description: Rosita signed up for her membership with PMPC and obtained the needed capital to start up a sari-sari (general) store business. She is thankful for the capital that was extended to a small-time borrower like her. Rosita has been able to turn the tide in her favor and is making good sales these days. She wants to take advantage of the good fortune. Recently, she took a loan to restock her store with basic commodities, like canned goods, oil, and soy sauce. In the future, she hopes to build a decent home for her family.

name: Carlos Bismarck
description: The love of technology has always been present in the heart of Carlos. That is why when he decided to go to college, he didn't think twice about majoring in computer science. Today he is a year away from finishing.   Because of that, he is asking for a loan to buy a computer and pay for an English class. This will help him because he can do his academic work with more efficiency and will finish his training when he speaks a foreign language. It is worth noting that Carlos plans on getting a master's degree and starting a computer repair business.

name: Alberto José
description: Alberto José is from the city of Managua.  He works as a Well Drilling Technician.  He’s been working for twenty years.  He’s married and has five dependents.  He is honest, responsible with good values and moral principles.  He came by this Ceprodel office to request a loan that will be used to repair the roof on his house which is in poor condition.  He will buy building materials and supplies like:  zinc metal sheeting, purlines and will pay labor costs.  He thanks Ceprodel for the opportunity this disbursement has provided him.

name: Soda
description: Living in a rural area of Phnom Penh, Soda is a university student and 19 years old. Nowadays, she earns income to support herself and her studies by working as an IT assistant in a company. For Soda, this is her first time with VisionFund and she will use her loan portion to pay for the tuition fees for studying administration which she will study abroad. Soda hopes that this loan will help her get a good job after graduation, so that she can earn a higher salary and help her family have better living conditions.

name: Erna
description: Erna is 38 years old and married with seven children.  Erna works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 13,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy more items to sell such as canned goods, eggs, milk, sugar, soap, coffee, noodles, etc.  Erna has borrowed and paid back three loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for one year and also earns an income from food vending.  Erna aspires to save money to expand her business.

name: Rebecca
description: Rebecca sells drinks, foodstuffs and frozen food and she has been in the business for the past ten years. She lives in Lagos. Rebecca is 35 years old and married with three children.  Rebecca is requesting the loan of N50,000 to purchase more drinks, foodstuffs and frozen food to sell. She thanks you.

name: Arselinda
description: Two years ago, Arselinda joined ASHI for a loan to start up a business of her own. At the age of 57 and with an unemployed husband, she needs to be productive to be able to support her two children, who do not have enough education and are 26 and 28. Before ASHI came into her life, Arselinda and her family succumbed to poverty. The income she had raising and selling goats wasn't enough for her to be able to finance her family's daily needs. Goat is not salable in the province and not as expensive when sold to people unless one has a large volume of goats for selling.  Through loans, she was empowered to start up another business fattening hogs in addition to her current business. This business gives her profits as much as double the capital. However, she wanted to request a much bigger loan to be able to grow her business further and to be able to make it more sustainable with larger profits. Arselinda also wants to reinvest her profits into opening a variety store in the next few years.  For her personal and family life, she wishes that she will be able to build a concrete house for better shelter.

name: Cheryl
description: Cheryl N. is from the village of Malipayon, Pangantucan Bukidnon. Cheryl is married and has 2 school-aged children. Cheryl owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) retail shop. The main source of income for the business comes from selling a variety of different products in the local community. Cheryl has been involved in her business for over 8 years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month from these activities.  In 2008, Cheryl joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Cheryl has successfully repaid a previous loan of 14,000 PHP from HSPFI. For her 6th loan, Cheryl is requesting the same amount of 14000 PHP which will be used to invest in expanding the business. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to support her children's education .   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Ofik
description: This nice lady is 25 years old, and she lives with her beloved husband (they are just married) and mother-in-law in Lchashen village of Gegharkunik region.   With her mother-in-law, Ofik is engaged in farming and agriculture. In the farm she has cows, sheep, and chickens.   Though still young, Ofik makes very tasty macun (a national dairy-product), cheese and curd from her farm milk.  She sells all that with her farm’s milk and meat.   Ofik is also skilled in potato cultivation, and she sells her potatoes to a re-seller right from her farm.She also has a sweet harvest of strawberries in her garden.   Ofik’s husband says he is pleased and proud of his young wife, who manages farming so skillfully and overcomes any hardships. Shealso thinks of increasing her number of farm cattle.  Ofik asks for this loan of 700,000 Armenian drams to buy several more sheep and also fodder for all her cattle.

name: Rugiatu
description: Meet 35-year-old Rugiatu from Kandeh town Bo in Sierra Leone. She is a single parent with two children between the ages of 9 and 18 years. Her children are currently attending school. In 1999, Rugiatu established her clothing business. She began her business because she did not go to school; her mother trained her in business. Rugiatu works at her business seven days per week and 9 hours per day. She says despite the challenges of single parent life and insufficient capital to expand her business, she is very hard working and intends to give her children a quality education.  Rugiatu requires a loan in order to buy different kinds of clothing material like shoes, crepe and men's T-shirts for resale. She hopes that the extra income from this loan will allow her to increase her business and improve her and her children's lives. In the future, Rugiatu plans to build a big residential house. She thanks you for your support.

name: Jeneveb
description: Jeneveb is 38 years old, married, and has one child who is in school. She is a very hard-working entrepreneur. She has a general store business in the Philippines. She has been doing this work for three years.Jeneveb requested a PHP 10,000 loan amount through NWTF. She will use this amount in order to purchase more items to sell, like snack foods, sugar, noodles and other groceries.In the future, Jeneveb would like to build and expand her business.

name: Beatrice
description: Beatrice is a hardworking married woman with 10 children living in Bundibugyo Uganda. Her business is cocoa farming and selling on top of palm oil business for supplementary income.   She is in need of a loan to buy more cocoa to supplement it to her own harvests to sell. She has a great desire of accumulating more capital and becoming a prominent cocoa dealer in her area although she complains of the difficulty of unpredictable weather changes and limited capital.

name: Al Malaika Group
description: Thanaa is the featured borrower of Al Malaika group. She joined her other group members to acquire a loan from Kiva partner, Al Majmoua, because they have always been neighbors and friends.  Thanaa is a 40-year-old married mother of two children and responsible for her family's living. She is employed in a furniture showroom where she receives a low income. She hopes that one day she can start her own business. The applied-for loan will be invested in paying her children's school tuition fees.  In the picture, Thanaa is the one wearing brown in the middle. As for the other group members, Marleine is the one at the left and Chris is the one at the right.

name: Allah Jawai's Group
description: Allah jawai lives in a city called Jaranwala which is located in Punjab province and is known for its agriculture industry in Pakistan. She lives there in the area named Mughalpura in a 2 roomed brick house with her family. She came here 3 years ago. She doesn’t have any children yet. So to spend her time she does her household responsibilities and also weaves carpets. She is an expert in her work and makes very good quality carpets on order. She receives orders from carpet sellers and earns well by fulfilling the orders on time. Her husband is a loader by profession. He uses his donkey cart to load different items such as construction supplies and fruits & vegetables. He offers good loading services to his clients by delivering their items to the designated places safely.    Allah jawai has applied for a loan from Kiva partner Asasah to financially assist her husband in purchasing of a new donkey cart, because his old cart has become rough and rotten. His work is being affected and he is losing his customer base. She is hopeful that a new cart will help her husband's business and to retain his clients as well.   Allah jawai is a new loan applicant of Asasah and hopes that an investment in her husband’s business will take his business to a more profitable position and she will be able to repay the loan easily.   Note: In the photo, the lady with a book (called Asasah Passbook) is Allah jawai.

name: Marydel
description: Marydel is 36 years old and married with two children, both of whom are in school. She works hard to provide for her family. She has been running a general store in the Philippines for 10 years and also earns an income from rice retailing.She requested a PHP 12,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy more items to sell, like canned goods, diapers, noodles, and other groceries.Marydel has borrowed and repaid seven loans from NWTF before this loan. She aspires to save enough money to expand her business and repair her family's home.

name: Mercy
description: Mercy is a 25-year-old mother of two boys aged 4 and 2.  She has a business selling onions, lemons, and mangos in the Oile market of Kisumu, Kenya.  She has been running her business on her own for over two years.  She has also been volunteering on the side to educate her friends, family, and neighbors about health issues.    Like many sellers in her position, Mercy faces the challenge of obtaining her produce, getting it to the market, and selling it all before it goes bad.  Her dream is to become a wholesale seller of fruits and vegetables, delivering them to others to sell.  She has identified this as a good market opportunity.

name: Cecilia
description: Cecilia is a married woman with three children, all of whom are in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Cecilia is 45 years old.  Cecilia has a furniture making business in the Philippines. Cecilia requested a PHP 10,000 loan amount through NWTF in order to buy raw materials for her furniture making business.  Cecilia has been in this business for nine years. In the future, Cecilia would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Balcon 3 Group
description: Daniela, 25, lives with her partner and three children: a newborn baby who is two months old, a 2-year-old and a 3-year-old.  She sells bread for a living.  She is a good mother and entrepreneur who is dedicated, consistent, kind, responsible and very hard working.  She works in the town of "El Torno" which is a community that has experienced demographic growth over the last few years due to immigration of people from further inland in the country.  The climate is subtropical as is it between the plains and mesothermic valleys, although there are strong winds and thunderstorms at certain times of year.  Daniela has a dark complexion, brown eyes, long brown hair that she ties back, is of short height and has a robust physique.  Her mother tongue is Guaraní which is spoken locally and she uses Spanish for general purposes and in her business (she is the one seated in the photo).  She and her partner, who delivers bread, live in their own brick and concrete house which has a metal roof and concrete floor.  They have running water, electricity and a sewage system.  The need to pay for postnatal medical expenses for her three small children is what obliged her to set up a communal bank which includes businesses such as selling natural juices, stationery goods, second-hand clothing, food, fabric crafts, "Sao" hat manufacture and a keysmith.  The loan is to improve the group's businesses.  Daniela makes and sells traditional bread such as rice flour bread, corn bread, milk bread, wheat cakes and others.  She works out of a room in her home that was remodeled into a bakery.  Her husband is the one who delivers the bread to different stores and stalls.  "I work from home and start in the wee morning hours while my children sleep.  I have the rest of the day to care for them..." she says.  The advantage of her business is that she can attend to both family and work responsibilities.  The disadvantage is the lack of capital to buy flour on a continuous basis and reach out to more customers.  Her dream is to raise healthy, strong children.    She wants to buy different types of flour by the quintal.  This is her second loan through the institution in the four years she has been in business.  Her aim is to make different kinds of bread every day and care for her children the rest of the time.

name: Eudulia
description: Eudalia, 38 years old, is a single mother and lives in her own house made of rustic material with her son in Pucará district, Jaén province, Cajamarca department, in the country of Peru. She has very good personal and work references from the people in the area. The inhabitants of this place work primarily in agriculture, trade, and raising animals.   She works selling general products, such as belts, dyes, watches, etc. with over 5 years of experience in the field. The destination of the loan will be to invest in the business by purchasing merchandise such as thread, fabric, etc. In this way, she will be able to improve her quality of life and that of her family. Eudalia is a returning borrower with Edpyme Alternativa.

name: Robina
description: Robina, a 26-year-old woman living in Rawalpindi, Pakistan with her husband and son, is very hard-working. She wishes to uplift her family from poverty, thus she is working so hard to provide for the needs of her son.   Robina has applied for a loan from Kiva partner BRAC Pakistan to repair her husband's taxi, which he has been running for five years. She supports her husband, and looks to satisfy the needs of her family.   She hopes, with the help of this loan, she will reach her desired net income and be able to save for their future.

name: Fungai
description: Fungai is a young entrepreneur eager to grow her poultry business in the rural area of Chikomba East, Zimbabwe. The business supports her husband and one child. She currently sells broiler chicks to community members at a fair price and is thankful to have loyal customers. She loves her business and knows that it can expand with the help from a Kiva loan.   With the requested Kiva loan, Fungai will buy chicks and chick feed in bulk in order to increase her sales. She hopes to use the additional profits to improve her family’s standard of living and to support families in need in her community. Fungai currently volunteers as a Camfed Learner Guide. As a Learner Guide, she gives her free time to students in local schools by teaching them valuable life skills that can help them improve their well being.

name: Suraiya
description: Suraiya is 58 years old, a vigorous, married woman and the mother of five children. She has had a business doing hand embroidery for the past seven years. She is passionate about her work, and client demand is strong.  But business challenges, combined with family expenditures, frustrate her nearly every day. Her husband is employed as a salesperson in a grocery store but he does not earn enough to support his family well. Suraiya’s embroidery patterns are very popular on her street, and she is the best earning resource in her household. She wants to grow her business so she requested a loan of Rs 25000, to buy raw materials such as thread, sequins and pearls in large quantities to meet the increasing demand. She is in her second loan cycle and hopes to have a good experience with this new loan. She shared her dream of running a training center for girls of her village.

name: Violette
description: Greetings from Kigali,Rwanda!   M. Violette is 37 years old, she is married, and she has four children with the ages 16,14,10 and 8 years old.   She has 10 years of experience in selling various drinks as found on the icluded picture.Her monthly profit is 250,000. Now she needs her first loan of 500,000 RWF from Vision Finance Company.  With this requested loan, Violette hopes to expand her business through purchasing more drinks in order to get more profit than before.  Once that purpose is achieved, she hopes to be able to pay school fees for her children for good schools and also to save for the future.

name: Rogina
description: Mrs. Rogina T. is a housewife who lives in Kulashwor, Kathmandu, in a family of four. She and her husband, Mr. Rabi T., and opened their grocery shop nine years ago. Her daughter and son are studying in primary school. During the month of October, the Nepalese observe two big festivals, Dashain and Tihar. During these festivals people buy many grocery items. This month is a great month for businesses, whether they are big or small. Mrs. Rogina T. is asking for her first loan so that she can invest in more varieties of grocery items in this season to meet the customers' demand.

name: Bodurin
description: Mrs. Bodurin T. is 45 years old. She is divorced with 4 children, and lives in Mushin, Lagos State, Nigeria. She sells fish and has been in business since 1993. She needs a loan of $400 to buy more fish for sale. She thanks you.

name: Akouavi Jeanne
description: Akouavi Jeanne is a 40-year-old woman. She is married to a construction electrician and has two children.  Akouavi Jeanne has worked as a retailer of traditional pagne cloth since 2001. She sells to her customers at the marketplace in Lomé, where she also purchases her wares.  Akouavi Jeanne has requested her second WAGES loan in order to purchase traditional pagne cloth.

name: Edson
description: Edson used his previous loan to buy sugar, soap and paraffin to sell. He lives in Kamwenge, Uganda and still owns a retail shop to get income and cater for his family. He also earns an extra income from bodaboda (motorcycle) transport and coffee growing.  With the proceeds from his shop, he has been able to pay school fees for his children. Edson appreciates Kiva for the support given to him, which has enabled his cash flows to increase. Edson hopes that in the future, he will own a wholesale business; though he faces a challenge of high inflation rates and inadequate capital to meet the high demands.   Edson intends to use the loan to buy salt, sugar, and cooking oil to sell.

name: Amani Kwetu Group
description: The client, Noella, is a saleswoman and member of the business collective, "Amani Kwetu." She is an entrepreneur who is 46 years old and a widow. She has seven children, three of whom go to school, and four of whom left school.   The client sells fresh milk and cakes. She displays her goods on a street in a lively local district. She started her business with funds from her brother. She has been working on this business for four years.   This new loan will help her buy 20 liters of milk, two bags of wheat flour, and 10 liters of oil. She would like to grow her capital, and educate, clothe, and feed her children.   Finally, she would like to thank Hekima strongly for their empowerment of female entrepreneurs not served by the banking system. She is especially thankful in this critical post-conflict time in the east of the country.   She would like to point out that among the kneeling clients, one is holding her baby in front of her.

name: Mwanakombo
description: Mwanakombo has operated a retail shop business, selling household consumables like wheat flour, maize flour, and sugar. She faces a major challenge of seasonality in her business. With this loan, she wants to purchase stocks of sugar, rice, maize flour and wheat flour. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business. Mwanakomo appreciates the support from her previous loan, which helped her with good profits, and which in turn boosted her living standards.

name: Nguyễn's Group
description: "T. Nguyễn Thị (10107050007) is a 25-year-old female living in the town of Đông Anh - Hà nội.  T. is the group leader of a four-member group L. offered by SEDA.  While each member of the group receives an individual L., they are all responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults.  The official name of this borrowing group is Văn Thượng (5).  T. is married and has two infant children.  To make a living, T. operates a service-based business.  The main source of income for the business comes from providing repair services to local community members.  T. has been engaged in this business for over five years and earns approximately $153 a month from this activity.  In 2007, T. joined SEDA to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities.  T. has successfully repaid a previous L. of 4.452.000 VND from SEDA.  This previous L. was used to purchase materials needed to provide service.  She is now requesting a new L. of 5.450.000 VND which will again be used to purchase needed materials.  The will be her 4th L. from SEDA.  T. plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About the Other Borrowers in the Group:  1.  Đào Thị T. (10107050011) is a 54-year-old female who is requesting a 4.142.000 VND L. to support her business in the food sector operating a butcher shop.  2.  Lê Thị L. (10107050009) is a 32-year-old female who is requesting a 5.014.000 VND L. to support her service-based business.  3.  Nguyễn Thị T. P. (10107050008) is a 29-year-old female who is requesting a 5.014.000 VND L. to support her business in the agriculture sector raising livestock.   About SEDA:  The mission of SEDA (Center of Small Enterprise Development Assistance) is to provide micro-finance services to the low income and disadvantaged people in rural areas of Hanoi and the Northern provinces of Vietnam.   *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this L. was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in Vietnamese while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.   T. Nguyễn Thị (10107050007) là 25 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy sống ở thành phố Đông Anh - Hà nội.  T. là trưởng nhóm của nhóm vay gồm có 4 các thành viên.  Mặc dù mỗi thành viên trong nhóm nhận được từng khoản vay cá nhân, nhưng tất cả họ đều chịu trách nhiệm hoàn trả lại khoản vay của các thành viên trong nhóm của mình nếu một người nào đó trễ hạn hay không trả được nợ..  Tên chính thức của nhóm vay này là Văn Thượng (5).  Trong khi không phải chỉ có các P. thức tạo nên T. nhập, mà nguồn T. nhập chính của công việc kinh doanh chủ yếu từ cung cấp các dịch vụ sửa chữa cho người dân trong cộng đồng địa P..  T. thực hiện công việc kinh doanh này trong hơn 5 năm.  Từ các hoạt động này, T. kiếm được khoảng 2.800.000 VND.  Vào 2007, T. đã tham gia SEDA để có thể tiếp cận với các dịch vụ tài chính giúp cải thiện  sinh hoạt và khả năng tham gia vào các hoạt động kinh doanh của cô ấy/ anh ấy.  T. đã hoàn trả hết khoản vay trước đây là 4.452.000 VND từ SEDA.  Khoản vay trước đây được sử dụng mua vật tư cần thiết để cung cấp dịch vụ.  Cô ấy hiện đang đề nghị một khoản vay mới là 5.450.000 VND.  Khoản vay sẽ là 4th khoản vay của người vay từ SEDA.  Về Những Người vay khác trong Nhóm:  1.  Đào Thị T. (10107050011) là 54 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 4.142.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực thực phẩm.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là kinh doanh cửa hàng T.t.  2.  Lê Thị L. (10107050009) là 32 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 5.014.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực dịch vụ.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là vận hành công việc kinh doanh trên cơ sở dịch vụ.  3.  Nguyễn Thị T. P. (10107050008) là 29 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 5.014.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực nông nghiệp.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là chăn nuôi gia súc.   Về SEDA:  Nhiệm vụ của SEDA (Trung Tâm hỗ Trợ Phát Triển các Doanh Nghiệp Nhỏ) là cung cấp các dịch vụ tài chính vi mô cho những người có T. nhập thấp và kém may mắn trong các vùng nông thôn tại Hà Nội và các tỉnh phía Bắc Việt Nam   *Lưu ý: Để phát huy tối đa hiệu quả & giảm chi phí, khoản vay này đã được thông báo bằng biểu mẫu để có thể được Kiva tự động biên dịch. .  Do việc biên dịch thủ công các danh mục rất tốn kém, nên Kiva đã tạo biểu mẫu này cho phần Field Partner (Trường Đối Tác) cho phép họ tiếp tục thông báo các khoản vay bằng  Vietnamese trong khi cung cấp thông tin có chất lượng & chính xác cho người cho vay Kiva.  ."

name: Toyibah
description: T. is 24 years old and married with one child aged 3. She sells fruit-flavored blended ice in front of her house. She usually earns a profit of $1.50 per day. Her husband, Sukron, is a fisherman whose income is unpredictable, ranging between $2 - $3 per day.  She very much needs to have this $50 loan to expand her business. She is willing to repay this loan within a period of 12 months.

name: Regina
description: Regina is thankful that she was granted a 25,000 PHP loan, which she used to purchase various grocery items and products needed in her general store. Through her earnings she is able to send her children to school and meet their daily living expense. Aside from her general store, she also has a tricycle for transportation service.  She would now like to apply for a 30,000 PHP loan, which she will use as part of her working capital to buy more grocery items like rice, coffee, soda, rice noodles and frozen foods, which she sells at retail. Part of the loan she will use for the maintenance of her tricycle unit. Her income from her store and tricycle service is a stable source to sustain her family's basic needs and for the education of her children. She is thanking God and you in advance for the financial help that will be given her.   Regina hopes to sustain and grow her two businesses to give her family a better life. She aims to give her children the best education possible, to allow them better opportunities in life. Every week, she meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her work and to draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God which she studies .   *All Center for Community Transformation (CCT) community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital and repay Micro-Finance loans.

name: Nueva Esperanza Group
description: Martha has four children, is married and has worked with Edaprospo for six years together with the "Nueva Esperanza" group. The group is made up of 11 people that make their livings in varied businesses in sales.   Martha makes a living raising chickens and works selling eggs and chicken meat. She started this business after taking a course through the municipality in her district. After some time she has a loyal customer base. Thanks to her effort and dedication, she has been able to give her children technical educations like computing and gastronomy.   In an effort to continue growing, she has requested a new loan to sell food (milk, rice, spices). Martha will achieve her goals with a lot of work and effort as well as the loans from Edaprospo that will help her.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth F. is from the village of Villa Verde, Iligan City. She is 51 years old. Elizabeth is married and has five adult-aged children. To make a living, Elizabeth owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) retail shop. The main source of income for the business comes from selling both food and daily-use products. Elizabeth has been engaged in her business for over five years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month.  In 2010, Elizabeth joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Elizabeth is requesting a loan of 5,000 PHP so she can purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be Elizabeth's first loan from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is an accredited partner of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation.  Because manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template so field staff can continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.
town: Villaverde, Iligan City, Lanao del Norte

name: Mamie
description: Mamie lives in Airport area. She is 33 years of age, and she stopped her education in the 7th grade. She is married, and her husband is a security guard. They have three children who are between the ages of 9 and 15, all of whom live at home and attend school.   For the past four years, she been dressing hair in the local market. She started this business with money given to her by her husband and learned this way of selling from friends. She enjoys the business because of the experiences she receives every day. She asked for a loan to purchase more artificial hair to attract more customers. Her plan is to build a shop in the near future.

name: Elsa
description: This is Elsa, 46, a resident of Tanza, Cavite City, Philippines. Her husband is Marcial, a security guard, and she is mother to her two children. She, together with her husband and children, manages their own household while operating the business. At this time, she is working hard to continually provide income for their everyday expenses.  Elsa operates a variety store. In the Philippines, a variety store is basically a small convenience store which retails groceries, toiletries and beverages piecemeal to the local neighborhood. It is the place to go to buy one sachet of shampoo, 5 PHP-worth of cooking oil or an egg. She earns by getting supplies at wholesale prices and selling by the piece. She also sells direct-selling products for additional income.  Her store is located adjacent to her house. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community. She earns a minimum of 350 Philippine pesos (PHP) in sales every day.  To help her continue operation of her business, she is requesting a 10,000 PHP loan. She will be utilizing the loan to buy groceries, toiletries, beverages and other products needed in her business.  She expects a boost in her business income as she expands her business.   Elsa hopes her business will grow into a mini-grocery and dreams to be able to give her children a good and high quality education through all her hard work on her business. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her work every week, and this is where she also draws strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans.

name: Leitisia
description: Leitisia is 32 years old and single. She has one child. She has a small garden where she grows taro, bananas, and yams, which she can sell in her community or at the market. She has been doing this for two years.  Leitisia needs a loan to buy a new wheelbarrow, a shovel, a rake, some bush knives, a weedkiller spray and some tiapula (taro for planting). She is a new member of SPBD, having joined in 2012. Leitisia will use the profits from her business to increase her family's assets.

name: Elisa
description: Elisa is married and works hard to support her family.  She runs a fishing business in the Philippines.  Elisa requested a PHP 10000 loan through NWTF to buy additional materials for her fishing business.  She has been in the fishing business for 42 years.  Elisa would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Yeap
description: Yeap, 45, is a married woman from Kampong Cham Province. She has four children. To make a living, she manages and operates a farming business, growing rice and selling her agriculture product to the local dealers. So far, she has been involved in this business for 30 years. She is able to make an income of USD $5 per day, on average.    Recently, some parts of her house have deteriorated and they need to be fixed to provide a suitable living place for the household. Due to the lack of funds, she has applied for a Kiva loan via HKL to pay for her house renovation. She and her family will be thankful to the lenders for helping them with the loan funding to improve their living standards.

name: Anita
description: Anita is 61 years old and married; she lives in Sindangan, Zamboangadel Norte. For a living,  Anita and her husband have cultivated a rice land; she is also engaged in swine production business.  Anita mastered doing these activities for twenty years now. She joined Paglaum Multi Purpose Cooperative on May of 2012. She is hardworking and has strong determination to pursue her goals to sustain her family needs.  Anita requested a loan to purchase fertilizers to increase crop yield on her rice farm, and purchase bags of feeds and vitamins for her pigs. This will greatly help Anita to boost her income. Someday, she wishes to buy rice land to cultivate and hopes to venture into rice retailing business.
town: Sindangan - Tabon, Jose Dalman, Zamboanga del Nort

name: Kizlarsara
description: Kizlarsara is 46 years old. She is married and has six children. She loves her children and tries to provide them with a high quality of living. Her husband is a man who cannot find enough money for improving the family's living conditions. He is a labor migrant, working in Russia. It is difficult for Kizlarsara to buy food and clothing, and to pay for the other expenses of six children. Sometime her relatives help her with money, but it is not enough.  Kizlarsara wants to organize a new business in animal husbandry, because her house is big and suitable for animal husbandry. She studied at the course ‘To Get Ahead’ of a women's organization and earned her certificate. She is asking for a loan of 3,500 Somoni to buy two cows, for organizing her new business. Her children will help her with managing the business. She awaits your support.

name: Gavy Yessenia
description: Gavy is 42 years old. She went to school until the ninth grade. She has two children, only one of them lives with her and a grandson.Gavy has worked in a shop for the last two years, she works there for three days a week. Previously she worked in a shop making and selling pupusas (filled corn tortillas), where she gained experience, and this is why she is now planning to set up shop in her home and sell pupusas in the afternoons.She needs this loan to buy corn, fresh cheese, beans and a griddle to make the pupusas. She will also buy a blender to sell fruit smoothies. Her plans for the future are to have a high customer demand to which she is committed to providing excellent service so that she will be their preferred choice, and to make good profits.

name: Yuvicsa
description: 20-year-old Yuvicsa is a hard-working and tenacious young woman.  She is also kind and supportive.  She lives comfortably together with her parents in their own home.  Yuvicsa's business is renting out her home.  She rents out half the house to a private company at a rate of 350 soles a month.  She also has some rooms which are set up to rent out to young students.  This enables her to make more income.  Yuvicsa started this business as she wanted to make the most of the empty spaces in her home.  She has been in this business for one year and, up to now, she has had the support of her parents.  Yuvicsa enjoys her business as it leaves her time free to work in other areas and also allows her to make income without much effort.  Owing to how profitable the rental business has been, she has plans to expand and build more rooms in her home so that she can rent them out and thereby make more income.  This will be Yuvicsa's fifth loan from MFP.  She is very happy to know that she has financial support as it makes her feel certain that she will make progress in her business.  She will invest the sum of 1,000 soles in repairing and fixing up her home for the comfort of her tenants.

name: Efua
description: Efua sells palm oil at Abura. She has been making palm oil for sale for ten years. She is going to add the money she will be receiving to her capital to be able to buy sacks of palm fruits to produce oil for sale. She is married to a driver and together they take care of their dependents. She hopes to use the new profits from her business to buy land.

name: Sandra
description: Without a lot of capital to start a business that generates good income to pay for her home's expenses, Sandra has looked for a way to start her own manicure business.  She has made income with this, which contributes to paying for her home's expenses.  She lives with her husband and two children.  Since her husband's wages are very low, they didn't cover all of their expenss.  Sandra decided to start her own business, and with a lot of effort, she positioned it so her customers come to her for the good service that she offers.  Thanks to the fact that her business has recently grown, Sandra has started to require a larger quantity of tools and that they be of a better quality.  This is why she is looking for a loan that will offer her the possibility of buying products like nail polish, nail files, and other supplies that her manicure business needs.  Sandra hopes that in this way, her business will keep growing and she can continue offering her customers good attention and service.  Sandra also hopes to help her children get ahead and offer them a good education and better economic opportunities in their lives.

name: Janice
description: Janice works hard to support two children. She is married and has a solar lamp business in the Philippines.  She requested a PHP 1,800 loan through NWTF to buy a solar lamp.  She is getting the solar lamp because she wants to provide her children with bright light when they study at night.  Janice is aware that by using the solar lamp, she is not only saving money, she is also helping the environment and reducing health and hazard risks to her family.

name: Gena
description: Gena is 32 years old and married with five children. She earns a living by raising pigs in the Philippines. Gena is borrowing PHP 20,000 through NWTF to buy feed and vitamins for her pigs.  Gena has been raising pigs for 6 years and also earns additional income from rice sales. She works tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Capuyo Group
description: The group is called Capuyo and they named it this because it is a flower that continues to be reborn. The group is located in the state of México and is maD. up of new members. ManueL. M. is the treasurer of the group. She is thirty-eight years old and studied up until high school. She is a business owner, married and has a son who is twelve years old. She started in the business world about fifteen years ago. She started by selling bread with her neighbors and she currently has had her own store for two years now. She requests the loan to invest in some things she doesn't have such as a refrigerator for dairy products. She also wants to make her store bigger because she has a lot of customers and she wants to have even more. She feels very proud for requesting the loan and hopes to reach her goal with the support of her family.

name: Bernice
description: Bernice, who was born in 1965, is married to Mr. Muh Francis and is blessed with five children. She has two mates and they all live in a two-room apartment in the Tumuku Belo subdivision. Bernice got her first loan of 50,000 XAF from GHAPE in 2009, which she used for farming.  Bernice is requesting a second loan to buy planting seeds and more goats. She knows that her business will succeed since she has enough land for cultivation and for her goats to graze. She is helping the community since she is a good supplier of food items from her farm. Bernice had some difficulties when her brother died and when her mother was sick. Bernice will use the profit from her loan to improve the family's standard of living and to pay the children's tuition fees. She prefers loans from GHAPE since they train their borrowers how to use to their loans.  About GHAPE  The Grounded and Holistic Approach to People's Empowerment (GHAPE) is a non-profit NGO based in Bamenda, Cameroon.  GHAPE works towards the empowerment of the poor and poverty alleviation through a highly multi-faceted approach.  Every client is trained in business management, basic health, life skills, financial management, profits and losses, and family values.  Clients are also required to contribute a small amount into a personal savings account; most clients save much more than the minimum requirement.  GHAPE instils a sense of family and community within its clients and staff and has developed a strong bond of trust between the organization and its clients.

name: Eléonora
description: Éléonora is 42 years old and the mother of three children. She is married to a manager. She has been a retailer of colored pagnes (West African cloth) since 1999. She buys her supplies in Lomé. She has hired one person. Éléonora came to the microfinance institution WAGES and applied for her first loan to buy pagnes.

name: Basilia
description: This member belongs to the communal bank VIRGEN DEL CARMEN DE YUNCAYPATA. This is a friendly communal bank that is located 30 minutes from the city of Cusco in the village called Yuncaypata. This is a typical little village in that it retains its pure Andean heritage, and they live together in a supporting community, planting and harvesting, caring for their children and their animals, in a very pretty town where they speak Quechua, and in the department of Cusco.  Brasilia, a member of the communal bank is 45 years old, married with 5 children who are 26, 24, 20, 18, and 15 years old. She works in agriculture and raising animals such as poultry, pigs, sheep and cows. She sells her products such as cereal in various markets in the city of Cusco.  She is asking for a loan at this time to finish her house. She and her husband completed building their house and now want to cover the facade. She is very happy to be able to finish off her own house where each step cost so much and now only wants to complete it. She is asking for the loan to invest in the purchase of plaster, stucco, and related expenses to pay the workers for covering the facade of her home. She is thankful and grateful for the loan and promises to make her payments on time as she has done in her previous loans.

name: Pheap's Group
description: Pheap, 35, is a mother of three children. She deals with her family’s financial burden via rice farming which has generated her about 8,600 KHR per day.   Pheap has never been with VisionFund (Kiva's partner) before. Now, she has formed a group of three to get a new loan of 170,000 KHR each. She is the leader and will use her entire portion to build a proper latrine for her kids to promote a hygienic practice in her family.

name: Rodina
description: Rodina works hard to support her family. Rodina is married and has a buying and selling of ready-to-wear clothing business in the Philippines.  Rodina requested a PHP 18,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more ready-to-wear clothes to sell like T-shirts, shorts, slippers and other ready-to-wear products.  Rodina has been in this business for six years now.  She would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Consulate
description: Consulate, a 26-year-old mother of two children, has been operating a salon business for five months now, having begun it with savings accrued from her teaching job. Inadequate capital and high transport costs are factors affecting her business growth.   Having used her previous loan to buy cosmetics for her salon, Consulate is requesting a new loan for the same purpose. She wishes to expand her business into other new markets and buy land for growing crops. Consulate also has a dream of building a permanent home and educating her children.

name: Francis Musyimi
description: Francis Musyimi is a 63 year-old a businessman who sells livestock. He is married to Peninah and they are blessed with five children. Three of the children are working and two are in secondary school. Francis has been selling livestock for the past 25 years. His current monthly income is Kshs. 30,000.  Francis is servicing his second loan with Kiva partner KADET Ltd.  He plans to start a butchery to sell meat to his customers. With the anticipated profits from his business he intends to renovate his rental houses to modern ones with modern facilities. His hopes and dreams are to construct rental houses and buy pieces of land in his home town, Mwingi, and in other towns.

name: Salome
description: Salome M. is 53 years old and a mother of five. She had five male children: Benedict– 36 years old, a high school graduate; Bernardo– 34 years old, a high school undergraduate; Jil– 32 years old, also a high school graduate; Mamerto– 30 years old, a college graduate in agribusiness; and the youngest, Sabelo– 29 years old, a college undergraduate. They live in a flooded area in Yeban Sur, Benito Soliven, Isabela.    Salome is engaged in selling secondhand RTW’s (ready to wear clothes) in their village. She started in this kind of business when her children stopped their studies. She plans to buy more secondhand clothes from abroad to sell in their village. For this, she would like to borrow a loan of PHP 4,000 that will greatly support her business financially.  Salome prays that her loan will be granted and for her business to grow so she can have her own stall in the public market of Benito Soliven. For her, diligence and perseverance are the keys to success. She would always like to be strong in order to overcome the challenges in life.

name: Aineah
description: Aineah is a married man. He has three children, with ages ranging from 3 to 12 years. He describes himself as motivated. He operates a transport business, where he transports customers using his motorcycle. He has been involved in this business for four years. His business is located in a populated area, and his primary customers are travelers. He says his biggest business challenge is insecurity.He will use the KES 20,000 loan to buy a motorcycle engine for his old motorcycle. His business goal is to have a vehicle, within five years. He hopes that in the future, he will have a good life for his family and expand business. This is his first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: Mujeres Luchadoras Group
description: The 21 members of this group each have their own businesses and each wants to improve her status through her work and by giving her all to get ahead.Brasilia is one of the members and she sells clothing on foot and has many customers who always buy clothing from her. She is a very hardworking woman who strives to improve her living conditions and those of her loved ones.She is asking for this loan to buy clothing such as shirts, jeans, pants, and other things so she can continue to improve for her loved ones.

name: Peter
description: Peter is 49 years old and married to Rose.  They are blessed with one child who is 14 years old child. Peter sells building materials in a business he started four years ago and earns 64,000 KES per month.   He has requested his first loan of 30,000 KES to purchase more bricks, iron sheets, glass, timber, and sand for sale. The profit he earns will help with pay his child's school fees. Peter's dream is to practice farming and give his child a good education.

name: Sule Nadanko
description: Sule Nadanko is a maize farmer from Kwankwani village in Kaduna state. Before he became a Babban Gona member, Sule Nadanko would have had to sell his maize for low prices soon after harvest, to cater for his immediate cash needs. With this loan and Babban Gona’s support, Sule Nadanko can now store his maize at harvest time and sell it a few months later for up to 40% higher than the market price at harvest. Sule Nadanko, like other members of Babban Gona, intends to use the extra income to expand his farmland, and hopes to become the most profitable farmer in his community.

name: Juan José
description: Juan is 43 years old. He is in a relationship and has four children. He studied up to Grade 6 but could not continue as the school was far away.Juan has had a mill in his house for 29 years. He decided to install it there as he lives in a fairly populated area and it had no mill. His partner helps him to care for the clients who come to have grains milled. They have two periods for milling, one from 8 am until 11 am and again in the afternoon from 3 pm until 5 pm. Juan needs the loan to buy two pieces for the mill as it is damaged and if it is not repaired he will have little income and lose his clients. Juan's dream is to have another mill to completely cover the demand that exists and have more income.

name: Monserrate (Montecristi) Group
description: The communal bank "Monserrate" meets every two weeks in the city of Montecristi, known for its rich pre-colonial culture and crafts that are renowned both nationally and internationally.  It is the place of the famous Panama straw hat.  This group of people decided to get together three cycles ago and set up the communal bank which has helped them greatly.  With the loans they have received they have improved their small business and lifestyles.  They are involved in different businesses such as agriculture, general commerce, services and other activities.    One of the members of the group is Mr. Carlos, 48, who is married and has five children, four adults and a minor son who is 17 and in school.  All of his children live at home.  His wife is a homemaker.  He works for a compny in the city of Manta, but is also a merchant and in his free time sells all kinds of clothing, sheets and comforters.  In the evenings he goes out to visit his customers to sell his products which he leaves on credit and then collects in two payments.  He collects payment on the weekends.  He buys merchandise in Guayaquil when necessary.  He has been in business for six years and it is going well for him.    This loan will be used to buy trousers, shirts, blouses, children's clothing, sheets and comforters.  This is his third cycle with the communal bank and he enjoys the benefits offered by the institution.  His dream is to buy a car.

name: Amador Roque
description: Roque lives in the city of Ica, which is characterized for having a very warm and inviting climate. Agriculture has developed there, especially the cultivation of cotton and asparagus, among others. Roque is a single father. Due to other circumstances, he had to become father and mother to his two children, who are now 18 and 6 years old and for whom he strives every day to be able to make them good people and above all to be better than himself. Roque works every day as a laborer on a property in his city, with which, and with great effort, he is able to pay his household expenses. He works about 8 hours a day, and he believes that his work is going well for him because he is very friendly with the customers and above all because he has a great will to advance and to be a source of pride for his children.  Roque is very grateful to the Kiva lenders, since this is the second time that they have offered him their great support, and thanks to that he will be able to buy a stove, since he is now cooking with firewood. In this way he will avoid accidents, and in this way he will be able to offer a better quality of life to his children and continue striving every day to be able to make his greatest dream a reality: to have his own house.

name: Rolando
description: Rolando is 37 years old and still single at his age. He lives in Southern Looc, Plaridel, Misamis Occidental Philippines. For the past five years, Rolando has sold fish to earn a living. He has been a member of PMPC for three years and earns 10,000 PHP each month.  Rolando is requesting a 10,000 PHP loan to purchase fish to sell. In the future, he hopes to have enough savings to provide for his future needs.

name: Annah
description: Annah is 39 years old from Nyahururu. She is married and her spouse produces some additional income to the family. They have two children, age 16 and 10 years old.  She is a farmer and has been in this occupation for the past one year. Her monthly income at present is KES 5,000.  She has applied for a loan of KES 20,000 from KADET Ltd., which she plans to use for buying chicken and chicken feeds.   Annah's dreams for the future are to raise a happy family and to be financially stable.

name: Cherlita
description: Cherlita is 44 years old and has three children.  Cherlita is married and has two children who are in school.  She is in the agricultural business raising pigs in the Philippines. Cherlita requested a PHP 20000 loan through NWTF to buy feeds and other supplies to raise her pigs.  Cherlita has been raising pigs for 7 years now, and has borrowed 22 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, Cherlita would like to save enough to build a house for her family.

name: Remedio
description: Remedio, aged 50, is a resident of Tanza, Cavite City, Philippines. He is married to Jesselyn, a caregiver and mother to their three children. The eldest child is already in high school while the other two are still at home. Remedio, together with his wife, manages their own household while operating the business. At this time, he is working hard to continually provide income for their everyday expenses.  Remedio operates a rolling store. His rolling store is basically a small household products store, which retails plastic containers, dippers, pails, plastic flowers and basins to the local neighborhood. He drives the rolling store within the local community to sell the products. He earns by getting supplies at wholesale prices and selling by the piece. His regular customers are his neighbors and the local community. He earns a minimum of PHP 800 in sales every day.  To help him continue operating his business, he is requesting a PHP 10,000 loan. He will be utilizing the loan to buy pails, plastic-ware, hangers, clothes pins, plastic flowers and other items to expand his product inventory. He expects a boost in his business income as he expands his business.   Remedio hopes that his business will continue to be successful and dreams of having a permanent store. He faithfully meets up with his co-fellowship members to share stories of his work every week and can also draw strength and inspiration there from the Word of God that he studies.   * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans.

name: Aba
description: Aba is a single parent and has five dependents. They live together in Abreshia near Elmina. Aba is a petty trader. She sells plastic bowls which she has done for four years. As a single parent, she uses her income to feed and clothe her children and pay for their school fees. Aba will use her loan to purchase more plastic bowls to sell. She will expand her business with the new profit.

name: Kabundaire United Ass Group
description: Noah is a 33-year-old married man with two children. He lives in his own permanent house in Fort Portal, Uganda. His dream is to own a big produce store in town. Noah owns a store containing maize and cassava flour and he has been operating it for 10 years. His major challenge has been inadequate capital to meet the increasing demands of his customers. Noah needs the loan to buy cassava flour for resale.

name: Adelaida's Group
description: Adelaida V., from the village of Centro Sur, Alcala, Cagayan, is the 58-year-old group leader of a four-member group loan offered by ASKI. While each member of the group receives an individual loan, they are all responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults.  A married mother of five grown children, Adelaida raises pigs for fattening and sale. Adelaida has been engaged in her business for over two years and earns approximately 3,400 whenever she sells her raised animal.  In 2010, Adelaida joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She is requesting a loan of 5000 PHP to purchase livestock to raise and sell in the future, and she plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to make improvements to her house.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 25 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partners to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Faustina
description: Faustina N. is 39 years old. She is married and the mother of three children who are in school.  Faustina sells washing supplies like detergents, soaps, bleaches, etc. She does her selling through hawking - that is, house to house selling. She balances her stock on her head and walks miles to sell to her customers at their doorsteps.  Faustina needs the loan the enable her to inject more capital into her business to make progress. She plans to use the loan to buy more supplies of detergents to increase her stock. This will make more income to provide her children with a good education.

name: Rahma
description: Rahma, aged 30, is a married woman with three children, all of whom attend school. She owns a house that has electricity and piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is food for the family.  For the past three years she has operated a boda boda (motorcycle) business and a second hand clothes selling business. She sells her clothes from home to her neighbours and passersby. She faces a major challenge of high cost of purchasing clothes at the market for resale. Rahma dreams of expanding and establishing a shop at the market to sell her products.  With the Kshs 50,000 she wants to purchase bales of clothes for resale. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Hachem
description: Hachem is a 54-year-old divorced man, who has spent his whole life taking care of his three children. He was father, mother and friend all at the same time.  Hachem is a hardworking man, sacrificing himself for his children's best interests. He has owned a specialty home products and gift shop since 1995. It's his only source of income and that's why he invests a lot in it to give him back what he's seeking.  Hachem's shop needs some necessary maintenance to be done, in addition to expanding his product range with a new released collection, and that's why he applied for a loan from Kiva partner Al Majmoua to obtain requested needs.  It's his fourth cycle as an Al Majmoua borrower, and he describes his experience as a smart step taken to move forward. He hopes to keep on improving his business as much as he can.

name: Salomat
description: Salomat is 39-years old. She is married and has four children. She is very industrious and clever. She has a 3.50 ha land and grows maize and wheat. Her children help her with business. Salomat must work hard as her children become older and demand more money. She is going to start a new business with animal husbandry in order to generate additional income for improving her living condition. She is asking for a loan of 1000 somoni to buy cows. In this way, she will provide her family with s high quality living condition. Moreover, she will enter her children in good schools. She promises to make her payment on time. She awaits your support.

name: Yolanda
description: Yolanda is a 44-year-old, married woman and a mother of three children. She is from Leyte, Philippines. Yolanda is engaged in a hog-raising business. For more than 13 years now, this business has supported Yolanda in meeting the needs of her family. Yolanda is now asking for a loan to buy piglets and animal feed. With this loan, she will be able to raise healthy pigs which she can sell to the market in a few months. In the future, Yolanda hopes to make her business more sustainable.

name: Joseph
description: Joseph is a thirty-five-year-old married man with four children who owns a house in Kasese, Uganda. He has been in the textile business for ten years. He got the initial capital from his previous employment, started a retail shop, and later transformed it into a textiles shop. His hardship comes from debtors who take long to pay. His vision is to grow into a large-scale textiles shop and to have a poverty-free educated family. Joseph needs the loan facility to buy textiles for sale.

name: María Ercilia
description: The communal bank “Dinámicas” meets every fortnight in the city of Tosagua, which is known for being very dynamic and where the majority of its inhabitants make a living from agriculture and raising animals as it is an area with a lot of vegetation.  Maria lives in Tosagua and is 68 years old. Several years ago her beloved husband passed away, but she has three children from her marriage and they were her strength in that difficult time. They are now grown up and are independent of her.  Maria has always liked earning a living for herself and her family. Together with her husband she set apart a space in her house, in which she set up a stationary store and bookstore, which is now the largest and busiest in the city. She and her children work there every day. In the months when there is more work due to classes starting, her sisters and their children come to help her. In this way she gets ahead and so does her family.  She is going to use this loan to purchase all types of school supplies and books with which to stock her business. She has been a part of the communal bank for fourteen years and she likes it because the loans are fast and are a lot of help. Her dream is to continue getting ahead in life.

name: Ishaka
description: Ishaka is 46 years old and lives in the town of Ntungamo in the Mbarara region of Uganda. He is married and has five children, with three of them currently in school. For the past 16 years, Ishaka has been working hard to manage his farming. He owns a banana farm.   To help expand his business, Ishaka has requested a loan of 4,000,000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy more banana seedlings, and will help Ishaka to generate greater profits and improve his family’s well being. Ishaka hopes that in the future, he will be able to expand the business.   Ishaka is a member of BRAC's Small Enterprise Program (SEP). The program primarily serves small entrepreneurs like Ishaka who do not have enough collateral for commercial loans, but have businesses that have grown too large for microloans.

name: Olurunti
description: Olurunti is 30 years old and married with one child. She sells provisions, foodstuffs and drinks in her shop. Olurunti is requesting a loan of N 50,000 to purchase more provisions, foodstuffs and drinks to sell. She says thank you.

name: Julieta
description: Julieta is a 70-year-old widow from Talibon, Bohol, Philippines. She has been engaged in the rice farming business for several years now. She also runs a sari-sari store business selling various goods to the people in her community.  Julieta is requesting a loan to buy fertilizer for the rice and additional items to sell such soda, biscuits, bread and others. Julieta hopes that through this loan, she can augment her income and experience fullness of life.

name: Gularus
description: This is Gularus. She is 26 years old. She lives in the area with her husband and her father-in-law and mother-in-law. Gularus does not yet have children. She is a serious and hospitable woman. Gularus sews women's clothes to order. She has been doing this for two years. Gularus wants to buy a new Yamata brand sewing machine in order to improve her workflow and attract more clients. She does not have enough money to buy the desired sewing machine, and so she has applied for a loan.

name: Ma. Anna
description: Ma. Anna A., 41, a mother of four and the wife of a shoemaker, lives and manages their home business in Balubad Settlement, a poor community in Marikina City, Philippines.   Anna sells and delivers the shoes and sandals made by her husband, who formerly worked as a shoemaker in a prominent shoe manufacturing company in Marikina. They have been in the business for almost fifteen years. Their products are noted for their good quality. They are now distributed through their dealers to private and government offices,  which earns them a minimum P500 per day. In addition, Anna cooks and sells snacks to some small offices in Marikina and San Mateo.  This loan will be used to purchase some raw materials directly from the manufacturers. They can save as much as 70 percent of the total cost of what they would have paid to retailers.  Anna prays that they will be blessed with enough capital that they will be able to produce more shoes and sandals. This will enable them to sell their products in the provinces at prices that are much higher than in Metro Manila.

name: Harriet
description: Harriet is a married woman with one child and lives in Kasese, Uganda. She has been operating a human medicine drug shop for a period of five years in order to look after her child and build a better future for her. Harriet is faced with a challenge of inadequate capital to buy all the necessary medicines that her customers demand. She is requesting money to buy medicines like children's syrups, tablets, and others to sell.Harriet is a hardworking, honest person with an aim of serving the community. She has a dream of expanding her business into a renowned pharmacy in her area.

name: Wiñay Huayna Group
description: Señor Manuel was born in Juliaca, a city in the Department of Puno. He currently lives in the city of Cusco. (Señor Manuel has his hand raised in the photo).  Señor Manuel is married and his two children are the product of his happy relationship. He is a hard-working and responsible father who supports his children. He is a representative of a private company and he recruits people to be included in various market networks. When he recruits people he sells them a nutritional product and in turn these people do the same, recruiting other people to incluD. them in the market networks. He has now been participating in this type of business for three years and it is going very well thanks to the effort he puts into his work.  Señor Manuel is a member of the Communal Bank “Wiñay Huayna” and on this occasion he requires a loan to buy educational material to train and recruit people.  The members of the Communal Bank “Wiñay Huayna” meet every thirty days in the city of Cusco. The Communal Bank is maD. up of hard-working and enterprising people who are constantly looking for opportunities to get ahead and to create a better future for their children through their daily efforts. The majority of the members live in the city of Cusco and the economic activities of the other members are, for example, art sales, cosmetic sales and food sales among other activities.
