Cusco is an area known for its tourism, commercialism, for the traditional festival of Inti Raymi and also because “Machupicchu”, one of the seven wonders of the world, is found there.

name: Budondo Development Group
description: Feibe, aged 56, is now eight years down the road in her farming business in Jinja. The happily married mother of eight says she began this business with savings from her taxi transportation business. She still operates her taxi business although much of her emphasis now is on the farming business.   Feibe also deals in cattle. The cattle sales business which she began recently has started picking up steam and she reckons she will earn a lot from it in the not so distant future. She mostly grows and sells beans, maize and bananas. Recently she has begun selling milk too. This business generates her profits to the tune of 150,000 shillings weekly. With this loan, Feibe says she is going to purchase more cattle to resell.

name: Catalina
description: Catalina is a member of the Santa Rosa de Lima communal bank in the district of Juli, Chucuito province, department of Puno.  She is 52 years old and separated.  She has two grown children.  She did not finish secondary school  Señora Catalina has worked with the Movimiento Manuela Ramos for 10 years.  Her first loan was for 300 new soles, money which added to the capital of her business selling groceries.   She tells us that she is also engaged in the sale of embroidery on flannel.  With this new loan of 1500 new soles she will buy merchandise such as sugar, rice, noodles, milk, and flannel for embroidery.  Catalina also has hatcheries for trout and receives assistance from her children.  Her dream is to improve the hatchery enclosures.  What she likes most about the communal bank is the ease of getting loans, the meetings, and the timeliness of assistance.

name: María De Jesús
description: María, 48, has two children.  She’s married and lives with her family in a community in the municipality of Taulabe, Comayagua Department.  María’s business is selling snacks and food she makes herself.  She sells meat pies, tortillas with string cheese, ‘baleadas’ [thick flour tortillas filled with eggs, beans and other ingredients], soft-drinks, candy, cookies and packaged snacks.    She’s currently asking for a 5,000 Lempira loan to buy soft-drinks, snacks, vegetables, lard, Maseca [corn flour], wheat flour, dairy products and chicken.  She hopes to increase sales and improve her income in order to have a better life with her children.

name: Cecilia Cruz
description: Doña Cecilia Menchú is 28 years old.  She is married and lives with her husband and 2 children.  Both she and her husband are tailors and make traditional women's clothing. They have three looms and 2 employees working for their business.  They have been making traditional garments for 6 years from their home in the Vásquez Village, located in the Totonicapán district in Guatemala. Although customer demand has increased, the current economic situation makes it difficult for them to increase their capital.  For this reason, Doña Cecilia has turned to the Asociación ASDIR to request a loan to purchase raw materials so that she and her husband can increase their weekly sales.  With this loan, they hope to help their children succeed and improve their quality of life.Translated from Spanish by Priya Bapat, Kiva Volunteer

name: Alice
description: Alice J. is currently in the business of selling used clothes and is requesting a loan to purchase used shoes to sell.  Alice is 42 years old and is Married with a husband that is a mechanic. She has 5 children and her children go to school.  With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to open up a super market BRAC's holistic approach to poverty alleviation and empowerment of the poor encompasses a range of core programs in economic and social development, health, education , and human rights and legal services which are delivered through an extensive network of village organizations. BRAC has become one of the world's largest NGOs as a measured by the scale and diversity of its interventions.  In 2007, BRAC started operations in Southern Sudan. The microfinance program, which is targeted towards returning war refugees, has already formed 418 village organizations with more than 14,000 women members.

name: Ofelia
description: Ofelia is 69 years old and married.  She has eleven children.  She earns a living by farming sugarcane in the Philippines.Ofelia is borrowing PHP 14,000 through NWTF in order to buy fertilizers and other farm supplies.Ofelia has been farming sugarcane for fifty years and also earns additional income from fattening pigs and general store businesses.She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream, to save money to expand her business.

name: Gloria
description: Gloria works hard to support her family. She is married and has a buy-and-sell charcoal business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for two years now.  Gloria requested a PHP 12,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more sacks of charcoal to sell.  In the future, Gloria would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Helen
description: Helen is thankful that she was granted a 25,000 PHP loan which she used to purchase various grocery items and products needed in her General Store. Through her earnings she is able to send her children to school and meet their daily living expenses.   She would now like to apply for a 30,000 PHP loan which she will use as part of her working capital to buy more quantities of grocery items like rice, coffee, soda, rice noodles and frozen foods, which she sells at retail. She knows that more items in her store will yield more sales and thus increase her earnings. Her income from her store is a stable source to sustain her family's basic needs and for the education of her children. She is thanking God and you in advance for the financial help that will be given her.   Helen dreams of having a bigger General Store and aims to give her children the best education possible for them to have a better future. Every week, she meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her work and to draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God which she studies.   *All Center for Community Transformation (CCT) community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay Micro-Finance loans.

name: María Carmen
description: María is a very responsible, hard-working person who would like to improve her quality of life and that of her family in order to triumph in life.  María lives with her husband and her five children in Riobamba.    María works along with her husband in agriculture.  They plant artichokes in large quantities in order to sell them in the markets.  Currently due to the poor climate they need to invest in the purchase of fertilizers and fungicides in order to save their harvest.  If they don't the production will be damaged and they will have losses.  They also need to invest in the purchase of seeds and other products like corn and beans in order to increase their income and to pay the harvesters of the artichokes.    María dreams of exporting her products to various countries and improving the quality of life of her children.

name: Irene's Group
description: L. Irene is the leader of her lending group in Mukono. She is 30 years old and married with 2 children aged 9 and 7, both in primary school. She also helps to take care of her parents in the village who are sickly. She is very hard-working and has had a motor vehicle spare parts business in Kisekka market in Kampala for 7 years. She is able to make 200,000/= as weekly profits.   She started up her business in 2002 after being an employee earning a salary, but now she is the one who employs others. She is faced with a lot of competition, high rent costs, taxation, and high transport costs for bringing the spare parts to Kampala from Dubai.   Irene has a plan of starting her own reflector workshop so that she would be able to increase her income; and in future, she plans, together with her husband, to build commercial houses in their home area of Mukono. She needs a loan to be able to buy more spare parts that are currently missing in her shop. The profits will help in catering for her household including the children’s school fees and saving for future developments.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth makes a living by running a tailoring business in the town of Nakuru town. She is 33 years old, a single mother of two children, and has been in her current line of work for four years. She is requesting her first loan from KADET LTD and plans to use it to buy more materials and threads to use in her business. In the future, Elizabeth hopes to open a boutique and beauty shop in her town.

name: Edmond
description: Edmond is a motorcycle mechanic and has been in this business for 4 years. He is 27 years old, married and together with his spouse they have been blessed with one child.   He will use this loan to buy motorcycle spare parts such as nuts and bolts,springs and brakes as well as oil for use in his business. He will use the anticipated profits to expand his business by buying more stock of spare parts.   This is his first loan term from VisionFund Kenya and in future he hopes to expand his business, be successful and provide for his family's needs.

name: Teopister
description: Teopister is 46 years old and has 14 children. She lives in Fort Portal, Uganda. She deals in agriculture growing matooke. She also earns a salary as a teacher. She faces the challenges of limited capital and weather changes.   Teopister is requesting a loan, which which will use to improve her banana plantation by weeding and pruning it. She hopes to educate all her children to higher levels of learning.

name: Navy
description: Kaeiv Navy is married and father of children. He is working at the National Assembly of Cambodia, as a support staff. He applied for a $500 loan for his wife to open a grocery shop. She used to run a similar business but the family sold it a few years ago, when her eldest son got married. Navy’s wife will use the money as a running capital to purchase spices and other goods to be sold in the shop. They are expecting 10,000 Riel ($2.5) profit from the shop every day, which will cover daily expenses for food.This is the first time Navy is borrowing money. “If we are successful, we will increase the size of the business step by step with our future loans”, he said.

name: Dasola
description: Dasola A. is 32 years old and married with 3 children. She sells drinks and pepper soup. She makes a lot of profit from this business. She needs the loan amount of N60,000 to purchase more drinks to sell. She says thanks to all who made this loan possible.

name: Javier
description: Javier, age 59, is a strong man who is single.  He lives with his parents and looks after them in the house that they purchased approximately 48 years ago.  His work consists of providing recycling services.  In a space set aside in his parents’ house, Javier stores bottles and paper that he collects every day off of the streets of the city.  “People are not accustomed to recycling since the streets are full of products that can be used,” he says.  Javier begins his work at night and ends at sunrise.  “At night I collect everything that is left out during the day whether it is at restaurants, hotels, on the streets, or at various public and private institutions.  They give me paper that is thrown out as trash and everything else that can be recycled,” he explains.  When he has a considerable amount of recyclable products stocked up, he sells them to a specialty company that pays by the kilo.    This is his second Kiva loan and he is grateful for the financial support he has received.  In addition, he promises to be punctual with his loan payments.  Javier will invest 1,000 PEN in the cost of transporting these recyclable materials as well as cleaning products for washing the recyclable bottles.

name: Benkadi  2 Group
description: The Benkadi 2 group is composed of married women from the Dangasso village in the San prefecture, in the Segou Region (the fourth administrative region of Mali). The women live in traditional families. They are on the average 44 years old and have nine children.   They cultivate fonio [a local sort of millet], sorrel and  “gombo” [okra]. In order to make their agricultural work profitable, they have decided to join the Soro Yiriwaso credit program two years ago. After having duly repaid previous loans, they are now on their second agricultural loan.   Fanta D. plans to use her loan to purchase a sufficient supply of  fonio seeds, small tools and agricultural inputs, specifically at the big market in San. After the winter season, the harvest is stored for a while as its price increases, before being sold at the big markets of San, Dah, and other nearby markets, retail (often wholesale) for cash to customers mostly coming from big towns. After selling their products, the group members expect to obtain an income from 17,500 to of 40,000 West African francs each, which will be used to pay off the loan interest and cover ongoing family expenses.   Translated from French by Ekaterina Sukhanova, Kiva Volunteer

name: Isaac
description: Isaac B. is 33 years of age, married to Mercy Komen, and they have been blessed with five children Jepkorir 12 years old, Kibet 10 years old, Kipruto eight years old, Jelagat six years old, and Gideon five years old. B. has been in the butchery business for the past two years and he gets a monthly profit of Kshs. 3,000.  Isaac is borrowing a loan of Kshs 15,000, his first loan with KADET LTD. He intends to use Kshs. 9,000 to buy five goats, two sheep for Kshs 3,000, and 10 hens for Kshs 3,000.  In case he get profit from this loan, Isaac anticipates expanding the business and also saving some money for the education of his children. Isaac dreams and hopes to expand his business and have enough income to support his family.

name: Christine's Group
description: Pictured above is Christine, often described as an extremely hardworking individual. She is 29 years old, and as a group leader, she is representing her group of 15 farmers in Teso District, Kenya.  She is married and has four children.Christine is returning this season to work with One Acre Fund again, as this means that she is able to have access to quality training and acquire new farming methods, which is why she decided to join in the first place. Christine says that she is happy to have made that decision, because since she first joined in 2014, she has had more profits from each harvest, which has improved her day-to-day life significantly. Christine will use the profits from this season to buy a cow.The group will use this loan to purchase seeds and fertilizer to plant a total of 9.25 acres. Given that some members of the group will also be purchasing a solar light, with this loan, the group will also receive a total of 3 solar lights.

name: Miriam
description: Miriam is married and has two children.  They live in a rented house with small rooms and a dirt floor.  Miriam resides in the District of Pasankeri in the city of La Paz.  She needs this loan in order to buy supplies, such as peanuts and sugar, so that she can generate income from making candied peanuts.  She spends more than 12 hours selling as a street vendor, which leaves her exposed to many dangers, such as robberies and traffic accidents, since she must walk around in the late hours of the evening.  She also has access to the income of her husband, who works in public transportation.  They both help one another with the expenses such as rent, food, and the education of their oldest daughter who wants to finish high school and enter the university.    Miriam dreams of having a house of her own so that she can provide greater comfort to her family and be able to open a shop so that she can stop traveling through the streets.  This is the fifth time she has worked with Kiva.

name: Hany
description: Hany is 33, married with one son, and is financially responsible for his aging father, who lives with him in the same house. He has a small fattening business that he started to provide a stable source of income for his family. He is requesting a 5,000 EGP loan to buy a head of cattle to expand his business and increase his income for his family.

name: Musa
description: Musa is a 38-year-old farmer from Galadima.  As a Babban Gona member, Musa, is excited about the opportunity to finally have access to credit, good markets and a trained agronomist. Like all Babban Gona members, Musa can earn up to $2000/ha this season from growing maize, more than three times the Nigerian farmer’s average annual income. The average Babban Gona farmer yields 30 bags/hectare; double the national average of 14. However, Musa is ambitious and is hoping that as a result of this loan, he will be able to access quality inputs such as fertilizer and improved seeds that will  result in a yield of 35 bags of maize per hectare this season.  Musa is hopeful about what the future holds; he  hopes that with the increased income as a result of a high yield, he will finally be able to afford to educate his children: Salim and  Yamima. Musa’s dreams do not end there: “ultimately, I want to ensure my children are educated and have professional jobs”, he expressed.

name: Mutasem
description: Mutasem is a 24-year-old single man from the city of Ramallah. He is an engineering student at the university who wants to earn the BA degree and find a job in the future to support his family. His father works as a driver, earning a low and unstable income that barely covers all of the family's needs.   Mutasem requested a USD loan from FATEN to help him pay his university fees for the last semester. This loan will enable him to register and pay part of the urgent expenses he has.

name: Maria Berenice
description: Berenice is a 53-year old woman who makes her living as a third-party dress maker.  She has generated employment for one person and is just about to generate another job.  However, it depends on getting a loan, with which Berenice will purchase a motorbike to use for delivering her merchandise.   Berenice relies solely on her business to support her family.  She herself started her business, and she is very motivated by the opportunity for growth that is being presented to her.   An opportunity such as this will mean growth and strength for Berenice.

name: Nasreen
description: Nasreen is a 47-year-old woman and the mother of a son. She lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. Her husband has been running a food stall where he sells different types of edible items such as samosa, vegetable rolls, chicken tikka, Kabab paratha, etc. He is the one responsible to feed the entire family and manage the household.  Nasreen's husband needs to purchase different types of edible and other items for his business so that he can increase the size of his business, improve his sales growth, and earn maximum profit. But due to his unfavorable financial position, he is not able to purchase these items for his business. Therefore Nasreen has applied for a Kiva loan from its field partner BRAC Pakistan so that she can help her husband to purchase the above items for his business. She is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Liza
description: Liza is grateful for the financial assistance granted to her because she was able to purchase more quantities and varieties of grocery items and products needed in her business. Her earnings were a big help for her child’s education and in their personal, household, and business expenditures.  She would like to apply for another 20,000 PHP loan for her to buy groceries, toiletries, beverages and other products to add to her inventory. The more items displayed at the store, the better. More items to sell will result in better profit. Her profits from business will definitely help sustain her family’s daily needs and child’s education expense. She looks forward to this financial increase with gladness and thankfulness in her heart.  Liza dreams that her business will continue to expand to help her provide for their needs. In the future, she dreams to have a peaceful and sufficient living with her family. She meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her life and business every week and where she can also draw strength and inspiration from the fellowship and the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay micro-finance loans.

name: Ibrahim
description: Ibrahim used his previous loan to buy stocks of clothes to sell. He started his clothing sales business with a hope of earning an income. Ibrahim is also involved in farming, growing bananas and maize for commercial purposes. He faces challenges of competition that hinder expansion of his business. Ibrahim needs a loan to buy more clothes to sell.

name: Mariyam
description: Mariyam  is a 27-year-old married woman and has enjoyed the work of making Parandas for so many years. A paranda is considered to be a traditional hair accessory in a country like Pakistan. Women use it for a traditional look on special occasions, like Eid (a holiday) and weddings. Mariyam makes beautiful Parandas, especially for bridal hairstyles. She initiated her business with the support of Kashf Foundation. Taking a loan from Kashf helped her account for expenses she thought she could never bear. She is striving hard to meet her family's expenditures. She is responsible for providing them with a good environment, with good food, clothing, and education. She needs a loan of 40,000 PKR to buy raw materials, including colorful thread, beads, mirrors, and pearls for embellishment. This would help in attracting more customers. She desires to utilize the earned revenue for building a separate room for her children

name: Ever Benjamín
description: Ever is a 23 year old man. He studied computer science and at this time is single and has no children. He lives with his father and three brothers. His mother passed away, and he has no dependents.   Ever works as a facilitator or instructor for computer classes in a course given by the community's town hall. Another source of income is growing basic grains. Previously, he worked in a Chinese restaurant. The place where he works now is 2 km and a half from his house and he gets there on foot. His work schedule is variable and sometimes he works in the afternoon and other times in the morning.   He needs the loan to buy a dairy cow, since sometimes his father's crop stubble goes to waste, buy with a cow it can used for feed.    His dream is to teach classes at the elementary or middle school level. To do that he has to become a government employee. He also dreams of having a cyber cafe to offer a good service to the education community.

name: Caroline
description: Caroline is 35 years old and lives in Nakuru. She is married and has one child, who is six years old and is in school.  Caroline has a retail shop that she has been running for the past three years. She has applied for her second loan from KADET LTD to enable her to buy grocery items to add to her inventory, like rice, cooking oil, and soft drinks.  She hopes to own a wholesale shop, in the near future.

name: Sakina
description: Sakina is a 52-year-old, married woman. She has three children. Sakina’s son (also shown in the photo) has been running a ‘Dahi Bhallay’ stall from many years, near their house, with Sakina’s assistance. ‘Dahi Bhallay’ is a special food of the subcontinent, prepared by soaking deep-fried balls, made from ground lentils, in thick yogurt.   Sakina is a very hard-working woman. Her husband also helps by taking orders from customers and handling delivery of food to respective places.   In order to meet the daily expenses of the business, Sakina has requested a loan of PKR 40,000 to buy from the market at lower rates, stocks of yogurt and ‘bhallay' (deep-fried balls), along with spices, vegetables, and packs of oil. In this way, Sakina would be able to increase her sales. Sakina wishes to utilize her earned profit on her family’s well-being.

name: Maryamu
description: Maryamu is a maize farmer from Gambo village. As a Babban Gona member, Maryamu is excited to have access to a trained agronomist and superior inputs that will give her the chance to yield up to 8 metric tonnes of maize per hectare of land, which is 5.5 times higher than yield of the average Nigerian farmer. Before joining Babban Gona, Maryamu had to sell her maize at harvest, when the price is at its lowest, to meet her immediate cash needs for items such as food and clothing. As a Babban Gona member, Maryamu can store the maize she harvests and sell it later in the season when she can earn up to 37% more than the market price at harvest.Thanks to support from Babban Gona’s marketing services, Maryamu no longer feels the pressure to sell her maize at low harvest prices. With the potential to earn up to $2,000 per hectare of land, Maryamu hopes to realize better yields and plans to use her additional income to acquire more land to put into the Babban Gona program.

name: Ike
description: Ike is 44 years old and a resident of Dulag, Leyte. He sells food supplements such as vitamins and minerals that are essential for health. He has been operating this business for many years.  Ike requested a loan, which he will use to buy more supplies of food supplements such as vitamin C and medicines. He can now cater to the needs of his customers as well as improve his earnings. He provides a nutritious diet which is essential in his day-to-day livelihood activities. In the future, Ike hopes that with an additional capital he can continue making a better profit from his business.

name: Philomina
description: Philomina sells eggs and sarongs. She is 41 years old, married, and has four children. She hopes for a loan of NGN 80,000 to purchase more eggs and sarongs to sell. She is thankful for Kiva lenders.

name: Thieu
description: Mrs Thieu is a hardworking 43-year-old woman. She is married with three children. She has been running her own cattle farming business for the past 20 years. She is responsible for fulfilling the needs of her entire family and for managing the household.   She wants to purchase these animals for her business, but cannot due to financial constraints. Therefore, she has requested a Kiva loan from its field partner QB WDF.

name: Susan Yatta's Group
description: Meet teachers of The SLC (Sierra Leone Church) Primary School, situated in Kenema, a city in eastern Sierra Leone. SLC Primary School was built in 1909 by the Anglican Mission. SLC primary school is staffed with 42 teachers and has an enrollment of 1,025 pupils.  This is the first loan that teachers of SLC primary school are accessing from SMT/Kiva lenders.  With the help of this loan, these teachers’ standard of living will improve.   Susan is the leader of this group of teachers. She is age thirty-one. Susan was born in N’Jalah, a village near Bo city. She is married and has two children – one in primary school and one in secondary school. Susan has been a teacher for five years now. Susan will use her share of this loan for developmental purposes; she will use it to pay school fees for her children.   (Attached to this photo is a snapshot of Sylvester, a borrower who was not able to be present for the group photo).

name: Jeannethe
description: Jeannethe, 45, provides garaging services.   She’s been in this business more than 20 years.  She is a very hard working person who enjoys her work.  She is very dynamic because she has to be watchful of the cars that arrive to request this service.  The reason behind the loan request is to make some improvements to the booths the cars are located in to be able to offer more space.  She dreams with improving service every day.  She is a very responsible persona and she needs to make these improvements to obtain profits.

name: Jenny
description: Jenny C., 29, a resident of Commonwealth, Quezon City, Philippines, is married to Cubreguito C., a vendor; she is the mother of two children, one of whom is in elementary school, while the youngest is toddling around at home. By the grace of God, Jenny has managed to support her older child's schooling. At this time, she is working hard to be able to send her children all the way through college, a dream of most Filipino parents like Jenny who herself has been a college undergraduate and believes that a college diploma is the best legacy parents can give to their children.  Jenny operates a variety store. In the Philippines, a variety store is basically a small convenience store which retails groceries, toiletries and beverages piecemeal to the local neighborhood. It is the place to go for to buy one sachet of shampoo, a Php5-worth of cooking oil, or an egg.   Her store is located adjacent to her house, and her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community.  She earns a minimum of Php300 in sales every day.  To help her continue operation of her business, Jenny is requesting a Php21,000 loan to buy more quantities of products including groceries, toiletries and beverages to expand her product inventory. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands her business.    Jenny dreams of being able to give her all her children a good and high quality education through all of her hard work on her business. She dreams of becoming a successful businesswoman someday, and faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her work every week.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners who gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Bin
description: The picture is Mrs. Bin R., 40, who lives in Phnom Penh City and is the mother of five children who are single. One of her sons works as a local building worker.   To make a daily income, she usually buys raw ingredients from the local market to make cakes and sells them to the villagers who live near her house. Beside this, she always has cultivated rice for income. She is married to Mr. Sokhon, age 41, who makes a a living by fishing, and who works with her in the farming business.   The mature rice season is approaching, The family is lacking the money to hire a harvester to harvest their rice crop. Therefore, R. has decided to ask for US$400 to be able to make that possible.

name: Férmina
description: Sra. Férmina has four school age children.  She has a small food pantry along Km. 7 in Ciudad Nueva.  Her sales continue to increase, allowing her to generate a good income.  With the help of her husband and her entire family, she has been able to move forward with great sacrifice and effort.  Today she is a successful businesswoman with many loyal customers because of her kindness.  Férmina has demonstrated that she is a responsible and honest person with her commitments, so she has been provided with the necessary support.  She is requesting this loan in order to buy merchandise for her food pantry such as flour, noodles, rice, meat, baked goods, and canned goods.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth S. is from the village of Iligan City. She is 52 years old. Elizabeth is married and has four adult children. To make a living, Elizabeth owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) retail shop. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling both food and daily use products in the local community. Elizabeth has been engaged in her business for more than four years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Elizabeth joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities. Elizabeth has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5,000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to purchase additional products to sell. Elizabeth is requesting a new loan of 8,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the second loan taken out by Elizabeth from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and reaches out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Carmen
description: Carmen is a member of the La Fortaleza community bank.  Carmen, 33, is in a common law marriage and has a 3 year old son.  She could only go to elementary school because her grandparents, who were raising her, died.  She had to work starting at 8 years old.    For six consecutive years she was recycling plastics, paper, and everything she could find by hand.  Then she got her money together, and with the help of her husband, she rented a stall in the market. She started selling groceries.    Carmen needs a loan of 1000 PEN to buy rice, sugar and Chinese noodles.  Since she has been with Finca, her business has developed.  She started with a small grocery store, and now she has another business.  She rented another stall and started selling spices.  She learned to have confidence in herself and to be firm in her decisions.    Carmen’s dream is to have her own house. Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Jameela
description: Jameela is a married woman who has 3 children. She used to work in a tailoring and sewing place, but since she's talented and wants to rely on herself more, she decided to work from home. There was a lot of attention to her handmade clothes from her neighbors, so she decided to take a loan to buy better fabrics, buttons, and sewing tools. These will help her improve her productivity and make a better income to provide her family with better living standards.

name: Rosa Edith
description: Rosa lives in the warm and delightful city of Pucallpa.  In the city, which is located in the Peruvian jungle, you can see impressive flora and fauna. Its scenery is so beautiful that it makes one disconnect from the noise of the city and appreciate the beauty of nature.  It has a varied cuisine, and it is well known for the amiability of its people.  In her free time Rosa really likes to go for walks with her daughter.  Together with her daughter, she also likes to eat one of their favorite dishes, the delicious “ceviche [raw fish marinated in lime or lemon juice].  With a great deal of effort, and most of all, dedication, Rosa works at a school as an elementary school teacher.  The school is in an area a bit outside of the city.  She works around nine hours a day.  She also has a small business of renting rooms, which gives her another income to use for the household expenses.  She believes it is going well for her in her work and her business because she is very amiable with her students and her customers.  Above all, she works with a great desire to get ahead.  Rosa is very grateful to the Kiva lenders.  Thanks to the help they have given her she will be able to make improvements to the rooms that she rents.  She will put down cement floors because the rooms currently have dirt floors, and she will be able to fix up the walls.  This way she will be able to offer better service to the tourists she tends to, and she will be able to improve her income.  This will allow her to continue working and struggling each day to make her biggest dream come true, which is to give her daughter a profession and to be able to have a hotel as a business.

name: Chansrey's Group
description: Chansrey’s group live in a rural village in Kompong Thom province in Cambodia. Chansrey makes a living cultivating rice to support his family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help Chansrey and his co-member to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Savin's Group
description: Savin’s group lives in a rural village in Battambang province in Cambodia. Savin makes a living cultivating rice to support her family. In their village, there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these men and this woman to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses, and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Fagaitaua
description: Fagaitaua F. is 43 and married with 6 children.  She owns a business venture, selling puletasi (Samoan formal wear).  Fagaitaua has 2 years of experience in this business.  Fagaitaua needs a loan of WST $1250 to purchase additional fabrics & materials.  She plans to use the earnings from her business (estimated to be 400 talas or US $167 per week) to pay for her children's tuition fees.  Fagaitaua joined SPBD.  This is her 3rd loan with SPBD.   SPBD's loans are Fagaitaua's only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with traditional banks.  The following social metrics for Fagaitaua F. are provided by SPBD*: Overall Social Metric Score:                1.6 out of 3 Level of Education:                              1.4 out of 3 Level of total Household Income:         1.8 out of 3 Quality of Household Assets:              2.3 out of 3  *SPBD measures the living conditions of each of its borrowers to track her loan progress. The overall social metric score, provided by SPBD, is based upon a number of factors, such as the condition of the house/household assets, health, education, income level, and family reputation. A higher number represents a higher score. For example, a ""3 out of 3"" on education would mean that the borrower has graduated from university; a ""2 out of 3"" = secondary/high-school, and a ""1 out of 3"" would mean that the borrower is uneducated.  For more information on this score, please see SPBD's partner page at: http://partners.kiva.org/about/aboutPartner?id=15  About SPBD In 2000, Greg Casagrande founded SPBD and since then, it has expanded from the main island of Upolu in Samoa to Savaii, as well as Tonga. SPBD's philosophy of lending is based upon the Grameen Bank lending method.  Please join SPBD's lending team on KIVA to receive on-the-spot updates on SPBD: http://www.kiva.org/community/viewTeam?team_id=8375

name: Maxwell
description: Maxwell lives in Hoima Uganda. He is aged 23 married with one child aged 2. He owns a retail shop and raises extra income through brick laying. He began his business fout of necessity. Lack of enough capital and too much competition are his major challenges. He is a hard working and loving person who will use the loan to buy more soap, sugar, matchboxes for resale and to grow his brick laying side business.

name: Nyanzi Chriatine Group
description: Christine is 24 years of age, and she is married with 2 children, ages 3 and 1 year. Her children are still too young to go to school. Ms. N. rents a single room with neither electricity nor water  and they are four people staying in that room. She has one meal a day and the greatest expense for her in a month are food and medications for her family.  Christine sells charcoal to earn a living for herself ,  and she sells from home; she works six days a week. She receives about 20 customers a day and they can be men, women, and children. She sells on a retail basis. She has done this type business for three years now.  The main challenge she faces in her business is that at  times they supply her with poor quality charcoal and her customers complain. The rainy season also affects the supply of charcoal since most suppliers don’t go to villages to collect the charcoal when it rains a lot because of the poor roads.  Christine has worked with MCDT for 2 years now and the reason why she chose to work with MCDT is because it serves the poor. She wants to use the loan she receives from MCDT to increase her stock. She also would like to expand on her business and be able to sell on a wholesale basis.

name: Dorcas
description: Dorcas is a single woman. She has three children with ages ranging from 6 years to 17 years. She describes herself as ambitious.   She operates a tailoring shop where she makes clothes. She has been involved in this business for 17 years. Her business is located in a busy area and her primary customers are locals. She describes her biggest business challenge as the high cost of products.   She will use the KES 20,000 loan to buy more stock of tailoring materials. This is her second loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: Juana Dominga
description: Juana is a member of the Communal Bank “Palccaraqui”, which is part of Asociación Arariwa.  She is 45 years old, married, and has a son named Jhon William.  He is 23 years old and works as a teacher.  Juana lives in the Province of Urubamba, Department of Cusco.  The city of Urubamba is 1½ hours away from the city of Cusco.  Juana sells vegetables.  Her vegetables are shipped daily to the city of Puerto Maldonado by Olimpia, one of her customers.  Juana has been selling vegetables for four years and has done very well as a result of her hard work.    She needs a loan so that she can begin planting crops on her farm.  Juana will acquire seeds for growing lettuce, snap peas, sunflowers, corn, and other vegetables.  She is a hardworking mother and entrepreneur who wants her family to get ahead.  This loan of 2500 soles will allow the work on her farm to continue.  Juan is grateful for this opportunity and promises to complete her payments on time.Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Pamela Ivett
description: Pamela and her husband have decided to give the best to their two children, who are of school age, and one of the most important things is their home. Pamela works selling cosmetics and clothes and her husband has his own taxi.   She is asking for a loan to buy construction materials like iron, cement, sand, and bricks because, little by little, she has built her own house.  She is grateful for the help and for the trust Kiva and Afodenic have placed in her.

name: Cissy
description: Cissy's group is made up of hard working women. Cissy is 22 years old and lives in the town of Luwero in the Luwero region of Uganda. She is single and has two children; one of them is currently in school. For the past 3 years, Cissy has been working hard to manage her farming business, which deals in maize and beans.   To help expand her business, Cissy has requested a loan of 450000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to get a watering can for her farming business, and will help Cissy to generate greater profits and expand in farming. Cissy hopes that in the future she will be able to widen the farm for other produce.   Cissy is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities, and a forum for life-skills training.

name: Chum
description: A medium-size wooden house and a grocery store in Pursat Province belong to Mrs. Chum M.. She is 51, a widow, and currently lives with her one daughter who is a grocery seller. She also helps her daughter sell groceries and is the good grandmother who spends time caring for her two grandchildren; they are still young and enrolled in school. The whole family's expenses are met by M.'s daughter. M. has requested a loan of $800 for her daughter to buy more groceries to sell and to increase the size of the grocery store. (Mrs. M.'s daughter is pictured because she was not available.)

name: Nozigul
description: Meet Nozigul, an 18-year-old resident of the Sarband region, and a kind and responsible girl. Nozigul sews women's clothes. She finds it very convenient to work from home, as this activity allows her to take care of the household at the same time. From the earnings that she gets from sewing, she has already saved some money to renovate her house, but she still doesn't have enough. She is therefore taking a loan which will help her to buy the necessary building materials to repair her house. This loan will help Nozigul to achieve her goals, as she really needs to renovate her house. Nozigul relies on you and your support.

name: Nasira
description: Nasira N. lives in Kochkor, a village located four hours from the country’s capital. She has decided to take a loan to purchase two cows. Currently, she breeds and sells cattle after fattening them. Her husband helps. In her free time, and also to earn additional money, Nasira sews Kyrgyz national caps for men. Her husband is retired. She is 61 years old and has three children all of whom are married and live separately.  She has been breeding livestock for four years and makes 8000 soms each month. She would like to increase the number of cattle that she owns in order to earn more for her family.  Mol Bulak Finance is particularly proud of this loan since it is the organization's first individual loan! Please help us support Nasira!   --- Where Did This Loan Come From? ---   This loan is brought to you by Mol Bulak Finance (MBF), a young, ambitious and socially-focused Microfinance Institution in Kyrgyzstan.   MBF is strongly committed to the principles of sustainable development and upholds the triple bottom line – People (building human capital and taking care of its customers as well as society), Planet (keeping environmentally friendly) and Profit (earning revenue to expand autonomously). MBF is the only Microfinance Institute in Kyrgyzstan that delivers its services to customers 365 days a year. To learn more about MBF and view a Video presentation about the organization, please visit: http://www.kiva.org/about/aboutPartner?id=135   If you would like to support and learn more about Kyrgyzstan and microfinance in Central Asia, please join our Lending Team - Supporters of Kyrgyzstan – Mol Bulak Finance at http://kiva.org/team/kyrgyzstan. Members will get special updates and news from Kiva Fellows in Kyrgyzstan and from the MBF staff.

name: Juanita
description: Juanita is 68 years old and widowed with three children.  She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Juanita has a buy and sell dry goods business in the Philippines.  Juanita requested a PHP 20,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy additional stocks of dry goods like slippers, blouses, t-shirts, etc. to sell.  Juanita has been in this business for 11 years.  Juanita would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Hassane
description: Hassane is a 25-year-old married man, who has been working as an electrician since 2005.  He is talented in his business and most of his customers recommend him to others.  Hassane is a hardworking man, he has developed himself and seeks to improve his business as much as he can.  Most of Hassane's customers are constructors in addition to his neighbours, relatives and friends.  Hassane is applying for a loan from Kiva partner Al Majmoua, in order to buy the necessary products and tools for a new project he is going to work on.  Hassane is experienced in Al Majmoua loans, with a previously requested loan, which reflected positively on both his social and financial situations.  Hassane hopes to expand his business in the future through opening a special electric maintenance company.

name: Rovelyn
description: Rovelyn is 35 years old and has four children. She is married and has four children who are in school.  Rovelyn is in the agricultural business, raising pigs in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy feed and other supplies to raise her pigs.  Rovelyn has been raising pigs for two years now, and has borrowed three times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.  In the future, she would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Spartak
description: Spartak is 67 years old and he lives with his wife in Kapan city of Syunik region. He has higher pedagogical education and now he works of his specialty at the city’s college. Spartak has three daughters; two of them are already married and they live with their families and their smallest daughter is in Russian Federation now and works there. Spartak has very nice vineyard with the perfect harvest and having all the best sorts of grapes (kishmish, muskat and areni), which are used in wine making. He manages to have good profit of its sales. He sells all his grape harvest to the factories that produce wine and profitably sells it. As he says he likes his nice vineyard and manages all the work in it with great pleasure. Now this loan of 700.000 Armenian drams he asks as he must buy a new water tank, also new watering pipes, some seedlings and young grape trees so that doing all these works now he will surely have good harvest next year.

name: Leonilda
description: Leonilda, 52, lives with her husband in her own house, made of modest materials.  She has no children in her care.  Leonilda's from the area.  She lives in the rural part of the district and has water and electricity.  Her community is located in the Colasay district of the province of Jaén in the Cajamarca region in the northern highlands of Peru.  The people work mainly in agriculture, ranching, and commerce.  Leonilda's job is selling staple products to her own customers in the area.  She also raises small animals.  She's going to use the loan to buy merchandise to better stock her store.  This will generate more income for her and she'll be able to improve her quality of life.  There's no greater competition in this business in the area, and she gets the best prices.

name: Bianeth Del Socorro
description: Bianeth, 31, is single and has been employed as a supervisor at URACCAN University for the last 9 years; she has a two-and-a-half year old daughter.   Her life partner works as a bricklayer and contributes to family expenses.  She is requesting her 4th loan to buy building materials to build a bedroom for her baby so that the home will be more comfortable.  This is her 2nd loan with Kiva funds and she states that she is very grateful for the support provided.  Her dream is to gradually improve her living conditions and to continue to study to become an experienced professional. Translated from Spanish by Michael Bujazan, Kiva Volunteer

name: 06.09.04 Đông Vệ Group
description: Ngần is applying for a loan to purchase vegetables to resell. She operates a food stall/restaurant selling vegetables.  Ngần is 63 years old and she is married with two children.. Ngần is the group leader of the 06.09.04-Đông Vệ solidarity group, which consists of four members.  Ngần lives with two dependents in Thanh Hoa city, an urban town in Thanh Hoa province.  This is Ngần's first loan with Thanh Hoa Fund of Poor Women. Ngần has been involved in this business for more than 10 years. The main hardship that Ngần faces in her business is the lack of capital.  With her business profit, Ngần hopes for her business to do well, to remodel her house and for her family to be healthy and happy.

name: Salvacion
description: Salvacion A. is a 49-year-old married woman who supports her family with peanut processing (salted, coated, boiled peanuts) and a vegetable garden. She lives in Brgy Asia Hinoba-an, Negros Occidental with her husband, Artemio, and their three children who are between 24 and 29 years old.  She has been a member of NWTF-Project Dungganon since 2004 and has improved her living conditions with the help of her loans from NWTF and through her own efforts. By working hard in her peanut processing (salted, coated, boiled peanuts) and vegetable garden businesses, she is gradually making her family more economically stable. She now earns an average monthly income of PHP 5,000.  Salvacion is now borrowing PHP 15,000 so that she can expand her peanut processing (salted, coated, boiled peanuts) and vegetable garden. This will be her eighth loan from NWTF-Project Dungganon. Her previous loan of PHP 15,000, which she paid off within its term, was just another step in her journey towards economic freedom. Salvacion aspires to elevate her family’s living conditions and ensure their future wellbeing by following the “Dungganon” way.    About NWTF: In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means Honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress out of earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem that is bestowed to a member of a community who has earned the respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work.

name: Saáde
description: Saáde is a Babban Gona maize farmer. Thanks to Babban Gona’s support, Saáde is thankful that days of poor yields are long gone. As a Babban Gona member, she has the opportunity to achieve yields of up to 8 metric tons of maize per hectare of land, 5.5 times the yield of the average Nigerian farmer. Traditionally, Saáde would have had to sell her maize for low prices at harvest to meet her immediate cash needs such as food and clothing. With Babban Gona’s support, Saáde will store the maize she harvests and delay it’s sale until a date later in the season when she can obtain a significantly higher price for her maize at a premium up to 37% more than the harvest price. With the opportunity to earn up to $2,000 per Hectare of land, Saáde now has the opportunity to realize her dream to grow her agriculture business for herself and family members and would like to use this additional income to acquire more land to put into the Babban Gona program.

name: Reun
description: Reun R., 58, lives in Siem Reap Province, Cambodia. She earns a living by selling grocery inventory from her house, selling items such as cooked food and sweets for children. She is experienced and has been in this business for a long time. Reun R. is married andcurrently takes care of two school-aged children, with three other children already married. Her husband sells water to the neighbors for a profit. In the past, Reun R. always hired a taxi at a considerable cost for traveling purposes. She right now hopes to reduce those expenses by using a Kiva loan to purchase a motorcycle for her and her family's commuting needs.

name: Uldash
description: Uldash M. resides in the town of Yavan, where he lives with his family.  He is 66 years old and has six grown children who help their father.  Together, they farm a rented parcel of land, which they sow with wheat.  They want to use the loan to purchase seed and fertilizer.  The harvest will be sold in the market for a reasonable profit.  Uldash will be able to repay the loan within 12 months. Translated from Russian by Joyce ., Kiva Volunteer

name: Jessica
description: Jessica belongs to the Banco del Desarrollo communal bank, located in the Wanchaq district which is part of the province and department of Cusco.  Jessica is 24 years old and single.  She alternates her daily activities with her business buying and selling clothing.  She sells pants, shirts, and t-shirts for men and women.  She has a store where she works from 9am to 7pm, but she wants to expand her store.  Jessica is requesting the loan to purchase merchandise for her clothing store.  She is grateful to everyone who is making this dream possible and promises to make her payments in the stipulated time frame.

name: Aminata
description: Aminata is a married woman, 38 years old and the mother of five children. She lives with her ​​children and her husband in the North Hérémakono district of Bougouni.  Having quit school at an early age mainly due to her parent's poverty, she decided to undertake income-generating activities such as the purchase and sale of pagnes (colorful West-African fabric) and clothing. With over 8 years' experience, she is highly sought after and appreciated in Bougouni.  Having successfully repaid her four previous loans, this is her fifth which will be used to buy 10 sets of men's clothing and 10 pagnes. She resupplies in Bamako (capital of the Republic of Mali). Her goods are sold from her home and in various districts of Bougouni.  She intends to achieve monthly profits of 50,000 FCFA, which will serve to help her parents, assist her husband with family expenses, pay interest on the loan and expand her business.

name: Regina
description: Regina is a single woman. She has two children. She describes herself to be ambitious. She operates a rental houses business where she owns houses for rent. She has been involved in this business for 15 years. Her business is located in an area with potential and her primary customers are of all types. She describes her biggest business challenge to be inadequate finances. She will use the Kes 20,000 loan to buy materials to renovate the rental houses. Her business goal is to be financially stable within five years. She hopes that in the future, she will own more rental houses. This is her first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: En's Group
description: En, 31, lives in Battambang province and she is a married mother of three children. Growing rice has been the main source of her family’s income for 10 years and working for other's farms for a fee is an additional income for her. She could earn about 31,000 KHR per day. Now she is leading the group of two to apply for this third loan with her portion used to buy fertilizer and seeds and to pay for plowing fees. She hopes that she will have enough ability to expand her current business.

name: Nemia
description: Nemia A. is from the town of Sto. Niño. She is 32 years old. Nemia is married and has four school-aged children. To make a living, Nemia owns & operates a business planting and harvesting rice for sale. Nemia is working hard because she wants to give the best to her family. She says she wants to be able to sustain her children's education.  Nemia joined CEVI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Nemia has successfully repaid a previous loan from CEVI. Nemia is requesting a new loan of 10,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase fertilizers, seeds and other farm inputs. This loan will be the third loan taken out by Nemia from CEVI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the family's income.   About CEVI:  Community Economic Ventures, Inc (CEVI) has increased its portfolio significantly over the recent years.  Based in Bohol, they have numerous branches throughout the Philippines.  In 2009, CEVI was awarded a CGAP silver award for transparency in social performance monitoring.  CEVI not only provides credit for its clients but additionally savings, insurance, and training which are provided through regular cluster group meetings.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Minh's Group
description: Mrs. Minh is 62 years old and she is married with two children. She has worked in agriculture, raising pigs for eight years. Minh lives in Hau Loc district, a rural town in Thanh Hoa province. Her family is a low-income household in the village. In addition, the market need is low in this region. The main hardship that Minh faces is a lack of capital.  She is requesting a loan to purchase baby pigs to raise and sell in the future.In 2013, Minh joined Thanh Hoa Microfinance Institution to improve her business. Minh has successfully repaid three loans from Thanh Hoa Microfinance Institution.She is the group leader of Minh's Group, which consists of five members. With her business profit, Minh hopes to build a new house, for her children to find good jobs, and for her family to be healthy and happy.

name: Aidah
description: Aidah is 48 years old and lives in the town of Mbale in the Mbale region of Uganda. She is single and has 3 children who are all currently in school. For the past 12 years, Aidah has been working hard to manage her small business, where she sells clothes.   To help expand her business, Aidah has requested a loan of 2,000,000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy more clothes for resale, and will help Aidah to generate greater profits and expand her business. Aidah hopes that in the future she will be able to increase her profits.   Aidah is a member of BRAC's Small Enterprise Program (SEP).  The program primarily serves small entrepreneurs like Aidah who do not have enough collateral for commercial loans, but have businesses that have grown too large for microloans.

name: Rosie
description: As a married parent of three children, Rosie works hard to support her family. She has a fishing business in the Philippines.  Rosie is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF to buy fishing gear and other equipment for her fishing business. She has been sustaining her business activities through her past 21 loans from NWTF and more recently, through Kiva. Rosie hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough money to expand her business.

name: Mohammad
description: Mohammad is a 21-year-old university student, majoring in Historical Resources maintenance and management. He is in his third year. He is seeking to finish his studies and find a job in his field in the future. Because he doesn't have enough money to pay for his upcoming semester fees, he has applied for this loan.

name: Khayri
description: H. Khayri is 53 years old. She is married with two children. Both of her children are married. Khayri has been running her business for more than five years. She started her business to be able to support her husband and family, as her husband’s income was not enough for the family needs. She rents a place at the market.   She sells shoes for kids. First, she purchased goods from suppliers but now her son is traveling to the neighboring country to purchase new goods. Khayri is trying to purchase goods of good quality and the prices acceptable for the clients with an average level of income.   Being a very nice and friendly woman by her nature, Khayri is working hard and trying to serve her clients so they have a positive experience and want to come back. Now Khayri is planning to purchase new summer shoes for kids in order to increase the variety of goods to sell. With this purpose, she requests 950 $ US Dollars for the term of 10 months. Having a positive credit history, Khayri promises to repay the current loan promptly. She has gratitude for everyone supporting her.

name: Naseem
description: Naseem, 36, is a married woman. Five years ago, she started her own business of making sehra. The sehra is a veil of flowers that a groom wears on his face as he approaches his bride. Her product has a seasonal demand, but that doesn’t stop her from conducting business. She learned the art of making sehra from her father and is proud of it. When Naseem told her family that she wanted to sell her sehrras in the market, everyone supported her because they had seen her father make money out of it. She has 3 children and is happy to be sending the eldest son to school and her younger daughter to an embroidery stitching center. She has gradually improved her business and has requested a loan of 15,000 PKR to purchase material such as cardboard, glittering paper, ribbons and artificial flowers. She intends to use the earned profits to fund her children’s education.

name: Marcela
description: Marcela owns a shop, where every afternoon from 6.00pm onwards she sells fried chicken and 'salchipapas', a type of fast food that consists of thinly sliced pan-fried beef hot dogs or sausage and french fries, mixed together and eaten with different sauces. Her husband works as a taxi driver. These two activities make up their principal income sources, with which they cover the costs of raising their three children. The family lives in a rented house in the Villa Mariscal Sucre Rio Seco zone of the city of El Alto.  The loan will be used to buy basic food supplies in bulk, including potatoes, chicken and rice. In this way she can reduce her expenses and try to increase her income.  This is her third loan with Impro. Thanks to her good repayment history with the institution she is able to apply for a new loan. Translated from Spanish by Sally Bolton, Kiva Volunteer

name: Oulimata
description: Ms. Oulimata G. is a married woman who is 42 years old.   She lives in the Grand Thiès district and has five children in her care.   She has been doing commerce for six years that involves selling cloth, shoes, and cosmetics in the marketplace.  Her business is doing well, and she decided to join the micro-finance institution IMCEC.  She is on her first loan, which she wants to use to bolster her business.  She hopes to realize a profit of 200,00 francs CFA on the whole with these goods (cloth, shoes, and cosmetics).  The profit will be used to make loan interest payments, to help her husband with family expenses, and to invest the rest in her commerce.  Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Karisa
description: Karisa is a 24-year-old single man. He describes himself as honest. Karisa has been operating a water supply business for one year in which he provides water to customers. His business is located in a residential area and his primary customers are individuals. He describes his biggest business challenge as the shortage of water.   Karisa will use the KES 20,000 loan to buy handcarts for supplying water. His business goal is to employ more workers within five years. He hopes that in the future, he will own more handcarts and be a successful family person.

name: Aurelia Guadalupe
description: ln the department of León, Mrs. Aurelia H. prepares food to be sold in her area, and she is visited by many clients.  The reason why she has approched Ceprodel is to request a loan to buy raw material to prepare the dishes which is urgent for her to be able to continue improving her business selling food and keep her clients satisfied.      Translated from Spanish by Lene Struck Christensen, Kiva Volunteer

name: 02060103 _ Tiền Phong _ Hoằng Châu Group
description: Danh is 55 years old and she is married with five children. She lives in Hoang Hoa district, a rural town in Thanh Hoa province.Danh works in agriculture raising poultry. She has been involved in this business for more than 10 years. One of the most critical business difficulties that concerns her is the lack of capital. She is requesting a loan to purchase more baby poultry to raise and sell in the future.In 2014, Danh joined Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women to improve her business. She has successfully repaid two loans from Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women.Danh is the group leader of the 02060103 _ Tiền Phong _ Hoằng Châu solidarity group, which consists of three members. With her business profit, Danh hopes for her family to be healthy and happy, for her children to do well in school, and to make enough money to provide for her kids.

name: María Olivia
description: María, age 54, is very enterprising.  She loves to accumulate successes (on the right in the orange color blouse).  She has a business selling miscellaneous goods in the Jardín municipality in Antioquia.  She has recently opened another in Itagüí in Antioquia.  Fortunately, it is very well-received, thanks to the support of the loan from Interactuar.  She wishes to expand her business even more and generate more jobs like she is currently doing with her employee on the left, in the blue shirt.  However, this requires that she buy an ample inventory of products that she normally sells like school supplies, posters, some candy, DVD’s, and some personal hygiene products.  With these items she will be able to expand her reach, and she will be able to have a higher level of sales because she will always have products available for the customers.  She states that she really enjoys her business activity as a merchant, and she is passionate about it.  Her family life has improved considerably because she has managed to obtain a better quality of life.

name: Jose
description: Jose O. is from the village of Holy Friday. He is 58 years old. Jose is married and has five adult children. To make a living, Jose owns & operates a business planting and harvesting rice for sale. Jose has been engaged in his business for over 30 years and earns approximately 9,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2008, Jose joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve his living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Jose has successfully repaid a previous loan of 34,000 PHP from ASKI. This previous loan was used to purchase fertilizers such as manure. Jose is requesting a new loan of 39,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase fertilizers such as manure. This loan will be the seventh loan taken out by Jose from ASKI. He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand his business.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 38 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: San Vicente Group
description: The group named San Vicente is in its 6th cycle. They joined together with the purpose of being able to help each other and, according to this work, be able to go on improving each of their standards of living.  Lorena is very good at what she does, that is why she works so hard to be able to grow. She makes various foods that she is responsible for preparing and then going out to sell in her neighborhood. She has earned many customers and wants to continue growing until she is able to one day have a large food establishment.   She is requesting this loan to be able to buy supplies, such as meat, greens, seasonings and vegetables, etc., in order to make her food. In that way she will be able to continue with her work. She is thankful for the opportunity received to be able to improve her standard of living.

name: Nelly Margarita
description: Nelly Margarita lives with her daughter in the city of Santo Domingo de los Colorados.  They live in a humble house which they were able to obtain after several years of hard work.  Despite not being able to count on the father of her daughter for help, Nelly has been able to provide for the family.  She works every day at a company where she has been peeling shrimp for several years.  In the afternoons, while her daughter comes home from school, she spends time with her business raising chickens.  She feeds them and keeps the pen clean.  Nelly says that thanks to this business she has been able to give her daughter an education, because the small income she earns at the company does not cover all her expenses.  Nelly is a very humble, hard-working woman.  With the loan she will buy more chickens and balanced feed.  She wants to grow the business since it is becoming more popular.  She is happy and grateful to all the members of the institution who are allowing her to support herself and get ahead.

name: Flor De Libertad 1 & 2 Group
description: Clara is the coordinator of her group Flor de Libertad 1 & 2 (Liberty Flower). She makes her home here in a simple structure with her husband and their six children. They have raised and educated their children by working hard. Her most difficult challenge is to finish a university career. In the meantime, she plans to continue enjoying to read the Bible. She is part of the microfinance program because these loans are for business and she really likes that.  Clara is excited to be taking her first loan with Esperanza. She has had her business for around one month, starting with some savings she had. After she started was when she discovered the Esperanza program. She plans to use this loan to invest in her business by buying clothing like 10 skirts, 10 pairs of pants, blouses and shirts. She will use the profits to save and to study. She is dreaming to have enough income to help her children in everything they need, especially in their studies.  This Esperanza associate's story is representative of her group and of Esperanza's Haitian and Dominican clients, many of whom recently emigrated to the DR from Haiti. Her group is located in Los Arcarrizos, a dusty, industrial area north of the capital where free-trade zones are common. This area, like nearly all impoverished areas of the Dominican Republic, suffers from unreliable running water (none of which is potable) and electricity.

name: Dam
description: Dam was born in 1964. She lives in Ngoc Loi village, Duc Tu commune. She has two children, one of whom was married. She not only grows rice but she also sells fish in the market.   She has this job for three years. Her husband is a carpenter. He works in his wood workshop with Dam's help. They have a monthly income of about 7.000.000 Vietnamdong. Since 2006, she has participated in SEDA and always pays loan punctually. In this loan cycL., she would like to borrow 8.066.000 VND to buy fish to resell.

name: Idalia Del Carmen
description: Idalia del Carmen R. D. D. is 44. She lives with her 3 children, ages 20, 17 and 11. The oldest works and is a great help to Idalia, helping them to have a better life. She has worked very hard for years to get her children ahead, since she is a single mother who has not had any sort of help. Idalia works selling fattened chickens which she raises in her home. She sells them in her stall in the Usulutan Municipal Market; this is the same municipality in which she and her children live. Through this work, she is able to get food and proviD. all the necessary care for her chickens to grow up healthy and fat, so that they are very attractive for her customers. Idalia is requesting a loan through which she will be able to purchase more small chickens, and concentrate to feed them. This way she will be able to have everything necessary to make her business prosper and continue to be profitable for her and her children. Translated from Spanish by Christine Cooper, Kiva Volunteer

name: Abdurahmonkhoja
description: Abdurahmonkhoja lives in Isfara.  He is a 57-year-old married man with two children.  Abdurahmonkhoja has been engaged in the furniture-making business for over 30 years.  He makes furniture at home.  He is taking out a loan to buy furniture boards.

name: San Jose Group
description: The members belong to the “SAN JOSE” communal bank which is located in the  district of Cusco, belonging to the province and department of the same name.Maximiliana is 47 years old. She is single and has two children. The member alternates her daily activities with her business of selling flowers. She sells different kinds of flowers like daisies, lilies, roses, etc. to people who request them from her.. She has done this for a long time and things are going well thanks to the effort she puts into her business every day. She wants to continue to do this in order to continue to support her family.Maximiliana is requesting  a loan to buy roses for her business.  She thanks all those who participate in her dream through this loan and promises to pay her installments on time.The members who appear in the inserted photos asked permission to be late for the meeting due to their work commitments.

name: Sitora
description: Sitora is a young divorced mother.  In spite of the fact that she has a young child, she is working to support herself.   She lives at home with her family, which includes her mother, sister and nephew.  Sistora's father was killed during the civil war.  Sitora also has two brothers who are currently working in Russia.    Sitora's sister is a reseller: she buys perfumes from wholesalers and distributes them to various clients who own retail outlets at markets and shopping centers.  Sitora herself works as an accountant in the public sector and is also studying part-time at the university.  She wants to receive a loan to repair the kitchen, bathroom, and change the doors inside the family's house. She is taking a loan of 3,000 USD to buy some building materials and doors.  She is awaiting your kindness.

name: Rogelio
description: Rogelio is from the village of Taguitic, Kapatagan Lanao Del Norte. He is 49 years old and married. Rogelio grows rice for sale. Rogelio has been engaged in his business for over 12 years and earns approximately 6600 PHP a month.  In 2008, Rogelio joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services. Rogelio has successfully repaid a previous loan of 15000 PHP from GDMPC. The previous loan was used to purchase seeds, seedlings and young crops. Rogelio is requesting a new loan of 15000 PHP to purchase fertilizer such as manure. This will be his third loan from GDMPC. He plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve his family's general living conditions.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has seven branches covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolk and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Evelia
description: Evelia is 58 years old and married with one child. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Evelia has an abaca weaving business in the Philippines. Evelia requested a PHP 13000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase additional raw materials like abaca fiber, etc. for her business.
