She successfully paid back her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her business.  Evelia has been in this business for 42 years. Evelia would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Leidy Lorena
description: Lorena is just 25 years old and lives in the municipality of Medellin. She has a beautiful daughter, who is only 6 years of age and is the biggest present life has given to her. She’s a single mother, so in order to provide better for her daughter, she started a restaurant in 2012.This woman is an excellent cook and she learned to be, thanks to her mother, who taught her everything about this activity. She wants to optimize the operation of her restaurant, so this is the reason why she’s asking for a loan, so she can make some adjustments to the restaurant, so she can take advantage of all the space. She dreams with improving her house. Support this single mother and loan now. If you want to know more about the entrepreneurs and the loans from Interactuar, you can join the Lending Team called: “Friends of Interactuar Colombia”: http://www.kiva.org/team/interactuar_colombia

name: Anyela Andrea
description: Anyela learned how to manufacture shoes when still very young and thanks to this managed to get a good job in a firm where she worked for nine years.  When she got married and had her son who is now 13-years-old she decided to leave her job and start a shoe-making workshop at home so that she could care for her son and improve the quality of life they had at home.    Despite not having much capital, her efforts made it possible for the business to move forward but because of her lack of capital and the great amount of competition in this sector she went bankrupt six years ago and has to look for other alternatives to get ahead.  With enormous effort she’s managed to recuperate the business and continue working to generate household income and seeking now to find a way to continue making progress is looking for financing to buy an industrial sewing machine and raw materials needed for shoe repair.  In this way she will overcome this problem of capital that has prevented her from responding to large customer orders and she will be able to continue making progress with her family and improving the quality of life at home.

name: Lina
description: As a married parent of two children, Lina works hard to support her family.  She has a pig fattening business in the Philippines and also earns additional income from poultry. Lina is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to  buy feed and vitamins for her pigs in her pig fattening business.  She successfully paid back her previous loan and now she has requested an additional loan to further build her business.  Lina has been sustaining her business activities through her past 4 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Louv
description: Y. Louv is a happy mother of a large and busy family. She has five daughters and one son who all live at home. Y. Louv currently sells fruit near a school that is close to their home. She earns about $3.75 from this each day. Y. Louv's husband is a security guard and he earns a salary of $50 per month. Their four oldest daughters all work in a local factory and each earn a salary of $90 per month. Their 15 year old daughter and 7 year old son are both still attending school.   This large bustling family is currently facing transportation problems, and therefore Y. Louv is requesting a loan of $1,000 in order to purchase two motorbikes which cost $500 each. These motorbikes will allow her daughters to safely get to work each day, as well as allow her husband and other two children to get to work and school. Ultimately, this will also allow the family to eliminate the cost of using motorbike taxis.   In the future Y. Louv would like to expand her fruit sales business near the school to include selling water cane. This is popular with the children in the area, and she believes it will help to increase her sales.

name: Aileen
description: As a married parent of six children, four of whom in school, Aileen works hard to support her family.  She has a buy and sell fish business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from porticulture business. Aileen is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to buy additional boxes to sell for her buy and sell fish business.  Aileen has been sustaining her business activities through the past seven loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Cyrille
description: Twenty-five years old and single, B. Cyrille is a computer technician and seller of computer equipment. He’s a young man who really applies himself in his technical field, but who lacks financial means. To re-energize his activities and possess capital would give him greater bargaining leverage with his suppliers, so he’s seeking a loan of $1200 for the purchase and resale of computer equipment and also to open a small word processing and photocopy service. This is a young man with lots of experience and courage who deserves assistance that will help him really go far.  Translated from French by Liana Bianchi, Kiva Volunteer. Jeune célibataire de 25 ans, B. Cyrille est un technicien en informatique et vendeur des consommables informatiques. C’est un jeune homme qui exerce réellement dans son domaine de formation avec une très grande expérience mais les moyens financiers lui font défaut.  Pour redynamiser son activités et avoir un fonds de commerce conséquent lui permettant de disposer d’une force de négociation avec ses fournisseurs, il sollicite un crédit de $1200 pour l’achat et la vente de consommables informatiques et ouvrir à côté un petit service de traitement de texte et de photocopie. C’est un jeune pétri d’expérience et courageux qui mérite d’être propulsé loin.

name: Elna
description: Elna is a 61 year old widowed woman with three children. One of her children is still in school. Elna has a food vending business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for 2 years. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Elna requested a PHP 11000 loan amount through NWTF to buy ingredients like flour, oil, sugar, etc for her food production business. She would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Rebecca
description: Rebecca, a  40-year-old lady from Vihiga County, is a widow with three children. She is a dairy farmer, a business she has done for the past five years with a monthly income of KES. 2,000.   She has now borrowed her second loan of KES. 5,000 from KADET LTD and intends to use this amount to purchase dairy feeds. The profit she earns will be used to buy more dairy cows.    Her dream is to run a successful dairy business and educate her children.

name: Margret
description: Margret is currently in the business of selling soft drinks. She is 40 years old. A widow, she has three children, all of whom go to school. Margret requested a loan to stock more soft drinks to sell. With the extra profits, she hopes to expand her business in the future.

name: Dúo Monte Carmelo Patzicia Group
description: This is the Dúo Monte Carmelo Patzicia Group. Señora Lucia comes from the village of El Caman. These ladies grow and sell green vegetables.  She learned this work with her parents, and now that she is grown, she does the same work.   She has been getting ahead, along with her family, and now that she has been able to purchase her own land, she is requesting a loan to be able to purchase what she needs to continue planting crops, as this is the only way she provides for her children’s needs.   Her desire is to leave property to each one of her children as an inheritance, and she will continue working hard to fulfill it.

name: Saturnina
description: Saturnina lives a simple life with her family in a town of Baybay, Leyte. She is 61 years old and a mother of six children who are already grown up. Her husband has already passed; that is why Saturnina needs to work hard. She does a tailoring business. Her main goal in life is to improve her livelihood to have a better life and means of living. For this, she is asking for a loan to buy tailoring materials like cloth and other sewing materials. Another part of her loan is to buy feed, as Saturnina also does a hog raising business.

name: Rita
description: Mrs. Rita B. is a 38 year-old woman who lives in Tangal with her husband and one son and one daughter. Both her children are now studying.  Mrs. B. opened her tailoring shop 4 years ago. She makes school uniforms for boys and girls. She prefers to make popular dresses like kurta salwar, blouses, ladies’ long dresses, and other such clothes. Before starting her own business she trained In tailoring for six months.  Mrs. B. is requesting a loan of 30000 NPR to buy raw materials for her tailoring work.

name: Derlis
description: Derlis is studying surgical instrumentation, he is in his second year, and he strives to be a good professional in order to be able to help others. He is studying in order to be someone in life, and through his knowledge, to be useful not only to himself but also to his family.He is asking for this loan in order to be able to pay his university fees, and in this manner be able to continue fighting to realize his goals.

name: Gina Isabel
description: Our associate is a member of the “Mi Peru” communal bank, located in the Santiago district of the Cusco department.  Gina is 28 years old and a single mother with two children.  She runs a small clothing business and fills her orders by bringing her merchandise from Lima and Juliaca.  She needs to increase her inventory because she has an order for pants and turtle neck sweaters from an institution.  She is asking for this loan in order to be able to increase her inventory.  She is grateful to those who participate in this dream through this medium and is committed to making her payments on schedule. Translated from Spanish by Hugo Reyes, Kiva Volunteer

name: Evelyn
description: Evelyn is 62 years old and lives in Punta, Panaon, Misamis Occidental. She is married with three children now at their adult age.   Evelyn is engaged in operating a multi-cab for hire business with her husband as the one driving the said unit. She earns approximately PHP 5,000 each month doing this type of business activity. She has requested a loan to be used in purchasing multi-cab spare parts for maintenance.   Evelyn has been a member of PMPC for almost 10 years. In the future, she hopes to purchase an additional multi-cab unit for hire.

name: Tumejidhatiti Group
description: Riziki J. has been a soup seller in the Mikunguni neighborhood of Zanzibar for 1 year.  She currently earns an average monthly profit of $35. Every day she works at her business for 12 hours.  She is requesting her first loan from BRAC Tanzania so that she can buy more items for her business.  She is hoping that through this loan, her profit will increase and she will be able to grow her business and save money for future use.    Riziki J. is 45 years old, married, and has six children: aged 19, 17,16,14, 11 and 9.  She will be sharing this loan with her fellow group members, Riziki S. and Sikudhani. Each woman also has her own small business in Zanzibar.

name: Mariam
description: Mariam is 34 years old, a resident of Kitende, divorced, with three school-going children. She has the sole responsibility of looking after their tuition and other basic needs.  Mariam deals in poultry farming in order to increase her daily income. She started rearing chickens in 2010. Mariam’s major clients are restaurants, hotels, and neighbors in surrounding areas.   She has the challenge of inadequate capital to help her grow her business and even help her meet operational expenses, like treatments, feed, and labor, in addition to fluctuating poultry feed prices, high prices for the chicks from breeders, inflation in the market, and weather changes.  She requested a loan to help her improve her business by acquiring more birds and poultry feed such that she is able to increase her earnings and compete in the market.

name: Nhor's Group
description: Nhor is 55 years old living in Kampong Cham province and she is a mother of five children. Nowadays, she does rice farming as the main source of her family’s income. Meanwhile, she is also working for others for a fee to earn additional income. She has been involved in her job for thirty-seven years. The crops do not grow well, which is the problem for her business.   She has never been with VisionFund before, and now she has decided to take this first Kiva loan. As the leader of four members, she will use her entire loan portion to buy fertilizer, seeds and pesticide for her farmland. She hopes that this loan will help her to get more income to improve her family’s living standard.
town: Kampong Cham province, Ou Reang Ov district

name: Fausto Francisco
description: Professor Fausto is single, 51 years old, and has two daughters. His older daughter is 13 years old, was adopted and has a disability; she is in third grade.  His younger daughter is 12 years old and in her first year of high school.  He leaves home every day at 5:00 A.M. to work in the region of Hato Grande and returns at 2:00 P.M.  He has been working in the rural schools for 21 years.  He is asking for this, his seventh loan, which he will use to build an addition to his small home which measures 3 "varas" wide by 4.5 "varas" deep [about 8 feet by 12 feet].  This addition would allow for a home-based food sales business which his partner would run, thus creating another source of income for the family.  Professor G. is rated an "A" client because he has repaid his six previous loans before their due dates.  He is an example to the rest of his colleagues at "Isaac Deleo" school association in the community of Hato Grande and deserves great respect as a teacher.Translated from Spanish by Laure Kwon, Kiva Volunteer

name: Marivic
description: This is Marivic, 34, a resident of Dasmarinas, Cavite, Philippines. She is a mother of 3 children. She, together with her children, manages their household while operating the business. At this time, she is working hard to continually provide income for their everyday expenses.  Marivic operates a variety store. In the Philippines, a variety store is basically a small convenience store, which sells groceries, toiletries, and beverages to the local neighborhood. It is the place to buy one sachet of shampoo, a Php 5-worth of cooking oil, or an egg. Marivic sells supplies at wholesale prices and by the piece. Her store is located adjacent to her house. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community. She earns a minimum of Php 400 in sales every day.  To help her continue the operations of her business, she is requesting a Php 13,000 loan. She will be utilizing the loan to buy groceries, toiletries, and beverages to expand her product inventory. She expects a boost in her income as she expands her business.   Marivic hopes to be able to expand soon. She also hopes to send her children to school so they can graduate from college. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her work every week. She also draws strength and inspiration from the Word of God that she studies.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans.

name: Saiah
description: Saiah, 45, is single and lives at West Point with her three children who are between the ages of 3 and 12.  She would like to give the best education to her children, but lacks financial support.   For the past ten years she has been selling nails, hammers, door locks, hinges and painting brushes. She is proud of her business because with the profits she can buy more goods and attend to the needs of her children.   She has requested this loan to purchase more nails, hammers, door locks and hinges to improve her sales. Her plan for the future is to educate her children.

name: Anita
description: Anita A. is from the city of Hinagdong Ozamiz City. She is 40 years old. Anita is married and has seven school-aged children. To make a living, Anita owns & operates a business planting & harvesting seaweed for sale. Anita has been engaged in her business for over three years and earns approximately 4,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2009, Anita joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Anita is requesting a new loan of 5000 PHP, which will be used to invest in expanding the business. This loan will be the first loan taken out by Anita from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines. It has four branches and three units, with offices covering the provinces of Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental. Its membership is composed mostly of farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Sros
description: Mr. Sros S. (pictured above) and his wife, Mrs. Sithorn Bang, live in a suburb of Phnom Penh, about 20 kilometers away from the capital. They have three children--two sons and one daughter. Both sons are in school and the daughter is married and lives outside the family home.    Sros has full-time employment, and his wife is a garment factory worker. He is asking for his first loan of US$ 1,000 to pay school fees for his son who is attending university.

name: Agnes
description: Agnes is married with two children who are in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.  Agnes operates a food market business in Mombasa. Agnes requested a 20,000 KES loan amount through Yehu Microfinance to purchase additional ingredients for her food market business. Agnes has been in this business for 10 years.  In the future, she would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Marichu
description: Marichu is 51 years old. She is married and has four children who are all in school.  Marichu is in the agricultural business, raising pigs in the Philippines. Marichu has requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to buy feeds, vaccines and vitamins for her pigs.  Marichu has been raising pigs for 12 years now and has borrowed from NWTF five times in the past to sustain her business.  In the future, Marichu would like to save enough money to be able to send her children to college.

name: Emily
description: Emily is married and has four children. She describes herself to be social. She operates a restaurant, which she has been doing for three years. Her business is located in a good area and her primary customers are locals. She describes her biggest business challenge to be inadequate working capital.   Emily requested her fourth loan from SMEP Microfinance Bank for 120,000 KES, which she will use to buy more stock of ingredients for preparing food. She hopes that in the future she will have a successful business.

name: Dúo Mujeres De San Bartolo Group
description: Dúo Mujeres de San Bartolo  This pair was formed by Maria Llanuaria, 64, who has sold fruit and vegetables at the terminal market and orchids, irises and eggs in bulk at the la cuchilla market for many years.   Maria is applying for a loan to purchase fruit and eggs to stock up her business. Her dream is to continue to make home improvements with the earnings from her business.

name: Benson
description: Benson, age 28, runs a produce business and a motorcycle transport business in Kagadi. He has been engaged in these ventures for the past four years. He started his business with capital received from harvesting and selling his maize and beans. In order to shorten the supply chain, he then decided to buy from other farmers and sell at a profit. He used his previous loan to buy maize and beans to offer for sale.   Inadequate capital is the factor affecting his business. His dreams are to ensure the education of his two children and to own one of the biggest food stores in town.   Benson intends to use this loan to buy maize and beans to offer for sale.

name: Alicia
description: Alicia is 46 years old and married with two children. With one child currently in school, she works very hard to provide for them.  Alicia runs a general store in the Philippines, and requested a PHP 12,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional items like canned goods, biscuits, cooking oil, coffee, noodles, shampoo, fabric conditioners, etc. to sell.  Alicia has been in this business for two years, and sells a variety of items such as canned goods, biscuits, cooking oil, coffee, noodles, shampoo, fabric conditioners, etc.   She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Nieta Group
description: The Nieta group consists of a majority of monogamous women. They are on average 42 years old with four children. They all live in Kanadjiguila in the Mande municipality, which is part of the Kati Circle, and became acquainted through neighborhood ties.  Group members are small retail merchants dealing in firewood, kitchen utensils and food preparations. To increase their stock-in-trade, the group decided to collaborate with Soro Yiriwaso and are in their third group loan cycle.  Mrs. Fatoumata (the woman sitting on the right in the photo) is a reputed seller of firewood. She intends to use her loan to buy two loads of firewood from villages surrounding Bamako. Retail sales are conducted at the market and from her home in Kanadjiguila, to a clientele composed mostly of women.  With this loan Mrs. Fatoumata hopes to attain average monthly profits of 50,000 CFA francs, to be reinvested in her business. Her objective through this relation with Soro Yiriwaso is to cope with possible family needs.

name: Pheap Group
description: Pheap, aged 53, is a widowed mother with three dependent children. She resides in a village in Prey Veng province, Cambodia. Pheap is pictured first on the right. She is a grocer and has been doing her business since 1996. Two of her children are factory workers and the other one is a student. Together, they can make approximately USD 7.5 per day. Pheap is a group leader and would like to request a loan as part of a group of three members. She will use her share to buy additional groceries such as sugar, eggs, candy, soap and shampoo etc. to sell and improve her family’s income. In the future, she is going to enlarge her business, and support her youngest child to finish a bachelor’s degrees.

name: Lorena
description: As a married parent of four children, Lorena works hard to support her family. She has a buy-and-sell rice business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from farming rice. Lorena is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to purchase additional sacks of rice to sell for her buy-and-sell rice business.Lorena has been sustaining her business activities through her past six loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Nzota's Ngeta B Group
description: Nzota is 28 years old and is a married woman with 1 child, aged 6 years old. Nzota is a clothes seller, which she started doing in 2006. Everyday, she works from 7am to 5pm at her business and can earn a monthly profit of about $70 from her sales.  In the past, Nzota has taken out 2 successful loans from BRAC Tanzania to expand her business. She now hopes for a loan to buy more clothes for her business. She will share this loan with her subgroup members Asha and Mejumaa, who have businesses dealing in clothes sales and food vending.

name: Flor De Tuna Ii Group
description: The Flor de Tuna II Communal Bank is entering its first cycle  and will be part of the Alto Lima center. Although they do not have any experience working as a communal bank, they are confident that this cycle will help them get to know each other and strengthen the bonds of friendship. The group consistes of 8 persons, 7 women and 1 man. Each of the members has their own business, among which are: crafts made from rubber, sale of seafood, sale of silver jewelry, sale of shoes by catalog, a bazaar, and a parts store. The Flor de Tuna Communal Bank is governed by a board composed of a president, a treasurer and a recording secretary. The president, Narda, has participated for 15 years in the Flor de Tuna Communal Bank, this is her first cycle with the Flor de Tuna II Communal Bank. Over time she has developed two businesses. First has a bazaar that she opened herself and on the other hand she makes piñatas. The loan she is requesting will help buy supplies for making piñatas: foam, plastoform, glue. She has the support of her brother to help in both businesses. The piñatas are distributed to stores that order them. When asked why she is in Pro Mujer she answers "health", referring to the health service.

name: Liana
description: Liana is an entrepreneur from Kamenka. She sells groceries in the local city market. Liana started her business seven years ago with the help and encouragement of her family. She has gained much needed experience working in this sphere of trade. Liana has about 25,000 Grivnyas (roughly $US3000) in turnover capital. Her monthly profit is about 3,000-5,000 Grivnyas.  Liana is seeking a loan of 12,836 Grivnyas to buy and install plastic rolling doors at her kiosk. She has a hard time opening heavy metal shutters of her small vending facility every morning and decided to substitute them with lighter plastic ones. One of her short-term business plans is to plan her kiosk to store merchandise better and install a good quality door to secure stored inventory.  Liana is very outgoing. She is known for her kind heart and willingness to help those who are in need. She has a son and grandkids who bring much joy into her life.

name: Rosa Mistica Group
description: Rosa Mística is in its first loan cycle of the Women's Committee program. It is a close-knit group that formed between friends and neighbors in the city of Mariano R. Alonso. The group is participating in the poverty elimination program.   Justina is requesting this loan in order to invest in her business selling foods. She will buy vegetables, meat, greens, and other items so that she can continue expanding her business. Justina comments that with her efforts she has been able to help her family and loved ones. Justina is putting her whole self into her business in order to grow and get ahead. She is inspired by a vision of a better life for her loved ones.

name: Nefoz
description: Nefoz is a 22-year-old single woman from a village near Hebron City. She lives with her family in a small house. Nefoz has a sewing business where she makes different types of clothes. She sells her products in the local market.  Nefoz took a USD loan from FATEN. This loan will help her to buy a new sewing machine for her sewing business. This will help her to increase her productivity and also her income. Nefoz appears in the photo

name: Aidee Margarita
description: Aidee is a member of the Amauta Huamanga communal bank. She 42 years old and is married with three children.   Aidee operates a “chicharroneria,” a restaurant specializing in “chicharrón,” fried pork rinds. The restaurant is called “El Sabroso” and is located in the city center. It is open every day.  Aidee requires a loan of 2000 soles to invest in soft drinks, meat, and tablecloths. Her dreams are to have her own house, and that her children become professionals. Translated from Spanish by jeffrey hersk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Meas
description: Meas S., 38, is married and lives with her husband and three children in Takeo province. She is a professional silk weaver, typically making US$ 2 of profit every day. She has been doing this business since 2004, while her husband works at a farm, growing rice and vegetables. He usually makes US$ 1 per day. Three of the children are in school. Meas S. would like to take out a loan of US$ 700 to purchase more silk.

name: Sylvia
description: Sylvia is 20 years old and lives in the town of Kamwenge in the Fort Portal region of Uganda. She is married and has one child. For the past two years, Sylvia has been working hard to manage her retail shop, which sells sugar, salt, soap and rice.   To help expand her business, Sylvia has requested a loan of 300,000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to buy more essential goods like sugar, soap, salt and rice for resale, and will help Sylvia to generate greater profits and improve her business by buying more items like more sugar, soap and rice for resale. Sylvia hopes that in the future she will be able to build a house of her own.   Sylvia is a member of BRAC's Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program. In addition to microfinance loans, the program provides both a safe place for young Ugandan women to take part in group activities, and a forum for life-skills training.

name: Yolanda
description: Yolanda C. is a 65 year-old generous and thoughtful woman. She is concerned not only about her only child but about her adopted children and neighbors as well. Her son Nelson is a hired laborer and is earning just a small amount of money; he can’t even support himself and his mother. Due to this, Yolanda wanted to have her own way to earn money and augment the income of her son to support them and her adopted children. She joined ASHI in 2008 and has been receiving loans since then. Via these loans she has been able to finance the farming of vegetables in her backyard with the help of her son. These vegetables, once harvested, are sold in the market and to the people in their village.   Proceeds of Yolanda’s vegetables farming business may be small, but her family is enjoying its ability to support their basic needs. Through the loans she will avail via her membership in ASHI, Yolanda is optimistic that someday her business will grow, allowing her to support the improvement of her family members' lives and the lives of others who may need their assistance.

name: Moses
description: Moses is an old client who is growing tea, which he started in 2009. He is a married man with three children who are seven, five and two years old. Two of the children attend school at the moment. He is a hardworking man who works eight hours a day and six days a week. He started his business to be able to have a sustainable source of income to cater for his needs and the needs of his family.  The business is done in Nyakazinga, Igara, Bushenyi district and his clients are tea traders and factories. With his previous loan, his output increased and so did his profits and income. He is now applying for a loan of UGX 1,200,000 (One million Two hundred thousand shillings) to buy organic fertilizers for his tea plantation so that he can produce high quality tea and in the long run, make more profit and educate his children. His major challenge is poor weather in the dry season but he is determined to succeed through his hard work.

name: Anik
description: Anik already had one very successful Kiva deal and she is impatient for her second partnership. She lives in Tsovagyugh village in the Gegharkunik region. She is farming together with her husband and they take care of cows, calves, a bull, pigs, sheep and chickens. As mentioned previously, she perfectly organizes her farm products for sale and earns an income for her family's living. Anik’s husband cultivates potatoes on their plot of land, and they are mainly for sale. Anik will be greatly thankful if Kiva lenders support her one more time. She needs this loan in order to buy one more cow for her farm and also fodder for her farm cattle.

name: Marife
description: As a married parent of three children, Marife works hard to support her family.She has a motorcycle transportation business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from a general store and selling charcoal. Marife is borrowing PHP 18,000 through NWTF to buy spare parts, gasoline, and maintenance for her business.She successfully repaid her previous loan and now she has requested another loan to further build her businesses.Marife has been sustaining her business activities for the past 13 loans already from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Jose Humberto
description: Jose is 68 years old and lives with his wife and four children in Ica. Ica is the only city along the southern coast formed by plains, also known as coastal plains, due to the Andes mountain range entering the region. In Ica there are vast deserts, such as Pampas de Lancha and Pampas de Villacurí, where it gets very hot. The area also has beaches and thermal baths, a variety of marine life, museums, and excellent hotel service.  Jose is a very hard-working and enthusiastic man. He always counts on the support of his wife. She is his right-hand woman and the one who always motivates him (along with his children) to keep going. One of Jose's favorite pastimes is singing and his favorite meal is delicious pasta alfredo.   With a lot of effort he was able to have his business selling groceries from his store. He also sings on the weekends for small events. He works at his store around 8 hours and can serve up to 30 customers. He will also occasionally rent his moto-taxi and this provides him with extra money for the home's expenses. He believes his business is going well because he provides kind and polite service.  Jose is very thankful with the Kiva lenders for the second opportunity they have provided him through their support. Thanks to the loan, he will be able to buy more merchandise for his business (rice, sugar, mixed vegetables, and more). He will also be able to pay for motorcycle permits to have the proper documentation for his moto-taxi, which will increase his earnings and help him keep working toward his dream "to have more motorcycles to rent".

name: Munuka Group
description: Rukia R., 33, is married with two children ages, 13  and 1.  She has a salon business at a place called Mazambalauni, some few kilometers from the city centre. She started this business about 10 years ago.  She works from 8am to 7pm daily. She is able to earn a monthly profit of around $191.  This will be Rukia’s 7th loan from Tujijenge Tanzania.  She used the previous loans to increase on the business, bought a fridge for keeping juice for selling at a nearby school and paid college fees for her your sister and has paid back her loan successfully.  She wants to use the new loan to increase on capital and to save half in the bank..  Rukia  will share this loan with her group  Munuka, which totals 16 members; The members hold each other accountable in paying back their loans. In the picture, Rukia is 1st on the right.

name: Kabir
description: Kabir is a Babban Gona maize farmer from Gwanki Village. Kabir joined Babban Gona to create a better life for his children. Through Babban Gona’s input loan, Kabir will have access to the best farm inputs in the market such as fertilisers, herbicides and improved seeds that will help him earn yields of up to 30 bags of maize/ hectare, double the Nigerian national average of 14 bags. This will see him increase his household income considerably. Thanks to Babban Gona's support, Kabir now has the opportunity to increase his yields and income and use his additional earnings to build a better home for his family.

name: Yadira De La Concepcion
description: Doña Yadira always works to get her family ahead.  Her two children are already getting big—one is a teenager and the other is school-aged.  Her priority is her children.  She has worked for a public school for a number of years.    She is asking for this loan to buy a bale of quality clothing and so increase her monthly earnings.  Her oldest daughter helps her with the clothing sales.  She is grateful for the support that Kiva and Afodenic have given her.

name: Rabiu
description: Rabiu is a 30-year-old farmer from Badamasi. As a Babban Gona member, Rabiu is excited about the opportunity to finally have access to credit, good markets and a trained agronomist. Like all Babban Gona members, Rabiu can earn up to 2,000 USD/hectare this season from growing maize. This is more than three times the average Nigerian farmer’s annual income. The average Babban Gona farmer yields 30 bags/hectare, double the national average of 14. However, Rabiu is ambitious and is aiming to reap 35 bags per hectare this season. When asked, Rabiu said “I plan to use the money I make to build a better home.” In five years, "I want to become the most profitable farmer in my community.” With this loan, he is well on his way to achieving this dream.

name: Stella
description: Stella is 44 years old. She is married and blessed with six children.   She has had a clothes business for 12 years and it has been profitable.   She has requested a loan from VisionFund Kenya; she will be using the loan to purchase more stock of new clothes for her shop. This will enable her to educate her children through university.  Her hopes and dreams for the future are to expand her business and provide well for her family.

name: Catalina
description: Mrs. Catalina R. M. is 40 years old, completed elementary school, and is married to Aurelio Mora with whom she has 2 daughters named Alma Rosa, 17 years old and studies in the CBT preparatory school, and Stephanie, 15 years old and studies in the community’s secondary school. Catalina and her family live in Jalapilla neighborhood of Acatlan de Perez Figueroa in Oaxaca state.  Cata, as her friends and neighbors call her, tells us that she has been raising and selling pigs for more than 3 years. She decided to start her own business because she wanted to help her husband with the household expenses, school expenses for her daughters, and to have a better quality of life.  Cata tells us when she began her business she didn’t have much money and she bought only a small pig which she put in an old corral, fed it for a few months, and then sold it. With the money from the sale she was able to buy two more pigs and she has been working to grown her business. She needs this loan to buy more pigs, feed, and also she wishes to buy a pair of sheep to begin raising sheep. Cata hopes that her business grows a little every day but she also knows the only way to achieve this is to work hard. She wishes that her daughters continue studying and she wants to repair their old pig pen which is very damaged. She also tells us that she is grateful to the Foundation because with this loan she will be able to buy her pigs and make her business prosper day after day and be able to pay for her daughters’ education.

name: Teresita
description: This is Teresita, 54, resident of Manila, Philippines. She is married to Pablito and mother to her children. Together with her husband, Teresita manages her own household while operating a variety store. She works hard to continually provide for her family's everyday expenses.  In the Philippines, a variety store is basically a small convenience store that retails groceries, toiletries and beverages piecemeal in the local neighborhood. It is the place to go to buy one sachet of shampoo, 5 PHP of cooking oil, or an egg. Teresita earns a profit by getting supplies at wholesale prices and selling by the piece. She also has a food stall and her regular customers are her neighbors and local community members. She earns a minimum of 500 PHP in sales every day.  Teresita is requesting an 18,000 PHP loan to buy groceries, toiletries, and beverages to expand her product inventory and continue operating. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands. Teresita hopes to grow her business and dreams of giving her family a good future through all her hard work. She faithfully meets up weekly with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her work and draw strength and inspiration from studying the Word of God.   * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners who gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and repay microfinance loans.

name: Nancy
description: Nancy is from the village of Lapasan, Clarin, Misamis Occidental. She is 53 years old, married, and has four children.   Nancy owns and operates a cafeteria business. She has been engaged in her business for two years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month from these activities. In 2007, Nancy joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and her ability to engage in business activities.   Nancy is requesting a new loan of 30,700 PHP, which will be used to invest in expanding her business. This loan will be her 18th loan from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve and expand her business and to pay for her family's basic needs.

name: Rosalie Fatou
description: Mrs. Rosalie Fatou F. became a member of the Banc Villageois of WANGO in 1996. She is a widow and the mother of three independent children.  She does however look after five of her grandsons.   She runs a small business selling bottled drinks (fruit juices, beer, etc.). She holds a sales license, and has been engaged in this activity for several years.  Her goal is to be able to feed herself and her grandchildren, and to pay the water and electricity bills.

name: Arcadio
description: Arcadio is a widower who earns through his pension. He is a full-fledged member of PMPC and enjoys the benefits of insurances and financial assistance. Recently, he applied for a loan to purchase medicines. At his age he maintains his body balance and agility.

name: Noor Jahan
description: Noor Jahan, daughter of Niam-U-Din, is 45 years old. She is married, has 8 family members, and right now lives in district 8 of Kabul City. She has a tailoring business and wants to take a loan for that. She is an uneducated woman because her family didn’t give her permission to study. However, she wanted to do something for her family, especially after her marriage, and that is why she started her tailoring business. She makes clothes and sells them in bazaar. When she first started her business, she didn’t have enough money. Therefore, her production was small, and she made little money. Then she heard about the loan process through AFSG from one of her friends, and she decided to start taking loans. Up to now she has taken 3 loan cycles from AFSG and wants to take a 4th cycle. Now her business has expanded, and she is making more clothes. As a result, her income has increased.

name: Jane
description: Jane is 54 years old and she sells clothes in Kisumu town. She is married and, together with her spouse, has been blessed with three children. Her spouse also provides additional income.  She will be using this loan to buy more stock of clothes such as shirts and jeans trousers to sell. She will use the anticipated profits to add more clothes.  This is her first loan term with VisionFund Kenya and in future she hopes to expand her business and be successful.

name: Saidmuhriddin
description: This cheery gentleman's name is Saidmuhriddin.  He's 30, and lives with his own big family in a village in the J.Rumy region of Tajikistan.  His family is  ade up of his mother, 3 brothers, his sister, and his wife.  Saidmuhriddin and 2 of his brothers are the only breadwinners in the family.  He would like to  pen his own grocery store to bolster his family's finances, and is seeking a loan to help set one up and stock it with various food products.  He believes he has what it takes to be a successful business owner, and is counting on your help.

name: Margaret
description: Margaret is 30 years old, widowed, with three children, two of whom she is supporting.  Margaret has been in the farming business in Ndunyu Njeru for nine years and she has applied for her first loan from Kenya Agency for Development of Enterprise and Technology (KADET), to enable her to buy potatoes and cabbages, among other vegetables to sell. With the anticipated profits, Margaret plans to buy a land.  In the near future, she hopes to expand her farming business to uplift her family's living standards.

name: Fe
description: Hard-working woman best describes Mrs. Fe. I., 40 years old, separated, and a resident of Talairon, Misamis Occidental. She has three children, one in college and two in high school. Twelve years has passed since she has been separated from her husband. She works hard to raise her three children. With the help of Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative, she was able to start-up a “sari-sari” store (small grocery store) with an initial capital of PHP 3,000. It all started with "one"-- one bottle of edible oil, vinegar, soy sauce, etc. She has managed it well. Until now, the business has existed. Now, she is requesting a loan of PHP 10,000 to buy longaniza to sell. Her other source of income is through the selling of AVON and SME products. She will be happy and fulfilled if she sees all her children finish their studies.

name: Mary Grace
description: Mary Grace is a married woman who lives in Clarin, Bohol. She is 41 years old and earns a living by selling dry goods. Her husband is helping her run this business. They successfully started this business four years ago.  Mary Grace is asking for a loan for additional capital to buy dry goods such as needles, thread, cloth, ribbons, belts and garters.  In this way, she will be able to improve her earnings for her children. She has three school-aged children who are 18, 15 and 13 years old. She wants them to finish their studies.

name: Rosas De Pucuro Group
description: The "Rosas de Pucuro" Communal Bank is starting its first cycle in Pro Mujer as part of the Achacachi Regional Office. There are ten members, governed by a board of directors. The head of the board is Señora Nely. The group members' businesses are varied and include: fish sales, bricklaying, artesanry, cheese production, and potato farming. Nely tells us that she has recently joined the group. She has had a fishing business, which she learned from her family, for several years. She will use this loan for the purchase of a fishing net from the markets in La Paz. After fishing, she will sell in the local market. This work allows her to support her family; she is married with two children. When asked what she likes about Pro Mujer, Nely responds that she likes the support that we provide.

name: Zabirov
description: N. Zabirov lives in the Gissar region. He is 36 years old, married and has five children. He works as a paramedic part time. He has a retail business on the days when he doesn't work. He has a store where he sells household products. He has been in this business for ten years now. He plans to get a loan to increase commodity circulation. This will give an opportunity to increase the variety of the merchandise and attract new customers.Translated from Russian by Elena Fedorchuk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Dilshad
description: Dilshad is a 31-year-old woman. She lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. She is a responsible mother of three children. Her husband is a rickshaw driver by profession. For the past many days his rickshaw has not been working properly so he is unable to generate any amount of income. He wants to repair it as soon as possible. However, due to the lack of money, he finds it difficult to cover the cost of repairing the rickshaw. Therefore Dilshad has requested a loan from Kiva's partner BRAC Pakistan to help her husband to cover the cost of repairing the rickshaw. This will help him to continue his business. Dilshad is so much thankful to Kiva and BRAC  Pakistan.

name: Xyris
description: Xyris, a 34-year-old mother of five children, helps operate her own cafeteria. In many years of serving food, she has been able to provide for the family. She was able to send her children to school. She had to be determined in her work to provide a better living for her family. In order to increase sales, she is borrowing a loan from GDMPC Microcredit to purchase raw ingredients to prepare food to sell. She hopes that someday her children will be successful in their careers, and she will sustain her business and work for more profit.

name: Rhodora
description: This is Rhodora, 52, a resident of Tondo, Philippines. She is married to Dionisio, a worker abroad, and is a mother to her children. She manages their household while operating the business. At this time, she is working hard to continually provide income for their everyday expenses.  Rhodora is a pedicab operator. She has one unit of side car or bicycle cart that carries up to two passengers to their destination within the community. Someone who uses her pedicab will just give her the rental for the day. She also has a variety store and a direct-selling business. She earns a minimum of 800 Philippine Pesos (PHP) in sales every day.  To help her continue operations of her business, she is requesting a Php 50,000 loan. She will be utilizing the loan for the maintenance of her side car. She expects a boost in her business income as she expands her business.  Rhodora hopes to expand her business in the coming years. She faithfully meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her work every week and where she can also draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Tonio
description: Tonio, age 45, is a smiling man.  He has 15 years of experience as an elementary school teacher.  He is of the Miskita ethnicity from the Waspam Rio Coco municipality.  He is married and has six children.  Four are adolescents attending elementary school, and two a minors.  His wife is a housewife.His plan is to change the wood on his house on stilts.  He is requesting a loan to buy construction materials like wood, zinc sheeting, and nails.He dreams of, little by little, building his house of concrete in order for it to be sturdier and safer.

name: Pablita
description: In the year 2011, Pablita learned about Paglaum MPC and the financial assistance it extends. As a farmer in Mahayag, Molave, she tried her luck and took out a loan to start her rice production. After several months, she was able to return her borrowed capital.   To this day, Pablita feels she owes her good fortune to the Cooperative for having trusted her with the money she used for her business. Recently, she got a loan to purchase farm supplies and fertilizer for the next cropping season. Pablita wishes to sustain her business and be able to supply rice to the neighboring towns.

name: Diana
description: Diana is married with one child. She is 25 years old. She is engaged in the hog-raising business. Diana is a hardworking person, and she ensures that she does everything she can to provide for the needs of her family. To this end, she is requesting a loan of 15,000 PHP to buy piglets and feed for her business. She hopes that her hog-raising business will be better than before so she can pay off the loan ahead of time and buy more pigs to raise.

name: Toch
description: Toch is 28 years old and a married woman of two dependent children. She operates a farming business in a small village of Siem province, which is well-known for its ancient temples, especially Angkor Wat. Every day, she goes in the field, where she spends most of her time of the day, especially during the rainy season from May to October. Though she has to work hard in her rice paddy, it doesn’t matter to her because the important thing is to provide enough for the sake of her family members.  As of now, she has applied for a loan amount of $1,500 U.S. dollars to buy farm supplies such as fertilizers and insecticides, which will be used toward the growth of her rice field. Also with a portion of the loan, she will buy construction supplies for her husband, who works in the construction field. She hopes that by this season, she can get better crop production to save for her children’s needs and education.

name: Nelly
description: Nelly is 23 years old and a hard-working woman.  She lives together with her husband José and her 6 year-old son Daniel, in a rental house, in the town of Tapo.  Nelly has been farming since she was young.  She started 7 years ago.  Over the years she has learned farming techniques and also the knowledge needed in order to be able to make progress and get ahead.  Her main crops are potatoes, peas and beans which she grows on rented land.  What Nelly most likes about her work is being able to share with her husband the desire to get ahead since they both go out to work every day.  The most difficult part of her work is obtaining her own working capital and the expenses that she incurs in paying the annual rent on her land and her son's education expenses.  Very soon, Nelly will harvest 25 sacks of potatoes and 15 sacks of beans which will make her good profits and this will increase her savings with which she is planning to buy her own plot of land very soon.  Nelly belongs to the "San Jerónimo de Queta" community bank and this is her seventh loan with MFP where she feels fulfilled since the support that she receives from her association helps her to improve her crops.  In a few months Nelly will harvest her potatoes and is planning to use her loan money to buy 2 bags of pea seeds and several sacks of potato which she will spread over her farmland after her harvest.

name: Flor Maria
description: Flor Maria has dedicated her whole life to caring for her husband and their 4 children.  She has always been ready to help them with whatever they need, and to do this now, she generates income to contribute toward the household expenses. In this way she can improve the quality of life of her husband and their 4 children.  Flor Maria has always wanted her children to have the best education possible.  However, the income that she and her husband earn has not been sufficient to allow them to access the best education in their area.  For this reason, Flor Maria works constantly and with a lot of care, so that her business will generate more income.  This way she could provide her children with a good education.  For some time now Flor Maria has been selling merchandise through a catalog, and thanks to her good service, she has attracted a good share of the customers in her area. The disadvantage that Flor Maria faces is that many times when she sells on credit her customers are late in making their payments, because money is very tight.  Flor Maria seeks to increase her sales, so that she can provide a better education to her children.  To do this, she plans to increase the variety of products that she offers to her customers.  However, because some of her customers are behind on their payments, she lacks the capital she needs to purchase this additional merchandise.  This is why she is requesting a loan that will allow her to make this purchase of personal care products, such as beauty products and lotions, so that she can offer more variety to her customers.  Flor Maria hopes that her sales will increase significantly, which will allow her to increase her earnings and save so that in the future her children can go to college.  This will allow them to have a high-paying job in the future.

name: Braulio
description: Braulio is from the city of Encarnación and he is married. He mentions that he makes a living buying and selling mobile phones, which he commercializes in Argentina. He has worked in this activity for the past nine years, which has helped him to form a good client base due to his experience. His goal is to continue working and in this way grow as a micro-businessman. His continual job in to provide everything that his family needs for a better future.   He is requesting a loan to buy various models of mobile phones with which to stock his business. Then he will have a greater variety to offer to his customers and can continue working. He appreciates the help he is receiving as it is very important to him.

name: Juan Marcos
description: Señor Marcos has been making cereal for a living for seven years now.  Previously, he worked in a factory where he made the same products.  He learned this process, then he became self-employed, and started his own business four years ago, making his sales at the local markets.  He currently lives with his uncle in the town of El Paso.  He also lives with his wife and three school age children, who also work with him to make his products.   He is requesting a loan to buy raw materials wholesale since the prices go up rapidly at the end of the year.  He urgently needs to stock up on raw materials to avoid the affect of the rising prices for supplies to make cereals.

name: Nelinda
description: Nelinda is 64 years old and married with three children.  Nelinda works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 20,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) loan through NWTF in order to purchase more groceries to sell.  Nelinda has borrowed and repaid 13 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 11 years and also earns an income from fishing.  Nelinda aspires to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Lawrence
description: Lawrence is a 26-year-old man who is still single. He trades in clothes and works with a company called Tracker Uganda. He needs this money to complete his house. When the house is complete he hopes to get married and start a family. He sells used clothes to university students. He does not have any private means of transport so he finds it challenging to transport the clothes to the university where most of his customers are. He is a very hardworking and humble man. He appreciates the opportunity to get a loan since it will help him achieve his dreams. The second person in the photograph with a bag is the loan officer

name: Hoeun
description: Hoeun is a married mother of an only son, who lives in the Kampong Chhnang province in Cambodia. Since 1998, she has run a business selling rice, palm sugar and prahok (prahok is salty fish kept in the jar for about a month or longer and needs to be steamed to have with fresh vegetables). Her husband is 47 years old and works as a worker in road construction. Her son is 18 years old and works as a carpenter. Hoeun has decided to take out a loan because she is lacking the finances to buy rice, palm sugar and prahok to sell. With this loan, she will be able to improve her business and earn more income. In the future, she is going to buy a motorcycle for her son for commuting to work. She also hopes that her son will pass his exam to work in Korea.

name: Jessierre
description: Jessierre is a hardworking entrepreneur who has been operating a ready-to-wear business in the Philippines for four years. She earns additional income selling cosmetics.  Jessierre has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of loans from NWTF. She is now requesting a loan of PHP 14000 to purchase more stocks to sell such as pants, shirts, etc.   Jessierre dreams of saving enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Adjovi
description: The married mother of one child, Adjovi is a woman living in Adidogomé. She is 22 years old and a retailer of jewelry, which is supplied twice a month from the market. She resells by going from district to district. Adjovi has need of this loan to order complete necklaces with the aim of responding favorably to customer needs and having considerable financial autonomy, so as to support her child’s education.

name: Bega Kwa Bega Group
description: Receive greetings from Bega kwa Bega Group in Western Kenya! Abdalla is the facilitator of the Bega kwa Bega group. This  group joined One Acre Fund in the year 2011 and will re-enroll in the 2012 program.   Abdalla is a father of two children. He joined One Acre Fund due to the firm's best prices offered and in order to access fertilizer and hybrid seeds to ensure quality harvest. In the recent 2011 season, Abdalla had a good maize yield, harvesting 10 bags on 3/4 acre of land. Before joining One Acre Fund, Abdalla was only able to harvest 2 bags of maize on 3/4 acre of land.   With this loan, One Acre Fund will purchase fertilizer, seeds, and other important inputs to distribute to Abdalla and his group during Kenya’s next planting season in February 2012. The distribution of farming inputs is part of One Acre Fund’s integrated agriculture package, which includes training, reliable input supply (such as fertilizer and seeds), credit and insurance.   With income from maize sales, Abdalla will save for future use and ensure food security for his family.   In 2012, the members of Bega kwa Bega group will each plant  between ½ and 1 acre of maize.   Abdalla is pictured with his group members in the photograph.

name: Isabel
description: Isabel, 32, is a very optimistic woman who has a lot of dreams.  She works very hard every day to give her family the best.  She's married and has six children and her husband.  She's a homemaker and she takes care of the household chores.  She very much wants to make a contribution and give her children a better life, however, so she does domestic work for other families and also grows corn.  She generates some income with these jobs, so she contributes to the family budget.  This gives her a lot of satisfaction because she wants the best for her children.  Isabel firmly believes that her family deserves a decent life, so she's requesting a loan to buy a plot of land to be able to grow more corn.   One of her main dreams is for her children to have professions so they have more opportunities and so they can improve their standard of living.

name: Arlyn
description: Arlyn is a married woman with two children who are still in school. She is a very hard working entrepreneur who is 37 years old.  She has a dried fish making business in the Philippines and requested a PHP 5,000 loan through NWTF to buy more fish and other materials for her business.  Arlyn has been in this business for 25 years. She would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Bo
description: Bo S. is thirty-one years old and married with two children, both of whom go to school. She lives in the Kampong Cham province. She and her husband sell rubber. Typically, they make only about $20 in revenue each day.  In light of these economic difficulties, Bo is asking for a loan to purchase rubber in bulk in order to get a special discount. This purchase can help increase her daily income.

name: Rosa Olivia
description: Rosa Olivia Pérez Pérez is 43 years old. She is a single mother. She has six children under her care. For more than 20 years, she has worked selling basic grains. In order to start this humble business, she first worked selling ice and jewelry. Rosa has always been a strong woman with a desire to succeed. With her earnings, she obtained a location from which to sell her products. At her customers’ request, she invested in detergents, soap, disinfectant and other products. The loan that she requests is for working capital to purchase basic grains that are necessary for daily consumption such as rice, sugar, beans, corn and concentrate. Rosa’s dream is to maintain her work, because she depends on the income as her only means of living.Translated from Spanish by Rebecca Towle, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sok Leang
description: Sok Leang, 45, is married and resides with her husband and two children in Takeo Province, Cambodia. She has been producing noodles to sell for over ten years, earning approximately USD 7 per day. Her husband runs the business of selling bread and earns about USD 10 per day. One of her children is employed in a garment factory and earns about USD 3 per day. Due to the difficulty in the family’s transportation, Sok Leang is requesting for a loan of USD 1000 to purchase a motorbike for commuting and delivering her noodles to sell. This purchase would enable her to use the saved money on her transportation expenses to support the family. In the future, she would like to expand her business, build a new wooden house and help her children get bachelor's degrees.

name: Wilson Leopoldo
description: Wilson is 46 years old. He is married and has 2 children who are in school. Wilson is a master builder. Since he was little, his father taught him this trade and now he works putting in tile floors. He wants to have more capital to be able to buy tools. With the loan, he will buy: tools, welding materials and a ladder.

name: Jean
description: Jean M., who is 55 years old, owns a small rice field in Santo Nino, South Cotabato. She said that she needs additional capital to run her rice farm business because the farm supplies are expensive.  Her family relies on the income she makes from the farm. The harvest is saved for family consumption while the remainder is sold to rice traders for additional income for the family.  She is hoping to receive a loan of Php 15,000 from Community Economic Ventures Inc.  She will use the loan to buy farm supplies to grow more of her crop and better support her family.

name: Mamlakat
description: Mamlakat is a strong woman. She was born in the northern part of Tajikistan in 1982. She is now living in small city with beautiful nature. She is married and has two children. Her husband is a construction worker and his work is seasonal.   Mamlakat has had a business for about four years. She buys and sells women's and children’s clothes. She has a place in the domestic market where she sells her goods. Her family lives in poor conditions because the money that they earn depends on the season and customers each day.  She wants to grow her business and buy seasonal goods to sell. She is asking a loan from Kiva lenders to buy a collection of women's and children’s clothes. She hopes she will have good business and earn money to feed her family. She awaits you kindness.

name: Kashasha Farmers Tukore Group, Ibanda
description: R. Felex is a happy and jolly man. He is shown at the top left and also happens to be in the big photo. He is 46 years old and married with 6 children; he also takes care of 3 more children.   Felex has been a mechanic in the Omukashasha trading centre for 20 years, and one of his strong points is being faithful to his clients. He repairs cars and motorcycles, and he needs a loan to be able to buy more spare parts for both motorcycles and cars. He would also like to have a section for bicycle repairs.  He operates from a garage, and he wants to expand his business in the future so that he will be able to educate his children as some of them join him in his business.

name: Rayhon
description: A. Rayhon lives in the Shahrituz region. She's forty-eight years old, married and has three children. Her husband works in Russia. For over eight years Rayhon has raised plants, specifically vegetables, for sale. She's asking for a loan in order to buy seeds, mineral fertilizers and fuel for her tractor. All this will enable her to reap a bountiful harvest.

name: Hauy
description: Hauy S. is 60 years old and lives in the Thmor Kor district of Kampong Cham province. Since 1979, she has been growing vegetables and rice to sustain her family. She also takes these vegetables to the markets to sell. She only earns 1 USD a day.   Her husband, Suon Sem, is also 60 years old and works on staff with a telephone company making 4 USD a day. Of their five children, three are married, while two are single and still live at the family home. The two children at home are garment factory workers, each earning 7 USD per day. She wants to use her loan to buy wood and repair their roof which has been leaking for some time.

name: Awa
description: Awa was born in April 1984 in Kadiolo. She is married and the mother of 5 children and lives with her husband and their children in a traditional family in Medine, a popular district of Sikasso town, in the third administrative region of the Republic of Mali.  Having tried several businesses without any success, this hard-working woman has started buying and selling onions and Maggi stock cubes. She gets her supplies at the Grand Market. She is requesting her second individual business loan from the MFI Soro Yiriwaso in order to satisfy the needs of her growing clientèle. The previous loan was properly repaid. This loan will enable her to buy 10 50-kilo baskets of onions and 5 boxes of stock cubes which she will resell at the market for cash or credit to a retail clientèle made up of men and women. She expects to make an average monthly profit of 35 000 francs. This profit will enable her to repay the loan and its interest and to build her savings.

name: Rosenia
description: Rosenia is 40 years old and married with two children. Both of her children are in school.  Rosenia works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 8,000 loan through NWTF in order to purchase more groceries to sell.  Rosenia has borrowed and paid two loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for three years and also earns an income from rice retailing.  Rosenia aspires to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Jovita
description: Mrs. Jovita, member of the La Libertad (Freedom) village bank, lives in the Bellavista district in the San Martin region in the small village of La Libertad.  She sells coconuts wholesale by the hundreds to other merchants in the city of Bellavista who sell them retail.  She started her business because she saw that there is great demand for this refreshing fruit and she decided to start the business.  With this $325 loan which she will repay in 6 months, she will purchase coconuts in very large quantities to sell to retailers.  She is already well-known and has fixed customers who look for her products as she always leaves a good impression on her customers.  Mrs. Jovita is 26 years old; she lives with her husband and her two children.  She is a long-suffering and responsible woman with great desires to help her children progress.  In the future, she'd like to be a producer of coconuts to improve her income.Translated from Spanish by Scott Crandall, Kiva Volunteer

name: Rita
description: Rita is 53 years old. She is a widow and lives alone in the capital city of Georgia. Her economic activity is a newly started business, in particular, a small store where tobacco and beverages are sold.  Rita requested loan from local financial institutions for the business expansion, but without any success. Her loan request was rejected because of low income and insufficient experience in her business.  Rita was involved in the same type of business for eight years. She had rented a commercial place and had a grocery store. This business was recently stopped because of financial problems. Her loan request was approved through a new joint initiative of Kiva and Credo. The startup loan program provides business startup and re-startup credits with soft conditions to the country's rural poor, who do not have access to credit products because they are regarded as “high risk borrowers” because of low income. With the received credit, Rita will expand and develop her store. She will purchase more tobacco and beverages at wholesale prices and sell for a higher price. The new business initiative, financed with the Kiva startup loan, will significantly increase her monthly income and Rita will reinvest the received profits in the same business. She awaits your help and kindness.

name: Shiela
description: Shiela is 39 years old and married with five children who are in school. Shiela works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a buying and selling of charcoal business in the Philippines and requested a 10,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) loan through NWTF to buy additional sacks of charcoal to sell.  Shiela has been in this business for eight years and also sells a variety of retail items.   In the future, Shiela would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Loraine Paola
description: Loraine, 22 years old, with great desire for personal and professional growth, found in grocery sales her opportunity to generate the income that she needed to cover her expenses, taking advantage of the experience that she got as a saleswoman at a neighborhood store and identifying that there was an unsatisfied demand in the neighborhood where she lives, due to the distance that her neighbors had to go to make their daily purchases. At the beginning, she began to bring basic products to her house to sell them to her neighbors and little by little, from her customers' suggestions, she got groceries such as rice, oil, grains, pasta, and more, until she established her own store which she opens from 6:00 am to 10:00 pm. However, she still needs to increase the stock in her business so she is asking for her first Kiva loan through Fundación Mario Santo Domingo, resources that she plans to invest in a greater quantity of groceries such as rice, oil, grains, pastas, fruits, vegetables and cold meats. Her dream for prosperity focuses on continuing to expand her business to generate more income which will allow her to improve her quality of life and finish her education.

name: Myra
description: Myra is very diligent person. She is 44 years old, married with three grown-up children. Myra has been engaged in selling recycled products for three years. Myra is requesting a loan of Php 11,000 to buy used materials in the community. She hopes that her business will expand to be able to provide the needs of her family.

name: Rosa Dilia
description: Rosa, 55, was born in Estelí.  She’s married and the mother of three children.  She sells clothes.  She started this business with help from one of her daughters and a loan she took out.  She’s had the business for 12 months now.  Her husband’s a farmer.  She used to be a housewife but now sells clothes.  The business is located in downtown Estelí where she sells her merchandise in a locale she leases.  Her daughter helps her sell while Rosa cares for her grandson because, above all, she’s a mother and it’s for her family that she works so diligently.  She is asking for the loan to buy three large bundles of used clothes, outfits.  With this investment she hopes to attract new customers, improve her sales and increase her profits.  She wants to expand the business enlarging it with new types of products to sell.  Her next goal is to improve her humble home’s infrastructure.

name: Shagufta
description: Shagufta is 51 years old and a widow. She has been successfully running a small canteen in her area.  She offers a variety of food items including biscuits, juices, snacks and chips etc. She earns a good amount of income through her business.  She is the mother of 3 children and is motivated to provide her family with good quality food, clothing and health. She wants to grow her business so she requested a loan of 45,000 PKR  to buy packs of sweets, toffees, biscuits and juices to handle increasing demand efficiently. She hopes to see a boost in her earnings which will help her expand her business in the future.

name: Fadia
description: Fadia is a 43-year-old widowed mother of three children. She is working hard since her beloved husband passed away to provide them with the necessities for living.   In 2005, Fadia established her clothes and lingerie-selling business to make sure that she can provide her beloved family with their needs, and cover almost all of their requested expenses.   Fadia is requesting a loan from Kiva partner Al Majmoua, to increase her business merchandise with special newly released spring and summer collections necessary for her business development and increase in income.  Fadia is very energetic, well known in her community, and supported by almost all of her customers who are mainly relatives, friends, neighbors and passersby. She aims to increase her faithful clientele and attract new ones through diversifying her products to suit everyone's requests.

name: Oykhon
description: This resident of the Shahrituz region is called Oykhon. She is a 49 years old, married woman. Oykhon lives with her husband, four sons, daughters-in-law and grandchildren. She works with livestock breeding together with her family. For a period of 6 years their family has bred cows and bulls for sale. This activity is widespread in their area, as the nature and climate is very favorable for this type of business.   Oykhon would like to increase the number of cattle, as she only has two cows left. She requests a loan to purchase cattle. Oykhon trusts in and hopes for your support.

name: Ernestina
description: Ernestina still has her travel agency which she has been involved in for several years.  The business is prospering thanks to the effort she puts into it every day.  She continues to sell tour tickets to her customers and foreign visitors, and wants to continue working so she can support her family.  The loan she is requesting is to buy tour tickets and other items.  She is happy to have funding and promises to make her payments.

name: Nenita
description: Nenita is a married woman with five children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Nenita is 58 years old, and two of her children are in school.Nenita has a rice-vending business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for 31 years. She requested a PHP 10,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy additional sacks of rice to sell.In the future, Nenita would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Miguel Angel
description: Miguel is a 22 year old young man.  He is brown skinned, thin, his hair is black as the night, and his eyes are brown.  He is single and has no children.  Miguel lives in the city of El Alto, which is located 4,000 meters above sea level and 30 minutes from the city of La Paz.  He has an enterprising character.  His current business is a bookstore that he has worked at every day for five years.  Now he has new material, including a binding machine and a public telephone.  He is always in search of ways to satisfy the needs of his customers.  His youth has given him a lot of desire to continue improving his business.  He is searching for a way to improve his stock and increase the products that he offers since the local festival is approaching and he wants to be prepared.
