Miguel dreams of continuing his schooling and thinks that his business will give him the opportunity he needs.    Miguel is requesting a loan to expand his bookstore and use the profits to pay for his studies.

name: Sony
description: Mrs. Sony S. (shown in the photo) and her husband, Mr. Samath Sao, live in a village along the Mekong River, about 15 kilometers northeast of Phnom Penh. They have been married since 1990 and have three children: one son and two daughters. All of them are in school: two are attending universities. Mr. Samath Sao is a weaver.   Sony runs a grocery store from home. She also assists in her husband’s weaving business when she is free. She is asking for a loan of $1,200 to pay for her children's education fees. She will also use a part of the loan to purchase weaving materials.

name: Shamshad
description: Both my husband and I work full-time, hard-working jobs in order to support ourselves and our four children.  I stitch outfits for a local boutique. I get $1 USD in profit for every outfit I make. In a given month, I am able to produce only 25 to 30 dresses. My husband is a rickshaw (local three-wheeled taxi) driver. The income we earn is just enough to sustain our basic needs.   My husband’s rickshaw is in a very deteriorating condition so we need to replace it with another second-hand rickshaw. Please lend us $325 USD to help us buy another rickshaw.

name: Eveling Del Carmen
description: Eveling is 56 years old and married. She has a son who is a minor. She is a native of Leon in the western part of the country. She is hard-working, responsible and wants to get ahead. In her spare time she likes to be with her son. Unfortunately she couldn't study as she had to work from a young age. Today she struggles day to day to provide a better future for her son.   Thanks to her effort  and her desire to succeed she has been selling cosmetics from her house and by order. She works at her business about 8 hours per day offering products like rouge, eye shadow, mascara, eye liner, moisturizing creams, perfumes, make-up remover, cosmetic cases and eyeglasses.   The goal of the loan is to invest in the working capital and stock her business so that in the near future she can generate more income. Eveling thanks the lenders at Kiva for the support they offer to people of low economic resources and poor countries like Nicaragua so they can have dignified work.

name: Lois
description: Mrs. Lois L. is 56 years old, is a widow with two children, and works as a farmer. On average, she earns $2 per day. Her children work in the factory to supplement their family's income. To generate additional revenue and income, Mrs. Lea L. is currently requesting a loan $300 from Kiva to purchase additional pigs to raise and breed.

name: Nengsih
description: Good day, lenders! Meet one of KSPPS BMI’s clients, Nengsih, who is a 48-year-old married woman. Nengsih is a housewife and her husband has been a builder for four years. Nengsih has asked for a loan of 7,100,000 IDR from KSPPS BMI. This loan will be used to build sanitary facilities at her home, in order to improve her family's access to sanitation and water sources. Her family's income is insufficient to build toilets and water sources, but Nengsih will be able to repay the loan received.She and her family want to live a healthy life with sanitation and clean water. She is very grateful for this opportunity and wants to thank to all lenders.

name: Bernard
description: Bernard operates three mobile money transfer shops in Kasama, Zambia. He received his first Kiva loan in December 2013 and utilized the funds to add to his working capital in order to serve additional customers.  Bernard speaks about how his business is providing an important service for his community to send money around the country without needing a bank account.   For Bernard, however, his money transfer business has an even more compelling impact; it allows him to support the 13 orphaned nieces and nephews he has raised as his own since losing eight of his own siblings. Later this year, the youngest two will complete their university studies. Bernard says he wanted to raise the children "to be independent and educated," and has taken on the responsibility of raising the children as his life's central purpose.   Bernard has requested a second loan from Kiva so that he can purchase a trading booth and open up his fourth mobile money transfer location. The loan will be used to pay for the booth and provide the starting capital his business needs to service customers sending and receiving money.    Bernard expresses how he appreciates the Kiva lenders and their continued support of his small business.

name: Gliceria
description: Gliceria is a 63 year old married woman from Bohol, Philippines. She has been engaged in a food vending business for more than ten years now, selling snack foods to the people in their community. This is her source of income.   Gliceria is asking for a loan worth 6,000 PHP to buy more ingredients for her food vending business. With the loan she will able to increase her sales, thus improving her profit. She dreams of expanding her business to generate more income. She also plans to save.

name: Patricia
description: Patricia is a 45-year-old mother of six children aged 28, 26, 24, 17, 11 and seven years. She has been selling fish for the past 17 years and earns a monthly income of KES 12,000.  She has requested a loan worth KES 20,000 to purchase more fish for sale. The profit she will receive will help her repay her loan. This is her first loan.

name: Ganchimeg
description: Ganchimeg is a 29-year-old widow who lives with her son and parents in a small apartment in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. Although she specialized in accounting, she supports her family by operating an office clothing business at a local indoor market.   Her long term aim is to create a great and comfortable opportunity to study and live with her son, so she is requesting a 3,500,000 Mongolian Tugrik (MNT) loan to purchase more office clothes to sell.

name: Dieu
description: Dieu is 58 years old and married with three children. He lives with his family in Ho Chi Minh City. He and his wife earn their income from selling soft drinks from their stall.    Dieu started his business ten years ago. He intends to take a loan to gradually expand his business by buying a variety of different beverages and repair the stall to better serve his customers.   He hopes his business runs smoothly and will help him to improve his family's living conditions.

name: Akpéné
description: Akpéné is a married woman residing in Adidogomé with four children in her care. She is a retailer of charcoal and gets her supplies at the market three time a month. She resells in front of her home. To finance her purchase, Akpéné needs this loan to order sacks of charcoal with the aim of having better sales and making more profit to support her husband in covering family expenses. This would allow her children a good education.

name: Elba Del Carmen
description: Doña Elba is an enterprising woman who has worked in her business for 10 years. The member sells scrub brushes, brooms, and all types of cleaning supplies. Doña Elba has the help of her husband, who contributes financially and also helps her with sales.   With the loan, Doña Elba wants to invest in the purchase of materials for her shop, as one of her dreams is to purchase a minibus and sell in the departments also. Thanks to the loans that have been given to her, the member has increased her sales.

name: Pean Group
description: Jackline is a 31-year-old married woman with two children aged 11 and 7 years old. She lives in Kamwenge, Uganda.   Jackline runs a drug shop as her main source of income, and she practices gardening where she grows millet and beans as her side income. It is from these businesses that she has been able to sustain herself and look after her family. High rental and license fees are a problem, but she has hopes of expanding her business into a big pharmacy in Kamwenge Town.  She is requesting a loan to buy more tablets to sell.

name: Ban's Group
description: A citizen of a rural village located in the Sangke district of Battambang province, Cambodia, Ban is 25 years old. She is married and has two children. Ban has been in rice farming for almost 10 years. In addition to this, her husband also contributes to the family's income by selling and buying rice in a local village. Their current business earns them about 60,000 KHR and they manage to save about 10,000 KHR each day after daily expenses.  Ban is in her first loan cycle with VisionFund. Now she is leading her group of two to apply for a loan of 300,000 KHR each. As the leader, she is going to use her portion to buy fertilizer for her farmland and to pay labor costs in plowing the field. Ban hopes to make more income so as to improve her lifestyle.

name: Jhumki
description: Jhumki is a 32-year-old woman of Maynaguri. She lives with her husband and two children. Neither she nor her husband completed their secondary level of education. Her children are now receiving education in grades 2 and 7.  Though her husband runs a small business of his own, his income is not sufficient for household expenses and the children’s education as well. That is why Jhumki has to face lots of financial hurdles. For this reason she decided to help her husband and contribute to her family on her own.   She applied for a loan from BJS (Kiva’s partner) to purchase a sewing machine for making cotton garments like blouses, petticoats, frocks, etc. As she has a sound knowledge of stitching from her childhood, she has chosen this tailoring business to start. She hopes she can earn sufficiently from this business because there is no good tailor nearby and people have to go to the proper town to meet their needs. Due to this demand of daily use garments in her locality, Jhumki started her new tailoring business with a hope that she will earn huge profits. With the profit, she hopes to give more education to her children, to protect them from poverty and to relieve the family’s financial difficulties and enhance her family’s well-being.  Now Jhumki hopes to become a renowned tailor in her locality, and she gives her thanks to BJS and Kiva both.

name: Hayrapet
description: Hayrapet is 28 years old. He has graduated from the Kadjaran Secondary School, then entered the Kapan College and graduated as a communications specialist. After college, in 2010, Hayrapet enrolled as a second-year correspondence student in the faculty of Electrical Energy of the Gorisk State University.  Hayrapet lives with his retired parents. For almost 5 years, he has been working at a hydroelectric station. He is also engaged in bee keeping. Hayrapet's family has a small parcel of land and a house in the village of Nor Astghberd in the Syuniksk region.  Hayrapet needs a loan of 170,000 Armenian dram to pay his tuition in 2013.

name: Tom
description: Tom is 27 years old and single with no children. He lives in Kasese, Uganda. For ten years, Tom has been running a retail shop. He also practices farming to earn an additional source of income.   Tom began the business to improve his standard of living and create employment for himself. Tom has a dream of expanding his business, although he is faced with the challenge of limited capital. Tom wants money to buy salt, rice, sugar, maize flour and other general merchandise for selling.

name: Adriana
description: For as long as she can remember, Adriana has been determined to own her own business. Two years ago, she saw this dream come true when she founded her home-based wholesale jewelry company in Miami, Florida. Her company primarily specializes in the sale of stainless steel jewelry. Ever since the founding of her company, she has loved the independence it has given her and she has seen overwhelming success. This success has inspired her to diversify her company into an individual seller of jewelry as well as a wholesaler. She also hopes that, through new business permits, she will be able to diversify the products that she sells to become a more well-rounded retailer and serve a larger variety of customers. Adriana is asking for this loan to help her purchase a larger inventory for future sales.

name: Rodolfo De Los Angeles
description: Rodolfo C. is 47 years old. He’s married and has two kids who are studying in school. They live in the neighborhood of Hialeah in the capital of Managua. He has made a living as a cabinetmaker and a carpinter for the past 31 years. His plans are to increase his assets. He started this business with his parents since he was able to be a helper, then he started working for himself. With this loan he plans to buy raw materials to make furniture, powder to make new designs and he will be able to supply his customers with products of great quality. This will allow him to obtain increased profits and to allow his business grow.  (Translated by Alexis of San Roque High School)Translated from Spanish by San Roque School, Kiva Volunteer

name: Mapatano B Group
description: Grace, age 23, is married with one child (age 1 yr 7 months). She owns a tailoring business where she also sells laundry soap and fabrics. She began this business in 2002 and now makes a monthly profit of about $95. She works from 7am to 7pm daily. She now requests a loan to increase her business, which she will share with her subgroup member Agripina (a shopkeeper). Grace hopes to one day buy modern sewing machines for her business.

name: Ulanbek
description: Ulanbek A. is 42 years old, married, and has four children. He lives with his family in Oruktam Village. After serving in the army, he graduated from State University and worked as a history teacher at the local school. Owing to his devoted attitude and high professionalism, in 2006, he was appointed to the post of School Director.   Unfortunately, salaries in rural areas are very low and do not cover all expenses of the household. To find an additional means of subsistence for his family, in 1994, Ulanbek started breeding cattle. With initial capital of 2,000 Kyrgyz Soms, he bought cattle and managed to enlarge its number to three cows, one bull calf, two sheep and three horses. Today he has an income of 5,000 Kyrgyz Soms per month.    Now, Ulanbek wants a loan 50,000 Kyrgyz Soms to buy more cattle. With the revenues from this loan, Ulanbek plans to expand his farm by breeding livestock.  About Bai-Tushum: Bai-Tushum and Partners uses Kiva funding to target the especially vulnerable population. Bai-Tushum and Partners is one of the leading Microfinance Institutions in Kyrgyzstan. As a reliable financial partner, Bai-Tushum contributes to the economic development of the Kyrgyz Republic through the delivery of microfinance services in rural and urban areas that lead to increased employment and meet the interests of its clients and investors.

name: Mary Jane
description: Mary Jane is 43 years old and married with four children. Two children are in school. They live in the Philippines.  Mary Jane raises livestock and has been in the business for eight years now. She borrowed four times in the past to sustain her business. Mary Jane has requested a 14,000 PHP loan to buy feed and vitamins for her livestock.  In the future, Mary Jane would like to save enough money to send her children to college.

name: Asliya
description: This is Asliya. She is 46 years old. She is a hard-working woman with a great desire to get ahead. Her husband is a businessman. They have 3 children they love very much. They live together in her husband’s parent's house.She sells a variety of groceries. She stores her merchandise in a room in her house. She acquires her products in shopping centers in the city and makes periodic trips to accomplish her goal. She began working this way over 7 years ago because she needed to earn money. Currently, her partner helps her to purchase her merchandise.  As a result of the good results she is having, she wishes to increase her business by selling clothing in addition to groceries. This is her second loan with this aim and she is grateful for the  financial support in helping her to realize her plans. She awaits your kindness.

name: Haya
description: Haya, 19, is a young, single lady, who lives with her parents in Hashmeye. She has a small ‎grocery in her region, and her friends encouraged her to set up her business in this location. ‎ Haya is from a poor family and they live in a difficult financial situation. She could not ‎complete here education, but that does not keep Haya from standing up to these obstacles ‎without doing anything. Conversely, she started her own business and opened her small ‎grocery. She gets a good income from her work and she is very happy to work in this field.‎ ‎ Haya needs a loan to pay for her new products; she wants to purchase more food supplies ‎to offer a wider variety of products.‎ Haya dreams of getting her university degree, and to have more branches from her grocery.‎

name: Arturo
description: Quillabamba is the capital city of the La Convención province.  It is an important commercial center for the Lares and La Convención valleys.  Its primary business activities are the production of coca, coffee, cacao, and fruits.  Arturo is 28 years old, and he has one child.  He was born in the city of Quillabamba, La Convección province, Cusco, Perú.  However, he now lives in the city of Echarate, which is an hour from the city of Quillamba (La Convención, Cusco).    He has a small family business, which consists of selling hardware.  The business has been operational for one year.  It is going very well for him thanks to the effort he puts into his work.  On this occasion he needs a loan to buy materials and tools like guides, paint, carpenters’ glue, and other things.

name: Ana Lila
description: Ana Lila R. M. is 49 years old and lives in the municipality of Soyapango, one of the most important cities in the department of San Salvador.  She lives with her husband, who works as a bricklayer, and his mother and a daughter.  Ana has a business selling clothing for men and women, which is located in the center of San Salvador.  This is one of the best sites for trade, since many people pass through this place.  She requests a loan to buy a larger quantity of clothing, in various colors, styles and sizes, so that she can offer better quality garments to her customers.  For Ana it is very important to have better earnings since this will allow her to help her husband cover the household expenses. Ana has the advantage of having daily earnings, which is different from her husband, who must knock on doors to get some work, and for this reason she wants to improve her clothing business. Translated from Spanish by Lisa Grobar, Kiva Volunteer

name: Patience
description: Patience is 49 years-old and married with three children. Her husband is a teacher. She is very happy because her eldest child is already a graduate. She sells drinks, food and groceries at retail prices to her customers. She is a focused and hard worker. She has been in this business for a long time. She hopes for a loan amount of NGN 60,000 to purchase more groceries, food and drinks to sell. She is indeed grateful to all Kiva lenders.

name: Mercedes
description: Mercedes is 53 years old, single, and her children already live independently.  Mercedes lives in San Pedro, a medium-sized village in TambogranD..  This is an agricultural area located in Piura province, more than four hours from the city of Chiclayo, capital of Lambayeque region.  For the past eight years, Mercedes has been raising and selling young animals and poultry.  She raises the animals in an area behind her home and when they have reached a good level of development she offers them for sale to the traders who visit her area.  Mercedes would like to invest her loan for 1,000 Peruvian soles in buying more animals such as turkeys and laying hens.  With this investment, she hopes to expand her business and thereby make acceptable profits that will allow her to make some repairs to her home and cover her personal expenses.

name: Serapio
description: Serapio C. M. lives in his own home in the Pasankeri zone on the western side of the city of La Paz with his wife Yolanda Chambi and their five children.  Serapio is a laborer, currently working in the public sewer system as an employee of the municipality of this city and his wife is a homemaker. The loan requested is for the construction of a retaining wall that will help to stabilize their home which is located on a slope.  This is the fifth time that he has applied for a loan and the socio-economic analysis carried out qualifies him favorably to be able to access a loan.   Translated from Spanish by Aimee Sostowski, Kiva Volunteer

name: Noel
description: Noel is a small coffee producer in the northern zone of Nicaragua. He lives on his small farm with his wife and his five children ages 6 through 15.  All his life he has been associated with coffee production, and for the past 20 years he has worked in this field as his principle job and income for his family.    For this loan cycle, he is asking for credit to purchase and apply fertilizers that will permit him to guarantee the maintenance activities for his farm and to continue increasing the productivity of his land.   His dream is that his "family can live in dignity" through the income from his land, and that he can give his children the opportunity to grow in a safe and economically stable environment.

name: Souheir
description: Souheir is a 40-year-old married woman, the mother of two children. She has been working in selling women clothes since April 2009, in order to help her husband in making a living and covering their family's expenses.   Souheir is a hard worker who puts much effort into pleasing her customers and expanding her business. Today Souheir is applying for a loan for the first time from Kiva's partner, Al Majmoua, in order to increase her merchandise by buying a new autumn/winter shoes collection.  Souheir hopes that this loan will be a step forward toward expanding her business and increasing her customers.

name: Esther's Group
description: Esther‘s group is comprised of three hard-working women. Esther, on the left, is a 21 year-old who lives in the town of Kasubi in the Kampala central region of Uganda. She is single and has no children. Esther has had a small hotel for one year.           To help expand her business, Esther has requested a loan of 200,000 Ugandan Shillings from BRAC Uganda. The loan will be used to purchase food to cook for sale in the hotel. With the help of the loan from BRAC, Esther hopes to generate greater profits and pay school fees for herself. In the future, Esther hopes to study and get some knowledge of the Red Cross. Esther is a member of BRAC’s Empowerment and Livelihood for Adolescents (ELA) program, which has helped her prospects by imcreasing capital for her business.

name: Dúo La Promesa De Dios Group
description: The La Promesa de Dios Duo. Bartolome is a very hardworking person. From 5 in the morning every day he is working in the fields already. He is a farmer and with this activity alone he has been able to get ahead, but he earns very little because the money isn't enough to buy seeds and fertilizer and that is why they plant very little. Now with this loan he is asking for, they will invest more in planting a little more and improve their earnings. This is the third loan he has asked for from Kiva  and he hasn't made any late payments. He hopes that you can help him again with the loan he has asked for.

name: Norhoda
description: Norhoda is a married woman with eight children. She is 37 years old and has five children are presently in school. Norhoda is a very hard working entrepreneur.Norhoda has a buy-and-sell gasoline business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for 7 years. She requested a PHP 15,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy additional containers of gasoline to sell.Norhoda would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Victor
description: Victor lives in the city of Pucallpa. He is engaged in agriculture, an occupation through which he has been able to support his 2 children, who are now grown. Victor loves what he does. Currently he has planted corn, and each day he dedicates himself to cultivation for around 9 hours. Victor believes that his crops are coming along well because he is responsible and, above all, careful.   Victor is grateful to Kiva lenders, as thanks to the help they have provided he will be able to purchase fertilizer and manure and pay for irrigation, among other things, with which he can improve his crops and ensure a good harvest. This way, he will improve his income and continue fighting to realize his greatest dream: buying a vehicle to transport his harvest.

name: Gideon
description: 43-year-old Gideon went to school until the third grade. He lives with his three children, who are 11 and 6 and 5 months old. His children are studying in the "Basic Education" level (this is the equivalent of primary and secondary school in Ghana). His wife, who works selling fish, has sold fish from the lake for the past 7 years.Gideon knows a great deal about catching and selling fish. He has worked at the trade for the past 7 years and he learned it from his father, who insisted on teaching him the trade so that he could have a steady source of income. With the help of his wife he also works growing grain.He needs the loan to buy fishing nets to better catch fish.Gideon hopes that his children will have greater economic stability and also that his business will allow him to provide for his family.

name: Sophat
description: A 45-year-old man named Sophat lives in Kandal province’s Kandal Stoeng district in Cambodia. He is married and blessed with four children, one of whom is still under his responsibility. Sophat and his wife earn a living through farming rice. To add more income to the family, Sophat also works as a construction worker. He is a second-time borrower with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). The first loan that he obtained and successfully paid back has enabled him to improve his standard of living and better meet the family’s needs.   He is now seeking a USD 1,000 loan to run a new business, which is a pig-raising business, by purchasing piglets to raise. Sophat will also utilize his requested loan to dig a well in order to sufficiently supply water to his rice field. After receiving and wisely using the loan, Sophat hopes to grow healthy and fruitful rice crop yields as well as raise fat and healthy pigs.

name: Riza
description: Riza is a married woman with three children, two of whom attend school. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Riza is 46 years old.  Riza has a fishing business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional fish net and gasoline, as well as to pay for maintenance for aspects of her business.  Riza has been in this business for 15 years. She would like to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Tahreer
description: Tahreer is a young woman from Rafah city in Gaza Strip. She is engaged and preparing for her wedding in a few months. Tahreer's fiance is a Palestinian National Authority employee. Tahreer took out a loan from FATEN in order to help her fiance prepare for the wedding. She will use the $700 loan to purchase bedroom furniture.  Tahreer's father appears in the picture here as she is a religious woman.

name: Nuufou
description: Nuufou I. is a 59-year-old woman living in the town of Laulii Maagila.  She is married and has 5 adult -aged children.  To make a living, Nuufou owns & operates a business venture in the retail sector selling home products.  While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling personal home products to tourists and local community members.    In 2009, Nuufou joined SPBD to gain access to financial services to help improve  her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Nuufou is now requesting a new loan of 1000 WST which will be used to purchase raw materials needed to make products for sale.  The loan will be the 1st loan taken out by the borrower from SPBD.  Nuufou plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business  to improve the general living conditions of the borrower's family.  About SPBD: SPBD's mission is to improve the quality of life of people living in poverty in the poor island nations of the South Pacific.  SPBD's philosophy of lending is based on a respect for each individual's innate human ingenuity, drive and self esteem.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Queen Estherkade Group
description: Theresa is thirty years old. She is married and has given birth to four children and all are in school. She lives with her husband and children in a rented apartment in Kade. Kade is a farming/commercial town in the Eastern Region of Ghana. Theresa is a trader. She sells slippers. She is the leader of a trust bank group called Queen Esther. Most of the group members are either into trading or farming activities. The group requestsa loan to procure goods in bulk to expand their businesses. Theresa, the group leader is in the middle of the photograph. It is their desire to give their children the best education they can afford.

name: Pov
description: Pov, aged 41, lives in a rural village in the Borseth district and has four children. She and her husband are rice farmers. She has been in this business for 23 years, earning about US$5 each day after daily expenses.   Pov is the first-cycled client with VisionFund. Now she is applying for a loan to pay for her son’s University course. She hopes that her son will get a good job after graduation.

name: Joseph
description: Joseph is 48 years old, married to Alice, and supports his family. He has run a poultry farm for the last three years, making a monthly income of KES. 16,000.   This is his first loan of KES. 75,000 from KADET LTD, with which he plans to buy additional chicks to sell at maturity. The anticipated profits will help him start a money transfer facility.    His future dream is to improve his family's living standards.

name: Margaret
description: Margaret is married to a taxi driver; they have three children and all their children go to school.  She doesn’t take care of additional family members.  She owns a stall in Nakulabye selling second-hand clothes.  She wants to use this loan to buy more bales of second-hand clothes. She buys bales of clothes from Owino market, one of the busiest markets in Uganda, and uses public transport to and from shopping.   Margaret has been in this clothing business for years.  She sells to all categories of people, both retail and wholesale. Margaret goes for shopping once a week. She works six days a week.  Her business challenges include seasonality and transportation  of bales of clothes from Owino to her stall in Nakulabye.  She is aspiring of improving her standard of living and even starting importing clothes from Dubai.  She decided to work with MCDT because she wanted additional capital.   She resides in and rents a three-roomed house and the family has access to electricity but no piped water.  Her monthly expenses includes school fees, food, and rent.

name: Sopheap
description: Sopheap, a 34-year-old fruit seller, and her husband, a  sugar cane seller, earn a combined daily income of $18. They have two children, one a 14-year-old worker, and the other a 6-year-old student. Sopheap's monthly expenses consist of $83 for food, $15 for electricity, $50 for rent, $15 for school fees, $45 for transportation and $50 for other expenses.   She is now requesting a loan of $1200 to buy more fruit to sell, her ultimate goal being to save enough money to buy a small store and to send her child to university to study law.

name: Trinidad
description: At 48, Trinidad is getting older. She wants to expand her hog raising and add a rice-selling business. Trinidad has been running a hog raising business for two years. She wants to maintain it and increase her income to save some of it for her future and her family. Trinidad's husband is a rice mill operator together with their relatives.   Trinidad and her husband are blessed with four children who are in college and high school. Trinidad's husband's income goes for their household and daily food. Thus, she is asking for a loan of P6,000 to buy feed for her pigs and to start selling rice in their village.

name: Bernarda
description: Bernarda has switched from selling snacks to selling "tabliya" (processed cacao). Her business is doing well as she worked hard to perfect the quality of her "tabliya". With her husband's help and her children's support, she has maximized her profits and keep pursuing her goals for the good of her family.   The reason why she availed herself of another loan from PMPC is to buy more kilos of raw and dried cacao seeds for her business. Today, Bernarda is able to help others do retailing business from her "tabliya" and they also earn money for their own family.

name: Vannet
description: Vannet (in the photo) is 32 years old and her husband Yat is 39 years old. They have been married since 1994 and have four children: one son and three daughters. One is in school and other three are still young. The family lives in a village across Mekong River about twenty kilometers from Phnom Penh City.   Vannet sells grocery items at home, while her husband is a construction worker. Vannet wants to generate income by investing with her mother to buy sugar cane under contract for sale.   Hence Vannet is asking for her fist loan of $550 to help her capital.

name: Yamili Zamir
description: Yamali, 28, lives in Ica, Peru. Ica is a warm and welcoming city, which has many tourist attractions like "The Huacachina Lagoon". Yamali is a young woman eager to get ahead, which is how, with a lot of effort, she was able to get a degree in primary education. As a result, she was able to get a job at a school in her city, where she currently works. She works around 8 hours a day and the fruit of her labor, she is able to help her parents with household expenses. She believes she is doing well at work because she is very charismatic with the children, and above all, she is very patient.  Yamali is very grateful to Kiva lenders because with their help, she can make improvements to her home, which is made of adobe. She will reinforce the walls with good-quality material and with this improvement she will be able to have a better quality of life and above all, give her family a better quality of life and keep striving to realize her dream of having a master's degree in education.

name: Rapheal
description: Rapheal is a thirty-year-old married man with two children. He lives in Kasese, Uganda. He has been in the soft-drink business for the last six years, and his major hardship is price fluctuations.  Rapheal intends to use the loan requested to purchase a plot of land. His business goal is to buy a plot and build commercial houses.

name: Janet
description: Janet is a 28-year-old married woman. She has two children. She describes herself to be focused. She operates a tailor shop. She has been involved in this business for three years. She describes her biggest business challenge to be capital.   She will use the 25,000 Kenyan shillings loan to purchase two sewing machines. Her business goal is to own a tailoring school within five years. She hopes that in the future, she may use the profits from her business to pay her children's school fees.  She would also like to buy a plot of land and build.   This is her second loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: Sabira
description: Sabira Y. was born in 1979 and lives in the Khirdalan settlement.   Sabira has been in the bakery business for two years. She bakes bread and biscuits, and needs a loan of 970 AZN to buy products needed for baking.

name: Concepcion De Maria
description: Concepcion yearns to work and be a good businesswoman. She is currently in her last year of studies to earn a degree in hotel and tourism business administration.  She is 21 years old and her mother helps her with her university expenses.  With a lot of hard work, Concepcion was able to scrape together the little bit of savings her mother gave her, and with the support of the loan she is requesting, she will be able to finish paying for the course she needs for her degree and achieve her goal of working in her profession.

name: Umbelina
description: Umbelina is 38 years old.  She is married and has 4 children, 2 of  them are in school.  Her husband is a farmer.   Umbelina has a kiosk in front of her home to supply people in her village with basic goods. She will purchase additional supplies for her store with the loan, including flour, oil, soap, and animals like chickens and pigs.   Umbelina started this business in 2006 with a working capital of $300.   She lives in her house made of bamboo for the walls and zinc for the roof. She wants to send her children to study in higher education and wants to open a big store in the future.

name: Elsa
description: Elsa is 62 years old and married with five children. She is in the agricultural business, farming rice in the Philippines. Elsa has been in this business for 30 years and earns additional income from pig fattening. She is borrowing 10,000 PHP through NWTF to buy fertilizer and other farm supplies.Elsa is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save money to expand her business.

name: Germana
description: A $600 loan is offered to Germana to improve her business. She is married with five children and opened her kiosk in 2009 with her own working capital. She will use the loan to buy stock to keep in her store like cigarettes, milk, sugar, salt, water, oil, bread and noodles. She is generating a good income from selling.  She has been thinking of running a big business after years of involving herself in doing business. She is living in a town with her family and her husband is a farmer.

name: Triunfadoras Leales De Motupe Group
description: Rosa is 50, married, and has two children who still depend on her.   She has been with Edaprospo for ten years, and sells candy in general, such as cookies, soft drinks, lollipops, etc. She has been in this business for ten years, which she started in order to help her children get the education they need, so that they can succeed in life.  With her hard work and effort she has managed to open a business, and has been able to provide her children with a proper education.   Currently, she is allocating her income to cover expenses for food and transportation, while her husband covers the cost of water, electricity, and telephone.   Her plan for the future is to expand her business, and finish building her home.  She used her loan to buy merchandise.   Rosa belongs to the "Triunfadores Leales de Motupe" (The Loyal Winners of Motupe) communal bank, which is made up of seven people. She has been the president for one year. It was formed with the objective of each member developing themselves, and "winning" in their business and in their life. This is the reason why they gave this name to the group.

name: Julia
description: Doña Julia is from Ciudad Victoria, Tamaulipas. For the past 20 years, she's lived in Monterrery, Nuevo León. She is divorced and lives with one of her children, who helps her at her grocery store, where she has worked for 15 years. She started the business in order to provide for her children after her divorce. This business has grown gradually. They began with small quantities of merchandise and now are a store that can serve the entire neighborhood. Doña Julia is a very hard working woman, and on the weekends she sells tacos and hamburgers in her home. At the moment Doña Julia needs a loan for $475, which she will use to buy merchandise so that she can offer her customers a greater variety of goods and increase her sales. Julia needs your support; please help her build up her business.    Translated from Spanish by Susanna Heinz, Kiva Volunteer.  Doña Julia es originaria de Ciudad Victoria, Tamaulipas, y desde hace 20 años vive en  Monterrey, Nuevo León. Ella es divorciada y vive con uno de sus hijos que le ayuda a atender su negocio de abarrotes, en el que ya tiene 15 años trabajando, lo inició por la necesidad de sostener a sus hijos después de divorciarse. Este negocio ha ido creciendo poco a poco,  comenzaron con pequeñas cantidades de mercancía y ahora es una tienda que puede cubrir las necesidades de todo el barrio. Doña Julia es una mujer muy trabajadora, y los fines de semana vende en su casa tortas, tacos, hamburguesas.   En estos momentos Doña Julia necesita de un préstamo por la cantidad de $ 475 dólares que utilizara en compra de mercancía para que su negocio siga creciendo, poder ofrecerles a sus clientes una mayor variedad e incrementar sus ventas. Julia necesita de tu apoyo y cariño, forma parte del crecimiento de este negocio y decídete a ayudar.

name: Carolino
description: Mr. Carolino R. is fifty years old and married with six children. He lives in Labuyo, Tangub City. Four of his children are married with their own families and the other two are dependents attending school.   Carolino has a chemical wholesale and repackaging business – he works with hypochloric acid and chlorine. His wife assists in repackaging. They started the business with an initial capital of just $17. They have recently started another line of business selling garlic and onions. They have many loyal customers and friends, and their distribution area is expanding.   Carolino was interested in joining the Kiva Partner, PAGLAUM MPC, for more than just access to loans – he also values the motivation to save that they inspire in their members.  He is applying for a loan in order to add to his capital for both of his businesses. He hopes to send his children to college and renovate his house in the future.

name: Faustina
description: This member belongs to the "Las Triunfadoras" communal bank.  The bank is located in the district of Andahuaylillas in the Quispicanchis province in the department of Cusco.  Faustina is 39 years old and married.  She has 5 children.  She alternates her daily activities with her business selling handcrafts.  She sells sweaters, bags, necklaces, and earrings, and she also works husking corn from time to time.  She sells the handcrafts in the central plaza in Andahuaylillas, and through this business she is moving her children forward.  She wants to expand and improve the handcrafts business.  She is asking for a loan to buy wholesale handcrafts.    She is happy because of the loan, and she is committed to paying back the installments on time.

name: Otamurod
description: Otamurod is a young, energetic man.  He is married and has one child.  His wife is a homemaker and spends her time rearing their offspring.  She also helps her husband run their business.  For five years, Otamurod has worked in farming, growing crops like potatoes, grains, etc.  He has supplemental income from working with livestock.  He works hard from early morning until late in the night in order to save money to build a home.  He lives with his family in an a small, old house.  He is asking for a loan of 1,000 USD to buy mineral fertilizers and fuel for his land.  He awaits your kindness and relies on your mercy.

name: Ma. Erma
description: Ma. Erma is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a candy making business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 40,000 through NWTF in order to buy ingredients for her candy making business.  Ma. Erma successfully paid back her previous loan, and is now requesting a new loan to further build her business.  NWTF is re-listing Ma. Erma's business profile again in support of her efforts to secure the future of her family.

name: Nellis
description: Nellis is 22 years old and lives with her family in the Muzarabani district. She runs a small grocery business to provide for her family. Nellis is requesting a Kiva loan to expand her shop and increase her business. She plans to use her profits to build a house and to help support her family. Nellis volunteers at the local high school as a Camfed Learner Guide and teaches students about active citizenship. The interest on her social-interest loan will be repaid through her weekly volunteer work at the school.

name: Estrella
description: Estrella is 55 years old and is married with five children.  She earns a living by farming vegetables in the Philippines.  Estrella has been farming vegetables for 5 years and also earns additional income from raising pigs.   She has successfully paid back her previous loan and is now requesting a new loan to further build her business.  Estrella is borrowing PHP 24000 through NWTF to purchase fertilizers and other farm supplies.   She is working tirelessly towards the attainment of her dream: to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Condrada
description: Condrada is a married woman with six children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Condrada is 50 years old and has one child who is still in school.  Condrada has a food vending business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 12,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy ingredients like flour, butter, sugar, etc. for her food production business.  Condrada has been in this business for eight years. She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Simona Del Carmen
description: Simona continues investing in her business, a small store that she has stocked over the years and that she is now devoting herself to full-time. For years she has sold clothing and she has expanded in part due to funding she obtained through  loan cycles from Afodenic.  Her children are now married and she has their support since they help her in the business and they all support one another as a family because they cannot rely on economic and moral support from their father.  With this new loan, Simona will buy basic grain products such as rice by the quintal (hundred pound weight), beans, sugar, drums of oil, Maseca corn flour, boxes of washing powder, Axe detergent, dairy products, soft drinks and sweets, thereby keeping her customers satisfied.

name: Virly
description: Virly is 60 years old, married, and has four children to provide for. She runs a ready-to-wear business to earn a living.  She has been in this business for two years already, and it has been a source of income for the family because it helps them a lot in providing their family needs.  She aims for a better income; that's why she borrowed a loan to buy more ready-to-wear items to sell. Having more sales, she can generate more income.  With profits from her business, Virly wants to invest in another business in the future.

name: Ricardo
description: Ricardo is married and has 3 children, 1 of whom attends school.  He owns the home where he lives with his family and does not support anyone else. He operates heavy machinery for a private company and he also has his own business.  With this loan he plans to purchase products (beer, rice, sugar, soft drinks, wine, etc.) to increase the stock of merchandise at his store.  In the future he wants to add on to his house and expand his store.  For this reason he promises to make his payments as scheduled so that he can request additional loans from Hluvuku.  His challenge is a lack of funds that prevents him from achieving all of this as quickly as possible.

name: Marilou
description: Forty-six-year old Marilou sells snack foods to the locals in her place. She sells biscuits and prepares banana cue (deep fried bananas in caramelized sugar), bibingka (rice cakes) and puto (steamed rice cakes).Marilou is married and has nine children, six of whom are still attending school. Her husband is a carpenter.Marilou would like to improve her daily production in order to gain higher earnings. She has requested a loan to invest in ingredients like flour, sugar, evaporated milk, and vanilla. These could help her prepare various snack foods to sell. In that way, she could able to set aside some of the profit to invest in other possible sources of income.She hopes that she will be able to continue providing the needs of her growing children for brighter futures.

name: Sohibchon
description: Sohibchon works as a handyman at a building materials establishment in the city of Isfary.  This is his primary job and the way he supports his family. Sohibchon is 27 years old, married and has two children.  They live with his parents. Several months ago his mother was diagnosed with an eye illness, and needs an operation.  Sohibchon has saved a small amount of money, but needs 1000 somoni to complete the full treatment.  After consulting with MicroInvest, he decided to take out a loan.Translated from Russian by Joyce ., Kiva Volunteer

name: Lilia
description: Lilia Lilia is 50 years old, a widowed mother of six children. She is a very hard working entrepreneur.   Lilia has a fish vending business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 8,000 loan amount through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. in order to buy more fish to sell in her food stall.  Lilia has been in this business for twenty years. In the future, Lilia would like to save enough money to expand her business and repair her family's home.

name: Flor Semira
description: Flor Semira is fifty-three years old and is married.  She lives with her children and husband in Chillanes, in the province of Bolivar.    She is a member of Arrayapamba Communal Bank, which is made up of twelve members who are all from the same community.  It takes twenty-five minutes to get to the office from their community.  The members make a living in agriculture, raising animals, and in trade.    Flor Semira makes a living in agriculture, in growing corn, beans, and blackberries, and also in raising pigs and chickens.  She is requesting the loan in order to buy urea, insecticide, herbicide, rice-based animal feed, dense corn, corn-based animal feed, and two chickens.  She buys all her items in Chillanes, and she sells her products in Montalvo.  Her dream is to improve her conditions and to have her own small house.   The challenges she faces are: low production and low prices for her products.    In her free time, she likes to visit relatives, watch television, and enjoy the community and Carnaval festivals.

name: Amalia
description: Amalia is a married woman with three children. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur. Amalia is 55 years old and has one child still in school.Amalia has a tailoring business in the Philippines. Amalia requested a PHP 10,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy garments, thread, and other supplies needed in her business.Amalia has been in this business for 10 years. In the future, Amalia would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Manuel Jose
description: Manuel José C. C. is 58 years old, married, and lives with his wife and children in San Miguel in the Tangara area, which belongs to the Province of Bolívar.  The name of this communal bank is “Campesinos Unidos” and it is located in the Tangara area, 15 minutes from the Canton of San Miguel.  The members of the communal bank work in farming and in business.  Manuel works in the field of agriculture, especially in planting corn to sell dried.  He buys his products in San Miguel and sells them at the market in the same canton.  He is requesting the loan to purchase farming supplies, fertilizers and seeds.  The loan will help his family business, as he will produce more and he needs to work to pay off the debt.  His dream is to have animals to sell.  The challenges he faces are pests and diseases among his crops.  He likes to play sports and work the land.

name: Mercy
description: Mercy is 30 years old and is married with 2 children. She sells newspapers. She loves this business, which she started in 2001.   Mercy is a LAPO client. She needs loan of N40,000 to purchase more newspapers to sell. She says "thank you" to all Kiva lenders.

name: Maria
description: María's separated and has a daughter.  She's a merchant who has earned a living for more than 12 years selling merchandise as a street vendor in the area of Formosa, Argentina.  In addition to her sales, María also has a small grocery store where she works.  With these jobs she's helping her family and getting ahead.  María's requesting this loan to buy items to sell as well as supplies for her store such as food, beverages, and other products.

name: María Elena Auxiliadora
description: María is 59 years old. Some months ago, she opened her own business in order to improve her financial condition and fill an unmet need in the area. She opened a cafeteria to the public and works there from 6 in the morning until 9 at night every day. She assures us that the business is in a growth stage and has been widely accepted in the area where it is located. Today she needs to buy ingredients to stock up on inventory and guarantee an adequate service. That is why she is asking for a loan to make such an investment.  She dreams of owning her own home and guaranteeing her family a better quality of life.

name: Yet
description: Yet who is 46 years old and is married. She earns a living through growing rice and cassava in her local area of Kampong Cham province. She has been involved in farming  for twenty-eight years. The challenge to her farming business is that the price of her cassava is decreasing in the market while cost of business such as fuel and organic fertilizer is high. She decided to apply for a loan from VisionFund to support her farming business by purchasing organic fertilizer to boost crop yields and purchasing pesticide to save her crop from threat of insects. She hopes to gain higher yields so as to meet her family’s needs and upgrade their standard of living.

name: Phylis
description: Phylis is a married woman. She has three children. She describes herself to be honest. She operates a farm where she grows tea. She has been involved in this business for six years. Her business is located in a strategic place and her primary customers are large scale. She describes her biggest business challenge to be the lack of finances. She will use the Kes 30,000 loan to buy farm inputs. This is her first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank.

name: Daisy
description: Daisy is 38 years old and married with six children.She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 15,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional items to sell like sugar, eggs, rice, charcoal, soap, oil, shampoo, groceries, etc. Daisy has borrowed and paid back 23 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for six years and also earns an income from pig fattening.She aspires to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Janty
description: Janty M. is 42 years old and is married. Her husband is a soldier. She has six children, and three of them go to school. Janty is currently in the business of selling food in a restaurant and is requesting a loan to stock more bags of food such as beans, rice, etc. With the extra profits from her loan, she hopes to be able to build a house.

name: Consuelo
description: Consuelo is a 49 years old married woman, and a hard working mother of a little girl who's 1 year and 8 months old. She lives with her family in the district of Cayalti, an hour from Chiclayo, in Peru. She makes a living by selling chicha (a typical beverage in that region) and ceviche, activity that she has been performing for the past 7 years. Her husband works as a farm labourer and doesn't make much money, so Consuelo wants to expand her business in order to contribute more to the household and give her daughter a better life.  She's always had many clients for being such a good cook and the kindness with which she treats everyone. She is hoping to start selling beer to increase her profits and is asking for a U$350 loan in order to make that a reality. Her dream is to have her own restaurant serving typical food for tourists.Translated from Spanish by Mariana Dauwe, Kiva Volunteer

name: Petronila
description: Petronila was born in Urubamba but currently lives in Ollantaytambo.  She’s 74 years old and is a hardworking enterprising woman.  Petronila works in Ollantaytambo, selling food from her small store, located in her home.  She’s been doing this for several years and things are going well for her, thanks to the effort she puts forth in her work.  He needs this loan in order to buy merchandise such as sacks of rice and sugar, cooking oil, and other things.  Petronila is grateful for the opportunity given her through this medium and she promises to make her payments on time.  She’s a member of the Señor de Choquekillca” communal bank of the Arariwa Association.

name: Badam Ghorband Group
description: Ashaqallah is the group leader of 'Badam Ghorband' group. There are six members in this group. All of them would like to receive money for their businesses. They have requested a group loan of 60,000 Afghani.  Ashaqallah and M. Nasar want to take a loan for their businesses selling wood. They want to make  their shops larger. And Farid and Abdull Qadeir want to take a loan for their restaurant business.  They want to buy new chairs and tables for their restaurant. Bibi Sharen and Meir Ahmad want to take a loan for their carpentry shops. They need the loan for purchasing wood and want to buy a new machine for their carpentry businesses.

name: Rosemarie
description: Rosemarie is 42 years old and married with two children. She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 22,000 loan through NWTF in order to purchase more groceries to sell.  She has borrowed and repaid ten loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for eleven years and also earns an income from food vending.  Rosemarie aspires to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Jeiko Porave Rekavo Group
description: “Jeiko Porave Rekavo” means, in search of a better future, and this group was formed for that reason. This is their 5th Women's Committee cycle, and they have all committed to work and help each other to get ahead. They are participating in the quest to eliminate poverty, as two of the 18 women live below the poverty line.    Del Carmen is part of this group.  She sells very good clothing, and has a good variety to choose from, which her customers like very much. Thanks to the high quality and good prices, she has been making her way. She says that the secret is to always have a good variety of clothing in stock and that is what attracts customers. This is why she is requesting a loan - so that she can buy a variety of clothing which will allow her to continue to sell, obtain more clients, and increase her income.

name: Emmanuel
description: Emmanuel D. is a 27-year-old man. He is married with one child. His child is in school. Emmanuel is a Christian dedicated to the service of his maker, God, and a very resourceful father. His daily dream is to be able to work hard to provide his child with quality education for a better future career.   Emmanuel's wife is a trader. He and his wife live together at Takroase in the eastern region of Ghana. He owns and operates a grocery shop in a busy local market and sells items like rice, sugar, vegetable oil, bottled water, canned food, peanuts, evaporated milk etc.   Emmanuel needs loan support to expand his business. With the loan, he wants to buy more bags of rice and sugar, cartons of evaporated milk, cartons of vegetable oil, etc., to increase his stock. He hopes to save more to finance his child's school fees.  Emmanuel belongs to a village bank called Divine and would be grateful for your loan support.

name: Faustina
description: Faustina is thirty-six years old. She is divorced and has one child in school. She lives with her child in a rented apartment in Axim. Axim is along the coast in the western region of Ghana and fishing is the major occupation of the people there.  Faustina is a seamstress by profession and has four apprentices in training. She wants a loan to buy many kinds of fabrics and other sewing accessories to be able to better serve her clients. Faustina has been in business for ten years.

name: Pedro
description: Pedro is a 59-year-old married man living in Trinidad, Bohol. He has been operating a motorcycle taxi business for a year, earning 2,000 PHP per month.  Pedro is asking for a loan to purchase tires and motor oil. This will help improve his business. In the future, Pedro hopes to have more motorcycles for his business.

name: Tupu
description: Tupu is a 56-year-old mother with eight children. Her business is selling taro at the market to earn a living. She has had this experience for more than a year. Tupu requested a loan to buy chemicals, a backpack sprayer, taro roots (seedlings), banana tubes (seedlings), a wheelbarrow, rake, and shovel, to help her run the business. She will use her profit to expand her business. Tupu became a member of SPBD in 2011.

name: James
description: As a married parent with two children, James, age 36, works hard to support his family. He buys vegetables, such as onions and carrots, from local farmers and takes them to the city market.   James is taking a loan to expand his business by adding more stock to his vegetable business, which he has been operating for the last two years. He has gained more customers in his enterprise and needs to ensure a consistent supply. He hopes that his business will flourish and go a long way in helping him to support his family by providing food and clothing.  James is happy for the support from Kiva and its lenders.

name: Chadi
description: Chadi is a 22-year-old single man from Lebanon. Chadi has owned an electronics and home products shop since 2007. Chadi is proud of the high quality of his work.   Today, Chadi, for the first time, is requesting a loan from Al Majmoua to purchase merchandise and install new stands in his shop. He hopes to keep on improving his business.

name: Felicidad
description: Felicidad B. is from the village of Daan Lungsod, Gingoog City. She is 40 years old. Felicidad is widowed and has 3 school-aged children. To make a living, Felicidad owns and operates a specialized retail store. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from buying and selling dried fish and vegetables like string beans and eggplants in the local community. Felicidad has been engaged in her business for over 3 years and earns approximately 5,000 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2010, Felicidad joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Felicidad has successfully repaid a previous loan of 5,000 PHP from HSPFI. This previous loan was used to to purchase additional inventory and working capital. Felicidad is requesting a new loan of 7,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional vegetables like squash and carrots. This loan will be the 2nd loan taken out by Felicidad from HSPFI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of the accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, we created this template for our field staff to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Venia
description: Venia is 39, is married and has three children. Her husband is a farm worker and has experience in managing his crops. The family lives in their own home in Cabisera 7, which is within the rural area of the municipality of Ilagan. They have electrical service to their residence.  For the past six years, Venia has raised and fattened pigs. She then slaughters them and sells them at the local market. Together, Venia and her husband are able to cover expenses.  Venia is requesting a 10,000 PHP loan from ASKI, which she will use to buy feed for the pigs and repair their sties, as well as repair her own home. She will be able to improve her family’s standard of living and satisfy more of their needs.

name: Rose
description: Rose is 45 years old. She is not married and supports no one. She has been in the farming business for the past two years and has applied for her second loan from KADET after paying her previous loan well. She intends to use the loan to buy a cow. With anticipated profits, she plans to buy a heifer.  In the near future, Rose hopes to become the top farmer in her area.

name: Ledilou
description: Ledilou is from the village of Purok 4, Villaflor, Oroquieta City. She is 35 years old.  Ledilou is married and has three school-aged children.  To make a living, Ledilou owns and operates a retail store (Sari-sari store).  Ledilou is about ten years into this business and earns approximately 3,000 PHP a month for this activity.  In 2005, Ledilou joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities.    Ledilou has successfully repaid a previous loan from PMPC amounting 12,000 PHP. Ledilou is requesting a new loan of 14,900 PHP which will be used to purchase additional inventory and working capital. This loan will be the tenth loan taken out by Ledilou from PMPC.  She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to financially support immediate members of her family.   About PMPC:  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.   *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Chea
description: Chea (in the photo) is thirty-three years old and his wife Phalla is thirty-six. They live in a village about fifteen kilometers from Phnom Penh, the capital city of Cambodia. They have been married since 2002 and have two children: one son and one daughter. One attends school and another one is still young.  Chea is a construction worker, while his wife is a garment worker. He currently lives with his grandmother because he does not have his own house. Hence, he is requesting his first loan of $700 to build a house to live in.

name: Bilha
description: Bilha is 31 years old, married, and a mother of two children. For the past seven years, she has earned a living by offering point-to-point transport services in Malindi, from which she earns a monthly income of KES 15,550.   She was introduced to KADET LTD by a credit officer and is applying for her third loan of KES 60,000. Bilha will use the loan to service and repair her motorbike.  She will use the profits to pay for her children's school fees while continuing to run her business. Bilha's goal for the future is to continue growing her business, so that she can improve her family's financial stability.

name: Manvel
description: Manvel is a farmer from the Shirak region. He is a 46-year-old father of four children. Manvel lives with his wife, son and three daughters. He keeps livestock, which currently includes 2 cows, 2 bulls, 15 chickens and 15 colonies of bees. Manvel also owns agricultural land where he cultivates wheat and potatoes.  As the family is big, it is very difficult for Manvel to cover basic costs. Agriculture helps him to gather income which is hardly enough for covering the family's daily costs. As Manvel has no sufficient financial means to expand his farm, he has applied for this loan.   With the loan's help, Manvel will purchase forage for feeding the livestock and potato seeds for cultivation. This will enable him to gather more income and ensure a better life for his family.

name: Helen
description: Helen I. is 45 years old and is married with 4 children. She lives in Benin City, Nigeria. Helen travels to Lagos and Onitsha to buy jewelry and traditional women's dresses, known as "wrappers,"  to sell to the people in her community. She learned this business in 2 years and she started her own business in 1982.   Helen needs a loan of $1, 200 USD to buy more wrappers and jewelry to sell. She has been a LAPO client for the past 5 years.

name: Cerenia
description: Cerenia is 59 years old, married and has four children. Cerenia is in the agricultural business, raising pigs in the Philippines. Cerenia requested a PHP 8,000 loan through NWTF in order to buy feed and vitamins for her pigs.Cerenia has been raising pigs for five years now, and has borrowed seven times in the past from NWTF to sustain it.In the future, Cerenia would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Getrudis
description: Getrudis is 60 years old and has two school-aged children who depend on her.  She lives in the southern zone of the Cochabamba province.  Her children attend school and are very good students.  She was able to do all of this, thanks to the little store that she was able to set up.  Her husband passed away 15 years ago.  Getrudis is a hardworking person with a desire to get her children ahead.  She also raises pigs and chickens, which she sells in the same zone where she lives.  She needs this loan so that she can build a pen for her pigs and chickens.

name: Fotima
description: Fotima B. is 52 years and is married.  She is a wholesaler of candy.  She started her business in 2003 with a small quantity of confectionary products.  Today, she sells her products at the wholesale market “Solor” in Dushanbe.  Everyday customers come from nearby areas in order to purchase her products. Fotima purchases her products from suppliers from Turkey and Iran and sometimes from firms.  She has a lot of customers.  Fotima’s product assortment includes candy made in Russia, Iran and Turkey, as well as candy made locally.   In order to increase her product assortment (purchase different types of candy), Fotima would like to take out a loan for 4100 somoni which she will pay back over 10 months.   Translated from Russian by Sabina Holzman, Kiva Volunteer

name: Riaz
description: Riaz is a 29-year-old woman and a mother of five children. She is doing a business of animal purchasing and sales for the last two years. Currently, she has two buffaloes and two goats.   With the help of her husband, she is running a successful business to lead them to a decent life. Riaz purchases baby cows and goats from the local market at a wholesale rate and then sells them to the people in her community. She is working hard to meet her daily household expenses.   Riaz has requested a loan of PKR 30,000/- to buy more baby goats, to expand her business. She is currently in her third loan cycle with Kashf Foundation and she has a good credit history. She is hopeful of getting an increase in her income by targeting more customers.   Riaz hopes to grow her business and dreams of giving a good and quality education to her children, through all her hard work in her business.

name: Neema's Tuimarike Group
description: Neema is a 20 year old single woman. She has been selling clothes since 2006. She works daily from 8am to 6pm and can earn a monthly profit of about $35 from her sales.   Neema is now requesting a loan to buy more clothes for the expansion of her business. She will share this loan with her subgroup member Ridhwana.

name: Sophorn
description: Living in a rural area located in the Sa Ang district of Kandal province, Sophorn is 30 years old and married with two children, both of whom are dependent on her and still in school.   To support her family, she has been selling fish in the local area for two years, while her husband also supplements his family’s income by working for others for a fee. From the current business, she can earn about US $7 per day and can save about US $2 each day after deducting daily expenses.   This is the third microloan for Sophorn with Kiva’s partner, VisionFund. The past loans have helped her better support her current business.   Now she is applying for a loan with VisionFund of US $1,100. She is going to use this loan to buy more fish to resell. With this loan, she hopes to increase a large income from the current business so as to better her living condition and keep her children in school.

name: Kasichana
description: Kasichana is a married woman with three children, all of whom attend school. She lives at her house that has neither electricity nor piped water.She has operated a butcher shop business for the past five years, selling goat meat. She faces a major challenge of transportation in her business.With the loan she is requesting, she wants to purchase stock of goats to slaughter and get meat for resale. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Rosa Marissa
description: Rosa Marissa is 42 years old, married and has three children.  She earns a living by raising hogs in the Philippines. Rosa Marissa has been in this business for two years and also earns additional income from a general store.  Rosa Marissa is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to purchase feeds and vitamins for her pigs.  She is working tirelessly towards the attainment of her dream: to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Maria Fidelina
description: Maria Fedelina lives in the Walter Ferreti neighborhood located in the capital city of Managua.  She is 54 years old and is married to Nestor Zeledon who is a supervisor. They have four children.  Maria Fidelina currently dedicates herself to the sale of lottery tickets and natural products.  She has been in this business for more than 13 years together with her husband.  They put a lot of effort into their work in order to help their family and improve their children's quality of life.  She is asking for a loan in the amount of $525 which she will repay in six months.  The loan will be used to purchase more natural products and lottery tickets. This will allow her to increase the number of clients and her income so that she can keep improving her family's life. Translated from Spanish by Cindy Manzo, Kiva Volunteer

name: Baheja
description: Baheja D/O A. Najib lives in District 6 of Kabul City. She is married to A. Alem and has nine family members. She and her son operate a grocery store. They buy grocery goods from the main market in Kabul and sell them in their shop. Baheja has finished her 1st cycle loan and now wants to begin a 2nd cycle. When they first opened their shop, they weren't able to offer much to their customers. Thanks to the AFSG loan program, they were able to increase their stock and their income. Now Baheja is requesting a loan of $225 so she can continue to grow her business.  ***Note: The picture featured in this business profile is the husband or relative of the female entrepreneur.  In Afghanistan, it is culturally unacceptable to post a picture of a woman to the internet, but the loan is to the female entrepreneur.***

name: Carla
description: Carla, age 39, is a very happy, dynamic, and enterprising woman. She is married to Julio, who drives a mototaxi. She and Julio live together with their five children in Carla's mother's home. Carla sells candy outside of a daycare centre located near her home. She has been doing this for six years, and one of her children helps her with the business. She likes that her job allows her to have an income to cover the household costs and gives her time to see her children. This will be her third loan with Kiva, and she is very grateful for the financial support that she is receiving to move forward with her business. With this loan of 1000 nuevos soles, she will purchase candies such as cookies, caramels, and chocolates.

name: Amina
description: Amina is a 25-year-old single business lady who runs a business selling clothes door to door. She has has been in business for two years. Amina is very hardworking and profit-oriented. Her business has grown tremendously. The desire to open boutiques is always ringing in her mind. Amina requires a loan of 20000 KES to buy more shoes and clothes for selling.

name: Hanan
description: Hanan is a 41-year-old Palestinian refugee and married mother of two children. She lives and works in a Palestinian refugee camp. The financial and social situation of Palestinian refugees in Lebanon is difficult, especially for those who live in a camp. Due to the limited income of her husband, she decided four years ago to open her own clothing shop inside the camp to help to cover her family's expenses.  Hanan is a hard worker and has a good reputation in her region. She is acquiring a loan from Kiva’s field partner, Al Majmoua, to increase her business merchandise and offer new fashionable clothing for the upcoming autumn season. Hanan hopes this loan will help her increase her monthly income and save for a better future for her beloved children.

name: Modesta
description: Modesta is a happily married 50 year old woman.  She lives in a small rural community in the process of developing that is located about 25 minutes from the district of Tambogrande.  Modesta has a business selling food and beverages at a stand located a few blocks from her house.  She has a lot of experience with her business, because she has been developing it for thirty years and she has an established customer base.  Modesta is asking for a loan of 1500 nuevos soles from Edpyme Alternativa to invest in the purchase of merchandise (sodas, beer, sweets), and to make improvements to her workspace.  Modesta wants to offer her customers a better variety of products and better service from the improvements in the environment.  This will allow her to continue growing her business and earn more income for the well-being of her family.  Modesta has good personal references.

name: Vilma Del Carmen
description: Vilma is 40 years old, divorced, and has five children.  She lives in a neighborhood in the town of San Francisco Atlántida.    For the past four years, Vilma has been selling new clothing such as blouses, shirts, trousers, dresses, and children’s outfits.  She also sells cosmetics and knickknacks.  Her business is located in her house and she has an established clientele.    Vilma decided to request a loan in the amount of 12,000 HNL so that she can buy more merchandise to maintain the inventory in her business.  She hopes this investment will result in more profits.
