Her goal is to work hard so that she can grow her business and provide food and an education for her children.

name: Mohammad
description: Mohammad, 25 years old, is married to a housewife and has a baby boy. He owns a small fattening project. Mohammad is requesting a 10,000 EGP loan to buy a head of cattle to use its milk for making cheese and butter for domestic use and for sale in the local market. He believes the income from the project will help him to provide better living conditions for his family.

name: Enma Georgina
description: At 52 years of age, Enma is a person who has a motivation and desire for success that no one can overshadow.  She is a mother, wife, grandmother,and student.  She obtained her high school degree in 1982, graduating with a degree in education with an 86% grade average.  Later, she started her university studies and obtained a bachelor's degree in education with an academic index of 80%.  At this time, she is enrolled in a master's program in HR management. Enma mentions the qualities that made her into an exceptional person who is different from the rest.  She maintains an attitude of service to others,she is kind, and has a strong desire to fight for her life, for her children, and for her family.  Enma's motivation is focused on improving the academic level of her students.  She loves her work, and wants to inculcate the best values in every one of her students.She wants to convey a sense of being able to overcome difficulties to her children, who have always been at her side to support her and love her through any situation.  This makes her proud of the family that she has formed over the years.  The power of continuing with her professional and educational life, in spite of the obstacles and difficult economic times in the country, is for Enma synonymous with success, and shows her contribution to the development of her country.  This is because through her occupation and study, many people have had productive lives.  In the future, Enma wants to continue to impart knowledge to those persons who have the desire to learn, and be able to overcome these difficult moments that society is going through at this time.  She wants to be the best possible example for her children and for the young ones in her household.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth H. is a Tanzanian married woman and a small-business entrepreneur. She runs a business selling a variety of fruits and vegetables at Makangarawe ward in Dar es Salaam.  Elizabeth purchases her goods from the city fruit market at Buguruni and sells to retail customers at her shop. Her business goods include: bananas, apples, oranges, mangoes and pineapples. She manages to meet her family’s daily demands and the capitalization of the business from her business incomes.  Elizabeth is requesting a loan of Tshs 600,000 to buy more produce to expand her business.

name: Sonia Sabina
description: The member continues working in the travel agency business. She sells tickets for trips to different places like the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu.  She has been in this business for five years.  In her free time she likes to go out with her children.   She's requesting the loan to buy tickets to tourist attractions.  She's happy about the loan and promises to make her payments punctually.

name: Tatiana
description: Tatiana is a member of the "Victories" Communal Bank.  She lives in the La Merced neighborhood, District of Juanjui, Department of San Martín.  She is 24, the mother of two children who are dependents, and lives with her partner.    Tatiana started her business with a small contribution from her mother. She began selling meals from her own home, and little by little began buying equipment for her business. She is still working in the same business, with residents of the community, neighbors and friends as her main customers.  She has been working with the Bank for two years.   With a loan of $500 to be repaid in 6 months, she would like to invest in the purchase of items to use in the daily preparation of foods and to better serve her clients, including sacks of rice, sugar, packaged oils, and chickens, as well as tables, chairs, glasses and pots. Tatiana makes decisions with respect to the earnings of her company.  Today she feels like an independent woman, responsible for making her own loan payments.  Tatiana gives thanks to Kiva partner Manuela Ramos for giving her the opportunity to grow as a person and as a businesswoman.Translated from Spanish by Kara Gibson, Kiva Volunteer

name: Svetlana
description: Svetlana is 51 years old, she is married and lives with her husband, middle son and her daughter-in-law. She is a mother of three sons - her oldest son is married and lives separately, her youngest son lives and studies in Bishkek (the capital of Kyrgyzstan).  Svetlana was born in a large family of a cattleman with five children. She is the youngest daughter. After graduating from school Svetlana enrolled in a technical school in the town of Tokmok in they Chuysk province of the Kyrgyz Republic to become a librarian. After she finished her studies Svetlana came back to her home village and began working in the local library, but because of the financial hardship she also got a job in the local farm as a milkmaid. Her future husband was also working there as a small truck driver. They met in 1983 and had married in the same year and a year later their first son was born. Because Svetalana's husband was youngest son in their family, according to the Kyrgyz tradition he is supposed to stay with his parents.  In 1987 and 1989 in the Onobasov family two more boys were born. In the beginning it was very hard for Svetlana and her husband - because of the collapse of the farm she and Siyazbek were left without jobs and decided to start their own business. They used the plot of land which was given to them earlier by the farm to grow cereals and used the profit gained from the sale of the harvest to buy cattle. Right now in Svetlana's household there are three cows, five male and four female calves, and three horses. During the past several years Svetlana had many expenses which had to do with the weddings of her older sons and tuition fees for her youngest son's education in the university, so she has come to ask for a loan in the amount of 40,000 soms (KGS) to buy a milk cow. Svetlana plans to further increase the headcount of the cattle and developing her business.   About Bai-Tushum and Partners: Bai-Tushum and Partners uses Kiva funding to target the especially vulnerable population. Bai-Tushum and Partners is one of the leading Microfinance Institutions in Kyrgyzstan. As a reliable financial partner, Bai-Tushum contributes to the economic development of the Kyrgyz Republic through the delivery of microfinance services in rural and urban areas which leads to job creation and serves the interests of its borrowers and lenders.

name: Gregoria Lurdes
description: Gregoria's main source of income is her neighborhood store, located in the Pasankeri area, where she sales soft drinks, groceries, canned food, and candies.  Her husband works in transportation.  They live in their home, which they own, in the Sopocachi area.  They both work everyday to take care of their kids.    As a client of Emprender for the last three years, Gregoria has been punctual and dependable.  She used to be a member of the communal bank Los Pinos.    The loan she is requesting will be used to buy fruit such as oranges, apples, which she has decided to sale during this time of year as earnings will be good.

name: Edith
description: Edith is married with three children, all of whom go to school. She doesn’t take care of additional family members. She has a tailoring business and has been in this business for seven years. She has applied for a loan of 800,000 Uganda shilling from MCDT-SACCO to buy more rolls of fabric. She works from home six days out of every week and sells on a retail basis only.   Her major business challenges include seasonality and defaulters. She is aspiring to become a wholesaler and also to own a tailoring school. She decided to join MCDT-SACCO because she wanted to acquire additional capital. She resides in a rented house where the family has access to electricity and piped water. Her monthly expenses include school fees and rent.

name: Sokun
description: Sokun, age 42, lives in a Phnom Penh suburb. She has one son and two daughters. One of her children is a garment factory worker and the other two are at university.    Sokun is a garment factory worker while her husband is a construction worker. Sokun’s daughter, who is a garment factory worker, commutes to work by riding her old motorcycle. The old motorcycle does not work well and uses more gasoline.  So Sokun decided to apply for a loan in order to add to her own money to buy a new motorbike for her daughter.

name: Diana
description: Diana is married and she has one child. She has been the pharmaceutical business with her husband for the past 10 years now. She wants to use her loan to buy more drugs like pain killers, anti malarial drugs, antacids, cough mixtures, blood tonic, etc., to enable her to reach more clients. She hopes to buy additional drugs to increase her inventory. Diana is a member of the group called Paul Amantem. Members agree to guarantee each other to repay the loan. Diana’s husband is in the photo since she was at the beauty salon during the interview.

name: Alicia
description: Alicia is 26 years old and a single mother. She has a seven-year-old daughter that is in third grade. Alicia lives on the street Tape Tuya of the city of Itá. For her profession, Alicia has had a grocery store for six years and also owns a cantina in the Panchito López School, the same work with the better objective to make a better life for her family. It is not easy to raise her daughter because she is a single parent. She decided to trust Fundación Paraguaya to make her business better and to sustain her family. Alicia took the loan and invested in her business to buy milk, candies, meat, noodles, soda, cold cuts, vegetables, and more for her pantry shop.

name: Khaled
description: Khaled Abu-Mousa, 28 years old, lives in Khanyounis. He is married and eagerly waiting his children to fill his life and fulfill his dreams with his wife.  He didn’t complete his education and works as salesman.  Khaled lives in a poor neighborhood so he thought how he can gain money in this place as well doing something that helps these people; especially after the war on Gaza.  For this reason, he had been worked as a taxi driver and collected some money. Then, he used them it to open a second hand clothes shop at a simple place in the street. Khalid’s current dream is to achieve the repairs to his home that had been destroyed in the war. At this time, his profits are not enough to cover all the requirements, so he applied for a loan. By gaining the loan his life will be better because the kitchen, bathroom, and the other parts of the home will be more suitable for human living. In details, the bathroom needs toilet, washbasin, shower, and he wants to cover the floor with new tiles and paint the walls. The kitchen also needs cooker, freezer, table, and wood cabinet. To sum up, Khalid’s home needs many things and his happy future depends on your financial support. He will acknowledge your contribution in helping him keep his dignity.

name: Patience's Group
description: This group is made up of 4 members who are all women. All of them have different lines of work. Patience is the leader of this group. She is 22 years old, married, and has two children who are 2 and 4 years of age.	  Patience earns a living by selling biscuits, toffees and chocolate drinks. She sells her products from house to house in Accra. This will be her fifth loan as part of the group and she will use it to purchase more biscuits, toffees and chocolate drinks from wholesalers and thus keep her business well stocked. Patience is requesting this loan in order to increase her merchandise. Patience faces various challenges in her business, such as competition, and she will use the benefits of the loan to continue purchasing merchandise and earn more income.  Patience is grateful for this opportunity, both for herself and the fellow group members, as many of them are the sole providers for their families.

name: Edna
description: Edna is 50 years old and married with five children, one of whom in school, Edna works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 29500 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell like canned goods, soap, milk, sugar, coffee, etc.  Edna has been in this business for 15 years.  She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Vilma
description: Vilma was born in the city of Cusco (Peru).  She is 33 years old, married, and has two children from her marriage.  Vilma currently lives in the city of Cusco and this is where she carries out her business activities.  She is a cosmetologist and owns a small beauty salon where she provides her customers with haircuts, dyes, hairdos, etc.  She has been in this business for five years and it is doing very well.  On this occasion, Vilma needs a loan to buy materials such as hair dyes, shampoo, conditioners, etc.  The 'Comuzone I' community bank meets every month in the city of Cusco (Peru).  Cusco is known as a very touristy and commercial area.  It is also known for its traditional Inti Raymi fiesta and because it is home to one of the seven wonders of the world: Machupicchu.

name: Adyabold
description: Adyabold is 25 years old and lives with his wife and daughter in Ulaanbaatar, the capital city of Mongolia. They all live together in an old, small house. His wife works in a department store as a salesperson. Adyabold operated a taxi service for the past few years by using his friend’s car. During that time, he gained much experience in conducting a business. He is currently employed at a taxi company as a taxi driver. Adyabold is a very hard-working person and is known for his good character.   His house is too small for his family, and it needs repair. So he is asking for a loan to purchase insulation materials for the house.

name: Asel
description: Asel is 30 years old, married, and together with her husband, is raising three children. Asel has a university education. As the main source of income for her family, Asel practices animal husbandry. She started this business 10 years ago, with an initial purchase of cattle in the amount of 10,000 som (KGS). Thanks to Asel's hard work, she currently has one milk cow and one horse on her farm. Her monthly income is 5,000 som (KGS). For the purpose of further developing her business, Asel turned to Microfinance Bank "Bai Tushum and Partners." She is requesting a loan in the amount of 50,000 som (KGS) to buy cows to increase the size of her herd. Asel plans to invest the earnings from the loan in the further acquisition of livestock. She also intends to save money for her children's future education.

name: Jacinta
description: The person in the photograph is Jacinta. She is fifty-three years old, married, and has six children. She joined Hand In Hand Eastern Africa in February 2013 and has received trainings on enterprise development and financial planning, which equipped her with skills to effectively manage her enterprise. She owns a maize mill where she also sells maize and maize flour. Jacinta is borrowing from Kiva in order to purchase maize for resale and for milling. She trusts this will increase her sales and therefore increase her income. She will therefore be able to improve her family’s living standards, including providing them with quality education. Jacinta is grateful to Kiva and their lenders and promises to make established payments.

name: Julieta
description: Julieta P. is from the village of Upper Puntod. She is 37 years old. Julieta is married and has three school-aged children. To make a living, she owns and operates a fishing business, harvesting and selling ocean-caught fish in the local community. She has been engaged in her business for over three years and earns approximately $125 a month for these activities.  In 2006, Julieta joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 10,000 PHP from PMPC. This previous loan was used to purchase additional fish to sell.   Julieta is requesting a new loan of 10,000 PHP which will be used to invest in expanding the business. This will be her 10th loan from PMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About PMPC:  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Luisa
description: Luisa R., 39, is making sure that her family has enough provisions for their daily needs. Married to Ricardo R., a driver, they are blessed with three children. She makes sure that she helps her husband earn money so that their family can have a better life.  She has been juggling three businesses in the past five years. She does direct selling for the country’s popular cosmetics and clothing brands, she has her own electronic cellular phone loading station, and a buy-and-sell business.  Luisa has been a regular member of Center for Community Transformation* (CCT) for more than a year now. She regularly attends their weekly fellowship meetings and pays her weekly dues consistently. Because of her good repayment performance with her previous loans, she has been able to borrow quite a few times in CCT’s Cooperative.  She is consistent in paying her dues because she used the money she borrowed to expand and improve her businesses.       Now with your help, she would like to apply for a 26,000 Philippine peso loan. This amount will be used as a source of added capital to her expanding business by buying more products to be incorporated into her inventory.  She dreams that her business will continue to grow so that she can provide for her children’s education. She also envisions herself having her own house.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay Micro Finance loans.

name: Cesaria Rosalia
description: Cesaria Rosalia is 54 years old and married with seven children.  Cesaria Rosalia is in the agricultural business, farming banana in the Philippines. Cesaria Rosalia requested a PHP 15000 loan through NWTF to buy fertilizers and pesticides.  Cesaria Rosalia has been farming banana for nine years now, and has borrowed 16 times in the past from NWTF and more recently, from Kiva to sustain it.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream, to save money to expand her business.

name: Rhoda
description: Rhoda is a 26-year-old lady who is married and blessed with four children. Her husband is employed and supports her in bringing in more income for the family. She has been running a retail shop business for five years now and is happy to make a profit of about 40,000 Kenya shillings every month.  This will be her first loan with VisionFund Kenya after she was introduced by her group members, and she plans to use it to add more stock of retail goods in her shop including sugar, flour, rice, margarine, cooking oils, etc. She plans to use the anticipated profits to take care of her family and also save some to help with the education of her children.  In future she plans to expand her business and see her children educated further.

name: Adjo
description: Adjo is a young woman of 31. She has two dependent children of seven and one year old. Only the older child goes to school. In 2008 she started a business selling charcoal from home. The profits from this business enable her to cover expenses for her children. This is her second loan from Wages and this loan will help her to stock up on merchandise in order to satisfy the demand of her customers. Adjo would like to insure the well-being of her family and make more orders.

name: Irma
description: Irma is 73 years old and sells tortillas and curds.  She has been in this business for more than 34 years.  Irma enjoys her work very much and wakes up very early each day to start making the curds to sell to her customers.  She is a very responsible woman who works hard to support her 14 year old child and provide everything that is needed.    This loan will be used as operating capital to purchase corn, curds, and firewood, which are the raw materials needed to make her products properly.  Irma hopes to succeed in this business since it is her only means of making a living.Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Edward's Group
description: Edward is a 60-year-old, proud father of 11 children. He is a group leader, often described as a very hardworking individual, and is representing his group of 16 farmers in Kakamega South District. Since joining One Acre Fund in 2013, Edward has noticed that he has had a healthier life due to better nutrition.  Edward described his harvest as good last year, but believes he can have a better one this year by continuing to work with One Acre Fund. He is very excited to also be purchasing a solar light, apart from fertilizer and maize, because he will now be able to have light during the night in order to feel safer. With the profits from this season’s harvest, he plans to send his children to school.  With this loan, Edward’s Group will be able to plant a total of 9.75 acres of land and purchase a total of eight solar lights.

name: Myrna
description: Myrna is 46 years old and a very hard working entrepreneur.   Myrna has a direct selling Avon, Natasha and Tupperware products business in the Philippines. Myrna requested a PHP 29000 loan amount through NWTF to purchase additional products like lotion, body spray, body soap, lipsticks, etc. to sell.  Myrna has been in this business for 20 years. In the future, Myrna would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Yolanda
description: Yolanda is 43 years old and married. She has four children. Three of her children are in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.   Yolanda has a feed and rice retailing business in the Philippines. She has been in this business for five years.  Yolanda requested a PHP 15,000 loan amount through NWTF in order to buy more stocks of feed and rice to resell.  In the future, Yolanda would like to save money to expand her business and continue to send her children to school.

name: Estela
description: Mrs. Estela B. is from the barangay (village) of Calabayan in Ozamiz City, Misamis Occidental. She is 32 years old, married, and blessed with one school-aged child. To make a living, she operates a internet café. She’s been engaged in this business for 2 years and earns at least Php 6,000.00 per month from computer service rentals.   In April 2008, Estela joined PMPC to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Estela as an active member of Paglaum MPC under the Regular Loan Program has successfully repaid a loan of Php 20,000.00. She is now requesting a loan of Php 30,000.00. This 2nd loan will be used to maintain and repair her computers. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve her family's living conditions, especially in meeting their basic needs, savings for future use, loan repayments, child’s education and possible business expansions.   About PMPC:  Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative (PMPC) is one of the most progressive cooperatives in northwestern Mindanao. It reaches out to the rural poor using the Grameen model.   *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Ntease Group
description: Lympia is fifty – one years old. She is divorced and has give birth to three children, all in school. She lives with her children in a rented apartment in a town called Wiawso in the Western Region of Ghana. Wiawso is a commercial and farming town. She is a seamstress and the leader of a trust bank group called ‘Ntease’, meaning understanding. The group members are engaged either in farming and/or trading activities. They sell/supply in their local market and nearby communities. They sometimes trek to nearby community markets. They want a loan to buy goods in bulk to expand their businesses.

name: Elsa Marina
description: Elsa, 43, lives in her own home with her 3 dependent children.  For 15 years, she has had a business selling groceries, drinks, cosmetics, and other staple consumer goods.  Her customers are her neighbors and friends who visit her daily.  Elsa's business is located in a good area, and this is where she makes her sales every day.  She lives in a community in San Lorenzo, in the southern part of Honduras.  Elsa is requesting a loan to buy soft drinks, beans, sugar, rice, cheese, coffee, bread, water, flour, eggs, and milk, and also to buy cosmetics and sandals.  With the support of this loan, she hopes that her business will grow, helping her to improve her family's quality of life.  Elsa is requesting her second loan, and she wants to have a good credit history with Prisma.  Her dream is to improve her business and make it grow.  San Lorenzo, Honduras - May, 2013

name: Liberty
description: As a married parent of two children, Liberty works hard to support her family.  Liberty has a food vending business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from frozen foods and raising livestock. She is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to purchase additional ingredients for her food vending business.  Liberty has been sustaining her business activities through her past four loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business.

name: Felicidad
description: Mrs. Felicidad S. is 57 years of age.  She live in Tabon, Jose Dalman and has four children. One of her children is married and the other three are already working.  Mrs. S. is a member of Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative, which could be described as PAGLAUM DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR LANDLESS PEOPLE. She has been a member for two years now.   She is happy to be a member of this program because it can help her raise additional capital for her business.  It can also help with life insurance and savings deposits. She is already on her third cycle of loans.   She deeply wishes that her little business will succeed.

name: Estela
description: As a married parent of five children, Estela works hard to support her family.  She has a fishing business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from a general store. Estela is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to buy additional fishing nets for her fishing business.  Estela has been sustaining her business activities through her past loan from NWTF.   She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: K. Geneviève
description: Born on May 16, 1981 in Cotonou, the econimc capital of Bénin, K. Geneviève NOUTAÏ is married to Victorin ADEGUELOU, a teacher. The couple has two children both of whom are in school. Seven years ago Geneviève moved to Ekpè, in the Sèmè-Podji commune, where she lives with her family. The couple shares the various familial responsibilities.  Geneviève only attended primary school, but then learned how to be a hairdresser.  She has been operating this business for two years. As a side business, Geneviève sells hair pieces and hair products, which provides her with several sources of income. Given the considerable customer demand, Geneviève would like to increase her stock of products and be able to better satisfy her customers.  This is why she is requesting a first loan from ALIDé. Translated from French by Connie Archea, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sophat's Group
description: The members of Sophat’s Group live in a rural village in Kompong Thom Province in Cambodia. Sophat makes a living cultivating rice to support her family. She has one young son in her family. In their village, there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women to safeguard the health of their families, save money on medical expenses, and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Ruben
description: Ruben is 39 years old. He is a mechanic and he also works as a driver.  Ruben needs a loan to buy spare parts for his vehicle. He will install the spare parts himself. Ruben works hard and he is married with two children. His wife is not working right now, so that is why he needs your help.  He hopes that you will understand and support him.

name: Lilia
description: Lilia works hard to support her family. Lilia is married and has a furniture making business in the Philippines.  Lilia requested a PHP 9,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more materials like wood, nails, paints, etc. for her business.  Lilia has been in this business for five years now.  In the future Lilia would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Efrina
description: Efrina is a 53-year-old married woman and a mother of five children. They live in Duero, Bohol, Philippines. She has been engaged in a vegetable gardening business for more than ten years now. Efrina is asking for a loan to buy seedlings, fertilizer and pesticides. With this, she will be able to improve her vegetable farm and her harvest.  In the future, Efrina has hopes of making her venture a success and profitable.

name: Hoa
description: Mrs Hoa  is 45 years old and she is married She has worked in agriculture raising poultry for more than 10 years.Hoa  lives in Thieu Hoa district, a  rural town in Thanh Hoa province.Her family is a low-income household in village, moreover the market need is low in this region. Her family has no latrine.One of the most critical difficulties that concerns her is the latrine is not hygienic. She is requesting a loan to purchase sand, cement, brick and equipments to build toilet.This is Hoa's first loan with Thanh Hoa microfinance institution.With her business profit, Hoa  hopes for her business to do well, for her family to be healthy and happy and for her children to find a good job.

name: Jadgarzhan
description: Jadgarzhan is 45 years old, a widower and the father of four lovely daughters. The two eldest, despite their young age, happily help him with his business. He has been self-employed buying, selling and repairing jewelry for over ten years.   He also bakes and sells samosa, and leases out part of his shop for hamburger sales. He makes 7,000 KGS in rent. In the clothing market he repairs clothing and sells hats. Jadgarzhan is very responsible and entrepreneurial, always looking for a new income source with which to support his beloved daughters.   However, on the night of July 15 there was an accidental fire in his jewelry workshop which spread to the roof of the house. This impacted his main source of income and his regular customers--now his workshop stands idle.   Thus Jadgarzhan took a loan of 150,000 KGS from micro-finance bank, Bai-Tushum, to restore his workshop. He is an honorable man: friendly, punctual, a good communicator with strong work experience and technical knowledge. He knows how to do business and invest wisely. The income from the loan will help him restore his favorite business and provide a decent education to his daughters.

name: Kokouda
description: Kokouda is 32 years old, single and the father of one child. He has been selling second-hand clothes since 2000. He buys his supplies in Lomé. Kokouda came to the microfinance institution WAGES and applied for his second loan to buy shirts, T-shirts and jeans.

name: Honorata Yolanda
description: Yolanda is a member of the Orchids Communal Bank.  Yolanda is married, 40 years old, and has three children.  She makes traditional breads from her region using a wood-fired oven.  She makes the breads with the help of her employees, and then sells them in local stores.  Yolanda needs a loan of 1,050 soles which she will invest in the purchase of flour and sugar.  Yolanda dreams of building a house of high-quality materials, having more capital, and buying a mototaxi.Translated from Spanish by Laura Westin, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sita
description: Sita is 21 years old, married and has one daughter. She stays home to look after her elderly parents, but recently began to help her husband meet the needs of their family by opening up a small business selling shoes. This business is off to a good start, and she has come to us for a loan of $300 to buy additional inventory to sell from tables she has set up on the side of her house. With this loan, she believes that she can expand her business and fulfill her dream of helping her family live a better life.

name: Toshtemir
description: Toshtemir, 32 years old, is a young and industrious man. He is married and has 3 small children. Toshtemir began his own business growing wheat, cotton, onion, potatoes, carrots, maize, etc. 5 years ago. He has 8 hectares of sowing land. Toshtemir’s wife and some of his relatives help him to grow agricultural products.   Toshtemir lives with his wife, children, parents and brother. He has a big family. He uses his income to provide his family with all necessary things. Toshtemir is going to make a new sowing but he doesn't have enough money to buy seeds, mineral fertilizers and fuel. He is asking for a loan of 5,000 TJS (Somoni) to buy seeds, mineral fertilizers and fuel. He awaits your support.

name: Lorna
description: Lorna is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a fishing business in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 12,000 through NWTF to purchase bundles of fishing net for her fishing business.Lorna has been in this business for 15 years. She earns additional income from pig fattening.Lorna has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Erika
description: The member continues working in the transportation business.  She rents out a taxi to work in different streets in the city of Cusco.  She also is selling products such as panettone, Champagne, and wine.  She sells independently.  With this business the member is able to get ahead.  Her dream is to have a place to sell the products.  She is requesting the loan to buy panettone, Champagne, and wine wholesale.  The member is happy about the loan and is committed to making her installment payments.

name: Sandra Mercedes
description: Sandra L. is a woman known for being a very good shopkeeper who sells clothing and backpacks of all types in her section of the Central Market in the city of Chinandega. Her business has been developing in a satisfactory way thanks to her many efforts. She is now looking for support from Kiva partner Ceprodel in order to purchase backpacks. As it is the beginning of the year her sales will increase because school classes are starting, and it is important to have enough merchandise to offer in order to satisfy her clients.Translated from Spanish by Emily Martyn, Kiva Volunteer

name: Kadie
description: This is 43-year-old Kadie. She is married and has three children aged 17, 12, and 9 years. In 1983, Kadie established her local food stuff (palm oil and garri) business. She began her business because she wants to help take care of her family. Her business is located in the outskirts and her main customers are women, men, and children. Working seven days a week and 16 hours a day, she earns about SLL 800,000 every month from this business.   Kadie would like a loan in the amount of SLL 3,000,000. She requires this loan in order to buy more garri and palm oil to re-sell. In the future, Kadie plans to build a house and give quality education to her children. She thanks you for your support.

name: Stella
description: Stella has a farm where she plants maize and pineapple. She is 44 years old and married with five children. She hopes for the loan of N70,000 to purchase more pineapple suckers to plant. She says thanks to all Kiva lenders.

name: Aydee Filonila
description: Aydee is a member of the Rikchari communal bank. She is 57 years old and a hotel owner in the province of Sucre. She has four hectares of land where she plants quinoa and potatoes. She is the mother of four children and has been a member of Finca Perú for 14 years. A friend of hers who is also now co-mother-in-law with her invited her to join and since that time she has never left Finca. She has made very good friends in her communal bank.   Aydee devotes herself to many things, among them making children's clothing and skirts. Thus she arrived at her native land of Sucre and with the loans she has been receiving began to build her hotel.   The loan she is seeking now will help her buy a neighboring plot of land in order to expand her hotel. She is very appreciative of everything she has been taught; Aydee values it highly.

name: Mwanahamisi
description: Mwanahamisi is a 25-year-old entrepreneur and volunteer Camfed alumnae member (cama), living with her family in the Kilosa district. As she currently braiding hair to her nearby villagers, she is now requesting a Kiva loan in order to launch a venture in a hairdressing salon.   She will use the loan to buy the equipment and rent the space necessary to open her own salon. Mwanahamisi plans to use the profit she earns to pay for her siblings' schooling fees, buy a plot of land and pursue success as an entrepreneur. The interest on her “social-interest” loan will be repaid through Mwanahamisi's volunteering, which are so valuable for Camfed’s younger women.

name: Wilfredo
description: Wilfredo, 42, lives in the city of Ica, known as The Land of the Eternal Sun because you can always enjoy the sun in any season of the year.  It is also known for its traditional dances and for the Huacachina Lagoon, known as The Oasis of America, and above all as a city whose residents are welcoming and generous as well as optimistic since they came out ahead in spite of the 2007 earthquake in which many lost their lives or were injured.  Peru is well known also for the delicious food, and one of the dishes that Wilfredo likes very much is the delicious chicken and rice, which has rice combined with chicken, in pieces or stuffed, vegetables (corn kernels, diced carrot, green beans), and other spices.  Wilfredo works at his job as a locksmith, which consists of repairing door locks, repairing padlocks, and making keys.  He works about 10 hours a day, which he does with great effort despite the intense heat in his city.  He waits on around 10 customers a day and can earn up to 380 PEN, and 500 PEN in a very good day.  He believes that his business is going well for him because he does a good job and above all he is hardworking in doing it.  He also takes care of the customers in a pleasant way.  Wilfredo is very grateful for the support of the Kiva lenders because thanks to this help he will be able to buy more tools and materials to improve his locksmith shop to do his work.  With this improvement he will have more materials and will do an even better job and have a better equipped shop.  With this he will get more income so he will be able to continue saving and be able to realize his biggest dream, to have a service enterprise.

name: Caroline
description: Caroline is a forty-six-year-old lady from Kisumu City. She is married to Lucas and they have two children aged twelve and twenty-six.   Caroline operates a hotel  business, a business she has had for the last ten years. She makes a monthly income of KES 15,000. She is taking a second loan from KADET Ltd. which she will use to buy plastic seats for the hotel business. Her profits will be used to pay school fees for her children.  Her dream is to grow her profits so that she meets her family’s needs fully.

name: Chab
description: Chab, 62 years old, lives in Kampong Speu Province of Cambodia. She is a mother of four children; three are single and one is married. She is an active and experienced farmer. By growing rice and selling the crops to local dealers, she can make a decent income to support her family. So far, she has been involved in this career for almost 30 years.   Chab wants to improve the general living conditions of the entire family by having a latrine to use, because there is no latrine in her house now. Therefore, she is borrowing a loan from Kiva to build a latrine. By doing this, she can help her family members gain access to sanitation, promote their health, and help to lessen environmental deterioration. She is thankful for the loan granted through HKL with a much lower interest rate than other general loan products.

name: Geronima
description: As a married parent of five children, Geronima works hard to support her family.  She has a food vending business in the Philippines, and earns additional income from buying and selling vegetables and running a general store. Geronima is borrowing PHP 11,000 through NWTF to purchase ingredients like bananas, sugar, bamboo sticks, etc. for her food vending business.  Geronima has been sustaining her business activities through her past three loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Amigas Unidas Group
description: The communal bank "AMIGAS UNIDAS" will begin its tenth loan cycle through Pro Mujer at the Centro Santiago II.  The group is comprised of nine members and has a board of directors chaired by Mrs. Lucila.  The business activities of the members are varied and include: sales of softdrinks, corn, jewelry, food, potatoes, a sheetmetal workshop and a store.  Mrs. Lucila has been working with Pro Mujer for four years and joined the institution through neighbors and friends in her neighborhood.  She currently sells corn, which is a trade she learned from her mother.  The loan she is taking out will be used to increase her capital to buy corn in Zorata and sell in the street.  This activity generates income to help support her family as much as possible.  She is married and has three children.  When asked what she enjoys most about Pro Mujer, she says the training and health-related activities.

name: Pulu
description: Pulu is 51 years old and a widow with four children.    She has a small vegetable garden where she grows cabbages and tomatoes that she can sell in her community or at the market. She has been doing this for one year. Pulu needs a loan to buy fertilizer, chemicals, sprayers, a tiller, a crowbar, new boots and a pair of overalls.   She has been a member of SPBD since 2014. Pulu will use the profits from her sales to pay for her family's weekly expenses.

name: Ramatou Eveline
description: Ramatou Eveline is a married mother of one child who goes to school in the town. She has a shack where she sells cosmetic products, fruit juices and food products, and has done so for several years now. She gets her supplies in one of the markets in Benin, and her customers are from Nigeria and Benin.  To increase her working capital and satisfy the requests of her ever-growing customer base, Ramatou Eveline has applied for and obtained a loan from Finadev. With her profits she will be able to provide for her child’s schooling and other needs.

name: Carlos Gilberto
description: Carlos's business has been growing little by little throughout these eight years of hard work. At the beginning of 2014, he made a lot of progress. His customers and his income increased a lot since he had a loan with which he bought eggs, flour and sugar, among other things. He used this for his quality baking, having the opportunity to continue paying for his studies. Because of this he's very grateful to Kiva, Mi Crédito and with all of the people who supported his previous loan.  Carlos is 27 years old. He has one son and a beautiful wife that supports him in everything. He's a university student and he dreams of continuing forward with his bakery business. He also dreams of finishing his studies and helping his wife finish hers as well, which is why he knows that he has to keep working hard. The main reason he's asking for a loan is to buy flour, sugar, eggs, butter, and spices in bulk. This way he'll be able to increase his income and accomplish his goals of opening up a savings account, to fix his house and become independent.

name: Dora María
description: Dora is a 44-year old woman who has three children, one of them living in USA and two living with her. Dora attended high-school and became a single mother. She has worked in tailoring since she was 20 and learned the job by helping her parents. Her mother also worked in that same activity.   She is requesting a loan to buy a sewing machine. She makes the uniforms for several schools, which involves a lot of work. Thanks to the loan, she will be able to meet the demand.   Her dream is for her children to attend university. She expects her business to grow a lot.

name: 19 Thắng Hùng Hải Lộc Group
description: Nhung is 28 years old, and she is married with two children. Nhung is the group leader of the 19 Thắng Hùng Hải Lộc Solidarity Group, which consists of seven members. For five years, Nhung has operated a food stall/restaurant selling cake, sweets, sugar, milk, and other items. The main hardship Nhung faces in her business is the lack of capital. In 2014, Nhung joined Kiva's partner, Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women, to improve her business. She is requesting a loan to purchase items to sell at her food stall. Nhung has successfully repaid two loans from Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women. With her business profit, Nhung hopes to build a new house, for her family to be healthy and happy, and for her business to do well.

name: Catalino
description: Catalino is from the town of San Miguel, Bohol. He is 50 years old and operates a sari-sari (convenience) store in his community, which he has done for two years. He sells household basic commodities like detergent, seasoning, toiletries, chips, canned goods and soft drinks. In addition to this, he owns a vulcanizing business.   He is asking for a loan to buy more items to resell, like coffee, sugar, toiletries, canned goods, noodles and rice. These items are in high demand and sell well on a daily basis. With a loan, Catalino is confident that his sari-sari business will be more prosperous. He will use his profits for the school fees of his four children who are 7, 9, 12, and 14 years old.

name: Tindolo
description: Tindolo is 45 years old. She is a widow with three children. One of her children is in school. She has a business of selling groundnuts in Kator Branch in South Sudan. She has been in this business for three years.  Tindolo requested this loan through BRAC South Sudan with the hopes of expanding her business. She says that she will use the profit from this loan to build a house in the future.

name: Rhoda
description: Rhoda is a married woman with three children, two of whom are in school. Her children are between the ages of three and 12 years. For the last five years, she has operated a grocery selling as retail, and she aspires to expand this business to reach more customers. High transportation costs and seasonality of some goods is a major challenge facing her business. She lives in a rental house that has both electricity and piped water. The loan will help her purchase fruits and vegetables.

name: Luz Noemi
description: Luz Noemi is 51 years old and she sells fried chicken with fries and tortillas. She has many clients because the flavor of her chicken is super delicious and the prices are affordable. She has several years in this type of business. Her business is located near the Guasaule customs office on the border of Honduras and Nicaragua. Luz starts her day at 5 in the morning every day to start frying her chicken and to attend her clients. On her spare time she visits her children and grandchildren. Luz has 5 children and they are all grown and married.

name: Luz
description: Luz is 40 years old and lives with her partner and children, who are her main reason to live. Together they inhabit a cozy house that they own. She is dedicated to Internet kiosks, a business that she has started some years ago with much effort. Now, this business is the main source of income for her family. Her older son has been helping her for some time because sometimes she needs to leave to make some shopping for the house and it is imperative that she lives someone who she trusts taking care of the business. Fortunately, the equipment works well and she hopes that in the future she will be able to buy a number of them in order to expand her business, thus obtaining a bigger income and improving her house finances. Besides, she hopes her income to improve with the holidays season, since there will be a higher quantity of people willing to communicate with their loved ones. This is her sixth loan with MFP, and she has been very punctual with her payments. For this reason, her partner with whom she takes loans trusts her very much. With the requested money she wants to buy one new computer for her Internet kiosks to start expanding her business. Translated from Spanish by Giovanna Fernandes, Kiva Volunteer

name: Vicente Ramón
description: Vicente Ramón Vázquez M. is 40 years old and lives with his wife and two children.  He's a father who's always worrying about how to support his family.  He has a grocery store and he's been in this business for more than nine years.  His economic difficulties have gotten in the way of him being able to build up his business.   As time goes by the profits he obtains are used to stock up his grocery store which is located inside the municipal market.  Working with Fundación León 2000 has been very helpful.  He is requesting this loan in order to buy more products and satisfy the needs of his customers.  He would like to establish another business for his wife to run.Translated from Spanish by Daniel Kvaka, Kiva Volunteer

name: Gulinar
description: Gulinar is a brave married woman who works hard for the good of her three children. The strict discipline she uses with her children allows her to count on her household’s advice and support in working the fields. Gulinar’s children’s grateful attitude continues to encourage her and they have gathered many lessons that they can use when they form their own households. What Gulinar urgently needs right now are fertilizers and other chemicals for the care of their crops so that they can produce a product that is in line with the demands of the market. Gulinar doesn’t just need good land; she also needs a friendly hand to help her out.    More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is perhaps best known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road; the end of Alexander the Great's rule; and with its famous great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets as: Rudaki, Ibn Sina (Avicenna), Firdousi, Omar Haiyam, Jomi, Mavlavi Rumi and many others. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium BC.  And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But, Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics.  The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy.  In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable.  These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia.  While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.   IMON's History Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Francia Jazmin
description: Francia lives in Guayaquil.  She started her sewing business so that she could have more income to help with the household expenses.  Francia works alone in her business of making clothes.    The problem she faces in her business is not having enough machines for all of the sewing jobs that are submitted to her.  She is in a common-law relationship with her partner, who works as a bricklayer.  Francia has three children (ages 2, 3, and 5).  The oldest child attends a state school.    With this loan, she will buy fabrics and machines.  Her dream is for her children to grow up with God’s blessing and become workers.

name: Jessica
description: Jessica is 44 years old and married with two children. Jessica works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a 11,000 PHP loan through NWTF to purchase additional stocks like soap, shampoo, rice, etc. to resell. Jessica has borrowed and paid back five loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for five years and also earns an income from pig fattening and raising livestock. Jessica aspires to save enough money so that she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Shehnaz Begum
description: Shehnaz Begum is a 40-year-old active borrower of BRAC Pakistan, residing in Rawalpindi, Pakistan with her spouse and four children. Her husband has been running his own tailoring shop in the local market for 20 years. He alone is responsible to fulfill the needs of the entire family.  Shehnaz Begum's husband needs to buy different types of tailoring accessories, e.g., pieces of clothes, laces, needles and sewing machine accessories, but due to some financial constraints he is not in a suitable condition to buy the above items for his business purpose.   Therefore, Shehnaz Begum has applied for Kiva loan from its field partner BRAC Pakistan. With the help of this loan amount she will financially assist her husband to obtain the above tailoring accessories to fulfill his business needs, so that he can earn a more profitable income.  For this financial assistance, Shehnaz Begum is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Maria Erlinda
description: Maria Erlinda is 35 years old and she has a convenience store business. She has 2 children in her care. She has had this business for 10 years and she started out thanks to her husband. He was previously employed at a company and with savings he managed to purchase some products. This is how they slowly started to increase their inventory and to earn a large clientele. She requests a loan to use as working capital and to purchase sweets, soft drinks, basic grains, breads, and other products. Maria wants to see all of her efforts support her children and to have a good education.

name: Hilda Yaneth
description: Hello!  My name is Hilda and I have a shop selling new clothing in the main square of my town.  I have been in business for a number of years and have a good clientele. I am a single mother with two kids in school and thanks to my shop I can support them.  Thank you!    Translated by Kiva volunteer Alexis Hult    Hola mi nombre es Hilda, mi actividad es el comercio cuento con un negocio de venta de rupa nueva ubicado en la plaza de mi ciudad, tengo  varios años de dedicarme a este negocio, cuento con buena clientela, gracias a este negocio puedo cubrir los gastos familiares, soy madre soltera tengo  2 hijos los que estan estudiando gracias.

name: Edy
description: Edy is 33 years old.  She lives in a house with her 3 children in the nieghborhood of an educational center of her region.  She has been selling food in the cafe of a neighborhood school for a year and a half.  Edy serves people everyday during the school year.  Her children help her with the work, as during the refreshment break a lot of people come and she can't keep up by herself.  Likewise, she needs help during the evening when it is the other shift.  Working like this, she has been able to generate more sustainable capital, which has allowed her to improve her finanaces and to pay for her children's necesities.  Her children are her main motivation to keep working.  In her sales post she sells sweets and various sodas, and her establishment has been very well recieved.  That is the reason she needs more capital- to ensure greater earnings and to implement improvements to her stall, such as adding display cases and tables.  This is her 3rd loan with MFP.  During the time Edy has worked with her commual bank, she has seen the benefits of uniting efforts for the common good of financial growth, and she is very grateful.  She will continue to move forward with the same effort.  With the loan that she is requesting, Edy will invest in the purchase of boxes of wholesale sweets and sodas.

name: San Juan Group
description: The “San Juan” committee formed thanks to one of the member’s initiative.  They are currently in the 3rd cycle with 14 members.  They are from the city of Curuguaty, a city quite far from the capital, with scarce access to certain securities that continues striving to grow.  One of the members is Elena who comments that among the things she does is buying and selling animals to earn higher income for her family.  She participates in the training and is striving this way to improve her life in all ways.  She’s asking for this loan to buy animals and also to buy articles of clothing, shoes and others to sell from place to place which is something she’s just starting and that will help her fulfill her business plan which in turn will help her increase her income.

name: Fridah's Rehema Group
description: Fridah is a 37-year-old widow  with two children, ages 10 and 17. She owns a small grocery store, which she started in 2007. She works from 8AM to 11PM and can earn a monthly profit of about $50 from her sales.   Fridah has taken out one successful loan from BRAC Tanzania to expand her business. She now hopes for a loan to buy more crates of beer and soda for her business. She will share this loan with her subgroup members, who have  businesses dealing with fish sales, food sales, grocery stores and vegetable sales.

name: Pacifica
description: Pacifica is a humble person who sells milk and puts forth the effort she needs to in order to provide the basic needs for her family.  Each day she looks for a better future and penny per penny she sees the future as being the fruits of her sacrifices and her husband’s active participation in the milk business.  She works in a very agricultural dairy zone.  Pacifica needs a loan to be able to strengthen her activity by increasing her number of dairy cows.  She is very hardworking and persevering.  This loan will be of great help to her in improving her financial situation.  She is very well known and respected in the zone.

name: Mwanaisha
description: Mwanaisha is a married woman who owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is food for the family.  For the past four years, she has operated a dressmaking shop business, selling from home to her neighbours and passersby. She faces a major challenge of seasonality in her business, and dreams of establishing a clothes-selling business in the future.  Having decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business, Mwanaisha wants to purchase cloth materials for resale with a loan of Kshs 20,000.

name: Kilapei Ole
description: Kilapei Ole K. is 37 years old. He is married to Naramat K. and is the father of three children who are going to school.  Kilapei is a farmer and he does the farming on his own piece of land which he has been doing for the last seven years.  He learned about KADET from a market awareness done by KADET staff in his area of residence. This will be his first loan which he is planning to spend to prepare his ten acres of land for maize planting. Maize has been doing well in his area due to good climatic conditions and also a market is readily available as a local miller comes to buy the produce from the farms. He hopes to use the profit from the proceeds of this loan to expand his farming activity from small scale to commercial farming.  Kilapei dream is to do large scale farming and buy some farm equipment.   He is a hard working man who is determined to achieve his set goals.

name: Nodari
description: Nodari is 32 years old. He lives in Gurjaani District with his wife and pensioner mother. Nodari requested a loan from local financial institutions several times for a family business start-up, but without any success. His loan request was rejected all the time because of low income and the family’s poor living conditions.   Nodari works as a fitter at a local cable TV company, and his mother works as a baker locally. It is hardly enough for food for the family. According to Credo estimations, the family belongs to the subsistence poor category.   Nodari requested a loan from Credo to start up a family business. Nodari has now been approved for a loan within the framework of the new joint initiative of Kiva and Credo. The start-up loan program envisages provision of business start-up and re-startup credits with soft conditions to rural poor people, who do not have access to credit products. These rural poor people are regarded as “high-risk borrowers” because of their low income.   With his credit, Nodari will open a bakery. After the bakery is opened, they will be able to bake Georgian bread for selling. As his mother has a rich experience in this field, Nodari thinks that the business will be profitable. The new business initiative, financed with the Kiva start-up loan, will significantly improve the living conditions of the family.

name: Argie
description: Argie is 28 years old and married with one child, who is currently in school. She works very hard to provide for her child.  Argie runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to buy more items to sell in her general store. She has been in this business for nine years and sells a variety of items such as snack foods, milk, juice, soft-drinks, biscuits, candies, etc.   Argie would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Trần Thị's Group
description: N. Trần Thị (10117110018) is a 39-year-old female living in the town of Đông Anh - Hà nội.  N. is the group leader of a six-member group loan offered by SEDA.  While each member of the group receives an individual loan, they all are responsible for paying back the loans of their fellow group members if someone is delinquent or defaults.  The official name of this borrowing group is Xóm Thượng 11 (3).   N. is married and has two school-aged children.  To make a living, N. operates a butcher shop, butchering & selling pork in the local community.  N. has been engaged in this business for over four years and earns approximately 2.000.000 VND a month from these activities.   In 2003, N. joined SEDA to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities.  N. has successfully repaid a previous loan of 6.750.000 VND from SEDA.  This previous loan was used to invest in expanding the business.  She is now requesting a new loan of 5.886.000 VND, which will be used to invest in expanding the business.  The loan will be the eighth loan taken out by N. from SEDA.  N. plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to pay the tuition fees of her children.   About the Other Borrowers in the Group:   1.  Vương Thị T. (10117110039) is a 45-year-old female who is requesting a 5.450.000 VND loan to support her business operating a butcher shop.   2.  Hoàng Thị T. (10117110023) is a 35-year-old female who is requesting a 7.194.000 VND loan to support her business operating a service-based business.   3.  Hoàng Đình M. (10117110021) is a 49-year-old male who is requesting a 7.194.000 VND loan to support his business raising livestock.   4.  Nguyễn Thị H. (10117110022) is a 27-year-old female who is requesting a 7.194.000 VND loan to support her business operating a butcher shop.   5.  Hoàng Thị L. (10117110020) is a 51-year-old female who is requesting a 7.194.000 VND loan to support her business operating a specialized retail store.   About SEDA:  The mission of SEDA (Center of Small Enterprise Development Assistance) is to provide microfinance services to the low income and disadvantaged people in rural areas of Hanoi and the Northern provinces of Vietnam.   *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in Vietnamese while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.   N. Trần Thị (10117110018) là 39 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy sống ở thành phố Đông Anh - Hà nội.  N. là trưởng nhóm của nhóm vay gồm có 6 các thành viên.  Mặc dù mỗi thành viên trong nhóm nhận được từng khoản vay cá nhân, nhưng tất cả họ đều chịu trách nhiệm hoàn trả lại khoản vay của các thành viên trong nhóm của mình nếu một người nào đó trễ hạn hay không trả được nợ..  Tên chính thức của nhóm vay này là Xóm Thượng 11 (3).   Trong khi không phải chỉ có các phương thức tạo nên thu nhập, mà nguồn thu nhập chính của công việc kinh doanh chủ yếu từ giết mổ & bán thịt heo trong cộng đồng địa phương.  N. thực hiện công việc kinh doanh này trong hơn 4 năm.  Từ các hoạt động này, N. kiếm được khoảng 2.000.000 VND.  Vào 2003, N. đã tham gia SEDA để có thể tiếp cận với các dịch vụ tài chính giúp cải thiện  sinh hoạt và khả năng tham gia vào các hoạt động kinh doanh của cô ấy/ anh ấy.  N. đã hoàn trả hết khoản vay trước đây là 6.750.000 VND từ SEDA.  Khoản vay trước đây được sử dụng đầu tư mở rộng công việc kinh doanh.  Cô ấy hiện đang đề nghị một khoản vay mới là 5.886.000 VND.   Khoản vay sẽ là 8th khoản vay của người vay từ SEDA.   Về Những Người vay khác trong Nhóm:   1.  Vương Thị T. (10117110039) là 45 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 5.450.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực thực phẩm.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là kinh doanh cửa hàng thịt.   2.  Hoàng Thị T. (10117110023) là 35 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 7.194.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực dịch vụ.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là vận hành công việc kinh doanh trên cơ sở dịch vụ.   3.  Hoàng Đình M. (10117110021) là 49 tuổi nam.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 7.194.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực nông nghiệp.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là chăn nuôi gia súc.   4.  Nguyễn Thị H. (10117110022) là 27 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 7.194.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực thực phẩm.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là kinh doanh cửa hàng thịt.   5.  Hoàng Thị L. (10117110020) là 51 tuổi nữ.  Cô ấy đề nghị khoản vay là 7.194.000 VND.  Khoản vay này sẽ được sử dụng để hỗ trợ công việc kinh doanh trong lĩnh vực bán lẻ.  Mục đích chính của việc kinh doanh là kinh doanh cửa hiệu bán lẻ chuyên dụng.   Về SEDA:  Nhiệm vụ của SEDA (Trung Tâm hỗ Trợ Phát Triển các Doanh Nghiệp Nhỏ) là cung cấp các dịch vụ tài chính vi mô cho những người có thu nhập thấp và kém may mắn trong các vùng nông thôn tại Hà Nội và các tỉnh phía Bắc Việt Nam   *Lưu ý: Để phát huy tối đa hiệu quả & giảm chi phí, khoản vay này đã được thông báo bằng biểu mẫu để có thể được Kiva tự động biên dịch. .  Do việc biên dịch thủ công các danh mục rất tốn kém, nên Kiva đã tạo biểu mẫu này cho phần Field Partner (Trường Đối Tác) cho phép họ tiếp tục thông báo các khoản vay bằng  Vietnamese trong khi cung cấp thông tin có chất lượng & chính xác cho người cho vay Kiva.  ."

name: Jomar
description: Jomar is 22 years old and still single. He planned to earn and save more income to help his parents in financing the education of his younger brother and sisters. Due to lack of job opportunities, Jomar engages in buying and selling of betel nuts and tobacco in their community to generate income. He aimed to strengthen the business in order to generate sufficient income. Due to insufficient capital, he is requesting an additional loan of PHP 10,000 to buy more stocks of betel nuts and tobacco to sell in the community. He is hoping that this loan will make it possible for him to improve and strengthen the business.

name: Roselyn
description: Roselyn, 36 years old, is married and has one child. Roselyn works very hard to provide for her family. For the past six years, Roselyn has run a general store in the Philippines. She has requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to buy items such as canned goods, personal care products, milk, coffee, spices, drinks, snack foods, shampoo and other products to sell. In the future, Roselyn would like to save money to expand her business.

name: Abigail
description: Abigail sells soft drinks, biscuits, and bread at Mpohor near Takoradi. She has been selling biscuits and drinks for two years now. Abigail is married and her husband is a mason. She uses her income to support her husband in the general upkeep of their family.   Abigail will use this loan to buy more soft drinks, biscuits, and bread for sale. With the new profit, she will operate a grocery shop.

name: Kimlang
description: Kimlang, village chief of Chhnok Tru village, is a farmer and also a fisherman. He loves working, even though he has almost reached the age of retirement. Even though all his children are independent, he never stops working to keep himself from becoming a lazy man.   He wants to buy solar energy system to save money and have security. Therefore, he is applying for a loan through Kiva to buy a reliable solar energy system for his home. With a solar energy system, he would not be concerned about security at night and safety in the house.
town: Chhnok Tru Village,Chhnok Tru Commune, Boribo Dist

name: Hau
description: Hau is 51 years old and married with three children: two sons and one daughter. He and his wife have had a store for five years.  He would like to borrow a loan to increase the working capital for his business, which will enabL. him to buy better goods to sell at higher margins.   He hopes that through the loan he can improve his family's living conditions.

name: Virgenia
description: Virgenia is 39 years old, married with three children. All of her children are attending school.  Virgenia works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 12000 loan through NWTF in order to purchase more groceries to sell.  Virgenia has borrowed and paid 4 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for four years and also earns an income from frozen foods.  Virgenia aspires to save enough money so she can continue to send her children to school.

name: Sophea
description: Mr. Sophea M., 31, and his wife, Mrs. Sophak Mon, 30, live in a small village along National Road Two, about twenty kilometers south of Phnom Penh.They were married in 1998 and have three children; one son and two daughters. Two of their children are still in school.  Sophea has been a mason for ten years. He does his work in Phnom Penh, while his wife has been a garment factory worker for ten years as well. He is requesting a loan of US$300 to purchase construction materials for expanding their home.

name: Julie
description: Julie works hard to support her family. Julie is married and has a rice retailing business in the Philippines.  Julie requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to purchase more sacks of rice to sell.  Julie has been in this business for 10 years now.  She would like to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Aiga
description: Aiga T. is 55 and married with 5 children (ages 7 - 26).  She owns a business venture, selling ice-cakes (flavored ice in styrofoam cups).  Aiga has 2 years of experience in this business.  Aiga needs a loan of WST $1500 to buy sugar, styrofoam cups, and codial (flavoring).  She plans to use the earnings from her business (estimated to be 400 talas or US $167 per week) to improve/expand the business.  Aiga T. is a strong, motivated client and wishes to have not only the ice cake busines but also a back up business to assist her with planting and elei as well.  In 2009, Aiga joined SPBD.    This is her 2nd loan with SPBD.   SPBD's loans are Aiga's only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with traditional banks.  The following social metrics for Aiga T. are provided by SPBD*: Overall Social Metric Score:                1.5 out of 3 Level of Education:                         2 out of 3 Level of total Household Income:            2 out of 3 Quality of Household Assets:                2 out of 3  *SPBD measures the living conditions of each of its borrowers to track her loan progress.  The overall social metric score, provided by SPBD, is based upon a number of factors, such as the condition of the house/household assets, health, education, income level, and family reputation.  A higher number represents a higher score.  For example, a ""3 out of 3"" on education would mean that the borrower has graduated from university; a ""2 out of 3"" = secondary/high-school, and a ""1 out of 3"" would mean that the borrower is uneducated.    For more information on this score, please see SPBD's partner page at: http://partners.kiva.org/about/aboutPartner?id=15  About  SPBD  In 2000, Greg Casagrande founded SPBD and since then, it has expanded from the main island of Upolu in Samoa to Savaii, as well as Tonga.  SPBD's philosophy of lending is based upon the Grameen Bank lending method.    Please join SPBD's lending team on KIVA to receive on-the-spot updates on SPBD: http://www.kiva.org/community/viewTeam?team_id=8375

name: Buenerge
description: Buenerge is a gentleman who works growing corn and beans.  He is 56 years old and lives in San Rafael Oriente, in San Miguel department, together with his wife and three children aged 22, 20 and 16.  He has been farming for 35 years and works every day of the week.  He works longer during the sowing and harvest seasons.  Buenerge currently needs a loan as he is starting the process of preparing his land and he needs to buy agricultural supplies (manure and fertilizers).  The winter is approaching and the time is right to start sowing his crops.  This loan will help him to cover the expense and he will have everything he needs to care for his new crops.  He hopes for a good harvest.  Buenerge's main goal is to work his land.  He has been in this business for many years and he does not plan to stop.  He will continue helping his family, in particular he will support his children in their education.
town: San Rafael de Oriente, San Miguel

name: Edarlina
description: Edarlina, 40 years old, is married with seven grown-up children. She lives in a village of San Pedro province of Isabela. Edarlina is engaged in selling different products in her community.   Edarlina is asking for a loan amounting 8,000 PHP (Philippines pesos) to buy canned goods, spices and commodities for her store. She hopes that her dream is granted for her family.

name: Rosalie
description: Rosalie owns and operates a garden in the village of Salimpuno, Pana-on, Misamis Occidental. Her husband is a farmer and provides their main source of income.   Rosalie joined Gata Daku MPC in 2012 and she has borrowed 3,000 PHP to purchase fertilizer for her flower garden. While her three children are young, she is saving a portion of her income for their education in the future.

name: Dominga De Los Angeles
description: Dominga de los Angeles is 50 years old and she has a butcher shop. She has had this business for more than 2 years. She started this business with very little working capital but with a great deal of effort she has been able to succeed. She has always enjoyed to work and to support her family. She requests this loan to purchase chicken, eggs, and meats. She dreams of always having an active lifestyle.

name: Toshbibi
description: Toshbibi is very glad that you helped her. Thanks to you, she is advancing her business. Her sons help her with sowing and harvesting. Toshbibi has decided to plant melons and watermelons. She is requesting a loan in order to obtain mineral fertilisers and seeds. Toshbibi believes in you and your support.

name: Ingrid
description: Sra. Ingrid is a seamstress who makes satchels for all ages.  She sells her products at a market in the city of La Paz.  Her husband works in the interior of Bolivia.  The loan she is requesting will be used to buy an industrial sewing machine in order to speed up the sewing process in making satchels so that she can sell more.  This business enables her to cover the family expenses.  Ingrid lives at the home of her in-laws in the District of Villa Cooperativa in the city of El Alto.    Ingrid has been a client of IMPRO since 2010 and this is the first time her loan has been referred to Kiva for funding.

name: Angela
description: Angela is 33 years old and married with four children. With three children in school, she works very hard to provide for them.  Angela runs a general store in the Philippines, and requested a PHP 13,000 loan through NWTF to buy additional items to sell like canned goods, beverages, groceries, etc..  She has been in this business for one year now.   In the future, Angela would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Mildred
description: Mildred is 48 years old, and a married woman with three children. Two of her children are in school. She is a very hardworking entrepreneur.   Mildred has a food vending business in the Philippines. She requested a PHP 10,000 loan amount through NWTF to buy ingredients for her food business.  Mildred has been in this business for three years. In the future, she would like to save enough money to expand her business and continue to send her children to school.
