name: Honn's Group
description: The members of Honn’s group live in a rural village in Prey Veng Province in Cambodia. Honn makes a living cultivating rice to support her family. In their village, there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each of these women safeguard the health of her family, save money on medical expenses, and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Rosita
description: Rosita is 44 years old and married with two children. She works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 13,500 loan through NWTF to buy additional stocks to sell in her general store.  Rosita has been in this business for two years and sells a variety of items such as rice, feeds, eggs, diapers, canned goods, soft drinks, etc.   She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Sarah
description: Sarah B. is married, has one child and has received an education through Senior High School. Since 2006, she has worked as a trader selling canned tomatoes, beans and rice at Elmina. While Sarah works as a trader, her husband is employed as a computer mechanic. Sarah will use the loan to purchase more food supplies for selling. With the new profits from her expanded business, Sarah plans to save towards buying a piece of land.

name: José Ismael
description: José is 54 years old and did not have the opportunity to go to school as his parents were very poor. José has a partner, and a son who now lives abroad.  José has been working in farming since his childhood. He is growing a hectare of corn just now, and also does fishing work. José learned to fish from a friend; he has been doing it for five years.  José needs this loan in order to buy manure, fertiliser and fishing equipment.  José's dream is to have a good harvest and to improve his income from fishing work. He knows that he will be able to do this with the help of a loan.

name: Flores Marie
description: Flores Marie is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a vegetable farming business in the Philippines. She is borrowing PHP 18,000 through NWTF to purchase additional seeds and fertilizers for her vegetable farming business.Flores Marie has been in this business for nine years. She earns additional income from selling vegetables.Flores Marie has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She hopes to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Mavludahon
description: Mavludahon is from the Rudaki region. She is married and the mother of three children. Mavludahon is 62 years old. She has worked for 43 years as a hospital nurse. Mavludahon is a caring, joyful and kind woman. She loves to help and to do good to others. Her son is very ill. He needs an operation in order to save his life. Mavludahon has not been able to collect the money because her monthly salary is not sufficient for her living expenses. She has been obliged to turn to you for a loan. Mavludahon very much hopes for your support. She loves her children and does not want to lose them. Her children are still young and their lives are ahead. Any mother would do the same in Mavludahon's place. Please support her!

name: Gladys
description: Gladys is 29 years old and a member of Faulu Kenya under Maono group.  She sells electronics and plastic containers such as disposed basins and pegs.  She has engaged in the business for five years.  She hopes to succeed in the business so as to help her community.  She is glad to be a member of Faulu Kenya because she has gained knowledge on business management.  She has requested for 20, 000 Kes to buy radios, bulbs, plastics and spanners.

name: Van
description: Van K., 61, is married and resides with his wife and five children in Battambong Province, Cambodia, an area known for its good quality rice products. He is a security guard and is able to earn an income of about USD 2 per day, while his wife produces traditional lamps, earning an income of USD 3 per day to help cover the family expenses.  K. is requesting a loan of USD 1200 to purchase construction material to repair the house.  This is his first loan from CREDIT, a long-standing Kiva partner in Cambodia.

name: Los Claveles De Jojutla Group
description: This group is called "Claveles de Jojutla" (the Jojutla Carnations) because that’s the name of the street where the members of the group live.  They are located in the state of Morales in Mexico.  The group is made up of 12 members and this is the first time they have applied for a loan.    Verónica García B. is the group’s treasurer.  She is 44 years old and studied through primary school.  She is involved in the sale of cosmetics, a business she began 12 years ago.  She is applying for the loan in order to enlarge her business and is planning on investing it in the purchase of more merchandise such as perfumes, creams, deodorants, and cosmetics in general.  Her customers prefer her because she is an attentive, pleasant person and because she always delivers their orders on time.  She is very happy to be applying for the loan.  She wants to use the loan to buy more merchandise for her business and, with the earnings she obtains, invest in the business in order to offer her products to more people.  She also wants to improve her house in order to offer a more respectable life to her family.

name: Fatima's Group
description: Fatima is a 38-year-old mother of two sons. She lives in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. Her husband is a mason by profession, and he is responsible for feeding his family and managing the entire household. Fatima has been running her own business selling clothes for the past six years. And she also contributes her income with her husband's to fulfill the needs of her family.  Fatima needs different types of clothes for the purpose of reselling, but she does not have enough money to buy these clothes in bulk. Therefore, she has applied for a Kiva group loan with other two members. With the help of this loan, she can easily purchase clothes in bulk for her business purpose.  For this financial assistance, Fatima is very thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan.

name: Marife
description: Marife landed at a right place for her needed capital when she joined PMPC. She knew this would be her last chance to get back on her feet when she went broke after her first business went bad. PMPC to Marife came as a rescue for lending her money when she needed it the most. Now, she availed another loan for the next cropping season. She will use the loaned amount for land and seedbed preparation.  Marife perseveres and always believes to reach her goals to continuously provide for her family.

name: Carmen Idilia
description: The 'La Amistad' (Friendship) community bank meets every two weeks in the beautiful city of Calceta.  This city is known as 'Calceta la sin par' (Calceta, the city with no equal) because of the beauty of its women and because, as far as the locals are concerned, there is no more beautiful city in the world.  Here we meet Carmen.  She is 52 years old, separated, and has four daughters.  Three of her daughters are grown up and her youngest is 16.  Two of her daughters live at home and are studying at university and high school.  Carmen works as a civil servant in a State institution.  She also sells clothing and Avon products (beauty products, cosmetics, perfumes and ladies' accessories).  In addition, she has a business renting out marquees which are used by her customers at social events.  Carmen makes her sales in her free time and on her days off.  She leaves her products on credit and collects payment every two weeks.  She has been in business for more than five years and is doing very well.  Carmen will use this loan to buy perfumes, creams and cosmetics.  She will also have another marquee made as they make her very good profits.  This is her fourth loan cycle with her community bank and she likes it because the payments are easy to make.  Carmen's dream is for her daughters to finish their education.

name: Mercy
description: Mercy, 27 years old, is married and has four school-going children. She has had a cereals business for the last seven years and the business gives her a good income. Mercy will be using the loan to purchase cereals, and she hopes this will help her pay school fees. Her hope and dream for the future is to have a better business.

name: Jane
description: Jane is a widowed lady and mother of two children.  She has a photo studio which she has been running for eight years.  She gained her skills for photography because she was previously a camera lady.  Faulu Kenya is an MFI which offers training for her clients.  Therefore, Jane appreciates that she has learned how to keep her business records.  She intends to buy a photocopy machine hence she has requested for a loan of Kes.30,000.  She hopes to open other outlets of the same business.

name: Clarita
description: As a married parent of 10 children, Clarita works hard to support her family.  She has a vegetable vending business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from running general store.  Clarita is taking out a loan of 5,000 PHP through NWTF to buy additional vegetables to stock and to sell in her vegetable vending business.  Clarita has been sustaining her business activities through her previous four loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so that she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Martina
description: Martina is a 47-year-old married woman and a mother of six children from Getafe, Bohol. She is engaged in selling firewood at the market. Her husband works as a fisherman.  Martina is asking for a loan to buy more firewood to sell and new fishing nets. Martina believes that this loan can help her in improving her business.

name: Catalina
description: Mrs. Catalina was living with a partner, but he is now working as a tailor in Brazil. She has a son in school and they live in her in-law’s house, where they have two rooms: the bedroom and the living room. The bedroom has plastered brick walls and a cement floor. The house is located in the Villa Bolívar area, city of El Alto. Catalina works cleaning a food establishment and receives a monthly salary. She pays for the food and utilities at home.  Catalina is requesting a loan to buy school supplies for her son, now that the season has started again and he needs them. Her dream is to have her own grocery store at home and receive an income that can help her improve her quality of life.  This is Catalina’s second loan with Kiva and her fourth with IMPRO.

name: Carmen Liseth
description: Carmen Liseth is 34 years old and resides in Delgado City.  She lives with her 4 children who are all students.  Carmen has a clothing store for children, women and men in the Delgado City Municipal Market.  Her two eldest daughters help her with the business, attending to customers.  Carmen requests a loan to buy a greater variety of clothing, since she has a very good clientèle and  wants to be able to offer them more options in sizes and colors, in order to obtain greater earnings.  Carmen is a single mother but this hasn't stopped her from working in order to offer everything that her daughters need.  On the contrary, this motivates her to forge ahead and continue struggling for them.Translated from Spanish by Harold Sims, Kiva Volunteer
town: Ciudad Delgado en el departamento de San  Salvador

name: Juana Alexandra
description: Juana Alexandra is 21-years-old, she is single, and she lives in her family home together with her parents and siblings. They live in the Zaña district in Chiclayo, in the Lambayeque department in Peru. She has many great personal references as well as professional references from her neighbours in the area. The majority of the other inhabitants in this area make a living from agriculture, trade and cattle breeding.   Juana Alexandra makes a living from selling groceries such as rice, sugar, milk, oil etc, and has one year of experience in this line of work. She is requesting this loan in order to invest in buying more stock such as soaps, detergents, tuna etc. In this way she can stock her business and pay for other various expenses.   Juan Alexandra is a new member with Edpyme Alternativa.

name: Ameera
description: Ameera is a 45-year-old housewife. Her sons and daughters are now able to care for themselves. Her husband is a farmer who plants vegetables and fruit, and then sells his produce to shops in Jenin.  Because her children are grown, Ameera thought she might help her husband by renting a small shop to sell the vegetables and fruits he produces. Ameera took a $1,000 loan to rent the shop and prepare it to exhibit vegetables and fruits. Ameera sells at a good price in order to have regular customers.  Ala, Ameera's son, appears in the photograph in the Faten office, because Ameera is not comfortable having her picture online.

name: Mildred's Group
description: Mildred is a proud 27-year-old mother of 6 children. She is a group leader, often described as a very hardworking individual, and she is representing her group of 13 farmers in the Teso District. Since joining One Acre Fund in 2014, Mildred has noticed that she has been able to consistently feed her family.Mildred described her harvest last year as good, but believes she can have an even better one this year by continuing to work with One Acre Fund. She is very excited also to be purchasing a solar light, apart from fertilizer and maize, because she will now be able to reduce her consumption of paraffin fuel and therefore save more money. With the profits from this season’s harvest, she plans to buy a cow.With this loan, Mildred’s Group will be able to plant a total of 5.75 acres of land and purchase a total of 8 solar lights.

name: Virginia
description: Virginia lives in Monterrey in the state of Nuevo León. She is 44 years old and is married and at the moment does not have children. She works as an administrator and recently her vision has been affected by an ailment. This is reflected in her work performance. With the loan that she requests, she will have a treatment that will help her recover her health. Along with her husband, they have the desire to be parents so she doesn't want the ailment to impede her from forming the family that she has wanted so much.

name: Jeanne
description: Jeanne is 39 years old and is married with five children who are 5, 9, 11, 13 and 15 years old. Jeanne and her family live in Rulindo, a region of the Northern Province of Rwanda. Here, Jeanne lives by selling domestic animals including cows and goats. This is her ninth successful year in this business and her business hours are from 7 a.m. until late in the evening hours.  As Jeanne has gained experience in selling domestic animals, her number of customers has increased to the the extent that her original investment seems to be too low to purchase enough cows and goats for sale. She would like to request a Kiva loan via Vision Finance Company so that she can increase her sales.  With this loan, and with her hope to satisfy the demand of her customers by selling at the cheapest price, Jeanne will do that and, of course, her profits will increase. With those profits, one portion will be used to build a secure future for her family and another portion will be used to reinvest in her business.

name: Akote Group
description: Patrick is pictured on the right with his hand raised amongst his Akote Group members. The 23 of them, 15 women and 8 men, are farmers in the Teso District. Farming inputs will be delivered to him on credit consisting of the necessary materials to plant ½ acre of sweet potatoes, millet, and sorghum. Patrick is a new One Acre Fund farmer and is excited for the 2013 Long Rains season. He joined One Acre Fund in order to grow enough food for his family and use the increased profits to send his children to school.  Patrick described his harvest last year as good, but hopes he can have an even better one as a One Acre Fund farmer. He plans to use the money that he earns from his next harvest to send his children to school and save for the future. During the 2013 Long Rains season, each group member will receive ½ an acre of agricultural inputs on credit. Patrick’s group will receive 11.5 acres worth of inputs on credit.

name: Rosa Amelia
description: Rosa is 53 years old and lives with her life partner and two of her four children.    She has been selling all types of merchandise at the market for 26 years. She sells clothing, vegetables, and anything else that she can sell for profit. Rosa buys her merchandise at 5:30 in the morning at the market at wholesale prices and she later walks through the markets with baskets selling it at retail.  She is asking for a loan from Fundación Campo in order to buy a stall in the market. Then she will no longer have to walk about with her merchandise and her customers will know where to find her. This will help her a great deal in that she will earn higher income, which will help her give better food to her family and improve their standard of life. Furthermore, she is supporting her daughter who is studying to be a nurse and her dream is that she finishes her studies and also that she can expand her business and carry more merchandise.

name: Julia
description: Julia has a business selling car brakes.  She works from 8am to 6pm.  She has done this work for many years and it is going well.  Her dream is to expand her business.  She is requesting a loan to purchase car brakes.  She is happy to receive this loan and promises to make her payments as scheduled.

name: Phoey's Group
description: Phoey, 45, is married and lives with her husband and three children in a village of the Srey Snom district of Siem Reap Province. One of her three children is a dependent and still in school. She and her husband are rice farmers. She has been in the rice farming business for 25 years, earning about 20,000 KHR per day to feed her family.   Phoey just joined VisionFund this cycle. Now, she is leading her group of four to ask for a loan. As the leader, she is going to use her portion to buy fertilizer for her farmland. With this loan, she hopes to increase her crop yields and earn more income to better her family’s living condition.
town: Siem Reap Province, Srey Snom district

name: Lesther Vidal
description: Lesther Vidal is 23 years old,single, and lives in Villa del Carmen, located in the department of Managua.  He has a 2 year old son.  His goal is to improve his quality of life to benefit his family.  He now works in the Villa del Carmen mayor’s office.  Before, he worked in a bakery.  He has found it difficult because his salary is not sufficient to make improvements for his house.  With the Afodenic loan, he will purchase construction materials such as cement, iron, blocks, flooring, and others.  The infrastructure in his house is worn out and requires retouching, which will offer protection and security for his family. Translated from Spanish by Kathleen O'Connell, Kiva Volunteer

name: Felisa
description: Felisa is a married woman with one child who is in school. She is a very hard working entrepreneur. Felisa is 43 years old now.  Felisa has a food vending business in the Philippines and requested a 5,000 PHP loan through NWTF to buy ingredients for her food production business.  Felisa has been in this business for three years. In the future, she would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Etelvina
description: The associate belongs to the community bank "Sumac Puririsun".  The bank is located in the district of Cusco, belonging to the province and department of Cusco. The member is Mrs Etelvina, she is 34 years old, lives with a partner and has 2 children.  She divides her time between her daily family activities and a restaurant business.  She runs it by herself because her husband works on construction projects (master builder).  She is a very enterprising woman with desires to get ahead.  The associate is requesting a loan to buy more products for her business, such as sugar, rice, mixed vegetables among others.  The associate thanks all that are part of this dream and promises to comply with the loan payments within the time established.

name: Ramathan
description: Ramathan is a married man with 3 children. He describes himself to be ambitious. He operates a retail business where he sells groundnuts, tomatoes. He has been involved in this business for 3 years. His business is located in a good area and his primary customers are locals. He will use the Kes 30,000 loan to buy more stock of groundnuts, tomatoes. This is his second loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. The previous loan was repaid successfully. He will use the anticipated profits to expand the business.

name: Kuña Kyrey Group
description: The Kuna Kyrey group is in its third loan cycle in the Women's Communal Bank program.The member's goals are to help one another and in this manner to grow, not only economically, but also personally.  Rossana helps to support her family by selling shoes by special order. The purpose of the loan that she is asking for is to obtain more capital in order to buy shoes for resale. Rossana is very enthusiastic and by means of the trainings hopes to grow and to help her family. This group stands out because each member puts forth their best efforts so that their families will not have to be needy and will have a better lifestyle.

name: Memuna
description: Salone Microfinance Trust (SMT), a partner of Kiva.org in Makeni, northern Sierra Leone, is very pleased to present to you Memuna, a small-scale entrepreneur who has come to SMT/Kiva lenders to apply for a loan of 5,000,000 SLL (Sierra Leone leones) in order to invest in her business.   Memuna sells ready-to-wear clothes, gara cloth (locally dyed cloth), Bamako cloth (ones dyed in Mali), portmanteaux, etc. She has been doing business for 20 years now.   She is a wife and a mother of three children. Her husband is a trader, too, and two of her children are attending primary and secondary school.   Memuna has requested this loan in order to buy ready-to-wear clothes, gara cloth, Bamako cloth, portmanteaux, etc., to add to her business.

name: Epefania
description: Epefania has been growing rice to provide for her family. She gets up early and has to go to her farm where she oversees her crops. She solely provides for her family and she is hoping to have better farm produce.   She has repaid successfully her previous loan used for farming. She took a new loan recently to purchase fertilizer for this cropping season. In the future, she wants to provide a better living to her family.

name: Jesús Alfonso
description: Jesús, at the age of 26, works as a practicioner of accounting in a consulting business located in the town where he lives. But, in the spirit of generating income on his own account, he wants to begin a productive project, a fast food business, since he has knowledge about the management of this type of business because he had the opportunity to work in this field at the age of 18. His entrepreneurial spirit, his enthusiasm, and his will to achieve and progress drive him to apply for the loan, with which he wants to buy a fast-food cart, cooking utensils, and wholesale stock (breads, salsas, cold meats, cheeses, and soft drinks, among other items). Thus he will be able to start up his business idea, with which he hopes to generate the necessary income to assist his family with the economic burden of the household. Furthermore, he has the advantage of having knowledge in accounting, which will allow him to better track his income and expenditures in order to make this business a source of income that in time is profitable and sustainable. Jesús shows his eagerness to start his project, since he wants to get a reputation and become known in the district and in the future be able to set up his business in a well-located commercial location with a greater flow of people, generating greater income to offer his family a better quality of life and well-being.

name: Nhóm 02 Thôn Trung 01 Group
description: Mrs Sử operates a food stall where she sells fish. She is requesting a loan to purchase fish to resell.  Sử is 49 years old and married with nine children. Sử is the group leader of the Nhóm 02 thôn Trung 01 solidarity group, which consists of four members.   Sử lives in a rural town in the Quang Xuong district, which is in the Thanh Hoa province.  In 2007, Sử joined the Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women to improve her  business. Sử has successfully repaid eight loans from the Thanh Hoa Fund for Poor Women.  Sử has been involved in this business for more than 10 years.  The main hardship that Sử faces in her business is a lack of capital.  In the future, Sử hopes for her business to do well, to travel and take a vacation in the country, and for her family to be healthy and happy.

name: Susan
description: This is Susan. She was born in 1983 in Kirinyaga county, Kenya. She is married with three children. Without any formal employment, horticulture farming has helped her face the challenge of providing for her family. She has seen progression in her farming and has been able to meet the basic need of the family without much struggle. Her dream is to grow her agribusiness activities to a big enterprise where she will transport products using her own pick-up vehicle.  A loan from Kiva will fast track her business growth towards achieving her dream.

name: Samina
description: Samina's husband is a milkman by profession and sells milk in his community. He is very expert at producing milk from a buffalo and he produces milk from his all buffaloes in no time. He has many buffaloes. This is the reason he has to do very hard work to feed them.Samina is taking Kiva loan for her husband. He wants to buy a buffalo so that he can increase his monthly income and educate his children.She hopes that her husband would be able to buy a buffalo and he will be successful in increasing his monthly income as well. Samina thanks Kiva and field partner, BRAC Pakistan.

name: Stanley
description: Stanley is a married man. He has 2 children. He describes himself to be focused. He operates a constuction business. He has been involved in this business for 6 years. His primary customers are the general public. He describes his biggest business challenge to be lack of enough funds. He will use the Kes 20,000 loan to purchase additional stock to expand his business and to improve the services. His business goal is to be successful within 5 years.

name: Lilian
description: Lilian is 42 years old, married, and the mother of two. She lives with her husband and her minor son who is in fifth grade. Lilian is a hardworking woman with an entrepreneurial vision. Her business is called “Digicentro MyL,” where she provides photocopy services, transcription, printing, photographs, and also sells school and office supplies. She’s been doing this for approximately eight years and things have been going well thanks to her good management. Sometimes she gets some special contracts from schools, friends, or other companies in the community. She will use the money from this loan to buy supplies and equipment to better satisfy her customers.  She has been responsible with her previous loans and paid them back on time.

name: Jose
description: Mr. Jose is 32 years old. He was born in Chuquissaca on the 12 of November, 1978. He is married to Ms. Elodia who is 31 years old. They live in the town of Liras which is 25 km from El Torno, towards the west. He was fortunate that the agrarian syndicate endowed him with 12 hectares, where he lives and works raising corn, yucca, rice, and peanuts. All their harvest is sold in the market in El Torno. The money he is asking for is to buy a motorcycle so that he will be able to travel the long distances that he needs to. Buying this mode of transportation will help a lot. It is hard work and he is very grateful to Emprender and Kiva for the confidence and support provided to him in authorizing the loan.         .    						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 						 Translated from Spanish by Machelle Wilson, Kiva Volunteer

name: Elisa
description: As a married parent of four children, Elisa works hard to support her family.  She has a restaurant business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from her general store.  Elisa is borrowing PHP 29,500 through NWTF to buy ingredients for her restaurant business.  Elisa has been sustaining her business activities through her past 21 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Pinky
description: As a married parent of three children, Pinky works hard to support her family.  She has a buy-and-sell rice grains business in the Philippines and also earns additional income from farming rice. Pinky is borrowing PHP 8,000 through Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation, Inc. (NWTF) to purchase additional sacks of rice grains to sell through her buy-and-sell rice grains business.  Pinky has been sustaining her business activities through her past two loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money to buy more farm land.

name: Tutikhon
description: Tutikhon A. is 52 years old and a widow. She has a son and a daughter. Tutikhon is a market vendor and she sells trousers and shirts for men in the local market. Her children help her in the business. Tutikhons’s daughter is pictured in the photo as Tutikhon had left that day for the neighboring city. Tutikhon has been in this business for eleven years already. During these years she has managed to make her business stable and profitable, generating the main income for her family. Tutikhon is trying to satisfy the needs of any client with various tastes and income levels. She works very hard to give her dearest children a good education and to make them happy. In order to cover the higher education expenses of her daughter as she’s going to enter the university, Tutikhon is planning to increase her working capital in order to purchase the new summer goods to sell. With this purpose Tutikhon requests $870 US Dollars for the term of 3 months. Tutikhon promises to repay the loan promptly and thanks all supporting her. Your support will really help her. Be an important part of the growth of Tutikhon’s business.

name: Rosario Del Carmen
description: Rosario, 32, finished primary school. She could not continue studying because she was the only one helping her mother to generate some income for the family. She is married and has three children aged 8, 4, and 5.  Rosario’s parents taught her to work and take care of farm animals when she was a little girl. When she got married, she continued with this activity, remembering what she learned from them. Now, she owns a broilers farm, although she also sells vegetables. Her partner sells fish, bought in a nearby lagoon. He sells it door-to-door to his customers, using a motorcycle.  She will use this loan to build a pen with a larger capacity, and to buy more chickens and feed for them.  Rosario dreams of giving her children a good education. She also dreams of building a house, because the one she has is made of metal sheets. She would also like to have a bigger farm.

name: Luciano
description: Luciano is studying in the fourth year of an agricultural engineering program. Through his studies, he wants to make something of himself in life in order to help others. He is a hard-working student who, while studying, also works as a way to fund his studies.   He is asking for this loan in order to cover the costs of his degree, and thus to continue studying.

name: Alamoka
description: Alamoka S. from Mbeya is 50 years old. She is married and has 5 children, all between the ages of 13 and 30. Additionally, she is responsible for supporting one other dependent, because the child is an orphan.  Alamoka has been running her own shop since 2006, purchasing and re-selling a variety of commodities. She works 9-12 hours per day, and can earn about US$ 90 a month from her business. She is now requesting a loan in order to purchase commodities in bulk for re-sale. In the future, she plans to open a new business. Alamoka thanks you for your support!  ABOUT SELFINA: SELFINA has taken a lead role as a pioneer of micro-credit in Tanzania through Micro-Leasing. The organization is engaged in the economic empowerment of women in Tanzania through the provision of a leasing and leaseback microfinance facility. Customs and traditions in Tanzania make it difficult for women to own land and assets, thus they are termed non-creditworthy by financial institutions. This leads to poor financial support and poor access to basic needs and services for women with low incomes. One of the primary advantages of micro leasing is that is allows clients to use the equipment as collateral for future loans with SELFINA, thus enabling them to borrow larger sums in the future.

name: Magdalena
description: Magdalena C. is from the village of Cabisera 5. She is 60 years old. Magdalena is married and has 4 adult children. To make a living, Magdalena owns and operates a general store. While not the only means for generating revenue, the main source of income for the business comes primarily from selling  vegetables in the local community. Magdalena has been engaged in her business for over 10 years and earns approximately 3,700 PHP a month for these activities.  In 2007, Magdalena joined ASKI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Magdalena has successfully repaid a previous loan of 25,000 PHP from ASKI. This previous loan was used to purchase additional products to sell. Magdalena is requesting a new loan of 28,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase additional products to sell. This loan will be the 8th loan taken out by Magdalena from ASKI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve/expand her business.   About ASKI:  ASKI is one of the most successful microfinance institutions in the Philippines. It has 29 branches covering the Central and Northeastern areas. Its clients are mostly farmers, fisherfolks and small entrepreneurs.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Imara De Los Angeles
description: Imara has worked at a teacher in a public school for the past 6 years. She teaches children between the ages of 8 and 10.   She currently needs this loan to buy construction materials such as zinc, cement, bricks and beams for her house which was affected by the earthquakes that occurred in April 2014. She is grateful to Ceprodel for their support in obtaining this loan which she will use to repair her home and provide a better life to her children.

name: Rebecca
description: Rebecca is 46 years old. She is married with 3 children. She has had a business farming in Nakuru town for the past 10 years.   Rebecca will be using her loan to purchase seeds and fertilizer so she can plant and raise more farm produce. She hopes this will help her sell more maize and vegetables to her customers and increase her overall income to support her family.   Rebecca's hopes and dreams for the future are to become a large scale farmer and earn greater profits so she can provide for her children's needs such as food and education.

name: Aura Lidia
description: Mrs. Aura Lidia E. G. is an active worker for the Ministry of Health. She is an Assistant Nurse and has worked for this institution for twenty five years. She is presently married. She has taken out six loans from CEPRODEL and has taken out each one to purchase construction materials to enlarge and improve her home.  The loans with Ceprodel have really benefitted her since she has been able to improve the quality of life for herself and for her family.

name: Sajida
description: Sajida is 40 years old, a married woman and a mother of 4 children. The income generated by her husband is insufficient to cover all household expenses, so she initiated her business of milk sales. She has been doing it for many years and has become famous for providing good quality milk in her locality.   With the support of Kashf Foundation, she has gradually improved her business; currently she has requested for a loan of 45,000 PKR  to purchase another buffalo to increase her sales and earn profits so she can provide her family with the basic necessities of life.

name: Milagros
description: As a married parent of four children, Milagros works hard to support her family.  She has a business selling purified drinking water in the Philippines. She also earns additional income from selling ready-to-wear clothing. Milagros is borrowing 19,000 PHP through NWTF to purchase additional containers of purified drinking water to sell.  Milagros has been sustaining her business activities through her past 21 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to build and expand her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Jane Wambui
description: Jane has been operating a boutique shop in Ndunyu Njeru town for the last eight years.  She is a 47-year-old lady married to David G. Kamau. They have seven children.  She was introduced to KADET LTD by her friend and this will be her first loan. She plans to use the loan to boost her boutique shop stock and also buy a dairy cow.   In the future she hopes to expand her boutique business and be able to import clothes from other countries.

name: Bant Bway (North) Village
description: Located in Central Myanmar’s Yin Mar Pin township, this community currently has 47 village customers, including 7 CBO (Community Based Organization) committee members who help to lead the loan program in the area. This village is located in Myanmar's dry zone, where insufficient rainfall is very common. Most villagers are Buddhist and struggle finding access to affordable credit, as the state-owned agricultural bank is not active in the area.  Additionally, the land of this village is made up of salty sand, which makes farming and getting access to fresh water difficult.   This new loan will help borrowers hire labor for the planting and harvesting seasons and purchase high quality farming inputs such as topsoil and fertilizer, which will boost crop yields. This boost in crop yields will lead to an increase in crop sales, and this additional income will be invested in a tractor, which will cost about $2,400.  As farmers cannot currently afford their own tractor, most of the farmers have to lease a machine for $12 a day, plus diesel fees.  Mechanization is especially important in this village, as many young people who would be hired as day laborers are migrated to urban centers in search of economic opportunities.  Pictured above are the committee members from the village CBO: U Win, U Htay, U Thein, U Aung, U Shwe, and U Zaw. Included in the photo (second from the left) is U Htay, who is 52 years old and has seven family members, including three small children who attend primary school in the village. He aspires to use his loan to buy fertilizer and topsoil to enrich his sesame and bean crops.

name: Jean
description: Jean is 41 years old and has two children. She has land that she cultivates and also plans to raise goats on her farm. She approached Paglaum MPC to buy goats. She wants to take advantage of the high demand for goat meat. In the future, Jean hopes to sustain her business and  open an eatery.

name: Sreypao's Group
description: Sreypao’s group lives in a rural village in the Prey Veng province in Cambodia. Sreypao makes a living growing rice and working construction to support her family.   The village has no reliable access to safe, clean, drinking water.  A home water filter will help each member to safeguard their family's  health,  save money on medical expenses, and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Rose Marie
description: Rose Marie works hard to support her family. She is married, and has a restaurant business in the Philippines.  She has requested a loan of 35,000 PHP through NWTF to purchase more stock of ingredients such as spices, vegetables, meat, etc.  Rose Marie has been in this business for 14 years.  She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Hikmatullo
description: N. Hikmatullo is 27 years old and is married with three children. Five years ago he started his business selling cell phones. He believes that this business is profitable and the generated income allows him to support his family.  However, Hikmatullo thinks that it is expensive to purchase cell phones locally and it will save money for him if he purchases the goods in China. With this purpose in mind, he requests a loan of 1,800 USD.  This being his second loan, Hikmatullo is grateful to all supporting him and promises to repay the loan promptly.   More about Tajikistan and IMON International Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium B.C. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj.

name: Elvire
description: Born in 1984 in Sakété in Bénin, Elvire L. is married to Joseph AKPATA and is mother to two children. The couple have two other children in their care. Some of the children are at school. Elvire lives with her children and her husband in the Kpakpakanmé district of Cotonou, the economic capital of Bénin. She has lived in this district for the past four years and helps her husband to cover the family expenses. Elvire is a hairdresser. She has her hairdressing salon at home and also sells hairpieces and cosmetics. She gets her stocks at Dantokpa, the international market in Bénin. Elvire has been carrying out this activity for seven years. She is applying for the first time for a loan from ALIDé, in order to expand her activity and make more money. Translated from French by Alison Le Bras, Kiva Volunteer

name: Alixis Esplenda
description: I sell quality second-hand clothing, and I use my earnings to support my children. I have been doing this job for two years since I have been unable to find steady work and need to help my family. Selling used clothing is a good business since not everyone is economically able to pay for new clothes in stores.

name: Hasina's Darajabovu Group
description: Hasina  is 25  years and is married with a 1 year old child. She has been a  bites seller since 2006. She works everyday  from 6am to 5pm and can earn a monthly profit of about $20 from her sales.   In the past, Hasina  has taken out one successful loan from BRAC Tanzania to expand her business. Hasina is now requesting a loan to further expand her business. She will share this loan with her subgroup members, who have  businesses selling clothes, bites, firewood and charcoal.

name: Gladys
description: Gladys G. is the mother of two children, both boys, who are currently in the senior high and the primary schools. She is thirty-six years old and divorced. She lives with her children in a rented apartment in Dwenase, a suburb of Sefwi-Wiawso in the Western Region of Ghana.  Gladys is a food vendor. She fries and sells doughnuts in her community. She supplies other retailers and sells the rest by hawking (selling door-to-door). She buys bags of flour from nearby towns.  Gladys has been in business for two years and wants a loan to buy bags of flour and other ingredients such as cooking oil, sugar, etc. in bulk. She desires to expand her business and to give her children a good education.

name: Damir
description: Damir is a cheerful young man who loves his work. His woodwork is always in high demand even though his pieces cost more than similar ones made of plastic and other materials. According to Damir, his higher prices are due to the cost of the natural materials he uses and the complexity of the process. Wooden furniture can make any room more inviting and wooden frames and doors are considered to be more environmentally friendly. Some things just cannot be made from a material other than wood. He feels that his carpentry business needs a relatively small investment, though it is true that the profits are also fairly small. He understands that this is due to a few factors, the most important being the range of his business activities, the quality of his products, and his methods of marketing. He does everything on his own without any advertising and makes a variety of furniture, including traditional chests.   Damir is planning to purchase the materials to make furniture. He hopes that it will help his business to take a loan to buy lumber and increase his production.

name: Benkadi Group
description: The group Benkadi comprises five married women and one widow. They average 30 years of age and three children each and live for the most part in traditional families in the Massablacoura district in Bougouni City. They know one another through ties of community, friendship, and commerce. To bolster their financial capacity, so as to work in commerce better, they joined the microfinance institution Soro Yiriwaso and are now on their second loan.  This group of women does commerce in grains, cosmetics, firewood, shoes, clothing, and general merchandise.   N’tenin, who is the group member with papers in hand in the photo, buys and sells clothing. She intends to use her loan to purchase 15 lengths of 'pagnes' (the colorful cloth of western Africa) of different sorts from Bougouni wholesalers. She makes her sales at the market and at home at the retail level. Accepting cash or credit, she sells to a customer base composed of men and women.   She envisions making an average monthly profit of 30,000 francs CFA that will be used to invest in her business and to repay the loan.

name: Sandra Milena
description: This small two-burner cooktop gave Sandra the opportunity to generate her own income.  She uses it to sell dishes that her mother taught her how to prepare.  This lovely 21-year-old woman started her business out of financial necessity.  She aspires to create jobs and also wants to improve her conditions at home.  On many occasions, she has had to go without food in order to pay another bill.  This motivated Sandra to look for opportunities and capital so that she could help her mother.  With the help of this loan, Sandra wants to buy utensils and expand her business by acquiring another cooktop.  As a result, she will have more equipment for preparing food for a greater number of people.  With the assistance that Sandra hopes to receive, this young woman will be able to support her mother and both of them can sustain their household and move their family forward.

name: Efua
description: Efua is a single parent and has four children.  Efua produces fanti kenkey (a type of dumpling) for sale. In the picture are the leaves she uses to cover the maize dough in the kenkey preparation.    Efua has been in this business for 20 years now. Efua will use her loan to purchase maize in large quantities to enable her to produce more kenkey for sale. With the new profit from the expanded business, Efua wishes to produce kenkey in large quantities to distribute to a retailer.

name: Bukuroshe
description: Bukuroshe wants this money to buy some equipment for her hair salon. She has been operating her salon for some time now, and it has been going well according to her.  She is 31 years old and a mother of a 6-year-old. She lives in the suburbs, a little town in northern Albania. Her husband works as a teacher, and his salary is around $480/month, while her pay varies between $100-$300/month. The fact that they do not have any sources of income from agriculture/livestock makes it difficult, Bukuroshe said during her interview. “Our pays are just to cover food and basic things. We’ve got to buy all food items, and food is not cheap at all. Should we have a cow or a little garden here to plant some veggies for our family needs, it would be awesome.”

name: Natividad
description: Natividad is 63 years old, single, and lives together with his family in Chepito Bajo sector, in Mórrope district.  This is an agricultural district which is located in Lambayeque province, more than one hour from the city of Chiclayo.  Natividad has been raising and selling pigs for eight years.  He raises the animals in a farmyard behind his home.  He feeds his animals natural grains and when they have reached a good level of development he offers them for sale to the traders who frequently visit his area.  In addition, he also farms.  Natividad would like to acquire more pigs (piglets) to fatten and also balanced feed.  This will enable him to increase his business and make more income.  For this reason, he has requested a loan for 1,000 Peruvian soles from Edpyme Alternativa in order to help him achieve his goal.

name: Abigail
description: Abigail is 21 years old and lives with her parents and six siblings in the Gomoa West district. She sells cellphone airtime from a small stand, but plans to expand her business to also sell wigs and bags. Abigail is requesting a Kiva loan to purchase wigs and bags in bulk. She plans to save the profit she earns to put herself through nursing training college. Abigail volunteers as a Camfed Learner Guide and leads life skills sessions for students in the nearby high school. She focuses on effective communication and on building her students’ confidence. The interest on Abigail’s social-interest loan will be repaid through her weekly volunteer work. Abigail's dream is to become nurse in her community

name: Lucia
description: Lucia is a 24 year-old woman from Bugumbe, located in the west of Migori county.  She supports four people in her family.  She is married to Mahiri, who is also a businessman from the same location and supports the family.  She has three children who are eight, six, and three years old, respectively.  She is a hawker, selling different varieties of goods. She has been doing this business for the last four years and generates a monthly income of KES 20,000.  She is taking her first loan with KADET LTD, which she intends to use to purchase more varieties of commodities.  Lucia will use the anticipated profit to expand the current business.  Her dream is to extend the business and to change her life and that of her family, too.

name: Veronica
description: Veronica K. is married and has 2 children. She has received schooling through Diploma in Business Studies. Veronica sells corn, yams, groundnuts, and other items at Abura, which she has done since 1998. Her husband is a driver. Veronica uses her income to pay her children's school fees and the family's utility bills.   Veronica will use the loan to purchase beans, groundnuts, corn, and yams for sale. With the new profits from her expanded business, Veronica plans to purchase a plot of land.

name: Zandra
description: Zandra is 53 years old and lives with her husband.  They have four dependent children; two are ten year old twin boys who attend school.  Another daughter is about to complete junior high school, and their eldest son who is weak because of mental disorders.  Zandra’s daily life if very concerning because of her son’s health.  He needs daily attention and they don’t always have enough money to pay for it.  She raises pigs in rustic pens.  Her husband works at a water services company.  She hopes to be able to improve her husband’s, her children’s, and her own quality of life through this loan.

name: Faith
description: Faith O. is 36 years old and married without children.  She lives in Benin City, in the Edo state of Nigeria.  Since 2005, she has been selling clothing materials and offering sewing services.  In order to expand her business, Faith is requesting a loan of $450, which will be used to purchase more tailoring materials.

name: Marlyn
description: Marlyn is a married woman with two children. Marlyn is 32 years old, residing at Poblacion 3, Clarin, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. Marlyn owns and operates a banana farm, planting banana to earn a living and she's been one year in this business.   Each month, Marlyn earns 2,000 PHP doing this type of business. She requested a loan of 5,000 PHP to purchase pesticides for banana growing. Marlyn is been a member of GDMPC for almost a year. In the future, Marlyn wants to build her own house and to see her children finish their studies.

name: Jinna
description: Jinna operates a sari-sari (variety) store, selling various commodities ranging from noodles, canned goods, soft drinks, sugar, eggs, tuba (coconut wine), soap and beverages. In addition to that, she also prepares meals for locals in her place. She is a 43 year old married woman with four dependents aged 18-13 years old.. She is asking for a loan to buy stock of things like tuba (coconut wine), vegetables and meat. These will keep her store full of stocks and could attract more buyers to come. Thus, her earnings will start to improve and enable her to provide her family with nutritious diets and continue to send them to school. With these, she could start to save and be able to do some expansion. Jinna  is hoping that someday, she will become a successful entrepreneur and be able to support the needs of her children as well.

name: Harriet
description: Harriet is a single mother of three children and two of her children go to school. She also takes care of additional family members (her mother). She has a business of selling used clothes and has been in this business for 5 years. She has applied for a loan of 400,000 Uganda shillings from MCDT-SACCO to buy more bales of used clothes. She doesn’t have any other income-generating activity. She works at the market seven days out of every week and sells on a retail basis. Her major business challenges include seasonality and thieves. She is aspiring to become a wholesaler and also to buy a plot of land and build her own house. She resides in a rented house and the family has access to electricity and not to piped water.  Her monthly expenses include rent and school fees.

name: Tanzeela
description: Tanzeela is a 28-year-old married woman and the mother of three children. The income generated by her husband is insufficient to cover all of their household expenses, so she started her milk sales business. She has been doing it for many years and has become famous for providing good quality milk in her locality.  With the support of Kashf Foundation, she has gradually improved her business. Currently, she has requested a loan of 45,000 PKR to purchase another buffalo to increase her sales and earn profits for providing her family with the basic necessities of life.

name: Shirmo
description: This is Shirmo. She lives in the Vakhsh region. Shirmo was born and grew up in the Kurgan-Tubinsk   district. She is married to a butcher. Shirmo has a n son, who works as a taxi driver. He is grown up and independent. Shirmo makes   "chakka" at home.  "Chakka" is a type of traditional strained youghurt made from milk. Shirmo prepares chakka for sale locally. This is a good business for her. Shirmo would like to expand and increase her income. She needs funds to buy milk. This is why she is asking for your help. She puts her trust in you.

name: Janet Magda
description: Ms. Janet T. started working together with her mom, a candies street vendor, since she was very young. Four years ago, once married, she decided to open a little store at her parent's home.  Ever since, she has been able to provide her sons and husband with an extra income. She is about to graduate as a policewoman and she wants her savings to be available whenever her kids will need them. Translated from Spanish by Jimena Almendares Leistner, Kiva Volunteer

name: Edoh
description: Edoh, a young 29-year-old man, is married to a retailer. Edoh himself sells CDs, DVDs and ready-to-wear clothing at the market. He gets his supplies locally and is requesting his 4th loan from WAGES in order to buy more merchandise. He hopes to be able to reinvest in his business and to ensure his family's food self-sufficiency. He started his business in 2002.

name: Nataliya
description: Twelve years ago, Nataliya opened her bakery and candy goods kiosk. A wife and mother, Nataliya was determined to improve the welfare of her family by contributing to their income. With a personal love for sweets and a keen eye for a business opportunity, Nataliya chose to sell candy and sweets as they are in constant demand. Warmhearted and hard working, Nataliya has successfully developed her business over the past decade and has secured a favorable location at the central market.   Currently, Nataliya is seeking a loan for 15,000 UAH to purchase additional inventory for the upcoming holidays. With her profits, Nataliya plans to continue developing her business and providing stable income for her family.

name: El Bosque Group
description: The members of this group chose the name El Bosque ["The Forest"] because where they live or hold meetings is a place with a lot of trees, vegetation, and corn fields. The place where they meet is really pretty; everything is starting to flower and become green, which is what makes it look especially nice. It is a community where their traditions, such as the handshake, are still maintained. Some people still speak their mother tongue and wear traditional clothing.Ma Isabel is a very kind and hard-working person, but above all, she has a great enterprising spirit. She is 49 years old. She has lived in a common law marriage for many years. Together, they have formed a family with three children, one of whom is currently attending secondary school.For the past 24 years, she has made a living by raising and fattening pigs. She says that she started the business because it was a very easy business for her, without any difficulty, because she keeps the pigs enclosed, cleans them, and feeds them. She gets up very early to start tending to her animals. Even though in her community a lot of her neighbors make a living by raising lambs, that is a trade with a lot of difficulties for her.She says that she buys the pigs when they are very little, only 30 days old. For 4 months, Isabel works caring for them in order to grow and fatten them so she can sell them later. She says that her earnings are very good. Little by little, her quality of life has improved. She has been part of VFMexico for a few years now, which has been very helpful because she now has 30 pigs. Her difficulty is when the price of corn goes up because she can't buy it in large amounts for her animals, due to the price. But thanks to the loan, Isabel can get the feed and the corn for her pigs, in order to feed them.She has grown not only with the animals, but she also has a grocery store from which she makes money. "One season my husband got sick, and our two businesses were a great help in order to get my husband's treatment," she says happily.Currently, her only job is to return to having the number of pigs that she used to have. In recent years, the price of corn and animal feed has not been favorable for her. She has two pens, and each one of them has 10 little baby pigs.The members of the group are Lilia, Ma Areli, Maricela, Maria Catalina, and Rosa Aurelia (who will invest in lambs), Crecencio (who will invest in groceries), and Silvia (who will invest in fabric and threads).*The photograph was taken on the steps of the municipal kiosk. Isabel is the one in the white sweater behind the woman in the hat.*

name: Cinthia Mabel
description: The young woman Cinthia, 24 years old, lives with her husband and has two children who depend on both of them. She lives in her own house in a community in San Lorenzo, a valley in the south of Honduras. For 5 years she has had a business selling new clothing.  Cinthia sells door-to-door. She is a hard-working woman with a desire to move forward.  She is asking for the loan in order to buy new clothing such as blouses, dresses, skirts, shirts, pants, shorts, sandals, etc. With the help of this loan she hopes to improve her income and thus her quality of life. She is happy to continue working with Prisma and her desire is to have a good supply of clothing. This is the fifth loan she has requested.  San Lorenzo, Honduras - May 2015

name: Christine
description: Christine is 20 years old and single. She lives in Mukono in the Mukono region of Uganda. For the past year, Christine has been working hard to manage her shoe shop, which sells second hand ladies' and children's shoes.   Christine requested a loan from BRAC Uganda for 300,000 Ugandan Shillings, which she will use to buy more shoes. The loan will help her to generate greater profits and expand her business. Christine hopes that in the future she will be able to open up another shop in town.

name: Lady
description: Lady is a friendly and happy 36-year-old woman. She lives in a house she owns with her husband Luís, who works at a company as a tractor driver. She has three children aged 21, 14, and 4 years respectively. Lady's work consists of selling carbonated beverages like soft drinks of different flavors, beers of various brands, and sweets like cookies, caramels and gum, among other things. She has a refrigerator to keep her drinks cold. She has had this business in a space inside her home for 3 years. She started this business to help her husband with their living expenses.  In the future she thinks she will rent a commercial space in a good location to sell sweets wholesale. This will be her 4th loan with Kiva and she feels very grateful for the financial support that she receives to continue with her work. With the requested amount of 1,000 Peruvian nuevos soles, she will buy carbonated beverages like beers of different brands and soft drinks of various flavors. She will also buy sweets like cookies, chocolates, caramels, etc.

name: Liliana Veronica
description: Liliana is a member of the Communal Bank “Inka Wasi” which is located in the District, Province, and Department of Puno.  She is 30 years old, in a common law marriage, and has two children who are financially dependent on her.  Liliana studied for her higher education.  She has been working with Manuela Ramos for one year.  Her first loan was in the amount of 400 PEN and used for her business of selling cosmetics.  With this loan of 400 PEN, Liliana will buy more beauty products.  Her husband works as a teacher.  Her dreams for the future include growing her business even more and having a store that is well-stocked with beauty products.  Liliana says she is grateful to Manuela Ramos for being able to access a loan with great ease.

name: Melinda
description: Melinda is 43 years old, married and has four children.  Melinda works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 29,500 loan through NWTF to buy stocks to sell like canned goods, eggs, toothbrushes, spices, bread, etc.  Melinda has borrowed and paid 23 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for eight years and also earns an income from buying and selling water buffalo and pre-paid mobile loads.  Melinda aspires to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Wil Alfredo
description: Wil, 31, has a sixth grade education, because he had to help his parents with work. He is in a common-law relationship and his partner works as a homemaker. He has three children, but only two attend school.  Wil has been working for a long time, offering transportation services with his motorcycle taxi, and it is profitable work in the area. Previously, he worked with another person in a motorcycle taxi business, but he decided to become independent.  He needs the loan to do repairs on his motorcycle taxi, which is very important, because it is his main source of income.  His dreams are to increase the size of his home and to pay for his children to attend school.

name: María Vilma
description: Marîa Vilma is 33 years old and has two dependent children. She lives in her own house with her husband. Her house is located in a rural zone in the Illimo District. The area has electricity and is a small community of about 200 families. She has been buying and selling animals for the past four years. Her husband sells grain, vegetables and also farms so that the family has additional income for their sustenance.  Marîa Vilma is asking for a loan from Edpyme Alternativa for 200 new soles, which she will use to buy animals and the food they need to reach their optimum weight and sell for a good price. It is close to the Christmas season and during this time her sales increase. Marîa Vilma is an enterprising woman and really wants to succeed. She is thankful for the helping hand of the people that support this loan.

name: Paul
description: Paul K. has been running his Agrovet business in Naivasha town for three years now. He attributes the success of his business to his local community, which consists of many farmers. Paul is 42 years old and married to Ruth Nyambura; they have a pair of twin sons who attend secondary school fifty miles from Naivasha town.  Paul was introduced to KADET by his friend. He is in repayment for his first loan and has applied for the education loan, which KADET offers to existing clients at zero percent interest. Paul plans to use the loans to pay academic fees for his sons' educations.  His future business plan is to grow his business and be a major supplier in Naivasha town, conducting both retail and bulk sales.  About KADET: The Kenya Agency for the Development of Enterprise and Technology (KADET) is dedicated to economically empower her clients by providing financial services to improve the living conditions of micro-entrepreneurs and their children across Kenya. KADET is the microfinance subsidiary of World Vision Kenya. Obtain more information on KADET from the website: www.kadet.co.ke.

name: Tessie
description: Tessie is 40 years old and married with five children.  She earns a living by fattening pigs in the Philippines. Tessie is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to buy feeds and vitamins for her pigs.  Tessie has been in pig fattening for 4 years and also earns additional income from farming sugarcane.  She is working tirelessly towards the attainment of her dream: to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to school.

name: Evelyn
description: As a married mother of five children, Evelyn works hard to support her family.  She has a food-vending business in the Philippines, and also earns income from farming rice. Evelyn is borrowing PHP 6000 through NWTF to buy ingredients for her food-vending business.  Evelyn has been sustaining her business activities through her past two loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save money to expand her business and repair her family home.

name: Shahnaz
description: Shahnaz is a hardworking and kind woman. She is a responsible housewife and the mother of 3 children. She lives in Lahore, Pakistan. She belongs to a very poor family and sustains her family life by facing many hurdles.    Her husband is a cobbler by profession and his income is inadequate for their household needs. Shahnaz has requested a loan from Kiva's partner BRAC Pakistan to purchase leather, soles and Rexine (artificial leather) for her husband's shop so that he can increase his income.  Shahnaz hopes that her children can live a better life in the future. She is thankful to Kiva and BRAC Pakistan for the loan.

name: Abdurasul
description: Abdurasul is a young family man who has recently moved out of his parents' house and into a separate one. He is married and has children. In his new home, he has many household expenses related to construction. Abdurasul himself works as a programmer for a mobile phone company, and does not have any other supplementary income. For this reason, he has decided to take out a loan so he can cover his roof from the rain and cold. He cannot save up enough money from his salary, so he has come to Arvand in the hopes of receiving a loan that will allow him to do a lot of work on his new house. Abdurasul plans to use the loan to buy building materials to cover the roof.

name: Patrick
description: Patrick is a 26-year-old married man with 3 children living in Fort Portal, Uganda. He operates a bakery alongside motorcycle transport in order to earn a living. Price fluctuations and inadequate capital to meet his customers' demands are his greatest challenges while his dream is to own a bakery that supplies bread to all the major towns of the country. Patrick intends to use the loan to buy baking flour to use in his bakery.

name: Douglas Antonio
description: Young Douglas, 22, is a Bachelor’s Degree student majoring in public accounting and finance.  He’s employed in a private firm as an accounting aide.  His salary is insufficient to cover costs for his final course; he’s in his final year of university.  He’s looking for support from a loan to cover the cost of this course.  If the loan were not possible, he’ll be delayed a year while he saves up enough to pay for the course.  His profession is very important to him because he will develop as a professional and will be able to help people who need him.

name: Alma
description: Alma is requesting a loan that will serve as start-up capital for her fruit and vegetable business. She will buy eggplants, green leafy vegetables, cabbage, squash and other food to sell. She wants to do this because she wants to assist her husband support the family.   Alma is 47 years old. Married to a carpenter, they are blessed with four children. She was 22 years old when she got married. Together with her family, she happily living in a simple village in the Nueva Vizcaya Province.

name: Umarboy
description: Umarboy K. has successfully completed his previous loan in March and decided to get another loan to expand his animal husbandry business. After his previous loan he has increased the number of livestock and amount of fodder. Right now he wants to spend the loan to buy pedigree rams. Umarboy is very happy to collaborate with MicroInvest.Translated from Russian by Elena Fedorchuk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Carmen
description: Carmen is 32, and she lives in her parents’ house with her three children.  Bryan is 18, Johan is 12, and Maricielo is 8.  She has a great desire to get ahead in order to give her family the best in spite of the fact that she is separated from her life partner.  When she was very young she learned what hard work is.  It is for that reason that, when confronted with raising her children alone, she had not doubts about undertaking a business that would be profitable and allow her to keep taking care of her children.  That is how she started selling clothes by order and on credit ten years ago.  She noted the good earnings she obtained.  She currently buys merchandise according to the time of year.  For example, it is now the school season, and she is selling school uniforms.  This woman puts forth much effort looking to get ahead everyday.  She likes her work because it is peaceful, and she does it from her house.  In the future she plans to set up a clothing store in a commercial center where there are a lot of people.   This is her first loan with MFP.  She is very grateful to the people who make it possible for her to access a loan in order to keep working.  Knowing that classes start in March, Carmen plans to use the money she is requesting to buy a bigger quantity of uniforms and school shoes. Translated from Spanish by Ginny Kalish, Kiva Volunteer

name: Garnik
description: Garnik is engaged in a fruits and vegetables wholesale trade. He buys the merchandise using his car in the Republic of Georgia and from villages of Ararat region.    The main part of the goods he sells to retailers. The other part he sells in small shops in Vanadzor city. Garnik's mother from time to time helps him in trading. This activity he has performed for more than five years.  Garnik is 30 years old. He is married and lives in Vanadzor city with his wife, son and mother. Trading is the only source of family income, and with the profit from trading, Garnik solves his family needs, pays all bills for the flat, etc.    Garnik is seeking a 500,000 Armenian Drams loan to buy and resell citruses and tropical fruits from the Republic of Georgia.

name: Zainabu
description: Zainabu is a hardworking married woman with two children living in Kamwenge,Uganda.  She is a farmer and earns additional income as a brick layer. Her goal is to become a model farmer in the near future.  Her efforts  are limited by prolonged drought.   She  requests a loan to hire laborers to clear her land and prepare for the next season.

name: Adheu
description: Adheu is a 30-year-old married woman with three children, two of whom are in school. She has had a business of selling food from a stall in Bor, South Sudan for two years.  Adheu is requesting this loan through BRAC South Sudan to purchase milk and sugar for sale. She will use her extra income from this loan to build a house.

name: Noeli Yolibeth
description: Noeli is a 32 year old single mother with one son. She lives in a village in the municipality of Puerto Cortes.   Over 3 years ago she decided to start her own business to generate revenue.  She sells clothing, sandals, tennis, shorts, shirts and perfume out of her home.   She is requesting a loan of 6,000 lempiras and will buy clothes, shoes and perfume to sell.   She believes that by keeping a variety of products she will be able to increase sales and customers.

name: Macaria
description: Macaria is 51 years old and married with eight children. With four children in school, Macaria works very hard to provide for them.  Macaria runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 13,000 loan through NWTF to purchase additional items like eggs, soft drinks, biscuits, rice, etc. to sell.  Macaria has been in this business for 10 years. In the future she would like to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college.

name: Ernesto
description: Ernesto, 44, has lived with his wife and two children in his own house, made of semi-noble materials, in the village of Colasay for eight years. The village is dedicated to agriculture, trade, and livestock. It is located in the province of Jaén in the region of Cajamarca in the northern mountains of Peru.  Ernesto works in agriculture, specifically growing coffee. His wife supports him in this labor, preparing food for the day laborers who maintain his crops. Ernesto has applied for a loan of 2500 Peruvian nuevo soles to pay for the maintenance of his coffee crops, thereby having a better production to offer his clients.

name: María Rosa
description: María Rosa, 60, is single and has no children. She wants to buy chicks and feed.  She’s been a poultry farmer for many years and she wants to grow and also wants her project to be productive.  She cares for her father who is a senior citizen.    This is her second Fudecosur loan.  She’s had no other loans from state banks or cooperatives and Fudecosur offered the best loan terms and the interest rate is much lower.  She also wants to provide better quality of life for her family and to be able to face life more easily.

name: W_F_Khamulati_Naliakawanjala Group
description: Naliaka is the group leader of her group in Webuye District, and she is representing 10 farmers, including herself. She is married and a proud mother of 3 children. Naliaka joined One Acre Fund for the first time this season, but she has been a farmer for 10 years.Like many other farmers, Naliaka decided to work with One Acre Fund in order to have access to quality training and acquire new farming methods. She hopes that by joining One Acre Fund and using the seeds and fertilizer she will get with this loan, she can join the ranks of One Acre Fund farmers that have doubled their harvest in their first year of the program. She plans to use the profits she earns from this year’s harvest to send her children to school.Naliaka's Group will use the farming inputs received with this loan to cultivate a total of 4.5 acres of land. They will also receive a total of 5 solar lights, as, even though Naliaka decided not to, some of the farmers in the group will be purchasing a solar light as part of their loan package.

name: Hever Alexander
description: Hever has decided to take a loan to strengthen his business.  He will purchase supplies and cell phone accessories.  For example, backpacks, keychains, cases, batteries and keyboards.  This investment will increase the amount of merchandise available to his customers.  With his previous loan, he was able to purchase materials to sell at his store.  That loan helped him establish his business with the intention of moving forward.

name: Sharon
description: Sharon is applying for a second loan to support her studies through her graduation in December 2016 at the Maharishi Institute. She has provided the following update on her progress since receiving the first loan: “The loan has helped me through my studies, because if it was not for the loan, I wouldn’t have managed to complete my third year. I also got extra cash to help me with transport and other materials needed for my academic year. I am really grateful for the help I got and I will continue to be grateful."

name: Antony Mwaura
description: Antony Mwaura N. is a 35-year-old man, married to Margaret Njoki. Together they have three children.
