Margaret supports the family by adding income, while Antony works as a mechanic in Eldoret town. He has been in this business for 15 years now and gets a monthly income of 15,000 shillings.  This will be Antony's fifth loan from KADET LTD. He has repaid all other loans successfully, and with this loan he plans to use it entirely to buy spare parts for his mechanic job. His dream is to become richer and have a happy family.

name: Benita
description: Benita is 53 years old and is a long-term client of the institution. She sells hats and also has a second job selling vegetables from a stall that is located in the Chasquipampa area. She used her previous loans to buy hats at wholesale, and on this occasion, she is going to use the loan to buy vegetables and tomatoes at wholesale. Her reason for requesting the loan is that she wants to stock up on these products. Benita has to overcome many challenges to make her business work. She wakes up very early in the morning to buy her vegetables and there is a lot of competition from other sellers. She is going to use the profits to buy things for her house. She feels happy and grateful to the institution for the support that it has offered her.

name: Cherimai
description: This is 42-year-old Cherimai.  She is married and has two children aged 23 and 18.  In 1999, she established her vegetable farming business.  Working seven days a week and four hours a day, she supports her family.  She has already received and successfully repaid four loans from Patan BPW and used her most recent loan to buy seeds and fertilizers.  In the future, Cherimai plans to uplift the economic condition of her family.  She thanks you for your support.     Over 70% of Nepal's economy is agricultural.  Typically, Nepali households grow crops on small plots of terraced land.  Rice (bhat), lentils (daal), and vegetables (thakari) are the staples of the Nepali diet.  With a Kiva loan, BPW's borrowers are able to purchase greater amounts of seed and fertilizer.  With more seeds and fertilizer, a borrower is able to grow cash crops to be sold in the local market.  Such crops allow households to move beyond subsistence and provide much-needed cash income throughout the year.

name: Fely
description: Fely is from the village of Cabaruan, Naguilian, Isabela. She is now 35 years old and already married to Ernesto Villoria Jr., 34 years old. They are blessed with two children: Erwin, 11 years old and the youngest is Jayvee, 10 years old. Both children are attending the primary level of education. Fely is very thankful for having a happy family and having a good bonding with each other.  Aside from the passenger tricycle that her husband manages, she is also engaged in a poultry raising business. With their income from their business activities, they can provide the basic needs for their family. But she plans to expand their business in order to earn more profit to save funds for the schooling of their children. For this, she is requesting to avail a loan amounting to PHP 5,000 for both the maintenance of their motorcycle transport and her livestock raising business. She also wants to start a rice vending business to earn extra income. However, Fely said that she cannot do all of these at the same time considering the availability of funds. Thus, she is praying that her loan will be approved to be able to make her business successful. She believes that all her business plans, if pursued, will be of big help to her family. She hopes to become successful in the business by being patient and by exerting more efforts in doing her work. According to her, she will only believe that she has already achieved her goals in life when she sees her children finish their studies in college and find a better job.

name: Iruguincho Group
description: Luis, Maria Angelita and Anita are the members of Iruguincho Group located near the city of Ibarra in northern Ecuador. Luis, 22, is the group leader. He is single and lives with his family. He has one son who is three -years-old. He is a hard-working man who wants to get married soon, have another child, and continue forward with his girlfriend. Luis is a farmer, currently growing beans on his parents' land. He is seeking this loan to grow corn and some more beans. He began his life as a farmer when he finished school. His father and brother brought him to the country and taught him all they knew about farming. Since then, he has dedicated himself to farming and still works alongside his father. He hopes that this loan will help change his business, his life, and the life of his family. With hard work everyday, he has hopes to build his own house and get some of his own land. His goal is to live with his family in his own house and hire workers to help him with his farming work.

name: Sri Manikkanatchiyamman Shg - Ayyanallur Group
description: Sri Manikkanatchiyamman Shg - Ayyanallur Group consists of eighteen members; Devi is the leader of the group.      Devi has two children and lives in her own house in Ayyanallur village, Tanjore district. Her husband is a small marginal farmer working for daily wages.               A large number of people, especially in rural places in India, still use wood as the main source of heat for cooking, many of them using open fires. Open fires are not only inefficient but they produce smoke, which is harmful to health, and present a risk to children of burning. The inefficiency of open fires results in large amounts of wood being burned, contributing to deforestation, and hard work for the women and children collecting it.   For the above reasons, women from this group are requesting a loan to buy smokeless stoves, which will help them to save money, time and keep their families healthier as well.

name: Francis
description: Francis is 52 years old and has been a farmer in Nakuru town for the past seven years. He is married to Margaret and they have five children. He plants cash crops such as maize and potatoes and it has been very profitable.  This will be his fifth loan from KADET LTD and he plans to use it to buy more seedling for planting in his farm. He also plans to use part of it to pay workers. This being the rainy, planting season he anticipates to make more profits with which he will pay school fees for his children.  In the future, Francis hopes to grow his farming business and be able to improve the family's living standards.

name: Zahra
description: Zahra lives at her own house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is household consumables.  For the past one year, she has operated a clothes-selling business, selling from door to door to her neighbors and passersby. She faces a major challenge of the high cost of transportation. She dreams of expanding and establishing a boutique business in the future.   With the loan that she is requesting, she wants to purchase bales of clothes for resale. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Oeu
description: Oeu is 59 years old, a resident of Baray district of Kompong Tom province. He has a common law relationship with his wife and has eight children. Five of his children are already settled for marriage while the other three are single. Oeu’s living completely depends on his agricultural businesses, including a farming and a fishing business. Oeu, together with his wife, usually go fishing along the Tonle Sap River and bring fish to sell in a local market of the province, earning approximately USD 3.00 per day. He has been doing the business for almost 17 years.  Oeu wants a motorcycle to transport his fish to the marketplaces, but due to insufficient funds he would like to take out a loan to add to his savings to purchase a used motorcycle. Oeu is very happy with the given loan because it’ll help the family for their business and personal uses. Oeu has already paid off his previous loans successfully as it is now his third loan from HKL.

name: Claudia Faisuly
description: With her energy and perseverance, Claudia has made progress and been able to educate and raise her family. She has always sought ways to earn money for her family so she has had many jobs in the municipality of Medellín.After deciding that she wanted to work independently, Martha now makes crafts and other items made of wood. For this reason and many others she is seeking a loan to buy wood and other supplies such as vinyl, porcelain, fabric etc. The loan will ensure the sustainability of her business and thus support for her family. If you make a loan, you will be supporting Colombian progress and energy!If you want to know more about the entrepreneurs and the loans from Interactuar, you can join the Lending Team called: “Friends of Interactuar Colombia”: http://www.kiva.org/team/interactuar_colombia

name: Benicio
description: Benicio is 48 years old and he has a stable home with his partner and their son. He lives in a home of his own made out of rustic materials in the rural part of the district of Pimpingos, located in the province of Cutervo, in the region of Cajamarca in the northern highlands of Peru. The population in this district works in agriculture, cattle and commerce.  He works raising and selling cattle (cows), which he has done for 14 years. He is also a teacher in a school in the district. He has very good personal and professional references in the area.  He will use the credit to purchase more cattle as well as to maintain the corral where he raises them. With this, Benicio hopes to increase his income and be able to improve his quality of life and that of his family.

name: Mari Luz
description: Mari is a member of the "Las Divinas" community bank which is located in Calleria district, in Ucayali department.  She is 46 years old, single, and has three children.  Mari owns a carpentry workshop and has a master carpenter and an assistant working for her who make the furniture which they sell.  Mari will use her new loan for 1,700 soles to buy 6 planks of cedar wood, 10 planks of capirona wood (capirona is a native hardwood tree), 2 kilos of glue and 2 kilos of nails.  In order to keep her carpentry workshop running, Mari has to go out and find customers.  She also personally takes care of buying the wood and supervising the assembly of the pieces of furniture.  Her workshop is located inside her home owing to the space that is needed for this work.  Mari hopes that Manuela Ramos will continue supporting hard-working women who have to provide for their families on their own.

name: Ramber
description: Mr. Ramber O. M., 22, is a young, hard working, single man living with his parents; he helps them with expenses for his two sisters who are in school.  They live in the Sauces community in the municipality of Mizque in Cochabamba Department.  He works farming alongside his father; they grow onion, carrots and broad beans that they sell there as well.  He is a much respected person in his community because of his dedication to work ad for being responsible for the education of his two sisters.  Ramber is asking for this loan to buy more seed and farming supplies and to increase the surface of his plantations to increase his income, support his sisters more and improve the living condition of the entire family.

name: Norizhon
description: Norizhon is a young and industrious woman. She is 21 years old and married. Her husband doesn’t work anywhere. Four months ago, she began a new business. She sells fabrics in a local market. Little by little, Norizhon has improved the business. She is going to increase her working capital for the new business and with this aim, she is asking for a loan. Norizhon took part in a course ‘To Get Ahead’ from a women's organization and got a certificate. She is asking for a loan of 1,500 Somoni to buy fabrics for increasing her working capital. She awaits your mercy.

name: Anibal Jose
description: Anibal Jose M. L. is 42 years of age. He is married and lives with his wife and children. He has 3 children: Mónica (16), Francisco (10) y Maria Jose  (9 months). He lives in the village of Chillanes in the province of Bolívar.    Anibal is an associate of the 'King of Kings' rural branch, which is located an hour and a half from Chillanes. There are 23 associates in all, the majority dedicated to agriculture. This is the first loan that he has requested from the San José cooperative  Anibal is dedicated to breeding animals such as chickens and hogs. He carries out his purchases every three months in Matilde Esther and sells his animals in the local community.   He requests a loan to purchase more animals in order to increase his production and realize his dream. He thinks that the loan is an opportunity to get ahead.  His dream is to have the money to purchase a house.  He faces challenges such as diseases.   He likes agriculture and raising his animals. Translated from Spanish by Barbara (B) Brown, Kiva Volunteer

name: Maripe
description: Maripe is a 52-year-old married father of five children between 9 and 21 years of age. For the past eight years he has been farming wheat on his own piece of land.  Because of the area's climatic conditions and fertile soil, wheat has proven to do very well, and the market is readily available for both retail and wholesale buyers.   Maripe, who learned about KADET from women who were already members, is now requesting his fourth loan of kes 120,000, having repaid his previous ones. He will use the money to prepare his land and buy seedlings and fertilizer for his wheat farm.    Maripe hopes to use the profit arising from this loan to expand his farming activity from small-scale to commercial farming. He is a self-motivated man who is determined to achieve his set goals.

name: Leovigilda
description: This is Leovigilda, 46, a resident of Silang, Cavite, Philippines. She has two children, and they manage their household while operating the business. At this time, she is working hard to continually provide income for her everyday expenses.    Leovigilda operates a food stall. In the Philippines, the whole working community and most of the families only eat home-cooked meals during evenings when all of the family members are home to take part in the meal. This is not only a usual family tradition, but a matter of convenience and frugal living. It is considered a waste of money and time to spend cooking gas and food for one to two persons, when buying cooked rice and viands cost less than raw food. Her regular customers are her neighbors and the local community.  She earns a minimum of Php 500 in sales every day.  To help her continue the operation of her business, she is requesting a Php 11,000 loan. She will be using the loan to buy more quantities of products like meats, rice, vegetables, condiments and seasonings, and frozen food products.   Leovigilda dreams of expanding her business, and hopes to have a beautiful life. She meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her work every week and where she can also draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God he studies.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Vainuu
description: Vainuu is a 34-year-old married woman with 4 children. She has a small plantation and grows taro, taamu and bananas to earn a living. She has been doing this for many years. Vainuu has requested a loan to buy chemicals, fertilizer, a backpack sprayer and a rake.  She has been a member of SBPD since 2009. With her profits, Vainuu hopes to improve her house and save more for her children's education.

name: Eva
description: Eva is a 34-year-old lady who is applying for a loan of UGX 600,000 in her first loan cycle. She is a single mother of two children, who she looks after with the help of her young sister. She occupies a single room in her parents’ home in the outskirts of the city, and she sells second-hand clothes in order to survive. She moves from market to market on various days to sell the clothes, but she has always been challenged by her limited capital. Because of this challenge, she has applied for a loan of UGX 600,000 to give her business a boost and to be able to meet client demand, especially for those who place orders and prefer to make payment after delivery. She has hopes that, given the loan, she will be able to make more sales and, some day, find it easier to look after her children and to construct a decent residence for her family. She is hardworking. In the photo are Eva (the client) and Michael, the Ugafode staff member for her business.

name: Maria Doraliza
description: María is a 61-year-old mother.  She lives in her own home which has water and electricity.  Her home is located in Zaña district, in Chiclayo province.  This area is noted for its farming, livestock raising and tourism.  María has a food business.  She works as a itinerant street vendor in a very busy area.  She has been in this business for several years.  She has her own customer base and is requesting this loan for 2,000 Peruvian soles from Edpyme Alternativa to buy supplies and utensils so that she can continue providing a good service and meeting the needs of her customers.  She will use the income she makes to repay her loan and improve her daughter's quality of life.  Through her work and her desire to get ahead in life, María has gained the trust and respect of her neighbors, showing that when somebody sets themselves a goal, they can achieve it.  Her goal is to create a better future for her daughter.

name: Mency
description: Mency is a 52-year-old married woman with four children who works hard to provide for her family. She has run a general store for 9 years and requests 15,000 PHP through NWTF  to purchase groceries to sell.She has previously received funds through Kiva.Mency aspires to save enough money to expand her business and repair her family's home.

name: Nhoem
description: From the province of Kompong Cham, Nhoem, 30 years of age, is a hard-working woman who generates an income by cultivating rice on her own farmland. Her husband is also a rice farmer, and both earn a profit of about USD$4 a day to support their expenses. They are blessed with a child still in the public school.   To increase their revenue, Nhoem wishes to buy a plot of her neighbor's farmland, for which she is seeking a loan from Kiva leaders; she will use this land to grow more rice.

name: Ununio Group
description: Clara is in her early 40s. She is single and has three children, one of whom is in school. The others are grown up. She has been a food vendor for seven years. She works from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily and is able to make a good monthly profit. This will be Clara’s second loan from Tujijenge Tanzania. She used the previous loan to increase the stock in her mama lishe (food stall). She has paid back her loan successfully. She used the profit from her business to pay for school fees, to repay her loan, and cover household expenses. With this loan, she will restock items in her mama lishe store. Clara dreams of being a big business woman and to build her own house. She will share this loan with her loan group Ununio, which consists of two members who will hold each other accountable for paying back the loan.

name: Liliet De Los Ángeles
description: Liliet is hardworking woman and strives to improve the condition of her life and the lives of her family members, who she loves. She is a lady who always strives to get ahead and is characterized by always trying to supply the necessities for her home.  The loan that she is requesting will be directly invested in the purchase of construction materials to improve the condition of her home and to have a decent roof under which she will live with her family.

name: Naomi
description: Naomi is 63 years old and lives in Sta. Cruz, Jimenez, Misamis Occidental. She is married with two children now at their adult age. Naomi is a Lady Pastor in one of the religious congregations in the country. She receives a monthly love gift in the amount of not less than PHP 5,000 each month doing this type of ministerial work.   She has requested a loan to be used in purchasing additional sacks of cement, paints, tiles and home accessories for the ongoing house construction. Naomi has been a member of PMPC for one year. In the future, Naomi hopes that all her family and church members will become members and be active participants of the cooperative’s activities.

name: Faamaopo
description: Faamaopo is a young lady of 35 years, with six children. She is very talented in making elei materials, which is one of the most sought-after Samoan types of painted materials for making clothes and lavalavas. By operating this business, she spent her first loan of ST$750 to purchase paints, elei wood and different types of materials. Money earned from the business helps support her family needs.

name: Erlita
description: Erlita is 24 years old. She lives with her husband in the district of Oyotún, two hours from the city of Chiclayo, which belongs to the Lambayeque region on the north coast of Peru. The population of Oyotún is involved in agriculture, commerce, and cattle. Erlita makes her living selling beauty products such as perfumes, powders, cosmetics, and creams. The majority of her customers are women, and she is known for the good service and advice that she provides.  She has requested a loan of 500 nuevo soles to buy beauty products so that she can have them in stock and therefore be able to offer them to her customers when they need them, generating more income for her family.

name: Elena
description: Elena R. is a farmer and owns a small parcel of land in Sta. Josefa, Agusan Del Sur. She also grows chickens and pigs in her backyard. It is her dream to grow her business so that she can provide for the needs of her family.  She would like to apply for a loan at Community Economic Ventures Inc. to buy fertilizers and rice seeds.  The reason for choosing CEVI as her MFI was that she likes the Micro Insurance package of CEVI.

name: Bernarda
description: Bernarda is a hardworking, xxx person.  In her store, every day she works from early morning until well in the evening. She says that, thanks to her previous loan, she was able to supply her business with a variety of products. Now she is asking for a new loan to be able to invest again in the purchase of products to stock her business with vegetables, canned goods, drinks, fruits and other items. She appreciates the opportunity to receive again the possiblity to grow.

name: Ashot
description: Ashot lives in Ddmashen village of Gegharkunik region. Ashot is a pedagogue with many years of experience in this field and now he also works at the school as a teacher of mathematics. He also has pupils who attend private courses at his house, getting prepared for the entrance exams. Ashot likes his occupation and his pupils as well;  he is eager to give knowledge and help them if they have any hardships in their learning process. Ashot is married and he lives with his wife, son and daughter (she is also a pedagogue). Ashot asks this loan as he wants to buy a computer, accessories for it, and also professional literature in order organize his private courses properly and be more interesting for his pupils.

name: Grace
description: Grace is 29 years old, married to Francis and has two children. For the past three years she has sold fresh fruits and vegetables, earning a monthly salary of 9,000 KES.   This will be Grace’s first loan with KADET. She is requesting a 30,000 KES loan which she will use to grow her business. Her ambition is to use her profits to purchase a plot of land and build her own house.

name: Abla
description: D. Abla resides in Kégué, a district of the city of Lomé.  She is married and works to earn an income in the grocery business.  Her stock of goods is exhausted.  She wants to resupply herself and is requesting a loan from WAGES to buy ten sacks of aromatic rice, eight drums of oil, four boxes of soap, and six boxes of pasta. Translated from French by Dan Kuey, Kiva Volunteer

name: Gregoria
description: Gregoria has a store in which she works every day, beginning very early in the morning. She is a fighter, and has sacrificed a lot; thanks to her efforts, she has been able to raise a family.   She used her previous loan to stock her store, which was really helpful. Now, she is asking for a new loan with which to buy sugar, flour, rice, and drinks. With this, she will again stock her store. She is very grateful for the opportunity that she has received.

name: Rosalía
description: Rosalía is a member of the San José de Viñaca communal bank.  She is 27 years old, married, and has two children.  She works planting and selling vegetables and has land where she plants them.  However, during the seasons when her vegetables are growing, she buys from her neighbors and sells them at the Nery García Zarate market and distributes them among her regular customers.  She will invest the loan requested in the purchase of seeds and medicines.  Rosalía likes Finca because they give her loans and she can save.  Her dream is for her business to grow and to be able to educate her children.

name: Enma
description: Enma, 55 years old, went to school up to the third grade. She is married, her husband was a day laborer but a few years he got an illness which made it impossible for him to work. She is the mother of 5 children, her oldest daughter is a teacher and is married, the second has a degree in anesthesiology and works in a national hospital and is married, the third went to school through secondary school, and works in hauling and is married, the fourth went to school through secondary school and works as a day laborer and is single, and the fifth is studying in his third year in the agronomy program at the National School of Agriculture. Enma works in a corn mill, and also has a business selling basic products, she has worked in the mill for 14 years and has had the store for 2 years, she decided to establish these businesses by her own initiative, because her husband was only a day laborer and she wanted to help with the household expenses as well. Previously, she only took care of the household tasks. Enma needs the loan to purchase agricultural supplies such as pumpkin seeds, fertilizers, and herbicides and also to pay labor costs to plant corn and restore a plot of land with pumpkin cultivation. For this, her son will help with the agricultural labor. With the help of this loan, she will be able to purchase the supplies and avoid expenses. Also, she will be able to improve her harvests and have more income for her family. Enma's dream is that her son finishes his degree and finds dignified work, which will allow him to have income to have more economic stability in the family. She also plans to increase production to get more earnings and, so, to be able to purchase dairy cows.

name: Nasraddin
description: Nasraddin (his sister is pictured) is 47 years old, married, and has four children. He lives with his family in the Khachmaz region, in the Ashagi-Zeyid village. He and his sister need a loan of $825 to buy fruit seedlings and  fertilizer for improving their orchard. They have run this business for four years.

name: Wonadia 2 Group
description: Salmata is fifty years old, married, and a mother of six. She has retailed vegetables (onions) since 1999.  Her business thrives because of the quality of the onions. She wants the loan to purchase 100,000 XOF worth of onions for the months of November and December. The loan is useful to purchase in sufficient quantities to resell during the holidays.  She has already been granted loans more than twice, and has repaid ACFIIME punctually.

name: Tumaini
description: Tumaini lives with her husband and two children. She runs a fuel business as a way to help her husband cover the household expenses, as well as to generate income to be able to cover other expenses. She sells diesel and kerosene from her home. It is a business she has been running for two years.  She is requesting this loan in order to be able to purchase a pump and more fuel. This loan will help her improve and boost sales.  She hopes that through this business, she will be able to improve her family's quality of life little by little, and that she will help educate her children.

name: Damaris Raquel
description: Damaris began her store eleven years ago when she needed to find a way to support her children. She is 34 years old and is a single mother with two young children. She had a small general store in front of her house, but now focuses her business on the sale of clothing and jewelry.   This loan will go towards the purchase of more merchandise, since Damaris wants to have a good inventory for the Christmas season. Damaris dreams of establishing a store in the market in Jinotepe so she would not have to continue selling her products on foot, but ultimately the most important aspect of her business is to continue to support her children.

name: Elizabeth
description: Elizabeth dreams of working in the tourism industry. Elizabeth was accepted into the Universidad Mayor de san Andrés and now, with the chance to achieve her dream, she is concerned about affording tuition fees. She plans on graduating in December, 2014, but often there are fees for earning your degree before graduating. Without a loan from Vittana she fears that she will need to defer her graduation. Elizabeth plans on using this loan to cover the cost of her graduation fees.   In addition to her responsibilities at school, Elizabeth currently works 30 hours a week and earns $10 a day. With a career in business, she expects to earn $25 a day, a substantial increase from before. Unfortunately, Elizabeth's parents never had the opportunity to complete their high school education. Without the opportunity for a higher degree, her parents never had the chance to move up. Growing up, finances were always tight.   As the youngest of six, with one older sibling attending college already, Elizabeth is unsure how she will be able to finance her education on her own without the assistance of a Vittana loan.

name: Tuyet
description: Tuyet requests a new loan to repair her bssauty shop and buy tools and shampoo to better satisfy her customers. Her previous loan enabled her to improve her business, processing capacity, and sales.   She hopes that her new loan will help her to increase the size of her business, her income, and  help her to improve her living conditions.

name: Javier Antonio
description: In the year 2014, guided by economic necessity, Javier started a business selling beer and sodas.  He has the responsibility of supporting his family, consisting of 4 children and his common law partner.  Thanks to his perseverance he has moved his family forward.Javier has converted his business to a small distributorship, as he only sells wholesale, which is good news for the customer.  With a promise to continue progressing and fighting for his family -- that is the path he's on.  As the December season is the season when the most liquor is consumed, Javier seeks a loan to buy beer in large quantities.

name: Lydia
description: Lydia O. is from the town of Talibon. She is 37 years old. Lydia is married and has three school-aged children. To make a living, Lydia provides photography services to local community members. She also makes photo frames. Lydia has been engaged in her business for over seven years.  Lydia joined CEVI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. Lydia has successfully repaid a previous loan from CEVI.   Lydia is requesting a new loan of 10,000 PHP, which will be used to purchase materials needed to provide service. This will be the third loan taken out by Lydia from CEVI. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to supplement the family's income and improve their living conditions.   About CEVI: Community Economic Ventures, Inc., (CEVI) has increased its portfolio significantly over recent years.  Based in Bohol, they have numerous branches throughout the Philippines. In 2009, CEVI was awarded a CGAP silver award for transparency in social-performance monitoring. CEVI not only provides credit for its clients but also offers savings, insurance, and training programs, which are provided through regular cluster group meetings.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva. Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Nelia
description: Nelia is 45 years old and married with two children.  With one child in school, Nelia works very hard to provide for them.  Nelia has a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 21,000 loan through NWTF in order to purchase additional groceries to sell.  Nelia has been in this business for five years and sells a variety of items such as spices, personal care products, school supplies and other groceries.   In the future Nelia would like to save enough money to expand her business.

name: Felicia
description: Felicia is the enthusiastic mother of a nineteen-year-old daughter.  She has been selling undergarments at a small stand in a crowded alley of central Kumasi for fifteen years.  This is her second loan through Sinapi Aba Trust.  With her first loan, she saw a marked increase in sales.  She plans on using this loan to further increase her inventory of lingerie and to buy better quality products.   With her increased sales, she hopes to save more and support her daughter.    Felicia is a member of the trust group Pillar of God.  The trust group uses peer pressure as a form of social collateral to help ensure that each member of the group repays their share.    Felicia is pictured on the right.  To the left is Annastasia, her loan officer.

name: Grace
description: Grace, is a married mother of 3 and a farmer and salesperson, who has access to many sellers in the food chain. On her half an acre farm, she keeps dairy cows, poultry, pigs and a garden full of bananas and trees. To make better income, Grace makes commission on sale from helping arrange the logistics of getting farm produce from local farmers to their buyers.   She has been doing this business for 30 years. She understands her strength is the strong relationship she has with sellers and buyers. Given that Grace can arrange a sale more easily than regular farmers can, she prefers to deal with larger volumes of produce. She is seeking a loan to aggregate more produce from local farmers at fair prices and use her better understanding of the market conditions and prices to sell at a profit.   Your loan will help Grace’s clients to focus on production, rather than sales, as it will her family to make better incomes and uplift their livelihood.

name: Winfred
description: Winfred lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is married with two children, both of whom go to school. She is also looking after two of her sisters. She has been selling clothes at retail from door-to-door for fifteen years, working six days a week. She also earns money from a motorcycle she hires out to the public.  She has requested for a loan of UGX 600,000 from MCDT- SACCO to be able to stock more skirts, blouses and dresses to sell.  Her challenges include seasonality and transportation. Her dream is to become an importer of both new and secondhand clothes. She joined MCDT because of the loans at relatively low interest and no assets for collateral. Her goal is to buy a plot of land. She stays in a rented house with access to electricity, but no piped water.  Her major monthly expenses include rent and fees.

name: 2 De Febrero Group
description: The communal bank “2 DE FEBRERO” [2 OF FEBRUARY] is beginning its third loan cycle with Pro Mujer through the regional office of Senkata.  The communal bank is made up of six members and is directed by a board of directors, of which Ana María is president. The businesses of the members are varied and include weaving jackets, selling blankets, selling potatoes and potato flour, a butcher’s stall, traditional skirts and shawls, and selling condiments.  The loan they are requesting will benefit small businesses in which Ana María is a participant.  She says she joined Pro Mujer eight months ago at the invitation of the members of her group, who are members of the institution. Currently, she has a business selling condiments (seasonings, herbs, spices).  She says that she learned this business from her mother, whom she helped with sales.  Later she decided to open her own, independent business.  Ana María will use this loan to increase her capital by buying condiments wholesale in the markets of the city of El Alto.  She will later sell the condiments as a travelling vendor (without a fixed sales stall).  This form of work allows her to generate resources to support herself, as she is single and lives with her parents.  When she is asked what she likes about Pro Mujer, she says that she likes the training relating to health.

name: Fredelyn
description: As a married parent of two children, Fredelyn works hard to support her family.  She has a fishing business in the Philippines and earns additional income from fish vending. Fredelyn is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to buy additional fish net, pay for maintenance for her boat and buy other materials for her fishing business.  Fredelyn has been sustaining her business activities through her past five loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream of saving enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Josephine
description: Josephine lives in the Mariakani area of Coast Province, Kenya. She is married and has three children. She owns a green grocer, a business which she has been operating for 6 years. She started the business from the income she received while selling buns. Her main challenge is the high cost of transport while sourcing for the goods.   Josephine learned about Milango through friends who invited her to the group and she joined with the aim of accessing credit to improve her business operations. She is applying for a loan of 41,850 Kenya shillings to buy vegetables and fruits wholesale. Her extra income from the loan will be added to her savings to construct a rental house and improve on the living standard of her family.

name: Sajida
description: Sajida is a 42-year-old mother with one boy and three girls. Her husband is a taxi driver and she sells clothes and perfume from home.   Sajida is requesting a loan to buy more perfume and increase her profits.

name: Maria Cecilia
description: María is 35 and aspires to grow her sales of clothing, formal wear and boutique items.  Her story began when she began to work in a business run by her sister, who travelled out of the country.  Maria was able to grow the business, working alone every day and confronting difficulties such as crime.  Maria is married and has a daughter; her dream is to establish a separate locale for the shop and to help her family. She wishes to use this credit to buy clothing, formal wear and boutique items.

name: Rose
description: For years, Rose has operated a poultry farming business, selling to restaurant operators and to her neighbours and passers-by through the support of the previous Kiva loan. She gives much appreciation to Yehu and Kiva at large. She faces a major challenge of infectious diseases leading to loses. Rose dreams of establishing a hotel in the future.   With the KES 50,000 she wants to purchase chicks, both layers and broilers, and chicken feeds. She decided to join Yehu to access loans to boost her business.

name: Nhork
description: Nhork, 45, is married and resides with his wife and three children in Kampong Chnang Province, Cambodia. He is a construction worker. His wife runs a grocery store at home. Two of his children are employed in Thailand.   In order to improve his family’s economy, Nhork is requesting a loan of USD 1,000 to purchase rice to resell at the rice mill to generate more income for the family. In the future, he would like to expand his wife’s business and send his youngest child to a good school.

name: Analyn
description: As a married parent of seven children, Analyn works hard to support her family.  She has a fishing business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from food vending. Analyn is borrowing PHP 13,000 through NWTF to purchase additional fishing materials like net, bamboo, gasoline, etc. for her fishing business.  Analyn has been sustaining her business activities through her past 17 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: David
description: David lives in the Litein area of Kenya. He has three children and has been doing his business for eleven years.  His primary income source is milk.  He has stated what is most enjoyable about farming as 'farming.'  His biggest challenge is 'poor weather like drought.' Animals on the farm have been given the names of 'Karo.'  David was asked why he chose Juhudi Kilimo for this loan, to which he replied: 'because of fast loan processing.'  This client was also asked what was learned during Juhudi's required micro-finance training session, he responded: 'it has a grace period.'  David's highest monthly expense is school fees. When asked 'how will this loan benefit his family', David replied 'it will provide more income.'  As part of Juhudi's loan appraisal process, each borrower's assets are evaluated. David owns the following ' acow' but does not own 'pigs, poultry, pumps, bicycles, motorcycles or automobiles.' Juhudi Kilimo also tries to measure any change in living standards based on this loan. This borrower has in the household 'a mosquito net' but does not have 'electricity, solar power, running water, a sewing machine, a TV or a DVD.'  Note: To create this loan profile, Juhudi Kilimo used a mobile device to gather information in the field and send the data to a central online repository, thus reducing paper use, making the process more efficient, and keeping costs down."

name: Beatriz
description: Beatriz is 47 years old.  She is married and has three school age children.  She sells seasonal clothing and shoes.  She sells her products on foot and visits various markets and fairs.  She is in her first loan sequence with the institution.  Beatriz is going to use this loan for the purchase of wholesale clothing and shoes such as sweaters and jackets to stock her business as the cold season in nearing and during this season, she has many sales and even orders.  The reason she is requesting this loan is because she doesn’t have capital.  In her business, Beatriz faces the challenge of daily competition.  She is going to use the benefits to buy a sales stand.  She wants to stock her business and offer a variety of products to her customers.  Beatriz feels happy and grateful to the institution for the support they provide because it permits her to improve her business.

name: Antonieta
description: Antonieta is separated. She has four children and lives in La Paz in a brick house that is her own. Antonieta sells food. She works selling dishes to masons and other construction workers. It's pretty heavy duty work because she must go out with pots, dishes, and cutlery. Antonieta is asking for a loan to buy sacks of rice and noodles since these ingredients are very expensive to buy. Antonieta is the only source of income in her home and needs your help.

name: Charles
description: Charles is a 56-year-old married man with six children, living in Fort Portal Uganda. He is a dairy farmer, the business he does daily, and works seven hours every day. He started this business with an aim of earning more income as he supplies to major dairies in Fort Portal town. He is faced with the challenge of unpredictable weather changes which cause low milk production. Besides that, he is working very hard in order to get a bright future. Charles has asked for a loan to buy barbed wire, poles and nails to fence his farm.

name: Mao's Group
description: This loan group is made up of five members, who are shown in the picture. The group leader, Mrs. Mao K., is a 32-year-old farmer who lives in Kompong Chhnang Province. She is married to Oum Sok, age 44. This couple, who work together in the farming business, has given birth to five children. One of the children is married and four are single. She and her husband also fish along the river in order to earn extra profit. As she lacks money to buy fishing gear and supplies, she has decided to request a loan from Kiva, and she will use these funds to buy nets and traps for the fishing business.  The other four borrowers: Mrs. N. is asking for a loan to buying fishing equipment for earning extra profit. Mrs. Y. is asking for a loan to purchase nets and traps.   Mrs. E. is applying for a loan to buy fishing tools for additional revenue.    Mrs. T. is applying for a loan to buy nets and traps for extra income.

name: Carmen
description: Carmen H. is from the village of Panduma, Tukuran Zamboanga Del Sur. She is 50 years old. Carmen is married and has 5 adult-aged children. To make a living, Carmen operates a specialized retail store and her main source of income from the business comes from selling seafood products  including fish and shrimp in the local community. Carmen has been engaged in her business for over 10 years and earns approximately 10,000 PHP a month.  In 2008, Carmen joined GDMPC to gain access to financial services to improve her living situation with the ability to engage in business. Carmen has successfully repaid a previous loan of 7,000 PHP from GDMPC. This previous loan was used to to purchase additional fish to sell. Carmen is requesting a new loan of 10,000 PHP which will be used to invest in expanding the business. This loan will be the third loan taken out by Carmen from GDMPC. She plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.   About GDMPC:  GDMPC is one of the most progressive cooperatives in Mindanao, Philippines.  *Note: To maximize efficiency and reduce costs, this loan was posted using a template to automate the translation by Kiva.  Given that manual translation of entrepreneur profiles is costly, Kiva created this template for our Field Partner to allow them to continue to post loans in English while providing quality and accurate information to Kiva lenders.

name: Lidia Beatriz
description: Lidia is in her fourth loan cycle, which she is doing with her friends and group mates in the "Sector 3 Marias" credit group. She likes this form of credit because it allows her to deviate from the work routine and share pleasant moments with her friends. She lives in an area that is part of the Turi parish in Cuenca. This is a very touristic area because it has a vantage point of the city. Her people work in agriculture, animal raising, and sales.Lidia, 34, lives in a civil union and has four children who are 14, 6, and 3-year-old twins. Her oldest child is in high school, and her second is in primary school. Her husband shines shoes for a living. They live in their own home.Lidia takes care of the household chores. She also takes care of her children and raises chickens and guinea pigs.She will invest this loan into buying guinea pigs and chickens. Her goal is to have her own business such as a fast food place.

name: Félix Arnulfo
description: Félix Arnulfo has his own business, a small saddlery where he makes packsaddles and accessories.  His business is located in the town of El Sauce.  Currently he is a young man with the spirit of improving his life.  He has two children in his care.  He had the opportunity to come again to CEPRODEL with the goal of growing in his own business.  He knows that CEPRODEL always has helped him in his work.  This is why he came to request a loan to buy tanned cowhide, stirrups, acid, rope, tule fiber, and other leather working supplies.  This will be of great importance because he will be able to make more packsaddles, which will be useful to him for the growth of his business.  It will allow him to stay stable and have a good income in his household.

name: Pedro Antonio
description: Pedro lives in the administrative division of Granada. He is married, and has an auto bodywork and car paint workshop. He started in the family business 15 years ago as an assistant. Over time working with his family he felt that he had enough experience to work alone, and set up his own business when he was 28 years old.  His business currently has two employees and an apprentice, who he pays on a weekly basis. He offers his services in the local community and the areas around Granada. He has many customers due to his experience, and is well-known for the good work he does. He has no other income and depends on his auto bodywork shop. He hopes to continue with the business, delivering good work and being punctual to keep his customers.  He has requested this loan to buy paint and tools to finish some pending jobs he has. This will help him as he will be able to deliver his work on time, which will give him more income and help his business.  In the future he hopes to buy his own plot of land and build a house to provide for his family’s future.

name: Margie
description: Margie is 45 years old married with one only child and lives in Clarin, Misamis Occidental. Margie owns and operates a food selling business at the market in the local community to earn a living. She has been in her business for many years and earns enough to sustain their daily needs. With her revenue, her previous loan used for the business was successfully repaid. Recently, she took a new loan of 30,000 PHP to purchase additional raw ingredients for her pork barbeque. Margie plans to use the additional revenue generated from the business to improve the general living conditions of her family.

name: Lucilyn
description: As a married parent of three children, Lucilyn works hard to support her family.She has a buy and sell vegetables business in the Philippines, and she also earns additional income from a general store.  Lucilyn is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to buy additional vegetables to sell, such as beans, squash, bitter gourd, eggplant and other green leafy vegetables.Lucilyn has been sustaining her business activities through her past 10 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her to attain her dream to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Sunatullo
description: Sunatullo is a resident of the city of Vahdat.  He is 24 years old, married and has one child.  Sunatullo provides a taxi service and has been in this business for three years.  The goal of obtaining this loan is to install natural gas equipment.

name: Ali
description: Ali, a 19 year old single man, lives in Taiz, Yemen. He is a very hardworking individual who strives for a better future. He is working for a company and he has accumulated his salary in order to provide for his family (brothers and parents).   The house the family lives in has been deteriorating over the past years. He is requesting a youth loan of 300,000 YER to purchase construction materials for repairing the ceiling and windows. He hopes with this loan the family can live in a more comfortable place. This will also contribute to the efforts against air pollution by emitting less smoke.

name: Lorna
description: Lorna is 59 years old and married with four children. She  works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 9,500 loan through NWTF to purchase more stocks to sell in her general store.  Lorna has borrowed and paid three loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for two years and also earns an income from food vending. She aspires to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: María Selsa
description: María is a 60-year-old housewife. She attended school until sixth grade. Her husband died 29 years ago, leaving her a widow. She is also the mother of a 35-year-old son who is already married and works to pay for his own household expenses.   María lives with her niece and her husband but no one is financially dependent on her. María makes a living looking after 4 cows that produce a lot of milk for her. She has been doing this for 22 years and it is a job that her parents taught her how to do. To get to work, María walks 1 kilometre, she then works from 7:00 am to 11:00 am and in the evenings she works as a seamstress.   The loan that she is asking for is to purchase 4 more dairy cows so that she can produce more milk. She will sell the milk to make income, which will enable her to improve her quality of life.   María's dream is to increase her cattle heard so that she can produce more milk and therefore always maintain the sustainability of her business.

name: Maximiliana
description: Maximiliana is a 54-year-old mother of a very happy and hardworking family. She lives with her son, Maycon, in a house inherited from her mother. Her biggest wish is to improve their quality of life.   The products that Maximiliana has farmed with so much effort and dedication have helped her to progress in life. Every morning, she starts to work on her fields. She knows that the quality of her harvest will depend on the care she brings to her potato and pea crops.   What she enjoys most about her work is caring for her crops because she feels pleased when the harvest is large and abundant. Maximiliana has been been farming for 24 years and considers the most difficult part to be carrying her harvest to the market in Tarma, the place where she sells, because the sacks are extremely heavy. She also raises bulls and sheep, which she can sell if necessary.  Going forward, she hopes to improve her produce as a means to obtain better prices. She belongs to the “Señor de Muruhuay” communal bank. This is her fourth loans with the MFP, where she knows that she must submit her payments on time and is willing to do so.

name: Mirella Yvone
description: Mirella is a 33 year old woman. She lives in the city of Chincha with her son, whom she loves and who is her main reason for living. She is a very kind, hardworking and enthusiastic person who puts all of her effort into getting her son ahead, because she is both mother and father to him. Unfortunately, due to a lack of financial resources and because she has had to wrk since she was very young, Mirella was unable to study law, but she would have really liked to. In her free time, she likes to see movies and on occasion cook a delicious carapulcra to share with her family.  On her own initiative, with much hard work and dedication, Mirella works at her own business selling food and beverages. She works every day starting in the early morning hours. She can work for approximately 8 hours. She is happy with her work and believes that it is going well for her because she is a good cook and because she is friendly to her customers.  Mirella is grateful to the Kiva lenders, since thanks to their help she will be able to buy shelving, display cases and materials. These will be very useful for improving her business, because she will keep working and striving to achieve her biggest dream of having her own home.

name: Bikram
description: Bikram is a 48-year-old physically-challenged person living with his wife and two sons, ages  25 and 20 years old. He runs a variety shop where he sells betel, tobacco sachets, biscuits, toffees, tomatoes, potatos, detergents, soaps, shampoo sachets, snacks, etc. He earns 8,000 Indian rupees (INR) per month. One of his son works as a laborer in his village and the younger one is pursuing his graduation.   Bikram wants to repair his shop and purchase more stock of what he sells to increase his inventory. He would also like to add new products like cell phone talk value recharge vouchers and soft drinks. He has requested a loan of 50,000 INR to purchase recharge vouchers, a refrigerator for keeping soft drinks, and more stock. He wants his younger son to study more and get admitted to a good college and work in a public sector unit. He wants his elder son to help him run the shop and make it much bigger.

name: Savy
description: Savy (pictured with her loom) and her husband, Dy, live on an island in the Mekong River about 15 kilometers from Phnom Penh City. They have three sons. Two of her sons have full-time employment, and the other is in school.   Savy is a weaver, and her husband is a house builder. She is asking for loan of $400 to buy weaving materials. She will also use a part of the loan to fill in the land behind her house because there are some small ponds behind her, which she needs to fill in.

name: Rehema
description: Rehema is taking another bigger loans of KES 100,000  to use in the construction of her house. With the loan, she wants to purchase sacks of sand, cement, timber and pay for labor. She dreams of establishing real estate houses in the future.

name: Precilla
description: As a married parent of six children, Precilla works hard to support her family. She has a dried fish vending business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from motorcycle transportation and buying and selling meat. Precilla is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF to buy stock of assorted dried fish to sell. Precilla has been sustaining her business activities through her past 6 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her attain her dream to build and expand her business and secure the future of her family.

name: Francisco
description: Francisco is 46 years old and lives with his wife and children in his own home.  He has been farming and raising livestock since he was very young.  He now owns his own land which allows him to carry out these activities freely.  Francisco works from very early in the morning, delivering what he has harvested and, according to the season and when it is necessary, he sells animals. His animals are taken to the livestock markets in his area.  Francisco enjoys this business because it allows him to be in touch with nature.  This is his first loan from MFP.  He has good references from working with other community banks.  He was keen to join this group and pledges to be a good member.  He will use the loan he is requesting to buy sacks of manure.

name: Francis
description: Francis is a married man. He has three children. He describes himself to be honest. He operates a retail business where he sells bananas, tomatoes, and other vegetables. He has been involved in this business for four years. His primary customers are locals. He describes his biggest business challenge to be high purchase prices.   He will use the 15,000 KES loan to buy more stock of vegetables. He hopes that in the future, he will be prosperous. This is his first loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. He will use the anticipated profits to expand his business.

name: Jefwa
description: Jefwa lives in the Mombasa area of Coast Province, Kenya. He is a married father of six children, although only the youngest three are still in school.   Jefwa owns a café, which he has been operating for a six years. He employs three other people in the café. He also runs a retail shop and rents houses.  He learned about Milango through friends who invited him to the group, and he joined with the aim of accessing credit to improve his business operations. His main challenge is the high cost of food products/raw materials.   Jefwa is applying for a loan of 36,650 Kenya shillings to buy food stock, such as rice, cereals, wheat flour, cooking fat, etc., for the café. His extra income from the loan will be added to his savings to pay school fees for his children and improve his living standards. His dream is to build other rentals.

name: Nicanora
description: Nicanora is 76 years old and a widow with eight children.  She earns a living by raising pigs in the Philippines. Nicanora is borrowing PHP 29,500 through NWTF to buy additional feed and vitamins for her pigs.  Nicanora has been raising pigs for 30 years and also earns additional income from a general store.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save money to expand her business.

name: Maria Teresa
description: Teresa is an enterprising woman. She is married and her husband works as a driver for a freight transportation company, forcing him to be frequently out of town. They have three small children still in primary school, which aggravates their expenses day by day. Due to the above mentioned, two years ago she decided to start a small business preparing food. Her business has enjoyed great acceptance among her customers since she offers home deliveries.    Because her business has been growing, she requires your support with her work capital. Teresa is requesting a $250 USD loan to purchase raw materials such as: beef, pork, chicken and disposable plates and boxes to pack the delicious meals she prepares for her customers. She plans to repay the loan within 3-6 months and she hopes that her business will grow even more. **   Translated from Spanish by Isabel Tan, a Kiva Volunteer.  Teresa es una mujer muy emprendedora, está casada y su esposo trabaja como chofer en una línea de transportes de carga, por lo que frecuentemente sale fuera de la ciudad. Tienen tres hijos pequeños, los cuales estudian en la escuela primaria, es por eso que los gastos son cada día mayores. Debido a lo anterior, hace dos años se decidió por iniciar su pequeño negocio de elaboración de comidas, el cual ha sido muy bien aceptado por sus clientes, ya que tiene el servicio de entrega a domicilio.   Debido a que su negocio ha estado creciendo ella requiere que la apoyen para su capital de trabajo, es por eso que solicita un préstamo por la cantidad de $ 250 USD para comprar sus materias primas como por ejemplo: carne de res, puerco, pollo, desechables y materiales para empacar las sabrosas comidas que prepara para sus clientes. Su deseo es pagar su préstamo en un plazo de 3-6 meses y para entonces espera contar con un mayor volumen de su negocio.

name: Nila
description: Nila is 65 years old with five children. She is working hard for her family doing retailing. She is known in Tudela for her dried fish. She has saved for the renovation of her house but her finances are not sufficient. She has approached Paglaum MPC for a loan to purchase housing materials like cement, hollow blocks and plywood. Nila hopes to pay off her loan in a timely fashion.

name: Hippolyte
description: Hyppolyte is a young Cameroonian, aged thirty two, and married with a child who is a year old. He has been in this business for year now which makes him experience and stable.  His business is likely to succeed because it is located in an urban area with many potential customers. This loan will increase his turn over by fifty percent. His standard of living will as well be improved

name: Binish
description: Binish is a 38 years old married woman. She has been manufacturing belts from many years and is proud to be contributing to her household income. When Binish was not earning, her family was going through severe financial crisis that compelled her to use her stitching skills in a productive manner.   Binish's husband was the sole bread winner of the family. Due to limited resources, none of their six children were sent to school. Binish felt it obligatory to change her family’s living standards and started her business at home. She is a brave woman and hard work has helped her establish a good clientele. Now she is facing difficulty in fulfilling large orders. Therefore she has requested for 45,000 PKR to buy stock of good quality leather, threads and cutters for manufacturing more belts. Her dream is to expand her business in future.

name: Heng's Group
description: Heng’s group live in a rural village in Kandal province in Cambodia. Heng makes a living cultivating rice and he also does extra work as tailor to support his family. In their village there is no reliable access to safe, clean drinking water. Having a water filter at home will help each member of this group to safeguard the health of their families and save money on medical expenses and save time collecting fuel and boiling water.

name: Dania Maria
description: Dania, 29, is a very responsible, honest, and hardworking young woman.  She lives with her husband and daughter in a community in Choluteca, in the south of Honduras.  Dania has a grocery store business and needs the loan to buy soda, meat, corn, milk, beans, sugar, rice, coffee, toilet paper, cookies, "churros" [fried dough], and fruit juice.  With the loan she hopes to have more merchandise to sell to her customers and cover the requests she gets every day and more frequently in this Christmas season.  With the income Dania hopes to improve somewhat the financial situation in her household.  In the future she wants for her business to be a mini-market and have a greater variety of products to sell.  Dania dreams of seeing her daughter graduate and become a good person with principles and values.  Choluteca, Honduras, November 2012

name: Edwin
description: Edwin is 33 years old. He is single and he has no children.  He lives with his brother and he helps him with the expenses.  Edwin is a farmer and he sells vegetables. He goes to many fairs to offer his products. He needs a loan to buy seeds for his business.  In that way, he will have a better income.

name: Rosario
description: Rosario L. is from the village of Kabayan, Salvacion, Kadingilan, Bukidnon. She is 44 years old, married and has three school-aged children.  To make a living, Rosario owns and operates a sari-sari (variety) retail shop, selling both food and daily use products in the local community.  Rosario has been engaged in business for over four years and earns approximately 8500 PHP a month.  In 2009, Rosario joined HSPFI to gain access to financial services to help improve her living situation and ability to engage in business activities. She has successfully repaid a previous loan of 11000 PHP from HSPFI to purchase additional inventory. Rosario is requesting a new loan of 14000 PHP to expand her business. This loan will be her fourth from HSPFI.  Rosario plans to use the additional revenue to improve her business.   ---------------------------------------- About HSPFI:  HSPFI is one of accredited partners of Opportunity International in the Philippines. It is based in Cagayan de Oro City and is reaching out to the poor households of Northern Mindanao.

name: Pepitas De Cobre 27 Group
description: Blanca  is a 64 year old woman who's married, childless, and her business is baking and selling pastries and cakes. She's independent, generous, understanding, patient, responsible, and hard-working. She does her work in the "1ro de Mayo" area, a place known for the constant growth of its population and commerce in every sector. It's a location that brings together different cultures and ethnicities from the mountain plateaus. It's elevation is 4,070 meters above sea level, which makes it the city with the second highest elevation in the world.   Blanca has a dark complexion, long black hair that she ties, dark eyes, and her native language is Aymara but she speaks spanish because of the overall culture and because of the business she's involved in (in the picture she's standing in the first spot on the right side, wearing a beige jacket and a black sweater). She lives with her husband who runs the business, her children are independent and don't live with them, and the house she lives in with her husband is built out of brick, with a corrugated iron roof, and has potable water, electricity, sewage service, and natural gas.   The need to expand her business drove her to form a group of people that own businesses like selling quilts, making leather wallets, transportation services, making skirts, a video store, selling meat pies, selling silverware, and selling cell phones, to apply for a loan. Her business is baking and selling pastries and desserts, a business that she launched at home with a minimal investment by selling sandwich cookies, vanilla cakes, and chocolate pastries with ingredients that are easy to find in the market. As she made back her capital, she invested it in desserts for sale to her customers. She says, "Who doesn't like a chocolate pastry or a vanilla cake? You can eat one at any time and in any place."  Her dream is to save up to travel to far away places, she wants to purchase flour wholesale and the necessary ingredients for her business. This is the first loan she's applied for with this institution in the 18 years that she's been in this line of work. These are the reasons Blanca's requesting a loan to purchase flour and other ingredients wholesale to bake a variety of pastries and cakes.

name: Betzabe
description: Betzabe, age 45, lives at her husband’s side with their two children in their own house.  She has been selling woven garments, which she makes in her own house.  Sometimes her mother helps her.  She makes the quantity of garments that are ordered each month.  This is how she manages to get good earnings.  She works in an organized way, and she always strives to be up to date with the fashion and the new designs that are shown.   Later she wishes to increase her quantity of woven garments and learn other stitches in order to have a greater demand in the market.  This is her 6th loan with MFP.  She feels that this is a great opportunity to have had access to loans.  They have been extremely beneficial to the economic growth of her family, and she is very grateful.  The loan is to buy wool wholesale.

name: Hilda
description: Hilda is 34 years old and lives with her husband, an employee of the local municipality, and their 2 children in primary school. For 5 years she has owned 4 motorcars, with which she contracts particular drivers to transport passengers. The good thing is that these people maintain their vehicles in good condition and are reliable. In addition, the business is very profitable because within the zone where they work people prefer to move in motorcars than in another vehicle. But, the difficulty that she has is that she does not have an appropriate place to keep her vehicles so that they are safe during the night. Additionally, Hilda has been a seller of beauty products for 6 months, a business with which she is obtaining extra income for her family; and moving forward, she would like to have a grocery store, since there is no store nearby. This is her second loan with MFP and she is happy with her community bank because each person is responsible and pays their quotas on time. With the money that she is requesting, she will buy spare parts to repair and maintain her motorcars so that they function without difficulties. Translated from Spanish by Pamela Reynolds, Kiva Volunteer

name: 07.04.75 Phú Sơn Group
description: Mrs. Sơn operates a food stall/restaurant selling fruit. She has been involved in this business for 6 years. She is requesting a loan to purchase fruit to resell.  Sơn is 62 years old and she is married with 3 children. She is the group leader of the 07.04.75 Phú Sơn solidarity group, which consists of 4 members. Sơn supports herself with her business in Thanh Hoa city, an urban town in the Thanh Hoa province. Her children are grown up.  This is Sơn's first loan with Thanh Hoa Fund of Poor Women. One of the most critical business difficulties that concerns her is the lack of capital.  Sơn hopes for her children to find a good job, for her business to do well, and for her family to be healthy and happy.

name: Grace
description: Grace lives in Kitale. Kitale is located in the Trans-Nzoia district of western Kenya, and at over 6,300 feet above sea level, is one of Africa’s most elevated towns. The rich soil of the area makes it one of the nation's biggest maize producing regions, lending it the nickname of “the breadbasket of Kenya".   Many farmers in the region have started projects planting bluegum trees on their land, which complement the region’s natural forests and provide bees with a variety of food sources. The people around Kitale have been beekeeping for centuries, and the area is dense with strong bee colonies.  Grace is married and has four children. She is a Pastor and her husband is a Reverend. They are also farmers. They have been farming for fifteen years now and they are currently growing maize and beans, and they also keep cattle and poultry. Grace is excited about beekeeping as it will earn her some income from the sale of honey.   This is Grace’s first loan with Honey Care and she plans to use the proceeds from her beehives to pay school fees for her children and improve her livelihood. Grace’s hope for the future is to live a better life.

name: Agapita
description: Agapita O. is a 46-year-old married woman who supports her family by operating two business ventures:  hog raising and manicure/weaving businesses. She lives in  Brgy. San Sebastian, Samboan, Cebu. She has been a member of NWTF-Project Dungganon since 2004 and has improved her living conditions with the help of her loans from NWTF and through her own efforts.    By working hard at her   hog raising and manicure businesses, she is gradually making her family more economically stable. She now earns an average monthly income of PHP 5,000. Agapita is now borrowing PHP 12,000 so that she  can continue to fund the operations of her business.   This will be her 15th loan from NWTF-Project Dungganon. Her previous loan of PHP 15,000, which she paid off well within its term, was just another step in her journey toward economic freedom.   Agapita aspires to elevate her family's living conditions and ensure their future well-being by following the  Dungganon way.   About NWTF:  In a world full of challenges, Negros Women for Tomorrow Foundation (NWTF), is making a difference in the lives of thousands of women through Project Dungganon (a Hiligaynon word that means Honorable). Through the alleviation program, NWTF is empowering these women to progress from earning less than $1 a day to achieving realities that surpass even their dreams. They have taken a life path that will ultimately make them Dungganon - a title of esteem that is bestowed on a member of a community who has earned respect through a lifetime of hard and honest work.Help NWTF continue its mission to help the poorest in the Philippines by clicking  the link to the  NWTF Kiva lending team  on Kiva.org to join our team.

name: Zakhir
description: Zakhir G. is thirty-three and married with one six-year-old son, who will be going to school this year.  He and his family live in the Fuzuli region.  For five years Zakhir has worked as a taxi driver.  He learned how to drive from his father.  He loved driving and was good at it so he decided to become a taxi driver.  Zakhir currently needs 2000 AZN to buy spare parts so he can fix up his car.Translated from Russian by Jill Heske, Kiva Volunteer

name: Lout's Group
description: Lout is a single woman originally from Kampong Cham province's Dambae district in Cambodia. She is a peasant who grows rice on a 2-hectare area and plants cassava on 1.5 hectare of farmland in order to earn a living. She has been with this business for five years and is challenged by the fruitless crop caused by drought.   Lout received her first loan with VisionFund and has finished the past three loans already with success. She has managed to repay the entire loans, which have helped her to manage her daily expenses, especially decent food.   To continue better support for her business, she formed a group of two members to request a new loan. As the leader, she will use her loan portion to buy fertilizer, seed and insecticide for her farm. She hopes to receive more yields and sell it for a good price in order to double her income and make her living better.

name: Pov's Group
description: Age 30 and a mother of one son, Pov is a local citizen from Kampong Cham province. She struggles against her family’s hardships via rice farming and her husband helps to supplement the family’s income via working at rubber plantation, tapping rubber trees for latex. The current business which she has been with for 10 years, generates about 18,300 KHR per day.   Pov is a four-cycle client with VisionFund (Cambodia) and has repaid her past loans successfully. This has enabled her to increase her income and keep her children in school. Now, she is in a group of two to apply for a new loan. She and her joint borrower are seeking 1,400,000 KHR each. She is the group leader and she will use her loan to pay for plowing fees and to buy fertilizer and cassava seedlings. She hopes to grow her crops in a timely manner and earn more income.

name: Nato
description: Nato is a 45-year-old married woman, from the village Mitsabogira. She lives with her son and mother, who gets monthly assistance from the local government. Nato is involved in agricultural activities. Particularly, she takes care of 3 dairy cows, produces cheese and milk and uses the products for local trading. Nato generates approximately 350 Gel monthly, and this income is hardly enough for covering all of their daily costs. She applied for a loan several times but couldn’t obtain one from the local financial institutions, because of their requirements to have business experience or stable revenue, until the Start Up program began which is a joint product of Kiva and Credo. The program allows rural poor people, such as Nato, to have a chance to start or re-start a business. With the requested money, Nato will build a greenhouse, plant vegetables and greens and then sell them in the local market.   The family's living conditions will significantly improve, and the family will have enough income to access regular credit products available on the country’s capital market, in case of need. Nato awaits your support.

name: Cecilia Narciza
description: Cecilia is 49 year old, single, and lives with her father who is 94 years old. Three years ago, she began with three sets of sheets, visiting her customers door to door. With a lot of effort, she leaves home very early to sell her products. Cecilia needs money to invest in purchasing sheets and blankets, thus managing to increase her sales and obtain higher income, in order to be able to pay for food and some medicines for her father. She aspires to have her own house.

name: Ariel
description: Ariel is 32 years old and has one child. He has managed a farming business for 10 years.  According to Ariel, while managing a farming business, he has experienced a lot of difficulties like weather conditions. But, through his faith and hard work, he overcame all the obstacles in life.  Due to these difficulties, he is requesting a loan of 15,000 PHP to purchase sacks of fertilizer and seeds for his farming business.  Ariel hopes to obtain his requested loan amount so he can keep his farming business productive and profitable all throughout the growing season.

name: Peter
