description: Peter lives at Alcala with his wife, and they had five children. Three of them are studying. He gets his income through farming activities. He plants and harvests rice to sell to traders. His spouse also raises hogs for future sale. Together, they work hard to sustain the needs of the family.   He wanted to earn more profits in the farming business, but he needs additional revolving capital. His income from the previous harvest was just enough to cover school expenses and bills at home. So, he is now asking for another loan of 25,000 Philippines pesos to buy fertilizers, pesticides and insecticides to use for crop maintenance. With enough sustenance, his crops will grow fruitfully, thus giving him a profitable harvest someday.

name: Thuy
description: Thuy is requesting a new loan to buy rice, bran and many kind of products to sell in her store. Her previous loan enabled her to expand her business and earn a higher income to support her family. She hopes that another loan will assist her in increasing the size of her business, attract new customers and increase her sales. She also hopes that through the loan she can increase her income and improve her family's living conditions.

name: Emilia
description: Here is Emilia, a resident of Caloocan City, Philippines. Recently she had a loan which she had used for her business. Actually, she sustains all her needs through her business while ably helping her family at the same time. This is why she would like to give her gratitude to those who lent her assistance previously.   To improve sales, Emilia would like to apply for a new loan to purchase additional products such as additional cloth, needles, and other materials needed in her rug-making business. With PHP 9,000, she can certainly improve her livelihood and eventually grow it with the grace of God. For now, it is her desire to have people like you who will assist her in her prospect.   In the future, Emilia hopes to give her family a more favorable kind of living and simultaneously drive her inventory into progress. She meets up with her co-fellowship members to share stories of her work every week and where she can also draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God she studies.  * All CCT community partners / clients are organized into fellowship groups that meet on a weekly basis. A fellowship group is composed of 15 to 30 community partners. The fellowship groups gather each week to study the Word of God, build social capital, and pay microfinance loans.

name: Khaled
description: Khaled is a 28-year-old young man from Jenin. He is married and has a one-year old son. Khaled works for the National Palestinian Authority. He was married 3 years ago and is still trying to furnish his house, which is a hard task with the basic salary he receives. Therefore, he took a $1500 loan from FATEN to pay for home furniture.  Khaled's house is very simple and consists of the very basic needs and lacks a lot of of furniture. Khaled is thinking of taking another loan after finishing with the home furniture, and of starting a business as a second source of income, so he can afford a better living standard and secure his wife and son's life.  In the picture, Khaled is leaving FATEN's office.

name: Judith
description: Judith continues to make her living in the business of clothing sales.  She sells pants, blouses and t-shirts.  She is an enterprising and determined woman, who by means of this business, wants to get her family ahead.  She is asking for this loan to buy shoes, t-shirts, pants, sweaters and blouses.Judith is happy to have the loan and she promises to make the repayments on the loan.

name: Lutviyar
description: Lutviyar M. is 44, married with three children, lives in the small village of Saatli district, where he now works as a farmer. His main business is agriculture and livestock breeding, which provides him with the means to meet the needs of his family. Lutviyar owns a large piece of land where he cultivates different kinds of vegetables. Due to the poor quality of the soil and the insects, he is no longer able to satisfy market demand. Very hard-working, he is asking for a loan of 1000 AZN to buy seeds, fertilizer and calves. The loan will greatly improve Lutviyar’s income and his family's living standards.

name: Liezel
description: Liezel is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a hollow blocks-making business in the Philippines.   She is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to purchase additional materials for her hollow blocks-making business.  Liezel has been in this business for a year. Liezel earns additional income from motorcycle transport.  Liezel has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams of building and expanding her business to secure the future of her family.

name: Jane
description: Jane is a woman with all the spirit for work, who resides in a remote village in the Kapsowar area of Kenya. For the past five years, Jane has been involved in mixed farming. Her primary sources of income has been planting different varieties of crops and some personal business she engages in to earn additional income. Jane has been able to provide nutritious food for her family. She passionately loves dairy farming. Villagers have nicknamed her Mrs. Cow. Jane sells milk to her neighbors and to the local market, but the demand has been overwhelming and she cannot meet it. For this reason, she is requesting a loan to buy an extra dairy cow, which will assist in increasing milk productivity. The dairy cow that she plans to buy is not just an ordinary cow; it is a quality breed of dairy cow that will be producing between 10-20 liters of milk a day. This milk production will immediately translate to increased profit margins and increased income levels. Profits from selling milk will be used to repay the loan. The extra income will be used to increase her business enterprise. Jane is very visionary, and she intends to start adding value to her milk business. All that she patiently waits for is for your kindness.

name: Nataliya
description: Nataliya lives in the city of Drogobych in western Ukraine.  She is 39 years old and works one of the local resorts as a director of operations.  She is a person with disability (Category III) and receives a disability pension which, unfortunately, is very small.  She lives in a one-bedroom apartment which is poorly heated and constantly feels "damp".  For a long time now, Nataliya has been dreaming about installing an individual heating system in her apartment, so that she will finally stop feeling like she is freezing during the cold season.  But to do so, she needs an additional 16,000 hryvnia, because her income and her pension are far from sufficient to cover those costs.

name: Sena
description: As a married parent of two children, Sena works hard to support her family.  She has a ready-to-wear business in the Philippines, and also earns additional income from food vending. She is borrowing PHP 15,000 through NWTF to purchase more items of ready-to-wear like pants, shorts, t-shirts, shirts, slippers, etc. for her business.  Sena has been sustaining her business activities through her past 9 loans from NWTF. She hopes that her hard work will help her to attain her dream, which is to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Sumac Puririsun Group
description: These members belong to the “SUMAC PURIRISUN” communal bank. This bank is located in the district of Cusco, which belongs to the province of Cusco and department of Cusco.Hilaria, one of the members, is a hard-working and modest person who sells fruit. She starts her work early in the morning when she buys her produce wholesale, then she goes to the markets and sells to her customers. She finishes her work late, which is why she wants to have a place of her own where she can sell fruit, so she can spend more time with her family. Hilaria is 47 years old and has four children, and is making progress in life with them. She is asking for the loan to buy bananas, oranges and mandarins.The other members have businesses selling beauty products, selling handicrafts, selling animals, and a grocery shop.The members are grateful to the Kiva lenders for putting their faith in them and promise to be punctual in making their agreed repayments.

name: Brenda Xiomara
description: Brenda is 35 years old. She studied up to ninth grade. She is married and her husband has a motorcycle-taxi with which he transports people from the community. She has three children, but only two of them are attending school. Brenda has worked for 10 years baking bread to sell. She learned this job because her mother also used to make bread, and Brenda now took over the business. She decided to continue selling it, because she had the customers already. She makes bread three times a week, and her daughter and husband get also involved in baking it. Her schedule is from 8:00 a.m. until 3:00 p.m. when she finishes selling it. Brenda needs the loan to build a homemade oven, because the one she has is not hers and she has to go to her neighbor to bake the bread. Brenda dreams of seeing her children graduate with a college career and of improving her house.

name: Celia Aydee
description: Celia Aydee is married. She has a daughter who is ten years old. She is requesting a loan for the construction of a wall around her house. Now she needs buy supplies like bricks, sand, cement and bars. With this, her family will feel more protected and safer. Celia Aydee and Antonio, her husband, want to give their family the best. Celia Aydee works as a domestic worker in a private home. Antonio works in shopping center.

name: Sukufa
description: Sukufa, 49 years old, is married and has a son and two daughters. Her husband works as a laborer. Sukufa has been raising seasonal fruit trees (apples, pears, etc.) for 20 years and has good skills in this field. Her monthly salary is 170 AZN. The family lives in an IDP (Internally Displaced Persons) settlement because they are refugees.   Azerbaijan people like fresh fruits and have a high demand for them. Refugees, especially, can’t buy fresh fruit when they need them because of prices. That’s why Sukufa tries to sell her harvest as cheaply as possible because she knows that refugees have a hard life.   Unfortunately, Sukufa’s income is too low to cover the family’s living costs. Seasonal fruits don’t bring as much earnings as needed. Sukufa has applied for a loan of 1,500 AZN in order to supply seeds to raise and sell other kinds of fruit. She hopes that this is a good way to increase her income. Let’s help Sukufa and her family.

name: Matlubakhon
description: Matlubakhon is a smart, promising young entrepreneur.  She has been running this entrepreneurship independently for six years and has experience in this business.  She started the business with $2500, and now her merchandise is valued at $5000.  Matlubakhon has a selection of quality perfumes and women's goods that are in high demand.  She has a reputation of an honest and responsible entrepreneur.  Matlubakhon wants to obtain a loan in the sum of $3000 for the purchase of goods and business expansion.  Matlubakhon hopes to receive your support and expresses her gratitude.

name: Rosemarie
description: Rosemarie is 44 years old and married with two children; she works very hard to provide for them.  She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 12,000 loan through NWTF to buy stocks of household good to sell like shampoo, soap, canned goods, milk, noodles, spices, etc.  Rosemarie has been in this business for 30 years.   She would like to save enough to provide a secure future for her family.

name: Catherine
description: Catherine is a single woman. She describes herself to be an ambitious woman. She operates a retail store where she sells home products such as sugar, tea leaves, steel wire, maize flour, bread, salt, cooking oil, etc. She has been involved in this business for 3 years. Her business is located within a conducive business environment and her primary customers are local residents. She describes her biggest business challenge to be insufficient funds for improving the business. She will use the KES 20,000 loan to buy more home products. Her business goal is to run a wholesale shop.  Catherine hopes to buy a piece of land with the anticipated profits which she will get from the business.

name: Sat
description: Sat M., 42, has been selling beef. She sells beef that she buys in bulk, on credit, from butchers and runs her business in the busy local market. She always pays her suppliers after she finishes selling her items. She starts selling in the morning and is finished in the late afternoon, with much income.   Sat M. wants to generate extra revenue by investing in a new business as a silk clothes seller in the market. Her capital is not sufficient to open. Therefore, she would like a loan of $1000 for capital to use to rent a market kiosk and buy silk clothes to begin selling.  Sat M. was married, but divorced her husband years ago, and she has a daughter who is married. Her daughter and her son-in-law live with her in the family home. She and her grandchild are in the photo.

name: Firuza
description: H. Firuza is 32 years old, married, and has 4 children. Her husband is an entrepreneur. For more than 6 years, Firuza has been engaged in the business of selling fabrics for national dresses. She gets up at 6 a.m. to prepare breakfast for her husband and children and afterwards, she is busy selling her merchandise until 5 p.m. With this loan, Firuza plans to buy fabrics to increase the range of her selling goods. She is very happy that, thanks to her effort, she has less worry, can help her children with their homework, and is able to make a contribution to her family. Firuza is very grateful for the support that IMON International, with the help of Kiva, provides for her business.     More about Tajikistan and IMON International  Tajikistan is known for its rich history, which includes a key post along the Silk Road and the end of Alexander the Great's rule. It has also produced great thinkers, philosophers, scientists and poets, including Rudaki, Avicenna, Ferdowsi, Omar Khayyam, Jomi, and Rumi. The country is home to communities that still speak the ancient Sogdian language, epic mountain passes, and a civilization that dates back to the 4th millennium B.C. And, even today, it is a complex mixture of the Islamic faith, Soviet culture, New West culture and Central Asian traditions.  But Tajikistan is also the poorest of the former Soviet republics. The civil war, which ignited soon after its independence from the U.S.S.R., further damaged the already weak economy. In addition, 93% of the country is mountainous and only 7% of the land is arable. These conditions have resulted in high levels of unemployment and have forced hundreds of thousands to seek work in other countries, mainly Russia. While the people of Tajikistan are working to improve its agricultural production and manufacturing sector, nearly two-thirds of the population still live in abject poverty.  IMON's History  Since December 2007, IMON International has worked closely with Kiva and Kiva lenders to ensure that poor and low income clients represent a viable business proposition. Funds raised through Kiva have already been distributed to thousands of IMON International's clients and will continue to provide thousands more with permanent access to the varied financial services they need. To learn more about IMON International's work, please visit: www.imon.tj

name: Gayane
description: Gayane is 57 years old. She lives with her husband and son in Sevan city. She graduated from Dilijan Medical College. After education, Gayane is working as a medical nurse in Sevan hospitals. Gayane's husband is a driver and her son is working as a military specialist. They are solving the whole family's needs together.   Gayane’s son studies at Gavar State University in the field of history. Gayane asks for Kiva lenders to loan 180,000 Armenian drams to pay her for son’s education.

name: Kisshen
description: Kisshen is 19 years old and from Dipaculao, Aurora, in the Philippines. She is now taking up a Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Science. She chose this course because she believes that she will be able to use what she learns to help her fellow countrymen. She wants to finish college to help her family financially. Her financial difficulties are what drives her to study harder. Because her parents cannot fully support her studies, Kisshen wants to take out an education loan of 15,000 Philippines pesos (PHP) so she can reduce her financial burden. She is hopeful that KIVA lenders will approve her loan.

name: Josephine
description: Josephine is 22 years old and live in Paynesville. She is single and has two children, ages 8 months and 6 years old. They are in school and live at home. For the past five years she has been selling bitter ball and pepper. She is requesting a loan to purchase more bitter ball and pepper for her business. She says her main challenge is a goods shortage. Josephine says she started this business by rock crushing and she learned this business from her mother. What she like about her business is that it gives her money to support her home. She hopes to build a house in the future.

name: Malai
description: Malai is a farmer living with his wife and child in Sampong Village. On his seven hectare farm, he grows black pepper to enable his family to live in comfortable conditions. Malai wants to save money on utility fees since he spends a lot of money every week charging a battery that has a short life span and is unreliable.   Sometimes when he is busy, Malai doesn’t have time to charge the battery, so the whole family is left in pitch black conditions. He is therefore applying for a Kiva loan to buy a high quality home solar system. With solar energy, Malai  believes his family's living conditions will be better and safer. He will also save time and money on utilities.
town: Sampong Village, Thma Andeurk commune, Chetr Borei

name: Zaina
description: Zaina lives in Kampala, Uganda. She is single and has four children, all of them attending school. She is not looking after any additional family member. She rents a house without access to either electricity or piped water. Her major monthly expenses include school fees, transportation and rent.  She has been selling banana leaves, charcoal and jackfruit in the market, at retail, for many years. She works seven days a week. She does not earn any additional income.  Zaina has requested a loan of UGX 200,000 from MCDT-SACCO, to enable her to stock more banana leaves, charcoal and jackfruit for sale. Her challenges include seasonality and transportation. Her dream is to eliminate the middlemen, by going to the villages to get the commodities from the suppliers, themselves. She joined MCDT because of convenient terms tied to enrolling as a member.

name: Khadra
description: Khadra is 46 year old woman, married, with one child. Khadra is interested in renting wedding dresses, and she works at her home. The financiA. state of this family is terrible, so she’s obliged to help her husband in raising their child. She needs a small loan from A. Majmoua to enhance her job. Her essentiA. purpose is the continuity in her work as a woman. Her dream is to create more and more ideas to develop her business. Her clients are her relatives and friends, but in the future she would like to attract a big number of clients from all over the country.

name: Anna
description: This young lady’s name is Anna and she is 28 years old. She lives with her parents and brother in Vanadzor City in the Lori region. Anna has a higher pedagogical education and already five years of experience in this field. She works at the school as a teacher of Armenian Language and Literature. She also gives private paid courses of Armenian Language and Literature, in this way preparing the pupils for the entrance examinations for the higher educational institutions. Despite her young age, Anna has already managed to excel in her profession of pedagogue as a clever and intellectual person, and her pupils distinguish her among many other teachers for her patience and kindness towards them.  Anna asks for a loan of 300,000 Armenian Drams in order to buy a computer and several professional literature items connected with teaching methodology.

name: Burihol
description: Burihol is a 50 year-old married woman.  She has four children.  Burihol and her family live in the Jilikul district.  She has a secondary education.  She is a kind and decent woman.  Burihol has been involved in two types of business concurrently: farming and gardening.  Her family also works in agriculture.  Thus, they earn a living together.  Burihol leases a plot of land, where she grows vegetables, primarily carrots.  She is requesting this loan to purchase fuel and mineral fertilizers in order to treat the land, and want to use the rest of the sum to pay for the land lease.  In the future, Burihol plans to buy land and expand her business.

name: Faaoloviti
description: Faaoloviti Faleilua is 35 and married with 5 children (ages 2 - 6).  She owns a business venture, planting & harvesting taro for sale.  Faaoloviti has 5 years of experience in this business.  Faaoloviti needs a loan of WST $1750 to purchase weed-killers such as Gramoxome.  She plans to use the earnings from her business (estimated to be 400 tala or US $167 per week) to improve/expand the business. This is her 3rd loan with SPBD.   SPBD's loans are Faaoloviti's only access to capital because she was never able to qualify for a loan with traditional banks.  You can view pictures of a typical plantation in Samoa, taken by a Kiva Fellow, at:   http://picasaweb.google.com/agnes.p.chu/SamoanPlantation  The following social metrics for Faaoloviti Faleilua are provided by SPBD*: Overall Social Metric Score:                1.4 out of 3 Level of Education:                              1.3 out of 3 Level of total Household Income:         1.3 out of 3 Quality of Household Assets:              1.3 out of 3  *SPBD measures the living conditions of each of its borrowers to track her loan progress. The overall social metric score, provided by SPBD, is based upon a number of factors, such as the condition of the house/household assets, health, education, income level, and family reputation. A higher number represents a higher score. For example, a ""3 out of 3"" on education would mean that the borrower has graduated from university; a ""2 out of 3"" = secondary/high-school, and a ""1 out of 3"" would mean that the borrower is uneducated.  For more information on this score, please see SPBD's partner page at: http://partners.kiva.org/about/aboutPartner?id=15"  About SPBD In 2000, Greg Casagrande founded SPBD and since then, it has expanded from the main island of Upolu in Samoa to Savaii, as well as Tonga. SPBD's philosophy of lending is based upon the Grameen Bank lending method.  Please join SPBD's lending team on KIVA to receive on-the-spot updates on SPBD: http://www.kiva.org/community/viewTeam?team_id=8375

name: Sok
description: Sok S. is 41 years old and lives with her husband in Phnom Penh. Since 2005, she has been making and selling detergent at the local market to earn a living. She is able to make a profit of about US $4.00 every day. Her husband is a bus driver for a private company. On average, he is able to make US $2.00 in profits each day. Sok S. is asking for a loan of US $1000.00 to purchase materials to make detergent.

name: Kankelen Group
description: The four members of the Kankelen group are married and living in polygamous families. The average 43 years of age, with three children. They all live in the Togo village in the Segou Region (the fourth administrative region of Mali) and know each other as neighbors and relatives by blood or marriage. They retail cereals,  gourds, firewood,  mortars and pestles.   In order to expand their working capital, the group members have decided to collaborate with Soro Yiriwaso and are no on their 7th solidarity loan. Mrs. Mamou (the one standing on the far left in the photo) is a real artist known in her village and the nearby region for engraving gourds, mortars and pestles. She plans to use her loan to buy 30 mortars and 30 pestles. She will then engrave them with beautiful designs and slogans, as per her clients' wishes, using a cutting tool heated on the fire. She sells for cash and on credit, out of her home and in various areas of Segou, as a street vendor, to a customer base consisting mainly of women. Thanks to this loan, Mrs. Mamou hopes to earn an average monthly revenue of 35,000 West African francs, which will be used to reinvest in her business and provide for her children’s healthcare expenses.

name: Hearty
description: Hearty is driven by passion in selling. At the age of 53, she is married. In Plaridel, she runs a bakery that primarily supports her family. Every day she never gets tired tending her store.    Hearty is a full-fledged member of PMPC and has taken several loans already. She religiously paid her obligations without records of default. Now, she borrowed another loan to pay for inventory of sugar and milk for her bakery business. Having enough inventory would mean income opportunities. In the future, she dreams of sustaining her store to continuously provide for her family.

name: Susan
description: Susan lives in Kitale. Kitale is located in the Trans-Nzoia district of western Kenya, and at over 6,300 feet above sea level, is one of Africa’s most elevated towns. The rich soil of the area makes it one of the nation's biggest maize-producing regions, lending it the nickname of “the breadbasket of Kenya.” Many farmers in the region have started projects planting bluegum trees on their land, which complement the region’s natural forests and provide bees with a variety of food sources. The people around Kitale have been beekeeping for centuries, and the area is dense with strong bee colonies.  Susan is married and has two children. She is the women's leader in her local church. She also does farming with her husband. They have been farming for twenty-four years now, and they are currently growing vegetables, bananas, tea, and fodder. Susan is excited about beekeeping, as it will earn her some income from the sale of honey and provide her with honey for food and medicine.  This is Susan's first loan with Honey Care. She plans to use the proceeds from her beehives to support one of her children, who is unable to speak. Susan's hope for the future is to have her children educated and to live a better life.

name: Ankadjidia 1 De (Ankadjidia De Zoha) Group
description: The 10 women of the ANKADJIDIA 1 group are all married and live in Zoha, a village in the Sous-Prefecture of Fakola, Prefecture of Kolondièba in the third region (Sikasso) of the Republic of Mali. They have an average age of 28 and 3 children each on average, and they live in polygamous families. They met due to bonds of kinship and neighborhood.   When Soro Yiriwaso began to give rural loans which correspond to their work as farmers, these women seized the opportunity. They are on their fourth rural loan, and the three preceding ones were correctly reimbursed.   They want to use this new loan to pay for plowing and weeding, and to buy seeds, fertilizer, and herbicides. They want to plant 7 hectares of peanuts, rice, and millet. These women hope to have an average harvest of 2 tons per hectare, or 14 tons in all. A part of the harvest will be sold in the various weekly markets and the rest destined for consumption.   The profit on their sales (estimated at 55,000 F CFA per woman at the end of the growing season) will be used to reimburse the interest on the loan, cover school fees, for the health of their children, and for buying wedding trousseaus for their daughters.    Translated from French by Teresa Kramer, Kiva Volunteer

name: Juan
description: Juan needs the loan to buy electrical goods for repair, and so have a variety of merchandise to sell his customers.  Juan has been repairing and selling electrical goods for more than 15 years.   He has a permanent shop where he carries on his business, and in addition, on the weekends he sells in different parts of the city. This how he covers his household and personal expenses.  Juan has had four loans with Kiva, which he paid off on time, and he hopes to have your cooperation in this loan.

name: Maria Lourdes
description: Maria is 31 years old.  She is a hardworking woman who has a small store in which she sells basic necessities such as rice, beans, canned goods, beverages, and other products.  Maria has many aspirations for her business and wants to increase the inventory of merchandise in her store.  She begins her work very early and manages the store by herself.  Maria wants to continue working in the future and acquire merchandise to keep her store well-stocked.  With this loan, she wants to buy rice, beverages, canned goods, and other products.

name: Gemma
description: Gemma is a hardworking entrepreneur who has a business buying and selling spices in the Philippines. Gemma has been in this business for 16 years. She earns additional income from selling gasoline.  She is borrowing PHP 29,500 through NWTF to purchase additional spices to sell.  Gemma has been sustaining her business activities through her own efforts with the help of the loans from NWTF. She dreams to save enough money so she could afford to send her children to college in the future.

name: Lobo Group
description: The LOBO group is made up of 4 women, all of whom are married, and 35 years old on average, with 5 children. They live in nuclear families in the town of Yanfolila. They met via neighbours, friends and business. In order to boost their working capital and better run their businesses, they joined the Soro Yiriwaso microfinance institution, with whom they are on their third loan. The two previous loans have been successfully repaid. This group of women sells various items via Ina who is the woman sitting down on the left in the photo. She aims to use her loan in order to purchase various items from Yanfolila's wholesalers for her shop. She sells her wares for cash or credit at the market to a mixed customer base.  She aims to generate an average monthly profit of 25,000 FCFA which will be reinvested into her business, and used to repay the loan.

name: Juliet
description: Juliet is a 26-year-old married woman with three children living in Kagadi, Uganda.  She is a teacher by profession and has been in service for a period of one year.    She also deals in spare parts, a business she started by using the savings from her salary.  Juliet is requesting a loan to buy spare parts for resale.  She says price fluctuations and inadequate capital are the main factors hindering this business.    In the future, Juliet would like to educate her children, upgrade her studies and build a permanent house.

name: Twizigire Group
description: Mathieu is a member of Twizigire Group and lives in Gitega. He is 72 years old and is married to Victoire, a farmer. They have two children together, one 12 years old and the other 15. Mathieu has been selling cow and goat hides for 40 years.Mathieu is on his sixth loan from Turame. With this Kiva loan, he will increase his capital and purchase a large quantity of cow and goat skins to sell in order to earn more.

name: Ann Joy
description: Ann Joy is a 26-year-old married woman from Agusan del Sur. She has a 6-year-old child whom she loves taking care of. She has dreams for her family, which she is eager to achieve. She is involved in rice farming and currently owns a hectare of rice field. She says her rice crops need some supplies in order to grow healthy. She requested a loan of 10,000 PHP from CEVI, which she will use to purchase the necessary supplies for her farm.

name: Patria
description: Patria is 72 years old, and married with six children. Patria is in the agricultural business, raising livestock in the Philippines. Patria requested a 15,000 PHP loan through NWTF in order to buy feeds and other supplies to raise her livestock.  Patria has been raising livestock for 40 years now, and has borrowed 26 times in the past from NWTF to sustain it. In the future, Patria would like to save enough money to expand her business and support the financial stability of her family.

name: Phương
description: Mrs Phương is 49 years old and she is married.  She has operated a food stall/restaurant selling fish for more than 10 years. Phương lives in Hoang Hoa district, a  rural town in Thanh Hoa province. Her family is a low-income household in village, moreover this region often suffered by natural disasters such as storms because it is near the sea.   One of the most critical difficulties that concerns her is not having clean water to drink. She is requesting a loan to purchase clean water filter machine . This is Phương first loan with Thanh Hoa microfinance institution.  With her business profit, Phương hopes for her business to do well, to maintain  a successful business, and to be able to buy more supplies and equipment for her business.

name: Sofia
description: Sofia, 72, lives in Dicoloc, Jimenez, Misamis Occidental. She is married with four adult children.   Sofia is engaged in cooking and vending snacks, particularly sweet potato and banana cue (fritters). She has also been engaged in the dressmaking business for five years and earns approximately 5,000 Philippine pesos each month from her business activity.   Sofia has been a member of Paglaum Multi-Purpose Cooperative for almost five years. She has requested a loan to purchase additional stock of sweet potatoes, bananas, sugar and oil for her cue cooking and vending business.  In the future, she hopes to expand her cooking and vending business.

name: Les Gédéons Group
description: The client Apoline has been a merchant for the past three years and is member of "Les Gideons" business association. A dynamic 56-year-old entrepreneur, she is married and the mother of 12 children, four of whom are in school and the others are already grown.  She sells a variety of manufactured items and is shareholder of a store. She is requesting a loan from Hekima to increase her business. She started with funds received from her husband, who is a teacher in a local school.  She will buy soap, boxes of sweets, biscuits, sugar, rice, oil, soap powders, cosmetics, one box of notebooks, five boxes of pens, matches, iodized salt, etc.  In the future, she plans to build her house, educate and feed her children. So she thanks Hekima for its support to women entrepreneurs excluded from the traditional banking system.

name: Yolanda
description: .Yolanda is 37 years old. She is a woman who is hard-working and purposeful and has a great will to advance. Her partner is Wilder, with whom she has five daughters: Jennifer, 15, Tania, 12, Dalixa, 9, Olga, 7, and Vanesa, 5. They live together in their own house.  Her work is making and selling indigenous handicrafts (blankets, skirts, necklaces, and other items), which she makes at home and sells as a walking vendor in the tourist plaza; tourists are her principal customers. She has the help of her older daughters, who help her in the preparation and sale of the handicrafts. She began more than 4 years ago, learning this business from her mother. She considers her business profitable because of the good earnings that it leaves her to pay the household expenses and help her husband. What she doesn't like is that it is tiring to have to walk every day looking for customers; for that reason, she would like to rent a shop where she would have everything ready to be seen.  This is her fifth loan with the MFP institution, so she hopes to meet her goals. In addition to getting along well in her community bank, since she was able to note that it is a united group, she hopes that they will continue in the same way.  With the 1200 PEN that she has applied for, she will invest in the purchase of materials to make tablecloths with indigenous designs, necklaces, bracelets, and other articles that she sells.

name: Teresita
description: Teresita is 43 years old and married with five children. She earns a living by fattening pigs in the Philippines. She has been in this business for one year and also earns additional income from farming rice.  She is borrowing PHP 10,000 through NWTF to purchase additional feeds. Teresita is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save money to expand her business.

name: Mercedes
description: Mercedes, age 49, lives with her husband.  They have four children between the ages of 16 and 30.  She started her business when she left Buenaventura, the most important seaport in the Pacífico Colombiano region.  She arrived in the city to look for better ways of living peacefully and productively for her family.  Mercedes had acquired store experience in her native land.  Once she moved to Barranquilla, she took it up again.  She turned it into her way of generating income.  She was supported by her family, and she was very well-received.   Her goal is to manage complete sustainability in her business.  To do so, she needs to grow at the same rate as her clientele.  However, she does not have enough inventory to respond to her customers with the merchandise that turns over the most.    This is exactly the reason she turns to a Kiva loan.  This is her second loan with the Fundación Mario Santo Domingo.  With the previous one she bought groceries, snacks, and vegetables in greater volume in order to get discounts.  This capitalized her business a little more.  Now she will look to make it more profitable because she has added cell phone plans and recharges, which means a new income for her.   She intends to use part of her Kiva loan to strengthen her communications business by adding new cell plans and recharges.  This is exactly what she will do so that her Kiva loan will be potentially successful.  This is because it will gradually impact the growth of her store with a new service.  She will use the other part of her loan to pay for her daughter’s semester at the university.  This is why Mercedas says to her lenders, “Thank you for the support.  In my situation of not being from this place, I am managing to get ahead with my family, and this is thanks to Kiva.”

name: Warmin Antawipa Group
description: The “WARMIN ANTAWIPA” communal bank will begin its third cycle in Pro Mujer, as a part of the Centro Villa Exaltación. It is made up of eleven members and led by a board of directors headed by Mónica. The businesses that the association members have are various. Among them, we have:  a store and an employment agency, a beauty shop, DVD and CD sales, selling fruit, selling pastries, selling candies, a variety store, selling cosmetics, selling paints, and a book store.   Mónica indicates that she has been a member of Pro Mujer for seven months, on the invitation of older members. At present, she has had a business organizing parties for seven years.  The loan she will now take out is to grow her business, since she is going to include pastry-making. She will buy an oven, which she will acquire from La Ceja and she will sell from her store. This type of work will allow her to generate income to support her family as much as possible. She is married and has a son.     When asked what she likes about Pro Mujer, she responds that she likes the meetings.   In the photograph, Gary does not appear due to cultural reasons.

name: Luis Angel
description: Luis, age 32, studied until first grade. He didn't have the opportunity to continue studying. He lives with his partner, who devotes herself to the household duties.  Together they have 7 children, three of whom are studying.Luis has been selling bread for 6 years. A nephew who did the same work taught it to him, and from then on, he decided to sell bread. He gets up at 4:00 in the morning in order to go to the bakery and go out to sell in the neighboring cantons.  He makes his sales in two trips: one shift is from 4:30 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. and one is in the afternoon, from 3:00 to 5:00 p.m.The loan that he is requesting is for the purchase of a replacement part for his motorcycle, as he needs it to be in good condition because that is what he uses for his work selling the bread.Luis's dream is to have his own bakery, because it's a good business.

name: Israa
description: Israa is well known in her region with the good quality she provides in her business with affordable set prices. A 20-year-old married mother of one child, she started her home based clothes selling business two years ago to support her husband in making their living and to improve their child’s social and financial situation.  Israa is working hard to increase her business capital to make sure that she can acquire a good income which will help her in establishing her separate clothes selling shop outside her house. She is acquiring a YOUTH loan from Kiva's field partner Al Majmoua, to increase her business merchandise with specialized mother, children and baby winter and spring collection clothing.  This is Israa's first experience as an Al Majmoua borrower. She is looking forward to future cooperation to expand her working sector.

name: Bona Nathalie Mariam's Group
description: This group consists of two members in a joint guarantee. Bona Nathalie Mariam, the manager, is 34-years old, married, and mother of one 10-year old child who attends a neighborhood school. She has sold yam flour, corn, and onions for five years.  She restocks at one of the markets in Benin. In order to strengthen her working capital and to satisfy customer demand, she asked for and obtained financing from Finadev to increase her additional income and to contribute to the education of her children. The manager is on the left of the photo.

name: Somean's Group
description: A mother of four children who are students in a local primary school, Somean is 43 years old. She is a farmer who grows rice and vegetables. Having been in her current business for 25 years, she earns up to 23,000 KHR per day. This is not the first loan for Somean with VisionFund (Kiva’s partner). She repaid her past loan wisely, and it enabled her to upgrade her living status. For now, she is taking out a loan with her co-borrower in the amount of 1,000,000 KHR each. Somean will spend her loan portion to buy fertilizer for her farmland. She hopes to increase her income and make a good living.

name: Marissa
description: Marissa is 30 years old and married with three children who are in school.  She works hard to provide for her family. She runs a general store in the Philippines and requested a PHP 10,000 loan through NWTF to buy items to sell such as shampoo, groceries, etc.  Marissa has borrowed and paid 9 loans from NWTF before this loan. She has been running the general store for 4 years and also earns an income from seaweed cultivation.  She aspires to save enough money so she can afford to send her children to college.

name: Estela Raquel
description: Estela is 22 years old, she is partnered, her partner is a farmer and also works as a bricklayer. They have a 4-year-old daughter.  Estela takes care of the household tasks and also supports her partner with the agricultural crops, to allow him to be able to work, to be able to bring sustenance to the home since he also works in construction.  Estela needs the loan to fix the roof on her house, since winter is approaching and the roof is damaged and has many leaks and the wood is no longer good. With the help of the loan, she will manage to provide better security for her family.   Estela wants to be able to provide the necessary education for her little daughter.

name: Jardin De Las Lomas Group
description: This group is called “Jardin de Las Lomas” (Garden of the Little Hills), which is also the name of the community where they live.  The group consists of four people and their business activities are noted below:  -	Sofia L. sells soft drinks. -	Rafaela R. sells handicrafts. -	Maria Guadalupe sells shoes through a catalog. -	Maria Isabel L. sells clothing.  Sra. Sofia L. S. is married and has five children.  Their names are David, Maria del Rosario, Joaquin, Josue, and Evelin.  She sells soft drinks out of her home as well as a few groceries since there are no stores nearby, otherwise her neighbors who have to move to the central part of town since they live in an isolated area.  Sofia believes she has a good business that generates sufficient income.  With this loan, she will buy soft drinks of all flavors and sizes.  In addition, Sofia plans to purchase some sugar, eggs, milk, and powdered soap to sell so that her children can get ahead.  She says she feels at ease with her group since they are genuine people who are talented and punctual with their loan payments.  Sofia is grateful to Fundacion Realidad and Kiva for giving everyone the opportunity to know her group and supporting them in their continued success.Translated from Spanish by Ronan Reodica, Kiva Volunteer

name: Dora
description: Dora, 49, has two minor children in her care.  She lives in her own house with her spouse and children in Motupe District, Lambayeque Department.  They have electricity and they get their water from artesian wells.  Dora’s main activity is raising turkeys, ducks, chickens, sheep and goats to sell.  She feeds them nutritionally balanced feed (corn, ‘polvillo’ [made from rice], etc.) and when they reach exact size and weight she sells them to local wholesalers.  She’s been in this line of work for ten years and she has well-established customers in the zone.  The amount of the loan granted will be 1500 new soles to buy turnkeys, ducks and chickens to have better income for her home and thus be able to improve her quality of life.   She doesn’t have much competition in this line of work in the area because she already has a well-established clientele.

name: Fatema
description: Fatema is a young Palestinian woman who is married with two children.  Fatema’s husband used to work in Israel but after the closure they decided to open their own business. Two years ago they started this sewing workshop and currently they have five sewing machines. They both work in the workshop. They obtain cut cloth which they sew, in addition to making special designs upon request.  Fatema requested 2,000 USD from FATEN to buy some cloth and to buy a new sewing machine. They hope that after the loan they will hire a new employee to help them in the workshop.  Fatemah and her husband appear in the photo at their workshop.

name: Derick
description: Derick is a twenty-six-year-old hardworking man living in Kasese, Uganda. He has a number of businesses such as poultry raising, a video library a and  mechanic's and spare parts shop all located in town. He says that if he had enough money he would like to have over 2000 chicks, a modern garage and an entertainment centre. He has challenges of poultry diseases and high cost of feed. Derick intends to use the loan to buy poultry feed and more chicks.

name: Roseline's Group
description: Roseline, pictured above, has been a farmer for more than 20 years and is now proud to represent her group of 12 farmers in Teso District. She is 45 years old, is married and has nine children.  Roseline likes to think of herself as a very reliable person. She has been working alongside One Acre Fund since 2014 and decided to represent her group because she wanted to be more active in her community. She says that being part of the One Acre Fund community has meant that she has been able to consistently feed her family. Roseline plans to use the profits from this coming season to send her children to school.  In total, Roseline’s Group will receive inputs to cultivate 5.5 acres of land. Given that some members of the group will also be purchasing a solar light with this loan, the group will also receive a total of eight solar lights.

name: Fokognouma 4 Group
description: Most of the ten female members of Fokognouma 4 Group of Samako are married and live in large traditional families. They average 37 years of age and three children. They all live in Samako, Koulikoro Region (second administrative region of Mali) and got acquainted through ties of kinship, marriage, and community  In order to have farm inputs available at the start of the planting season, they decided to work with Kiva's partner, the MFI Soro Yiriwaso, from which they are seeking their third farming loan. The members are going to grow peanuts, rice, okra, and black-eyed peas.  Mrs. Sitan (sitting on the left in the photograph) intends to use her loan to buy 50 kg of peanut seeds and hire the village's young people's association to carry out plowing and weeding work. She gets her supplies of seeds from the fair in Bancoumana.  With an area of one hectare, she intends to harvest 30 sacks of peanuts. One part will be sold to pay her children's school expenses, the other part will be consumed by her family.

name: Teresita
description: Teresita is 36 years old and married with four children.  She earns a living by farming rice in the Philippines. Teresita is borrowing PHP 11000 through NWTF to purchase fertilzer and other farm supplies.  Teresita has been farming rice for 18 years and also earns additional income from selling vegetables.  She is working tirelessly toward the attainment of her dream: to save money to expand her business.

name: Sauni
description: Sauni, a 50-year-old married mother of five, is a peasant farmer involved in the growing of cassavas, pineapples and bananas, an enterprise she has been operating for the last 30 years as a source of income to look after her family. Her major challenges are the changing weather patterns and price fluctuations of agricultural products.  Sauni is requesting a loan of 1,500,000 shillings to complete the construction of her residential home so that her family can have a decent living environment. Her dream is to advance her agricultural business to a commercial level and thereby enjoy a good financial return.

name: Karina
description: Karina, 27, is single and the mother of two small children.  She also has her own house where she has set up a display case to show her merchandise.  Karina's job is selling cosmetics and perfume products such as talcum powder, deodorant, perfume, cologne, and other things.  Her customers are located on different streets throughout the city and are mainly family members, neighbors, and friends.  Karina has worked under a system of credit for four years.    She likes her job because it allows her to be constantly active during the day and generate her own income.  She hopes to continue working this way so she can set up a grocery store in her house in the future.  This time she'll request 600 soles [PEN] to buy cosmetics such as eye shadow, body lotion, talcum powder, and others.  She promises to make her loan payments very punctually.

name: Adelaida
description: Adelaida is a diligent farmer. She tills her rice field with her husband. At 60, she is still strong enough to take care of her farm. She was able to produce 70 sacks on her last harvest. She aims to produce more on the next cropping. To achieve that, she has applied for a loan of 10,000 PHP from CEVI. She will use this loan to purchase fertilizer and other supplies that her farm needs. Adelaida is positive that this loan can help her achieve her goals.

name: Cecilia
description: Cecilia is a hardworking entrepreneur who has earned a living for the past 36 years by running a general store in the Philippines. She has requested a loan for PHP 29,000 through NWTF to buy items such as shampoo and groceries to sell to her customers. In addition to running her store, Cecilia earns money on the side from fishing and pig fattening. She has sustained her business through her own hard work and with the help of loans from NWTF. She dreams of saving enough money to expand her business and continue sending her children to school.

name: Muchakata Group
description: Greetings from Zimbabwe! This is 31-year-old Lovemore from Masvingo. He is married with one child who attends school.  Lovemore runs a retail business selling sugar beans, dried fish and soya meat. The business has been in operation for 10 years. He says the main challenge he faces is high transport costs. Lovemore has requested a loan of $400 to buy sugar beans, dried fish and soya mincemeat. He says the extra income generated as a result of this loan will allow him to be able to take care of his family. In the future, Lovemore plans to own a shop in Masvingo Central Business District.

name: Sem
description: Sem P. is 54 years old and lives in Phnom Penh with her husband and their 3 children.  Her husband earns $3/day as a construction worker, while 2 of her children work with their father and each make $2/day.  The recycling system in Phnom Penh is not very organized, and consists of people buying and reselling plastic/paper/metal and other recyclables until they finally reach a place (and bulk quantity) where they will actually be recycled.  Sem P. will use this loan to buy recyclable products and resell them in bulk for a small profit.  In the future, she feels she can use CREDIT to have the ability to buy larger quantities and make more money.  She hopes to earn enough to send all of her children to high school.

name: David
description: David is a married man. He has four children. He describes himself as determined. He operates a retail business where he sells clothes and bags. He has been involved in this business for two years. His business is located in a busy area and his primary customers are locals. He describes his biggest business challenge as inadequate working capital. He will use the KES 20,000 loan to buy  more stock of clothes. He hopes that in the future, he will be prosperous. This is his second loan with SMEP Microfinance Bank. He repaid the previous loan successfully. He will use the anticipated profits to pay school fees.

name: Sameang
description: Mrs. Sameang S. (in the photo) and her husband, Mr. Sokcheat Keun, live on an island in the Mekong River about 15 kilometers from Phnom Penh, the capital city of Cambodia. They have been married since 2005 and have two children: one son and one daughter. Both of the children are in school. Sameang is a weaver. She also invests with her parents in a rice farming business. Her husband is a security guard. She is asking for a loan of $300 to purchase seed, fertilizer and pesticide to maintain her rice farm.

name: Lucy
description: Lucy is a 29 year old business lady. She is married to Josphat who is a P.V.S driver. They are blessed with one child, aged 12 years.   Lucy has been running green grocer business in an open air market for the past ten years with the monthly income of KES 10,000, which she uses to support her family. She has applied for her second loan term from KADET LTD., after repaying the previous loan successfully. Lucy will use the loan to buy vegetables and fruits to add to her stock.    With the anticipated profit from the business, Lucy will expand the business by renting a house. Her hopes are to open a retail shop, to educate her child up to university level and to improve the living standards of her family.

name: Binta
description: This is 51-year-old Binta. She is a widow and has three children, ages 12, 20, and 22. She has one additional dependent who lives with her to help with the household chores.  In 1994, Binta established her business selling provisions and beverages. She began her business because she wanted to be self-reliant after losing her husband. Her business is located in the outskirts and her main customers are adults. Working 7 days a week and 12 hours a day, she earns about 2,000,000 SLL every month from this business.   She would like a loan in the amount of 5,000,000 SLL. Binta has already received and successfully repaid six loans. She now requires a new loan in order to buy additional drinks. She hopes that this loan can improve her inventory and increase her profits. In the future, Binta plans to expand the business to wholesale. She thanks you for your support.

name: Marcial
description: Marcial is 35 years old and lives in the city of Nazca, Ica, Peru. Nazca is a city whose inhabitants are very generous and hospitable. It has a cultural heritage: as Peruvians, we are very proud of this city since it has the Nazca Lines. They were drawn over extensive fields and were used by the Nazca culture in its agriculture; they are a type of calendar whereby one could determine when the rainy season might arrive. Because of these majestic lines, the city welcomes an infinity of tourists every year.   Marcial only studied up to the 6th grade of primary. His parents had few economic resources. He would have liked to study music in a center or specialized school, since music is his life and his work tool.   Marcial is an example of struggle, evidence that when one desires to get ahead, come what may, it can be achieved. Some years ago, Marcial suffered a terrible accident while traveling with his wife. She lost her life and he nearly became blind; he still has very poor vision. As a result, he was left a widower with a son to care for but he has advanced despite adversity. This demonstrates that, at times, we lack awareness that there are people who need more help than we do. With effort and dedication, and especially, much love of life, he struggles every day without tiring or giving up.  At present, Marcial is committed to the music business, composing, especially, Peruvian folkloric music. He also performs his music at events and concerts which he presents throughout his city, which he does very well, despite his limited vision. He travels to diverse parts of the city to give his concerts, and does so alongside his faithful companion, friend and right hand, his son, who would give his life and struggle against all and everyone, to see his father happy. Marcial works around 15 hours a week, depending on how many events he schedules. They usually occur on weekends. Marcial earns around 700 new sols a week and in a good week he can earn up to 1,500 new sols. He comments that his business is doing well because God is on his side every day, as He was at the time of the accident, since Marcial is alive and can care for his son who at that time was very small; also because despite not seeing very well, he can play music with feeling and, therefore, very beautifully. Also, he is much appreciated by his clients and they often recommend him owing to his good work and punctuality.  Marcial gives thanks to God and to Kiva investors for the help he has received, since thanks to them, he can now make a publicity video to deliver to Peru's TV networks. With that, he will become known at the national level and give more monthly concerts and earn more income, enabling him to continue saving to achieve his dream: to travel to Cuba for an operation to recover his sight, then continue struggling for a good life and, most of all, to see his son become a professional that he can be proud of.

name: Afi
description: Afi K., 24, is still single and has no children. She has a shop where she sells "pagnes" (lengths of African print cloth) and high-quality fabrics in the big open-air market of  Lomé, the Togolese capital. In order to keep track of her sales better, she has bought a small computer on which she keeps her accounts. She has been working in this sector for two years and hopes to expand her business further by buying merchandise for re-sale. Translated from French by Teresa Kramer, Kiva Volunteer

name: Lenny
description: Lenny needs a loan to pay for the paperwork that will allow her to work at her own law firm. She is divorced. She pays rent. Lenny is starting to have more clients so it is very important for her if you help her again. She works hard. She is healthy and she likes to have people with legal problems.

name: Elvira
description: Elvira is 54 years old.  She has been married for a long time and lives in her own home in the city of Encarnación.  She has been working as a shopkeeper for long time.  She has a well-stocked grocery store in her home where she sells food and drinks.  She also has a volleyball court.  Elvira tells us that her business is doing very well because she has good customers and is well known in her area for her good customer service and the good prices she offers.  Thanks to her work, she is able to maintain her household and cover any out-of-pocket expenses.  Elvira is requesting this loan to buy basic household products for her business such as yerba mate, sugar, canned food, meat, drinks, etc.  She is grateful for the help that she is receiving as it will be very useful to her.

name: Ameena
description: Ameena, 39, is a responsible mother who lives happily in the area of Lahore, Pakistan. This is her sixth loan with BRAC and the first with Kiva.   Her husband owns a scrap shop and deals with scrap iron, aluminum, plastic bottles, and other items. He purchases scrap goods from the common people and sells them to recycling factories. Nowadays, due to household expenses, he does not have cash in hand to buy scrap goods and does not have scrap to sell to generate money.  Therefore, Ameena requested a loan for her husband, so that he can buy scrap goods, establish his enterprise, and make some savings to meet sudden needs or incidents.   She is very impressed with this honorable support and wishes to take more loans after the payment of this loan. She thanks Kiva and its field partner, BRAC Pakistan.

name: Mouniatou
description: Mrs. Mouniatou Y. was born around 1972 in Aneho, in the south of Togo. She has been living in Benin for about 10 years. She is responsible for 3 children, of whom Afi, the youngest, age 9, is in school. Married to Mr. Adjanakou Abou, a night-time guard working in Cotonou, Mrs. Y. sells rice on a street corner in her neighborhood. She is requesting this loan in order to offer her customers a more varied selection of dishes. Translated from French by Teresa Kramer, Kiva Volunteer

name: Sơn
description: Sơn is 30 years old, married, and has two 2 children. Sơn lives in Hoang Hoa district, a rural town in Thanh Hoa province. Sơn works in agriculture, farming poultry and cattle. Sơn has been involved in this business for six years.  This is Sơn's first loan with Thanh Hoa Fund of Poor Women. One of the most critical difficulties that concerns her is not having a water tank. She is requesting a loan to purchase sand, cement and brick to build a toilet.  Sơn hopes to make enough money to provide for her kids, to maintain a successful business, and for her family to be healthy and happy.

name: Petronilla Mueni
description: Petronilla Mueni is a 25-year-old grocery store owner who lives and works in the village of Voi. She is a single mother with one child.  She has run her store for one year and is doing very well. Petronilla is applying for her first loan from KADET and plans to use it to buy more potatoes, oranges, cabbage, onions, tomatoes and kale to sell to her customers. She will use the additional income she earns to pay for the education of her child.

name: Victoria
description: Victoria is a member of Village Bank El Sembrador. She and her live-in partner have three children, now adult and married. Victoria is a nurse by profession, and worked in many diffferent hospitals. She was laid off due to recession, however, and had to find work independently. Seven years ago she began selling breakfast, and gets up at 5 in the morning to begin preparation.   Since joining the bank Victoria's business has improved, allowing her to buy items like shelves and tables for her business, in order to provide better service to her customers. Victoria requires a loan of 1600 soles in order to purchase supplies - rice, sugar, milk, and legumes -  to prepare breakfasts. Victoria hopes to continue succeeding in order to leave a well established business to her children.  Translated from Spanish by Emily Martyn, Kiva Volunteer

name: Victoria
description: Victoria is 45 years old and has an incomplete elementary school education to fifth grade, due to her parents’ lack of sufficient resources for her to continue.  In time she married and she and her husband had six children, one is two years old and another is 18 months old.  The oldest is 29 and studied to sixth grade and in time married and has a daughter, she and her husband later separated and now she helps her parents in the fields.  The next oldest is 24 years old and only studied to fifth grade because he didn’t like school and decided to work with his father.  He and his wife now have an 18 month old son and at they live with their mother.  The next one is 13 years old, recently completed elementary school, and will continue his schooling the following year.  Like his siblings, he is also involved in raising coffee.  Victoria has 2.5 plots in production, which she got through her own effort and which are located 6 km from her home.  She walks there and they transport the harvested grains by pack animal.  Her children are also involved in the field activities since they are a very close family.  Her challenges are the drop in coffee prices and that the wholesaler will not pay a fair price.  Victoria has a goal of improving the state of her coffee crops by planting a better and greater variety.  In this way she can increase her production and income so that she can continue to provide for her children’s wellbeing.  She is asking for a loan to buy farming supplies so she can help her crops and prevent damage, drying out, blights, or disease.

name: Maritza
description: Maritza is 38 years old, works independently.  She has been working as a receptionist and promoter of puppet shows, inflatable games, and other things on the weekend for nine years.  She also sells merchandise such as women’s shoes and  generates the income she needs to help her husband with the household expenses.  Her labor is arduous and she put forth lots of physical effort, because she must carry lots of material to do her work, however this motivates her to forge ahead.  She hopes to have her own means of transportation in the near future that will make it easier to move her things faster and more comfortably.  She is asking for this loan to buy supplies (fabric, thread, nylon, etc.), and stock up on items (shoes, blouses, jeans, sandals, etc.) so she can offer more for the December season.  This will allow her to have more supplies in stock to make puppets for each show and she will also be able to provide more complete service and increase her income.

name: Mwanasha
description: Mwanasha is married and has eight children, two of whom are in school and the rest of whom are adults. She owns a house that has neither electricity nor piped water. Her greatest monthly expense is food for the family.  Mwanasha has operated a fish-selling business at the market for the past three years, selling from home to her neighbors and passersby. Her major challenge is seasonality in her business.  Mwanasha is requesting a loan to purchase bundles of fish for resale. She decided to join Yehu to access loans at lower cost to improve her business

name: Eufronia
description: Eufronia is a farmer from Lawa-an, Oroquieta City. She accesses her financial assistance for her farming business from Paglaum MPC, where she is an active member. She's doing well through this activity and has sent her children to school. Recently, she availed a loan to purchase bags of fertilizers.

name: Rachael
description: Racheal is married and has 2 children. They live at Ankyernyin near Takoradi.  Rachael used to sell cooked beans and gari but now, for 2 years, she has been selling clothing like jeans and men & ladies underwear.   She uses her income to support hre husband to feed and cloth their children.  Rachael will use her loan to purchase more jeans, ladies and men underware to sell.  With the new profit from her expanded business, Rachael wishes to acquire a shop to sell her goods.

name: Ashurhon
description: On the photo you see the daughter of Ashurhon. Ashurhon is working and her children are looking after the livestock. Ashurhon is 44 years old, married and has three children. Besides her main job she is an entrepreneur - she buys and sells cattle. She does not have a lack of fodder because she has though of it beforehand and made sure to stock up in advance and has small overhead. This is her first loan at MicroInvest and she plans to use the loan to buy a calf.Translated from Russian by Elena Fedorchuk, Kiva Volunteer

name: Naziran Hameed Masih Group
description: "My name is Naziran and I’m a 38-year-old married lady.  I reside in a place called Kot Radha Kishan which is 24 km from the city of Kasur, Pakistan. I own a two-room brick house and have been living in it for the past 18 years. My husband's name is H. M. and he works as a cook in an army office. I’ve six kids: four sons and two daughters. My first two sons are daily wage laborers. The others don't have any work right now. My daughters help me sell milk. We get up early and milk the buffalo,  then we transfer the milk into milk pots and go to the shops to sell milk. This work earns us Pak rupees 3000 per month. I am requesting a loan to expand my milk-selling business by buying another buffalo.   I am the group leader for two more women. Anayatan baji and Asia baji each want a loan to buy a donkey cart to transport loads."   This is a group loan. The loan funds will be distributed among the group members, each of whom will invest in her own business. The members mutually guarantee one another's loans. If one member does not repay, the other members are responsible.

name: Esther
description: Esther is a 47 year-old woman with four children, ages 27, 23, 20, and 17. She lives in Cusco with her spouse and two youngest children; the others have now left their childhood house and live on their own. Esther is a member of the community bank María Auxiliadora, which is comprised of eleven members all hailing from the Cusco region.   Esther makes a living running a tienda de abarrotes, or grocery store, in the San Sebastian neighborhood of Cusco. Here she sells staples such as eggs, rice, and pasta. She will use the loan as business capital for her store, buying items that she needs to sustain the enterprise. Esther is thankful for and appreciative of the loan, and promises to pay her monthly payments on time.

name: Maha
description: Maha, a 38-year-old conservative woman, asked her daughter to take her place in the photo.  Maha is a mother to four children. One of them is Aya, who is a 21-year-old single lady who is attending the university to study financial economics. Now Maha wants to support her daughter, so she has applied for a loan to pay for her daughter’s semester fees.

name: Sok
description: Mrs. Sok S. has been in the farming business for years. She plants various crops to earn a living and typically generates an income of over $3 per day. She is married, but her husband died of senility years ago. She has five children, all of whom are now married and live independently. Sok S. lacks money to buy a piece of farmland on which she plans to plant crops for additional income. Sok S. is therefore applying for a $300 loan to buy land.

name: Yolisa
description: Yoliza is 29 years old and lives with 39 year-old Román.  They have three children who fill them with satisfaction.  They live in their own home which is located in Pichari district.  Persistent and hard-working since she was a girl, Yoliza started out in this business, alongside her beloved parents, as an itinerant vendor.  Over time, she gathered together a good sum of money which helped her to open her own clothes store.  Yoliza is happy with the business that she runs because, thanks to the business, she is able to provide her three dependent children, who support her in making her sales, with a good education.  In the future, Yoliza would like to own a chain of stores but, in order to achieve this dream, she must work hard in order to gather together a good sum of money.  For this reason, she came to MFP to request her second loan and she pledges to make her repayments on time.  She hopes to receive the support of each and every one of you in helping her achieve her goals.  Yoliza will use the 2,000 Peruvian soles she has requested to acquire more clothes with which to stock her store.

name: Gulayim
description: Gulayim is 41 years old and married. Ten years ago, she was looking for a way to support her family and so began her cattle breeding business. Using 10,000 som (KGS) as starting capital to buy cattle, Gulayim was able to start her farm, which produces a monthly income of about 6,000 som (KGS). She makes additional income working as a hairdresser. In order to further develop her business, Gulayim turned to Bai-Tushum and Partners for a loan of 70,000 som (KGS) to buy cows and calves. With the profit she makes from this loan, Gulayim plans to increase her livestock in the near future.

name: Merlita
description: Being single and the sole provider of her 44-year-old mother and 15-year-old niece, Merlita M. has enjoyed being productive as a woman. In 2009, she joined ASHI and has received loans since then. Because of that opportunity, she was able to finance a small business vending/selling food. At first, the food she produced was being sold to people in her village. Through her hard work and determination to rise above poverty, along with her family, she tried to build up a savings fund from her small profit to sustain her business. Eventually, her business grew a bit. Now, she is renting a small stall at the public market to display food for sale.   With the loan she is requesting presently, Merlita wishes to increase the variety and amount of food she sells to supply the demands of her growing number of customers. Then her profit will also increase and she will be able to improve their lives little by little.

name: Em's Group
description: Em is 46 years old, married, and a villager residing in a rural village of Moung Russey district in Cambodia’s Battambang province. She is blessed with six children, three (daughters) of whom are dependent on her and currently in school. To make a living, Em and her husband have a rice farming business, with which they have been involved for 10 years. Em has been with VisionFund, Kiva’s partner, for a loan cycle already, which enabled her to improve the living condition of her family. Now Em is in need of money to support the family's rice-growing business. Thus, she is leading a group of three female members to apply for a loan in the amount of 3,400,000 KHR in total. Em will use her requested loan portion to support the current business by purchasing fertilizer and paying wages to farm laborers. After receiving and effectively using her requested loan portion, Em highly hopes that the rice field will provide higher and better crop yields so that she can sell them for greater profit. Em is willing to use the anticipated income to move her family ahead and advance her children’s education.

name: Unidos Al Futuro Group
description: Unidos al Futuro Group is made up of seven hardworking members who are in their eleventh loan cycle.  Sabina, 54, is married and has adult children.  She's the secretary of the group, having been elected by the members.  She set up her grocery store in her home years 10 years ago.  She used to work in communal banks in the area where she lives, so she was able to help her husband with her children's education when they were minors.  She'll invest the loan in buying rice, sugar, and oil.  Her greatest desire is to develop her business more so she can improve her family finances.  The group is grateful to the Kiva investors for the loan.  Sabina's the one wearing a black leather jacket.  At the upper left is the photo of Angélica, who couldn't attend the meeting because of work.

name: Constancia Daniel
description: Constância Catela E. was born in Maganja da Costa in the northern province of Mozambique.  She is 34 years old, married and the mother of three children aged 1, 7 and 12 years.  The two oldest children go to school.  She is in her third year at the faculty of pedagogical sciences at the Pedagogical University.  She lives in her own house with her family and a niece.  Her husband works for himself as a locksmith.  When she was still young, she left Zambezia for Maputo with her sister for the purposes of continuing with her studies.  Since then she has not returned again to Zambezia, as she later moved into her residence in the district of Boane, where she still lives today.  She has been a teacher for six years and works five hours a day, having graduated from IMAP-Matola (Institute of Elementary Education of Matola) seven years ago.  Currently, she receives a monthly salary of 5,676 MT, and saves some every month in the commercial bank BIM.  She has already had a loan from PROCREDIT (a Mozambican credit institution) in the amount of 50,000 MT, which was intended for the acquisition of a means of transportation, but she decided not to continue with it afterwards for various reasons.  She got to know about Hluvuku through a friend, and this is her first loan in the amount of 15,000 MT, with which she plans to buy bricks, stones, sand and other items.  She promises to repay the loan faithfully, since she plans to continue to ask for more money in order to be able to finish construction and then get furniture.  Translated from Portuguese by Heidi Petersen, Kiva Volunteer

name: Rosibel
description: Rosibel is an exemplary mother who works hard to give her children a good quality of life.  She sells clothing in a shop that she created in her house, and has a large number of customers who have motivated her to move ahead with this business.  He efforts have resulted in an increased number of customers, for which she needs a larger inventory in order to meet their needs.  She is requesting a loan of four hundred thousand colones (400,000) to buy merchandise and supply her business.

name: Emelia
description: Emelia is thankful that she was previously granted a 10000 PHP loan which she used to purchase various grocery items and products needed in her General Store. Through her earnings she is able to send her children to school and meet their daily living expenses.   She would now like to apply for a 20000 PHP loan which she will use as her working capital to buy more quantities of grocery items like rice, coffee, soda, rice noodles, and frozen foods which she sells at retail. She knows that more items in her store will yield more sales and thus increase her earnings. Her income from her store is a stable source to sustain her family's basic needs and for the education of her children. She is thanking God and you in advance for the financial help that will be given her.   Emelia dreams of having a bigger General Store and aims to give her children a College Education to allow them better opportunities in life. Every week, she meets up with her co-fellowship* members to share stories of her work and to draw strength and inspiration from the Word of God which she studies.  * All CCT community partners/clients are organized into fellowship groups composed of 15 to 30 community partners.
